local_offer: By embracing the Montessori and Forest School philosophies, along with our knowledge of child development, we support the holistic growth of each unique child and embrace their infinite potential. Our aim is to nurture emotional intelligence, encourage social responsibility and cultivate an attitude and skill set for each child to build a life they love.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We strive to ensure that all children and families feel welcome and valued as individuals. Our flexible curriculum brings out children's strengths and builds on those, and makes provision for extra time, support and care around any challenges. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We have a highly qualified team of staff incl a SENDCO and a BSL trained practitioner, who all undergo ongoing professional development to meet the needs of the children in our care. This includes SEND specific training such as Understanding Autism, Developing Good Autism Practice, SEND Code of Practice, and Speech and Language Development. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents and families into our setting and value their in put. Parents 'participate' as much as they want and are able, including contributing to their children's individual learning plans, setting development plans, and volunteering time at the nursery. We also have a strong parent education component with a parent coach supporting parents through education and Q&A sessions each term. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Information is shared both informally (chats at drop off and pick up) and formally, through our online record keeping system where parents receive photographs and observations of their children in the setting. All children have regular consultations and children with SEND will usually require more regular consultations so that we can monitor their needs and progress closely - celebrating successes and planning strategies for support and development together. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our classroom and garden is wheelchair accessible, but unfortunately, we are not in a purpose-built building and the bathrooms are not. Mobility needs need to be assessed on an individual basis to see if we can make accommodations. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please ask for more details on our admissions process. Renuka Rao, our Senco, would be happy to talk through things in more detail of our offering. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan that the whole team to continue to undertake additional SEND training. We are keen to continue to add resourses that suit individual needs of each child at our setting, especially in regards to SEND.

description: Boys' secondary school in Maidenhead, Berkshire 11 to 18-year-olds. From day one our students are supported to become independent learners and thinkers, and to develop their talents and abilities outside of the classroom. Outside of the classroom, our students enjoy a diverse enrichment programme, and are encouraged to become leaders, coaches, mentors, performers, and athletes throughout our school community. Our students are expertly supported and guided as they consider their future pathways, with a robust process in place to ensure that all options are explored and are accessible to all students. I’m confident that our ever-improving learning environment and resources, as well as a dedicated team of teachers, tutors, and support staff, makes Desborough College the ideal environment for our students to accomplish their goals. Should you like any further information, or would like to come and see our Sixth Form in action, please get in touch.

description: Desborough Recreation Ground (Wycombe). The recreation ground is an attractive and quiet area in this busy part of the town. It is bounded on both sides by the River Wye and benches are situated in various locations for people to sit and admire the views. The recreation ground is used mainly by children and parents using the popular play area. There are also two football pitches and three hard tennis courts. The tennis courts are free on a first come first serve basis. Dog walkers also use the area and they are reminded to clean up after their dogs by placing dog poop in the red bins provided. Co-operation in this scheme is appreciated as it helps keep our parks clean and safe for all users.

name: Everything Birth Baby Sleep- 1:1 Hypnobirthing, Antenatal, and Relaxation Sessions
description: At Everything Birth Baby Sleep, I offer personalised 1:1 Hypnobirthing, Antenatal, and Pregnancy Relaxation sessions designed to support you through pregnancy, birth, and early parenthood with confidence and calm. These tailored sessions provide evidence-based information, practical tools, and gentle relaxation techniques to help you understand your options, feel informed about labour and birth, and develop strategies to manage fear, anxiety, and discomfort. With a warm, supportive, approach, each session is adapted to your individual needs and preferences, empowering you to feel prepared, relaxed, and supported as you approach birth and the postnatal period. My Hypnobirthing course covers: understanding the physiology of birth, self-hypnosis, breathing and relaxation techniques, planning for birth including calm caesareans, decisions and choices in labour and birth, the birth partner’s role, bringing your newborn home, what to expect in the postnatal period - plus much more! Pregnancy Relaxation sessions are separate weekly 1 hour sessions utilising gentle breathing techniques, some time for light discussion around birth planning and preparation, plus a beautiful guided meditation specifically designed for pregnancy, to end the session. These can be booked in addition to the 1:1 Hypnobirthing course, or instead of, if you don't want to do the full course. Both of these 1:1 options can be arranged at a mutually convenient time in the comfort of your own home, or in a cosy log cabin in Terriers, High Wycombe (HP13). Dependent on location, additional costs may apply to cover travel costs or room hire. Sessions always end with a beautiful guided relaxation, and if you are doing the Hypnobirthing course, you will also receive 3 recordings of guided meditations that are perfect for birth and birth preparation, a goody bag, plus access to my client resources folders, which include a wealth of information and guides to everything pregnancy, birth and postnatal. As an experienced Newborn Care Specialist, Holistic Sleep Coach and Antenatal Educator, I can support you right through pregnancy, birth - and beyond! Overnight Newborn Care, Breastfeeding and Reflux Support, New Baby home visits and Birth Fear and Trauma Release Sessions are also available. Please visit my website for more information or to book a discovery call!

name: Designated Clinical Officer
description: The Designated Clinical Officer (DCO) has a key role in implementing and embedding the SEND reforms and in supporting joined up working between health services, local authorities, and other SEND partners. The DCO role includes oversight across services delivering healthcare to disabled children, young people, and those with special educational needs. Key responsibilities include: - Supporting health professionals to contribute to the Education, Health and Care Plan process. - Working with others in the local area to improve the quality of Education, Health and Care Plans. - Supporting the iSEND team at the local authority with questions and queries. - Promoting links between the SEND team, education professionals, social care, and health services. - Supporting the commissioners and senior leadership team with regards to meeting and assuring the SEND health requirements. - Working alongside commissioners and stakeholders including children and young people, parents, and carers to identify and raise any commissioning gaps some of which may require joint commissioning to resolve. - Ensuring we can evidence a good local offer of health services and clear health journeys for those aged 0 to 25 years with SEN.

Key responsibilities include: - Supporting health professionals to contribute to the Education, Health and Care Plan process. - Working with others in the local area to improve the quality of Education, Health and Care Plans. - Supporting the iSEND team at the local authority with questions and queries. - Promoting links between the SEND team, education professionals, social care, and health services. - Supporting the commissioners and senior leadership team with regards to meeting and assuring the SEND health requirements. - Working alongside commissioners and stakeholders including children and young people, parents, and carers to identify and raise any commissioning gaps some of which may require joint commissioning to resolve. - Ensuring we can evidence a good local offer of health services and clear health journeys for those aged 0 to 25 years with SEN.

local_offer: At RAFAKidz Walter’s Ash, we recognise that children are individuals with their own personalities, needs and preferences. Therefore, we plan their experience carefully and sensitively, working together with you to understand their individual needs and requirements to ensure they learn and develop at their own pace. For every child that comes through our doors, no matter their ability, background or circumstances, we will provide experiences and opportunities that will help them grow, be confident and reach their potential.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We want the children at RAFAKidz Walter’s Ash to get the best start in life irrespective of what their SEN needs are. We ensure that support is provided, both internally and externally, to help with children’s individual needs and requirements for their developmental journey. We also look to support parents, carers and families, including signposting them to networks and teams to help with young people with SEN. We have Early Years SEND advisors come to the setting to advise us on any additional support that is needed for the children, staff and parents. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Annabel, our manager and SENDCO, has completed her Bucks SENDCO qualification and attends regular SEN liaison and local network meetings. Chloe, our deputy manager and SENDCO, has completed a Level 3 in SEN. Several of our staff have also completed PALS (Playing and Learning to Socialise) training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents will be invited to be involved from the start of any SEND journey. We have an online platform where the staff and parents can provide daily updates to each other. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Within our setting, we use an online platform called Famly which allows us to record and track children’s development and progress; provide observations; and complete assessments and two year checks. Parents have access to view these as well as an option to have two way messaging service in addition to having good face to face relationships with the staff in the setting. RAFAKidz Walter’s Ash also use WellComm which is a screening tool for all children to identify needs for early intervention for speech and language skills. For those with SEN needs, we use the Differentiated Early Years Outcomes (DEYO) which is an adapted version of the Birth to 5 guidance that contains additional statements that have been inserted to ensure progress of all children can be recognized. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? RAFAKidz Walter’s Ash is located on the ground floor with clear and easy access throughout indoor and outdoor learning environments. We also have disabled parking; ramps and rails for accessibility at our entrance; and a disabled toilet. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact our setting to enquire about current availability in the nursery. Once a place is allocated and before the child starts, we would invite them in for some settling in sessions to help the child become familiar with their new environment and meet the staff. We can also arrange home visits if we feel it would benefit the child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We continuously look to improve and develop our SEND provision. This can include in house training for all staff and SENDCOs; to make use of a wide range of courses, including Bucks training; speech and language courses; and Lego therapy.

A positive and active participation with all parents/carers. To identify needs promptly and to introduce appropriate teaching/learning strategies. To monitor and evaluate progress effectively. All staff involved in teaching children with special needs are supported and enhanced through working alongside various external agencies. The preschool has established a programme of assessment to identify the needs of individual pupils in all areas of the curriculum (fact/Fact +) . These assessments identify children who may be experiencing difficulties and the appropriate provision is made to meet these needs. We ensure that every child with special needs joins in all the activities of the preschool with their peers as far as is reasonably practical. We aim to integrate children fully within the setting and achieve this by: Extra input from the keyworker 1-1 inclusion support as required Differentiated activities. Methodology appropriate to particular needs. Working in small groups or one-to-one. Involvement with the occupational therapist, speech therapist, educational psychologist, health visitor Regular dialogue with parents/carers and professionals to ensure that children are developing and making good progress both inside preschool and at home. Buttons is a provider of choice, offering excellent provision for all children regardless of "ability" or need, children are offered home visits prior to enrolling within the preschool and IEP are put in place ready for the child to join us.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Fully inclusive Individual Education plans specific to each childs' needs Highly trained and motivated staff teams with a passion for early years and SEND What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Upon registration a home visit is booked, the setting Senco alongside the senior Sen manager will visit the child and family to ascertain the need, a bespoke care plan and IEP will be written and adopted together, thus ensuring the child's needs are fully met. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use Eylog (early years education log) as a platform for sharing all aspects of the preschool, this encompasses learning and development alongside the targets a child is working towards, the platform is two way and parents can access and add to every area. We have open door policy and parents are encouraged to chat with keyworkers/manager . How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The building is fully accessible inside and outside, there are raised planting beds in the large garden, wheelchair ramps lead into all areas of the preschool gardens, the inside rooms are spacious with lots of exciting and stimulating resources. We access the school hall, library and secret garden as part of the preschool curriculum. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact us via email or telephone to request registration paperwork and prospectus, arrange a visit to the setting (we do offer an open door policy), book a home visit, register and look at sessions available, start date will be confirmed once we have everything in place to ensure the child will be fully supported from day one. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The need for services across the sector has continued to grow, Buttons is committed to continue to be a provider of choice, future plans include upskilling staff further in the areas of need, delivering training via our internal training academy, supporting local families to ensure places are available across the portfolio.

name: Support Following Suicide
description: Amparo means ‘shelter’ or ‘safe haven’ in Spanish and provides support for anyone affected by suicide Amparo is completely confidential and can provide short-term or longer-term support, depending on what you feel it is you need – we are guided by you. Support can be provided one-to-one, to family groups, groups of work colleagues – whatever you prefer and is most appropriate to your situation. Amparo is currently offered by telephone or video link, in person, ‘walk and talk’ or in community venues, wherever you are most comfortable. You can refer at any stage in your bereavement or (with your permission) other agencies can make a referral on your behalf (your GP, the coroner, a police officer or a funeral director, for example). The service is not just for ‘next of kin’ – anyone who has been affected by suicide and is living in the following areas can access Amparo: Cheshire and Merseyside, Lancashire, South Yorkshire, Kent and Medway, Thames Valley, Coventry and Warwickshire, Lincolnshire, Southampton, Hampshire, the Isle of Wight, Portsmouth Mid and South Essex and for serving personnel within the British Army. The Thames Valley area covers Oxfordshire, Berkshire and Buckinghamshire excluding Milton Keynes. Amparo’s local Liaison Workers aim to make initial contact within 24 hours of a referral being made. If you’re a professional and want to learn more about the Amparo service and the support we offer, book onto one of our free briefing sessions. Amparo Thames Valley is a free and confidential service. Amparo is part of the Listening Ear Family.

name: Organise a Play Streets Session
description: Organise a Play Streets session. Play Streets sessions allow groups of neighbours to temporarily close off their road so that children can play safely outside their homes and neighbours can get together. The sessions typically last for up to 2 hours and have many benefits, including: encouraging children to play outdoors allowing adult neighbours to connect and interact promoting healthy living bringing communities together Find out more about Play Streets on the Playing Out website and the Play Streets Bucks Facebook group. How to apply for a Play Streets session: To hold a Play Streets session you need to apply for a Temporary Play Streets Order (also known as an Events Road Closure Order). The order gives you permission to close your road for the purpose of children’s play. The road will be closed to vehicles but stay open to all pedestrians. You should submit an application, risk assessment and method statement at least 8 weeks before your planned Play Streets session. This allows us to process the application and carry out any training. To request an application form, email us at events. If you need help completing the form, contact the Play Streets Support Activator by email.

name: The Disraeli School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in High Wycombe for 3 to 11-year-olds. Has Additionally Resource Provision (ARP) for Autism. Disraeli School, High Wycombe is a three-form-entry, inclusive school that celebrates and values the rich diversity of our community and our motto: Learning is a journey, not a race, underpins all we do. We believe that every child deserves the best, and all staff at Disraeli strive to ensure that every second of a school day counts. Our learning environment is bright and spacious and well-resourced and children are engaged in their learning across an exciting and rich Courageous and Contagious curriculum. For our pre-school children, we offer two sessions a day for two-year-olds in their own setting and for our 3 and 4-year-olds we offer both 15 and 30-hour nursery sessions. We are proud to be able to make a difference to the lives and education of children and families all the way from two through to eleven years old. All the adults at Disraeli are learners too – we are energetic and enthusiastic, always looking for new ideas, reading up on research and developing ways to make our practice more effective, so that we can be the best we can be for the children.

local_offer: Disraeli School has an 18 place ARP (Additionally Resourced Provision) for children with Autistic Spectrum Disorder and an Educational Health Care Plan (EHCP). Our ARP aims to support the development of the children by providing specialist support within a mainstream school. We support children through specialist teaching, ASD intervention, for example, PECS (Picture Exchange Communication System) and TEACCH (Autism, research and training program), small group interventions, individualised learning and access to flexible teaching arrangements. Our ARP aims to support children in joining a mainstream class and inclusion with peers. Our ARP is not a standalone classroom but is a “base” within the school to support the children with ASD. The ARP consists of 2 rooms. Our Key Stage 1 room has a toilet and small sensory room. Both classrooms lead onto our outside courtyard where children have access to various play, learning and sensory equipment. name: Dogs Trust's Freedom Project
description: Dogs Trust’s Freedom Project is a dog fostering service for people who are fleeing domestic abuse. Dogs are often not allowed to stay in a refuge which leaves some people fleeing domestic abuse reluctant to leave their home until they know it is somewhere safe for their pets. For up to 6 months, Dogs Trust will help to place dogs with volunteer foster carers in their homes until their owners are rehoused and can take them back. All the dog's expenses during that time, including food and veterinary costs, are covered by Dogs Trust. If you would like to refer your dog to their service, or you are interested in becoming a volunteer foster carer, please visit the website or call them.

local_offer: I have been a childminder for 22 years and have helped to identify children with autism and other special needs and provide all the help and support required for each child individually. My provision is very inclusive and I am open to caring for and supporting ALL children. I have helped children with autism, ADHD, ADD, delayed speech, dyspraxia, dyslexia and life-limiting genetic conditions. I work extremely close to all the children's parents and outside agencies/external specialists, as needed. The children I care for are an extension of my own family and I feel proud and blessed to be a second mum to them all.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The absolute best outcome is possible for each child. I achieve this by involving all the professionals I can access for their help and advice and in turn, I can advise the families directly. Each child has their own personal journey so all the individual aspects of each child have to be taken into account in every case. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? On-line training and face to face with several providers How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I pride myself on my relationship with my parents. I am always very open and honest and I find they in turn treat me the same way. I encourage and value lots of two-way communication. Respected and valued relationships build very quickly with parents when honesty and openness are the priority from both sides. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I provide daily information of achievement and next steps plus a range of daily photos so the parents can be fully involved in all aspects of their children's experiences. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? I have no access issues. There is just one step into the house from the back and front, I have a wheelchair ramp I can use if this is required. I am happy to make changes to make my house more accessible if required specifically. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I am highly visible in the community, at the school, helping to run two playgroups and I am in a childminders network group where we hire a local hall for after school activities together. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am aware that being reflective is very important and I always look at my provision through new eyes to ensure that I have up to date information, training, links to resources and other professionals. The other childminders and I do regular good practice sessions and share ideas and help each other. We do training together and individually particularly for SEND as it's important to always be up to date on the latest help and information in this area.

name: MindJam
description: At MindJam our primary focus is to support young people’s emotional wellbeing. We believe that the key to doing so is by engaging them in a world in which they feel safe and comfortable, namely video games. Through online 1-to-1 sessions, MindJam provides mentorship and guidance to young people to support their emotional needs and SEN identity through positive, non-judgemental, and low-demand sessions. We support young people between the ages 6 to 25. Our mentors' shared passion for gaming provides a platform to build a trusting, long-lasting relationship from which we can support their individual needs, whether emotional or SEN. All mentors are experienced and trained in supporting neurodivergent individuals including autistic young people and other additional needs such as Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA), ADHD, anxiety, stress, and trauma. We also empower young people to have greater online awareness and safety. Support can take many different forms; it can be playing Fortnite, Minecraft, or Roblox. Or through developing a digital skill such as game design, 3D design, digital art, animation, music editing, or video editing. MindJam is also an ASDAN, AQA, and Arts Award provider. However, our focus for all mentees is the same – to support their emotional wellbeing. local_offer: Through online 1-to-1 sessions, MindJam provides mentorship and guidance to young people to support their emotional needs and SEN identity through positive, non-judgemental, and low-demand sessions. We support young people between the ages 6 to 25. Our mentors' shared passion for gaming provides a platform to build a trusting, long-lasting relationship from which we can support their individual needs, whether emotional or SEN. All mentors are experienced and trained in supporting neurodivergent individuals including autistic young people and other additional needs such as Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA), ADHD, anxiety, stress, and trauma. We also empower young people to have greater online awareness and safety. Support can take many different forms; it can be playing Fortnite, Minecraft, or Roblox. Or through developing a digital skill such as game design, 3D design, digital art, animation, music editing, or video editing.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? In private and online one-to-one sessions, we provide a safe environment in which children are encouraged to express themselves, to talk about anything that interests them, their loves and fears, worries, problems, and goals. Session goals may look like support with: - Social interactions and communication - Understanding differing viewpoints - Turn taking - Emotional regulation and understanding anxiety/ worries - Listening skills, maintaining attention, and focus - Building confidence, self-esteem, and resilience - Building a relationship with a trusted adult - Understanding and implementing boundaries - Understanding and accepting their SEN identity These are set in line with the child’s needs and any outcomes that are already in place, such as in their EHCP. We can also set secondary aims with mentees that focus on building digital skills in, for example, coding, game design, animation, or digital art, as well as supporting mentees in obtaining a bronze, silver or gold Arts Award, LSC and short courses through ASDAN, as well as AQA Unit Awards. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Kieran Rose Autism Training PDA Society - Introduction to PDA PDA Society - PDA best practice – The professional voice In-house SEN induction and training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All enquiries and referral requests can be sent to hello@mindjam.org.uk. Once an active service user, parents can join our MindJam Parents Group on Facebook where they can access resources and support from both MindJam and other parents using the service. We also run events where we encourage young people and parents to come and get involved, meet others using the service, and have an evening of playing and discovering new skills. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Your mentor will ensure they keep in regular contact to ensure that both mentee and parent are happy with the sessions, and are getting the most they can from them. Mentors can provide formal reports and attend meetings as required. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Due to our sessions being run online, they can be accessed by anyone with a digital device and access to the internet. Sessions can include a webcam, voice chat, or text chat, and will be run to the mentees preference to ensure that they are comfortable at all times. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Through contacting MindJam via email or via our website. We will then add you to our waiting list, and send a link to our online referral form. We will use this referral form to assign the most appropriate mentor to your young person. Before sessions begin, the mentor will contact you to arrange a virtual meeting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are always looking for ways to bring more options into our provision, such as offering Arts Award, AQA Unit Awards, and tailored in house training through ASDAN. We are now looking to offer community projects in geographical locations where we can provide everything from mentoring, through to health and wellbeing sessions, courses and events.

We provide both small group and 1:1 intervention. This allows all children to receive support in their access to the curriculum. We have trained ELSA's supporting children with their emotional needs. Staff are trained each year to ensure that their knowledge and understanding of SEN is maintained. The training may be provided by specialist agencies, as well as from the SENCo. SEN training forms part of the continuing professional development of all staff and is organised in accordance with the needs of our children. Support is purchased for individuals and for staff CPD when required from Specialist Teaching Services, including the Cognition and Learning team and the ASD team. Professionals provide the intervention that may involve assessing pupils, supporting class teachers and the SENCo to allow strategies to be developed to meet the needs of SEND pupils. Professionals also may provide staff training. Dorney School also has access to other services when required, which include Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists, Educational Psychologist, Pupil Referral Unit (PRU), and an SEN Link Officer. We also have a link Mental Health Support Worker, who we can refer into for children with social, emotional and mental health needs. During a pupils’ transfer to secondary school, staff and the SENCo liaise closely with secondary school teachers to ensure a smooth transition occurs. This involves not only a verbal handover but also a handover of all paper copies of records being sent on. local_offer: At The Downley School, we are committed to creating an inclusive environment where every child with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND) is valued, supported, and empowered to achieve their best. We recognise each child's unique strengths and challenges, tailoring high-quality education to meet their individual needs. Our vision is to nurture independent learners by removing barriers, building self-confidence, and fostering personal growth. We celebrate the diverse talents of our SEND pupils, ensuring their education goes beyond national benchmarks, recognising and honouring individual achievements. To help SEND pupils thrive academically, socially, and emotionally, we are committed to: • Centring their needs, interests, and aspirations in their learning. • Providing a challenging, adaptable curriculum. • Equipping them with skills for confidence and independence. • Delivering personalised teaching that meets their learning requirements. • Offering tailored interventions and resources for specific needs. • Ensuring access to a broad curriculum with enriching activities. We believe every SEND pupil deserves success both academically and personally. Our goal is to prepare them for the next stage of education, building their confidence, resilience, and skills. We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive, nurturing environment where SEND pupils can thrive and engage fully in their learning journey. https://www.downley.bucks.sch.uk/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs&pid=717 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We prioritise effective progress monitoring to ensure all pupils fully grasp and retain the curriculum, providing teachers with valuable insights into each child's learning. This process not only highlights achievements but also identifies areas that require further attention. Our class teachers continuously observe and assess the academic, social, and emotional development of every pupil. While academic levels and test results offer snapshots of progress, we employ a variety of measures to gain a comprehensive understanding of each child's development. We also value strong partnerships with parents and carers, fostering open communication to support each child's learning journey. For pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), we implement a detailed assessment process that includes entry and exit assessments for interventions to measure their impact. Personal Learning Plans (PLPs) are created with specific targets and are regularly reviewed by our SENDCo and class teachers. This review process uses data to assess progress, evaluate the effectiveness of interventions, and adjust targets as necessary. Each term, we follow the Assess-Plan-Do-Review approach, involving both parents and pupils in setting goals and reviewing progress. We also collaborate with external agencies and ensure that children have a voice in shaping their learning experience. This comprehensive approach helps SEND pupils feel safe, confident, and independent, actively engaging in their learning while developing essential skills for future education. Through regular updates to Personal Learning Plans (PLPs)s and review meetings, we ensure that every pupil receives the personalised support they need to thrive. name: Dr Challoner's High School (Girls')
description: Selective Girls' secondary school in Amersham 11 to 18-year-olds. We are here to provide the best possible education for girls. We are passionate about the breadth of aspiration and opportunity, and ensure that our girls are empowered with the skills, habits, and attributes needed to thrive in the Twenty First Century and to contribute significantly to the world. A leading selective grammar school for girls, Challoner’s High has a strong tradition of academic excellence, consistently placing in the top 50 in state school examination league tables. Judged by Ofsted as ‘Outstanding’ in 2012, we subsequently became only the ninth school in the country to gain the Exceptional Schools Award in July 2014. Nearly all of our students choose to go to university, with most going to Russell Group institutions, including Oxford and Cambridge. Beliefs so often shape reality. For decades our values have led to a supportive, joyful, and intellectually ambitious education. We believe that girls learn best when all are valued, inspired, curious, and happy. We believe that all girls, whether naturally quiet or gregarious, can become confident, resilient, and courageous; free to follow their own paths; discover their own passions, and achieve their personal bests. Therefore, at the heart of our school is a tightly-knit and highly purposeful community of students and teachers – a warm-hearted community characterised by compassion, commitment, and a strong instinct for the fun, creative, and clever. An infectious vibrancy and a generosity of spirit underpin Dr Challoner’s High School as a ‘home from home’ for approximately 1315 girls aged between 11 and 18. Our girls have the potential to help shape the world over the coming decades and it is our mission to provide them with the best possible preparation, whilst also daily recognising that learning is inherently joyful.

description: Mixed-gender primary school in Milton Keynes for 4 to 7-year-olds. Welcome to Drayton Parslow Village School. We cater for children between four and seven years old. name: Action4Youth | Duke of Edinburgh's Award
description: Action4Youth is proud to be an Approved Activity Provider for The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award, delivering high-quality Bronze, Silver, and Gold expeditions for schools across Buckinghamshire, Milton Keynes, and the wider region. With a team of experienced leaders, outdoor specialists, and assessors, we help schools bring the DofE to life through safe, expertly run, and inspiring expeditions. We offer fully supported packages for schools and education providers, tailored to your requirements. Whether you’re launching DofE for the first time or expanding an existing offer, we’ll help deliver a seamless and memorable experience for your students. We do support a small number of young people who are not able to complete their DofE through school, so if this applies to you, you can sign up for an expedition by visiting our website.
organisation: Action4Youth Action4Youth changes lives and creates better chances for young people by creating opportunities to discover their personal strengths and potential. We work with young people from all backgrounds and all abilities to make a real difference to their futures. We are a respected and dynamic charity based in Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes but reaching young people across the wider south east region. What we do Action4Youth is a leading delivery partner for the National Citizen Service (NCS) and consistently over delivers in terms of both quality and quantity. Action4Youth takes the strategic lead for the voluntary organisations supporting children and young people aged 5 – 25 years across its area. It has around 100 organisations in membership and offers a range of essential support and services. Our outdoor centre, Caldecotte Xperience in Milton Keynes, creates opportunities for young people to have amazing, challenging, fun and sometimes transformational experiences. local_offer: The SpLD Hub provides specialist SEND assessment and support for children, young people, and adults with specific learning differences (SpLDs), including dyslexia and dyscalculia. Support is tailored to the individual and may include diagnostic assessment, specialist 1:1 teaching, literacy and numeracy intervention, study skills, Functional Skills support and strategies to develop confidence and independence in learning. We also provide ADHD screening and Exam Access Arrangements assessments, alongside support for individuals with processing, memory, and executive functioning difficulties. Our approach focuses on understanding each individual's strengths and areas of difficulty and translating this into practical, realistic, strategies that can be used at home, in education and, where appropriate, in the workplace. We work collaboratively with families, schools, education providers and other professionals to help individuals access appropriate support and make progress.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To help children and young people understand their strengths and difficulties, build confidence and develop effective strategies for learning. We aim to give families and education settings clear, practical recommendations so that assessment leads to meaningful and appropriate support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Recent and ongoing specialist training includes SpLD diagnostic assessment, dyslexia and dyscalculia, SEND, ADHD screening (QbCheck), and adult DCD screening. I hold an Assessment Practising Certificate (APC), AMBDA and a PGCert in SEND, alongside regular CPD to maintain and develop specialist practice. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are involved throughout the process, providing background information and sharing their observations and concerns. Assessment findings and recommendations are explained clearly, with opportunities to ask questions and discuss appropriate next steps and support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents and carers receive clear feedback on progress, including strengths, areas for development and recommended next steps. For children with SEND, support is individualised to their specific learning profile, with progress reviewed and strategies adapted where needed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The SpLD Hub provides a quiet, comfortable and low-distraction indoor environment, with support adapted to individual SEND needs. The assessment and teaching space is on the ground floor. Please contact us in advance to discuss any specific accessibility requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact The SpLD Hub directly to discuss their needs or book an assessment or support service through the website. No formal referral is required. We are happy to discuss which service may be most appropriate before booking. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to continue developing our specialist SEND provision through expanded assessment, teaching and support services, alongside practical resources for families and education settings. Provision will continue to evolve in response to individual needs and current evidence-based practice.

local_offer: I am an Ofsted-registered childminder committed to providing individualised, quality and flexible care for children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disability.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Support them with individualised programmes and implement appropriate provison to help them progress; to help them overcome any barriers in their overall learning and development by working closely with parents and other professionals. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 2 Certificate in Special Educational Needs and Disability Dated: 05 August 2022 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents’ views and the children’s interest, strengths and weaknesses are taken into consideration during planning. I work closely with parents to share information about their child’s progress through parents' consultation twice a year and a 2 year progress check. A home-setting diary would be proived to enhance two- way communication. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children’s learning, development and progress will be observed and shared with parents on a regular basis. For children with SEND, a joint action plan would be implemented to offer support that is consistent; this would be reviewed and updated regularly, and in accordance with the child’s needs. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is on the ground floor. There are steps at the entrance to the property and to the garden, however temporary ramp could be fitted for easy access. I work with parents to make reasonable and practicable adaptations so children can comfortably fit in their daily routines. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If a child is attending another setting, I would work in partnership with them to ensure effective transition. I encourage families to come for transitional visits with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ document, this is so that I could gather valuable information about them, which would offer a smooth starting point. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I aim to keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review my provision to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I will undertaking ongoing, and specific training if required, to develop and improve my professional practice in SEND.

name: Time-Matters UK Supporting Children Affected by Parental Imprisonment
description: We help at any stage of the criminal justice system. This means that children, tweens and teens are welcome when a parent has been arrested and awaiting trial, or whilst their parent is in custody, or after a parent has been to prison and is now released. We are “ACE” aware. This means we understand that having a family member sent to prison is an adverse childhood experience. We therefore take a trauma informed approach to practice. We aim to mitigate against this childhood trauma by providing an early intervention service to help children build their resilience, particularly through positive relationships with mentors and peers, and by providing wider opportunities for learning, relaxation, community leadership and fun. Families can self-refer, or professionals can make a referral with consent from the family. Our key focus centres on supporting children and young people, ages 5 to 18 years who have a parent in prison.

name: PACT - Prison Advice and Care Trust
description: Pact is a pioneering national charity that supports prisoners, people with convictions, and their children and families. We provide caring and life changing services at every stage of the criminal justice process: in court, in prison, on release, and in the community. Our vision is of a society that understands justice as a process of restoration and healing, that uses prisons sparingly and as places of learning and rehabilitation, and that values the innate dignity and worth of every human being. We work for the common good of Society, taking a public health-based approach. We work at the intersection of criminal justice, child and family welfare, mental health, wellbeing provision and health and social care. You can find our volunteers and staff in courts, prisons, probation services, and in communities across England and Wales. We are a diverse, inclusive, modern, and collaborative charity. We build effective partnerships and sustainable solutions based on our well-established understanding of the systems in which we work, and on our historic values and ethos developed through our 120 years of service delivery.

local_offer: The type of SEND provision that East Claydon School caters for is that every child is entitled to inclusive and high quality first teaching. Teaching is differentiated for individual needs with additional intervention and support when necessary. The school’s Accessibility policy can be found here on the schools website under policies. The school’s policy (including pupils who do and do not have an EHC Plan) for identifying and assessing pupils with SEND is: Termly pupil progress meetings with class teachers and the head identify children who are not making expected progress. Children not making expected progress are identified, monitored, and reviewed within half term, and if necessary after discussion with parent/ carer and child, an SEN support plan will be put in place. When a child joins our school we also receive and consider information from the previous school or setting. When parents or carers have concerns about the progress or attainment of their child they should in the first instance make an appointment to speak to the class teacher to discuss their concerns who, if necessary, will liaise with the SEN co-ordinator as appropriate. Evaluating the effectiveness of its provision for pupils with SEND is: Children receiving additional support are closely monitored by the class teacher, the SEN co-ordinator and the head. If children are not making expected progress, the provision is reviewed and altered immediately to improve the impact on the child. Assessing and reviewing the progress of pupils with SEND is: The progress of SEND pupils is monitored termly by the class teacher and the SENCO. Progress made towards the outcomes is shared with the child and the parents in termly meetings. The SEN Governor will monitor provision termly and report to the governing body annually on progress of SEND children. The school’s/Pre-school’s arrangement for training staff in relation to pupils with SEND is: We invest time and money in training our staff to improve provision for all students, to develop enhanced skills and knowledge to deliver short term group support interventions and individual support and interventions. We have an experienced SENCO who holds the NASENCO. All our teachers hold qualified teacher status and all staff members, including Teaching Assistants and Higher Level Teaching Assistants receive regular training to best support pupils with SEND. Specialist expertise is obtained by the schools/pre-school’s by: We involve educational outside agencies including the specialist teaching service, educational psychologist service, occupational therapists and speech and language therapists. Specialist health services we draw on include the school nurse, disability nurse and CAMHs. name: TCES National Online School
description: TCES - The Complete Education Solution - is a social enterprise providing Therapeutic Education to neurodiverse pupils at our five schools and services in and around London and nationally via TCES National Online School, supporting students who are often marginalised and fall through the education net. Our therapeutic approach nurtures and supports pupils to find their talents and skills and give them the best opportunities for positive social, emotional, and academic outcomes. We never exclude pupils; we never give up on them. The TCES National Online School offers a full curriculum and therapeutic support to children and young people aged 5 to 25 who are unable to attend school. This can be for a variety of reasons and can be linked to school anxiety, special educational needs, emotionally based school avoidance (EBSA), or where a current school isn't meeting needs. Pupils on our programmes typically have an Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP) but we also support those either at the start of the EHCP process or without an EHCP. We offer the core subjects of English, Maths and Science plus additional subjects and we can support pupils to take GCSEs and A levels, including providing invigilators in the family home where needed. Our experienced and qualified therapy team offers Speech and Language, Occupational Therapy and psychodynamic therapies (e.g. Art and Drama Therapy) based on our assessments of each child's need. The TCES National Online School approach Our team work collaboratively with each pupil and their family (plus school and Local Authority where appropriate) to create an online education programme which can include therapy where required. This will be regularly reviewed to ensure that it continues to meet the child or young person's needs. Our aim is for each child or young person we support to be able to re-engage with education and move back into an appropriate school setting. In 2021/2, after an average placement of six months, almost 80% of TCES Online School pupils were ready to reintegrate to school or college. Parent feedback "Since starting with TCES National Online School a has been amazing. She wants to learn and gives 100% to her tutor." TCES promise We do not exclude pupils. We never give up.

local_offer: Edlesborough School and Pre-School is a welcoming, inclusive school which strives to ensure that all children reach their full academic potential and develop a love for learning which will last a lifetime. We ensure equal opportunities for all pupils, regardless of gender, age, ability, religion, race, cultural or ethnic background. Staff at Edlesborough School and Pre-School work tirelessly to enable all children to achieve their maximum potential as individuals and members of society. Ensuring the equality of opportunity and treatment for all members of our school community is paramount to all we do. Every teacher at Edlesborough School and Pre-School is a teacher of every child including those with special educational needs and/or disability. All children are individuals with differing learning needs. We tailor our curriculum to meet the needs of individuals aiming to close gaps in learning and accelerate progress. We hope this over-arching information answers your questions; please feel free to contact the school for additional information should you require. https://epa-primary.org/Key_Information/SEND/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Edlesborough School is committed to providing a quality education for all pupils, including those with special educational needs and disability (SEND) which can be met at a mainstream school. We believe that all children have individual needs, strengths and talents, which should be met through an inspirational school curriculum which allows each child to work at their own level and pace, while being appropriately challenged. We recognise that to achieve this, many children will require additional support or additional challenge throughout their time in school. Edlesborough School and Pre-School strives to ensure that all children reach their full academic potential and develop a love for learning which will last a lifetime. We ensure equal opportunities for all pupils, regardless of gender, age, ability, religion, race, cultural or ethnic background. Staff at Edlesborough School and Pre-School work tirelessly to enable all children to achieve their maximum potential as individuals and members of society. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Edlesborough School and Pre-School is committed to providing ongoing professional development opportunities to all members of staff. This training is based on staff and pupil’s individual needs. All teaching members of staff hold Qualified Teacher Status and all members of the Pre-School Team hold their own Early Years Professional Qualifications. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Pupil Progress evenings are held termly and all pupils receive a written progress report annually. Short term outcomes for children with an EHCP or School Support Plan are reviewed termly and reviewed and new outcomes are shared with parents. Parents and Pupils are also able to make an appointment with their class teacher or the school SENDCo at any point in time. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All pupils regardless of special Educational Need or Disability are included in all aspects of the school curriculum. We aim for all pupils to be included in PE and in school trips. Pupils will be asked to take part in all activities as best they can but will not be expected to do anything which they are unable to. Each year pupils attend school trips linked to the topic they are studying. On some occasions we ask for volunteer parent helpers but staff will always be available to support individual children if needed. A risk assessment is carried out prior to each trip, this may name specific children who need additional help. In the unlikely event that it is considered unsafe for a child to take part in an activity, then alternative arrangements will be provided in school. Pupils at school with medical conditions will be properly supported so that they have full access to education, including school trips and physical education. The Governing body will ensure that arrangements are in place in schools to support pupils at school with medical conditions. Governing bodies will also ensure that school leaders consult health and social care professionals, pupils and parents to ensure that the needs of children with medical conditions are effectively supported. Our site is equipped with ramps and soft surfaces where required. We respond to each child’s individual needs and are committed to making arrangements to accommodate individual needs as required. Please feel free to contact the school about your child’s individual needs for more information. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Edlesborough School Admissions is determined by the Buckinghamshire Council Admissions Policy in accordance with the schedule laid out by the Cabinet Member for Achievement, Learning and Skills. Parents wishing to admit their child into Edlesborough School must do so in accordance with the Buckinghamshire coordinated primary admissions scheme. Allocation of places is determined by Buckinghamshire Council. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to ensure that through a rolling cycle of CPD staff have recent and relevant knowledge of best practice in supporting children with different learning needs to ensure inclusive provision through quality first teaching.

name: Action4Youth | Breakout Programme
description: The Breakout Programme is a hard-hitting 12-week, anti-knife and gang programme, designed to bring positive change to the lives of young people at risk of being sucked into crime and of losing purpose in their lives. Developed to have maximum impact, The Breakout Programme is tailored to individual needs and uses a package of mentoring, classroom sessions and outdoor education. We work with schools to identify participants, typically those displaying various early indicators of susceptibility to crime, for instance, risk of exclusion from school, disruptive behaviour, poor school attendance, anti-social behaviour and possibly already having had some negative contact with the police. Some schools also like to target pupils for very early intervention to reduce certain behaviour patterns occurring.
organisation: Action4Youth Action4Youth changes lives and creates better chances for young people by creating opportunities to discover their personal strengths and potential. We work with young people from all backgrounds and all abilities to make a real difference to their futures. We are a respected and dynamic charity based in Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes but reaching young people across the wider south east region. What we do Action4Youth is a leading delivery partner for the National Citizen Service (NCS) and consistently over delivers in terms of both quality and quantity. Action4Youth takes the strategic lead for the voluntary organisations supporting children and young people aged 5 – 25 years across its area. It has around 100 organisations in membership and offers a range of essential support and services. Our outdoor centre, Caldecotte Xperience in Milton Keynes, creates opportunities for young people to have amazing, challenging, fun and sometimes transformational experiences. They learn what they can do rather than what they can’t, building their confidence and self-belief. Action4Youth is the operating authority for Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes for Open Awards Groups for the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme. office@action4youth.org http://www.action4youth.org

name: Action4Youth | The Inspiration Programme (TIP)
description: The Inspiration Programme broadens the horizons, thinking and experience of young people. This programme enhances existing provision and creates opportunities for young people, providing direct and meaningful experiences with unique and unprecedented access to important elements of our community: working life, arts and culture, police and criminal justice, community and environment as well as personal health and wellbeing. The programme is a valuable addition to a young person’s life experience, CV, personal statement and understanding of the wide range of careers available to them. local_offer: Qualified and experienced teacher, with mainstream and SEN experience. Qualified, practising SENDCo and former Local Authority specialist teacher. Expertise in supporting children and young people with social, emotional and mental health issues, particularly those arising from neurodivergence. Trauma-sensitive practitioner and qualified senior mental health lead and designated safeguarding lead.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My perspective is different, as a neurodivergent adult, supporting my own neurodivergent children through the SEND system has been challenging and I am still very much navigating and learning from children, their parents and other parents. I never stop learning and all children are unique individuals, I tailor their tuition packages to their own interests, strengths and regulation style. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? BA (Hons) PGCE NASENDCo Trauma sensitive approaches to education AET lead professional training Senior mental health lead and mental health first-aider Zones of regulation, sensory regulation, anxiety Designated Safeguarding Lead Language Disorder and DLD How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in planning and provision of support for their children. Individual feedback on progress. I learn and adapt my teaching continuously and following each session. It always helps if parents can understand the techniques I use and I'm happy to share these as we go along together. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I am committed to celebrating neurodiversity and each individual child's strengths. I am a trauma-sensitive practitioner and am fully aware of the impact that the current school system can have on children. I can teach children to understand that they can succeed despite the rigid structures in place in schools. There is more than one way to learn and I will help your child find their way. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We live within a school site and have a learning space in the garden which is accessible by its own entrance. The 'shed' can be reached by a gravel path and two steps. I can also travel to your home, on request, or work online where this is suitable (although I believe that a relationship of mutual trust is important for successful learning and this is more difficult online) How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact via whats app. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I also offer support with advocacy for parents. Attending meetings and reviews in schools. Observations and advice on how best to support individual children inclusively in school. Training for schools in inclusive teaching strategies, adaptive teaching and SEND needs. Support for parents and schools in making an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) Needs Application. Support for parents in appealing Local Authority decisions. EHCP checking. Appeals to tribunal-making an appeal, making a response. In the near future - Social groups for parents and children who are no longer attending school.

local_offer: Who Can Egerton Rothesay School (ERS) Help? Egerton Rothesay is a school that has developed a high level of expertise and practical experience in helping children with a wide range of needs, including some who have a Statement of Special Educational Needs from their Local Education Authority (LEA). Whilst most of our children could attend other mainstream schools, the provision at ERS enables them to flourish rather than just survive. Before entry, each child is considered individually and a decision to offer a place is based on that child’s need, our available provision and the balance of needs within the appropriate year group. We accept children who: • need a small class and a supportive environment • are particularly shy or vulnerable, or who have had a poor school experience, for example, have been bullied or have refused to go to school • have dyslexia (mild to severe) • have dyspraxia (DCD) • have speech and language difficulties • would benefit from focused language and social interaction activities. Aims and Values: Egerton Rothesay School aims to provide an environment where learning can flourish, enabled by excellent teaching and care. We want each child to achieve to their individual highest potential, we want each individual to be valued for who they are, and we want each member of our community to fully respect and be respected by others. All ERS values are underpinned by our Christian basis but the school welcomes children (and staff) of all faiths or none, asking only that the child’s parent or guardian is aware and supportive of the basis of the school. We encourage children to learn about their community, and about the beliefs of both Christian and other faiths. We share with them the need to be aware of others who are less fortunate than themselves and to contribute in some way to help such groups. There are a number of specific strands of Christian input within the school, including assemblies and RE lessons (which we expect all students to attend) and church services to celebrate key Christian festivals or school milestones. name: Dimensions
description: In 1976, armed with a single phone in a rented office, Dimensions began supporting people with learning disabilities, autism and complex needs out of institutions, helping them lead ordinary lives in their local communities. Forty years on, our work is fundamentally unchanged: we support people with learning disabilities and autistic people to have a louder voice, choice and control in their lives. Our 7000 colleagues deliver ambitious, effective, personalised support often with those whose previous support has not been successful. Working alongside our colleagues are family members and many of the people we support. They could be quality checkers, interviewers or members of our Council. Their voices and experiences inform the research we use to deliver improved outcomes. Together, we continue to prove that life really can get better. Through our person-centred approach we support: - People with profound and multiple learning disabilities - People with complex autism - People needing full time support, and those needing a little less - People with complex health needs - People whose behaviour may challenge those around them - People in assessment and treatment units - Young adults leaving school and college - People with forensic support needs - People looking for a place to live - People and families needing a break - People seeking employment

name: Dimensions: Autism Friendly Environments
description: Looking for autism-friendly things to do? Dimensions UK work with cinemas, libraries, museums, and Belong by GAME Arenas. Each venue’s autism-friendly training is tailored to its environment and guests. Adjustments include reduced sensory stimulation, increased signage and autism training for staff. Our training is developed with autism and industry experts, so it works for both our guests and the venues. Autism-friendly screenings are held at over 300 cinemas nationwide: ODEON, Cineworld, Vue, Showcase, Picturehouse, Everyman, Light, and some independent cinemas. The screenings take place regularly and have adjustments to make the cinema experience more enjoyable for people with autism or sensory sensitivity. To find out more about Autism Friendly screenings, you can visit the Dimensions website, the Dimensions Facebook page, or your local cinema.

local_offer: We have SEN experienced staff and SENCO in our setting  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have high aspirations for all our children and our aim is that every child has a fun nursery and preschool experience in a caring atmosphere. We aim that all children will be supported to the best of our ability to make the best progress they can, relative to their stage of development. We aim that all our families feel included in our nursery life and realise that we are partners in supporting their child to reach their potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO, Sign along, Understanding autism level 2 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they can approach us about anything relating to their children. We will have opportunities for contact with parents regularly. There are also many informal opportunities to chat and when parents request a meeting, we aim to meet with them as soon as possible. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child will have a online learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time. We will discuss progress with Key Person regularly, and through our 2-year-old progress checks and end of year summary assessment sheets. For children with SEND we will ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We consider the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We created homely, calm, tranquil areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning and we created a separate room for sensory play to support children with sensory processing issues. We will also use 'sign along' to help children communicate. We have boards outdoors that teaches signing to children in a fun way. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents and families are welcome to come along to our open day sessions to look at the setting, meet the team and talk through any queries. Parents with children with SEND are invited to make a special visit to discuss how we can best meet their needs We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavor to make this as smooth as possible. We will liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We will visit the local schools with children who are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will to review and update our visual resources and training regularly to support children’s needs.

description: Learning to Empower. I am Jane Gale, a Qualified Dyslexia Assessor with The Dyslexia Guild, based in Chalfont St Peter, Gerrards Cross, Buckinghamshire. Learning to Empower provides full diagnostic dyslexia assessments for children aged 8 to 14 across Buckinghamshire, including assessments in schools and privately at Jordans Quaker Meeting House in Beaconsfield. I provide full diagnostic assessments for dyslexia for children aged 8 to 14. Assessments are carried out in line with current SpLD Assessment Standards Committee (SASC) guidance and explore each child’s individual pattern of strengths and difficulties, rather than looking at literacy skills in isolation. As part of the assessment, I consider areas such as expressive and receptive language, working memory, processing speed, phonological processing, reading, spelling, writing, and handwriting speed. Background information is also gathered from both home and school so that the assessment reflects the child’s wider learning profile. Following the assessment, I provide a detailed written report with clear findings, a formal diagnosis where appropriate, and practical recommendations for support at home and school. My aim is to help families and schools understand not only whether dyslexia is present, but also how the child learns best and what support is likely to make the biggest difference.

name: Alcoholics Anonymous
description: Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) is concerned solely with the personal recovery and continued sobriety of individual alcoholics who turn to the Fellowship for help. The Fellowship has adopted a policy of "cooperation but not affiliation" with other organisations concerned with the problem of alcoholism. Traditionally, Alcoholics Anonymous does not accept or seek financial support from outside sources, and members preserve personal anonymity in print and broadcast media and otherwise at the public level. AA experience has always been made available freely to all who sought it - business people, spiritual leaders, civic groups, law enforcement officers, health and welfare personnel, educators, representatives of military establishments, institutional authorities, representatives of organised labour, and many others. The Importance of Anonymity Traditionally, AA members have always taken care to preserve their anonymity at the "public" level: in the press, radio, television, films, and new media technologies such as the Internet. First, we know from experience that many problem drinkers might hesitate to turn to AA for help if they thought their problem might be discussed publicly, even inadvertently, by others. Newcomers should be able to seek help with complete assurance that their identities will not be disclosed to anyone outside the Fellowship. Then, too, we believe that the concept of personal anonymity has a spiritual significance for us - that it discourages the drives for personal recognition, power, prestige, or profit that have caused difficulties in some societies. Much of our relative effectiveness in working with alcoholics might be impaired if we sought or accepted public recognition. While each member of AA is free to make their own interpretations of AA tradition, no individual is ever recognised as a spokesperson for the Fellowship locally, nationally, or internationally. Each member speaks only for themself. You may wish to message one of our team of AA Member volunteers - use the live chat pop up found via the website introduce yourself with your first name, and if one of the team is online at that moment, they will respond and seek to answer your questions. If there is no responder available, you will still be able to email us and you will be answered as soon as possible.
