local_offer: Gerrards Cross Montessori Nursery is a privately owned Nursery that will cater for up to 79 children per session. We provide for an environment in which all children, including those with special educational needs and disabilities, are supported to reach their full potential. We identify the specific needs of children with special educational needs and/or disabilities and meet those needs through a range of SEN strategies. We work in close partnership with parents and other agencies in meeting individual children’s needs. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Gerrards Cross Montessori Nursery prides itself in having high aspirations for all our children and our aim is that every child reaches their full potential in a caring atmosphere. We aim that all children will be supported to the best of our ability to make the best progress they can, relative to their stage of development. We aim that all our families feel included in nursery life and realise that we are partners in supporting their child learning and development What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO (Special Education Need Co Ordinator) Training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they can approach us about anything relating to their children. We have formal opportunities for contact with parents at our termly Key Person Meetings. There are also many informal opportunities to chat and when parents request a meeting, we aim to meet with them as soon as possible. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time by asking their child’s Key Person. We will discuss progress at Key Person Meetings, and through our 2-year-old progress checks and end of year summary assessment sheets. For children with SEND we try to ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We consider the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We try to create areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning and to create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing issues. Children have access to forest school sessions once a week and we make a variety of adjustments to ensure all children can participate. We use Makaton with all children to aid communication. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents and families are welcome to visit us for a look around, meet the team and talk through any queries. We have an information booklet that gives details of the application process. Parents with children with SEND are invited to make a special visit to discuss how we can best meet their needs We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We regularly visit the local schools with children who are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We aim that all our staff have attended Buckinghamshire SEND course and that it is everyone’s responsibility to be able to support children with their additional needs

name: Independent Provider of Special Education Advice (IPSEA)
description: IPSEA offers free and independent legally based information, advice and support to help get the right education for children and young people aged 0 to 25 years with all kinds of special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). IPSEA has a suite of free downloadable guides, resources and template letters available to parents and carers. These guides are complemented by a free Advice Line and Call-in Helpline which provide legally based information and next step advice on any educational issue that is a result of a child's SEND. IPSEA’s Tribunal Helpline gives next step advice on appeals and disability discrimination claims to the SEND Tribunal and is also the gateway to our Tribunal Support Service where a referral can be made for more extensive casework support from a volunteer, including representation at the hearing. Our advice services are delivered by a national network of around 100 highly-trained volunteers, supervised and supported by IPSEA’s Legal Team members. IPSEA provides legal training for parents, school staff, parent carer forums, support groups and other organisations in order to increase their knowledge and understanding of the SEN legal framework. The proceeds raised from our training courses helps fund IPSEA’s core services (Advice Line, Tribunal Helpline and Tribunal Support Service). We also work to challenge unlawful SEND policy and influence policy development at both a local and national level. Our policy work is informed by information and evidence captured through our training and advice services, and has been instrumental in shaping law and policy in the field of special educational needs and disability.

local_offer: As a tiney registered childminder, I am committed to promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion in all aspects of my childcare provision. My home is a welcoming, safe, and inclusive environment where all children, including those with diagnosed disabilities, additional needs, or developmental challenges, are supported to thrive and reach their full potential.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To ensure no child or family is discriminated against or disadvantaged due to gender, ethnicity, religion, language, disability, socioeconomic status, or additional needs. To create an inclusive environment where every child can develop, learn, and participate alongside their peers. To work closely with parents/carers to identify and meet individual needs, respecting their values and contributions. To celebrate diversity through play, resources, and experiences, promoting understanding and respect. To follow the graduated approach of “Assess, Plan, Do, Review” to provide effective support for children with additional needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed various online training modules through tiney such as celebrating uniqueness and the Shrec approach. I will continue to work on my CPD and access resources and training through tiney and The Bucks Early Years sector. I am committed to learning from families and professionals to continually improve my practice. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and children are welcome to visit my home to ensure its suitability for their needs. I work in partnership with families to create an environment that meets the physical, emotional, and developmental needs of every child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every parent will have access to the tiney app were I will give regular updates throughout the day, observations linked to the EYFS as well as termly reviews. For children with SEND I can develop Individual Support Plans (ISPs) with parents/carers to outline short-term, measurable targets. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Reasonable adjustments will be made to my home environment to accommodate children and families with disabilities. I will ensure that activities and routines are accessible to all, including those with physical or sensory impairments. I will ensure that activities and routines are accessible to all, including those with physical or sensory impairments. There are 2 steps in get into the house. No steps downstairs where I will have activities, meals and sleep. There are 2 steps to get out into the garden. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? My setting is open to all children, and reasonable adjustments will be made to accommodate specific needs. I work in close collaboration with parents/carers, valuing their input and expertise about their child’s needs. When children start parents will fill out information telling me all about their child (likes, dislikes, routines etc). After 6 weeks I will complete a review of how the child has settled and what we are aiming to achieve, short term and long term. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I regularly update my knowledge through training on SEND, equality, and inclusion to provide the highest level of care and support.

local_offer: Best Start Family Hub Elmhurst offers inclusive services where opportunities are provided for all children. We offer universal and specialised support to families in the local area. We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. We can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families. Our site is accessible and has facilities for disabled visitors. We have strong links with the health team, the speech and language therapy service and other agencies offering support.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our provision provides support services for all families with children aged 0 to 19 years and up to 25 years for those with a SEND. Our aims are to improve parenting, health and children’s development and to provide a safe and stimulating environment for children, young people and their families to flourish, develop and learn. Parents provided with good information so they can make decisions, which will have a significant effect on their children’s life chances. Parents to know, what support and services are available to help them bring up their children, and how to access them. Families signposted into support as appropriate feel confident to provide good life chance for their children. Children to develop social skills in preparation for starting pre-school, nursery or school. Children to enjoy a variety of fun activities and play and learn through this participation. Parents to feel confident in parenting and picking up parenting skills and support through attendance. Personal, Social and Emotional Development. Physical development. Communication and Language Development. Outreach support, action plan to specifically help the family with individual needs. Emotional and practical support from Outreach Worker. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Safeguarding First Aid Early Language Development Programme Hey Programme (Healthy Eating in Young Children) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We welcome all families to all of our services, staff are dedicated to supporting families using our Hub and its services. Our building is fully compliant with the disability requirements. We provide a warm, welcoming and fun learning environment for children and their families. Large and inviting outdoor play environment. Sensory equipment available during sessions. Accessible toilets. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can attend our services and register by completing a Membership form. Outreach support can be provided by self-referral or by referral from a health visitor or other professional. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: Elmhurst School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Aylesbury for 4 to 11-year-olds. Elmhurst School, Dunsham Lane Aylesbury is a Mainstream school. We understand that choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions that you will make and we hope that the information you find here will support you in making this decision. On 1 June 2019 Elmhurst School joined the Great Learners Trust. The Great Learners Trust, which was established in 2014, is a local multi-academy trust specialising in primary education based in Buckinghamshire. The aim of the trust is to provide local, responsive, practical and strategic support for all partner schools; Elmhurst, Great Missenden, Princes Risborough, Wooburn Green, Bearbrook Combined, Bedgrove Junior, Great Kimble and West Wycombe. As a school we are rapidly improving and we are determined to provide a high quality education for all of our children and ensure that each pupil achieves their very best. We ensure that every child is known and cared about as an individual whilst learning in a safe, stimulating and challenging environment. We are continually striving to improve outcomes and life chances for our pupils and make our school the best that it can be. We have high expectations of our community; pupils, parents and staff and our three core school values 'Aspire, Create, Think' run throughout all the work that we do; driving us towards our aim of providing the very best education we can. Elmhurst is a well-resourced primary school; all classrooms are equipped with up-to-date Information Communication Technologies (ICT) and other learning resources. We have a dedicated adult learning space, children's kitchen, counselling hub, sensory room and a well-stocked library. As well as computers in our ICT suite and a class set of tablets for the children to use.We have recently redeveloped our EYFS reception outdoor learning space, our parent/pupil entrance and an artist has worked across the school site to enhance our learning environment. We know that a close partnership with parents is vital to the successful education of all of our children and we encourage parents to communicate with us as a school at every opportunity. Parents are regularly invited into school for our authentic outcomes linked to our Guerrilla Curriculum, end of term productions/performance, sporting events, parent workshops and stay and play sessions. We also have two Family Support Workers on the team who are available to support parents in a wide variety of different ways. Life at Elmhurst reflects our determination to secure the best possible learning outcomes for all. We take every opportunity to celebrate success whilst also ensuring that our children are happy and learn the skills and values to become successful citizens of the future. We have a very dedicated team of staff who work hard to support all of our families. Educating children is a great responsibility and privilege. If you are a parent of a child already attending Elmhurst School, thank you for entrusting us with that job. If you are considering sending your child to our school, please do come and visit; meet the children and staff and talk to us about our vision for the school. We operate an open-door policy and welcome current parents, potential parents and other visitors to come and see the school in action and we look forward to meeting you. Mrs R Lee and Miss K Needham - Co-Headteachers.

local_offer: At Elmhurst, we recognise that sometimes learning can be challenging for some pupils. We provide quality first teaching for all pupils and when pupils have been identified as having additional needs we offer individualised support.Every child on the SEND register has an SEN support plan. This outlines desired outcomes, type of provision, time and financial costings. These are shared with parents and carers three times per year. We have Learning Support Assistants to support those children with additional needs. They are trained to run a number of interventions including: Talk Partner and Shape Coding - to support pupils with speech and language difficulties. Precision Monitoring - to support pupils with specific numerical or literacy difficulties. First Class at Number - to support pupils with Numeracy difficulties. Rainbow Road - to support pupils with gross/fine motor difficulties. Toe-by-Toe - systematic, one-to-one, phonics teaching. New Reading, New Thinking - specific reading activities to develop inferential thinking. local_offer: At Elmtree Infant and Nursery School, we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve their potential. Quality first teaching is mandatory for all children, however, for some children, there are occasions during their school life when additional support may be needed to help them to achieve their goals. All our Local Offer details for Elmtree Infant and Nursery School can be found in our SEN report. https://www.elmtreeschoolandnursery.co.uk/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our regular monitoring of the progress and development of all children throughout their school years enables the identification of any need for additional support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work with staff and parents to carry out an analysis of a child’s progress and implement additional support matched to their area of need. If there is not a sufficient improvement in the child’s progress, we arrange for specialist assessment to be carried out from agencies beyond our setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Our regularly reviewed provisions provide support across the four broad areas of SEN; • Communication and interaction • Cognition and learning • Social, emotional and mental health • Sensory and/or physical needs How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? In addition to our mainstream provision, we also provide education through our Additionally Resourced Provision (ARP). This is for children with an EHCP (Education and Health Care Plan) who have a diagnosed Developmental Language Disorder and require support in Speech, Language and Communication (SLCN). In our ARP we provide specialist teaching along with direct therapy from a qualified Speech and Language Therapist.

Fundraising committee Keyworker information mornings Social events (coffee mornings, discos, quizzes for example) Parent volunteers in the nursery How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? local_offer: I am a self-employed childminder registered with a top-rated and highly supportive childminding agency (tiney co) that allows me to provide the best home-from-home learning and nurturing environment for all young children. Starlight tiney home nursery aims to give local families opportunities to care for their children whatever their needs. Learning through play is key to my setting: the age and stage of the child is considered as well as their individual needs to ensure they enjoy their time with us.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to provide a caring environment where all children are welcomed, respected and supported. We will make our best endeavours to meet the needs of all children so that they can take part in all aspects of our setting in procedures to reach their full potential. I will work closely with any involved professionals to help us to support the children. I will involve parents at every opportunity and work to support them as well as their children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? AET (Autism Education Trust) Making Sense of Autism September 2023 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents, priding myself on clear, regular updates on about their child’s learning, development, and progress on a regular basis via the free tiney phone. I ask parents to share information about their child’s likes and dislikes, the activities which they find difficult and those which they enjoy the most. I aim to ensure that activities are extended to support children to meet their potential within the setting and share ideas with parents for use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children and where there is a particular need, I support the preparation and implementation of a joint action plan for the child. With parents’ permission I may involve other services. I provide increased opportunities for communication for families of children with SEND and are flexible in how we communicate, for example, in person, on phone, email or electronic messages although a strong focus is on the tiney app. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My Starlight tiney home nursery setting is a home from home setting. It is accessible to most children and families. We are on a regular bus route for those needing public transport, and although there is a small step to the front door, the path could be used for wheelchair access. I have a cosy spot for the children to rest when needed and would always discuss options with parents during registration. My outdoor area is mainly laid to lawn with mature borders and shady trees, although not large it is accessible for all from the back door. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All families are welcome to visit me to see my home before registering to attend. I have all of my details on the tiney app which details my policies and most other information parents need to know, but I am also happy to answer any questions. When children arrive, I encourage families to complete an ‘initial contact’ sheet, and if registering complete the child’s ‘passport’ page on the app. I strongly encourage parents to have some ‘settling in visits’ with their child according to my settling in policy. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am constantly aware of the need for flexibility within my setting to ensure that children’s needs can be met. I access training as necessary and will likely will be recruiting an assistant to support me in the future. I keep updated with new guidance from the Local Authority and use their website regularly. I am keen to develop any new strategies such as ‘Hungry Little Minds’ and would like to earn ‘Millie’s Mark’ and Montessori training.

name: Dyslexia Assessments - Your Way Psychology and Education
description: Your Way Psychology and Education is based in Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire, with a clinic in Thame on the Buckinghamshire border. name: Emily Forde
description: My name is Emily and I’m an Ofsted registered childminder offering a nurturing and warm setting from my home in Holmer Green. I’m a member of the Professional Association for Childcare and Early Years (PACEY), I’m paediatric first aid trained and DBS checked. I live with my husband, our two young boys and our cat. I have a dedicated play area, providing a wide range of toys and activities in a safe and stimulating environment. We also have a good size garden space with lots of play equipment to aid physical development. All activities are planned to meet the Early Years Foundation Stage, as well as the needs of each child. I am a Forest Childcare provider as I recognise the importance that outdoor learning has on a child, positively impacting their well being and development. I have two lovely woodland settings with beautiful walks in very close proximity to my home which provides daily opportunities to explore, teaching children to appreciate spending time in the natural environment. As well as this, I am lucky enough to have a wonderful common and play park just 200 yards away. I visit toddler groups weekly and live a 10-minute walk from the Holmer Green Sensory Gardens, which offers a fantastic opportunity to stimulate their minds whilst exercising. I decided to become a childminder as I have a genuine love and passion for spending time with children, encouraging them to play and explore, and watching them develop and grow as a result of this. I’m a very positive person and my motto in life is to always try new things with a ‘can do’ attitude.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes so that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with us. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst in the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared regularly. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling-in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

description: Explore and get messy at Black Park! Relaxed Forest School family sessions for all! Join us in Black Pines Camp for some fun in the woods. local_offer: When a new child starts the setting the child's keyworker will undertake a baseline assessment on the child, this is normally done after the first 6 weeks. During this time the keyworker will carry out observations and plan activities based on the child's interests and most crucial the next step. If a child's key person identifies an individual need at this time or a later point during the child's time at the setting then a meeting will be arranged between the parents, SENCO and; key person. A plan will be devised to ensure the child's individual needs are met and the best possible outcome can be achieved to support you and your child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Here at Aktiva we work alongside the specialist services involved with your child and they are welcome to visit us at any time. Working closely with you and your child will enable us to ensure you and your child receive the best possible outcome, you will be supported throughout by us. We can attend external visits with specialist services should you wish us to be there for support, providing ratios allow. Buckinghamshire Early Years Service supports us to ensure Early Years practitioners provide the best possible experience for all children in our setting. The team will support practitioners in meeting children’s individual needs through offering phone advice, observing individual children in their setting, suggesting ways to support individual needs, planning next steps with practitioners and parents and signposting to training. The parental agreement will always be obtained before the Early Years Service become involved with any individual child. The Early Years Service will support settings in working together with other agencies that may already be involved with a child. We have contact with the following professionals: Speech and Language Therapists Paediatric Occupational Therapists Health Visitors Paediatricians Specialist Teaching Service What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO training (for new and aspiring): Michela Dell, Rachael Mckenzie-Rowland SENCO Level 3: Sarah Blyth Makaton Training level 1: Michela Dell, Sarah Blyth Autism awareness training: Whole staff team Dysphagia, eating and swallowing: Michela Dell HCP Abbott pump training: Michela Dell, Sarah Blyth, Rachael Mckenzie Diabetic Training: Michela Dell, Rachael Mckenzie-Rowland, Sarah Blyth, Ellie White, Jack Deacon, Amber Oldham Step On training: Michela Dell, Rachael Mckenzie-Rowland How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We thrive on creating a warm welcoming nursery. Our aim is to ensure all parents and carers feel part of our Aktiva Family. We have introduced 'Aktiva Storytime' virtually on our social media page as well as in termly newsletters. We have take home bags which include activities for parents to engage in with their children, this will encourage families to engage with their children using the knowledge and expertise of our staff here. We hold parents evenings 3 times a year where you are able to discuss any concerns with your child's keyworker as you look through your child's individual learning journey. Parents have access through our remote parentzone system at all times to be able to view their child's learning journey development, a meeting can be arranged at any point to discuss if needed. As a setting, we like to celebrate families and their individualities by celebrating different festivals throughout the year. We do this by organising different events or days to be had at the nursery such as mothers day breakfast, fathers day tea, grandparents storytelling sessions and many more. We offer various stay and play sessions throughout the year inviting all parents into the setting to see the activities we provide for their children's learning needs. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We have an online system called parentzone where your child's development is recorded through observations. Your keyperson will carry out spontaneous and next step observations to ensure they capture every moment in their development. Each 2 to 3 year old will have a 2-year progress check carried out which will include a written summary of the child's development. We encourage parents to be included in this and write their own comments on the form. For children with SEND, we like to work very closely with the parents and any outside agencies that may be involved. Assess plan do reviews and SEN support plans will be carried out on each individual child who has an additional need. An assessment plan do review can be done on any child who we may feel needs some additional support before SEN intervention. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is all on one ground floor which is accessible via steps or ramps. We have large double doors to enter the building at 2 entrances. We provide free flow to the children throughout the day whereby they make the choice as to whether they would like to play in or out. We go outside in all weathers as we believe children can have the same learning experiences both indoors and outdoors. We believe that cultural capital is giving children the best possible start in life and providing them with opportunities they may not always get at home. Each room within the setting has a quiet area where the children can relax and reflect on what's going on around them. We use in the moment planning where the children's interest and most crucial next steps are used to determine what we provide for the children on a day to day basis. This can be changed at any point to reflect the children's needs and each child as an individual. For SEN children we engage the children in a distraction-free environment called our well-being room, to help fulfil their additional needs and support in regulating their emotions. We also have our very own nursery library where we engage in small group interventions with the children. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When starting the setting you and your child will be offered 2 settlings in sessions. If we feel the child needs more after this or as a parent you need more then these can be arranged. All about me forms are completed by the parent to ensure we have as much information to help your child settle into their new environment. When a child moves to the next room to further their development, settling in sessions will be arranged internally for the child. A transition document is completed by the current keyworker and passed onto the new keyworker to ensure everything about the child is known to them. With our pre-schoolers transitioning to big school your child's keyworker will complete a transition report and we have created links with our local schools in order to pass this information on to them. When it comes closer to the time we will provide as many opportunities as possible for the children to talk to us about going to big school, this helps the transition and change easier for children and the parents. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our children's needs are always paramount, we will continue to look for any new training our staff may need additional to what we have and any new resources we feel may benefit the children in our setting. At Aktiva we strive to provide a safe, fun and friendly environment where our children build confidence and broaden their experience.

Please be aware that children must be supervised by parents at all times. Are you struggling with the cost of living crisis and need support with a number of different issues? If you need extra support, email the community support team to find out more.

name: Next Steps Parent and Toddler Group
description: Next Steps is run by the Community Support Team at One Can Trust. It is open to everyone who would like a friendly place to come with their under-4s. As with all of our projects, our sessions are completely free! Our ethos is to recognise the importance of developing early years social skills, learning and play for our little ones, and for parents, a place to visit for a coffee and a chat. The group runs from the Wesley Methodist Church, on Priory Road in High Wycombe, every Tuesday morning from 10am to 12 midday. Please be aware that children must be supervised by parents at all times. Are you struggling with the cost of living crisis and need support with a number of different issues? Our First Steps parents and toddler group is by invitation only, is a closed group, and our families are supported and nurtured by a team of qualified and experienced staff and volunteers. If you need extra support, email the community support team to find out more.

name: Learning for Life
description: Learning for Life is a project covering personal health, emotions, relationships, and appropriate behaviour. We will be releasing new material in sets of videos covering particular areas of need for our community. Built to support young people in primary and secondary school and beyond, Learning for Life provides critical teaching on key areas of social and emotional development. While many typically-developing young people will understand many of these concepts without being taught, learners with Down’s syndrome and other special educational needs may not learn so well through inference. We provide the clear-cut, specialist teaching that is so desperately needed for our learners. From privacy and appropriate touch, through to introspection and emotional rollercoasters during puberty, Learning for Life is made to cover specific areas for the benefit of learners with Down’s syndrome and SEND. As with everything we do here at Learn and Thrive, Learning for Life is totally free to sign up to and access, for use at home, in school, and in support groups. Check out our website below for more information.

name: Weekly Mentoring Sessions
description: As a child, the transition from primary school to secondary school can be a challenging and formative time. That’s why Spark2Life’s Buckinghamshire Transition Project focuses on mentoring those children while employing a person-centered and trauma-informed approach. The young people are carefully paired with a suitable mentor who provides guidance through the transition process while also supporting the children through any other daily challenges they may face. Mentoring sessions are carried out by volunteers who complete Spark2Life’s 8-week AQA accredited Wholistic Mentoring Training course fully equipping and empowering them to become culturally competent Community Mentors. The Transition Project works with young people from ethnically diverse communities and in addition to our mentoring sessions, we deliver a PSHE session on culture and identity. Our sessions are currently delivered in four primary schools across Buckinghamshire where our mentors meet 1:1 with the young people on a weekly basis, for an hour during term time. The project aims to build trusting relationships and aspirations, increase both self-confidence and self-awareness, while developing resilience within the young people as they transition to secondary school. Interested in becoming one of Spark2Life’s Community Mentors? Please visit our website to register your interest. If you would like to refer a young person, please use the referral form on our website.

description: At art-K, our goal is to nurture creativity and build confidence in our students through engaging and inclusive art classes. We’ve tried and tested many different programmes over the past 25 years, before arriving at the one we teach today. Our projects teach artistic skills, whilst encouraging students to bring their individuality to the classes. We offer weekly art classes and workshops in a supportive, non-competitive environment, featuring projects in drawing, painting, 3D modelling, mixed media, papier mâché, and more. We celebrate each student’s unique artistic journey with a personalised approach tailored to the individual, prioritising self-esteem and a sense of belonging. Our teachers are fully trained in the art-K programme, health and safety, and safeguarding. They are professional, caring, and DBS-checked, with a max ratio of 7 students per teacher.

Our projects teach artistic skills, whilst encouraging students to bring their individuality to the classes. We offer weekly art classes and workshops in a supportive, non-competitive environment, featuring projects in drawing, painting, 3D modelling, mixed media, papier mâché, and more. We celebrate each student’s unique artistic journey with a personalised approach tailored to the individual, prioritising self-esteem and a sense of belonging. Our teachers are fully trained in the art-K programme, health and safety, and safeguarding. They are professional, caring, and DBS-checked, with a max ratio of 7 students per teacher.

description: With 10 acres of fun and adventure at Tumblestone Hollow and the Gardens at Stonor to explore we’re certain you’re in for a great day of fun and fabulous play together. Tumblestone Hollow has been designed for children and families to play together. It is suitable for all ages but will be enjoyed by younger children up to around 12 years of age. Open February too July and from early September. The average time that visitors spend at Tumblestone Hollow and the Gardens at Stonor is four hours but many visitors stay all day, enjoying lunch at our Rumble and Jumble Huts that serve mouth-watering wood-fired pizzas, soft serve Italian Gelato ice cream, hand-blended American style milkshakes and soon to come loaded fries and classic hamburgers made from organic Longhorn Beef from English Farm and organic cheese from the Nettlebed Creamery, both located within a couple of miles of Stonor.

local_offer: I provide an inclusive and nurturing environment in my home where all children are treated equally and are given the opportunity to reach their full potential. I observe and monitor individual needs to ensure that activities and resources can be adapted and made accessible by all. All children are welcome in my home regardless of their gender, race, culture, special needs or disability. I will develop my knowledge further by undergoing SEND training over the year and will seek out any specific training to ensure I can support a particular child’s needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to provide a calm, welcoming and nurturing environment for all children where their well-being remains high during their time with me. Settling in sessions will be adapted to each individual child’s needs to ensure they settle in happily. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All about me forms are provided and filled in by parents to gain a better understanding of the child before a settling in visit. Parents are involved with initial settling in visits and then updated by conversations at the end of the session and during the day with updates on the app Babydays. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents are given regular updates on the app with photos and observations and are invited to have a conversation over the phone or in person at the end of the day. Meetings will be held to discuss observations and next steps and possible intervention with outside agencies to support the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Settling in sessions will be adapted to meet the needs of both the child and family before starting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I have undergone various SEND training in my teaching career, however plan to access a range of SEND courses over the next year and when needed to develop my knowledge and ensure I can support the children I care for.

name: Burnham Football Club
description: Burnham Football Club is proud of its association with grassroots junior football, especially when it comes to developing the skills of young players from the local community. Our vision is to create a pathway for young players into a senior squad including our own first team. Our current Burnham Football Club junior and youth teams are: Burnham FC Under 18 years and Burnham FC Under 15 years We also offer: Football Development Centre (5 to 3 years) Little Blues Toddler Football (2 to 5 years) Our Football Development Centre is typically on a Friday evening. Whether your child plays for a club, or a school team or simply wants to give it a go for the first time the Football Development Centre is an ideal environment to discover, learn and improve. We utilise our FIFA Certified state-of-the-art 3G pitch and excellent onsite facilities, ensuring players aged from 5 to 13 years develop as skilled footballers, and remain safe, while still having lots of fun. We aim to initiate and support the long-term development of your child’s journey in football, providing skills they can use at school or at their regular football club. Players benefit from: Fun and engaging coaching sessions, within a safe environment, managed by qualified professionals. Actively developing individual ball skills, communication, confidence and teamwork on a state-of-the-art FIFA Certified 3G artificial pitch in groups based on age and ability. Providing no end of fun, regardless of the weather conditions. Parents benefit from: Free on-site parking, indoor and outdoor toilets, undercover seating, a pitch-side snack bar, and a licensed bar with Sky Sports and BT Sports. Football Development Centre - Fridays, 5:45pm to 7pm | £30 per month. Our Little Blues Toddler Football is for children aged 2 until their 5th Birthday, every Saturday morning and it’s held indoors on a soft play floor. Little Blues Toddler Football - Saturday mornings from 10am | £30 per month. To book a free trial register via the link provided or visit the club's main website.

description: The Employment Service in Buckinghamshire Talking Therapies has been set up to provide support for people experiencing anxiety, depression or other common mental health issues and who are in need of support related to employment. Waythrough Employment Specialists, working as part of the Bucks Talking Therapies team, can provide employment support whether you are currently employed, off sick from work or unemployed and looking to find work. Our Employment Specialists can: Offer support on how to job search, disclose a mental health condition, CV’s, making applications and interview techniques. Signpost you to where you can access voluntary work or training. Work with you to understand your preferences, values, experiences, and skills. Help you to identify any adjustments that may be required to enter the workplace. Who we help The service is for anyone with a mild to moderate mental health condition who is aged over 18 and registered with a GP in Bucks and referred to us by Bucks Talking Therapies.

description: PreSchool Disco is a fun, feel-good, multi-sensory disco service that offers weekly classes for children up to age 8. Our toe-tapping tunes and boredom-busting props get everyone up and dancing - think lights, bubbles, giant balloons, musical instruments, and so much more! The energetic music, traditional party games, and constantly changing activities help keep children of all ages (and their adults) engaged throughout the session. Every day is a party with PreSchool Disco! Weekly sessions last around 45 minutes and can be booked on a pay-as-you-go basis. Advance tickets (booked up to midnight of the day before) are priced at £6 for the first child and £3 for walking siblings. Tickets booked on the day are £7 for the first child and £3 for siblings. No prior experience is necessary.

name: Support for Families with Sickle Cell
description: Cianna's Smile is a registered charity which offers information, support, free activities, and advocacy for children with sickle cell in Reading and across the UK. What We Do Our programmes are vibrant, inclusive, and full of energy. We support children, young people, and their families through: Online Youth Entrepreneur Club – Inspiring 8 to 16 year olds to explore skills in digital marketing, podcasting, cooking, and more. Create and Connect Club – A safe space for children with Sickle Cell to enjoy workshops inspired by art, music, and nature. Art Club: Drop-In Sessions – For young adults aged 18 to 25 living with a health condition to express themselves through themed art activities. Young Adult Walks – Friendly walks around Reading town centre, followed by snacks and a chat back at our office. We also screen our short film on sickle cell and blood donation as well as delivering informal talks in school, colleges, universities, and workplaces to increase understanding about sickle cell and promote blood donation. We also offer free days out, respite breaks, community family fun day events free for children and their families impacted by Sickle Cell.

description: The Education Safeguarding Advisory Service helps protect and safeguard children by training and supporting staff in schools, colleges, and other educational settings. We provide services to all forms of educational establishments in Buckinghamshire so that they can fulfill their responsibilities under current legislation and government guidance on safeguarding. We are located within the Children’s Services Directorate and play a key role in representing educational establishments at a range of multi-agency meetings and forums in order to promote inter-agency work. local_offer: First Steps First is a family run day nursery for children aged from 0 to 5 years olds, where we are an enthusiastic and fun loving team, who strive to meet the needs of all the children in the setting and give them the best start in life as possible and plan and meet their needs on a individual basis.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? First Steps First prides itself for having high aspirations for all our children and our aim is that every child has a fun experience in a caring atmosphere across all age groups. We aim that all children will be supported to the best of our ability to make the best progress they can, relative to their stage of development. We aim that all our families feel included in nursery life and realise that we are partners in supporting their child to reach their potential by working together. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Natasha Andree-NSPCC- Safeguarding children and young people with SEND. Pediatric first aid that includes anaphylaxis. Lisa Francis- Initial SENCO Training with Bucks council, Autistic Spectrum Disorders (ASD) in early years, Makaton and Paediatric first aid with anaphylaxis. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they can approach us about anything relating to their children with an open door policy. We have formal opportunities for contact with parents at our termly Key Person Meetings. There are also many informal opportunities to chat and when parents request a meeting, we aim to meet with them as soon as possible. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time by asking their child’s Key Person and via our Tapestry app. We will discuss progress at Key Person Meetings, and through our 2-year-old progress checks and end of year summary assessment sheets. For children with SEND we try to ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes with additional observations monthly to track progress How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We consider the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We try to create areas where distractions are minimized for focused learning and to create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing issues. We use Makaton with all children to aid communication and will provide visual aids that include pecs. We encourage exploring our feelings and have resources to support this. First Steps First is all on one level and has direct access to the outdoor environment. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents and families are welcome to come along to our open day sessions to look at the setting, meet the team and talk through any queries. We have a registration process along with All about me forms to fill in all the information needed. Parents with children with SEND are invited to make a special visit to discuss how we can best meet their needs. We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavor to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We regularly visit the local schools with children who are transferring. We will offer as many settling in sessions needed to ensure the transition is a positive experience for all. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Natasha is due to start her training with Bucks Council to further her qualification in SEND, and Lisa Francis is fluent in Makaton and will be sharing this with all staff members. We will widen our SEND resources and build on having visual routines and sensory play areas. Staff will carry out all the appropriate training and regular courses through bucks council or online training providers. Information for parents will be available for example how to access Speech and Language through SLT and local services and work alongside other professionals that can support us as a setting and all our families.

name: Everlief Child Psychology Clinic
description: Everlief have opened a private family-friendly clinic in the beautiful and historic West Wycombe. All our clinical psychologists hold a Doctorate in Clinical Psychology and are Chartered Psychologists. All our clinical psychologists are registered with the BPS and the HCPC (Health and Care Professions Council). Our psychologists can support any child but also have areas of special interest such as anxiety, autism, or eating disorders. Dr Lucy Russell, our Clinical Director is also an associate fellow of the British Psychological Society, and is on their list of registered supervisors. Lucy is also a guest lecturer on the Oxford Doctoral Course in Clinical Psychology at the Oxford Institute of Clinical Psychology Training (University of Oxford). Everlief offers assessments, 1 to 1 therapy for children, parenting support, and workshops. We work with all areas of emotional and behavioural difficulties in children and specialise in psychological therapies including CBT. Please consider Everlief for: - Families seeking ASD diagnosis - Difficulties associated with autism, Asperger’s syndrome - Behavioural issues - Worry and anxiety - Low self-esteem, low mood, depression, or self-harm - Fears and phobias - Faddy eating or eating difficulties - Toileting issues - Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) - General parenting support and advice Everlief is also a specialist in carrying out autism assessments. Finally, Everlief also have an educational psychologist available for one-hour appointments. These are designed to help you plan the best way forward for your child's education needs.

name: Exclusions and Reintegration Team
description: The Buckinghamshire Exclusion and Reintegration Officers work closely with parents and carers, schools, governors, and local authority colleagues to provide advice on: - Preventing suspensions and permanent exclusions - Ensuring that the DfE exclusion guidance and other policies and procedures are followed correctly The DfE Exclusion guidance, in the case of permanent exclusion: - A member of the team will contact the pupil’s family and inform them of the permanent exclusion process and appeals process - The team will arrange educational provision from the sixth day of the permanent exclusion - The team will bring the pupil’s case to a Fair Access Board Meeting and facilitate the transfer of the pupil back to a mainstream school Where a parent or professional tells us that a child has no educational placement, details will be logged and progress tracked, with intervention and support offered as appropriate. Advice for parents is also available from: - Buckinghamshire Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Information Advice Support (SENDIAS) - The School Exclusion Project - Independent Parental Special Educational Advice (IPSEA): - The Children's Legal Centre - Buckinghamshire Council School admissions

name: Bellboating for Families With Disabled Children or Adults
description: We can enable families who have disabled children or adults to enjoy the water at Bisham Abbey in a bell boat (like a double canoe and very stable). We supply safety equipment and a qualified helm with a safety boat to ensure all trips on the river are safe. We can cater for individual families or groups and have shore-side facilities (toilets and a large stretch tent with picnic tables) and, as Kenneth Graham said in Wind in the Willows, "Believe me, my young friend, there is nothing - absolutely nothing - half so much worth doing as simply messing about in boats." We are a charity and as such do not charge for activities for families but appreciate donations from £10 to £30 for a family if possible, but the cost should never be a barrier to participation. All staff and trustees are unpaid volunteers. We operate from around the start of April until the end of September depending on the state of the river. Registered Charity number 1181307

description: The school is set in rural Derbyshire with close transport links to the diverse cities of Derby and Sheffield and we specialise in working with young people with Autism and Developmental Language Disorder. We have over 30 years of nationally recognised skill and experience within the educational field of Autism and Communication and our team of Speech and Language Therapists and Occupational Therapists is one of the largest in any school across the country. This, alongside our Mental Health Team provides us with an unrivalled level of expertise. Our underpinning ethos of “Unconditional Positive Regard and fulfilment in life” guides all that we do and our outstanding outcomes, we believe, speak for themselves. We provide each young person with academic and social challenge through highly personalised, creatively designed programmes and curricula along with an extremely strong, well-established pastoral system of support, care, and guidance. I am extremely proud to be the Headteacher of our school, a school which I believe, gives young people an exceptional chance to fulfil their academic, social and independence potential.
organisation: SENAD Group Alderwasley Hall School and Sixth Form is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 5 to 19 years with Specific Language Disorders, Aspergers Syndrome and High Functioning Autistic Spectrum Disorders, all of whom experience complex speech, language and communication needs. The School and Sixth Form are located on separate sites within five miles of each other and are situated in Derbyshire, close to the towns of Matlock, Belper and Wirksworth. The City of Derby is also within easy access. The aim of all aspects of the curriculum is to prepare students for adult life by fulfilling their social and academic potential. Young people are supported to develop and achieve academic and vocational plans, develop independent living skills and a clear sense of identity, enabling them to contribute to society in adult life. The individual needs of students, as set out in their Education, Care and Health Plan are met through Therapy and educational programmes, underpinned by high-quality care. info@senadgroup.com https://senadgroup.com/alderwasley/

name: Family and Carer Service | One Recovery Bucks (ORB)
description: Family and Carer Service One Recovery Bucks (ORB). Living with someone who uses drugs and/or alcohol can be difficult and we recognise that it can cause extreme stress. It’s common to experience a range of emotions such as have feelings of anger, guilt, disappointment, fear, and isolation. We have a range of activities where you can get the right help for you and your family. We can provide face-to-face, telephone, and email information advice and support: Support groups for carers and family members. Information and advice specific to drug and alcohol use, via written publications, drop-in sessions, online support, and helpline. One-to-one support. Safeguarding information, including information on duty of care to protect any individuals affected by someone’s substance use. Signposting carers to Buckinghamshire Council commissioned carers services for a specialist carers assessment where appropriate. Enable families and carers to form and access community networks. Support to family members and carers who wish to train as volunteers inside the service. There’s nothing to lose, if you’re worried about getting in touch, we have so much positive feedback from parents and loved ones who have learned to navigate the difficulties and distress of a loved one’s drug use, and consequently, the choices and behaviour this can bring. They are now out on the ‘other side’ of their dark times and this doesn’t always mean their loved one has stopped using, it just means they have learned skills to help them manage the relationship, communication and problems.

description: Looking for the ultimate holiday experience for your child? Our MegaCamps run during all the school holidays (excluding Christmas) at Amersham School and Davenies School in Buckinghamshire offer a fun, safe, and high-energy environment for children aged 5 to 12 years. Each camp is led by our experienced, DBS-checked coaching team. Whether your child loves multi-sports, football, dance, or simply making new friends, MegaCamps are designed to keep them active, engaged, and smiling all day long. With flexible booking options, extended hours, and exciting add-ons like Swimming Inflatables, Go Karting, Clip ’n Climb and Seasonal Excursions, there's something for every child, every day. Join us for an unforgettable holiday filled with fun, friendships, and fantastic memories! Whether your child is a total beginner, a seasoned pro, or simply curious to try something new, they’ll find plenty to love here. And the best part? Flexibility is key! If they decide to switch things up and try a different course during the camp, no problem at all—just let us know, and we’ll make it happen. Adventure and fun await at every turn! Whether your child is new to sports, has plenty of experience or just fancies trying something different, there's something for everyone at our MegaCamps! organisation: Family Fund Family Fund supports families living across the UK who are raising a disabled or seriously ill child or young person up to the age of 17. Our support is focused on those on low incomes with a child/children who have a high level of additional support needs. At Family Fund, we believe that all families raising disabled or seriously ill children and young people should have the same choices, quality of life, opportunities and aspirations as other families. We support this by providing grants for a range of essential items. Families can apply for kitchen appliances such as fridges, freezers and cookers, as well as clothing, bedding, games, books and music, laptops and tablets, family breaks, sensory toys and more. If you’re thinking of applying to Family Fund, you can apply online or download or order an application pack. comms@familyfund.org.uk https://www.familyfund.org.uk/

I work closely with parents/carers and professionals to ensure that every child is supported and encouraged to ensure the best outcomes.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat each child as an individual and support their progress in all arears of their development. I will have close contact with parents/carers and involve them within my childminding practice. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed a course on autism and make a point of keeping up to date with recent updates and new beneficial activities. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I communicate daily with parents via WhatsApp both individually and as a parent group for Bumble Tots. Daily routines, activities, events, current learning subjects and how families can support ideas along with photographs are posted. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Each parent will have their own private whatsApp link where daily updates and photos are shared. All children attending are monitored and observed. Any concerns about a child's development are shared with parents and support plan made to help the child. I will discuss if further support is needed or parents would like the help of other services. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? I am happy to discuss a child's individual needs and accommodate where possible. My setting has a sloped drive to front entrance and a step. Inside is open plan with easy access to the rear garden. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I have contact with other childminders, playgroups, schools and pre schools. we work in close partnerships and ensure effective transitions for all children. I offer all new children settling in sessions. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I intend to continue with training courses to extend my knowledge. I want to extend my outside space and offer forest school.

name: Christ Church United Reformed Church | Marlow
description: Christ Church is a local congregation of the United Reformed Church (URC). We are in a 'joint pastorate' with Maidenhead URC, Bracknell URC and Windsor URC, sharing the ministry of Reverend Chris Parker. Every week our church offers the chance to worship, but in different ways and sometimes in different places. We normally have a fairly traditional form of worship that lasts just under an hour on Sunday mornings at 10:30am. This is followed by refreshments. Everyone is welcome to come and join us. Please note that you won’t be expected to do anything you’d rather not do, there is no money offering in the service (although donations can be taken), and simple guidelines such as ‘please be seated’ (for example) are given throughout the service. On the third Sunday of the month, we offer a Zoom service to help those housebound, away on holiday, or just simply for those who prefer it. Feel free to email the church secretary for the Zoom link. On the fifth Sunday of the month, we do something special with one of our sister churches. If no update is showing here, please check our website or Facebook page. We have extra worship around special events, around Easter, Christmas and other times. Together with our sister church in Maidenhead, we run an Aid for Ukraine project. Our church is open on Fridays from 10am to 11am and on Sundays from 4pm to 5pm to receive donations. The list of goods needed is on our website. These donations are then sent to communities in Ukraine, mainly in Kherson and surrounding villages, that desperately need our help.

name: Embracing Autism Course
description: The Embracing Autism course is for you if your child has recently been diagnosed. It is also suitable if your child is on a waiting list to be assessed for autism. By the end of the course you will have a deeper understanding of your child and how to help them thrive. You will understand how to support their social skills and confidence and their emotional development. Unlike the other courses, this course cannot be started at any time. It runs approximately every 2 to 3 months and all parents start and finish at the same time. A module is released every Monday for 7 weeks from the start date. Watch or listen to the videos on your computer or mobile device. Each module is a total of around an hour. The topics are: 1. All About Autism 2 Coping and Behaviour: School and Home 3 Sensory Processing (including Eating) 4 Social Communication and Interaction 5 Anxiety and Stress 6 Sensory and Emotional Regulation 7 Sleep 8. Live workshop: At the end of the course, we will meet for a live Q and A online workshop on Zoom. All topics relate to young children through to young people up to 18 years of age.
organisation: Everlief Child Psychology Clinic Everlief have opened a private family-friendly clinic in the beautiful and historic West Wycombe All our clinical psychologists hold a Doctorate in Clinical Psychology and are Chartered Psychologists [Doctorate in Clinical Psychology, Chartered Psychologist]. All our clinical psychologists are registered with the BPS and the HCPC (health and care professions council). Our psychologists can support any child but also have areas of special interest such as anxiety, autism or eating disorders. Dr Lucy Russell, our clinical Director is also an associate fellow of the British Psychological Society, and is on their list of registered supervisors. Lucy is also a guest lecturer on the Oxford Doctoral Course in Clinical Psychology at the Oxford Institute of Clinical Psychology Training (University of Oxford). Everlief offering assessments, 1-1 therapy for children, parenting support and workshops. We work with all areas of emotional and behavioural difficulties in children and specialise in psychological therapies including CBT. Please consider Everlief for: Families seeking ASD diagnosis Difficulties associated with autism/Asperger’s syndrome Behavioural issues Worry and anxiety Low self-esteem, low mood, depression or self-harm Fears and phobias Faddy eating or eating difficulties Toileting issues Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) General parenting support and advice Everlief is also a specialist in carrying out autism assessments. Finally, Everlief also have an educational psychologist available for one-hour appointments. These are designed to help you plan the best way forward for your child's education needs. mikerussell@everlief.co.uk https://www.everlief.co.uk/

description: The SpLD Hub provides specialist assessment and support for children, young people, and adults with dyslexia, dyscalculia, and other specific learning differences (SpLDs). Services include diagnostic dyslexia and dyscalculia assessments, combined assessments, ADHD screening, Exam Access Arrangements assessments, specialist teaching, study skills, and individualised SpLD support. Led by APC-qualified Specialist SpLD Assessor and Teacher Emma Stokes, who has worked specifically within SpLD practice since 2017 and completed more than 200 in-depth assessments, The SpLD Hub combines assessment expertise with practical specialist teaching experience. Assessments provide a clear understanding of an individual's strengths and difficulties, alongside practical recommendations for support at school, in further or higher education, and in the workplace. local_offer: The SpLD Hub provides specialist SEND assessment and support for children, young people, and adults with specific learning differences (SpLDs), including dyslexia and dyscalculia. Support is tailored to the individual and may include diagnostic assessment, specialist 1:1 teaching, literacy and numeracy intervention, study skills, Functional Skills support, and strategies to develop confidence and independence in learning. We also provide ADHD screening and Exam Access Arrangements assessments, alongside support for individuals with processing, memory, and executive functioning difficulties. Our approach focuses on understanding each individual's strengths and areas of difficulty and translating this into practical, realistic strategies that can be used at home, in education and, where appropriate, in the workplace. We work collaboratively with families, schools, education providers and other professionals to help individuals access appropriate support and make progress.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To help children and young people understand their strengths and difficulties, build confidence, and develop effective strategies for learning. We aim to give families and education settings clear, practical, recommendations so that assessment leads to meaningful and appropriate support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Recent and ongoing specialist training includes SpLD diagnostic assessment, dyslexia and dyscalculia, SEND, ADHD screening (QbCheck), and adult DCD screening. I hold an Assessment Practising Certificate (APC), AMBDA and a PGCert in SEND, alongside regular CPD to maintain and develop specialist practice. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are involved throughout the process, providing background information and sharing their observations and concerns. Assessment findings and recommendations are explained clearly, with opportunities to ask questions and discuss appropriate next steps and support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents and carers receive clear feedback on progress, including strengths, areas for development and recommended next steps. For children with SEND, support is individualised to their specific learning profile, with progress reviewed and strategies adapted where needed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The SpLD Hub provides a quiet, comfortable, and low-distraction indoor environment, with support adapted to individual SEND needs. The assessment and teaching space is on the ground floor. Please contact us in advance to discuss any specific accessibility requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact The SpLD Hub directly to discuss their needs or book an assessment or support service through the website. No formal referral is required. We are happy to discuss which service may be most appropriate before booking. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to continue developing our specialist SEND provision through expanded assessment, teaching and support services, alongside practical resources for families and education settings. Provision will continue to evolve in response to individual needs and current evidence-based practice.

local_offer: Our tailored support for children and young adults encompasses a holistic approach to address the unique challenges they may face. For those with autism, our programs are designed to provide a supportive and understanding environment, focusing on individual needs to enhance social interaction, communication skills, and overall well-being. For individuals dealing with social, emotional, and mental health difficulties, our dedicated team offers empathetic guidance. We prioritize emotional well-being through specialized interventions, fostering coping mechanisms, and building resilience. Cognition and learning support is personalized to accommodate diverse learning styles. Our educators employ adaptive teaching methods, aiming to enhance cognitive skills, address learning gaps, and empower students to succeed academically. In all aspects, our goal is to create an inclusive and nurturing space, promoting the overall development and success of every child and young adult in our care.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our primary goal is to empower children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) along with their families by fostering a positive and inclusive environment. The outcomes we aim to achieve include: 1. Individualised Growth: Tailored support to facilitate personal development, promoting independence, and enhancing skills that lead to greater self-confidence and autonomy. 2. Academic Success: Providing specialised education to bridge learning gaps, ensuring that every child achieves their academic potential, irrespective of their learning needs. 3. Social and Emotional Well-being: Nurturing a supportive community where children and young people with SEND can thrive socially and emotionally, building strong interpersonal skills and resilience. 4. Inclusive Environment: Fostering an inclusive setting that celebrates diversity, ensuring that each individual feels valued and accepted for who they are. 5. Family Engagement: Establishing strong partnerships with families, offering guidance, resources, and a collaborative approach to support both the child and their family throughout their educational journey. 6. Transition Readiness: Equipping young adults with the skills and confidence needed for transitions, whether it be moving between educational stages or preparing for employment and independent living. 7. Holistic Development: Recognising the uniqueness of each individual, we aim to promote holistic development – encompassing cognitive, social, emotional, and physical well-being.
