Our commitment to providing the best support for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) is reflected in the recent training completed by our dedicated staff and volunteers. Some of the specific training includes: 1. Autism Awareness and Strategies: Training focused on understanding and effectively supporting individuals on the autism spectrum, including strategies for communication, sensory considerations, and promoting inclusivity. 2. Emotional and Mental Health Support: Workshops addressing the emotional well-being of children with SEND, equipping our team with strategies to recognize and respond to emotional and mental health difficulties. 3. Differentiated Instruction Techniques:Training in varied teaching methods to accommodate diverse learning styles, ensuring that each child receives personalized and effective support tailored to their unique needs. 4. Behavior Management: Techniques and approaches for positive behavior management, fostering a positive learning environment and addressing challenging behaviors with empathy and understanding. 5. Communication and Language Support: Training to enhance communication skills, including alternative communication methods, to better support children with speech and language difficulties. 6. Inclusive Education Practices: Workshops emphasizing the importance of inclusive education and providing tools for creating an environment that celebrates diversity and promotes equal opportunities. 7. Legal and Policy Updates: Keeping our staff informed about the latest legal and policy developments in the field of SEND to ensure compliance and the highest standard of care. 8. This training underscores our dedication to creating a secure and protective environment for all children, where their safety and welfare are paramount. Support Networks: Facilitating parent support networks, where parents can connect with each other, share experiences, and provide mutual support. Accessible Resources: Providing parents with accessible resources, including information on SEND, strategies for home support, and relevant educational materials to empower them in their role. 7. Feedback Mechanisms: Establishing open feedback mechanisms to encourage parents to share their thoughts, concerns, and suggestions, creating a dynamic dialogue for continuous improvement. description: Registered Childminder – High Wycombe (Micklefield Area) My name is Yasmin, and I am a registered childminder since 2023, offering high-quality childcare in a warm, safe, and nurturing home-from-home environment. I am based in High Wycombe, Micklefield area, and provide care that supports children’s individual needs, routines, and stages of development. My setting includes a dedicated playroom with direct access to a secure side garden, allowing children to enjoy a balance of indoor and outdoor play. I offer a wide range of age-appropriate resources that support the seven areas of learning and development in line with the EYFS. Children take part in a variety of home-based activities and regular outings, which may include: National Trust parks Local playgroups Soft play centres Libraries Farms These experiences help promote confidence, social skills, independence, and a love of learning. What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? In my setting I will ensure that every child has the support and will have individualised programmes suited to their needs. To make sure they are progressing in all aspects of their development. I will work with a flexible attitude to include all children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Attention Hillingdon (2013) The intervention was put in place to better equip setting based practitioners to meet the needs of young children with a diagnosis of ASD or with social communication difficulties. Attention Hillingdon is an exciting and innovative project currently running within nurseries, playgroups and children's centres within the borough. The intervention supports the development of attention and listening skills and promotes the development of social communication skills. SEN Training Sign language Pecs Communication folders I would attend online courses to update and further knowledge with SEND Speak to Early Years Team and keep update with their information. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? In my setting I will make sure myself and parents/career work together to get the best outcome for their child. we will work together to discuss their child needs and daily routine to make it consistent. I will also have daily catch up with parents/carers on what the child has done daily at my setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working closely with parents to share information about their child’s learning development and progress is shared on a regular basic. Every child that is at my setting will be monitored and observed to support their individual needs. Any concerns I have regarding a child I will share with parents/careers and work out a next plan of action to support their child. If I felt I need additional help, I would contact my Early Years Authority team. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is accessible, however children with mobility difficulties, my setting does not provide a ramp and doors are not wide enough to cater this. I would try to be accommodating where is possible. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I would work closely in partnership with parents/career, childminders, schools, pre – schools, nursey and my early year’s authority team to ensure that every child has a smooth transition into my setting. I will work closely with parents/careers to discuss their child needs for example ‘all about me booklet’, ‘Learning journey’. If a child has been to another setting, I would ask parents/careers to provide their learning journey from that setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

local_offer: The Buckinghamshire Early Years team are delighted to be able to offer parents of autistic young children (with or without a diagnosis) the opportunity to learn together with their child’s settings. They will work closely together and learn about autism and strategies to support learning at home and in the setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to help families and settings to learn together about autism so that they can work collaboratively to support their autistic child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All trainers are also Neuroinclusive Education Network Trainers and undertake regular Continuing Professional Development relating to autism. Recent training has included: - Autism Communication and social interaction - Current autism research; Autism Young Experts Panel - Education - Sensory Processing, anxiety and Autism - Attention Autism Training - Understanding and supporting children with PDA - Autism and masking - Autism and Double Empathy How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We use venues across the county and try to ensure that they are accessible for families and practitioners. local_offer: At Little Hands, we do not discriminate against any child. I will place in measures if I feel a child in my setting requires help and anything that needs to be addressed. I will make parents aware of these requirements and measures I put in place beforehand and keep them up to date on any changes I feel would need early intervention by health professionals. I aim to provide the best quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each child. I am a mum to two little ones, a 2 year old boy and a 5 year old girl having two children myself I have lots of experience in nurturing and putting health provisions into place. Within Little Hands Childminding I make sure children within the setting are not excluded and ensure that all activities can be adjusted to accommodate every unique child and promote trying new things. Little Hands childminding-Aylesbury is a home from home setting, offering a fun, encouraging and happy environment for children. I make sure children, whilst in my care feel safe, secure and have the confidence to try new things all whilst making them feel like a part of the family. In the week I venture out to local toddler groups and clubs, this I find helps to build on the child's social, socialising with children their age or older, meeting friends and emotional development that would help towards when they eventually start school. I have a secure garden which is accessible all the time with a range of toys and activities suitable for all. I am paediatric first aid trained and I am more than happy to extend my training to include specific needs if needed. With my first aid training, I attended epi-pen training.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a registered Ofsted childminder, I will work with my Key contact within the Early Years Teams at Buckinghamshire Council. Having the child's parental permission, I may in some cases contact them for further advice for the child's needs. I will provide parents and promote helpful websites such as Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and Salt websites that may be useful for them and help them out the best I can. I intend to welcome other specialists and health professionals into my setting who I currently have contact with and may have been involved with a child already. I am very keen to access further training to support each child's needs that come into my setting. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I am continuously taking courses to accommodate Autism and ADHD. If I had a child with SEND I would go on the correct training for the particular area I need to. Supporting early language and SEND code of practice. I work and have first contact with and in partnership with the NHS physiotherapy team and Portage Workers. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Working in close partnership with parents/carers. The child's learning, development and progression will be shared regularly with the parents and carers. Their child's likes and dislikes will be monitored and shared with the parents. I will bring in activities to support the child's learning and monitor how they interact and show enjoyment within the activity. All routines within the setting and at home will be discussed before starting and throughout time within the setting. Helping consistency throughout the day. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Within my setting, my aim and plan is to monitor and observe children to support their individual needs regarding their learning and development. If I have any concerns at all with regards to a child's development I will raise this with the parent/carer and put into action what we could do to help their needs and development. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? At this time my house and garden are reasonably accessible to all children. there is a small step going onto the garden patio and back setting double doors ledge. I would be happy to adapt my setting and put the necessary ramps etc in place if needed. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? On first contact with the families and to start as smoothly as possible and make the child feel settled within my setting, I would arrange for the family to come and visit and find out what needs they require, find out about the child and the family. For every family, I always get the parents to go through my welcome pack and fill in the paperwork before their child comes to me. I allow the children to have a few settling-in visits before they start properly, this is normal 1-2 weeks before they start for a few hours. When I welcome them into my setting I will help them fill in relevant documents and they will fill in an 'All about me' form before coming, special needs they may have. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I need to revisit my training and adapt my home and garden when I find out the needs of the child. I plan to keep up to date with SEND information and build on this with training through my Local Authority and my Key Contact at Buckinghamshire Council. Within my setting, I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences that give encouragement and are suited to each child's needs, this would be offered to my family ensuring each child’s needs are met.

local_offer: Field House Day Nursery is a 141 place nursery open from 7:30am to 18:30pm Monday to Friday 52 weeks the year. We have a warm and welcoming environment ensuring that your child’s individual needs are prioritised and their interests nurtured. We promote positive relationships with the families and children within our care, offering regular reviews of long and short term goals to ensure we are meeting children's individual needs. Children’s days are packed full of activities designed in line with EYFS principles and implemented by our highly trained and knowledgeable staff. Each age group has their own outdoor space and children are encouraged to access this daily. We are lucky to have an onsite Forest School that is led by a qualified Forest School Teacher. This provision is available for children aged from 3 years through to 5 years. We provide a fully inclusive service to all families which includes freshly prepared meals (catering for all diets and requirements) which are cooked onsite, formula milk, bottles, nappies, wipes, creams, sun cream.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Here at Field House we have two experienced SENDCo's who are available to offer any support needed with families and their child's development. Room based staff who are working directly with the children are confident to communicate with the SENDCo's if families have raised any concerns about their child and their individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 3 Early Years SENDCo Level 2 Certificate in Understanding Autism Designated SENDCo training - Childbase Supporting Children with Additional Needs - Childbase Supporting Children with Emotional Needs - Childbase Supporting Children with Neurodiversity - Childbase Speech and Language training Sing and Sign training for under two's age group How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? In the Reception area at Field House, we have a SENDCo information board which offers hand outs to families, as well as an introduction of the two SENDCo's within the setting. We have an open door policy, therefore we are always available to offer confidential meetings and support for those families who may require this. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Here at Field House we offer all families a bespoke learning journey of their child's development. You will be given access to Parent Zone, electronically, where you can log in and see your child's individual observations, photos and reports. We pride ourselves on our communication with our families, and to support this, parents have the opportunity to add observations from home. This allows us to work together, share important information and milestones about the individual child and their development. We offer 1:1 meetings to discuss any long term and short term goals for individual children with SEN requirements, to allow us to work together to monitor and support the child where needed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have an easily accessible large open plan Reception area where we will welcome you into. All age groups of children have their own individual garden area which are located in various spaces around the setting. The Forest School area is accessible through a fence within the nursery grounds, therefore the children have a short walk to access this provision. All of the room based resources and learning experiences are at the children's own level, therefore this allows for every child to partake and create their own choices within their play and learning. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When we welcome new children to the setting, if there is already an additional need, we would arrange a time for the family to meet with our SENDCo team. This would involve a walk around the setting together, so families can see the space and we can discuss any potential changes in the environments that may be required. Staff carry out regular observations and progress reviews with the children to monitor individual children and their milestones. If we notice an area of need, we would invite the family in to discuss these with the key person and SENDCo. This allows us to put any strategies in place that would support the individual child. We would continue to meet regularly to review and discuss next steps. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Here at Field House we will continue to put all children's individual needs first, working closely with the families and any outside agencies.

local_offer: Here at Hoppers of Dinton Pre-school, we specialise in the care of children and young people with additional needs alongside those who do not as part of our inclusive practice. Our Settings SENDCO is Corinne who can be contactable on 07813 880 153 or via e-mail admin@hoppersofdintonpreschool.co.uk The settings registration certificate and OFSTED poster are displayed on the settings notice board within the hall and the display board that is outside. A policy & procedure booklet is shared with parents/carers when they join the setting. The setting has a set of policies and procedures available for parents to look at. These are printed in English. For families that require it, an electronic or printed version can be provided using a font size of their choosing. We are also able to provide the book in audio if required. The setting is equipped with resources to cater for all areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage. Children have free choice of resources and are able to access them independently in our fully equipped setting. The children are offered regular opportunities throughout the day to enjoy the many toys and activities on offer and the fresh air in our outside space. There is a Wendy house and area of grass along with hard standing for ride on toys. We have a water wall, Sand tray, outdoor Kitchen and mark making area available at all times with additional activities being set up daily. The setting works within the framework of the EYFS. The setting is resourced according to the ages and needs of the children. The setting uses Development Matters and the Statutory Guidance for the EYFS along with characteristics of effective learning, Every child a talker and schemas to plan provision and activities for the children in their care. The EYFS identifies three prime areas of learning and development and four specific areas of learning and development. In the 0-2 age bracket the prime areas of learning and development (Communication and Language, Physical and Personal, Social and Emotional Development) are the areas of focus. In the 2-3 age bracket the prime areas remain significant but there is an emergence on the specific areas of development and learning. In the 3+ age bracket the prime areas continue to be a focus but there is an increasing balance between focusing on supporting children's development in these areas and the specific areas. Activities and provision are adapted to suit the needs of all children in each age bracket. For some children, a greater level of differentiation is required because they have additional educational needs. When children first start in the setting parents and any 3rd party practitioners are asked to highlight the development grid to create a starting point. Continued observations and tracking using the EYFS are then regularly carried out so that a learning journey can be put together. Children and parents are able to access their learning journey at any time via the app. A daily diary to include photo’s are also completed that outline the child’s routine and activities. Parents can make comments on their daily diary and use it as a way of communicating. As well as uploading observations. Children are actively encouraged to express their views. This is done by asking them open questions e.g ‘what did you like about ………..’ etc. They are also encouraged to look back through their learning journeys or photos and share any feelings they may have. On their return after the weekend break they are asked what they have done, where they have visited etc. and this is sometimes incorporated into future planning. Each age group is provided with resources that are developmentally appropriate for their age and stage of development. The setting ensures that there are resources available that overlap with the age phase below and above so that children who are developing more slowly or more quickly can access resources appropriate to their stage of learning and development. The setting works closely with other professionals, and they are encouraged to share their reports so that individual needs can be met. Where children need specialised equipment discussions would take place with parents and other agencies to see what could be provided. The setting regularly purchases new resources, and these are bought with the needs of the children in mind. The setting accesses the playground in the local area. Risk assessments are completed for trips outside of the setting and all children’s individual needs and reasonable adjustments are made where necessary. All trips and outings are planned and discussed with parents.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The setting is supported by an Early Years Consultant based at the local Authority. They are the dedicated SENCO for the area. Corinne Banham, business owner along with the settings Manager Yvonne Sharman manage all aspects of the childcare setting and have set policies and procedures that are adhered to to meet OFSTED requirements. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff are working towards their level 3 qualification in childcare and education. We are members of the Early years alliance and attend regular training including safeguarding, food hygiene, fire safety and Paediatric first aid. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The setting carries out regular observations and links these to the EYFS. If a child is not developing as expected for their age, then this would be highlighted in their learning journey and discussed with parents. Parents are actively encouraged to become involved in their child’s education and any comments are gladly received. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents/carers can ask about their child’s development at any time. They have regular contact at drop off and pick up times and are also able to phone, text/WhatsApp or email the setting. At the end of each term, A review is completed by the child’s key person detailing their progress this term, what they are working on and their next steps. Parents are invited to attend the setting, have a telephone conversation or have a home visit to discuss the report. Parents are then asked to make comments and sign the report. Children’s progress is closely monitored within the setting. Each child has their on-line learning journey which includes detailed written observations and links to the Framework. This information is shared with parents regularly and a progress check is completed sometime between the child’s second and third birthday. Where the progress check suggests that a child may be experiencing some difficulties or delay in their development this is shared with the parents and appropriate next steps are discussed. For some children, the next steps may involve targeting a specific area of development and planning additional opportunities for the child to have experiences designed to support the area of learning and development identified. This would then be reviewed to see if there had been any progression or whether additional steps need to be taken. For other children, the next step may also include developing a targeted learning plan where specific aims are developed with parents to support their child’s development. Referral to other agencies (with parents’ consent) e.g. speech and language therapy services will also be considered at this time. Another next step would be to ask the Local SENDCO to visit the child at the setting and provide some additional advice and guidance to support in meeting the child’s needs. This visit would be supported by the Health visitor where possible. Parental consent would also be sought first. The setting will then receive continued support via the SENDCO ensuring that all the child’s needs are met. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is based in a community hall and access is available at ground floor level through the front double doors and fire exit door at the rear. The front door is level with the pavement and has two sides to give extra width for wheelchair access. Due to the age of the building internal doors and corridors are narrow and may be a hazard to those that require a wheelchair or use of a walking aid. This would have to be assessed on a case-by-case basis. For security the front door is lockable with a key that is placed out of reach of the children. There is a wireless doorbell system to alert staff to anyone trying to access the building. The back door is a fire exit. This is not lockable due to safety reasons but does have an alarm to alert practitioners if it is opened. Children who require access to the toilets will be supervised by a practitioner. Access to the outside space is through the main front doors. The outside space is fenced off from the road and parking area. When children are using the outside space, the gate is chained & padlocked. Children are not outside without supervision. There is on-street parking directly outside the building on a quiet village road. A limited number of Staff are able to park on the grounds of the hall. There are two toilets and a disabled toilet with baby changing. Children who are too long or heavy for this are changed on a mat on the floor. Children can use the potty as well as the toddler toilet seat. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents/carers will be asked to complete a child record form through their Eylog app detailing any additional needs, previous illnesses, dietary requirements or allergies their child may have. If an additional need is identified within these documents a Health Care Plan will be put into place. If any medication has to be administered on a long term basis we will undertake child specific training for this. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

description: People concerned they are at increased risk of fire can self-refer or be referred with their consent for a Fire and Wellness Visit. These visits are conducted by operational firefighters or community safety staff who can, where appropriate, make an onwards referral to relevant support services or agencies. Areas covered in a Fire and Wellness Visit include: fire safety advice the provision of smoke detection where required escape planning the importance of bedtime checks electrical safety, including registering appliances safe smoking practices and referral to a smoking cessation service falls awareness and referral to the relevant service social isolation with signposting to ways to address this A Fire and Wellness Visit may be appropriate for a person if: there is anything which places their home at increased risk of fire. This could include hoarded materials, clutter from overcrowded living arrangements, multiple electrical devices plugged into extension leads, burn marks or signs of previous minor fires. there are no working smoke alarms on any level of their home and they are not able to replace the alarms themselves they are not sure if the smoke alarms they have are working correctly and they are not able to replace the alarms themselves they cannot respond to a smoke alarm quickly because they are affect by a long-term disability, other health need, medication, drugs, alcohol, mobility difficulty or frailty

description: Health on the High Street Service (two sites now available). Health on the High Street (HoTHs) is a free, drop‑in wellbeing service delivered by Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust. The service now operates across two locations in Buckinghamshire: - Unit 33, Friars Square Shopping Centre, Aylesbury - High Wycombe Library, Eden Shopping Centre, High Wycombe HoTHs provides friendly, accessible support to help people improve their health and wellbeing in everyday life. Visitors can drop in without an appointment to speak with our Health Connectors, who offer personalised signposting, guidance, and encouragement. What We Offer - Blood pressure checks - Use of the Sisu Health Kiosk (self‑service wellbeing checks) - Support with mental wellbeing, loneliness, confidence, and resilience - Help accessing local community groups, charities, and social support - Signposting on long‑term conditions and healthier living - Digital support (help with NHS App, online forms, local service access) - Information on cost‑of‑living support, housing, employment, and more Our Approach HoTHs is not a clinical or diagnostic service. Instead, it is a friendly, welcoming space where residents can receive practical help, motivation, and information to support healthier living. The service works closely with community organisations and local health partners to link people into the right support at the right time. Who Can Visit Anyone living in Buckinghamshire is welcome. No referral or appointment needed. Current opening times, drop-ins, and events are available on the Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust webpage.

description: Health on the High Street Service (two sites now available). Health on the High Street (HoTHs) is a free, drop‑in wellbeing service delivered by Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust. The service now operates across two locations in Buckinghamshire: - Unit 33, Friars Square Shopping Centre, Aylesbury - High Wycombe Library, Eden Shopping Centre, High Wycombe HoTHs provides friendly, accessible support to help people improve their health and wellbeing in everyday life. Visitors can drop in without an appointment to speak with our Health Connectors, who offer personalised signposting, guidance, and encouragement. What We Offer - Blood pressure checks - Use of the Sisu Health Kiosk (self‑service wellbeing checks) - Support with mental wellbeing, loneliness, confidence, and resilience - Help accessing local community groups, charities, and social support - Signposting on long‑term conditions and healthier living - Digital support (help with NHS App, online forms, local service access) - Information on cost‑of‑living support, housing, employment, and more Our Approach HoTHs is not a clinical or diagnostic service. Instead, it is a friendly, welcoming space where residents can receive practical help, motivation, and information to support healthier living. The service works closely with community organisations and local health partners to link people into the right support at the right time. Who Can Visit Anyone living in Buckinghamshire is welcome. No referral or appointment needed. Current opening times, drop-ins, and events are available on the Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust webpage.

description: Are you concerned about a child? If you are contacting us for the first time about a child or young person you are concerned about, you will find that all new referrals to social care, including children with disabilities, will be processed by the First Response Team. For urgent safeguarding concerns the quickest way to let the First Response team know is by calling them. If you have a safeguarding concern that is not urgent, please use the online form link (monitored during normal working hours). Referrals will be assessed by the team to check the seriousness and urgency of the concerns and whether Section 17 and/or Section 47 of the Children Act 1989 apply. The First Response Team will ensure that the referral reaches the appropriate team for assistance in a quick and efficient manner. More information is available on the website.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs.I work with parents /careers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life with in my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents on all aspects of their child’s time with me, I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared and acitivites are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children inside and outside, I have a small step by the front door and back door. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodations where possible e.g adaptations to meet sensory needs or accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I encourage families to have Settling in period with the child and complete an ‘all about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘ learning journey’. When a child moved settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the local authority and my key contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each Individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

local_offer: First Steps Pre-school aims to ensure that we are fully inclusive in meeting the needs of all children in our care. We are committed to anti-discriminatory practice to promote equality of opportunity and valuing diversity for all children and their families. We aim to provide a secure and accessible environment in which all our children can flourish. If your child has specific needs and you would like some more information about how we can accommodate them into our setting, please don't hesitate to contact us.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? In the first instance in discussion with parents/carers the setting will seek advice from the Early Years Team via telephone consultations. This can be followed up as needed with child-specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor with parent/carer agreement. In recent years First Steps has worked with Early Years SEND Advisors and Speech Therapists as well as being involved in Multi-Professional Meetings (for example Paediatrician Involvement). What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At First Steps Pre-School we welcome parent/carer involvement and support. Parents/carers can work together with the setting in order to support those with additional needs. On admission parents/carers are asked to complete an initial child profile form as well as telling us a little about their child’s likes/dislikes, important family members they may talk about and how to comfort them. There is informal feedback on the collection of the children on a day to day basis. We run annual parent/carer consultation sessions however parents and carers are free at any time to discuss their child’s progress and view their child's individual progress reports. Annually we issue a questionnaire to parents/carers to determine their opinions and see if there is anything we can help with or improve on. We have social events during the year such as the end of term parties, Sports Day and other celebrations. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Some methods of how the setting works together with parents and carers have been mentioned above. In addition, the setting also completes Two Year Checks for our younger children and discusses these with parents/carers. With regards to those with any SEN First Steps has worked with relevant professionals to help support those children with additional needs. We have completed Assess, Plan, Do Review Forms and SEN Support Plans with both parents/carers and Early Years SEND Advisers or Speech Therapists as needed. Parents/carers of children with SEND are welcomed into the setting to discuss their child’s progress or help support their child as needed. We regularly monitor any short-term outcomes for children with SEND and reassess their targets and discuss these with parents/carers and any relevant professionals involved with supporting the child. If any professionals contact the setting with regards to visiting a child in our care, we make sure that the parents/carers are aware of this and ideally able to attend. We also use an online system called Tapestry which keeps parents updated on what their child is doing during their time at the setting. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We occupy a large, bright and airy room where there is plenty of space for children to move around and explore indoors whilst in session. There are toilet facilities including an accessible one. Access to a secure outside flat grassed area allows our children the same opportunity to move around in an outdoor environment, with a variety of appropriate toys and objects. Whilst there are 3 steps down to the outside area from the main room of the setting it can also be accessed via a ramp. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children all have their own individual personalities and needs with regards to endeavouring to ensure a smooth transition into any setting. At First Steps as mentioned, we are happy to work with parents/carers to try and find a way to settle each child into our setting in a way that best suits them – be it having the parent/carer stay with them until they get used to coming or having a transitional object (special toy) to bring into the setting with them. We provide parents/carers with a Prospectus about the setting when they visit or decide to join us and offer induction settings for the children which can also be attended by the parents/carers as needed. If parents/carers believe it would be helpful we would be happy to arrange a home visit before the child starts. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We always endeavour to provide the best possible care for every child in our setting, including those with SEND needs. We are always keeping updated with recent guidelines and advice, and ensure we attend training relevant to our roles and ensure a consistent approach.

description: Wild for Life is on a mission. A mission to put schools and families in greater control of their own mental and physical health and wellbeing. We have created an exciting learning programme for teachers, parents/carers and children which fills the academic year with nature-inspired learning, and supports positive mental, social and physical well-being and development. This is suitable for delivery in school, at alternative provisions, and at home by a parent/carer for a learner who is unable to attend school. The learning programme is called My Wild Life, and there are six core value-led themed kits (‘My Wild Kit of...Change, Respect, Strength, Confidence, Friendship, and Hope’) which use imaginative storytelling and nature to bring themes to life. It is suited to KS1 and KS2 learners and is a fully resourced kit with a delivery guidance pack for the adult working with the child. local_offer: I aim to give families access to childcare whatever their child's individual needs and will do my very best to accommodate children with SEND needs. I work closely with parents and professionals with the aim of the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As with all registered Childminders in Buckinghamshire, we have a Key Contact within the Early Years Service, from whom we can access advice and information. They are happy to answer our questions or signpost to other appropriate services. Professionals are welcome to meet the child at our setting if parents wish. We are keen to expand our knowledge and expertise. We will undergo further training when it is required. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents on a regular basis to share information about their child and their learning and development in a manner that suits the parent. All children have a settling in session and parents are asked to share information before their child starts so that I can seek to understand their likes and dislikes. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children and plan activities in accordance with these observations to extend and extend their learning. Any concerns regarding a child's development are shared with the parent so that an action plan can be formulated together, using the support of other services if agreed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our home is accessible for most children and their families. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible for example adaptations for access to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All children are offered a settling in session and in advance, parents are asked to complete a child information booklet to help me familiarise with their child's likes and dislikes, routines and needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to consider training to help meet the particular needs of a child in my care.

local_offer: Flower Pots Day Nursery believe that all children are individuals, they have an equal right to be valued and listened to, and are entitled to access all the nursery facilities. Flower Pots is committed to providing an inclusive environment and ensure that all children have the opportunities to reach their full potential where every child is able to access nursery care and education that stretches their learning and development. Children and their families are treated fairly regardless of race, sex, disability, age, religion or sexual orientation. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace. We aim to build positive relationships with all children and their families, we want parents to be involved as much as they can within the nursery and to share the children's successes, achievements and hopes for the future.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We encourage parental involvement at every opportunity at Flower Pots Day Nursery and understand how important it is to always have direct contact with your child’s nursery. Flower Pots seeks the views and opinions of our parents on a regular basis and has a great focus on parental involvement within the setting. We use Tapestry, an app that allows parents to view photos of activities their children have taken part in, food is eaten throughout their day, as well as developmental assessments and observations. It is a very useful tool and allows our parents to have an insight into their child's nursery day. At Flower Pots, we love to see what our children get up to at home and parents are encouraged to upload their own home observations and any other information they may wish to share with the setting. This allows our staff to develop a truly holistic understanding of their key children and identify any interests they are showing whilst at home. In turn, we can use all this information to enhance their learning experiences whilst nursery. Parents can email or call our nursery manager at any point throughout the day. In addition to this, we hold parents’ evenings twice a year. Communication between nursery and home is an incredibly important aspect of nursery life; at Flower Pots, parents are given a full handover via Famly Care Diaries where all information of their day is detailed. In addition to this, we also give a verbal handover when children are collected. We encourage parents to share details of their weekend/evening with us at drop off, so we can gain an understanding of how their child is feeling on that day, for example, if they have woken several times throughout the night then they may be more tired than usual. All of this information is encouraged to be shared so we can give your children the best learning experiences at Flower Pots. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At Flower Pots Day Nursery, we encourage our children to learn through a variety of ways: adult-led experiences, child-led experiences, and play. We believe that through these experiences and using ‘In the moment planning’ we can offer children the best start in life and ensure they thrive in the world. To measure progress, we use a range of tools, such as a ‘starting point assessment’ to establish an understanding of what skills children already possess, regular developmental reports and one in-depth observation per week. Staff at Flower Pots will use the online app, Famly to share all this information with our parents. For our children with SEND, we will also follow the Assess, Plan, Do, Review guidance. These will be shared with parents on a regular basis and we will always work in partnership with parents How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Flower Pots Day Nursery in Chesham is spread across two floors. On the ground floor we have our baby and toddler room with their own dedicated garden which is accessible via a pathway. On our first floor (accessed via stairs only) we have our Pre-school and Classroom. We also have a second garden which is accessed from the pre-school room using a small set of steps. We have a dedicated sensory room which creates a lovely atmosphere and provides children with a quiet area should they require it. The sensory room is within the baby room and can be accessed and used by all children within the setting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Flower Pots Day Nursery understands how important transitions between settings or rooms are. We offer 3, complimentary settle sessions for children enrolling at our setting. This allows your child to become fully settled at nursery and in their new environment. The first settle session is accompanied by a parent and allows for discussion about their routine, likes/dislikes. We arrange several transition visits for our children when they are moving into the next playroom. During these visits, we ensure children are presented with the opportunity to build relationships with the staff members in this room and become familiar with their new surroundings. We have ‘transition display boards’ within each of our rooms which prepares children for moving into the next room or for going to school by displaying photos of the next room and the staff within this room. This creates a point of conversation for our children and something which we can discuss together to ensure transitions are not daunting. For transitions between nursery and school, we will always work in partnership with their new school and provide any information necessary (with permission from parents) What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? description: The Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, And Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust (BBOWT) is concerned with all aspects of nature conservation in the three counties it covers. We protect 85 nature reserves, monitor species, run special projects, and advise landowners in how to care for habitats and species. The Chilterns Group of the BBOWT works to help the charity by raising the profile of the vital work we do. We fundraise, organise special events, increase membership and arrange work parties for conservation work. Our work is far-reaching to benefit our wildlife and environment as far as we can. We focus on the Chilterns mainly in our immediate work, but all fundraising helps the Trust overall.
organisation: Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust (BBOWT) One of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England. This large Living Landscape covers an area between Oxford, Bicester and Aylesbury. It includes 48,400 hectares of woodland, mixed farmland and floodplain meadows across the boundary between Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire. The entire area is ecologically linked through the River Ray, which rises in Quainton, close to Finmere Wood nature reserve, and flows west alongside some of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England, to join the River Cherwell at Islip, north of Oxford. Since 1981 BBOWT (Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust) has been buying and restoring floodplain meadows in the upper reaches of the River Ray, and working with neighbouring farmers to create a stronghold for wading birds including curlew. info@bbowt.org.uk https://www.bbowt.org.uk/wildlife/living-landscapes/bernwood-forest-and-ray-valley-living-landscape

name: Green Planet Forest School Ltd at Buckingham Primary School
description: The Green Planet team prepares for sessions by setting up stations or situations such as for whittling, fire lighting, campfire cooking, shelter building, crafting, tree climbing, construction using tools, and supports children on whichever activity they choose to explore. In order to fully appreciate the range of fun activities on offer, a very detailed list of those activities and their benefit to child development can be found here. Of course all of this goes on in a woodland area giving access to nature which itself is both a great educator and an amazing place to play. The Green Planet Forest School team welcomes children from any primary school in any area, with any level of ability. Children with SEN needs are not only welcome and well catered for, they traditionally excel in this environment. And if you are unsure about booking your child please read our excellent reviews on Trust Pilot or by all means contact us directly for a chat. ‘Best Days Ever’ happen at Green Planet Forest School holiday clubs! ​ Open February, Easter, May, Summer and October half terms and holidays. *Open to: Any child, from any school or home education, from any area *For ages: 4 to 13 (in Reception to Year 8 at the time of event) *SEND welcome: Absolutely! (however please contact us before booking if your child has specific needs*) *Allergies & dietary requirements: Catered for, add them to your child’s profile *Nut free setting: Yes! *OFSTED Registered 2776260/2776261 *Childcare Vouchers & Tax-Free Childcare scheme: We accept both *Drop off & Collection times: Our clubs are full days, not drop-in sessions, from 09:00-15:00 and/or 08:00-16:00 (depending on location). What’s included: A full day of fun-packed fantastic and exciting outdoor Forest School activities! ​​ Our activities regularly include: ​ *Shelter building *Mini-beast hunting, bird spotting and nature walks *Nature based crafts like whittling and weaving *Campfire building, lighting and cooking *High ropes, swings and hammocks in the trees *The use of tools from hammers to knives and axes *Mud kitchen catering *If it’s fun and it’s outdoors it happens at our clubs! **Please see our FAQs for further details about children with additional needs. For announcements of our holiday club dates and locations follow our Facebook page.

description: FM Training is a First Aid Training Provider based in High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire. We are looking to help individuals and organisations who may require assistance with fulfilling staff first aid training requirements. We are proud to be accredited through Training Qualifications UK (TQUK), TQUK is an awarding body who develop and offer qualifications regulated by OFQUAL (exam regulators in England and Wales). TQUK monitor our quality assurance; verify qualifications to ensure the training we provide is of a high standard and in line with the latest protocols. We provide all workplaces First Aid Courses, and these are delivered in-house at a date and time to suit you. All you need to do is provide a room which is large enough to accommodate all the delegates and suitable for carrying out practical exercises. We take care of the rest. Alternatively, we run regular open courses at our training venue in High Wycombe and Marlow. These are ideal for individuals or if you only want to book a first aid course for a small number of people. For further details or to enquire about our workplace first aid courses, then please email us or visit our website.

description: Follyfoot Healing with Horses is a therapeutic centre using our horses to help children and families who may benefit from spending time in a tranquil, peaceful, setting and interacting with some of our beautiful horses. We specialise in supporting children and young people with SEN needs via 1:1 sessions with our horses as well as adult with mental health needs and families affected by cancer We aim to improve self-esteem, communication, and social interaction skills, enable people to build lasting bonds and relationships, re-engage individuals and improve general well-being through the healing powers of horses. We offer support to anyone who can benefit from the interaction of horses in a therapeutic setting including people with special needs or disability. Our aim is to help improve peoples lives and enable them to feel accepted and included during their time spent at Follyfoot. Horses allow people to interact with them in a non-judgemental way and will mirror their behaviour thus helping them have a greater understanding of themselves and the outside world.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I don’t have any as of yet but happy to get any training that will be beneficial to the child’s development. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work closely with the parents sending pictures and updates of the child through out the day through the App. I will ask the parents the child’s interests and dislikes are and will encourage this into the child’s play. Each month I will include the parents with the child’s next steps and any recommendations would be great. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At the setting I am continually observing and assessing. Planning the child’s next steps. We work closely with the parents and will discuss what areas they think their child needs help with and will set up an action plan. We also work closely with other SEND professionals in the community and can access extra help and opinions too. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My front door is wheelchair accessible and we also have a side/back entrance to the garden. We have a cosy play area inside with a nice open Kitchen. The garden is spacious with grass and decking area. There is a bus stop at the end of our round which comes regularly from the town. Happy to discuss any changes that can be made to suit the child. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? At my childcare setting, everyone is welcome to visit before applying for a place. I provide a welcome pack that I will send out prior to your visit, which may help you prepare any questions you might have. Once your application is accepted, we will arrange several settling-in sessions. The first session will include the parent, during which I will gather some necessary information and set up your child on the app I use (Babydays). What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? My local authority keep me up to date with any SEND updates through email. I am also able to access any courses that may be beneficial to the child.

We are constantly looking at our equipment and making sure we can offer a broad spectrum of toys and equipment for every child. Our SENCO is making sure we keep that up to date along with disseminating the information to all staff. local_offer: The setting is very accessible, we have a dedicated parking area for SEND families, double opening doors for easy access. Lots of flat areas inside and outside of the setting. A dedicated toilet for SEND.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We will access the Early Years Team for any assistance, using their expertise or specialist services to aid us as a setting. We have good links with Speech and Language therapists and the paediatric consultants are aware of our setting as we have dealt with them on numerous occasions over the years. We are forging partnerships with local schools, this will enable us to link with the schools their approach to phonics, maths, reading and writing and take on board what we can achieve in the first steps to these milestones. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The SENCO attends briefing meetings laid on by Early Years and if necessary takes an update course and qualifications when required. Our SENCO qualified in Autism training and disseminated this information to the rest of the staff. We have a strong base knowledge of Makaton sign language. Our SENCO completed SENCO Level 3 training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have a parent rota where you can put your name down to attend a morning session and you can see at first hand the routine of the morning and how the staff interact with the children. Your duties will be to assist the staff in any activities to include reading, going outside, playing and interacting with the children. If you are unable to attend on the days we run the parent rota you can speak to the supervisor and arrange for an afternoon or morning to suit you. (This opportunity is currently unavailable due to covid restrictions, we hope to resume very soon) Parents can also be involved in the fundraising committee for Chuf. Their aim is to raise funds in order to buy new equipment or pay for visitors. Chuf is a Charitable Incorporated Organisation and as such we have a group of trustees. If any parent is interested in joining as a trustee you are more than welcome. All information can be obtained by asking a supervisor or emailing us. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At Chuf we have an observation platform called Tapestry. All parents can receive notification of their child's progress via Tapestry on their phone, iPad, tablet or PC. Parents can also reciprocate by sending in their views and observations to aid the keyworker in building a rounded assessment of each child. Tapestry also applies to SEND children but the key worker and SENCO will be in constant contact face to face, by phone or email. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The village hall was rebuilt two years ago and has taken on board the accessibility for all. There are flat areas, ramps and double doors for easy access. A toilet for SEND with an alarm. All lights in the toilets turn on/off automatically. A defibrillator is situation in the entrance of the main hall. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We are in contact with most of the local infant and primary schools in the area. Near to the time we take some children to their prospected school for the morning and the reception teachers and welfare assistants make visits to our pre-school. If there is any information parents require near the time of transition we are more than happy to assist with any enquiries. The SENCO and key worker will take any SEND children on several small visits as part of their transition into school. Meet with their teachers, along with the parents and give any advice or information that would aid a smooth transition and settle in period. We will also carry out this service for any child who is experiencing difficulties in the transition process. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We have been developing our knowledge and qualifications for SENCO and staff in Autism. Our SENCO has good Autism knowledge. Our SENCO has completed SENCO Level 3. The whole staff team has house training in the Early Years on Autism We want to develop our knowledge of speech and language difficulties and are presently looking into courses for this. We are always looking at new courses available for the SENCO to attend to broaden her knowledge.

name: Fortune College
description: Fortune College, part of The Fortune Centre of Riding Therapy (FCRT) works with horses to help people with learning difficulties and disabilities to learn life skills. The residential FETH Course (Further Education Through Horsemastership) enables students to transfer skills that they want to learn into skills they need to learn, thereby developing the ability to lead more independent lives. The skills learned in the course improve literacy, numeracy and communication, broadening social horizons and relationships at home, at Fortune College and in the wider community. Students become more competent in daily living. They increase self-care and awareness and learn how to approach household tasks, including cooking and laundry. They learn safety awareness, personal money management, how to use public transport and benefit from the opportunity for work experience. An equine-based setting is eminently suited to providing the context and motivation for learning in practical ways rather than in a conventional classroom setting. How the FETH Course operates naturally promotes health and fitness.

local_offer: Fortune College mission is to enable people who are motivated by horses and who have special needs, to relate more successfully to others and develop greater independence and skill and have more control over their own lives. (This is done through their involvement with horses. This unique, specialist use of horses, to allow and encourage people to learn and develop is the core of Fortune College's work. It is the reason for its existence and has been the mission since its foundation in 1976.) The majority of the course is based on kinaesthetic learning and is not contained within a classroom-based setting. Some students benefit from visual aids, particularly for forming new routines. Working with the physical element of the horse and the use of body language, through touch and sight, is an effective way of learning for the student motivated by the horse. The students also assist in the teaching of the mounted session to aid their communication skills as well as using the phone and message taking as part of their every day working life when out in the yard. The horse is the main resource for the horse motivated student. Fortune College also have touch screen boards, netbooks, tough books, and keyboards for those with visual impairment and dyslexia. Hearing aids with remote microphones are available when required. Some practical tools, such as wheelbarrows with two wheels, are used for those who lack motor skills or balance. Fortune College use many notices and simple charts to help students connect visual information to practical use. Fortune College have a high student to staff ratio throughout the learning programme including in the residence. Accredited qualifications include: Equestrian Qualification GB Limited (EQL) Levels One and Two Diplomas in Work Based Horse Care. The British Horse Society Complete Horsemanship Awards: Stage One Care, Stage One Ride; Ride Safe; Stage Two Care, Ride and Lunge. description: Foxes Piece provides a happy, caring, and nurturing atmosphere where everyone is encouraged to achieve their full potential. We work hard to develop our pupils' self-esteem and believe that we have created an atmosphere in which all our pupils feel equal. As a result, staff and governors are very proud of our school. We offer a wide range of opportunities in a caring and supportive environment where pupils strive to make the best of the time available to them to experience success. organisation: Foxes Piece School Foxes Piece Combined School is situated on Newfield Road, Marlow. The First School was established in 1955 and extended in 1969 when a separate Middle School was built on the adjoining site. The two schools were amalgamated in September 1997. The school is on a large level site and the grounds have many attractive natural features including excellent playing fields. The classroom blocks each have four separate rooms, with shared central areas for small group learning and access to the Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 extensive libraries. There is also a separate teaching block with classrooms and a fitted food technology area. The safety of our children and staff is paramount, all classrooms are accessed via key combination codes and a fence runs around the site. The main building houses the main hall, a dining hall, an ICT suite and administrative offices. The well-maintained buildings provide a bright, pleasant environment for the children to work in. Further use of the buildings on this site has enabled us to house the Stepping Stones Playgroup, the Little Roos Day Nursery and Newfield Community Church. We also host the Marlow Family Centre. office@foxespiece.bucks.sch.uk http://www.foxespiece.co.uk/

local_offer: Everyone is Someone at Foxes Piece School. Foxes Piece is an inclusive mainstream school. Children are treated as individuals and have equal access to the curriculum in an environment that fosters friendship, co-operation and high-quality learning. https://www.foxespiece.co.uk/page/?title=SEN&pid=40 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The school aims to: - Promote a whole school ethos that values all children and their families. - Help pupils develop their personalities, skills and abilities. - Provide appropriate teaching which makes learning challenging and enjoyable. - Provide equality of educational opportunity and promotes inclusion in all aspects of education and learning. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The quality of the teaching environment and the commitment of all the staff ensures a high quality of education. Staff take part in training throughout the academic year to ensure their knowledge on how to support all children is up to date. The school's SENCo ensures relevant training and CPD is shared with all members of staff to reflect current needs of the children attending our school. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENDCo) is Mrs Loren Irvine. If you have any queries related to SEN you can contact her through the School Office or via the SENCo e-mail address (senco@foxespiece.co.uk). How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? SEN plans are created using Provision Map software and used for those children on the SEN register. These outline the targets, interventions, resources and progress they are making. These are created, compiled and kept up to date by the class teacher and SENCo. They are shared with parents termly. Those children who have an EHCP have annual reviews which are organised and led by the SENCo and attended by parents and all professionals involved with the child's progress. Children with SEN plans and EHCPs gain additional support in areas of the curriculum relevant to their need. This can vary greatly from SALT and OT activities, to daily pre-learning and booster sessions. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Pathways are accessible to all and ramps have been included up to main, wide doorways. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Teachers complete an Initial Concerns Checklist if they have concerns regarding a pupil. Following this, observations by the school's SENCo are made and feedback about strategies and next steps are shared with class teachers and parents where appropriate. Further assessments by outside agencies such as Community Paediatricians, SALT, PRU, OT or EP may be appropriate if progress is not being made from advice and guidance from the school SENCo and in collaboration with parents/carers. Appropriate intervention and provision will then be assessed and put in place and recorded on a SEN plan, where appropriate. The school SENCo can also be contacted through the school office or by email (senco@foxespiece.co.uk). What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To continue with the high level of support and adapted learning appropriate for each individual, to ensure they make and reach their full potential whilst feeling happy, safe and nurtured.

name: Blue Willow Day Nursery Holmer Green
description: Blue Willow Day Nursery is a home-from-home setting offering childcare from 0 to 5 years. We offer funded spaces for 2,3 and 4-year-olds, both 15 and 30 hours if eligible. Blue Willow Day Nursery started as Blue Willow Childminding Services in 2009. With a background working from home with mixed-aged children, we opened our nursery in Slough in 2015 with clear values in mind. A homely environment for children, offering mixed play socialising, and a strong emphasis on outdoor play. Our Holmer Green Nursery opened its doors in April 2023. The homely aspect provides comfort and security for children. If children are happy they will be engaged, and ready to learn. Mixed-aged socialising offers excellent learning opportunities for children. Younger children learn from the older children around them, and older children learn to be tolerant and caring towards younger children. We use authentic resources such as teapots, cups and limited plastic toys that do not always allow a child to use their imagination. Using real things that may break, gives the children a real sense of looking after things and taking care of their environment. Outdoor play is encouraged for children as much as possible through all seasons. Our doors to the garden are always open, and children enjoy active learning and a healthy lifestyle. We have a ‘meadow ‘ area in our front garden along with a small nature pond. In the back garden, we have vegetable plots where the children really do see food grown from seed, cared for by them, onto their plates at snack or teatime. Children are taken in small groups to our ‘Nature Garden’ where they experience a campfire and an opportunity to use real tools. All is done with respect and safety in mind at all times.
