local_offer: Blue Willow Day Nursery started as Blue Willow Childminding Services in 2009. With a background working from home with mixed-aged children, we opened our nursery in 2015 with clear values in mind. A homely environment for children, offering mixed play socialising, and a strong emphasis on outdoor play. The homely aspect provides comfort and security for children. If children are happy they will be engaged, and ready to learn. Mixed-aged socialising offers great learning opportunities for children. Younger children learn from the older children around them, and older children learn to be tolerant and caring towards younger children. Outdoor play is encouraged for children as much as possible through all seasons. Our doors to the garden are always open, and children enjoy active learning and a healthy lifestyle. Blue Willow is an inclusive nursery, offering an open door policy and family buddy system, offering direct support to families when needed, and encouraging open communication from the first visit. Families are provided with good handovers during drop-off collections, and invited into the nursery to talk to key workers in more detail about what's happening both at home and in the nursery. When queries are raised, or additional support is needed, families are directed to the family buddy who will work with them for as long as needed.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our primary outcome for families and children with SEND is to be able to access sessions at the nursery. Depending on the needs of the child, full sessions may not immediately be available, particularly if one-to-one support is needed. An initial stay and play are offered for children identified with possible SEND before they start with us, and sessions are always offered but could be tailored depending on the availability of practitioners. For example, hours could be reduced until a plan is in place to offer full sessions. We would always prefer a child can access the nursery for reduced hours initially if needed then not at all. Once children are in the nursery, our SEND team will tailor the environment and activities to meet the individual needs of children. Funded applications will be submitted to access one-to-one support if we think a child would benefit from this level of support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 3 SENDCO Best Practice Network Kasia Olesinska Level 3 SENDCO Best Practice Network Emily Boycott Makaton Level 3 and 4 (SBC) Emily Boycott Dingley's Promise (SBC) Emily Boycott Level 2 Autism Awareness (SBC) Emily Boycott How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Families are involved with the SEND process very quickly. If SEND is identified, families are invited into the nursery to speak with key workers about the needs of their child. Permission is obtained throughout the journey to ensure families are aware of additional support requested for their child, and that they agree with strategies from the beginning, until the end of their journey with us. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children's progress is shared daily with parents during drop-off and collections. Effective 2-way communication ensures both home and nursery have lots of information about your child so we can both teach and support effectively. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Outdoor learning is promoted all day in all seasons for all children. Access for all including wheelchair users is through the side gate. The installation of a ramp will allow easy access for all including wheelchair users to access to the downstairs of the nursery which includes the toilet and hand washing facilities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If families have identified SEND needs, a stay-and-play session can be booked with the SEND team to meet your child a start making adjustments for your child to start as quickly as possible. This could be reduced sessions to start with to meet supervision needs, tailoring settling sessions to offer more, or over shorter periods to help with anxiety. Throughout the start-up process, and ongoing through your child's journey, we are here to support and effectively communicate with families to achieve the best outcomes for your child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To grow our existing SEND team to have more available practitioners with SEND experience working directly with children who require additional support. We would also like to be a full communication nursery and use Makaton all the time while talking to children. This is a long-term plan for us, but we already have trained Makaton practitioners that encourage the use of signing in the nursery to help communication skills, along with other communication aids.

description: Blue Willow Day Nursery is a home-from-home setting offering childcare from 0 to 5 years. We offer funded spaces for 2,3 and 4-year-olds, both 15 and 30 hours if eligible. Blue Willow Day Nursery started as Blue Willow Childminding Services in 2009. With a background working from home with mixed-aged children, we opened our nursery in Slough in 2015 with clear values in mind. A homely environment for children, offering mixed play socialising, and a strong emphasis on outdoor play. Our Holmer Green Nursery opened its doors in April 2023. The homely aspect provides comfort and security for children. If children are happy they will be engaged, and ready to learn. Mixed-aged socialising offers excellent learning opportunities for children. Younger children learn from the older children around them, and older children learn to be tolerant and caring towards younger children. We use authentic resources such as teapots, cups and limited plastic toys that do not always allow a child to use their imagination. Using real things that may break, gives the children a real sense of looking after things and taking care of their environment. Outdoor play is encouraged for children as much as possible through all seasons. Our doors to the garden are always open, and children enjoy active learning and a healthy lifestyle. We have a ‘meadow ‘ area in our front garden along with a small nature pond. In the back garden, we have vegetable plots where the children really do see food grown from seed, cared for by them, onto their plates at snack or teatime. Children are taken in small groups to our ‘Nature Garden’ where they experience a campfire and an opportunity to use real tools. All is done with respect and safety in mind at all times.

name: Pathway Ponies
description: Pathway Ponies is an equine-assisted learning and alternative provision based in Wendover, Buckinghamshire. An utterly unique and tranquil setting where individuals are supported to not just grow, but truly thrive. Our calm and gentle miniature ponies provide a safe sanctuary, offering comfort, connection, and a place where everyone can feel free to truly be themselves. We offer programmes in: - Equine-Assisted Wellbeing; these are our most informal sessions designed to allow you to take a pause from life and allow time to reflect and recharge. You can choose how you want to spend time interacting with the ponies with activities on offer such as grooming the ponies, helping care for them or taking them for a little walk. - Equimotional (Equine Assisted Learning): a fun and interactive hands-on way to build confidence, social skills, and emotional growth. Each week, you'll engage in different hands-on activities, using experiential learning to work towards your chosen goal, build personal understanding, and achieve a specific outcome, such as designing and developing your own personal strategy to aid you in emotional regulation and anxiety. Interactions with the ponies help to develop various skills, enhance personal growth, and address specific challenges. ASDAN accredited short course, Employability Skills Development and LifeSkills challenges: Tailored to suit individual needs, these practical, and engaging certified courses prepare young people and adults for success in life and work. You can work at your own pace, selecting modules from a wide range of options tailored to your interests and goals. Evidence of your learning can be showcased in creative and fun ways that suit your unique style. With the flexibility to complete between 10 and 60 hours of activities, you’ll build a personalised portfolio of achievements. These skills-based courses are highly adaptable, and your portfolio will be moderated, quality-assured, and rewarded with a certificate upon completion. Regardless of your chosen programme type, every session is tailored to suit individual needs and learning styles, helping young people (2 years plus) and adults, including those with Special Educational Needs (SEN), to develop emotional resilience, confidence, and essential life skills. Our vision is to empower individuals to flourish in a supportive, calming space, ensuring they grow and learn in ways that work best for them. With a team of experienced, knowledgeable and certified facilitators, we provide encouragement and understanding at every step of the journey. Whether connecting with our ponies, building new skills, or finding a moment of peace, Pathway Ponies offers a truly special place to learn, grow, and thrive. Pathway Ponies proudly supports individuals of all abilities, schools, our SEN community, those with EHCPs, and young people educated through AOTAS (Alternative Provision), funded or self-funding. Visit our website to discover more. Fully licensed and Insured. DBS Checked. Safeguarding trained.

local_offer: Stellar Nursey is a privately owned Nursery. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We are a family run business and pride ourselves in our personal approach. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share in their children’s achievements with us. Throughout our weekly planning we ensure that we are using different areas of our setting including indoor and outdoor space. The children are also given the choice of where they want to play. We have activities set out ready for the children to play with. If we were to have a child that came in with physical needs they would be able to access the whole of our setting unaided, as it is on one level. name: Freda Gurney School of Dancing
description: Freda Gurney School of Dancing offer ballet, tap and theatre craft classes for adults and children aged 2 and a half and older. Classes are held at Booker Memorial Hall, High Wycombe. The Freda Gurney School was established over 60 years ago, and is still running today. Principal, Kim Jenkins, has been running the school for 30 years since taking over the dance school from her mother. Kim's daughter, Cara, is now involved in the day to day running of the school and teaches alongside Kim. Weekly Ballet, Pointe, Tap and Theatre Craft classes are offered for both children (from the age of 2 and a half) and adults. Pupils are prepared and have the opportunity to take IDTA examinations which are held locally every year. These examinations give the students the opportunity to progress in individual grades and medals, and also take part and be examined in team dances. The school continues to enjoy excellent results in all areas. Classes are taught by fully qualified and registered IDTA teachers, whose experience will ensure that the students will be taught in a safe, fun and effective environment. To ensure that the work each week is built upon the previous week's teaching, the classes are always given by the same teacher. The aim of the dance school is to help students achieve their personal best and adopt a love for dancing. The classes help the pupils to gain co-ordination, musical awareness and self confidence. Adult Ballet and Tap Dancing classes are also available.

description: Sensory Children's Parties, we want every child to feel special, whether it's on their birthday or part of a community celebration. We know how difficult it can be to find a party entertainer able to accommodate the needs of every child. We’ve built on our experience of performing interactive shows for children with complex needs to create a special party performance. This includes puppetry, music, keyword signing, lights, textures, props and instruments. We offer a choice of stories or can create a new one around a theme or story that your child particularly enjoys. Embracing Arts Parties bring the entertainment to you in a venue/space where your family feels most comfortable - no living room is too small. name: Godstowe Preparatory School
description: Our ethos is simple. All we want is for our girls and boys to be Confident, Happy and Successful. Indeed, if the first two are true, the third will almost certainly follow. Success is defined in many ways, and we mean successful in the broadest sense: successfully kind, successfully courteous as well as successful in achieving a wide range of goals. We keep our pupils busy and engaged, we entertain and intrigue them, encourage them, and excite them. Happy children are easy to teach. With outstanding, highly qualified teaching staff as well as a strong and experienced pastoral team, excellent facilities, wonderful surroundings, a non-selective intake policy and a more positive, exuberant and industrious atmosphere than you will find in other schools, most of our children will likely be happy to learn, happy to stretch themselves, happy to support each other, and happy to do whatever they can to take an active part in their education.

name: SENDCARE
description: We provide educational care and support to young people with complex needs. A service created by a SEND specialist with experience supporting young people to access education or community services. Our goal is to provide support and care for young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities, whether they are in school or not. We are here to ensure that each individual receives the educational support and care they deserve. Through our personalised approach, we aim to make a positive impact on the lives of those we support. Together, we can create a brighter future for young people in need. Each young person will receive a visit and full assessment from a qualified specialist, at this point, they can take other professional reports to incorporate any recommendations or targets into the plan for the specialist support worker to follow. This plan will be reviewed regularly by the director and specialist support workers. Recommendations of educational activities to carry out at home or in the community will be given to be carried out to support the development of the young person.

local_offer: Holiday Clubs: Designed for children with SEND, these programs include a variety of activities like baking, sports, sensory activities, and soft play, all aimed at fostering an inclusive environment. Wraparound Care: Before and after school clubs provide tailored care that meets the needs of each child, ensuring that every family can afford high-quality childcare despite the barriers they might face. Physical Education Lessons: Entire Club's educators deliver inclusive PE lessons that allow every child to participate, promoting physical activity and inclusion as core elements of the curriculum.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? - Equal Opportunities in Education and Care - Holistic Child Development - Physical and Mental Engagement - Relief and Resources for Families - Community and Parental Engagement - Nurturing Environments - Raise awareness and shift perspectives on inclusivity in childcare - Sustainable, long term SEND Support Systems What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? - Inhouse CPD for intimate care - Diabetes training - Peg feeding training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Regular Feedback Mechanisms - Parents are invited to provide feedback through surveys, meetings, and informal chats, ensuring that their voices are heard and their concerns are addressed. Direct Contact with Staff - Parents can always reach out to staff members, including SEND specialists and family liaisons, to discuss their child’s progress or any concerns they might have. Social media platforms and regular telephone communications. To start getting involved, you can reach out directly to Entire Club. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? It is very situational to the activity and service they are attending, hand overs and drop offs are key to ensuring the individual receives the best care and so we are aware of their current state to refrain from heightening a child. Hand overs are vital so that parents and carers are aware of what their child has done during the day and if they need to be aware of any situations. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor environment in our camp services includes sensory equipment, a bouncy castle, access to activities including arts and crafts and baking, soft play room, toilets with a hoist, all wheelchair accessible with a lift, and all key carded. Outdoor areas include Swings and other play equipment, wheelchair equipment and accessibility, climbing frames, muga. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Firstly explore the available services and what we have to offer, contact Entire Club LTD through our website, telephone or email. We will then schedule a consultation to speak to one of our members of staff to get to know your child and ensure we can tailor to their needs and provide a positive and personalised care plan. We will then go through the registration process, whereby you book on to one of our services. After accessing our service we will then provide ongoing communication, support and feedback to ensure effective care is given. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? - Establishing Holiday Club Provision - Entire plans to set up more inclusive holiday clubs that provide a safe and engaging environment for children with SEND. - Expanding Physical Education Contracts - There is an initiative to increase the number of schools and educational institutions that Entire works with to deliver inclusive physical education. - Creating work placements for school leavers - Entire Club aims to develop work placement opportunities specifically designed for young adults with SEND, facilitating their transition into the workforce. - Expanding geographic coverage - By 2027, Entire Club aims to make its inclusive childcare and SEND services available across four counties, making it easier for families outside the immediate vicinity to access high-quality, affordable SEND provisions.

name: The Freedom Programme
description: Freedom Programme is a domestic violence programme which was created by Pat Craven who holds the copyright (all rights reserved) and evolved from her work with perpetrators of domestic violence. The Programme provides information, not therapy. Read the mission statement. The Programme was primarily designed for women as victims of domestic violence since research shows that the vast majority of cases of serious abuse are male on female. However, the programme, when provided as an intensive two-day course, is also suitable for men, whether abusive and wishing to change their attitudes and behaviour or whether victims of same-sex domestic abuse themselves. The Freedom Programme examines the roles played by attitudes and beliefs on the actions of abusive men and the responses of victims and survivors. The aim is to help them to make sense of and understand what has happened to them, instead of the whole experience just feeling like a horrible mess. The Freedom Programme also describes in detail how children are affected by being exposed to this kind of abuse and very importantly how their lives are improved when the abuse is removed. The programme usually lasts for 11 or 12 weeks and is free. It is provided by hundreds of agencies across the UK. For example, some of them are rolling so women can join at any time but this varies according to local needs. Search for one in your area or contact our Freedom Programme helpline. The National Domestic Violence 24 hour free helpline number is 0808 2000 247 Online programmes are also available for men and women.

local_offer: Dynamic Minds was founded by Dr Kevin Jones, Chartered Clinical Psychologist. Dr Jones aims to provide holistic, evidence based and collaborative psychological assessment and treatment to enable clients to move forward purposefully with their lives. Dr Jones is a highly experienced, senior Clinical Psychologist who specialises in working with children, young people and young adults. He has extensive experience in the assessment, diagnosis and ongoing support for children, adolescents and young adults who are neurodiverse, and also with people across the life span who live with a long term health condition.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our service provides specialist psychological assessment and individual / family support for children with social, emotional and learning needs. The specific outcomes will be dependent upon the presenting needs and reasons for seeking psychological support (e.g. diagnosis / formulation of needs, targeted cognitive assessment, improved psychological health etc.) What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Dr Jones maintains regular CPD in line with his professional accreditations. Dr Jones has regular training and development within his specialist NHS team and also with external training providers. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Telephone and email. Communications and materials used to support therapy will be tailored to a particular child's level of understanding and communication abilities. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Dr Jones runs his practice in a relaxed, home office setting in the Buckinghamshire village of Waddesdon. Dr Jones currently runs his clinic on a Tuesday between the hours 9.30am-2.30pm. There is dedicated parking, and a comfortable waiting area for parents which can be used for any parts of assessment or therapeutic sessions where Dr Jones is working 1:1 with the young person. The office and waiting area are all ground floor, the majority of which is level access throughout except for a 4" threshold at the entrance. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact us via the contact form on our website. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? In time the aim would be to offer a wider range of opening hours to give more flexibility to families who wish to access our service.

description: The Adventure Playground holds a Fun Club the last Thursday evening of every month from 6:30 pm to 8:30 pm. local_offer: Our nursery aims to provide the best inclusive care and education for all children under the age of five. This includes any child who may require additional services or help to reach their full potential and improved outcomes. We will work with external support systems as well as utilising our well-trained staff to help all children to develop.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We liaise with the Buckinghamshire Council Early Years Service and follow their support and advice, as well as the LA SEN team. We speak with speech and language therapists, health visitors and outside agencies such as occupational therapists who give us extra support should we need it. We also have two other nurseries with which we work closely and share our experiences and tools to support children in our care. Our manager holds a level 3 in supporting childrens speech and language development, and has recently completed her SEND training. Our deputy holds a level 3 SENco. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Manager has recently completed her SENco training with Buckinghamshire early years team. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We use an app called FAMLY where we share updates on childrens progress and their next steps. We encourage parents to share photos and updates on children's progress from home as well. We hold termly parents consultations to discuss children's development, we meet with parents to discuss children's APDR's (Assess,plan,do,review forms) half termly. Where possible a child's key person will hand them over at the end of the day, each parent has a verbal handover each day, detailing their child's day. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use APDR's to share targets with families for those children with SEND, these are reviewed and discussed half termly, unless advised otherwise. WE write a termly report detailing their development. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Outdoors has a small step up a curb to the lawn area. All of the rooms are currently on the ground floor, with double doors into some rooms. There are steps into the building through each doorway, some smaller than others due to the building being listed. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that leaving your child for the first time can be a big decision and can be very emotional. We always reassure parents with telephone calls and photos when they collect. We also encourage parents to call during the settling sessions and their first day to put their minds at rest. We offer settling in sessions to each family, tailored to each child's individual needs, so they can all meet the staff within the room and complete the relevant paperwork to support their child’s journey with us. We offer a welcome leaflet which gives them an idea of what we offer and expectations within that specific room. We make notes on their all about me forms if parents tell us anything which we feel is relevant. We tailor the settling in sessions to each individual child, with flexibility on start dates should they need longer to settle. We offer three initial sessions and for babies, we offer more to fit with their routine. If a child transitions from another setting we seek parental permission to contact this setting and discuss their development, to ensure we find out all information regarding the child and their family. We seek parental permission to contact any professionals that are supporting their child and ask for any relevant and up to date reports to ensure we can meet their needs during their settles as well as on their first day and beyond. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Manager to access the SENDco training and as we are a new setting we will seek to support staff with any training needs that arise when we have new children and families joining us.

description: Buckinghamshire Council is working in partnership with YC2 Young Carers, Forever Colours Children's Hospice, and The White Hart to provide a drop-in for Parents and Carers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (diagnosed or showing signs of SEND). The SEND Peer Support drop-in is an opportunity for Parents and Carers to meet informally and build their support networks. Wherever you are on your SEND journey, you are welcome to come along to discuss the challenges of parenting a child with SEND and share things that have gone well. Professionals will be available to provide signposting support and information. Please note that although we will be able to provide support around general processes, we will not be able to comment on individual EHC Plan queries or outcomes. The drop in is held at The White Hart, Market Square, Buckingham 10am to 12 midday on the third Tuesday of the month Tea and Coffee provided

name: Easely Does It
description: Easely Does It is a great way for people to enjoy creativity without the intimidation of not knowing where to start. Join one of our sessions, have some fun and just generally unwind. We offer live and online art and craft workshops, life drawing classes, corporate events, private parties and paint nights in and around Buckinghamshire. Get Creative Whether you’re joining for one of our paint nights at our partner venues in and around Buckinghamshire or for one of our recorded art tutorials. Our sessions are guided, but not dictated, we demonstrate a technique to achieve the look of the theme of the session, but it’s totally up to you how closely you follow. We always give variations and actively encourage you to “go off piste” and create your own original piece of art. No Experience Necessary It doesn’t matter if you haven’t picked up a paint brush since school or you’re a seasoned painter who just wants to be creative and sociable. Unlike other paint and sip companies we try and introduce at least one new technique or piece of art theory into each session, so everyone can take something away to help improve their painting or their appreciation of other peoples' art. Everything Supplied We supply everything you need and if you join us for one of our “Painting and Prosecco” nights we even include glasses of bubbly. Soft drinks, snacks, easels, paints and canvases are all supplied. We even provide an apron, although we recommend you wear something you don’t mind if you get a bit of paint on. Check out our website below for more information about upcoming events.

local_offer: Furze Down School is a Community Special School which supports the development of children aged 4 to 19 with Communication and Interaction Special Educational Needs. The school has Specialist School Status in this area. Pupils at Furze Down School and Sixth Form have complex needs. Children and young people with complex needs include those with co-existing conditions or significant learning disabilities and/or autism. As a result of their difficulties some children and young people will present with behaviour which is challenging. Furze Down School and Sixth Form have expertise in supporting young people with special educational needs and communication differences. Specialism: Specialist School for Communication and Interaction Overarching Aims Furze Down School aims to anticipate and respond to the needs of individuals experiencing difficulties with communication and interaction. The school works in partnership with families, individuals, and other professionals in order to reduce the impact of these difficulties and enhance the pupil’s ability to participate in daily life. A Graduated Approach to SEN support at Furze Down At Furze Down School Special Educational Needs goals are targeted through a shared educational, health and social care approach. High Quality Teaching and an environment supportive of all aspects of communication and interaction inform personalised provision leading to excellent outcomes for all pupils. See latest SEND report. SEND needs met: - Autism - Hearing - Communication and interaction - Cognition and learning Furze Down School follows a ‘Total Communication and Interaction’ approach which encourages the use of verbal and non-verbal communication to maximise communication, develop empathy and promote self-advocacy. “We believe that everyone should have the opportunity to make choices through empowerment and self-advocacy.” Strategic Management A ‘Total Communication and Interaction’ approach is strategic and involves all staff in: - assessment and identification of barriers to learning - multi professional planning - implementation of specialised teaching and learning strategies, classroom procedures and practices detailed assessment, record keeping, reporting, tracking and evaluation in terms of pupil progress and outcomes. This allows the school to produce short term goals (STGs) linked to the Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). It is important that children and young people are empowered to think about what they want now and in the future. At Furze Down, we work together to encourage our students to make plans and work towards their goals with the right support; - raising aspirations and motivation - reviewing learning and progress - informing choices (14 to 19) - establishing personal, learning and career goals - And preparing young people for a successful transition to adulthood https://www.fds.org.uk/key-information/policies What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Furze Down School is a county resource and Buckinghamshire Council is the placing authority. All pupils at Furze Down School have an Educational Health Care Plan It is, however, the policy of the school to meet all pupils and their parents or carers prior to admission. Where possible a member of staff will visit the child in their referring school in order to establish the needs of each pupil and whether Furze Down School would be an appropriate placement to meet those needs. As a group, the new pupils have an introductory visit to the school during the half term prior to starting as part of transition arrangements. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our sixth Form pupils as from September 2024 are now based at our new Well Street Site in Buckingham. This provision will continue to expand.

It is our aim to provide students with a stimulating and supportive environment that not only maximizes academic achievement but also that gives all young people who study here a uniquely rewarding and fulfilling experience. One of the defining characteristics of our Sixth Form is the warm and welcoming atmosphere and all our students, including the many who choose us from other schools, find it easy to settle into life here at Furze Platt. We are committed to being a fully comprehensive Sixth Form offering a broad and varied curriculum that is specifically tailored to the requirements of our students. Our curriculum is made up of over 25 discrete subjects, all expertly taught by subject specialists, ensuring Furze Platt students receive excellent academic tuition throughout their time in Sixth Form. Class sizes are smaller than students have been used to so far and academic staff regularly monitor academic progress, with clear advice and guidance being given to make sure students maximize their potential. Sixth Formers are given excellent opportunities to develop powerful independent learning skills, and our approach allows students to balance the independence and responsibility needed for them to be successful, regardless of their personal career aspirations beyond the Sixth Form.

name: Guided Tudor Walk
description: Join a guided Tudor Walk to learn about life – and death – in Sixteenth century Amersham These walks are led by guides in Tudor costume and start from the museum at 2.30 pm on the last Saturday in each month (April to September). The walk visits the church (weddings permitting!) then leaves the town and follows field paths. It includes a steady climb, which is taken slowly. Baby buggies have successfully managed the route and we did once get a mobility buggy up the hill! The walk usually lasts about 2 hours and 15 minutes. There will be the following topics covered during the walk: Food and drink Markets and fairs Buildings and burgage plots Clothing and work Health and cures Religious beliefs and the Lollard martyrs Note- if you would like to visit the museum on the same day as your walk, this is possible from 12 noon before the walk starts. There is not time after the walk finishes. Pre-booking is recommended.

description: Our 9-week Wellbeing and Nature Course uses seasonal nature-based activities, including conservation, crafts and arts, to help people build resilience and improve their wellbeing. This course is designed for adults aged 18 plus who are experiencing mild to moderate depression, low mood, anxiety, struggling to return to work or looking to boost their confidence. Course runs 5 times a year - check the website for next dates.
organisation: Lindengate Our free drop-in support sessions are for anyone who may be struggling with their wellbeing or mental health. Set on a 5-acre site, our therapeutic gardens and wildlife haven are accessible to anyone who needs space and time to "be". Finding time to give yourself space can be difficult in the best of weather, but in Winter, the challenge becomes even greater. There are many benefits to spending just a few minutes a day outdoors. Here are a few of them: 15 minutes outdoors every day can improve both our moods and our physical health, leading to reduced stress and increased self-esteem Builds our immune system, as the cold weather actually kills off bacteria. With the current restrictions in place, we can meet up with a friend, which will improve our mental wellbeing, through social interaction. We have plenty of sheltered areas dotted about to meet with a friend or family member for a chat or to bring a book and enjoy the peace, amongst the wildlife. charlie.hughes@lindengate.org.uk http://www.lindengate.org.uk

name: Premier League Kicks
description: Premier League Kicks is a flagship programme established by the Premier League in 2006 to encourage sports participation in youngsters from some of the most high-need areas within local communities. The initiative offers free workshops and football and sports sessions to provide kids with the opportunities and support to reach their full potential. It involves football club community organisations, such as WWF, who work closely with young people and authorities within their local area. This includes ties with the police and other key partners to create stronger, safer, and more inclusive communities. The programme encourages young people by getting them involved in constructive activities, such as a wide variety of sports, coaching projects, music, education, and personal development. Since its conception, Premier League Kicks has seen communities across the country transformed with greater football and sports participation rates and authorities reporting significant reductions in anti-social behaviour in the same area. The programme started with four pilot projects. These were based at Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester City, Fulham, and Brentford. Since then, it has engaged more than 300,000 young people at hundreds of venues across the country. It also encourages thousands of youngsters to find routes into education, training and employment with volunteering offered in multiple fields. name: Wellbeing Walk
description: Here at Wycombe Wanderers Foundation, we strive to help our community and understand the huge demand for mental health recovery and prevention projects. Our Keep Moving Forward Wellbeing Walk gives participants the opportunity to meet a friendly group of people who are all on a recovery journey. The walk helps to keep people active whilst walking and talking with people who can support them. It is a very relaxed environment and we even stop for a cup of tea on the way around. The Walk takes place every Tuesday from 11am to 1pm and begins at the Wycombe Lido, just by the car park, a little way up from the tennis courts. There is no need to book onto the walks; you can simply turn up on the day, and there is no cost to take part. Wycombe Wanderers Foundation recognise that physical activity can play an important role in the lives of people facing mental health challenges. We also recognise that there can be certain barriers faced by those facing mental health challenges when it comes to participating in physical activity. Considering this, should you have any questions or concerns before attending, please feel free to email or call us on the contact details below.

local_offer: - Highly personalised home tuition service for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities. Self-referrals are accepted from families as well as from Local Authorities and schools. - School-based support is provided to ensure school placements don’t break down including transitions into and out of school. - Delivery of therapies including Speech and Language, Occupational Therapy, Educational Psychology, Clinical Psychology, and Positive Behaviour Support. - Access arrangements and testing in schools and homes. - Provision of specialist staff to schools including SENCO’s, Teaching Assistants, Mentors, Dyslexia Specialists, SEND teachers, and Inclusion Leads. - Supportive audits and specialist training for schools and Local Authorities that intend to improve their SEND practice. - Managing and supporting EOTAS packages. - Provision of SEND expert witnesses for independent review panels. - Working in collaboration with Open Awards, we can offer a range of Online Functional Skills examinations from Entry Level 3 to Level 2 (GCSE equivalent).  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Helping children and young people re-engage with learning. Helping children without a school place to make progress academically and socially. Providing transition in and out of school. Fulfilling Section F of the Education, Health and Care Plan. Providing outstanding support and signposting for families. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Safeguarding, low arousal approaches, Autism and PDA, Team Teach, Health and Safety, Risk assessing, Positive Behaviour Management, complex needs, learning difficulties, creating a total communication environment. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We involve parents as a key part of the team around the child. They contribute to the Personal Plan that we complete for child or young person we support. The voice of the family and child is of the upmost importance to us. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Tutors write a weekly progress report which covers the activities, progress and engagement of the young person. These can be shared with families. Tutors regularly assess young people and are happy to share their feedback with parents and carers. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We work in schools, community settings or homes and will always find the most appropriate environment to support the young person. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families, who have children with EHCP's, can speak to their Local Authority caseworkers who can refer to us directly. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? ASEND services are now being delivered nationally and we aim to continue providing outstanding SEND provision all across the United Kingdom.

name: GamCare Young People's Service
description: The young people service is a dedicated team that helps young people between the ages of 11 to 18 with gambling-related problems. The team can help if you are struggling with gambling yourself or if you are affected by someone else’s gambling. The Young People Service can also provide information and advice to parents and professionals. local_offer: Gateway School believes that all pupils are entitled to high quality, well-planned and well-organised teaching, which will enable them to participate in a broad and balanced curriculum and to be part of the social life of the school  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Gateway School takes a whole school approach to the provision for pupils with SEN through assessing, planning, delivering, reviewing and recording of information, to ensure that all children achieve their potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Gateway School welcomes parental involvement and seeks to gain as much information as possible about the child from the parents/carers; all staff read any paperwork submitted. All discussions are dealt with confidentially and in a sensitive manner. In partnership with parents, pupils with special educational needs will be encouraged to contribute to the assessment of their needs, the review and the transition process. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The school will continue to use the system of Pupil Passports to record the steps taken to meet the needs of individual pupils. The SENCO is responsible for ensuring that records are kept and available when needed on the School drive. These are available to share with parents at parent consultations twice a year. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The process of ongoing assessment demonstrates what has been learned, identifies successes and gaps in learning and should identify what the next learning stage should be. It also provides valuable information about how the curriculum could be suitably adapted and which methodologies should be adopted to meet individual needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To work in cooperation and productive partnerships with the Local Education Authority and other outside agencies, to ensure there is a multi-professional approach to meeting the needs of all vulnerable learners

name: Woburn Safari Park
description: Keep the kids entertained with an unforgettable safari adventure. Bring your troop to experience the wonders of nature and enjoy a full day out at Woburn Safari Park, filled with fun, learning and playtime. Enjoy seeing the look on their faces as your little monkeys meet the amazing wildlife, right through the windscreen of your car! They'll be amazed as they meet all kinds of endangered and exotic animals at the Safari Park. See the magnificent elephants, rhinos, lions, tigers, monkeys, giraffes, lions, zebra and many more as you explore the Road Safari. Continue the fun wildlife activities in the Foot Safari, home to sea lions, lemurs, penguins and meerkats. Stop off to watch fascinating keeper talks and demonstrations to get to know the individual animal residents. Plus there are loads of indoor and outdoor play areas, all included in your ticket price! Book tickets online or pay on arrival at the gate. If you plan to arrive after 3pm, standard day tickets are available on arrival. Enter in your own vehicle and enjoy unlimited circuits of the Road Safari. The re-entry route can be found through the concrete car park, past Elephant Meadow. Open daily from 10am to 5pm (last entry), closing at 6pm.

description: Kumon study in Chesham aims to ensure that every child develops a love for learning. We offer maths and English programmes to help students of any age and ability to progress their skills and build key foundations for learning. Traditional maths and English tuition helps students progress, but Kumon goes one step further by helping each child develop self-learning skills, enabling them to tackle challenging work without reliance on a teacher. Students complete daily worksheet study developing ability and fluency gradually over time, progressing in small steps and building confidence. They also visit their local study centre up to twice a week for guidance from their Instructor. This means that they can strengthen their key skills or progress beyond school grade level without restriction. Kumon offers a cost-effective and convenient way to help your child build strong English and maths skills for a successful future.

name: Stonewall
description: At Stonewall, we stand for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, questioning and asexual (LGBTQ+) people everywhere. We imagine a world where all LGBTQ+ people are free to be themselves and can live our lives to the full. Over the last 30 years, we have helped create transformative change in the lives of LGBTQ+ people in the UK. Today, we have equal rights to love, marry and have children, and our lives, families and relationships are represented as part of the national curriculum in most of the UK. Our campaigns drive positive change in public attitudes and public policy. We ensure LGBTQ+ people can thrive throughout our lives by building deep, sustained change programmes with the institutions that have the biggest impact on us, whether we’re learning, working, praying or playing sport. We make sure that the world hears and learns from LGBTQ+ communities, and our work is grounded in evidence and expertise. And we’re committed to empowering people to create change in their own communities. We face rising intolerance degrading our hard-won rights. But we won't be silenced. Not until all of us are free to be proud, free to be loved, free to be together, free to be who we are. Our work continues until the world we imagine is the world we live in.

name: The Proud Trust
description: The Proud Trust is an LGBTQ+ youth charity empowering young people to be proud of who they are. The Proud Trust delivers youth work and one-to-one support across Greater Manchester. The charity also runs a national training and inclusion programme for schools, Proud Connections Live Chat, and manages Manchester’s LGBT+ Centre, The Proud Place. We can trace our roots back to the 1970s and the Gay Youth Group, which met in Manchester, initially in Waterloo Place and, from 1988, the Sidney Street purpose-built Gay Centre. In the years since, we have continued to put LGBTQ+ young people at the forefront of our work. We support young people across the UK through youth groups, mentoring programmes and more. We also offer a live chat for LGBTQ+ young people, their families and the professionals supporting them. We work with and support adults in trusted positions, including schools and other children’s services, helping them make spaces more LGBTQ+ inclusive as well as improving confidence in tackling discrimination and celebrating diversity. We also provide online resources for young people, parents/carers, and organisations.

GIRES is a professionally managed membership charity supported by volunteers that, in collaboration with other groups in its field, hears, helps, empowers, and gives a voice to trans and gender diverse individuals, including those who are non-binary and non-gender, as well as their families. description: Group singing is for well-being, health, and fun! Are you in need of some ‘Me-Time’? What better way to make time for your well-being in 2024 than with happy, relaxed singing? Group singing has been proven to lift mood, reduce stress and anxiety, reduce pain, increase immunity and improve respiratory function, but most of all, it is fun. Sing Your Pain Away sessions are on Fridays from 11:30am to 12:30pm. Sessions are £6.80 per person. A limited number of free places are available to those who need them. Please get in touch with Queens Park Arts Centre for more information. Our singing group is super friendly and inclusive, without pressure or judgment. It is open to everyone regardless of singing ability. We welcome people with long-term health conditions, those going through an emotionally challenging time, carers who need respite and anyone who needs relaxed singing and laughter. We sing uplifting and happy songs from the shows, songs from the 40s, 50s, 60s and 70s, spirituals, funny songs, the odd new song and more. It’s a great way to meet other local people and enjoy some relaxed singing, laughter and fun. There are no performances, no pressure, just lots of happy singing, well-being, health and fun. name: Waddesdon Hall Community Fridge
description: Our community fridge is thriving thanks to daily food donations from local supermarkets and bakeries. This fridge is run by Volunteers who pick up, sort, and display the food for everyone. We record all items and their weights, so please be patient as we log and organise the goods. To speed up the process, we may ask you to wait outside. Our volunteers also prepare food boxes for families in the village and beyond, often delivering them directly to neighbours. Social workers pick up food regularly to distribute during their visits. Unusable food isn't wasted. These donations benefit local pig farms, aviaries at Manor, and chickens. There's extensive logistics behind this operation, ensuring everything runs smoothly. Our fridge is open to everybody; this is about food waste, not poverty. Always be mindful: take what you need and share it with others. By reducing waste and supporting our community, this fridge is not just a local initiative; it's a global effort to save the planet.

name: Princes Risborough Photographic Society
description: Photography is a fun activity and in Princes Risborough Photographic Society (PRPS) this is what we encourage. The club has a wide range of membership from beginners through to some excellent professional photographers. Hence, we are catering for all levels of creative skill, whether they are using simple low budget cameras, the high end DSLRs or indeed mobile phones; the latter having advanced tremendously in the past few years. Meetings are held on a fortnightly basis from September through to July. The club runs competitions throughout the year, these are on various set subjects, chosen by the committee in advance and are for both printed photographs and digital projected images. We have talks by a wide range of speakers, including trade ambassadors on numerous subjects. There are member’s nights when individual members give talks about their own photography, equipment, and places they have visited. Some of these are audio-visual presentations. We have a sub-group named; “Society Snappers” this group meets twice a month throughout the year, either on location or in a local hostelry. Each meeting is carefully structured and covers subjects of specific interest to members.

What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I have over 20 years of experience and have been SENCO in my previous job at an infant school so have had experience in a wide range of SEN. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed my SENCO training in the past. I will be looking to update within the next 6 months. I have also completed Makaton signing. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I pride myself at making my setting warm and friendly for both parents and children. I use Babydays to communicate to parents on a daily basis and the parents are able to access their child's next steps and progress easily. Parents know that they can ask any questions when dropping off or collecting about their child's development. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I make sure every child has a few settling in sessions and I spend time talking to the parents about their child's needs. Two year progress checks are carried out and sent to parents via the Babydays app. Parents are given the opportunity to add and discuss my findings. If SEN support is needed I will invite the parents for a meeting to discuss a plan and get other professionals involved if needed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Access to my setting is via the back gate leading to a patio and small step into the cabin/play room. A small step onto large grass area. I have two steps leading into the house but if needs be a ramp could be fitted. And access to a downstairs toilet. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I offer two settling in sessions but if a child needs more then I will make sure this is possible. I spend time talking to the parents and find out if they have been to a previous setting and ask to see any documents they may have. I have good links with local schools and pre schools and when the child moves to a new setting I will be happy to meet and discuss the child's needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I constantly reflect on my environment and adapt to what is needed for the individual children attending my setting.

local_offer: With over 30 years of experience in education, I have developed a deep understanding of the needs of children across Early Years and Primary settings, particularly those with Special Educational Needs (SEN). I have worked closely with a wide range of professionals, including Occupational Therapists, Speech and Language Therapists, the SEND Team, and the Visual Impairment Team, to provide tailored support that enables every child to thrive. Throughout my career, I have supported children with a variety of needs, including Autism, Attachment Disorder, Dyslexia, Dyspraxia, Epilepsy, Global Developmental Delay, and Visual Impairment. I am passionate about creating inclusive learning environments and am committed to promoting equality of opportunity, valuing diversity, and meeting the individual needs of every child. This includes respecting and accommodating cultural backgrounds and dietary requirements.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My aim is to work together with families and professionals to provide an inclusive home-based setting with a welcoming and nurturing centre. I am trained in supporting children with SEND and provide all children with a rich and accessible early years experience. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Autism Awareness/ Understanding Autism How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I respect every parent as their child's first and most enduring educator. I will work closely with you before your child joins me to understand their needs, likes, dislikes and the aspirations you have. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending the setting are continually observed. Progress is shared daily at the end of the child’s session and through the Baby Days app, where parents receive photos and observations to celebrate their children’s learning. Two year progress reports are written after their 2nd birthday. Any areas of concern are raised and discussions about the child’s and next steps are planned. The Assess, Plan, Do, Review cycles is a key part of the graduated response to meet the child’s needs. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My services are on ground floor with double doors leading into the garden. There are three steps leading to the top of the garden, however a portable ramp can be purchased to accommodate wheelchair access. There is sufficient space for children to free-flow safely between indoors and outdoors and I have a downstairs bathroom. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact can be made through email to check availability. Children will be accepted on a first come first basis where the needs of individual children can be met. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am always looking for ways to ensure that I provide the best service for all children.

local_offer: We support through specific OT assessments to establish client centered needs and develop targeted OT programmes to increase their participation and performance in daily lives. The may include supporting a child or young person to overcome sensory barriers in order to access community services. Another example, by strengthening fine motor skills to develop handwriting and other functional skills. We undertake parent trainings, coaching and support group sessions to enable parents understanding towards their children's needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to achieve client-centered goals, which are mostly towards becoming independent, learning to carry out daily life skills, overcoming sensory and motor barriers, improving play skills, and social skills. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We are trained at a post-graduate certificate level in sensory integration and 500 hours of yoga teacher training from British Wheel of Yoga. We have a number of short trainings which we complete as a part of regular CPD. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in every step from assessment to carrying out interventions during OT sessions. Depending on the type of input, parents are encouraged to take part in goal setting, identifying motivating activities for their children, carrying out holiday time activities at home and giving feedback on a regular basis. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents are involved on a regular basis and always have time to ask questions at the end of the session. Sometimes, a more formal and protected time called supervision sessions can be offered for tutors, OT assistants and parents who carry out OT intervention programmes with their children, to ask questions or discuss specific issues. This is agreed between the therapist and parents before starting the programme. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The clinic is set on the 1st floor but our service includes both coming to the clinic and visiting clients at their schools, homes and nurseries. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? By contacting us on info@kidspire.co.uk or m.tokekar@kidspire.co.uk or calling us on 07730772609 What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to offer as many parents and caregivers our service but we also hope to run short workshop sessions for children and parents targeted on specific skills development which might benefit parents who cannot afford weekly sessions or the clinic is simply too far for them. We are heavily invested in bringing parent trainings and coaching sessions to empower parents by understanding specific difficulties their children may be having.

Girls will also start to do letter formation and engage in activities which will strengthen their fine motor skills. Girls will begin to read using blending and breakdown techniques through the Little Wandle phonics scheme. Our Pre-Reception class caters for individual needs and offers lots of differentiation within the activities to support and challenge those girls who are more able at this young age. Our bespoke curriculum ensure each piece of work is appropriate to each individual child ensure they make significant progress. Ambitious targets are set with the intention of achieving all Early Years Learning goals by the end of their Reception class year. It’s all about giving them the best possible start to achieve high expectations so that they exceed as they move through the school. Many of our children come to us from nearby Milton Keynes and other towns and villages in Buckinghamshire.

name: Animal Antiks Alpaca Walks
description: We run a weekly walk with Bucks Mind to meet our friendly team of Alpacas with a community bus collecting from the Whiteleaf Centre. Getting out into the fresh air, making new friends, and doing a little gentle exercise in the beautiful countryside greatly boosts your mental well-being. So, if you are feeling isolated, are new to the area, struggle with anxiety, or have recently lost a long-term loved one, then a new experience is one step forward for you. Once at the farm, you will be introduced to our alpacas and then head out across the tracks and fields with them. We will walk for about an hour around the farm and then back to the yard for a well-earned tea or coffee. Those who booked a space on the community bus will then be returned to the Whiteleaf Centre. Please wear suitable footwear and outerwear for the weather. Places must be booked in advance. We require you to complete a referral form, which is then sent to Bucks Mind so that they can manage participants on each walk. To receive a copy of the form or for more information, please contact us using the email or phone number below.
organisation: Animal Antiks Education Limited Animal Antiks is a day provision supporting both children and adults on a 220-acre working farm in the beautiful Buckinghamshire countryside. Providing a safe environment supporting all ages and many disabilities Animal Antiks unique approach is non-segregated, allowing the opportunity to normalise anxieties and build confidence along with life, social and functional skills. Some choose to spend time with their favourite animal, grooming a miniature pony, walking goats, alpacas, or sheep, or sitting with the chickens and collecting the eggs. Others enjoy getting involved with the more manual tasks around the farm or group activities working on projects. For young adults struggling within the conventional school settings, we work with our training provider (Haddon Training) to provide the opportunity to complete Level 1 and Level 2 animal care qualifications, alongside function skills (various levels) in English, mathematics, and ICT. For more information or to arrange a visit please contact us. How to get here: We are based on a working farm, the Number 60 bus from Aylesbury or Buckingham stops in the village and we are about a 10 minute walk from the stop. office@animalantiks.co.uk https://www.animalantiks.co.uk/

local_offer: Buttons have an excellent reputation for childcare provision and supporting children with SEND. Our staff teams are highly trained with several years of experience, the teams are supported by a SEND Manager.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our philosophy and ethos is for all children to achieve regardless of ability, we strive to ensure that outcomes for all children are positive and that they experience the very best within a preschool environment which is fully inclusive. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff have attended the SEND training provided by Buckinghamshire Council alongside the level 3 qualification which is accredited by Educare. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work alongside parents/carers, advising on strategies which can be mirrored at home, parents/carers are invited into preschool to discuss progress and to observe the child's development and engagement. Full support plans are written in conjunction with parents that are bespoke to the individual needs of the child, these documents are then available should additional support/transitions be required. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use Eylog as a learning journey for all children, an individual PDR (Plan, Do, Review) will also be in place, Eylog is a two way process and milestone, achievements and events from home life can also be uploaded. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Fully accessible settings which cater for all levels of need. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Once registered a home visit will be booked, the child and family are invited into the setting, a care plan will be written to ensure that the needs of the child are met, taking into account the other children and needs within the setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Buttons are a SEND specialist provider, we are always looking for new and innovative ways to extend our outstanding offering.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through personalised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? October 2024 - Understanding autism, the three areas of difference and strategies to remove barriers to learning How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with us. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a small step leading to the front door but easy access via a side entrance. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

name: Beat Eating Disorder Charity
description: Founded in 1989 as the Eating Disorders Association, we aim to end the pain and suffering caused by eating disorders. Around 1.25 million people in the UK suffer from eating disorders, many in secret. They are of all ages, genders, and backgrounds. Eating disorders include bulimia, binge eating disorder, avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID), other specified feeding or eating disorder (OSFED), and anorexia, which has the highest mortality rate of any mental illness. Eating disorders can steal childhoods, devastate relationships, and pull families apart. But, with the right treatment and support, recovery is possible. Our national helpline exists to encourage and empower people to ger help quickly, because we know the sooner someone starts treatment, the greater their chance of recovery. People can contact us online or by phone. We listen to them, help them to understand the illness, and support them to take positive steps towards recovery. We also support family and friends, equipping them with essential skills and advice, so they can help their loved ones recover whilst also looking after their own mental health. And we campaign to increase knowledge among healthcare and other relevant professionals, and for better funding for high-quality treatment, so that when people are brave enough to take vital steps towards recovery, the right help is available to them. The work we do means that every year lives are saved, families are kept together, and people are able to live free of eating disorders. We share the vision of an end to the pain and suffering caused by eating disorders. We are inspired by the people we serve, by the difference we can make, and by our commitment to each other.

name: Beat Eating Disorder Helpline
description: Beat provides Helplines for people of all ages, offering support and information about eating disorders no matter where you are in your journey. These Helplines are free to call from all phones. If you contact our Helpline you will speak to a trained Support Worker experienced in providing support, information, and signposting to people in a similar situation to you. Our Helpline is action-focused, giving you a space to explore your concerns and identify next steps. You do not need a formal diagnosis to use our Helpline. Support on the Helpline is available by phone, email, webchat through our social media accounts and by letter. Calls to the helpline are free from landlines and mobile phones within the UK and do not appear on itemised bills. Sometimes our lines are busy. If you can't get through immediately, please do try again or try our one-to-one web chat or send us an email. If you are in need of urgent help or medical advice for yourself or someone else please contact 999 or the Samaritans on 116 123 if you or someone else is in immediate danger. If you are looking for medical advice contact your GP or 111. Staff will end telephone calls if they consider the caller aggressive, abusive or offensive.

searchText:
name: Peer Support and Online Development for Carers | Eating disorders
description: Peer support and Online Development (POD) is a space designed for people who are supporting a loved one with an eating disorder. We have worked closely with our service users, ambassadors and eating disorder clinicians to help us to shape this platform, ensuring that the information we are sharing is clinically sound and is meeting the needs of those who will be accessing it. POD is an e-learning platform and community for carers that provides you with online modules, resources and spaces to talk with peers to help you better support your loved one. With POD's catalogue of free online e-learning modules you can learn more about eating disorders and how to be an effective carer. Our instructor-led workshop are accessible through POD: - Developing Dolphins - Raising Resilience - Harnessing Hope - Coping with Celebrations When the sessions are over you'll have the chance to continue conversations started in your group in a dedicated workspace. Through POD, you can access a wide range of interactive e-learning modules. Using a combination of written, visual, and video-based learning tools, you’ll learn more about the basics of eating disorders, the psychology behind what your loved one is experiencing, and what to expect from treatment. You’ll also learn about useful tools to support your loved one in recovery, such as motivational interviewing, the stages of change model, and how to avoid accommodating or enabling behaviours. You’re not alone in supporting a loved one with an eating disorder. With POD, you can connect with others who have the same experiences and worries as you. Through our peer support forums, you’ll be able to discuss what you’re learning, and share information, resources and ideas with others caring for someone with an eating disorder. These forums will be regularly reviewed by the Beat team to protect the safety of the community. Each week, you’ll also be able to access drop-in spaces to meet with Beat’s Clinical Associate Trainers, who’ll be on hand to offer you guidance and support.

description: Following a referral from the Community Mental Health Team (CMHT) from your GP, you may be allocated a Navigator. Navigators can only accept referrals from within this referral route. Community Navigators work with you to support your social, emotional, medical and practical needs. You will then meet weekly or fortnightly for 4 to 6 weeks. One-to-one meetings will be online via video link or within a suitable NHS or community premises. Your Community Navigator will discuss the type of meeting and location that is best for you. Your Community Navigator will work with you to identify community support that will help meet your needs, make referrals, and help you access services and community groups. Community Navigators are approachable, empathic and flexible. They will listen to you and help you identify coping strategies and manageable goals.
