name: Green Futures
description: Green Futures 2G is a Buckinghamshire-based project that is funded by The Rothschild Foundation to support the local green economy, address youth unemployment, and reconnect young people with land and nature. We aim to do this by: - Creating new local career pathways in the Green Economy for young people from minority groups, challenging or disadvantaged backgrounds - Providing career advice and support through safe and empowering experiences for young people aged 11 to 17 from marginalised backgrounds - Supporting organisations to trial new collaborative projects which support young people to develop green employability skills and enhance the local food and farming sector - Working with local schools and youth groups to create local campaigns tackling food-related issues. We offer funded pilot partnership projects, sector exposure visits, and talks and events across the county promoting green jobs and careers. This is to generate innovation and collaboration between the great work happening across the county. We have internship opportunities for those aged 18 to 24, seed funding for schools and youth organisations, and training and development for our Green Futures Network members. This training includes health and safety, safeguarding, working with people with additional needs, and inclusive employment practice. Feel free to contact us if you have any queries or would like to join in.

suitabilities: 
local_offer: At ROKIL CIC, we provide tailored, specialist-led, support for neurodivergent children under 14, including those navigating Autism, ADHD, SEMH (Social, Emotional, and Mental Health) needs, and school-based anxiety. Our approach utilizes evidence-based methodologies- including therapeutic arts, music, and play-based learning- to foster emotional regulation, functional communication, and executive functioning. Our specialised SEND provisions include: 1-to-1 Alternative Provision (AP) and EOTAS: Bespoke, trauma-informed daytime support for children experiencing school avoidance, exclusion, or those requiring Alternative Provision to meet Section F outcomes of their EHCP. Specialist Respite: A safe, sensory-adapted, and low-demand environment where children can engage in therapeutic play while parents receive essential respite. Inclusive Rhythms: Small-group, specialist-led music sessions designed specifically for decompression, sensory regulation, and zero-judgment social connection. All of our programs are delivered by highly experienced practitioners in sensory-friendly spaces. We work collaboratively with parents, schools, and Local Authorities to directly align our interventions with a child’s EHCP targets and personal developmental goals.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? For children and young people, our primary outcomes are increased emotional regulation, improved executive functioning, and enhanced functional communication. Through our arts, music, and play-based interventions, we aim to build resilience, reduce school-based anxiety, and foster a genuine sense of belonging and academic readiness. For families, our goal is to reduce isolation, provide essential specialist respite, and empower parents with the confidence and tools to support their child’s unique developmental journey through our dedicated coaching and workshops. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our highly qualified team possesses deep expertise in cognitive, emotional, and behavioural science. Staff are trained in Evidence-Based Methodologies, including NDBI (Naturalistic Developmental Behavioural Interventions), play therapy techniques, and affirming behavioural support. All staff and volunteers hold up-to-date Enhanced DBS checks, comprehensive Safeguarding training, and specialized continuing professional development (CPD) in supporting children with SEMH, Autism, and ADHD. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We view parents as our most vital collaborative partners. Families can get involved through our specialized Parent Coaching sessions, monthly Parent Topic Workshops, and Q and A panels, which are designed to build a supportive community of knowledge. We share information through regular, informal feedback after each session, as well as through structured, written progress reports. For commissioned or EHCP placements, we track progress directly against a child’s specific Section F outcomes and provide comprehensive reports perfectly timed for Annual Reviews. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children with SEND benefit from a highly tailored, zero-judgment environment that accommodates their specific sensory and regulatory needs. Additional provisions include access to our 1-to-1 Alternative Provision (AP) and bespoke EOTAS packages, as well as our specialist-led "Inclusive Rhythms" and messy-play initiatives. We offer tailored staff-to-child ratios, individualized emotional regulation strategies, and therapeutic decompression spaces designed to prevent dysregulation and promote active engagement. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We meticulously select and partner with venues to ensure they are fully accessible, safe, and secure for all physical and neurodivergent needs. Our environments feature sensory-adapted indoor spaces—including specialized music and art rooms, and quiet zones for decompression—alongside access to secure, enclosed outdoor areas for physical regulation. All of our operating spaces are wheelchair accessible and designed to offer a low-demand, highly supportive atmosphere. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families, SENCOs, and Local Authority caseworkers can initiate support by contacting us directly via our website (www.rokilcic.com) or by email to arrange an initial consultation. We are highly flexible and accept private bookings, EHCP Direct Payments, and Local Authority or school-commissioned (SLA) placements. Thanks to our National Lottery funding, we also offer heavily subsidized rates and funded places for qualifying families to ensure our specialist services remain highly accessible. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our strategic vision includes establishing a permanent, full-time Alternative Provision and Respite residency within a major local SEND hub. This expansion will allow us to offer consistent, on-site structured respite, expand our age-tiered well-being initiatives (like 'Art to Heart'), and host larger community parent workshops. Ultimately, we aim to anchor a holistic "SEND Village" model, providing a seamless blend of specialist education, therapeutic play, and family support for the Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire communities.

local_offer: Gillotts values the abilities and achievements of all its students and is committed to providing, for each student, the best possible environment for learning by: • ensuring the identification of SEND as early as possible in students’ school careers • monitoring progress • working collaboratively with parents/carers and outside agencies • involving students and parents in decision-making • personalising learning for students • promoting independence • ensuring that the responsibility for SEND held by all staff and governors is carried out • removing barriers to achievement and success https://gillotts.org.uk/about-the-school/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Gillotts we have adopted a whole-school approach to SEND policy and practice. Students identified as having SEN or disabilities are, as far as is practicable, fully integrated into mainstream classes. Every effort is made to ensure that they have full access to the school’s curriculum and are included in all aspects of the school. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Training for our staff, teachers and Learning Support Assistants, is ongoing as part of our staff development programme. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Gillotts firmly believes in developing a strong partnership with parents and that this will enable students with SEND to achieve their potential. The school recognises that parents have a unique overview of their child’s needs and how best to support them, and that this gives them a key role in the partnership. Depending on age and appropriateness, SEND students will also be encouraged to participate in the decision-making processes affecting them. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The Governing Body believes that the admissions criteria should not discriminate against students with SEND and has due regard for the practice advocated in the Code of Practice. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Applications to join the school in Year 7 should be made to your home local authority. Applications for other year groups should be made through Oxfordshire County Council. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are developing our provision to include more short term interventions, and to increase our focus on developing skills in English and mathematics.

local_offer: Childlink extends all provision to support the needs of any child with SEN or a disability. Childlink do there up most to support the child to achieve and progress to their individual ability. Childlink Learning Centre is a day nursery and pre school, We opened in 1990. We provide quality and considered day care, Every Little person in our nursery family are valued, respected and listened to.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We work alongside all necessary professionals needed to support the child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO Training September 2019 Sophie Jones How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We Aim to Create a home from home environment that is loving and welcoming to all; we aim for all our Parents to feel comfortable to approach us about anything related to their families. We provide regular meetings with Parents to discuss their child’s progress and how we are going to move forward in their development. The parents also have informal opportunities to speak to any required member of staff at pick up and drop off times as well as through our eyLog App. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Each of our children have their own learning journal on Eylog in which both Parents and members of Staff can post Observations and updates. This can be accessed at all times of the day/year. Using the eyLog app we are in constant contact with the parent. Each term every Practitioner completes next steps on each of their Key children which can be also viewed on the eyLog app. With children with SEN we provide more frequent meeting with the parents to discuss their childs progress towards their short term outcomes and work together to plan the next steps for the child. We work alongside external Professionals to ensure the most appropriate support for children with SEN. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take into account all the needs of the children; the layout of Childlink is on one ground floor and there are no stairs throughout. All our doors are wheel chair accessible. We ensure that all walk ways are kept clear and wide enough for additional support where needed. We provide quiet sections of the room where children can take themselves off to if they need quiet time without over simulations. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have a lengthy and considered settling in sessions for any new children starting the nursery. When a child transitions from room to room we ensure that they do so with their current key worker to ensure a smooth and comfortable transition between rooms. We also have breakfast all together in the main room so that the babies feel included and part of the main room. When our Children go off to school we ensure that we keep in contact with their new schools and provide them with any information which is relevant. We also plan for teachers to come into the nursery to meet the children in a familiar environment before they transition into school. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to continue to work with relevant external professionals and to adapt our nursery accordingly.

name: Go Beyond
description: Go Beyond is the charity giving children and young people facing serious challenges in their lives the chance for a break that lasts a lifetime. On breaks under wide open skies in the countryside, Go Beyond’s expert staff and committed volunteers give children and young people who have been bereaved, abused, or bullied, who are living in poverty or caring for loved ones the chance to escape their worries and pressures. To have the moments and experiences they need to believe in themselves and think beyond the day-today for a bigger, brighter future. From splashing in the river in their wellies to braving the dizzying heights of a rock-climbing wall, each break is packed with activities intended to encourage self-belief and inspire adventure. Our breaks usually run from Monday afternoon to Friday morning and run all year round. By getting out and getting involved, Go Beyond’s biggest hope is for each child to go home knowing they can achieve more than they ever thought possible, inspired by what the world can offer them, and what they in turn can offer the world. Every break is totally free of charge for the children and young people.

name: Go Play Holiday Club run by SWCCP
description: Go Play Holiday Club, run by Southcourt and Walton Court Community Project, is for children aged 4 to 11 years old. Based at Ashmead School, the playscheme runs every school holiday, except Christmas. We have limited places for SEND children, email our manager for information. local_offer: NHS England Choices College is a specialist College providing tailored educational support, and a supported internship course for young adults aged 16 to 24 with learning disabilities/ difficulties and/or Autism.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Providing tailored educational support, and a supported internship course for young adults aged 16-24 with learning difficulties and/or disabilities, and/ or Autism. Our support is tailored to each Learner, based on their skills and interests. Interns spend 1 year learning maths, English and employability skills and attend up to three, 12-week placements with a Choices College Partner. The College is supported by the NHS as part of the ongoing commitment to improving employment outcomes for vulnerable groups. The main feature of the programme is a long-term work experience placement providing an on the job learning opportunity in a real work setting. The expected outcome is a paid job, further education, apprenticeship or volunteering. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Mentor Awareness Training TSI Disability Awareness Training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Feedback is collated from each placement on how the intern is progressing. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? To apply, go to our website and complete the online form or download and send us a hardcopy application form or can call us of the number provided. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will be partnering with Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust from September 2025 to deliver a Supported Internship.

description: Happy Hedgehogs provides high quality before and after school childcare for children attending the onsite preschool, Little Forest Friends and Haddenham St Marys school. We can provide your child with a healthy breakfast before school. After school, all children will be offered a snack. Children staying with us for a full after school will be provided with a light tea. organisation: Haddenham St Marys' C of E School and Wraparound Care Haddenham St Mary's Church of England School, founded in 1868, provides education for all children aged between 4 and 7 within a Christian ethos. With highly qualified teachers and a nominal roll of 180 children in three "year groups", class sizes are generally of 30 or under. Overlooking open fields at the southern end of the village and next to St Mary's Church, the school aims to create a challenging, yet supportive environment, within which a broad and balanced curriculum is adapted to the individual needs of each child. All children are encouraged to be independent and use their initiative to develop their full potential. Haddenham St Mary’s School, as part of the village and wider community, encourages a feeling of respect for people of all ages and beliefs in an ever-changing world. The overall aim is to awaken the children’s skills and personal qualities providing a foundation for a fulfilled and constructive life. The classroom teacher endeavours to create an atmosphere where individuals are recognised, appreciated and encouraged. Learning to work and play together is a prime consideration. The school has successfully run a hub kitchen, "Homemade at Haddenham St Mary's", since the introduction of Universal Infant Free School Meals and the team deliver homemade hot lunches to over 400 children a day both at Haddenham St Mary's and other local schools. The school is managed by a committed Governing Body, comprised of eleven local people with a broad range of backgrounds. It is supported by an active Parent Teacher Association which raises substantial funds to enhance pupil’s learning experience through educational visits and provide additional facilities to complement National Curriculum activities. office@haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk https://haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk/

local_offer: At Robertswood School we aim to support all children to enable them to achieve their potential. This is no different in our Breakfast Club and After School Club. We have high expectations of our children and want them all to feel a valued part of our school community. We operate a ‘whole pupil, whole school’ approach to the management and support of pupils with Special Educational Needs. We aim to raise the aspirations and expectations of all children, including those with SEND. https://www.robertswoodschool.co.uk/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs&pid=38 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Appropriate Continued Professional Development is provided to staff in order to support the needs of children with SEND within our school. Specialist expertise is obtained by the school by engaging professional advice as necessary. Training can take the form of child-specific training, support or be of a wider SEND nature. Examples of recent training include: • Paediatric First Aid training and Paediatric Handling. • Emotional Literacy support. • Nurture Networking including how nurture supports well-being. • Autism Awareness. • Sensory Integration. • Identifying and supporting children with anxiety. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents/carers and children are central to the school’s SEND processes and procedures. Teachers and the SENDCo work closely with parents/carers in the support of children with Special Educational Needs through: • Ongoing dialogue and active partnership. • Parent consultation meetings. • Provision Maps outlining targets and reviewing progress. • Reports from outside agencies. • SEND events run by the SENDCo/SEND team to inform and share knowledge. • SEND noticeboard. • Where appropriate, children are involved in their target setting and reviewing their learning with the teacher and/or SENDCo. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Robertswood school is fully accessible to wheelchair users. There is a designated disabled parking space at the front of the school and flat access to the school’s main entrance. The school has facilities for personal care, including toilets, for pupils with physical disabilities in both the main school and the nursery. Ancillary aids and adaptions are made to accommodate the needs of individual children following guidance from specialists. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We fully understand that each child’s transition needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including home visits, settling in sessions, shortened sessions, if appropriate, and transition booklets. We are also happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible, where possible, to meet your child’s needs. For further information on our Transition arrangements please read our Transition policy. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We regularly audit the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and carry out specific training or continuous professional development accordingly. Our SENDCo shares national and local SEND developments. Our resources and facilities are continually reviewed to ensure they meet the needs of all children in the setting.

local_offer: We provide out-of-school childcare for all children attending the Carrington Infant or Carrington Junior Schools.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to ensure all children attending the Carrington Infant or Carrington Junior Schools are able to access our out-of-school services and we adapt our service according to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff undertake regular playwork training and a range of courses on specific topics such as autism, adhd, caring for children with medical conditions, etc. These courses are repeated every 2 to 3 years. We liaise closely with the staff at both the Carrington Schools and join in with school SEND-specific training sessions whenever appropriate to our service. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We will communicate with you on a daily basis when you drop off and collect your child. We will liaise with you about the specific needs of your child and will meet with you for more in-depth discussion as required. General information about our service will be sent out to you by email each term. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? You will have the opportunity to chat to our staff whenever you drop off or collect your child and we will keep you informed about the time your child has spent time with us. We will arrange a meeting with you whenever a more in-depth discussion is required. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The school premises is partially accessible. There is a ramp to our main entrance and most of the facilities we use are on a level surface. Where there are steps to the cloakroom area and the outdoor play area, we would be able to use an alternative route to access these facilities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Any child aged 4 to 11 and attending the Carrington Infant School or Carrington Junior School from Reception class to Year 6 is able to use our service, subject to places being available. Our Registration Form and Booking Form can be obtained from office@ourtimecs.co.uk. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to train staff to meet the needs of all the children. We will also continue to liaise closely with the staff at both the Carrington Schools in order to provide consistent care that is compatible with the support being provided by the schools.

Here at Grasshoppers, you are welcome to speak with any member of staff if you have any concerns about your child, who will in turn relay this information to our SENCO coordinator. Rebecca Powell is our coordinator for special educational needs and disabilities (SENDCO) and is available to help and offer support where needed. She has many years of experience supporting various education, medical and care need of children in our setting. Rebecca is able to gain advice from the early years team, assess and inclusion team, through telephone consultations or with parental permission, specific advice from an early year SEND advisor. Rebecca is able to give advice regarding higher needs funding, SEND support plans and education, health and care plans EHCP. Rebecca liaised with a range of professionals including those from the Early Years team, Speech and Language Therapist and Occupational Therapist (OT) and many more. Rebecca attends the Early Years SENCO Liaison Groups. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO Training initial and advanced. Leading Behaviour Autism PALS Early intervention Makaton Identifying speech and language needs and developing targets How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they are able to approach us about anything relating to their children. We have formal opportunities for contact with parents at our parent's evenings as well as stay-and-play sessions. There are also many informal opportunities in that you will be given verbal feedback on your child’s progress daily. You are always welcome to discuss your child’s progress with your key person or Corinna, or contact us via email or phone. Our online learning journeys are available for you to access at any time using your login and password. On this app, you will be able to see your child's observations, four monthly reports, two-year checks and transition reports. We have a parent involvement section on our curriculum boards for parents to detail their child's interests at home. Parents can also make comments on the parent zone app. Catch-up meetings can also be arranged as and when is needed. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Our staff pride themselves on the detailed learning opportunities feedback that is given at the end of every session. This will enable you to understand what your child has learnt during their day at nursery. Every child has a learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time by accessing the parent zone app. This will show the observations that the key person has made, the child's 2-year-old progress check, reflecting on progress forms and transition forms. For our parents with children that have a SEN, we ensure that we are able to meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. We also share all the reports sent to us from external agencies like speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, physiotherapists and Integrated SEND Service with the parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? As you enter the building there is a ramp leading to the front door, and the entrance hall and reception area is large and spacious. Access to the garden is round the back of the nursery through the gate, where both Astroturf and a grassed area can be accessed by all. We have a disabled toilet on the ground floor and wide doors for easy access to a room. Our nursery consists of four rooms our Ladybird room (under twos room) and Bumble bees room (2 to 3-year-olds) are on the ground floor and our Caterpillar room (under two’s) and preschool room (3 to 5-year-olds) are on the first floor of the house. We have purpose-built toys and equipment at your child’s level and could make necessary changes where required. As a setting, we thoroughly enjoy the sensory-based play. Reasonable adjustments will of course be considered and thought through if a child needed a special requirement depending on their needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If your child has an identified special need before joining our setting, Corinna and Rebecca will liaise with you the parent on how we can best support your child and help them thrive in the setting, feeling happy and secure in our care. Looking into additional training needs for the staff, and specialist equipment required if needed. If the key person felt that your child needed some extra help or support, as when reflecting on their progress it did highlight some specific areas of need, the key person would discuss this with you and Corinna and set clear targets and strategies on how together we can help your child progress and develop confidently. Your child’s key person will have a vital role in assisting Corinna with putting into place targets, planning ahead with activities and assisting with a flexible routine that fits around your child. Open communication between you as parents and us at Grasshoppers is key and vital for the well-being of your child. We have outside agencies in Buckinghamshire that support us within the setting such as Health Visitors, Speech and Language Therapists, Educational Psychologists and Inclusion Coordinators. They all have a vital role in providing us with the correct amount of support and guidance to enable us to provide the very best care and educational opportunities for your child. We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We regularly visit the local schools with children who are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We would like to continue to support our children, staff and parents with any needs they require to the best of our ability. We are an education and care setting that has high standards in the way we keep developing our staff’s knowledge so they can best support the child and their families.

description: Mixed-gender primary school in Great Horwood, Milton Keynes for 3 to 11-year-olds. Great Horwood School is a well-resourced, rural primary school with pupils ranging in age from 3 to 11 years. We cater for children from Nursery through to the end of Year 6 including Wraparound Care as part of our large rural site just ten minutes from both Buckingham and Milton Keynes. name: Aylesbury Sailing Club
description: Aylesbury Sailing Club is run by its members for its members. We have three main types of sailing: Casual sailing (or cruising or messing about in a boat) in beautiful surroundings is therapeutic. On some Saturdays in the summer, there will be a volunteer manning the support boat- so if you are a little unsure- look out for those days on the calendar. Racing - we have a regular racing programme open to Adults and Juniors alike, using single-handed or double-handed boats. The main racing formats that we use are class racing and handicap (also known as ‘points’) racing. We also run a number of fun pursuit races during the season. The official racing season tends to run from April to November, but we also run some informal racing throughout the winter. Youth group: from May to September (with a break for the school summer hols) from 3pm to 5pm, we provide a safe environment for the club’s younger members to practice their skills and enjoy time on the water. We offer support boat cover and activity suggestions. It’s not formal training, but they do learn a lot while having fun. We don’t have any age limits, but activities are geared toward 12 to 14-year-olds and are unlikely to be suitable for those under 9. As this is not formal training it is a requirement that each junior is supervised by a parent/guardian, or someone acting on their behalf.

description: Founded in 1965 Maidenhead Sailing Club has a long tradition of being a friendly family sailing club, over the last couple of years we have also expanded this to offer paddle sports as well. Please note that the fees quoted are the annual fees to be a member from April to March. If you have any questions about other fees, please look at our website or contact the club on the advertised phone number. We are a non-for-profit organisation run by member volunteers, so you can always find a helping hand and a friendly face. We offer sailing and paddling throughout the year and have activities for novices through to experts. So, whether you are looking to relax, race on the water, or enjoy our fantastic facilities from shore we've got something for you. We offer extensive Royal Yachting Association (RYA) training programmes that members can benefit from all year round, for sailing, and powerboating. Sailing is a fantastic way to have fun on the water and inspires confidence, friendship, and teamwork in young people. There are many opportunities for young people aged all the way from 8 to 16 at Maidenhead Sailing Club. If you are looking for a relaxed, social, and friendly club then look no further than Maidenhead Sailing Club. Come down on a Thursday night, Saturday or Sunday morning to learn more about what we can offer at great value for money.

name: Maidenhead Sailing Club
description: Founded in 1965 Maidenhead Sailing Club has a long tradition of being a friendly family sailing club, over the last couple of years we have also expanded this to offer paddle sports as well. Please note that the fees quoted are the annual fees to be a member from April to March. If you have any questions about other fees, please look at our website or contact the club on the advertised phone number. We are a non-for-profit organisation run by member volunteers, so you can always find a helping hand and a friendly face. We offer sailing and paddling throughout the year and have activities for novices through to experts. So, whether you are looking to relax, race on the water, or enjoy our fantastic facilities from shore we've got something for you. We offer extensive Royal Yachting Association (RYA) training programmes that members can benefit from all year round, for sailing, and powerboating. Sailing is a fantastic way to have fun on the water and inspires confidence, friendship, and teamwork in young people. There are many opportunities for young people aged all the way from 8 to 16 at Maidenhead Sailing Club. If you are looking for a relaxed, social, and friendly club then look no further than Maidenhead Sailing Club. Come down on a Thursday night, Saturday or Sunday morning to learn more about what we can offer at great value for money.

local_offer: We are a mainstream school who welcomes all children into a caring, Christian, community where each child matters and is valued for their individuality. We embrace children from all cultures and faiths. Our aim for all pupils, including those with SEND, is to help pupils develop their skills and abilities, as well as their self-esteem and confidence. We place a high emphasis on personalised learning, and differentiate according to the needs of the individual child. https://www.greatkimbleschool.co.uk/special-educational-needs-and-inclusion/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? When deciding whether special educational provision is required, we will start with the desired outcomes, including the expected progress and attainment, and the views and the wishes of the pupil and their parents. We will use this to determine the support that is needed and whether we can provide it by adapting our core offer, or whether something different, or additional, is needed. Our planning is differentiated to enable all learners to achieve their lessons’ learning objectives. Planning and teaching is adapted on a daily basis if needed, to meet your child’s learning needs. Differentiation can occur through variation in questioning; a different activity where the outcome in terms of learning is still the same; a more practical approach, or a change in support resources where learning is scaffolded more clearly. We are keen to ensure that children with SEND are still challenged. Learning Support Assistants (LSA) under the direction of the class teacher can adapt planning to support the needs of your child where necessary. Specific resources and strategies will be used to support your child individually and in groups. At Great Kimble CofE School, we have a number of interventions that are run within the class, outside of the classroom environment. For children with SEND support plans, we will ensure there are suggestions for how you can support your child’s learning (including their interventions) at home. Interventions can be offered at times to every child (SEND and non-SEND) at Great Kimble CofE School to support their learning of key concepts through Keep Up Not Catch Up or PiXL intervention sessions. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENDCO is qualified with the National Award for Special Educational Needs Co-Ordinators and has worked as a class teacher in mainstream settings. The SENDCo’s job is to support staff in planning for children with SEND. We have a team of 4 teaching assistants, including 1 higher level teaching assistant (HLTA) who is trained to deliver SEND provision. Great Kimble CofE School provides training and support to enable all staff to improve the teaching and learning of children, including those with SEND. This includes whole school training on SEND issues, such as Social, Emotional and Mental Health and supportive behaviour management. Individual teachers and support staff also attend training courses run by outside agencies that are relevant to the needs of specific children in their class, for example, ‘Dyslexia Explained’ by Nessy and ‘Sensory Processing’ by Bucks OT Service. There are regular staff meetings and Learning Support Assistants (LSA) and Support Staff meetings on SEND. EHC Plans and Support Plans are accessible to all teachers and learning support assistants detailing how the child can be best supported. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Great Kimble CofE School, we are keen in involve parents and carers as much as possible in their child’s education and welfare. We hold regular meetings and operate an open-door policy. If you wish to speak to the class teacher, SENDCo, or Headteacher more formally, we are happy to arrange an appointment at a time convenient to you. We ensure all paperwork is kept up to date and copies of reports from outside agencies are sent home. We also send out annual questionnaires to parents of children with SEND to gain feedback and to adapt and improve our services to ensure they are the best we can provide. Our school website is updated to support pupils, parents, and carers. We are also keen to signpost parents and carers to other support agencies such as childcare for children with SEND, Short Breaks for Carers, and Mental Health Services all of which can be accessed through the Buckinghamshire Council Local Offer. Links to further useful websites can be found on the school website. We will also notify parents/carers of useful services, courses, and opportunities through email and our school newsletter. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We hold 2 termly parents’ evenings with the added opportunity for an additional meeting with the SENDCo if needed. If you child is on the SEND register, each term you will have an additional meeting time with your child’s class teacher and SENDCO to discuss their support plan. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We make the following adaptations to ensure all pupils’ needs are met: - Differentiating our curriculum to ensure all pupils can access learning opportunities, for example, by grouping, 1:1 work, teaching style, content of the lesson, and so on. - Adapting our resources and staffing - Using recommended aids, such as laptops, coloured overlays, visual timetables, larger font, and so on. - Differentiating our teaching, for example, giving longer processing times, pre-teaching of key vocabulary, reading instructions aloud, and so on The school is fully compliant with Disability Discrimination Act (DDA) requirements. The school’s learning spaces are at ground level with easy access with ramps or gradual slopes to most areas (exception is Fire Class outdoor area space steps to the tarmac playground). Please refer to our School Accessibility Plan on our school website for more information through the ‘SEN, Equality, Diversity and Cohesion’ section. There are two disabled toilets with changing areas on site. We ensure, wherever possible, that equipment used is accessible to all children regardless of their needs. All areas of the school are accessible via a wheelchair. Extracurricular activities are accessible for children with SEND. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Buckinghamshire Council admissions. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are planning to develop further outdoor sensory spaces and introduce a dedicated ELSA (Emotional Learning Support Assistant) space.

description: Milton Keynes Canoe Club (MKCC) is a recreational club based at Caldecotte Lake in Milton Keynes. The club offers members a wide range of courses and workshops throughout the year in canoe, kayak and SUP. The club also offers a Junior Club during the summer months for 8 to 14-year-olds. An extensive range of trips and paddles are on offer too, both locally and further afield. You don't need any prior experience to join the Club and you don't need your own equipment either - plenty is available to borrow. During the year the club also offers introductory canoe, kayak and SUP sessions for members of the public. We are a friendly, welcoming club which is committed to inclusion. The club is managed by a committee of volunteers and is affiliated to Paddle UK and we are recognised as a Paddle UK Quality Club.

local_offer: I have been a childminder since 1994. I work from my daughters home which is a warm, safe, friendly environment where children can play and learn. We have a playroom with lots of toys and resources to encourage children's learning and development.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a registered childminder I have a key contact in the Early Years team at Buckinghamshire Council, whom I am able to access advice and information from. I will undergo further training when required. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I will attend training and seek support to help me to care for children with special needs and also work closely with other providers and parents. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All parents are asked to share relevant information about their child with me. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I encourage families to visit with their children and offer a settling in period before the children are due to start. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I will keep up to date with training and SEND information through the local authority and my key contact.

We recognise a continuum of special needs: any child may experience a special need at any stage of their education and for short or extended periods of time. Our aim is to raise the expectations and achievements of all children. We recognise that responsibility for SEND is a whole-school issue and lies collectively with all staff, supported by the SENCO and the Leadership Team. local_offer: Great Missenden Church of England Combined School is committed to providing Challenge For All pupils in order to ensure that every pupil, including those with SEND, achieves their full potential. We believe all children have individual needs, strengths and talents which should be met through a challenging, enjoyable and enriched curriculum which provides opportunities for all children to work at their own level and pace. We recognise that many children may require additional support or additional challenge at some point within their learning journey.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We believe that all children should be equally valued in school. We strive to remove any barriers to learning which could hinder or exclude individual pupils with SEND. We believe all children should have the opportunity to flourish and feel safe. We support the development of the whole child, whilst valuing and celebrating the many and varied abilities displayed by all children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff receive training opportunities in relation to their personal needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Appointments can be made with the class teacher or Inclusion Manager to discuss individual pupils in detail at any time during the school year How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Termly progress meetings identify all children’s current level of attainment and the amount of progress they are making. Pupils with SEND can be identified if limited progress is being made or if progress differs significantly in one specific area of the curriculum. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We plan accordingly to every child’s individual learning and developmental needs, with a focus on the characteristics of effective learning. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: Hogshaw Farm and Wildlife Park
description: Experience the best of British farming and the countryside in a fun-filled family day out. Get hands-on with our rare breeds, come face-to-face with wildlife, explore the nature trails and go wild in our adventure play areas, whatever the weather. Hogshaw Farm and Wildlife Park is an environmentally friendly rare breeds farm attraction, located in 44 acres of beautiful, wide-open countryside in North Buckinghamshire. There is plenty of space to relax, to build memories and enjoy the freedom to explore. • Daily animal encounter and activity programme • Animal Barn • Pets Corner • Wildlife Zone, with optional bird display • Pygmy Goat Walkthrough • Seasonal events • Two indoor play barns • Outdoor adventure play, bouncy pillows and pedal go-karts • Nature trail There's fresh homemade food in the Farm Kitchen that's supplied by local producers and from our own walled garden, where we grow heritage fruit and vegetables. At the entrance to the farm, we also have a Farm Shop and Café, open to all. We are a dog-friendly site and welcome cyclists and walkers too. We offer: • Day visits and Annual passes • Group discounts for schools and community groups • Seasonal events and workshops • Children’s birthday parties • Room hire for corporate events and special occasions Opening hours: • Term time: Wednesday to Sunday, 10am to 5:30pm (Open for school visits and corporate functions on Mondays and Tuesdays) • School holidays: Every day, 10am to 5:30pm Pre-book tickets by visiting our website.
organisation: Hogshaw Farm and Wildlife Park An environmentally friendly 44 acre rare breeds farm attraction in Aylesbury Vale for all ages. Located in beautiful open countryside where there is plenty of space for children to play and explore outdoors and indoors. As well as special seasonal events, the Animal Barn, Pets Corner and Wildlife Zone, we have a daily programme which children will love. They also have the chance to let off steam inside the two indoor play barns, or outside where there is plenty of play equipment and a nature trail. There's fresh homemade food in the Eco Centre Cafe and Barn Cafe that's supplied by local producers and from our own walled garden, where we grow heritage fruit and vegetables. The restaurant is on the ground floor of our lovely timber-framed building, whilst on the first floor with stunning views is our purpose built conference/party room available for hire. We have 'Farmer for a Day', 'Ranger for a Day' and 'Animal Experiences' available for all ages. info@greendragonecofarm.co.uk https://www.greendragonecofarm.co.uk//

local_offer: At Green Ridge, we believe that each pupil has individual and unique needs. However, we know that some pupils may require more support than others to achieve well. We acknowledge that a significant proportion of pupils will have Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEN/D) at some time in their school career. Many of these pupils may require help throughout their time in school, while others may need a little extra support for a short period of time to help them overcome more temporary needs. If these pupils are to achieve their full potential, we must recognise this and plan accordingly. Our school aims to provide all pupils with strategies for dealing with their needs in a supportive environment, and to give them meaningful access to the National Curriculum. In particular, we aim to: - enable every pupil to experience success; - promote individual confidence and a positive attitude; - ensure that all pupils, whatever their special educational needs, receive appropriate educational provision through a broad and balanced curriculum that is relevant and differentiated, and that demonstrates coherence and progression in learning; - ensure that all pupils with a special education need or disability make progress which is at least in line with the national expectation; - give pupils with SEN/D equal opportunities to take part in all aspects of the school’s provision, as far as is appropriate; - ensure that children with SEN/D have opportunities to receive and make known information, to express an opinion, and have that opinion taken into account in any matters affecting; them; - identify, assess, record and regularly review pupils’ progress and needs; - involve parents/carers in planning and supporting at all stages of their children’s development; - work collaboratively with parents, other professionals and support services; and - ensure that the responsibility held by all staff and governors for SEN/D is implemented and maintained. https://www.greenridgeacademy.co.uk/policies/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our setting aims to provide an inclusive, supportive environment where children and young people with SEND can thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. We strive to ensure access to a broad and balanced curriculum tailored to individual needs, while promoting high expectations and progress for every learner. Beyond academic achievement, we focus on building confidence, resilience, and independence, encouraging positive relationships and participation in all aspects of school life. We work in close partnership with families, offering clear communication, guidance, and opportunities to be actively involved in their child’s education. Our approach also prepares pupils for life beyond school by developing essential life skills, supporting smooth transitions, and fostering self-advocacy. Through staff training and reasonable adjustments, we maintain an inclusive environment that celebrates diversity and ensures every child feels valued and supported. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Teachers and teaching assistants take part in weekly professional development sessions to continually enhance their skills and knowledge. A number of these sessions focus specifically on strategies to support children with SEND. Topics covered include: Attention Autism, Zones of Regulation, Therapeutic Approaches, Sensory Processing, Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA), the Escalation Curve, Attachment and Trauma, and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). These training opportunities ensure staff are equipped to provide high-quality, inclusive support tailored to individual needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Green Ridge, we operate an open-door policy, welcoming parents to contact the school office to arrange a meeting with the SENCo and/or their child’s class teacher to discuss any concerns. Parents also have online access to their child’s Learning Plans, which are updated termly to ensure transparency and collaboration. In addition, we host termly SEND Coffee Mornings where parents and carers can meet with staff and hear from Local Authority specialists who share their expertise. We also offer ‘Stay and Learn’ sessions, inviting parents into the classroom to observe and participate in their child’s learning. To further support families, we provide practical workshops designed to help parents address challenges they may face at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Most children with SEND have a Learning Plan that outlines their individual strengths and areas of difficulty, along with short-term SMART targets to support their progress. These plans are reviewed termly by the class teacher and shared with parents via our secure online platform. For children with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), we hold an Annual Review meeting to update the plan, celebrate achievements, and set new goals in collaboration with parents and professionals. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? name: The Green Room School (Berkshire)
description: Mixed-gender independent secondary school and sixth form in Windsor, Berkshire for 11 to 25-year-olds. The Green Room Foundation runs schools in Windsor, Berkshire (GRW) and Kingsley, Hampshire (GRK) for young people who can no longer access mainstream education. We also run a Sixth Form that is designed to help pupils continue on their path to adulthood. Many of the pupils have already attended The Green Room School, and this extra time helps to prepare them for post 16 education or work. Pupils who have graduated from GR6 can progress to The Graduate Scheme. The scheme aims to assist pupils to bridge the gap between leaving school and the world of work with a bespoke programme of preparation and experience. Both GR6 and Graduate Scheme pupils are based at The Swan Pub in Windsor. The Swan provides a unique setting for pupils to continue their education, gain useful skills and become part of their community. The environment will be safe and nurturing but also provide opportunities for challenge and change.

local_offer: Fostering children's unique strengths and weaknesses is our main aim. Our Workshop Department supports all children with a range of learning differences, enabling them to access the curriculum to ensure they reach their potential, to allow them to thrive. This includes enhancing the learning of our more able children through distinct and discernibly different personalised learning opportunities which enables our more able pupils to work at higher cognitive levels. They will be given opportunities to develop specific skills or talents and strategies to heighten motivation and reach their full potential. Discussions will be held with our specialist support staff, class teachers and parents to ascertain any area of difficulty and what support will be given. Many children will have a Pupil Passport which indicates strengths and weaknesses and any support strategies in place in the workshop and in the classroom. We have a dedicated, resource filled room where many children can enjoy the warm and nurturing environment that our specialist staff promote. We offer literacy and numeracy support, organisational skills, typing skills, Zones Of Regulation for developing the ability to understand emotion and feelings, and study and thinking skills.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to help children achieve what they are capable of despite any difficulties they might have and to develop their understanding of themselves and the world around them in order to be best prepared for their future and the move to Secondary school. We also work with Gifted and Talented students and are keen to offer them further differentiated work to encourage their development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved every step of the way, including regular meetings and telephone conversations as well as strategies and work for home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? SEND children will have a Pupil Passport which outlines their strengths and difficulties and the strategies we will use to support them at school. We also work closely with outside agencies and with County. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact the office and we will be delighted to show you around the school at your convenience. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue building up our resources and aim to carry out and facilitate more specific assessments on sight.

local_offer: The school considers a pupil as having SEND if they have a learning difficulty or disability, which calls for special educational provision to be made for them. Children have a learning difficulty if they have: • A significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of pupils of the same age. • A disability, which prevents or hinders them from making use of facilities provided for their peer group in mainstream schools. Special educational provision is educational provision that is additional to, or different from, that made generally for other children of the same age in school. Needs can be categorised in four key areas, as detailed in the SEND Code of Practice 2015: • Communication and interaction, autistic spectrum and speech, language and communication needs • Cognition and learning dyslexia, dyspraxia and dyscalculia, moderate learning difficulties and global development delay • Social, emotional and mental health difficulties, ADHD, ADD, attachment disorders, emotional difficulties, mental health difficulties• Sensory and/or physical needs, hearing or vision impaired, multisensory impairment, physical disability Some pupils may have difficulties in more than one of these four categories. The school aims to: • Work closely with parents and pupils to take into account their views and aspirations and the families’ experience of, and hopes for their child. • Invite families to be involved at every stage of planning and reviewing of the SEND provision for their child. • Ensure that pupils benefit from ‘Quality First Teaching’: teachers assess, plan and teach all pupils to allow them to progress their learning. The school implements focused interventions to target particular skills. • Have high expectations for all pupils. local_offer: The school employs a full time SENCo, known as the Head of Learning Success. The role of Early Years SENCo (EYSENCo) is fulfilled by a member of EYFS teaching staff. The EYSENCo oversees SEND provision for Nursery, Kindergarten and Reception pupils. This role is combined with a class teaching commitment. As of September 2024, staffing for the Learning Success Department also includes two full-time Learning Success Assistants (LSAs), five part-time LSAs, one Pastoral Support Assistant (PSA), four parttime 1:1 Learning Support Assistants who are responsible for the support of pupils with high needs, for whom the school receives additional funding through Education Health & Care (EHC) Plans, and two part time SEN administrators. Our guiding principle is one of inclusion and every child is entitled to have their needs identified and barriers addressed. We recognise that all teachers are teachers of children with SEND and that all children are entitled to access a broad and balanced curriculum. The school is committed to fostering high aspirations and expectations for young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), aiming to deliver an education that empowers them to reach their full potential, develop confidence, lead fulfilling lives, and smoothly transition to their senior schools. As an inclusive school, we believe that every child is unique and brings their own strengths, experiences, and qualities. We aim to meet the needs of all children, including our children with special educational needs and disabilities, through a rich and varied academic and social curriculum. The school is dedicated to helping pupils with SEND reach their full potential by implementing a whole school approach to learning support. This approach includes a tiered programme that offers in-class adaptions, small-group interventions, and one-on-one support, all of which are integrated with the broader school curriculum. All pupils at Beachborough work within mainstream classes with access to a wide-ranging curriculum. local_offer: At Bee Happy Preschool, our teachers are dedicated to supporting all children, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). We provide a nurturing and inclusive environment, tailored to meet each child's individual needs, ensuring they thrive and develop at their own pace. Our approach focuses on creating a supportive atmosphere where every child feels valued and included.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Promote Inclusion and Independence: We create a supportive, inclusive environment where every child can engage in activities alongside their peers, fostering independence and confidence. Individualized Support: We tailor our approach to meet the unique needs of each child, ensuring they receive the appropriate resources and care to reach their full potential. Skill Development: Through Montessori principles and EYFS standards, we encourage the development of key skills—social, emotional, physical, and cognitive—at each child’s own pace. Strong Partnerships with Families: We work closely with families to provide guidance, regular updates, and involve them in decision-making to ensure the best outcomes for their child. Holistic Growth: Our goal is to nurture children’s overall well-being, ensuring they feel valued, safe, and supported in their learning journey, both in the classroom and through outdoor activities. Smooth Transitions: We help prepare children for their next steps, whether progressing in preschool or transitioning to primary school, ensuring they feel ready and supported. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO training (for new and aspiring SENCOs)- two-day training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Regular Communication: We keep parents informed through daily updates, progress reports, and regular meetings to discuss your child's development and any specific needs. Open-Door Policy: Parents are always welcome to visit the preschool, observe their child’s activities, and meet with staff to discuss any concerns or suggestions. Collaborative Planning: We involve parents in creating individualized learning plans, particularly for children with SEND, ensuring that your input and goals for your child are integrated into our approach. Workshops and Meetings: We offer workshops, information sessions, and parent meetings to share strategies for supporting your child’s learning and development at home. Volunteering Opportunities: Parents are encouraged to participate in events, trips (such as woodland school trips), and classroom activities, giving you a chance to engage directly with the preschool community. Feedback and Suggestions: We value parent feedback and regularly seek your input on how we can improve our services and support your child’s needs more effectively. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Regular Progress Updates: We provide regular updates through daily reports, parent-teacher meetings, and written progress reviews, covering your child's development across different areas. Personal Meetings: For children with SEND, we offer more frequent, in-depth meetings to discuss their progress, review any tailored strategies, and adjust support as needed. Communication Channels: We maintain open communication through emails, phone calls, or face-to-face meetings, especially if there are any significant developments or concerns regarding your child’s progress. Observation Reports: Detailed observation reports highlight key milestones and developmental progress, with special attention to areas where additional support may be needed for children with SEND. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Indoor Accessibility: Our classrooms are designed with ample space for movement, making it easy for children with mobility aids to navigate. Furniture is arranged to allow flexibility and easy access to learning materials. We also use visual aids and sensory resources to support different learning needs. Outdoor Accessibility: Our outdoor learning area is designed to be accessible to all children. Pathways are clear and stable, ensuring easy access for children with mobility challenges. The space includes sensory and nature-based activities that cater to a variety of abilities. Adaptations: We can make additional adjustments to meet specific needs, such as ramps, modified seating, or sensory tools, ensuring every child can participate fully in all activities. Inclusive Facilities: Our preschool is equipped with accessible toilets and changing facilities, designed to accommodate children with varying physical needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Initial Inquiry: Families can contact us directly via phone or email to express interest in enrolling their child. We welcome any questions or concerns about how we can support your child's specific needs. Tour and Consultation: We invite families to visit our preschool, meet our staff, and explore our environment. During the visit, we can discuss your child's needs, explain our support services, and answer any questions about SEND provisions. Assessment of Needs: For children with SEND, we will work closely with you to understand your child’s specific requirements, including health, educational, or developmental needs. This may involve consultations with external professionals, such as therapists, if applicable. Settling-In Sessions: To help your child adjust, we offer settling-in sessions, where they can explore the environment and get familiar with our staff and routine at their own pace. Ongoing Communication: Once your child is enrolled, we maintain open and regular communication with families to ensure the best possible support, making any necessary adjustments to the care plan as your child progresses. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Ongoing Staff Training: We will provide regular professional development for our staff to stay updated on the latest SEND strategies, techniques, and best practices, ensuring they are well-equipped to support a range of needs. Specialist Support Services: We aim to strengthen our partnerships with external specialists, such as speech therapists, occupational therapists, and educational psychologists, to provide more tailored interventions for children who need additional support. Enhanced Resources: We plan to expand our range of sensory and adaptive learning resources, ensuring that we have a variety of tools to engage children with different learning styles and needs. Monitoring and Feedback: We will develop a robust feedback system to regularly review our SEND provision, ensuring that we adapt our services based on the needs and feedback from families, children, and external specialists.

local_offer: As a fully qualified early years teacher I have experience of working with a wide range of SEND needs including autism, cerebral palsy and I have worked with number of children with cognitive, social, emotional and communication difficulties. A close relationship with families is vital to ensure that I can offer a nurturing and inclusive environment where all children are able to thrive with the right support from other professionals and outside agencies. Children will learn through play and exploration in our setting and children's needs will be carefully considered when activities are being planned to ensure accessibility and enjoyment for all.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to provide an environment where families feel supported children are given the right scaffolds and support to be able to reach their full potential in a caring and inclusive setting. The needs of the child are considered at every opportunity and I will work closely with involved professionals to help children access all parts of the provision and will take part in any training required and work to make adaptations to the setting where recommended. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? January 2021 - Place to be Mental Health Champions Foundation Programme. October 2022 - Autism training January 2023 - Dyslexia training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents know their children best and I build close relationships with my parents so that we can provide the best support for their child to thrive. I encourage them to share information about what their child enjoys, what they may find difficult, what they like or dislike and what provides comfort for them. I share information about the children's day, what they have learned, their progress and any areas for development and provide additional activity ideas at home to help children work on particular skills. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I will observe and assess all children when they begin at the setting, and will provide an action plan for any children with a particular need which will be compiled with the parents and may involve outside agencies with the parents permission. I am open in how I communicate with parents of children with SEND, for example, in person, on the phone, text message or WhatsApp, email or providing a communication book. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is accessible to most children and families. The front door, hallway and doors within the house are wide enough to accommodate a wheelchair. We would work with parents to ensure that the rooms work for accessibility with their child's individual needs. The garden has a small patio and the rest is grass and gravel with a slight incline. The patio doors to the garden has a large step, however, again we would work with parents to ensure we can make the garden safely accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I welcome visits so we can meet before making a decision and I am happy to answer any questions parents may have. I also provide a welcome booklet that has most information about our setting. When children register with us, parents are asked to provide information that helps me to get to know their child and they are welcome to provide any comforters or any belongings which may support their child with settling. I also encourage settling in sessions before the child's start date. I am more than happy to support with transitions to and from our setting and welcome visits from children's current or future providers. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I aim to keep up to date with all the new guidance from the local authority and access training where necessary and would like to build on my existing learning and awareness of children's mental health. I also plan to remove the gravel in the garden and add more grass to improve accessibility.

name: Guide Dogs Children's Services
description: Guide Dogs Children's Services. Our experts can help you to live actively and independently with sight loss. Whether you’re asking for yourself, a member of your family, or your child, speak to someone from our friendly team today for more information. Family support Our team is here to give advice and emotional support from the moment your child is diagnosed with a vision impairment. Our experts can share their experience to build your whole family’s knowledge and confidence and provide tools that are right for your child’s specific needs. Education support Our specialist team can offer independent and tailored advice to help your child receive the educational support they are entitled to. From supporting you when you are choosing the right nursery, school or college, to working with teachers and special education staff or advising on assistive technologies. Technology grants and sensory toys For children with sight loss, technology and sensory play is vital. Our expert team can provide personalised advice to help you choose the right technology or sensory toys for your child’s age and stage. We can offer grants to help buy the specialist technology or sensory equipment your child needs. We also have a range of sensory packages with toys carefully selected by our experts for different age ranges. My life skills We’re here to help your child learn invaluable practical skills for life. From supporting physical development and learning in the early years, to navigating streets safely, preparing food, handling money, using technology and managing their appearance they grow older. My time to play My Time to Play helps children aged 0 to 4 years with a vision impairment develop through play and provides parents with the opportunity to network, share experiences and pick up skills and knowledge to support their child’s development with confidence. CustomEyes books CustomEyes Books are for everyone aged 0 to 25 years with a vision impairment, or dyslexia. Whatever reading format your child needs, we’ll tailor their books to meet their individual requirements; font type and size, line spacing, paper colour and more. What’s more, if the book they want isn’t already on our catalogue of over 4,200 titles, we’ll do our best to add it. All books are available at the recommended retail price, regardless of format. Family events Guide Dogs family events are a great day out where your family can relax and have fun together and meet other families with similar stories. They allow children with a vision impairment to build confidence and make lifelong friends. Buddy dogs Our buddy dogs bring a new friend into the lives of children with sight loss. By helping to develop their self-confidence, improve relationships and build a greater sense of trust, these dogs can have a hugely positive effect on your child’s wellbeing and your family, too. Call us to sign up for a Discovery Session.

Technology advice service, including grants Our grants help cover the cost of sensory equipment and assistive technology (also called access or adaptive technology), which can empower children, helping them become independent learners through apps and games. We can also offer advice on technology and software that can help children and young people access information and online resources on their own. Early diagnosis family support Our specialist team can offer information, advice and guidance from the early stages following diagnosis. Further help can include health and welfare advice, practical and emotional support and signposting to other organisations and services. Family Events Every year we host a UK-wide programme of family activity days. Here your child and their siblings can play and take part in activities together – alongside other children with sight loss. Meanwhile, parents can share experiences, support each other and access specialist advice from our team. We also host an early diagnosis weekend to support families at this critical time. Life skills We’re here to help your child learn and practise tasks that are important to daily life, confidently and safely. We support children and young people of all ages. From supporting physical development and learning in the early years, to navigating streets safely, preparing food, handling money, using technology and managing their appearance as they grow older. This training programme (also known as habilitation) will give your child invaluable practical skills for life. We also offer tailored courses for children with additional and complex needs: these include early motor skills, sensory development, body awareness and wheelchair mobility. Guide dogs for children and young people A guide dog could give your child the confidence to get out and about safely. Whether it’s to go to school or college, to a regular exercise class or to meet up with friends, they provide life-changing practical support every single day. Buddy dogs Our buddy dogs bring a canine friend into the lives of children with sight loss. By helping to build your child’s confidence in themselves and trust in their surroundings, these dogs have a positive effect on your whole family’s wellbeing. children@guidedogs.org.uk http://www.guidedogs.org.uk
