local_offer: Gumboots and Roots Pre-school Ltd is a privately owned pre-school that cares for up to 22 children per session. Children are aged 2-5 years old. We welcome all children and families and endeavour to adjust to meet all children’s needs as much as possible. We are a small setting and pride ourselves on our personal/welcoming approach. We aim to build positive relationships with all children and families and focus on establishing good parent/carer relationships.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our SENCO Kerry Lewis-Smith attends the termly Local Authority SENCO Liaison Groups. The setting has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child-specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor. We are happy for professionals involved with the child to visit and welcome this opportunity to develop our knowledge, we feel this is very important for all professionals to be working together. We will attend any Multi-Professional Meetings where necessary. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Proprietor: Safeguarding for Designated officer Sep 2020, Autism Education Training Nov 2020 Manager: Safeguarding for Designated officer Sep 2020 Deputy manager: Safeguarding for all Jan 2021, making sense of Autism Sep 2019 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they are able to approach us about anything relating to their children. Parents have access to our online record system and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents are given feedback daily about their child’s day and can request a meeting with their child’s Key Person if they would like. We also have termly parents’ meetings where you will receive an update on your child’s progress and have the opportunity to discuss their likes, dislikes, achievements and any concerns you may have. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents/carers but in addition to this, we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND. We also offer updates through daily feedback, email or phone calls. We will regularly monitor the short-term outcomes for children with SEND and would encourage parents to have input. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor environment is open and spacious with lots of natural light. We aim to keep our indoor environment calm and as natural as possible to ensure children are not overstimulated by their surroundings. This allows for an enabling environment for children to learn in. We have a large outdoor space with a variety of areas for the children to explore. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have a flexible approach to transitioning children into our setting and will adapt the settling in sessions to the individual child as best we can. We encourage parents to share information from previous settings and to fill in our ‘All about me forms’ to give us the best starting point. As we are a new setting, we are in the process of establishing relationships with the local schools to be able to support children when they are transferring. We work with schools to arrange sharing of information (with parents’ consent) to allow their transition to be as smooth as possible. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently making plans and gathering resources to be able to create a sensory area in our small side room. This room will also be used for small group activities/ one-to-one etc.

local_offer: Learning Support At Thorpe House School we recognise that our pupils may need some support for their learning at some point in their time with us. We are passionate about the importance of recognising, supporting, and celebrating the strengths and Individual abilities of each pupil. We are proud of what we offer and do our very best to enable all pupils to achieve their potential in all aspects of school life. We cater for mild needs also collaborating with external agencies including speech therapists, occupational therapists, and educational psychologists as appropriate. We are able to provide individualised support as we are a small school and know all of our boys very well. We strongly believe that all teachers are teachers of SEND and the Learning Support department works in close partnership with all members of staff. Important information relating to how pupils learn best and areas they find challenging are discussed regularly in staff meetings Our Learning Support Department consists of an experienced team of specialist staff who deliver regular training and provide strategies and techniques, for pupils and staff, to support and enable learning within the curriculum. In some cases we offer additional learning support in the class. Additional learning support is accessed through our dedicated Learning Support Base, a space for pupils and staff to use for small group sessions and 1:1 interventions. We have an additional base in the Lower School. We believe that communication is vital. We work in partnership with the pupil, their parents, and their teachers. We aim to help boys overcome any barriers to learning and achievement, and support all teaching staff to put in place effective measures to help boys achieve their personal best. We are encouraging, non-judgemental, patient, and easy to talk to, and we make sure that our parents are supported too, with clear communication, collaborative involvement, and continual acknowledgement of their son's progress. The Admissions Process We can support a limited number of children with mild learning difficulties each year. During the application process, we will ask you for additional information about any known or suspected difficulties or diagnoses relating to your child’s health, wellbeing, or learning abilities – such as a formal Educational Psychologist, Medical or Specialist Teacher’s report – and will seek an informal conversation with your child’s current school. This information will help us see if we could reasonably meet your child’s needs so that they can benefit from everything the school has to offer and be able to contribute in full to the life of the school. description: Gymnastics and trampolining club for children and young people aged 4 to 16, based around Marlow and High Wycombe, running club sessions at Hazlemere Youth Centre on a Wednesday and Thursday after school. As a club our focus is providing a safe and fun environment for children and young people of all ages to develop their gymnastics and trampolining skills, improve their agility, balance, and coordination, and make new friends. We also focus on the development of coaching and leadership skills for our volunteers and coaches of all ages, and specialize in introducing young people to coaching. Springbucks Gymnastics Club was started in September 2009, working together with the local schools sports partnership to provide affordable and sustainable gymnastics around the South Bucks, and is run by Head Coach Ruth Middleton, along with a team of paid coaches and parent volunteers. We are affiliated and compete annually with UK Gymnastics, who provide full insurance cover for all our coaches and every child who is a member of the club, and in 2012 we were accredited the Wycombe Sports Mark by Wycombe District Council.

name: Autism Acceptance- 6 Week Online Course
description: Spectrum Gaming has a huge focus on advocacy - ensuring autistic young people's voices are heard, and one way we are aiming to do this is by offering in-depth autism training, focused on the lived experience of autistic young people. This training is co-produced with autistic young people, and delivered by autistic adults, or young people themselves, with the focus on helping professionals, parents/carers and more improve their understanding of autism. The training is focused on some key areas that are often misunderstood: - Knowing what autism actually is - Trauma - Anxiety - Understanding meltdown - Motivation and behaviour - Improving wellbeing The sessions focus on bringing together both theory, and authentic lived experience of autistic young people who are often unheard. This training will not be like any training you have attended before and will challenge a lot of what you think you may know about autism. But it is also filled with content and resources so you won't just hear theory and lived experience, but will also be able to take away practical solutions to challenges you may currently be experiencing. There are 6 training sessions and buying a ticket through the booking page below gives you access to all 6 sessions. All sessions run from 7 pm to 9 pm. Find more details about what the training entails on our website below and when the next cohort will run.

local_offer: The type of SEND provision that Haddenham Community Junior school provides is in a mainstream environment. It is on an individual needs basis and includes: - Literacy interventions/support, - Numeracy interventions/support, - Dyslexia interventions, - Emotional, social and mental health support. The school's Accessibility policy can be requested at the school office. The school’s approach to identifying and assessing pupils with SEND (including pupils who do and do not have an EHC Plan) is: - Concerns raised by parents/carers, teachers, other professionals or the child - Information from feeder schools - Limited progress being made - Low scores in termly spelling and reading tests (GL Assessment) - A change in the pupil’s behaviour or progress Evaluating the effectiveness of its provision for pupils with SEND Assessing and reviewing the progress with SEND: A pupil’s support will be detailed on an SEN Support Plan which will state the desired short term outcome and how progress will be monitored and assessed. This will be shared with parents/carers each term. The effectiveness of additional support will be monitored regularly through the school’s planned programme of termly SEND review days and decisions will then be taken about the future actions that may be taken to meet a pupil’s needs. These may be: - To reduce the amount of support - To continue with the existing level of support with new targets being set - To increase the level of intervention or change the intervention if there has been little progress The school’s approach for teaching pupils with SEND (including pupils who do and do not have an EHC Plan) is: - Our teachers are teachers for all pupils, including those with SEND. We ensure that all pupils are equally valued by having equal access to a broad and balanced curriculum which is differentiated to meet individual needs and abilities. This is achieved through Quality First teaching, which includes the use of ordinarily available provision, effective differentiation and monitoring of all pupils. - Risk assessments are carried out and procedures put in place to enable all pupils to participate in all activities provided by the school. - Teachers and Learning Support Assistants (LSAs) are given training on strategies to use in the classroom with students who have specific needs. - Emotional, social and mental health development is supported through various avenues including social groups. Some pupils may require more targeted support which is offered through the Pupil Referral Unit (PRU) and sometimes the Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS). The school’s facilities: Haddenham Community Junior School is Disability Discrimination Act (DDA) compliant. The school’s training in relation to pupils with SEND: All our class teachers have qualified teacher status. The school has a yearly plan of Continual Professional Development (CPD) to ensure all staff are kept up-to-date with issues relating to SEND. This may include training through: - Staff meetings - In-Service Training Days (INSET) - Compulsory training such as Health and Safety or Child Protection - Participation in training courses organised and run by external agencies At times it may be necessary to refer some pupils to outside agencies for their more specialized expertise. These may include from Buckinghamshire Council: - Educational Psychologists - Family Resilience - First Response - Social Care - Child Protection Services - Pupil Referral Unit - CAMHS - CAHBS From the Aylesbury integrated SEND team: - The Specialist Teaching Service including the Cognition and Learning Team - Occupational Therapists - Speech and Language Therapists - Physiotherapists - School nurse - Community Paediatrics - CAMHS The school’s arrangements to consult with and involve: Parents/carers of pupils with SEND via: - Meetings with school staff including class teachers, LSAs and SENDCo throughout the year to discuss the current provision, evaluate its impact and discuss any referrals that may be required. - Home/School Liaison books provide a daily link for feedback where necessary - SEN Support Plans are shared with parents/ carers and their views incorporated - The discussion of reports from outside agencies, for example, Speech and Language Therapists - School website The pupils about their education via: - Discussions with the pupil about what would help them in school with their learning - Invitation to participate in their Annual Review and the completion of a pupil comment sheet - School Council The school’s partnerships: The school's governing body involve other bodies to meet the needs of pupils with SEND and their families by using a range of outside agencies: See Point 5 The school’s transition arrangements: We recognise that transition is an important time for all pupils but especially for a child with SEND. We work closely with parents/carers, pupils and staff to ensure these transitions run as smoothly as possible. Transition within the school from one year group to the next takes place towards the end of the summer term it includes: - Additional visits for SEND pupils to their next classroom, teacher and LSA. - A photo book to take home made showing staff and key places in the next class. - A passport is created with the pupil for the staff indicating how they learn best and their interests. - A folder containing up-to-date SEND history and SEN Support Plans are passed to the next teacher. From one setting to another, for example, junior school to secondary: - Meetings are undertaken between staff of both settings to discuss SEND needs of the transferring pupils. - Opportunities for parent liaison are supported - Participation in planned transition activities with our local secondary schools - Additional visits to the next setting, sometimes accompanied by HCJS LSAs. - Provision of an up-to-date SEND history and SEN Support Plans - Assessment records - A passport is created with the pupil for the staff indicating how they learn best and their interests. - A photo book is made showing key staff and key places in the next setting for the pupils to take home. The school communicates the contact details for the support listed above to pupils with SEND and their families by: - School prospectus - School website https://www.haddenhamjun.co.uk/website - Parent consultation evenings - Annual Reviews - Termly SEN Support Plan reviews - 1:1 discussions - Parental permission forms for outside agency involvement https://www.haddenhamjun.co.uk/website/send/523423 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? description: South Bucks Down's Syndrome Group (SBDSG) runs the Beat It! Music and Movement Group monthly. Venue has changed and dates vary– attendance is for SBDSG members only once they contacted us This group is for our primary school members (aged from 4 to 13). Provided by Curly Cath from CreateED, the sessions engage children in high-quality ensemble sessions that challenge, develop, and progress musical, social, and personal skills for life. Music sessions are broken down into six key areas: - Understanding Musical Differences (using percussive instruments and performance opportunities) - Playing together tuned instruments (creating melodies using ukuleles, chime bars, handbells, and more) - Movement- Exploring musical differences (using sensory props) - Rhythm (Simple rhythm, beats, and performance opportunities) - Songwriting (led by the children) - Listening (tuning in and sharing thoughts) Every month the musical differences are changed and the children use a variety of instruments to enable them to listen, respond, and feel the differences, including: - Allegro and Lento- Fast and Slow - Pitch- High and Low - Dynamics- Loud (forte) and Quiet (piano) - Crescendo and Decrescendo- Increasing and decreasing sound - Major and Minor- Happy and Sad music - Rhythm versus Beat Please contact us below to find out more and to express interest in attending.

name: Haddenham St Mary's Church of England School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Haddenham, Aylesbury for 4 to 7-year-olds. Haddenham St Mary's Church of England School, founded in 1868, provides education for all children aged between 4 and 7 within a Christian ethos. With highly qualified teachers and a nominal roll of 180 children in three "year groups", class sizes are generally of 30 or under. Overlooking open fields at the southern end of the village and next to St Mary's Church, the school aims to create a challenging, yet supportive, environment, within which a broad and balanced curriculum is adapted to the individual needs of each child. All children are encouraged to be independent and use their initiative to develop their full potential. Haddenham St Mary’s School, as part of the village and wider community, encourages a feeling of respect for people of all ages and beliefs in an ever-changing world. The overall aim is to awaken the children’s skills and personal qualities providing a foundation for a fulfilled and constructive life. The classroom teacher endeavours to create an atmosphere where individuals are recognised, appreciated, and encouraged. Learning to work and play together is a prime consideration. The school has successfully run a hub kitchen, "Homemade at Haddenham St Mary's", since the introduction of Universal Infant Free School Meals and the team deliver homemade hot lunches to over 400 children a day both at Haddenham St Mary's and other local schools. The school is managed by a committed Governing Body, comprised of eleven local people with a broad range of backgrounds. It is supported by an active Parent Teacher Association which raises substantial funds to enhance pupil’s learning experience through educational visits and provide additional facilities to complement National Curriculum activities.

Integral to our approach is the Christian ethos of caring for one another in school, in the local community and in society. At Haddenham St Mary’s, every child matters and everyone cares. https://haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk/general-info/special-educational-needs/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our supportive environment aims to: - enable every pupil to experience success - promote individual confidence and a positive attitude - ensure that all pupils, whatever their special educational needs, receive appropriate educational provision through a broad and balanced curriculum that is relevant and differentiated, and that demonstrates coherence and progression in learning - give pupils with SEND equal opportunities to take part in all aspects of the school’s provision, as far as is appropriate - identify, assess, record, and regularly review pupils’ progress and needs - involve parents/carers in planning and supporting at all stages of their pupil’s development - work collaboratively with parents, other professionals and support services - ensure that the responsibility held by all staff and governors for SEND is implemented and maintained. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? - NEN training - An Introduction to Autism, whole staff training, - Early Years Good Autism Practise, - Shine Charity Supporting Pupils with Spina Bifida, - ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistants), - SALT Creating communication-friendly environments, - Strategies for working with pupils with ADHD, - Drawing and Talking wellbeing intervention, - Supporting Deaf Pupils, - Step-On Training, - Using the Professional Portal Training for the SENDCo, - all staff complete anaphylaxis and asthma training annually, - Supporting children with Down Syndrome, - Makaton Level 1, - Virtual School Trauma training All staff attend statutory safeguarding, prevent and first aid training. Some staff attend additional paediatric first aid training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Meetings, email, telephone calls, open events, professionals meetings How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Termly parent meetings and looking at children's work, annual written report to parents, pupils' SEND support plans are reviewed at least 3 times during the academic year and the review and new outcomes are shared with parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Haddenham St Marys School is on one level for pupils with a small step. We have a vast outdoor space with easy access to the forest school area. We have 2 disabled toilets on the main school site, one has a height adjustable changing table. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Further developing the use of our inclusion space to allow small groups of pupils to work in a quiet environment away from the busy classroom if needed, and for use for wellbeing and learning interventions.

name: Haddenham St Mary's Church of England School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Haddenham, Aylesbury for 4 to 7-year-olds. Haddenham St Mary's Church of England School, founded in 1868, provides education for all children aged between 4 and 7 within a Christian ethos. With highly qualified teachers and a nominal roll of 180 children in three "year groups", class sizes are generally of 30 or under. Overlooking open fields at the southern end of the village and next to St Mary's Church, the school aims to create a challenging, yet supportive, environment, within which a broad and balanced curriculum is adapted to the individual needs of each child. All children are encouraged to be independent and use their initiative to develop their full potential. Haddenham St Mary’s School, as part of the village and wider community, encourages a feeling of respect for people of all ages and beliefs in an ever-changing world. The overall aim is to awaken the children’s skills and personal qualities providing a foundation for a fulfilled and constructive life. The classroom teacher endeavours to create an atmosphere where individuals are recognised, appreciated, and encouraged. Learning to work and play together is a prime consideration. The school has successfully run a hub kitchen, "Homemade at Haddenham St Mary's", since the introduction of Universal Infant Free School Meals and the team deliver homemade hot lunches to over 400 children a day both at Haddenham St Mary's and other local schools. The school is managed by a committed Governing Body, comprised of eleven local people with a broad range of backgrounds. It is supported by an active Parent Teacher Association which raises substantial funds to enhance pupil’s learning experience through educational visits and provide additional facilities to complement National Curriculum activities.

local_offer: Monkey Puzzle Day Nursery Chesham is committed to providing an environment in which all staff, children and their families including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), are supported to reach their full potential. All children have the right to be cared for and educated to develop to their full potential alongside each other through positive experiences, to enable them to share opportunities and experiences and to develop and learn from each other. We aim to provide a positive and welcoming environment, where each child is viewed as unique and plan for their individual needs. We adapt our activities and differentiate according to the specific needs of each child. Monkey Puzzle Day Nursery Chesham believes that all children have a right to experience and develop alongside their peers regardless of their individual needs. Each child’s needs are unique, therefore any attempt to categorise children is inappropriate. Monkey Puzzle Day Nursery is committed to working alongside parents in the provision for their child’s individual needs to enable us to help the child to develop to their full potential through a range of SEND strategies. We have a graduated approach for working with other agencies in meeting individual children’s needs in line with the local authority guidelines. Wherever possible special facilities or adaptions will be made to meet the individual needs of children. The nursery is committed to working with any child who has a specific need and/or disability and making reasonable adjustments to enable every child to make full use of the nursery’s facilities. All children have a right to a broad and well-balanced early learning environment. We have a named designated person, The Special Educational Needs and Disabilities co-ordinator (SENDCO), however it is the responsibility of all staff to care for all children. We have a system in place for planning, assessing, implementing, monitoring, evaluating and reviewing all children’s developmental needs. name: Farm Days at Hemley Hill Farm
description: Farm Days provides a safe, happy, calm and nurturing environment to support children and adults with a vulnerability. A place where everyone feels valued and has the opportunity to grow, engage in purposeful activities, connect with nature, and thrive. Engage in fulfilling activities from grooming a gentle donkey or pony, feeding the chickens and collecting their eggs, making mud wallows for our pigs, bottle feeding lambs in springtime, having cuddles with our friendly alpacas, guinea pigs and rabbits, to growing beautiful flowers and tasty vegetables. Hemley Hill Farm is home to a wide selection of native animals and growing garden where we can all enjoy the benefits to our mental and physical health outside in nature. When visiting Farm Days at Hemley Hill Farm you will meet: - Our beautiful, kind and gentle ponies Jasmine, Sarah, Rosie, and Princess for Equine Therapeutic Sessions - Our very own ‘wonky donkey’ Henry who loves to be everyone’s friend - Pig perfection with Clarissa and Patsy our British Lop sows, they love to be fed, have a good scratch and play in the mud wallows. - Woolly wonders Susie, Cilla, Norah, Pearl, Panda, Sweet Pea, and their growing group of inquisitive sheep, not forgetting their alpaca friends! - Lots of chirpy chickens and quackers ducks, they’re always on the lookout for a tasty titbit whilst you’re collecting their eggs! - Fluffy rabbits and loveable guinea-pigs to cuddle and make friends with. - Sweet smelling flowers and tasty vegetables in the nursery area, our Horticultural Therapeutic Sessions cover every aspect from seed planting to harvesting. For more information on bookings and referrals please contact us, we’d love to chat

name: South Bucks Down’s Syndrome Group | Sing Out Loud Choir
description: South Bucks Down's Syndrome Group (SBDSG) runs the Sing Out Loud Choir monthly. Sing Out Loud is for those aged 14 and above with Down’s Syndrome and engages them in music activities including singing, playing instruments and connecting through music.[ It supports the local down’s syndrome community by offering an accessible creative and social group for peers and their families. Curly Cath from CreateED runs the choir and says it creates an opportunity for young people to socialise, sing and have fun using their voices to explore a wide range of music including pop, rock, folk, musical theatre, and film songs. Everyone is welcome. Makaton and musical instruments support the experience to make it multi-sensory, engaging, and accessible to all and enabling all involved to create their own music. We have exciting ambitions to collaborate across the Choir, Drama and Arty Crafts Saturday Club groups on a production in the future. The University of Oxford has published research showing that group singing has many benefits including forging social bonds and a sense of connection, improving breathing, posture and releasing muscle tension, stimulating cognition and generally improving mood, wellbeing and happiness. What’s not to like? We hope you will join us to Sing Out Loud. This group is run monthly during term time. Locations and dates vary. Please contact us below if you would like to attend.
organisation: South Bucks Down's Syndrome Group (SBDSG) Families who have a member with Down’s Syndrome (DS) are welcome to join this local group which aims to provide friendship, support and activities for families at all stages – babies, pre-school, primary school-age, teenage and adulthood: New parents of children with DS can meet with us for advice, support. Music and Movement Group with Curly Cath for 5 to 7-year-olds meets monthly. Horse Riding - group lessons are for school-aged children and young people., The Drama group is aimed at teenagers and adults. ADS is a group for adults with Down's Syndrome to meet and share activities. SBDSG also has an annual barbecue for all members to meet together across the age range. Venues vary for different groups - please see our web site for details or contact Judy Pantridge (Chair). chair@sbdsg.org.uk http://www.sbdsg.org.uk/

name: Inspiring Futures Partnership Trust
description: Inspiring Futures Partnership Trust is a flourishing collaboration of academies, ITT providers and professional development centre working in partnership to secure the best educational provision possible for the children of the communities we serve. Inspiring Futures Partnership Trust is also committed to providing our staff with working conditions and professional support that result in extremely high levels of job satisfaction and well-being. We are driven by a shared passion to do our very best for the children in our care. Every day, each member of staff strives to add value to our academies to ensure they are vibrant, exciting, welcoming and nurturing places for our children to be inspired and excel. We are very proud that our Trust serves several different communities and we recognise that each academy is unique we value and celebrate their differences and the communities they serve. The individual characteristics of our academies, together with the diverse skills of our inspirational leaders and talented staff make IFPT an exciting place to work, collaborate and professionally grow as we create rich learning opportunities for all our children. This is an exciting time for IFPT as we continue to grow and support schools, academies and other multi-academy Trusts across Bucks and England. IFPT has developed the capacity and capability to raise standards collectively and has made a demonstrable impact on our learning communities. Our academies benefit from ambitious leadership and governance, robust business management and outstanding professional development. IFPT welcomes both faith-based and non-faith-based academies/schools into the Trust.

description: Welcome to Orchard View Primary Academy, a brand new primary academy opening in September 2025. If you have children starting Foundation Stage (Reception) in September 2025 and would like to know more about Orchard View, please register to attend one of our open evening events If you have children starting Foundation Stage (Reception) in September 2025 and would like to know more about Orchard View, please register to attend one of our open evening events. Orchard View Primary Academy will be joining Inspiring Futures Partnership Trust. Orchard View Primary Academy’s planning application is for a 3-form entry primary academy offering places from nursery up to year 6, with 12 places for special education needs additionally resourced centre to support children with social, emotional and mental health needs. Orchard View Primary Academy will initially be constructed as a 2-form entry primary academy offering places from Nursery up to Year 6 and may expand in the future subject to need. In September 2025, it will offer 30 places in the Foundation Stage (Reception), 30 places in Year 1 and 30 places in Year 2. All staff at Orchard View Primary Academy will be committed to delivering inspirational learning opportunities that are fun, purposeful and challenging, as every child has the potential to achieve and excel and make positive contributions to life in modern Britain. This means that Orchard View Primary Academy will: • Provide an excellent primary education for all children attending the academy • Deliver the highest standards of attainment and outcomes for all children • Be a member of the Inspiring Futures Partnership Trust, drawing on the expertise and capacity of the Trust to deliver outstanding provision • Be a key focal point of the new local community and help it thrive • Meet the individual needs of children and their families within a Trust-wide framework based on a proven knowledge and understanding of excellent teaching and learning • Recognise the need for diversity by ensuring the individuality of the academy within the Trust • Provide an environment where everybody matters: children, parents and staff.

local_offer: Our aim is to provide all children with the care and learning experience that they need. Our setting is safe, secure, fun, exciting and challenging. Our setting is inclusive to all children.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are willing to access services that are needed to ensure that we are providing the best service that we can. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENCo has achieved the Level 3 SENDCO qualification and attends regular liaison group meetings Our staff are willing to go on any training that is required to ensure that we can provide a great service to our children and families How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are invited to visit the setting, parents can stay and help if they wish. Parents are asked for their feedback each term Families can talk to us anytime if they have anything they want to talk about or have any concerns. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? In our setting, we use the software Tapestry where families can check the progress of their child, staff upload photos and videos, update progress tacker, add next steps. Our setting will arrange regular meetings with the family and outside agencies to ensure that their child is progressing well. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting is very accessible, in the classroom everything is on one level and there is a small step into the garden, we have a wheelchair ramp to access the garden. We are willing to make reasonable changes to suit an individuals needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We do everything we can to ensure a smooth transition, each family is invited into the setting for visits, chats where they can talk about their needs and requirements. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our SENCo attends regular liaison meetings to ensure that we are up to date with any changes or guidelines. Our SENCo checks the training calendar regularly to see if there are any training courses that she would like to attend. We will make changes to our facilities to each individuals needs.

local_offer: We are a fully inclusive nursery, and will make reasonable adjustments to care for and to educate all children. We have well trained staff who can support children with different complex needs. https://www.hamiltonacademy.org.uk/docs/Policies/Special_Educational_Needs_and_Disabilities_Annual_Report_2023-2024.pdf What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The nursery, which is attached to the school, has access to a wide range of education, health and social care services, which offer guidance to support children with SEND. This includes the Specialist Teaching Service: Cognition and Learning Needs, Communication and Interaction, Visual and Hearing Impaired and support for pupils with Physical Disabilities. Health specialists such as Occupational Therapists, Physiotherapists and Speech and Language Therapists may visit regularly to support children with Education Health and Care Plans (EHCP). It also includes the Education Psychology Service and Pupil Referral Unit. We are committed to using the expertise and advice provided by other professionals. With parental permission, referral forms can be completed to request formal assessments if appropriate. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff attend termly meetings with the SENDCo. If a specific need is identified, staff will receive relevant training from other agencies. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are invited to a stay and play session every half term. We have regular parent volunteers to read with the children. Bi-annual parents evenings. End of year report; parents are invited to respond to their child's report. Friends of Hamilton school events. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Bi-annual parents evenings. End of year report; parents are invited to respond their child's report. Daily opportunities for parents to speak confidentially with nursery staff about their child. For children with SEND regular Assess, Plan, Do Review (APDR) plans are written. SEN support plans are written with parents three times a year. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There is a level entrance gate which leads into the playground. A ramp leads down into the indoor nursery setting. Toilets are accessed off of this level, including a toilet for use by adults and children who are disabled. Where possible, we make reasonable adjustments to meet the needs of children within the school. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? For children transferring to Hamilton Academy in reception, regular visits are made to the reception environment in the summer term. A meeting for all new parents is held in the summer term followed by a transition visit for all children, with their parents, to meet their class teacher and to explore the environment. Reception staff complete home visits before the children come in to school in September. Additional visits to feeder nurseries may be undertaken by the SENDCo if needed. For children who transfer to a different setting, Nursery staff share relevant information with the professionals in that setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Ongoing CPD when needed. Termly SEN staff meetings with the SENDCo.

local_offer: Hampden Way Family Hub offers universal and specialised support to families in the local area. We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. Hampden Way Family Hub can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our provision provides support services for all families with children aged 0 to 19 years and up to 25 years for those with a SEND. Our aims are to improve parenting, health and children’s development and to provide a safe and stimulating environment for children, young people and their families to flourish, develop and learn. Parents provided with good information so they can make decisions, which will have a significant effect on their children’s life chances. Parents to know, what support and services are available to help them bring up their children, and how to access them. Families signposted into support as appropriate feel confident to provide good life chance for their children. Children to develop social skills in preparation for starting pre-school, nursery or school. Children to enjoy a variety of fun activities and play and learn through this participation. Parents to feel confident in parenting and picking up parenting skills and support through attendance. Personal, Social and Emotional Development. Physical development. Communication and Language Development. Outreach support, action plan to specifically help the family with individual needs. Emotional and practical support from Outreach Worker. We welcome all families to all of our services, staff are dedicated to supporting families using our Hub and its services. Our building is fully compliant with the disability requirements. We provide a warm, welcoming and fun learning environment for children and their families. Large and inviting outdoor play environment Sensory equipment available during sessions Accessible toilets How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can attend our services and register by completing a Family Hub Membership form. Outreach support can be provided by self-referral or by referral from a health visitor or other professional. name: In This Together Bucks
description: Welcome to In This Together Bucks CIC, where our dedication to creating a safer and more cohesive community is unwavering. Founded in 2021 by Afzaal Hussain and Adele Webb, our organization is deeply rooted in personal experience and a shared commitment to transformative change. ​The origins of our organisation are both poignant and inspiring. Afzaal's best friend was tragically stabbed to death. Adele, a member of the public who did not know Afzaal at the time, found his friend, called for an ambulance, performed CPR, and stayed with him until his last breath. This profound experience brought Adele and Afzaal together and inspired them to establish In This Together Bucks CIC, driven by their mutual resolve to prevent similar tragedies and support those affected by violence. ​Afzaal, who also has lived experience, and Adele, have been at the forefront of addressing both the immediate challenges and the underlying causes of knife crime. Since our establishment, we have taken a holistic approach to create transformative change in Aylesbury and beyond. Our commitment extends to all those affected by violence, whether directly or indirectly. We offer mediation, mentoring, and support through various programs, including gang mediation, mentoring sessions for victims of violent crime, and assistance for survivors of domestic violence. Our tireless efforts have led to a significant reduction in anti-social behaviour and crime in Aylesbury, fostering a greater sense of safety and security among residents. Among our proudest achievements is the collection of over 1,000 knives in just three years. Through knife amnesty bins and proactive outreach initiatives, we have removed dangerous weapons from our streets and taken tangible steps toward preventing future tragedies. However, our work is far from complete. As we continue to grow and evolve, we remain steadfast in our commitment to building a community where every individual can thrive. Check out our website below for more information.

local_offer: Hello We are Hannah & Laura we are both Ofsted registered childminders who work together and are committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. We work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child. We have both worked within childcare & educational settings for over 11 years within this time we have worked with a mixed range of ages from newborn to 11years. During this time we have had the opportunity to gain a huge amount of professional development and also a wealth of knowledge of children. I (Hannah) have had hands on experience and training with children who are deaf, blind, down syndrome and other physical disabilities. We ensure that no one is excluded and ensure that all activities can be adjusted to accommodate every unique child. We have both recently attended epi-pen training. We are a home from home hygge setting and pride oursevlves on offering a beautiful learning environment for children to feel safe, secure and have the confidence to try new things al whilst making them feel like a part of the family. We attend local toddler groups and clubs. With our setting we have a large secure garden which is accessible all the time with a range of toys and activities suitable for all. We are both paediatric first aid trained and have a level two in children and young people with mental health concerns. We are more than happy to extend our training to include specific needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As registered childminder’s we have a Key Contact (Sharon Bell) at Buckinghamshire County Council with the Early Years Team, and with parental permission we may contact them for further advice. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites…) are available for us to access. We welcome other professionals into the setting who may have involvement with a child and we are keen to access further training to support a child’s development e.g. speech and language (Speech Therapist). We are happy to attend Multi-Professionals Meetings if required. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Makton – 2010 BSL Level 3 – 2010 Epi-pen training - 2020 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis via the Family app where parents can access photos, daily diary & child development. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and we will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. We have 3 steps leading to the garden and cabin door but easy access via a side entrance, once down the steps everything is on one level and easily accessible for all children and families, we can also provide a temporary ramp to get down the steps if needed. We are happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g. adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. We encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We also ask families to provide photos of the family for the children to share in the setting. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings we will encourage the new provider to visit the child at our setting and in their home environment and ensure they have the opportunity to visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and our Key Contact. We regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences we offer to our families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

local_offer: OFSTED OUTSTANDING Childminder located in Stoke Poges in the District of South Bucks. It is my aim to provide the highest quality childcare service. I will promote learning through fun and structured play activities whilst adhering to the statutory framework for the Early Years Foundation. I believe that the service I provide reflects the care I would expect my own children to receive. All children will be cared for in a safe, welcoming and learning environment.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I am a forest childcare provider ensuring children get the opportunity to spend time in the great outdoors on a regular basis. Outdoor play and outings contribute to learning and health and hep children grow to appreciate the natural environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Speech and Language, Behaviour Management How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents play a very important role in my setting. I value their input and welcome and respond to all feedback that they give. Alongside the standard required personal information I ask parents to complete a starting point questionnaire about their child/ren to help give me a better understanding of their abilities and achievements after all they know their children better than anyone! I complete and provide parents with a personal development plan for each child every 3 months and suggest ways in which we can work together to ensure child/ren are continually developing in a fun learning environment. I ask for regular feedback from both the parents and children. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I liaise with all other settings that the children in my care attend (with written parental consent) to ensure continual child development and consistency of care. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There are no steps leading up to the house and downstairs is completely open plan. There are 2 steps from the back door to the decking and again from the decking to the grass area. There is a small step down into the outdoor play room. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they have the opportunity to visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

local_offer: We welcome children with all manner of needs and abilities. There is good access into the setting and inside rooms are all on one level with toilets conveniently located within the main hall where the children play. The outdoor environment is accessed via a shallow step and comprises a paved area at ground level, with a further 2 levels, one paved and one grassy, accessed by steps. The main ground level area can also be accessed via a ramp. We have experience applying for additional funding and EHCP's where appropriate, and one staff member holds their SENCO Level 3 qualification.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to make our setting inclusive for all children and to facilitate their needs as best as we can. We want all children to reach their full potential in a safe, nurturing environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 3 SENCO qualification Specific autism training Self regulation Managing feeling and behaviours in the early years training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have an open door policy and promote and value all parents views and opinions. We carry out annual parent questionnaires asking for feedback on our provision. We encourage parents to email or phone us directly if they have any comments or concerns. We encourage ongoing dialogue with their child’s key person. We produce a newsletter twice termly, a regular email update to parents including highlights, and share weekly observations on our online learning journal, which parents are also encouraged to contribute on. Parents are invited to help in the setting with cooking, gardening or ICT and are encouraged to share their interests and skills. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We have an online learning journal with weekly observations, a phone call with the child's key person at the end of the autumn term, parents evening in the spring term and an in depth end of year report in the summer. If children require an individual support plan in the setting, parents are invited in to meet with the SENCO and key person to update this every half term. If parents have any concerns, they are encouraged to contact us. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? description: Happy Hedgehogs provides high quality before and after school childcare for children attending the onsite preschool, Little Forest Friends and Haddenham St Marys school. We can provide your child with a healthy breakfast before school. After school, all children will be offered a snack. Children staying with us for a full after school will be provided with a light tea. Happy Hedgehogs is held within the school offering a range of indoor and outdoor activities, toys and games within a fun and safe environment. For more information please contact Playscheme Manager - Amelia Booth
organisation: Haddenham St Marys' C of E School and Wraparound Care Haddenham St Mary's Church of England School, founded in 1868, provides education for all children aged between 4 and 7 within a Christian ethos. With highly qualified teachers and a nominal roll of 180 children in three "year groups", class sizes are generally of 30 or under. Overlooking open fields at the southern end of the village and next to St Mary's Church, the school aims to create a challenging, yet supportive environment, within which a broad and balanced curriculum is adapted to the individual needs of each child. All children are encouraged to be independent and use their initiative to develop their full potential. Haddenham St Mary’s School, as part of the village and wider community, encourages a feeling of respect for people of all ages and beliefs in an ever-changing world. The overall aim is to awaken the children’s skills and personal qualities providing a foundation for a fulfilled and constructive life. The classroom teacher endeavours to create an atmosphere where individuals are recognised, appreciated and encouraged. Learning to work and play together is a prime consideration. The school has successfully run a hub kitchen, "Homemade at Haddenham St Mary's", since the introduction of Universal Infant Free School Meals and the team deliver homemade hot lunches to over 400 children a day both at Haddenham St Mary's and other local schools. The school is managed by a committed Governing Body, comprised of eleven local people with a broad range of backgrounds. It is supported by an active Parent Teacher Association which raises substantial funds to enhance pupil’s learning experience through educational visits and provide additional facilities to complement National Curriculum activities. office@haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk https://haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk/

All staff have been on a Makaton course. Recently we had staff training for a child with deafness. The SENCO's have also been on autism, communication and language courses How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work together with the parents to work out what is best for their child. We work together to find out ways to involve the parents and how best to do so eg: going home book, speaking to key workers each visit, telephone calls, emails, and/or regular meetings. We hold regular events/days when parents/family can come and be part of the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? This all depends on your child's needs, how much information-sharing there is, and who we need to share the information with. Together, we can look at this and decide the best way to share information for example telephone conversations, emails, duplicate paperwork, meetings etc. All information shared will be done with the permission of the parents How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There are no steps into the hall, there are only door frames to get over. The playground is also on one level. We have a disabled toilet (adult). Where possible we will make changes to help with the accessibility of all aspects of the pre-school environment. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We will work closely with the parents and any outside agencies already involved to support the child's transition both to preschool and when they leave going into school. In whichever way is appropriate for the child, settings and parent we are willing to help with all transitional needs. when starting preschool we can offer shorter sessions if the child needs time to adjust, they can bring with them their favourite toy, comfort blanket etc. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to take part in the SEN meetings arranged by Buckinghamshire Early Years and where possible attend meetings to further our knowledge and support for all our children and SEN needs

description: Founded in 1870, Maidenhead United FC is one of the oldest football clubs in England. We are proud to be a community-focused club, which has experienced significant progression over recent years across our elite and grassroots football and wider community programmes. Our Men’s and Women’s teams are both playing at the highest levels in the club’s history, with the Men’s Team playing in the Vanarama National League and the Women’s Team playing in the FA Women’s National League Southwest League. Our National League-accredited Maidenhead United FC Academy programme is delivered in partnership with Berkshire College of Agriculture. Our Maidenhead United FC Juniors section has grown significantly since its establishment in 2019 and is now one of the largest grassroots football clubs in the Thames Valley, running boys and girls teams covering U7s to U18s age groups and with 650 plus members (and growing!). We also run an extensive community programme with our Maidenhead in the Community and Maidenhead United FC Community Trust teams deliver a range of football, wellbeing and education programme

name: CYPITS Occupational Therapy Support, Resources, and Training
description: Children, Young People’s Integrated Therapies (CYPITS) Occupational Therapy Service supports children and young people to perform everyday activities, become as independent as possible, and interact with others and the world around them. The children who use our service find things like dressing, feeding, handwriting, socialising and play difficult. This could be due to a problem with their fine motor skills, coordination skills, perception skills and/or sensory processing (the ability to make sense of the world around them). We also provide advice and recommendations for equipment such as splints, sensory strategies, adapted cutlery, writing aids, specialist seating and switches. We work with children and young people, their families, and health, education, and social care colleagues, to help them get the most from their lives and achieve their potential. We offer a variety of training and resources to parents, carers, and early years settings through our website in the form of live webinars. These webinars include topics such as Tool Use, Picky Eating and Sensory Challenges (Problem Feeders, Sensitive Eaters, and Selective Eaters), Sensory Processing, Managing Fatigue, and Foundation Skills of Handwriting. These webinars can be watched at your own pace and are free to access. Please visit our website for more information and to get started.

name: CYPITS Speech and Language Therapy Support, Resources, and Training
description: Children, Young People’s Integrated Therapies (CYPITS) Speech and Language Therapies Service assesses and treats children and young people with specific speech, language, communication, eating, drinking, and swallowing difficulties. This helps them to communicate and participate in daily activities to the best of their ability. We see children and young people with a range of speech and language challenges, including Developmental Language Disorder (DLD), cleft lip and palate, complex communication needs, deafness, Down’s Syndrome, selective mutism, stammering, and Speech-Sound Disorders. We work with children and young people from 0 to 19 years in community clinics, homes, and early years settings including family centres and mainstream schools. We have a strong focus on upskilling parents and those in educational settings to maximise children’s progress in their daily communicative environment. Speech and language therapists can advise and help with: - attention and listening skills - play skills - understanding and using spoken language - recognising and producing speech sounds - using language socially - communicating, for example, using signing and symbols - fluency / stammering. We offer a variety of training and resources to parents, carers and early years settings through our website in the form of pre-recorded and live webinars. These webinars include topics such as Developing Joint Attention, Speech Sounds, Receptive Language, Attention and Auditory Memory, Makaton, and Creating Sensory Friendly Environments. These webinars can be watched at your own pace and are free to access. Please visit our website for more information and to get started.

name: Hartbeeps (Amersham)
description: Hartbeeps offers a totally unique 'age/stage' programmes which has been carefully crafted to support and delight every baby during their very important first year. We have worked on our content, changed and moved with the times to keep our classes, approaches and teaching up to the minute and following the latest research into early education. Everything we do in Hartbeeps is centred around learning through play. For our youngest customers, classes are designed to ignite and delight those freshly acquired senses and help babies to uncurl and release trapped energy. name: Quainton Parish Council
description: Quainton Parish Council has 7 councillors who stand for election every four years. The duties and functions of a parish council are many and varied. The Council meets monthly and considers planning applications and any other matters referred to it by residents and other bodies. All meetings are open to the public and there is a forum before or during the meeting at which members of the public can raise concerns and ask questions. There is also an annual meeting which all parishioners are invited to attend where the chairman provides a report on council activities during the preceding year. All meetings are advertised on the council notice board at the bottom of The Green and online. Residents can bring to the attention of the parish council anything that concerns them, either directly or through the clerk. If matters raised are not the responsibility of the council, the clerk can bring them to the attention of the proper authority. Our councillors attend some of our meetings and remain in close contact with the Parish Council. As a body, we hope to be an asset to you all by being approachable, supportive, diligent and wise in our judgements and actions. We are keen to hear your wishes and views and will do our best to keep Quainton as a happy and caring community.

name: Introductions to Solids Webinar
description: Buckinghamshire Health Visiting Service offers a free live webinar, ‘Introducing Solids Food’, which is aimed at parents who have babies aged around 16 to 24 weeks of age. It is also suitable if your baby is younger, and you want to be ready when the time comes to start introducing solids. Evidence based guidance recommends the introduction of solids when your baby is around 6 months of age. Encouraging good eating habits from the start is the best foundation for future healthy eating behaviour. It is good to learn how to get started and what to expect. These one-off sessions are delivered in a virtual (video link) format lasting for 60 to 75 mins and includes the following topics (all sessions will deliver the same information): - Expectations around weaning - When babies are ready to start solids - Developmental readiness - Food ideas – to try or avoid - Meal examples - Common worries or obstacles. There’s no need to pre-book. You can access the webinar through our website.

name: Hartbeeps (Wendover)
description: Hartbeeps offers a totally unique 'age/stage' programmes which have been carefully crafted to support and delight every baby during their very important first year. We have worked on our content, changed and moved with the times to keep our classes, approaches and teaching up to the minute and following the latest research into early education. Everything we do in Hartbeeps is centred around learning through play. For our youngest customers, classes are designed to ignite and delight those freshly acquired senses and help baby to uncurl and release trapped energy. Sessions focus on bonding and building confidence. From sitting to first steps, we offer BIG fun in full colour, with larger than life puppet characters, rhymes, raps, claps and rhythmic beats; supporting baby’s blossoming speech and language development. Once you reach the Happy House for steady walkers, we take a different sound journey every week, it’s fun fun fun all the way while we explore social learning, gorgeous puppet characters, dress up and excitement thrown in…. and oh the photos to keep forever!!

Our setting creates an environment that is welcoming and inclusive where parents feel comfortable in approaching staff about anything relating to their children or what maybe going on in their lives at that time. There are many informal opportunities for parents to have a ‘chat’ to their key person either at drop off or collection time or an appointment can be made at a more convenient time. Parents have access to our online record system and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home to their children’s online journal. Our online system also allows us to keep parents up to date on news from the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has an online learning journal that parents can access at anytime using their personal log in and password. In addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed with parents.Short term outcomes are regularly monitored for children with SEND and parents are invited to be part of this review, including the planning of new outcomes. If other professionals are visiting the setting for instance speech and language, occupational therapist, we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet them if they wish. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor and outdoor areas are fully wheelchair accessible. The community centre consists of one large room which is light and airy, toilets (including a wheelchair accessible one) and foyer. We create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing issues. We have a quiet area where distractions are minimised for focused learning. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child’s transitional needs are individual and we have a flexible approach, listening to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We have close relationships with local schools and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We continue to audit the SEND skills and knowledge of our practitioners and plan the training accordingly. Vanessa our SENCO leader is currently attending the training for the new paperwork that has been implemented.

name: Haybrook College (Berkshire)
description: Mixed-gender secondary school in Slough, Berkshire for 11 to 19-year-olds. Haybrook College Trust offers students personalised teaching and learning pathways that will allow them to achieve both academically and socially; we want them to be and to feel like valued members tr of society. An important part of this is for our young people to move on to further education courses of study and to secure employment that matches their needs and skillsets. The most important aim for the College is to equip all students with the qualifications and skills needed to progress in their education and/or gain employment upon leaving the College. We are extremely proud of our record on this front. Haybrook College Trust comprises a small special school called Millside School, a Pupil Referral Unit, which offers five unique programmes at KS4, as well as a range of ‘revolving door’ provisions at KS3 that have proven to be highly successful in supporting young people to maintain their place at or return to mainstream schools. Since September 2013 we have also provided a Post 16 provision called The Gateway through an innovative collaboration with Slough Pitstop Project charity. This has also ensured that we are in a position to offer a range of vocational courses in Motor Vehicle and Construction, as well as hospitality and catering at our highly successful provision Kitchen Craft. Young people from local schools can also access this provision and have benefited greatly from this vocational pathway.

name: Little Kickers
description: Little Kickers is a football club which supports children aged 18 months to 8 years to get into football. We have four different football classes each tailored to a different age group. However, we have two core beliefs that we take into every session: - We believe in something we call “Play not Push”. It means teaching football in a fun, pressure-free environment. We want to give children a positive introduction to sport as a whole, not just football, so they’re more likely to stay healthy and active throughout their lives. - We believe football can be educational. Coached in the right way it can stimulate imagination and aid early development skills such as learning colours and numbers, following instructions and playing as a team. It’s an approach that has bagged us numerous awards and helped us expand globally over the last 16 years. And like all our Kickers, we never stop learning. We’re continually improving and updating our classes, based on feedback and input from child health specialists as well as our network of over 2,250 football coaches worldwide. Our classes are split into the following: Little Kicks- 18 months until 2 years and 6 months Junior Kicks- 2 years and 6 months until 3 years 6 months Mighty Kickers- 3 years 6 months until they turn 5 Mega Kickers- 5 years to 8 years Local to Buckinghamshire we run classes in: Aylesbury Wendover Berkhamsted Chesham Amersham Thame Princes Risborough High Wycombe Marlow Beaconsfield Chalfont St Peter To find out more about us and find your local classes, please visit us at our website.

name: Little Kicks
description: Little Kicks is the perfect introduction to the fun world of Little Kickers. Children are introduced to the basics of football (dribbling, striking, goal scoring and so on) in a play-oriented yet structured format, using child-friendly but realistic football equipment. Each child is given the opportunity to work within their ability level but taught in a group environment. Classes also provide a fantastic opportunity for you to assist in your child’s early education, helping them develop physically as well as improving cognitive and social skills. Little Kicks is for children aged 18 months to 2 years and 6 months. Parent participation is required. Each child receives a football kit. Classes are run weekly, last 45 minutes, and are available at multiple locations across Buckinghamshire. There are 4 unique badges for your child to collect across the Little Kicks programme. The main focus of Little Kicks is ‘learning to learn’. Our coaches are taught specific techniques that enable children to get the most out of our classes. We believe that play is one of the greatest development tools and when combined with repetition and structure, ensures effective learning. Classes involve a number of games that require parents to put on their running shoes and get actively involved in the session. However, some games are specifically targeted at developing independence. These transition games mean children as young as two will be able to play independently of their parent or guardian. The primary goal is to settle children into the structure of the session, improve their confidence and attention, develop their basic motor skills and develop a good kicking technique. To learn more about Little Kicks and find your local class please check out our website.

name: Junior Kickers
description: Junior Kickers builds on the foundation skills and football basics learnt in Little Kicks. Using a familiar structure, children are challenged both physically and mentally. For those children who started in Little Kicks, independent participation is encouraged. If your child has just joined us you may need to stay close-by for a few weeks, but the ultimate goal is for children to be able to participate on their own. The format remains learning through play and because children are allowed to work to their own ability, it is suitable for complete beginners. Junior Kickers is for children aged between 2 years, 6 months, and 3 years, 6 months. Parent participation not required but parents/carers are required to stay with their children during the session. Classes are run weekly, last 45 minutes, and are available at multiple locations across Buckinghamshire. Play and games are at the heart of everything we do. Our games cleverly disguise the learning aspect so the children just think they are playing. The more the children enjoy the games, the more they participate. This enjoyment leads to greater confidence, which in turn leads to self-initiated participation and independent play. Junior Kickers teaches the fundamentals of football in a fun learning environment through a series of games using our tried and tested structure. Our Junior Kickers receive quarterly badges which highlight the key physical, cognitive and football skills they are exposed to in our programme. Our Little Kickers absolutely love showing their badges to their teammates and family! The primary goal is for children to love their classes and further develop their skills. This passion builds enough confidence for children to participate independently. To learn more about Junior Kickers and find your local class please check out our website.

Our games are fast-paced and increasingly football focused, with fun still at the heart, meaning that even new starters easily pick them up. Children begin to understand the importance of team play and matches are gradually introduced - Children play independently of their parent/guardian - 45-minute class - Weekly classes - Two coaches for up to 18 children (max) - Each new starter receives a football kit - 6 unique badges to collect across the Mighty Kickers programme Mighty Kickers is for children aged between 3 years, 6 months, and 5. Classes are run weekly, last 45 minutes, and are available at multiple locations across Buckinghamshire. Mighty Kickers classes incorporate our rounded learning approach of play, practice and understanding. Play is the motivator and promotes continued and repeated practice. This disguised learning in itself is a powerful tool, however we believe in not only teaching the children how to perform the skills, but also to understand why and where to use the skill in the real world. This transcends all six areas of our curriculum: - Personal, social, and emotional development, - Communication, language, and literacy, - Mathematical development, - Knowledge and understanding of the World, - Physical development, - Creative development. Mighty Kickers teaches the fundamentals of football in a fun learning environment through a series of games using our tried and tested structure. Our Mighty Kickers receive quarterly badges which highlight the key physical, cognitive and football skills they are exposed to in our programme. Things start to get very exciting at the Mighty Kickers age group. This is where all the skills learnt to date are transferred into team play and basic football matches.
