name: Mega Kickers
description: Mega Kickers is the culmination of the preceding age groups. It brings together all the skills learnt and introduces them into real football matches. Children continue to develop the social and cognitive skills as well as honing their football skills, putting them to use at the end of each session during the 20-minute match. There is a focus on fair play, as well as a focus on knowledge, understanding and practical application of the rules of play. More touches on the ball lead to faster and greater skill gain. Every child has their own ball throughout the session and our games are specifically designed for maximum touches of the ball. The games are progressively challenging enabling new skills to be learnt each lesson, however children are able to work within their ability. Children become more competitive at this age and are taught to challenge themselves and one another. The match becomes the climax of the session and is the perfect outlet for channelling children’s competitive energy as well as transferring their skills into a real world situation. Mega Kickers teaches the fundamentals of football in a fun learning environment through a series of games using our tried and tested structure. Our Mega Kickers receive quarterly badges (8 to collect) which highlight the key physical, cognitive and football skills they are exposed to in our programme. Mega Kickers is for children aged between 5 and 8. Parent participation not required but parents/carers are required to stay with their children during the session. Classes are run weekly, last 50 minutes, and are available at multiple locations across Buckinghamshire. Mega Kickers classes aim to be challenging. Children are able to transfer their football skills into a real match environment. Children are also taught valuable life lessons such as fair play, teamwork and the importance of hard work. To learn more about Mega Kickers and find your local class please check out our website.

name: Forge Learning Forest School Training Courses
description: Forge Learning is an established company founded in 2012. We are your one-stop shop for Outdoor Learning, Forest School Training, and continuous professional development in your local area. Our trainers have 20 years worth of experience with hands-on delivery of Forest School, Environmental Education, and Curriculum-based Outdoor Learning with a variety of groups as well as 18 years worth of experience of delivering high-quality training courses. These courses are appropriate for anyone working with children and young people of all ages and abilities. Courses include: Level 2 Award for Forest School Assistants Training Course All Forest School Assistant Courses are priced at £900 per person which includes all training, assessment, certification, and support. The Level 2 Award for Forest School Assistants qualification is for people wishing to assist with Forest School sessions and for those already assisting and wishing to gain an accredited qualification. You will need to be able to assist at a Forest School to gain this qualification. The course covers; outdoor play and learning, activities ideas, basic health and safety and risk assessment, plus, using tools, campfires and building shelters safely with children. Please note, this qualification does not qualify you to run or lead a Forest School project Included with your course; A resources bag containing your starter kit of essential items; A Tarpaulin, Work gloves, Fire Steel, Tinder, Fire gloves, a Knife and Sharpening stone. And 6 months free Forest School membership to Forge Learning's online resource library. Level 3 Certificate for Forest School Leaders Training Course All Forest School Leader courses are priced at £900 per person which includes all training, assessment, certification, and support. This course covers all elements of Forest School, including; child-led learning, outdoor play, activity ideas, site management and environmental impact. It will also cover managing health and safety outdoors and risk assessment. Combined are important ingredients of all Forest Schools, using tools, campfires and building shelters safely with children. Included with your course; A resources bag containing your starter kit of essential items; A Tarpaulin, Work gloves, Fire Steel, Tinder, Fire gloves, A Knife and Sharpening stone. AND 6 months free Forest School membership to Forge Learning's online resource library. Our courses are blended learning courses, you will join us to cover the practical parts of the training totally outdoors on your chosen course dates. The theory side of the course will be completed via our bespoke distance-learning structured plan with support from an assigned tutor. For course details, booking, and enquiries please contact us using the email address below.

name: Path Hill Outdoors - Alternative Education Provider
description: Our one-to-one student programme is designed to meet often complex and challenging needs and provides students with the chance to develop skills in a supportive educational setting. The programme is bespoke to each individual, but all students will spend time working in the outdoors taking part in a range of activities tailored to their interests. Our staff includes qualified teachers, youth workers, Forest School and bushcraft experts, but more importantly people passionate about our work and the young people we support. We are also fortunate to have a qualified SENCo, Play Therapist, and Counsellor on our team. Our referral process is relational and starts with a conversation to understand the needs of the student. This is followed by a visit which helps us get to know each other and ensure the perfect Instructor is matched to the student.

local_offer: We offer a 1:1 programme based in the outdoors. Our practical and physical activities are vehicles for working with our students on coping strategies, social skills, re-engaging in learning and confidence building.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are a bridge from one educational setting to another. We can support students to stay in education and we can prepare students for their post 16 step. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? In the past six months we have had specific external training on PDA, critical thinking, eating disorders, play based therapy, sleep. We collectively debrief everyday and as a group discuss and problem solve challenges that face our students. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We communicate all the time with parents/carers on their child's progress. When appropriate we will invite a parent/carer to be with their child in outdoors. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The one to one programme and the small number of children attending Path Hill each day (maximum 10) means we are readily available for discussions on the phone and support parents at home. We prepare a more formal report at the end of each term (3x p.a.) How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We are based outside with some structures such as A frames, pods, yurts and round houses dotted around our site for cover and indoor learning. Our environment is not suitable for wheelchairs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? A child needs to be referred to our programme either via school or the local authority SEND team. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We hope to put on family camps and parent support groups in the future.

local_offer: Our outdoor learning experience enables children of all abilities to access each individual area of learning through a broad, balanced and differentiated access to the curriculum. We pride ourselves on being a totally child-led environment. This approach to learning enables children, of all abilities, to be able to be in control of their own learning. We aim to provide opportunities for children and young people with SEND to access the Early Years curriculum. We hope that it is this positive and relaxed environment that enables children with SEND to excel in other areas of their development, including toileting and emotional regulation. Our child-led journey aims to enable children to control their own learning, ensuring that their next steps for learning are achievable and manageable. We aim for children and young people with SEND to be thoroughly supported within their own learning, just as all of our children are. We also aim for a child to create new relationships with both staff and peers and support them in creating firm foundations for their future. We offer flexible settling in sessions, following both parent and child’s needs and wants. We will also be offering home visits to ensure that the transition period is as smooth as possible for the child. When transferring to a new setting/school, we will make close connections to each setting so that information can be shared to guarantee a smooth transition. Our indoor area has wide door frames, ensuring that children with additional equipment can access inside. There are steps up to the indoor area and the decking area, which can be easily adapted by small ramps for those who may not be able to use the steps. Our indoor area also has tie-up blinds, enabling the yurt have low lighting if required. Our outdoor area is all on the same level. The ground is mud and can be soft when wet. To ensure that all children, especially those with extra equipment, can access this area, we have bark chippings that enable easier access to every area of the outside space. We offer an open door policy, which allows parents to share any concerns that they may have at any point. We also encourage parents to meet with their child’s Key Person regularly, to share observations and the Learning Journey’s. We aim to encourage parents onto any trips that we may have and, in the future, we hope to have regular parent-helpers for snack times, reading and other activities on site. Our SENCO will be responsible for ensuring that all members of staff access regular training to support children with SEND. Areas of training include Behavioural Management, Autism Awareness, Makaton Sign Language and then training which is required for individual children’s needs at that moment in time. We will be regularly reviewing our Barriers to Learning and Provision, ensuring that facilities and resources can be adapted or provided when needed. We will also be accessing regular training, for all staff, to the needs of their key children. Our indoor space is an open yurt which there is a step into, however it is possible to make this into a ramp. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We tailor our transition arrangements to the child and families personal needs. name: Growing Hope High Wycombe
description: Growing Hope is a charity which provides free therapy for children and young people (0 to 18) with additional needs in collaboration with local churches across the UK. Growing Hope aims to grow hope for children, hope for families and hope in Jesus. Free therapy services such as occupational therapy, physiotherapy, speech and language therapy, and counselling can all enable children to reach their developmental potential. We currently have clinics in London- Brockley, London- King's Cross, High Wycombe, Maidstone, and Redbridge. Growing Hope High Wycombe runs in collaboration with St James’ Downley with a vision to see all children and families thrive. We accept referrals for children and young people with diagnosed or undiagnosed additional needs who live in High Wycombe. Parents, carers or professionals can make a referral on a child’s behalf. Growing Hope is open to all regardless of belief. Our Therapy Intervention Flow is as follows: 1. Referral- Parents, carers, or professionals make a referral though our website 2. Assessment- Families come to an assessment at the local clinic. Therapists send families a short report of their findings after the assessment. If Growing Hope can provide support, families will join a waiting list for a block of therapy sessions. 3. Therapy Sessions- Therapy intervention consists of weekly sessions. During these sessions, children will work towards individualised goals. Parents and carers are encouraged to attend these sessions to learn strategies to continue at home. 4. Further Support- After 3 months has passed, re-referrals will be accepted if there are new or on-going areas of difficulty. Children will join a waiting list for review sessions. Please contact us or visit our website for more information.

local_offer: At Tingewick Pre-school every child is treated as a unique individual and each child has a key worker. Their role is to develop trusting sensitive relationships with parents and children to enable the respectful sharing of information and support. If you have any concerns about your child’s development, you can ask for a time when you can discuss this in private with them. We will work with you to support your child together, listening to you and your child. Our designated SENDco is Level 3 trained and understands the importance of having good communication, not only with parents but with any external agencies that may be/or become involved with your child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We always strive for every child in our setting to be able to learn and develop in a safe and positive environment. This gives children the best possible chance to be able to reach targets and milestones. We value our partnerships with parents and understand that their involvement and working closely together will have a positive impact on their child in their development whilst in our setting. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENDco, Heidi, has completed Attention Autism training most recently. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We offer a variety of ways for parents to get involved. At Tingewick Preschool we use an online learning journal, Tapestry, here you can view and comment on observations that have been added and we actively encourage parents to add photos of things they have been doing at home for us to extend on this in the setting. We also use Tapestry record assessments, these allow you to find out how your child is developing and make any comments, should you wish to do so. Informal feedback at pick up/drop off, a time where you can also bring up any concerns and arrange for a more formal time to discuss these. Tingewick Preschool is a committee-run charity and we encourage parents to join the committee. We send out a weekly newsletter each week, with information on what the children will be doing each week and our learning intentions. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Using our online learning journal, Tapestry, we complete 2-year progress checks and assessment summaries. These will inform you of how your child is progressing in areas and what areas your child's keyworker is going to be focusing on in the next steps. For children who require an SEN Support Plan, these are always completed with your involvement. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We are a big open plan room, with plenty of space around tables and activities. This also means we can create quiet areas if required. There is small part of our outside space which is accessible, to gain access to the bigger part of our garden, there are 3-4 steps. In our setting, we have a variety of resources and offer activities to suit all of our children's individual interests. If we find that a child likes something particular, we will purchase resources to suit that child e.g. sensory objects. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact us to let us know what sessions they would like. We will then ask you and your child to visit our setting to ensure it is the right environment for both of you. If it is we will arrange some settling-in sessions to build up familiarity with the setting, children and staff. This is also a good time to discuss any concerns you may have about your child's development or share a SEN support plan if one is already in place. When we all feel your child is ready, they can begin their sessions. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Further training in Autism and Makaton for our staff.

description: The Whole School SEND consortium regularly publishes resources to support you with all aspects of SEND. These include our SEND Review Guides and Frameworks, leaflets for parents, practical resources to support your work in educational settings, resources for specific contexts such as Continuous Professional Development and Learning (CPDL) webinar recordings and more. As a member of Nasen and the Whole School SEND Member Community, you have free access to all of our resources. We have a number of pre-recorded webinars including: - Embracing Inclusion: Supporting learners with Down's Syndrome and other learning disabilities in the mainstream classroom - Positive Beginnings: Supporting children with SEND at the start of their school journey - How to ensure balance between the role of SENCO and personal wellbeing. As well as webinars, we have also have free to access online CPDL training. Topics include: - Creating an emotionally safe environment - Understanding and promoting resilience - Specialist Spotlight: Developing maths skills (Secondary/Further Education) - Specialist Spotlight: Person Centred Learning - Listening and Working with Learners and Their Families (Secondary/Further Education) - Preparation for Adulthood (PfA) Professional Development Group Visit our website for more information on our resources and how to access them.

description: Mixed-gender primary school in Hazlemere, High Wycombe for 3 to 11-year-olds. We believe that every child has a talent and can experience success as they grow and develop through the supportive and caring environment we provide. We have an extremely dedicated and supportive staff, who work hard to provide the best opportunities for all of our children in a safe and happy environment. Our school improvement strategies over the last few years have ensured our attainment levels are above national and the Bucks average, as shown through our reported data. We are without a doubt a consistently respectable school offering a well-rounded education. We have worked to establish an ethos where we strive for high academic standards while ensuring that children are offered a broad, balanced, stimulating and ambitious curriculum. We place value on the importance of forming positive and constructive relationships within the school and aim to support all children to achieve their potential and to have high aspirations in everything they do. We pride ourselves on putting the child at the centre of our educational vision with a clear shared ethos, supporting children to be successful. We are forward thinking, creating and developing our book based curriculum and environment to provide our pupils with experiences which capture their curiosity and enthusiasm for learning.
organisation: Hazlemere Church of England Combined School and Nursery We are a primary school and Nursery catering for children aged three to eleven. We place our Christian values at the heart of our work and we aim to work closely with our families to enable each child to be the very best young person that they can be - developing intellectually, physically, emotionally, socially and spiritually. As a school we aim to be a God-centred learning community which includes children, parents and families, staff, governors and the wider community. The bible tell us that through his youth Jesus, "grew in wisdom and stature and in favour with God and men (Luke 2 v52). This is also something that we want for every one of our children and for the school as a whole. We want to be a community working together for excellence and high achievement across a broad curriculum. We aim to provide the opportunity for everyone to achieve their potential within a caring mutually supportive learning environment reflecting our Christian ethos. enquiries@hazlemere-ce.bucks.sch.uk https://www.hazlemere-ce.bucks.sch.uk/

name: Early years Autism support
description: We are a Charity providing free support to young autistic children (aged between 0 and 4) and their families. Provided by qualified Child Psychologists and Pediatric occupational Therapists, we work both in the home and online. Our First Steps programme is already operating in Buckinghamshire, Essex, and Oxfordshire. We also provide free online support to parents of Autistic children aged between 5 and 12 years. This includes Confident Parenting Workshops, which support parents and carers to feel confident to do their best for their child and build rewarding relationships. This course is run over 10 weeks and covers key areas such as behaviour, sleep, social interactions, eating, and sensory processing. To find out more, please visit our website.
organisation: Transforming Autism We are committed to empowering the families and carers of autistic children to optimise their life prospects and unlock their true potential. Our unique conception of autism, emphasising its potential and not seeing it as a disability, is at the heart of all we do. We aim to support parents to transform the lives of their autistic children by helping them to truly understand the needs they are not able to clearly express, and to respond to these in ways that make them feel safe, protected, looked after and strongly connected to those close to them. We aim to do this through support in the home, parent groups, our proposed intentive Mifne Clinic, and online materials including webinars, articles, interviews, online tools and eventually our comprehensive Autism Parenting Hub. Early Intervention is a key part of giving the right foundational support and understanding to an autistic child that will provide them with the strength and confidence to be able to find the best in themselves in later life, and we aim to work with and advocate working with children at the earliest possible opportunity in order to achieve this. services@transformingautism.org https://transformingautism.org/

description: To support our early help professionals and those supporting other families, the Early Help Partnership have developed a multi-agency training programme which is being made available for everyone working with children and families in Buckinghamshire and partners within Family Hub Networks. name: Neuroharmony SEND Advice and Support
description: Neuroharmony is a charity providing advice and support to develop a deeper, more personalised, understanding of autism, ADHD and anxiety for parents and young people up to 25. We draw upon our personal and professional experiences to deliver a flexible and bespoke approach. Access to our support and services is not dependent on meeting certain thresholds or specific diagnoses. We recognise that all children and young people thrive when they feel safely connected and understood. Our aim is to create broader recognition and understanding that relational safety and connection is paramount We work with the whole family to empower parents so that they can help their child in moments of challenge and distress. Providing support in the home environment, allows us to become familiar with the unique dynamic of each family. This enables us to respond to the needs of the family in a compassionate and holistic way. Please visit our website to learn more.

name: Health Visiting Service (Amersham)
description: We offer the same services to all families with children under school age, with more targeted and tailored support for those who need it. A health visitor will work with parents who are pregnant or who already have children under five in the household. We are available to offer advice or answer questions on: - How to take care of yourself and your family - How to encourage your child to develop and grow - How to keep your child safe - The support available for parents and carers. Health Visitors offer every family a programme of screening tests, immunisations, developmental reviews, information and guidance to support parenting and healthy choices. We ensure that children’s health needs are assessed as part of the Healthy Child Programme, a national framework, based on best evidence, to improve and protect the health of children as they grow. The majority of our child health drop-ins are run at your local Family Hub.

As well as seeking the public’s views ourselves, we encourage services to involve people in decisions that affect them and can influence decision-making at a local level. Our sole purpose is to help make care better for people.

name: Edgewood School
description: At Edgewood School, we offer a rich, varied, ambitious and carefully planned curriculum that prepares our pupils for the next steps in their lives. Each child’s programme is individualised to meet their specific needs, enabling them to access learning and be successful in meeting their goals. The school is purpose-built with light, airy and flexible education spaces that are designed to meet the social, educational and sensory needs of the pupils. We are located adjacent to a large play area, skate park, football pitches and footpaths through woodland. In addition, we have enclosed outside spaces providing interesting and stimulating environments for the pupils to play and learn. The school is situated in the heart of Lingswood Park, a suburb of Northampton, with great transport links to a wide range of amenities in the city as well as access to parks and the countryside. Providing individualised education programmes for ages 7 to 16 Specialising in Autism, Moderate to Severe Learning Difficulties, Speech, Language and Communication Difficulties and Associated behavioural difficulties.
organisation: SENAD Group Alderwasley Hall School and Sixth Form is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 5 to 19 years with Specific Language Disorders, Aspergers Syndrome and High Functioning Autistic Spectrum Disorders, all of whom experience complex speech, language and communication needs. The School and Sixth Form are located on separate sites within five miles of each other and are situated in Derbyshire, close to the towns of Matlock, Belper and Wirksworth. The City of Derby is also within easy access. The aim of all aspects of the curriculum is to prepare students for adult life by fulfilling their social and academic potential. Young people are supported to develop and achieve academic and vocational plans, develop independent living skills and a clear sense of identity, enabling them to contribute to society in adult life. The individual needs of students, as set out in their Education, Care and Health Plan are met through Therapy and educational programmes, underpinned by high-quality care. info@senadgroup.com https://senadgroup.com/alderwasley/

name: Healthy Start Scheme | Low income families
description: If you’re pregnant or have a child under 4, the Healthy Start scheme can help you buy basic foods like milk or fruit. If you qualify for the scheme you’ll be sent vouchers you can use in over 30,000 shops in the UK. You can also get coupons to swap for: pregnancy vitamins breastfeeding vitamins vitamins for children aged 6 months to 5 years old What you'll get: If you qualify, you’ll get vouchers to spend on: milk fresh fruit and vegetables plain frozen fruit and vegetables infant formula You get 1 voucher a week if: you’re pregnant you have a child aged between 1 and 4 You get 2 vouchers a week if you have a child under 1. You can also get free vitamin supplements. Eligibility: You will qualify for the Healthy Start scheme if either: you’re at least 10 weeks pregnant you have at least 1 child under 4 years old In addition, you must be receiving any of the following: Child Tax Credit (depending on family’s annual income) income-related Employment and Support Allowance Income Support income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance Pension Credit Universal Credit (but only if your family earns less than the stated amount per month from employment) Working Tax Credit (but only if your family is receiving the 4-week ‘run-on’ payment) You’ll also be eligible for the Healthy Start scheme if you’re pregnant and under 18, even if you do not receive any benefits. How to claim: Apply for Healthy Start vouchers by filling in the online form and printing it out.

name: Forest School Training
description: Accredited Forest school leadership and forest school assistant courses, including Level 2 Award in Assisting at Forest School and Level 3 Certificate in Forest School Leadership. Level 2 Award in Assisting in Forest School: This 5-day course is designed for those who are assisting a Forest School Leader at Forest School. This course does not enable you to run Forest School Programmes. You will be assessed through a portfolio and peer assessment. This course typically takes 6 months to complete. You will be required to assist in the delivery of Forest School sessions to achieve your qualification, so you will need to have identified a Forest School Leader with whom you can work. Entry requirements for this course include being 16 years old or older, having an identified Forest School Leader to work with, and having a Level 1 qualification or equivalent. Level 3 Certificate in Leading Forest School: This 8-day course is for those who wish to lead Forest School programmes. T You will be assessed through the completion of a portfolio, practical skill assessment days, work-based assessments, and peer assessment. This course normally takes 9 to 12 months to complete. You will be supported to set up and deliver a Forest School programme, and so you will need to identify a site to work from before enrolling on this course. Entry requirements include being 19 or over, holding a Level 2 qualification or equivalent, experience of working with the client group, and a potential site to deliver Forest School programmes. 19 or over Level 2 Qualification or equivalent Experience of working with the client group A potential site to deliver Forest School programmes. Please visit our website for more information and to book onto upcoming courses.

description: Perform is a unique type of children’s drama school. Focusing on child development, Perform uses a specially formulated mix of drama, dance and singing to bring out every child’s true potential. Small class sizes ensure lots of individual attention from experienced actor-teachers who focus on developing the 4 Cs: Confidence, Communication, Coordination, and Concentration, as well as having the best fun of the week. Perform offer no-obligation free trial sessions to all newcomers. To book a free class visit our website.
organisation: Perform Workshops Ltd Drama, dance and singing workshops and parties for children aged 4 to 12 years old! Every child is different and so are the things they enjoy. Some children are energetic and outgoing, others are quieter and more sensitive. Whatever your child is like, you'll know that the most important thing is that they are happy and fulfilled. Perform is a different type of drama school. We use a unique mix of drama, dance and singing - specially developed and written by us - to bring out every child's true potential. Classes are kept small to ensure lots of individual attention by our experienced teachers - hand-picked for their warmth, energy and professionalism. They'll focus on your child's enthusiasm and engagement in the activities rather than their precision and ability to learn moves. And they'll be with your child every step of the way to guide, inspire and encourage. As well as having fun at Perform, your child will enjoy real benefits: greater confidence, improved concentration and an increased awareness of what they can achieve. enquiries@perform.org.uk https://www.perform.org.uk/

name: Heatherton School (Independent)
description: Heatherton is an independent girls’ school in Amersham, with a co‑educational Nursery, offering an education built for girls, not adapted for them. Educating Girls to Lead, Think, and Achieve: being academically ambitious and intentionally small, our girls are given a wide range of opportunities to develop intellectual curiosity and succeed through individualised learning. From the earliest years, our pupils benefit from outstanding teaching, early exposure to STEM subjects, specialist teachers, and purposeful leadership development, all underpinned by exceptional pastoral care. We are delighted to be registered to offer the universal 15 hours per week of Government‑funded provision for children aged 3 to 4, providing families with access to our exceptional early education within a purposeful and aspirational school environment. Nurtured to excel, Heatherton girls are prepared not only for a strong range of senior schools in the local area, but also to succeed in the world they are growing up in.
organisation: Heatherton School (Independent) Heatherton is a nursery and independent day school for girls aged 3 to 11 in Amersham, Buckinghamshire. It a forward-thinking school with a very special family feel that has a reputation for building strong academic foundations. Its outstanding nursery welcomes both boys and girls from the term they turn three. The school and nursery also offers a wrap-around care service, with care available for all children from 7:30am to 6:30pm. office@heatherton.com https://www.berkhamsted.com/heatherton/

name: Doctor Jo Online Parenting Plan
description: Psychological support specifically designed for parents of neurodivergent children. We understand that parenting a neurodivergent young person comes with some unique challenges. Often routine parenting suggestions - star charts, the naughty step, rewards - simply don't work in the same way for neurodivergent young people. The differences continue into adolescence and beyond! Everything Doctor Jo does is with the needs of neurodivergent young people in mind so you'll know that the explanations and suggestions are aimed at you. Neurodivergent people often need to 'fit in' to what is expected, but not here! Our parenting plan includes: - Unlimited access to a growing library of Doctor Jo workshops with at least 2 new workshops added per month. - Content available in manageable chunks, perfect for accessing on your commute, lunch break or post bed-time - Free downloadable worksheets and resources - Monthly live Q and A sessions with Doctor Jo - Online support in our Neurodiverse-City which includes opportunity to suggest future workshop topics specific to your child's need

local_offer: Little Learners Nursery is a privately owned Nursery that caters for up to 24 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. Everyone at Little Learners has a passion for helping all children achieve their best and we pride ourselves in our personal approach. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share in their children’s achievements with us. We also want to provide an environment where parents can share their hopes and concerns too. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to give children the best possible start to their education. To ensure this happens, if appropriate, we will work with families to seek support from outside agencies and will implement recommended strategies according to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? NASENCo July 2010 Catherine Young Autism Awareness January 2022 Catherine Young Supporting children with speech difficulties March 2021 Catherine Young Makaton introduction February 2021 Catherine Young Attention Autism (Bucket Time) June 2018 Catherine Young Introduction to autism Sept 2024 All staff Joint Attention Jan 2025 All staff How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents into the setting each morning to support the transition for children and to help parents see for themselves what activities have been set up for the children. Parents have access to our online record system, and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can request a meeting with their child’s Key Person at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible. We also have termly parents' sessions where parents will receive an update on their child’s progress and can discuss their child’s likes, dislikes, achievements, and any concerns they may have. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents/carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed and agreed with the parents. We also offer updates through home/schoolbooks, email or phone calls if this is more convenient. We will regularly monitor the short-term outcomes for children with SEND and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT) …) are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We make every effort to make our environment as accessible as possible. There is step free access through the front of the building. Access to outdoors can be achieved through alternative routes and ramps where necessary. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child’s transition needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including home visits, frequent settling sessions, shortened sessions and transition booklets. We will be happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible to meet their needs. We encourage the local schools to liaise with us and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently auditing the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and will plan our training accordingly. We are constantly reviewing the use of space in our Nursery to ensure it meets the needs of all our children and are considering the use of other spaces in the building that can be used for additional focussed work as needed.

name: Helen and Douglas House Children's Hospice
description: Helen and Douglas House provides specialist hospice care for babies, children, and young people with life-shortening conditions and those who are seriously and terminally ill (0 to 18 years). The charity also supports the wider family through a baby, child, or young person's illness and bereavement. Helen and Douglas House works in close partnership with other health and care professionals in hospital and community settings to provide age-appropriate palliative care tailored to individual needs. We provide nursing and medically supported stays at the hospice, offering specialist palliative and symptom management care for complex and developing conditions, including at the end of life. We seek to enable a quality of life in line with individuals' capabilities and desires. In-patient care is provided at the hospice located in east Oxford as well as in your own home or hospital setting supporting other professionals.

name: SEND Alternative Provision Sessions
description: Here at The Bucks Goat Centre we provide an alternative provision for children and young people. We provide a safe learning environment where child, young people, and vulnerable adults can develop and grow their confidence and self-esteem through the education of animal welfare and management. We offer 1-1 or small group sessions run by passionate, trained staff. We strive to achieve positive outcomes through the use of our therapeutic animals in a secure and friendly environment. We tailor each session to the individuals’ own needs and recognise that our sessions are part of a bigger picture of the child’s, young persons or vulnerable adults’ growth and development.
organisation: The Bucks Goat Centre COVID update 29 December 2020 Tier 4 | we are allowed to open in Tier 4 as an outside venue only. We follow strict COVID rules. Restricted numbers may apply at certain times, please call us to find out. The Bucks Goat Centre is a friendly open farm situated in Stoke Mandeville. Animal Handling Sessions available every day and at selected times at weekends. We have a wide selection of animals here on the farm, playful piggies, cheeky chickens, very inquisitive alpacas, cuddly rabbits along with lots of friendly goats. Pet and feed our clean and friendly farm animals in a child-friendly environment. Childminder Wednesdays Every Wednesday Children go FREE with one full paying childminder. name: The Henry Allen Trust
description: Bringing happiness to families battling childhood cancer. The Henry Allen Trust provides advice, support, fun, and laughter – you’re not alone. We want to provide more than just help and support, with Team Henry you’ll find happiness. When a child becomes ill with Cancer, life can become all about appointments and medical necessities. We’re here to make sure you and your family doesn’t miss out on the fun you need. We can’t promise to take all your worries away, but we can promise to share them – and to help you create magical smiles and precious memories. We work alongside local hospitals to bring you hope and help you manage the hospital environment and the distress from a diagnosis which has turned your life upside down. We offer the following: - Support to nurses through their oncology training - Advice on process improvement, considering how we can support families better -Our wellness counsellor, Cat, can come into hospitals to support family members with CBT or hypnotherapy, helping families find laughter again -Toy packs, arts and crafts packs, and even food packs for families dealing with unexpected hospital stays. - Treats and Wishes to bedsides – helping children meet their heroes and get the equipment that will change their future. Our purpose is to give families the opportunity to create some treasured memories. - Dolly – our pet therapy dog, visits families in the hospital, bringing smiles everywhere she goes. Our aim is to provide benefits for the patients of children's hospital oncology units: - To help relieve sickness and preserve health by providing - or assisting in the provision of - equipment and facilities, recreation, and services - To promote and protect physical and mental health through financial assistance, support, education, practical advice, and counselling. - To relieve the sickness of child oncology patients by offering respite through the provision of short breaks and holidays. - To advance the education of the general public in relation to life-threatening diseases and terminal illnesses in children – including the hope and encouragement that can be found through better understanding and survivors' success stories. Please visit our website for more information on how The Henry Allen Trust can help you.

suitabilities: 
local_offer: To provide a fully inclusive development for all children in our care. To work closely with the family and carers to encourage the development and progress of each and every child in our care enabling them to reach their full potential. To sign-post families and to support them to engage and receive professional support in a timely fashion. To reassure and work alongside families during their time with us to seek support from external agencies as and when appropriate. To offer parental courses on development, behaviour management, how do we learn, why do we play, healthy eating, oral hygiene to name a few.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? For each and every child to reach their full potential and to support their families during the process. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The setting has a trained Lead SENCo and Assistant SENCo All staff working with the children attend in-house training courses and are able to access external on-line training courses in support of the development of all children. Paperwork is in place to ensure that any concerns are recorded in a timely fashion and brought to the attention of the Manager and SENCo. The SENCo accesses and regularly researches information regarding SENCo either on line or in specific publications, i.e. NMT, National Day Nursery Association, Nursery World. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The SENCo, Key Carers and parents will work together to decide the best way forward for the child. The setting will always include the child. The SENCo, key carers and parents carry out observations as part of the child’s learning profile to ensure they are hitting the milestones and where necessary early intervention is discussed with the parents. Some parents are very engaged and some need extra support. The setting is very supportive and works closely with everyone in a sensitive manner sharing information and offering guidance when appropriate and where necessary working closely to put an action plan in place. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The SENCo, Key Carer and Owner of the nursery will work closely with the parents/Carers to ensure they agree with the best way forward and they are kept fully informed during the process. The Setting holds termly parents' evenings to share a child’s progress and next steps. Also when handing over during the AM and PM collection times. The SENCo and Parents/Carers will work together when preparing reports for external professionals in the support of their child’s development needs. The key carer will ensure the SENCo is fully aware of any concerns about a child’s health or development. The Manager, SENCo and Key carer will carry out observations to support their planning and the next steps for each and every child. The setting has good links with Bucks Council Early Years Team and when necessary receive support and guidance. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is very accessible and has indoor and outside spaces. The setting is on one level and has a fantastic allotment which enables all children to enjoy watching vegetables grow, learning how to look after them, harvest them and enjoy them with their meals. The setting has a level outside area with lots of activities and toys to enjoy. We work closely with families with English as an additional language to ensure everyone understands. Where necessary the setting will access extra funding to support a child’s access to learning and if applicable will borrow specialist equipment from Occupational Therapy to support a child’s development. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The setting is very welcoming. All our families are valued and their input and support are necessary in helping us all to achieve the best outcomes for each and every child to build a caring and trusting relationship. The parents attend a welcome meeting when joining the nursery to build the partnership necessary to support them. This is a very important time to support the parent especially if their child has SEN as this can be a very difficult/sensitive time for them. The parent will complete a Child Development Record, age-specific as a starting point for their child’s onward progression and to be linked to their Learning Profile. The setting holds 3 parent’s evenings a year and has an open-door policy to engage at all times. Every morning and every evening hand-overs are given continuing the dialogue to support each child and family in building the partnership required to support each child’s development The setting holds family events, i.e. preparing your child for school meetings, pirate parties; Christmas party teas to enable parents to meet and socialise with the setting and to network with other parents and to gain knowledge on how to support/develop their own child of the moment and also for their onward transition to school. The setting believes early intervention is key with the child being the number one priority and will always seek the child’s voice. The setting will guide the parents/carers in sign-posting to external professionals at the earliest opportunity, preparing documentation as and when necessary. The setting will support all children in their move to big school, either by settling them in during visits to the school or by inviting the school/Reception Teacher into the setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To continue to reflect, review and update the setting to ensure it is fully inclusive to everyone. Each and every child is important to us and their well-being and development are paramount to their future. To build upon our allotment and outside area for the enjoyment of the world around us.

local_offer: To provide a fully inclusive development for all children in our care. To work closely with the family and carers to encourage the development and progress of each and every child in our care enabling them to reach their full potential. To sign-post families and to support them to engage and receive professional support in a timely fashion. To reassure and work alongside families during their time with us to seek support from external agencies as and when appropriate. To offer parental courses on development, behaviour management, how do we learn, why do we play, healthy eating, oral hygiene to name a few.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? For each and every child to reach their full potential and to support their families during the process. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The setting has a trained Lead SENCo and Assistant SENCo All staff working with the children attend in-house training courses and are able to access external online training courses in support of the development of all children. Paperwork is in place to ensure that any concerns are recorded in a timely fashion and brought to the attention of the Manager and SENDCo. The SENCo accesses and regularly researches information regarding SENDCo either online or in specific publications, i.e. NMT, National Day Nursery Association, Nursery World. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The SENCo, Key Carers and parents will work together to decide the best way forward for the child. The setting will always include the child. The SENCo, key carers and parents carry out observations as part of the child’s learning profile to ensure they are hitting the milestones and where necessary early intervention is discussed with the parents. Some parents are very engaged and some need extra support. The setting is very supportive and works closely with everyone in a sensitive manner sharing information and offering guidance when appropriate and where necessary working closely to put an action plan in place. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The SENCo, Key Carer and Owner of the nursery will work closely with the parents/Carers to ensure they agree with the best way forward and they are kept fully informed during the process. The Setting holds termly parents' evenings to share a child’s progress and next steps. Also when handing over during the AM and PM collection times. The SENCo and Parents/Carers will work together when preparing reports for external professionals in the support of their child’s development needs. The key carer will ensure the SENCo is fully aware of any concerns about a child’s health or development. The Manager, SENDCo and Key carer will carry out observations to support their planning and the next steps for each and every child. The setting has good links with Bucks Council Early Years Team and when necessary receive support and guidance. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is very accessible and has indoor and outside spaces. The setting is on one level and has a fantastic allotment which enables all children to enjoy watching vegetables grow, learning how to look after them, harvest them and enjoy them with their meals. The setting has a level outside area with lots of activities and toys to enjoy. We work closely with families with English as an additional language to ensure everyone understands. Where necessary the setting will access extra funding to support a child’s access to learning and if applicable will borrow specialist equipment from Occupational Therapy to support a child’s development. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The setting is very welcoming. All our families are valued and their input and support are necessary in helping us all to achieve the best outcomes for each and every child to build a caring and trusting relationship. The parents attend a welcome meeting when joining the nursery to build the partnership necessary to support them. This is a very important time to support the parent especially if their child has SEN as this can be a very difficult/sensitive time for them. The parent will complete a Child Development Record, age-specific as a starting point for their child’s onward progression and to be linked to their Learning Profile. The setting holds 3 parent’s evenings a year and has an open-door policy to engage at all times. Every morning and every evening hand-overs are given continuing the dialogue to support each child and family in building the partnership required to support each child’s development The setting holds family events, i.e. preparing your child for school meetings, pirate parties; Christmas party teas to enable parents to meet and socialise with the setting and to network with other parents and to gain knowledge on how to support/develop their own child of the moment and also for their onward transition to school. The setting believes early intervention is key with the child being the number one priority and will always seek the child’s voice. The setting will guide the parents/carers in sign-posting to external professionals at the earliest opportunity, preparing documentation as and when necessary. The setting will support all children in their move to big school, either by settling them in during visits to the school or by inviting the school/Reception Teacher into the setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To continue to reflect, review and update the setting to ensure it is fully inclusive to everyone. Each and every child is important to us and their well-being and development are paramount to their future. To build upon our allotment and outside area for the enjoyment of the world around us.

name: Talkback Supported Internships
description: A supported internship is a programme primarily focused on a work placement, for students aged 18 to 24 in receipt of an Education, Health, and Care Plan (EHCP). This programme is typically 3 days a week, with students seeing the majority of their time based in the workplace. The remainder of time is spent in college to earn qualification in English and Maths or a relevant employability qualification. Talkback offers a range of options that include 6 month, 9 month, and 12 months internships that meet the required 540 guided learning hours. Our flexible approach aims to transition people away from a traditional academic calendar and towards the world of work. If you have already experienced the world of work through your careers provision in secondary school or post-16 education and have a strong motivation to work, then our programme is for you. To join the programme, you need to meet the following criteria: - You are 18 to 25 years old. - You will have an Education, Health, and Care Plan (EHCP). - You will have undertaken some form of work experience and have realistic career aspirations that enable us to match you to an employer. - You have had good attendance at your previous provision. - You have completed an employability or other school/FE programme. - You have previously accessed independent travel training. - You have achieved Entry Level 3 or above in Literacy and Numeracy. The Talkback Job Coach shadows you in the workplace. As your confidence and ability grows the Job Coach reduces their time with you, so you can work independently. We work with the employer and you to ensure you are contributing to the business, and to identify further skills needs, which will feed into the ongoing design of the off-the-job programme. Please visit our website for more information and to get involved.

Our roots are in self-advocacy and this has allowed us to develop consultancy support around a whole range of life solutions. local_offer: A supported internship is a programme primarily focused on a work placement, for students aged 18 to 25 in receipt of an Education, Health, and Care Plan (EHCP). If you have already experienced the world of work through your careers provision in secondary school or post-16 education and have a strong motivation to work, then our programme is for you. To join the programme, you also need to meet the following criteria: - You are 18 to 25 years old. - You will have an Education, Health, and Care Plan (EHCP). - You will have undertaken some form of work experience and have realistic career aspirations that enable us to match you to an employer. - You have had good attendance at your previous provision. - You have completed an employability or other school/FE programme. - You have previously accessed independent travel training. - You have achieved Entry Level 3 or above in Literacy and Numeracy. - You are enrolled at Buckinghamshire College Group.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Work experience takes place over a short period of time or for one day a week. With this you learn about the world of work and develop strategies to gain general employment skills. A supported internship includes a placement matching your hopes for longer-term employment. It is focused on helping you develop the skills and independence for that role, or a similar role. The expectation is that you can and will progress to employment. This programme is typically 3 days a week, with students seeing the majority of their time based in the workplace. The remainder of time is spent in college to earn qualification in English and Maths or a relevant employability qualification. Talkback offers a range of options that include 6 month, 9 month, and 12 months internships that meet the required 540 guided learning hours. Our flexible approach aims to transition people away from a traditional academic calendar and towards the world of work. The application process and timings: - Talk about your hopes for employment in your annual reviews. - Apply for a place on the Supported Internship Programme through your local college (between October and April). - We check you meet the criteria and for those eligible we meet to discuss your hopes, and whether we think we can help you move towards employment. - All being good, we will confirm your starting arrangements (by July). - You start your Supported Internship journey with us! (September) Will you have a job coach? Yes. The Talkback Job Coach shadows you in the workplace. As your confidence and ability grows the Job Coach reduces their time with you, so you can work independently. We work with the employer and you to ensure you are contributing to the business, and to identify further skills needs, which will feed into the ongoing design of the off-the-job programme. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We provide an extensive range of training to our staff. The entry requirements for all our staff working on the education contract is Level 2 or equivalent in English and Maths. Our staff are expected to complete a comprehensive safeguarding and compliance training programme within the first four months of joining Talkback. They then complete refreshers on these as per training cycle. The other professional qualifications that staff are expected to complete are as below: Level 2 Learning Support Qualification/SEND Certificate Level 3 City and Guilds in Education and Training Gateway Qualifications Level 3 BASE (British Association Supported Employment) on Supported Employment (Level 3) Each staff member has an electronic training record, which notifies us in advance of renewal dates to ensure the Training Coordinator can keep training up to date. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Members and their families/carers give us their feedback by participating in: - Annual Reviews - Session Evaluations - Accessing our Complaints, Concerns and Compliments procedures - Annual Family and Member Feedback Surveys. So that we continue to meet the aspirations and needs of people with a learning disability and/or autism, all Talkback services are reviewed, shaped and new opportunities are continuously being developed, following the feedback given by members, their families/carers and the Management Groups. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? - Session Evaluations - Annual Reviews - Annual Family and Member Feedback Surveys. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Accessible indoors and outdoors environment How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Survey interviews will be conducted with people with learning disabilities and their families/carers where appropriate, to obtain feedback on the support they receive from Talkback. The outcomes of the surveys will inform support and service quality improvement across the organisation. People with learning disabilities are directly involved in the planning and review of the support and services that Talkback provides to ensure that their needs, hopes and aspirations are met.

When students first attend they are assessed as part of their induction to enable staff to identify and understand their strengths and needs for support. The resulting information is used to plan the most appropriate programme and support package so as to ensure students’ learning and progress. Aspire encourages parents who have concerns or queries about a student’s learning difficulties to contact the Special Educational Needs Coordinator. As all our students are taught in small groups, students receive close monitoring and support to ensure their needs are met. Exam access arrangements are made for students when appropriate, for instance when a student has a reading or writing difficulty. If students need some additional, ongoing support above what they receive in the classroom it may be that they have some form of SEND. There are 4 areas of SEND: Cognition and Learning: for instance, perhaps a student has Dyslexia or struggles to process information at the same speed as their peers. Sensory and Physical: a student may have a visual impairment or Cerebral Palsy. Communication and Interaction: An example of this may be a speech and language delay or problems with social interaction. local_offer: Special Educational Needs Aspire is committed to providing outstanding SEN Provision to meet the needs of all students. When students first attend they are assessed as part of their induction to enable staff to identify and understand their strengths and needs for support. The resulting information is used to plan the most appropriate programme and support package so as to ensure students’ learning and progress. Aspire encourages parents who have concerns or queries about a student’s learning difficulties to contact the Special Educational Needs Coordinator. As all our students are taught in small groups, students receive close monitoring and support to ensure their needs are met. Exam access arrangements are made for students when appropriate, for instance when a student has a reading or writing difficulty. If students need some additional, ongoing support above what they receive in the classroom it may be that they have some form of SEND. There are 4 areas of SEND: - Cognition and Learning: for instance, perhaps a student has Dyslexia or struggles to process information at the same speed as their peers. - Sensory and Physical: a student may have a visual impairment or Cerebral Palsy. - Communication and Interaction: An example of this may be a speech and language delay or problems with social interaction. - Social, Emotional and Mental Health: A student may have this as their primary SEND, such as clinical depression or it may be a secondary SEND as a result of other learning differences such as ADHD or ASD. https://www.aspireap.org.uk/SEN-at-Aspire/SEND-at-Aspire/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? description: Princes Risborough Town Council is an elected body of 13 unpaid councillors who have statutory responsibilities for certain aspects of the town, including street lights, public parks, grass cutting, and maintaining listed buildings. Full Council meetings take place at 7pm monthly, on the last Tuesday of the month in the Wades Centre, Stratton Road, and are open to the public. Typically the meetings last 2 hours and will usually include a report from the police. The first 10 minutes of the meeting are available for the general public to raise any issues they may have with the council.

name: Princes Risborough Town Council
description: Princes Risborough Town Council is an elected body of 13 unpaid councillors who have statutory responsibilities for certain aspects of the town, including street lights, public parks, grass cutting, and maintaining listed buildings. Other non-statutory areas the council is involved in are planning applications, forward planning for the town as a whole, and as a community voice to Buckinghamshire Council as well as local business. Full Council meetings take place at 7pm monthly, on the last Tuesday of the month in the Wades Centre, Stratton Road, and are open to the public. Typically the meetings last 2 hours and will usually include a report from the police. The first 10 minutes of the meeting are available for the general public to raise any issues they may have with the council.

name: Accessibility at The Caldecotte Xperience
description: For many people with SEND, their time at The Caldecotte Xperience can be life changing. We offer the largest range of accessible land and water-based outdoor education activities in the region for young people with disabilities- including those with the most complex needs. Our instructors and staff all have additional needs specialist training and are experiences in delivering sessions with varying support requirements so all activities can be enjoyed by everyone, whatever their ability. The freedom and exhilaration for a wheelchair user to be able to abseil is a triumph in itself, but we've also found that activities at the centre lead to long-term positive change in their self-belief and future aspirations. Special equipment for The Caldecotte Xperience: - Sailing- accessible sailboats so everyone can easily and safely participate in all water activities - Wheelyboat- a fully-accessible Wheelyboat (for wheelchair users and those with high dependency needs) - Inclusive activities- harnesses for adventure sports such as wheelchair abseiling We still have some winter availability left and are running a promotion on certain bookings before January 2025. Contact us using our email or telephone number to see how we can accommodate your class or group.
organisation: Action4Youth Action4Youth changes lives and creates better chances for young people by creating opportunities to discover their personal strengths and potential. We work with young people from all backgrounds and all abilities to make a real difference to their futures. We are a respected and dynamic charity based in Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes but reaching young people across the wider south east region. What we do Action4Youth is a leading delivery partner for the National Citizen Service (NCS) and consistently over delivers in terms of both quality and quantity. Action4Youth takes the strategic lead for the voluntary organisations supporting children and young people aged 5 – 25 years across its area. It has around 100 organisations in membership and offers a range of essential support and services. Our outdoor centre, Caldecotte Xperience in Milton Keynes, creates opportunities for young people to have amazing, challenging, fun and sometimes transformational experiences. They learn what they can do rather than what they can’t, building their confidence and self-belief. Action4Youth is the operating authority for Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes for Open Awards Groups for the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme. office@action4youth.org http://www.action4youth.org

name: Councillor Shadowing Scheme
description: Buckinghamshire’s Councillor Shadowing Scheme provides young people and local councillors with skills, experience, and insight, by giving young people and councillors an opportunity to get to know each other! Youth Voice Bucks is on hand with our Councillor Shadowing Guidance to make sure everyone feels able, confident, and well-equipped to take part. The scheme supports young people to become active citizens who can help to make Buckinghamshire the best place to live by: - Increasing young people's knowledge of politics and the decision-making processes that they can be a part of - Showing young people what being a councillor is like, which may lead to them becoming a councillor - Fostering young people's interests and engagement in elections - Developing councillors' understanding of issues facing young people and upskilling them to work with young people. Activities that young people and councillors can take part in together include: - About the Council – a meeting for the councillor to introduce the Council’s structure and function, its relation to other authorities such as Town and Parish Councils and central government, and elections - Councillor duties – the young person could shadow the councillor doing their resident surgeries, attending meetings, and going on visits Attending council meetings – such as Full Council, Scrutiny, and Sub-committee meetings - Tour – The councillor could give the young person a tour of Council buildings, their ward, and/or local venues/projects of interest - Training – Young people could come along to councillor training opportunities, for example with the governance team or the Local Government Association - Networking – The young person can attend events with the councillor to meet other councillors, council officers, professionals from partner organisations, and other people of interest - Young interviewer – The young person could write questions and interview the councillor and/or people of interest about their role and experiences to create a blog The Councillor Shadowing scheme is an opportunity for young people to develop themselves and their experiences. It can be especially useful for young people building up their CVs and personal statements, and those who are interested in careers in the public sector or Politics. Councillors and young people can express their interest by contacting us on the provided email address. Send us an email with you name and a little about yourself. We would love to know why you are interested in taking part.

We aim to engender a sense of community and belonging and to offer new opportunities to children and their families. We intend to support families to make informed choices and have greater control over services they wish to access. We aim to set out a local offer of services for children with Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities and their families. How do we support children? Listening to parents/carers and other professionals regarding their concerns. Listening actively to the views of the child and as far as possible involve them in their education. Provide a safe and caring environment and ensure that all children are treated with understanding, sensitivity and respect. • Ensure that all children who have special educational needs are quickly identified. Identify gifted and talented children and make provisions to meet their needs. Ensuring that all children’s needs are met by providing relevant resources and a differentiated curriculum. Implementing different and varied teaching practices to meet the needs of individuals and the different ways that individuals learn. Keeping staff fully informed and updated on individual children’s strengths and areas for development. Ensuring that children are referred to, and have access to specialist external professionals. Working as a multi-professional team to promote effective provision for individual children. Working with our allocated inclusion officer to support children and their families. Children identified as having special educational needs will have a SEN support plan which highlights individual targets. Targets will be set according to the child’s needs. These will be monitored and reviewed by the SenCo and discussed with parents / key person to identify the next steps. Providing individual and/or small group work where necessary to support children in different areas across the curriculum. Toileting programmes and provision of nappy changing facilities. Tailored intervention programmes as advised by external agencies such as a Speech Therapist, Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, the Specialised Teaching Service and the Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS) Provision of specialist equipment and toys, such as large-handled puzzle boards, sand timers, adult support scissors, wobble boards, and toys to support the development of fine and gross motor skills. Provision of a quiet room in the garden. The using of Makaton signing, visual timetables, and PECS. These are used during teaching sessions, target sessions and when singing nursery rhymes. At Henry Allen Nursery School we are committed to inclusion; we strive to develop policies and practices that include all children and their families. Our admission policy reflects our views, and no child with Special Educational Needs will be discriminated against. We aim to engender a sense of community and belonging and to offer new opportunities to children and their families. We recognise that children learn at different rates and that there are many factors affecting achievement, including ability, emotional well-being and age. We believe that many children at some time may experience difficulties which affect their learning, and we recognise that these may be long or short term. In accordance with the Disability Discrimination Act (2005), we aim to identify these needs as they arise and provide teaching and learning contexts which enable every child to achieve his or her full potential. We believe that all children have the right to be included in everything that takes place at the Nursery, and that inclusion happens when everyone feels appreciated and welcome to participate. We endeavour to make all nursery activities inclusive. We are lucky to be extremely well resourced across the Nursery, and children benefit from individual and small group support in our garden room. We support children with additional needs through SEN support plans, where children work towards personal targets often on a 1:1 basis or within a small group. The children are provided with specialised support by experienced and trained staff and are supervised by the SENCO. We work together as a team and in conjunction with external professionals, such as speech and occupational therapists. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Makaton Training Making Sense of Autism Autism Awareness Speech and Language Training ELSA Training Manual Handling (paediatric) Attention Autism Seeing Beyond Behaviour Down Syndrome Conference How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We listen to and value the views and opinions of children and their parents, believing that working together will produce the best possible outcomes for the children involved. Please look at the Buckinghamshire family information website for more details regarding our work with children with Special Educational Needs. Please feel free to contact any of the staff to discuss your child’s specific needs and requirements. For specific advice and expertise please contact the SENCO. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents are welcome to speak to their child’s key person at drop-off and pick-up and the SENCo is available at any time to discuss any concerns you may have. We additionally offer a settling-in consultation, 2-3 weeks after your child has started to discuss how they are getting on and allowing you to voice any concerns or worries that you would like to share. There are additional termly consultations and then a final written report for each child when they are transitioning to primary school. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The environment is completely accessible, our building was purpose-built in 2012. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?
