description: Chalfont St. Giles Memorial Hall was built in 1924 to commemorate the servicemen from the village killed in the Great War. It continues to be used for a variety of village activities. The Hall has its own car park and is an ideal venue for meetings and village activities. The main Hall measures approximately 13 metres by 9 metres and can accommodate up to 200 people. Seating is provided for up to 150. All events must finish by 11pm. There is a large kitchen with facilities for the provision of meals. The Hall may be hired for commercial and private events. Hourly rates are dependent on the type of hire and range from £35 down to £16 We began upgrading the audiovisual equipment in December 2024. This will benefit all Hall users who need audio or projection equipment. Please get in touch with us below to enquire about booking the Hall or any related queries.

We are great in all weathers and welcome well-behaved dogs on leads as well as children of all ages and we do our best to help our disabled customers.

name: Herschel Grammar School (Berkshire)
description: Mixed-gender selective secondary school in Slough, Berkshire for 11 to 18-year-olds. Herschel is a selective, co-educational secondary school serving Slough and its surrounding areas. In our latest inspection the school was deemed outstanding in all categories by Ofsted. Herschel has a warm and vibrant atmosphere built on an ethos of mutual trust, high academic standards and a commitment to nurturing and developing every individual pupil. We provide the very best opportunities to ensure every child achieves their potential. ‘Pupils thrive in the school’s academic, yet very caring and secure environment’ (Ofsted) And our pupils don’t just achieve very good examination results. Their progress between Year 7 and Year 11 places the school in the top 11% of schools nationally. The school’s success is built on genuine collaboration and partnership between governors, staff, pupils and parents; a partnership which has great aspirations for every child. Teachers have high expectations and work very hard to provide challenge and support. As Ofsted said in their verbal feedback the teachers are ‘enthusiastic, passionate and inspirational’. Pupils themselves have positive attitudes to learning and work well together. They take responsibility for their own behaviour and have strong emotional intelligence and empathy. As a result, our young people leave us as responsible, active citizens ready to contribute confidently to university, the workplace and their communities. There is a wealth of information on the website that I hope will help you to increase your understanding of the school and to serve as a first point of information.

description: Discover the world of science behind our botanical collections, with over 50,000 living plants to be found across our UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) World Heritage site. From the vast Arboretum to an Alpine rock garden, there's something to see in every corner. You can also enjoy tasty seasonal food and drink at our cafés and restaurants. Takeaway, indoor and outdoor seating available. We also have shops full of gorgeous homeware, award-winning books, stationary, and gift ideas. We are situated only 30 minutes from central London. description: Hills Cafe is a community cafe in the heart of Micklefield. The One Can Trust homework club runs on a Tuesday afternoon from 3.30pm to 5.30pm and offers a quiet space for parents and school age children to come and study. Each week, we offer a warm space and have tutors who are able to offer free grammar school entrance exam tuition, tuition for GCSEs, and SATs. Free coffee and tea are available for parents while they wait. (Parents must stay with children.) There are free resources to use, including laptops and printers, and each table has a variety of stationery to use. Please email the team on communitysupport@onecantrust.org.uk to express an interest.

name: Roman Park Hall
description: Roman Park Hall welcomes hirers and visitors from Berryfields and surrounding areas and offers a range of choices for community, commercial, and personal use. We cater for many different events from the smallest business meeting to big parties, events, corporate meetings, wedding receptions, engagement and christening parties, wakes, as well as children's parties up to 12 years of age. Our halls are fully equipped and the premises are fully licensed to serve alcohol and music. A bar and catering are available to hirers and their guests. With plenty of outside space to enjoy better weather and cosy spaces indoors, we are happy and able to tailor each event to exact requirements. We can arrange entertainment from bouncy castles to painting lessons, musicians, discos, staging, and decor. Full event management service available. We are situated on the outskirts of Aylesbury in Berryfields. We have plenty of free parking and are served by Aylesbury Vale Parkway rail station and local bus stops. Highlights - Licensed Bar - Village Hall (capacity 60) for smaller parties, classes, social gatherings, and more. - Kiosk with takeaway facility and arts centre adjacent to the cycleway. - Roman Park Hall (capacity 180 seated), Piazza access for outdoor seating. Conferencing facility for up to 220 delegates using modern AV system and catering. - Meeting room (capacity 10) with Audio Visual and business facilities. - Free Wi-Fi throughout the premises. - Full disabled access throughout with disabled parking spaces outside the entrance. - Tennis courts To book or find out more please call or email our office. We will arrange a visit where we can discuss your individual requirements and put a package together for you.

name: Thames Valley Violence Prevention Partnership
description: Established in 2019 and funded by the Home Office, our aim is to reduce the number of people affected by Serious Violence across the Thames Valley, working with our communities. We are a partnership body supported by a central programme team. We bring together representation from policing, local authority community safety, children's services and social care, prisons and probation, education, youth offending, and the voluntary and community sector. Our partnership covers the large and diverse Thames Valley area. Through our core programme team, we provide strategic leadership, coordination, and training and support the local response to Serious Violence under the umbrella of the Serious Violence Duty. We work with nine separate local partnerships which are consistent with the upper-tier local authority boundaries, covering all of Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire, Berkshire and Oxfordshire. Our central team oversees a programme of activity structured under the following standards: - Leadership and coordination - Testing interventions - Evaluating what works - Sustainable training - Data sharing Please visit our website to learn more.

description: Mind Over Mountains is an award-winning charity that helps people to overcome their mental health challenges through therapeutic outdoor experiences. Our specialist wellbeing walks and retreats bring together professionally guided hill-walking, mindfulness, and quality time with experienced coaches and counsellors. We work with individuals with a wide range of mental health challenges, including common forms of mental ill health (such as depression, anxiety, and stress), diagnosed mental illness (such as bipolar disorder, eating disorders, and phobias), and the impacts of trauma. description: Dare to Dream Pony Parties and Equine Activity Centre is a vibrant, inclusive provision that aims to provide a welcoming and positive experience to every individual we are lucky enough to meet on the yard. Our ponies are a much loved part of our Dare to Dream family and love to spend time supporting people, whether that be lending an understanding ear or sharing an apple! We specialise in working with children with SEND, including ASD, ADHD, behavioural needs and anxiety as well as those with high support needs. With the help our beautiful ponies, we firmly believe that all children, young people, and adults should have the space and opportunity to succeed. Our aim is to help individuals learn, achieve, and promote positive well-being by cultivating mindfulness and emotional agility, translating their work with horses into positive and sustainable actions. We can provide tailored and customised support programs for individuals from all backgrounds to facilitate personal progress and growth. If you can dream it, we'll sprinkle our magic to make it happen!

local_offer: Kiddies Cove Preschool is a private owned Nursery that caters for up to 45 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. Building positive relationships with the children and their families is very important to us. Here at Kiddies Cove Day preschool, we understand that every child is unique and we have high aspirations for all children. We encourage working together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Jo Ashmore has a level three certificate for Early Years Special Needs Coordinators in Private, Voluntary and Independent Settings. She completed this qualification in July 2021. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an inclusive environment where parents and carers can feel happy and confident communicating openly with us regarding their children. We are regularly available to have formal catch-ups with parents to discuss their child’s needs and provide term reports regarding each child’s progress that the key worker will discuss in detail with the parent. We speak daily with parents at drop off and pick up and communicate through our online parent app, Blossom Educational. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journal that parents/carers can look at any time by asking their child’s Key Person. Parents also see these at our informal parent's evenings that we hold twice a year. We will discuss progress when we complete termly key worker reports, through our 2-year-old progress checks and during our termly COHORT evaluations. For children with SEN, we try to ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and work together to plan new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take into account the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We try to create areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning and to create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing issues. Our setting has access to wheelchair uses on the ground floor and has a disabled toilet that is accessible for wheelchair users. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We would like to further our sensory resources by creating a sensory area in our soft playroom. We feel that this would benefit many of our children and help support their development.

description: Back in 1952, John and Christine Carter purchased Millets Farm, which was originally a dairy farm. Over the many years that have followed, the family has grown the farm into the site it is today. From investing in new infrastructure, landscaping, adding multiple attractions, and welcoming partners to the site. All whilst maintaining their central commitment to growing and producing the best quality food and providing the local community with a space to enjoy many memorable days out with their families. Now over 70 years later, two generations of the family continue to run Millets Farm on a day-to-day basis. Whilst the site may look different these days, the commitment to their farming heritage and the community remains that same. We host a variety of activities for children and young people throughout the year. Please visit our website for more information.

name: Baby Massage, Yoga, and Mums and Bumps
description: Here at mamadada, we offer a variety of services covering all stages of pregnancy and beyond. Our 3 main services are: Baby and Bumps Cafe- Where bumps, mums, and newborns meet for peer support and socialisation Baby Massage- suitable for babies 0 to 6 months old. Baby massage helps you to establish a warm, positive parent-child relationship. The nurturing touch helps the baby's emotional and physical development, it soothes and eases discomforts, colic, constipation, and teething. it also promotes relaxation and sleep and makes for a secure and confident child. Baby Yoga- suitable for babies 4 months to crawling. Baby yoga uses gentle stretches, massage, movement, and playful interaction providing the perfect balance of activity and relaxation. You will become familiar with baby yoga poses and sequences, relaxing holds, walks, lifts, swings, and dips alongside rhythm and rhyme. For mothers a few simple yoga moves to relieve physical and emotional tension, to strengthen and heal aiding a healthy postnatal recovery. No previous yoga experience is required. Please visit our website for more information and to book onto upcoming courses.
organisation: Amanda Baby Massage and Baby Yoga | Mamadada support Baby Massage A special time to share, learn how to massage your baby, group sessions, one to one or private groups in your home. The International Association of Infant Massage Course is designed for babies and infants, strokes are easy to learn, fun and they work. Amanda is an experienced midwife and therapeutic aromatherapist who is an independent infant massage therapist. The course is suitable for babies from 6 weeks old. Classes are relaxed and because of Amanda's profession include tips for mums to help with common problems such as colic, reflux, sleep. The emphasis is on teaching the baby to relax in response to touch and for mums to enjoy meeting others, to be able to relax themselves and have fun whilst learning a skill which makes the baby feel secure and nurtured. Everything provided for the course. Baby yoga has been designed for babies, it's fun and safe, suitable for 3 to 8 months. It encourages natural sensory, cognitive and physical development You learn baby yoga poses, relaxing swings and dips, giving baby strength and confidence through movement with rhyme and rhythm No previous yoga experience required, Birthlight baby yoga. Another great way to meet other mums and babies. Amanda offers Bumps drink and meet and newborn support and advice for parents. Amanda offers private therapeutic massage for children with disabilities and those with life-limiting illness specialising in oncology in their own homes. Currently, Amanda works for Rosie's Rainbow Fund at the John Radcliffe Children's Hospital supporting the families with seriously ill children, life-limiting illnesses and disabilities. amanda@mamadada.com https://mamadada.com

name: High Wycombe Chair Making Museum CIC
description: Visit our Chair Making Museum CIC at Kraft Village in High Wycombe. We are now a CIC company. Wycombe has a wonderful chair making heritage, we made 4,700 chairs a day here in 1875. Our Museum tour explains how the Bodgers in the local Beech woods cut and turned the round parts for the chairs, the Bench men that made the other chair parts and Framers that assembled the Windsor chairs. We include a demonstration of rounding a billet on the shave horse and show how a chair leg is turned on the pole and treadle lathes. Besides the various old tools, we also have a display of chairs and provide an explanation of the history and different types of Windsor chairs. Kraft Village also has a contemporary art gallery, craft gift shop and Kraftinwood wood-turning workshop, enquire about wood-turning lessons from Robert an RPT registered turner supported by the Worshipful Company of Turners.

local_offer: Any pupils identified as SEN are treated equally and given access to an appropriate curriculum. All teachers in the school are responsible for carrying out the agreed provision for children with SEN or a disability in their class. They must ensure that the child receives their entitlement in terms of a differentiated curriculum and the LSA support that enables the delivery of specialised programmes. The SENCO and other outside agencies may at times offer advice, guidance and support in order to ensure that the provision is tailored to accelerate the child’s learning. Types of support: In class support Pupils with an EHC plan are supported in class according to the requirements of the statement. If a pupil does not have an EHC plan, but has been identified on the SEN Support register, they will be offered support; for example in small groups activities if possible. Where a need is great or there is a significant barrier to learning a child may be taken out of class for a period of interventions. Interventions At High Wycombe Church of England school we have a wide variety of interventions which are used to support the pupils. These include interventions such as literacy and maths catch up, speech and language sessions and Fresh start. A decision would then be made by the class teacher, SENCO or Headteacher as to whether or not the pupil could attend. description: Our Online Gaming Counsellors are qualified Counsellors or Psychotherapists and are university-educated, trained, and experienced specialists and registered with a governing body. local_offer: We support SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) adults and children with, autism, Down syndrome, ADHD, acquired intellectual disabilities, intellectual challenges, mental health issues, anxiety, depression, or any issue that affects concentration or communication.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our gaming therapies boost confidence, social skills, and communication skills for participants, all while enjoying the game. The participant is guided to complete fun challenges with a qualified and experienced therapists working together to achieve the participants goals in line with their therapeutic needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our Gaming Therapy programs are designed for those that require tailored specialised care that can only be provided by a qualified, experienced and understanding Therapist who is also a registered Counsellor or Psychotherapist. The game acts as a familiar place for the participant so the therapist can provide effective therapy. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? organisation: Thomley We welcome disabled people of all ages from babies to adults, and their families, carers or friends. We support people at any stage of their diagnostic journey, whatever their additional needs. We offer regular days for disabled visitors and their families. We also offer focus days for preschool children, adults, schools, respite groups and the wider community when any family can join us to enjoy our facilities. Each day our friendly and experienced staff run fun and educational activities which cater for all ages and abilities. We are open 10am to 3:30pm, Tuesday to Saturday. In the school holidays we open on Mondays too. We also run evening youth clubs for disabled teenagers and take bookings for birthday parties and disability events. Take a look at our website to see when would be best to visit our website. local_offer: We are an inclusive setting. For children with SEN, we ask Buckinghamshire Early Years team to work in conjunction with us to ensure the child(ren) are receiving the best outcomes. We also attend SENCO liaison groups within the county.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have a key worker transition form that is filled out when each child moves between rooms, we liaise closely with parents and the local council to ensure we can provide the most up-to-date information to our parents and carers. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? There are two SEND staff on site. both who are passionate at getting the best start in life for these children in our nursery. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We consider parents to be partners and we welcome parent feedback and discussion throughout the child’s time at nursery. We use an app-based learning journey to track a child’s development and this includes parent interaction, which we encourage. We have formal opportunities for our parents at our bi-annual parents' evenings with their child’s key worker. We also have an open-door policy for our parents for informal chats upon the parents' request. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has an electronic learning journey to which the parents have unlimited access to. We discuss any progress made during parents' evenings as well as submitting assessments each term. Any child with SEN is given short-term targets for their individual SEN support plan, which are reviewed regularly by the key person, parents, and SENCO. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We always plan for each child within the rooms and take into account parent wishes and any plans in place. We have a separate sleep room for our babies, and a sensory room where children can regulate and have some rest bite if and when needed. We have a forest school programme which runs once each term for our preschool children. We have a large garden that is used throughout the year alongside our on-site allotment. We also ensure all activities are able to be moved outside so all children can participate indoors or outdoors. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We aim to develop the children though ensuring that the SEND staff are trained and are aware with the current affairs.

local_offer: As a dedicated childminder and nanny, I am committed to providing a nurturing and inclusive environment for all children, including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). My approach centres on understanding each child’s individual requirements, fostering their development, and promoting their well-being. Personalised Support: I offer tailored support to meet the unique needs of each child. This includes: • Individualised Learning Plans: I work closely with parents and relevant professionals to create personalised learning plans that cater to each child's specific strengths and challenges. • Flexible Activities: I provide a variety of adaptable activities to suit different abilities, ensuring every child can participate and benefit from the learning experience. This includes sensory play, arts and crafts, and outdoor activities that encourage exploration and social interaction. • Communication Support: I utilise various communication methods to ensure all children can express themselves. This may include visual aids, sign language, or alternative communication devices, depending on the child’s needs. Inclusive Environment: I strive to create an inclusive atmosphere where every child feels valued and accepted. This involves: • Diverse Resources: I incorporate a range of resources and materials that reflect diverse backgrounds and abilities, promoting understanding and acceptance among children. • Peer Interaction: I facilitate opportunities for children to interact with their peers in a supportive setting, encouraging the development of social skills and friendship.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My goal is to create a safe, engaging, and supportive environment where children with special educational needs and disabilities can thrive. By providing personalised support, fostering an inclusive atmosphere, and collaborating with families and professionals, I aim to empower each child to reach their full potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I am committed to ongoing professional development in SEND practices. This includes attending relevant training courses and workshops to stay informed about best practices and new strategies in supporting children with additional needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Collaboration with Families and Professionals: I believe in the importance of collaboration and open communication with families and other professionals involved in the child’s care. This includes: • Regular Updates: I provide parents with regular feedback about their child’s progress and development, as well as any challenges that may arise. • Partnerships with Specialists: I am open to working alongside specialists, such as speech therapists or occupational therapists, to ensure that the support provided is consistent and effective. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? This includes: • Regular Updates: I provide parents with regular feedback about their child’s progress and development, as well as any challenges that may arise. • Partnerships with Specialists: I am open to working alongside specialists, such as speech therapists or occupational therapists, to ensure that the support provided is consistent and effective. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Indoor and outdoor environments are accessible in my setting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? How to Access My Services for Children and Young People with SEND 1. Initial Inquiry: • Families can contact me via phone, or email to express their interest in my services. I encourage families to share any specific needs or concerns they may have regarding their child’s support requirements. 2. Consultation Meeting: • I offer an initial consultation meeting (in-person) to discuss the child’s individual needs, preferences, and any relevant background information. This meeting allows us to establish rapport and ensures that I understand the family’s expectations and the child’s unique requirements. 3. Assessment of Needs: • During the consultation, I may conduct a preliminary assessment to better understand the child’s strengths, challenges, and any specific support strategies that may be beneficial. Families are encouraged to share any existing assessments or reports from professionals (e.g., educational psychologists, therapists). 4. Creating an Individualised Support Plan: • Based on the information gathered, I will work collaboratively with the family to develop an Individualised Support Plan (ISP). This plan outlines the specific strategies, resources, and accommodations that will be implemented to support the child’s learning and development. 5. Trial Sessions: • I recommend scheduling trial sessions to allow the child to experience the environment and activities. This also helps families assess how well my approach aligns with their child’s needs. Feedback from these sessions will be used to make any necessary adjustments to the support plan. 6. Ongoing Communication: • Following the trial sessions, I will maintain open communication with families, providing regular updates on their child’s progress and any observations I have made. Families are encouraged to share their insights and concerns to ensure a collaborative approach. 7. Regular Reviews: • I will arrange regular review meetings with families to discuss the effectiveness of the support being provided, make any necessary adjustments to the ISP, and celebrate the child’s achievements. 8. Feedback and Suggestions: • Families are always welcome to provide feedback or suggestions regarding the service. I value their input and strive to create a responsive and adaptable service that meets the evolving needs of their child. 9. Accessing Additional Resources: • I can assist families in connecting with additional resources, such as local support groups, specialists, and community services that may enhance their child’s experience and support network. By following these steps, families can feel confident in accessing my services and know that their child’s unique needs will be met with care and professionalism. I am dedicated to creating a positive and inclusive experience for all children and their families. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am committed to ongoing professional development in SEND practices. This includes attending relevant training courses and workshops to stay informed about best practices and new strategies in supporting children with additional needs and developing my setting further.

We offer a wide variety of activities for the children to take part in and we do our best to adapt any activity to suit all needs so everyone can join in equally. At Highworth After school club/Breakfast club we aim to achieve a welcoming environment where both child and family feel comfortable discussing any issues they have so we can improve the care we give to each individual. By doing this and working along side the school we hope to achieve that the child feels comfortable at all times and gets to enjoy all activities that are on offer. organisation: Positive Psychology and Coaching for Parents and Children - Best Of You Consultancy I am passionate about helping parents when they need a little support as we all can at times. As a mother of six I understand some of the challenges. As a coaching psychologist I work with parents but also with teenagers or whole families. iI am the author of the kindle book ‘parenting the child with conduct disorder under author name Caralyn Bains, which provides a useful resource for parents. I also have a strengths based positive psychology book for parents on Amazon kindle. I was one of the first people in the UK to hold a Masters in Applied Positive Psychology (MAPP) from Buckinghamshire New University and this is my predominant focus or knowledge base that I use when coaching.My research interests are savouring and its application, mindfulness and resilience. I am a well-being practitioner and utilise my BSc (Honours) in Psychology with my knowledge base from the MSc in Applied positive psychology to enable clients to find their best version of themselves.

name: Hoarding Support Group
description: Hoarding support groups have proved successful in helping those with hoarding behaviour, as well as family and friends, know that they are not alone, and that support is available. The aim of this group is to bring people together who have experienced or are experiencing hoarding issues. This could be those with hoarding issues themselves, or friends, partners, or family of those currently experiencing hoarding. Within a safe, caring, and supportive environment group participants are invited to share experiences and to offer encouragement to others. You do not need to have a clinical diagnosis, or have a GP referral, to join these meetings. If you feel you are not coping with managing to maintain your home the way you would like, and this is causing you distress or concern, this group is for you.

As of the summer term 2021 we are also delivering Mind fullness and wellbeing programmes to all our families, our in house Well being therapist is able to deliver emotional well being for children identifying with PSE difficulties which in turn can lead to stress and anxiety. we are incredibly pleased to advise our parents that during the Summer term 2024 we accessed and qualified in ELSA training which will be embedded through the preschool day to support children that may find transitions, or emotional regulation difficult.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have a close working relationship with both private and NHS paediatricians and speak and language specialists. We are the first port of call in the process of setting up EHCP for the relevant children. We work closely with the health visitors team and children's services We have a close working relationship with the county inclusion team and our developmental work has been recognised by them. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? During the Summer term 2024, Karen was invited to participate and qualify in ELSA training, which helps aid children developing their emotional intelligence. Both Jodie Hawkes and Karen Hazell have obtained the recognised Level 3 SEN qualification through Aylesbury college in May 2020. Alongside Karen and Jodie all members of staff are actively encouraged and supported whilst engaging in ongoing training relating to all areas of special educational needs including Speech and Language, understanding Autism, Understanding behaviour management, supporting children's learning and development in a pre-school setting to name a few. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have regularly invite parents/carers to come along and read stories and help with cooking. We openly welcome the help from parents/carers with fund raising events. Some of our ex-parents are now members of staff, We thoroughly enjoy the little activity hunts that all family members can join in with bringing a community together. . As we continued to be advised we will continue to update our parents. parents can become involved in a number of ways, coming and helping with the allotments, orchard or outside areas is always eagerly embraced these jobs are less child interactive but help SO much. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We undertake regular feedback sessions with our parents once a term. We welcome parent key person exchange through email, however we are always available to have chat on the door. We also welcome regular consultations with our parents if they have an area of concern or just need some feedback. We offer family workshops to come in and chat about child niggles such as toilet training and sleeping patterns. We work very closely with our parents and should a need be identified a child's SEN plan is put in place, the plan identifies targets that the key practitioner will support the child to reach, as the child develops parents are communicated with regularly and encouraged to participate. Should a child not make sufficient progress we continue supporting both parents and their child to gain evidence of difficulties and begin to request help from other agencies with the view to close the learning gap. through out the whole learning process parents have access to all targets, Sen plans, professional reports and are actively encouraged to participate to all of the above We work in smaller groups with our SEND children to help them with their speech and language and socialising. We take these children around our farm on a daily basis where their interactions are further developed. We offer small pod group activities to enhance the children's listening and attention skills. As well as the smaller group work we also help and encourage our children to integrate with larger groups of children. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is all on one level with appropriate ramps to access outdoor facilities. We continue to reflect upon the children and families we cater for to ensure we provide a safe and welcoming setting for everyone. over the last five years we have adapted most areas of the preschool to make it inclusive for all abilities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have regular consultations with our parents and attend network meetings in order to highlight issues. On transitioning to school we are provided with the next educational environment - we consult with the new teacher and invite them to the setting to view the child in our setting and then, with parental permission, we meet with the new educational establishment and share our records with them. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are setting up new systems to help develop our children with their communication skills as well as behaviour and social skills. We are currently in the process of employing an independent speech and language therapist to work alongside families on site. We have just completed works for a fully integrated sensory pod for those children needing additional stimulation or a space where they can explore freely. Jodie and Karen have just completed the new recognised SEN qualification 2020.

local_offer: As a childminder and mother to two children with additional requirements. I am aware that some children may have additional needs and I must unsure that the appropriate action is taken when a child is identified as having additional requirements or starts in my care. I will promote the welfare and development of the child in partnership with parents and other relevant agencies. I provide equal opportunities for each child to learn and develop to their full potential. If I feel that a child in my care has a additional requirements i will: Keep observational notes and share these notes with the childs parents as soon as it is reasonably possible. Investigate and discuss what support is available and at all times keep things confidential. If I am caring for a child with additional requirements I will include them by: Valuing and acknowledging their individuality and help them to feel good about themselves. Obtaining information from parents about the child's routines, likes and dislikes. Ensuring that activities are adapted to enable all children to take part. I will arrange access to specialist equipment, where required and consider any potential risks. Encouraging the childs confidence and independence at all times. I will work in partnership with parents to discuss: Any agencies that may be able to advise or assist with their child's support and care. Equipment that the child may require. Any other support or assistance that may be available. I will consider how I can ensure the privacy of a child with additional requirements whilst continuing to care and supervise the other children in my care. I will regularly monitor, review and evaluate to ensure I am providing the best possible care for all children using my services.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I will liaise with other professionals (with the parent's consent) such as early years inclusion officer, speech and language therapists and health visitors to gain further advise in supporting each individual child. I will ensure that these targets and strategies are implemented. I will regularly with all involved review and update plans to benefit the support for all children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed a listening skills course with Flick online courses. I am also very knowledgeable about autistic spectrum disorders, ADHD, sensory processing disorder and dyslexia. I have gained this experience from my own children who have a combination of all of the diagnosis above. I have personal experience of how challenging it is to find the right setting for any child but even more so for a child with additional requirements which needs to specifically fit the needs of the child. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents communication is very valuable and I will work together with parents to ensure every childs learning and experience is supported and nurturing. At the initial settling sessions I will work closely with parents to settle the child into my setting. I will ask parents to fill in the all about me booklet and discuss with parents full so I can completely understand each childs unique routines, needs, interests and abilities. Parents are encouraged to work with me to complete observations and activities from home and communicating that with me so that I can incorporate that in activities that we plan within my setting. We will together regularly view the childs progress. Every child has a learning journey and can be viewed at any time. Parents are encouraged to add their views and comments. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We will regularly review childs progress and requirements. We can do this as much or as little is needed and that is no problem at all. We can share information in which ever form of communication your most comfortable with i.e. face to face, email, text. I will provide as much support to the parents and child so that they settle well, regularly ensuring that our resources and environment are suitable and accessible to all. I will differentiate resources, experiences and activities to support the child. I will plan for each individual child based around their abilities and interests. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There is access from the back and the front of the house and a downstairs toilet. unfortunately, the kitchen is on the second floor of our town house but we will make adaptions where we can if that is necessary. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I like to do as much free settling as necessary for a child to be settled when they start. Taking things at the child's pace. Some children need more than others so settling sessions are tailored to each individual child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am looking into online courses that will be helpful for supporting families with SEND.

description: The Quirky Wedding Fayre brings together the most unique wedding suppliers in a truly quirky venue to help make your wedding one of a kind. Are you fed up of going around wedding fairs and seeing hundreds of suppliers offering the same thing? Sick of feeling judged for wanting something different? We are too! That's why we created The Quirky Wedding Fayre. Your wedding should be all about you. Get ready to swap the traditional for the extraordinary as we invite you to explore a world of unique possibilities. From this incredible unique venue to unconventional vendors, discover a treasure trove of ideas to craft your one-of-a-kind day. Indulge in whimsical delights, mingle with fellow lovebirds, and let your imagination run wild. Join us for a day where love truly knows no limits, and where your happily ever after begins with a twist. Standard entry to all of our fayres is free! You can also opt for VIP tickets with bubbles, goody bags, and exclusive gifts. All of our fayres are inclusive and accessible for all! Our suppliers abide by our zero-judgement ethos to create a safe space for you! We understand that wedding fairs can be an overwhelming place full of lots of people and lots of noise! To assist those who may be anxious, overwhelmed or neurodivergent, the hour between 2pm and 3pm at our fayres will be Quirky Quiet Hour. Quiet Hour is an individually ticketed timeslot where those who need a quieter browsing experience can attend. Please visit our website for upcoming Fayres.

name: Online Adaptive Box-Fit Class
description: Join WheelPower and Luiz Faye for a free online Adaptive Box-Fit Class from the comfort of your homes live on Zoom. Luiz Faye will be your fitness trainer for this live class from WheelPower. During this online class, Luiz will be taking us through a 40-minute workout that includes a short warm-up and warm-down. The new Adaptive Box-fit classes are the perfect introduction to the sport with no equipment needed, and are suitable for most people who are unable to participate in boxing from a standing position. The sessions are designed to incorporate functional fitness, strength, and conditioning; paying particular attention to the transfer of adaptive boxing skills and drills to increase core stability, mobility, and overall upper-body strength. Although all our sessions feature an element of adaptive boxing, experience is not necessary. In fact, you don’t even need to take the sport out of your living room so there’s no pressure to jump in the ring! Consider it to be boxing moves for the functional benefits and not for the fight! All the exercises are done from a seated position and can be adapted to suit varying abilities and fitness levels. You must, however, be guided by your body and work out to suit your needs safely. All you need is a laptop/computer or phone with access to Zoom, and a bottle of water. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Talkback - The Post-16 Specialist Provision
description: Equip offers young people between 16 and 25 personal support programmes in colleges and community. With over 25 years of experience, Talkback offers a nurturing, flexible alternative to other traditional education settings, designed specifically for young people with an EHCP, aged 16 to 25, who are autistic or have a learning disability. We have a track record of supporting young people to succeed. Over 540 students have successfully completed our programme over the last 10 years, reaching their aspirations and personal and academic goals. Engage. Educate. Employ. Our Pathways Talkback aims to support young individuals, who may struggle in the traditional education system, to thrive. Talkback’s educational programme integrates life skills, personal, and social development, and preparation for working life. This is combined with accreditation in English and Maths. Digital Skills are also embedded in our study programmes. Through personalised learning pathways and supported work experience with local and national employers, as well as Travel Training, Talkback supports young people to build independence and achieve their goals. Talkback students can also achieve qualifications in work related areas, with every individual being supported as needed. Engage A bespoke programme for young people aged 16 to 25 who are not in education, employment or training (NEET), or Post-16 re-engagement for young people who are home-schooled and need support transitioning to the next phase of their lives. We help them re-engage with others in a safe and effective manner. Duration: 12 to 36 weeks. Focus Areas - Pathways into education and employment. - Personalised pace for development. - Safe, supportive environment for personal and educational growth. Educate For 16 to 25 year olds seeking a nurturing environment with smaller group sizes to build essential life and work/volunteering skills. Duration: 1 to 2 years. Focus Areas - Life Skills: Money management, social development, anxiety management, communication, and travel training. - Qualifications: Functional Skills in English and Maths (Entry Level 1 to Level 2). - Work Readiness: Building confidence for employment through a unique, rotating work experience programme with local and national employers. Employ A supported internship for 18 to 24 year olds with an EHCP, aimed at leading to paid employment. Duration: 1 year, 3 days a week. Focus Areas - To build on previous work experience and help achieve realistic career aspirations, that enable Talkback to find suitable employment opportunities. - Workplace training and suitable qualifications relevant to future employment. To find out more visit our website.
organisation: Talkback Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update Following the announcement by the Prime Minister on 4 January 2021, the UK entered a new national lockdown. We regret to announce that our building-based services are currently closed. Talkback will continue to operate a full virtual service to its students and members. Stay safe everyone. We are still here for you. With over 21 years of experience working in Buckinghamshire, and roots in self-advocacy, Your Voice works to give people self-confidence, self-esteem, and a voice. We support people to think about what their life is like, how they would like it to be, and if there’s anything missing. We work for and with people with learning disability or autism. Our roots are in self-advocacy and this has allowed us to develop consultancy support around a whole range of life solutions. We build self-confidence and self-esteem to enable people with a learning disability and autism to Use the skills that will enhance their quality of life Be as independent as they are able and want to be. We want to see respect for all people with a learning disability and autism. Outcomes we have seen Increased confidence and self-esteem Decreased social isolation Engagement in the planning and development of statutory and non-statutory services Increased engagement in their local communities Informed choice making Network of social and life skills groups Voices feeding into local/national government, health, and support providers to effect positive change in quality of life What we offer professionals Consultancy and research around areas of: Care Act and community advocacy Co-production and consultation Community engagement One-off consultancy services Life-long support services Co-facilitated training for frontline services Expert by experience and quality checkers Self-advocacy workshops Health passports Easy read talkback@talkback-uk.com https://talkback-uk.com/our-services/supporting-professionals/

local_offer: Holmer Green First School and Pre-School is committed to providing a quality education for all pupils, including those with SEND and values all children equally. We believe that all children have individual needs, strengths and talents, which should be met through an inspirational school curriculum and high quality teaching which allows each child to work at their own level and pace. In order to achieve this, some children will require additional support or challenge in school. We strive to remove any barriers to learning which could hinder or exclude individual pupils. We believe that all children should feel safe and valued in school and work hard to eliminate prejudice and discrimination. We support the development of the whole child, whilst valuing and celebrating the many and varied abilities displayed by all children. Holmer Green First School and Pre-School currently caters for children with a range of SEND needs and we are happy to discuss individual requirements. We strongly encourage parents to make an appointment with the Headteacher before applying for a school place to ensure specialist provision can be put in place. Currently we can offer: • A flat, wheelchair accessible site with a disabled toilet. • Experience of successfully including children who have autism, are partially sighted, have significant hearing loss, have physical co-ordination difficulties, as well as those that have speech and language difficulties. https://www.holmergreenfirst.co.uk/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff regularly participate in SEND training throughout the academic year. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are keen to work closely with parents. Please see the Annual SEND Report (Local Offer) for more information. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There are no parts of the school to which disabled pupils have limited or not access as the site is flat and single storey. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children access specialist provision whenever they need it and this may start at any points during the school year. If you are interested in finding out more about how our school supports children with SEND or you would like to discuss any SEND needs your child may have before they start our school, please contact the school office to make an appointment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: We are a mainstream Junior School that works to provide support based on need. Please see the link to the school website for more information. https://www.hgjs.co.uk/page/?title=SEND%2FInclusion&pid=18 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Holmer Green Junior School is committed to providing quality education for all pupils, including those with SEND. We believe that all children have individual needs, strengths, and talents, which should be met through an inspirational school curriculum which allows each child to work at their own level and pace, while being appropriately challenged. We recognise that to achieve this, many children will require additional support or additional challenge throughout time in school. We believe that all children should be equally valued in school. We strive to eliminate prejudice and discrimination and to remove any barriers to learning which could hinder or exclude individual pupils. We believe that all children should feel safe and valued in school and support the development of the whole child, whilst valuing and celebrating the many and varied abilities displayed by all children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Recently, we have completed training focused on adapting learning. Members of staff also receive training based on the needs of children they are working with. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We believe that communication with parents is key. We have worked hard to improve our communication, particularly surrounding Inclusion. We host SEND and pastoral coffee mornings throughout the year. Our Inclusion team has expanded which means parents/ carers have a wider range of staff they can talk to if they need to. If parents/carers have any Inclusion questions, they should email sen@hgjs.co.uk for further information. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents Evenings are held in the Autumn and the Spring term. In the Summer term, every parent/carer receives an annual report about their child. In addition to this, support plans are sent home 3 times per year for pupils on the SEND register. At the end of the academic year, a transition meeting is also held for pupils who have children on the SEND register. Meetings can be made with members of the Inclusion team through the SEND email address whenever needed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our playground is easily accessible from the school via a slope. We have a lift which enables pupils to reach the Year 5/6 area in the school. Both sets of downstairs girls toilets include a disabled toilet cubicle. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If you would like to discuss our facilities or have any queries, please contact us via sen@hgjs.co.uk . What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As a school, we feel it is essential that we are continually monitoring and assessing to identify where adjustments can be made. This year, our focus is on ensuring that all pupils have the correct amount of challenge throughout the curriculum. Moving forward, we will be continuing to ensure that all staff have a range of training.

local_offer: Holmer Green First School and Pre-School is committed to providing a quality education for all pupils, including those with SEND and values all children equally. We believe that all children have individual needs, strengths and talents, which should be met through an inspirational school curriculum and high quality teaching which allows each child to work at their own level and pace. In order to achieve this, some children will require additional support or challenge in school.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We strive to remove any barriers to learning which could hinder or exclude individual pupils. We believe that all children should feel safe and valued in school and work hard to eliminate prejudice and discrimination. We support the development of the whole child, whilst valuing and celebrating the many and varied abilities displayed by all children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We recognise that training is essential if staff are to meet a wide range of diverse needs. All staff receive training opportunities in relation to their personal needs and the children they are working with. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are encouraged to share concerns they have with the school at the first opportunity. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Working closely with parents is very important to us if our children with SEND are to learn and thrive. We actively seek to engage parents in their children’s learning process and value parental input and insight. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Appropriate support and procedures are put in place so that all children can participate in enrichment activities. If any individual has a need for specialist equipment or facilities the Inclusion Leader will be happy to discuss this and liaise with the local education authority’s SEND department and the specialist teaching service. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? If a pupil is deemed to have significant needs the school may apply to the Local Education Authority for Higher Needs Block Funding or an Education, Health Care Plan.

organisation: Holmer Green Senior School I welcome you to the Holmer Green Senior School (HGSS) website. HGSS is an 11 – 18 academy situated in Holmer Green Village. description: Fun Fest holiday club is different, we offer children the choice about how they spend their holidays. local_offer: Holy Trinity School is a mainstream setting. At Holy Trinity School we will ensure that all children are valued equally, regardless of their abilities and/or social, emotional or behavioural problems. The school recognises that all children are entitled to have access to a broad and balanced curriculum which is differentiated to meet their individual needs. Additional needs or disabilities which can affect a child’s ability to learn can include: behavioural/social (difficulty making friends) reading and writing (dyslexia) understanding things concentrating (Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder) physical needs or impairment. Full details of the school's contribution to the Local Offer can be found in our SEN Annual Report available through this listing. https://holytrinityandlittlemarlowfederation.org.uk/HolyTrinity/School-Policies/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Holy Trinity is a church aided Junior School which takes pupils from Marlow C.E. Infants and Little Marlow C.E. schools as well as pupils from other schools in the local area. The Governing Body of the school, not Buckinghamshire Local Education Authority (the LA), is responsible for deciding on admissions to the school, but works closely with the LA who coordinate admissions to all maintained schools and academies in Buckinghamshire. Details of the LA arrangements for entry to Year 3 are in the Buckinghamshire ‘Guide for Parents’ booklet, available from the Buckinghamshire Council Website. Applications for entry to Year 3 at Holy Trinity C.E. (A) School will be dealt with under the Buckinghamshire Co-ordinated Scheme for Primary Admission. In-year admissions are also coordinated through Buckinghamshire LA and the application form is available through their website. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Holy Trinity actively seeks to improve its services and facilities for all pupils including those with SEND. Full details can be found in the School's Annual Improvement Plan which is available to view by request to the Headteacher.

name: Broadwater Sailing Club
description: We are a friendly, dinghy sailing club offering every day access to Broadwater Lake for members and regular racing on Sunday mornings and Wednesdays (mornings in the winter, evenings in the summer) plus open meetings, regattas and social events. The club has a large boat park and accepts all monohull dinghies up to 16'. We run an active Junior Sailing training programme for children aged 5 and above on Saturday mornings from May to late September (except August) and 'fun days' during the first week of the school summer holiday. Visitors are welcome by prior arrangement because our access road has a locked gate. Many people will be familiar with the site because it's the lovely lake with islands that can be viewed from the car park of the Old Orchard in Harefield.

name: MK Gallery
description: MK Gallery brings world-class exhibitions and events together with pioneering learning and community programmes to Milton Keynes. This expanded building, which launched in 2019, features an independent café and shop, a Curzon cinema, and spectacular views over Campbell Park. Three major exhibitions are presented annually across five elegant and spacious galleries, from thematic group exhibitions to in-depth solo presentations. Alongside our exhibitions, we offer workshops, talks, and conferences, mixing emerging and locally based talent with established names. We also deliver a weekly film programme featuring the best of independent cinema in partnership with Curzon. We offer schools and family activities throughout the year and our artist-designed play area is open 365 days a year. MK Gallery works with partners locally, nationally, and internationally to bring the best cultural activities into the region. The Gallery is part of the Arts Council’s National Portfolio and a member of the Plus Tate network.

name: Hope Cafe at Restore Hope
description: Are you a local parent who needs a place to relax, chat and meet other people? Then Hope Cafe is the place to be every Tuesday morning in The Dairy. Hope Cafe is a safe space to come and enjoy limitless coffee, tea and toast for parents (pre-schoolers welcome). We aim to provide friendly support, a listening ear, laughter, and encourage meaningful friendships to form. Hope Cafe is the core element of our Hope Hub and provides signposting and a pathway to our own family support (Circle of Security parenting course, other personal development courses for parents), family activities, one-to-one support, volunteering opportunities, and signposting to other agencies as appropriate. We can provide a minibus (subject to availability) to those who live in the Little Chalfont, Amersham, and Chesham areas. Restore Hope is a Christian charity formed in 2002 and our team openly lives our faith and will offer prayer in Hope Cafe.
organisation: Restore Hope Restore Hope Latimer is a family focused charity based at Latimer Park. A special space in the countryside set in the heart of the Chilterns, just outside Amersham and Chesham and has been operating since 2002 and has a proven record of bringing change and help to people in need. We believe in the value of healthy, happy and stable families. We also believe that no matter how bad a situation may seem there is always hope. Our vision is therefore that every struggling family in the Chilterns finds help and hope for the future. This is clearly a big aim and one that requires us to continually increase our influence, effectiveness and reputation. We aim to achieve our vision by advancing and developing the programmes that we offer and continually looking for ways to engage with those most in need. We operate a clear strategy, with deliberate focus and dogged determination. We empower and equip key volunteers to lead various elements of our work, and support a motivated core staff team. RHL seeks to make best use of the fantastic facilities that Latimer Park offers and, where appropriate, grows into other spaces in the community to offer easy access to our programmes and to further develop the reputation of the charity. naomi.meech@restorehopelatimer.org http://www.restorehopelatimer.org

name: FLYERZ Hockey
description: In partnership with Access Sport and England Hockey, we are launching FLYERZ Hockey in Spring 2025. FLYERZ Hockey is the name widely associated with disability-inclusive hockey in England. FLYERZ Clubs are friendly and inclusive, welcoming disabled and non-disabled people of all ages and abilities as well as their families. The sessions and equipment are adapted to ensure inclusivity of any disability and long-term health condition. This disability-inclusive program, for young people aged 7 to 16, offers player-centered sessions focusing on fun, skill development, and promoting an active lifestyle. Sessions are tailored with adapted equipment and led by our volunteer SEN specialist coach, supported by volunteers with personal experience in SEN and disability. Our clubhouse and pitch are fully accessible with nearby disabled parking. For more information and to sign up for our taster sessions please contact Emily on the email address provided.

name: Hope UK | Drug education and training charity
description: Children and young people are at the heart of Hope UK’s mission. For more than 160 years, we have equipped young people to make drug free choices, working with groups and individuals in formal and informal settings helping them develop the knowledge and skills they need to live healthy lives. Our trained volunteers and staff, who work with children and young people in schools and youth groups, provide interactive, age-appropriate educational sessions about drugs. Life skills that build confidence, enhance peer resistance, and develop helpful, transferable skills are woven into sessions designed to encourage healthy choices and enable children and young people to realise their potential. Drug Education: As well as bespoke sessions and workshops for groups, we run informal drug education in libraries, local high streets, and other public places, engaging with members of the public and allowing them to explore drug issues in a safe and non-judgemental way. Young People: Our youth organisation, Generation Hope enables young people to get involved with Hope UK in a variety of ways from attending residential weekends and skill development workshops to representing the organisation. We are always welcoming new young people to come to our events, search for Hope UK or Generation Hope on Eventbrite. Training: We also offer training for adults who work with or have contact with young people, for example, youth workers, parents, social workers, teachers, and street pastors. “Habits adopted in the teenage years can form behaviour for a lifetime. For example, adolescent binge drinkers are twice as likely as their peers to be dependent on alcohol or taking illicit drugs by the time they reach 30 years, while someone who starts to smoke aged 15 is three times more likely to die of smoking-related cancer than someone who starts smoking in their 20s.” Sir Liam Donaldson, former Chief Medical Officer.

name: Child Weight Management with Be Healthy Bucks
description: At Be Healthy Bucks we offer face-to-face and online support for children over a healthy weight. This support includes engaging and fun discussions on healthy eating and some physical activity led by our fitness coach. From dodgeball and games to stretches and intentional exercise, there is something for everyone! Is my child eligible? Your child must be aged between 4 to 13 (extended from 7 to 13 years), with a BMI over the ninety-first centile. Families who complete the programme are also offered a leisure centre membership for the whole family, including: - 6 months’ membership at selected leisure centres (the first 3 months fully subsidised and the following 3 months partially subsidised) - Access to both wet and dry activities such as swimming, soft play, and gym use for adults.” Exclusions: - Our programme isn’t suitable for children or young people with an eating disorder or an underlying medical cause for obesity - Children with more complex needs, such as learning difficulties or mental health issues, will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please visit our website to learn more.

We can also support you with the emotional challenges of managing your long term condition, and support families to manage a child’s weight. We are experts in working with members of the public and supporting them to make changes to their lifestyles that lead to a healthier life.  https://www.livewellstaywellbucks.co.uk/

description: Offers a transportation service for individuals with mobility challenges in Haddenham and nearby villages. Journeys should be booked in advance by calling or emailing a week or so before your journey. Our co-ordinator will discuss your needs: the date, time and address for pick-up; destination; wheelchair need (we can provide one) and so on. The coordinator will seek a volunteer driver from our team and, once secured, your booking will be confirmed. Short notice bookings may be difficult to accommodate. The bookable service is provided free of charge within our defined area. We welcome clients from Haddenham and all the surrounding communities within the area shown below. Our destinations can be up to a maximum of 20 miles radius from Haddenham. Typical journeys are within a range which includes Aylesbury, High Wycombe, Amersham and Oxford.
