local_offer: At Care at Your Home | Domiciallcry Care, we understand that caring for a loved one with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) requires a holistic approach that supports both the individual and their family. Our domiciliary care services provide tailored assistance to ensure a safe, nurturing, and empowering environment at home. Through personalised care, specialist interventions, and a commitment to fostering independence, we strive to enhance the well-being of the entire family unit. https://www.careatyourhome.co.uk/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Care at Your Home, our Domiciliary Care service for children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) aims to achieve the following outcomes: - Personalised & Compassionate Care: Providing tailored, one-to-one support that meets the unique needs of each child, ensuring comfort, safety, and well-being in their home environment. Promoting Independence & Life Skills: This involves Encouraging children and young people to develop daily living skills and fostering confidence and self-sufficiency. - Family Support & Respite Care: Offering practical assistance to families, including respite care, to give parents and caregivers time to rest while knowing their child is in safe hands. Consistency & Routine: Helping to establish and maintain structured daily routines that support stability and positive behaviour. Social & Community Engagement: Assisting children in accessing social activities and integrating into their communities, promoting inclusion and interaction. Specialist Care & Assistance: Supporting children with physical disabilities, sensory impairments, or complex health needs by providing personal care, mobility assistance, and medication support where required. Collaborative Approach: Working alongside families, schools, and healthcare professionals to ensure a cohesive and holistic approach to care. Our dedicated domiciliary care service aims to enhance the quality of life for children and young people with SEND while empowering families with the support they need. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? At Care at Your Home, we are committed to ensuring our staff receive ongoing training to provide high-quality care for children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Our in-house Specialist Trainer offers SEND-specific training, which includes: - Understanding SEND & Inclusive Care: Providing foundational knowledge on various special educational needs and disabilities, ensuring staff can deliver personalised and compassionate care. - Supporting Communication & Social Interaction – Training on effective communication strategies, including using visual aids and other alternative communication methods. - Managing Challenging Behaviours: Equipping staff with specialist techniques to recognise triggers, de-escalate situations, and promote positive behaviour support. - Sensory Awareness & Adaptations: Helping staff understand sensory processing differences and how to create a supportive environment for children with sensory needs. Personal Care & Mobility Support: Training on assisting children with physical disabilities, including safe manual handling, use of assistive equipment, and promoting independence. Autism Awareness & Support Strategies: Providing insight into autism spectrum conditions and practical approaches to support children effectively. Safeguarding Children with SEND: Reinforcing the importance of safeguarding, recognising vulnerabilities, and ensuring a safe and supportive care environment. Investing in continuous in-house training ensures our team is well-equipped to provide specialist care that meets the diverse needs of children and young people with SEND. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Care at Your Home, we believe that parents and families play a vital role in the care and well-being of children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). We actively involve parents in the care process through: - Personalised Care Plans: We work closely with parents to create tailored care plans that reflect their child's unique needs, preferences, and routines. - Regular Communication & Updates: We maintain open and ongoing communication through phone calls, meetings, and written reports to ensure parents are informed and involved in their child’s progress. - Parental Feedback & Involvement in Decision-Making: We encourage parents to share their insights and feedback to continually improve our services and ensure the best outcomes for their child. - Family Training & Support – We offer guidance and practical advice on care techniques, behaviour management, and other relevant skills to empower families in supporting their child at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At Care at Your Home, we prioritise open and transparent communication with parents to ensure they are fully informed about their child’s care and progress. We provide updates through: - Daily Care Reports: A summary of your child’s daily activities, well-being, and notable observations. - Regular Check-Ins: Scheduled phone calls or in-person meetings to discuss progress and any concerns. - Progress Reviews & Updates: Formal progress reviews where we assess care plans and adjust support as needed. - Emergency & Immediate Updates: If any urgent concerns arise, we will contact you immediately. - Individualised Care Plans: Regularly reviewed and updated to reflect your child's evolving needs. - Multi-Professional Coordination: Liaising with therapists, educators, and healthcare providers to ensure a holistic approach to care. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? At Care at Your Home, we provide care in familiar home environments, ensuring accessibility is tailored to the specific needs of each child and family. While we do not operate from a fixed centre, we work closely with families to create a safe, accessible, and comfortable space within their own homes. Our approach to accessibility includes: - Indoor Accessibility Support Home Environment Assessments: We provide guidance on making the home safer and more accessible for children with mobility challenges or sensory needs. - Assistance with Daily Living: Our caregivers support children with movement, transfers, and positioning to promote comfort and independence. - Adapted Communication Methods: For children with communication difficulties, we use visual aids and other alternative communication methods to enhance accessibility. Outdoor Accessibility Support - Support for Community Engagement: Our staff assist children in accessing outdoor spaces, participating in social activities, and attending appointments safely. - Transport & Mobility Assistance: We provide support for families in coordinating accessible transport for outings, school, or therapy sessions. - Safe & Inclusive Outdoor Activities: Where possible, we work with families to facilitate safe outdoor play and social interaction. Tailored Accessibility Solutions We recognise that every child’s needs differ, and we work closely with parents to adapt care to their home environment and outdoor activities. If additional accessibility modifications or specialist equipment are required, we can liaise with occupational therapists and local services to help families obtain the right resources. We aim to ensure that children and young people with SEND can thrive in a barrier-free, supportive environment—both at home and in the community. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? At Care at Your Home, we strive to make our services accessible and tailored to the unique needs of children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Families can start using our services through the following steps: 1. Initial Contact & Inquiry Parents or guardians can contact us via phone, email, or our website to express interest in our domiciliary care services. We provide an overview of our support options and answer any initial questions. 2. Needs Assessment & Consultation We schedule a free consultation to understand the child’s specific needs, preferences, and family requirements. Our team works closely with parents to identify the right level of care and support. 3. Personalised Care Planning Based on the assessment, we create an individualised care plan outlining the type of support required, from personal care to social engagement and mobility assistance. We ensure the care plan aligns with any existing education, health, and therapy support the child is receiving. 4. Service Agreement & Onboarding Once the care plan is finalised, we discuss schedules, introduce key caregivers, and agree on a start date. Families receive guidance on what to expect and how to communicate any updates or changes. 5. Ongoing Support & Review We provide continuous monitoring and regular reviews to adapt the care plan as the child’s needs evolve. Parents are encouraged to provide feedback and stay actively involved in their child’s care journey. Referral Options Families can self-refer or be referred by local authorities, healthcare professionals, or social services. We collaborate with schools, therapists, and other professionals to ensure seamless care coordination. If you are interested in learning more or starting the process, contact us today at 01494 977 397 to discuss how we can support your child and family. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? At Care at Your Home, we are committed to continuously improving and expanding our domiciliary care services for children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Our future plans include: - Expanding Specialist Training for Staff Enhancing in-house training on autism, ADHD, sensory processing disorders, and complex medical needs. Providing advanced behaviour management and communication support training, including Makaton and assistive technology use. - Introducing More Personalised & Flexible Support Options Offering more flexible care packages to accommodate changing needs. Enhancing Collaboration with Professionals & Families - Strengthening partnerships with schools, therapists, and healthcare providers to ensure a holistic approach to care. Increasing parent workshops and support groups to provide families with practical skills and peer support. Technology-Enhanced Care - Implementing digital care plans and communication platforms to provide real-time updates to families. Exploring the use of assistive technology to enhance independence and engagement for children with SEND. Developing Community-Based SEND Activities - Expanding opportunities for social engagement, including supported outings and community activities tailored for children with SEND. Introducing group sessions for social skills development and sensory play. Advocating for Greater Inclusion & Awareness - Running awareness campaigns to promote inclusive care practices. Working with local authorities and SEND networks to improve access to quality home care services. Our goal is to ensure every child with SEND receives compassionate, high-quality care that supports their independence, well-being, and family life. We welcome feedback from families to help shape our future plans—get in touch to share your thoughts at info@careatyourhome.co.uk.

name: Hughenden Manor | National Trust
description: Set in an unspoiled Chiltern valley with views of ancient woodlands and rolling hills, Hughenden offers a restful retreat from the pressures of everyday life, just as it did for Victorian Prime Minister, Benjamin Disraeli, and his wife Mary Anne. Outside, the surrounding views of the parkland invite you to explore the estate, following picturesque walking trails that take in the historic landscape of the Chiltern beech woods. In contrast to the exotic trees on the North Lawn, the Italianate formal gardens showcase annual beds full of the bold colours the Disraelis loved. Inside the manor, you can discover the top-secret Second World War operation codenamed ‘Hillside’. This venue was visited on Tuesday 2 June 2026 by Buckinghamshire Council's SEND Young Inspectors. name: National Paralympic Heritage Trust
description: The National Paralympic Heritage Trust was established in July 2015 to protect and share British Paralympic Heritage. We exist to enlighten and inspire future generations by celebrating, cherishing, and bringing the Paralympic heritage and its stories of human endeavour to life. In our role as caretakers of the World’s most important disability history collections, the Paralympic movement, we aim to become, and help others become seamlessly inclusive. We have created accessible and inclusive learning resources that are free for families and schools to download on our website, and we run events in the community throughout the year.
organisation: National Paralympic Heritage Trust National Paralympic Heritage Centre is widely acknowledged as the birthplace of the Paralympic movement, Stoke Mandeville Stadium is the home of the first National Paralympic Heritage Centre. Our small Museum brings the history of the Paralympics and its stories of human endeavour to live. The story begins in the late 1940s at Stoke Mandeville Hospital where Professor Sir Ludwig Guttmann encouraged wounded veterans to play sport as an aid to rehabilitation from spinal injury. This led to local competitions, to the Stoke Mandeville Games, and to the Paralympic Games which today attracts national and international public support and interest. The interactive displays include: The life and work of Professor Sir Ludwig Guttmann Key milestones in the journey from the 1948 Stoke Mandeville Games to the present day Paralympic Games The development of wheelchair sports Paralympic ceremonies Visitor Information: You can visit us virtually Free Admission Open daily for the general public School and group bookings available Audio and BSL Tours available Please visit our website for more information about accessibility and family activities. admin@paralympicheritage.org.uk https://www.paralympicheritage.org.uk/Event/heritage-centre

local_offer: Hughenden Primary School provides a holistic, personalised, education which is underpinned by quality teaching throughout. Our aim is for each child to fulfil their whole potential and develop lifelong skills; supporting, encouraging, and challenging every child to recognise their achievements and build on their individual strengths. We understand that for some children there are times during their school life when additional support may be needed. We are very proud of the excellent relationships we have built both with parents and with a wide range of outside agencies which enables us to meet the needs of individuals when a potential special educational need has been identified. https://www.hughendenprimary.co.uk/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs+%26amp%3B+Disabilities+%28SEND%29&pid=23 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our school is an inclusive setting where every child is valued. We aim to address children’s needs and support their development in the most appropriate way possible and celebrate effort and progress as much as achievement and attainment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff have received training on support plan writing/graduated approach, Attachment, Role of the LSA, Behaviour, Ordinarily Available Provision, Dyslexia, Autism, Sensory Circuits. Staff have been trained in the Buckinghamshire Steps positive behaviour programme and the SENDCo is a Buckinghamshire Steps tutor. We have a trained Nurture Practitioner and Emotional Literacy Support Assistant. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are proud of our open-door policy and encourage parents/carers to speak to staff about any concerns they might have. Our SENDCo is very happy to meet by appointment. Children with SEND will have an Individual Learning Plan written with them and their parent/carer and reviewed every term. Recommendations for new outcomes will be discussed alongside suggestions for supporting their child in the home setting, where appropriate. Some pupils who are being supported by a specific LSA will require more frequent communication with the parent/ carer and it may be appropriate to use a communication diary. Pupils with an EHCP will have an additional, formal Annual Review (an Interim Review may be set up if deemed necessary). Parents and children are invited to these meetings. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? You will be invited to termly ILP Meetings with the SENDCo in addition to two Parents' Evening appointments with the class-teacher. Children are assessed individually for needs by professionals involved with their education and progress is monitored on a regular basis by the class teacher and SENDCo. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Hughenden Primary is situated on a small, level site with good access for wheelchair users and those with restricted mobility. We have a two hard surface playgrounds and a large, level field for sports activities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Admission inline with County Admissions policy. Provision is then provided through discussion with Headteacher and SENDCo tailored to match individuals needs where appropriate, within a mainstream setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently undertaking a project to build a 'Calm Room,' where our Social, Emotional and Mental Health interventions will take place. These include Nurture, Lego Therapy, Check-Ins and Play Therapy.

local_offer: The Hughenden Valley Pre-School embraces all children and will strive to enable each child to access and enjoy his/her pre-school experience with the appropriate level of support which meets his/her individual need.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Larina, our SENDCO has experience in supporting children with a range of SEND, including Autism and speech and language needs. She has liaised with a range of professionals including those from the Early Years SEND team, Occupational Therapists, Educational Psychologists and Speech and Language therapists. Larina ensures that parents are informed, supported and included at all times. Larina attends regular SENDCO liaison groups. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO training, Speech and Language training, Autism How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All staff encourage open dialogue and good relationships with parents. Hughenden Preschool has an open-door policy, and parents are welcome to help for the morning and talk to staff whenever they need to share concerns or achievements! We hold formal parent’s meetings where parents can meet with their child’s key worker. Hughenden Preschool prides itself at being part of the community, and as such take part in village day. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a ‘wow’ book that parents can access at any time by asking their child’s key person, progress is discussed at key person meetings. Hughenden Preschool completes developmental checks for two-year-olds in conjunction with the parents. Children with SEND are also encouraged to take home a home/school diary. This enables the parent and key person to communicate daily regarding short term outcomes and to work together to support the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The needs of individual children are taken into account to make our setting as inclusive as possible. Hughenden Preschool welcomes the opportunity to discuss specific areas of need with parents before their children attend the setting. The Pre-School operates from a village hall that is not owned by the Pre-School itself. This may mean we are unable to make certain changes to the building; however we endeavour to work with parents to accommodate needs wherever possible. The pre-school operates out of two rooms; however, areas can be sectioned off for quiet time and focused learning. We have plenty of outside space from our enclosed patio area, to the swing park next to the hall, large grass area and the opportunity to walk up to the allotments and fields. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We are sensitive to the transition process and liaise with other settings to ensure that transitions are as smooth as possible. Records are passed onto schools, and teachers are invited to visit the children during a session at Hughenden Preschool before the children have a school visit themselves. Larina communicates with the school SENDCOS for children with SEND to ensure the children are supported in their new environment, and parents are invited to share in the process. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are keen to provide all staff with the skills to support children in resilience. Giving children the skills to bounce back from stress, challenge and transition makes children braver, more adaptable and more curious. The team at Hughenden Preschool would like to enable children to learn strategies at an early age that will give them vital skills and encourage more self-assurance and strength of character that will benefit them throughout life. Larina is keen to develop speech and language training for all staff ensures staff are able to use the graduated approach to support children with English as a second language and speech delay allowing them to flourish.

We liaise with GP's, health workers, Local Authority Area SENDco, SALT and others, to ensure we continue to support the child and their families throughout their time with us. We have a trained Nursery SENDCO who will work with key workers and children and their families to ensure we have the relevant information for each individual child, to enable us to support them in the best way possible.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We work closely with Buckinghamshire Council and are able to gain support and advice from trained practitioners, as well as accessing courses for nursery staff to develop their own knowledge and understanding. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are able to discuss their child's individual needs during their child's settling in sessions 'Settles'. The key worker will gather as much information as possible to make sure we can support the child from their very first session with us. We hold a parent conference with key workers/ SENCO and manager (Wherever relevant) to take a holistic approach to their child's learning and development. We establish next steps for both nursery and at home and will work together to ensure the child has consistency. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Each child's parents will have access their online learning journal, where you will be able to see regular observations and how they link to the EYFS and see their development. Parents are able to use this portal to share photos/ observations from home, where staff can use these interests as trigger points to plan to meet the child's needs through their ever-changing interests. SEND children may have additional targets set within the setting and these will be developed and adapted over time, to suit the changing needs of the child. The Keyworker, Nursery SENCO and parents will be able to discuss theses targets as they are set and as the progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All-access doors to the setting are wide and accessible to those using a wheelchair. There is a downstairs toilet facility suitable for wheelchair access. The baby room, catering for children under the age of 2 years, is on the first floor. there is no lift access but adaptations would be made to ensure this area is accessible to all. The children aged 2 to 5 years old, have access to the ground floor, with door to the garden that open out, using bi-fold doors, to ensure all can have access to this area. There are no steps on the ground floor, making it easily accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children and families are able to take advantage of our settling in sessions, we recommend between 3 to 4 settles but this can be increased dependent on the needs of the child and how they adapt to being away from parents/carers. Children are supported when moving into another room by having settling in sessions, key person handover and children are encouraged to spend time in other rooms when possible. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will be regularly accessing further training for our staff team to ensure that we are up to date with all relevant information to continue to best support children and their families.

description: Join us for our Mindfulness Activities Group sessions at, St Mary’s Church, Aylesbury. organisation: Space (Aylesbury) Due to Tier 4 restrictions, we have needed to alter our schedule of activities over the next few weeks. We support people who are going through relationship difficulties, depression, bereavement, unemployment, mental health problems, loneliness or any combination of these issues. There is no fixed charge, but we ask for a small donation if you are able. We offer one-to-one counselling from trained counsellors. local_offer: Our service provides 1:1 tuition online or in person to children and young people with SEND who may be unable to attend school, who attend school on a reduced timetable, or who need additional support outside of school hours.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to reduce the learning gap between abled students and student with SEND, enabling children and young people to engage with education and improve their outcomes. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Recently, our staff and select tutors have undertaken the CPD qualified course "Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in the Classroom". How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We begin all schemes with a discussion (via phone or email) with parents about their child's specific needs, interests, and other ways to engage them with tuition. We also allow parents to be present during tuition if they wish, in order to support learning. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We offer recordings of lessons and reports that can be sent to parents following each session so they can keep track of their child's progress. If there are specific targets for SEND pupils, we can include these in any reports that are sent. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We cary out sessions online or in the pupil's home, so they feel comfortable and at-ease. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? They can fill in a form on our website or contact the office by phone. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? If possible, we would like to extend SEND training opportunities to a larger pool of our tutors, or even to include it as part of standard tutor training.

local_offer: I am an Ofsted registered childminder offering care for children in my setting following the EYFS framework.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to provide a stable and welcoming environment for Children with SEND and their families. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Training is due to take place in May 2025 to further support and understanding of the sector. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work with parents to ensure all needs are met for the child. Regular communication with parents on progress and arranging visits when possible, to see how the child is settled within the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We observe and assess all children and where there is a particular need, we support the preparation and implementation of a joint action plan for the child. With parents’ permission we may involve other services. We provide increased opportunities for communication for families of children with SEND and are flexible in how we communicate, for example, in person, on phone, email or electronic messages. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The environment is accessible via the front door through the hall way and the side gate via a flat service. There is one step through the back door but all other areas in the garden are accessible. The upstairs of the setting may not be accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are welcome to visit the setting after being sent a welcome pack to review the setting and myself. We offer a warm setting with an open arm policy. We encourage families to fill out information sheets so we are aware of the child's needs and any special requests can be added to this sheet. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are constantly aware of the need for flexibility within our setting to ensure that children’s needs can be met. We access training as necessary and are recruiting an assistant to support us. We keep updated with new guidance from the Local Authority and use their website regularly.

local_offer: We offer specialist SEND education support through our experienced tutors in our very own classroom-based setting, online via Zoom, on-site at school or in the home. Our focus is on providing a safe and nurturing environment for our students to learn using a stage-not-age approach. We can support with maths, science and English as well as other subjects. We also encourage our students to engage in life skills such as cooking and baking, accessing the outdoors and integrating with the local community.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Success looks different for everyone who comes to Limitless, ranging from our students attending our sessions and building a relationship with their tutor to completing Functional Skills exams and moving on to other education provisions. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All of our staff have extensive experience working with individuals with SEND and receive tailored support from the management team to best support their students. A variety of additional training courses are available to our staff at their discretion. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers can attend sessions with students while they become more comfortable with the environment and their tutor and are welcome to use the facilities at Fairford Leys Community Centre or in Hampden Square. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Progress can be communicated to parents and carers verbally at the end of session or written on a regular basis at their request. We complete reports each half-term and can also provide these on request. We are able to support with EHCP reviews, annual reviews and a variety of child-based meetings. We can support by meeting with Occupational Therapists, Psychologists and a variety of other specialists as well as accommodating specialists attendance during student session times. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Fairford Leys Community Centre has accommodations for individuals with physical disabilities such as a wheelchair lift to access four of our classrooms. There is a garden attached to the church that we have access to - however, advance notice is needed for this so we can set up the garden safely. Our students are often encouraged to access the local community by visiting the local coffee shop, park and playgrounds. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact our CEO & Founder, Christopher Reeves who can support with regular session times and advice for using our service. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

description: Clinical Hypnotherapy is a gentle and positive way to help bring about change. Clients describe this as an enjoyable process in which, refreshingly, there is no need to talk about the past or discuss the more private areas of your problem, unless you actually want to. It's not easy being a parent, and it’s painful to see your child struggling with anxieties, fears, fussy eating or feeling unsettled at school. Hypnotherapy for children is a different process from adults, so I will talk you through it beforehand. As a parent, you play a valuable role in helping your child. And you’ll be pleased to hear that children respond incredibly well to positive change and tend to make the changes they need in fewer sessions than an adult. When a child under 8 years old is struggling, it is more beneficial to work with just the parent and support them in facilitating the changes that will bring about the desired positive changes in your child. You are welcome to phone me for a chat to decide what might be your best route. I offer a private service just outside of Oxford City. I do not book clients back to back and offer plentiful free parking for your convenience. Clients under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian. Known for helping with anxieties, fear, phobias, low mood, confidence, bad habits, insomnia, eating disorders and disordered eating and pain, Hypnotherapy helps with anything that is in some way affected by the mind. And sometimes our problems can be rooted in trauma. Trauma (including PTSD or PTS) can benefit from the Rewind Technique (RT). Trained by Dr Muss, his Rewind method has a recovery rate of 89% after 1 session. And there is no need to discuss your trauma in any depth to use this technique. Steph McGee BSc, DSFH, HPD, Hyp Dip (Paediatrics)

name: The MoneyHeave Community Project
description: The MoneyHeave Community Project works to break down barriers to economic equality, improve overall wellbeing, and promote healthier financial habits. We focus on empowering and educating young people and adults about money. Through relatable and accessible initiatives, we help individuals take control of their financial and mental wellbeing. In today’s digital age, physical money is less common. This shift has affected how many people perceive money’s worth, especially among young people. Technology has made transactions easier, but the lack of physical money has changed many people’s perception of its value. This is why financial education is so important to aid an individual’s prospects. This goes hand-in-hand with the effects on mental health – feelings of worthlessness, depression, and suicidal thoughts. Policy Institute states that over 420,000 people in problem debt consider taking their own lives in England each year. Results signify that the lack of understanding when it comes to financial literacy has led to poor financial decisions generating early debt – Young Enterprise (2021) collated data showing that 52% of teenagers have been in debt by the time they are 17. Our services and products include research, events, coaching, discussions, courses, workshops, workbooks, and digital resources. We strive to equip individuals with the knowledge and tools they need to make informed decisions and shift behaviours. Visit our website for more information and to see upcoming projects.

local_offer: We offer tailored support to meet the individual needs of children and young people with SEND. This includes one-to-one or small group support, adapted activities, and the use of visual aids, sensory tools, and communication strategies. We work closely with families and professionals to create personalised plans that promote development, wellbeing, and independence. Our inclusive approach ensures every child feels safe, valued, and able to thrive.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We ensure that all children and young people, regardless of their needs, are fully included and able to participate meaningfully in all activities. We promote equal access to opportunities and experiences that support their development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Focused on understanding the spectrum of autism and using practical strategies to support communication, sensory needs, and transitions. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work closely with families to ensure they feel heard, supported, and empowered. We value the expertise of parents and carers and involve them in planning and reviewing the support their child receives. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We value strong partnerships with parents and carers. Information is shared regularly through daily conversations, communication books, emails, and scheduled meetings. We provide updates on progress, wellbeing, and any concerns, and we encourage two-way communication to ensure consistent support between home and our setting. All information is shared respectfully and confidentially. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor and outdoor environments are designed to be inclusive and accessible for all children, including those with SEND. We ensure clear, wide pathways, appropriate lighting, and minimal sensory overload indoors. Furniture and resources are arranged to support mobility and independence. Outdoors, we offer level surfaces, sensory-friendly areas, and accessible play equipment to support engagement and participation for every child. Adjustments are made as needed to meet individual needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can get in touch with us directly by phone, email, or by visiting our setting. We offer an initial conversation or visit to discuss the child’s needs and how we can support them. We then complete a registration or referral form, and work closely with parents and any professionals involved to ensure a smooth transition. description: I am a qualified coach and founder of Dream Ladder Coaching, specialising in helping individuals achieve their professional goals. I also support individuals with ADHD and Autism in their career journeys, helping them harness their unique strengths and overcome challenges to achieve professional success by integrating ADHD and autism-informed coaching techniques into my solutions-focused career coaching practice. I provide support to individuals at various stages of their career journey, whether you’re feeling unfulfilled in your current role and contemplating a career change but don’t know where to begin, or if you feel undervalued or overlooked in your position and are seeking to elevate your professional profile or navigate workplace challenges, I am able to help. I also support clients experiencing challenges with executive functioning, such as planning, organisation, time management, and follow-through that may be impacting their confidence or career progression. Together, we work towards actionable steps that align with your goals and aspirations. Please contact me for a free discovery call.

name: Vache Baroque
description: We are Vache Baroque: musicians passionate about connecting the broadest possible range of people to the power of Baroque music. We produce critically-acclaimed music and drama projects. From operas and concerts to children’s shows and youth residencies, we create experiences for all to be inspired and challenged by. As an award-winning UK charity, we give special focus to offering young and disadvantaged people opportunities to participate alongside leading professionals. Our work is impactful and unexpected, often devised in collaboration with exciting cross-artform partners who share our values. Since our September 2020 launch we have produced operas, multi-disciplinary concert projects, international tours, in-school workshops for KS2 children, young artist programmes for emerging singers, projects for deafblind young people in partnership with Bucks Council SEND Service, and community workshops in collaboration with Wycombe Refugee Partnership, Wycombe Arts Centre, the Dove Café, and One Can Trust. We use music to inspire, empower, and transform lives. Our income goes straight back into our activities, so the more funding we have, the more work we can do. If you are in the position to support us, please do consider joining our VBFriends scheme.

description: Childminder registered with Suffolk Childminding Agency SCA170409 31/03/2025 Hello, we are Faye Weafer and Kayleigh Thomas-Petford and we have recently started our childminding business together. We are both in happy marriages and have a son and daughter each. Having both worked with children for more than 15 years each, we decided it was time for a new and exciting challenge. As our own children are in childcare settings, we realise the importance of building positive relationships between the families and childminders. We want to offer parents, carers and their children a home-from-home setting where they feel happy and welcome. As we are both working together, we can have more children which allows us to run a mini nursery style setting. We are a very active setting and aim to go out every morning. This could include visits to the library, local parks, nature walks, soft plays, toddler groups and trips into the local community. Throughout the day, the children will have access to a free-flow garden where they can use age appropriate toys and be creative with water play and mud kitchens. We follow the EYFS framework and carry out daily observations which contribute towards a learning journey for each child which will be shared with parents/carers at regular intervals throughout the year. We offer school drop offs and pick ups to Robertswood School and in the future we will be offering drop offs and pick ups from Chalfont Infant School. We accept 15 and 30 hours funding for 9 month to 4 year olds and also accept tax free childcare. Please feel free to message, email or call us if you would like further information.

description: Minis Classes (ages 1 to 2 and a half years) This interactive class explores sounds and rhymes and develops and enhances speaking and listening skills, as well as activities to improve gross motor skills. The Minis classes are carefully designed in conjunction with a speech therapist, so each child develops an understanding of language and speech development. The class is a fun introduction to phonics through songs, role-play, and rhymes, all with the help of our cheeky friend, Robot Reg. Pre-School Classes (ages 2 and a half to 4 years) Each Pre-School class includes games and activities that teach sound recognition, segmenting, and oral blending - the necessary foundations for reading and writing. This high-energy class also includes activities to improve gross and fine motor skills, which support a child’s handwriting. Expect songs, dancing, disco lights, and, of course, our cheeky friend Robot Reg!

name: Low-Cost Counselling Service
description: We offer remote, low-cost counselling, providing high-quality, inclusive, and accessible counselling. Initial assessments are free of charge, and counselling session fees are offered on a sliding scale, based on individual annual income, with sessions starting from just £10 per hour. Counselling is a confidential, safe, and non-judgmental space to talk with a therapist about your feelings, emotions, and behaviours. Our counsellors help you to explore and process your thoughts and feelings, gain a better understanding of your emotions, processes, and behaviours, and find your own solutions to your problems. Our service focuses on inclusivity, compassion, and respect, ensuring that everyone who seeks help feels valued and understood. We also offer youth and adult workshops, youth mentoring, and organisational training. The Altering Group was founded with a deep commitment to supporting young people and adults, particularly those from disadvantaged backgrounds or underrepresented groups, to address the lack of opportunities, guidance, and support available to these individuals. We welcome all individuals, regardless of their circumstances, as we believe everyone has the right to access the support and services they need. We are committed to making a positive impact in the lives of our service users, in communities and society. This service is not a crisis service, so we are unable to support those in need of immediate support or crisis interventions. Visit our website to find out more and make a referral.

local_offer: Ickford Pre-School offers wrap-around care (7:45am to 6pm) to children from the local and extended community. We are open to children from all backgrounds and are accessible to all. We include and cater for all ethnicities, cultures and religions, social and economic backgrounds, home languages, disabilities, learning difficulties, genders and abilities. We believe in each child receiving quality care and achieving their full potential by learning through play in a caring, supportive setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Suzanne has been our SENDco since 2024, Suzanne works/has worked with external agencies including Speech and Language therapy, specialist nurses, paediatricians, psychologists and the local authority SEND advisors. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO Training: Makaton Foundation: Autism in The Early Years: November 2018 Behaviour Management: Seeing Beyond Behaviour: Positive Play for Early Years: Understanding and Addressing Behaviour in the Early Years I'm not the SENCo but what should I look for. Child Behaviour in the Early Years: November 2019 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We encourage all parents/carers to come to us at any time (in person or via email or telephone) with concerns about their child(ren). We share next steps and ideas for aiding progress and development outside the setting via activities sent home by email or in book packs (targeted at specific needs). All parents/carers are invited to join our management committee either as an officer (chair, secretary, treasurer) or a general member. We usually hold 3 to 4 fundraising events each year for which we always need extra hands (bakers, stall-manning, setting up venues). We also welcome any additional help on an adhoc basis in sessions (for example, reading to children or joining in village walks). If you have a particular skill/interest, we would love to borrow you! How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children have 'Tapestry e-learning journals' which are updated on a (minimum) weekly basis. We track progress of individuals and cohorts through this journal and invite parents/carers to add their own observations from home and comments on activities undertaken in pre-school sessions. We have an open-door policy whereby parents/carers may speak to management/key workers at any time about their child. We regularly monitor and review targeted plans (either our own or those written by other professionals) and work in partnership with the home and external agencies to set new targets. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our building is fully accessible to all users, with no steps, and level access throughout. Doorways are wide enough for use by those with limited mobility and we have a designated disabled toilet. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We offer taster sessions for prospective parents and children at a time that suits, as well as settling-in sessions where parents/carers may stay or leave their child - as necessary. We ask for 'All About Me' forms to be completed to give us a broader understanding of the home environment, and a baseline assessment on entry to judge the child's stage of development. We also ask for additional 'interest' information - for example dual-nationality or EAL needs, as well as any cultural experiences that we can build on. Each child is assigned a key worker when they start who works closely with them and is a direct point of contact for parents/carers. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Staff are always kept abreast of new guidelines and ideas and are offered the opportunities as they arise to undertake training. We review our provision, practices and policies to ensure we are reflective and build on past experiences. Our provision includes adaptations to activities and equipment to ensure its suitability for all users.

The hub also emphasizes reducing food waste and promoting healthy eating. It's a fantastic place for young people to develop new skills, find support, and build lasting friendships.

name: The Castlefield Hangout
description: The Castlefield Hangout Youth Hub is a vibrant community space designed for young people to connect, learn, and grow. Here are some key features: Inclusive Environment: The hub provides a safe and welcoming space for youth to hang out, make friends, and participate in various activities. Activities and Events: From arts and crafts to sports and educational workshops, there's always something happening. Youth can also get involved in planning and running events based on their interests. Support Services: The hub offers support with employment, education, housing, and mental health resources. Staff are available to help with resumes, job applications, and more. Life Skills: Youth can learn valuable skills such as cooking, budgeting, and meal prep. The hub also emphasizes reducing food waste and promoting healthy eating. Community Engagement: The hub encourages youth to take on leadership roles and contribute to the community through volunteer opportunities. It's a fantastic place for young people to develop new skills, find support, and build lasting friendships.

With our fully accessible on-site accommodation and catering, we have the perfect venue for a training camp or event in an excellent variety of Paralympic, Olympic, and other sports. The centre boasts a fantastic range of facilities suitable for all ages and abilities, including an air-conditioned gym, a 25-metre swimming pool, a versatile sports hall, and a workout area where we hold a variety of workout classes. name: Dyslexia Bedford
description: Based in Bedford, Bedfordshire, we specialise in providing comprehensive diagnostic assessments for dyslexia, dyscalculia, and other specific learning difficulties (SpLDs) for both children and adults. Our other services also include educational progress assessments, exam access arrangements, and tailored specialist tuition to meet individual learning needs. Louise is a highly qualified specialist teacher and assessor with over 25 years of classroom experience. She brings a mix of both personal and professional understanding to her assessments, supporting individuals to achieve their full potential. Louise has worked across primary and secondary mainstream schools as well as specialist settings, serving as an Assistant Head Teacher, SENDCO, and dedicated dyslexia assessor and tutor. She holds an AMBDA qualification and has a current APC with PATOSS.

description: Mini Monets' "Newbies After School Art Club" is perfect for children in Reception to Year 3 who love to be creative. Held in our brand-new studio at Saddlers Yard, Chalfont St Giles, the club runs midweek after school — with drop-off at 3:45pm for an hour of fun and imaginative art activities. This class benefits young children by: - Encouraging creativity and self-expression in a fun, relaxed environment. - Building fine motor skills through painting, drawing, and crafting. - Boosting confidence as they explore different materials and techniques. - Helping them unwind after a busy school day with calming, focused activities. - Supporting social skills as they meet and make new friends with similar interests. It's the perfect creative outlet to inspire young minds and nurture budding artists!
organisation: Mini Monets Art School (Amersham) Mini Monets offers unsurpassed inspirational weekend art and holiday art camp workshops for children aged 5 to 15 years. Children not only get a real art education where they learn about techniques, materials and the great subject of ART from a professional artist. They also make new friends, relax, develop confidence and try out exciting things like pottery, graffiti, T-shirt design, have art exhibitions and much more. Above all, it is a unique opportunity to express themselves creatively. Established in 2013 by international artist Debra Franses Bean. This special community of young artists provides a wonderful break from their school week. Many children have been attending the art school since it opened and others return after taking a break from other activities. This year all her masterclass students were awarded Art scholarships at their chosen secondary schools, St Mary's Gerrards Cross, Pipers Corner, Godstowe, RMS, Royal Hospital Horsham. dfbean3@mac.com https://www.minimonetsuk.com/

name: Niki Bell Art Studio
description: I am a printmaker, painter, potter, and Art Tutor for children and adults in Buckinghamshire. Everything I do in my artwork is based on the foundation of drawing, so much so that you may even see some pencil lines in my watercolours! I enjoy exploring various artistic media and the unique inspiration each brings to my creative expression. I am always learning, hopefully progressing, and I try to be brave and experimental. At the centre of every class and workshop run at my studio is a love for art and a passion for sharing the joy of making. My goal is not only to teach techniques but also to inspire confidence and spark creativity in each student. Whether you're creating your first sketch or refining your artistic skills, you'll find encouragement, guidance, and a warm, welcoming environment at Niki Bell Art Studio. Come and discover just how rewarding making art can be, and leave with something beautiful you've created yourself. Our regular classes include: - Watercolour Painting – Learn the delicate balance of water, pigment, and paper to create luminous, flowing works. - Drawing – From the basics of line and shading to more advanced techniques, we’ll help you develop a strong foundation. - Mixed Media – Experiment with different artistic media like ceramics, felting, weaving, printing, drawing, and painting. It all goes on in this diverse class. - After School Art Clubs – Specially designed for young artists, these sessions encourage creativity, confidence, and skill-building in a fun and supportive environment. Weekend Workshops Our Saturday Workshops are a perfect opportunity to dive into something new or deepen your understanding of a particular medium. These one-off sessions vary throughout the year and cover a wide range of artistic and craft techniques, allowing for both spontaneous exploration and focused skill development. Venue Niki Bell Art Studio is based in Chesham, Buckinghamshire and serves Amersham, Berkhamsted, Wendover, Tring Chalfont's and Beaconsfield.

description: Independent Lives is a user-led charity working with disabled people, people with care needs, and those with caring responsibilities, to enable people to lead full, active and independent lives. We work directly with disabled people, and parents and carers of disabled children: Providing a Direct Payments support service to help people arrange and manage their own personalised care and support. We offer banking, payroll, and recruitment services so people can manage their own budgets and personal assistants. Our care service Lend a Hand provides personalised home-based care and support. We work with health and social care professionals: Providing training and training materials, consultancy, and recruitment support. We work closely with local authority social care teams and Clinical Commissioning Groups on support planning, personalisation and co-production, and health and social care integration

local_offer: The Buckinghamshire Vision for EHC Plans (Co-produced between parents and professionals) EHC Plans are the result of a collaborative partnership between parents/carers, children/young people and professionals and are owned jointly by everyone involved. Children and young people are at the centre of outcome-focused planning of provision to enable them to make a successful transition to adult life. Parents, carers are empowered to confidently advocate on behalf of their children and their views are respected by professionals. EHC Plans are live documents, reviewed regularly to ensure that the changing needs of children and young people are responded to.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We support only children and young people (and their families) who have SEND and who are under assessment for an Education Health and Care Plan (EHC Plan) or already have an EHC Plan. Our aim is to support children and young people with complex and long-term SEN to access their education and achieve their potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We do not work directly with children and young people on a day-to-day basis. However, front-line staff have undertaken person-centred approach training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Because our work is governed by legislation, much communication is in writing. However, we also communicate via the telephone and in face-to-face meetings. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Information is available on the Local Offer website. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If the child or young person, their family and professionals who support them within their educational setting feel it is necessary to seek an EHC Needs Assessment, a request should be made to the SEND Service. This should be accompanied by evidence of the SEN and support that has been provided to date, and its effectiveness. It is usually expected that all available mainstream resources to have been appropriately deployed before a request would be made. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? In light of the SEND Reforms, it is important that all members of the SEND Service are aware of the changes and how they influence our work. We undertake training as required. We also work with other services to give training to educational settings and other services.

name: Towards Meaning Counselling: Burnout Recovery for Autistic Professionals
description: Looking for autistic-affirming therapy near Gerrards Cross, Buckinghamshire, or online across the UK or the Republic of Ireland? Are you a late-diagnosed autistic professional in a demanding career? You've achieved success. You have a respected career, financial security, perhaps a family. But you're exhausted from decades of workplace masking. local_offer: Educational Psychologists (EPs) undertake a range of work aimed at promoting inclusion, psychological well-being, and raising standards for children and young people aged 0 to 25 years, across the full range of abilities. The Buckinghamshire Integrated SEND Service includes qualified EPs registered with the Health and Care Professions Council, Trainee EPs on supervised placements, graduate Assistant Educational Psychologists, and a leadership team. Educational Psychologists offer a consultation service to Buckinghamshire maintained schools, academies, and specialist settings. Consultation is used as a tool to explore how schools meet the needs of their students and operates at an un-named level. The aim of consultation sessions with schools is to: enhance knowledge and understanding of assessment, needs, and intervention for children and young people; illuminate recurring issues and themes which may require additional support from ISEND; engage in problem-solving. All maintained schools, academies and specialist provision in Buckinghamshire have a named link Educational Psychologist, who undertakes consultation sessions and, where possible, statutory work arising through that setting. It is hoped that Link EP support to settings will be increased in the future to include pre-statutory referrals. EPs also offer training to schools and deliver a range of specialist therapeutic interventions through the ELSA, Holding Hands and Nurture Group Programmes.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? EPs have a statutory role in relation to SEND. They provide professional advice to the local authority under the Children and Families Act 2014 in relation to assessment of SEN, Annual Reviews and Tribunal appeals and contribute to decision-making panels. They also take the role of SEN Expert in Independent Review Panels for excluded pupils. EPs also provide consultative support and training to schools in order to enhance the quality of SEND provision in LA schools and education settings. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? EPs have a first degree in Psychology, experience of applying psychology in their work with CYP, knowledge of safeguarding and SEND legislation, and professional applied training to Masters or Doctorate level in Educational and Child Psychology. Some EPs have undertaken additional training, for example in Video Interaction Guidance, specialist therapeutic approaches, specialist assessment and, or particular areas of SEND. EPs are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council www.hcpc-uk.org and are required by law to keep up to date with professional training and practice. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? EPs will use a range of communications, phone, email, letter. Initial contact is often by telephone and then either direct or virtual meetings with parents. EPs will always involve parents in planning and decision-making. EPs have skills in eliciting the views of children and young people and represent these in meetings or in reports. Formal reports are written when required, for example for Statutory Assessments or Tribunal Appeals. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Currently, EP input is accessed directly by CYP and families through a successful request for statutory assessment only. Either parents or schools may make a request for this assessment. Parental consent is essential before any individual casework is undertaken. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The EP Team is working on plans to extend the pre-statutory service and engage in more direct work with children and families in the future.

description: BSL Plus provides communication and support services to Deaf, Deafblind, Deafened, and Hard of Hearing people. We are based in Reading, Berkshire, working throughout the surrounding areas and various parts of the UK, according to demand. We design, develop, and supply custom-made care packages pertaining to both the Service User and official Commissions, also known as Purchasing Authorities - collaboratively working together to provide an exceptional level of professionalism, due care, and considerations required in this expert field. Whilst working alongside often-vulnerable Deaf and Deafblind Service Users such as babies, children, adults, and young adults alike with varying degrees of physical and mental capacities, autistic spectrum, SEN, Disabilities, and/or specific needs and so on, we believe that a foundation based on establishing rapport, connections, and trust is crucial. We are, therefore, proud to endorse a host of BSL Communication Support Assistants (CSA’s), DB CG’s and Interpreters on our books so that we can tailor support to requests, criteria, geographical proximity, skill, diversity, cultural preferences, applicable habits, and more. What is our aim? Our aim is to promote equality and empowerment for the Deaf and Deafblind Community. We acquire this through fair access to communication, information, mobility, and independence. We continually familiarise ourselves with relevant advocacy, rights, current policies, and codes of conduct and ethics, which serve to meet the requirements of a safe and bespoke working relationship. We are committed to allocating assignments that match the specific criteria of the individual Service User. The Service User will be afforded opportunities inclusive of educational, physical, creative, and social aspects via a structured development process. BSL Plus Ltd. endeavours to allocate the appropriate BSL CSA(‘s)/DB CG’s to the Service User in order for a complimentary working relationship and to continually build rapport. Why use BSL Plus Ltd.? We strive to provide excellence in our services to the Deaf, Deafblind, Deafened, and Hard of Hearing. We aim to promote equality, respect and fairness through enabling people the chance to acknowledge and access their rights to communication, information, and mobility.

name: British Sign Language Communicate Support and Deafblind Communicator Guide
description: BSL Plus provides communication and support services to Deaf, Deafblind, Deafened, and Hard of Hearing people. We are based in Reading, Berkshire, working throughout the surrounding areas and various parts of the UK, according to demand. We design, develop, and supply custom-made care packages pertaining to both the Service User and official Commissions, also known as Purchasing Authorities - collaboratively working together to provide an exceptional level of professionalism, due care, and considerations required in this expert field. Whilst working alongside often-vulnerable Deaf and Deafblind Service Users such as babies, children, adults, and young adults alike with varying degrees of physical and mental capacities, autistic spectrum, SEN, Disabilities, and/or specific needs and so on, we believe that a foundation based on establishing rapport, connections, and trust is crucial. We are, therefore, proud to endorse a host of BSL Communication Support Assistants (CSA’s), DB CG’s and Interpreters on our books so that we can tailor support to requests, criteria, geographical proximity, skill, diversity, cultural preferences, applicable habits, and more. What is our aim? Our aim is to promote equality and empowerment for the Deaf and Deafblind Community. We acquire this through fair access to communication, information, mobility, and independence. We continually familiarise ourselves with relevant advocacy, rights, current policies, and codes of conduct and ethics, which serve to meet the requirements of a safe and bespoke working relationship. We are committed to allocating assignments that match the specific criteria of the individual Service User. The Service User will be afforded opportunities inclusive of educational, physical, creative, and social aspects via a structured development process. BSL Plus Ltd. endeavours to allocate the appropriate BSL CSA(‘s)/DB CG’s to the Service User in order for a complimentary working relationship and to continually build rapport. Why use BSL Plus Ltd.? We strive to provide excellence in our services to the Deaf, Deafblind, Deafened, and Hard of Hearing. We aim to promote equality, respect and fairness through enabling people the chance to acknowledge and access their rights to communication, information, and mobility.

name: Closing the Gap
description: This free service is a partnership between Buckinghamshire Mind and Citizens Advice Bucks to provide wrap-around support and advice for adults experiencing both mental ill-health and financial challenges. This service is delivered in partnership with Citizens Advice Bucks and Bucks Mind to provide two forms of support; financial and mental health. Financial Capability Support: Provided by Citizens Advice Bucks by their Money Advice team. An assessment with one of their advisors will allow them to understand the challenges you are facing and provide advice, information, and practical steps to help you move forward. Mental Health Support: We will carry out an initial assessment to ensure the programme is right for you. If it is, then you will be assigned a Supported Self-Help (SSH) practitioner who will work with you to understand the challenges you are facing and to co-design a six-week tailored programme of support. This will be a one-to-one guided self-help programme supported by materials to help you understand and manage your feelings.

name: The Lotus Psychology Practice Ltd
description: We are a team of highly specialised Health and Care Professional Council (HCPC) registered Clinical and Counselling Psychologists. All Psychologists working at The Lotus Psychology Practice have been specifically selected for their professional expertise to work within our Child and Adolescent, Perinatal and Parent-Infant, and Adult Services. We are able to provide a range of services including: - Psychological assessment and evidence-based therapy for children, young people, and adults for a range of mental health and emotional difficulties. - Our team of Perinatal and Parent-Infant Psychologists have specialist expertise in perinatal and parent-infant mental health and wellbeing. This includes working with individuals, couples and families to help them manage the difficulties associated with conception, pregnancy, the post natal period or early infant years. - We support parents and carers in managing managing challenging behaviour and reducing anxiety in their children. This also includes parenting interventions in the context of complex physical health conditions, neurodevelopmental conditions (such as Autism and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder). - The multi-disciplinary team specialise in comprehensive assessments of Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC), in line with NICE (National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence) guidelines. - Cognitive assessments to understand a young persons learning strengths and areas of difficulty, and to identify general and/or specific learning difficulties such as Dyslexia. - Expert Witness services for both private and public proceedings. We offer online and in-person services in Berkhamsted in Hertfordshire. Out reach appointments are available in London, Herfordshire, Buckinghamshire and surrounding areas.

description: Inclusive football sessions for children and adults with a disability and/or learning difficulty. Pan disability football sessions for all aged 8 years and up. The Aylesbury United pan-disability team is a fully inclusive side for both children and adults with physical or learning difficulties. The team is affiliated with the Berkshire, Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire Inclusive (BOBi) League, one of the largest pan-disability leagues in the country. Sessions take place at Ashmead School in Stoke Mandeville on Saturday mornings from 9am to 10:30am. If children or adults you know would be interested in playing football, please come along to a session, or get in touch. Siblings, family, and friends are also welcome to come along. There’s no need to book, just bring suitable clothing, a football, and something to drink. The team was first established by James Byrne when his disabled son wanted to start playing football. He coached the team for four years, and it’s now organised by Nick Gurney and his team of coaches. If you have any questions, please get in touch with the team below.

name: The Inclusion Project
description: The Inclusion Project is a multi-award-winning innovative initiative that promotes a healthy, social and active lifestyle for Neurodiverse adults, including, but not limited to: ADHD; Asperger's and Autism Spectrum Disorder; Cerebral Palsy; Down Syndrome; Epilepsy; Fragile X; Global Development Delay; Williams Syndrome, and more. The emphasis is on participants being included in the local community. Post-education life can be an abyss for people with learning disabilities; it can be difficult to find activities during weekdays that will facilitate the lifestyle that young adults desire. The Inclusion Project is set to solve this issue. We offer group-based sessions, meaning that there is a ratio of up to three Participants to one Group Leader. Participants will be collected and dropped off at home (or whichever location is requested) by a Group Leader at a pre-agreed time.

name: Home From Home Care
description: Family Values, Data Informed Care; Home From Home Care provides specialist residential care to support adults 18 plus with learning disabilities, autism, and complex physical and mental health needs. Combining a family perspective with an uncompromising approach, we offer outcomes-based services and design exceptional environments and bespoke care and support packages around each individual’s needs, setting goals for an ordinary life – ‘The World On My Terms’. "Inspired by Laura, our daughter, and Hugo's sister, we created Home From Home Care. Combining our family perspective with experienced professionals, we create dynamic and therapeutic services around each person in exceptional environments. We offer a full and active life to meet personal aspirations, delivering meaningful outcomes and fulfilled days." - Paul, Ann, and Hugo de Savary. We use creative solutions and technology to promote independence, support individuals to lead fulfilled lives through meaningful activities, and build on the life skills that young people have been taught at school and college. Home From Home Care has 11 separately registered services across Lincolnshire – please contact us directly for more information. Our high-tech, award-winning, data-driven approach empowers colleagues to deliver outstanding therapeutic services, and we embrace new and innovative ways to deliver outstanding care to meet any individual’s changing needs. We have been awarded Platinum by Investors in People and we’re also the winners of Care Home Group 2020 at the National Care Awards and Tech for Good in the Lincolnshire Technology and Innovation Awards 2021. As a family of a loved one with special needs, we understand how important information is when making those difficult and daunting decisions for their adult future. Please do not hesitate to get in touch for more information about our services, or to make an appointment to visit.

local_offer: We believe that the best learning happens in an honest nurturing environment which is full of friendship, fun, and laughter and promotes mutual respect, tolerance, and understanding. Everyone, children and adults, in our caring and supportive school community achieves their full potential and becomes ‘the best they can be’ because they feel valued, listened to and cared for in our safe, secure and inclusive environment. We believe that all children are individuals and that their true potential and love of learning can be inspired and developed best through high-quality teaching taking into account the varied and evolving needs of the whole child. We believe that by building self-esteem, independence, resilience and adaptability in the individual we can aim high in all areas of their unique learning journey without restriction allowing each child to ‘blossom’. We believe that is our privilege to work together to achieve the highest possible expectations for all our children. We aim to provide a creative holistic approach to learning which excites and enthuses children through first-hand ‘real-life’ experiences promoting curiosity self-evaluation, questioning, imagination, risk-taking and teamwork. We believe passionately in the power of learning through play - giving time and experiences for all learning styles. We all work together to inspire and support each other, taking pride in our unique school community. We aim to build our children’s understanding of themselves as an important part of the wider world by developing responsibility, respect and a love for life through an enriching learning environment both indoors and out. We believe we should work together with parents, carers, families and the wider community to provide the best level of social, emotional and academic support for all our children. We value and celebrate diversity and individuality whilst building trust and understanding within a supportive network.
