name: MegaCamps Holiday Sports and Activities in Beaconsfield
description: Looking for the ultimate holiday experience for your child? Our MegaCamps run during all the school holidays (excluding Christmas) at Amersham School and Davenies School in Buckinghamshire offer a fun, safe, and high-energy environment for children aged 5 to 12 years. Each camp is led by our experienced, DBS-checked coaching team. Whether your child loves multi-sports, football, dance, or simply making new friends, MegaCamps are designed to keep them active, engaged, and smiling all day long. With flexible booking options, extended hours, and exciting add-ons like Swimming Inflatables, Go Karting, Clip ’n Climb and Seasonal Excursions, there's something for every child, every day. Join us for an unforgettable holiday filled with fun, friendships, and fantastic memories! Our MegaCamps are packed with fun and excitement, offering an incredible variety of activities and sports to suit everyone! Whether your child is a total beginner, a seasoned pro, or simply curious to try something new, they’ll find plenty to love here. And the best part? Flexibility is key! If they decide to switch things up and try a different course during the camp, no problem at all—just let us know, and we’ll make it happen. Adventure and fun await at every turn! We offer a range of different activities and sports at our MegaCamps to accommodate all. Whether your child is new to sports, has plenty of experience or just fancies trying something different, there's something for everyone at our MegaCamps! There is staggered drop-off and pick-up times available based on age. Please check website for more information. If your child wants to change courses at any point during the camp, there's plenty of flexibility to swap over even on the day, so just let us know so we can help. Please visit our website for all information and to sign up.

local_offer: We will assess each pupil’s current skills and levels of attainment on entry, which will build on previous settings and Key Stages, where appropriate. Class teachers will make regular assessments of progress for all pupils and identify those whose progress: • Is significantly slower than that of their peers starting from the same baseline • Fails to match or better the child’s previous rate of progress • Fails to close the attainment gap between the child and their peers • Widens the attainment gap This may include progress in areas other than attainment, for example, social needs. Slow progress and/or low attainment will not automatically mean a pupil is recorded as having SEN. SEN information report When deciding whether a special educational provision is required, we will start with the desired outcomes, including the expected progress and attainment, and the views and the wishes of the pupil and their parents. We will use this to determine the support that is needed and whether we can provide it by adapting our core offer, or whether something different or additional is needed. local_offer: At The Iver Village Infant Academy and Nursery we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve their highest standards in a secure, safe, stimulating environment. Quality teaching is vital however for some children there are occasions during their school life when additional support may be needed to help them to make progress and achieve their targets. SEN (Special Educational Needs) provision at Iver Village Infant Academy and Nursery is on an individual needs basis and accessible after identification by the School. This comes from interaction in lessons; work in books, homework, pupil understanding, poor personal progress and from assessments https://www.iver-inf.bucks.sch.uk/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs&pid=42 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have interventions such as: - Programmes such as focussed Writing, phonics and reading are carried out by trained LSA’s for pupils who are identified by the School as having weak literacy skills. - Interventions for basic Numeracy skills - Reading intervention as resources allow increasing reading accuracy and fluency for students making slow progress in reading. - Phonics, following the Read, Write Inc resources - Additional 1:1 support in specific subjects in exceptional cases as deemed necessary by the school - Nurture group sessions are provided for pupils who need more targeted support - Fine and gross motor skills including handwriting support - Where a student needs more specialised support, external agencies and other professionals may become involved (see school’s partnerships). What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Training for staff to help them support pupils with SEND - Specialist training/advice and support is available if needed and can be accessed through the specialist teaching service, the Educational Psychology service and Cognition and learning. - Individual staff have had further or more specific training on how to support students with individual needs from specialists or through external training courses. - Training in specific medical needs is also provided by School Nurse and other relevant medical staff e.g. epilepsy, maintaining hearing aids How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The School’s arrangements for consultation - If parents have a concern they should contact the class teacher in the first instance who will liaise with the SENDCo. Specific concerns which relate to the pupils special need or disability should be raised with the SENDCo - Each pupil who has been identified as having special needs will have a Assess, Plan, Do Review (ADPR) that is written by the Class Teacher and shared with their parent/carer - Assessment data is collated out on a termly basis and can be discussed with parents/carers at parents’ evenings - Parent evenings are held twice a year when parents/carers can meet with class teachers How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The school communicates the contact details for the support listed above to students with SEND and their families via: - The School website - 1:1 discussions. - Annual reviews - Newsletters - Website How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. The Ivers Children’s Centre can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families. We offer universal and specialised support to families in the local area. We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. We can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our provision provides support services for all families with children aged 0 to 19 years and up to 25 years for those with a SEND. Our aims are to improve parenting, health and children’s development and to provide a safe and stimulating environment for children, young people and their families to flourish, develop and learn. Parents provided with good information so they can make decisions, which will have a significant effect on their children’s life chances. Parents to know, what support and services are available to help them bring up their children, and how to access them. Families signposted into support as appropriate feel confident to provide good life chance for their children. Children to develop social skills in preparation for starting pre-school, nursery or school. Children to enjoy a variety of fun activities and play and learn through this participation. Parents to feel confident in parenting and picking up parenting skills and support through attendance. Personal, Social and Emotional Development. Physical development. Communication and Language Development. Outreach support, action plan to specifically help the family with individual needs. Emotional and practical support from Outreach Worker. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Safeguarding First Aid Early Language Development Programme Hey Programme (Healthy Eating in Young Children) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We welcome all families to all of our services, staff are dedicated to supporting families using our Hub and its services. Our building is fully compliant with the disability requirements. We provide a warm, welcoming and fun learning environment for children and their families. Large and inviting outdoor play environment Sensory equipment available during sessions Accessible toilets How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can attend our services and register by completing a Family Hub Membership form. Outreach support can be provided by self-referral or by referral from a health visitor or other professional. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

description: The Ivers Family Hub brings local support together for families, children, and young people from birth to 19 (up to 25 with SEND). name: OLOPS SEND Toddler Group
description: A small, friendly baby and toddler group for parents and carers with babies and children under 5 with special educational needs and disabilities. Sessions are limited to a maximum of 10 children at a time and the atmosphere is calm and relaxed, to suit children who may struggle in a louder or busier environment. No diagnosis is necessary - if you feel that you and your child would benefit from attending this group, you are very welcome. There is also no commitment to attend every week - just come when you're free. The guildroom is behind the church, through the gate to the left of the building. There is no parking on site, but Clifton Road nearby has unrestricted parking and the guildroom is wheelchair/buggy accessible. We request that when it is not raining, buggies that are not needed for mobility are left outside. This group operates on Fridays during term time from 1 to 2:15pm. We have a WhatsApp group to keep you in touch with any special events, visits and holiday dates.

local_offer: At Ivingswood Academy we recognise that every child has their own needs and abilities. We embrace our responsibility to help each and every child fulfil their potential, including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Our commitment is to: - Identify the needs of pupils with SEND as early as possible - Carefully monitor the progress of all children in order to identify possible SEN needs - Intervene when progress is less than expected, to ensure that all pupils achieve their full potential - Provide a qualified Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator (SENDCO) - Provide relevant training for all staff through CPD and external courses relevant to the needs of the pupils they work with - Work with and maintain relationships with external agencies when the child's needs cannot be met by school alone - Communicate and work with parents to gain a better understanding of their child - Provide equality of educational opportunity - Make appropriate provision to overcome all barriers to learning and ensure that children with SEND have full access to the curriculum - Help children develop their personalities, skills and abilities - Operate a “whole child, whole school” approach to the management and provision of support for special educational needs. All teachers are required to respond to a child’s learning needs and set suitable learning challenges. This will incorporate ‘quality first’ teaching. https://www.ivingswood.school/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs+%26amp%3B+Disabilities+%28SEND%29&pid=44 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents are requested to contact the SENCO via the school office to make an appointment if they would like to discuss additional provision for their child. local_offer: We are a husband and wife team who provide a home from home enviroment where children feel happy, safe and secure and ready to learn. All children new to us are assessed to give a starting point from where we can work on their individual progress. Any concerns we may have will be discussed with their parents and we are happy to work with any professionals to enhance the childs learning and development should it be required.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? All registered childminders have a key contacts within the Early Years Service and, from this contact, advice and information can be accessed. They can also answer questions and offer advice on other appropriate services. Professionals are very welcome to meet the child in our setting if that is desired. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Effective Health and Safety for Children with Send and ASN - Aug 2022 Introduction to children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder - April 2015 Improving childrens learning through play - Oct 2017 Supporting Children with Speech, Language and Communication Needs - Nov 2018 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work in partnership with parents and share information about their child's/children's development and progress. This is done regularly in an agreed way to suit the parents. We ask parents to share information regarding their child's likes and dislikes, activities that they enjoy the most and those they may be having difficulty with. This information is used when planning activities and to offer support so that children may reach their potential within this setting. We share ideas with parents for use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We observe and assess all children in our care. Where a need is identified we support the parent/parents with preparing and implementation of a joint action plan for their child . If appropriate, and with parental permission, other agencies may be involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? This setting is accessible to most children. We have a level drive from the street level to the front door. There are two steps to our entrance then the remaining setting is all on the same level and can accommodate prams, pushchairs and wheelchairs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have formed links with local pre schools and schools and we work together to support children through transition. We are happy for practitioners from other settings to contact us. We encourage parents to make use of settling in sessions for their children. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are aware of the need for flexibility within this setting to ensure that all children reach their full potential and that all their needs can be met. We keep updated with new guidance from the Local Authority and use their website regularly. We acknowledge the need for training where appropriate and strive to improve our CPD.

local_offer: In my setting every child is treated as an individual and any concerns about the children would be flagged up immediately to the parents. Parents are also encouraged to discuss concerns with me, confidentially. Every child is viewed as ‘unique’ therefore I plan for your child’s development based on observations of your child and evidence gained. Settling in sessions are encouraged to allow the child and parent to familiarise themselves with me and my environment. I always promote positive behaviour and any behaviour issues will be dealt with immediately which keeps consistency between the home and childcare setting. More details can be found in my policies which are available to you during a visit.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I have experience of autism as my own daughter is autistic. I have an insight of EHCP as I have had first hand experience. I did all the paperwork and took control of my daughter EHCP. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Looking at Autism as a fruit salad Inclusion level 3 Lazer learning Managing behaviour (Laser learning) Mental health workshop Autism workshop Full traning from Camhs as a parent How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and children are involved in the planning and learning. There views and the children’s interest and strengths and weaknesses are taken into consideration when planning. We continually looks at and update the child’s next steps Each child is planned for individually and set achievable goals but with high expectations. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I work closely with other settings depending on the child’s needs I would set up an individual plan with parents and any other agencies that are involved with the child. MASH How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is on the ground floor. There are steps at the entrance to the property and to the garden. But temporary ramps could be fitted. I have a large downstairs toilet area, the toilet has a step and a raised seat could be fitted as could grab handles. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I offer as many settling in visits as needed free of charge. I start visits as soon as possible to insure a smooth transition. I do starting points with the parents from day one so that I can effectively see exactly where the child is in there learning. If applicable I would obtain a copy of the 2 year progress report to see where the child’s learning is. We would discuss any additional needs that the child may have, what has been put in place already. We would then make a plan for future goals and next steps trying to bridge the gaps that they might have in there learning. If a child is exceeding the expected levels then a plan would be put in place to extend there knowledge outwards as well as upwards to consolidate there learning. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To continue to update my own practice by attending different courses. To be as inclusive as possible.

description: Relaxed Tours allow neurodivergent people and other people who would benefit from a calm and safe environment to enjoy the zoo. local_offer: Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Policy Written by: Jass and Mani Jeetla. As a registered childcare providers, we aim to follow the requirements of the EYFS (2014) and the Childcare Register (2014) and provide an inclusive environment for ALL children and their families. We are also required to comply with the requirements of the Equality Act 2010 and the SEND (special educational needs and disabilities) Code of Practice 2014. We will do this by: Regularly talking to parents/carer’s about the individual needs of each child Talking to children about their likes/dislikes and interests. Encouraging parents/carers to tell us about family culture/religion/beliefs. Providing a wide range of resources and activities which reflect the diversity of our local area and further afield. Supporting each child through sensitive observation, regular assessment and individually planned activities to achieve their full potential. Providing individual support depending on the child’s needs. Using the 2-year progress check to highlight if I believe a child is falling behind in any of the prime areas of learning. Focusing on the positive things that each child can do. Leading by example and challenging any form of prejudice. Providing resources which challenge stereotypical ideas. Sharing information about children’s learning and development – and providing ideas for home learning - with parents/carers as required by the EYFS. Seeking permission to ask for support from outside agencies where appropriate, for example, Portage workers, Speech and language therapist, Quality improvement partners, Attending appropriate training to ensure we have the skills and knowledge needed to support children and their families. Encouraging children to respect each other as individuals. We welcome your feedback on our service at any time. We provide all the parents with a PDF of our policies and we are happy to discuss our policies verbally, or provide them in a different format under certain circumstances. If we believe a child needs additional support, we will speak to parents and ask their permission to approach agencies which will support their child. description: Postnatal depression advice and support (PANDAS) is here, whatever the weather, to offer hope, empathy, and support for every parent or network affected by perinatal mental illness. Postnatal depression (PND) is a type of depression that many parents experience after having a baby. It can affect any parent, regardless of whether they've suffered from a mental health condition before. PND is linked directly to giving birth and is a common problem, affecting 1 in 10 women within a year of giving birth. It can also affect dads and partners. We offer support in a range of ways including through groups (online and in person), WhatsApp, social media groups, email, and telephone. Please visit our website for more information.

name: Peer-to-peer PANDAS Parents Group | Haddenham
description: PANDAS Foundation UK is launching a new free peer-to-peer support group for parents in Haddenham. We want to give parents a safe, stigma-free space to connect, share experiences, and support one another through the emotional challenges of pre- and postnatal life. Why this matters: - Perinatal mental illness, defined as any mental health problem arising during pregnancy or in the first postnatal year, affects around 1 in 5 women in England. - Systematic reviews focusing on UK cohorts put the figure at 10 to 20% of women experiencing some form of mental illness during pregnancy or within 12 months postpartum - 1 in 10 new fathers experience perinatal mental health difficulties, yet very few have a dedicated forum to talk openly. - By bringing men together, whether they’re expecting their first child, navigating sleepless nights, or facing baby-related anxieties, we foster resilience, reduce isolation, and help prevent more serious mental‐health breakdowns down the line. This group will launch on Wednesday 25 June and run the last Wednesday of each month at Haddenham Baptist Church. To learn more or to register, please email us using the contact details provided.

CoramPACEY (Professional Association for Childcare in Early Years) Buckinghamshire Early Years Services SEND Training Feeding Specialists (Tube Feeding, Dietary concerns) Speech and Language Therapists (accessed through Children's Centres) Occupational Therapy (in the home setting, here and at local hospitals) Play Therapy Liaising with other professionals to prepare EHC Plans Visual Impairment Clinics Hearing Clinics Involvement in the preparation of EHC Plans What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? December 2019 - Communication, Speech and Language - PACEY Conference February 2020 - Good Autism Practice (Autism Education Trust) June 2020 - Bereavement Training (PACEY EYSmart Training) November 2023 - Early Years Conference (What comes before Phonics & Chatting Together Right from the Start) - in line with Government's concerns post-Covid-19 Pandemic with rise in Speech and Language Delays in Under 5's Termly South Area Childminder Network Update Meetings (Bucks Early Years - Microsoft Teams) November 2021 to date: Early Years/SEND Team Liaison Group Meetings and SENCO briefings - online - Ongoing Safeguarding briefings and Training (Face to Face and via Webinar) - ongoing 5.3.2025 Early Years AET Professional Development Programme - Toileting in the Early Years 16.12.2025 National Autistic Society/Neuroinclusive Education Network Training: Making Sense of Autism in the Early Years 28.2.2026 Out of School Conference incorporating Using The SEND Toolkit in a Practical Way How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Face to face (on collection/delivery of the child) Involvement in their child's learning and development here, understanding how to support their child at home/here/other settings, recognise any concerns which may become apparent and how we can jointly access professional advice and support where relevant, eg. EHC Plans. Parental consent is obtained before approaching other professional services. Parents are encouraged to promote their culture and heritage with us through food, stories, songs etc. Since Coronavirus restrictions I have used WhatsApp and Emails to contact parents virtually but my preferred method is face-to-face conversations. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Daily Diaries/Learning Journeys provide a record of progress, achievements and any concerns which may become apparent necessitating outside professional support. 2 Year Old Progress check and liaising with the child's Health Visitor. In addition, I expect parents/carers to be fully transparent with me to ensure we all have a full awareness of all medical/learning difficulties the child may present within a variety of settings and how we can access/provide the most appropriate professional support. Drafting of EHC Plans in conjunction with other settings/professionals. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Children who are unable to walk are carried up and down our front steps and around our premises. Quiet Area/tent (specifically for Children on the Autism Spectrum/Neurodiverse) Full integration with all children who attend here How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Initial meetings with 2-way communication relating to the child's needs/parents' expectations/what I can offer here to establish whether this is an appropriate setting for the child and for me to understand as fully as possible what needs the child may have. When a child is ready to move on to Nursery/Pre-school/School, I provide a detailed up to date report to appraise the new setting of where the child is at under the EYFS. I attend prospective settings with the parents so that we can ascertain which may best be able to meet the child's ongoing specialist needs most effectively. Representatives from the new setting are welcome to visit here to see the child in surroundings in which he/she is confident. I continue to link with those settings to ensure the child is benefiting from a rounded experience under the EYFS across all the settings. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Accessing training as relevant to each child's needs. Currently, specifically focusing on Speech and Language; Autism/Neurodiversity Offering flexible all-inclusive SEND childcare alongside a range of ages and stages of other children all of whom help me support our SEND children here daily. Awareness of future legislation, Government strategies (eg 'Hungry Little Minds), and expectations relating to the childminding of SEND children.

description: Safe Space Mediation provides family mediation services to anyone seeking to reach an agreement regarding their children or finances. Practicing in England and Wales, and as a member of Resolution, Safe Space Mediation offers mediation services via online mediums such as Zoom, as well as limited in-person mediation where required in the West London and Berkshire area. We are specialists in family mediation services, catering to a wide range of clients across the UK. Mediation offers a fast, cost-effective, and robust foundation for future communication compared to solicitor-led negotiations or court applications. It helps to reduce conflict, stress, and anxiety, empowering you and your ex-partner to exert greater control over the situation rather than entrusting the outcome to a judge in a court setting. Our mediation services provide comprehensive support, including the formulation of a parenting plan and the negotiation of a financial settlement should you need one. Should an agreement be reached through mediation, it can be formally documented into a legally binding consent order by a solicitor.

name: Princes Risborough Lawn Tennis Club
description: Princes Risborough Tennis Club was formed in the mid-1920s and has an excellent reputation for its friendly welcome to members of all standards, ages, and abilities. The club has three well-maintained synthetic clay courts, all with floodlights for year-round use. A general programme of development and improvement is supervised by an active committee, with court surface and lighting upgraded in Summer 2022. The clubhouse was completely refurbished in Spring 2019 and is used extensively during both club sessions and matches. Parking for members and visiting guests is available in our dedicated club car park on-site. Courts can be booked by members using the Bookr app up to two weeks in advance of play, and we have various member WhatsApp playing groups to help members set up ad hoc games. The club has men's, ladies', and mixed teams playing in both Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire leagues, and we have enjoyed some excellent results over the past few years. We also have a healthy junior section with coaching opportunities for all ages from tots to teenagers, and play friendly matches against other local clubs. Our club sessions are our main social tennis play in the club, taking place on Wednesday evenings from 6:30 to 9:30pm and on Sunday mornings from 10am to 1pm. You can just turn up to these sessions whenever suits you and join in. There will always be someone there to help organise singles or doubles matches, with mixing in encouraged. The format is flexible, and it depends on who turns up to play, but it’s always a lot of fun and played with great enthusiasm. For more information, please get in touch with Stu Lindsay on the email provided. We also run open ladies sessions on Tuesday afternoons (1:30 to 3:30pm) and Friday mornings (9:30am to midday) and for veterans on Thursday mornings (9.30am to 12.30pm).

local_offer: All support for all children is on an individualised basis and tailored to meet the needs over every child with enhancing and enriching activities which are designed to develop and strengthen where needed, in line with any EHCP, APDR and in collaboration with any additional services that are involved. We will engage with all agencies as needed, to ensure that we are reaching the best possible outcome for all children  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Fir Trees Nursery aims to achieve the best possible outcome for all children and specifically those with needs. To ensure that each child reaches their full potential and develops their independence and sense of belonging at the same time. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The Nursery Manager has a Level 3 SEN qualification How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Fir Trees Nursery is an inclusive nursery where all parents and carers are involved as much or as little as is needed for each individual child. We welcome support and guidance from all associated professionals. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children are constantly observed and these feed into any next steps and developmental planning. There are 3 written assessments each year, with children with SEN or concerns around progress also having monthly APDR to monitor progress in more detail but also to enable us to alter our approach, if needed, swiftly and in line with any guidance from outside agencies such as S and L. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Fully accessible with ramp access at the front of the nursery, an accessible toilet on the ground floor and wheel chair accessible doors throughout. Low level units, tables and chairs ensure that full access is throughout the setting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact the nursery directly What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? All future plans will be developed around the needs of the individual children.

description: At Mindful Support Ltd, we provide tailored intervention and support services for children, their families, and educational settings in and around Buckinghamshire. We work closely with schools and families to support children with social, emotional, and mental health struggles, including those with SEN. Our team offers compassionate counselling for parents and life coaching to help navigate personal and family challenges. We believe support should be accessible when needed most—that's why we offer discounts for siblings and full-time university students. Because when it comes to mental and emotional well-being, no one should have to wait. While it’s always a good idea to speak with your GP, you don’t have to wait to get support. At Mindful Support Ltd, we provide timely and compassionate support for children and families navigating emotional challenges. Whether your child is struggling with big feelings, family challenges, or needs help understanding their emotional world, we’re here for you. We aim to book your consultation within a week of your enquiry, so your family can access the help you need without facing another long NHS waiting list.

local_offer: All children in my care are observed in line with the EYFS. The needs of new children are identified through discussions with their parents/carers and any other professionals involved, An 'All About Me' pack is also given to parents/carers to complete. This all enables me to identify your child's starting points. I am happy to discuss a child's progress at any time. A 2-year development check is also carried out and shared with parents and any concerns regarding the development will be discussed. I give continuous care to each child to support them, build up confidence and positive self-esteem, helping them to feel secure emotionally and physically. The planning for each child is 'child led' so that their learning is built around the child's interest. I provide activities for your child to learn within the area of need and use the EYFS as a guide for the children's development. Each child is observed continuously and I track their progress using ‘Development matters’ and ‘ Birth to 5 matters’ and other child development books and online information. Any concerns are shared and discussed with parents on a regular basis. If a child is not making progress I can access support from the local authority or from other professionals. I have detailed policies and procedures in place to ensure each child's well being. My house and garden is risk assessed each morning before children arrive. My childminding service is an inclusive setting. Through a close relationship with each child, I ensure each child feels valued and supported. I have previously worked as a home carer providing support to children and adults with learning disabilities and also worked at Chesham Grammar school for their learning Support Department, supporting children with Cerebral Palsy, Autism. Training is undertaken regularly to ensure necessary knowledge and to enhance my professional development as the need arises. I am first aid trained and also attended a Safeguarding course. Previously I have attended a number of courses on Autistic Spectrum Disorders. I have also worked alongside Physiotherapists, supporting with Physio activities for children. I am always happy to work closely with parents/carers and outside agencies to learn specific skills to support children with additional needs. When planning activities or outings I will make sure every child can be involved. We regularly visit the library, local parks, farms and the zoo. I'll make sure I risk assess the place first to ensure it is safe and suitable for each child's individual needs. My house is a terraced house with ground floor access. It has a step up into the front door and this could possibly be accessible for a light wheelchair. The ground floor of my house is used for childminding and I have downstairs toilet facilities. I have a secure, enclosed rear garden. There are 2 steps down on to decking to get to the garden so no wheelchair access to the garden at the moment. I provide toys and resources for each child's individual needs. All children's individual needs are closely monitored and where additional equipment is required this is either purchased or sourced from the local toy libraries. I regularly review my toys and resources to ensure it supports the EYFS. I have recently bought some books and flashcards in Welsh to support one of the children I look after learning Welsh as an additional home language. I have also purchased some new equipment helping another child who was born premature and needed support with learning to sit unaided. For any further information please feel free to contact me. I'm always available for an initial chat and also encourage prospective parents/carers to visit me. You can then get the feel for my setting and discuss your child's interests and needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I am to provide an environment where all children are welcomed and supported. I will support the children with their own individual needs and plan activities that all children can take part in. This will help each child reach their own next steps and their full potential. I will work closely with any other professionals involved with the child. I will also work closely with parents and also support them as well as the children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Equality and inclusion in Early Years settings Supporting Early language development How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Before a child starts with me I will invite parents and child to my setting to get to know child and parents. We will discuss the Child’s needs, next steps and interests. When a child has started with me, parents are kept up to date on a daily basis regarding their child’s day with me, their learning and development and any concerns. I do this via WhatsApp, email, chat at drop off, pick up, meeting in person or phone call. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? See above. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My available space for the children are all on one level on the ground floor with a toilet situated near the front door. There are suitable areas for all ages for nap/ rest time. The outside play area is mainly grass but also 2 decking areas with one small step up and down. I am happy discuss and where possible make adaptions based on a Child’s needs. There is plenty of off street parking. There is also 2 bus stops near by on 2 different bus routes How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All families are welcome to arrange a convenient day and time to meet with me at the setting. I also work closely with other settings and happy to communicate with any other settings a child attends. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with guidance and training from the LA and use their website regularly. I regularly review the environment, toys and resources, activities to make sure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to do further training specific to needs of the children I am caring for.

name: Jewish Women's Aid (JWA)
description: Jewish Women's Aid, for Jewish women and children affected by domestic and sexual violence A counselling and outreach service that helps Jewish women and their children escape domestic violence and sexual abuse. Our services include: Domestic Violence and Abuse: Domestic violence and abuse affects 1 in 4 women during their lifetimes. JWA supports women and children affected by it, both short-term and long-term. Our range of domestic abuse services includes immediate practical and emotional support, counselling, children's therapy and support groups. Sexual Violence: The Dina Service: 1 in 5 women are victims of sexual violence in the UK. We support Jewish women aged 16 plus who are survivors of sexual violence, both current and historical. This project is staffed by specialist sexual violence workers and is the first of its kind in the UK. Sexual Harassment at Work: JWA has been invited by the Jewish community to support Jewish organisations with training and policy development dealing with sexual harassment at work. Jewish organisations wishing to find out more can contact our project coordinator directly. Education in schools: JWA delivers a Healthy Relationships education programme in Jewish schools in the UK, as part of our prevention work for relationship abuse and sexual violence. Working with 11 to 18 year olds, the programme helps young people distinguish healthy from unhealthy relationships, working to empower young Jewish people to prevent abusive relationships before they start, and also helps young people understand the importance of consent in their relationships. Safer Dating project: Young people aged 16 to 25 years are most at risk of experiencing abuse within their relationships. Healthy Relationships sessions provide a safe space to explore the issues faced by this age group and are delivered in a variety of different settings including 6th forms, University JSocs and youth movements. Professionals' Training: It is vital that Rabbis, educators and community carers learn about domestic and sexual violence so that communities are equipped to recognise the signs and give appropriate support. JWA runs training 3 times a year at head office and offers bespoke training for synagogues, kindergartens and schools. Ask Me project: JWA is proud to have been appointed by Women's Aid to deliver the inspirational Ask Me project, for training and developing Ask Me, ambassadors, in the Jewish community. This project is designed to build up a team of ambassadors so that synagogues are safe places for women to disclose and seek help. Email us if you are interested in becoming an Ask Me, ambassador.

description: We provide much more than just a roof – we are a place of positive change and growth, enabling people to move on and lead independent lives. Teen Spaces provides supported accommodation services to young people aged 16 and above. Along with accommodation, we employ and partner with local specialists to make a positive impact on the lives of individuals. Our purpose is to promote semi-independent supported living by empowering young people. name: The African Cultural Centre (TACC)
description: The African Cultural Centre (TACC) is the place to be! We use whole family approach system where Africans and friends of Africans who need a space to connect, relax, integrate, and feel part of something positive are all welcome. A welcoming, safe, free space where laughter, creativity, and community thrive. We run Early Years and Family Learning sessions on Sunday mornings at the Elmhurst Best Start Family Hub. Activities include stay-and-play, early communication and language development support, home-learning support, and school-readiness activities. We particularly welcome families where English is an additional language, and offer a supportive space where parents and carers can build confidence and engage in their children's early learning. This session is part of our wider whole-family Sunday programme, so other family members can take part in age-appropriate activities at the same time. Family Wellbeing and Community (Sunday 12 midday): A Sunday session offering shared family time, wellbeing and awareness activities, and practical and creative sessions such as sewing, crochet, gardening, and planting. We also provide discreet one-to-one support and signposting where appropriate, drawing on the professional knowledge and experience within our volunteer community on areas such as wellbeing, housing, education and employment. Children and Young People (Sunday afternoons): A Sunday-afternoon session for children and young people. Activities include education support, youth mentoring, our new Boys to Men project, fitness activities, and sessions focused on positive choices, personal development, and online safety. We help young people build confidence, social skills, and positive relationships in a safe and supportive environment. All sessions are inclusive of children and young people with SEND. All sessions are free to attend, open to all, with no referral needed.

description: Before and after school wraparound care providing a range of activity clubs including sports activities, crafts, science, cooking, Nerf and more.
organisation: S4A Group Ltd, Sports Development and School PE Provision S4A offer holiday camps in Buckingham, Grendon Underwood and Patishall. Providing childcare during the school holidays. We offer activities such as football, basketball, science and seasonal craft activities, a full list of which can be found on the s4a website. S4A also work in 13 different schools in Buckingham and surrounding areas providing high-quality PE provision. We teach a huge variety of different Sports with our coaches' being highly qualified in a range of Sports. We tailor our lesson plans to suit each classes specific needs, giving children the opportunity to learn new skills and develop existing ones whilst always maintaining the importance of enjoyment and fun. As well as providing PE provision in these schools we also provide extended care across in the area. We run breakfast and after school clubs offering a range of activities tailored to meet the interests of the children in attendance, from science clubs to sports clubs S4A cater for all. Helping them develop physically, emotionally, socially and mentally in an environment that is fun and exciting. S4A Development is about helping children reaching ''their'' next level. Our Boys and Girls Development Centre sessions are on a Monday evening in Buckingham with our Juniors section on a Saturday morning in Buckingham and Gawcott. All sessions are professionally designed and delivered in line with the 'England DNA' to offer a player-focused approach and develop players on an individual basis while allowing them to progress at their own speed and in a low pressure but testing environment. All skills and attributes developed will be in the following areas: Technical/ Tactical/ Physical/ Psychological and Social. matt.ogle@s4asports.co.uk https://s4asports.co.uk

name: JG Dance Theatre College
description: JG dance Theatre College holds classes in nine venues, introducing girls and boys between the ages of two and a half and eighteen years to Ballet, Modern Jazz, Tap, National Dance, and Acrobatics. We also offer Drama, Singing, and Street Jazz in some venues. We have a Theatre College for those children who show outstanding potential, where the training is more specialised. It is held all day on Saturday, and entry is by twice yearly audition. At our weekly classes we welcome beginners, who are taught in friendly groups by qualified, experienced, and very caring teachers, many of whom are former pupils, who give individual attention to each child. Shy children develop confidence, and extroverts have their energies channelled into a disciplined art. Above all, our classes are fun. We are most fortunate to be affiliated with a well-established Theatrical Agency based at the world-famous Pinewood Studios. This gives pupils the opportunity to gain professional work on television and film. If your child is hoping for a career in show business, this could be a wonderful opportunity for them. All prospective pupils are offered a free trial lesson before committing themselves to enrolling. About JG Dance: Jeannine Greville has been established in the Thames Valley for over 50 years, with many thousands of children passing through the doors. Many enrol for a few years, but others are enjoying very successful careers in the West End, on television, with The Royal Ballet Company, Royal Shakespeare Company, and annually in Pantomime. A former pupil was nominated for a prestigious BAFTA award.

local_offer: we openly invite families requiring support surrounding SEND, the building is one level only with extra wide doorways to enable children to gain access to all areas. we are based on an natural open area where children use their senses to explore with support and direction of the practitioners. The staff team are trained and qualified to cater, support and reassure as well as encourage direct and challenge the children, All staff are fully paediatric first aid qualified. there is room to investigate inside and plenty of freedom outside as well as a sensory pod. We have animals where the children can engage and take on a role during their sessions with us.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We would like for families to have an open inviting and welcoming place to come, make new friends, have a support network, build a new hobby alongside others, enjoy the outdoors and embed well being and acceptance What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Early Years Senco Level 3. advanced Autism understanding level 3 ELSA Behavioural management Communication training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are currently organising and fundraising for the community garden, where families can come to a safe place with of road parking and enjoy the wonders of being outside, we have allotments that we aim to grow our own food stuffs, chickens that provide our eggs, a rabbit that loves a cuddle, we have an abundant pond with frogs, newts, fish and many insect that we openly invite families to come and help manage, we always have something to do, and somewhere to just sit and have a picnic while the children are safe to feel involved and accepted, parents can volunteer with the many jobs in our outside area, we always have something to build or look after How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? we have an open communication line, where we make ourselves available whether this be a chat on the door or a more detailed feedback through email communication. we also offer updates through the session by phone call. we are able to share activities and also sign post to other organisations that can also offer support How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? we are a single ground level building with easy access throughout, we have wide doors for equipment to pass through with ease. although we are based on a farm, we do have private parking and an access route to all a outside areas, there are no steps currently as we use the natural incline of the bank. there are rest areas with seating both inside and outside and plenty of space. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? we can be contacted either by telephone, email, through our webpage, or even through our social media contact form. once we have been contacted we will send out an application pack and you can join once application is completed and returned What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continuously reflecting, and building upon what we have, we are just trying to widen the communities knowledge of us. we are currently finding ways to raise money for outside egg chairs and sensory areas.

local_offer: As and OFSTED registered childminder I offer a safe, nurturing and stimulating environment where I aim for children feel valued, respected and supported in their individual development. My aim is to create a home from home setting that promotes emotional wellbeing, encourages curiosity and fosters independence. I follow the EYFS to support each child's learning and development through age appropriate activities and play based learning. I will work closely with each child to build trusting relationships, helping them express feelings, develop resilience and learn social skills such as sharing, taking turns and empathy. I believe in working in partnership with parents and carers, ensuring open communication and regular updates on their child's progress, needs and achievements. By working together, we can offer children the consistency and encouragement they need to thrive.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I want all children in my setting to feel happy, secure and empowered to reach their full potential. I build strong relationships with children and support them in building their confidence and independence. I aim to support families as well as children by working in partnership with them, offering consistent two way communication. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed training in developing children's learning. I am working towards my Level 3 in Homebased Childcare. I am happy to take on additional training which may help me to meet children's individual needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents. When a child first starts I ask parents to complete an all about me form and information about their daily routines. I like to gain a good understanding of the child's interests and their current stage of development so that I can plan activities which engage and excite them whilst extending their current abilities. I communicate with parents through the baby days app for daily diaries and photos. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children are monitored and observed and I will share information about children's progress and daily routines through the baby days app. Any concerns about a child's development will be discussed with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is accessible for children, both inside and outside. I am happy to discuss a child's individual needs and will be accommodating where possible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I can be contacted by phone or email. I am happy to discuss individual needs and care with families. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information from Buckinghamshire Council and my key contact. I am happy to complete further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for. I regularly review my environment, toys and experience to ensure each child's individual needs are met.

name: AuDacity
description: I deliver workshops and information sessions for young people who fall under the neurodivergent umbrella, focusing on topics that impact them differently than their neurotypical peers. With a background in senior HR, I’ve long held a strong interest in workplace inclusivity- particularly neuro-inclusivity- and how, given the right tools and environment, neurodivergent individuals can not just survive but thrive. This passion came into sharper focus following my diagnosis of AuDHD (a dual diagnosis of Autism and ADHD) in 2024. Having been on my journey of self-discovery, learning to understand my brain and work with it rather than against it, I now aim to empower others to do the same. My work combines lived experience with up-to-date research, practical strategies, and real-world tools to support neurodivergent young people in being their best selves, whatever that may look like for them.

name: Joanne Dudman
description: Jo’s Little Sunflowers Childcare I’m an OFSTED Registered childminder with 10 years experience and achieved a Good grade in my last inspection (June 2024). I offer childcare in a safe, caring, friendly, and homely environment, providing fun educational toys for all ages in a creative and learning environment. I follow the EYFS framework and support learning through play, curiosity and exploration. About me: I set up my business ‘Jo’s Little Sunflowers Childcare’ in January 2016 and have been caring for children from the ages of 6 months to 12 years ever since. I am a very honest, reliable and understanding person with a warm, approachable and friendly personality. I am extremely flexible and have lots of patience and time for children and adults. Having used childminders myself in the past, I can fully understand how important it is to leave your child with someone who prioritises their safety and well-being, supports their learning and development and encourages them to be the best they can be. My Setting: I live in Loudwater with my fiancé and our 3 teenage children. We also have 2 pet cats and pet bunnies. We live on a very safe and quiet no through road, less than 2 minute walk to farmland, nature trails, woodland and grassed adventure playground for ages pre-school upwards. Children have access to the whole downstairs open planned area which includes toy units with a variety of educational and fun toys, mark-making and reading areas, play rugs, a table for crafts/activities/meals and a secure patio area accessed by patio doors. The gated outside patio area leads down some steps to a 120’ garden (the top third is surrounded by a 6ft fence and has a secure gate leading to the lower part of the garden). I provide upstairs travel cots for infants to sleep during the day. Activities: I provide lots of fun activities such as arts and crafts (painting, play dough, themed crafts for special events), role-playing (dressing up, food shop, cook and tea party, small world animals and people, dolls house, cars, trains and garage), musical sessions (action songs, musical instruments, dancing), reading (including activity learning books), cooking, tent play and outdoor play. We frequently do theme tuff trays for adventure and sensory play inside and out. Outdoor activities also include garden play (sand and water table, sandpit and paddling pool), walks to my local farm to see the sheep and chickens plus shire horses and woodland walks to include learning about nature and tiny beasts, trips to the library, various parks and duck ponds/rivers. I attend regular local playgroups, singing and rhyme groups and soft play centres. I am a member of the Forest Childcare Association (giving small children the opportunity to spend time in the great outdoors on a regular basis). I am a National Trust member and frequent the sites. Qualifications: I have attended many courses including Level 3 Preparing to work in Home-Based Childcare, Paediatric First Aid (refreshed and up to date), Safeguarding Children (refreshed and up to date), Level 2 Basic Food Hygiene, Effective Curriculum and Assessment and Supporting language development in the early years. I am a member of PACEY (Professional Association for Childcare and Early Years), DBS checked and registered with the Information Commissioner's Office. I have a full clean driving license and drive a 7-seat people carrier. I am on the Directory of Early Education Funding and can offer 3 and 4-year-olds and eligible 2-year-olds up to 30 hours per week of free childcare during term time. Baby’s Days: I use a system called Baby's Days - outstanding software for EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage) management. Parents can view the system's features via a mobile phone app or PC, including their child’s progress, daily diary notes and photos. Please get in touch and I can send you my Information Pack, which includes my Parent Feedback Document.

local_offer: I aim to give families opportunities to access care for their children whatever their needs. Learning through play is key in my setting: the age and stage of the child is considered as well as their individual needs to ensure they enjoy their time with me. Every child is unique and will be treated as an individual. I have experience of caring for children with Dyspraxia, ADHD, Learning difficulties. I am keen to work closely with both parents and other professionals to support each child to reach their full potential. I am able to support families with additional needs. I have experience with children that have ADHD and dyspraxia and learning difficulties.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As with all registered Childminders in Buckinghamshire, I have a Key Contact within the Early Years Service, from whom we can access advice and information. They are happy to answer my questions or signpost to other appropriate services. Professionals are welcome to meet the child at our setting if parents wish. I am keen to support all families and develop my own knowledge. I will undergo further training if it is an area where I need more training. I am Epipen trained and very aware of allergic reactions or intolerances. I have experience with children that have learning difficulties, ADHD, DCD and can support children in their early years. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have undertaken various training courses in understanding learning difficulties. I have experience with ADHD, DCD, learning difficulties children. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work very closely with parents and other third parties to enable the best for the child. Learning journeys and trackers are shared with parents and daily communication is key. Resources or equipment will be adapted for each child depending on their needs. Information, activities and advice will be shared with parents to enable some transition for the child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child is different and requires different support or resources. I will work with parents and discuss on a 1 to 1 their child's needs and requirements. Working with relevant third parties and sharing information. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to most children and families. I am located within walking distance from the hospital and have a regular bus route for those needing public transport, on the next road. I have a very small step to the front door, and to the back garden. My garden is all one level and has astroturf grass so that all children regardless of age can access the garden without hazards or getting muddy. I use the ground floor for play and activities. This is all on one level and free-flowing from room to room. Children can sleep up or downstairs depending on their needs and requirements. My toilet is located upstairs but provision can be made if an alternative is required. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? As an established childminder, I have links with the local schools and pre-schools. We work closely supporting children through transitions. I provide a transition pack when the child moves to a different setting. When children arrive families complete an ‘All about Me’ sheet, provide family photos and any special comforters (regardless of the age of the child). I am happy for practitioners from other settings to come and visit me before a child starts to help them to settle (whether new to us or moving on elsewhere). I encourage parents to have some ‘settling in visits’ with their child. Settling in sessions are provided to all families but can be adapted to each child. name: Joanne Talbot
description: Welcome to Joanne's Place, an OUTSTANDING Ofsted registered childcare setting run by myself, Jo Talbot. I have been childminding for over 20 years and have been awarded my Outstanding grade 4 times by Ofsted of which I am hugely proud!! I provide a warm, loving and secure environment in which children can learn and develop. We have a huge range of toys and resources for all ages/stages of children's development. The children enjoy a wide variety of activities, both indoors and outdoors together with regular trips out in the community. The children I look after have become part of the family and really enjoy coming to our home every day. I have completed an "Introduction to Childcare Practice" course, I am DBS checked, I am First Aid qualified, I have a Level 2 in Food Safety in Catering, Child Protection and Safeguarding children, "Introduction to EYFS" and NVQ Level 3 in Children's Care, Learning and Development plus many others! I am an Accredited Childminder which means I am able to offer eligible children, from 9 months to 5 years, 15 hours of early education funding per week, much the same as they would have at a pre-school/nursery. I can also offer 30 hours of early education funding for parents that are eligible. I am able to provide an information pack to prospective parents which explains a little bit about me, my family and the way in which I run my childcare setting. Please get in touch if you would like me to send you a copy.

local_offer: My setting is all inclusive and does not discriminate against any child. I have a Special Educational Needs and Disability Policy (which I am happy to share with parents) which clearly explains the measures I will go to if I feel a child in my setting has special educational needs or disabilities. I am always happy to talk to new parents if their child has these needs and will discuss whether my setting would be suitable for them and whether changes could be made to accommodate their needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a registered childminder, I have a Key Contact at Buckinghamshire Council with the Early Years Team, and with parental permission, I may contact them for further advice. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites…) are available for us to access. I welcome other professionals into the setting who may have involvement with a child and I am keen to access further training to support a child’s development, for example, speech and language (Speech Therapist). I am happy to attend Multi-Professionals Meetings if required. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Supporting early language and SEND code of practice. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and we will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a small step leading to the front door. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible for example, adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they have the opportunity to visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

name: Free Baby Classes at The Little Gym Handy Cross
description: The Little Gym Handy Cross is offering free baby classes for parents and their little ones aged 10 to 15 weeks. These sessions are designed specifically to support new parents during what can be a very isolating time - when partners may have returned to work and NHS support begins to taper off. What are the classes? Our Pre-Bugs sessions are a four-week course of baby development classes, led by our specialists, that combine: - Gentle movement and sensory play to aid development - Music, singing, and massage - Early cognitive and motor skill development - Practical support and knowledge for parents The classes offer a unique blend of bonding, education, and fun - helping babies build strong foundations and helping parents feel supported and empowered. Locations: - The Little Gym Windsor - The Little Gym Handy Cross (High Wycombe) They’re warm, welcoming, and completely free – no catch, no hidden costs. Families can now book in advance for classes beginning in September and beyond. If baby isn’t quite 10 weeks old yet, parents can still join the waitlist to secure a place. Please visit our website for more information and to book.

description: Brindley House Day Nursery and Preschool cares for children aged from three months to five-years-old. There are bright and spacious open plan rooms, with each area designed to enhance your child’s development and well-being. Trained staff organise daily activities to help your child to settle in quickly and to socialise and build friendships. Your child’s creativity and language skills are encouraged by a wide range of learning and play activities. The nursery provides beautifully designed external play areas for toddlers and preschool children with a fantastic water wall feature - great for those summer days! We also have a new refurbished Sensory Room which is available to all children attending our nursrey. Our Ready for School Programme designed by our expert early years team prepares children for school transitions; children will graduate from Bright Horizons Preschool ready to have more fun developing their reading, writing and mathematical skills. Children will benefit from our nutritionally balanced menus; our on-site chef freshly prepares all the food and can cater for everyone's needs.

local_offer: We have a highly qualified SENCO of 16 years who comes with lots of knowledge and experience. Our SENCO puts in early intervention that is required to support your child in all areas of needs. Your child will also be taken out to complete intervention sessions 1:1 so the intervention is of high quality. Our SENCO also provides staff with important information and skills on how best to support your child within the room. Our SENCO also meets with and keeps in regular contact with the parents of our children who are needing early intervention or continuous support provision. EHCP are also applied for here at nursery as well as any funding we may intitled to to support with the intervention sessions. We also have a newly refurbished Sensory Room where are intervention session are held. A nice calming environment for quality sessions.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? CACHE level 3 Award for SENCO’s , Autism awareness, 2-day SENCO training, Good Autism practise, Speech and language specialism, Occupational Therapy Needs, Sign-along, ADHD training, Transition training, Attention Autism Bucket Time training, Curiosity Programme Training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome the parents into the setting firstly during the settling-in week when their child first starts nursery. These sessions are a great opportunity for the parents to see the room their child will be based in and how they interact with the staff and other children. The staff use this as an opportunity to gain as much information about the child to ensure they have a smooth start to nursery. Throughout the year the nursery holds events where the parents are invited in such as Father’s & Mother’s day breakfast, Teddy bears picnics and nursery graduation. We use our app ‘Family’ to communicate not only daily with the parents but also for all observations and 4 monthly assessments. Once the assessments have been completed the parents can have a meeting with their key person to discuss this. Parents can request to meet with their key person at any point to discuss or share anything and the nursery will also accommodate this as soon as possible in person or a phone call whichever the parents prefer. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The nursery would meet frequently with the parents to discuss any targets/ progress of any children with SEND. Offering clear feedback on what we’ve achieved at nursery and how we can work together to support. If any external agencies were due to visit the nursery would ensure the parents are aware in advance so they have the opportunity to attend if they are able to. If they are unable to attend feedback from the visit would be shared with the parent after the visit has been completed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor environment has been adapted to be fully wheelchair accessible. The garden is fully accessible by all too. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please enquire about starting to use our services by emailing or giving us a call on 01494 312 562 What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Lots more training available to all staff as our SEND provision changes all the time and all our staff are kept up to date.

What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We will undertake any training required to support the specific needs of any child in our care. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We prioritise open communication with parents from the start, gathering as much information from parents as possible, and sharing details of children's progress regularly. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use Tapestry to give daily updates as well as progress reports. We will implement the Assess-Plan-Do-Review system to support children with SEND How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have a step up to the front door and 2 steps down to the garden. A ramp can be provided and the doorways and hallways are wide enough for a wheelchair. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?
