local_offer: My home-based childminding setting provides a nurturing and communication-friendly environment. I support children with communication and interaction needs using visual aids, Makaton signs, consistent routines, and play-based language development. I adapt interactions and activities to suit individual communication styles and work closely with parents to ensure a consistent approach.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? aim to help children with SEND, particularly those with communication needs, to feel confident, understood, and included. My setting focuses on building strong relationships and supporting early language, social interaction, and listening skills. I work in partnership with families to celebrate progress and overcome barriers to communication. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed the following training: · Safeguarding · Supporting Children with SEND in the Early Years These courses have helped me understand how to identify and support a range of additional needs, with a focus on early intervention and inclusive practice. I plan to continue my professional development with further training in communication strategies such as Makaton and early speech development. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I involve parents through daily conversations, regular progress updates, and shared learning goals. Parents are welcome to share strategies from home, provide insights into their child’s needs, and contribute to planning support. I value ongoing communication and encourage a strong home-setting partnership. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Progress is shared through verbal feedback, observations, photos, and learning updates. For children with SEND, I offer more frequent updates and may create an individual learning plan with specific targets. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home setting is a first-floor maisonette, with clearly organised play areas, low-level resources, and visual cues to support communication. A quiet space is available for children needing time to regulate. While I do not have a garden, I regularly take children on local outdoor outings and visits to parks to provide fresh air and physical play opportunities. I am happy to make further adaptations to meet a child’s specific communication needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact me directly to arrange a visit. During this visit, I will learn about your child’s needs and explain how I can support them. A settling-in period is offered to build familiarity and ease the transition. I tailor routines and interactions based on each child’s profile from the outset. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I’m keen to keep learning more about how to support communication and interaction. I plan to do more SEND-related training, use more visual aids to help children, and build stronger connections with local services like Speech and Language Therapy. My goal is to make sure my setting is welcoming, supportive, and meets every child’s needs.

local_offer: Our teaching staff undertake a rigorous programme of professional learning to help them meet the needs of our diverse cohort of SEND learners in line with our school approach to quality first inclusive teaching. name: John Colet School
description: Mixed-gender secondary school in Wendover, Aylesbury for 11 to 18-year-olds. The school opened in the 1950s, catering for children between the ages of 11 and 15. At this time the school had around 400 students. During the 1960’s it expanded when the Modern Languages and Humanities block and the Gym were built. In the 1980's a lot of dramatic changes to the school took place. In 1982 the Biology Labs were built, before major renovation in 1989 saw the original part of the school being demolished because maintenance costs were too high, with the school being substantially rebuilt over the following three years. The school now has over 1000 pupils aged 11 to 18.

local_offer: At John Colet we regularly and carefully review the quality of teaching for all students,including those at risk of underachievement. This includes reviewing and, where necessary, improving, teachers’ understanding of strategies to identify and support vulnerable students and their knowledge of the SEND most frequently encountered. Key stage managers and subject team leaders review the data for each learning cycle to target students where extra intervention may be required. The teacher/STL/HOY as appropriate and SENCO will consider all of the information gathered from the available sources and from within the school about the student’s progress, alongside national data and expectations of progress. This should include high-quality and accurate formative assessment, using effective tools and early assessment materials. Once a student has been identified as having SEND needs the best way of offering assistance needs to be planned. A student with SEND should be distinct from a student with ‘behavioural issues or concerns’ where the underlying issue needs to be identified and addressed or supported. As part of this process an assessment of possible SEND will be undertaken through feedback from teachers and possible diagnostic tools as appropriate. Graduated Response: The following methods are used to identify need, implement learning strategies and evaluate progress: - transfer documents from previous schools - visits to primary schools - information from parents/carers - screening for literacy difficulties - testing for exam concessions - staff meetings/liaison - classroom observations (I.L. local_offer: At John Hampden Grammar School (JHGS), we strive to create a community in which all students can flourish and #BeMore in all aspects of their academic and personal development. However, we acknowledge that each pupil is an individual with unique needs and experiences and so some pupils require more support than others in order to thrive. If these pupils are to achieve their full potential, we must recognise their needs and plan accordingly; some pupils require help throughout their time in school, whilst others may need a little extra support for a short period of time to help them overcome temporary needs. John Hampden Grammar school aims to provide all pupils with strategies for dealing with their needs in a supportive environment and ensure that they all have meaningful access to a broad and balanced curriculum. In particular, we aim to: - Encourage all pupils to #BeMore Ambitious, Kind, Resilient, Independent, Knowledgeable, and Involved, irrespective of personal challenges. - Enable every pupil to experience success. - Promote individual confidence and a positive attitude. - Ensure that all pupils, whatever their special educational needs, receive appropriate educational provision through a relevant, broad, and balanced curriculum that prioritises High Quality Teaching and demonstrates coherence and progression in learning. - Give pupils with SEN equal opportunities to take part in all aspects of the school’s provision, as far as is appropriate. - Identify, assess, record, and regularly review pupils’ progress and needs. - Involve parents/carers in planning and supporting at all stages of their son’s development. - Work collaboratively with parents, other professionals, and support services through the Local Offer. - Deploy the resources of the Learning Support Department in an effective way. - Use the SEN Code of Practice as a framework for identification of, and provision for, pupils with special educational needs. - Ensure that the responsibility held by all staff and governors for SEN is implemented and maintained. https://www.jhgs.bucks.sch.uk/49/sen-and-learning-support What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? name: John Hampden School Wendover, Early Years Nursery Class
description: Our school runs an Early Years Class for children who are rising four and we are offering the 30-hour flexible entitlement, meaning that children in this class may attend for six hours a day, with the option of a chargeable lunch club. Our expectation is that all children who are offered a place should eventually attend at least every morning session each week (8:45am to 11:45am) following a staggered start if preferred. Priority is given to the oldest children in the cohort and parents can apply for a place in this class to start in the Autumn Term. If by January, the class is not full (26 places) parents may apply for a place for their child in the Early Years Class starting in the Spring Term. Applications for a place in the Early Years class should be made directly to the school. In the event of oversubscription, criteria outlined in the school’s admission policy apply. Please note admission prior to Rising 5 does not guarantee admission to the reception class. Applications for the Early Years class are made separately and managed by the school.

description: We provide both Breakfast Club and After School Club for children attending the John Hampden and Wendover Junior Schools. I have a dedicated team who enjoy the challenge of making everyday fun and entertaining for the children attending. name: Jonathan Page Play Centre (After School Club)
description: Jonathan Page Play Centre Afterschool Club and Holiday Scheme, welcomes all children from the age of 4 up to their thirteenth birthday from all schools, so it's a great place for your child to make new friends in a safe, stimulating and, above all, fun environment. Your child can choose between structured activities and free play opportunities which take place indoors and outdoors ranging from arts and crafts, board games, table football, ball games, pool table, role play, a wide range of toys and books and much more. The secure outdoor area has a multi-use games area, football pitch, go-kart track, activity climbing frames, and a Learning Lodge which enables the children to spend plenty of time in the fresh air no matter what the weather is like. Our qualified and DBS-checked playworkers understand the importance of play, taking a keen interest in each child’s development, providing fun activities that meet each child’s social, physical, intellectual, creative, and emotional needs. Caring for your children after school in our After School Club: We offer a friendly and relaxed environment for your child to enjoy after the school day. To attend After School Club, children must be 4 years of age and in reception. We know and understand that most children are hungry straight after school. This is why we provide a healthy snack sat at a table so everyone can socialise and catch up. The children help clear up and are encouraged to try new foods. After their snack, the children play with our vast range of toys, get creative at the craft table, play outdoors, and generally have lots of fun with their friends until they are collected by their parents, guardians. Our team has regular feedback sessions with the children talking about ideas for future topics, what they enjoy and what they don’t do that the team can plan effectively. Hours: The After School Club runs from 3:15pm to 6pm Monday to Friday during term time. School Collection Service: A collection service from a number of schools in and around Aylesbury is offered for a small daily fee: Walking Collection Service: Thomas Hickman School Minibus Collection Service: Buckingham Park School St Louis Catholic School If your child’s school is not listed above, please contact us and register your interest in a school collection to be arranged where possible. Bookings: We accept advance and last-minute bookings for the After School Club and Holiday Playschemes through our online booking system. To register and book activities for your child please visit our website.

local_offer: Jonathan Page Play Centre recognises that some children have additional needs or physical disabilities that require particular support and assistance. We will assess the individual needs of each child in consultation with their parents prior to their attending the centre. Whilst we are unable to offer 1 to 1 care, we will make reasonable adjustments within our setting to ensure all children can take part in play opportunities at a level appropriate to their needs. We are a play setting offering an After School Club for children between the age of 4 up to their thirteenth birthday. As a play setting we do not have a curriculum we have to adhere to. Each week has a different topic and we plan arts, crafts and games around these topics. To ensure every child can take part in these activities we will adapt them to their relevant skill level.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a Play Centre, we do not offer any specialist services and expertise but we are happy to signpost parents to services we know of or ask the Buckinghamshire Council Early Years team for advice. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Rebecca Murphy is our Play Centre Manager and has attended the course “Initial SENCO Training” and will be attending the “SEN Support and the Graduated Approach” course. Information from any training attended is shared with all staff at monthly meetings. The majority of staff are qualified within Early Years. We continually reflect upon our practice and will attend training when a particular need is identified. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The Jonathan Page Play Centre is managed by Aylesbury Town Council. We have an open-door policy and promote and value all parents’ views and opinions. We carry out a parent and children survey after every Holiday Playscheme and twice during the school year for the After School Club. We encourage parents to email or phone us directly if they have any comments or concerns. We encourage ongoing dialogue with their child’s key worker. We regularly update our Facebook page. We hold an Open Day once a year in July and for After School Club we have a Parent/Children Evening twice a year, where parents are welcome to stay and play with their child and see the child in the setting of the centre. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We give regular feedback when parents drop off or pick up the children and we do observations on Early Years children, which we share with the parents. We contact the school (with parent’s permission) to see what procedures or actions the school have put in place so that we can try and continue with these whilst the child is attending the play centre. We are also happy to attend relevant meetings with other settings, outside agencies or specialists if parents would like us to attend. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The Play Centre is all on a ground floor and there are no steps to access the centre and the outdoor area. We have one main play hall and one smaller room for quieter activities. The outdoor area is large and secure with climbing frames, go-kart track and multi-use games area. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? At our setting, we treat every child as an individual. Initially, we arrange for parents to visit with their child. We show you around the facilities, introduce you to the team and discuss your child’s requirements and discuss any reasonable adjustments we can make to the running of the After School Club, Holiday Playscheme. Once we established that we are the right setting for your child we will allocate your child a Keyworker. The key worker will get to know your child and together with other members of staff carry out observations which we will share with you, and with consent we will contact other professionals and your child’s school if required. If you have any concerns about your child you should speak with your child’s key worker who will be able to advise you further Your child’s Key worker will work with both you and your child. This relationship will ensure that we share knowledge concerning your child and their development. This knowledge begins with the ‘Additional Information Form’ for Early Years children and ‘All about Me’ section from the Journals. We will discuss observations with you and with your consent can share them with your child’s school, to identify next steps for your child. With your permission, we will contact the Buckinghamshire Council Early Years’ Service if required, either for advice or to make a referral with any concerns. Our setting is all on one level including the outside area. The centre has two accessible toilets. Visuals aids are used to assist children with the daily routine. Whilst we are unable to offer one-to-one care we will make reasonable adjustments to ensure that children can access our services and are made to feel welcome. We can provide photos for booklets, are happy to arrange multiple visits so the children get to know the team and the environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continuing to encourage our staff to attend training courses and if we identify that there is an increase of a particular special need of the children who are attending our sessions, then we will look for appropriate training for staff like we have done when we noted an increase of children on the autism spectrum attending our setting.

description: Our aim is to offer as many young people as possible the opportunity to enjoy learning and playing the beautiful game of football. Through football, we help young people develop with an interest in exercise, outdoor activity, decision making, responsibility, respect, and teamwork. We are a FA accredited Youth Football Club with approximately 400 registered players. Coaches emphasise development over results, creating a welcoming and supportive environment for all players, whatever their ability. We are also one of the first clubs in Buckinghamshire to establish a girls-only team 10 years ago. We currently have girl's teams from Under 6s through to Under 18s. in 2025, we will also have our first men's team - made up mostly from our youth players who left for university and have returned 4 years later, now wanting to play for us again. We must be doing something right...

name: Jonathan Page Play Centre (Holiday Playschemes)
description: Jonathan Page Play Centre Afterschool Club and Holiday Scheme, welcomes all children from the age of 4 up to their thirteenth birthday from all schools, so it's a great place for your child to make new friends in a safe, stimulating and, above all, fun environment. Your child can choose between structured activities and free play opportunities which take place indoors and outdoors ranging from arts and crafts, board games, table football, ball games, pool table, role play, a wide range of toys and books and much more. The secure outdoor area has a multi-use games area, football pitch, go-kart track, activity climbing frames, and a Learning Lodge which enables the children to spend plenty of time in the fresh air no matter what the weather is like. Our qualified and DBS-checked playworkers understand the importance of play, taking a keen interest in each child’s development, providing fun activities that meet each child’s social, physical, intellectual, creative, and emotional needs. Holiday Playschemes: Whether your child wants to come and join us for half a day, only on some days or the entire school holidays, we offer a wide range of activities that will ensure that your child has lots of fun at each and every visit. Our friendly and experienced team of Play-workers ensure that every day is bursting with fun activities for every child. No matter what time your child arrives with us, they will be greeted with a smile, made welcome and are able to relax and play straight away. At about 9:15am, we have a morning meeting where we go over the safety rules and any news that the children or staff would like to share. We tell the children which adult-led crafts are available, and any special events and activities that are coming up. After the meeting, the children are free to play. We provide healthy snacks in the morning and afternoon and water is available for the children throughout the day, however, you will need to provide a packed lunch for the picnic-style lunch, which is followed by organised team games for all. After team games, it’s free to play again. A light snack is served at 3:45pm, followed by more free play until they are collected. Bookings: We accept advance and last-minute bookings for the After School Club and Holiday Playschemes through our online booking system. To register and book activities for your child please visit our website.

local_offer: Jonathan Page Play Centre recognises that some children have additional needs or physical disabilities that require particular support and assistance. We will assess the individual needs of each child in consultation with their parents prior to their attending the Holiday Play schemes. Whilst we are unable to offer 1 to 1 care, we will make reasonable adjustments within our setting to ensure all children can take part in play opportunities at a level appropriate to their needs. We are a play setting offering a Holiday Play scheme during the school holidays for children between the age of 4 up to their 13th birthday. As a play setting we do not have a curriculum we have to adhere to. Each week has a different topic and we plan arts, crafts and games around these topics. To ensure every child can take part in these activities we will adapt them to their relevant skill level.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a Play Centre, we do not offer any specialist services and expertise but we are happy to signpost parents to services we know of or ask the Buckinghamshire Council Early Years team for advice. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Rebecca Murphy is our Play Centre Manager and has attended the course “Initial SENCO Training” and will be attending the “SEN Support and the Graduated Approach” course. Information from any training attended is shared with all staff at monthly meetings. The majority of staff are qualified within Early Years. We continually reflect upon our practice and will attend training when a particular need is identified. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The Jonathan Page Play Centre is managed by Aylesbury Town Council. We have an open-door policy and promote and value all parents’ views and opinions. We carry out a parent and children survey after every Holiday Playscheme and twice during the school year for the After School Club. We encourage parents to email or phone us directly if they have any comments or concerns. We encourage ongoing dialogue with their child’s key worker. We regularly update our Facebook page. We hold an Open Day once a year in July and for After School Club we have a Parent/Children Evening twice a year, where parents are welcome to stay and play with their child and see the child in the setting of the centre. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We give regular feedback when parents drop off or pick up the children and we do observations on Early Years children, which we share with the parents. We contact the school (with parent’s permission) to see what procedures or actions the school have put in place so that we can try and continue with these whilst the child is attending the play centre. We are also happy to attend relevant meetings with other settings, outside agencies or specialists if parents would like us to attend. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The Play Centre is all on a ground floor and there are no steps to access the centre and the outdoor area. We have one main play hall and one smaller room for quieter activities. The outdoor area is large and secure with climbing frames, go-kart track and multi-use games area. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? At our setting, we treat every child as an individual. Initially, we arrange for parents to visit with their child. We show you around the facilities, introduce you to the team and discuss your child’s requirements and discuss any reasonable adjustments we can make to the running of the After School Club, Holiday Playscheme. Once we established that we are the right setting for your child we will allocate your child a Keyworker. The key worker will get to know your child and together with other members of staff carry out observations which we will share with you, and with consent we will contact other professionals and your child’s school if required. If you have any concerns about your child you should speak with your child’s key worker who will be able to advise you further Your child’s Key worker will work with both you and your child. This relationship will ensure that we share knowledge concerning your child and their development. This knowledge begins with the ‘Additional Information Form’ for Early Years children and ‘All about Me’ section from the Journals. We will discuss observations with you and with your consent can share them with your child’s school, to identify next steps for your child. With your permission, we will contact the Buckinghamshire Council's Early Years Service if required, either for advice or to make a referral with any concerns Our setting is all on one level including the outside area. The centre has two accessible toilets. Visuals aids are used to assist children with the daily routine. Whilst we are unable to offer one-to-one care we will make reasonable adjustments to ensure that children can access our services and are made to feel welcome. We can provide photos for booklets, are happy to arrange multiple visits so the children get to know the team and the environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continuing to encourage our staff to attend training courses and if we identify that there is an increase of a particular special need of the children who are attending our sessions, then we will look for appropriate training for staff like we have done when we noted an increase of children on the autism spectrum attending our setting.

local_offer: First Steps First is a family run day nursery for children aged from 0 to 5 years olds, where we are an enthusiastic and fun loving team, who strive to meet the needs of all the children in the setting and give them the best start in life as possible and plan and meet their needs on a individual basis.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At First Steps First, we aim to provide an inclusive, nurturing environment where children with SEND are supported to thrive. Through personalised support plans, a dedicated key worker system, and the use of visual timetables and structured routines, we ensure every child can engage meaningfully in nursery life. We work closely with families, recognising them as key partners in their child’s development, and provide regular updates and guidance. Our focus is on promoting wellbeing, confidence, independence, and preparing children for a smooth transition to their next stage of learning. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? At First Steps First, our team regularly undertakes SEND-specific training to ensure we are equipped to meet the diverse needs of the children in our care. Recently, staff have completed training in areas such as supporting children with autism, understanding sensory processing difficulties, and promoting inclusive practice in early years settings. Team members have also received training on the use of visual supports and strategies for managing behaviour in a positive, consistent way. Ongoing professional development is a priority, and we are committed to keeping our knowledge up to date to provide the highest quality support for children with SEND and their families. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At First Steps First, we believe in strong partnerships with parents and carers. We involve families through regular communication, including daily updates, parent meetings, and shared planning for children’s individual needs. Parents are encouraged to contribute to support plans and are always welcome to share insights, concerns, or ideas. We also invite families to take part in nursery events, stay and play sessions and parents evenings to support the children's learning and development. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? local_offer: Jordans Village Nursery School regards every child as an individual, with individual needs. All children will have access to a varied and well balanced curriculum in line with the EYFS guidelines, in which we will take into account their individual and special educational needs. We adhere to the government and LEA SEND code of practice.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have close links with Buckinghamshire Council SENCO Team. We can give advice on outside specialists. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENCO has attended a 2 day SENCO course which details paperwork needed should your child ever need extra funding. We have a member of staff who has a level 3 SENCO qualification A speech and language course. An autism course. All staff have attended Makaton training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are always grateful for parental support, whether it be reading a story to the children, gardening, helping with cooking or sharing some news. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share information using our on-line record keeping system called Tapestry. We also have an open door policy where you are welcome to talk to your child's key worker or indeed any member of staff whenever is convenient to you. Our SENCO is available to give advice on targeted activities for you to do at home with child to aid their progress. Parents, key workers and the SENCO will be involved with writing and reviewing all targets for the child, these targets will fully consider the parents and child's view. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The village hall, where the nursery operates from is an older building. Whilst the doors are wide enough and the floor is on one level, we unfortunately do not have a disabled toilet or a toilet with a large enough space for a wheelchair. Our outside space is one level. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have close links with local schools to ensure a smooth transition. Reception teachers visit us to talk to the child and key worker. With respect to Jordans school, the older nursery children attend on a weekly basis to familiarise themselves. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our SENCO attends regular SENCO briefings this keeps us up to date with current practise.

name: Senior Youth Theatre
description: Join our Youth Theatre and make friends, learn new skills, and discover the magic of performing. Work with professional artists, experience the Wycombe Swan’s rehearsal and performance spaces, and learn all about theatre in a fun, inclusive, and friendly environment. This group is ideal for anyone looking to explore performance, as the focus of these sessions are on drama and creativity – but please note that we’re not a dance/singing group! Our terms usually run for 10 to 12 weeks – depending on school and bank holidays. Our Senior Youth Theatre costs £90 a term (or £50 for half a term) and is for Ages 12 to 18. Workshops are every Monday from 7pm to 9pm in the Oak Room in Wycombe Swan’s Old Town Hall venue. It is our belief that the arts are for everyone, and that no young person should miss out due to financial constraints. For this reason, we offer full and partial bursaries so that anybody can take part. If you would like to apply for a bursary, please get in touch. When you have paid for your place, please email the Creative Learning team for a registration form to confirm your place. Please visit our website for more information and to book.
organisation: Wycombe Swan Theatre (Trafalgar Entertainment Trust) The Wycombe Swan is one of the UK's leading regional theatres. Presenting an eclectic mix of productions throughout the year, the Wycombe Swan is home to great comedy acts (including the Chuckle Brothers), dance (including Swan Lake), drama, musicals (including Hairspray), special local events, as well as the Wycombe Swan Summer Youth Project - an annual musical production featuring 250 local young people. It is also home to the Wycombe Swan Youth Theatre - a permanent Youth Theatre Company open to 10 to 19 year olds. As well as running workshops and performance-based activities, the Youth Theatre present a show every year. The Wycombe Swan complex consists of the main theatre, Wycombe Swan Town Hall, and the Oak Room - an ornate setting for functions and parties. It has a capacity of 1076. admin@wycombeswan.co.uk https://wycombeswan.co.uk/Online/

local_offer: Courses and support for Students with Learning Difficulties through: - Mainstream Courses and Apprenticeships - The Life Skills Centre - Therapies - Exam Access Arrangements - Assistive Technology - Support for Vulnerable Students - Staffing Our Foundation Learning provision offers a range of courses specifically designed for students with learning difficulties and disabilities. Courses range from Entry 1 to Entry 3 and support the development of a range of areas such as literacy, numeracy, ICT, employability and independent living skills. Courses are based on the college campus but could include work experience placements. Referrals for Foundation courses are through our central admissions team. Most courses start in September. Support on Mainstream Courses and Apprenticeships We also offer Learning Support to any student with a learning difficulty or disability on our Foundation and mainstream courses and on apprenticeships. This could include LSA support in or out of class, loan of specialist equipment, exam access arrangements and tutor adaptations. Specialist support such as BSL interpreters can also be arranged if needed. Referrals for learning support can be made at any time during the year by phoning the local offer number. The Life Skills Centre Our Life Skills Centre is a specialist provision for students with more complex needs. Students follow individualised programmes designed specifically to meet their interests and long-term goals. Learning can take place on the college campus, on work experience placements or out in the local community. The Life Skills Centre is based in a separate building on the Aylesbury College site. Referrals for this provision are through Buckinghamshire Council only. Therapies We currently have Speech and Language Therapists, Physiotherapists and Occupational therapists working with students across our Life Skills, Foundation and mainstream provisions. Exam Access Arrangements We can provide access for exams such as a reader, extra time of a scribe provided that we have up to date evidence of the young person's need. Where this is not available we will arrange for an assessment with our external specialist teacher. Assistive Technology We have a fully equipped assistive technology room which as a range of software and hardware to help students access their course more easily. Students can also borrow laptops and voice recorders if required. Support for Vulnerable Students Students who are unable to access the college campus independently can be supported by LSAs during breaks and lunchtime. local_offer: Fulmer Nursey is a privately owned setting that caters for up to 38 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We are a family run business and pride ourselves in our personal approach. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share in their children’s achievements with us. We also want to provide an environment where parents can share their hopes and concerns too. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Fulmer nursery aim to give children the best possible start to their education. To ensure this happens, if appropriate, we will work with families to seek support from outside agencies and will implement recommended strategies according to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Inclusion Development-speech and language - all staff Sen training for new SENCOs - Deputy Managers supporting children with SEN in the early years - all staff How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We operate an open-door policy and strive to provide a warm, friendly, welcoming setting so that parents feel confident in talking to us regarding their children. Parents are invited in if we have any concerns regarding their childs development, to discuss any action plans or strategies we may need to put in place. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time by asking their child’s Key Person. We will discuss progress at Key Person Meetings, and through our 2-year-old progress checks and end of year summary assessment sheets. For children with SEND we try to ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? . We provide a safe and accessible indoor and outdoor environment, where we help the children to reach their goals by learning through play, having fun and developing their interests. The children’s personal, social, moral and spiritual development will be nurtured, with emphasis on developing personal values and independence. At Fulmer nursery we have full disabled access to the setting, there is also a large disabled toilet and changing area.We are a pack-away setting so we are able to adapt the layout of the room as needed. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents and families are welcome to come along to our open day sessions to look at the setting, meet the team and talk through any queries. We have an information booklet that gives details of the application process. Parents with children with SEND are invited to make a special visit to discuss how we can best meet their needs We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We endeavour to visit the local schools with children who are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently auditing the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and will plan our training accordingly. At present we are developing a ‘quiet area/sensory area’ in the quiet room within the hall to provide somewhere for children to get away from the busy environment of the nursery and to do focused individual, paired and small group activities.

local_offer: Fulmer Nursey is a privately owned setting that caters for up to 38 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We are a family run business and pride ourselves in our personal approach. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share in their children’s achievements with us. We also want to provide an environment where parents can share their hopes and concerns too. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Fulmer nursery aim to give children the best possible start to their education. To ensure this happens, if appropriate, we will work with families to seek support from outside agencies and will implement recommended strategies according to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Inclusion Development-speech and language - all staff Sen training for new SENCOs - Deputy Managers supporting children with SEN in the early years - all staff How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We operate an open-door policy and strive to provide a warm, friendly, welcoming setting so that parents feel confident in talking to us regarding their children. Parents are invited in if we have any concerns regarding their childs development, to discuss any action plans or strategies we may need to put in place. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time by asking their child’s Key Person. We will discuss progress at Key Person Meetings, and through our 2-year-old progress checks and end of year summary assessment sheets. For children with SEND we try to ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We provide a safe and accessible indoor and outdoor environment, where we help the children to reach their goals by learning through play, having fun and developing their interests. The children’s personal, social, moral and spiritual development will be nurtured, with emphasis on developing personal values and independence. At Fulmer nursery we have full disabled access to the setting, there is also a large disabled toilet and changing area.We are a pack-away setting so we are able to adapt the layout of the room as needed. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents and families are welcome to come along to our open day sessions to look at the setting, meet the team and talk through any queries. We have an information booklet that gives details of the application process. Parents with children with SEND are invited to make a special visit to discuss how we can best meet their needs We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We endeavour to visit the local schools with children who are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently auditing the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and will plan our training accordingly. At present we are developing a ‘quiet area/sensory area’ in the quiet room within the hall to provide somewhere for children to get away from the busy environment of the nursery and to do focused individual, paired and small group activities.

local_offer: Music Technology Club provides a safe, inclusive online learning environment where young people can develop creativity, confidence and digital skills through music production. Sessions are delivered live in small groups by experienced industry practitioners who are fully DBS-checked and trained in safeguarding. We adapt delivery to meet a wide range of SEND needs, offering clear step-by-step guidance, flexible pacing, visual resources, and opportunities for learners to engage in ways that suit them (cameras on/off, written or verbal participation, sensory breaks). Our tutors are experienced in working with learners with autism, communication and interaction needs, social, emotional and mental health difficulties, and sensory or physical needs. Our approach has been proven in SEND schools, alternative provision, and with looked-after children, ensuring learners feel supported while building both musical understanding and transferable digital skills.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to provide a safe and inclusive space where young people can build confidence, creativity, and digital skills through music technology. We help learners develop practical music-making and production skills while also improving communication, self-expression, and resilience. Families benefit from knowing their child is engaged in a structured, supportive activity that develops both artistic and transferable digital skills. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our tutors have experience working in SEND schools, alternative provision and with looked-after children. Training has included safeguarding, autism awareness, and strategies for supporting learners with SEMH needs. We also complete regular CPD in inclusive online teaching practice and adapt sessions in line with individual learner needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are invited to attend our free tasters, receive full joining instructions, and are kept updated on session progress. We encourage parental involvement in setting up learners’ equipment and providing feedback on their child’s experience. We also offer opportunities to discuss learner progress and needs directly with tutors via email or arranged calls. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We provide informal feedback after sessions and are available for direct communication with parents. Where appropriate, we can supply written notes, resources or short recordings to support ongoing learning. For learners with SEND, we tailor feedback to individual needs, focusing on strengths, engagement, and achievable next steps, with flexibility to adjust delivery methods based on parent input. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All sessions are delivered online, making them fully accessible from home with no physical barriers. Learners only need a laptop, tablet or computer with internet access. Materials are shared digitally and tutors can adapt resources to suit different needs, ensuring accessibility regardless of location. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can sign up via our website for a free 45-minute online taster session. This gives learners and parents the chance to experience the programme and ask questions before committing. After the taster, families can choose to enrol for a 10-week term/121 sessions at an affordable rate, with sibling discounts available. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to expand our SEND provision by creating more flexible daytime sessions for home-educated learners, increasing one-to-one or small-group options for those needing extra support, and developing specialist resources that address different learning styles. We also aim to build further partnerships with SEND schools, local authorities and family support networks to ensure our offer continues to meet the needs of a wide range of learners.

local_offer: SEN and Disability; Local offer Here at Little Hoppers Daycare we specialise in the care of children and young people with additional needs alongside those who do not as part of our inclusive practice. Our Settings SENDCO is Corinne Banham who can be contactable on 07813 880 153 or via e-mail Corinne@littlehoppersdaycare.co.uk The Setting The setting is home based and is a large bungalow. The setting is registered for a maximum of 18 children under the age of eight. Of these 128 children a maximum of 9 maybe young children (A child is a young child until September following his 5th birthday) and there should be only 3 children under the age of one. Places are available for all ages however the setting is aimed at those not yet at school. Funded education (15 universal hours and 15 extended hours) for eligible 2, 3 and 4 year olds now being offered. Before, after school and holiday care is available for older children. The setting is open Monday to Thursday 7am to 7pm however times can be flexible to accommodate parent’s needs. Corinne and Trisha are registered childminders. Together they employ 2 part time assistant. All Staff members are supported by a PACEY Quality improvement Partner, based at the local Authority. They are the dedicated SENCO for the area. Corinne manages all aspects of the childcare setting and has set policies and procedures that are adhered to in order to meet OFSTED requirements. What the setting provides The setting is based in a private Bungalow and access is available at ground floor level through the front and back doors. The front door has a small step but the back door is level with the pavement All external and internal doors are wide enough to allow access for those with walking aids. For security, the front door is lockable with a key and also a safety chain and there is a Door bell that can be heard in the garden. The back door is also lockable with the key placed out of sight. Entrance to the garage from the garden is locked and so are the gates with the gate at the front locked with a combination padlock. There is room to park outside the building with on street parking or there is availability to park on the drive way. There is a family bathroom and children can use the potty as well as the toddler toilet seat. There is a separate walk in shower room that can be accessed by wheelchair. We have a changing unit for smaller children and all children who are too long or heavy for this are changed on a mat on the floor. The settings registration certificate and OFSTED poster are displayed in the setting. A policy booklet is available on request. The setting has a set of policies and procedures available for parents to look at. These are printed in English. For families that require it, an electronic or printed version can be provided using a font size of their choosing. We are also able to provide the book in audio if required. The local Children’s Centre along with the staff at PACEY are able to provide multilingual staff that can translate for parents speaking English as a second language. The setting is equipped with resources to cater for all areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage. Children have free choice of resources and are able to access them independently in our fully equipped playrooms. We have a secluded rear garden offering the children and young people time to enjoy the many toys and activities on offer and the fresh air. There is a large play frame with slide and area of grass along with hard standing for ride on toys. We have a water wall, Sand tray, Playhouse, Kitchen and mark making area available at all times with additional activities being set up daily. Access to the garden is free-flowing whatever the weather. Identification and early intervention What the setting provides Parents will be asked to complete a child record form detailing any additional needs, previous illnesses, dietary requirements or allergies their child may have. Parents are given and asked to sign a set of permission forms which include permission to administer medications, Outings and transporting children in the car. If an additional need is identified within these documents a Health care plan will be put into place. If any medication has to be administered on a long term basis we will undertake child-specific training for this. Children’s progress is closely monitored within the setting. Each child has their own learning journey which includes detailed written observations and links to the EYFS. This information is shared with parents on a regular basis and a progress check is completed some- time between the child’s second and third birthday. Where the progress check suggests that a child may be experiencing some difficulties or delay in their development this is shared with the parents and appropriate next steps are discussed. For some children, the next steps may involve targeting a specific area of development and planning additional opportunities for the child to have experiences designed to support the area of learning and development identified. This would then be reviewed to see if there had been any progression or whether additional steps need to be taken. For other children, the next step may also include developing a targeted learning plan where specific aims are developed with parents to support their child’s development. Referral to other agencies (with parents’ consent) for example, speech and language therapy service will also be considered at this time. Another next step would be to ask the Local SENDCO to visit the child at the setting and provide some additional advice and guidance to support in meeting the child’s needs. This visit would be supported by the Childminder, sure start Children’s Centre and Health visitor. Parental consent would also be sought first. The setting will then receive continued support via the SENDCO and Children’s Centre ensuring that all the child’s needs are met. Prior to a child starting school, a summative assessment is carried out and this information is given to the parents to share with the school. If parents have any concerns they have the opportunity to talk to the childminder at drop off and pick up times, or they can telephone, use text or email. Teaching and Learning – Practitioners and Practice What the setting provides The setting works within the framework of the EYFS. The setting is resourced according to the ages and needs of the children. The setting uses Development Matters and the Statutory Guidance for the EYFS along with characteristics of effective learning to plan provision and activities for the children in their care. The EYFS identifies three prime areas of learning and development and four specific areas of learning and development. In the 0 to 2 age bracket the prime areas of learning and development (Communication and Language, Physical and Personal, Social and Emotional Development) are the areas of focus. In the 2 to 3 age bracket, the prime areas remain significant but there is an emergence on the specific areas of development and learning. In the 3 to 4 age bracket, the prime areas continue to be a focus but there is an increasing balance between focusing on supporting children's development in these areas and the specific areas. Activities and provision are adapted to suit the needs of all children in each age bracket. For some children, a greater level of differentiation is required because they have additional educational needs. When children first start in the setting parents and any 3rd party practitioners are asked to highlight the development grid to create a baseline assessment. Continued observations and tracking using the EYFS are then regularly carried out so that a learning journey can be put together. Children and parents are able to access their learning journey at any time. A diary is also completed that outlines the child’s routine and activities. Parents can make comments in this diary and use it as a way of communicating. Children are actively encouraged to express their views. This is done by asking them open questions like, ‘what did you like about ………’. They are also encouraged to look back through their learning journeys or photos and share any feelings they may have. On their return after the weekend break, they are asked what they have done, where they have visited. and this is sometimes incorporated into future planning. Teaching and Learning - Provision and amp; Resources What the setting provides Each age group is provided with resources that are developmentally appropriate for their age and stage of development. The setting ensures that there are resources available that overlap with the age phase below and above so that children who are developing more slowly or more quickly can access resources appropriate to their stage of learning and development. The setting works closely with other professionals and they are encouraged to share their reports so that individual needs can be met. Where children need specialised equipment discussions would take place with parents and other agencies to see what could be provided. The setting regularly purchases new resources and these are bought with the needs of the children in mind. The setting accesses a number of playgroups in the local area. Risk assessments are completed for trips outside of the setting and all children’s individual needs and reasonable adjustments are made where necessary. All trips and outings are planned in advance and discussed with parents. Child developmental reviews What the setting provides: Parents are able to ask about their child’s development at any time. They have regular contact at drop off and pick up times and are also able to phone, text or email the setting. At the end of each term, parents are given a summary of their child’s development and a progress check is completed and shared with them sometime between their child’s second and third birthday. The setting carries out regular observations and links these to the EYFS. If a child is not developing as expected for their age then this would be highlighted in their learning journey and discussed with parents. Parents are actively encouraged to become involved in their child’s education and any comments are gladly received. Staff Training What the setting provides All staff are working towards their level 3 qualification in childcare and education. We are members of PACEY (professional association of childcare in early years) and attend regular training including safeguarding, food hygiene and paediatric first aid. All training certificates are kept in our files and are available for parents to see. name: Teenage Pregnancy Support
description: Finding out you're pregnant when you're a teenager can be daunting, especially if the pregnancy was not planned. But help and support is available. First, if you think you might be pregnant but you're not sure, it's important to take a pregnancy test as soon as possible to find out. I'm pregnant. What should I do next? If your pregnancy test is positive, it's understandable to feel mixed emotions: excitement about having a child, worry about telling your parents, and anxiety about pregnancy and childbirth. You may also be feeling worried or frightened if you're not sure that you want to be pregnant. Make sure you talk through your options and think carefully before you make any decisions. Try talking to a family member, friend or someone you trust. Whatever your age, you can also ask for confidential advice from: - A GP or practice nurse - A contraception or sexual health clinic - NHS 111 – available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year It's your decision, but do not ignore the situation, hoping it will go away. Your options are: - Continuing with the pregnancy and keeping the baby - Having an abortion - Continuing with the pregnancy and having the baby adopted If you decide to continue your pregnancy, the next step is to start your antenatal care. If you decide not to continue with your pregnancy, you can talk to a GP or visit a sexual health clinic to discuss your options. They can refer you for an assessment at a clinic or hospital if you choose to have an abortion. If you decide to continue with your pregnancy, there are a wide range of services to support you during pregnancy and after you've had your baby. You can get support and advice from: - Brook – visit your nearest Brook service for free confidential advice - Family Lives – visit the website or call for support for families, including young parents - Tommy's – visit this website led by midwives for the latest information for parents-to-be - Family Nurse Partnership – a family nurse may be able to visit your home, if you're young parents, to support you from early pregnancy until your child is 2 - Shelter – a national housing charity that can advise you about housing options and housing benefits for young parents; visit their website or call them. If you're pregnant and on your own, it's important there are people you can share your feelings with who can offer you support. Find out more about having a baby if you're on your own by visiting our website.

local_offer: I provide home tuition for students with additional learning needs, including those with SEN, dyslexia, ADHD, or other learning differences. My lessons are tailored, engaging, and interactive, helping students build confidence, improve understanding, and make measurable progress in their studies. I support students from primary through secondary level, particularly in Science and core subjects, both during the day and in the evenings.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My service aims to improve academic confidence, understanding, and engagement for children and young people with SEND. I provide tailored, interactive lessons that cater to individual learning needs, helping students make measurable progress. For families, I aim to provide clear guidance, reassurance, and practical strategies to support learning at home. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed specialist training in SEN and learning differences, including strategies for supporting dyslexia, ADHD, and other neurodiverse learners. I regularly update my knowledge through online courses, webinars, and workshops focused on inclusive teaching methods and differentiation for SEND students. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved through regular communication, including updates on progress, discussion of lesson plans, and suggestions for activities at home. Parents can be involved by reviewing learning materials, giving feedback, and supporting practice at home, and I encourage an open, collaborative approach to ensure the child’s needs are met. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Progress is shared through weekly summaries, progress trackers, and feedback on specific tasks or assessments. For children with SEND, I provide detailed, visual, and accessible updates, including annotated work examples, tick-box progress sheets, and strategies for areas needing extra support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? As lessons are delivered at home or online, the environment is fully accessible and flexible, tailored to each child’s needs. I ensure the learning space is comfortable, low-distraction, and supportive of different learning styles, including use of visual aids, assistive technology, and adaptive resources. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can start by contacting me directly via email or phone to discuss their child’s needs. I offer an initial consultation to assess requirements, establish goals, and create a tailored learning plan. Once agreed, lessons can begin at a mutually convenient time, during the day or evenings. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I plan to expand my range of interactive and multisensory resources for SEND learners, incorporating more online simulations, educational apps, and hands-on experiments. I aim to develop structured progress trackers for families, provide specialist workshops for parents, and continually update my training to reflect best practice in SEND teaching and inclusion.

local_offer: Big Top Nursery is a privately owned Nursery that caters for up to 42 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We are a family run business and pride ourselves in our personal approach. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share their children’s successes, achievements, concerns and hopes for the future. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our SENCO Sylvia Robinson attends the termly Local Authority SENCO Liaison Groups. The setting has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites) We are happy for professionals involved with the child to visit and welcome this opportunity to develop our knowledge. We have close links with the local Children’s Centre and Health Visitors’ team. We are happy to attend Multi-Professional Meetings What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Sylvia has many years experience of working with children within the setting who have additional needs. Sylvia has attended SENDco training, and attends termly meetings. Other team members attend relevant training as required within the setting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents have access to our online record system and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can request a meeting with their child’s Key Person at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible. We will meet regularly with parents to update on your child’s progress and discuss their likes, dislikes, achievements and any concerns you may have. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents/carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed and agreed with the parents. We also offer updates through home/school books, email or phone calls if this is more convenient. We will regularly monitor the short term outcomes for children with SEND and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT)) are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits too. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor environment has been adapted to be fully wheelchair accessible; the whole garden space has ramps to allow full accessibility. The main play areas are bright and airy, with furniture set in a way that allows access to all areas. The nursery is set over 1 main floor and is accessible via a ramp at the main entrance door. Our outside space is all on one level and consists of wet pour and fake grass. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child’s transition needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including home visits, frequent settling sessions, shortened sessions and transition booklets. We will be happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible to meet their needs. We have close relationships with the local schools and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We constantly review all aspects of the nursery and will develop areas when they are identified.

local_offer: We value and accept all children at Windmill Pre-School, viewing each child as unique and planning for their individual needs. We adapt our activities and differentiate according to the specific needs of each child. Specific strategies and interventions to support children will be assessed and monitored through Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) cycles, and we can work with external professionals to further enhance the support and provision needed.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To give children the best possible start to their education and work with families to seek support from outside agencies if required, and implement strategies according to individual needs. We also work closely with our feeder schools to support and prepare children in the next steps of their educational journey. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENDCO regularly attends SENCO briefings and qualified SENCO network groups from the local authority. SENCO Training - Oct 2021 Qualified SENCO - Level 3 - Jan 2022 Attention Autism - Autism and play, making sense of Autism. Bucket time Makaton level 4 Curiosity Programme Trauma-informed practice sensory and motor strategies seeing beyond behaviour I'm not the SENCO what should I be doing? How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are fully informed and involved in all aspects of their child's journey with us. We recognise that the SEND pathway can seem daunting, especially if there are multiple agencies and professionals involved, we empower parents and carers with knowledge and support, as well as full inclusion of the decision-making processes surrounding their child. Speaking to SENDCO - Emma Williamson or a member of the team to answer any queries regarding SEND and support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? There are many ways we can share information, typically we will share information at handover times (drop off/ pick up times) and have termly parent consultations, however, we can arrange meetings to discuss a child's progress at anytime. Parents are encouraged to share information with members of staff and as a team we endeavour to collaborate and work in partnership with parents throughout their time at preschool as this will lead to best outcomes for children. Children's development is tracked, monitored and assessed through our online learning journals and through our In The Moment planning/ focus child of the week. Children that already have a statement of educational needs or are in the early stages of identifying needs, will have APDR's to monitor specific interventions and their impact, SEN Support Plans - this is a working document which is updated regularly and has a development tracker for prime areas of development. All of the above will be shared with parents and they will be given regular updates on progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Windmill Pre-School is fully accessible. Through the information that we gain from observations and assessments we are able to adapt activities and environments to provide a bespoke learning experience for all children. Our resources and provisions are carefully designed/ placed to ensure all children can access and engage in play and learning. We have a ramp to access the building and outside space and we have cosy spaces inside and out for children to access when needed. We have a range of sensory resources, including bubble tubes, gym ball, swings, etc. Sensory circuits and Occupational Therapy approaches to support the well-being and emotional regulation are integrated throughout the day. Reasonable adjustments can be made to accommodate specific needs such as earlier drop offs/pick ups to avoid very busy periods etc. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that every child and family is unique and we ensure that our transitions - moving in and moving on, is flexible to make this a positive experience. Children with SEND are encouraged to visit the setting for stay and plays and as well as, key members of staff visiting them at home. We understand that leaving parents can be tricky of our children, especially if it is their first experience of being in a setting/away from parents. Therefore, we can make reasonable adjustments by staggering their start/ finish times and building up to increase hours if needed and a range of other adjustments tailored for individual children. Moving out - this is where children transition to primary schools or other settings. This is quite a large transition which requires lots of planning and often individual support for children with SEND. We support all children to prepare for the transition to school by encouraging independence, social skills, communication skills and ensuring high levels of wellbeing. We endeavour to work collaboratively with our feeder schools to promote smooth transitions. Liaising with professionals, making transition plans/ enhanced transition plans to ensure everyone involved is on the same page. This not only supports a smooth transition but will help maintain continuum of support in the next setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our goal will always be to ensure children have the best opportunities to learn and thrive. The SEND system is changing and with it we will adapt. We will always explore and develop our knowledge, skills and approaches to ensure children can reach their full potential. We are proud of the support we provide from our Ordinarily Available Provision to our tailored/individualised support strategies and want to continue excelling and growing in the experiences we can offer children.

description: A mixed-gender primary school in Flackwell Heath, High Wycombe for 4 to 11-year-olds. Juniper Hill School is a two-form entry mainstream combined primary school with a Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) unit for children with an EHC plan, from 1 September 2024. Our vision is to ensure that Juniper Hill is a happy, caring school that promotes individual development and enables all our children to achieve their full potential. To promote independent and inclusive learning; developing confident, responsible and ambitious children. The school supports children with a range of Special Educational Needs and these children are fully included in classroom activities. Teachers are teachers of all pupils including those with SEND. This is achieved by quality first teaching which includes effective differentiation and monitoring of all pupils. Children admitted to the school through the ARP are taught alongside their peers in mainstream classes but also have access to individualised speech and language programmes, physiotherapy and occupational therapy programmes if needed.
