local_offer: See link to the SEN Policy and SEN Annual report. SEMH unit for children with an EHC plan. The School identifies children with SEND in line with the Buckinghamshire SEND policy. Pupils are identified as needing extra support from information such as concerns raised by parents/carers, information provided by pre-school settings, termly pupil progress meetings and regular assessments and tracking of pupil progress. Outside professional agencies are also used to give advice and support. The effectiveness of any intervention programme delivered is monitored regularly by the staff delivering it and the SENCo. Termly data and information from class teachers, parents, learning support assistants and the pupil, where appropriate, are all used to assess the effectiveness of the provision and the progress of the pupil with SEND. All staff are given training in different strategies which are needed to enable them to support children in accessing the curriculum and make progress, whatever the barriers to learning might be. More specific training is given to staff who support children with physical difficulties if needed. All reasonable and appropriate adjustments are made in order to support children in their education at the school. Where a child has a Statement of Special Educational Need (EHC plan) a review is held annually with parents/carers, staff, other relevant professionals and the pupil present – if age appropriate. Parents’ evenings are held twice a year when parents/carers can meet with the class teacher and additional 1:1 appointments can also be made with the SENCo on these evenings. Appointments can be made at any time during the year to meet with the SENCo and/or class teacher to address any parental needs/concerns. All relevant information is passed onto parents through 1:1 meetings. The SENCo meets with both parents and professionals at the current setting prior to a child with a Statement/EHC Plan joining the school so the child can be supported in the most appropriate way during this transition. Links with other settings also enable Juniper Hill to support pupils as they leave the school. https://www.juniperhill.bucks.sch.uk/send-semh-unit/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The school has a flat site and is accessible to wheelchair users. There are two accessible toilets on-site as well as changing rooms with hoisting facilities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The majority of pupils follow Buckinghamshire Council admissions policy. Pupils are admitted to the Additionally Resourced Provision (ARP) if there is the capacity and if the school is identified on their EHC plan following an assessment in line with the ARP entry criteria. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To further develop the expertise of all our staff, both teaching and support staff, in supporting children with SEN by with continued training aimed at identified areas of need. To continue to work with children, parents/carers and other agencies to implement the new SEND reforms in the best way to give support children and their families.

name: Jordans Quaker Meeting House
description: Built in 1688, Jordans is one of the first Quaker meeting houses built after James II issued his Declaration of Indulgence in 1687, which allowed Quaker and other non-conformist groups to worship lawfully for the first time. The Meeting House has several important historical associations: it is the burial place of William Penn, the founder of Pennsylvania, his first wife, Gulielma, his second wife, Hannah, and nine of his children. Other early Quakers who worshipped here and are buried in the grounds include Isaac Penington and his wife Mary Springett, Thomas Ellwood (poet and friend of John Bunyan and John Milton), and Joseph Rule. We have modern information displays, books, leaflets, and a short film about Jordans Meeting House. All are welcome to visit us. Please visit our website to view our opening times.

name: Mental Health Safety Planning
description: The Mental Health Safety Planning Service in Buckinghamshire provides support for those who are at risk of self-harm or have thoughts of ending their life. If you live in Bucks and have attended Accident and Emergency and have been seen by the Psychiatric Liaison Service (PLS) or have been referred to PLS because you have had thoughts about ending your life and/or are at risk of self-harm, then this service aims to support you. The Team will work with you on a one-to-one basis for six sessions. These sessions will involve listening and working with you to develop a Safety Plan, which includes; - Working with you to increase connections and reduce isolation. - Supporting you to identify and develop coping skills. - Signposting you to other services and sources of support. - Providing educational strategies to help manage situations that trigger self-harm or thoughts of ending your life. Referral to the service is only via: - PLS, if you have a presentation of self-harm, suicidal ideation or attempt of suicide. - If you have been discharged from Accident and Emergency after attending with suicidal ideation and/or self-harm injuries, and prior to discharge, do not meet the threshold for secondary mental health care. - If you have been referred into the Psychiatric Liaison Service, possibly through a primary care route or through community interventions.

description: Juvenile Arthritis: our vision is a better life for young people and families affected by Juvenile Arthritis (JIA). Our Mission: The National Rheumatoid Arthritis Society aims to support children, young people, and adults living with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, their families, and carers by: Ensuring that all people affected by JIA have the information, tools, and support to be able to access high-quality care and services best suited to their individual needs and preferences. Do everything we can to raise standards of care and ensure equitable access to high-quality care and treatment for all with JIA. Pioneer innovative and effective ways to support all those living with JIA to lead full and active lives with maximum well-being and be able to pursue their individual goals. Campaign at government level in each of the four nations to ensure that the needs of families, children, and young people affected by JIA are understood and prioritised.

local_offer: For children with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND), we provide: Regular observations and assessments to identify individual needs. Close partnership with parents to share concerns and agree next steps. Tailored planning within the EYFS to meet each child’s learning style and developmental needs. Individual Support Plans (ISPs) with clear targets, reviewed regularly with parents. A SENCo (Special Educational Needs Coordinator) who oversees SEND provision. Working with external professionals Liaison with speech and language therapists, educational psychologists, occupational therapists, and the local authority SEND team. Support in making referrals where specialist input is needed. Adaptations to the environment, routines, and resources to ensure accessibility. Regular meetings with parents to review progress.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To make good progress in their learning and development, in line with their individual starting points. To feel safe, happy, and confident in exploring, learning, and playing. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Nursery Manager and Deputy Manager have had training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Regular two-way communication through daily handovers, emails, and our online learning journals. Regular meetings to review progress, discuss support plans, and agree next steps together. Involving parents in setting targets on Individual Support Plans (ISPs) for children with SEND. Opportunities to share expertise about their child — we value parental insight and use it to guide our practice. Open-door policy with our SENCo and key person so parents can raise questions or concerns at any time. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Daily updates and handovers with child’s key person. Regular posts and observations through our online learning journal system. Regular progress reviews and parent meetings. An open-door approach, so you can speak with staff or the manager whenever you need to. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Indoors - Our rooms are set up to be open, bright, and welcoming with space to move freely. Furniture and resources are arranged at child height to encourage independence and easy access. Visual timetables and picture cues can be used to support children’s understanding. Where possible, adjustments are made to meet individual needs (e.g. quiet areas, sensory resources, specialist seating). Outdoors - The garden space is fully enclosed, with a variety of surfaces and equipment for different ages and abilities. Activities and equipment are planned to be inclusive, with adaptations made where required. Outdoor learning opportunities are provided daily, regardless of weather, to ensure all children can benefit. We work closely with parents and external professionals to make any reasonable adjustments required for a child with SEND. Risk assessments are carried out and reviewed regularly to ensure the environment remains safe and accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Initial enquiry and visit – Families are invited to look around the nursery, meet our team, and discuss their child’s needs in an open and supportive way. Sharing information – Parents can provide details of their child’s strengths, interests, and any additional needs. We encourage families to share reports from health visitors, therapists, or other professionals (if available). Planning support – Our SENCo will work with you to identify the right strategies, resources, or adjustments your child may need before starting. Settling-in sessions – These are tailored to each child and may be extended or adjusted for children with SEND to ensure a smooth transition. Ongoing partnership – We will continue to review your child’s support regularly with you, and adapt as their needs change. Families can contact us directly by phone or email to arrange a visit and discuss how we can best support their child from the very start. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Continue this work and build on links with other professionals.

local_offer: Ladybird Nurseries is a privately owned chain with six locations across various boroughs. We work collaboratively, sharing strategies and knowledge across all our settings to provide the best care. Opening in Autumn 2025, Ladybird Chalfont will be our newest setting, with a capacity for 74 children from 3 months to 5 years old. We pride ourselves on inclusive practice, welcoming all children and families while tailoring our approach to meet each child's individual needs. Our team of skilled practitioners has extensive experience supporting children with a wide range of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where every child's wellbeing is a priority. We achieve this by adapting our environment, activities, and outings to meet each child's individual needs. Working closely with families and outside agencies is essential to providing the best start for the children in our care. Our approach is centered around the child, and we believe that by celebrating both small and big achievements together, we can build a strong and positive partnership with parents. Our open-door policy encourages parents to seek us out for advice, support, and to share their concerns or aspirations. We feel this is crucial for a child's development and learning, allowing us to support them at their own pace and help them reach their full potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Autism in Girls Role of SENCO Makaton ADHD Communication & Language Visuals Bucket Time & Sensory Circuits Children with Downs Syndrome Promoting Positive Behaviour Children’s Mental Health How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Our core philosophy is centered on building strong, positive relationships with parents. We want every family to feel comfortable and confident approaching us with any questions or concerns about their child. Our open-door policy welcomes parents to pop in for a chat at any time. We also use the 'Famly' app, which allows us to share reports, observations, and assessments, while also giving parents a way to contribute to their child's online learning journey. The app's two-way messaging feature makes it easy to communicate directly with staff or the SENCO. The Key Worker system provides another layer of support. In addition to twice-yearly parent evenings, we also encourage informal chats between parents and key workers whenever needed. We also host a variety of special events throughout the year, giving you the chance to meet other families and connect with our team. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Using the Famly app, parents have a unique login to access their child's online learning journey, view their achievements, and review their reports and assessments at any time. In addition to the daily verbal handover, which includes a daily diary on the app for our under 3s, we also have formal and informal meetings with parents. These include: - Key worker meetings during our twice-yearly parent evenings to discuss a child's progress. - Termly assessments shared via the app. - Two-year-old progress checks and transition reports for children leaving for school. - More frequent SEND Support Meetings for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). During these meetings, we collaborate with parents and other professionals to create strategies and set targets, ensuring the best possible outcomes for the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting is designed to support children's development and wellbeing. Our Preschool is located on the ground floor with direct, free-flow access to the main garden. The Baby and Toddler rooms are situated on the first floor, with a separate, dedicated garden on the ground level. The indoor spaces feature wide doors and ample room for children to move freely, along with quiet, cosy nooks for self-regulation. We also have a state-of-the-art sensory room to support children's mental and physical development. We believe in an 'in the moment' approach, so our environment is rich with a variety of resources and materials for children to explore. All furniture is set at an appropriate level for all ages. We are fully adaptable and can adjust the physical environment to meet the needs of any child. We use visuals and Makaton to support children with communication needs or who have English as an additional language. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We invite parents and families to book a tour of our setting. We simply ask parents to contact the nursery to arrange a suitable time and day. This visit provides a great opportunity to see our environment, meet our team, and speak with our nursery SENCO. During the tour, we encourage parents to discuss their child's specific needs. We are dedicated to tailoring our support to ensure a smooth and positive transition for every child. For children with more complex needs, we will arrange a pre-start meeting with parents and any relevant outside professionals. This allows us to plan for their individual requirements, including arranging additional staff training if necessary. We are flexible with our settling-in process and will work at a pace that is comfortable for the child to ensure a smooth start to nursery life. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our future plans include training all staff to use Makaton and visuals, further supporting communication and inclusion. As a new nursery, we will continuously review and refine our practices. This commitment to ongoing development ensures we remain responsive to the needs of every child and family in our community.

organisation: Space (Aylesbury) Due to Tier 4 restrictions, we have needed to alter our schedule of activities over the next few weeks. Updates will be published on our website and on our Facebook page. You may feel alone and isolated. These times can be difficult and even traumatic, but organisations like Space can offer you support. We support people who are going through relationship difficulties, depression, bereavement, unemployment, mental health problems, loneliness or any combination of these issues. There is no fixed charge, but we ask for a small donation if you are able. We offer one-to-one counselling from trained counsellors. We can help you through difficult situations and make positive changes in your life, with the aim of moving forward. We are open to anyone over 18. We accept referrals and self-referrals We provide: A safe place to unwind and think Someone who will listen to you without judgement and in confidence Information about other organisations A chance to meet with others We offer: A free and confidential listening service Weekly group drop-ins on Tuesdays and Fridays, 10:30am to 12 noon (currently running online - please contact us for details) A Sunday drop-in from 2pm to 4pm (as above) A place to gain further information about other helpful organisations Phone to find out more. admin@spaceaylesbury.org https://www.spaceaylesbury.org

name: Animal Celebration Days at Whipsnade Zoo
description: Join us throughout 2025 as we celebrate a menagerie of animals at Whipsnade Zoo. From somersaulting bats and waddling penguins, to sleeping lions and soaring parrots, each celebration day will highlight their animal in its own unique way. Whether it's special talks, animal feeds, family friendly activities, or extra animal experiences; we're honouring a whole variety of different animals, why they're important, and how ZSL is helping them. What dates are we celebrating animals? Some days include extra talks and animal feeds whilst other days will include games, quizzes, or activities. More information can be found by checking signage at the Visitor Centre or by clicking the links to their unique webpages. Our animal celebration days are included in the cost of your ticket or membership. Additional talks, demonstrations, and activities are happening throughout the year so download the Whipsnade Zoo app for the latest talk times, interactive map and other useful information. All events and activities are subject to change and some activities are at an additional cost.

name: Manor Farm Bourton
description: At Manor Farm, visitors can enjoy a delightful experience at our Larder Café, which serves a variety of child-friendly meals perfect for little appetites. Just next door, the Mill Barn offers seating and a charming toy area, while the adjoining garden features a playhouse and ride-on toys for outdoor fun. We host a vibrant mix of events throughout the year—from children’s activity sessions and local history talks to bustling craft markets and hands-on kombucha-making workshops. For the full schedule and details, please visit our website. Café guests are welcome to visit our nearby animal barns free of charge during opening hours (Tuesday to Saturday, 8am to 2pm), making it a perfect outing for families. In addition to the café, Manor Farm is home to a traditional Butchery, a Cheese Room showcasing artisanal selections, and a beautiful Flower Farm bursting with seasonal blooms.

description: I am an OFSTED Registered childminder located in Wendover in the District of Aylesbury Vale. I have been childminding since 2006. I have been rated Outstanding, three times. I have my Childcare ICP Certificate, a certificate for Food Hygiene and have been inspected by the Food Hygiene Standards Agency and was given an excellent rating. I have up-to-date Paediatric First Aid and Safeguarding Certificates. I am a member of Pacey. I have a great connection with children of all ages and I love to see them grow and develop in a fun structured environment. We do lots of activities including toddler groups and music groups, soft play, parks, and walks along the canal. I also have a large range of toys for all ages. I provide childcare in a safe and secure home environment. My home is in Wendover where I live with my husband and two children, cats, duck, rabbits and fish. I am based near to the local schools, pre-schools and town centre. We have a great garden where we can do lots of activities, we have an allotment directly outside the gate of our garden, so we can pick and grow vegetables, fruit and salad produce. local_offer: Karen Sawyer Art Therapy Services offers tailored support for pupils and school staff, in line with the Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Code of Practice. How Art Therapy Can Help Art therapy can be especially effective for children and young people with additional needs. As a non-verbal, creative approach, it doesn’t rely on spoken language- making it accessible to those who may struggle to express themselves through words. Through art therapy, pupils can: - Develop stronger social relationships - Improve emotional regulation and resilience - Enhance communication and interaction skills — both in small groups and within the wider school setting - Increase focus, reduce distractions, and build confidence in learning environments Art therapy creates a safe, structured space for self-expression, offering an alternative way for pupils to process their thoughts and feelings. Supporting School Staff and Professionals We also work closely with school staff, offering flexible, needs-led support that fits within each school’s unique environment. This includes: - Consultations and advice for staff working with pupils with SEND - Professional support and reflective space for staff managing challenging relationships - A collaborative, problem-solving approach to strengthen relationships and emotional understanding - Whole-school or staff group training to raise awareness of mental health and emotional well-being in children and young people Our goal is to support both pupils and the adults around them — encouraging full participation in school life and helping schools build emotionally aware, inclusive environments.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Karen Sawyer Art Therapy Services aims to support children and young people with SEND to improve their emotional wellbeing, develop greater self-understanding, and build on their strengths. Through a creative and therapeutic approach, children and young people are supported to express thoughts and feelings, develop confidence, strengthen relationships, and find ways of managing challenges that are meaningful to them. We recognise that every child and young person is unique. Therapy goals are agreed collaboratively and may include supporting emotional regulation, self-expression, resilience, social relationships, self-esteem, adjustment to change, or coping with difficult experiences. We work in partnership with families, schools and other professionals to promote consistent, supportive and inclusive environments around the child or young person. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? As an HCPC-registered Art Psychotherapist, I undertake regular continuing professional development (CPD) to ensure my practice remains informed by current research, best practice, and evolving understanding of SEND and neurodiversity. Recent and ongoing professional development includes: Autism and neurodiversity-affirming practice ADHD and executive functioning differences Sensory processing differences Attachment-informed and trauma-informed practice Emotional wellbeing and mental health in children and young people Emotionally Based School Avoidance (EBSA) Inclusive therapeutic approaches for children and young people with additional needs My practice is informed by many years of experience working with children and young people in both educational and child mental health settings, alongside ongoing engagement with current research and evidence-informed practice relating to SEND, neurodiversity, emotional wellbeing and school attendance difficulties. I regularly review and update my practice to ensure support remains accessible, inclusive and responsive to the needs of children, young people and families. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers play an important role in supporting a child's emotional wellbeing. I aim to work collaboratively with families while maintaining the child's confidentiality and therapeutic space. Parents and carers may be involved through: Initial consultations Goal setting and discussion of support needs Review meetings Parent consultations where appropriate Signposting to additional sources of support I welcome open communication and aim to ensure parents and carers feel informed and supported throughout the therapeutic process. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Information may be shared through telephone calls, email, review meetings, written reports (where agreed), and discussions with other professionals where appropriate and with consent. Information sharing is always managed in accordance with confidentiality, professional standards and data protection requirements. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? I am committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive environment for children, young people and families. The therapy space is calm, private and can be adapted where possible to meet individual sensory or communication needs. Visual supports and alternative methods of communication can be used where appropriate. Access to the main entrance is step-free; however, there is a single step into the building. Please contact me to discuss any access requirements and I will do my best to identify suitable adjustments or alternative arrangements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact Karen Sawyer Art Therapy Services directly to arrange an initial consultation. The initial consultation provides an opportunity to discuss concerns, understand the child or young person's needs, and consider whether art therapy is the most appropriate form of support. This may be followed by a further meeting involving the child, young person and/or family members. Where ongoing art therapy is recommended, sessions usually take place weekly and are reviewed regularly to ensure support continues to meet the child's needs. I aim to make the process welcoming, collaborative and responsive to each family's circumstances. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am committed to continuing professional development and ensuring that my practice remains accessible, inclusive and responsive to the needs of children and young people with SEND. Future developments include: Continuing professional learning in neurodiversity-affirming practice Strengthening collaborative working with families, schools and other professionals Further developing consultation and support opportunities for parents and carers Keeping practice informed by current research in SEND, mental health and creative therapies

local_offer: Horizons Short Breaks provides safe, nurturing and enjoyable experiences for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Our aim is to give families respite after school, weekends and during school holidays, whilst helping each young person build confidence, independence, and social skills in a caring, structured environment. We welcome children and young people who: - Have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) or additional support needs. - Have autism, ADHD, learning difficulties, physical disabilities, or social and emotional needs. - Benefit from a small, calm, and therapeutic setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Horizons Short Breaks, our aim is to help children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) enjoy meaningful, safe, and rewarding experiences — while supporting families to rest, recharge, and sustain positive home life. We focus on outcomes that make a real difference to wellbeing, independence, and family resilience. For Children and Young People We aim for every child to: - Feel safe, valued, and understood within a nurturing environment. - Develop confidence and independence through fun, achievable activities. - Build positive relationships with peers and trusted adults. - Improve communication and social interaction skills. - Experience new opportunities that promote creativity, movement, and wellbeing. - Increase self-regulation and emotional awareness with staff trained in trauma-informed, inclusive practice. For Families and Carers We aim for every family to: - Feel supported and reassured that their child is in safe, expert hands. - Have time to rest and recharge, promoting family wellbeing and stability. - Work in partnership with a responsive, understanding team who listen and adapt to their child’s needs. - Benefit from consistent communication and progress feedback after each short break. Our Commitment Horizons Short Breaks helps children grow in confidence and joy, while giving families the time and trust they need to thrive. Every outcome we deliver supports inclusion, emotional wellbeing, and quality of life for the whole family. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Recent SEND-specific training that our staff have completed, to demonstrate our ongoing commitment to developing expertise and best-practice in supporting children and young people with additional needs: - Training in autism awareness and supporting children on the spectrum, including practical strategies for engagement and communication. - Certification in Positive behaviour support and safe intervention techniques. - Training in sensory regulation and processing, enabling staff to recognise sensory needs and adapt the environment and activities accordingly. - Modules on trauma-informed practice, attachment, and emotional wellbeing, helping staff to understand how past experiences can affect behaviour and engagement. - Upskilling in communication and augmentative tools (for example Makaton, picture exchange systems / PECS), to support children with limited or non-verbal communication. - Training in cultural competence and inclusive practice, ensuring staff are aware of and responsive to the diverse cultural, religious and family contexts of the children and young people we support. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Horizons, we see parents and carers as partners in everything we do. You know your child best, and your insight helps us make sure every session is positive, safe, and meaningful. Before a child joins, we invite parents to complete an “All About Me” form and take part in a welcome meeting or visit, where you can share routines, preferences, and any strategies that help your child feel comfortable. This helps us plan activities and support around their individual needs. We keep communication open throughout your child’s time with us — through informal updates, feedback forms, and progress notes after sessions. Parents are always welcome to contact the team directly to discuss goals, changes, or new ideas. Families can get involved in several ways: - Parent feedback and consultation – taking part in surveys or informal focus groups to help shape future sessions and activities. - Family events and open days – opportunities to visit, meet staff, and see what children have been creating and achieving. - Parent advisory input – interested parents can join our small advisory group that meets termly to share ideas and help us keep the service family-led. We believe that when families and staff work together, children gain the confidence and stability they need to thrive — both during their short breaks and beyond. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At Horizons, we know that families want to stay informed about their child’s experiences, achievements, and development. We provide regular, clear updates in ways that work best for you, including: - Session summaries and progress notes – After each short break, staff record what your child has done, how they engaged, and any key achievements or challenges. - Regular feedback meetings – You can meet with your child’s key worker to discuss progress, review goals, and plan next steps. - Communication via email, phone, or secure online platforms – So you can stay connected even between sessions. Additional Support for Children with SEND For children with additional needs, we provide extra personalised reporting and support: - Individual Learning or Care Plans – Detailing specific targets, strategies, and adaptations used for your child. - SEND-focused observations – Staff record progress in areas such as communication, social interaction, emotional regulation, and sensory engagement. - One-page profiles / All About Me updates – Reviewed and shared termly so all staff are aware of your child’s current needs, strengths, and preferences. - Multi-agency liaison – Where appropriate, updates and progress can be shared with therapists, schools, or other professionals involved in your child’s care, with your consent. This approach ensures that you are always informed about your child’s growth, and that any support can be adjusted quickly to meet their evolving needs. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Children have access to a large indoor and outdoor space which is fully accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please email us for a referral form or give us a call to discuss further. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? At Horizons, we are committed to continuously improving and expanding our SEND offer to ensure children and young people receive the highest-quality, inclusive, and personalised support. Our future plans include: Staff development and specialist training: Continuing to upskill our staff in autism, ADHD, sensory processing, trauma-informed practice, and positive behaviour support. Introducing advanced SEND training modules and external CPD opportunities to strengthen specialist knowledge and inclusive practice. Partnerships and multi-agency collaboration Strengthening links with schools, therapists, and local SEND networks to provide seamless support and continuity of care. Engaging with parent-carer forums to ensure the service evolves in line with family feedback and local need. Monitoring, evaluation, and innovation Exploring new creative and therapeutic approaches such as arts-based interventions, digital engagement, and adaptive sensory environments.

name: Play Minded - Mental Health Support Services and Coaching
description: Hello, I’m Laura and I am a child-centred play and creative therapist working with children and families in Southeast Buckinghamshire, Berkshire, Hertfordshire, Northwest London, and West London. I set-up Play Minded with the single vision to help support children, young people, and families during times of difficulty and change. Central to my work is the trusting relationship I build with each child and young person. I believe that healing begins when a child or young person feels safe, accepted, and truly understood. This connection lays the foundation for self-discovery, resilience, and emotional growth. My role is to provide the space, safety, and support for that process to unfold. As a therapist I strongly belief in the power of play and creative expression holds to help young people make sense of their experiences. Children and young people often have the power within for therapeutic change and will know in their own way, how to communicate this through a medium they feel most comfortable with. Going at the child and young person’s pace, always guided by their needs whether talking, playing or using creative tools to express what might feel too big or confusing to put into words is vital so that therapy is provided in a safe way. In addition to therapeutic work with children, I also offer Circle of Security parenting support through one-to-one or group sessions. This evidence-based programme is designed to strengthen the attachment relationship between parent and child by enhancing emotional connection and understanding. It helps parents better interpret their child’s emotional needs, support emotional regulation, build self-esteem, and foster a secure, trusting relationship that promotes positive behaviour and long-term wellbeing. I am registered and accredited with the British Association of Play therapists (BAPT); I hold a current DBS on the update service. I also have public liability insurance and operate in accordance to GDPR policies and procedures.

description: We are excited to introduce our SEND Skills Bootcamp! Funded by Buckinghamshire Council, this course supports local people into employment or experience in SEND education roles. This 16-week programme is designed to fast-track individuals into careers as Learning Support Assistants or classroom-based SEND professionals. The bootcamp provides participants with in-depth knowledge, practical skills, and sector-specific qualifications including: - Safeguarding children and young people - Supporting learners with special education needs and disabilities (SEND) - Understanding mental health in young people - Emergency First Aid and Young Mental Health First Aid (NUCO certified) - Hands-on experience with SEND-specific resources and equipment We are currently looking to partner with local schools to either host a short work placement for learners to gain valuable experience or enrol current staff (for example- Teaching Assistants or Learning Mentors) to upskill through the bootcamp. An employer contribution may apply for existing staff – we’re happy to discuss this further. This is also a fantastic opportunity to meet potential future employees who are trained, motivated, and ready to support learners with additional needs. Please visit our website to learn more.

local_offer: Amersham Hospital Day Nursery is situated on the grounds of Amersham Hospital. Our garden overlooks the valley and we take advantage of the beautiful setting with walks to the nearby Memorial Gardens and paddle in the stream on warmer days! The staff group is a well-established team, with some staff having worked in the nursery for over 10 years. The team and management support parents and carers throughout their time at the nursery. Where possible, we are flexible with the needs of individual families and children. We support the needs of each individual child. Each child has their own Learning Journey throughout their time at the nursery. We have a dedicated team that ensures all children can access all that we offer. We have experience in multi-agency working and are building strong relationships with the local Child Development Team, speech and language therapists and physio and more.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We access relevant training for our staff through Buckinghamshire Council and work closely with trained professionals. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The SENCO attended the level 3 for the SENCO training. Introduction to Down syndrome training. Assess, plan do and review training. Makaton. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? On Induction to the Nursery, parents are asked to share as much information to make sure we can support the children throughout their time with us. Through observation we can establish 'Next steps' with the parents to share at home and Nursery. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We have an 'Open house' policy where parents can arrange to meet with their child's key person, nursery Manager or SENDco to discuss their child's individual needs. We hold Open Evenings throughout the year. Send children may have targets set through outside child professionals and through home and nursery Observation that can be discussed with parents to develop and adapt them to suit the changing needs of the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The entrance and all of the building is on one level. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? As long as we have availability, we have a settling in period of one or two weeks, this can be increased if we feel the child may need more time to adapt to the setting and being away from their parents/carers. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? All staff involved with caring for children with additional needs will access relevant training to help support the needs of the children.

name: Katherine Henry
description: Childminder located in High Wycombe in the District of Wycombe. I live with my husband, two children and Labrador who loves children. We have made our family home and garden a relaxing, friendly and fun place to stay. I make sure we have fun in everything we do, from mealtimes to playtime, and by following the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework, these activities also help the children to learn and develop. description: Ofsted graded OUTSTANDING Childminder located in High Wycombe in the District of Wycombe. I live in a quiet cul-de-sac in Totteridge with my husband, two teenage children and my cats Pablo and Dexter. I have been childminding since 2012. I was graded as OUTSTANDING in my most recent inspection in September 2024. I have a dedicated playroom with a wide range of resources covering every area of learning, for every age and stage. I plan additional activities daily following the children’s interests and next steps within the curriculum and using the best style of learning for the individual child. We also go out on trips to local parks, woods and toddler groups. I have a safe, enclosed large patio/AstroTurf area attached to the house which the children have access to most of the time with a tepee, ride-on, slide, basketball, small tyres for building/rolling and sand and water also a large lawn area for running around on and playing parachute games. This year I’ve also added a new nature area with mud kitchen for making mud pies, growing herbs, bug hunts and a music wall. I have a holistic approach and strongly believe that children need to feel safe, comfortable, loved and valued in order for them to learn. I promote good manners, respect and resilience. We recognise, respect, accept and celebrate our differences. I use a combination of child and adult led activities with a strong emphasis on communication and language as this underpins all other areas of learning.

name: Kathryn Ghag
description: OFSTED OUTSTANDING in all areas - with over 13 years experience Before and After School care - Widmer End School Term Time or Full Year Childcare 1 space available from September 2026 - flexible with hours and days Based Hazelmere/Widmer End near to Cosy Corner shops For those who's children would benefit from a more home to home environment offering a calm, nurturing and safe place to relax and unwind after a full day at school. Where children can enjoy a two course well balanced and healthy home cooked meal that's in line with the Department of Educations new - Nutrition Guidelines. I offer fully funded places for 9 month olds/2yr olds and 3yr olds. I'm an Ofsted Outstanding childminder. I work alongside another local childminder (Co-Childmind), this benefits the children with a slightly larger social circle and learning environment, but it not overwhelming and overstimulation. I provide an ambitious curriculum - which is what I want the children to learn in the time they are with me. My curriculum is based on the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) through the seven areas of learning. It is unique to my setting and follows the children’s curiosities and interests. Underpinning everything is: • British Values • Independence • Kindness • Communication Children learn through play, by adult-modelling, by observing each other and through adult-guided learning. I incorporate elements from the Curiosity Approach, Hygge, Montessori and Forest School. I work to nurture each child’s natural desire to learn and understand the world around them through play and by following their interests. Children are unique, naturally curious and thrive in mixed-age environments focused on hands-on discovery and self-motivated growth. I place emphasis on independence and learning new applicable life skills. It is very important for children to spend time outdoors and to have a variety of experiences to develop a rich culture capital. We visit local parks, meadows and woodlands, museums, National Trusts sites, farms and animal sanctuaries, the library, the local green grocer and many others. Children play and learn in a ‘home from home’ environment that incorporates the Hygge concept – a cosy, contented mood evoked by comfort, happiness and feeling welcome. My continuous provision includes real, everyday items for the children to use and explore, to evoke their natural curiosity and support them to figure out the world around them. Most resources are made of natural materials, and encourage creativity and problem-solving. Working as co-childminders, the children benefit from two different settings, two adults and additional children with whom to play and learn. Children learn to be strong and independent through positive relationships in enabling environments. By the time children leave my setting, I aim for them to be: • Kind, with a positive sense of self and the ability to manage their emotions • Resilient, able to set themselves goals and persist to achieve them • Independent, able to look after their bodies and make healthy choices • Well-developed in the spoken language with an extensive vocabulary • Able to climb, balance, run and jump, as well as make fine motor movements like sewing a running stitch • Voracious readers with a love for all kinds of books, rhymes, poems, and songs • Confident and grounded in numbers 0 to 10, understanding relationships between them and patterns within them • Well-rounded individuals, having had many personal experiences in the cultural, social, technological, and ecological world around them • Imaginative, creative, and expressive through a variety of media and materials I work in partnership with parents and, where children also attend other early years providers, with those settings - to ensure the best outcomes possible for each child.

local_offer: I will support children with SEN or disabilities. I give all children in my care the opportunity to reach their full potential. Sometimes this means adapting an activity to the child's ability and stage of development, providing additional resources or giving one child more attention and support than others during a particular activity or routine. All children in my care are given the opportunity to play with all the toys (subject to health and safety with children under 3 years of age). No toys are just for girls or just for boys. I try to ensure my toys reflect positive images of children and people from different cultures and with different abilities and challenge stereotypical ideas on what careers are open to men and women. No child in my care will be discriminated against in any way, whether for their skin colour, culture, gender, ability or religion. I will challenge any remarks that I feel are inappropriate. I encourage the children in my care to learn more about their own culture and to find out about other children. We do this in a fun way through sharing books, colouring sheets, multicultural skin tone resources, dress-up, and cooking and eating food from around the world. I encourage the children to develop a healthy respect of each other's differences and to value everyone as an individual. I encourage Parents to share with us any special occasions, festivals, resources or ideas which may enhance the children's learning and understanding. description: OFSTED OUTSTANDING in all areas - with over 13 years experience Before and After School care - Widmer End School Term Time or Full Year Childcare 1 space available from September 2026 - flexible with hours and days Based Hazelmere/Widmer End near to Cosy Corner shops For those who's children would benefit from a more home to home environment offering a calm, nurturing and safe place to relax and unwind after a full day at school. Where children can enjoy a two course well balanced and healthy home cooked meal that's in line with the Department of Educations new - Nutrition Guidelines. I offer fully funded places for 9 month olds/2yr olds and 3yr olds. I'm an Ofsted Outstanding childminder. I work alongside another local childminder (Co-Childmind), this benefits the children with a slightly larger social circle and learning environment, but it not overwhelming and overstimulation. I provide an ambitious curriculum - which is what I want the children to learn in the time they are with me. My curriculum is based on the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) through the seven areas of learning. It is unique to my setting and follows the children’s curiosities and interests. Underpinning everything is: • British Values • Independence • Kindness • Communication Children learn through play, by adult-modelling, by observing each other and through adult-guided learning. I incorporate elements from the Curiosity Approach, Hygge, Montessori and Forest School. I work to nurture each child’s natural desire to learn and understand the world around them through play and by following their interests. Children are unique, naturally curious and thrive in mixed-age environments focused on hands-on discovery and self-motivated growth. I place emphasis on independence and learning new applicable life skills. It is very important for children to spend time outdoors and to have a variety of experiences to develop a rich culture capital. We visit local parks, meadows and woodlands, museums, National Trusts sites, farms and animal sanctuaries, the library, the local green grocer and many others. Children play and learn in a ‘home from home’ environment that incorporates the Hygge concept – a cosy, contented mood evoked by comfort, happiness and feeling welcome. My continuous provision includes real, everyday items for the children to use and explore, to evoke their natural curiosity and support them to figure out the world around them. Most resources are made of natural materials, and encourage creativity and problem-solving. Working as co-childminders, the children benefit from two different settings, two adults and additional children with whom to play and learn. Children learn to be strong and independent through positive relationships in enabling environments. By the time children leave my setting, I aim for them to be: • Kind, with a positive sense of self and the ability to manage their emotions • Resilient, able to set themselves goals and persist to achieve them • Independent, able to look after their bodies and make healthy choices • Well-developed in the spoken language with an extensive vocabulary • Able to climb, balance, run and jump, as well as make fine motor movements like sewing a running stitch • Voracious readers with a love for all kinds of books, rhymes, poems, and songs • Confident and grounded in numbers 0 to 10, understanding relationships between them and patterns within them • Well-rounded individuals, having had many personal experiences in the cultural, social, technological, and ecological world around them • Imaginative, creative, and expressive through a variety of media and materials I work in partnership with parents and, where children also attend other early years providers, with those settings - to ensure the best outcomes possible for each child.

Each workout is tailored to the postnatal body, with options for all fitness levels. You can bring your baby along- and older children are very welcome too! description: Our Cancer Rehabilitation Class is a gentle, supportive exercise session designed for anyone recovering from or living with cancer. Whether you’re currently having treatment, recently completed it, or rebuilding your strength afterwards- this class provides a safe and encouraging space to move at your own pace. Each session focuses on improving strength, flexibility, balance, and confidence, while helping to reduce fatigue and boost overall wellbeing. Exercises are tailored to individual needs, and everyone is supported to work at a level that feels right for them. Led by a qualified instructor experienced in cancer rehabilitation, these classes offer not only physical benefits but also a sense of community and understanding. You’ll be surrounded by others who truly “get it,” in a calm, welcoming environment where you can take time for yourself and your recovery.

name: Amersham Music Centre
description: Amersham Music Centre provides ensemble opportunities for all children from 4 to 18 age range who play an instrument, enjoy singing or wish to start their musical journey. Making music is a great way to learn, make friends and have fun. We also have ensembles for adults as well. Ensembles include Guitar groups, children and adults, Orchestras, children and adults, Wind and Brass Bands, Choirs, children and adults, Percussion, Flute, String and Clarinet groups. For 4 to 6-year-olds we have 'Music for Munchkins' and 'Musikids' for 6 to 8-year-olds, which are aimed at making music fun and engaging for our younger members. Our ensemble leaders cover a wide variety of genres and styles within their rehearsals, so there really is something for everyone. Most music centre groups are progressive allowing us to support beginner through to advanced players. Weekday activities are held at the Amersham Music Centre (School House, Stanley Hill) Saturday Music Centre is also held at The Amersham School

name: Baby Loss Remembrance- Saying Goodbye Services
description: The Saying Goodbye Services are the first set of international remembrance services for people who have lost a child at any stage of pregnancy, at birth or in infancy, whether the loss be recent or 80 years ago. In addition, anyone who has been through fertility treatment or who has never been able to have children for whatever reason, is most welcome. Since 2012, over 240 services have been held across the UK, North America, Ireland, and France, allowing tens of thousands of people to remember the babies they have lost. The services are completely free to attend, and are open to anyone of any faith or no faith. They have been strategically located, to make them accessible to as many people as possible, and services take place within 60 to 90 minutes of the majority of the UK population. Mariposa International is a non-religious charity, but has seen the importance of the Saying Goodbye services taking place in magnificent Cathedrals, Minsters, and Abbey’s. These venues are used for the most important events of state, from coronations and weddings to important civic events, and services of remembrance should take no less a place within society. The services follow an Anglican format, and include secular music, poetry, acts of remembrance, and other elements. Services have a limited capacity, please visit the link provided to view upcoming services and reserve your place.

name: Welsh Lane Day Nursery
description: We are a small family-run nursery offering childcare within separate playrooms for two different age groups: Acorns (babies) and Oak Trees (our 2-4 year old group). We providing funding for eligible working parents and the universal and extended funding for all 3 and 4 year olds. We have ten members of staff, 9 of who are qualified to a Level 3, one of which has the Early Years Foundation Degree. We have one unqualified member of staff. We also have a cook on-site who prepares fresh meals every day for the children, she also holds food hygiene awareness and allergen certificates. At Welsh Lane Day Nursery our aim is to provide a safe, secure, happy and stimulating environment within a purpose-built nursery, set within its own grassed and wooded grounds, with access to a purpose built Forest School area. The nursery is registered to take 42 children in total. We celebrate different festivals throughout the year, such as Chinese New Year, Diwali, Holi and Christmas through creative activities, music and books so that children learn about different cultures and beliefs taking into account the diversity of the children in our care. We cater for any dietary requirements whether it be a parental wish or allergy. Each child who has a requirement is added to our allergies, special diets or medical conditions list, each room has a copy of this and every child with a dietary requirement is on an allergy list that is checked by the cook every day they attend.

local_offer: At Welsh Lane Day Nursery value every child equally, regardless of age, ability, culture and religion, and recognise that every child has individual needs. We will work towards helping each child through the Early Years Foundation Stage (referred to as EYFS) to realise their full potential by meeting their needs through the EYFS using a differentiated curriculum and adapting activities where necessary.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We work with all professionals as required for each child and always encourage these persons to come and visit the relevant children in the setting. If required we will contact and work with the Buckinghamshire Council Early Years’ Service. We will obtain parental consent before contact is made and we will include parents in all decisions made and meetings held where possible. If speech and language concerns are identified by the setting, we will advise the parents to take their child to the Speech and Language screening sessions. We work with Speech and Language therapists and use the reports they provide to support the children in their language development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Lucy Durham our setting SENCO has completed the Advanced SENCO training in February 2023 and she attends regular SENCO liaison groups. The staff continually receive and refresh their training. 9 member of staff are qualified within Early Years to a level 3 NVQ or above, there is one unqualified member, and the cook. Staff attend courses such as; Safeguarding, Pediatric First Aid, Promoting positive behaviour, language and communication, Food hygiene, then information from these courses are fed back to all staff at regular staff meetings. We continually reflect upon our practice and will attend training when a particular need is identified. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? A strong relationship between the setting and parents is important to us at Welsh Lane Day Nursery. You have access to view your child’s Learning Journal at any time using the online learning journal "Tapestry" and your child’s key person will be available to discuss your child’s development and next steps with you. Assessment systems are in place such as the 2 year progress check, summative assessments or APDR if we feel they are needed and learning journal which are all linked to the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS). We are always available to discuss any concerns you have regarding your child’s learning. We carry out annual parent questionnaires asking for feedback on our provision. We encourage parents to email, phone or speak to us directly if they have any comments or concerns. We encourage ongoing dialogue with their child’s key worker and we produce a newsletter regularly throughout the year which are sent to all parents via e-mail, and regularly update parents via Tapestry using care diaries for our youngest children and send memos. We try and involve parents at nursery as much as we can, through things such as mother’s/father’s day tea parties and a parents breakfast " Stay and Play" is held nearly every month, so that parents can stay, play and talk to their child’s key carer while enjoying a croissant and drink. It is also an opportunity to bring home and nursery closer together. We use this opportunity to do some fund raising, so when there is an event like Children in Need or Jeans for Genes, we sell bacon sandwiches and hot drinks at the parent breakfast for the charity and to raise the children’s awareness. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The Manager and SENCO will work closely with you and other professionals to determine your child’s needs. We have regular team meetings to involve all practitioners in any support required. In addition the Key Person will be able to identify any additional support through the observation procedure required by the Early Years Foundation Stage and individual education plans will be made as necessary. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We will work closely with all parents to access any specialist equipment that may be required. The main entrance hall is fully accessible by wheel chair. There is one step down into the garden from the entrance hall however once outside the garden area is flat. The Oak Trees room has an accessible toilet and the nursery is all on one level to allow for wheelchair access. Visual timetables are used to assist children with the daily routine when needed. We can explain the limitations of the building and would make adaptations to existing resources to ensure all children can access them, if possible. Through observations staff will ensure age and ability appropriate equipment is available for the children to access. Staff will attend any specific training for SEND if there is a child with a specific need and will work closely with our setting SENCO. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Before your child joins the nursery we encourage you to visit the setting several times so that you can both become acquainted with the environment. If a child attends another setting or is moving to a different setting we share the child’s ‘learning journal’ or ask for any information the previous setting has on your child. description: We are a small family-run nursery offering childcare within separate playrooms for two different age groups: Acorns (babies) and Oak Trees (our 2-4 year old group). We providing funding for eligible working parents and the universal and extended funding for all 3 and 4 year olds. We have ten members of staff, 9 of who are qualified to a Level 3, one of which has the Early Years Foundation Degree. We have one unqualified member of staff. We also have a cook on-site who prepares fresh meals every day for the children, she also holds food hygiene awareness and allergen certificates. At Welsh Lane Day Nursery our aim is to provide a safe, secure, happy and stimulating environment within a purpose-built nursery, set within its own grassed and wooded grounds, with access to a purpose built Forest School area. The nursery is registered to take 42 children in total. We celebrate different festivals throughout the year, such as Chinese New Year, Diwali, Holi and Christmas through creative activities, music and books so that children learn about different cultures and beliefs taking into account the diversity of the children in our care. We cater for any dietary requirements whether it be a parental wish or allergy. Each child who has a requirement is added to our allergies, special diets or medical conditions list, each room has a copy of this and every child with a dietary requirement is on an allergy list that is checked by the cook every day they attend.

name: Laser Tag at Wendover Woods
description: Step into the ultimate adrenaline fuelled experience with laser tag in Wendover. Whether you’re organising a birthday, corporate event, or just a weekend outing with friends, our arena delivers an action packed adventure for all ages. Players gear up with lightweight, eco-friendly infrared blasters and battle it out in an immersive, specially designed area full of obstacles, hiding places, and dark corners. Nonstop excitement- it’s safe, fun and social. This activity is perfect for teamwork, strategy, fitness (running, ducking, and diving), stress relief, and making unforgettable memories. Get ready to grab your laser, work with your squad, and dominate the battlefield Wendover style.
organisation: Wendover Woods Situated in the beautiful surroundings of the Chilterns, Wendover Woods is home stunning trails, Go Ape and picturesque views Before your visit, you can download the glide parking app which enables contactless payment for car parking. Wendover Woods is a truly special place in the Chilterns and we hope you enjoy a safe, relaxing visit. Please remember that it is your responsibility to follow the guidance on staying safe outside your home. Try the new Gruffalo Spotters 2 trail. Download the app, buy the pack for from the Information Point and follow the trail to interact with all the Gruffalo characters in the woods and finish at the Gruffalo sculpture! Please think carefully before you visit and come prepared: BBQs are not allowed in any of our forests Make sure you have suitable footwear, and if you plan to cycle, an appropriate helmet Plan for what you will do if the site is closed or looks busy and be prepared to go somewhere else less busy, or return home and visit another time Be kind. Be patient. This is a new experience for all of us. We need your help to make this work. At a glance we offer: 4 walking trails Juniper cycle trail 3 running routes Fitness trail Horse riding Orienteering trails Go Ape Nordic Walking Play area Picnic Area and barbecues - no barbecues Café - open for takeaway only Dogs welcome How to Get There: Chiltern trains to Wendover, then short taxi ride or 50 minute walk. London Midland trains to Tring, then short taxi ride. Bus 50 (Monday to Saturday) and T1 (Monday to Friday) to Wendover/Halton Camp, then 40 minute walk. Bus 161 (Sunday and Bank Holidays) to near entrance gate, then 20 minute walk. Entrance located on St Leonards Road, off B4009 Wendover to Tring road. wendoverwoods@forestryengland.uk https://www.forestryengland.uk/wendover-woods

name: Free Baby Classes at The Little Gym Windsor
description: The Little Gym Windsor is offering free baby classes for parents and their little ones aged 10 to 15 weeks. These sessions are designed specifically to support new parents during what can be a very isolating time - when partners may have returned to work and NHS support begins to taper off. What are the classes? Our Pre-Bugs sessions are a four-week course of baby development classes, led by our specialists, that combine: - Gentle movement and sensory play to aid development - Music, singing, and massage - Early cognitive and motor skill development - Practical support and knowledge for parents The classes offer a unique blend of bonding, education, and fun - helping babies build strong foundations and helping parents feel supported and empowered. Locations: - The Little Gym Windsor - The Little Gym Handy Cross (High Wycombe) They’re warm, welcoming, and completely free – no catch, no hidden costs. Families can now book in advance for classes beginning in September and beyond. If baby isn’t quite 10 weeks old yet, parents can still join the waitlist to secure a place. Please visit our website for more information and to book.

local_offer: At Amersham School we understand that every child is unique, and their learning needs differ. However, some students require more support than others. If these students are to achieve their full potential, we must recognise this and plan accordingly. We acknowledge that a proportion of students will have special educational needs at some time in their school career. Amersham School aims to provide all students will strategies for dealing with their needs in a supportive environment whilst giving them meaningful access to the National Curriculum. When students complete their education at Amersham School, we aim for them to feel ready to confidently tackle new challenges and become a successful and fulfilled member of society. Amersham School is a mainstream school that is inclusive. In our school we support children with different needs, and we are committed to whole school inclusion. We seek support and training from SEND services where appropriate. https://www.amershamschool.org.uk/Policies/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff can access the following documents: - Amersham School SEND Policy - Amersham School Information Report - The Local Offer - Provision Maps and/or One-Page Profiles - SEND Student Information on SIMs - Copy of the New SEND Code of Practice - SEND lists - Information on different types of SEND through a the National College and the school’s personal CPD book collection and subscriptions. By accessing the above every staff member will have complete and up-to-date information about all students with special needs and their requirements, enabling them to provide for the learning needs of all students - We seek support and training from SEND services where appropriate. All teaching assistants undergo training which includes working to support learning in particular subjects and supporting particular conditions such as ASC and ADHD, Safeguarding and Behaviour for Learning. - Training is routinely provided on strategies to use in the classroom with students who have specific needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Amersham School works in partnership with parents/carers. A progress report to parents and carers will be published three times a year, following each Purposeful Practice Week. Where a student receives SEND support, the school will liaise with parents/carers in reviewing progress and setting outcomes if needed. A member of the Personalised Learning Team, supported by the SENDCO and subject teachers, will review the provision in place for each student with SEN K or an EHCP. There will be three reviews in total throughout the academic year. These reviews will take place through parents’ evenings, Academic Review Days (ARDs) or Annual Reviews. The planning which the school implements aims to help parents and students with SEND express their needs, wishes and goals. The school will; - Focus on the student as an individual. - Be easy for students and their parents to understand by using clear, ordinary language and images, rather than professional jargon. - Highlight the student’s strengths and capabilities. - Enable the student, and those who know them best, to say what they have done, what they are interested in and what outcomes they are seeking in the future. - Tailor support to the needs of the individual to the extent that it is ‘reasonable’ to do so. - Organise meetings to minimise demands on parents. - Bring together relevant professionals to discuss and agree the overall approach. Where the Local Authority provides a student with an EHC plan and accompanying regarding how the school can best implement the plan’s provisions to help the student engage in their education. This process will identify the intended impact of the provision on the student’s progress. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? A member of the Personalised Learning Team, supported by the SENDCO and subject teachers, will review the provision in place for each student with SEN K or an EHCP. There will be three reviews in total throughout the academic year. These reviews will take place through parents’ evenings, Academic Review Days (ARDs) or Annual Reviews. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Due to the nature of the buildings, the school’s facilities are limited in their ability to be fully inclusive. However, the adaptations that can be made are; - Most blocks are accessible on the ground floor and the timetabling of lessons can be orchestrated so that there is not the need to access lessons on the top floor. - Where classrooms have to be accessed on a top floor, these buildings have access to a disabled lift. - The Gym and Drama studio are accessible via two flights of stairs or via temporary ramps which are put in place manually. - There are two disabled parking spaces at the front of the school site. - Personal Emergency Evacuation Plans (PEEPs) are in place for every child with a physical disability to identify exit routes from every classroom they access, in the event of a fire or emergency. - M block is a single-story is building with disabled access and disabled toilet. – This block is only available to the Sixth Form. - Changing levels with steps from reception to the dining hall/café can be accessed by a stair lift which can be operated by reception staff. - There are an additional 2 cubical toilets and a disabled toilet in reception area. - Please be aware that blocks on two floors only have one staircase (except M and L block) so only one exit route is available in an emergency. name: Online Family Learning for Parents of School Age Children
description: The Family Learning schools team run free online courses and workshops across Buckinghamshire for parents and carers of school-age children. Our courses and workshops will help you understand how to support your children with their learning and give you confidence and resources to support your children at home, making learning fun as well as understanding new teaching methods used in schools. Courses offered include: - Support Your Autistic Child at Home -Support Your ADHD Child at Home - Help Your Child with Handwriting - Maths Reasoning and Problem Solving - Support Your Child with Maths: Geometry, Statistics, and Measurement - Support your child with Science - Support Your Child with Writing and Grammar - Support Your Child with Phonics and Reading - Developing Writing through Stories Workshops - Develop Your Child’s Self-Esteem and Self-Belief through Problem Solving - Help your Child to Think Critically to Gain Confidence and Self-Esteem - Becoming Independent in Readiness for Secondary School- Part 1 - Getting Prepared for Starting Secondary School – Part 2 - Money Matters – Teach Your Child the Value of Money Booking is essential for these courses. Please visit our website to learn more and to enrol on an upcoming course.
organisation: Family Learning The Family Learning team run a variety of free courses and workshops in schools and family centres across Buckinghamshire, as well as online. Family Learning is provided by Buckinghamshire Adult Learning. Our courses are designed to help parents understand how they can best support their children throughout their Early Years and at school. In Family Centres we offer a range of Early Years courses and workshops for parents and their children up to the age of five years. These include, among others, Fun with Stories, Play and Learn Together, Story Explorers, Let’s Get Crafty and Little Music Makers. In schools we offer courses that cover all aspects of English, Maths, Science, Crafts, Cooking, Supporting your Child’s Wellbeing and Internet Safety. All our courses are designed to give parents more confidence in supporting their children at home, making learning fun and understanding new teaching methods used in schools. Our courses are fun, practical and parents who start one course with us often choose to come onto more. Parents attending our courses are also encouraged and supported to start developing their own skills so that those who are thinking about returning to learning, or those who are looking to boost their skills in preparation for returning to work feel ready to take the next step to achieving these goals. Our courses are targeted at adults who do not have 5 GCSEs at 9 to 4 (or equivalent) and run in a range of Primary Schools and Family Centres across Buckinghamshire. Our other courses include cookery, play and language, literacy and numeracy. Many courses offer accreditation. For more information, please contact us.
