name: Stars at Stowe Stargazing
description: Back by overwhelming demand! Prepare to embark on a mesmerising journey through the cosmos beneath a breath-taking starlit canopy! Join us, in collaboration with UK Astronomy, for an unparalleled opportunity to delve deep into the mysteries of our solar system and its celestial wonders, all against the backdrop of Stowe’s enchanting surroundings. Our evening commences with an enthralling talk that unravels the enigmatic tales of our solar system. Discover the captivating stories behind the planets that have fascinated humanity for centuries, setting the stage for a night of unparalleled stargazing. As twilight descends upon us, we’ll venture outdoors to the South Front, where telescopes to be shared amongst the group await your eager gaze. Amidst a group of fellow stargazers, you’ll navigate the vastness of the night sky, guided by seasoned experts from UK Astronomy. They will help you track distant planets and constellations, bringing you closer to the cosmos than ever before. Full of knowledge, ask them any burning questions you have during the night. Essential information: Timings: 6pm to 9pm. Light refreshments are included in the ticket price. Dress Comfortably: Wrap up warm and wear appropriate footwear for a winter’s evening outdoors. Bring with you: Feel free to bring your own telescopes or binoculars alongside the shared equipment we provide. Suitable for: This event is perfect for families, as we welcome young and old alike to open their eyes to the enchanting magic of the universe. Discover together, learn together, and create lasting memories under the stars.
organisation: Stowe House (Buckingham) Stowe House is a family-friendly place to visit.Children (under 16 year of age) enter free with a paying adult. To get maximum value, and for no extra cost, the grown-ups can take out an Annual Pass. This allows you to revisit again and again throughout the year.We have unisex baby-change facilities, we are buggy-friendly (we have a platform lift on entry to the House), and we have plenty for everyone to do. We can also heat milk on request.Families are welcome on all of our guided tours. community&learning@stowe.co.uk https://www.stowe.co.uk/house/for-families

local_offer: Independent specialist day school. The school meets the needs of a diverse group of pupils who have a range of Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, complex educational needs, communication difficulties and challenging behaviours. Your local authority will formally consult with the school to establish whether your child’s needs can be met. All children require an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We pride ourselves on having high staff ratios and small classes to enable us to best meet the needs of each young person and be able to differentiate the work accordingly. Therefore, we have no more than 8 young people in a class with a teacher and up to 2 teaching assistants. When a referral is received the initial needs are gathered through reading the EHCP and accompanying paperwork, liaising with other professionals as required, as well as meeting with the young person and their family, both on a school visit and subsequent home visit. During the young person’s initial 12 weeks at the school there will be baseline assessments carried out, which could include numeracy, literacy, and wider curriculum needs, so that the school can gather fresh data on what level the young person is working at and staff will be informed to make sure work is tailored accordingly. They will also have therapeutic assessments where needed, following which sensory diets and other therapeutic supports are put in place. There is a 12-week Post Admission Review which the parents and SEN Officer are invited to, to discuss how their child is getting on at the school and their educational plan going forwards. Every half term there is an Internal Team Around the Child (ITAC) meeting where all of the key professionals involved with that young person meet to discuss any progress, concerns, and strategies which would best support that young person. If a young person is receiving any therapeutic support, needs would also be shared with relevant staff to ensure appropriate training is given, or strategies are provided to make sure the young person is best supported throughout the school day. Every year there is an Annual Review held, which both the parents/carers and SEN Officer are invited to and any other key professionals. At this Annual Review the progress of the young person is discussed as well as anything further that may need to be put in place. There is also an EHCP Review meeting that takes place in this Annual Review meeting at every key-stage transition period. On top of this there are learning walks done throughout the term to monitor our teachers and teaching practices to ensure that we are providing the pupils with the best education we can. Witherslack Group also has a Quality Assurance and Monitoring Team who provide further advice, support, and guidance around our teaching practices and pupil progress. The Pastoral Care Team provide pastoral support to the pupils and families and attend any additional meetings, where needed. They will also be the first point of call to address any safeguarding concerns, attendance, and support young people with anxieties and mental health needs. How will we support school leavers and where do they go when they leave us? Throughout their Key Stage 4, we will give our pupils lots of opportunities to experience career options. They will attend careers fairs, work experience placements and speak to careers advisors. They will also learn how to write job applications and practice interview techniques. We will also support them with liaising with Post 16 Colleges to help them find the best courses for them to do when they leave us. We aim to provide all of our young people with the confidence and skills to be able to go on and live independent and fulfilled lives and careers. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? What is the general school staff structure and what specialist training do they receive? Senior Leadership Team – Head Teacher, Deputy Head Teacher(s) Head of Pastoral Care – oversee the running of the school, staff management, school curriculum and all safeguarding. Pastoral Care Team – Provide all behaviour support, support around medication, safeguarding concerns, attendance and general support for parents. They are also supported by the Safeguarding, Behaviour and Inclusion Team within Witherslack Group. Therapy Team – Mental Health Practitioners, Occupational Therapists, Speech and Language Therapists and Psychologists (Educational or Forensic). They are also supervised and supported by the Clinical Services Team within Witherslack Group. Teachers – Teachers who teach a range of Key Stages and both academic and vocational subjects, including teachers of specialist subjects. Higher Level Teaching Assistants (HLTAs) – Provide additional support to young people where needed. This may be through joining a specific lesson to provide extra support or through one to one and small group work for areas such as numeracy, literacy, social skills, CSE, restorative practice and recognising and managing emotions Teaching Assistants (TAs) – TAs are appointed to class groups therefore they will move around the school with the class throughout the day providing support, understanding and guidance. Admin, Maintenance and Catering Staff All staff who work with young people receive training in Autism, ADHD, Attachment Disorders, Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA) and further staff are also trained in other more specialised areas, such as Dyslexia, Social Skills, Anxiety, and so on. All staff also receive training in Positive Behaviour Support, Safeguarding, PRICE, First Aid and GDPR, to name a few. What therapeutic support is there? We have our own in-house therapy team which consists of Mental Health Practitioners, Occupational Therapists, Speech and Language Therapists, and Psychologists. All of these work between 1 and 5 days a week and are able to offer a variety of support depending on the needs of the young person. These can include undertaking assessments, specific training for staff, attending Internal Team Around the Child Meetings (ITACs), small group work with young people, providing therapeutic packages to be delivered throughout the day by teaching assistants and also direct 1 to 1 with the therapists themselves. This enables a much better, all round approach to supporting the young person throughout their school day. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We place a great deal of importance on communicating effectively with all parents and carers as we appreciate that the majority of our young people arrive and leave school by taxi. Therefore, we have dedicated staff to help ensure excellent standards of communication with parents. All parents will receive regular phone calls or emails home or will use a home/school diary, depending on which format best suits the needs of the parents. We ensure that communication includes lots of positives and isn’t just done if there has been a difficult day. Parents are also invited to attend a Post Admission Review in the first 12 weeks of their child starting at the school and subsequent Annual Reviews. There are also termly reports sent home on progress and targets. A parents’ evening will take place at least once a year and this will be an opportunity to meet teachers and discuss pupils’ progress and successes. Parents may also be invited to school for special assemblies, celebrations or events. Parents are always welcome to ring in to speak to the Pastoral Care Team or to arrange a meeting to come into the school. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents are welcome to contact the school directly themselves if they would like to arrange a visit, however referrals are made to the school by the local authority (LA). The school will then read the paperwork and if they have capacity and can meet need, they will contact the LA to discuss the young person further and whether they can invite them in for a visit. Once the school has met the young person, if they are happy to offer a place they will let the LA know formally in writing and this will usually then need to go to panel. If the place is accepted, someone from the school will come and do a home visit prior to the young person starting, to get any further paperwork signed, give them their school uniform and help to support that transition. New pupils can start any time throughout the school academic year as long as there is capacity within the school. Most young people travel to school via taxi. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: SEMH, ADHD, ASD Independent specialist day school. Your local authority will formally consult with the school to establish whether your child’s needs can be met. All children require an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We pride ourselves on having high staff ratios and small classes to enable us to best meet the needs of each young person and be able to differentiate the work accordingly. Therefore, we have no more than 8 young people in a class with a teacher and up to 2 teaching assistants. When a referral is received the initial needs are gathered through reading the EHCP and accompanying paperwork, liaising with other professionals as required, as well as meeting with the young person and their family, both on a school visit and subsequent home visit. During the young person’s initial 12 weeks at the school there will be baseline assessments carried out, which could include numeracy, literacy, and wider curriculum needs, so that the school can gather fresh data on what level the young person is working at and staff will be informed to make sure work is tailored accordingly. They will also have therapeutic assessments where needed, following which sensory diets and other therapeutic supports are put in place. There is a 12-week Post Admission Review which the parents and SEN Officer are invited to, to discuss how their child is getting on at the school and their educational plan going forwards. Every half term there is an Internal Team Around the Child (ITAC) meeting where all of the key professionals involved with that young person meet to discuss any progress, concerns, and strategies which would best support that young person. If a young person is receiving any therapeutic support, needs would also be shared with relevant staff to ensure appropriate training is given, or strategies are provided to make sure the young person is best supported throughout the school day. Every year there is an Annual Review held, which both the parents/carers and SEN Officer are invited to and any other key professionals. At this Annual Review the progress of the young person is discussed as well as anything further that may need to be put in place. There is also an EHCP Review meeting that takes place in this Annual Review meeting at every key-stage transition period. On top of this there are learning walks done throughout the term to monitor our teachers and teaching practices to ensure that we are providing the pupils with the best education we can. Witherslack Group also has a Quality Assurance and Monitoring Team who provide further advice, support, and guidance around our teaching practices and pupil progress. The Pastoral Care Team provide pastoral support to the pupils and families and attend any additional meetings, where needed. They will also be the first point of call to address any safeguarding concerns, attendance, and support young people with anxieties and mental health needs. How will we support school leavers and where do they go when they leave us? Throughout their Key Stage 4, we will give our pupils lots of opportunities to experience career options. They will attend careers fairs, work experience placements and speak to careers advisors. They will also learn how to write job applications and practice interview techniques. We will also support them with liaising with Post 16 Colleges to help them find the best courses for them to do when they leave us. We aim to provide all of our young people with the confidence and skills to be able to go on and live independent and fulfilled lives and careers. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? What is the general school staff structure and what specialist training do they receive? Senior Leadership Team – Head Teacher, Deputy Head Teacher(s) Head of Pastoral Care – oversee the running of the school, staff management, school curriculum and all safeguarding. Pastoral Care Team – Provide all behaviour support, support around medication, safeguarding concerns, attendance and general support for parents. They are also supported by the Safeguarding, Behaviour and Inclusion Team within Witherslack Group. Therapy Team – Mental Health Practitioners, Occupational Therapists, Speech and Language Therapists and Psychologists (Educational or Forensic). They are also supervised and supported by the Clinical Services Team within Witherslack Group. Teachers – Teachers who teach a range of Key Stages and both academic and vocational subjects, including teachers of specialist subjects. Higher Level Teaching Assistants (HLTAs) – Provide additional support to young people where needed. This may be through joining a specific lesson to provide extra support or through one to one and small group work for areas such as numeracy, literacy, social skills, CSE, restorative practice and recognising and managing emotions Teaching Assistants (TAs) – TAs are appointed to class groups therefore they will move around the school with the class throughout the day providing support, understanding and guidance. Admin, Maintenance and Catering Staff All staff who work with young people receive training in Autism, ADHD, Attachment Disorders, Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA) and further staff are also trained in other more specialised areas, such as Dyslexia, Social Skills, Anxiety, and so on. All staff also receive training in Positive Behaviour Support, Safeguarding, PRICE, First Aid and GDPR, to name a few. What therapeutic support is there? We have our own in-house therapy team which consists of Mental Health Practitioners, Occupational Therapists, Speech and Language Therapists, and Psychologists. All of these work between 1 and 5 days a week and are able to offer a variety of support depending on the needs of the young person. These can include undertaking assessments, specific training for staff, attending Internal Team Around the Child Meetings (ITACs), small group work with young people, providing therapeutic packages to be delivered throughout the day by teaching assistants and also direct 1 to 1 with the therapists themselves. This enables a much better, all round approach to supporting the young person throughout their school day. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We place a great deal of importance on communicating effectively with all parents and carers as we appreciate that the majority of our young people arrive and leave school by taxi. Therefore, we have dedicated staff to help ensure excellent standards of communication with parents. All parents will receive regular phone calls or emails home or will use a home/school diary, depending on which format best suits the needs of the parents. We ensure that communication includes lots of positives and isn’t just done if there has been a difficult day. Parents are also invited to attend a Post Admission Review in the first 12 weeks of their child starting at the school and subsequent Annual Reviews. There are also termly reports sent home on progress and targets. A parents’ evening will take place at least once a year and this will be an opportunity to meet teachers and discuss pupils’ progress and successes. Parents may also be invited to school for special assemblies, celebrations or events. Parents are always welcome to ring in to speak to the Pastoral Care Team or to arrange a meeting to come into the school. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents are welcome to contact the school directly themselves if they would like to arrange a visit, however referrals are made to the school by the local authority (LA). The school will then read the paperwork and if they have capacity and can meet need, they will contact the LA to discuss the young person further and whether they can invite them in for a visit. Once the school has met the young person, if they are happy to offer a place they will let the LA know formally in writing and this will usually then need to go to panel. If the place is accepted, someone from the school will come and do a home visit prior to the young person starting, to get any further paperwork signed, give them their school uniform and help to support that transition. New pupils can start any time throughout the school academic year as long as there is capacity within the school. Most young people travel to school via taxi. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: InterLync - Robotics, 3D Printing, and AI Learning Hub
description: The UK’s first weekend hub uniting Robotics, 3D Printing, and AI, led by university student mentors. InterLync is a not-for-profit youth hub dedicated and believe every child should have the chance to tinker, invent, and feel confident with technology. We empower young creators to learn, build, and shape the future. We run structured weekend sessions, workshops, and special project months each designed to grow confidence, practical skills, and creativity. Hands-on robotics and electronics- From Arduino basics to sensor-driven robots, students learn circuits, controllers, and mechanical design through step-by-step projects and team challenges. 3D printing- Students design and print parts and learn to turn ideas into physical prototypes using classroom-safe 3D printers. AI and creative computing- We introduce practical AI awareness- how to use modern AI tools safely, ethically, and effectively, and how AI can be used to support young learners' creative projects. Please visit our website for more information.

description: Take dedicated time to unwind, de-stress, and deeply connect with your body and your baby. These sessions offer a nurturing blend of gentle movement, guided meditations, hypnobirthing tools, and calming breathing techniques- all designed to help you feel grounded, relaxed, and supported. Relaxation during pregnancy is more important than we often realise. Enjoy a few hours of pure zen through meditation, breathwork, hypnobirthing practices, and soft, mindful movement, all within a circle of like-minded women. To book a block, please reserve any single session and note in the free-text area that you’d like the block of 4. I will then send an invoice for the remaining £36. Please note that blocks apply to four consecutive sessions. Location Sessions are held at the beautiful rural setting of Oving Village Hall, HP22 4HD. local_offer: I offer a calm, caring and inclusive childminding environment where every child is valued as an individual. I focus on kindness, understanding and building strong relationships, helping children feel safe, confident and ready to explore and learn. I have experience supporting children with autism and a range of additional needs, and I adapt routines, activities and my environment to suit each child’s strengths, interests and stage of development. I believe children learn best when they feel supported and understood, and I always work at their pace. I use visual supports, sensory play and consistent one-to-one interactions to help children develop emotionally, socially and physically. I follow the Assess, Plan, Do, Review approach and work closely with parents and other professionals to make sure each child receives the best possible support.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My goal is for every child in my care to feel safe, happy and included. I support children to build strong communication and social skills, develop confidence and independence, and enjoy learning through positive experiences and play. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I am committed to keeping my practice up to date and evidence-based. My recent SEND training includes: Effective Interactions in the Early Years Improving SEND Provision SEND Assessment Guidance Supporting Children’s Mental Health and Wellbeing Understanding Autism Neurodiversity Awareness Webinars This training supports me in identifying needs early, adapting provision appropriately, and nurturing every child’s emotional wellbeing. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I share regular updates on how children are getting on, including daily feedback at pick-up as well as termly assessments to review progress and development. I value parents’ ideas and insights from home and encourage open communication at all times. By working together, we can celebrate achievements, identify next steps and set realistic goals, ensuring support is consistent, positive and clear for both children and families. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As above How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home-based setting is on two floors, with all childcare taking place on the ground floor, which is spacious, accessible, and thoughtfully arranged. I have wider doorways and a free-flow layout to support independence and easy movement between play areas. Children also enjoy outdoor play in my secure garden, which provides space for sensory exploration, movement, and lots of learning opportunities in a nurturing environment. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are welcome to contact me directly to discuss their child’s individual needs. I offer settling-in sessions so that each child can build familiarity and confidence at their own pace. I work with parents from the start to make any adaptations that ensure every child feels fully supported and included. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am passionate about continuing to develop my knowledge so I can support a wider range of children and needs. I am always keen to learn and reflect on my practice, and I plan to complete further training in areas such as dyspraxia and motor coordination, sensory processing, trauma-informed practice, and supporting anxiety and selective mutism in the early years. By continuing to build my skills and understanding, I aim to make sure my setting remains a place where every child feels welcomed, supported and celebrated.

description: Legal advice and information on child, family, and education law for parents, carers, and young people in England. Child Law Advice is operated by Coram Children’s Legal Centre, the UK’s leading children’s legal charity and part of the Coram Group of charities. What we do We are a digital-first service providing family and education law advice to parents, carers, and young people in England. We have lots of free-to-access content on our website that is clear and easy to understand. If you need extra help after reading the information on this website, we also offer initial legal advice through email, webchat, and telephone. Family Law Legal information on family and children law matters in England. The information ranges from private law matters such as contact, domestic abuse, and adoption, to public law matters including local authority involvement with children and child protection. Education Law Legal information on education law in England. The information ranges from the law on bullying, transport and home education, to school admissions, exclusions, and the duties of schools and local authorities to children with Special Education Needs. Attending Court For individuals who have made their application in private law cases. Features information on the court processes and different types of hearings, explains the rules of evidence and the role of Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service (CAFCASS). There is also practical advice on representing yourself in court. The difference we make A recent survey showed that 90% of users have a better understanding of their legal position and 94% of users have a better understanding of the options available to them after receiving advice from our service. name: Rachel Daley
description: I’m passionate about creating a safe, happy, and nurturing space where children feel secure, supported, and free to be themselves. My approach centres on building strong relationships with families, understanding each child as an individual, and giving them the very best start in life. I follow the EYFS framework in everything I do, with safeguarding and high‑quality care at the heart of my practice. Learning through play is something I truly believe in. I’ve designed a warm, inviting home-from-home environment where children can explore, experiment, and grow at their own pace. If you’re looking for a childminder who brings both experience and genuine enthusiasm for early years development, I’d love to hear from you. With over 16 years of experience in the early years and family support sector, I bring a rich blend of knowledge and hands-on expertise. My background includes working as a nursery room leader, providing weekend respite care for children with SEND, and spending ten years as a family support worker across two local authorities. Most recently, I’ve supported families with children aged five and under—offering guidance around child development, SEND, behaviour, and daily routines. At home, children enjoy a cosy, child-led environment where they can choose their own activities and express themselves freely. Our garden is a favourite spot, complete with a slide, trampoline, sand pit, mud kitchen, and a wide range of indoor and outdoor toys. Each week, we head out for enriching activities such as music and toddler groups, library visits, fruit picking, and woodland walks. These experiences spark curiosity, build confidence, and help children develop a love of the world around them.

description: A regular support group for parents, run by parents at Thomley. Last Friday of the month, starting Friday 30 January at 11am. Tea and Coffee with a chat. There will also be a mental and physical health session in our gym arranged for members of the group. This will be run by parents with a personal trainer on hand to support in a relaxed environment.
organisation: Thomley We welcome disabled people of all ages from babies to adults, and their families, carers or friends. We support people at any stage of their diagnostic journey, whatever their additional needs. We offer regular days for disabled visitors and their families. We also offer focus days for preschool children, adults, schools, respite groups and the wider community when any family can join us to enjoy our facilities. Our site is spacious and secure, with an excellent range of fully-accessible facilities. Each day our friendly and experienced staff run fun and educational activities which cater for all ages and abilities. We are open 10am to 3:30pm, Tuesday to Saturday. In the school holidays we open on Mondays too. We also run evening youth clubs for disabled teenagers and take bookings for birthday parties and disability events. Take a look at our website to see when would be best to visit our website. Our centre is just outside the village of Worminghall between Oxford and Aylesbury. bookings@thomley.org.uk https://thomley.org.uk/

name: Milton Keynes Film Club
description: Hello, my name is Joanna and I have been the director of the Milton Keynes Film Club since June 2016. We predominantly run after school filmmaking clubs with Primary aged children in Milton Keynes and surrounding areas. We do occasional in school work, including Lunchtime clubs. I hold a Bachelor of Arts Degree (with Honours) in Drama and Media, my business is a fantastic way to use this knowledge and share what I love with children who have similar interests in the Arts. The club normally runs for 10 sessions, running with 5 sessions each side of the half term (there is some flexibility with this). The children are involved in the pre-production of making a film (storyboard planning), then make decisions about their character and costume. They then take part in the filmmaking process, acting in front of the camera, being part of the camera crew (for example as director, clapperboard assistant, and camera operator). We bring in a green screen, camera, tripod, clapperboard, and some basic props for the children to use. Parents then receive a downloadable copy of the films. All staff are DBS checked and the company has Public Liability Insurance.

description: We play short mat bowls — a sport suitable for all ages, though most of our current members are retired. Bowls is easy to learn and offers great benefits for both physical fitness and mental wellbeing. While players need a reasonable level of fitness, the game itself is not strenuous. We offer a free trial session. Anyone attending should bring suitable footwear, such as flat‑soled trainer‑style shoes to change into. Bowls can be borrowed at first, but members are expected to have their own once they join. Our club meets at the Amersham Community Centre, where you can enjoy friendly games and make new friends — both on the mat and at our occasional social events. We hold club ‘roll‑up’ sessions on Wednesday and Friday mornings, and we also take part in matches against other local clubs.

organisation: Transforming Autism We are committed to empowering the families and carers of autistic children to optimise their life prospects and unlock their true potential. Our unique conception of autism, emphasising its potential and not seeing it as a disability, is at the heart of all we do. We aim to support parents to transform the lives of their autistic children by helping them to truly understand the needs they are not able to clearly express, and to respond to these in ways that make them feel safe, protected, looked after and strongly connected to those close to them. We aim to do this through support in the home, parent groups, our proposed intentive Mifne Clinic, and online materials including webinars, articles, interviews, online tools and eventually our comprehensive Autism Parenting Hub. Early Intervention is a key part of giving the right foundational support and understanding to an autistic child that will provide them with the strength and confidence to be able to find the best in themselves in later life, and we aim to work with and advocate working with children at the earliest possible opportunity in order to achieve this. services@transformingautism.org https://transformingautism.org/

description: Accredited Forest School Leader training courses at Level 3. (Level 3 Certificate in Leading Forest School) Course Summary: This Forest School Leader course from Green Planet Forest School is for anyone interested in creating and running successful Forest School programs. The course is based on the 6 Forest School Principles and will give you the best start on your Forest School journey. It consists of five study units at Level 3: - Supporting Learning, Play, and Development in Natural Environments - Delivering Forest School - Observing and Evaluating Forest School - Sustainable Use and Management of Natural Resources - Teaching Outdoor Practical Skills You'll dive into both theoretical knowledge and lots of practical skills practice. As part of the course, you'll put together a Forest School Program for your own setting, complete a work-based assessment, and create a portfolio of evidence. About halfway through, there’s a one-day workshop to help solidify everything you've learned. You’ll have lots of support from your tutor, who’s available by phone or email for any questions or guidance during your training. By the end of this course, you’ll have the skills and understanding you need to inspire young people through regular, long-term play and learning in nature. Entry Requirements: - Relevant Level 2 Qualification or appropriate experience in education, youth work, or childcare. - Established link with a group and a potential Forest School Site. - 18 years or over. description: The Black Dragon School of Martial Arts is a true martial arts school, NOT a fighting sports school. So what’s the difference? A sports fighting school concentrates on fitness and application, whereas a Martial Arts School teaches the secrets of combat application (Martial) with the discipline and continuous passion/drive towards mastery (Art). The Black Dragon is a multidisciplinary martial Arts school offering traditional Kung-Fu and Tai Chi styles. The variety of martial styles offers a lifetime of learning, so you will never feel bored from learning the same old material every lesson. Our main styles all have direct lineage to the point of origin, ensuring quality knowledge. Being a school of Chinese martial arts, we don’t just kick, punch, push, strike, joint lock, break, shock and takedown; we also develop our inner selves with sensitivity training, Chi cultivation, Qi gongs, meditations, and more to nourish our souls, heal, and attack.

The audiobooks can be borrowed via their streaming and download platforms or posted out on a USB memory stick. The group will meet on the second Monday of the month, from 11:30am to 1pm. There is no obligation, so why not come along and try it out! Calibre Audio is a national charity based in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire, who loan audiobooks to anyone who finds reading print difficult. If you would like to find out more about Calibre's service, you can contact them by phone or visit their website.

name: Family Learning Early Years Sessions | Aylesbury
description: Our Early Years team offers a variety of free workshops and courses for parents and children to enjoy together. These are designed for children aged 2 to 4 years (and 1 to 2 years for our Wonderful Ones courses) and their parents. Sessions run during term time only. Our sessions explore practical ideas to help you support your child’s: - Communication and language development - Learning through play - Emotional regulation and wellbeing - Healthy lifestyle habits Each 2 hour session involves fun activities such as messy play, crafts, play activities, story and song time for parents to take part in with their toddlers/children. Courses take place at Family Centres and other local venues across Buckinghamshire. Please visit our website to view upcoming sessions.
organisation: Family Learning The Family Learning team run a variety of free courses and workshops in schools and family centres across Buckinghamshire, as well as online. Family Learning is provided by Buckinghamshire Adult Learning. Our courses are designed to help parents understand how they can best support their children throughout their Early Years and at school. In Family Centres we offer a range of Early Years courses and workshops for parents and their children up to the age of five years. These include, among others, Fun with Stories, Play and Learn Together, Story Explorers, Let’s Get Crafty and Little Music Makers. In schools we offer courses that cover all aspects of English, Maths, Science, Crafts, Cooking, Supporting your Child’s Wellbeing and Internet Safety. All our courses are designed to give parents more confidence in supporting their children at home, making learning fun and understanding new teaching methods used in schools. Our courses are fun, practical and parents who start one course with us often choose to come onto more. Parents attending our courses are also encouraged and supported to start developing their own skills so that those who are thinking about returning to learning, or those who are looking to boost their skills in preparation for returning to work feel ready to take the next step to achieving these goals. Our courses are targeted at adults who do not have 5 GCSEs at 9 to 4 (or equivalent) and run in a range of Primary Schools and Family Centres across Buckinghamshire. Our other courses include cookery, play and language, literacy and numeracy. Many courses offer accreditation. For more information, please contact us. Courses for parents of children under five – Karen Hayward Courses for parents of children in school – Kathryn Holmes Health, cookery and well-being courses – Mandy van Reysen flt@buckinghamshire.gov.uk https://www.adultlearningbc.ac.uk/family-learning/?_sf_s=Family+learning

name: Family Learning Early Years Sessions | Chiltern and South Bucks
description: Our Early Years team offers a variety of free workshops and courses for parents and children to enjoy together. These are designed for children aged 2 to 4 years (and 1 to 2 years for our Wonderful Ones courses) and their parents. Sessions run during term time only. Our sessions explore practical ideas to help you support your child’s: - Communication and language development - Learning through play - Emotional regulation and wellbeing - Healthy lifestyle habits Each 2 hour session involves fun activities such as messy play, crafts, play activities, story and song time for parents to take part in with their toddlers/children. Courses take place at Family Centres and other local venues across Buckinghamshire. Please visit our website to view upcoming sessions.
organisation: Family Learning The Family Learning team run a variety of free courses and workshops in schools and family centres across Buckinghamshire, as well as online. Family Learning is provided by Buckinghamshire Adult Learning. Our courses are designed to help parents understand how they can best support their children throughout their Early Years and at school. In Family Centres we offer a range of Early Years courses and workshops for parents and their children up to the age of five years. These include, among others, Fun with Stories, Play and Learn Together, Story Explorers, Let’s Get Crafty and Little Music Makers. In schools we offer courses that cover all aspects of English, Maths, Science, Crafts, Cooking, Supporting your Child’s Wellbeing and Internet Safety. All our courses are designed to give parents more confidence in supporting their children at home, making learning fun and understanding new teaching methods used in schools. Our courses are fun, practical and parents who start one course with us often choose to come onto more. Parents attending our courses are also encouraged and supported to start developing their own skills so that those who are thinking about returning to learning, or those who are looking to boost their skills in preparation for returning to work feel ready to take the next step to achieving these goals. Our courses are targeted at adults who do not have 5 GCSEs at 9 to 4 (or equivalent) and run in a range of Primary Schools and Family Centres across Buckinghamshire. Our other courses include cookery, play and language, literacy and numeracy. Many courses offer accreditation. For more information, please contact us. description: Amersham Town Council is the parish council for the town of Amersham. Its mission statement is to maintain and enhance Amersham for the well-being and prosperity of present and future generations. The Town Council is one of two tiers of local government and works with Buckinghamshire Council to provide a wide range of services for residents and visitors alike. The Town Council has direct responsibility for allotments, cemeteries, public gardens, children’s play areas, sporting facilities, residential street lighting (lighting in ‘A’ roads falls under the jurisdiction of Buckinghamshire Council) and a number of woodlands. name: Wild Minds Alternative Provision
description: Wild Minds Alternative Provision delivers specialist, trauma-informed education for children and young people aged 11 to 19 who are unable to access mainstream schooling. We support learners with EHCPs and a range of needs including Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) difficulties, autism, ADHD, anxiety, school refusal, and complex presentations. Learning is delivered through a blended model of classroom, farm, and workshop-based provision, offered in small groups or individualised programmes. Our work is supported by a multidisciplinary team, including teachers, therapists, nurses, social workers, and specialist mentors, ensuring joined-up, holistic support. The provision combines mentoring, personal development, and practical, vocational learning such as animal care, land-based skills, and construction. Support is relationship-based and outcomes-focused, with a strong emphasis on emotional regulation, safety, and re-engagement with learning, helping young people build confidence, routine, and readiness for education, training, or adulthood.

local_offer: Wild Minds Alternative Provision forms part of the SEND local offer for children and young people in Years 7 to 14 who are unable to access mainstream education due to additional needs or vulnerabilities. We support learners with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) and those awaiting assessment, providing trauma-informed, neurodiversity-affirming education. Our provision is suitable for young people with needs including SEMH, autism, ADHD, anxiety, school refusal, attachment difficulties, and complex presentations. Support is delivered through a multidisciplinary team, including teachers, therapists, nurses, social workers, and specialist mentors. Learning is personalised and delivered through a blended classroom, farm, and workshop-based model, with small group sizes and high levels of supervision. We focus on emotional regulation, safety, engagement, and meaningful outcomes, working closely with families, schools, and local authorities to support progress and transitions.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? This service is suitable for children and young people in Years 7 to 14 who: - Have an EHCP or identified SEND - Are unable to attend mainstream school or are at risk of exclusion - Experience SEMH needs, anxiety, autism, ADHD, or school refusal - Require a highly supportive, low-arousal environment - Benefit from practical, hands-on learning alongside structured teaching - Need small-group or individualised provision with consistent adult support What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff at Wild Minds Alternative Provision have completed a range of SEND-specific training and professional development, including: - Emergency First Aid at Work and Paediatric First Aid - Physical Intervention and De-escalation Training, focused on safety, regulation, and least-restrictive practice - AET Level 3 Award in Education and Training - Level 3 Mentoring Qualifications, supporting relational, trauma-informed practice - Safeguarding Children and Young People (regularly refreshed) - Trauma-informed and neurodiversity-affirming practice, embedded across the team Our provision is supported by a multidisciplinary team, including qualified teachers, therapists, counsellors, registered mental health nurses, social workers, psychologists, and specialist mentors. This ensures joined-up, holistic support for learners with complex needs and enables effective collaboration around EHCP outcomes and safeguarding. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? How to access the service Children and young people with SEND and their families can access Wild Minds Alternative Provision through referral and commissioning routes. Most placements are arranged via: - A young person’s school, local authority, or commissioning team as part of an EHCP, EOTAS package, or alternative provision placement - Professional referrals from SEN teams, social care, or other involved services Parents and carers may also make an initial enquiry directly. This allows us to discuss the young person’s needs, consider suitability, and explain the referral and funding process. To start the process, families or professionals can complete our referral form: https://www.wildmindwellbeing.co.uk/referral-form Where appropriate, families may be invited to visit the provision before a placement is agreed. All placements are subject to: - A suitability and risk discussion - Agreement of funding and intended outcomes - Completion of referral and induction paperwork We work closely with families, schools, and professionals to ensure the provision is appropriate and supports the young person’s education, wellbeing, and longer-term outcomes. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: SEND Inspired
description: Our distance learning provision is a gentle, personalised way to reconnect with education, especially for children where education other than at school (EOTAS) is more appropriate for them. We know that for some learners, education can feel overwhelming. Our Learning Activity Box service is designed especially for learners with demand avoidant or emotionally based school avoidant profiles, who may struggle to access education in traditional settings. Engaging resources: Each package includes a mix of games, creative activities, and independent tasks. Clear guidance: Every pack comes with simple instructions so parents, carers, or supporters know how to use them. Optional activities: Learners choose what feels right for them, nothing is compulsory, and nothing is marked unless learners decide it’s helpful. Pressure‑free progress: We monitor progress in flexible ways that avoid stress, focusing on confidence and curiosity. Future pathways: For those who wish, there’s the option to work towards Functional Skills qualifications at their own pace. Our approach is all about choice, flexibility, and encouragement: helping learners rediscover the joy of learning in their own time and way. Resources are delivered on a weekly basis (or a mutually agreed schedule) and are curated to meet academic and personal goals.

local_offer: SEND Inspired provides personalised, ready‑to‑use activity boxes designed specifically for children and young people with a Pathological Demand Avoidance or Emotional Based School Avoidance profile. Each box is created with a low‑demand, interest‑led approach that supports engagement, reduces anxiety, and helps learners re‑connect with education at their own pace. Our activities are sensory‑friendly, flexible, and tailored to individual needs—ideal for learners who may struggle with traditional settings or require a gentle way back into learning. We work closely with families, schools, and Education Other Than At School teams to ensure every box offers meaningful, achievable learning opportunities that build confidence and wellbeing  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Young people using our boxes make steady, supported progress towards their EHCP outcomes and academic targets, while families gain practical tools that reduce stress and help them feel more empowered in their child’s learning journey. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The organisation is set up and run by a qualified SEND teacher with 20 years experience working in specialist education settings. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents/carers are included throughout the process, from initial discussions to understand their child’s needs and special interests, to ongoing reviews and guidance that help them use the box contents in a purposeful and supportive way. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents/carers benefit from open communication by telephone and email and regular progress reviews and reflections. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Fully distance learning How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact for more information. Discuss the inclusion of activity boxes as part of an EHCP plan/EOTAS package with relevant SEND department. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? My future plans for developing SEND provision centre on maintaining and strengthening the quality of the service I offer. Rather than expanding rapidly, my focus is on refining the activity boxes, deepening personalisation, and ensuring that every learner and family receives a consistently high‑quality, well‑supported experience. This approach allows me to continue meeting the complex needs of children and young people with care, and reliability.

description: Your Way Psychology and Education is a specialist private clinic supporting school-aged children and families living in Buckinghamshire and surrounding counties They offer thorough and personalised assessments for ADHD and autism using best-practice tools. The personalised assessment provides insight into your child's strengths and needs, and whether they meet the criteria for a diagnosis. The company typically has a wait list of around eight weeks, although they can often offer an initial screening call within the same week. Your Way is committed to identifying your child's abilities, celebrating their uniqueness, and offering personalised support every step of the way. To explore the ADHD and Autism assessment pathway for children and our other child and family-centred services, please visit our website. Your Way Psychology and Education is dedicated to supporting families throughout their journey - from assessing their child's needs to providing the support they need in school or at home. Please contact us to find out more. We are neuro-affirming, which means we support and celebrate neurodiversity, valuing the strengths and rights of neurodivergent individuals and providing the necessary adaptations to help them succeed and thrive without attempting to 'fix' or change who they are.

description: Your Way Psychology and Education offers therapy delivered by a qualified clinical psychologist. They understand that every child’s emotional experience is unique, and we are committed to providing personalised therapeutic support tailored to your child’s needs. Therapy may include approaches such as: - Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) - Narrative Exposure Therapy - DNAV (Discoverer, Noticer, Advisor, Values) - Talking Therapies We support children and young people experiencing: - Low mood and depression - Anxiety and social anxiety - Body image issues - Separation anxiety - Phobias - Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) - Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) Therapy sessions aim to help children better understand their thoughts and feelings, build emotional resilience, and develop strategies to manage challenges in everyday life. Personalised recommendations and techniques can be shared with families and schools to support progress beyond the therapy room. To find out more and explore our other child and family-centred services.

local_offer: If your child’s Key Person has identified a possible individual need, they will discuss it with you in private, and plan together with you to support your child’s learning and development, in the setting and at home. We undertake a ‘progress check at 2’ which supplies parents/carers with a short written summary of their child’s development in the 3 ‘prime areas’: Communication and language; Physical development; and Personal, social and emotional development.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We will work alongside the specialist services involved with your child and they are welcome to visit Kids Kingdom Day Care. Working closely with you and your child will enable us to build stronger relationships and understand your support needs better. We are also happy to attend external visits with specialist services should you wish us to be there for support, providing ratios allow. At Kids Kingdom Day Care we are supported by the Buckinghamshire Early Years Service which aims to help Early Years practitioners provide the best possible experience for all children in our setting. The team will support practitioners in meeting children’s individual needs by offering phone advice, observing individual children in their setting, suggesting ways to support individual needs, planning next steps with practitioners and parents and sign-posting to training. Parental agreement will always be obtained before the Early Years Service becomes involved with any individual child. The Early Years Service will support settings in working together with other agencies that may already be involved with a child. We have contact with the following professionals: Speech and Language Therapists Paediatric Occupational Therapists Health Visitors Paediatricians Specialist Teaching Service What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENDCO training new and aspiring SENCO, Natalie Winstanley, October 2021 SEN Support and Beyond Completing Paperwork Effectively, April 2022 Supporting children with selective mutism and stammering, March 2015 Inclusion Team Behaviour Management, March 2009 Seeing Beyond Behaviour, Understanding and Supporting Children’s Behaviour in the Early Years, Feb 2020 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We like to create a warm welcoming environment and aim to get parents involved in nursery life on regular occasions as much as possible this includes termly parent’s evenings, events, home learning, termly newsletters and much more. Parent’s evenings consist of you meeting with your child’s key worker to discuss your child’s development and progress and gives you the opportunity to talk about any concerns you may have. In addition to this parents are able to request a meeting with their child’s key worker at any time and have access to their development folders. In addition, we have Mother's day tea parties, Father's day events, Graduation day for school leavers and other fun occasions in which we involve parents. We also send out questionnaires for parents to complete. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As previously stated parents' evenings are a great way to discuss their child’s strengths and gaps and the next steps for their development and learning. During these, they will have access to development records although they can request to view these at any time just by speaking to their child’s key worker. In addition to this 2 year progress checks are carried out by key workers and these are sent home for you to read and offer any comments you may have. For children with SEND, we offer more frequent meetings and catch-ups through phone, email or visits to discuss progress and to work together to plan the next steps. Assess Plan Do Review forms and SEN support plans are carried out by key workers and are supported by the nursery SENCO. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? In 1990 the semi-detached house which we run from was converted into the current nursery. Due to the structure and layout of the building, we regret that there is no wheelchair access. The nursery operates over 2 floors and the only access is via the stairs. We can explain further the limitations of the building and would make reasonable adaptations to existing resources to ensure all children can access them, if possible. Signs, posters and pictures can be translated or use dual languages. Visual cues will be used to support understanding. Each room in the setting has a quiet area for children to read stories and relax, the preschool room has 2 rooms where children can freely flow between. The two preschool rooms have various areas such as a creative area, maths area, construction area, role play area with a play kitchen opposite it, a small world area, a book corner and a literacy area. There is a free flow available in preschool for children to explore the outdoor area. Each room in the setting has a small family photo board, where children can look at pictures of their parents. If you are a parent/carer who has English as an additional language, we can arrange to get another family member involved who may speak English. Alternatively, we would contact an external agency that could support us with the translation of documents or to facilitate communication. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand all children’s needs are different so we are flexible with the transition stage. We offer up to 6 settling sessions which are free of charge, this gives them the chance to familiarise themselves with staff, routine and environment. If a child has attended a setting previously we liaise closely with them passing on records and any relevant information. Parents fill in a pre-start form and ‘all about me’ form prior to settling in sessions, these consist of routines, dietary requirements, likes and dislikes. They are able to stay for as long as they like during settling-in periods and are made aware they can call or email as many times as they like to see how their child is getting on. For children transitioning from nursery to school, we aim to make them as comfortable as possible by offering visits from their new school teacher to visit them at nursery also staff will talk about school frequently to help them become familiar with it. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are planning to book another member of staff to attend SENCO training. We will also be looking at further training we can offer to all members of staff. In addition to this, we strive to have a calm and stimulating environment for children of different ages and who have different needs and abilities.

local_offer: Footsteps Preschool Watermead provides an inclusive, nurturing environment for children aged 2 to 5, supporting each child's unique development and individuality. Individualised Care: Through a robust key person system, children build strong, secure relationships that allow them to grow at their own pace. Expert Staff: Our team completes regular training in core areas, safeguarding, and SEN, supported by a level 3 SENCO and Makaton communication tools. Tailored professional development ensures staff deliver the highest standard of care. Strong Partnerships: We foster close collaboration with parents through regular check-ins and engaging events throughout the academic year. Multi-Agency Collaboration: We work in partnership with outside professionals to ensure seamless, consistent support both at home and in the setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Footsteps Preschool Watermead delivers exceptional Special Educational Needs (SEN) provision, led by a dedicated Level 3 SENCO who ensures individualised care plans are consistently implemented across the team. Specialist Expertise: All staff receive comprehensive SEN training, including specialised autism education and paediatric first aid, with targeted instruction for specific medical requirements such as Epipen administration. Accessible Communication: Children benefit from structured visual resources during every session—including visual timetables, now-and-next boards, and snack boards—to support communication and independence. Multi-Agency Partnerships: We collaborate closely with external professionals, including Speech and Language Therapists (SALT), Occupational Therapists (OT), and local SEN advisors, to ensure seamless, holistic support for every child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 3 Senco Seeing Beyond Behaviour The Power of Visuals Understanding Autism Understanding Children and Young People's Mental Health How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Footsteps Preschool Watermead places great emphasis on building strong, collaborative partnerships with parents and carers to ensure every child thrives. Daily Communication: We maintain open lines of communication through daily handover chats at the start and end of sessions, as well as being readily available by phone for advice and guidance. Progress Consultations: We host formal parent consultation sessions twice a year, with additional meetings arranged as needed to support individual development—particularly for children requiring extra assistance. Engaging Events: Parents are warmly welcomed into the setting throughout the year for special events, including Story Cafes, celebration days (such as Mother's Day, Father's Day, and Christmas), and Graduation ceremonies. Online Learning Journals: We use Tapestry to document progress with regular observations, next steps for setting and home learning, and reports, while encouraging parents to share home experiences for children to discuss with friends. Secure Community Updates: Our private, secure Facebook page—restricted strictly to current staff and approved parents with explicit photo consent—keeps families connected with daily activities and important notices. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Footsteps Preschool Watermead uses robust tracking and assessment processes to ensure every child makes continuous progress and transitions smoothly to primary school. Ongoing Assessment & Tracking: Staff complete initial baseline assessments, statutory two-year checks, and termly tracking to quickly identify and address any developmental gaps. Parents and carers have access to this information through their personal Tapestry account as well as through regular parent consultation events. Personalised Learning Plans: Key persons maintain dynamic "Next Steps" documents to guide learning, supported by Tapestry observations. Children with SEND benefit from collaborative APDRs (Assess, Plan, Do, Review) and SEN plans incorporating outside professional advice. Seamless School Transitions: We facilitate thorough handovers for children moving to Reception, including welcoming teachers into the preschool for face-to-face meetings and prioritising early communication for children with additional needs. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Footsteps Preschool Watermead provides a fully accessible and inclusive environment, designed to meet the diverse physical, sensory, and linguistic needs of every child and family. Physical Accessibility: Our indoor and outdoor spaces are completely step-free and on the same level, featuring a dedicated disabled toilet and a flat garden that promotes independent outdoor play. Sensory & Visual Support: Children benefit from daily visual resources—including timetables, now-and-next boards, and snack boards—alongside welcoming accommodations for sensory aids such as personal ear defenders. Inclusive Communication & Languages: We offer a selection of dual-language books and utilise home-preschool communication books to bridge language barriers and ensure families whose first language is not English stay fully connected. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Footsteps Preschool Watermead provides tailored, proactive support for children with additional needs to ensure a smooth and confident start. Early Engagement and Home Visits: Our SENCO works closely with families from the beginning, using home visits to understand each child's unique needs and brief the staff team for a settled transition. Proactive Funding Support: Where necessary, we apply for additional funding prior to enrollment to increase adult-to-child ratios and provide enhanced, dedicated support. Collaborative Consultations: Families have access to regular, pre-arranged consultations with the SENCO and key person to discuss progress, answer questions, and address any concerns. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to access Makaton training using a Makaton lead initially which will then be used to train staff in house to ensure all children can communicate with confidence. We are planning to book staff members on specific Autism training. Following on from a trial with Talk Boost during the last academic year, we will be undertaking Talk Boost Training with Speech and Language UK.

name: Nurturing Anchors
description: Nurturing Anchors is a join project between Kids Charity and the Royal Navy and Royal Marines Charity. It aims to provide free tailored support to Royal Navy and Royal Marine families with SEND military children to: - Address their unique challenges - Provide a safe and supportive environment for sharing experiences, insights, and opportunities to find new strategies that work for these families. We run workshops such as the following: - Behaviour Workshop- A 2-hour workshop giving parents/carers insights and tips on parenting neurodivergent children. - Nurturing Anchors: A ten-week course focused on enhancing your health, well-being, and understanding as a parent of a SEND child. - Riding the Rapids: A ten-week course helping parents and carers of neurodivergent children understand and manage challenging behaviours. We also have an online version for those unable to make the Teams sessions. - Understanding Me, Parent Carer: A six-week course providing practical strategies to support your child's unique needs. - Understanding Me, Young Person: A six-week course offering practical strategies to support your unique needs as a young person. - Coffee and Connect: Drop-in sessions for parents of neurodivergent children to chat and connect with others. We also have pre-recorded workshops which can be found on our Navy Hub with access using a password through our colleagues. 1:1 support is available on request.

local_offer: Our area of expertise is giving children with Education Other Than At School (EOTAS) status, as indicated on their Education, Health, and Care Plans (EHCPs), specialised educational support. Our knowledgeable tutors are committed to identifying each child’s specific learning needs and creating individualised lesson plans to support their academic success. We enable children with EOTAS status to realise their full potential and succeed not only academically, but socially and with essential life skills - whatever is their 'best fit' for the 'right now'.' Tutors work closely with both managers and families to ensure a caring and supportive environment throughout with an individualised approach and dedication to excellence.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our service aims to support children and young people with SEND to feel confident, included, and able to reach their full potential, whether their provision is for the short term or a longer arrangement. Through a safe, nurturing, and inclusive environment, we help children develop communication, social, and independence skills, while supporting their emotional wellbeing and self-esteem. We offer short courses, life skills challenges and accelerating English and maths for those whose outcomes may be slightly different to National Curriculum goals. We also have subject specialists who teach all GCSE/iGCSE/functional skills and A Level subjects and support families through the exam process as private candidates. For families, our service aims to reduce isolation and stress by offering reassurance, practical support, and opportunities to connect with others who have shared experiences. We empower parents and carers with information, guidance, and confidence, helping them feel supported and better equipped to meet their child’s needs. Overall, our outcomes focus on improving quality of life for both children and their families, ensuring they feel valued, supported, and able to thrive. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our tutors come from many different backgrounds and therefore bring with them a wealth of experience and CPD from their various roles. Training into specific SEND is offered throughout the year for those who wish to continue their professional development. Our dyslexia assessors, careers advisors and teen coaches for example, offer our organisation training for tutors. In addition to core safeguarding training we also use guidance from external professionals, and ongoing learning to continually improve our SEND practice. Further SEND-specific training is planned to meet the evolving needs of the children we support. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents have access to our friendly team through phone and online meetings, and are fully involved in all aspects of provision. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Your child's progress can be shared with you in many different ways. Teachers can provide you session by session notes with progress made towards targets outlined in their EHCPs. Our Area Director and tutors will attend your progress meetings and reviews where necessary, to ensure consistency across their team. Parents can email and phone our team to discuss their child's needs at any time. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our teachers work in your own home, or in the community where applicable. We carefully consider any neutral environment we will access to ensure it is the right fit for your Young Person's needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We would always recommend you speak with us over the phone or online first. It's so important to us that you feel comfortable, and that we make a connection right from the start. Following our telephone conversation, our friendly Team Manager will come to meet you (and your Young Person, where applicable) at your home or other venue so that we can gain a fuller picture of how we can best support you. After our meeting, teachers/tutors/mentors or advisors will be introduced to the team and meet your Young Person to begin building rapport and getting to know how best your child learns. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our future plans include gaining accreditation to the Arts Award Scheme, as well as developing what we offer as ASDAN members. Furthermore, for those learners who wish to follow an exam pathway, Home-School Tutoring Bedfordshire and Buckinghamshire would like to open and run a local exam centre, offering access arrangements for every learner to be able to succeed.

I am providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I am aware about Autism, ADD and ADHD, disability in communication and interaction etc. Every child is unique and special for me. Always try to understand each child as every child are different from each other. Understanding their needs and support them accordingly to develop their skills. Even plan some group activities to learn interaction with others as part of social involvement. I always prefer to involve each child and support them to take part of every activities to develop their skills. I always try to give confidence to each child to turn their weakness in to strength. In my setting, I am very flexible and accepting a maximum 6 children to be within ratio guidance and allow for maximised 1:1 as well as group attention.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I believe every child is unique and differ from others. Always I provide my support as per their needs. My support is in accordance within their weakness and strength. Always try to understand them and give support as they need and try to convert their weakness in to strength. To develop their social skill I arrange group activities and support them to be within ratio guidance and allow for maximised 1:1 as well as group attention. And always motivate them for their involvement in each activities to develop their skills. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I am certified with NCFE CACHE LEVEL 3 - Understanding all kind of need for children and provide them my support accordance with their needs. I am trained to deal with AUTISM, ADD & ADDH, Communication and learning disability etc. Always support has been given to the children to develop their hidden skills within my setting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I always work with parents, carer and other professionals from SEND for better outcome. I always involve parents/carer in the children development and their achievements. In my setting often I do have meeting with parent/carer to discuss their needs, achievements and how can we improve it. As part of learning I always updates to parents/carer regarding the children's development. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As I work closely to parents/carer in accordance with the children's development, always communicate and share information to you about your child's progress regular basis. We will work in joint action plan to improve your child's skills and provide support accordance him/her need. Even I will discuss if further support needed or if parents would like other services involved. We can involve other SEND professional in case of special need to develop child's skill. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? In my setting, safe accessible for all children with plenty of room to enjoy and develop their skills. As my setting in flat, I have more then enough space to play and indoor activities with access of play room, hallway and wider doorway within safety measures. For safety measures, I always up to date with RISK ASSESSMENT of all property regular bases. I am happy to discuss all kind of needs with parents regarding their children and will provide my support accordingly. For outdoors activity we have communal park near by. I have full driving licence to allow safe commuting for outdoor activities. My setting is on prime location and accessible to bus stop and railway station. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I always prefer parents to have their settling in period with their child. We will complete an 'All about me' together to know more about the children and their need. So we can make learning journey plan accordance with their needs. I provide the settling setting in policy, where you can find more information on the settling in period and all settling in period can be adapted to suit the specific needs of each child individually for better outcomes. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As in our life learning never ends, I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of children I am caring of. I always be up to date with SAND information and training by the local authority and my key contacts.
