local_offer: Our SEN Swimming Classes At Swim Stars Swimming School, we are proud to offer dedicated SEN (Special Educational Needs) swimming classes designed to support children who require a more individualised and understanding approach. Our experienced, patient instructors create a calm, inclusive, and positive environment where each child can progress at their own pace. Lessons are adapted to suit individual needs, focusing on water confidence, safety, communication, and enjoyment. We work closely with parents and carers to ensure every swimmer feels supported, valued, and confident in the water.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Swim Stars Swimming School, our aims for children with SEND are to: - Create a safe, calm, and inclusive environment where every child feels welcome and respected - Build water confidence through positive, supportive experiences - Develop essential water safety and swimming skills at a pace that suits each child - Encourage independence and self-belief in the water - Support communication and social interaction, where appropriate - Use individualised teaching approaches tailored to each child’s needs and strengths - Ensure swimming is a fun, enjoyable, and confidence-boosting experience What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents can be involved with a variety of classes where parents can watch and support from poolside or participate with your child in a lesson. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children's progress is shared and updated through our parent and Teacher portal on our soakly app. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our pools are indoor with warm pools with a choice or quiet locations with dedicated swimming sessions. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact Aimee to have a chat as all children needs are different having a chat can help find the right class for you. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

Please visit our website to learn more and to book your sessions.

description: Amicus Trust is a charity that offers supported accommodation for up to 2 years to those that are homeless, or at immediate risk of being homeless, between the ages of 16 and 65 years. Applicants can be referred from an external agency, or download a self-referral form from our website. Applicants must be: - Aged 16 to 65 - Single (No couples or living with dependent's) Links to the area Our service provides accommodation in a shared house facility in Aylesbury, offering supported independent living, personal development plans, one-to-one weekly key work sessions, and support in obtaining sustainable long term housing. We help our residents to access external agencies that will benefit their personal development, as well as offer supported resettlement plans moving forward.

I recognise that every family's journey is unique and I aim for parents/carers to feel understood and supported. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Group Leader, SEND Nurture Programme (Family Links) – I have been trained to run the SEND Nurture Programme for parents/carers to attend. This programme focuses on family relationships, children’s emotional health and behaviour management through topics such as positive discipline, empathy and self-awareness. Little Talkers (NHS Speech and Language Therapy) – I have been trained to run the Little Talkers programme which is designed to support parents and carers who may have concerns regarding their child’s communication, speech and language. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work closely in partnership with parents and carers and place great importance on maintaining regular communication about their child’s learning, progress and development. I provide parents/carers with a folder which includes written observations and next steps. I encourage parents/carers to share information about their child’s interests, likes and dislikes along with any activities they may find challenging or particularly enjoy. This helps me to plan and adapt activities to support each individual child in reaching their full potential. I also share ideas with families to ensure they are involved and can support their child’s learning and development at home. Each day, parents/carers will receive a daily diary with an overview of their child’s day. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I continually observe and assess all children and parents/carers will receive a summary in their child’s folder at the end of each term. Children will also have a 2-year-old progress check between the ages of 2 and 3. If a particular need is identified, I will include parents/carers to implement a support plan for their child as soon as possible to intervene early. With the permission of parents/carers I may involve other services such as health visitors or request support from the Local Authority SEND team. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? I aim to provide an inclusive and welcoming environment for all children and families, however, due to the layout of my home, there is currently limited physical accessibility as the entrance and garden are not suitable for wheelchair access. However, I am committed to supporting children with a range of additional needs and will work closely with parents/carers and relevant professionals to consider individual requirements and make reasonable adjustments where possible. Within my setting, I use two main rooms which are connected by a clear sliding door. This allows me to create a flexible environment where children can either play together or have a quieter, separate space if they need time to regulate their emotions or reduce sensory stimulation. I can introduce the use of visual aids where appropriate, and most importantly – do my utmost to build trust to ensure that children feel safe and understood. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are welcome to visit my setting to meet me and see my home prior to making any decisions. A welcome pack including information, policies and an 'all about me' form will be provided. Settling in sessions will be arranged where parents/carers are encouraged to attend at least one, however, we will decision make together on the next steps for your child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I aim to attend webinars by the Autism Education Trust within my first year of childminding (April 2026-April 2027.) I also plan to attend Makaton training to build on supporting the speech and language development of the children in my setting.

The Town Council has direct responsibility for allotments, cemeteries, public gardens, children’s play areas, sporting facilities, residential street lighting (lighting in ‘A’ roads falls under the jurisdiction of Buckinghamshire Council) and a number of woodlands. Buckinghamshire Council is responsible for education, social services, highways and footpaths, libraries, council tax, planning, environmental health and waste. description: Strong Tower Learning Centre is an Ofsted-registered tuition service dedicated to promoting equity in education and closing the attainment gap. We provide high-quality academic support that prepares children to succeed in top schools. Our approach also embeds leadership, cultural awareness, and emotional resilience, ensuring that success is not only about gaining entry, but also about thriving within those spaces and building a strong future beyond them. At Strong Tower Learning Centre, we believe every child deserves the opportunity to thrive, regardless of background or circumstance. As an Ofsted registered supplementary education provider, we deliver an inclusive tuition service for all children, while specialising in closing the attainment gap for pupils from marginalised communities. Our mission is to empower all children including those from ethnic minority backgrounds, with special educational needs (SEN), or from low socio economic backgrounds by removing systemic barriers, making high-quality tuition accessible, and ensuring that every child, regardless of background, can achieve their full potential. 🌟 Give your child the strong start they deserve.

local_offer: Strong Tower Learning Centre (STLC) provides personalised, small group and one to one educational support for children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Our provision focuses on closing learning gaps, building confidence, and supporting emotional regulation, particularly for learners who find mainstream education challenging. Support is tailored through baseline assessment, structured learning pathways, and adaptive teaching strategies. We support children with needs including (but not limited to): Autism (ASC) ADHD Dyslexia and literacy difficulties Speech, language and communication needs SEMH (Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs) Mild to moderate learning difficulties  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? For children and young people, we aim to: Improve academic attainment in Maths and English Increase confidence, independence and engagement in learning Reduce anxiety associated with education Support emotional regulation and resilience Help learners experience success and progress at their own pace For families, we aim to: Increase confidence in supporting their child’s learning Improve understanding of their child’s needs Strengthen partnership between parents and educators Reduce stress and uncertainty around education and SEND support What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our staff and tutors have completed and/or are experienced in: Safeguarding and child protection (including SEND considerations) Supporting learners with autism and ADHD Differentiation and inclusive teaching strategies Supporting SEMH needs and emotional regulation Trauma-informed and child-centred approaches We also work alongside educational and child psychologists to inform best practice and continuously develop staff understanding of SEND. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are active partners in our provision. We involve parents through: Initial discussions to understand the child’s needs and history Regular updates on progress and engagement Clear explanations of strategies used and how to support learning at home Open communication via email and scheduled discussions Parents can get involved by sharing insights about their child, reinforcing strategies at home, and engaging in regular communication with our team. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share progress through: Ongoing tutor feedback Progress updates linked to learning goals Data from adaptive learning platforms For children with SEND, this includes: Clear explanations of progress in accessible language Focus on confidence, engagement and wellbeing as well as attainment Adjustments to learning plans where needed Honest discussions if a child requires different or additional support How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We aim to provide a calm, inclusive and low-stress learning environment. Our provision includes: Small groups to reduce sensory overload Flexible seating and teaching approaches Predictable routines and structured sessions Where required, reasonable adjustments are discussed with families in advance to ensure accessibility for each child. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can access our service by: Making contact via our website or email Having an initial discussion about the child’s needs Completing a baseline assessment Agreeing a personalised learning plan and pathway We welcome self-referrals, parent referrals, and referrals from schools or other professionals. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Strengthening partnerships with educational and child psychologists Expanding SEND-specific staff training Developing clearer SEND documentation and reporting Increasing capacity for 1:1 SEND support Enhancing use of adaptive and assistive technologies Exploring closer working with local authorities and schools

description: Holiday Camp Adventure Days are designed for young people who want to get active, try new things, and come home buzzing from a day outdoors. Expect a fun mix of water-based sessions, climbing-style challenges, bushcraft, games, and team activities, all delivered by our experienced instructors. Book one day, a few days, or build a full holiday plan by selecting multiple dates across 2026 in a single checkout. Action4Youth is Ofsted Registered. What's included? Holiday Camp Adventure Days are action-packed and varied, with activities that may include: - Water sports - Climbing-style activities - Bushcraft and outdoor skills - Team challenges, games, and more No previous experience is needed. Our friendly instructors guide everyone, from first-timers to confident adventurers. All specialist equipment is provided – you just need to bring lunch, a drink, and spare clothes for outdoor fun. All instructors hold enhanced DBS checks (including barred list) and relevant industry qualifications, with regular training in safety and safeguarding. They also have experience supporting a wide range of young people. Extended Day option If you need earlier drop-off and later pick-up, select Extended Day on the booking page. organisation: Action4Youth Action4Youth changes lives and creates better chances for young people by creating opportunities to discover their personal strengths and potential. We work with young people from all backgrounds and all abilities to make a real difference to their futures. We are a respected and dynamic charity based in Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes but reaching young people across the wider south east region. What we do Action4Youth is a leading delivery partner for the National Citizen Service (NCS) and consistently over delivers in terms of both quality and quantity. Action4Youth takes the strategic lead for the voluntary organisations supporting children and young people aged 5 – 25 years across its area. It has around 100 organisations in membership and offers a range of essential support and services. Our outdoor centre, Caldecotte Xperience in Milton Keynes, creates opportunities for young people to have amazing, challenging, fun and sometimes transformational experiences. They learn what they can do rather than what they can’t, building their confidence and self-belief. Action4Youth is the operating authority for Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes for Open Awards Groups for the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme. office@action4youth.org http://www.action4youth.org

local_offer: I am an Ofsted registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a registered childminder, I have a Key Contact at Buckinghamshire Council with the Early Years Team, and with parental permission, I may contact them for further advice. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites) are available for us to access. I welcome other professionals into the setting who may have involvement with a child and I am keen to access further training to support a child’s development, for example, speech and language (Speech Therapist). I am happy to attend Multi-Professionals Meetings if required. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Awaiting SEND courses How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst in the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and we will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a small step leading to the front door. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible, for example, adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period for their child and where time allows a home visit before starting. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they have the opportunity to visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each child’s needs are met.

local_offer: Kingsbrook View follow the graduated approach to supporting children with SEN. The SEN information report shows the type of provision (interventions and support) that is provided at Kingsbrook View. Kingsbrook View Primary Academy is an inclusive school and all staff: Do everything they can to meet the pupils’ special educational need Ensure pupils with SEND engage in learning and activities alongside their peers Provide high-quality teaching, scaffolded for individual pupils https://www.kvpa.org.uk/SEND/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Kingsbrook View, we use quality teaching to support all children to achieve both academically and in terms of their personal development. We recognise that some children may need additional strategies to support this development. Each child, who receives SEND support, has a pupil passport and relevant targets (APDR). In addition to this, parents are invited to discuss the support provided and progress made. Where parents have any concerns about their child’s progress, we hope that they will inform us as soon as possible so we can ascertain the nature and level of the need and implement appropriate support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The Academy's arrangement for training staff in relation to pupils with SEND is: Whole staff in-service training sessions are arranged as appropriate, in response to particular needs within the school. Reading and discussion of relevant documentation and keeping up to date with DfE guidance. SENDCo/teacher meetings are considered to be part of staff development, as well as a time to share information. The SENDCo and other relevant staff attend LA meetings and INSET as appropriate. Newly appointed teaching and support staff meet the SENCo to discuss SEND procedures in the academy. Specialist expertise is obtained by the school/nursery school. The Academy may make referrals to a range of external agencies if further specialist expertise is required. Each agency has its own referral criteria. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents of children on the SEN register within our Academy are invited to termly meetings where their input is valued and their views are included. Additionally, we encourage parents to become involved in the Academy's community through joining the PTA. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children's progress is shared through parents'/carers' evenings twice a year and a report at the end of the year. Children on the SEN register have an additional parents' evening (3 in total) which allows for parental input into the child's support plan (APDR). How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The academy is DDA compliant. Reasonable adjustments are made to make sure the school environment is as accessible as possible. Where there are steps, there is alternative access via ramp. Steps have handrails. To reach the second floor there is lift access. Modifications are made to fixtures as appropriate. There is an allocated disabled parking bay which can be used by parents who hold a disabled parking badge. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The academy follows the normal LA procedures for admission to a mainstream school. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Kingsbrook View provides ongoing SEND training for staff and actively updates and develops the SEND resources available to pupils.

local_offer: We provide an inclusive environment where all children are supported to access learning and development opportunities appropriate to their needs. Support may include: Individualised support plans following the Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) process Close partnership working with parents and carers Adapted activities and learning opportunities to suit individual needs Use of visual aids, routines and structured environments to support communication and understanding Smaller group work or 1:1 support where appropriate Creating calm, safe spaces to support emotional regulation Working with external professionals such as Speech and Language Therapists, Health Visitors and Early Years SEND teams Ongoing staff training to ensure best practice and inclusive support We aim to ensure all children feel included, supported and able to reach their full potential within our setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to ensure that all children with SEND feel safe, included and supported to reach their full potential. We aim to: Support children to make progress in their learning and development in line with their individual starting points Build children’s confidence, independence and self-esteem Support communication, social skills and emotional wellbeing Ensure children can access all areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) through adapted and inclusive practice Work in partnership with families to provide consistent and supportive care Provide early identification and appropriate support to help meet children’s needs as soon as possible Support smooth transitions within the setting and into school For families, we aim to: Provide clear communication, reassurance and ongoing support Work collaboratively with parents and carers in decision making Signpost to external services and professionals where appropriate Our overall goal is to create a positive, inclusive environment where every child and their family feels valued, supported and able to thrive. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Members of our team have completed the following SEND-specific training: Sophie Benson SEND Level 3 - completed June 2021 Lucy Garner Introduction to the role of SENCO - completed November 2025 In addition, staff access ongoing training and support through the Local Authority and Early Years services to ensure they remain up to date with best practice in supporting children with additional needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We believe that strong partnerships with parents are key to supporting every child’s development, including those with SEND. We involve parents by: Sharing regular updates on their child’s progress and development Holding meetings and reviews to discuss progress, next steps, and any support plans Working collaboratively with parents when creating and reviewing individual support plans Providing opportunities to speak with key staff, including the SENCO, whenever needed Parents can get involved by: Sharing information about their child’s needs, routines, and interests Attending meetings and reviews Working with us on agreed strategies to support their child at home and in the setting Speaking to staff at any time if they have questions or concerns We aim to maintain open, honest communication and ensure parents feel listened to, supported, and fully involved in their child’s journey. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share information with parents regularly to keep you fully informed about your child’s development and wellbeing. This includes: Daily verbal feedback at drop-off and collection Updates through our parent communication system Blossom Termly progress reviews and development summaries Regular opportunities to speak with your child’s key person For children with SEND, we provide additional support and communication, including: Individual support plans (e.g. SEN Support Plans) which are reviewed regularly with parents More frequent review meetings to discuss progress and next steps Close involvement of the SENCO to support planning and communication Collaboration with external professionals (with your consent), with updates shared with you Clear tracking of small steps of progress and tailored strategies We work in partnership with you at all times to ensure you feel informed, supported, and involved in your child’s development. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We aim to provide an inclusive, safe, and accessible environment for all children, including those with SEND. Indoors: Rooms are organised to allow clear pathways and easy movement for all children Resources are accessible at child level to promote independence Quiet areas are available for children who may need a calmer space Visual supports (where needed) are used to help children understand routines and transitions We adapt the environment and activities to meet individual needs Outdoors: Outdoor areas are secure and designed to be accessible for a range of abilities We provide a variety of play opportunities to support physical, sensory, and social development Activities can be adapted to ensure all children can take part We continually review our environment and make reasonable adjustments to ensure all children can access learning, play, and daily routines comfortably and safely. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can begin the process by contacting us directly to arrange a visit and discuss their child’s needs. The process includes: An initial visit to the setting to meet the team and view the environment A discussion with parents to understand the child’s individual needs, routines, and any existing support in place Completion of registration forms and sharing of any relevant reports or assessments Planning a tailored settling-in process to support a smooth transition Involvement of the SENCO, where appropriate, to ensure support is in place from the start We work closely with families from the outset to ensure each child is supported effectively and feels safe, settled, and included within the setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are committed to continuously improving our SEND provision to ensure all children receive high-quality, inclusive support. Our future plans include: Ongoing staff training to build knowledge and confidence in supporting a wide range of SEND needs Further development of our SENCO role to strengthen support planning and partnerships with families Enhancing our learning environments to better support sensory and individual needs Strengthening links with external professionals to provide joined-up support for children and families.

name: Music Education
description: Little Strummers is based in Buckinghamshire and has been providing fun and accessible individual and group guitar and ukulele lessons since 2019. We also include singing and piano in our teaching portfolio. Children and adults benefit from our teaching approach, which integrates music theory, aural skills, and practice techniques to provide a unique and supportive learning experience. We want to share music with everyone. In addition to weekly lessons, we run engaging music workshops and community strumming clubs, including regular sessions for local residents in care homes. These relaxed and friendly sessions promote wellbeing, connection, and joy through shared music-making, bringing people together regardless of age or ability. We also provide music lessons in schools. We manage all administration and lesson bookings, including contacting parents, arranging timetables, invoicing, collecting fees, and writing reports. Performing is an important part of learning an instrument, and we are always there to support school concerts and events. Little Strummers has also been running Home Education sessions for six months. Instruments and all materials are provided by HS Music CIC, our not-for-profit partner. The children are progressing brilliantly in their playing and learning, while also building friendships, developing communication skills, and working together in ways that can sometimes be more challenging outside a traditional classroom environment. Please let us know if we can help you with anything musical or if you need a welcoming space to run a club.

name: Odds Farm Park
description: Whatever the Season and whatever the weather you’ll find stacks of Animal Fun, Amazing Outdoor Adventure, and Giant Indoor Play here at Odds Farm Park! There’s something for everyone: - Hands-on animal encounters in the Animal Barn only - Rare breeds and daily animal activities - Outdoor adventure play areas - Giant indoor soft play - Seasonal events like sheep shearing, cowboy crafts, and more! We host a Christmas Cracker event with a Father Christmas grotto experience and a Pumpkin Festival in October. Open daily 10am to 5:30pm (last entry at 4:30pm). Closed Tuesdays between mid September and late March (open on peak Tuesdays during school holidays and February Half Term). Please visit our website to learn more and book your next adventure at Odds Farm Park.
organisation: Odds Farm Park Come and enjoy the fresh farm air, our wide-open spaces, and spend time with all our furry friends here at Odds Farm Park! We want you to enjoy an amazing day full of farm adventures, and for you to do this safely and with confidence, we have introduced numerous new measures to ensure we can be COVID secure at all times. All guests must pre-book tickets online ahead of their visit so we can carefully manage daily visitor numbers, and new routes, walk-ways and staggered entry to certain areas have also been added to maintain social distancing measures around the Farm. As an outdoor family farm park attraction, we have always actively encouraged regular hand-washing for all guests, and we are offering extensive hand hygiene facilities across the Farm Park, including: 5 dedicated hand-washing stations 18 hand sanitising stations 3 bathroom and hand-washing blocks Whilst our Indoor Play barn, Demonstration Barn and Adventure Maze are temporarily closed, here at Odds Farm Park there’s plenty of space for kids to run, tumble and play. There are acres of outdoor adventure to discover, including the extensive Adventure Log Play Area, H2Odds Water Play, Mini-Land Rovers, Sand Play Area, Adventure Fort, Go-Karts, Tractor and Trailer Rides (Apr to Oct), Fitness Trail, Under 5s Log Play Area - what will you do first? Of course, no farm visit would be complete without meeting the animals! Explore our Undercover Animal Barn, where you can see our rabbits and guinea pigs, and even hand-feed some of our sheep and goats! Adults and children alike can strut and cluck their way around Chicken World, and watch our feathered friends enjoy exploring their new home! In the summer months, guests can also visit our pigs, cows, donkeys, ponies and other animals out enjoying their paddocks across the Farm – you might catch a glimpse of some piglets, calves and a foal trotting and springing around in the sunshine! Feeling hungry? Our outdoor outlets, The Airstream and Ice Cream and Milkshake Parlour, are offering a contactless service, and visitors can now Click and Collect a range of delicious drinks and tasty treats via our new online ordering system. As always, guests are welcome to bring their own picnics to enjoy whilst visiting and which can be enjoyed throughout the park at any of our socially distanced picnic tables. For further information on how to book and what to expect from your visit, we have all the details you need on our Reopening page. To find out what’s on, guests can also check out our new interactive map to help plan their day and guide them through our amazing outdoor adventures! main@oddsfarm.co.uk https://www.oddsfarm.co.uk/

local_offer: Our Mission: We are committed to providing a happy, safe, and nurturing environment in the heart of Dorney Village. Encouraging our children to explore, learn and thrive through play. Our staff offers true team spirit, enriching the outcomes for all children in our care.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to give children the best possible start to their education. To ensure this happens, if appropriate, we will work with families to seek support from outside agencies and will implement recommended strategies according to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 3 Early Years SENCO, February 2026. Curiosity Programme Training, October 2025. Makaton Levels 1 and 2, March 2025. Making Sense of Autism, July 2024. Good Autism Practice, March 2024. SENCO Training, November 2023. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Volunteering, we welcome any parents to come in and do an activity with the children. On outings, we may ask some parents to come on trips. Events, most of our events, parents and grandparents are invited to join. Committee, we are run by a committee which needs to be made up mainly of existing parents. Always a great opportunity to get involved and help with the playgroup's fundraising. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At St Nicolas Playgroup, we are using Ovivio, which is an online journal that parents are able to access when they would like. The children's journals are updated regularly from the observations carried out in the setting, and families are also able to update, so that practitioners can see what fun children have had over the weekend. We have drop-in mornings, which are similar to a parents' evening. This takes place in a morning session, where we ask parents and children to come along for a short period, where the practitioners can show you any reports or trackers that identify your children's progress through their time at playgroup. Ultimately, we are always available to speak to parents/carers on any given day if there are concerns or enquiries about their children. We are happy to arrange meetings to discuss further if needed. For children with SEND we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents. Their short-term outcomes will be regularly monitored and parents are invited to be part of this review and planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist...) are visiting, we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have a 'free flow' setting. After registration, we open up all doors inside and outside, and the children are able to move around where they would like. We have staff in all areas and abide by a staff-to-child ratio. Around our outdoor area, we have a gate that is secure to stop the children from going any further. We make some adaptations when we are trying to meet individual needs. To ensure the safety of some children, we may keep some doors closed for a period of time. We have a quiet area and a place where we can have one-to-one interaction with individual children to help support their development. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? At St Nicolas Playgroup, we work with the children and families on what they think will be the best transition for them. We believe that every child is unique. We will support the parents' decision and will also advise what we may think will work. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We would like to attend more training and to provide more resources.

description: A childminder located in Buckingham in the district of Aylesbury Vale. I live with my partner and our two children in a welcoming home in Buckingham, we have a large living room and a large garden which opens out to the local woods. I work with another registered Childminder, Donna Cruickshank. We currently work 50% of our time from our homes and the other 50% from the Youth Centre in Buckingham; this has given the children more space to enjoy. There are a variety of activities whilst at the Youth Club which offers a large indoor room, a large kitchen and a large garden area. We also have two assistants, Maria and Sam who job share. Donna offers a lovely welcoming home with a large living room and kitchen, an enclosed child-friendly garden and is close to a number of parks. My home is only a short distance from Donna's home and offers a large living, dining, kitchen area and a large garden and also have access to a number of local parks. We attend local toddler groups, the library and parks on a regular basis. We aim to provide a relaxed yet stimulating environment and pride ourselves on our close relationship with all of the children we care for and their families.

name: Kirsty Rawding
description: A childminder located in Buckingham in the district of Aylesbury Vale. I live with my partner and our two children in a welcoming home in Buckingham, we have a large living room and a large garden which opens out to the local woods. I work with another registered Childminder, Donna Cruickshank. We currently work 50% of our time from our homes and the other 50% from the Youth Centre in Buckingham; this has given the children more space to enjoy. There are a variety of activities whilst at the Youth Club which offers a large indoor room, a large kitchen and a large garden area. We also have two assistants, Maria and Sam who job share. Donna offers a lovely welcoming home with a large living room and kitchen, an enclosed child-friendly garden and is close to a number of parks. My home is only a short distance from Donna's home and offers a large living, dining, kitchen area and a large garden and also have access to a number of local parks. We attend local toddler groups, the library and parks on a regular basis. We aim to provide a relaxed yet stimulating environment and pride ourselves on our close relationship with all of the children we care for and their families.

name: Sing and Sign Baby Signing | Thursdays (Gerrards Cross)
description: Sing and Sign Baby Signing classes are perfect for babies from 6 weeks to around two and a half years. Babies use all kinds of signs and gestures as a natural part of learning to talk. Encouraging your baby with extra signs like 'milk', 'more', 'change nappy', or 'tired' will help your baby communicate. Baby signing with Sing and Sign is easy because we make it fun to learn. Your baby will recognise important words sooner and can use the signs to “talk” to you before speech. Age-specific classes are developed with the help and approval of speech and language therapists, designed to build the framework of good communication through song, music, and sign. The programme is designed to develop and progress with your baby's development. Our 11 week in-venue courses are running on Mondays in Beaconsfield and Thame, Tuesdays in Downley and Thursdays in Farnham Common, Gerrards Cross, and Chinnor. We'd love to have you join us. Gerrards Cross class times are Thursdays: 9:45am - Stage 2: 15 months to 2 and a half years 10:45am - Stage 1: 6 to 14 months 11:45am - Babes: Birth to 6 months Our Autumn term will run from 17 September to 3 December. All classes will have a one-week half-term break week of 26 October. To book your spot please visit the link provided.

name: Heritage Crafts and Skills at COAM
description: Heritage Crafts: See Traditional Skills in Action Heritage crafts in the UK are living links to the country’s social, rural, and industrial history, rooted in skills passed down through generations. Practices such as blacksmithing, spinning, bodging, spoon carving, and bucket making developed out of everyday necessity, using locally available materials and deeply practical knowledge. From shaping iron at the forge to turning green wood on a pole lathe, these crafts reflect a close relationship between people, landscape, and labour. They embody not only technical skill but also regional identity, storytelling, and ways of working that predate mass production. Today, these crafts are valued not just for the objects they produce, but for the cultural knowledge they carry. In an age of industrial manufacturing and digital convenience, heritage crafts offer a slower, more mindful approach to making- one that prioritises durability, repair, and sustainability. Chiltern Open Air Museum showcases heritage crafts ensuring that these skills remain relevant and accessible for future generations rather than disappearing into history.

local_offer: Kiddies Cove Day Nursery is a private owned Nursery that caters for up to 100 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. Building positive relationships with the children and their families is very important to us. Here at Kiddies Cove Day Nursery, we understand that every child is unique and we have high aspirations for all children. We encourage working together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Shannon Whiteway Randall has a level three certificate for Early Years Special Needs Coordinators in Private, Voluntary and Independent Settings. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an inclusive environment where parents and carers can feel happy and confident communicating openly with us regarding their children. We are regularly available to have formal catch-ups with parents to discuss their child’s needs and provide term reports regarding each child’s progress that the key worker will discuss in detail with the parent. We speak daily with parents at drop off and pick up and communicate through our online parent app, Blossom Educational. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journal that parents/carers can look at any time by asking their child’s Key Person. Parents also see these at our informal parent's evenings that we hold twice a year. We will discuss progress when we complete termly key worker reports, through our 2-year-old progress checks and during our termly COHORT evaluations. For children with SEN, we try to ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and work together to plan new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take into account the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We try to create areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning and to create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing issues. Our setting has a wheelchair ramp for access to the ground floor and has a disabled toilet that is accessible for wheelchair users. We are set over three three floors. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We would like to further our sensory resources by creating a sensory area in our soft playroom. We feel that this would benefit many of our children and help support their development.

name: The Knolls (Church Street, Wingrave)
description: The Knolls is a southwest-facing steeply sloping field on the northwest side of Church Street just past Cobblers Wick. The field is used to graze a number of ponies but it has considerable recreational and amenity value to the village. For over thirty years it has been the location of the village bonfire and firework display to celebrate Guy Fawkes. In winter it has been used for more than living memory as the village tobogganing and sledging field as it has the most appropriate slope for such activities in the village. The field has spectacular far-reaching panoramic views over the Vale of Aylesbury to the Chilterns and on towards Chinnor. For all these reasons the field has considerable green space and amenity to the village. The Knolls is 1.4 hectares and is in character with the adjacent Church Street and the bounding agricultural land.

name: Parental Education Growth Support (PEGS)- Child to Parent Abuse Support
description: Parental Education Growth Support (PEGS) aims to reduce the impact of Child to Parent Abuse (CPA) by supporting parents, carers, and guardians who are experiencing CPA (including those with adult offspring), training frontline professionals, impacting policy, and raising awareness. We don't directly work with the child displaying the behaviours but have a network of partners whose expertise lies in this area. CPA is where a child (of any age) displays repeated abusive behaviours towards a parental figure. This abuse may be physical, verbal, economic, digital, coercive, or sexual. CPA is thought to occur in at least 3% of UK homes, although the real figure could be much higher. CPA is not 'normal' challenging behaviour experienced by most parents. It causes parents to feel fearful and isolated, forces them to leave their careers and change their routines and lifestyles, and has a profound impact on families. We've developed a range of virtual services for parents to enable access from anywhere in the UK, alongside training and policy consultancy for organisations looking to recognise CPA, improve their responses to it, and support those impacted by this type of abuse. Please visit our website for more information and to contact us.

description: Enrych offers a variety of services to adults with physical disabilities across Buckinghamshire. Our one-to-one volunteer service has been operating in Buckinghamshire for several years, helping hundreds of adults with physical disabilities to take up leisure, learning, and sporting activities, supported by a one-to-one volunteer who shares their interest. All of our services are offered free of charge to the service user and are funded by grants and community fundraising. Services include: Enrych Phone Pals Volunteer pairings sharing a phone call once a week. Enrych Connect Adults with physical disabilities and their carers are introduced to computers, tablets, and the internet with the aim of reducing social isolation and improve independence, quality of life, and well-being. We aim to provide advice and support on the best equipment to meet individual needs before offering basic training at the individual's own pace in whatever software is required. Enrych Interact Monthly Zoom programme with varied sessions including quizzes, bingo, seated movement, a book club, wellbeing sessions, and more. We offer something for everyone. Enrych Social Anyone joining any of our service will automatically be welcomed to the Enrych Social Community and will receive a Newsletter every quarter together with invitations to the numerous social events we run across Buckinghamshire. Please visit our website to learn more and to become part of the Enrych community.

description: Join us at College Lake with your pre-school little ones to explore the nature reserve and enjoy wildlife themed activities. Children must be accompanied by an adult who is able to encourage them and support them with the activities. This event is for children aged between 2 and 4 who can confidently walk. organisation: Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust (BBOWT) One of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England. This large Living Landscape covers an area between Oxford, Bicester and Aylesbury. It includes 48,400 hectares of woodland, mixed farmland and floodplain meadows across the boundary between Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire. The entire area is ecologically linked through the River Ray, which rises in Quainton, close to Finmere Wood nature reserve, and flows west alongside some of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England, to join the River Cherwell at Islip, north of Oxford. Since 1981 BBOWT (Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust) has been buying and restoring floodplain meadows in the upper reaches of the River Ray, and working with neighbouring farmers to create a stronghold for wading birds including curlew. info@bbowt.org.uk https://www.bbowt.org.uk/wildlife/living-landscapes/bernwood-forest-and-ray-valley-living-landscape

local_offer: I aim to provide an inclusive and supportive environment where every child feels valued and able to thrive. I work closely with parents to understand each child’s individual needs and adapt activities, routines and the learning environment to support their development. My setting promotes inclusion, positive relationships and equal opportunities for all children.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My setting aims to support children with special educational needs and disabilities to feel safe, included and confident in a nurturing home environment. I focus on helping children develop their communication, social and emotional skills through play-based learning and positive relationships. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Autism training, ADHD training, Providing support for SEND (3-5Y) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I believe that working in partnership with parents is very important to support each child’s development and wellbeing. I communicate regularly with parents through daily updates, conversations at drop-off and collection, and sharing observations about their child’s progress. Parents are encouraged to share information about their child’s interests, routines and any additional needs so I can provide the best possible care and support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? For children with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND), communication with parents may be more frequent and detailed. We may work together to set small, achievable targets and review progress regularly. I will share observations, discuss strategies that support the child’s development, and, where appropriate, work with parents and other professionals to ensure the child receives the right support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Indoor space for all children and a loved garden to explore. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact me directly to enquire about childcare places and to discuss their child’s individual needs. I welcome the opportunity to speak with parents before a place begins so we can talk about routines, interests and any additional support their child may require. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am committed to continuing to develop my knowledge and skills in supporting children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). I plan to attend relevant training and keep up to date with guidance and best practice so I can provide inclusive care and learning opportunities for all children.

organisation: Calm Little Minds Ltd Calm Little Minds is a leading specialist in Buckinghamshire, delivering prevention, intervention and treatment of emotional difficulties for children and families. Calm Little Minds offers an emotional wellbeing support service to children, young people and their families in the Buckinghamshire area. The service is friendly, private, confidential and affordable. We offer help for common challenges facing children and young people growing up in today’s pressured world. Whatever the issue, whether that be anxiety, anger outbursts, challenging behaviour at home or even toileting and fussy eating. Some causes of these behaviours can be due to a number of reasons including examination stress, parent separation or friendship problems. Calm little minds is here to offer support to your child and family. We work with your child at a time and place that works for you, usually in the comfort and safety of the school environment or your own home. We listen to you and assess your child to understand their unique situation. An average of six weekly sessions works well and we will keep you updated if there is a need for more or fewer than six, depending on the progress your child is making. We personalise the teaching of coping mechanisms to help with their needs, whatever is worrying them or detracting from them enjoying their childhood to the full, whilst increasing their resilience to help them with future challenges in life. Whilst it is always advisable to talk to your GP about these issues you can also fast track access to additional support through Calm Little Minds to help your child understand how to manage these issues and improve their emotional wellbeing. We act quickly so you are not on a long NHS waiting list to see if you even meet NHS criteria for treatment. hello@calmlittleminds.co.uk http://www.calmlittleminds.co.uk

local_offer: Bright Heart provides in-person tuition in London and surrounding counties, and online tuition worldwide. It works closely with local authorities to provide tuition to students with Education Health and Care Plans (EHCPs), including Education Other than at School (EOTAS) packages. It also supports schools and was an accredited National Tutoring Programme (NTP) Tuition Partner. In addition, it works with private families. Bright Heart offers a nurturing approach and focuses on supporting children and young people with learning challenges or social, emotional, and mental health (SEMH) needs. It also helps students lacking confidence or motivation or who have fallen behind at school and those needing interim education outside of school. Bright Heart is passionate about helping its students achieve their potential. Its education team, comprising three former teachers with qualified teacher status (QTS), takes the time to fully understand students’ unique learning needs to ensure they receive well-matched tutors. Pupils receive individual learning plans (ILPs) covering their academic goals and SEMH needs. Bright Heart carefully monitors tuition. Bright Heart’s tutors are carefully screened, personally interviewed by a director or education consultant, background checked (including Enhanced DBS with children’s barred list check) and met in person. They receive comprehensive training and guidance on tutoring and safeguarding and adhere to Bright Heart’s stringent tutoring standards and policies. Bright Heart covers from Reception to A-level and offers adult support. It offers supplementary tuition and interim education, covering the entire curriculum.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Bright Heart is a SEN-focused specialist tutoring agency providing tranformative tutoring with a nurturing approach. Tailored education is provided for each young person with academic and SEMH goals, tracked with an Individual Learning Plan. Bright Heart helps young people transition to their next step in their education journey or setting. We provide a free exam booking service for LA referrals. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Bright Heart tutors go through rigorous checks in our hiring process and have SEN experience as a pre-requisite. Our tutors receive SEND training from Nasen. Tutors also attend annual workshops with the latest in SEND presented by Nasen. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Every parent gets a free consultation regarding their child from our Education Consultants. We work with key stakeholders and have been recognised nationally by nasen for our co-production. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We provide daily lesson reports and an Individual Learning Plan. Our Education Consultants check-in to see the tutoring is going well and also partake in Annual Reviews. Our Education Consultants will also book exams if entering as a private candidate. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Bright Heart tutors will travel to your home or a community setting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please get in touch at hello@brightheart.co.uk and our Education Consultants will be happy to respond to you. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Bright Heart is growing across the UK, supporting many children with its transformative and nurturing approach.

name: Lace Hill Academy School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Buckingham for 2 to 11-year-olds. Lace Hill Academy is a vibrant one-form entry primary school located in Buckingham. We are honoured to be part of the Campfire Education Trust. Both at a school and Trust level, the children are at the centre of all we do, and we are very proud of them and our whole school community. Visitors often comment when they come into the school how calm the environment is and how polite our children are. We believe strongly that embedded values are at the heart of nurturing and developing children ready for the next stage of their education, and ultimately supporting them to become good citizens in our community. At Lace Hill, our core values are Resilience, Integrity, and Respect, which set the high expectations we have of all our children and staff. We are very lucky to have supportive families who are willing to work with us for the benefit of our children. We place great emphasis on collaboration between the school and families to ensure the best possible opportunities are in place for all the children. Parents support us in key elements of the school, such as the school uniform policy, the behaviour policy, and the attendance policy. Lace Hill also make great efforts to link itself with the immediate community and has close contacts with local industry, Well Street Church, Buckingham University, and the local printing office. Our broad and balanced curriculum is designed to be responsive to every cohort and child in our school. While we have a curriculum in place designed to enable rich and inspiring experiences with a focus on the learning extracted from exciting opportunities, we believe our curriculum is never finished because no child is the same and therefore deserves a curriculum that is adaptable and flexible to the children and classes in our school and the context they are living in. Our curriculum gives children the opportunity to showcase their talents beyond the classroom. We have specialist teachers in place teaching languages, music and sport with the chance to attend many festivals and be a valued member of the community. We have extended services on-site for parents who require wraparound care for their children. Breakfast Club is from 7:30am, and Afterschool Clubs are until 4:30pm and 6pm. The sessions are run by Sports 4 All, and you can find more information by visiting our website.

description: Lace Hill Academy Nursery offers sessions for children currently from when they reach their second birthday onwards Our early year’s provision offers a warm, welcoming, and safe atmosphere in an outstanding environment for learning. It is designed with the children at its heart, with playing and learning opportunities both inside and out. Here at Lace Hill Academy, we are a supportive, caring community, with elevated expectations for all children to be able to thrive and have the best possible start in education. We strongly believe that working in partnership with parents is essential to our children's success and happiness. Ensuring your child and family have a positive and personal transition into the nursery is our priority. We will tailor this to the individual child’s needs as our experience tells us children need different approaches and lengths of time to settle. Our staff will be in contact with you soon to begin to get to know you and your child and to plan their transition . Our aim is to ensure that each child receives the best start on the road to developing a love of life-long learning in a safe, nurturing environment which enables them to develop resilience, integrity and respect. We believe that children learn best through play. In nursery, we plan ‘in the moment’ to take account of each child’s interest and next steps in their learning and we strive to provide an environment where the children feel nurtured, safe, and secure. We aim to prepare them for the next stage in education by building the essential foundation skills. Our nursery takes full advantage of the outdoors. The outside environment provides children with a sense of freedom where discoveries can spark awe and wonder and where we can engage with the natural world and further our learning. Applications are currently being taken for the next Academic Year starting September 2026. name: Amy Connolly
description: Ofsted rated - OUTSTANDING 2022 My aim is to provide a welcoming, caring environment for your child and to become a home away from home while they are with me. I provide fun and interesting activities to engage your child covering all areas of the EYFS, for example, I have a mud kitchen in the garden and encourage sensory, messy play. From my experience of working in a nursery, I always have fun activities planned. Activities are a happy mix of planned and child-led, all based on your child’s individual needs and interests. I aim to provide an inclusive environment for all and encourage independence. I believe learning through play is vital for a child’s development and I ensure that each child has ample time to explore, play and be physically active. I’m a creative person and love to use this to influence my planning, from arts and crafts to cooking and dress-up fun. I also enjoy being outdoors and encourage outdoor learning as much as possible. All meals are planned in advance and I cook with fresh ingredients to minimise waste and to promote a healthy lifestyle with special dietary requirements catered for. We love to bake as a family and I will have planned weekly cooking activities for your child to engage in for all ages. I am trying to do my bit to help reduce waste in the home. I use natural homemade cleaning products as much as possible. I believe teaching the next generation to look after the world today will save their futures and I actively promote this in my setting. My qualifications: I hold a CACHE NNEB qualification, a CACHE level 3 in Home-based Childcare, and a level 4 in Childcare Management. I hold a valid Paediatric First Aid Certificate and Basic Food Hygiene. To continue my professional development I attend relevant courses (such as Safeguarding) and relevant online training. I worked for several years in a Nursery as a Nursery teacher and whole school coordinator, before becoming a Mother myself to my two wonderful children.

local_offer: I aim to provide an inclusive environment for all children. I will provide appropriate age and stage toys/activities to meet all needs in an inclusive environment. Although I have touched on SEND training in my last job, I feel this to be slightly out-of-date, and I am keen on attending new courses in the near future to help me in my own personal and professional development. I will work closely with the parent to provide the best support needed for each individual child. Where needed, daily communication books can be provided and regular meetings with parents to discuss progress or share ideas. Progress checks at 2 will be done and regular progress trackers kept which can be viewed at any time from parents/careers. I am happy to share information with any external support workers and will provide as much help and support I can. My home provides an easy access driveway to the front door and the downstairs in on one level with and lovely garden also on one flat level. I aim to provide separate areas both inside and outside of different types of play, for example, a sensory mud kitchen in the garden. Transition periods for all children are done on an individual basis. We can take as much or as less time as each child needs in order for them to feel happy with me and in their new environment.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Qualified Nursery Nurse up to Cache level 4. Several years of experience working in Nurseries as a Nursery Teacher and Nursery Coordinator. Vast experience in messy play offered, for example- Mud Kitchens and an endless supply of songs for all. Music and dance sessions. Treasure baskets, puppet play and story sacks. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? New training required. Previous training out of date. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Learning Journeys will be created for your children. Daily feedback. Private WhatsApp communication set up between ourselves. Stay and play sessions when convenient. Daily communication books for your child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Progress checks done at 2 years old. Progress monitored throughout your child stay with me. This information will then travel with your child to the next stage to their education provider or kept by yourselves. Any concerns that arise from my assessments will be shared with parents/carers to help aid your child's development. Photos shared with parents of their child's progress. Parents meetings arranged. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Private drive with a path. Step up to front door. Downstairs toilet. Large garden. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I believe a child should be happy and settled before they start with me for the arranged hours. This will mean a 'settling in' period will be arranged between ourselves and will be individual for every child needs. To start your child will have already been introduced to myself while the parents or careers are there. After this, a short visit alone will take place. Depending on how well the settling in period goes, we extend each visit until we feel happy the child is settling well. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Training to be arranged.

local_offer: At First Place we recognise each child as a unique individual and every child is entitled to equal rights and opportunities. We are committed to reviewing and evaluating our practice to ensure we are continually inclusive to all, celebrating differences and diversity. We recognise each child develops at their own pace, and the care our staff provides, supports each child to thrive.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Through regular observations and interactions, key carers will work with the SENCO and parents to assess the needs of each individual child. Staff are able to create and support individual care plans and needs and support early intervention, so children can reach their full potential. Specialist services we are working with are: * Buckinghamshire Early Years * Speech and Language * Occupational Therapy * Hearing support * Specialist Teaching * Paediatrician * Health Visitors * Feeder School SENCOs What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SEND - code of conduct AED - training Inclusion How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We pride ourselves on our parent partnership at First Place, as we know this is essential for children to flourish. We will support your child in developing a bond with the Key Carer and helping them to settle happily into nursery. The SENCO will liaise with other professionals as appropriate to your child’s needs, ensuring that you are fully involved throughout. For our children with additional needs, the SENCO invites you for regular meetings to keep you updated on your child’s progress, and with your permission our SENCO will support your child's Key person to complete tools such as Assess, Plan, Do, Reviews, and SEN support plans to identify areas and support your child’s development. Your child’s key Carer will share learning observations on our Famly app, and share how you can be supporting your child at home. We hold stay and play sessions where you are invited into the setting to play with your child, so you can see how the team supports your child’s individual needs, providing continuity for your child. We also keep you informed about parent specific training that is available in Buckinghamshire and how you can access further support as a family. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share information with parents about children's progress through: * Daily collection handovers * Parent consultations * 2-year-old checks * Termly summaries * Regular development updates In addition, for children with SEND we complete the above as well as: * Co-producing Assess Plan Do Review (APDR) * Co-producing SEN Support Plan * Co-producing Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) and 6-month reviews How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting has an accessible environment both indoor and outdoors, some aspects are: * Wide door frames * Adjustable tables * Quiet areas for 1:1 sessions * Resources suitable to support children with SEN * Occupational Therapy equipment, such as: a peanut ball, sensory wobble cushions, sensory toys to support self-regulation and concentration, a trampette. * Basket time - individual children or small groups to help with concentration/ integration. * Risk assessments are carried out to evaluate the environment to ensure it is safe and meets children current needs. Resources are purchased when and if necessary to meet individual children's needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please get in touch with the nursery SENCO, to discuss your child's specific needs. We will then arrange a tour so you can see the nursery in person and we can effectively plan and ensure our environment and resources will support your child's individual needs. When your child has registered, we will support your child to settle through as many settling in sessions as they require. Each child will be allocated a key Carer who will tailor their practice to meet your child's needs and work in partnership with you and other professionals if required, to support their development. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We continue to reflect on our practice and develop in all areas. The SENCOs will continue to attend regular training and meetings to ensure all information is kept up to date. We will continue to access appropriate training for staff and ensure their knowledge is shared with parents so we are working together to support each child. We will continue to work in partnership with outside agencies, to enable us to gain their expertise in certain areas if required.
