local_offer: We support all children and their families with their development to access the curriculum and to help them be ready for their next stage in life. Where required, we will provide enhanced ratio care within the setting to ensure the safety and development of the children are met. Any guidance provided by outsourced professional agencies is taken on board and implemented as required and we aim to work closely with them and the families on a regular basis.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Pollyanna Pre-School CIO's aim is for children to have the best possible start in life, ongoing support and good well-being. Early intervention is crucial for these children. Identifying their needs and seeking the right support in their education and development will give them the best possible outcomes. We aim to support these children and their families by sharing information, liaising and working together with parents, carers and professionals involved. We implement an inclusive environment, however, we also recognise that those children with SEND can sometimes need an adapted curriculum. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Training that has been completed to date: Makaton EHCP Training SEN and Beyond AET Training L1 Speech and Language SEND Code of Practice Supporting Children with SEND In-House SEN Training Curiosity Approach Seeing Beyond Behaviour Intensive Interaction Neli Language Intervention Program How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Pollyanna, we are dedicated to creating great parent partnerships and encouraging our parents and carers to feel involved with what we do. We operate an 'open door' policy and staff are available to talk to at the end of each session. We are also available via telephone and email at any time. We ask parents to be involved through our learning journals, where they can comment on observations, and add their own. For families where people other than parents do drop off or collect (such as grandparents or childminders), we have home and preschool communication diaries so parents have a direct method of communication with their child's key person. We hold coffee mornings, where families and childminders of current children can come in, sit and have a drink while their children play. They can chat to other parents and staff, and have the opportunity to see how we run. We have open mornings, where prospective families can come and visit the preschool during a session, as well as regular fundraising and social events. We communicate regularly with parents using email, newsletters and social media. We are also run by a voluntary management committee, so parents and carers and their families can be involved in the running of the setting by joining our committee. We have parent evenings two times a year where we have the opportunity for parents and carers to discuss their child's development with their key person. This also gives them the opportunity to discuss any concerns they may have. Every term, we complete the next steps for the children, which incorporates ideas of how parents can support their learning at home, and at the beginning of each term, parents are asked to complete an all-about-me update which they share with the preschool any new milestones their child may have reached, or any new interests they have, or any activities they do. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Pollyanna works closely in partnership with families to ensure the best possible outcomes for their children. Observations and development outcomes are shared with parents constantly using our online learning journal, and the targets that are being worked on with each child are discussed verbally with the family. Each term we complete written next steps which are uploaded onto their online learning journal for parents to view and comment on. All staff are aware of any additional support that is being given to a child, and how the child is progressing so that they can work with the child during the sessions. Our planning and next steps are linked directly to each child specifically so the curriculum will cater for the needs of the individual child, any specific SEND requirements are noted on their individual plans. Children with SEND will have a SEN support plan or APDR where targets are noted and reviewed regularly. The SENDco has regular meetings with multi agencies and parents, to ensure communication is clear and everyone is working towards the same outcomes for the child. Professionals are encouraged to regularly come into the setting to observe the children when required and will review targets with us and parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The indoor environment is on a single level, with the entire play space accessible to all. We have small children's toilets, and access to a disabled toilet if the small toilets are not adequate for space. We have a private space near the toilets to enable us to change children that cannot be changed on the changing unit. The side door (main entrance) to Pollyanna has a step, but there is a large double front door and side access that has a ramp to enter the building. We have an enclosed play area to the rear, which is laid to astroturf and can be accessed by the main entrance, or via the ramp at the rear if required. We have free-flow access to our garden all year round and also access to the park and surrounding areas. We include all children with SEND and adjust play accordingly. We complete a risk assessment as required for outside visits and use enhanced ratios for children with SEND when on an outing. The APDR and support plans are used to identify any resources or equipment that we may need for the child. We will discuss required resources any with any other professionals that are involved with the child, and provide these where possible. Additional funding may be sourced if required. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When a child comes to Pollyanna from another setting, we will discuss the child and any needs they may have with the family, and contact the previous setting for information on the child's development and any support they require if necessary. If the child has additional needs, we will gather information from the other professionals working with the child, and discuss them coming into Pollyanna before the child starts to ensure we have everything we need for the child when they come in. All children that start at Pollyanna will have a home visit where possible. The key person will go to the child's house to meet them and their family. The staff will talk about the child's likes and interests, their strengths and any support required. The child will then come into the setting and have 2 settling sessions prior to starting. If the child needs more time to settle, we will adopt this process to meet the needs of the child and their family. If a child is leaving Pollyanna for another setting, we will contact the new setting and discuss the child's development and any support they have had. We can transfer our online learning journey to them if appropriate, and share information with any additional settings that children attend to ensure the best possible outcomes for the child and provide continuity across the settings. If a child leaves Pollyanna, who we feel may need additional support, we can visit the setting with the child and their family to help with settling at their new setting, we also invite the new setting to come into Pollyanna to see the child here. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our SENDco and other staff continue with their professional development throughout the year, by attending courses, training, meetings and workshops. We attend relevant network group meetings to liaise with other settings and share good practices and have staff trained in Speech and language development and behaviour management. We have Speech and language-focused group sessions, to encourage speech and language development, for any children with a delay or for our younger children. We have recently invested in the WellComm Pack to enhance our provision. We also are improving our behaviour management, with lead staff who create plans and targets to support children who struggle to manage their own behaviour. We are exploring different ways of assessing children and finding what fits best for our children and our setting. For example; the 'AET progression framework', 'Mary Sheridans 0-5 Years', and 'I Can's Universally Speaking'.

description: 22 Music Academy – Alternative Education Provision 22 Music Academy provides a creative and supportive alternative education provision for school-age children and young people who may find mainstream education challenging. We specialise in using music as a therapeutic and engaging tool to help students rebuild confidence, develop skills, and reconnect with learning. Our provision supports young people with SEND, Social and Emotional Mental Health (SEMH) needs, anxiety, school avoidance, or those at risk of exclusion, offering a safe and structured environment where they can thrive outside of a traditional classroom setting. Based in a professional recording and rehearsal studio, students take part in hands-on, practical learning through music production, song-writing, recording, and performance. This real-world environment helps to increase engagement, motivation, and a sense of achievement, while supporting personal development and emotional wellbeing. We offer flexible placements tailored to individual needs, including part-time and full-day provision. We also provide a range of qualification options for all learners, including Level 1–3 and diploma pathways, ensuring every young person has the opportunity to achieve and progress at a level that suits them. At 22 Music Academy, we aim to: - Re-engage young people with education - Build confidence, resilience, and self-esteem - Develop communication, teamwork, and life skills - Support progression into further education, training, or employment We work collaboratively with schools, SENDCOs, local authorities, and families to ensure each young person receives the right level of support and achieves meaningful outcomes.

local_offer: 22 Music Academy provides a specialist alternative provision for school-age children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) who may find mainstream education challenging. Our provision is centred around therapeutic music sessions, using creative, practical activities to support young people with SEMH (Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs), anxiety, school avoidance, low confidence, and engagement difficulties. Music is used as a structured tool to help students develop emotional regulation, communication skills, and a positive connection to learning. Based in a professional studio environment, students engage in music production, song-writing, recording, and performance, allowing them to build confidence and achieve success in a setting that feels safe, supportive, and motivating. We offer flexible placements (1 to 3 days per week or full-day provision), tailored to meet individual needs. Students can work towards recognised qualifications (Level 1 to 3, diploma pathways and progression routes into further education) or focus on therapeutic engagement and personal development outcomes. 22 Music Academy works closely with schools, SENDCOs, local authorities and families to ensure that each placement is appropriate and supports the young person’s wider education plan, including EHCP outcomes where applicable. Our aim is to help young people: - Re-engage with education - Improve confidence and emotional wellbeing - Develop social, communication and life skills - Achieve meaningful qualifications - Progress into further education, training or employment We provide a safe, inclusive and supportive environment where every young person is valued and given the opportunity to succeed through creativity and music.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? 22 Music Academy aims to achieve positive, meaningful outcomes for children and young people with SEND by helping them re-engage with education, build confidence, and improve emotional wellbeing through therapeutic music-based learning. We support young people to develop communication, social, and life skills, while providing opportunities to achieve recognised qualifications and experience success in a supportive, non-traditional environment. For many students, our provision helps reduce anxiety, improve attendance, and increase motivation, creating clearer pathways into further education, training, or employment. We also aim to support families by offering a provision where their child feels safe, valued, and understood, while maintaining open communication and working collaboratively to ensure the best possible outcomes. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff at 22 Music Academy have extensive experience working with children and young people with SEND and have completed a range of relevant training to support their roles. This includes training in safeguarding and child protection, SEND awareness, behaviour support strategies, mental health awareness, and inclusive practice. Our team regularly refreshes and updates their knowledge to ensure they are able to meet the needs of young people with a variety of SEND profiles. In addition to formal training, staff bring many years of hands-on experience supporting students with SEMH needs, anxiety, school avoidance, and additional learning needs, enabling them to provide a safe, understanding, and supportive environment. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are an important part of each young person’s journey at 22 Music Academy, and we aim to work in partnership to provide the best possible support. We encourage open and ongoing communication, and parents are welcome to contact us at any time to discuss their child’s progress, wellbeing, and experience within the provision. We involve parents by sharing updates on engagement, achievements, and development where appropriate, and by working collaboratively with families, schools, and other professionals to ensure the provision is meeting the young person’s needs. Parents can also be involved in discussions around placement planning, goals, and next steps. We welcome parent involvement and are happy to arrange conversations, meetings, or visits to the studio where appropriate. By working together, we can ensure that each young person feels supported both within the provision and at home, helping them to achieve positive outcomes. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share information about your child’s progress through a secure online portal, which documents each young person’s journey with us, including their engagement, achievements, and development over time. This allows parents, carers and referring schools to access clear and consistent updates about how the young person is progressing within the provision. In addition to the portal, we are always available to discuss progress through phone calls, emails, or meetings where needed, ensuring open and supportive communication. For children and young people with SEND, we provide more personalised updates that reflect their individual needs and goals, including progress in areas such as emotional wellbeing, confidence, communication, and engagement with learning, as well as any work towards qualifications. All information is shared in line with GDPR regulations, ensuring that personal data is handled securely and only shared with appropriate individuals involved in supporting the young person. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? 22 Music Academy provides a welcoming, safe, and supportive studio environment designed to meet the needs of children and young people with a range of SEND profiles. Our indoor space is set up to be calm, structured, and low-pressure, which helps reduce anxiety and supports positive engagement with learning. Sessions take place in small groups or individually, allowing us to adapt the environment to suit each young person’s needs. The studio is designed to be accessible for a variety of learners, with flexible use of space, equipment and seating to support comfort and participation. We aim to create an environment that is inclusive, sensory-aware and supportive of emotional wellbeing, where young people feel safe and able to express themselves. Outdoor access is limited as the provision is primarily studio-based; however, we ensure that students have appropriate breaks and opportunities to step away from sessions where needed. We are happy to discuss any specific accessibility requirements with parents, carers or referring professionals to ensure appropriate arrangements can be made to support each individual young person. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children and young people can access 22 Music Academy through a referral process from schools, local authorities, or other professionals involved in their education and support. Most placements are arranged by a SENDCO, pastoral lead, alternative provision coordinator or local authority team, who will contact us to discuss the young person’s needs and suitability for the provision. Once a referral is received, we work collaboratively with the referring school or local authority, and where appropriate the parent/carer, to gather relevant information and agree a suitable placement. This may include discussing the young person’s needs, interests, timetable and whether they will be working towards therapeutic outcomes, engagement goals or accredited qualifications. We are also happy for parents or carers to make an initial enquiry directly. In these cases, we can provide guidance and liaise with the school or local authority to support the referral process. Visits to the studio can be arranged where appropriate, allowing the young person and their family or professionals to see the environment before starting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are committed to continuously developing and strengthening our SEND provision to ensure we offer the best possible support for young people. We are always exploring new ways to enhance our service, including expanding our programmes, introducing additional qualification pathways, and further developing our therapeutic music approach. Our aim is to maximise each young person’s potential by providing more opportunities for progression into further education, training and employment. We also seek to build stronger partnerships with schools, local authorities and other professionals to ensure our provision remains responsive to the needs of young people and their families. Through ongoing development, training and reflection, we strive to create an inclusive, innovative and supportive environment where all young people can achieve and succeed.

name: Cookery Holiday Workshops - Smart Raspberry Cookery School
description: Are you looking for a fun and educational activity for your child during the holidays? Look no further! Whether your child already knows their way around the kitchen or is a complete novice, our cookery workshops provide children with a fun cookery experience during the school holidays. Not only teaching them a wide range of savoury and sweet dishes but giving them the confidence and skills needed to produce their own delicious creations. Workshops are available for children aged 5 to 15 years old. This does vary by location and are often split into age groups. At Smart Raspberry we believe in hands-on learning so everyone rolls up their sleeves, puts on their aprons, and gets stuck into cooking.
organisation: Smart Raspberry Cookery School Founded in 2007 our passion has always been for children to take an interest in food and healthy eating, while having lots of fun! At our heart is our key aim: “to teach children how to cook nutritious food from scratch, helping them to learn a valuable life skill”. So we run cookery parties, clubs and classes during term time and the school holidays as well as workshops, Duke of Edinburgh courses and lots more; teaching basic cooking skills and inspiring an interest in food among children as young as 3 up to teenagers in their first years away from home. info@smartraspberry.com http://www.smartraspberry.com

name: Langley Grammar School (Berkshire)
description: Mixed-gender, selective secondary school in Langley, Berkshire 11 to 18-year-olds. We are an innovative and forward-thinking school, committed to developing our students into well-rounded, confident and successful young men and women. Our students come from a wide range of backgrounds to form a friendly and harmonious community. We provide a supportive and secure environment that enables them to flourish as individuals and achieve excellent examination outcomes. We have a very dedicated and well-qualified body of staff who are innovative, enthusiastic and committed to our school ethos. They are dedicated to building our students' academic confidence and to helping them develop the wider skills needed for higher education and the twenty-first-century workplace. In addition to high-quality teaching, our staff provide an outstanding range of opportunities for personal and physical development beyond the classroom, including an extensive range of sporting, musical and other activities. local_offer: All children in my setting have a right to be included in everything I offer. Each unique child will be supported and enabled to reach their full potential as part of my commitment to them.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Here at Haddenham’s Mini Explorers, I pour my heart into creating a space where every child feels truly seen, valued, and cared for. It matters deeply to me that each child is welcomed just as they are and supported in a way that helps them grow, explore, and shine in their own unique way. -Nurturing Every Child’s Potential I am committed to doing everything I can to meet the individual needs of every child. My aim is to make sure they can join in with all aspects of our setting, feel confident in themselves, and reach their full potential at their own pace. -Working Hand in Hand When other professionals are involved in a child’s journey, I work closely with them to ensure that the support we offer is thoughtful, consistent, and truly beneficial. Collaboration helps us give each child the very best start. -Supporting Families with Warmth and Respect Parents and carers are such an important part of a child’s world. I value every opportunity to work alongside families, offering support, listening with care, and building trusting relationships that help children flourish both here and at home. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? My Personal Experience and Understanding- Here at Haddenham’s Mini Explorers, I believe that understanding and empathy are just as important as formal training. While I haven’t completed specialist SEND training yet, I have taken time to learn from the SEND guidance on the Government website, and I continue to build my knowledge so I can offer the best support possible. On a personal level, I also bring lived experience that shapes the way I care for children. I have dyslexia myself, and I have close family members with ADHD, Autism, and Asperger’s. These experiences have given me a deep appreciation for the different ways children learn, communicate, and see the world. They help me approach each child with patience, understanding, and genuine respect for their individuality. I am always open to learning more, working with professionals, and listening to families so that every child feels supported, included, and celebrated for who they are. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Here at Haddenham’s Mini Explorers, I work closely with parents because you know your child best. I share regular updates about their learning and development via Whatsapp chat and allow time to talk on drop off and pickups, and I always welcome your thoughts about what they enjoy, what they find tricky, and what helps them feel secure. For children with SEND, partnership is especially important. I listen carefully to parents, follow any professional advice, and adapt activities so every child can take part and thrive. I’m always happy to share simple ideas you can use at home too.If you’d like to be more involved — whether by sharing information, joining an activity, or simply spending time in the setting — you’re warmly welcomed. Together, we can give your child the best possible experience. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I regularly observe and assess every child to understand how they are developing and what support they may need. I share this information with you in a way that works best for your family — whether that’s chatting in person, by phone, or Whatsapp message. For children with SEND, I offer additional support. If a particular need is identified, I work with you to create a joint action plan so we can support your child together. With your permission, I may also involve other professionals who can help. Families of children with SEND are given extra opportunities to communicate with me, and I stay flexible in how and when we talk so you always feel informed, included, and supported. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to children and families. We are on a regular bus route for those using public transport, and the property has wheelchair‑friendly access with slopes outside and wider door frames to make moving around easier. Although I don’t have an outdoor space at the property itself, we are very lucky to have a lovely green area just over the bridge — complete with open lawn, trees, and a park. This gives the children plenty of opportunities for fresh air, play, and exploration in a safe and natural environment. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All families are warmly welcomed to visit Haddenham’s Mini Explorers before deciding to join. This gives you the chance to meet me, see the home environment, and talk through any questions you may have. I also provide a welcome pack with the key information you’ll need. When a child starts, I encourage families to complete an All About Me sheet, share family photos, and bring along any comfort items that help their child feel settled — this is especially helpful for children with SEND. I offer flexible settling‑in visits so children can get to know me and the space at their own pace. If your child has SEND, we can take extra time, talk through their needs in detail, and plan together to make the transition as smooth and supportive as possible. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? At Haddenham’s Mini Explorers, I’m always looking for ways to grow and adapt so every child’s needs can be met. I know how important flexibility is, and I regularly review my practice to make sure children with SEND are fully supported. I continue to access training whenever needed, and I’m in the process of recruiting an assistant so I can offer even more individual support. I also keep up to date with the latest Local Authority guidance and use their website and resources to strengthen my SEND knowledge. My aim is to keep improving, keep learning, and keep creating a setting where every child can thrive in their own way.

description: Nudge Education exists for young people who are chronically disengaged or unable to access education. We work with those who are often the hardest to reach, including young people with SEND, Social, emotional and mental health (SEMH) needs, social care involvement, care experience, trauma histories, or significant anxiety around school. Our interventions are intensive and carefully tailored. We typically work one-to-one, sometimes two-to-one, in three-hour sessions at home, in the community, or alongside a school placement. Each young person is matched with a practitioner who is chosen for their skills, experience and ability to build a safe, consistent relationship. From there, we focus on two linked pathways: A Personal Pathway, which supports emotional regulation, confidence, routines, and coping strategies, underpinned by trauma-informed and restorative practice. An Academic Pathway, which starts with the young person’s interests and gradually reintroduces learning in a way that feels achievable, building back towards school, college, training, or other appropriate routes.

name: The M Word (Emotional Problem Solving) CIC
description: The M Word (Emotional Problem Solving) CIC is a not for profit Community Interest Company (CIC). We are the only CIC in the UK that offers a one stop shop that supports all ages with mental health around neuro-diverse presentations. We provide: - Mental Health Assessments - Initial screening to support as evidence (including ADOS-Stage 1) - EHCP and IEP support - Therapy - Coaching and training in Mental Health and Autism We support young people with anxiety, depression, self-harming, and suicidal ideation who are struggling to access CAMHS. Rather than lengthy waits, or being rejected, we can support by completing assessments and provide therapy following NICE guidelines. On average, 40% of our caseload at any one time are situationally mute. local_offer: In Larks nursery all children are valued and celebrated for their wonderful, unique talents. Following the early years curriculum, we plan enriching, fun activities, which help support and challenge your child at the stage of development they are at. All children are allocated a key worker when they join our setting to support good communication and happy transitions. We tailor settling in sessions where children may need more time to settle or a different approach. We work closely with parents early on, to support with any barrier to learning, planning in additional activities to meet that need and seeking additional expertise (SALT or OT for example) as required. When a SEN need is identified we will make reasonable adaptations to our setting inside and out. We support parents by signposting to additional services and services. If your child has a specific learning need or SEN diagnosis we encourage parents to speak to the SENCo so we can plan and adapt our setting to offer your child the best possible start to Larks. Please contact the school office if you would like to find out more about how we can meet your child's needs. https://www.leecommon.org/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We want all children with SEND and their families to feel supported and listened to. Staff will meet regularly with parents to review progress and plan new areas of development What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff have recently completed autism training and occupational therapy webinars on sensory processing needs. A number of staff have also completed their Level 1 Makaton training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents know their children best and we work in partnership to tailor learning and activities, regularly update and signpost to services. Parents receive a monthly SEND Newsletter with up to date information and links covering a vast range of needs. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? - Tapestry Observations - Termly review meetings - SEN parent consultation slots (longer time given to discuss your child's needs) How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting has a single step from the entrance at the front and the side entrance. Inside Larks and Wrens classroom we have access to two inside rooms all on the same level, the outside is accessible as a single step down. We have handrails positioned at key points in the school environment to support with stepping up/down to different levels. We also have handrails positioned in the pupil toilets to support with stability when toileting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact the school office to ask for a school visit with the SENCo or Headteacher. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Each cohort is unique and we are always learning new ways to better support SEND. Currently, we are supporting families with a range of SEN needs including: ASD, Speech, Language and Communication difficulties, sensory processing, global delay and other specific learning needs. We are supporting staff to access SALT and OT training through Bucks, focusing on these specific needs.

description: Based in Bicester, Tooting Tots provides fun, engaging ride-on toy party hire and play sessions for young children across Oxfordshire and beyond including Brackley, Kidlington, Buckingham, and Banbury. Whether you’re planning a birthday celebration or looking for an exciting toddler play session in a local hall, we offer a stress-free solution that children love and parents trust. Our ride-on toy parties are perfect for birthdays and special occasions, transforming homes and venues into exciting play spaces. We also run and support ride-on toy play sessions in village halls and community venues, giving toddlers and young children the chance to explore, ride, and play in a safe, structured environment. Choose from a wide range of high-quality ride-on toys, including popular construction vehicles, tractors, and mixed toy setups suitable for different age groups. Just let us know the ages and interests of the children, and we’ll create a setup that works perfectly for your party or play session. We take care of delivery, setup, and collection at your chosen venue, whether that’s a birthday party venue or a local hall in Bicester, Brackley, Kidlington, or Banbury. Optional activity add-ons are also available to keep little ones entertained for even longer. local_offer: As an OFSTED registered childminder I’m committed to providing quality flexible, nurturing childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work closely with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child. I have experience with Autism, ADHD, Stutters, Emotional Dysregulation and Sensory Processing Difficulties  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My aim is to provide a caring, nurturing environment where all children feel welcomed and supported. I will do my absolute best to meet the needs of all children so that they can take part in every aspect of my setting and reach their full potential. I will work closely with all involved professionals to help us to support the children. I will involve parents at every opportunity and work to support them as well as the children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Autism Awareness course - October 2021 ADHD Awareness course - October 2021 Understanding Autism course - October 2022 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work closely together in partnership with parents, on sharing information about their child’s learning, development, and progress via an online system and through physical learning journeys. I ask parents to share information about their child’s likes and dislikes, the activities which they find difficult and those which they enjoy the most on a regular basis to ensure I am providing up to date activities to fulfill each child’s needs/abilities. I aim to ensure that all activities can be extended to support children’s potential within my setting and share idea with parents to use with their children at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children on a regular basis and where there is a particular need, i support the implementation of an APDR plan ( Assess, Plan, Do, Review) plan, alongside Bucks Early Years Advisory team to provide small steps to work towards together. With parents’ permission i may involve other services if beneficial to the child. I will provide increased opportunities for communication for families of children with SEND and I’m completely flexible in how we communicate, for example, in person, on phone, email or electronic messages. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to most children and families. There is a step up to both my front door and back door, so provisions would need to be made to allow wheelchair assess if needed. The approach to my house from the road is level and assessable My back garden is assessable via a wide alley, through a large gate and is mainly lawn with a concrete path. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All families are welcome to visit, meet me and see my home before deciding they would like their child to attend. Im more than happy to answer any questions. Before children attend my setting, I ask families to complete an ‘All about Me’ form, provide starting development points and any special comforters (regardless of the age of the child). I encourage parents to have some ‘settling in visits’ with their child and I provide as many settling in sessions as the child needs As a long-established childminder, I have links with St Paul’s school and some local pre-schools who I can work closely with to support all children through any transitions. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I’m constantly aware of the need for flexibility within my setting to ensure all child’s needs are met. I will keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Bucks County Council and the Early Years SEND Advisors team. I will regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

local_offer: We support children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) through a fully inclusive approach, ensuring all children can access and engage in the curriculum. Our support includes: Individualised planning tailored to each child’s needs and stage of development Close partnership working with parents and carers Regular observation, assessment and targeted next steps A designated SENCo to oversee support and coordinate interventions Adapted environments and resources, including access to a sensory room Working in partnership with external professionals where required (e.g. Speech and Language, Health Visitors) We focus on early identification and early intervention to support each child’s progress, wellbeing and independence.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to achieve positive, meaningful outcomes for children with SEND by ensuring they are fully included, supported and able to reach their individual potential. For children, we focus on: Making good progress from their starting points across all areas of development Developing communication and language skills, including confidence in expressing needs Building independence and self-help skills Supporting emotional wellbeing, self-regulation and positive relationships Preparing children for the next stage of their education, including school readiness For families, we aim to: Provide clear communication, reassurance and ongoing support Work in close partnership to understand and meet each child’s needs Offer guidance and signposting to relevant services and professionals Ensure families feel confident, informed and involved in their child’s development Overall, our approach is centred on early identification, inclusive practice and tailored support to help every child thrive. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our staff have completed a range of SEND-specific and inclusive practice training, including: Promoting positive behaviour Equality and diversity SEND awareness Introduction to supporting children with SEND Vocabulary development and early language skills Understanding schemas in early years ADHD awareness Autism awareness Our SENCo holds a Level 3 SENCo qualification in Early Years, providing strong leadership in SEND provision, early identification and targeted support. Training and learning are regularly shared across the team to ensure a consistent, inclusive approach and high-quality support for all children. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work in close partnership with parents and carers, recognising that they know their child best. We involve parents by: Maintaining regular communication through daily feedback and updates Sharing observations, progress and next steps in their child’s development Holding meetings where needed to review progress and discuss support strategies Working collaboratively to create and review support plans for children with SEND Signposting to relevant services and professionals where appropriate Parents can get involved by: Sharing information about their child’s needs, interests and routines Attending meetings and contributing to support plans and reviews Continuing strategies at home to support consistency Communicating openly with staff and raising any questions or concerns We aim to build strong, supportive relationships so that parents feel informed, confident and actively involved in their child’s development. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share information about your child’s progress through regular communication and ongoing assessment. This includes daily feedback, informal conversations at drop-off and collection, and observations shared via our online learning journal, Tapestry. Through Tapestry, parents can view their child’s development, achievements and next steps, and contribute their own observations from home. We are also always available to arrange meetings to discuss your child’s progress in more detail. For children with SEND, we provide additional, more structured support and communication. This includes: Individual support plans (e.g. SEN Support Plans) with clear targets Regular review meetings with parents to monitor progress and next steps Closer tracking of development and targeted interventions Involvement of the SENCo to oversee support and ensure strategies are effective Working in partnership with external professionals where appropriate Our aim is to ensure you are fully informed, involved and supported, with clear and consistent communication about your child’s progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment is designed to be inclusive and accessible for all children, including those with SEND. Indoors, we provide a well-organised, calm and adaptable space with clear areas for learning and play. Resources are accessible at child level, and activities can be adapted to meet individual needs. We also have a dedicated sensory room to support children who may benefit from a quieter, more regulated environment. Outdoors, we offer a safe and secure space that promotes physical development and exploration. Activities can be adapted to ensure all children can participate, with staff providing additional support where needed. We continually review and adapt both our indoor and outdoor environments to meet the needs of the children attending, making reasonable adjustments where required to ensure full inclusion and access. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can access our setting by contacting us directly to arrange an initial conversation or showround. This gives us the opportunity to understand your child’s needs, routines and any existing support in place. For children with SEND, we take a personalised approach from the outset. We gather relevant information from parents, and with consent, liaise with any professionals already involved to ensure a smooth transition. We offer settling-in sessions to help children become familiar with the environment, staff and routines at their own pace. Once a place is agreed, we work in partnership with families to put appropriate support in place from the start, including any individual plans or adjustments required. local_offer: I am a registered childminder providing a safe, nurturing, and inclusive home environment for children aged up to 3 years. I support children with a range of special educational needs and disabilities. I offer personalised care and learning opportunities tailored to each child’s individual needs, interests, and developmental stage. This includes adapting activities, routines, and the environment to support communication, social interaction, and emotional wellbeing. I work closely with parents, carers, and other professionals to ensure consistent support and to help children make progress at their own pace. My aim is to build children’s confidence, independence, and readiness for the next stage of their learning.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My setting aims to support children with SEND to feel safe, valued, and included, enabling them to develop confidence and a sense of belonging. I support children to make progress in their individual areas of need, including communication, social skills, emotional regulation, and independence, through tailored activities and consistent routines. I aim to help children build positive relationships, develop self-esteem, and become more confident in exploring and learning at their own pace. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I aim to provide reassurance, regular communication, and a supportive partnership, helping parents and carers feel confident that their child’s needs are understood and met. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I share information with parents and carers through daily verbal feedback, as well as regular updates on their child’s activities, development, and wellbeing. I also provide observations and progress summaries, which show how children are developing in line with their individual needs. For children with SEND, I offer more frequent and detailed communication to ensure parents are fully informed and involved. This may include regular review meetings, individual support plans, and sharing strategies that can be used consistently at home and in my setting. I work in partnership with parents and, where appropriate, other professionals to monitor progress and adapt support as needed. My aim is to ensure clear, open communication so that every child receives consistent and effective support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is based in a ground floor flat with good access, making it easily accessible for children with a range of physical needs. The entrance is step-free and whole setting is step free. Indoors, I provide an environment where resources are easily accessible to children. I adapt the layout and activities to meet individual needs, including providing space for quiet time and supporting children who may need a lower-stimulation environment. Outdoors, I ensure children have regular access to outdoor play and activities, adapting these where needed to ensure all children can take part safely and comfortably. I am happy to discuss individual access needs with families and make reasonable adjustments where possible to ensure all children can fully participate in my setting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact me directly by whatsapp or through social media to discuss their childcare needs and arrange an initial conversation. I offer visits to my setting so that parents, carers, and children can meet me, see the environment, and ask any questions. I take time to gather detailed information about each child’s needs, routines, and preferences to ensure I can provide appropriate support. Where a child has SEND, I work closely with families from the start to understand their individual requirements and plan suitable support. I offer a settling-in period, tailored to the child, to help them feel comfortable and build confidence in the setting. My aim is to make the process as smooth and supportive as possible for both children and their families. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am committed to continually developing my knowledge and skills in supporting children with SEND. I plan to attend relevant training, such as SEND awareness and specific needs-based training, to improve my practice and better meet the needs of the children in my care. I will continue to review and adapt my environment, resources, and routines to ensure they are inclusive and accessible for all children. This includes developing my use of visual supports and strategies to support communication and emotional wellbeing. I also aim to build links with other professionals and local services to ensure I can access advice and provide the best possible support for children and their families. My goal is to provide a fully inclusive setting where all children feel supported to reach their individual potential.

name: Forest Play
description: Play your way through nature at Black Park! Join us at Black Pines Camp for Forest Play! Children can play and explore through activities like the mud kitchen, games, sand pit, bug hunting, water play, balancing, and more. Outdoor play is proven to support physical health, confidence, social skills, and early learning- giving little ones space to grow in nature. Forest Play is aimed at children aged 1 to 5 years (from when they can walk independently till they are in full-time education). Sessions take place on most Fridays during term time throughout the year and run from 1pm to 2pm. This is a shorter Forest School session with a focus purely on play. Unlike our other sessions, it doesn’t include a craft activity or refreshments. If you’d like to explore our other offerings, please visit our website. The sessions are child-led, with the children being encouraged to choose what they would like to do to help them build on their self-esteem, confidence, and independence. You can casually book the date(s) you'd like to attend, or block book the full half-term (6 sessions) to guarantee a place each week. We go ahead in all weathers - unless deemed unsafe - so please dress appropriately!
organisation: Buckinghamshire Country Parks Black Park has 530 acres of attractive woodland, grassland and heathland with a centre-piece lake. SSSI heath land and Local Nature Reserve. It has miles of surfaced tracks and woodland trails through the woods; tarmac path around the lake with seating every 100m; lakeside cafe and toilets; orienteering course and children's woodland play area. Picnicking is welcome but not fires or BBQs. Dogs are welcome but must be kept under control. Go Ape hire wire adventure course We host a range of events throughout the year for children and adults. This includes open air cinemas, trails, forest school and much more! For events please check out our Facebook page. Black Park has achieved the Green Flag Award which recognises quality green space in the UK. countryparks@buckinghamshire.gov.uk https://www.buckscc.gov.uk/services/culture-and-leisure/country-parks/black-park/

local_offer: This includes Social Emotional Mental Health (SEMH) needs, Emotional Based School Non Attendance (EBSNA), anxiety, disengagement, ADHD, and ASD. We specialise in working with students with Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, anxiety, and school avoidance, providing a calm, supportive environment where they can rebuild confidence and re-engage with learning.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Bloom Alternative Provision, we aim to achieve meaningful, long-term outcomes that support both the individual young person and their wider support network. For children and young people, we aim to: Rebuild confidence, self-esteem and a positive sense of identity Improve emotional regulation and overall mental wellbeing Increase engagement with education through a personalised and supportive approach Develop social and communication skills, including forming positive relationships with peers and adults Build independence and essential life skills to support preparation for adulthood Improve attendance, routine and readiness for learning Reduce anxiety associated with education and unfamiliar environments Support successful transition into further education, training, employment or reintegration into school where appropriate For families, we aim to: Provide reassurance that their child is in a safe, nurturing and understanding environment Reduce stress and anxiety linked to school non-attendance or disengagement Offer consistent communication and updates on progress Work in partnership to ensure a shared approach to supporting the young person Support families in understanding their child’s needs and strengths Our overall aim is to help each young person re-engage, achieve and develop the confidence and skills needed to move forward positively in education and life, while ensuring families feel supported and involved throughout the process. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff at Bloom Alternative Provision Will have completed, and continue to engage in, a range of SEND-focused training to ensure they can effectively support young people with a variety of needs, particularly Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) difficulties. Recent and ongoing training includes: Safeguarding and Child Protection (including KCSIE updates) Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) training Understanding and supporting SEMH needs Trauma-informed practice and attachment awareness Autism awareness (including strategies to support communication and sensory needs) ADHD awareness and support strategies De-escalation and behaviour support techniques Mental health awareness and supporting anxiety-based school avoidance (EBSNA) Inclusive teaching strategies and adaptive approaches for SEND learners Risk assessment and safe working practices We are committed to continuous professional development and regularly review training needs to ensure staff skills remain up to date and aligned with the needs of the young people attending Bloom. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Regular communication: We provide ongoing updates on your child’s progress, engagement and wellbeing through informal check-ins, emails or scheduled reviews Progress reviews: Opportunities to discuss development, set shared goals and review outcomes Open and responsive contact: Parents can contact us at any time to discuss concerns, updates or changes Collaborative planning: We involve parents in shaping support strategies to ensure consistency between home and provision Support and guidance: We share strategies and advice to help support your child’s needs at home How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Regular updates: Informal feedback via email, phone or messages to share how your child is engaging and progressing Progress reviews: Scheduled review meetings to discuss development, set targets and review outcomes Daily/weekly feedback (where appropriate): Brief summaries of attendance, participation and wellbeing Open communication: Parents can contact us at any time to discuss concerns or updates Collaborative discussions: Ongoing dialogue to adapt support strategies as needed Additional support for children with SEND: Individualised tracking: Progress is monitored against personalised outcomes, including EHCP targets where applicable More frequent communication: Increased contact where needed to provide reassurance and consistency Detailed feedback on wellbeing and engagement: Not just academic progress, but emotional regulation, social development and confidence Multi-agency working: Information may be shared (with consent) with schools, the Local Authority and other professionals to ensure a joined-up approach Flexible review arrangements: Meetings can be adapted in frequency and format to suit the needs of the child and family Our aim is to ensure you feel informed, involved and confident in the support your child is receiving, with a strong partnership between home and provision. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have access to 2 large indoor spaces, with a kitchen and a secure outdoor area to aid with Gardening and growing produce to eat. Indoor environment: A small, low-stimulation setting designed to reduce anxiety and sensory overwhelm Flexible use of space to allow for quiet areas, breakout spaces and small group work Clear routines and structured sessions to support predictability and emotional safety Adaptable seating and working arrangements to meet individual needs A focus on creating a safe, welcoming and nurturing atmosphere Outdoor environment: Access to outdoor activities and community-based learning, supporting wellbeing and engagement Opportunities for physical activity, fresh air and movement breaks, which are particularly beneficial for regulation and focus Planned outings to support independence, confidence and real-world skills Accessibility and inclusion: Activities are adapted to meet individual needs and abilities Staff provide personalised support and reasonable adjustments where required We work with families and professionals to understand and meet specific access needs Risk assessments are carried out to ensure all environments are safe and appropriate How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children and young people can access Bloom Alternative Provision through a referral process, ensuring that the support offered is appropriate for their individual needs. Referral routes: Schools or educational settings Local Authority (including SEND teams) EHCP consultations Other professionals (e.g. SENCOs, social workers) Parental enquiries are also welcomed Getting started: Initial enquiry: Contact us via email or phone to discuss your child’s needs and suitability Information gathering: We may request relevant information (e.g. EHCP, reports, or school background) Consultation/visit: An informal meeting or visit can be arranged to ensure Bloom is the right fit Placement agreement: Days, support levels and start date are agreed in partnership with parents and/or professionals Transition support: A gradual and supported start can be arranged to help the young person settle comfortably We aim to make the process simple, supportive and flexible, ensuring both the young person and their family feel confident and comfortable from the outset. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Gradually increasing capacity while maintaining small group sizes Expanding the curriculum to include more vocational, creative and life skills opportunities Enhancing outdoor and community-based learning experiences Continuing staff training in areas such as SEMH, autism, ADHD and trauma-informed practice Developing targeted interventions for emotional regulation, anxiety (including EBSA) and social skills Strengthening partnerships with schools, the Local Authority and external professionals Improving systems to track and evidence progress against individual and EHCP outcomes Our aim is to remain a responsive, high-quality provision that supports positive outcomes in education, wellbeing and future pathways.

local_offer: Hello I am Laura I am a Ofsted registered childminder who works closley with another childminder Hannah Cole and I am ommitted to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child. I have worked as a childminding for 4 and a half years and within this time I have worked with a mixed range of ages from newborn to 8years. During this time I have had the opportunity to gain a huge amount of professional development and also a wealth of knowledge of children. I ensure that no one is excluded and ensure that all activities can be adjusted to accommodate every unique child. I have also attended epi-pen training. I am a home from home setting and pride myself on offering a fun and happy environment for children to feel safe, secure and have the confidence to try new things all whilst making them feel like a part of the family. I attend local toddler groups and clubs. With the children and I have a large secure garden which is accessible all the time with a range of toys and activities suitable for all. I am paediatric first aid trained and I am more than happy to extend my training to include specific needs if needed  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools and the local day nursery to ensure effe We ctive transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. I also ask families to provide photos of the family for the children to share in the setting. I will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at our setting and in their home environment and ensure they have the opportunity to visit and settle in their new environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Epi-pen training - 2020 Paediatric first aid - 2020 Childcare level 3 As registered childminder’s I have a Key Contact (Sharon Bell) at Buckinghamshire County Council with the Early Years Team, and with parental permission we may contact them for further advice. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites…) are available for us to access. I welcome other professionals into the setting who may have involvement with a child and I am keen to access further training to support a child’s development e.g. speech and language (Speech Therapist). I am happy to attend Multi-Professionals Meetings if required How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis via the Family app where parents can access photos, daily diary & child development. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending my setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. I will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g. adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? By contacting myself Laura Read to arrange a visit at my setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and our Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

name: Holiday Activity Days for 8 to 12 Year Olds
description: Holiday Activity Days are for young people between the ages of 8 and 12 who are looking to explore some adventurous activities and get a day of fresh air (no screens!). Participate in four of our adventurous activities throughout the day, with a packed lunch included. Drop off from 8:30am ready to start activities at 9am, pick up at 5pm. The activities are varied day to day and are not confirmed until the morning of each day as we wait to see: 1. What the weather is doing, 2. If we have any repeat visitors, 3. The age range and abilities of those booked on. So best to pack them clothes for all eventualities. We run in all weathers so no matter what they will be outside and active all day! We have no indoor activities, no arts/crafts, no screens - just outdoor adventures, all day. The aim is (roughly!) one high rope activity, one land activity, and two water activities - however we cannot stress enough that this is varied for the benefit of the participants. A typical day might be Laser Tag, Crate Stacking, Rafting and Kayaking, as an example. Please note that February dates will not include any water activities as the river will not be safe or legally usable. Participants must be able to remove all jewellery and earrings in order to participate in roped activities. Earrings must be removed. They cannot be covered with plasters or tape. Please make sure your young person is covered in sun cream when you drop them off, and make sure you have reminded them to reapply during the day. Please note; Whilst we always try our best to organize it so that friends attending together are placed in the same groups, it is not possible to guarantee this. Pairs are often possible, but any request larger than 3 will always be split across groups. Booking together on one booking makes no difference to this and does not guarantee they will be placed together. Please be aware that these days may not be appropriate for all of those with additional needs, and young people who attend must be in mainstream school without additional support. If your young person has additional needs, please get in touch with us directly rather than booking online so that we can work together to find a day suitable for them. Most activities can be adapted for those with physical additional needs, but this does need to planned in advance so please get in touch before booking. Please visit our website for more information and to book.
organisation: Longridge Activity Centre Marlow Longridge is part of the Adventure Learning Charity family of activity villages. It is an outdoor activity centre open to all aged over 8 years, recognised by British Canoe Union, British Rowing and Royal Yacht Association and able to provide training from beginners to coaching qualifications in a range of BCU (canoeing and kayaking), sculling/rowing and RYA (sailing and power boating) recognised activities, in addition, offer climbing, ropes courses, laser maze, dragon boating, bell boating, rafting and have a playground and adventure course. Visitors come from schools, youth groups, families and businesses to the centre for the day, part of the day or stay on-site either camping or in our range of indoor accommodation. Accessibility The boating centre has a boat for disabled children, hoist and fully accessible changing and shower areas. bookings@adventurelearning.org.uk https://www.longridge.org.uk/

description: Minis Classes (ages 1 to 2 and a half years). This interactive class explores sounds and rhymes and develops and enhances speaking and listening skills, as well as activities to improve gross motor skills. The Minis classes are carefully designed in conjunction with a speech therapist, so each child develops an understanding of language and speech development. The class is a fun introduction to phonics through songs, role-play, and rhymes, all with the help of our cheeky friend, Robot Reg. Pre-School Classes (ages 2 and a half to 4 years) Each Pre-School class includes games and activities that teach sound recognition, segmenting, and oral blending - the necessary foundations for reading and writing. This high-energy class also includes activities to improve gross and fine motor skills, which support a child’s handwriting. Expect songs, dancing, disco lights, and, of course, our cheeky friend Robot Reg!

name: Lauren Fitzpatrick
description: I am an Ofsted registered childminder with 16 years of childcare experience and a Foundation Degree in Early Years. I provide a home-from-home environment for children aged 0 to 10 years. I live on the Manor Farm Estate in Hazlemere with my partner and 3 children (10, 6 and 3). We have a great sized open plan space for the children to play, a dedicated playroom and a practical garden. I was inspected by Ofsted in December 2021 and awarded Good in all areas. I am passionate about providing a safe, loving and fun environment for the children in my care. I work in partnership with parents to ensure I support the children’s learning and development to make sure they reach their full potential. We enjoy visiting the local parks, toddler and music groups and library as well as trips to Bekonscot, National Trust sites and the like. We are always busy crafting or baking during time spent at my house as well as enjoying imaginative play, construction, messy play and reading to name a few activities. I offer to drop offs and collections for the Manor Farms schools and pre school where my own children attend. If you have any questions please get in touch and I’ll be happy to help you.

description: I am an Ofsted registered childminder with 16 years of childcare experience and a Foundation Degree in Early Years. I provide a home-from-home environment for children aged 0 to 10 years. I live on the Manor Farm Estate in Hazlemere with my partner and 3 children (10, 6 and 3). We have a great sized open plan space for the children to play, a dedicated playroom and a practical garden. I was inspected by Ofsted in December 2021 and awarded Good in all areas. I am passionate about providing a safe, loving and fun environment for the children in my care. I work in partnership with parents to ensure I support the children’s learning and development to make sure they reach their full potential. We enjoy visiting the local parks, toddler and music groups and library as well as trips to Bekonscot, National Trust sites and the like. searchText:
name: Holiday Activity Days for 12 to 16 Year Olds
description: Based on our ever popular Holiday Activity Days, we have created a new program suitable for those aged 12 plus. A full day outdoors with no screens - outdoor activities only! Activity Days are for young people between the ages of 12 to 16 who are looking to explore some adventurous activities and get outside in the fresh air. Participate in four of our adventurous activities throughout the day, with a packed lunch included. Drop off from 8:30am ready to start activities at 9am, pick up at 5pm. Please make sure your young person is covered in sun cream when you drop them off, and make sure you have reminded them to reapply during the day. Participants must be able to remove all jewellery and earrings in order to participate in roped activities. Earrings must be removed. They cannot be covered with plasters or tape. The activities are varied day to day and are not confirmed until the morning of each day as we wait to see: 1. What the weather is doing, 2. If we have any repeat visitors, 3. The age range and abilities of those booked on. So best to pack them clothes for all eventualities. We run in all weathers so no matter what they will be outside and active all day! We have no indoor activities, no arts/crafts, no screens - just outdoor adventures, all day. The aim is (roughly!) one high rope activity, one land activity, and two water activities. Please be aware that these days may not be appropriate for all of those with additional needs, and young people who attend must be in mainstream school without additional support. If your young person has additional needs, please get in touch with us directly so that we can work together to find a day suitable for them. Most activities can be adapted for those with physical additional needs, but this does need to planned in advance so please get in touch before booking. Please visit our website to learn more and to book your place.

name: S4A Group Ltd Holiday Club at Stone
description: Our Holiday Club at Stone School is designed to keep children entertained, active, and social while giving you peace of mind. Who can attend? Your child does not need to attend this school to join – everyone is welcome! We welcome children aged 4 to 13 years (Reception to Year 8). What’s on? We have exciting Theme Days scheduled throughout the holiday. If your chosen day doesn’t have a theme, no worries! Every day is packed with sports, crafts, adventures, challenges, and more – ensuring your child has a fantastic experience. 📅 Theme Days: 🎯 Multi-Activity Day • ⚔️ Battle Quest Day • 🦎 Reptile Day The best part? All of this runs alongside our usual holiday club activities, so there’s always something to suit your child’s interests – whether they’re into sports, games, arts and crafts, or just want to try something new. After you book, you’ll receive: The school address and directions Drop off and collection procedure A checklist of what your child needs to bring Guidance on what to wear for different activities We know flexibility is important, so if plans change, we’ll happily accommodate adjustments. We’re here to make the holidays fun and stress-free for you and your child.
organisation: S4A Group Ltd, Sports Development and School PE Provision S4A offer holiday camps in Buckingham, Grendon Underwood and Patishall. Providing childcare during the school holidays. We offer activities such as football, basketball, science and seasonal craft activities, a full list of which can be found on the s4a website. S4A also work in 13 different schools in Buckingham and surrounding areas providing high-quality PE provision. We teach a huge variety of different Sports with our coaches' being highly qualified in a range of Sports. We tailor our lesson plans to suit each classes specific needs, giving children the opportunity to learn new skills and develop existing ones whilst always maintaining the importance of enjoyment and fun. As well as providing PE provision in these schools we also provide extended care across in the area. We run breakfast and after school clubs offering a range of activities tailored to meet the interests of the children in attendance, from science clubs to sports clubs S4A cater for all. Helping them develop physically, emotionally, socially and mentally in an environment that is fun and exciting. S4A Development is about helping children reaching ''their'' next level. Our Boys and Girls Development Centre sessions are on a Monday evening in Buckingham with our Juniors section on a Saturday morning in Buckingham and Gawcott. All sessions are professionally designed and delivered in line with the 'England DNA' to offer a player-focused approach and develop players on an individual basis while allowing them to progress at their own speed and in a low pressure but testing environment. All skills and attributes developed will be in the following areas: Technical/ Tactical/ Physical/ Psychological and Social. matt.ogle@s4asports.co.uk https://s4asports.co.uk

How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As before, talking, face to face, whatsapp are all channels of communication in order to share and update parents/carers on a childs progress. The frequency of these will be in accordance with the needs of the child and levels of communication required. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Unfortunately my home where I am based is not wheelchair accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can arrange a visit to come and meet me, and discuss individual needs to decide whether my setting is correct for their child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I will continue to provide an all inclusive, supportive and caring setting. All children will continue to be offered opportunities to develop, learn and grow with me.
