local_offer: I am a registered Tiney childminder dedicated to creating a safe, caring and inclusive environment where every child feels valued and supported. I work closely with parents/carers and, when needed, alongside other professionals to help each child reach their full potential. I understand that every child is different, so I adapt activities, routines and learning opportunities to meet individual needs and interests. I promote equality, inclusion and positive relationships, ensuring all children are able to participate and feel confident within my setting. Daily communication with families is very important to me, and I use the Tiney app to share updates, observations and children’s progress regularly.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My aim is for every child to feel happy, secure and included while making progress at their own pace. I support children through personalised care and learning opportunities that encourage development in all areas, including communication, confidence, independence and social skills. I believe strong partnerships with parents are essential, as working together helps provide consistent support for the child both at home and within my setting. I want families to feel listened to, involved and reassured that their child’s needs are understood and respected. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? At present, I have not completed specific SEND training; however, I am fully willing to attend relevant courses and training to better support the needs of any child in my care. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I value open communication and regularly discuss routines, interests, achievements and any concerns to ensure consistency and the best support for the child. Parents are welcome to share ideas, preferences and information about what works well for their child. Meetings or conversations can be arranged whenever needed, and I aim to build positive relationships where families feel comfortable and supported. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I work closely with parents to monitor and support each child’s learning and development. Observations, updates and daily information are shared regularly through the Tiney app, alongside ongoing conversations with families. If I have any concerns about a child’s development, these will always be discussed sensitively with parents so we can work together on appropriate next steps and support strategies. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is accessible to most children and parents, both indoors and outdoors. I am happy to discuss each child’s individual needs and make reasonable adjustments wherever possible, including adapting activities, routines or resources to support sensory /physical needs. I encourage parents to visit the setting, meet me and discuss their child’s requirements informally to ensure the environment is suitable and supportive for their child. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work closely with parents and other settings to support smooth transitions for children entering my care. I encourage families to attend settling-in sessions and complete the “All About Me” section on the Tiney app so I can better understand the child’s personality, routines and needs. I understand that every child settles differently, so settling-in arrangements are planned individually with families. Some children may need more time and reassurance than others, and I work flexibly to make the transition into my care as comfortable and positive as possible. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I regularly review my environment, activities, toys and resources to ensure they continue to meet the individual needs of all children in my care. I am committed to developing my knowledge and skills by attending relevant training and learning opportunities linked to SEND and inclusive practice. My goal is to continue improving my setting so that every child and family feels supported, respected and included.

description: If you’re experiencing isolation due to your mental health, come and join our Peer Support Bucks groups. Increase your social network and make new friends with adults of all ages who support each other by sharing experiences. Come and join us at our new and friendly social groups in High Wycombe. We meet every Tuesday and Thursday. Attendance is by referral or self-referral, please scan the QR code for access to the referral form or visit our website. For more information, please email Bucks Mind using the contact details below.
organisation: High Wycombe Library Please follow us on our Twitter account or visit our website to find out more. The library opened in June 2008 and is in the Eden Shopping Centre, close to the Bus station. It has three floors, sharing the building with the Registrars Office. local_offer: I am committed to providing an inclusive, nurturing environment where every child feels valued and supported. I work closely with parents and other professionals to meet children’s individual needs and adapt activities and routines to help all children thrive.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to provide a safe, nurturing and inclusive environment where all children feel valued, supported and able to thrive at their own pace. I work closely with parents and other professionals to understand each child’s individual needs and adapt activities, routines and communication styles to support their development, confidence and wellbeing. I strive to help children build positive relationships, independence and a love of learning through play-based experiences. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I am committed to ongoing professional development in SEND and inclusive practice. My current training includes safeguarding and EYFS training, and I continue to develop my knowledge to support children with additional needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I believe strong partnerships with parents are essential to supporting children’s wellbeing and development. I maintain open and regular communication through daily updates, observations and discussions about each child’s progress, interests and individual needs. Parents are encouraged to share information, ideas and goals so we can work together to provide consistent support and positive experiences for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I believe open and honest communication with parents is essential. I share regular updates through daily conversations, observations, photos and feedback about children’s learning, wellbeing and development. I work closely with parents to discuss progress, interests and any support strategies that may benefit their child. For children with SEND, I provide additional support tailored to their individual needs, which may include adapting activities and routines, using visual aids or alternative communication methods where appropriate, and working in partnership with parents and outside professionals to help children achieve positive outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? I aim to provide a welcoming, safe and inclusive home environment where children can access a variety of play and learning opportunities both indoors and outdoors. Risk assessments are carried out regularly and reasonable adjustments will be considered wherever possible to support children’s individual needs and accessibility requirements. The setting includes access to outdoor play opportunities and local community outings. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are welcome to contact me to discuss their child’s individual needs and arrange an initial meeting or settling-in visit. I work closely with parents from the beginning to understand routines, interests, strengths and any additional support required to help children feel safe, secure and settled within the setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am committed to continuing my professional development and expanding my knowledge of SEND and inclusive practice through ongoing training and research. I aim to continue developing resources, strategies and partnerships with families and professionals to ensure all children feel supported, included and able to thrive.

local_offer: At Lee Common C of E Infant School we are an inclusive school which values diversity and celebrates difference; this is at the heart of everything we do. Our school community works hard to ensure every child thrives, feels valued, and succeeds. We recognise the importance of challenge and understand how 'challenge' may differ for each child with their individual needs, including SEN and unique starting points. Working closely with parents, seeking advice from specialist teachers as required, we quickly identify any barriers to learning and personalise and adjust teaching to meet the needs of a child. We plan a varied, engaging, child-centered, and challenging curriculum for all children, meeting children at their starting points. We are supporting families with a range of range of SEN needs including: ASD, Speech, Language and Communication difficulties, global delay, and other specific learning needs. Please contact the school office if you would like to find out more about how we can meet your child's needs. https://www.leecommon.org/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We want all children with SEND and their families to feel supported and listened to. Staff will meet regularly with parents to review progress and plan new areas of development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff have recently completed autism training and occupational therapy webinars on sensory processing needs. A number of staff have also completed their Level 1 Makaton training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents know their children best and we work in partnership to tailor learning and activities, regularly updating and signposting to services. Parents receive a monthly SEND Newsletter with up to date information and links covering a vast range of needs. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? -Tapestry Observations (EYFS) - Termly review meetings - SEN parent consultation slots (longer time given to discuss your child's needs) How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting has a single step from the entrance at the front and the side entrance. Inside Larks and Wrens classroom we have access to two inside rooms all on the same level, the outside is accessible as a single step down. We have handrails positioned at key points in the school environment to support with stepping up/down to different levels. We also have handrails positioned in the pupil toilets to support with stability when toileting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Our admissions are handled by Buckinghamshire Council. Towards the end of the Summer Term, teachers review SEND support and conduct thorough transition meetings with the next teacher so that SEND provision can start at the very beginning of the next academic year. Any child can be brought onto the SEND register at any point in the school year, but this will follow a period of close observation and targeted intervention as part of our school SEND policy. Contact the school office to ask for a school visit with the SENCO or Headteacher. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Every child and cohort is unique and we are always learning new ways to better support SEND, working with parents. Currently, we are supporting families with a range of SEN needs including: ASD, Speech, Language and Communication difficulties, sensory processing, global delay and other specific learning needs. We are supporting staff to access SALT and OT training through Bucks, focusing on these specific needs.

local_offer: All children have the right to feel valued, be free from discrimination and to be treated as individuals. I ensure that each child is looked at on an individual basis and their specific needs realised. I have arrangements in place to support children with SEN or disabilities but am also always flexible in how I can adapt my setting to suit the specific needs of any child in my care as and when any new needs are identified.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to provide children with SEND with an enriching environment that they are able to thrive and develop to their full potential in a way that suits them and their individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have varied experience working with children that have had a range of SEND needs including deaf children, children with autism and a range of medical conditions. I have also completed the following training: Autism Awareness – completed 16/03/2026 Mental Health and Young People – completed on 18/02//2026 Equality and Diversity – completed 18/02/2026 Play Therapy (including ASD, ADHD and anxiety) – completed 04/12/2018 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I complete a daily diary for each child that gets sent home with them everyday. This includes information about nappies, sleep times etc. as well as a brief description of how the child has been, activities we have done and any concern I would like to raise with parents. Parents are also welcome to use this to pass any information onto me that they feel I should know. I am also in contact with parents via text, Whatsapp etc. and have in-depth handovers at the end of each day for feedback. Parents can always approach me in various ways with suggestions and concerns surrounding their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All families will receive a 2 Year Progress Check breaking down all areas of learning within the EYFS and information on how their child is progressing as well as any concerns regarding the child’s development and the plan in place to support the child. At the end of each term, each child will get an end of term report which includes photographs and a summary of what the child has achieved and what their next steps are. If I have any concerns regarding a child’s development, I will always raise this with parents asap. If a child has an EHCP, this is reviewed with parents approximately every 3-6 months as outlined in the CoP and I will organise a general review every 6 months for an early years child (annually for a child over 5). How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is fully accessible. It has plenty of parking right at the front door with lots of space. Everything that the children require is spread across the ground floor so no steps are required. I have large patio doors that open up into the garden, again with no steps. A ‘quiet area’ is always provided to the children. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I always encourage all families to come and meet me and see my home before securing a place with me so that each family can be sure that my setting is the right one for them and their child. I have a welcome pack that includes all of the information that parents need to know about my setting but am always happy to answer any questions or clarify any information with parents. An all about me document is sent to parents to fill in so that I can get to know their child more before they start with me and I can fully understand what their starting points are as well as techniques used at home to best support the child. I always encourage ‘settling-in’ sessions so that each child can gradually get to know me, the other children and my home before fully starting the placement. Transitions to any new provision including when a child starts school is thoughtful and tailored to the needs of the child at the time. I am happy to provide any information or supporting documents to any new settings that the child may move on to if it will benefit the child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am aways willing and open to complete any further training that may be relevant and beneficial to any child in my care including SEND. I will also stay up to date on any courses and training that I have already completed. I keep up to date with any SEND information via the Local Authority and my key contact. I regularly review my toys, equipment, activities and experiences that I am providing the children with to ensure that every child’s needs are being met.

description: Horizon Education Services provides specialist 1:1 tuition and Alternative Provision (AP) for children and young people with SEND, SEMH needs, and those out of education. We support learners with EHCPs, complex profiles, ASD, ADHD, Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA), Emotionally Based School Avoidance (EBSA), Social Emotion Mental Health needs (SEMH), medical needs, Children Missing Education (CME), and Looked After Children (LAC). Our qualified teachers and specialist SEND tutors provide structured learning, reintegration support, and outcome‑focused reporting aligned to EHCP targets and school expectations. Our safeguarding framework includes Enhanced DBS/PVG‑cleared staff, safer recruitment, risk assessments, professional indemnity and public liability insurance, and continuous monitoring of tutor suitability. What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We work closely with families and professionals to ensure consistent, high‑quality support that reduces barriers to learning and promotes long‑term success. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our staff complete ongoing training in safeguarding, Prevent/WRAP, trauma‑informed practice, Autism (ASD), ADHD, PDA, SEMH, EBSA, behaviour regulation, de‑escalation, mental‑health awareness, and working with LAC/CME learners. We are also strengthening our training programme to include advanced Autism practice, trauma‑informed approaches, and assistive technology for learners with complex needs.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder who is passionate about providing caring, flexible, and high-quality childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work closely with parents, carers, and other professionals to help ensure every child is supported to achieve the very best outcomes.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I believe every child is unique, and I aim to support each one through tailored activities and individual plans so they can make progress in all areas of their development. I work flexibly to help children feel included in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I like to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with me, as I really value their input, advice, and opinions. I discuss routines with parents to help provide consistency for each child throughout the day. I also share information about children’s likes and dislikes, and use this to extend activities so they can enjoy themselves and continue learning while at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working closely with parents, I share regular updates about their child’s learning, development, and progress. All children at the setting are observed and monitored to help support their learning and development. If I have any concerns about a child’s development, I will talk them through with parents and work together on an action plan to support their child. I will also discuss whether any further support may be helpful, or whether parents would like other services to be involved How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children, both indoors and outdoors. I am always happy to talk about a child’s individual needs and will do my best to make any suitable adjustments where possible, such as supporting sensory needs or accommodating dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work closely with other childminders to help make transitions as smooth and positive as possible for all children. I encourage families to have a settling-in period and to complete an “All About Me” booklet together. We then focus on each child’s starting points, which helps shape their learning journey in the setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to make sure they continue to meet the needs of each individual child and family. I am also very happy to undertake any further training that will help me support the children I care for.

name: Level 2 SAFE Parenting Programme
description: What is the SAFE Parenting Programme? Safe Parenting is a therapeutic approach which stands for Secure Attachment Founded on Empathy. It is a therapeutic parenting programme devised by The Centre of Therapeutic Parenting Studies at Inspire Training Group, part of The Centre of Excellence in Child Trauma. SAfE Parenting is based on the parenting model of Therapeutic Parenting devised by Sarah Naish (2017) which support parents in their ability to look at the root cause of their child’s behaviour and respond consciously rather than emotionally. In this Programme you will: Gain further knowledge on the main principles of SAfE Parenting. Provide parents with underpinning knowledge of Therapeutic Parenting strategies Learn how to build the foundations of a trusting relationship. Understand how to meet the needs of the growing and developing child. Be able to create a SAfE Parenting Environment. Look deeper into safe parenting – Look after ourselves. Who is the SAfE Parenting Programme for? The SAfE Parenting Programme is aimed at Parents looking after children that have suffered early like trauma through pre or postnatal stress, neglect, domestic violence, and, or abuse. Programme Benefits: Not only will parents be able to learn and put into practice Therapeutic Parenting strategies, which will help them to develop a trusting relationship with their child, they will also gain certification of our CACHE Accredited Customised Qualification in SAfE Parenting. Programme Length: Online: Approximately 5 guided learning hours per unit a total of 4 units A total of 20 hours of study. Face to Face: 20 hours which can be delivered over 10 weeks in 2-hour sessions. Alternatively, it can be delivered over 2 to 4 training days (the equivalent of 20 hours).

Browsing the directory and messaging tutors is free for both parties. name: Level 3 Diploma in Therapeutic Parenting
description: The Level 3 Advance Therapeutic Parenting Programme is an unregulated qualification which is accredited with the Awarding Body NCFE. It is aimed at parents who are caring for children who have experienced developmental trauma. It is also aimed at supporting professionals who are working with families in order to support them and can be used as evidence for Continual Professional Development (CPD). This course is delivered online, with the option of full-time (1 year) or part-time (2 years) study. To achieve The Level 3 Advance Therapeutic Parenting Programme, learners will complete 400 guided learning hours through our online learning platform, which comprises of video-based tuition and knowledge check throughout, to enable the learner to complete the end of unit assessments. Learners will be provided with tutor support as well as peer supported learning through a forum where there is the opportunity to access online training and online assessment workshops to support their learning. A handbook, including all relevant information, will also be provided at the start of the course. local_offer: I provide an inclusive, nurturing and supportive environment where every child is encouraged to develop at their own pace. I adapt activities, routines, communication and the learning environment to meet each child’s individual needs, working closely with parents/carers and, where appropriate, other professionals. I observe children’s development, identify any areas where additional support may be needed and use appropriate strategies to help children access and participate fully in the setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My aim is for every child with SEND to feel safe, valued, included and supported to reach their individual potential. I aim to provide opportunities for children to develop their confidence, independence, communication, social skills and learning at their own pace, with appropriate adaptations and support where needed. I also aim to work closely with parents and carers so that families feel listened to, supported and involved in decisions about their child’s care, learning and development. Where appropriate, I will work in partnership with other professionals to ensure that children receive consistent and effective support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed training as part of my early years professional development, including training relating to SEND and inclusive practice. I hold a Level 6 Early Years qualification and have experience supporting children with a range of individual needs within early years settings. I continue to keep my knowledge up to date and will undertake further SEND-specific training where appropriate to meet the needs of children attending my setting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Yes. I believe that parents and carers know their child best, so I work closely with families to ensure they are involved in all aspects of their child’s care, learning and development. I encourage open and regular communication through daily discussions, progress updates and planned meetings where needed. Parents and carers are encouraged to share information about their child’s strengths, interests, needs and any strategies that work well at home. They can contribute to observations, planning and reviews of their child’s individual support, and I will work with them to agree appropriate next steps. Where other professionals are involved, I will support parents in working collaboratively with them, with appropriate consent. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I will share information about your child’s progress through regular conversations, daily handovers, observations and updates on their learning and development. Parents and carers will be kept informed about their child’s strengths, interests, achievements and any areas where they may need further support. For children with SEND, I will provide more individualised communication and regular opportunities to discuss their progress and support needs. I will work closely with parents to identify appropriate strategies, review what is working well and agree next steps. Where appropriate, I will also work with the child’s SENCO, Buckinghamshire SEND services and other professionals involved in their care, with parental consent, to ensure information is shared appropriately and support is consistent. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is a welcoming and inclusive home environment, and I will make reasonable adjustments to support children with SEND to access all areas as independently as possible. The main access to the garden through the back door has a step down; however, alternative access can be provided via the front of the property and around to the upper part of the garden if required. I will discuss each child’s individual accessibility needs with their parents/carers and make appropriate adaptations wherever possible. I will also consider the accessibility of activities, resources, furniture and the learning environment to ensure that children can participate fully. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact me directly to enquire about a place and discuss their child’s individual needs, strengths and any additional support they may require. I will arrange an initial meeting or visit so that parents/carers can view the setting, ask questions and discuss how I can support their child. Before a child starts, I will work in partnership with the family and, where appropriate, other professionals involved with the child to understand their needs and agree any reasonable adjustments or support required. This helps to ensure that the child has a positive and settled start at the setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As a new setting, I am committed to continually developing my SEND provision to ensure that I can meet the individual needs of all children. I plan to undertake further SEND-specific training and continue to develop my knowledge of inclusive practice, communication needs and different learning and developmental needs. I will regularly review my provision and resources and make reasonable adjustments where needed. I will also seek advice and guidance from parents, Buckinghamshire SEND services and other relevant professionals to ensure that my practice continues to develop and that children with SEND are fully included and supported.

description: Book a free tactile tour or a hands-on workshop designed for adults with additional needs. Get up close to real specimens, enjoy crafts, or take an audio-described highlights tour. Visiting with an adult group who have additional needs? We provide free handling workshops and tactile tours for groups of 5 to 30 people. Activities may be split into two sessions, each session lasting 30 to 60 minutes. We usually offer them in the afternoon during term-time weekdays, but they shouldn’t start later than 4pm. Sessions might occasionally be scheduled in the morning. Tactile Tour Join us for a special, audio-described highlights tour of our best specimens, specially created for blind and partially sighted adults. From bizarre cassowaries to a charismatic polar bear and a larger-than-life giant ground sloth, we have plenty of specimens for you to get to know. Plus, you’ll get to touch some of our handling specimens to bring the tour to life. SENDsational Adults: Choose between the following two themes and get hands-on with real specimens: Discover the wildlife that lives in your local area, including foxes, hedgehogs, and invertebrates, and craft a stag beetle to take away with you Let our Oceans Workshop transport you to the seaside with shells, turtles, and animals that you may not have seen before You must book at least two weeks in advance. Speak to our team to discuss options for dates, times, and logistics for your group. These activities are subject to staff availability.

local_offer: Emberfield Growth is designed around neurodivergent nervous systems. A regulation-first, relationship-led approach ensures every young person is known deeply and supported individually within a maximum group of four learners.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim for every young person to re-engage with learning at their own pace, build emotional regulation and confidence, work toward recognised qualifications through the Cambridge IGCSE pathway, and develop practical life skills and independence. Families gain a transparent, professionally governed provision with termly Impact Reports mapped to Section F of their child's EHCP. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? DSL Level 3 Safeguarding (May 2026), Prevent Awareness and PMAP (August 2025), Emergency First Aid at Work L3 (December 2025), TQUK Level 2 Certificate in Understanding Specific Learning Difficulties, CACHE Level 2 in Understanding Autism, Makaton Certified Levels 1 to 4, Foundation Certificate in Counselling and Psychotherapy (The Minster Centre). The Founder has extensive experience in Learning Support and brings lived experience as the parent of neurodivergent children. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are central to the Emberfield model. I hold an initial Discovery Call before any placement is confirmed, share termly Impact Reports, and maintain an open relationship throughout. The Guardians panel includes an Independent Mediator available to parents if needed. Parents can get in touch by visiting our website emberfieldgrowth.com. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every learner has a Student Compass- a personalised digital portfolio tracking progress across academics, life skills, social and emotional development, and critical thinking. Termly Impact Reports are mapped directly to Section F EHCP outcomes, providing a professional evidence base for annual reviews. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Emberfield operates from a home-based setting with a dedicated indoor learning space, enclosed garden, and woodland. The environment is low-arousal, sensory-considered, and phone-free. The small group size and consistent adult presence ensure the space remains calm and predictable. The setting is not currently wheelchair accessible. I discuss individual access, mobility, and sensory needs with every family at induction and adapt the environment wherever possible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can make initial contact via emberfieldgrowth.com or email fenella@emberfieldgrowth.com. I begin with a Discovery Call to explore fit and suitability. Local Authority referrals and EOTAS commissioning enquiries are welcome. Opening September 2026. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am committed to continuous professional development and plan to expand training in outdoor learning facilitation and trauma-informed practice. My long-term vision is to develop a network of small, nature-based alternative provision settings rooted in the same philosophy, offering the Emberfield model to more neurodivergent young people across the region.

local_offer: Bridge Online School, part of Cambridge Online Education, provides flexible live online learning for children and young people within the UK and internationally. We support students with a wide range of educational needs and circumstances, including SEND, SEMH, emotionally based school avoidance (EBSA), medical needs, alternative provision requirements, and reintegration support. Our qualified teachers deliver personalised learning through flexible timetables, small group teaching and individual pathways designed to help students engage with education in a safe and supportive online environment. https://bridgeonlineschool.com What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Bridge Online School aims to help children and young people with SEND access education in a flexible, supportive and inclusive way that meets their individual needs. Our provision aims to improve educational engagement, emotional wellbeing, confidence and academic progress for students who may be struggling to access mainstream education full time due to SEND, SEMH, anxiety, emotionally based school avoidance (EBSA), medical needs or other barriers to learning. We work collaboratively with families, schools, local authorities and professionals to provide personalised learning pathways, flexible timetables and supportive online education that helps children and young people re-engage with learning, build independence and achieve positive long-term outcomes. We also aim to support smoother transitions into further education, employment and adulthood by helping students develop confidence, resilience and positive learning experiences in a safe and nurturing environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Bridge Online School staff have experience supporting children and young people with a range of SEND, SEMH and alternative provision needs. Staff undertake ongoing professional development and training relating to safeguarding, SEND support, emotional wellbeing, inclusive teaching approaches and supporting students with additional needs including autism, ADHD, anxiety, and emotionally based school avoidance (EBSA). How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We believe strong partnership working with parents and carers is essential in supporting positive outcomes for children and young people. We work collaboratively with families through regular communication, reviews and ongoing discussions regarding student wellbeing, engagement and educational progress. Parents and carers can contact the school directly to discuss support needs, provision pathways and ongoing involvement in planning and decision-making processes. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Bridge Online School maintains regular communication with parents, carers, schools and professionals regarding student progress, engagement and wellbeing. Updates may include progress reviews, feedback from teachers and discussions around personalised learning targets and support strategies. For children and young people with SEND, support is tailored to individual needs and may include flexible timetables, personalised learning pathways, smaller group teaching, emotional wellbeing support and adjustments to help students access education successfully in a supportive online environment. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? ONLINE How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? An initial consultation helps identify the most appropriate educational pathway and support package for each child or young person. We work collaboratively with families and professionals to ensure support is tailored to individual educational, emotional and wellbeing needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Bridge Online School is committed to continuing to develop and strengthen its SEND and alternative provision support through ongoing staff development, partnership working and flexible learning approaches. We aim to continue expanding personalised learning opportunities, emotional wellbeing support and flexible educational pathways to help more children and young people successfully access education and achieve positive long-term outcomes. We are also continuing to build relationships with schools, local authorities and SEND professionals to support wider access to inclusive online education and alternative provision services.

name: 1 Day Screen Acting Workshop
description: Wannabe actors (17 years plus) can prepare for the limelight with our screen acting workshop at the world famous Pinewood Studios. Targeting those with minimal or no experience, the workshop offers a practical syllabus setting a strong and broad base for participants to build on. Covering a variety of screen scripts, students will be taught etiquette on the set, how warm up both body and voice, and how to bring scripts to life on screen. Budding actors will shoot a scene with an experienced Director who will share knowledge on shot sizes, continuity and eye lines, before providing an insight in to the audition process and the business of being a screen actor. This is ideal for those looking to take their first step into acting on camera and experience their first course with Actors Studio. 1 Day Screen Acting Workshop at £95.00. Earlybird booking discounts may apply. Location: Pinewood Studios. Time: 10 am to 5 pm. Young Actors’ Weekend Crash Course Theatre, TV and Film Training for Young Actors Acting classes designed for Children/Teenagers who show a passion for acting and wish to enhance their skills in acting for screen and stage. Actors Studio offers weekend crash courses in Theatre, Television and Film for young actors aged 7 to 17 years at the world-renowned Pinewood Studios. Children will work alongside experienced actor and acting coach Paul Lockwood to learn the difference between stage and screen performances while developing a high set of skills to achieve a truthful performance. Lights Camera Action widens a young actors skill-set with sessions that include, acting techniques, devising short scenes, script work, audition techniques, screen and stage acting, listening and reacting skills. Our young actors are encouraged to work collaboratively, learning to give and accept constructive criticism and feedback to make them better actors. Our course also inspires confidence, social interaction, creativity and most of all fun in a secure and supportive environment. Children will film and receive an edited digital version of their scene. Special sessions in Audition Technique and Casting Advice will be offered where appropriate. Classes are held in our studio at Pinewood Studios over weekends. info@actorsstudio.co.uk

name: Shannon Martin
description: Childminder with tiney Childminding Agency under reference TY0626029. I’m a childminder based in Chalfont St Peter offering a stimulating, nurturing and safe environment, where babies and children feel safe, seen, and excited to learn. I have always been passionate about early years and - after having 2 little ones of my own - decided to make my passion a career. I understand how important flexible childcare is to working families, having tried to juggle it myself for years, so I am open to discussing ad-hoc childcare (including meeting different shift workers’ needs). In my setting, I spend time teaching tolerance, respect and kindness: foundations of healthy emotional connections later in life. It is fundamental that children are nurtured, they feel respected, and they are given the confidence to try things even if they fail. My mantra is ‘try and try again ’, and I use both yoga and meditation to encourage children to be connected to their bodies and emotions. I am outdoors with the children every day, whether that is for an adventure at Black Park or Forest School, the farm or a nature trail. I have my own little vegetable patch and adore gardening, so your little ones will be green-thumbs before you know it! Our outings also include trips to the local greengrocer to purchase fresh produce for cookery as a group. All meals are home-cooked and upf-free; the children are involved in food preparation as much as possible, and we bake our snacks from scratch (all sugar-free, as per nutrition guidelines). We love reading at Hill Farm! Every day will be a new literary adventure, and we use stories to inform play, create songs and develop early literacy. We also go to the library every week for bounce and rhyme sessions. All activities are informed and guided by the EYFS, and you will receive regular updates on your child’s progress throughout the day. You will also receive formal reports at key points and be invited to parents’ evening. I am also available for wraparound care, transfer test tutoring, GCSE tutoring and homeschooling support for children of school age. Families choose me for my love of reading, Forest School sessions, my home-cooked meals and my warm and open communication. Message me to arrange a visit - I’d love to show you around.

name: Shannon Martin
description: Childminder with tiney Childminding Agency under reference TY0626029. I’m a childminder based in Chalfont St Peter offering a stimulating, nurturing and safe environment, where babies and children feel safe, seen, and excited to learn. I have always been passionate about early years and - after having 2 little ones of my own - decided to make my passion a career. I understand how important flexible childcare is to working families, having tried to juggle it myself for years, so I am open to discussing ad-hoc childcare (including meeting different shift workers’ needs). In my setting, I spend time teaching tolerance, respect and kindness: foundations of healthy emotional connections later in life. It is fundamental that children are nurtured, they feel respected, and they are given the confidence to try things even if they fail. My mantra is ‘try and try again ’, and I use both yoga and meditation to encourage children to be connected to their bodies and emotions. I am outdoors with the children every day, whether that is for an adventure at Black Park or Forest School, the farm or a nature trail. I have my own little vegetable patch and adore gardening, so your little ones will be green-thumbs before you know it! Our outings also include trips to the local greengrocer to purchase fresh produce for cookery as a group. All meals are home-cooked and upf-free; the children are involved in food preparation as much as possible, and we bake our snacks from scratch (all sugar-free, as per nutrition guidelines). We love reading at Hill Farm! Every day will be a new literary adventure, and we use stories to inform play, create songs and develop early literacy. We also go to the library every week for bounce and rhyme sessions. All activities are informed and guided by the EYFS, and you will receive regular updates on your child’s progress throughout the day. You will also receive formal reports at key points and be invited to parents’ evening. I am also available for wraparound care, transfer test tutoring, GCSE tutoring and homeschooling support for children of school age. Families choose me for my love of reading, Forest School sessions, my home-cooked meals and my warm and open communication. Message me to arrange a visit - I’d love to show you around.

name: Babies1st - Circle of Security
description: Babies 1st is a non-profit organisation dedicated to supporting families of all shapes and sizes to build strong, secure relationships with their babies and children. This September, we are pleased to offer a seven-week Circle of Security Parenting course, delivered online through Zoom. The Circle of Security programme helps parents and caregivers better understand their child's emotional needs and strengthen their relationship through increased connection, confidence, and understanding. At its core is the idea that children thrive when they feel secure enough to explore the world, while knowing they can return to a trusted adult for comfort and support when needed. During the course, we will explore topics including: - Reading Cues - Learn to look beyond behaviour and recognise the emotional needs your child may be communicating. - Being With - Discover how to support your child through difficult feelings and big emotions in a calm and responsive way. - Understanding Parental Triggers - Reflect on how your own experiences and attachment patterns may influence your parenting responses. - Rupture and Repair - Explore how repairing everyday misunderstandings and mistakes can strengthen your relationship and build resilience in your child. Whether you are a new parent or have years of parenting experience, Circle of Security offers valuable insights and practical tools to help you nurture a secure and positive relationship with your child. To register your interest, please complete the Expression of Interest form on the training page on our website. Places are limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

Sessions are tailored to the individual learner and can support home-educated students, Education Other Than At School (EOTAS) learners and those finding mainstream education challenging.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? - Building confidence and resilience in learning. - Helping students re-engage with learning and education when anxiety, overwhelm or previous experiences have created barriers. - Developing greater awareness of how they learn, what supports them, and strategies that help them succeed. - Increasing independence so students can tackle learning and problem-solving with greater confidence. - Reducing anxiety and overwhelm around maths and learning. - Supporting positive engagement with education in a way that feels manageable and sustainable. - Improving maths knowledge, skills and understanding through personalised support tailored to the individual learner. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I believe that parents and carers play an important role in supporting a student's progress. Support begins with an initial meeting to understand the student's strengths, challenges, educational background and support needs. Ongoing communication is encouraged so that parents and carers can discuss progress, ask questions, share concerns and celebrate successes. I aim to create a supportive and collaborative environment where parents feel comfortable discussing what is working well, areas of difficulty and any changes in a student's circumstances. Communication can take place through a range of methods, including email, telephone, online meetings and written feedback, depending on the needs and preferences of the family. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Information about a student's progress can be shared through a range of communication methods, including email, telephone, text message, WhatsApp, online meetings and written feedback, depending on the needs and preferences of the family. Progress updates may include areas of strength, topics covered, improvements in confidence, engagement, independence, learning strategies and mathematical understanding, as well as any areas where additional support may be beneficial. For students with SEND, communication can also include information about engagement, emotional wellbeing, learning approaches that are proving effective, and any adjustments that may help support progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Its online. Therefore there is no out door work. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Through an initial consultation to ensure that we are the right fit. This can be arrange by contacting me to arrange a suitable time and day. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Providing pre-recorded lessons and accompying materials

local_offer: As a previous primary school teacher of 13 years, I have taught children with various SEND. As a result I have attended appropriate training each year in preparation of having that child in my class - training has included for pupils who have/are ADHD, Asperger’s, Selective Mute and Physical Disability including Muscular Dystrophy. At Lisa’s Little Learners I feel it is of most importance to build a good understanding of the child’s needs by communicating in depth with the parents and then building that trusting, understanding relationship with the child. I work with the child to set realistic, fair boundaries in terms of behaviour, independence and space, as well as ensuring the child feels happy, confident and has good self-esteem. Other childmindees are made aware to prevent any issues of conflict and unfair reasoning to occur.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To ensure all children are treated the same and at no time will any favouritism be shown. Every child is welcomed and is respected with their individual needs being recognised and valued, whatever their class, disability, colour, culture, religion and belief. I aim to encourage the children to learn more about their own culture and to find out about the cultures and religions of other children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have lots of varied experience of working with children with SEND and have received training for ADHD, Autism, Speech and Language. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work closely with parents who have children with SEND, arranging pre-settling in conversations, settling in visits and meetups with the parent and child. I ask parents to share their knowledge and experiences, providing me with support ideas and techniques. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Any child between birth and 4 years will be assessed against the Early Years Foundation Stage, where activities are planned, assessed and recorded using the Tapestry online tool. Children with SEND are assessed in the same way. For school-aged children, weekly communication is held with parents about interaction with other children and their behaviour - daily updates are shared if there are any problems or issues. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? A pavement runs alongside the front of my house, which is on a side road. There is plenty of space to gather out front and parking in a designated space and on the roadside. My house is a 3 story, so the entire ground floor is open to any children in my care. This allows free flow activity space between the playroom, hallway, kitchen and rear garden. There is a small step from the kitchen out into the garden. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please feel free to message or email me to arrange a visit. During a setting visit, any/all SEND discussions and concerns can be shared, discussed and addressed. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To update my knowledge through new training, and to work with any childminders who have experience or children at their setting with SEND - to share and learn provisions and techniques.

description: SkillSum Bucks Support provides free advice, advocacy, and practical help for asylum seekers and post-decision refugees across Buckinghamshire. We help people navigate complex systems and access the support they need to settle safely and build stable lives in their communities. We support a wide range of needs including housing and homelessness, benefits, healthcare access, school admissions, immigration signposting, employment and training, digital support, and general wellbeing. We work closely with local authorities, charities, and community organisations to connect people to the right services quickly and effectively. Our approach is person-centred, aiming to reduce barriers, prevent people from being passed between services, and ensure clear, practical guidance tailored to each individual. local_offer: We are committed to the inclusion of all children at Hawkswood Children's Nursery. We ensure all children are cared for and educated to develop to their full potential alongside their peers through positive experiences. We enable them to share opportunities and experiences and develop and learn from each other. We provide a positive and welcoming environment where children are supported according to their individual needs and we work hard to ensure no child is discriminated against or put at a disadvantage as a consequence of their needs. Each child’s needs are unique and we do not attempt to categorise children. We are committed to working in partnership with parents in order to meet each child’s individual needs and develop to their full potential. We are committed to working with any child who has a special educational need and/or disability and making reasonable adjustments to enable every child to make full use of the nursery’s facilities. All children have a right to a broad and well-balanced early learning environment.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? • Designate a named member of staff to be the SENCo and share their name and role with all staff and parents • Have high aspirations for all children and support them to achieve their full potential • Develop respectful partnerships with parents and families • Undertake formal Progress Checks and assessments of all children in accordance with the SEND Code of Practice January and statutory framework for the EYFS • Provide a statement showing how we provide for children with special educational needs and/or disabilities and share this with staff, parents and other professionals • Ensure that the provision for children with SEN and/or disabilities is the responsibility of all members of staff in the nursery through training and professional discussions • Set out in our inclusive admissions practice on how we meet equality of access and opportunity • Make reasonable adjustments to our physical environment to ensure it is, as far as possible suitable for children and adults with disabilities using the facilities • Provide a broad, balanced, aspirational early learning environment for all children with SEN and/or disabilities and differentiated activities to meet all individual needs and abilities • Liaise with other professionals involved with children with special educational needs and/or disabilities and their families, including transition arrangements to other settings and schools (see our Transitions policy) • Use the graduated approach response system to assess, plan, do and review to ensure early identification of any SEND • Ensure that children with special educational needs and/or disabilities and their parents are consulted at all stages of the graduated response, taking into account their levels of ability • Review children’s progress and support plans every 4 weeks and work with parents to agree on further support plans • Provide privacy of children with special educational needs and/or disabilities when intimate care is being provided • Raise awareness of any specialism the setting has to offer, e.g. Makaton trained staff • Ensure the effectiveness of our SEN and disability provision by collecting information from a range of sources, e.g. additional support reviews, Education, Health and Care (EHC) plans, staff and management meetings, parental and external agencies’ views, inspections and complaints. This information is collated, evaluated and reviewed annually • Provide a complaints procedure and make available to all parents in a format that meets their needs, e.g. Braille, audio, large print, additional languages • Monitor and review our policy and procedures annually What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our nursery Special Education Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENCo) is Maream. Maream holds a Diploma in Special Educational Needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? • Ensure parents are involved at all stages of the assessment, planning, provision and review of their child's care and education and include the thoughts and feelings voiced by the child, where possible • Signpost parents and families to our Local Offer in order to access local support and services How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Hawkswood Nursery will share information about your child’s progress through the Famly app, including details of their daily routine and observations. This information will be sent directly to parents to ensure they are kept informed and involved in their child’s learning and development. For children with SEND, we will follow the APDR (Assess, Plan, Do, Review) process in partnership with the family. Reviews will take place every four weeks to ensure a strong and supportive partnership is maintained, enabling us to work together to provide the best possible start for each child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Hawkswood Nursery provides a highly accessible environment, with easy access between the indoor and outdoor areas. The nursery is equipped with both ramps and steps to ensure safe and convenient access for children, families, and visitors. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children and young people with SEND and their families can start to use Hawkswood Nursery by contacting the nursery directly to arrange an initial visit and discuss their child’s individual needs. During this process, families will have the opportunity to meet staff, view the nursery environment, and share any relevant information about their child’s development, routines, strengths, and areas where additional support may be required. We work closely with families from the outset to ensure a smooth transition into the nursery. Where appropriate, we will gather information from parents, carers, health professionals, and other agencies involved with the child to help us plan suitable support and provision. Once a child starts at Hawkswood Nursery, we will continue to work in partnership with the family through regular communication, observations, and reviews. For children with SEND, we will follow the APDR (Assess, Plan, Do, Review) process, with reviews taking place every four weeks to ensure the child receives the appropriate support and the best possible start to their early years education. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Hawkswood Nursery is committed to continually developing and improving our SEND provision to ensure that all children receive high-quality, inclusive support that meets their individual needs. Through these developments, Hawkswood Nursery aims to provide a nurturing, inclusive environment where every child feels valued, supported, and able to thrive.

description: Our Wild Wood Adventure Playground is currently closed whilst we complete the exciting transformation. organisation: Waddesdon Manor | National Trust Surrounded by views of Oxfordshire, the Chilterns Hills, the Vale of Aylesbury and just a train ride away from London, Waddesdon Manor, is an ideal place for relaxing with family and friends. Explore this French Renaissance-style château built by Baron Ferdinand de Rothschild in 1874 to entertain the fashionable world and to house his collection of fine art. We're continuing the tradition today of entertainment and hospitality with events celebrating food and wine, and opportunities for you to explore our history, collections and gardens through changing exhibitions and special interest days. Step back in time in the Victorian style gardens, gaze at flamboyant colours on the parterre amid the ornate fountains and statuary. Unearth the rare and exotic birds housed in the rococo style Aviary found in the heart of the gardens or you can spend a fun-filled day with the family, be an adventurer in the woodland playground which winds through the trees, making use of the natural environment to create a magical area to play. Why not explore the trail around the gardens; hunt for bugs and spot wildlife along our woodland walk? There's fresh, homemade food including cakes and other treats for you in our restaurants and food-to-go outlets. Shop for wine, great gifts and unique pieces inspired by the collection in our Manor shop. For more information, visit our website. enquiries@waddesdon.org.uk https://waddesdon.org.uk/

description: Being a sibling to an autistic person can bring a whole range of experiences, feelings, and complexity to your life that it can be hard for others to relate to. Connecting with others who just ‘get’ what sibling life is like can help you to feel more confident and less isolated in your sibling role. Who can join this group? The group mainly focuses on siblings of autistic people who are verbal and who might need support in some areas of life, but not others. That’s because this is a specific experience that differs from other disabilities or neurodivergent conditions. To join this group you need to: - Be aged 18 or over - Currently live in the UK - Have a brother or sister who is autistic (includes Asperger syndrome) - Enjoy meeting others! local_offer: Introduction Little Home Learners is a warm, inclusive childminding setting in Aylesbury. We welcome all children, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Our aim is to ensure every child can learn, develop and thrive at their own pace, with the right support in place. We follow the SEND Code of Practice 0–25 (2015), the Equality Act 2010, the Children and Families Act 2014, and the EYFS 2024/2025. Who is the SENCO? As a childminding setting, the SENCO role is held by: Charlotte Shefras Charlotte is responsible for: - Coordinating SEND support - Working with parents and professionals - Monitoring progress - Ensuring inclusive practice - Completing SEND paperwork (APDR, support plans, referrals, etc.) How we identify SEND - We monitor each child’s development closely through: Observations - Learning journals Two‑year progress checks - Ongoing discussions with parents If we notice a child: - is not making expected progress - has emerging needs - shows differences in communication, behaviour, physical development or learning We will discuss this with parents sensitively and openly. We follow the Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) cycle to understand the child’s needs and plan support. How we support children with SEND We provide: Ordinarily Available Provision (OAP): - Differentiated activities - Visual supports - Sensory‑friendly adjustments - Small‑group or 1:1 support where needed - Adapted routines - Calm, predictable environment - Close partnership with parents We make reasonable adjustments to ensure all children can access the full curriculum and daily experiences. Working with parents and carers Parents are central to everything we do. We share observations and progress regularly, listen to parents’ views and expertise, co‑create APDR plans, agree targets together, review progress at least every 6–8 weeks, provide information in accessible formats if needed and we always include the voice of the child in planning. Working with External Professionals With parental consent, we may work with: - Early Years SEND Team Portage - Health Visitors - Speech and Language Therapists - Occupational Therapists - iSEND Team - Educational Psychologists - Social Workers (where relevant) We follow professional advice and integrate strategies into daily practice. Funding and referrals Where appropriate, we may apply for: - Inclusion Fund (low‑level or emerging needs) - High Needs Funding (HNF) Education, Health and Care Needs Assessment (EHCNA) We support families through the process and contribute to EHCP applications and EHCP reviews (every 3–6 months for under‑5s). Supporting transitions We ensure transitions are smooth and tailored to each child’s needs. This may include: - Transition meetings - Sharing APDR or SEND Support Plans - Visits to new settings - Photo books or social stories - Liaising with receiving SENCOs - Following the Buckinghamshire OAP Transition Guidance Accessibility We aim to make our environment accessible to all children. This includes: - Flexible layout Adapted resources - Visual supports - Quiet spaces - Sensory‑friendly adjustments - Alternative communication methods Documentation can be provided in: - Different languages - Larger print - Verbal explanation Inclusion and Equal Opportunities - We do not discriminate against any child or family - We challenge discriminatory language or behaviour and promote: Respect, Empathy, British Values and positive attitudes towards diversity. How to raise a concern We encourage parents to speak to Charlotte at any time. If further support is needed, families can contact: Buckinghamshire SEND Local Offer https://familyinfo.buckinghamshire.gov.uk/send-local-offer/ Buckinghamshire Early Years SEND Team Via the Family Information Service website iSEND Team For EHCP queries or assessments Reviewing this Local Offer This Local Offer will be reviewed annually or sooner if guidance changes. Next review: February 2027  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our setting aims to ensure that every child, including those with SEND, can thrive, feel included, and make meaningful progress. We focus on: - Building confidence, independence and communication skills through personalised support. - Creating a nurturing, predictable environment where children feel safe and understood. - Supporting social and emotional development, helping children form relationships and express themselves. - Working in partnership with families so that children experience consistent support at home and in the setting. - Early identification and intervention, ensuring needs are recognised quickly and support is put in place without delay. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our team regularly updates their knowledge to ensure high‑quality SEND provision. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are central to everything we do. We involve you by: - Regular conversations and check‑ins at drop‑off and pick‑up. - Inviting you to share your child’s interests, strengths and home routines so we can build on them. - Collaborative planning meetings when additional support is needed. - Sharing strategies that work well at home or in the setting to ensure consistency. You can get involved by: - Talking to us about any concerns or observations. - Joining review meetings. - Sharing your child’s achievements or challenges at home. - Working with us on agreed support strategies. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share progress through: - Termly written updates linked to the EYFS. - Ongoing observations shared via Tapestry. - Face‑to‑face conversations whenever needed. - SEND review meetings for children receiving additional support. Additional for children with SEND: - Individual support plans or SEN Support Plans. - More frequent progress reviews. - Joint meetings with external professionals. - Clear targets and strategies tailored to your child’s needs. - A named key person who oversees SEND provision for your child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment is designed to be as accessible as possible: Indoors: - Calm, low‑stimulus spaces for regulation. - Visual supports (timelines, symbols, choice boards). - Adaptable furniture and flexible layouts. - Resources stored at child height for independence. Outdoors: - Safe, enclosed outdoor play area. - Opportunities for sensory play and movement. - Clear pathways and accessible equipment. We continually review accessibility and make adjustments based on individual needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can begin using our service by: - Contacting us directly to discuss your child’s needs. - Visiting the setting to meet staff and see the environment. - Sharing any existing reports or assessments. - Working with us to create a smooth, personalised transition plan. - Agreeing any additional support or adaptations needed before your child starts. We welcome children with SEND and will always explore reasonable adjustments to support their inclusion. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are committed to continually improving our SEND support. Our future plans include: - Further staff training in autism, sensory integration, and communication strategies. - Expanding our sensory resources and calm‑down spaces. - Strengthening partnerships with local SEND professionals. - Developing more visual supports and structured routines. - Introducing additional parent workshops on topics such as behaviour regulation, communication, and early SEND identification. - Continuing to refine our transition processes for children with more complex needs.
