local_offer: At Little Acorns Kindergarten, we are committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and nurturing environment where all children, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), are supported to reach their full potential. We recognise that every child is unique and develop at their own pace, and we carefully plan a wide range of activities and experiences tailored to meet individual needs. Our experienced and caring staff work closely with parents and external professionals to ensure each child’s best interests are at the heart of everything we do. We are proud to have been awarded an Outstanding grade in our most recent Ofsted inspection (September 2025), reflecting our inclusive practice and high standards of care and education.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are able to access support and training from outside agencies including the Local Family Centre, Buckinghamshire Early Years, Specialist Teaching Services, Speech and Language, Occupational Therapists, Educational Psychologists, Health Visitors. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Little Acorns Kindergarten has a highly experienced and dedicated staff team with extensive knowledge of Early Years education and supporting children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Our experience includes supporting children with a wide range of needs, including Down Syndrome, Rett Syndrome, Autistic Spectrum Disorder, Cerebral Palsy, Speech and Language difficulties, and children with English as an Additional Language (EAL). All staff are qualified, or working towards a Level 3 or above qualification in Early Years Education. Our Assistant Manager and SENCO hold Level 3 SEND qualifications and regularly attend Early Years SENCO Liaison Groups and other professional networks to stay up to date with the latest research, guidance, and innovative approaches. Ongoing professional development is a key priority at Little Acorns. Staff training is regularly reviewed, and team members are actively encouraged to attend courses and workshops. In-house training ensures consistent, high-quality inclusive practice, while our Makaton training supports effective communication, helping all children feel understood, valued, and confident. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have an Open Door policy and actively encourage parental involvement as much as possible. Our family’s opinions and views are imperative and we value any input both positive and negative. This enables us to evaluate our offer to the families using our services. Parent/carers come in to play and observe their child in the setting, support special occasions, read stories, and share their interests and hobbies. A child identified as ‘needs additional support’ upon entry will be offered several transition visits. A meeting will be held with the SENCO/Manager, Key Person, family and any professionals already involved to identify specific needs and requirements prior to starting with us. A health care and education plan will be put into place if necessary. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Your child will be supported by a dedicated Key Person who works to build a strong, trusting relationship with both you and your child. This helps your child feel confident and ready to explore and learn independently. Each child is carefully assessed and observed, with their progress recorded in an online Learning Journal. A Starting Point Check is completed after the first two weeks to provide a benchmark, which will be discussed with you so we can work together to identify any additional needs. With your agreement, we may involve the Buckinghamshire Early Years Service or other specialist agencies to provide extra support. The SENCO and Manager ensure that all relevant information is shared with staff to provide consistent support for your child. Where needed, staff receive additional training, for example medical procedures, and a member of staff can be assigned to provide one-to-one support. In some cases, additional funding can be accessed to further support your child’s learning and development. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We operate from a purpose-built, one level location in Wendover this includes wheelchair access, a disabled parking space and toilet and low-level sinks. We strive to ensure that our activities are age/ability appropriate, and activities can be adapted so that each child can access them in some way. Additional resources and equipment are provided when necessary. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When a child is identified as requiring additional support upon entry to Little Acorns, we take a carefully planned and individualised approach to ensure a smooth transition. Several transition visits will be offered, giving your child the opportunity to become familiar with the setting, staff, and routines at a pace that suits them. These visits help to reduce anxiety, build confidence, and allow staff to begin understanding your child’s unique needs. Before your child starts, a meeting will be arranged with the SENCO/Manager, Key Person, family, and any professionals already involved in your child’s care or education. This allows us to gather important information, discuss your child’s strengths, needs, and preferences, and agree on the best strategies and support to put in place from day one. Where necessary, a personalised Health Care or Education Plan will be developed, detailing how your child will be supported within the setting. We work closely with families and external professionals to review and adapt support as needed, ensuring your child is fully included, confident, and able to thrive in our nurturing environment. Our goal is to provide continuity, consistency, and a positive start to your child’s early education journey. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are constantly reflecting on and evaluating our practice to make sure our SEND provision is up to date, effective, and evolving in line with the latest research and best practice. This includes reviewing our learning environment, activities, and teaching approaches, as well as staff training and professional development. Our aim is to ensure every child receives the highest quality early education and care, while promoting independence, curiosity, and a love of learning in a supportive and inclusive environment. We work closely with families, external professionals, and other agencies to ensure that the support we provide is tailored, consistent, and meets the individual needs of each child. By continually adapting and improving our SEND offer, we strive to provide the very best experience for every child, helping them to thrive and develop with confidence.

description: Cressex Dental Practice has been serving the local community of High Wycombe and surrounding areas for the past 30 years. The practice comprises of three surgeries, two of which are on ground floor level with wheelchair access. In our welcoming happy and vibrant practice, we ensure that every contact with us is helpful, caring, and professional. By mutual trust, respect, honesty, and good communication we provide you with treatment that focuses on your needs in total confidence. We always maintain high clinical standards in modern hygienic surgeries with state-of-the-art equipment. We offer NHS and private services. We are able to offer on-the-day emergency appointments (subject to availability) to current patients and individuals who are not already registered with us.

local_offer: Forest & Play is an inclusive outdoor early-years setting for children aged from 2½ to 5 years. We welcome children with a wide range of special educational needs and disabilities, with or without a formal diagnosis or Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Our SENCO, Inclusion Practitioner and each child’s key person work closely with families and relevant professionals. We use the graduated Assess, Plan, Do, Review approach to identify needs, agree appropriate outcomes, put support in place and regularly review its effectiveness. Support is tailored to the individual child and may include differentiated activities, visual timetables, Now and Next boards, choice boards, communication aids, predictable routines, additional support with transitions, sensory-regulation opportunities and access to quieter spaces. Our outdoor approach provides opportunities for movement, exploration, confidence-building and learning through first-hand experiences. Where a child requires additional staffing, specialist equipment, environmental adaptations or child-specific training, we work with the family and relevant professionals to identify what is needed and make reasonable adjustments wherever possible.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim for every child with SEND to feel safe, welcomed, understood and fully included in the life of Forest & Play. We work with children, families and professionals to agree meaningful and achievable outcomes based on each child’s strengths, interests and individual needs. These may include developing communication, independence, confidence, relationships, emotional regulation, physical skills, engagement in learning and participation in everyday routines and activities. Progress is reviewed regularly so that support can be adapted when necessary. We also aim to help families feel listened to, informed and confident that their child’s needs are understood. When a child moves to school or another setting, we support a carefully planned and positive transition. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? New setting opening in September, so no recent training has been completed yet. The manager is currently taking a SENCO Level 3 training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work closely with parents and carers, recognising that they know their child best. We gather information about each child’s strengths, interests, routines and support needs, and families can meet with our SENCO, Inclusion Practitioner and key person. Parents are involved in planning and reviewing their child’s support, with regular two-way communication and opportunities to provide feedback. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Each child’s key person shares regular updates with their family through conversations, meetings, and the Ovivio parent app. For children receiving SEND support, parents are involved in the Assess, Plan, Do, Review process. Individual outcomes and strategies are recorded and reviewed regularly. With parental consent, we also share relevant information with professionals and provide additional support during transitions. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Forest & Play is an outdoor woodland setting where children learn through movement, exploration and experiences in nature. Our base camp and cabin provide shelter and opportunities for quieter activities. The site includes naturally uneven ground, mud and surfaces that change with the weather. These features are an essential part of our provision and may present accessibility challenges that cannot always be removed or adapted. We encourage families to visit with their child so that we can discuss their individual needs and identify any potential barriers. Reasonable adjustments will be considered where they are practical and safe, such as visual or communication resources, adapted activities and access to quieter spaces. Any arrangements must take account of the woodland environment, available staffing and the safety and needs of the whole group. Where appropriate, we will seek advice from families and relevant professionals. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can request an information pack and complete our enquiry form before arranging a visit. They can meet the team and discuss their child’s needs with our SENCO and Inclusion Practitioner. We ask families to share any relevant plans or professional reports so that suitable support, reasonable adjustments and an individual settling-in plan can be considered. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As a new setting opening in September 2026, we have two experienced team members who have previously supported children with SEND and their families. We will build on this experience through ongoing SEND training and condition-specific professional development, such as autism, communication and sensory needs. Training and resources will be developed in response to the individual needs of the children attending, with advice from families and relevant professionals.

description: Little Berries, Berryfields Baby and Toddler Group. Mums, Dads, Grandparents, and childminders gather each week with bumps, babies, toddlers, and preschoolers to play with a huge variety of toys. There is always a different activity to enjoy with your child, from playdough to water, sticking and gluing to colouring, or something more seasonal like decorating a biscuit. There are books and puzzles, building bricks, dollies, prams, a café with play food, toy vehicles and garage, dressing-up clothes, and a dedicated baby area with appropriate toys. Whatever the weather, there is always a warm, friendly welcome awaiting parents, carers at Little Berries, the Berryfields Baby and Toddler Group. We meet every Thursday morning during term-time at Roman Park Hall. While the grown ups enjoy a chat and tea, coffee (and a biscuit), there’s a healthy snack for the children and then join in with a sing-along at the end of each session (with actions, of course). We ask for a small entrance fee. The group is open to everyone, babies to school age. Come visit us one Thursday. Can you help? We are always looking for enthusiastic and committed parents to join our committee and help with the running of this group. Please speak to us at the group or send a message if you'd like to know more. Find us on Facebook.

We meet every Thursday morning during term-time upstairs in the brand new Community Suite of Berryfields Church of England Primary School. Mums, Dads, Grandparents and childminders gather each week with bumps, babies, toddlers and preschoolers to play with a huge variety of toys. There is always a different activity to enjoy with your child, from Playdoh and sticking and gluing to colouring, or something more seasonal at certain times of the year. There’s books and puzzles, building bricks, dollies, prams, kitchen with play food, toy vehicles and garage, dressing-up clothes, and baby area with appropriate toys. After the children have played while the grown-ups enjoy a chat and tea/coffee, the children can sit down to a healthy snack, and then join in with a sing-along at the end of each session (with actions, of course!) description: There’s no better way to spend some time during the school holiday than by enjoying the snow at The Snow Centre Hemel Hempstead. Spend your school break flying down the slopes supervised by our qualified instructors who make ski holiday camps fun, educational, and, most importantly, safe for everyone. There are plenty of fun activities at The Snow Centre Hemel Hempstead, so book your child on one of our ski holiday camps and let them experience the thrill of the slopes. Start your children off down the exciting and rewarding path of becoming a skier from an early age. Our lessons for 4 to 6-year-olds make learning a brand-new skill fun and exciting, with our incredible instructors ensuring your child experiences the thrills of skiing while staying safe. We are running camps split based on your child's ability, with beginner, green, blue, and red camps available. Booking cost includes the Skis/Snowboard Boots and Helmets rental. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Little Chalfont Community Library
description: Little Chalfont Community Library is a local library operated and funded by people and businesses who live and work in the village. It works in the same way as a Buckinghamshire Council Library; you can use your existing library card or you can join the library - membership is free. We have everything you would expect to find in a local library; information, recreation, education and culture. As well as a wide range of books, we offer a number of facilities, including: - up-to-date adult fiction and non-fiction (including large print) - a big selection of children's and teenage fiction - audiobooks on both cassette and CD - periodicals, newspapers and local information - photocopying and laminating - free public internet access computers and free wi-fi access We hold regular events such as children's sessions, film nights, books groups and computer classes. Community groups and local businesses can also hire the library.

local_offer: At Little Chalfont Primary School we strive to support all our pupils to enable them to achieve their full potential during their time at the school. In order to do this, many steps are taken to support them through their learning journey. All pupils have access to excellent high-quality teaching. However, for some children, there are occasions when further additional support may be needed to help them achieve their targets. The Special Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCO) is Mr Jonathan Patten, who is supported by the Headteacher, Mr R Hacking, and a team of Class Teachers (CTs) and Learning Support Assistants (LSAs). The SENDCOs are responsible for the operation of the Special Educational Needs Policy and coordination of specific provision made to support individual children with SEND. We liaise with staff to monitor the pupil’s progress and plan further interventions where progress is slower than expected. We regularly have contact with a wide range of external agencies, who are able to give more specialised advice. The type of SEND provision that Little Chalfont Primary School provides is based on individual needs or a pupil’s educational healthcare plan, where their needs can be met within our mainstream setting. See Annual SEND Information Report for school's SEND information. https://www.littlechalfontprimaryschool.co.uk/send-information/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Ready To provide a high-quality and challenging education for all pupils. To consider that every pupil is entitled to reach the highest level of personal achievement. Respectful To include and embrace diversity and equal opportunities for all children regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, attainment, or background Resilient To adapt, deliver and evaluate the use of broad and balanced educational opportunities to meet the differing needs of the pupils attending. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Identifying and Assessing SEND Needs in the classroom. How to use evidence-based interventions across school. Using generative drawing to support reading. Using elements of 'Echo Reading' to support reading fluency. What is High-Quality Teaching and Support? The intervention process and the basics of the graduated approach. Supporting pupils with SEND in writing. Supporting pupils with SEND in maths. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We offer an open-door policy for parents to discuss any concerns they may have about their child(ren). This includes: A direct email for the SENDCo (sendco@littlechalfont.bucks.sch.uk) Additional contact via the school office to arrange meetings Termly SEND Meetings to contribute to, and discuss actions from, a child's provision map or Educational Health Care Plan (EHCP). Parents are involved in every stage of SEND planning and evaluation, including contributing towards the change of systems or proformas in place in school. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Via termly SEND Meetings to discuss and agree the content of their child's provision map. Via Parents Evening Via End of Year Report How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The school is single floor and accessible to all. Please see our accessibility plan on our website for more information. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact the school office or SENDCo to discuss availability of services and which might be most suitable for your child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To continue to offer high-quality teaching to all pupils; to continue to implement the use of effective in-school targeted support for pupils with SEND; and to continue to work closely with Buckinghamshire County Council to offer a large variety of specialist services for children, and training for staff.

name: Half-Day Workshop: Introduction to Screen Writing
description: With Colin Metcalfe in celebration of the National Year of Reading! This workshop is an opportunity to understand what knowledge is required to produce a screenplay, starting with basic script formatting rules. It will introduce storytelling structure, and what info an audience needs before the plot can begin. Colin will cover a variety of topics such as; How to launch the plot(s) and developing it to create challenges for characters to overcome, making characters interesting using different types of conflict personality traits, creating the right kind of drama/comedy, producing multi-purpose scenes that ensure that every second of screen time is completely taken advantage of, building the story up to a crescendo, and, of course, tying up all of the main characters’ story arcs and delivering that satisfying ending! Participants just need to bring a notebook and a pencil to make notes in! Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

description: Come and join us in the MINIS class (1 to 2 and a half years) as we dance, sing, and role-play, all whilst exploring sounds and rhyme! Designed in conjunction with a speech and language therapist, the MINIS class offers lots of opportunity to develop speaking and listening skills; it's just the perfect introduction to phonics! The Phonics with Robot Reg Pre-School class (2 and a half to 5 years) is high-energy, fast-paced, fun, and educational! We support your child's early learning through fun, engaging, and multisensory activities. With a focus on introducing letter sounds using songs, actions, games, and visuals to develop phonics, blending, and segmenting skills, your child will be having so much fun, they wont know that they're learning! All sessions include music, movement, and gross motor activities like dancing, playdoh fun during 'Reg’s Rave', or dancing with shakers in our stop an go disco, bubbles, parachutes, and more! Designed by a Primary School Teacher and aligned with the EYFS curriculum, Phonics with Robot Reg MINIS, and Preschool classes provide a gentle introduction to sounds and pre-reading skills through music, role-play, dance, and play!

local_offer: Little Chestnuts is an outstanding Preschool setting within Chestnut Lane School. The Preschool is for children for the academic year in which they turn four years old. We welcome children with special educational needs and disabilities whose needs can be met within a mainstream setting, and will make reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We have a wide range of expertise within our staff team to meet the needs of the pupils. Miss Amba Flitney is the special educational needs coordinator (SENCo) and is responsible for managing the special educational needs throughout the school and Little Chestnuts Preschool. https://chestnutlane.bucks.sch.uk/parents/policies What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have high aspirations for all the children attending Little Chestnuts and work together with families to support each child to develop and learn in their own way, and at their own pace. We communicate regularly with parents and regular reviews keep parents and staff working closely together. In addition we have close working relationships with a range of outside agencies who provide expertise within their fields. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCo (planning your year) Supporting pupils with medical needs Makaton Level 1 and Level 2 Developing Social Skills ASD Awareness Unmasking Anxiety for Autistic Pupils Speech and Language Creating an Inclusion Friendly Classroom First Words Phrases and Sentences Top Tips to Boost Vocabulary Magic Behaviour Management Annual Reviews SEN Code of Practice Making Sense of Autism Understanding ADHD Whole School SEND Review Supporting Pupils with Attachment Difficulties Smart Outcomes on EHCPs Ordinarily Available Provision Support Supporting Communication in Early Years DLD & Alternatives to Phonics and Reading Mental Health Awareness Introduction to Neuroscience in EYFS Safeguarding Children with SEND SEND online portal EHCP Annual Reviews Step ON De-escalation iSEND Reception Liaison OT Sensory Processing Down Syndrome Introduction EAL Adaptive Teaching for Primary Learners Conflict Prevention Management Physical Intervention Techniques How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents into Little Chestnuts Preschool regularly. Parents have access to our online learning journal platform, and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can catch up with the teacher informally at the beginning and end of the session, or can request a meeting with staff at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible. We also have termly parents' consultations where parents will receive an update on their child’s progress and can discuss their child’s likes, dislikes, achievements, and any concerns they may have. We provide age-appropriate suggestions of how your child’s development can be supported at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? In addition to the opportunities listed above, we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEN, depending on the needs of the child. We regularly monitor the short-term outcomes for children with SEN and invite parents to be part of reviews and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals E.g. Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT) are visiting regularly we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our buildings are all on one level. The main building has ramps, handrails and a disabled toilet. There is also a ramp into the Early Years block. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents of children with SEN are welcome to visit our setting and discuss their child’s individual needs with the preschool teacher and SENCo. We visit children and parents at home as well as liaising with other nurseries and preschools to ensure a smooth transition to Little Chestnuts. Children are invited to settling sessions and we will work with families to agree the best range of sessions for their child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to keep up-to-date with appropriate training and new strategies to support the needs of children with SEND in our setting.

name: The Elves and the Shoemaker
description: Elvis Schumacher, cobbler and craftsman, has worked all his life creating the most beautiful footwear. But now he’s hit hard times... Everyone’s buying boring shoes from the evil businessman, Bunyan Sole-less. Time is running out for Elvis. With one piece of leather left and Bunyan’s factory growing, can anyone help him? This well-known and well-loved tale - made popular by the Ladybird Classic - has been re-heeled by Theatre of Widdershins in their own inimitable style. Beautifully crafted set and puppets, sublime music, a kaleidoscope of miniature shoes and a comic mouse make this show a magical must-see. Age guidance: 3 plus years. Run time 55 mins. description: Sleep is like an old friend I’ve not seen for a long time. She’s stopped returning my calls. But some nights feel sort of magic. Just you and me watching a new day being born. A Tale of Us is a brand new play for parents and their babies. Join Ivy and her little one on a funny, frank and magical journey through their first year of life together. description: Step into Luca Silvestrini’s acclaimed new dance-theatre adaptation of Mozart’s opera, The Magic Flute. Join the fun-loving bird-catcher Papageno and the lost Prince Tamino as they set out to rescue Princess Pamina, uncovering the truth about the mysterious Queen of the Night and the powerful leader Sarastro. The Magic Flute is brought to life through Protein’s playful blend of dance, storytelling, singing, and stunning visuals, featuring rearranged Mozart alongside original music by composer Frank Moon. name: A Town Called Christmas
description: Far away, beyond the snow, and nestled in a perfect nook you’ll find a town called Christmas… Clementine dreams of a place where gingerbread houses glow under twinkling fairy-lights, and chocolate coins are currency. Where the streets are filled with snow-ball fights, and laughter hangs like baubles in the air! The happiest place on Earth. Or at least it used to be… Buckle in for a rollercoaster of magic, music, and mayhem as our hero crash-lands in a crumbling town where only the long-forgotten fables, a cantankerous caretaker and a glitching robot remain! Can they save the day, and the town called Christmas? A brand-new show for adventurers aged 3 plus and their grown-ups. Brought to you by Gala Durham and Wrongsemble. description: A nocturnal journey for early years by The Last Baguette, who brought A Winter's Tail to Norden Farm for Christmas 2025. Inspired by The Star by Jane Taylor. name: Play Centred Therapy
description: Play Centred Therapy provides mobile play therapy for children and young people across Buckinghamshire and surrounding areas. Play therapy offers children a safe, supportive, space to explore and communicate feelings, experiences, and difficulties through play, particularly when they may find it difficult to express themselves through words. I work with children experiencing a range of emotional, behavioural, social and school-related difficulties, including anxiety, low confidence and self-esteem, emotional regulation difficulties, changes or transitions, friendship difficulties, and challenges associated with SEND and neurodiversity. Sessions are child-led and use play, creative activities, movement, and sensory experiences to help children develop emotional understanding, coping strategies, and confidence. The therapeutic relationship is central to the work, allowing children to communicate at their own pace without pressure to talk about things before they are ready. I am a PTUK Certified Play Therapist and work within the Play Therapy UK ethical framework. I hold an Enhanced DBS on the Update Service, professional indemnity insurance and ICO registration, and undertake regular clinical supervision. I provide 40-minute sessions, usually delivered within the child’s school or educational setting. An initial block of 12 sessions is generally recommended, followed by a review to consider whether further therapeutic support would be beneficial. Play therapy can be funded by schools, including through appropriate school budgets, or privately by parents/carers. I am happy to speak with parents, SENCOs and other professionals to discuss whether play therapy may be appropriate for a particular child.

description: Making it REAL has been developed for parents and carers who would like to support their child's reading and writing from an early age. Making it REAL is a 6-week programme for Parents and Carers of children aged 18 months to 4 years. Children and parents/carers attend the workshops together. It includes an introductory session, 4 themed sessions and a one to one session designed to support you and your children to get started with the activities at home. The play-based sessions are fun and relaxed and have been based on the programme from the National Children’s Bureau. Parents and carers will also learn what they can do to support the child’s learning: opportunity, recognition, interaction and modelling.

description: Hearts of Young People Academy is a specialist online mentoring and intervention service supporting young people aged 11 to 18 who are experiencing barriers to education. We work with children and young people with Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, Autism, ADHD, learning difficulties, anxiety, Emotionally Based School Avoidance (EBSA), challenging behaviour, and those at risk of exclusion. Led by a JNC-qualified Youth Worker with over 15 years of experience, our personalised one-to-one mentoring helps young people build confidence, improve emotional wellbeing, develop positive behaviour, re-engage with education and achieve positive outcomes. We work closely with parents, schools, local authorities and other professionals to provide tailored interventions, progress reviews and practical strategies that meet each young person's individual needs. local_offer: Hearts of Young People Academy provides specialist online mentoring, tutoring and intervention for children and young people with SEND. We support young people with Autism, ADHD, SEMH, anxiety, emotional regulation needs, communication difficulties, learning differences, school avoidance and those at risk of exclusion. Every programme is tailored to the individual, helping young people build confidence, improve emotional wellbeing, develop positive behaviour, increase engagement with learning and successfully re-engage with education. We work closely with families, schools and professionals to ensure consistent, person-centred support.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to improve educational engagement, emotional wellbeing, attendance, confidence, resilience and independence. We support children and young people to overcome barriers to learning, develop positive relationships, improve behaviour, strengthen communication skills and achieve successful outcomes in education and daily life. We also work alongside families, schools and professionals to ensure consistent support and sustainable long-term progress. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? AQA Centre/Registered Centre training (AQA Unit Award Scheme) Safeguarding Children Child Protection Prevent Duty Working with Children and Young People with Challenging Behaviour Behaviour Management and Positive Behaviour Support Trauma-Informed Practice (only if you have completed this) Mental Health Awareness Online Safety / Keeping Children Safe Online Equality, Diversity and Inclusion GDPR / Data Protection Professional Boundaries and Professional Practice Youth Work Practice and Mentoring Risk Assessment and Health & Safety How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are an essential part of every young person's journey. We work closely with families from the initial consultation through to regular progress reviews. Parents are encouraged to share their child's strengths, challenges and goals, and receive ongoing updates, practical strategies and opportunities to discuss progress. We believe that working together with families leads to the best outcomes for young people. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We provide regular feedback through email, telephone or online meetings, depending on family preference. Progress is monitored against agreed targets, and parents receive updates on achievements, engagement, wellbeing and next steps. Where appropriate, we also work collaboratively with schools, SENCOs and other professionals to ensure consistent support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Hearts of Young People Academy delivers services online, allowing children and young people to access support from the comfort and familiarity of their own home. Online delivery removes travel barriers and can reduce anxiety for many young people with SEND. Sessions are adapted to meet individual communication, learning and sensory needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families, schools, local authorities and other professionals can contact Hearts of Young People Academy directly by telephone or email. We offer a free initial consultation to discuss the young person's needs, identify appropriate support and develop a personalised intervention plan. Referrals are welcomed from parents, schools, SENCOs, social workers and local authorities What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Hearts of Young People Academy is committed to continually developing its SEND provision by expanding specialist intervention programmes, strengthening partnerships with schools and local authorities, enhancing staff professional development and increasing access to high-quality online mentoring and educational support for children and young people across the UK.

description: Glow Project is a specialist alternative provision supporting children and young people aged 9 to 16 with SEND, autism, ADHD, EBSNA (Emotionally Based School Non-Avoidance), SEMH and other additional needs. We provide personalised Section 19 support, early intervention and bespoke programmes designed to prevent school avoidance, support reintegration into education where appropriate, and provide tailored educational pathways for those unable to access mainstream school. We work alongside families, schools and local authorities to deliver high-quality education through small group and 1:1 provision. Our programmes include AQA Unit Award Scheme qualifications, English, Maths and Science, mentoring, therapeutic support, life skills, vocational learning, outdoor education and social development, helping young people build confidence, resilience and positive relationships. local_offer: Glow Project is a specialist alternative provision supporting children and young people aged 9–16 with SEND, autism, ADHD, EBSA (Emotionally Based School Avoidance), SEMH, learning differences and sensory needs, including hearing impairments. We provide personalised Section 19 support, early intervention and bespoke programmes designed to reduce barriers to education, support children at risk of school refusal, support reintegration into education where appropriate, and provide tailored educational pathways for those unable to access mainstream school. We work alongside families, schools and local authorities to deliver high-quality education through small group and 1:1 provision. Our programmes include AQA Unit Award Scheme qualifications, English, Maths and Science, mentoring, therapeutic support, life skills, vocational learning, outdoor education and social development, helping young people build confidence, resilience and positive relationships. Glow Project delivers programmes from trusted community venues, including the XC Centre in Hemel Hempstead and Berkhamsted Hockey Club, providing safe, engaging environments where young people can thrive both academically and personally.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Glow Project aims to improve educational engagement, emotional wellbeing, confidence, independence and social communication. We work to reduce barriers to learning, prevent school refusal where possible, support successful reintegration into education when appropriate and provide personalised pathways for children unable to access mainstream education. We work in partnership with families, schools and local authorities to ensure every young person can achieve positive academic, social and personal outcomes. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our team undertakes ongoing professional development to ensure we provide high-quality support for children and young people with SEND. Training includes safeguarding and child protection, autism awareness, ADHD awareness, trauma-informed practice, mental health and wellbeing, positive behaviour support, neurodiversity, risk assessment and inclusive practice. Staff continue to access additional SEND training to meet the individual needs of the children and young people we support. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are central to every child's journey at Glow Project. We begin with an initial consultation to understand each young person's strengths, needs and goals before creating a personalised support plan. Families receive regular progress updates, reviews and opportunities to contribute to ongoing planning. Parents can contact us directly throughout a placement and are encouraged to work collaboratively with our team to ensure the best outcomes for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We provide regular written progress updates, review meetings and ongoing communication with parents, schools and referring professionals where appropriate. Progress is monitored against personalised outcomes, academic achievements, wellbeing, confidence, attendance, engagement and AQA Unit Award Scheme achievements. Support is adapted to meet individual SEND needs through personalised learning, flexible approaches, small groups, mentoring and therapeutic support where appropriate. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Glow Project delivers provision from accessible community venues, including the XC Centre and Berkhamsted Hockey Club. We complete individual risk assessments and reasonable adjustments for each learner where required. Our learning environments include indoor teaching spaces and outdoor learning opportunities, promoting wellbeing, physical activity and engagement. Accessibility requirements are discussed with families before placements begin to ensure individual needs can be met safely and effectively. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact Glow Project directly to arrange an initial consultation. Referrals are welcomed from parents, schools, local authorities and other professionals. Following an assessment of need, we work with families to develop a personalised programme tailored to the young person's educational, social and emotional needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Glow Project is committed to continually developing its specialist SEND provision. Future plans include expanding AQA Unit Award programmes, increasing vocational pathways, developing early intervention programmes to reduce school refusal, strengthening partnerships with schools and local authorities, expanding therapeutic support and increasing opportunities for social development, outdoor learning and life skills. We are committed to ensuring our provision continues to meet the changing needs of children and young people with SEND and their families.

local_offer: Exceptional Individuals supports neurodivergent young people as they prepare for adulthood and move towards employment. We provide free online career coaching, CV support, mentoring, online workshops, a neurodiverse jobs board, and guidance around Access to Work. We support people with a range of neurodivergences, including autism, ADHD, dyslexia, dyspraxia, dyscalculia, and Tourette’s syndrome. Support is available online across the UK, helping young people understand their strengths, build confidence, and access practical support when looking for work, training, or their next step after education.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to help neurodivergent young people feel more confident and better prepared for employment and adult working life. Depending on the individual, this can include helping them to understand their strengths, develop their CV, prepare for interviews, explore suitable career options, find neurodiversity-friendly employment opportunities, and understand the support available to them in the workplace. By providing this support online, young people can access help regardless of where they live in the UK. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Exceptional Individuals specialises in neurodiversity, and many members of the team are neurodivergent themselves, meaning lived experience is an important part of how our services are developed and delivered. The organisation also works with BACP-registered psychologists and is a Level 3 Disability Confident Leader. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Our support is centred around the individual young person and their employment and career goals. Where appropriate, parents and carers can help young people identify the support they may benefit from and explore the services available through Exceptional Individuals. As young people move towards adulthood, we aim to support them to build confidence and independence in making decisions about their future career and employment. Parents and carers can also explore the information and resources available through our website. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Where a young person accesses individual coaching or employment support, the focus is on their own goals, strengths, challenges, and next steps. Support is tailored to the individual and their neurodivergence, rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach. Any involvement of parents or carers in an individual young person’s support would be discussed as appropriate to that person’s circumstances and preferences. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our employment and career support is available online, so there is no requirement for young people to travel to a physical setting. This makes the service accessible to neurodivergent young people across the UK and allows them to access support from an environment in which they feel comfortable. Our online approach can also help remove geographical and travel barriers for young people who may find attending services in person more difficult. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Young people and their families can visit: https://exceptionalindividuals.com/ From there, they can explore the support available, including free career coaching, CV support, mentoring, online workshops, our neurodiverse jobs board, and information about Access to Work. As services are available online, young people can access support from anywhere in the UK. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Exceptional Individuals aims to continue developing its employment and career support for neurodivergent people and improving access to practical resources that help people move into and succeed in employment. As a neurodiversity-focused social enterprise, we will continue to use lived experience and feedback from neurodivergent people to inform the support, resources and services we provide. We also work with employers to improve understanding of neurodiversity in the workplace, helping to create more inclusive recruitment processes and working environments for neurodivergent people.

name: Family Event "Creepy Creatures and Nasty Nature"
description: Come along to Woolley Firs this Halloween. Spooky activities and trail inspired by our spectacularly strange, wild, creatures! We are very lucky to have some spectacularly spooky creatures living wild here at Woolley Firs, including owls, bats, spiders, and centipedes. Find out what is creepy about these creatures by following our trail around the site and taking part in our games and activities, indoors and out. Join us at our lovely site this October half term to discover what lives in a dark cupboard in our centre! Become a spider in the woods and catch your prey. Whether you believe in vampires or not, there'll be bat crafts for you to take home. Price includes sign up to our BBOWT expert led workshop too.
organisation: Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust (BBOWT) One of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England. This large Living Landscape covers an area between Oxford, Bicester and Aylesbury. It includes 48,400 hectares of woodland, mixed farmland and floodplain meadows across the boundary between Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire. The entire area is ecologically linked through the River Ray, which rises in Quainton, close to Finmere Wood nature reserve, and flows west alongside some of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England, to join the River Cherwell at Islip, north of Oxford. local_offer: We offer full day sessions to children and young people (CYP) with additional needs or those from adverse backgrounds. We are an outdoor based provision focussing on the use of mountain biking using this activity as a low demand setting allowing CYP to find and develop regulation techniques and to improve confidence, resilience, and to find structure without the typical demands mainstream education brings. We have fantastic success rates with unusually high attendance rates with all of our CYP being 90% plus in the last 4 years of our provision. We are focussed on supporting our CYP on finding a way back to education be it through tutoring or school.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We will do our best to achieve the desired outcomes that are in the EHCP but also those that have been shared with us by parents and the LA. We do not believe we are a replacement to education but a way to support, supplement and to allow the CYP we work with to do the best they can do to ensure they have the greatest chance for success. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We write reports but have regular conversations with both the parent and the commissioning authority. We believe in being collaborative with all parties to get the best for the children and young people we work with as they are the focus. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Outdoors but we try to include all those we can and will do our best to make adjustments to make it suitable. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact us either by email or telephone. We are always happy to try and accommodate any new referrals where possible. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We wish to grow our presence in Buckinghamshire to deliver the same great results we have had elsewhere. We truly believe in our provision and the good it can do and want to deliver that to all that we can to give every child the chance to succeed.

description: Women’s Health Physiotherapy can help during pregnancy and after birth (as well at other times during life) if you are experiencing symptoms such as pelvic girdle pain, back pain, bladder or bowel problems including leaking and prolapse, abdominal muscle separation, or difficulties returning to exercise/usual activities. Our specialist physiotherapists provide assessment, advice, and personalised treatment to help you manage symptoms, improve your wellbeing, and support a safe and confident recovery during the antenatal and postnatal period. To be referred to a physiotherapist during pregnancy or during the first 28 days postnatally, speak to your midwife or obstetrician about a referral to our team based at either Stoke Mandeville, Wycombe, or Amersham Hospitals. If you have already had your baby, and are over 28 days post-natal, you can self-refer to the Practice Plus Physiotherapy Service, through your GP. Learn more by visiting the link provided. Please visit the Buckinghamshire Healthcare website or speak with your midwife team to learn more.

name: Women's Health Physiotherapy
description: Women’s Health Physiotherapy can help during pregnancy and after birth (as well at other times during life) if you are experiencing symptoms such as pelvic girdle pain, back pain, bladder or bowel problems including leaking and prolapse, abdominal muscle separation, or difficulties returning to exercise/usual activities. Our specialist physiotherapists provide assessment, advice, and personalised treatment to help you manage symptoms, improve your wellbeing, and support a safe and confident recovery during the antenatal and postnatal period. To be referred to a physiotherapist during pregnancy or during the first 28 days postnatally, speak to your midwife or obstetrician about a referral to our team based at either Stoke Mandeville, Wycombe, or Amersham Hospitals. If you have already had your baby, and are over 28 days post-natal, you can self-refer to the Practice Plus Physiotherapy Service, through your GP. Learn more by visiting the link provided. Please visit the Buckinghamshire Healthcare website or speak with your midwife team to learn more.

description: We support families both before (antenatally) and after birth (postnatally) with help, information, and advice on feeding your baby (up to 28 days of age). We help you understand more about breastfeeding, address any concerns you may have, and help you to make the right decisions. All parents have the right to make their own choices as to how they feed and care for their babies. There are clinics on Mondays and Thursdays by appointment only. They’re in the Antenatal clinic, Waddesdon Wing at Stoke Mandeville Hospital (Monday) and in the Antenatal clinic, Wycombe Hospital (Thursday). To book an appointment, please contact us by email or phone and providing the following details: - Your name, telephone number, and NHS number - The date your baby was born or your due date if you are pregnant - A brief outline of what we can support you with Please visit our website for more information.

name: Visit Santa on the Nature Reserve | Sutton Courtenay, Grotto
description: Santa Claus is coming to the nature reserve! Bring your 3 to 11 year olds to get your wildlife-friendly Christmas off to a flying start. Meet Santa on his day out at the nature reserve and discover how you can help give all the animals a happy Christmas. The event will include a range of Christmas and wildlife themed, eco-friendly crafts and activities for children to take part in while waiting their turn to see Santa - some outdoors on the nature reserve and others in our cosy classrooms by the woodstove. Families will be allocated a Santa time slot on arrival. Each child will receive their eco-friendly Christmas gift from Santa - you are welcome to take photos of your child with Santa. Booking essential as places are limited. This event is aimed at children aged 3 to 11 years. All children must be accompanied by an adult. Younger siblings are welcome to attend too at no additional cost but only children with paid tickets will receive a gift from Santa. For preschool aged children (18 months to 4 years) we recommend our Storytime with Mrs Claus sessions on Tuesday 15 and Wednesday 16 December.
organisation: Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust (BBOWT) One of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England. This large Living Landscape covers an area between Oxford, Bicester and Aylesbury. It includes 48,400 hectares of woodland, mixed farmland and floodplain meadows across the boundary between Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire. The entire area is ecologically linked through the River Ray, which rises in Quainton, close to Finmere Wood nature reserve, and flows west alongside some of the last remaining traditional floodplain meadows in England, to join the River Cherwell at Islip, north of Oxford. Since 1981 BBOWT (Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust) has been buying and restoring floodplain meadows in the upper reaches of the River Ray, and working with neighbouring farmers to create a stronghold for wading birds including curlew. info@bbowt.org.uk https://www.bbowt.org.uk/wildlife/living-landscapes/bernwood-forest-and-ray-valley-living-landscape

name: Santa Steam Specials | Grotto
description: Our Santa Steam Specials are here again and we are holding our prices at 2025 levels. This enchanting journey is the ultimate festive treat for children, offering a magical steam train ride from Princes Risborough to Santa’s Grotto at his North Pole station. Here, little ones can share their Christmas wishes with Santa himself! All trains depart from Princes Risborough Station Platform 4 (SatNav HP27 9DN), where Santa's stewards will warmly welcome you onboard. During the journey, the Elves will entertain the children with activity packs, puzzles, handouts, children's games, and 'Letters-to-Santa'. The steam train will take you to Santa's Enchanted Workshop and Grotto at the North Pole station. Here, you can enjoy refreshments, chat with Santa, take memorable photos, and meet the big man himself! Each child ticket (for 1 to 12 year olds) includes a present. "Babes in arms" (under 1 year) do not need a ticket but they will still receive a small gift. Unfortunately, adults and teenagers will not receive a gift from Santa! And while the train is in the platform at Chinnor we have face painting for the 3 to 11 year olds. Won't this make a lovely photo and a wonderful memory of your trip to see Santa? Travel in comfort in our 1950s carriages, named after Santa's reindeers – Rudolph, Blitzen, Dasher, and Prancer. Seats are booked at tables to keep families together. Enjoy the traditional elements of our Santa experience: the steam train ride, hot and cold beverages, mince pies or biscuits, and a magical visit with Santa. Additional treats like sandwiches, hot sausage rolls, crisps, snacks, and mulled wine can be purchased at the station café, and you might find some last-minute presents in our station shop. Christmas comes but once a year, and we aim to make it truly memorable. Santa and our volunteers look forward to welcoming you and your family onboard for a festive experience filled with joy and magic. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

description: Our Santa Steam Specials are here again and we are holding our prices at 2025 levels. This enchanting journey is the ultimate festive treat for children, offering a magical steam train ride from Princes Risborough to Santa’s Grotto at his North Pole station. Here, little ones can share their Christmas wishes with Santa himself! All trains depart from Princes Risborough Station Platform 4 (SatNav HP27 9DN), where Santa's stewards will warmly welcome you onboard. During the journey, the Elves will entertain the children with activity packs, puzzles, handouts, children's games, and 'Letters-to-Santa'. The steam train will take you to Santa's Enchanted Workshop and Grotto at the North Pole station. Here, you can enjoy refreshments, chat with Santa, take memorable photos, and meet the big man himself! Each child ticket (for 1 to 12 year olds) includes a present. "Babes in arms" (under 1 year) do not need a ticket but they will still receive a small gift. Unfortunately, adults and teenagers will not receive a gift from Santa! And while the train is in the platform at Chinnor we have face painting for the 3 to 11 year olds. Won't this make a lovely photo and a wonderful memory of your trip to see Santa? Travel in comfort in our 1950s carriages, named after Santa's reindeers – Rudolph, Blitzen, Dasher, and Prancer. Seats are booked at tables to keep families together. Enjoy the traditional elements of our Santa experience: the steam train ride, hot and cold beverages, mince pies or biscuits, and a magical visit with Santa. Additional treats like sandwiches, hot sausage rolls, crisps, snacks, and mulled wine can be purchased at the station café, and you might find some last-minute presents in our station shop. Christmas comes but once a year, and we aim to make it truly memorable. Santa and our volunteers look forward to welcoming you and your family onboard for a festive experience filled with joy and magic. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

local_offer: I am experienced in supporting customers experiencing a range of barriers to accessing education or employment. I am trained in positive psychology approaches to supporting neurodivergent career planners and job seekers. I work with my customers to explore ways of making my support as accessible as possible for each individual. I also work alongside other professionals when appropriate and helpful.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Helping young people and adults to move confidently towards education or employment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Diploma in Careers Guidance, Level 3 Neurodivergence and Inclusion (Train the Trainer). Currently undertaking Level 7 research project into hope levels amongst autistic career planners and job seekers. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I often work with parents to enhance understanding of what learning opportunities are available, how current recruitment processes work, and how best to support your young person in planning their next career move. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? With young people and their parents I agree how communication will happen. However, depending on location and availability of venue in-person meetings can take place. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Check my prices and offer on https://www.careerswithintent.com and then contact me via kath@careerswithintent.com to discuss your needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am always happy to discuss workshops for groups of young people or adults at similar points in their career planning journey.

name: Christmas Cracker Grotto at Odds Farm
description: Step into a world of festive magic at Odds Farm Park with our Christmas Cracker, a heart-warming Christmas experience filled with twinkling lights, enchanting shows, and a special 1-to-1 visit to Santa’s Grotto! Your ticket includes a magical day packed with festive experiences, seasonal surprises and unforgettable family moments, including: - North Pole Experience - Step into a magical, immersive journey through the North Pole, guided by Santa’s cheerful elves. Wander through Santa’s bustling postal workshop, peek inside the cosy kitchen of Mrs Claus, and make a special Christmas wish at the Wishing Tree before taking a family photo at our sleigh! - Meet Santa Claus - Enjoy a magical 1-to-1 family visit in his enchanting grotto. - Make a Cuddly Bear - Visit the Elves’ workshop and create your very own cuddly bear to take home, complete with a special birth certificate. - Choose a Free Toy - Visit the Toy Shop and pick out a special gift to take home. - Festive Crafts - Get creative and make something special to help get ready for Christmas. - Live Interactive Shows - Join the festive fun in our Show Barn with lively Christmas character performances. - Tree by Twinklelight Shows – Gather together and watch our mesmerising illuminated Christmas tree displays. - The A Cappella Penguins – Be charmed by the smooth harmonies of our much-loved festive crooners. - Post Your Letter to Santa – Don’t forget to send your Christmas wishes Running on selected dates from 27 November to 24 December 2026, families can enjoy a full day of festive fun and unforgettable moments together, with dedicated SEN sessions available. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.
organisation: Odds Farm Park Come and enjoy the fresh farm air, our wide-open spaces, and spend time with all our furry friends here at Odds Farm Park! We want you to enjoy an amazing day full of farm adventures, and for you to do this safely and with confidence, we have introduced numerous new measures to ensure we can be COVID secure at all times. All guests must pre-book tickets online ahead of their visit so we can carefully manage daily visitor numbers, and new routes, walk-ways and staggered entry to certain areas have also been added to maintain social distancing measures around the Farm. As an outdoor family farm park attraction, we have always actively encouraged regular hand-washing for all guests, and we are offering extensive hand hygiene facilities across the Farm Park, including: 5 dedicated hand-washing stations 18 hand sanitising stations 3 bathroom and hand-washing blocks Whilst our Indoor Play barn, Demonstration Barn and Adventure Maze are temporarily closed, here at Odds Farm Park there’s plenty of space for kids to run, tumble and play. There are acres of outdoor adventure to discover, including the extensive Adventure Log Play Area, H2Odds Water Play, Mini-Land Rovers, Sand Play Area, Adventure Fort, Go-Karts, Tractor and Trailer Rides (Apr to Oct), Fitness Trail, Under 5s Log Play Area - what will you do first? Of course, no farm visit would be complete without meeting the animals! Explore our Undercover Animal Barn, where you can see our rabbits and guinea pigs, and even hand-feed some of our sheep and goats! Adults and children alike can strut and cluck their way around Chicken World, and watch our feathered friends enjoy exploring their new home! In the summer months, guests can also visit our pigs, cows, donkeys, ponies and other animals out enjoying their paddocks across the Farm – you might catch a glimpse of some piglets, calves and a foal trotting and springing around in the sunshine! Feeling hungry? Our outdoor outlets, The Airstream and Ice Cream and Milkshake Parlour, are offering a contactless service, and visitors can now Click and Collect a range of delicious drinks and tasty treats via our new online ordering system. As always, guests are welcome to bring their own picnics to enjoy whilst visiting and which can be enjoyed throughout the park at any of our socially distanced picnic tables. For further information on how to book and what to expect from your visit, we have all the details you need on our Reopening page. To find out what’s on, guests can also check out our new interactive map to help plan their day and guide them through our amazing outdoor adventures! main@oddsfarm.co.uk https://www.oddsfarm.co.uk/

name: SEN Christmas Cracker Grotto at Odds Farm
description: Step into a world of festive magic at Odds Farm Park with our Christmas Cracker, a heart-warming Christmas experience filled with twinkling lights, enchanting shows, and a special 1-to-1 visit to Santa’s Grotto! Your ticket includes a magical day packed with festive experiences, seasonal surprises and unforgettable family moments, including: - North Pole Experience - Step into a magical, immersive journey through the North Pole, guided by Santa’s cheerful elves. Wander through Santa’s bustling postal workshop, peek inside the cosy kitchen of Mrs Claus, and make a special Christmas wish at the Wishing Tree before taking a family photo at our sleigh! - Meet Santa Claus - Enjoy a magical 1-to-1 family visit in his enchanting grotto. - Make a Cuddly Bear - Visit the Elves’ workshop and create your very own cuddly bear to take home, complete with a special birth certificate. - Choose a Free Toy - Visit the Toy Shop and pick out a special gift to take home. - Festive Crafts - Get creative and make something special to help get ready for Christmas. - Live Interactive Shows - Join the festive fun in our Show Barn with lively Christmas character performances. - Tree by Twinklelight Shows – Gather together and watch our mesmerising illuminated Christmas tree displays. - The A Cappella Penguins – Be charmed by the smooth harmonies of our much-loved festive crooners. - Post Your Letter to Santa – Don’t forget to send your Christmas wishes Interested in attending a relaxed SEN-only session? We have some dedicated SEN-only Christmas Cracker experience sessions taking place on Saturday 28 November, and Sunday 6, Friday 11, Sunday 13, and Wednesday 16 December 2026. Please note, guests with additional needs are welcome to attend on any date and time. Our dedicated SEN sessions are set aside for families with children with additional needs, where extra provisions will be in place. Guests are advised that whilst our Christmas Cracker experience will be dedicated to SEN families during these sessions, the wider Farm Park will be open to other visitors during this time. For further information, do not hesitate to contact us. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Little Firefly Forest School, The
description: Welcome to The Little Firefly Forest School. We offer unique and high quality childcare for children aged 2 to 5 years. Our ethos is to use nature and nurture to help children grow. We are a fully outdoor forest nursery that immerses two to five year olds in nature, helping them become creative, resilient little learners. Our nursery connects children back to nature, inspiring them to live a naturally healthy lifestyle that builds resilience, confidence, independence and self-motivation; all the tools they need for a happy and successful life. We follow the core Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum, and incorporate learning in a safe and secure outdoor environment, where free play, fresh air, exposure to the natural world and physical activity are an integral part of learning. Our outdoor nursery is set in the beautiful Buckinghamshire countryside (between Thame and Aylesbury). Here we follow the core Early Year Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum, alongside free play and exploration of the great outdoors.

description: Little Forest Friends is our pre-school at Haddenham St Mary's CE School, set in our Eco Lodge and Forest School area in our beautiful rural setting. The children have constant access to the forest school and a large field as well as a warm and well equipped 'Eco Lodge.' At Little Forest Friends we follow the core Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework and incorporate learning in a safe and secure outdoor environment, where free play, fresh air, exposure to the natural world and physical activity are an integral part of learning. We provide the children with the option of free flow play between the inside and outside areas of the setting. Whilst promoting the great outdoors and we can offer a smooth transition into our Reception Year.
organisation: Haddenham St Marys' C of E School and Wraparound Care Haddenham St Mary's Church of England School, founded in 1868, provides education for all children aged between 4 and 7 within a Christian ethos. With highly qualified teachers and a nominal roll of 180 children in three "year groups", class sizes are generally of 30 or under. Overlooking open fields at the southern end of the village and next to St Mary's Church, the school aims to create a challenging, yet supportive environment, within which a broad and balanced curriculum is adapted to the individual needs of each child. All children are encouraged to be independent and use their initiative to develop their full potential. Haddenham St Mary’s School, as part of the village and wider community, encourages a feeling of respect for people of all ages and beliefs in an ever-changing world. The overall aim is to awaken the children’s skills and personal qualities providing a foundation for a fulfilled and constructive life. The classroom teacher endeavours to create an atmosphere where individuals are recognised, appreciated and encouraged. Learning to work and play together is a prime consideration. The school has successfully run a hub kitchen, "Homemade at Haddenham St Mary's", since the introduction of Universal Infant Free School Meals and the team deliver homemade hot lunches to over 400 children a day both at Haddenham St Mary's and other local schools. The school is managed by a committed Governing Body, comprised of eleven local people with a broad range of backgrounds. It is supported by an active Parent Teacher Association which raises substantial funds to enhance pupil’s learning experience through educational visits and provide additional facilities to complement National Curriculum activities. office@haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk https://haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk/

local_offer: At Little Forest Friends Pre-School, we are committed to excellence, care and fun for all. Integral to our approach is the Christian ethos of caring for one another in school, in the local community and in society. At Haddenham St Mary’s and Little Forest Friends, every child matters and everyone cares. https://haddenham-st-marys.bucks.sch.uk/general-info/special-educational-needs/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have visits from the Local Authority Early Years Consultants who support the setting to work at the highest standard. We have an Early Years SEND Advisor who visits to discuss any children we feel require additional support. We work closely with other professionals to support the children, such as Speech and Language therapist, Occupational Therapist. Any advice or targets identified are then shared with the parents and implemented in Pre-School. We encourage support and engagement with all outside agencies. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? An Introduction to Autism whole staff training All staff complete anaphylaxis and asthma training annually Specialist Teaching Service Supporting Deaf Children training All staff attend statutory safeguarding and first aid training All staff complete Level 2 food hygiene training every 3 years The SENDCo attends a termly network meeting and liaison group meetings and cascades the information to Pre-School staff We are able to attend any training necessary to support a child entering our setting. Makaton training Down Syndrome training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Little Forest Friends we operate an open door policy and staff are available to talk at the end of the session. Parents are involved in their children's learning through our online Tapestry journals, where they can comment on observations and add their own. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents and carers are welcome to talk to us anytime about their child's development and progress. Tapestry provides with an online monitoring tool to identify any additional support required. We have a termly parents evening where you are able to discuss progress and look at the activities and work your child has been doing. With the consent of parents we can contact outside agencies to access extra support needed to meet a child's needs within the setting. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Little Forest Friends Pre-School is on one level with a small step. We have a vast outdoor space with easy access to the forest school area. We have 2 disabled toilets on the main school site. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When a child starts at Little Forest Friends we will discuss the child during the first visit with the parents or carers. We talk about the child's development and any additional support they require. We will ask for information from any professional already working with the child to ensure continuity of care. Staff will chat to parents and carers about the child's likes, dislikes, interests and strengths and any support required to best settle the child into Nursery. When a child leaves Little Forest Friends we will contact the new setting and discuss the child's development and the support they have had whilst in our care. We would be happy to share information on outside agencies that have been involved in supporting the child. We would invite the new setting to come in and visit the child in their current environment to build their relationship and support their transition. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to reflect on our practise to ensure all children receive the best possible care. Our staff will attend appropriate training courses to enable us to develop the expertise needed to be able to support our children with additional needs and their families. We will also continue to liaise with outside agencies to access the support and care needed for the children in our setting. Our SENDCo attends the termly network and liaison meetings as well as the SEND conference annually and so is aware of any new developments as they arise.
