local_offer: We offer specialized tuition for students with additional academic needs, led by our fully trained specialist teachers. Additionally, we host termly workshops to help parents better understand and support their child's unique requirements.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At The Tutoring Company, our core philosophy is that academic success blossoms when students feel happy, confident, and secure. For children and young people with SEND, our aim is to empower them to realise their full potential, build lasting confidence, and foster a love of learning. We strive to make learning a joyful and empowering experience. For families, we aim to provide reassurance and practical support, ensuring parents feel equipped and confident in understanding and advocating for their child's unique educational journey. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All of the teachers working with our SEND students are fully qualified specialist teachers who are specifically trained to support additional academic needs. Our broader team consists of dedicated professionals, qualified teachers, and experienced tutors who undergo rigorous vetting and hold enhanced DBS checks. We are committed to using evidence-based methods and continuously updating our approaches to support effective learning for all students. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We believe that a strong partnership between parents, students, and tutors is essential for success. To specifically support our SEND families, we host termly workshops designed to help parents navigate, understand, and confidently support their child's additional needs. We encourage parents to be actively involved by maintaining an open dialogue with our team and attending these workshops to build a strong support network around the child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We offer several comprehensive ways to keep you fully informed about your child's learning journey: Formal Written Feedback: After key milestones, you will receive detailed written feedback through a secure email link, outlining your child's strengths and areas for development. Ongoing Progress Tracking: Parents can monitor real-time progress through weekly quizzes and assessments on our 24/7 Online Portal. Informal Verbal Updates: Our teachers are always happy to provide a brief update and answer quick questions at the end of a session when you collect your child. Scheduled Meetings: For a more in-depth conversation regarding your child's SEND provision, you can easily schedule a meeting (phone, Google Meet, or face-to-face) with your child's tutor. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our tuition centres are currently hosted within modern secondary school facilities (including The Mandeville School in Aylesbury and The Langley Academy in Slough). Because we operate out of these established educational environments, our settings benefit from standard modern school accessibility, including wheelchair-accessible entrances, accessible facilities, and appropriate indoor environments conducive to learning. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We offer a simple and welcoming onboarding process. Parents can also get in touch via the contact form on our website or by calling us directly to discuss their child's specific needs before enrolling. local_offer: Each learner receives a personalised programme based on their strengths, needs, interests, communication profile, sensory needs, and educational starting points. Support may include: - 1:1, 2:1 or small-group education - Individual learning and support planning - SEND- and autism-informed teaching - Support with emotional regulation, communication, and engagement - Functional Skills English and mathematics - Accredited creative, vocational, and life-skills learning - Independent living and preparation for adulthood - Music, outdoor, farm-based, and community learning - Pastoral mentoring and regular wellbeing check-ins - Support with attendance, routines, and re-engagement in education - Risk assessment and appropriate safeguarding arrangements - Progress monitoring and structured reviews with families and commissioners - Coordination with schools, SEND teams, and other involved professionals Where commissioned as part of the placement, KCL can also coordinate access to speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, and specialist assessment. Support is reviewed regularly and adjusted in response to the learner’s progress, wellbeing and changing needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? KCL aims to help children and young people with SEND re-engage with education, develop confidence, and make meaningful progress towards adulthood. Our intended outcomes include: - Improved engagement, attendance, and participation in learning - Increased emotional regulation, wellbeing, and resilience - Improved communication, interaction, and self-advocacy - Progress in English, mathematics, and wider curriculum learning - Achievement of appropriate qualifications and accredited units - Development of practical, vocational, and employability skills - Greater independence in daily living and community participation - Improved ability to manage routines, transitions, and unfamiliar situations - Progression into suitable education, training, employment, or supported opportunities - Successful reintegration into school or college where appropriate - A clearer understanding of each learner’s strengths, needs, and effective support strategies For families, KCL aims to provide consistent communication, greater confidence in the learner’s education, and clear evidence of progress. We work collaboratively with families, commissioners and professionals to ensure that programmes remain appropriate, responsive, and focused on agreed outcomes. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Recent SEND-specific training and continuing professional development completed across the KCL team includes: - Safeguarding children and young people - Autism awareness and autism-informed practice - Supporting learners with communication and interaction needs - Sensory processing and sensory-informed support - Social, emotional, and mental health needs - Trauma-informed and relational practice - Emotionally Based School Avoidance and re-engagement - Positive behaviour support, de-escalation, and risk management - Supporting emotional regulation, including the Zones of Regulation approach - Equality, diversity, and disability awareness - Online safety and safeguarding during remote education - Moving and handling within alternative provision settings - Emergency first aid and paediatric first aid, according to staff roles Training needs are reviewed through supervision, performance review, safeguarding updates, learner assessments, and changes in individual support needs. Staff receive additional learner-specific guidance before supporting children and young people with complex communication, sensory, health, mobility, or behavioural needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are important partners in each learner’s programme. We involve families from the initial enquiry and assessment through to planning, delivery, review, and progression. Parents and carers can be involved by: - Sharing information about the learner’s strengths, needs, interests, communication, and sensory profile - Contributing to the individual learning and support plan - Agreeing priorities and desired outcomes - Taking part in placement, EHCP, and progress reviews - Receiving regular updates about engagement, wellbeing, attendance, and progress - Sharing information about changes at home or strategies that are working - Attending meetings with KCL, commissioners, and other professionals - Providing feedback about the service and suggesting improvements - Supporting agreed learning, communication, or independence strategies at home Communication is adapted to each family’s preference and may include telephone calls, email, online meetings, and scheduled face-to-face reviews. To get involved, parents and carers can contact KCL to arrange an initial discussion, ask questions, visit an appropriate delivery setting, or discuss a potential referral. Where a placement requires public funding, KCL will work with the family and the responsible school, local authority, or commissioning organisation. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? KCL provides parents and carers with regular, clear, information about their child’s engagement, wellbeing, attendance, and educational progress. The frequency and method of communication are agreed at the start of the placement and may include telephone calls, emails, online meetings, written reports, and scheduled face-to-face reviews. Information shared may include: - Attendance and participation - Progress towards individual learning plan and EHCP outcomes - English, mathematics, and wider curriculum progress - Qualifications and accredited units achieved - Communication, emotional regulation, and social development - Independent living, vocational, and preparation-for-adulthood outcomes - Strategies that have been successful - Areas requiring further support - Agreed next steps and progression planning For children and young people with SEND, progress reporting is personalised rather than based only on age-related academic expectations. KCL records smaller steps of progress, including increased engagement, improved communication, reduced anxiety, greater tolerance of transitions, emotional regulation, and independence. Where appropriate and with consent, information is shared with the commissioning school, local authority, and involved professionals. Parents and carers contribute to reviews and help decide whether support or targets need to change. Significant safeguarding, health, or welfare concerns are communicated promptly in accordance with KCL’s safeguarding and information-sharing procedures. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? KCL delivers from a range of community, education, farm, and outdoor settings. Accessibility varies between venues, so each learner’s mobility, sensory, communication, personal-care, and environmental needs are assessed before a placement or activity begins. Reasonable adjustments may include: - Step-free or alternative access where available - Suitable seating and adapted learning spaces - Accessible or nearby toilet facilities - Quiet, low-stimulation spaces - Visual timetables, signs, and communication aids - Adjustments to lighting, noise and group size - Additional staffing and support with transitions - Flexible arrival, departure, and session arrangements - Adapted equipment and alternative activities Outdoor and farm-based environments may include uneven ground, mud, grass, animals, and changing weather conditions. Individual risk assessments are completed, and families are informed of any accessibility limitations. Alternative activities or venues are arranged where an environment cannot safely or appropriately meet a learner’s needs. Families are encouraged to discuss accessibility requirements before starting and to visit the proposed setting where appropriate. KCL will only confirm a placement once it is satisfied that the environment and agreed adjustments can meet the learner’s assessed needs safely. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? KCL placements are accessed through a local authority, school, or other authorised commissioning organisation. Families cannot normally begin a publicly funded placement through direct self-referral. Parents and carers who would like KCL to be considered should speak to their child’s: - Local authority SEND caseworker or Education, Health and Care Coordinator - School or college SENCO - Social worker or Virtual School representative, where applicable - Other professional coordinating the child’s education The local authority or responsible commissioner will send KCL a referral containing relevant information about the child or young person’s needs, EHCP, current education, desired outcomes, support requirements, and identified risks. KCL will then: 1. Review the referral and available documentation. 2. Meet the learner and family where appropriate. 3. Complete an initial suitability, safeguarding, and risk assessment. 4. Propose an individual programme, staffing arrangements, timetable, and intended outcomes. 5. Submit the proposed package and costs to the local authority or commissioner. 6. Arrange familiarisation and transition sessions once the placement and funding have been formally agreed. Families are welcome to contact KCL for information or to discuss whether the service may be suitable. However, attendance can begin only after the responsible local authority or commissioning organisation has approved and funded the placement. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? KCL plans to develop its SEND provision in response to learner needs, family feedback, and local commissioning priorities. Our development priorities include: - Expanding personalised 1:1 and small-group capacity - Developing additional vocational pathways in construction, electrical skills, cookery, creative arts, and independent living - Expanding the KCL Music Academy and accredited creative programmes - Increasing farm-based, animal-assisted, equine, and outdoor learning opportunities - Broadening access to Functional Skills, NCFE qualifications, AQA Unit Award Scheme, Arts Award, and GQAL PEARL - Strengthening preparation-for-adulthood, employability, and supported progression routes - Increasing access to speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, and specialist assessment where commissioned - Improving the accessibility and sensory suitability of learning environments - Developing staff knowledge through SEND-specific training and reflective practice - Strengthening transition planning with families, schools, colleges, and local authorities - Using learner and family feedback to improve programme design and service quality KCL’s aim is to develop a sustainable network of small, supportive learning environments while maintaining personalised planning, low learner-to-staff ratios, and clear evidence of progress and outcomes.

name: Voicebridge Solutions
description: Voice Bridge Solutions is an independent transition consultancy, future care planning, and crisis advocacy service operating across Oxfordshire and neighbouring borders. Led by a highly experienced consultant holding a Level 5 in Leadership and Management for Adult Care, the service supports young people (aged 14 plus) and adults with learning disabilities and autism, alongside their families. Specialising in the "Preparing for Adulthood" pathway, Voice Bridge Solutions acts as an objective, independent, bridge between families and statutory bodies. The service resolves complex transition blockages across housing pathways, Care Act 2014 thresholds, and health funding disputes. By working closely with families, deep person-centred insight is captured and translated into practical operational guidance- such as bespoke "Top 10 for Every Carer" profiles- to guarantee absolute continuity of care. Services include independent mediation to de-escalate care plan or EHCP conflicts before they reach formal tribunals, and practical housing readiness mapping. Operating on a private fee, Direct Payments, or Personal Health Budget (PHB) basis, Voice Bridge Solutions provides intensive, bespoke navigation support for self-funding families who require dedicated guidance through the health and social care landscape. Voice Bridge Solutions is a mobile and remote service. We do not have a public office or clinic for drop-ins. All support is delivered directly in the community, at the client's home, within statutory meeting settings, or remotely through secure video consultation.

local_offer: Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Local Offer sets out the support available in Haringey for children aged 0 to 5 with SEND. This includes children and young people with or without an Education, Health, and Care (EHC) plan. We aim to: - Provide clear, accessible information about available services and support. - Ensure that children with SEND, and their parents and carers, are listened to when local services are developed and reviewed. You can see the types of support you can get through the SEND Local Offer, including: - Education - Health - Social Care You can also use the local borough directory to see local organisations, services, and activities that support children and young people with SEND:  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to give children the best possible start to their education. To achieve this, we: - Work with families to seek support from outside agencies when appropriate. - Implement recommended strategies tailored to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SEND-specific training our team : - Supporting Children with a Hearing Impairment - Speech and Language Development - Understanding Autism - EY SENCO Training (local borough) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We actively involve parents through: - Regular stay-and-play sessions, events, and activities. - Providing access to an online record system for sharing observations and photos. - Termly parents' sessions to discuss children’s progress. - Frequent updates and meetings tailored to children with SEND. - Opportunities to meet professionals, such as speech and language therapists or occupational therapists. - Assess Plan Do review weekly catch ups How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? -Asses Plan Do review weekly catch up -Regular meetings and updates How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment at Kinderzimmer is accessible for all. The entrance area is flat for wheelchair accessibility. We have a disable lift and toilets. We provide disable parking. Our outdoor environment is set up to be accessible for wheelchair use as well as safe for different abilities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? To register an interest in our service a family can book a tour to visit our setting. During this tour the family would be shown the setting and have opportunities to discuss in further our SEND policy and procedures. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We continue to look at improving our services here at Kinderzimmer. We will be regularly attending training through the local authority as well as within other training platforms. We encourage feedback from families to look how we can widen our inclusivity further.

local_offer: First Steps First is a family run day nursery for children aged from 0 to 5 years olds, where we are an enthusiastic and fun loving team, who strive to meet the needs of all the children in the setting and give them the best start in life as possible and plan and meet their needs on a individual basis.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our setting aims to ensure that children and young people with SEND feel safe, valued, included and supported to reach their full potential. We aim to promote their communication, confidence, independence, social skills and emotional wellbeing through personalised support and inclusive activities tailored to their individual needs. For families, we aim to provide reassurance, clear communication and strong partnership working, ensuring parents and carers feel listened to, involved in decision-making and confident that their child’s needs are understood and supported. We also work closely with relevant professionals and other services where appropriate to ensure children receive consistent and effective support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff have recently completed SEND-specific training to strengthen their understanding of identifying and supporting children with additional needs. Training has included recognising early signs of SEND, supporting communication and language development, promoting inclusion and adapting activities and the learning environment to meet individual needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We involve parents and carers as an important part of their child’s learning, development and care. We maintain regular communication through daily discussions, updates, meetings and sharing information about children’s progress and individual needs. Parents are encouraged to share their child’s interests, routines, strengths and any concerns so that we can provide consistent and personalised support. Parents can get involved by speaking with their child’s key person or nursery staff, attending meetings and reviews, contributing ideas and feedback, sharing activities or interests from home, and working with us to identify and support their child’s individual needs. We welcome parents to be actively involved in their child’s nursery experience and decision-making. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We will keep parents and carers regularly informed about their child’s progress through daily conversations, observations, progress updates, parent meetings and communication with their child’s key person. We will share information about their child’s achievements, learning, development, wellbeing and any areas where they may need further support. For children with SEND, we will provide additional and more personalised communication. This may include more frequent meetings and progress updates, individual support plans, detailed observations, regular reviews and agreed next steps How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our nursery aims to provide an inclusive, welcoming and accessible environment for all children, including children with SEND. Indoors, we provide clear spaces, accessible resources, suitable furniture and a range of activities that can be adapted to individual children’s needs. We use visual support, sensory resources and different ways of communicating where appropriate. Our outdoor area is safe, accessible and provides opportunities for children to explore, play and develop their physical skills. Activities and equipment can be adapted to ensure that children with different abilities can participate fully. We regularly review the environment and make reasonable adjustments where needed, working with parents, the SENCO and other professionals to ensure each child can access and enjoy the setting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children and families can start using our service by contacting the nursery directly to arrange an initial visit or discussion. We welcome parents and carers to talk to us about their child’s needs, strengths, interests and any additional support they may require before starting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to continue developing our SEND provision by building staff knowledge and confidence through ongoing SEND training and professional development. We will regularly review our policies, resources and learning environment to ensure they remain inclusive and accessible to all children.

description: Online coding and game development clubs for children aged 6 to 16, plus a self-paced version with no fixed session time. Children work in small groups with a mentor, building games in Scratch, Roblox, Minecraft, and Python. Sessions run over the internet from home, so there is no travel and no busy hall to walk into. Mentors follow the child's lead rather than pushing them through a fixed lesson, which suits autistic and ADHD children and children with a demand avoidant profile. local_offer: Every session runs online in a small group, which removes most of the things children find hardest about a club: the travel, the noise, the crowded room, and the pressure to arrive on time. Cameras and microphones are always optional, and a child can type in the chat instead of speaking for as long as they need to. Mentors follow the child's lead rather than pushing them through a fixed lesson, which matters a great deal for children with a demand avoidant profile. A child who wants to spend a whole term on one game is allowed to. We hold the National Autistic Society's Autism Inclusion Award.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? That a child finds something they are good at and want to keep doing, and that they build a relationship with an adult outside the family and school. For a lot of the children we work with, coding is the first thing they have stuck at voluntarily. We are not aiming at qualifications or a set curriculum. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All mentors are DBS checked and complete safeguarding training. We went through the National Autistic Society's Autism Inclusion Award assessment, which included autism training for the mentor team and a review of how we run sessions. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents can talk to us before their child's first session about what does and does not work for them, and can email or call us at any point after that. Parents are welcome to sit in on a session with their child if that helps them settle. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We are in touch by email, and parents can call us. If something changes for a child, or a session has not gone well, we would rather talk about it early than let it build up. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There is no building to come to. Children take part from home on a computer or laptop, so a child can sit in their own room, wear headphones, move around, stim, or leave the call for a few minutes and come back. Nothing about the physical environment is under our control, which is the point: the child is already somewhere they feel safe. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Book a free taster session on our website, or call 0333 090 5697 and we will talk it through first. There is no referral, no waiting list and no assessment. The taster is genuinely free and there is nothing to pay unless the child wants to carry on. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continuing to work on the self-paced Academy option, which exists for children who cannot manage a fixed session time, and on keeping group sizes small enough that every child gets attention from a mentor.

local_offer: Individual Mentoring: GROVE’s Individual Mentoring provides a safe, affirming space for Autistic children and young people to feel heard, understood and supported. Mentoring is child-led and tailored, allowing young people to set their own goals or simply spend time being themselves in a supportive environment. Our Autistic Mentors bring both lived experience and specialist knowledge of autism theory and practice, enabling genuine understanding and connection. Sessions may include conversation, sensory play, gaming, creative activities, or exploring special interests. We adapt our activities to suit the young person rather than mentoring through one medium. Through shared experience and reflective practice, mentoring supports the development of self-understanding, self-compassion, and positive Autistic identity. Mentors draw on lived experience to provide language and insight that help young people make sense of their experiences and identity. Peer Groups: GROVE offers small online groups for social connection (typically 4 to 8 young people) facilitated by 1 or 2 Autistic Mentors. Groups provide opportunities for Autistic young people to connect over shared interests, build community, foster belonging, and feel understood as their authentic selves. Sessions are low-demand, flexible, and responsive, shaped by the group’s interests and needs, and may include games, creative activities, and meaningful discussion. Being Me: ‘BEING ME’ is a completely unique 10-week online group for Autistic young people, led by specialist Autistic Mentors and co-designed with our team of Young Leaders, using the latest affirming research on Autistic experience, identity and wellbeing. ‘BEING ME’ offers a safe, thoughtful, space for young people to begin a journey – with peers who ‘get it’ and Autistic Mentors who bring deep knowledge and lived experience. Together, we explore what being Autistic – and being ourselves – means, feels like and can look like in everyday life. At the heart of the programme is a gentle but powerful process: Getting to know ourselves. Learning to value what makes us who we are and finding ways to be more fully ourselves – in ways that feel safe, feel right, and feel possible. This programme is tailored to the specific group we’re working with. That means we adapt the content and approach to suit the individuals taking part. We aim to make each session meaningful, engaging, and relevant, supporting everyone to take part in ways that work for them. Our BEING ME programme is an ideal complement to individual mentoring where the Mentor can then expand upon, deepen concepts, and explore them in the real context of everyday life for the young person.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? GROVE'S Neuro-Affirming Foundations: - Our approaches are grounded in the principles of Neurodiversity Paradigm. - We recognise the pervasive role of ableism within society, including the influence of internalised ableism. We aim to challenge ableist narratives about neurodivergent people. - We are committed to being anti-racist. - We are committed to being LGBTQIA+ affirming. - We recognise and respect each individual’s intersectional identity and are committed to unpacking one’s own privilege. - We aspire to work in a way that is trauma informed. - We respect all forms of communication and presume competence. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? GROVE’s Founder and Director is a former teacher with a Master’s degree in Autism (Distinction). Across our team, Mentors hold qualifications including PGCert, BA, MA to PhD level in autism, and several contribute internationally to autism research, training and writing. This sets us apart from any other mentoring organisation in the country. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We offer regular feedback to families about their child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Provision is delivered online, allowing flexibility around time, energy levels and access needs. Support can be tailored to align with EHCP outcomes where this is compatible with a child-led, neuro-affirming approach. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact us at hello@gr0ve.org for more information on our services. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: Orkney New Adventures provides personalised 1:1 educational support for children and young people with SEND, including autism, ADHD, communication and interaction needs, cognition and learning needs, and social, emotional and mental health difficulties. Support is individually planned around the child or young person, with an emphasis on building trust, confidence, and engagement. I recognise that some children may have had difficult experiences within education or may currently be unable to access a traditional school environment, and sessions are adapted to their individual needs, abilities, interests, and communication style.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My aim is to help each child or young person feel safe, understood, and able to engage positively with learning. Outcomes are individual to each learner and may include increased confidence and independence, improved engagement and communication, academic progress, development of life skills and, where appropriate, supporting a gradual return to education. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Relevant training and qualifications include an Understanding Autism Diploma, Higher Level Teaching Assistant (HLTA), Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA), Child Mental Health, Safeguarding Children, Prevent/Extremism and Radicalisation, and Equality, Diversity and Inclusion training. Ongoing professional development forms an important part of my practice. A list of my qualifications can be found on my website. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers are an important part of the support I provide. I work collaboratively with families to understand their child's individual needs, interests, strengths, and areas where additional support may be helpful. Parents are encouraged to share information and discuss any changes or concerns that may affect their child's learning or wellbeing. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Regular communication is maintained with parents and carers, including feedback on learning, engagement, and progress. Where appropriate, written updates can also be provided. For children with SEND, progress is considered individually and may include confidence, communication, emotional regulation, independence, and engagement alongside academic development. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Orkney New Adventures does not operate from a fixed tutoring centre. Tuition is usually provided in the child or young person’s home, allowing them to learn in a familiar, comfortable, environment. Parents or carers can discuss any individual accessibility or support needs with me before tuition begins to ensure the learning environment is appropriate for the child. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents, carers, and professionals are welcome to make contact to discuss the child or young person's individual needs and whether the service would be suitable. An initial conversation allows us to consider the support required, proposed outcomes, location, and availability before any tutoring arrangement begins. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I aim to continue developing my SEND provision through ongoing professional development, keeping my knowledge and training up to date and continuing to develop personalised resources and approaches that reflect the individual needs of the children and young people I support.

description: Oh no! There’s been a Christmas disaster- Santa’s reindeer have escaped, and he needs your help to find them before Christmas Eve! Join us for a magical festive adventure at Didcot Railway Centre. As you explore our unique 21-acre living museum- home to Great Western Railway steam locomotives, carriages, wagons, buildings, and fascinating artefacts- you’ll help Santa track down his missing reindeer at special reindeer stations hidden around the site. Every child will receive a special passport and a Christmas stocking on arrival. At each reindeer station you find, you’ll collect a small gift as a reward for your detective work. Your journey ends with a visit to Santa’s giant toy workshop, where you can tell him what’s on your Christmas list and choose your own present from his festive selection! Your ticket also includes unlimited train rides on our main demonstration line throughout the day. Our café will be open serving a range of festive refreshments, and there’s plenty of time to explore our original 1932 GWR Engine Shed- where you can admire beautifully restored locomotives and even climb onto the footplate of some! Come and make magical Christmas memories for the whole family. Book now to avoid disappointment!

name: A Christmas Carol - Performed by Gerald Dickens
description: Join us for an exclusive performance of 'A Christmas Carol' performed by Gerald Dickens. We are delighted that Gerald will be back to Didcot Railway Centre for a fourth year after sell out performances in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Gerald is an actor, author, director, and producer, and is the great great grandson of the author Charles Dickens. In 1993 he created his first one-man show, a theatrical performance of A Christmas Carol inspired by Charles Dickens’ own energetic readings of the 1860s. A fascination with the life and works of Charles led him to write and direct further one-man shows including Mr Dickens is Coming!, Nicholas Nickleby, and Sketches by Boz. He regularly performs in major theatres and arts centres as well as at hotels and stately homes. He also appears at several arts and literary festivals in the UK and has been entertaining cruise ship passengers worldwide since 2007. You'll need to arrive for 5pm and gather in our patio area for transporting down to our transfer shed where the performance will take please. The performance will start at 6pm, so don't be late! There'll be a short interval and we'll transport you back up to the cafe where warming mulled wine and mince pies will be served, during which time Gerald will be available to talk to you about his experiences. After the performance, there'll be a chance to shop as our gift shop will be open. Gerald will be on hand to sign copies of his books 'Dickens and Staplehurst, A Biography of a Train Crash' and 'My Life on the Road with A Christmas Carol', which make perfect Christmas gifts. The evening will end at approximately 9pm. Please note to dress for the weather. Although the transfer shed is under cover, it is outside, so warm clothing is advised. Hand warmers will be provided.

name: A Christmas Carol - Performed by Gerald Dickens
description: Join us for an exclusive performance of 'A Christmas Carol' performed by Gerald Dickens. We are delighted that Gerald will be back to Didcot Railway Centre for a fourth year after sell out performances in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Gerald is an actor, author, director, and producer, and is the great great grandson of the author Charles Dickens. In 1993 he created his first one-man show, a theatrical performance of A Christmas Carol inspired by Charles Dickens’ own energetic readings of the 1860s. A fascination with the life and works of Charles led him to write and direct further one-man shows including Mr Dickens is Coming!, Nicholas Nickleby, and Sketches by Boz. He regularly performs in major theatres and arts centres as well as at hotels and stately homes. He also appears at several arts and literary festivals in the UK and has been entertaining cruise ship passengers worldwide since 2007. You'll need to arrive for 5pm and gather in our patio area for transporting down to our transfer shed where the performance will take please. The performance will start at 6pm, so don't be late! There'll be a short interval and we'll transport you back up to the cafe where warming mulled wine and mince pies will be served, during which time Gerald will be available to talk to you about his experiences. After the performance, there'll be a chance to shop as our gift shop will be open. Gerald will be on hand to sign copies of his books 'Dickens and Staplehurst, A Biography of a Train Crash' and 'My Life on the Road with A Christmas Carol', which make perfect Christmas gifts. The evening will end at approximately 9pm. Please note to dress for the weather. Although the transfer shed is under cover, it is outside, so warm clothing is advised. Hand warmers will be provided.

name: Royal Ballet and Opera: Manon
description: Event cinema screening. In the seedy underbelly of eighteenth-century Paris, money is king. Nothing is sacred – even love itself can be bought for the right price. A native of this hedonistic underworld, Manon is caught between twin desires when she falls in love with the student Des Grieux. Steadfast and devoted, he offers the possibility of an honourable life. Yet, the riches promised by the world of Parisian society remain tempting... Manon’s inner turmoil and struggle for survival lie at the devastating heart of Kenneth MacMillan’s 1974 adaptation of Abbé Prévost’s novel. In this signature work of The Royal Ballet, MacMillan’s nuanced understanding of human psychology makes for an unflinching look into the moral degradation of Manon’s Paris, while all its decadence and decay are brought to life through Jules Massenet’s score and Nicholas Georgiadis’s designs. description: A festive celebration showcasing the talent of local groups who call Norden Farm home. Connect with your community and celebrate through song, live music, and dance. All tickets go towards the Norden Farm Forever Fund, helping us secure our future for the next generation. Please visit our website to learn more and to book your tickets.
organisation: Norden Farm Centre for the Arts | Maidenhead Norden Farm is built on the site of an old Dairy Farm. It is an umbrella organisation of local arts groups committed to this vision. Back in the Café Bar, artwork on the walls keep you posted about upcoming films, gigs, plays and classes. The Box Office is open all day so you can book for something fun while you’re here. Tell staff what you’re interested in seeing or taking part in and they’ll recommend something special for you. The music you’ll hear comes courtesy of forthcoming gigs. A poster next to the specials board tells you who’s playing and when they’re on. boxoffice@nordenfarm.org https://norden.farm/

name: Braythorpe- Education Support for Parents and Families
description: Braythorpe helps parents and carers make sense of what is happening for their child in education and work out what to do next. Support is particularly suited to families navigating school anxiety, behaviour that looks different at home and school, difficult school meetings, transitions, SEND concerns, adoption, kinship care, and the impact of trauma or early experiences on education. Founded by a former Deputy Headteacher and adoptive parent, Braythorpe brings together an understanding of how schools work with the lived reality of being on the parent side of the table. Support includes one-to-one parent sessions, practical guides and resources, and help preparing for conversations with schools. Remote appointments are available, including evenings and weekends.

I have produced over 50 podcast episodes on a range of neurodevelopmental concerns, with experts as Invited guests. description: Bravecore Counselling CIC is a not-for-profit organisation providing affordable online counselling for adults across the UK, with no waiting list. Services are available every day of the week, evenings included (8am to 9pm). We offer a safe, confidential, and supportive space where individuals can explore challenges such as anxiety, stress, depression, low self-esteem, bereavement, relationship difficulties, and life changes. local_offer: I provide a warm, inclusive and nurturing environment where every child is welcomed, valued and supported, whatever their individual needs or abilities. I work closely with parents and carers to understand each child’s strengths, interests and needs, supporting early identification and putting appropriate strategies in place. Where needed, I will work in partnership with other professionals and agencies to ensure children receive the right support. I have experience supporting children with a range of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). I am committed to ongoing learning and will undertake relevant training where required to ensure I can provide the best possible care, support and learning opportunities for every child. My aim is for every child to feel safe, included, confident and happy within my setting, while being supported to learn, grow and thrive at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? For every child to feel safe, included, confident and happy within my setting, while being supported to learn, grow and thrive at their own pace. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I encourage open and regular communication so that we can work together to understand and support each child’s individual needs. I welcome parents sharing information about their child’s strengths, interests, routines and any concerns they may have. We can work together to agree ways to support their child both at home and within my setting. Parents are encouraged to share their ideas, ask questions and be involved in reviewing their child’s progress and next steps. Where appropriate, I will also work alongside other professionals involved with the child, with parental consent, to ensure everyone is working together to provide consistent support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Through daily conversations, observations and ongoing communication. I will share achievements, interests and any areas where your child may need additional support. For children with SEND, I will work closely with parents to identify individual needs and agree appropriate support. I will monitor progress regularly and review what is working well, making adjustments where needed. With parental consent, I can also liaise with relevant professionals and share appropriate information to help ensure your child receives consistent and effective support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Indoors, children have access to a range of age-appropriate resources and activities, with spaces that can be adapted to support different learning styles, sensory needs and abilities. I can provide quieter areas for children who may need time away from busy or stimulating activities. Outdoors, I provide opportunities for children to enjoy fresh air, physical activity, exploration and play. I will adapt activities and resources where needed so that children with SEND can participate as fully as possible. I will work closely with parents and, where appropriate, other professionals to understand any accessibility requirements and identify suitable adaptations or additional resources to support each child. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact me directly What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? My future plans include continuing to attend relevant SEND training and keeping up to date with guidance and best practice. I will continue to develop my range of sensory, communication and inclusive resources and adapt activities to meet individual children’s needs. I also aim to build positive relationships with local SEND professionals and other support services so that I can access advice and guidance when needed. I will regularly review my SEND provision, taking into account feedback from children, parents and professionals, and make changes where appropriate to ensure my setting remains inclusive and supportive for all children.

description: Farnham Maltings is proud to present a bold new adaptation of The Tailor of Gloucester inspired by the tale by Beatrix Potter, written by Alex Kanefsky (Cable Street) and featuring an electrifying original score by double Olivier Award winner Darren Clark (The Curious Case of Benjamin Button). In a town being drained of colour, a struggling tailor and a trio of sharp, ambitious, mice finally find themselves on the brink of success. Fame and fortune await but to what consequence for their friends and neighbours? Packed with live music that blends rock and pop, inventive puppetry, jokes, mischief, and surprises, a cast of four spin this classic story into something fresh, funny, and full of heart. A fast, funny, and big-hearted show about courage, community, and the power of doing good - even when no one’s watching! Bold, musical, and bursting with colour - perfect for all generations to enjoy together, age guide: 3 plus! name: Hogshaw School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
description: It’s time for some magic and mystery this Halloween as you enter Hogshaw School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Little witches and wizards of all ages are invited to join us for a nature-inspired Halloween day out this October half term. Your Halloween event ticket includes everything you need for a magical day out, including a free pumpkin for every child, pumpkin decorating, potion making, encounters with rare creatures, birds of prey display, and bags of indoor and outdoor play space to test out new spells! Explore the whole farm park, follow our Halloween trail and enjoy a packed programme of Halloween activities and animal encounters. Fancy dress is actively encouraged! Please visit our website to learn more and to book your tickets.
organisation: Hogshaw Farm and Wildlife Park An environmentally friendly 44 acre rare breeds farm attraction in Aylesbury Vale for all ages. Located in beautiful open countryside where there is plenty of space for children to play and explore outdoors and indoors. As well as special seasonal events, the Animal Barn, Pets Corner and Wildlife Zone, we have a daily programme which children will love. They also have the chance to let off steam inside the two indoor play barns, or outside where there is plenty of play equipment and a nature trail. There's fresh homemade food in the Eco Centre Cafe and Barn Cafe that's supplied by local producers and from our own walled garden, where we grow heritage fruit and vegetables. The restaurant is on the ground floor of our lovely timber-framed building, whilst on the first floor with stunning views is our purpose built conference/party room available for hire. We have 'Farmer for a Day', 'Ranger for a Day' and 'Animal Experiences' available for all ages. info@greendragonecofarm.co.uk https://www.greendragonecofarm.co.uk//

We believe in providing a broad, enriching and enjoyable curriculum that caters for children’s individual strengths and needs. https://www.littlemissendenschool.co.uk/page/?title=SEND&pid=41 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We recognise that some children will require additional support or challenge and to achieve this we will strive to eliminate any barriers to learning which could hinder or exclude individual pupils. We believe that all children should feel safe and valued in school and we will work hard to eliminate prejudice and discrimination. We support the development of the whole child, whilst valuing and celebrating the many and varied abilities displayed by all children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff may receive individual training from external sources related to any child with SEND they may be supporting for example supporting children with Speech and Language needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? It is important to engage parents in their children’s learning and value their input. Appointments can be made with the class teacher, SENDCo and Headteacher to discuss individual pupils in detail at any time during the school year. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Appropriate support and procedures are put in place so that all children can participate in extra-curricular activities. Risk assessments are carried out for pupils with SEND. If it is deemed that an intensive level of 1:1 support is required an additional adult will accompany the child during the activity. name: Making it REAL (Wycombe - September)
description: Making it REAL has been developed for parents and carers who would like to support their child's reading and writing from an early age. Making it REAL is a 6-week programme for Parents and Carers of children aged 18 months to 4 years. Children and parents/carers attend the workshops together. It includes an introductory session, 4 themed sessions, and a one-to-one session designed to support you and your children to get started with the activities at home. The play-based sessions are fun and relaxed and have been based on the programme from the National Children’s Bureau. Topics covered Based on the 4 strands of literacy – books, oral language, early writing, and environmental print. Parents and carers will also learn what they can do to support the child’s learning: opportunity, recognition, interaction, and modelling.

It includes an introductory session, 4 themed sessions, and a one-to-one session designed to support you and your children to get started with the activities at home. local_offer: Tuned for Growth provides personalised music wellbeing sessions for children and young people, using music and creative activities to support interoception, emotional awareness, self-regulation, confidence, communication, self-expression, and engagement. Sessions help children to notice and understand internal body signals, recognise how these can relate to emotions, and develop strategies that support their individual wellbeing and regulation. Sessions are adapted to meet individual needs and can support children and young people with a range of SEND needs, including autism, ADHD, communication and interaction needs, cognition and learning needs, and social, emotional and mental health difficulties.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to help children and young people develop greater awareness of their internal body signals and emotional states, build confidence and self-awareness, develop personalised regulation strategies, communicate and express themselves, and increase their engagement and sense of wellbeing. We aim to provide children with practical tools and experiences that they can transfer into everyday life and learning. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have experience supporting children and young people with SEND through my previous work as a Teaching Assistant, working alongside school staff to support individual needs, communication, emotional wellbeing, engagement, and participation. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents and carers can be involved in discussions about their child's needs, goals, and progress. Where appropriate, I work with parents and carers to understand what is important to the child and to identify strategies that may support them outside of sessions. Parents and carers can contact Tuned for Growth to discuss the service and their child's needs, ask questions, and provide feedback. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Progress will be discussed with parents and carers throughout the support, with feedback provided about the child's engagement, strengths, development and progress towards agreed goals. For children with SEND, sessions are adapted to their individual needs and progress is considered in relation to their starting point and individual outcomes. Where appropriate, I can work alongside parents, carers, and school staff to share relevant observations and identify strategies that may support the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The session space is accessed by steps and is not currently wheelchair accessible. The environment can be adapted where possible to support individual sensory, communication, and wellbeing needs. Please contact Tuned for Growth before booking to discuss any specific accessibility requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families, schools and professionals can contact Tuned for Growth directly to discuss the child or young person’s needs and whether the service is suitable. An initial discussion will help identify the child’s needs, interests, and goals and whether music wellbeing sessions would be an appropriate form of support. Sessions can then be arranged directly with the family or through the child’s school or other setting. Some sessions are also available for families to book directly through www.bookwhen.com/tunedforgrowth What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Tuned for Growth is continuing to develop its SEND provision by expanding opportunities for children and young people to access music wellbeing support. Future plans include developing partnerships with schools and other organisations, developing resources and approaches to support interoception, emotional awareness and self-regulation, and continuing to develop ways of measuring and demonstrating individual progress. I also plan to continue building my knowledge and training in SEND and related areas to ensure the provision develops in response to the needs of the children and young people I support.

local_offer: Children at Little Oaks at The Parish Rooms are aged 18 months - 3 1/2, moving from here up to Little Oaks at Tylers Green for their final year before school. We have high expectations of all children, regardless of their starting points or any additional needs. Our deliberate policy of recruiting a highly-qualified and experienced team in much higher numbers than is legally required means that we can address additional needs quickly and without waiting for additional funding. At Little Oaks @ The Parish Rooms we are proud of our personalised approach and always take great care to get to know our children and their families really well, in order to best serve them. We make all reasonable adjustments to meet children's needs and aim to run a fully inclusive, warm and welcoming nursery. We encourage parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share their children’s successes, achievements, concerns and hopes for the future.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We regularly interact with the Speech and Language (SLT) service from the Buckinghamshire Healthcare Trust, as well as any therapists employed privately by parents, as a relatively high number of children present with speech, hearing or social communication difficulties. We are also able to access the services of educational psychologists, paediatric doctors and organisations like Sparkles, which provides Speech and Language Therapy, Physiotherapy and Occupational therapy for preschool children with Down Syndrome. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Anna Cooper is our SENCO for all our nurseries. We have experience in writing EHC applications and working with outside agencies. Staff team follow in-house and online training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are included and embraced from the start, with a clear introduction to our philosophy. We believe children are best supported when parents and staff work together; working in close partnership with parents and other adults in a child’s life, we ensure that Little Oaks is a happy and nurturing place for all who are part of it. Parents are invited to participate in nursery life in a way that suits them - this could be visiting to play with their own child, liaising about settling in, sharing an area of interest to the whole nursery or a small group. We also fully understand that for some parents, their main need is to be able to leave their child in our care and head off to work, so we support them with regular communication to reassure and set minds at rest. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All parents receive at least one notification per week of their child's progress, via our online observation and record-keeping system, eyLog. Where there are specific concerns about a child's progress (whether flagged up to us by parents or noticed by practitioners once the child is with us), we will begin more frequent, possibly targeted observations, sharing with parents as we go. This enables us to put in place strategies to support a child, or to draft in additional professional support, or both. Children with SEND are treated, like all children, as individuals with their own specific needs, talents and skills. Depending on particular needs we may apply for additional support or we may offer it in-house from our own experienced team. All of these decisions will be taken in conjunction with parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Little Oaks at The Parish Rooms is accessed via the front garden, a flat and even surface from the road. There is a ramp to alleviate the step up into the building. Once inside, there are two rooms where a step down is required; the ramp can be moved anywhere in the building as required. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Every child and family is different, and so we have a range of strategies we might employ to support transitions. Our aim is for children to settle quickly and happily, allowing their confidence to grow so that they are able to benefit from all the learning experiences around them, without feelings of anxiety or insecurity. There are many potential approaches, so we'd be delighted to discuss these with you if you'd like to get in touch. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? From time to time there is a very good, focussed course available on a specific area of SEND, and to encourage staff to attend. Most practitioners engaged in Autism training in 2023-2024.

searchText:
name: Autumn Book Fair
description: Calling all book worms! Join us for a book fair at Stowe. From Friday 23 October to Sunday 1 November we encourage you to browse our wide selection of donated books as we expand our displays at New Inn. Come and celebrate books and reading with us at our Autumn Book Fair, showcasing our range of fiction, non-fiction, vintage, and collectable books. There will be best-sellers from last year to ones maybe 150 years old; complete sets to signed editions, old favourites to rare volumes. Every purchase you make raises valuable funds to help look after the beautiful landscape at Stowe for everyone, for ever. Please visit our website to learn more.
organisation: Stowe Gardens | National Trust Gardening on the grandest scale in this Georgian landscape garden and park The scale and beauty of Stowe have attracted visitors for over 300 years. Picture-perfect views, winding paths, lakeside walks and temples create a timeless landscape, reflecting the changing seasons. Full of hidden meaning, the gardens were created as an earthly paradise and still cast their spell today. Your visit starts at the New Inn visitor centre outside the gardens. This fusion of modern and restored eighteenth-century buildings was where visitors of the past were welcomed to Stowe. Stop by the light and airy cafe for delicious fresh food and the shop for unique products inspired by the gardens. The sheer size and space is perfect for those who love the outdoors and enjoy walking. Stowe is great to explore all day long when you combine a visit to Stowe House or explore the far reaches of the garden and parkland to make the most of your day. Come back time and time again to discover new routes by following the mown grass paths in the garden or take a vigorous ramble in the parkland where more monuments wait to be explored and see new views you won't find in the garden. stowe@nationaltrust.org.uk https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/stowe

name: Santa Paws Community Dog Walk
description: Get into the Christmas spirit with our festive Santa Paws Community Dog Walk, in collaboration with Tails on the Trails and Inspiring Tails. Gather your four-legged friends, pop on a Christmas jumper (for you or your pup!), and join us for a cheerful winter walk through the grounds. This relaxed community walk is the perfect opportunity to enjoy the fresh air, meet fellow dog lovers, and celebrate the season with like-minded canine companions. Along the route, the team from Tails on the Trails and Inspiring Tails will be on hand with friendly advice and practical tips on everything from lead walking and enrichment to confidence building and winter adventures with your dog. Meet your walk leader at the entrance to the gardens (Bell Gate) at 10:30am. The walk will take approximately one and a half hours, although you're welcome to head off earlier if your furry friend prefers a shorter stroll. Expect plenty of wagging tails, festive cheer, and the chance to make some new dog-loving friends along the way. Dogs must remain on leads at all times. Why not dress your pooch in their festive finest and join us for a paws-itively merry morning? This event is free, but normal admission charges apply. Please visit our website to learn more.

name: Christmas at Greys Court
description: The stories and characters of beloved childhood literature have spilled off the pages and into the house and gardens of Greys Court. Venture into the gardens to discover immersive worlds and characters amongst twinkling lights and festive touches. Explorers of all ages will be able to seek out favourite characters and items from the stories hidden amongst the foliage and greenery. With twinkling lights, sumptuously adorned trees and the lingering smells of Christmas baking, visit the warmth of the manor house and puzzle out the stories on display. Run off some energy and challenge your family and friends to games on the Old Tennis Court. Visit the Christmas second hand book shop on the first floor of the Cromwellian building whilst downstairs, find the spooky story of the Mistletoe Chest for a grown up Christmas story with a twist. Greys Court is closed on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day. This event is free with standard admission. Please visit our website to learn more.

local_offer: Little Oaks @ Tylers Green is a privately owned nursery based at Tylers Green First School. We are proud of our personalised approach and always take great care to get to know our children and their families really well, in order to best serve them. We know that we are well-loved within the community, having opened in 2002, and are keen to always maintain that relationship of trust and mutual respect that is crucial to our service. We make all reasonable adjustments to meet children's needs and aim to run a fully inclusive, warm and welcoming nursery. We encourage parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share their children’s successes, achievements, concerns and hopes for the future. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace. Our November 2022 OFSTED report was Outstanding. Little Oaks: Great Expectations!  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are in touch with all branches of professional services including Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists and specialist teaching services, helping us to aim for the very best outcomes for all children. We are happy to advise as needs are discovered. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Anna Cooper is our SENCO for all our nurseries. We have experience in writing EHC applications and working with outside agencies. Staff team follow in-house and online training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parental involvement is warmly encouraged right from the start. We are keen to be in regular communication by whatever method works best for you, whether this is face-to-face meetings, email, written feedback/discussions, phone calls or video calls. Please share your ideas, concerns and suggestions and you can be sure they will always be considered. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use our robust observation systems to identify any additional needs, and will talk to you as soon as we have a concern. From then on we will be in communication as we set plans together with you for your child's learning. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Even, flat entrance and wheelchair-accessible throughout. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please ask us about our transition programme! We prepare children exceptionally well for any change and this is no different. Do call 07437 689158 or email enquiries@little-oaks.org for a tour. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We offer in-house training every term and encourage practitioners to attend external training. Sometimes this may be connected to a specific child's needs, and at others is more general.

description: Connect with nature by exploring the site whilst having fun with your family! Family Fun Days are a great way to spend a morning or afternoon in nature! Activities are primarily aimed at children aged 3 to 11 years old, but the whole family can enjoy themselves! This October we are running a fire lighting workshop and roasting marshmallows. organisation: Iver Environment Centre (Iver Heath) Iver Environment Centre offers an inspiring industry accredited education programme based on exploring the world around us for Key Stages 1 to 3 and the Early years foundation stage (EYFS). Our highly skilled staff will provide the expertise and resources necessary to enable your children to develop their key skills across the full range of national curriculum subjects. Each experience is tailored to meet your children's learning needs and is delivered within our safe and exciting centre. Education opportunities we offer: Naturewatch River Detectives Food Growing Early Years Outdoors Rainforest Experience Other opportunities: Centre hire Birthday Parties School Holiday Family Fun Days If you are interested in volunteering at the Centre we have a wide range of opportunities from horticulture to web design available. Please contact Katy or Emily for more details. All our projects are suitable for people with special needs. iver.environment@groundwork.org.uk https://www.iverenvironmentcentre.org/

name: Pumpkin Festival at Odds Farm Park
description: Pick your own Pumpkin, free for every paying child whilst stocks last. This October, dive into a world of seasonal fun at our spooktacular Pumpkin Festival! With three unforgettable experiences to choose from: Pumpkin Weekends, Family Nights, and our enchanting October Half Term, there’s something for everyone to enjoy, including pumpkin picking from our pumpkin patch. Please visit our website to learn more and to book your tickets.
organisation: Odds Farm Park Come and enjoy the fresh farm air, our wide-open spaces, and spend time with all our furry friends here at Odds Farm Park! We want you to enjoy an amazing day full of farm adventures, and for you to do this safely and with confidence, we have introduced numerous new measures to ensure we can be COVID secure at all times. All guests must pre-book tickets online ahead of their visit so we can carefully manage daily visitor numbers, and new routes, walk-ways and staggered entry to certain areas have also been added to maintain social distancing measures around the Farm. As an outdoor family farm park attraction, we have always actively encouraged regular hand-washing for all guests, and we are offering extensive hand hygiene facilities across the Farm Park, including: 5 dedicated hand-washing stations 18 hand sanitising stations 3 bathroom and hand-washing blocks Whilst our Indoor Play barn, Demonstration Barn and Adventure Maze are temporarily closed, here at Odds Farm Park there’s plenty of space for kids to run, tumble and play. There are acres of outdoor adventure to discover, including the extensive Adventure Log Play Area, H2Odds Water Play, Mini-Land Rovers, Sand Play Area, Adventure Fort, Go-Karts, Tractor and Trailer Rides (Apr to Oct), Fitness Trail, Under 5s Log Play Area - what will you do first? Of course, no farm visit would be complete without meeting the animals! Explore our Undercover Animal Barn, where you can see our rabbits and guinea pigs, and even hand-feed some of our sheep and goats! Adults and children alike can strut and cluck their way around Chicken World, and watch our feathered friends enjoy exploring their new home! In the summer months, guests can also visit our pigs, cows, donkeys, ponies and other animals out enjoying their paddocks across the Farm – you might catch a glimpse of some piglets, calves and a foal trotting and springing around in the sunshine! Feeling hungry? Our outdoor outlets, The Airstream and Ice Cream and Milkshake Parlour, are offering a contactless service, and visitors can now Click and Collect a range of delicious drinks and tasty treats via our new online ordering system. As always, guests are welcome to bring their own picnics to enjoy whilst visiting and which can be enjoyed throughout the park at any of our socially distanced picnic tables. For further information on how to book and what to expect from your visit, we have all the details you need on our Reopening page. To find out what’s on, guests can also check out our new interactive map to help plan their day and guide them through our amazing outdoor adventures! main@oddsfarm.co.uk https://www.oddsfarm.co.uk/

name: Christmas at Claydon House: House of Bells
description: Something magical is coming to Claydon. This winter, the historic house transforms into a shimmering world of bells, candlelight, and festive wonder. House of Bells is a new Christmas tradition for Buckinghamshire - a multi‑sensory celebration of sound, light, scent, and story designed for all generations. Step inside and discover a joyful, uplifting experience where every corner rings with warmth and enchantment. From the first chime to the scent of pine and the glow of lanterns, you’ll feel Christmas reimagined. Create little moments of wonder with family and friends, and make memories that will last a lifetime. House of Bells is expected to be a popular highlight of the season, and early booking is strongly recommended. Secure your place now by visiting our website and begin your Christmas at Claydon- where festive magic rings through every room.
organisation: Claydon House (Buckingham) | National Trust National Trust Country house providing community events throughout the year. In the 1750s at his family seat in Buckinghamshire, Ralph Verney set out to create a country house of extraordinary grandeur that would dazzle his wealthy neighbours and outdo his political rivals. Thirty years on he was facing financial ruin. Today the interiors that remain are among the most ambitious and lavish ever created in the eighteenth century. Directions to Claydon House: Road: Between Middle and Botolph Claydon, 13 miles north-west of Aylesbury, 4 miles south of Winslow. Signposted from A413 and A41 (M40 Junction 9). Bus: Red Rose Travel. Train: Nearest station is Aylesbury. claydon@nationaltrust.org.uk https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/claydon

name: Stranger Folk at Cliveden
description: Head to Cliveden this autumn and download the Stranger Folk app and begin an immersive adventure inspired by British folklore. The interactive game features goblins and other creatures. description: See Father Christmas whilst enjoying a steam train ride, watch a pantomime, and meet Mrs Claus and the Elves – all in one amazing festive Christmas experience! Start your journey with our family-friendly pantomime, Cinderella, in our festive Visitor Centre. Enjoy your performance and then make your way to Platform 4 to board the steam train. You will be shown to your compartment and visited by Father Christmas, where each child will be given a special golden ticket. After the train ride, your adventure continues where you will be magically transported to Santa’s workshop to meet Mrs Claus and the elves, and your child can exchange their golden ticket for a gift of their choice. Pre-booking for Christmas is essential! Please visit our website to learn more and to book.
organisation: Buckinghamshire Railway Centre Buckinghamshire Railway Centre in Quainton occupies an extensive site in rolling Buckinghamshire countryside. There is so much to see and do! Exhibits range from large express passenger locomotives to the humble shunting engine together with a host of smaller items recreating the golden age of steam. Check our events programme to see what is happening on the day of your planned visit, steam trains operate on certain days and others are devoted to various special events. Types of Open Days Special Events: See 'Special Events' or 'Calendar' on the top options bar of our for more information on these and to find out when they are. Steaming Days: This is when we have a full-size steam train in action, ready to take you for a ride! We also have miniature ride-on steam trains. These are run by our sister Society VAMES, and there is a small charge for this. Steaming Days are every Sunday (March to October), and also Wednesdays during school holidays. Static Viewing Days: This is when the site is open, but no steam trains or rides will be running. These days are much quieter and ticket prices are lower. We are open for static viewing Tuesdays, Wednesdays (term time only), and Thursdays. The cafe is only open for snacks (crisps/chocolate/biscuits) and self-service drinks (hot and cold) on these days. description: Join UK Astronomy for a family-friendly evening of cosmic discovery and adventure. Begin with an engaging Solar System talk exploring planets, moons, and constellations. After a refreshment break, head outdoors for a stargazing experience using telescopes and binoculars (weather permitting). You may see the Moon, planets (if visible), or deeper-sky objects.
