If stargazing is not possible due to cloud cover, an immersive indoor night-sky presentation will be provided instead. Tea and instant coffee will be available during the refreshment break. Telescopes and binoculars will be provided for the stargazing session. Recommended for ages 12 plus. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Halloween Trail at Ascott House
description: Willow the Witch’s Magical Quest!! Deep in the enchanted gardens of Ascott Forest, Willow the Witch was busy brewing up a powerful magic spell… But OH NO! Something went terribly wrong! Instead of creating the magic she intended, Willow accidentally turned her poor cat, Jinx, completely green! Now Willow needs the help of some brave little warriors to embark on a spook-tacular magical quest and help her cast a reverse spell to turn Jinx back to his usual black! Follow the magical map deep into the gardens and complete a series of enchanted quests. Solve the challenges, discover hidden clues, and hunt down the special magical ingredients Willow needs. Find all the ingredients and add them to Willow’s bubbling cauldron to create the reverse spell! Once every ingredient has been found and the spell is ready, Willow will have a little bit of magic to work with… and as a thank-you for your bravery, she’ll reward every brave warrior with a very special prize! Are you brave enough to accept Willow’s quest? The magic awaits… Tickets include: - Spook-tacular trail around the gardens, including fun puzzles and games - Trail sheet and Halloween themed pencil - Family Pumpkin Photo Opportunity - Prize at the end of the trail Please visit our website to learn more and to book. Valid Garden Admission is required.

description: Our Pumpkin Patch is open every weekend in October, from Saturday 3 October, plus daily in October half-term. Free entry, no booking required – just come along (first come, first served). Why pick a Peterley pumpkin? - Approximately 15,000 homegrown pumpkins in various shapes, sizes, and varieties - No need to pre-book - Free entry to the patch - Free and plentiful parking on-site - Dogs on leads welcome - Plenty of wheelbarrows to use In addition to our pumpkin picking we will have some children’s activities including face-painting (for an additional fee), as well as photo opportunities, and pop-up food vans. During half-term Little Farmers will also be running in the Dutch Barn, this however is a ticketed event and must be pre-booked in advance. Please visit our website to learn more.

name: Christmas at Blenheim Palace | Illuminated Trail and Christmas Market
description: Britain’s Greatest Palace is unrivalled when it comes to Christmas. Step into sparkle at the world-class after-dark Illuminated Trail, glide within the iconic Great Court at The Great Skate and pose by a pumpkin carriage inside the magical fairytale world of Cinderella. Seasonally decorated and lavishly themed, it’s Christmas galore as the Palace is transformed into the story of Cinderella by a BAFTA award-winning team of designers. From the moment you enter The Great Hall welcomed by a twinkling tree, take time to enjoy the sights and sounds around you. Walk through a larger-than-life storybook into a glittering world, wander into State Rooms filled with ornaments, mistletoe, holly, and baubles. Midnight strikes, the clocks all chime … a glass slipper leads Prince Charming to a happy ever after Christmas wedding like no other. Out in the gardens tree-tops glisten and waterfalls shimmer. With new surprises around every corner, this spectacular trail boasting more than a million lights, has everything you need for an unforgettable adventure immersed in seasonal song. It’s a shared experience with friends and family that includes a glimpse of Father Christmas himself. Take your Christmas experience to new heights on our festive Observation Wheel. Enjoy breathtaking views of the Palace and Christmas Market, all dressed in their seasonal best. Soak up the festive atmosphere and tuck into seasonal showstoppers and sweet treats, grab a mulled wine or hot chocolate beside the covered Ice Rink and explore our Christmas Market. Featured in the top 10 of best UK seasonal markets year after year, it will once again be filled with a variety of hand-picked, irresistible gifts, uniquely made by a range of designers and crafts people. Blenheim Palace, it’s a picture-perfect place to celebrate your Christmas. We treat all Palace tickets as charitable donations to the Blenheim Palace Heritage Foundation and as a thank you we automatically convert them into Annual Passes at no extra cost. If you do not want your admission to be considered a charitable donation you can buy a Palace ticket by visiting our website. Please note that the Christmas market is only open between Friday 13 November and Sunday 20 December. Please visit our website to learn more and to book your tickets.

local_offer: Little Oaks Pre-school works on the belief that all children and their families have a right to be part of their local community, and to be welcomed and included on equal terms. Our setting will endeavor to ensure that all children have the opportunity to participate in the full range of activities and opportunities offered and that their individuality and potential will be recognised, valued and nurtured herein. Little Oaks Pre-School will welcome and include all children. Providing a broad-based curriculum, appropriately delivered to all children according to their level of need and ability.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We liaise with a range of professionals including those from the Early Years team (SEND), Speech and Language Therapist, Feeding Clinic specialists, Paediatricians, Educational Psychologists, Physiotherapists, and Occupational Therapist (OT). We regularly attend the Early Years SENCO Liaison Groups. We have experience in using the following approaches and strategies: Access, plan, do, review, SEN plan, applications for HNFB/EHCP, referrals, advice and support, Star Approach/ABC, SALT groups and support What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I CAN Accreditation Children's Communication Champion SENCO Training - Debbie Albrighton Level 3 Senco - Kirsty Johnson Positive Play for Early Years - Perry Taylor NAS Early Bird (Autism) - Perry Taylor/Maxine Drake Speech, Language and Communication Level 2 - Debbie Albrighton Various staff members have taken the Speech, Language and Communication Level 2, Supporting Early Language Development, Understanding and Addressing Behaviour, Equality & Inclusion, and Supporting Children with SEND in the Early Years Level 2, e-courses. As well as specific courses run by Apex Training for : First Words - supporting children to say their first sounds/words, Phrases and Sentences - supporting children to develop speech and language, and Autism, Communication and Social Interaction. The setting has completed Tier 1 Making Sense of Autism June 2017 The setting has completed Tier 2 Good Autism Practice January 2019 SEN Support and Beyond February 2021 - Debbie Albrighton Tier 3 Leading Good Autism Practise March 2021 - Debbie Albrighton Identifying Speech, Language, Occupational Therapy Needs - June 2021 Debbie Albrighton Developmental Language Disorder: The most common childhood condition you've never heard of! - September 2021 Debbie Albrighton Speech and language specialism: supporting children with speech sound disorders, stammering and selective mutism - June 2022 Debbie Albrighton Seeing Beyond Behaviour - Oct 2023 Deepika Sathe & Claudine Dunning Seeing Beyond Behaviour - June 2024 Helen Cade Championing early communication and language with BBC Tiny Happy People - December 2023 Debbie Albrighton Practical Inclusion for Childcare & HAF - July 2024 Debbie Albrighton Impact of Early Trauma for Childcare & HAF - July 2024 Debbie Albrighton Understanding and supporting behaviour in the early years - September 2024 Debbie Albrighton How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they are able to approach us about anything relating to their children. There are many informal opportunities to chat and when parents request a meeting we aim to meet with them as soon as possible. We share targets and suggest strategies for home and pre-school. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time by asking their child’s Key Person. We will discuss progress at parent's evening, through our 2-year-old progress checks and End of Year reports. For children with SEN we try to ensure that we are able to meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. We take into account the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavor to make this transition as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We regularly visit/liaise with local schools regarding children who are transitioning to primary school. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? description: This Christmas, make magical memories with a festive experience the whole family will remember.... Santa’s Grotto is back and this year, the experience is even bigger and better. description: Tail‑wagging autumn fun for you and your pup. Bring your furry friend along to our dog-friendly Pup‑kin Patch, where they can sniff, explore, and choose their very own autumn toy from our playful “patch”. Expect wagging tails, seasonal treats, and plenty of photo moments. Let your pooch follow their nose, pick their favourite toy, and enjoy some light‑hearted fun together – perfect for memory‑making (and a few great snaps). What’s included - Entry to our Pup‑kin Patch, where your dog can choose a toy to take home. - A fun, low‑level, obstacle course to test their agility (optional!). - Dog-friendly activities. - A digital “paw‑trait” in front of our autumn backdrop. - A free hot drink for you and a puppuccino for your pooch with purchase of a sliced cake or hot breakfast roll. - Money‑off vouchers to enjoy in-store. We’re proud to partner with Dogs Trust, the UK’s largest dog welfare charity. They care for over 14,000 dogs each year, supporting everything from rehoming and rehabilitation, to owner training and advice. You’ll have the option to add a donation when booking to help Dogs Trust continue their incredible work – making life better for dogs and the people who love them. For more info, visit their website.

local_offer: I provide personalised GCSE English tuition for students with a range of additional learning needs, including students with ADHD, autism, and dyslexia. Sessions are tailored to each student’s individual strengths, needs, and learning preferences, with a calm, supportive, and encouraging approach. I can adapt the pace, structure, and presentation of lessons to help students stay focused, build confidence, and develop their English skills. This may include breaking tasks into manageable steps, providing clear explanations and instructions, using a range of learning approaches, and allowing additional processing time where appropriate. My aim is to create a positive learning environment where students feel supported, understood, and able to make progress towards their GCSE English goals.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? My aim is to help children and young people with SEND develop greater confidence, independence, and enjoyment in GCSE English. Outcomes may include: - Increased confidence in English Language and Literature. - Improved understanding of texts, questions, and examination requirements. - Development of effective study, revision, and exam techniques. - Improved ability to organise and structure written responses. - Greater independence when approaching English tasks and revision. - Reduced anxiety around English and GCSE examinations. - Individualised support that recognises each student’s strengths, needs, and learning preferences. For families, I aim to provide reassurance through personalised support and clear communication about their child’s progress and areas for development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed training in ADHD, autism, dyslexia and Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). This training, alongside 18 years of teaching experience in secondary education, supports my ability to adapt teaching and learning approaches to meet individual students’ needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are kept informed about their child’s progress through regular communication and personalised feedback. I can discuss strengths, areas for development, and priorities for future sessions, helping parents understand how their child is progressing towards their GCSE English goals. Parents can get involved by sharing information about their child’s individual needs, learning preferences, and areas of difficulty, and by discussing any concerns or upcoming assessments. Where appropriate, I can also provide suggestions for revision and ways to support learning at home. I aim to work collaboratively with parents so that each student receives consistent, personalised support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I provide personalised feedback to parents about their child’s progress, strengths and areas for development. For students with SEND, communication can be tailored to the individual child and family, taking into account their learning needs and preferred ways of communicating. Additional support for children and young people with SEND may include more regular feedback where appropriate, discussion of strategies that support their learning, and recommendations for adapting revision or study tasks at home. I can also discuss any barriers to learning and agree appropriate approaches with parents. My aim is to ensure parents have a clear understanding of their child’s progress and feel involved in supporting their learning. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Tuition is delivered online through Zoom, allowing students to learn from the comfort and familiarity of their own home. This can provide a flexible and accessible learning environment for children and young people with SEND who may find travelling to a physical setting or learning in a busy classroom challenging. Sessions can be adapted to the individual student’s needs, including the pace, structure, and presentation of activities. Parents can discuss any specific accessibility or learning requirements in advance so that appropriate adjustments can be considered. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can contact Laura K Learning directly to discuss their child’s needs, GCSE English requirements, and the support they are looking for. An initial conversation allows us to understand the student’s individual strengths, learning preferences, and any additional needs before tuition begins. Tuition is delivered online through Zoom, so families can access the service from home. Sessions are available as one-to-one or small-group tuition, subject to availability. Parents are welcome to discuss any specific SEND requirements or reasonable adjustments before booking to ensure the support is appropriate for their child. To get started, please contact me using the email address provided. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As Laura K Learning develops, I plan to continue expanding my knowledge and professional development in SEND and inclusive education, particularly in relation to ADHD, autism and dyslexia. I aim to further develop personalised teaching resources and strategies that support different learning needs, as well as continuing to adapt my online tuition to make sessions accessible and engaging for individual students. As the service grows, I hope to develop a wider range of tailored GCSE English resources and support materials for students with SEND, while continuing to work closely with parents to identify individual needs and monitor progress.

Professional printed photography is available, allowing the whole family to be part of the memory. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Vintage Christmas Grotto at Bletchley Park
description: Come visit Father Christmas at Bletchley Park and uncover some secrets… Enter a world of festive magic and secret Christmas operations at Bletchley Park. Embark on a mission to help Father Christmas in our brand-new North Pole Plotting Room, where Christmas preparations have gone a little off track. Meet characters from the 1940s, enjoy festive craft activities and sit in the audience as the wartime Bletchley Park Drama Society rehearse their new Christmas production, Cinderella – you may even be called on to help out! Vintage Christmas Grotto: Mission North Pole Your Grotto adventure begins with Agent Sparkle, one of Father Christmas’ most trusted helpers, who is training a brand-new recruit who’s enthusiastic and eager to help… but has accidentally muddled up the Christmas post, and lost track of Father Christmas’ journey plans! Can you help to crack these Christmas conundrums before the big day? During each mission, families will be invited to meet Father Christmas himself. Children will have the opportunity to share their festive wishes and receive a special gift to take home. Filled with vintage charm, interactive fun, and plenty of Christmas cheer, this unique experience combines the magic of Father Christmas with the spirit of Bletchley Park’s remarkable secret story. Suitable for children of all ages. Advance booking essential. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Vintage Christmas Grotto at Bletchley Park
description: Come visit Father Christmas at Bletchley Park and uncover some secrets… Enter a world of festive magic and secret Christmas operations at Bletchley Park. Embark on a mission to help Father Christmas in our brand-new North Pole Plotting Room, where Christmas preparations have gone a little off track. Meet characters from the 1940s, enjoy festive craft activities and sit in the audience as the wartime Bletchley Park Drama Society rehearse their new Christmas production, Cinderella – you may even be called on to help out! Vintage Christmas Grotto: Mission North Pole Your Grotto adventure begins with Agent Sparkle, one of Father Christmas’ most trusted helpers, who is training a brand-new recruit who’s enthusiastic and eager to help… but has accidentally muddled up the Christmas post, and lost track of Father Christmas’ journey plans! Can you help to crack these Christmas conundrums before the big day? During each mission, families will be invited to meet Father Christmas himself. Children will have the opportunity to share their festive wishes and receive a special gift to take home. Filled with vintage charm, interactive fun, and plenty of Christmas cheer, this unique experience combines the magic of Father Christmas with the spirit of Bletchley Park’s remarkable secret story. Suitable for children of all ages. Advance booking essential. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Relaxed Vintage Christmas Grotto at Bletchley Park
description: Celebrate the most magical time of year with a visit to Bletchley Park’s Relaxed Vintage Christmas Grotto. Enjoy a gentle and festive visit to Father Christmas in the unique surroundings of Bletchley Park. We understand that every child experiences the world differently. Our Relaxed Vintage Christmas Grotto Experience has been specially designed for families who would benefit from a quieter environment, and is appropriate for children on the autistic spectrum, those with sensory conditions, who are neurodiverse or have other additional needs. Your visit begins in our charming 1940s-inspired North Pole Plotting Room, where Father Christmas’ helpers are making final preparations for Christmas Day. Families will be welcomed by friendly characters who will gently guide them through the experience before meeting Father Christmas himself and receiving a special gift to take home. Children are welcome to engage in whatever way feels comfortable for them, whether that means chatting with Father Christmas, observing quietly, or simply enjoying the festive surroundings. Alongside your Grotto visit, families can enjoy a variety of festive activities across Bletchley Park’s historic site, including: - Meeting friendly 1940s characters who are preparing for Christmas. - Watching a theatrical rehearsal of Cinderella by members of Bletchley Park’s historic Drama Society. - Taking part in festive craft activities inspired by the creativity of the wartime Codebreakers. - Exploring Bletchley Park’s historic buildings, exhibitions, and grounds. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.
organisation: Bletchley Park Bletchley Park, once the top-secret home of the World War Two Codebreakers is now a vibrant heritage attraction. Explore, experience and enjoy the once top-secret world of iconic Codebreaking Huts and Blocks set within an atmospheric Victorian estate. enquiries@bletchleypark.org.uk https://bletchleypark.org.uk/

name: Santa's Grotto at Lillingstone
description: Visit Father Christmas in his cosy Grotto where he will take you on a truly festive adventure! Experience the joy of meeting Father Christmas himself! Upon arrival, you will be welcomed by Father Christmas’ special Elves and taken through to his enchanting Grotto, where you will be able to share your Christmas wishes with him and listen as he brings the magic of Christmas to life with his heart-warming stories. Join Us for a Magical Christmas Experience! Step into the enchanting world of Father Christmas’ Elves and begin your festive adventure! You’ll be whisked away to Mother Christmas’ cosy kitchen, where little ones can decorate their very own gingerbread man and make a bag of reindeer feed to sprinkle on the lawn on Christmas Eve. Then, it’s time to visit Father Christmas’ Grotto for a heartwarming 15-minute storytime and chat with the special man himself. Every child will take home a small gift and memories to treasure forever. The Grotto experience will last for approximately 30 minutes. A truly magical experience for the whole family — full of festive fun, laughter, and Christmas spirit! Letters to Santa If you wish to send Santa a letter and receive a personalised reply in the post from him, this additional activity can be purchased upon check-out or on the day of your visit. Please bring your letter to Santa in a sealed envelope on the day of your visit to post in our special North Pole Post Box. Remember to include your full name and address in your letter so Santa knows where to send his reply! Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Christmas at Hogshaw Farm | Grotto
description: Father Christmas and his team of elves will be visiting the farm to gather Christmas wishes and sprinkle some festive cheer across the Buckinghamshire countryside. Join us for a magical Christmas event that the whole family can enjoy, with full farm entry included! Join us for a wander through our winter wonderland, plant a mini Christmas tree, and make magical reindeer food on your way to find Father Christmas in the big red tractor. Share your wish-list in a private meeting with the big man himself, before collecting a special present from our toy workshop. Hogshaw Farm – the place where Christmas memories are made! A Warm Welcome Start your Christmas journey at our welcoming entrance hut and feel the Christmas spirit building…. Warm up at our cosy fire pits, with the option to toast marshmallows Meet our cheeky Head Elf as you begin your Christmas experience Meet Father Christmas Take a seat in our cosy red tractor for your private meeting with Father Christmas. Share your Christmas wishes and see if you’ve made it to the Nice List. Time for photos with the big man. Play in our snowball pits and have a go at antler toss Festive treats Get Christmas-ready with festive treats and special gifts… Prepare your unique blend of magical Reindeer Food for Christmas Eve. Plant a miniature Christmas tree to take home. Decorate a gingerbread treat And of course….choose a special Christmas present from the Toy Workshop! Please visit our website to learn more and to book.
organisation: Hogshaw Farm and Wildlife Park An environmentally friendly 44 acre rare breeds farm attraction in Aylesbury Vale for all ages. Located in beautiful open countryside where there is plenty of space for children to play and explore outdoors and indoors. As well as special seasonal events, the Animal Barn, Pets Corner and Wildlife Zone, we have a daily programme which children will love. They also have the chance to let off steam inside the two indoor play barns, or outside where there is plenty of play equipment and a nature trail. There's fresh homemade food in the Eco Centre Cafe and Barn Cafe that's supplied by local producers and from our own walled garden, where we grow heritage fruit and vegetables. The restaurant is on the ground floor of our lovely timber-framed building, whilst on the first floor with stunning views is our purpose built conference/party room available for hire. We have 'Farmer for a Day', 'Ranger for a Day' and 'Animal Experiences' available for all ages. info@greendragonecofarm.co.uk https://www.greendragonecofarm.co.uk//

name: Old Station Nursery High Wycombe, The
description: The Old Station Nursery High Wycombe is a close-knit, home from home nursery set within the grounds of Manor Farm Infant School. The nursery has been carefully designed to help children thrive and flourish in a natural and engaging learning environment. Inside, the rooms provide a warm and welcoming space to enhance the children’s development. The nursery provides high-quality care along with a unique learning experience—a child-friendly cooking class inspired by Montessori principles. This hands-on approach nurtures meaningful connections between children and the world around them. Outdoor play is extremely important at The Old Station Nursery High Wycombe. The team believe in giving children plenty of opportunities to explore, touch and evoke curiosity in the world around them. The outdoor space is well equipped with resources, such as Grab and Go boxes, a reading corner, a sand pit and insect habitats, for the children to explore. The nursery benefits from fruit trees and a vegetable patch which the children enjoy engaging with and learning about. The nursery is ideally located on the grounds of Manor Farm School so that when the time comes, the transition to ‘big school’ is as smooth and seamless as possible. The team work closely with parents to ensure that the children are exceptionally prepared for their next stage of learning.

name: Santa's Grotto at Milton Keynes Museum
description: A magical Christmas experience with Santa and his elves – plus, a whole Victorian Christmas to discover. Step into the magic of Christmas at Milton Keynes Museum this December, where Santa’s Grotto comes to life alongside our enchanting Victorian Christmas experience. From Friday 4 to Sunday 20 December, bring your little ones to meet Father Christmas and his merry elves and enjoy a festive adventure packed with Christmas magic. Santa’s Grotto runs Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays only. What makes a visit to Milton Keynes Museum extra special is that Santa’s Grotto is just part of the experience. After meeting Santa, explore our Victorian Christmas, where the Museum is transformed for the festive season. Wander along our snow-dusted Street of Shops, see Christmas as it might have been celebrated in Victorian times, and soak up the atmosphere with mulled wine and mince pies for the grown-ups. It’s more than a trip to see Santa – it’s a whole Christmas day out for the family. The cost of the Santa visit covers entry to the grotto and a gift from Father Christmas. You must also purchase Museum tickets in advance or present your annual ticket on the day. Under 5s are free. All tickets to the Museum are converted to annual passes so you pay once and can visit for free all year. Please visit our website to learn more and to book your tickets.

name: Victorian Christmas and Market at Milton Keynes Museum
description: Step into the magic of a Victorian Christmas and experience the sights, scents, and sounds of the season at your local museum. Experience the Magic of a Bygone Christmas Wander through our beautifully decorated Victorian farmhouse, where twinkling lights and festive garlands set the scene for a nostalgic celebration. Join our cheerful volunteers for carol singing around the pianola, and savour the flavours of Christmas with mulled wine and mince pies. Browse the Festive Craft Market and Bar (Saturdays and Sundays only). Enjoy a tipple and discover one-of-a-kind handcrafted gifts and local creations in the Craft Market at the New Gallery atrium. It’s the perfect place to find those last-minute treasures made by talented local artists and producers. Family Fun and Festive Crafts (Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays) Keep the little ones entertained in our drop-in craft sessions or biscuit decorating workshops (small fee applies). name: A Christmas Carol at Stowe House
description: Celebrate the festive season with one of the greatest Christmas stories ever written. This Christmas, join us in the spectacular State Dining Room at Stowe House as This Is My Theatre brings Charles Dickens’ beloved festive classic to life. On Christmas Eve, Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his former business partner, Jacob Marley. As visions of Christmas Past, Present and Future unfold before him, Scrooge must confront the choices he has made and decide whether he can change his future. Packed with warmth, humour, music, and festive cheer, this acclaimed adaptation captures everything audiences love about Dickens’ timeless story. Whether you’re revisiting a favourite Christmas tradition or introducing younger family members to the tale for the first time, this atmospheric evening performance is the perfect way to embrace the spirit of the season. A Christmas Carol will be performed at 3pm and 7pm with an approximate run time of 85 minutes plus an interval. The venue is fully accessible. Please let us know of any access needs once you’ve booked your tickets by emailing us in advance. Booking essential. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Old Station Nursery Marlow, The
description: Set in a single story building, The Old Station Nursery Marlow provides an engaging learning environment for all children to flourish. At Marlow, each room has been purposely designed and resourced to encourage the learning and development of each age group. The team have paid attention to creating an environment that enables children to develop relationships with the world around them, themselves and others. The nursery provides high-quality care along with a unique learning experience—a child-friendly cooking class inspired by Montessori principles. This hands-on approach nurtures meaningful connections between children and the world around them. The team take pride in our outdoor learning area, which helps to provide new and exciting experiences for all the children. The children have access to varied resources in the garden, giving them the opportunity for exploring and discovering nature. All children spend their time at nursery developing key skills and aptitudes which will not only help them prepare for starting school but will encourage a love of lifelong learning. The nursery is ideally located on the grounds of Foxes Piece School so that when the time comes, the transition to ‘big school’ is as smooth and seamless as possible.

description: When the snow falls, magic fills the air. One snowy day a boy builds a Snowman and in the middle of the night the Snowman comes to life. Don’t miss out on the opportunity to join us on a magical journey to the North Pole this festive season as we welcome ‘The Snowman™’ Christmas experience to centre:mk! This nostalgic adventure begins with an exciting and heart-warming, live interpretation of ‘The Snowman™’, brought to life by actors portraying the well-loved characters from the original story! A snowy landscape provides the perfect backdrop to view some of the most memorable and magical moments from the original animated film and all children will be given the opportunity to decorate a Christmas biscuit treat and even meet ‘The Snowman™’ himself, before a one-to-one family meeting with Santa in his woodland cabin where children will receive a special gift! There is of course the opportunity to take home a family photograph with Santa as a memento of your special visit to ‘The Snowman™’ Christmas Experience at centre:mk. ‘Inclusive Relaxed Sessions’ are available for any families with special needs – the sessions are adapted in a variety of ways, including a more relaxed attitude to noise and lighting effects, in order to reduce anxiety and ensure a safe, enjoyable visit. During an ‘Inclusive Relaxed Session’ our team will try to help everyone feel comfortable enough to talk, sing, dance, and even shout out at any point during the experience. 'Inclusive Relaxes Sessions' will be held on Saturday 28 November, Sunday 29 November, and Wednesday 9 December. If you are unable to attend one of these sessions, then we recommend booking a weekday or earlier times at the weekend. Please ensure that you complete the special requirements section in the booking process and we will try to accommodate you wherever possible. Please note that it will not be possible to reduce noise and lighting effects in open sessions and the experience may well be quite busy at peak times. A truly immersive experience for all the whole family to enjoy and certainly one not to be missed this Christmas! Please visit our website to learn more and to book.

name: Old Station Nursery Taplow, The
description: The Old Station Nursery Taplow is set in a beautiful mock Tudor building, with a warm, welcoming and homely environment inside and out. Inside the nursery, each room is designed to include age-appropriate resources and equipment, to encourage skill-building and development. The rooms are light and spacious, giving the children the freedom to explore with curiosity. The nursery provides high-quality care along with a unique learning experience—a child-friendly cooking class inspired by Montessori principles. This hands-on approach nurtures meaningful connections between children and the world around them. Outside, the beautiful outdoor space encourages the children to explore and develop in a natural environment. The outdoor space promotes sensory and physical play, giving children the opportunity to become confident and independent individuals, equipped with the knowledge, skills and understanding for every stage of learning. When the time comes for children to progress on to ‘big school’, we are confident that the children will have the skills, aptitudes and attitudes required to thrive in their next stage of learning.

description: Visit the museum after dark this Halloween for our Creepy Doll Hunt: explore one of the oldest buildings in Aylesbury by only torchlight and discover the haunted dolls hidden throughout the museum. Now, at last, the dolls have been let out and it’s up to you to find them all. This trail will take you through our Tudor and Victorian rooms, museum galleries, and into our walled Victorian garden. Afraid of dolls? You soon will be…. Please bring a torch with you. Bookable slots are available between 6:30 and 8:30pm. Please visit our website to book.

name: Wildlife Wednesday Walks
description: Explore nature after hours — every third or fourth Wednesday evening of the month. Times will vary with the season. Join us for a gentle guided wander to see our countryside and what wildlife is active at dusk. Each month brings something different, and you’re warmly invited to come along, observe, listen, and enjoy the changing countryside. Led by our volunteer wildlife guide. Wednesday 21 October — 5pm Mushrooms and autumn treasures A twilight wander to spot fungi and other seasonal surprises. Bring your curiosity and a warm layer. Wednesday 18 November — 5pm Dark evenings, bright discoveries This may be a darker walk, but that makes it even more exciting. Let’s explore the night landscape together and see what reveals itself.

name: Monthly GOAT Club
description: Come along to our Goat Club monthly meet up on the second Thursday of the month. Following the fun and success of our recent blocks of Kindred Countryside sessions, we hope to continue to welcome people from a wide range of backgrounds, ethnicities, and generations to enjoy hands‑on farming and countryside activities through these monthly meet ups after school. Together we’ll grow, cook and eat food, get moving outdoors, and share stories that spark connection. These sessions are designed to support both physical and mental wellbeing while bringing generations together in a friendly, inclusive environment. This after‑school club invites a young family member (aged 8 plus) to attend with an older friend or family member who enjoys countryside memories, growing food, and staying well. It’s a chance to learn from one another, build confidence, and feel part of a supportive community. Please note there is a cost of £5 per family of 2 people per session. Please book all dates that you hope to attend.

name: Men Walking and Talking
description: Men Walking and Talking (MWAT) is a national peer-led support group founded by Dan Reid in 2021 following Dan’s own issues with mental health. It operates to bring men together in a safe space and to end the stigma around men’s mental health by supporting each other. With around 80 groups around Great Britain (with more in the pipeline), in 2022 we became a CIC and a member of the National Counselling and Psychotherapy Society (NCPS). We are signatories of the armed forces covenant with approximately 50% of those attending our walks a part of that community. The Walk Leader for Aylesbury MWAT is Scott. We meet weekly on Thursdays at 7pm in the Oakfield Road Car Park and we’re open to all men 18 plus. We walk for approximately 1 hour. Well behaved dogs are welcome. There are no fees, no registration, and no pressure to talk about mental health, we’re just a group of blokes walking, talking, and supporting. Men’s mental health is in crises with 75% of all suicides being men, and suicide being the leading cause of death for men under 50. This idea that “big boys don’t cry” and that we need to “man up and be strong” is literally killing us. Our message to you is “it’s ok to say you’re not okay!” Asking for help, is being strong. Supporting your brother is being manly! So join this fraternity where you ain’t heavy, you’re my brother.

description: Providing emotional support to parents of severely ill and disabled children. Harry’s Pals support parents of children with life limiting illnesses or disabilities through counselling, emotional support, and peer support groups. We provide emotional wellbeing support and counselling for families who are under significant emotional and practical pressure caring for their children. Applicants must have a child aged 0 to 18 who is severely ill or disabled. In some instances, a consultant's letter may be required. The full eligibility criteria can be found on our website. name: What's Love Got To Do With It? A Tribute To Tina Turner
description: After a sensational 2026 that saw over 60,000 Tina Turner fans across the UK singing, dancing, and having the time of their lives, What’s Love Got To Do With It? is back and bigger than ever! This electrifying tribute show celebrates the music and unparalleled career of the one and only Queen of Rock ‘n’ Roll, Tina Turner. Get ready for an unforgettable evening of high-energy, feel-good rock and soul, brought to life by a phenomenal live band. Packed with all the classic hits you know and love, the show delivers showstopping performances of Proud Mary, River Deep – Mountain High, Simply The Best, Private Dancer, Nutbush City Limits, and many more. Stepping into Tina’s iconic heels is Kent’s own Holly Bannis, the daughter of Greg Bannis, former lead singer of Hot Chocolate. Audiences can expect a show bursting with energy, emotion, and that signature Tina fire. The production kicks off with hits like Private Dancer, as Holly fully inhabits Tina’s powerful vocals and unmistakable moves, transporting fans to the heart of a live Tina Turner concert experience. Then, in the show-stopping second half, the audience is guaranteed to be on their feet, dancing and singing along to high-octane classics like Nutbush City Limits. What’s Love Got To Do With It? isn’t just a concert – it’s a celebration of Tina Turner’s legacy, a night of unrelenting joy, and a tribute to one of the most electrifying performers in music history. Please note that this is a tribute production and is not endorsed by or affiliated with the Tina Turner Estate. Please visit our website to learn more and to book your tickets.

name: Little Strummers Music Lessons
description: Little Strummers, based in Bucks, has been providing fun and accessible guitar and ukulele lessons since 2009. We now also offer singing and piano. We teach in schools, online, and at our school in Prestwood. Face-to-face lessons are available in Prestwood every day, and we also have a homeschool music hub on Tuesdays. We focus on making music education fun, interactive, and tailored to each student's abilities and interests.​ Instruments are available to borrow, hire or buy.
organisation: Little Strummers Music Lessons Little Strummers offers music lessons to everyone from 4 to 104 in guitar, ukulele, piano, violin, viola, recorder and music theory. We have studios in West Wycombe, teach in Beaconsfield, Prestwood, Amersham and Holmer Green and also run lessons, clubs and groups in many schools in Buckinghamshire. Lessons All styles of guitar and ukulele lessons are available - electric, acoustic, classical, bass, rock (and all combinations of these). Individual, shared and group lessons are all available, and we also run ensembles. Piano, recorder, violin and viola lessons suit all levels of player from beginner to diploma level. Workshops We hold introductory and players workshops during every school holiday. Instruments can be provided, no need for your own instrument. Parties We run parties for groups of 6 or more children and provide everything needed for a great musical experience. Performing We take part in concerts, assemblies, fayres, fetes and festivals as often as possible. We also organise a huge Christmas concert every year. Teaching We have eight highly experience, very friendly teachers, all fully insured and DBS checked. office@littlestrummers.co.uk https://www.littlestrummers.com/

description: This October half term, step into a world of Halloween magic at Dunstable Downs and help break The Curse of Chute Wood. Pick up your trail sheet and create your own magical spell book before setting off on a spooky adventure through the Downs and into Chute Wood. Along the way, you'll meet a cast of Halloween characters including Sergeant Skull, a giant spider, Luna the Black Cat, the Woodland Witch, and many more. There'll be pumpkin tossing challenges, following hidden clues left by Dunstable's friendly ghost, broomstick races, and potion mixing to create an 'anti-curse' at our ancient cauldron. Perfect for families, this outdoor adventure is a great way to enjoy the autumn countryside, get outdoors, and make magical half-term memories. £3 per child per trail. Booking not needed.

Guests are also very welcome to bring their own traditional sweet treats.

description: Meet Santa will be returning to London Zoo in 2026. We have a variety of session types available for Meet Santa this year including Meet Santa Little ones can take part in Christmas crafts before they meet Santa in his magical grotto at the heart of London Zoo and receive a very special early Christmas gift to take home. Perhaps they’ll even be lucky enough to spot our animals snuffling around next door as well! Meet Santa Penguin Feed Head over to Penguin Beach to slide our Humboldt penguins some tasty fish! Then, take a quick tour through part of the Zoo before meeting Santa in his magical grotto and receiving a very special early Christmas present. Please note: this is not a hand-feed experience; participants will feed the penguins fish though a tube into their pool. Not suitable for children under 3 or those with seafood allergies. Quick tour lasts 10 to 15mins. We also have relaxed Meet Santa and Meet Santa Penguin Feed sessions available. Please be aware that your Meet Santa ticket alone does not include Zoo admission. All visitors must have a valid Zoo admission ticket or Zoo membership in addition to their Meet Santa tickets. Please visit our website for more information and to book your tickets.

local_offer: Hoglets Preschool provides an inclusive, nurturing and child-centred environment for children aged 0–5 years with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND). We work closely with children, parents/carers and other professionals to identify individual needs and provide appropriate support and reasonable adjustments. Our support includes adapting activities and the learning environment, providing visual and sensory resources, supporting communication and interaction, developing social and emotional skills, and promoting independence and confidence. We use the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework to support each child’s individual development and learning. Where appropriate, we work in partnership with the child’s family, SENCO and relevant professionals to follow individual support plans and ensure children receive consistent support. We aim to provide an accessible, welcoming environment where every child can participate, learn, play and achieve their potential.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Hoglets Preschool, we aim to provide an inclusive, nurturing and supportive environment where every child, including children with SEND, is valued, listened to and given the opportunity to reach their full potential. We aim to support children’s individual development, communication, confidence, independence, social skills and emotional wellbeing through personalised support and appropriate activities. We work closely with parents and other professionals to understand each child’s individual needs, identify appropriate support and monitor progress. Our aim is for children with SEND to feel safe, included and confident within the setting, while ensuring families feel listened to, supported and involved in their child’s learning and development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff are committed to ongoing SEND training and professional development. We ensure staff have an understanding of the needs of children with SEND and are able to identify when a child may require additional support. Staff work closely with parents, the SENCO and relevant professionals to ensure that appropriate strategies are put in place. Further SEND-specific training will be completed as required to meet the individual needs of children attending Hoglets Preschool. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We believe parents and carers are key partners in supporting children with SEND. We encourage open and regular communication with families and provide opportunities for parents to share information about their child’s strengths, needs, interests and development. Parents are involved in discussions about any additional support, targets or strategies and are kept informed about their child’s progress. Parents can get involved by sharing information about their child, attending meetings and reviews, contributing to their child’s individual support and development plans, and working with staff to identify strategies that can also be used at home. We welcome parents’ views and feedback and aim to work together to ensure each child receives consistent and appropriate support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We will work closely with parents and carers to keep you informed about your child’s progress, development and wellbeing. We will share observations, learning updates and progress through regular communication and discussions with parents. For children with SEND, we will provide additional support where appropriate, including individualised targets, strategies and regular reviews of their progress. We will work in partnership with parents, the child’s key person, SENCO and other professionals involved to ensure support is consistent and tailored to the child’s individual needs. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Hoglets Preschool aims to provide an inclusive and accessible environment where every child can participate, play and learn. We adapt activities, resources and the environment to meet individual needs. We provide a range of accessible resources, clear routines and opportunities for children to learn through play both indoors and outdoors. We will make reasonable adjustments where required and work with families and relevant professionals to identify and overcome any barriers to participation. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are welcome to contact Hoglets Preschool to discuss their child’s individual needs before starting. We will work with parents and carers to understand the child’s strengths, interests and areas where they may need additional support. Where appropriate, we can arrange a visit or settling-in sessions to help the child become familiar with the environment and staff. We will work with the family, SENCO and any other professionals involved to put appropriate support and reasonable adjustments in place before and during the child’s time at Hoglets. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Hoglets Preschool will continue to develop our SEND provision by working closely with parents, the SENCO and other professionals to ensure every child receives the support they need. We will regularly review children’s individual needs and adapt our environment, activities and resources to promote inclusion and participation. We will continue to develop staff knowledge and training around SEND, follow children’s individual support plans and use the EYFS to monitor progress. We will also build strong links with local SEND services and professionals so that appropriate advice, support and reasonable adjustments can be put in place promptly.

name: Relaxed Meet Santa at London Zoo
description: Meet Santa will be returning to London Zoo in 2026. We have a variety of relaxed sessions available for Meet Santa this year including: Meet Santa Relaxed Little ones can take part in Christmas crafts before they meet Santa in his magical grotto at the heart of London Zoo and receive a very special early Christmas gift to take home. Perhaps they’ll even be lucky enough to spot our animals snuffling around next door as well! Meet Santa Penguin Feed Relaxed Head over to Penguin Beach to slide our Humboldt penguins some tasty fish! Then, take a quick tour through part of the Zoo before meeting Santa in his magical grotto and receiving a very special early Christmas present. Please note: this is not a hand-feed experience; participants will feed the penguins fish though a tube into their pool. Not suitable for children under 3 or those with seafood allergies. Quick tour lasts 10 to 15mins. These sessions are the same as their non-relaxed counterparts but with dimmed lights, quieter sounds, and other reduced sensory stimulation to make the area feel more relaxed, specifically designed for those with additional needs. Please be aware that your Meet Santa ticket alone does not include Zoo admission. All visitors must have a valid Zoo admission ticket or Zoo membership in addition to their Meet Santa tickets. Please visit our website for more information and to book your tickets.

description: Gabeth Education Consultancy provides specialist maths tuition for young people aged 11 to 18, from Key Stage 3 and GCSE through to A Level Maths and Further Maths. Sessions run online through Microsoft Teams, or in person in Buckinghamshire, and are taught by Eb Otoo, an experienced Secondary Maths teacher and former head of department who has taught since 2006. name: Suzy Lamplugh Trust and National Stalking Helpline
description: The Suzy Lamplugh Trust helps victims of stalking, domestic violence and abuse. To ensure that what happened to Suzy does not happen to anyone else. We do this by Campaigning, Educating and Supporting people. Mission Our mission is to reduce the risk of violence and aggression through campaigning, education and support. Vision Our vision is a society in which people are safer - and feel safer - from violence and aggression; we want people to be able to live life to the full. Diana and Paul Lamplugh founded Suzy Lamplugh Trust in 1986 following the disappearance and later presumed murder of their daughter. Today we continue the work of Paul and Diana to reduce violence and aggression in society, supporting workplaces to help their lone and frontline workers be safer and feel safer. We also run the National Stalking Helpline, offering advice and support to anyone concerned about stalking, as well as campaigning for victims of stalking. This reminds us once again of the continuing tragedy of Suzy’s story and the importance of staying safe at work.

local_offer: Long Crendon Pre-School provides a stimulating, active and nurturing environment, full of excitement and challenge for children within the local and extended community. We operate an inclusive policy that encourages and celebrates diversity and ensures that all children have access to and can participate in all activities and opportunities that arise. At Long Crendon Pre-School we believe every child has a right to an education and we help children reach their full potential by planning for their individual needs through play based activities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We invite multi-agencies into the setting if required. Staff’s training is up to date, with courses from the local authority and our online training system. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENCO's are up to date with courses offered by the local authority and our online training system. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work very closely with parents at Long Crendon Pre-School and Out of School Club. When a child joins the setting we recommend at least 3 settling sessions. This is where the Parent/guardian and child are asked to stay for about an hour to ensure they are happy and comfortable. These sessions are spent one on one with your child’s Key person, we have found this beneficial to build a relationship and bond between child and Key person. We are flexible with our settling procedure and some children may need more than settling than others, Parents will be able to discuss this with their child’s Key person. Parents have regular conversations with staff when dropping off or collecting their child. Parents receive weekly observations from their child’s Key person on online learning journeys. We hold regular Parents evenings, and Parents are welcome to book any further meetings with Key persons if desired. We are run by a Parent committee which all Parents are welcome to join, we also welcome any Parent to volunteer their time at our setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We ask Parental permission to share any information about their child to other settings and agencies. We write reports on the Parent’s behalf. We invite Multi Agencies such as Speech and Language into our setting. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting is accessible to all abilities, indoors and out. We have an accessible disabled bathroom. Depending on the Child's needs we can add resources for them, and make relevant adaptations. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When a child joins our setting we recommend at least 3 settling in sessions, this is to help the child feel happy and comfortable at their new setting. We produce transition reports for every child when they leave our setting. We hold meetings with both the previous/new settings and Parents, and invite them into our Pre-School. name: Longwick Pre-school
description: Longwick Pre-school is situated in the village of Longwick near Princes Risborough in the District of Wycombe. The pre-school has been situated at Longwick Village Hall since 1990. We have access to a spacious and airy hall area where children can engage in large play, small world play, and table-based activities. Longwick Pre-school aims to create a safe, secure, and stimulating environment in which children can: Be healthy, stay safe and enjoy and achieve through well-planned learning opportunities; Learn to respect others and be respected in return; Gain the confidence to move on to the next steps in their education; Experience a wide range of activities that will enhance their developmental progress through all six areas of development. At Longwick Pre-school children are able to explore a wide range of activities that cover each area of learning for the Early Years Foundation Stage. Children can explore our indoor and outdoor learning environments independently through free play and also in adult-led activities. We follow the children's interests and use this as a basis for providing activities and provocations that will help them to learn and develop. We run a lunch club each day of the week, 12 midday to 1pm. We are open everyday, 9am to 3pm, Monday to Friday with breakfast club from 8am to 9am every day of the week also. We have spaces for children aged 2 to 4 years. We can offer places to funded 2-year-olds whose families are receiving some additional forms of government support and for those working families too as well as 30 hours of flexible funding available for 3 to 4-year-olds. From Easter 2026, we are now accepting Rising Two's (children the term before they turn two years old) on three mornings a week; Monday, Tuesday & Thursday, 9am-12pm. Longwick Pre-school is a Registered Charity. Our Charity Number is 1026259.

local_offer: Longwick Pre-school runs from a spacious village hall setting on a village green. It has full accessibility for wheelchair users or those with limited mobility. The hall is also equipped with a Hearing Loop for those with a hearing impairment. We aim to provide early years education for children aged from 2 to 4 years (and from Easter, Rising Two's (the term before the child turns 2 years old). We have policies and procedures in place to cater to children with a SEND as well as staff trained in SEND areas and a wide variety of contacts that we can call upon to support families with a child with a SEND. This support ensures that we can help each individual child reach their developmental goals.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We follow the Early Years procedure for accessing guidance and referring children to external professional services. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our Manager is a Level 3 Award Special Educational Needs Coordinator and we regularly attend the SEND Network Meetings for up to date SEND information. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are invited to join the committee which oversees the pre-school's running. This includes attending meetings 2/3 times a year plus helping out at regular fundraising events. It's a great way to meet new people! Support the pre-school financially by attending fundraising events. We ask for snack donations which allow parents to directly contribute to the day to day running of the setting. Parents can share skills, pets, items of interest that enhances the children's experiences. We issue a Parent's Voice Survey three times a year and welcome feedback to improve our service. We share information with parents via our nursery management system called Famly on a daily basis with also a weekly round up of what the children have been experiencing at re-school throughout the week plus information on Facebook and email. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Practitioners are always on hand to share information about their child's day (verbal chat). A more confidential chat can always be arranged in private if necessary. We use the Famly Nursery software package for all children reporting observations and photographs of artwork and writing that they may produce. In addition, we hold a parents evening annually. Parents have access of their child's learning via our Famly app and can access at any time. When a child leaves the pre-school to go to school or another setting, the Key Person will produce a short report of their developmental progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Longwick Pre-school runs from a spacious village hall setting on a village green. It has full accessibility for wheelchair users or those with limited mobility. The hall is also equipped with a Hearing Loop for those with a hearing impairment. The village hall has a large car park for stress-free child drop off and collection. We endeavour to meet all users needs and would modify the environment accordingly. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We advertise local schools' open mornings to provide parents with a broad variety of schooling options. Local schools teachers arrange to visit the children who will be attending their school. Key persons will chat with these teachers to provide additional useful information. Those that will attend Longwick School have the opportunity to have lunch with the Reception Class and other transitions during the summer term. When a child leaves the pre-school to go to school or another setting, the Key Person will produce a short report of their developmental progress. name: Longwick Pre-school
description: Longwick Pre-school is situated in the village of Longwick near Princes Risborough in the District of Wycombe. The pre-school has been situated at Longwick Village Hall since 1990. We have access to a spacious and airy hall area where children can engage in large play, small world play, and table-based activities. Longwick Pre-school aims to create a safe, secure, and stimulating environment in which children can: Be healthy, stay safe and enjoy and achieve through well-planned learning opportunities; Learn to respect others and be respected in return; Gain the confidence to move on to the next steps in their education; Experience a wide range of activities that will enhance their developmental progress through all six areas of development. At Longwick Pre-school children are able to explore a wide range of activities that cover each area of learning for the Early Years Foundation Stage. Children can explore our indoor and outdoor learning environments independently through free play and also in adult-led activities. We follow the children's interests and use this as a basis for providing activities and provocations that will help them to learn and develop. We run a lunch club each day of the week, 12 midday to 1pm. We are open everyday, 9am to 3pm, Monday to Friday with breakfast club from 8am to 9am every day of the week also. We have spaces for children aged 2 to 4 years. We can offer places to funded 2-year-olds whose families are receiving some additional forms of government support and for those working families too as well as 30 hours of flexible funding available for 3 to 4-year-olds. From Easter 2026, we are now accepting Rising Two's (children the term before they turn two years old) on three mornings a week; Monday, Tuesday & Thursday, 9am-12pm. Longwick Pre-school is a Registered Charity. Our Charity Number is 1026259.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Supporting children with speech, language and communication needs. Recognising and supporting children with SEN level 3 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with us. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a large step leading to the front door but easy access via a back entrance. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

name: Louise Compton
description: Welcome to Mother Goose Day Care (based in Chalfont St Peter) – A Place Where Every Child Feels Loved, Safe, and Ready to Explore! At Mother Goose Day Care, we believe that a child’s environment plays a crucial role in their growth, happiness, and development. Our setting is carefully designed to provide a safe, welcoming, and stimulating space where children can thrive in every way. Our Home, Your Child’s New Home Away From Home We are located in a spacious, bright, and homely setting, where every corner is thoughtfully arranged to foster creativity, learning, and socialisation. Our home is filled with warmth and love, with spaces dedicated to both group activities and quiet, reflective moments. With the comfort and security of being in a familiar home environment, children feel at ease and free to explore their world in a way that suits them best. The setting itself is a carefully designed balance of comfort and practicality. We have large, airy rooms filled with soft lighting, natural materials, and cozy corners where children can curl up with a book, engage in imaginative play, or take a rest when needed. From the very first moment they step in, they’ll feel like they are part of our family—welcomed with open arms into an environment that is nurturing, joyful, and safe. Indoor Learning Spaces: Creativity, Exploration, and Growth Inside our home, we have dedicated spaces that promote various aspects of learning and growth. We’ve created rich, engaging areas where children can explore their creativity, practice their fine motor skills, and build social connections. Our playroom is filled with an array of carefully selected toys and materials, each chosen to inspire learning through play. From building blocks and puzzles to art supplies and musical instruments, each item is an invitation for exploration. The space encourages children to engage in imaginative play, experiment with different textures, and share stories or games with others. There is also a quiet area designed for calm, where children can explore books, engage in one-on-one time with caregivers, or simply unwind. Here, children can settle down after active play or enjoy a peaceful moment with a favorite toy or story. Outdoor Learning and Play: An Adventure Every Day Our expansive, fully enclosed garden offers children the opportunity to explore nature, learn about growing food, and enjoy endless hours of active play. With plenty of space to run, jump, and explore, our garden is a key part of the learning experience at Mother Goose Day Care. The outdoor environment is a living classroom, where children can engage in physical activities that support motor skills development, teamwork, and environmental awareness. We grow a variety of fruits and vegetables, allowing children to experience the joy and satisfaction of nurturing plants and watching them grow. They can also engage in sensory play, such as sand and water activities, or explore various outdoor toys and equipment that encourage physical exercise. The garden isn’t just a space for fun; it’s a place where children can experience the world around them—learning to appreciate the environment, observe nature, and play collaboratively with peers. Frequent Outings to Extend Learning Beyond the Home Beyond the walls of our home, we love to take the children on adventures that provide rich learning opportunities. We frequently visit local parks, libraries, farms, and toddler groups, and we also enjoy outings to soft play centers, bowling, and other exciting places. These outings not only allow children to interact with a wider variety of people but also encourage them to explore different environments and develop new social skills. Whether we’re visiting animals at a farm, discovering new books at the library, or simply enjoying the outdoors at a park, these experiences are integral to broadening the children’s horizons and providing learning moments beyond the day-to-day routine. A Family-Oriented and Supportive Environment Our setting isn’t just a daycare; it’s a warm, family-oriented space where everyone is treated like part of our extended family. With my husband Dave, a dedicated head teacher, and our children, also beloved pets—a playful cat, a guinea pig, and a friendly dog—our home is filled with love, laughter, and a sense of belonging. The presence of our pets adds a special touch, offering comfort and companionship to the children as they learn about empathy, responsibility, and caring for animals. As a family, we work together to ensure that every child feels welcomed, supported, and loved, creating a strong foundation of trust and security. Your child will feel safe and valued in our care, surrounded by a community that genuinely cares for their well-being. Your Child’s Progress – Keeping You Involved Every Step of the Way We believe in an open, transparent partnership with parents. To ensure you’re always involved in your child’s learning journey, we maintain detailed, personalized learning journals using Google Docs. This allows you to stay up-to-date with your child’s progress, milestones, and experiences, no matter where you are. You’ll receive regular updates and can share in the excitement of your child’s achievements as they grow. At Mother Goose Day Care, we are dedicated to offering more than just childcare; we offer a holistic, nurturing experience that supports your child’s emotional, social, and cognitive development. Our setting is designed with love, care, and thoughtfulness—creating a space where your child can thrive, feel loved, and develop into a happy, confident, and curious individual. We can’t wait to welcome you and your child into our wonderful, supportive setting—where every child is not just cared for but truly valued.

local_offer: I offer a warm, supportive, and inclusive environment for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities, providing tailored childminding services that nurture their development and well-being. Whether it’s pre-school care or wraparound support for school-aged children, I’m here to offer individualised attention and care during term time or school holidays. With a deep understanding of the unique challenges that children with SEND may face, I create a calm, structured setting where each child can flourish at their own pace. My approach focuses on creating a positive, enriching experience through personalised activities that support their growth, communication, and social skills. I’m committed to working closely with parents and caregivers to ensure that your child’s specific needs are met, allowing them to feel safe, valued, and supported at all times.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Mother Goose Day Care, we provide a nurturing and inclusive environment for children with SEND. We tailor our approach to each child's unique needs, fostering their emotional, social, and cognitive development. Our family-oriented setting promotes confidence, independence, and positive social interactions. We work closely with families, providing regular updates and personalised support to ensure every child feels valued, safe, and included. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have recently completed the Level 4 Diploma in SEND and hold other qualifications including Level 3 child psychology, deaf awareness and supporting children with Speech, Language and Communication Needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are supported and involved at both ends of everyday, pick up and drop off. SEND plans and assessments collected over longer terms are shared with the parents. Parental involvement can be visiting the children at a park or whilst we are visiting somewhere else too. Parents share assessments made and all achievements are developed between the parents and I. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I follow the assessment procedures and stages outlined for all Early Years providers. For SEND pupils these statements can be broken down into smaller steps with inclusive plans developed so that key indicators are targeted over the broad spectrum of assessments. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The childminding space is open and all laid out on the same floor. The property leads out into a flat garden space and patio. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Anyone can begin using the service by contacting me via the various channels shared including phone and email. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Sensory spaces are to be developed in the garden and the use the sensory toys in the home.
