name: Louise Compton
description: Welcome to Mother Goose Day Care (based in Chalfont St Peter) – A Place Where Every Child Feels Loved, Safe, and Ready to Explore! At Mother Goose Day Care, we believe that a child’s environment plays a crucial role in their growth, happiness, and development. Our setting is carefully designed to provide a safe, welcoming, and stimulating space where children can thrive in every way. Our Home, Your Child’s New Home Away From Home We are located in a spacious, bright, and homely setting, where every corner is thoughtfully arranged to foster creativity, learning, and socialisation. Our home is filled with warmth and love, with spaces dedicated to both group activities and quiet, reflective moments. With the comfort and security of being in a familiar home environment, children feel at ease and free to explore their world in a way that suits them best. The setting itself is a carefully designed balance of comfort and practicality. We have large, airy rooms filled with soft lighting, natural materials, and cozy corners where children can curl up with a book, engage in imaginative play, or take a rest when needed. From the very first moment they step in, they’ll feel like they are part of our family—welcomed with open arms into an environment that is nurturing, joyful, and safe. Indoor Learning Spaces: Creativity, Exploration, and Growth Inside our home, we have dedicated spaces that promote various aspects of learning and growth. We’ve created rich, engaging areas where children can explore their creativity, practice their fine motor skills, and build social connections. Our playroom is filled with an array of carefully selected toys and materials, each chosen to inspire learning through play. From building blocks and puzzles to art supplies and musical instruments, each item is an invitation for exploration. The space encourages children to engage in imaginative play, experiment with different textures, and share stories or games with others. There is also a quiet area designed for calm, where children can explore books, engage in one-on-one time with caregivers, or simply unwind. Here, children can settle down after active play or enjoy a peaceful moment with a favorite toy or story. Outdoor Learning and Play: An Adventure Every Day Our expansive, fully enclosed garden offers children the opportunity to explore nature, learn about growing food, and enjoy endless hours of active play. With plenty of space to run, jump, and explore, our garden is a key part of the learning experience at Mother Goose Day Care. The outdoor environment is a living classroom, where children can engage in physical activities that support motor skills development, teamwork, and environmental awareness. We grow a variety of fruits and vegetables, allowing children to experience the joy and satisfaction of nurturing plants and watching them grow. They can also engage in sensory play, such as sand and water activities, or explore various outdoor toys and equipment that encourage physical exercise. The garden isn’t just a space for fun; it’s a place where children can experience the world around them—learning to appreciate the environment, observe nature, and play collaboratively with peers. Frequent Outings to Extend Learning Beyond the Home Beyond the walls of our home, we love to take the children on adventures that provide rich learning opportunities. We frequently visit local parks, libraries, farms, and toddler groups, and we also enjoy outings to soft play centers, bowling, and other exciting places. These outings not only allow children to interact with a wider variety of people but also encourage them to explore different environments and develop new social skills. Whether we’re visiting animals at a farm, discovering new books at the library, or simply enjoying the outdoors at a park, these experiences are integral to broadening the children’s horizons and providing learning moments beyond the day-to-day routine. A Family-Oriented and Supportive Environment Our setting isn’t just a daycare; it’s a warm, family-oriented space where everyone is treated like part of our extended family. With my husband Dave, a dedicated head teacher, and our children, also beloved pets—a playful cat, a guinea pig, and a friendly dog—our home is filled with love, laughter, and a sense of belonging. The presence of our pets adds a special touch, offering comfort and companionship to the children as they learn about empathy, responsibility, and caring for animals. As a family, we work together to ensure that every child feels welcomed, supported, and loved, creating a strong foundation of trust and security. Your child will feel safe and valued in our care, surrounded by a community that genuinely cares for their well-being. Your Child’s Progress – Keeping You Involved Every Step of the Way We believe in an open, transparent partnership with parents. To ensure you’re always involved in your child’s learning journey, we maintain detailed, personalized learning journals using Google Docs. This allows you to stay up-to-date with your child’s progress, milestones, and experiences, no matter where you are. You’ll receive regular updates and can share in the excitement of your child’s achievements as they grow. At Mother Goose Day Care, we are dedicated to offering more than just childcare; we offer a holistic, nurturing experience that supports your child’s emotional, social, and cognitive development. Our setting is designed with love, care, and thoughtfulness—creating a space where your child can thrive, feel loved, and develop into a happy, confident, and curious individual. We can’t wait to welcome you and your child into our wonderful, supportive setting—where every child is not just cared for but truly valued.

description: Animal Antiks is a day provision supporting young people and adults on a 220-acre working farm in the beautiful Buckinghamshire countryside. Animal Antiks' unique approach is non-segregated, providing a safe environment that supports a wide mix of ages and disabilities. It allows the opportunity to normalise anxieties and build confidence along with life, social, and functional skills. Animal-assisted therapy and learning can help overcome anxiety and isolation, boost self-confidence and awareness of how a young person's behaviour affects those around them, and improve communication skills. Some choose to spend time with their favourite animal, grooming a miniature pony, walking goats, alpacas, or sheep, or sitting with the chickens and collecting the eggs. Others enjoy getting involved with more manual tasks around the farm or group activities, such as working on projects. For young adults struggling in conventional school settings, we provide the opportunity to complete Post-16 Level 1 and Level 2 animal care qualifications alongside function skills (various levels) in English, mathematics, and ICT. For more information or to arrange a visit, please contact us by phone or email. How to get here: We are based on a working farm. The Number 60 bus from Aylesbury or Buckingham stops in the village, and we are about a 10-minute walk from the stop.

local_offer: We support children and young people with additional needs throughout the year, offering a unique and alternative approach to normalising anxieties and building confidence. We offer education in functional subjects on-site for those young people who can't reach their potential in traditional settings. For young adults, our day provision provides opportunities to improve their skills and build the confidence needed for employment or volunteering.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our main area of work is Post-16 Training, which allows young people who have struggled with normal schooling systems to gain entry-level City and Guilds qualifications in Animal Care, Equine Care and Horticulture. These young people all have EHCPs and SEND needs. We also regularly work with children aged 10 and over, to help them be more education-ready or to learn in an alternative setting. This is often as a release from the confines of their classroom environment or in support of those who have disengaged from school. The new HAF activities will expand on our existing offerings and allow us to share the benefits of being around animals and working outdoors with even more children and young people. We provide a safe environment and activities that encourage self-confidence, improved communication, and teamwork skills through working with the animals on the farm, backed by individual support for each child or young person. Children and young people with SEND often say that they feel that they belong here. Anxieties can be normalised and reduced in the supportive environment, and there is always an animal to take timeout with if someone feels anxious. Individual needs are assessed, and our experienced and dedicated staff work with each child/young person to help them achieve their potential. Those with SEND are supported to try new things including contact with our friendly animals, outdoor activities or when we use the kitchen for baking or making healthy lunches. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All our staff are experienced and qualified to work with SEND. Volunteers all work with a member of staff. Both staff and volunteers are all DBS checked before they join us. Animal Antiks works with Action4Youth for training, and staff access the training opportunities provided, along with any additional training required. New staff are given any training they need to cover our basic requirements. We have regular training sessions throughout the year as required and have designated training days at the start of each academic year that include safeguarding, first aid, equality and diversity. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have a regular newsletter for parents and carers of our education/training students and they are encouraged to feedback or request articles in each issue. We also ask them to contact us via email or telephone if they have any suggestions or concerns. Due to the nature of Animal Antiks, we don’t expect parental help currently but we actively consider their feedback, and where appropriate we act on suggestions etc. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We communicate with our children and young people whilst we are supporting them, daily staff sessions allow any concerns/difficulties to be raised. Anything that needs to be shared with families is communicated either by telephone or by email. Regular contact with families is maintained directly, by telephone or e-mail - whichever method is preferred. For our education/training placements, we hold regular reviews and link in with SEND representatives at Local Authorities, Social Care and other organisations working with the family as required. We have a 'your voice' scheme for them to complete feedback cards, and we also carry out an annual survey to get input about what we offer and what development opportunities we will look for. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Whilst we are a working farm, we have clear, flat access up at the main farm and hard pathways around the fields to allow easy access to most areas. Some slightly undulating paths exist, but staff can support children/ young people if requested. Our barns all have flat access, and we can set up ramps if access to some of our low-stepped buildings is required. We have toilets and warm water hand washing on site including one disabled toilet. Sometimes, there can be a lot of noise from the animals or our machinery, but this is usually short-lived and part of the farm's day-to-day operation. We find that after a couple of visits, children and young people can accept it without causing any anxiety. Until then, we can move to a quieter area if required. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? For Post-16 Training or farm therapy through school placements, we suggest a referral is made directly to us and then we arrange a visit, followed by a trial session. For general farm therapy sessions, we have a form on our website. We also occasionally run holiday sessions, where the whole family can attend (details will be on our website). What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As our main focus is on SEND children, young people and adults, we are well placed to be able to offer something for most people. However, we continually look to expand the offer we can provide on-site as well as the therapy services and to bring in new innovative ways to improve the lives of those with SEND and mental health issues such as social isolation, anxiety, depression and dementia.

I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child. I have just completed an online Understanding Autism course to help me help the children I look after.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have recently completed a course on mental health in children and young adults and another about understand Autism. I have not been on any specific training yet but am happy to go on any training needed to support the children I care for. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents, and inform them about their child’s learning, development and progress on a regular basis in a manner which suits them. I ask parents to share information about their child’s likes and dislikes, the activities which they find difficult and those which they enjoy the most. I aim to ensure that activities are extended to support children to meet their potential within the setting and share ideas with parents for use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children and any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents. I am happy to discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Unfortunately my home has steps down to the front door and quite a large step to get into the house so accessibility is not very easy. My outdoor area is accessible through a side gate or shallow steps from my living room doors onto a fenced patio. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I have links with local schools and pre-schools and other childcare settings. When children arrive I encourage families to complete an ‘all about me’ sheet so that I have information to help a smooth transition and I encourage parents to have some ‘settling in visits’ with their child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and any training I need through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

description: M for Money Credit Union is a not-for-profit financial cooperative offering safe savings and affordable loans to people who live or work in Buckinghamshire. Members who have saved regularly for at least three months can then apply to borrow up to three times their savings. We are run by our members for the benefit of our members. Since we are a financial cooperative, any profit made by the credit union is given back to the members in the form of a dividend. We are a registered financial institution authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority. Reg No. 216633. Below are some of the services that we offer. 1. Savings: With M for Money Credit Union, saving is simple and helps secure your future. Set aside funds weekly, fortnightly, or monthly via standing order or payroll deduction—watch your savings grow! Withdraw anytime, unless a loan balance applies. Plus, your savings are protected up to £85,000 per person by the FSCS. We offer a wide range of savings accounts, including: - Basic Savings Accounts - Christmas Savings Accounts - Holiday Savings Accounts - Junior Savings Accounts 2. Lending: We understand that everyone's circumstances are different, which is why we offer a wide range of loans that enable all members to be considered on their own merit. Below are some of the loans that we offer: - Child Benefit Loan - New Member Starter Loan - Introductory Loan, available to those who sign up to our Salary Saving Scheme - Payroll Loans - Holiday Loans - Homeowner Loans - Savers Loan - Transport Loan 3. Salary Saving Scheme We have partnered with a few local employers, including Paradigm Housing, Buckinghamshire Council, Wexham Park Hospital, Frimley Park Hospital, Heatherwood Hospital, Hillingdon Hospital, and Slough Council, to name but a few. Employees can pay into their M for Money Credit Union account by saving from their salary. They can then apply for an introductory loan of up to £3000, repayable over up to 60 months. If you would like your employer to sign up for the Salary Saving Scheme, please get them to contact us by email. 4. Child Benefit Savings and Loan Plan: All parents are now eligible to apply for a loan of £500*, or £750* if Child Benefit payments are deposited directly into your Credit Union account. The loan is repayable over 50 weeks for parents receiving weekly Child Benefit payments, or 13 months for those receiving payments every four weeks. Please note that two loan schemes are available to successful applicants. Further details regarding the £250 Top-Up and Revolving Credit schemes can be found below. Members who have successfully repaid two or more previous loans may apply for a £1,000* Child Benefit Loan, provided they hold a minimum of £100 in savings. *APR: 42.6%, in comparison to a typical doorstep lender rate of 399.7%. You can find out more about us and our services on our website.

name: Mable | Online Speech and Language Therapy
description: If you’re concerned about your child’s speech, language, or communication, then Mable therapy can help. All of our therapists are fully qualified and trained to assess and treat a range of speech, language and communication needs. We are registered with the Health and Care Professionals Council as well as the Royal College of Speech and Language therapists so you can be sure you are receiving the best possible care. During the therapy process, we like to build a strong relationship with both you and your child, interacting with you online, through activities and games designed to stimulate engagement and encourage progress. Your Mable sessions are delivered through our online platform at a time of day which is convenient for you and your family. After each session, you will receive a report to remind you of your child’s therapy goals and to demonstrate their progress from week to week. Between sessions, your therapist will give you lots of ideas about how you can support your child to learn and develop. This is important for them to generalise their new skills in real-life situations. Mable Therapy, speech and language therapy that is innovative, impactful, and is as individual as your child.

name: Magdalen College School (Oxfordshire)
description: Mixed-gender independent school in Oxford, Oxfordshire for 7 to 19-years-olds. Magdalen College School (MCS) is a remarkable place. We are now well into our sixth century, and our former pupils include scholars, war heroes, musicians, Olympians, a Nobel Prize laureate, a Hollywood film director, and a saint. Our success in public examinations, in securing places at top universities, and in an astonishing array of extra-curricular pursuits ensure that we continue this proud tradition. We do so by nurturing the individual potential of each of our pupils, and above all, we believe that learning is as fun as it is fulfilling. We achieve so highly not because we teach to the test; the challenge of what we offer goes far beyond that. The quality of the conversations in our classrooms and beyond them gives you a sense of what makes MCS distinctive and inspiring. The atmosphere here is both relaxed and rigorous, both high-octane and down-to-earth. Everything we do focuses on the needs of the individual child. MCS was founded in 1480 by William Waynflete: schoolmaster, bishop of Winchester and Lord Chancellor of England. Being of humble origins, Waynflete was determined that others of ability should be given the opportunity to learn, to serve and to prosper as he did. And so Magdalen College School offers a transformative education in our global university city, the community to which we are proud to make a deep contribution. We also offer substantial help with fees as part of our mission to ensure that people of all backgrounds continue to learn together and maintain the school’s diverse strength.

description: Mixed-gender independent school in Oxford, Oxfordshire for 7 to 19-years-olds. Magdalen College School (MCS) is a remarkable place. We are now well into our sixth century, and our former pupils include scholars, war heroes, musicians, Olympians, a Nobel Prize laureate, a Hollywood film director, and a saint. Our success in public examinations, in securing places at top universities, and in an astonishing array of extra-curricular pursuits ensure that we continue this proud tradition. We do so by nurturing the individual potential of each of our pupils, and above all, we believe that learning is as fun as it is fulfilling. We achieve so highly not because we teach to the test; the challenge of what we offer goes far beyond that. The quality of the conversations in our classrooms and beyond them gives you a sense of what makes MCS distinctive and inspiring. The atmosphere here is both relaxed and rigorous, both high-octane and down-to-earth. Everything we do focuses on the needs of the individual child. MCS was founded in 1480 by William Waynflete: schoolmaster, bishop of Winchester and Lord Chancellor of England. Being of humble origins, Waynflete was determined that others of ability should be given the opportunity to learn, to serve and to prosper as he did. And so Magdalen College School offers a transformative education in our global university city, the community to which we are proud to make a deep contribution. We also offer substantial help with fees as part of our mission to ensure that people of all backgrounds continue to learn together and maintain the school’s diverse strength.

description: Maids Moreton Pre-school provides a learning environment that is safe, healthy and stimulating. We offer a child-centred approach, where children are encouraged to develop their self-confidence and imagination, and build and mark-making skills through child-initiated activities. We provide a well-resourced outside area, with our own mini-park area where the children are able to use their balancing skills and large motor skills while accessing the equipment. All are planned and organised by our Forest School Leader. We work together with parents to ensure that the needs of every child are met, on entry to pre-school and during their time with us through parental daily contact information and consultations.

local_offer: The setting is based on a one-level building - we have stairs at the entrance to the preschool with large double open-fronted glazed doors. The outside area is large and spacious, a covered area is accessible to all. All activities outside of the setting are subject to a risk assessment. following this process, the Manager would assess whether any adaptations to the activities would need to be made before a child could access them. We aim to provide a stimulating environment so that every child who attends has access to all we have to offer. We will consult with parents beforehand and outside agencies that are involved with a child's care, so that any emotional or physical needs are met by ourselves, along with dietary requirements. We will offer settling-in sessions beforehand to become familiar with any additional needs a child may require and work together with the parents to resolve them before their child starts.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Maids Moreton Pre-school we are able to access help and advice from Buckinghamshire Early Years service for : Speech and Language. Early Years Advisors. Specialist Teachers for (Hearing and Sight). Health Visitors. Our staff have attended courses on Autism, Makaton, Speech and language. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Members of staff completed training for Autism an AET Programme (Making sense of Autism) on 9 July 2019. The staff that attended were Kim Chaplin. Our SENCO Kim Chaplin has attended the Early Bird programme(for under five years) from January 2020 to March 2020. This is a support programme for parents and carers, offering advice and guidance on strategies and approaches for dealing with young autistic children. The programme works on understanding autism, building confidence to encourage interaction and communication, and understanding and supporting behaviour. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Maids Moreton Pre-School introduced in July 2019 a Parents Session for children new to the Pre-School, which involved showing parents what we provide during a session. We found that this session was very successful and gave parents the chance to talk with staff and join in with the children's activities that were provided. Maids Moreton Pre-School sends out Half termly Newsletters by email and paper-based to parents informing them of up-and-coming events (Fundraising) and the chance to be involved. We hold parent afternoons when you will have the chance to have an informal chat with your child's key person. As we are a small team, you will be able to talk with any member of staff, regarding your child or if you would like to share some time within Pre-school either reading a story or sharing any special talents you may have with the children, come and speak to a member of staff. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At Maids Moreton Pre-school we observe children's development daily through our online journals (Tapestry) parents are able to log onto their accounts and look at observations through pictures of children's activities during a session. We will also let you know through Tapestry about what your child is working towards. If you do not have access to any online devices, we will be more than happy to provide paper copies for you of your child's development. For children that may need extra help, we will work together with you to co-produce a support plan that works well for your child, this would mean regular meetings, some of which will be informal and some that may include other professionals that could help and advise us on the right path for your child from Buckinghamshire Council. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We are able to offer access to all areas of our setting. Due to access to the Pre-school building at present being 4 steps, we would be able to supply access through transportable ramps for wheelchair access when required. We would work closely with Occupational Therapists to make sure that tables and chairs were suitable for the children, Together with toilet access and accessories when required. We have child handrails to the entrance of Pre-school and at present, the edge of the steps are painted so children can judge the depth and edges. The majority of the outside area of our setting is flat and accessible for the children to use unaided, we have a small grassed mound, which children access also. We have a wooded area that the children can access weekly from the Spring Term onwards with supervision. For children that have mobility issues, we would work with parents closely to risk assess this area to cater for the child's needs, so they are able to access the learning with their peers. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Initially make contact with the Pre-School manager via phone or email, to arrange a visit and an informal chat about your child's needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? At present, our staff have recently attended Autism training and Speech and Language, Makaton. Our SENCO has attended an Early Bird Programme held by the Autism Society one day a week until March 2020. This course will give valuable knowledge and understanding about Autism and how we can help to understand the children's needs that attend our setting. Through Buckinghamshire Early Years and their SEND advisors, we are able to contact them for advice on appropriate training that may be available and refresher courses. The Manager and Deputy: Are both holders of the level 3 Sendco qualification and the manager has Speech and Language training.

local_offer: At Manor Farm Infant School we individually assess and monitor the educational needs of every pupil. We provide for those needs as effectively as possible, referring to specialist help, both internally and from outside agencies, whenever necessary. We aim to identify those pupils who are not making appropriate progress as early as possible and make provision for them accordingly. Each half term teachers, SENDCo and the headteacher meet to review children’s levels and discuss any children falling behind and the support put in place. Pupils may also be identified by parents and school staff through observation, ongoing formative assessment, and by tracking pupil progress through data analysis. The barriers to the learning of these pupils may be in the form of physical or sensory issues; social, emotional or mental health factors; cognitive needs or relating to their communication and interaction. We believe that parental involvement is essential at all stages and the school aims to encourage parents/ carers as partners in the learning process. The school aims to promote a happy, caring and secure environment enabling children to achieve their full potential academically, as individuals and as part of society. We believe that quality first teaching is of paramount importance for all pupils. We implement a curriculum of work based on the "small steps to learning" philosophy which encourages children with special needs to develop a growing confidence in their abilities, believing they can succeed. Teachers implemented a differentiated curriculum and this is accessed by all pupils including those with special educational needs. Teachers plan work carefully - differentiating input, support, task, and outcome, as appropriate, to meet the needs of every member of the class. Teachers differentiate according to pupil needs and using the ‘Ordinally Available Provision’ document where appropriate. This may take the following forms: - modification of language/questioning to pupils - use of visual clues to support visual learners; visual timetables - pre-teaching of vocabulary or concepts - differentiated tasks and work - adult intervention Monitoring and assessment of progress are carried out regularly. If there are still concerns over a pupil’s progress, then additional provision or interventions may be introduced. These may take the form of individual or small group support, or specific programs to address a need. An example of a specific program to support children with emotional and social development is our ELSA group to address issues and concerns in this area. https://www.manorfarm-inf.bucks.sch.uk/page/?title=SEND&pid=34 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The school aims to promote a happy, caring and secure environment enabling children to achieve their full potential academically, as individuals and as part of society. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? During the last year appropriate staff have received training on the following: - Lego Therapy - Specialist Teacher Advice Sessions - Hearing Specialist Advice sessions - SEND in Early Year Foundation Stage - Speech and Language Advice Sessions - Occupational Therapy Advice Sessions - Step On - Mental Health Awareness - Adapting the Curriculum for children with SEND - Managing Dysregulation for Complex SEND Pupils - An introduction to Downs Syndrome How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Manor Farm Community Infant School is on 2 levels and wheelchair access is available to the hall and main reception areas but not the upstairs classrooms. We have put in hand rails along steps to aid easy access for pupils and blocks to enable easy reach of hand basins. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: Anna Irwin
description: I have been married to my husband Paul for 30 years (in October!) and we have two grown-up children. We live in the Springhill area, Grendon Underwood. I am Ofsted graded ‘good’ with over 20 years experience of working in childcare. I enjoy music, playing the flute and often bringing this passion into my Setting, which the children enjoy. Since lockdown, we have also been enjoying yoga which is not only good for keeping fit it also helps our mental health as well as being lots of fun too! We have a large enclosed garden with the exciting new addition of our summer house for the children to play in. We are also very lucky that we back onto fields available for added outdoor play (which is great for hide and seek, conker/blackberry picking, scavenger hunts, nature walks and burning off energy) together with a large dedicated playroom and downstairs toilet. My home is within walking distance of local shops, schools and park. Positive feedback on questionnaires received by the parents. They value the fact that children are part of the family and enjoy the activities provided in a home-from-home environment together with the opportunity for lots of sensory and messy play activities. We meet up with other local Childminders and attend various groups which helps the children’s social skills and gives them the experience of being in larger groups. I often plan trips out during school holidays, which provides children with stimulation, variety and exercise. My Husband, Paul, who is registered as my Assistant, will often join us to assist on days out. I have also worked in a pre-school and ran the hot lunch facility at the local school. I care for all children in my setting with equal concern. Written references are available.

description: I have been married to my husband Paul for 30 years (in October!) and we have two grown-up children. We live in the Springhill area, Grendon Underwood. I am Ofsted graded ‘good’ with over 20 years experience of working in childcare. I enjoy music, playing the flute and often bringing this passion into my Setting, which the children enjoy. Since lockdown, we have also been enjoying yoga which is not only good for keeping fit it also helps our mental health as well as being lots of fun too! We have a large enclosed garden with the exciting new addition of our summer house for the children to play in. We are also very lucky that we back onto fields available for added outdoor play (which is great for hide and seek, conker/blackberry picking, scavenger hunts, nature walks and burning off energy) together with a large dedicated playroom and downstairs toilet. My home is within walking distance of local shops, schools and park. Positive feedback on questionnaires received by the parents. They value the fact that children are part of the family and enjoy the activities provided in a home-from-home environment together with the opportunity for lots of sensory and messy play activities. We meet up with other local Childminders and attend various groups which helps the children’s social skills and gives them the experience of being in larger groups. I often plan trips out during school holidays, which provides children with stimulation, variety and exercise. My Husband, Paul, who is registered as my Assistant, will often join us to assist on days out. I have also worked in a pre-school and ran the hot lunch facility at the local school. I care for all children in my setting with equal concern. Written references are available.

local_offer: The aim of this document is to enable families to see the support that they would receive for their child at Manor Grove Montessori. It provides clear information about what we have in place, to enable the child to achieve their full potential. We work within the guidance of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework and use this to promote each child’s learning and development. We regard each child as being unique and endeavour to meet their individual needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our settings outcome is to provide every child with the best possible start in life. Which will help them to develop and prepare for their future education. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The SENCO has recently completed the level 3 Cache Awards for SENCOs. She also attends the termly SEN meetings and any online training they offer through the network, such as 'Leading good autism practice'. All the staff within the setting take part in regular CPD courses throughout the year such as 'positive language', 'making sense of autism' and 'communication and language' to name just a few. Staff will undertake training in order to help the needs of children that are currently attending the setting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are a key part to their child's development. When a child starts at Manor Grove, we will do settling in visits with both parent/carer and child. During this time your child can get to know us, with the security of yourself being present. We can discuss your child's development, such as what their achievements are, their interests, anything that they may struggle with and if they require additional support with anything. Once your child is in our care, we update parents on a daily basis, by both speaking with them directly during hand over and by also using an app called 'blossom', which can be logged into to see your child's achievements. You can also add achievements, so that we can see what your child likes doing at home, and these could be incorporated into activities here at the nursery. You will be given a key person, whom will be your main point of contact and they will take care of your child during the day. In their absence another member of staff will cover for them. We are a very small nursery, so you will get to know all the staff as well as your key person. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As mentioned above we have our 'blossom app', which we update regularly with photos and observations of your child's achievements. At the end of both the Christmas and summer term, we write a short report on how your child has developed throughout the term, plus we hold an annual parents meetings in the spring term. Once your child has reached two years of age, we complete a two year check report. This looks at the three prime areas of development - Communication and Language, Personal, social and emotional development plus Physical development. This two year check may highlight concerns in one or more areas of your child's development. If this is the case we may do a 'assess, plan, do, review'. which will help us to set small targets for both you and us at nursery to work towards, to help your child develop. Or we may sign post you to the right professional for additional support, such as you health visitor or a therapist. The two year check you are able to share with your health visitor, when your child has their two year health review. If we or you begin to have concerns about your child, then we would have a meeting with you to decide the next steps to help your child. When it comes to the time that your child moves onto another setting or school, we will write a transition report, which you can take to your child's new setting. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We are a very small setting on one level. We do have a ramp up to the front door, plus another ramp going into the garden, with handles to help give support when accessing the garden. There is also a disabled toilet area. Within the nursery, all play equipment & activities are at the child's height for easy accessibility. The preschool, is made up of three interconnecting rooms, giving children the opportunity to have quiet time when they wish to. Chairs and tables can all be adjusted to suit individual children. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Firstly we would recommend that you arrange a time to visit the setting, to see if you like us and if our setting is suitable for both you and your child. If you would like to register your child, then you will be given a registration form. The nursery will be able to tell you at this point if they have space, or if you need to go onto the waiting list. Once a place has been offered, we then organise settling in visits for you and your child to attend before your start date. Due to the Covid restrictions we are currently not undertaking home visits but look to reintroduce these again soon. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continually assessing the SEND provision that we offer, to ensure that individual needs are met for the children attending the nursery. When reviewing a child's needs, we may need to work with an occupational therapist to make the necessary physical changes to the nursery environment so to support a child. Or the staff may attend additional training, in order to better understand a child's needs and to support them in the best possible way. Our nursery is continuously reviewing its practices in order to support all the children that attend.

local_offer: The aim of this document is to enable families to see the support that they would receive for their child at Marlow Bottom Pre-School. It provides clear information about what we have in place to enable your child to achieve their full potential. We work within the guidance of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework and use this to promote each child's learning and development. We regard each child as being unique and endeavour to meet their individual needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We work closely with other professionals as required for each child. If required, we will contact and work with Buckinghamshire Council's Early Years Team. We will obtain parental consent before contact is made and we will include parents in all decisions made and meetings held. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We work closely with the professionals involved with a particular child and their expertise has helped to increase our knowledge and support our skills. The SENCO takes time to research relevant areas of SEND in order to best meet the needs of a child. We attend training courses that we feel will support the needs of the children currently in the setting. The whole team has attended a course on Makaton for babies. In addition to this, the SENco has attended courses in Downs Syndrome, Stammering and Selective Mutism,Speech and Language workshop and the National Autistic Society's 12 week Early Bird Programme. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are a volunteer committee run pre-school. Therefore, every parent is a member of the pre-school and are welcome to attend meetings. We promote an open-door policy. Key workers, the manager and the SENco make themselves freely available to parents for informal chats. We will happily arrange more formal meetings if appropriate and try to support parents whenever we can. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We chat to parents informally at the start and end of each session. Our development records provide us with a monitoring tool that enables us to identify any additional support required. Our highly qualified team ensures children's needs are quickly identified and supported and this is fed back to parents. Children's yellow learning journey books are available for parents to view and parents can arrange a more formal meeting if desired. If a child has a SEND need, we will maintain paperwork, liaise with any relevant professionals and meet regularly with parents to review the child's progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The preschool is housed in a large ground floor hall accessible via a ramp. The toilets are easily accessible and include a larger, disabled toilet. There is a small, flat, paved outdoor area to the side of the building. There are four steps to our garden, which is slightly sloping. The garden could be accessed via a sloping side entrance if required. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Before your child starts pre-school, we encourage you to visit the setting where your child can become acquainted with the pre-school and the staff and especially with your child's key person. We have a close relationship with our local school. The children visit the school prior to leaving preschool and meet their new teachers. We will give the new setting time to make necessary plans for any changes they may need to make, sharing targets on your child’s SEND Support Plan and minutes of review meetings along with any other information that may be relevant to your child. All necessary paperwork will be passed onto the receiving setting/school. The development record will be passed to the parent. We also welcome the teachers to visit to see the children in the setting. If a child is anxious or has additional needs, we provide a photo album of the child’s new school for the parents to chat to the children over the Summer holidays, before they start. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our SENCo will continue to attend liaison group meetings to keep up to date with the latest information and relevant information and changes will be fed back to all staff during regular staff meetings. Staff will receive specialist training where needed depending on a child’s individual needs.

local_offer: Marlow C of E Infant School is a mainstream setting where the emphasis is on a whole-school approach. All staff accept responsibility for providing all children with realistic learning goals in a broad-based, balanced and appropriate curriculum that is differentiated to meet their individual needs. For some children, however, there are times when they require additional support to help them achieve realise their potential. The school attributes great importance to the early identification, assessment, and provision for any child who may have special educational needs. The earlier action is taken, the more responsive the child is likely to be, and the more readily intervention can be made without undue disruption to the organisation of the school, including the delivery of the curriculum for that particular child. When pupils are given additional support, then this usually happens in small groups or on a 1:1 basis with the child always being aware of what they are working towards. The teaching team and the support staff are highly motivated to make sure that every child has the care and attention that they need to thrive. This is done: by adapting the curriculum and learning environment; with additional support for learning; through activities that are available to pupils with SEND in addition to those available through the curriculum; through improving the emotional and social development of pupils with SEND Full details of the school's contribution to the Local Offer can be found in the school's SEN Annual Report on our website. The link for this can be found below. https://www.marlow-infant.bucks.sch.uk/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs+and+Disability&pid=174 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Marlow C of E Infant school is a community church school whose admissions arrangements are defined in its admissions policy. It admits children from the local area and its catchment is defined by the map that can be found on the Buckinghamshire Council website. The Governing Body of the school, not Buckinghamshire Local Education Authority (the LA), is responsible for deciding on admissions to the school. It does, however, work closely with the LA who coordinates admissions to all maintained schools and academies in Buckinghamshire. Details of the LA arrangements for entry to Reception are available in the 'Admissions and Moving school' section of the Buckinghamshire Council Website. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Marlow C of E Infant School actively seeks to improve its services and facilities for all pupils including those with SEND. Full details can be found in the School's Annual Improvement Plan which is available to view by request to the Headteacher

local_offer: At The Marlow Day Nursery, we value that every child is unique and nurturing the children in our care is at the heart of what we do. Children thrive from a base of loving and secure relationships. At the Nursery, we are very proud of the bond and the relationship that both our children and their parents have with their Key Person. It's through careful observation and through open communication with parents, that we can support all children, including those who might require some additional support. We believe that it is paramount that everybody works together to best meet the needs of individual children. Children develop at their own pace and in their own individual ways. Inclusion means that individuals are valued and that nobody is discriminated against. Young children are vulnerable but they are kept safe and develop resilience when their well-being is protected by adults. Health and well-being are an integral part of children’s emotional, mental social, environmental, and spiritual health.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are fortunate in that we have regular support from a SEND Advisor at Buckinghamshire Council who is instrumental in supporting the children, staff and parents. We also have regular support from other Multi-Disciplinary teams such as a Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist and Physiotherapist. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Louise, Lisa and Sana have attended relevant SENCo training. Staff have attended a variety of different SEND training, including behaviour management, sensory workshops, speech and language and ASD. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use an on online journal system for observing and recording the children. These observations are uploaded and then are instantly available for parents/carers to view. This is a great communication tool between the Key Person and the parents. We have daily feedback with each parent each day. We also use emails, telephone calls, parent meetings, and newsletters as another way of communicating. We operate an 'Open Door' policy and we are always available for parents whenever they need us. For children with SEND, we hold regular meetings between the Key Person, SENCo, and parents to discuss progress and anything else that is needed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We are very fortunate in that our setting is all on one level and is easily accessible for any disabled users. We have a disabled toilet and a ramp to make the outside space easy accessible. Where access isn't available, we will make any adaptions where reasonable and practical. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We are proud of our transition process. Not only when children transition between rooms at the Nursery, but also when they first start at the Nursery and when they leave to go to school. Before a child starts at the Nursery, we invite them to attend some 'settling' sessions. We recommend three settling-in sessions, but this is purely a guideline and we always put the needs of the child and the parents first, so those sessions are flexible. When a child transitions from one room to another, we have a robust system in place, whereby the children spend several sessions in their new room, meeting the new staff team. The staff complete a transition information sheet and share that information with the new Key Person. Parents also get the opportunity to contribute to the information sheet. Staff also complete a transition report, which again is shared with the staff in the new room as well as the parents. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: We aim to provide a safe, secure and stimulating pre-school setting for all children, whatever their additional needs. We will support the children with a staff ratio necessary to enable them to access all activities, whether or not they have an EHCP in place. As a minimum, we provide 1 to 2 support but all children are supported 1:1 at least until they are settled in the setting. We are fully inclusive and will undertake any necessary training to accommodate the children. We work very closely with associated therapists and other professionals to establish individual aims for the children. We have been operating as an independent charity for 20 years and previous to this were under the umbrella of the British Red Cross for almost 40 years.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? MOP has very good links with all therapists and specialist teachers. MOP has a wealth of experience in working with children with additional needs and has many resources in place to assist with this. Some of our team are parents of ex-pupils which gives them a great deal of knowledge and empathy. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We have recently undertaken epilepsy management training, tube feeding training and training on the use of oxygen in the setting. We have also undertaken See and Learn training this term, provided by the Specialist Teaching Service Down Support Team. Visiting therapists work closely with our support staff in relation to delivering therapy programmes for individual children. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in the following ways: Voluntary Management Committee Fundraising events Come and Play sessions Regular morning coffee mornings at the setting Invited to all outings Working with staff to set aims for IEPs Regular Parent Information Afternoons How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? A very close relationship with Key Person and management is always available for support, either in person or at the end of the phone/email. Feedback from key person at end of the session on a daily basis. Children on dual placement have an inter-setting diary which is completed daily. Parents are invited to the annual Information Afternoon where they have an opportunity to have longer feedback from the key person and also speak to all special schools in the area. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is accessible and is on one level. We have our own car park. Disabled facilities. Changing area for those children in nappies. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? After enquiries from families or professional associated with families, we invite them into the setting so that can see how the sessions are run. If they feel this is an appropriate placement for their child, we ask them to complete an application form and the child is placed on the waiting list. We keep in contact with families on the waiting list and invite them to our Parent Information Afternoons. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? MOP is always evaluating its service and takes advice and suggestions from professionals, families, staff members very seriously. If any training is recommended we shall, wherever possible or practical, undertake that training.

We offer an inclusive curriculum which we support all children to access. We organise our curriculum into exciting topics that the children find engaging. The environment is adapted if necessary so that all children can access all resources and that furniture generally matches the needs of the pupils. Adaptations for learning take place by differentiating teacher inputs, teachers modifying language they are using, supporting concepts with visual cues and pre-teaching concepts prior to the whole class being introduced to them. Work is differentiated and time is allocated for children to work on their targets on the SEN Support Plan or their Education Health Care Plan. As an inclusive school, we encourage all children to engage in extracurricular activities. Every effort is made to adapt this provision for all children and through discussion with the parents and children we do our best to meet the needs of all children. If a learner is identified as having SEN, we will provide support that is ‘additional to’ or ‘different from’ the differentiated approaches and learning arrangements which we provide as part of our ‘quality first teaching’. This is expectation for all of our children regardless of need. This support is set out in our whole school Provision Map. local_offer: Marsh Gibbon Preschool welcomes all children along with their parents/carers. We include and cater for all ethnicities, cultures or religions, home languages, social and economic backgrounds, learning difficulties or disabilities, genders, or abilities. We encourage parents/carers to be fully involved in their education. https://files.ofsted.gov.uk/v1/file/50242729 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We believe a child should grow, learn and develop in a stimulating, friendly, caring, and safe environment. Each child is treated as an individual. They are supported and praised for their efforts, not just their results. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Karen Maciejewski is our SENDCO, and she has completed her Level 3 award for Special Educational Needs Coordinators in Early Years- Awarded July 2023 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Here at Marsh Gibbon Preschool, we work hard to create a warm and inviting environment for all children and their families. All staff are approachable to all families. We have developed good bonds that enable fantastic parent relationships. Parents/carers are encouraged to enter the setting each morning with their child. It allows parents to be greeted by the staff, in particular, their key person. We use Tapestry as our learning journey platform, which enables us to share observations and development with parents or carers. Parents are also encouraged to send in observations from home so that we can develop a deeper understanding of their development, home life and achievements. In addition to this, we welcome any extra interactions, for example, if a grandparent wanted to help out one day or a parent wanted to visit us and share their knowledge, such as a dentist, fireman, vet, etc. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child here at Marsh Gibbon Preschool has their own Journal created and continuously updated by their Key Person. We use a secure platform called Tapestry to record observations and records. The children’s journals contain a starting point assessment, snapshot observations, 2-year-old checks (where applicable), and termly summative assessments. Our SENCO, Karen, will have weekly meetings with parents to discuss the child’s progress, future targets, and possible outside agency referrals that may need to be made to aid development. We pride ourselves on working closely with parents, and we believe that working together will always achieve the best outcome for any child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All staff take into account the needs of all children within our setting especially when setting up our environment, we aim to make all areas as accessible as we can. We are a one-story building based in a village hall, the building has no stairs/steps and has a ramp down into the outdoor space. We operate a free flow environment that allows all children to access all available space with supervising adults. We are lucky to have separate rooms in the village hall that we can use for group-focused times or intervention work. The children are then away from the free flow environment with accessible resources, this then minimises distractions at focused group times. The SENCO, Karen, is trained in sing and sign/ and will regularly use sign language during the Preschool day. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? 2 What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan on developing our inclusion groups rather than focussing on 1:1 provision as this has proved in recent studies to have a detrimental effect on children’s development with SEN. We are applying for government grants in order to send specific staff on behavioural training, first phase phonic training and current ASD training.

name: Marsworth Church of England Infant School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Marsworth, Tring, for 3 to 7-year-olds. Our classes are organised into Nursery and Reception, and Year One and Two. Our teachers are skilled at planning for mixed-age classes, and children work to their ability, not necessarily their age. We have a very high staff-to-pupil ratio to ensure all children are supported in their learning. Our school consists of two main classrooms and a well-equipped library. We have a large resources/dining room to the rear of our school and a canopy outside Class One. The school has a large secure all-weather playground and a large grassy play area. These contain some great facilities for playtime. We have a minibeast area, a small garden, and a growing area. There is a clatter bridge and a small climbing resource along with a wooden train. Unusually for a small village school, there is weekly access to all-year-round swimming lessons. Due to our size, we use the Village Hall for our weekly P.E. lessons during the Autumn and Spring terms. As a C of E school, we have close links to All Saints Church just down the road from the school. We also have a visiting football/athletics coach which are held during lunchtimes.

name: Mary Hare School (Berkshire)
description: A mixed-gender residential special school in Newbury, Berkshire for 4 to 19-year-olds who are deaf or have a hearing impairment. Mary Hare School is a residential co-educational non-maintained special school for deaf pupils in Newbury, Berkshire, England. It consists of around 180 pupils from year Reception to year 13. In September 2022 we relocated and opened our brand-new, state-of-the-art Primary School. The Mary Hare Foundation raised £4 million towards the project and the new school has been designed to maximise the learning experience for deaf young people. Mary Hare Primary School offers a vibrant curriculum that is tailored to meet the needs of our deaf pupils, with vocabulary and language at the heart of everything we do. Your child will flourish as they make friends with deaf peers and build on their self-esteem and confidence in their identity. We are the largest school for deaf children in the UK taking both day and boarding pupils. We teach through speaking and listening, so no there is no use of British Sign Language in our classes - our pupils thrive on learning to use their voice and the use of English is really important. Mary Hare is a national charity (registered charity number 1048386). Pupils' fees are paid for by the Local Education Authority where they live. We place great emphasis on language development. All children have access to the National Curriculum with a broad range of GCSEs, A-Levels, and BTECS and a growing number of vocational courses.

local_offer: Meadowcroft Munchkins is a privately owned preschool catering to up to 32 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We are a family-run business and pride ourselves in our personal approach. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the preschool and to share their children’s successes, achievements, concerns and hopes for the future. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our SENCO Sam Fallows attends the termly Local Authority SENCO Liaison Groups. The setting has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child-specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor, a range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites). We are happy for professionals involved with the child to visit and welcome this opportunity to develop our knowledge. We have close links with the local Children’s Centre and Health Visitors’ team. We are happy to attend Multi-Professional Meetings. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO Training for New and Aspiring SENCOs June 2018 Sam Fallows Focus on SEND, Early Years May 2019 Sam Fallows Manual Handling May 2019 Sam Fallows All About Speech and Language June 2019 Sam Fallows SENCO L3 Qualification Course June 2019 Sam Fallows British Sign Language level 2 June 2023 Sam Fallows How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents into the setting to see preschool life in action. Parents have access to our online record-keeping system and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can request a meeting with their child’s Key Person at any time and if it is not possible to speak to the Key Person on the day, an appointment will be made as soon as possible. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents/carers of SEND children in our care. We can also offer updates through home/school books, email or phone calls if convenient. We will regularly monitor the short-term outcomes for children with SEND and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT)) are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits too. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor environment is fully wheelchair accessible, as is our garden. The Community Centre hall that we use consists of a spacious foyer and one large hall. Toilets are adjacent to the hall and an accessible toilet is available in the Centre’s main foyer. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child’s transition needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including frequent settling sessions and shortened sessions. We will be happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible to meet their needs. We have close relationships with the local schools and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We regularly audit the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and plan our training accordingly.

local_offer: At Forest Tribe Friends Childminding i would aim to provide a safe, warm and engaging environment to all children. With a focus on Forest School principals, I believe in children having the opportunity to achieve through them succeeding in 'small achievable tasks' producing that child's WOW moments, whatever they may be. At Forest Tribe Friends we are outside a majority of the time and children in my care experience play and challenges in the great outdoors, visiting a number of local woods, these vary in accessibility, but there is many opportunities for all children to have access to Forest School activities. I like to provide parents with daily updates and photos of what their children have been doing during the day and I welcome feedback and comments from parents on daily activities as well as through questionnaires and of course have an open door policy. I work in partnership with parents and other professionals. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I use an electronic system called Babysdays, which is used for two way information sharing on your child's progress and achievements, both at my practice and at home. I look to work in partnership with my parents/carers to provide the best possible support for your child's development. Any areas where additional support is needed, I can work with other professionals and share (with permission) information as necessary. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Accessibility for individual needs can be discussed, as my home practice does have a step to access front and garden, with steps for differing levels in garden. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I like to carry out a home visit before starting at my practice, to enable to talk 'All About me' regarding your child. I'm happy to visit and discuss transition with other settings attended by child. Families are welcome to visit and we can discuss settling in plans, your child and family. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I will attend training as and when appropriate, working closely with local authority Early Years Consultant.

description: I am an Ofsted registered childminder. I am a happily married mother with 2 young daughters. We live in Totteridge near the park where we often go for picnics, exploring, and a run around. Before being a childminder, I was a nanny for 8 years and over that time I have amassed a wealth of experience with special needs including being fluent in Makaton and I have the basics of BSL. I have lots of energy and an enthusiastic outlook on life. I encourage and promote independence and enjoy helping the children in my care to develop their skills. local_offer: I am fluent in Makaton and have a basic grasp of BSL. I have lots of experience in a wide variety of special need including children with mild dyspraxia, downs syndrome, severe epilepsy with severe brain damage, limited vision, profound deafness, motor control, feeding (chewing and swallowing), peg tube and mickey button, spinal problems, heart defects and breathing difficulties. Through my experiences with all of these wonderful children I have learned a great deal and would love to put my knowledge to good use. I don't have any specialist equipment as such but have been shown many ways to adapt things often found around the home and am otherwise very resourceful.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To enable children and young people to develop their skills, confidence and independence. To allow their personality to shine. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Mental health, ADHD, supporting people with autism, How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Input from parents and carers is important to give me the best idea of your child’s likes, dislikes, successes, passions and struggles. Form this information I can tailor the care I provide your child to comfort, encourage and aid their progress. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Via videos and photos captured of new skills and magic moments, via observations. All artwork goes home with each child as soon as it’s ready, and verbal updates upon collection and via any support team meetings if applicable. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There is a small step into each of the 3 entrances to the setting. All of the ground floor is on one level with dining table, downstairs toilet, all toys and equipment is downstairs, garden is flat and enclosed. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact me. You’re welcome to come and meet and view what I offer. If my setting suits you and your child’s needs, you can start upon completion of contracts and child record forms. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Ongoing training. Equipment if needed.
