local_offer: At Millbrook Combined School and Nursery we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve their potential at school. In order to do these many steps are taken to support them through their learning journey. Quality teaching is vital; however, for some children, there are occasions when further additional support may be needed to help them achieve their targets. https://www.millbrookcombinedschool.org.uk/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Millbrook Combined School we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve their potential at school. To do this many steps are taken to support them through their learning journey. Quality teaching is vital; however, for some children there are occasions when further additional support may be needed to help them achieve their targets. Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) policy is available on request from the school office. You can find more information on Buckinghamshire Council’s local offer on their website. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? How to support pupils on the autistic spectrum. How to support pupils with social and emotional needs. How to support pupils with speech and language difficulties. How to support pupils with physical and co-ordination needs. How to support pupils with needs that become evident through behavioural changes. How to create a safe environment in the classroom for a child with selective mutism How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All parents are encouraged to contribute to their child’s education. This may be through: - Discussions with the class teacher. - Attending parents’ evenings. - Discussions with Mrs Goodman (SENDCo) or other professionals. - Parents/carers are encouraged to comment on their child’s SEN Support Plans or EHCP with possible suggestions that can be incorporated. - Attending open events, assemblies, and celebrations. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? You will be able to discuss your child’s progress at Parents’ Evenings. If your child has a SEN Support Plan, this will be shared with you termly. If your child has an EHCP, then this will be reviewed annually with the child, yourself and any professionals involved. SEN support plans will be used to set and monitor short term targets in line with the long term targets in the EHCP, giving you the opportunity to discuss these with the class teacher and SENDCo on a termly basis. Appointments can be made to speak in more detail to the class teacher or SENDCo by contacting/visiting the school office or emailing the SENDCo at sen@millbrook.bucks.sch.uk. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All pupils are welcome at Millbrook and we endeavour to make the school environment accessible to all. We are aware that in certain instances, pupils will have specific access requirements and these can be discussed on an individual basis. We aim for all classrooms to be optimally organised for disabled pupils; if a situation arises which requires classroom access by a disabled pupil then the layout will be arranged to enable them to participate fully. We aim for pupils with any disabilities, who may require a wheelchair or mobility aid, to be able to move around the school without experiencing any barriers to access. Our site is fully accessible: we have a lift available to enable access to the first floor and a stairlift to enable access to the playground and faith garden. There is disabled parking available on-site and individual arrangements can be made as needed with regards to dropping off and collecting a pupil. With this provision in place, we strive to ensure all pupils are treated equally and have access to the school environment and the curriculum taught within the school. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If your child has an EHCP then their school placement will be arranged through the Bucks SEN Team. If your child does not have an EHCP then you need to apply through the normal school application process with Buckinghamshire Council admissions team. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are always reviewing our SEND provision to ensure we are providing the most appropriate support for those children who have additional needs. We provide training to staff throughout the school year adapting this to suit the needs of current pupils.

local_offer: We understand that each child’s needs are different. For those children joining us here at Millwood House Nursery, we offer a settling session. We are always happy to discuss with you what works well for your child and are happy to meet their needs. We have internal transition forms for when our little ones move up to the older age groups, ensuring that there is a clear record of you’re child’s achievements, development and needs For those children leaving Millwood House Nursery to start school, we have good relationships with all of our local schools. We provide a report for the new setting of your child’s development and progress. We also provide supported transition visits for those of our children with additional needs/EHCP.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Millwood House, each child is encouraged to learn through play. Our curriculum covers all the areas of the Early Years Foundation Stages (EYFS) which sets standards for learning, development and care for children of all ages from Babies to 5 Years. Using the Dayshare app we are able to share all key information, milestones, activities and photographs with Parents on a daily basis. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our Room Leaders, David Shiel and Grace Butler, are our designated SENDCO, however all of our staff undergo SEND training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Our families are so important to us. We endeavour to find any available opportunity to invite them in to celebrate our children. We have always aimed to create a warm and welcoming ambience for all children and parents. We aim to get parents involved in nursery life on regular occasions. We hold regular family events, such as the Millwood House Bake Off, Easter Egg Hunt, Sports Day, Christmas Play, Carols in the Garden, Stay and Plays etc. We hold our Graduation and Garden Party in our large garden at which the whole Nursery celebrates. We update our Parents regularly with what is going on in the Nursery through our monthly Newsletter, weekly Whatsapp updates, Facebook posts and our Website. We use the Parenta Parent Portal (Footsteps and Dayshare) to provide daily updates for our Children which our Parents can access through the Parenta app. Our Staff are always available to provide an thorough update and answer any questions at Drop Off and Pick Up. Individual parent meetings are available at any time at a parent’s request. Parents of SEND Children are often more involved as we discuss with them the APDR Reports, SEND Support Plan and any other matters as they arise. We also send out questionnaires to gain the opinions of parents on various aspects and future plans of the Nursery. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parent’s of our younger children have access to “DayShare” which is a record of their day at Millwood House. Each Family receives its unique login details to access daily activity information about their child. This is available via the Parenta Portal app for all our Parents. In addition to this “Footsteps” is where all assessments and child development is recorded. This is completed by the child’s Key Person and is available to be shared with the child’s parents at all times. A “two Year Progress Check” will be carried out by the Key Person. This will also be available on the Parenta app and Parent’s have the opportunity to offer any comments on this. For children with SEND, we offer more frequent meetings and catch-ups via phone, emails or visits. This enables us to discuss progress and to work together to discuss the next steps. We also discuss any SEND paperwork (APDR or SEND support Plan) with Parents and provide copies. We understand that each child’s needs are different. For those children joining us here at Millwood House Nursery, we offer 2 or more settling sessions free of charge. We are always happy to discuss with you what works well for your child and are happy to meet their needs. As your child moves through the Nursery, a transition letter is sent to Parent’s when the time comes advising of the transition between rooms and how it will be managed. This letter also invites Parent’s to meet with both the existing and new “Key Workers” to discuss any concerns they may have. Our Parenta Footsteps ensure that your little ones move up to the older age groups with a clear record of your child’s achievements, development and needs. In addition to this, each child’s “Key Worker” meets with the new Room Leader to ensure that they are fully apprised of every transitioning child’s needs. For those children leaving Millwood House Nursery to start school, we have good relationships with all of our local schools. We provide a report for the new setting of your child’s development and progress. We also provide supported transition visits for those of our children with additional needs/EHCP. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Millwood House Nursery has always been and remains willing to listen to and facilitate Parent’s requests/Child needs. We have a sensory area and quiet areas to provide a quiet area for those children needing to get away from the busy environment, as well as an area for focused individual and small group activities. We have a large, level, wheelchair friendly private car park. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? For further information, please contact us on 01753 645500 or email at admin@millwoodhousenursery.co.uk. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Moving forward, more of our staff will be undertaking Makaton training ensuring its reinforcement as a supporting communication tool throughout all our age groups. We are constantly evaluating all our activities within the Nursery to ensure that they constantly remain inclusive for all our children. We aim to ensure that all our Nursery Key Staff have completed all relevant training to ensure that we continue to constantly deliver fully inclusive activities. Following the success of our new sensory room, we are planning to introduce sensory/quiet spaces in each of our individual rooms. We intend to install ramps on all our entrances to facilitate access to all the Nursery.

local_offer: We are fully inclusive and aim to provide a fun and stimulating environment for all children, no matter what their backgrounds and/or abilities. We recognise that each child is unique and we strive to plan to their individual needs and interests/characteristics of learning. We work closely with other childcare professionals and we have very close links with other settings that our children may attend.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to provide the best opportunities for all children to thrive in a school environment and achieve the best outcomes for their individual circumstances. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The manager has completed Level 3 Senco training Chatter Monkeys Language intervention Neli Programme Autism training Online training for children with physical needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We encourage parents to take an active role in their child's preschool experience and welcome them into our setting for stay and play sessions. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use Famly as an online Learning journal across the preschool but will also provide home/preschool communication books if required. Throughout the year parents are invited to parent evenings to talk about their child. We have an open-door policy and parents are always welcome. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment is very accessible with ramps from all doors making access easy for wheelchair users. Inside the preschool is spacious and on one level. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please call to arange a visit, where we can talk through your individual needs and how we can best support you, We take children from 2 years of age and places are allocated depending on adult-child ratios. We make every effort to accommodate children who require 1:1 support. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We hope that in time all staff will be trained in all areas of needs.

name: Money Carer | Inclusive Money Management for Vulnerable Adults
description: Established in 2009, Money Carer is an award-winning social enterprise providing specialist banking and money management services for vulnerable adults across the UK. Working with hundreds of solicitors, local authorities, care providers and families, we support over 6500 clients to manage their finances safely, independently, and with dignity. Our Services Appointeeship - Managing DWP welfare benefits and everyday financial affairs on behalf of clients. Deputyship - Low-asset deputyship services authorised by the Court of Protection for those unable to manage their own finances. Everyday Money Management - Paying rent, utilities and care bills, and handling general household expenses. Banking Services - Opening and managing FSCS-protected accounts via our Monika platform. Direct Payments - Supporting individuals, families and social workers in managing care budgets securely. Financial Safeguarding - Monitoring spending, identifying risks and ensuring transparency for families and professionals. Payment Wearables - Offering secure and inclusive ways to pay from Carer Cards to Biometric Payment Cards and RingPay payment rings and bracelets.
organisation: Money Carer The Money Carer Foundation is a national social enterprise that provides a trusted appointeeship service to protect vulnerable adults and to manage their everyday finances in line with our local partnership with the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP). This involves paying utility bills, care contributions, rent and dealing with a variety of other financial activity on behalf of the client. For more information please visit: Our ‘Carers Shopping Card’ is a fully managed service that is set up specifically so that carers can access small amounts of money to make everyday purchases or to withdraw cash on behalf of the client. refer@moneycarer.org.uk https://www.moneycarer.org.uk/

name: Monkey Music
description: Monkey Music classes in Amersham, Beaconsfield or Gerrards Cross. Amersham is on Monday and Wednesday, Beaconsfield Fridays and Gerrards Cross, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday. Music classes tailored to the social, linguistic and musical development of babies and toddlers. You will spend quality time with your little one; helping their learning and exploration as well as enjoying your time together. We have classes suitable for babies from 12 weeks, for toddlers and for those older little ones. For those clever older little monkeys of preschool age, we have our wonderful Ding-Dong curriculum where little ones are introduced to instruments of the orchestra and progress to beating crotchet, quaver and crotchet rest rhythms, a fantastic basis for learning a musical instrument when they are older. We won 3 awards in the HOOP Buckinghamshire Awards 2019, best class for babies, best class for toddlers and best music class. Monkey Music is fun and educational too. Our classes are grouped according to 4 age groups so that classes are tailored to the exact age of the child. We have four different classes where children are grouped according to their age and this means that classes can be tailored to the social, linguistic and musical development of that particular age group. Classes are small, no more than 15 in a class, so that the teacher can get to know your child and notice his or her progression.

local_offer: At Monkey puzzle Aylesbury we aim to provide a safe and stimulating learning environment for all children including those with Special educational needs. we aim to ensure that all children have access to educational resources and a caring environment, enabling them to achieve and progress. We aim to include all families and provide a caring , stimulating environment where the children can learn and reach their full potential. We aim to support children within the setting that have additional needs and also offer support to parents. To access our setting and the service we provide you would need to arrange a viewing. you would have a conversation with the nursery manager to discuss your child's additional needs and whether we feel we are the best provision for them. If all parties are happy you would need to register with us and book in some settling in sessions prior to the start date where you would have a discussion with the nursery SENCO We provide activities and resources relevant to the needs of the children we care for. our nursery is wheelchair accessible and has plenty of large open space. We have an open door policy and are happy to set time aside to discuss childrens needs and how we can help support them and the family. We tailor our method of communication to the individual needs of the child. we have staff with basic knowledge of British sign language and baby sign. We talk to the children and their level and keep our voices dear and calm. We communicate with parents via email, newsletters and face to face meetings. Our Deputy manager has attended various training courses aimed at caring for children with Autism and has completed a SENCO training course. We discuss childrens individual needs during staff meetings and ensure all staff are aware of individual childrens needs. As our occupancy increases we plan to train a 2nd SENCO and ensure all staff do basic training regarding children with Special educational needs. local_offer: Monkey Puzzle Day Nursery is committed to the inclusion of all children. All children have the right to be cared for and educated to develop to their full potential alongside each other through positive experiences, to enable them to share opportunities and experiences and to develop and learn from each other. Monkey Puzzle Day Nursery is committed to working alongside parents in the provision for their child’s individual needs to enable us to help the child to develop to their full potential. description: A Warm Welcome to Muddy Boots Nursery. Choosing the right nursery to meet your child’s needs can be a complex decision and an important one for both parents and children. Please take your time and explore what our nursery can offer you and your child. Muddy Boots is very much part of Grendon School life so do take time to find out about the school as well. At Muddy Boots Nursery, we provide a friendly, relaxed, safe and secure environment for children. We offer a child-centred approach where children are encouraged to develop their individuality, creativity, independence and self-confidence led by caring and highly skilled staff. We support the children so they feel positive in all areas of their lives and learning. We are a Growth Mindset Nursery and our values and motto are the same as the school. We also have a forest school on site run by our forest school-trained staff. Please contact us to arrange a viewing or to enquire about places.
organisation: Grendon Underwood Combined School The single form entry school sits in the lovely village of Grendon Underwood in rural Buckinghamshire. We offer complete wrap around care for our school aged children, provided by local company Sports4All who also provide school holiday clubs on site. Please explore the website and find out more about our school, described by Ofsted in July 2018 as a "happy, caring place ... where pupils look out for one another and know how to treat others with respect, regardless of background or other difference." We have a school nursery on site, Muddy Boots, which takes children from 2 years old, we offer 2, 3 and 4-year-old funding as well as the 30 hour funding. Finding a school for your child is a huge decision and we understand how hard it may be not being able to have a look round schools at the moment, we are hoping to have something virtually soon! name: Mursley Church of England School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Milton Keynes for 4 to 7-year-olds. Welcome to The Three Schools, a unique and successful initiative: to provide all-through primary schooling in a village setting yet with the facilities and opportunities beyond those that you would expect. To form ‘The Three Schools’, Swanbourne Church of England School, Mursley Church of England School and Drayton Parslow Village School came together, with the support of the Oxford Diocese and the Local Education Authority, to operate as a single entity with one Headteacher and leadership team. name: Muslim Parent's Association
description: High Wycombe is a thriving town with good race relations and the MPA (Muslim Parent's Association) is keen to improve the level of understanding between the largest ethnic minority of the town, (The Muslim Community) and the rest of the people of High Wycombe. One way to remove misunderstandings is to increase the level of contact among our diverse communities. The MPA has identified that in the field of education, due to various reasons (culture, language, religion and economic wellbeing) there is a large gap in the level of achievement between the mainstream pupils and those of Pakistani origin, as far as passes (at grades A* to C in 5 subjects) at GCSE are concerned. We are interested in increasing the interest of the Pakistani origin parents in the education of their children and are trying to push recruitment of school governors as a first step. We are also in the process of discussing this with the Local Education Authority and are making progress in not only identifying the relevant factors but possible solutions and need your help to combat the issue we are so passionate about. The MPA would therefore like to invite anyone living or working in High Wycombe, whatever their background, experience, ethnicity or religion to consider becoming an associate member of the MPA (a modest membership fee of £10 per annum is involved to cover admin and printing costs). You would be welcome to join us at our regular meetings and other events.

name: My First Playtime at Best Start Family Hub Elmhurst (Aylesbury)
description: My First Playtime is a free play session for babies aged 0 to 1 year or until they are walking. Babies can explore and learn through a range of activities, supporting their early development and helping to give them the best start in life. Activities may include messy play, arts and crafts, construction, and sensory play. The session also provides a space for parents and carers to connect with each other, learn practical tools and strategies to support learning at home, or speak to a member of the Family Hub Service for information and advice. Sessions run on a Monday (10am to 11:30am). There’s no need to book- just drop in during these times. Please note that we may need to limit numbers once the session is full to ensure a safe and comfortable environment for everyone. On street parking is available nearby to the hub. There are limited disabled spaces on site. If you need a disabled parking space please come to the car park barrier and press the intercom, to speak to a member of the team.

name: My Future Self Matters | Specialist Youth Support Service
description: Youth Mentoring and Counselling Services We want young people to find their purpose and have a sense of ownership over their future self. We believe all young people should be able to discuss their challenges with a safe, consistent, and trusted adult who can empower them to overcome their difficulties and lead a happy, fulfilling life. The one-to-one youth mentoring and counselling services for children and young people we provide are the best mental health services to build self-esteem and resilience in young people. Our youth support programmes are tailored to the specific needs of the young person, we set goals in collaboration with young people and start their journey towards achieving them. Our youth support programme has a clear vision, to make young people healthier, happier and reach their full potential. Every individual referred into our youth support programme will be offered the opportunity to get involved in local sports, apprenticeships and community-based projects to help connect them with their local community. Throughout their support focus will be placed upon various topics including: - The link between thoughts, feelings, and behaviour - Resilience and self-esteem - Strengths and interests - Support networks - Life and social skills - Positive relationships - Healthy coping strategies - Recognising and dealing with stress - Personal aspirations for their future selves Our support is provided either in school, at home or within the local community. We offer a variety of options in the community including ‘walk and talk’ sessions incorporating nature into the sessions and sports-based sessions to nurture and build on young people’s passions. To monitor outcomes My Future Self Matters, use the ‘Warwick–Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale’ at assessment and again at closure, this is an established emotional and behavioural screening tool. Funding for our services is either met through possible funding pots available for example pupil premium, EHCP, higher needs block funding or by families/carers directly. Please contact us to discuss our charges.
organisation: My Future Self Matters | Mentoring service for young people MyFutureSelf is a mentoring service that support young people with their mental health, lifestyle and wellbeing. We offer 1:1 support in person or online. MyFutureSelf successfully mentor young people equipping them with tools and strategies to increase their emotional health, resilience and improve their overall wellbeing. Our mentoring programme works directly with the young person however they are not the only person to benefit, the whole family will feel the benefit from their young person completing our mentoring programme. We recognise families are crucial to behavioural change and we aim to include families throughout our support. MyFutureSelf support a wide range of areas such as academic pressures, emotional wellbeing, isolation, relationship issues, low self-esteem, bullying / cyberbullying, social skills, independent living skills, lack of motivation, disengagement and challenging behaviour. MyFutureSelf does not aim to stand in as parents or teachers. We are there to offer impartial, trustworthy support without any judgement. MyFutureSelf can give a young person the chance to vent freely and confidentially about anything they want. For further information, please drop us a message or visit our website. myfutureself137@gmail.com https://www.myfutureself.org.uk/

name: Naphill and Walters Ash School
description: Mixed-gender primary school on the outskirts of High Wycombe for 4 to 11-year-olds. We, at Naphill and Walters Ash School, are proud of the support, education and progress of our children. We are a co-educational community school for children age 4 to 11 years, and have also been a 'Forest School' for over 9 years. Our children are happy and inspired to make good progress in the classroom with lots of activities to stimulate them both indoors and outdoors. We provide a safe and supportive learning environment that allows children to develop the skills and knowledge required to achieve their full potential both in their academic and personal development. Our school fosters an ethos of respect and we are really privileged that our children come from a range of different backgrounds including the RAF and village community. Our school values of Resilience, Resourcefulness, Responsibility, Reasoning and Reflectiveness motivate children to become independent learners and productive members of our community. Run by children from every year group, our Junior Leadership Team ensures that all children have a voice and contribute to how their school runs, including organising regular charity events to give back to their community. We can offer wrap-around care via Quackers out of school club. We also offer a wide selection of school clubs run by staff and outside professionals. We welcome you to come and visit our school community in action. OFSTED 2023 commented: Pupils are safe and well cared for in this inclusive school. As one pupil put it, ‘This is a school where it’s easy to fit in.’ Many pupils come from military backgrounds and must cope with change when moving schools or when loved ones are posted further afield. They, and their civilian friends, are taught strategies for coping with disappointment and loss, becoming emotionally intelligent and resilient. Pupils here know how to look after themselves and be good friends to others.

local_offer: Your child has Special Educational Needs. What can we at Naphill and Walters Ash offer you? At Naphill and Walters Ash, we celebrate the fact that every child is different, and, consequently the educational needs of every child is different. This is certainly the case for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities. We believe early intervention is key. Class teachers at Naphill and Walters Ash are alert to the needs of all their children, who are monitored carefully to measure the progress they are making. This ensures that any special educational needs are identified as early as possible. Our teaching is inclusive for all pupils, with lesson content and delivery considered in terms of the impact on differing levels of pupil ability. If a child is finding a learning area particularly difficult, the majority of their needs will still be met within the classroom through differentiated, personalised teaching. For some however, there are occasions when additional support may be required, for a variety of reasons, either through the support from Outside Professionals (SALT, OT, School Nurse, CAMHS) or through in-house programmes such as Talk Boost, Lego Therapy and Precision Monitoring. local_offer: The type of SEND provision that Abbey View Primary Academy caters for is: Special Educational Needs and Disabilities of children aged 4 to 11 years which can be met in a mainstream setting. These needs and disabilities may be categorised under: - Cognition and Learning - Communication and Interaction - Emotional, Mental and Social Health - Sensory and/or Physical https://www.abbeyviewprimaryacademy.org/SEND-13082024134017/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have the highest expectations of all our children and strive to reduce and remove inequalities and barriers that already exist so that all our children can reach their full potential academically, socially, and emotionally. We develop children’s resilience, independence and creativity. We provide a healthy, safe and happy environment where everybody matters (children, parents and staff) and feels safe. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The Academy's arrangement for training staff in relation to pupils with SEND is: - whole staff in-service training sessions are arranged as appropriate, in response to particular needs within the school - reading and discussion of relevant documentation and keeping up to date with DfE guidance. - SENDCo/teacher meetings are considered to be part of staff development, as well as a time to share information. - the SENDCo and other relevant staff attend LA meetings and INSET as appropriate. - newly appointed teaching and support staff meet the SENCo to discuss SEND procedures in the academy. - Specialist expertise is obtained by the school/nursery school. The Academy may make referrals to a range of external agencies if further specialist expertise is required. Each agency has its own referral criteria. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents of children on the SEN register within our Academy are invited to termly meetings where their input is valued and their views are included. Additionally, we encourage parents to become involved in the Academy's community through joining the PTA. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children's progress is shared through parents'/carers' evenings twice a year and a report at the end of the year. Children on the SEN register have an additional parents' evening (3 in total) which allows for parental input into the child's support plan (APDR). How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The Academy and Nursery facilities to include pupils with SEND and how you obtain new or specialist equipment and facilities is: The academy is DDA compliant. Reasonable adjustments are made to make sure the school environment is as accessible as possible. Where there are steps, there is alternative access via ramp. Steps have handrails. To reach the second floor there is lift access. Modifications are made to fixtures as appropriate. There is an allocated disabled parking bay which can be used by parents who hold a disabled parking badge. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please find our admissions policy on the website which follows the LA guidance to admissions. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are consistently reflecting on the needs of our children and tailoring the training to enable staff to meet their needs.

name: Aran Hall School (Dolgellau, Wales)
description: Independent special school in Dolgellau, Wales for 11 to 19-year-olds. Aran Hall Residential School set in Wales provides Day and flexible 30 to 52-week residential care with education to children and young people with a range of learning disabilities and autistic spectrum disorders, both with associated severe challenging behaviour. We have also developed a programme for young people who present sexually harmful behaviour (SHB). The programme aims to reduce SHB through a reward programme for appropriate behaviour, sex education, counselling, and cognitive behaviour therapy. Our focus is to provide a safe, stable, and nurturing environment where young peoples skills and aspirations can be encouraged to develop and they can prepare for adulthood. By providing care and education on the same site we ensure that children individual programmes are delivered consistently. We develop education, care, and behavioural management programmes for each student. These programmes are evidence-based which enable us to demonstrate students achievements. We are a leader in conducting and publishing clinical research that evaluates the effectiveness of innovative programmes we run. Referral information If you are interested in your child having a place at the school. Please contact Caroline Parker Group Referrals Manager. If we feel your child may benefit from a place at the school then we will request paperwork and arrange to carry out a Functional Behavioural Assessment of your child either in the home or in their current placement. Once we have completed this you and professionals working with your child will be invited to visit the school. The young person will be given a student guide to tell them more about the school. The transition planning for your child will then take place.
organisation: SENAD Group Alderwasley Hall School and Sixth Form is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 5 to 19 years with Specific Language Disorders, Aspergers Syndrome and High Functioning Autistic Spectrum Disorders, all of whom experience complex speech, language and communication needs. The School and Sixth Form are located on separate sites within five miles of each other and are situated in Derbyshire, close to the towns of Matlock, Belper and Wirksworth. The City of Derby is also within easy access. The aim of all aspects of the curriculum is to prepare students for adult life by fulfilling their social and academic potential. Young people are supported to develop and achieve academic and vocational plans, develop independent living skills and a clear sense of identity, enabling them to contribute to society in adult life. The individual needs of students, as set out in their Education, Care and Health Plan are met through Therapy and educational programmes, underpinned by high-quality care. info@senadgroup.com https://senadgroup.com/alderwasley/

description: Family days out with Science, Technology, Engineering, and Maths (STEM) activities. The National Museum of Computing (TNMoC) is home to the world's largest collection of working historic computers. Follow the development of computing: from the Turing-Welchman Bombe and Colossus of the 1940s through the large systems and mainframes of the 1950s, 60s, and 70s, to the rise of personal computing and the rise of mobile computing and the internet. Recognized as one of England’s top 100 ‘irreplaceable places’, we welcome corporate and group visits, schools, and individuals from all over the world. We have plenty to do to unlock imaginations, inspire, and entertain. Educational fun for all the family, providing Bytes sized tasters of coding on BBC micros, Sphero robotics, and retro gaming.

name: National Paralympic Heritage Centre
description: The National Paralympic Heritage Centre is widely acknowledged as the birthplace of the Paralympic movement. Stoke Mandeville Stadium is the home of the first National Paralympic Heritage Centre. Our small Museum brings the history of the Paralympics and its stories of human endeavour to live. The story begins in the late 1940s at Stoke Mandeville Hospital, where Professor Sir Ludwig Guttmann encouraged wounded veterans to play sports to aid spinal injury rehabilitation. This led to local competitions, the Stoke Mandeville Games and the Paralympic Games, which today attract national and international public support and interest. The interactive displays include: - The life and work of Professor Sir Ludwig Guttmann - Key milestones in the journey from the 1948 Stoke Mandeville Games to the present-day Paralympic Games - The development of wheelchair sports - Paralympic ceremonies Visitor Information: You can visit us virtually Free Admission Open daily for the general public School and group bookings are available Audio and BSL Tours are available Please visit our website for more information about accessibility and family activities.

name: National Problem Gambling Clinic
description: We are a free, confidential NHS service supporting people who are experiencing harm from gambling aged 13 to 18 years from anywhere in England, and 18 or over in London and the South East. The NGC acts as a centre of excellence, paving the way in treatment innovation and research. The clinic has played an active role in training healthcare professionals, shaping policies, and increasing awareness of gambling harms in England and internationally. Established in 2008, our clinic pioneered NHS gambling treatment in the UK. Our experienced team assesses the needs of people for whom gambling has been a problem as well as those of their partners, family members and significant others. Please note that we support those suffering from gambling harm and cannot offer crisis interventions. We can work jointly with mental health teams, aiming to provide a comprehensive package of care in collaboration with other professionals. In the event of a crisis, we would suggest you contact your GP, community mental health team, A and E or the Police.

local_offer: Problem gambling treatment in the UK is delivered by a number of providers. The National Problem Gambling Clinic, as an NHS provider, is commissioned to deliver care and support to problem gamblers who have difficulties that might be described as complex. These may include the following: A lengthy period of problem gambling, with little or no abstinence Previous unsuccessful structured psychological support for problem gambling Mental health difficulties Substance misuse or other compulsive behaviours Concerns about risk of harm to self or others Serious physical health difficulties Homelessness or unstable housing or chronic social isolation Frequent involvement with criminal justice system or history of serious offending Developmental disorders, such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or difficulties with cognitive or intellectual functioning Adverse experiences in childhood that may underlie the gambling problem. name: National Problem Gambling Clinic
description: We are a free, confidential NHS service supporting people who are experiencing harm from gambling aged 13 to 18 years from anywhere in England, and 18 or over in London and the South East. The NGC acts as a centre of excellence, paving the way in treatment innovation and research. The clinic has played an active role in training healthcare professionals, shaping policies, and increasing awareness of gambling harms in England and internationally. Established in 2008, our clinic pioneered NHS gambling treatment in the UK. Our experienced team assesses the needs of people for whom gambling has been a problem as well as those of their partners, family members and significant others. Please note that we support those suffering from gambling harm and cannot offer crisis interventions. We can work jointly with mental health teams, aiming to provide a comprehensive package of care in collaboration with other professionals. In the event of a crisis, we would suggest you contact your GP, community mental health team, A and E or the Police.

description: Mixed-gender special post 16 institution in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire for 16 years and over. National Star College Cheltenham, National Star is a UK–wide charity that prepares young people with disabilities for adulthood and supports them to realise their aspirations. From the world-class learning it provides via an Ofsted "good" college to specialist therapies, residential services, work-based training, social enterprises and work in the wider community, the charity is driven by its vision for a world in which people with disabilities are able to realise their potential as equal and active citizens in control of their lives. Rated “Good” by both Ofsted (2023) and the CQC, and Winner of the TES Sen Award for “Outstanding Specialist Provider” 2019. We’re here to help you create a brighter future. Whether you want to discover more about the world around you, actively contribute to the community or gain a job or voluntary role after college, National Star is the place for you. We are a specialist college providing personalised learning and transition services for people with disabilities. We work with students with complex physical, learning, sensory and communication difficulties, and acquired disabilities. We offer full and part-time, day and residential places, 36 to 52-week places, focusing on transition and achieving individual goals. Our college is a vibrant, inclusive and active environment – students have a wide range of abilities, come to us from varied social and ethnic backgrounds, and participate in a wide range of community activities.

local_offer: We have outstanding multi-disciplinary support, assistive technologies and equipment, plus excellent facilities. These include sensory, therapeutic, residential, and supported work environments. We use a variety of communication and engagement support methods. These are embedded across the curriculum and throughout the learners’ day to day activities and include, Intensive Interaction, Makaton, PECS, Visual Timetable, Objects of Reference, AAC devices, Tablets and other assistive technology, specialist support from Speech and Language therapy, IT access, and technical support for communication devices. Prospective students are encouraged to attend a college visit day with their parents. Students are offered a multi-disciplinary assessment with their parents or main carer where they have the opportunity to meet with a variety of members of the college team. Learners are inducted into college over a number of days and careful consideration is given to the views and wishes of them and their parents. Parents are given contact details in college and frequency and method of communication is agreed at admission. We also support and facilitate an active Parent and Carer Forum within the college.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff are trained in Safeguarding, Safer Working Practice, Health and Safety, Equality and Diversity, Moving and Handling and where necessary, Team Teach, Autism, Working with people with Acquired Brain Injuries, and other specialist training. National Star also employs specialist staff, listed below. Education: All teachers hold teaching qualifications. Personal Learning Coordinators hold teaching qualifications (minimum CTLLs). Therapy: All therapists are qualified and registered in their own particular disciplines. We employ a large team of therapists, comprised of physiotherapists, speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, music therapists, a drama therapist, a psychologist, behavioural specialists, and therapy assistants. Care: All residential (care) staff hold a Diploma in Health and Social Care (or equivalent) at level 2 or above, or are working to achieve this. Health: 24 hour specialist nurses are assigned to each residence, and are available if needed to all day and residential students. A twice weekly GP service is available on our main college site. We offer Designated Person training to staff, which enables non nursing registered staff to administer medication following extensive training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Learners are empowered to be involved in all aspects of the organisation. We have an active Student Union, student parliament and two student governors. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? National Star College has many years’ experience of working with people with limited mobility. Approximately 75% of learners are wheelchair users. All student areas are accessible for people who use wheelchairs including a ramped stage, hoists in some class rooms and in all accommodation areas, high low tables in most areas, and specialist equipment where necessary. All college transport is accessible for people who use wheelchairs. We use a variety of communication and engagement support methods. name: Stowe Gardens
description: The scale and beauty of Stowe have attracted visitors for over 300 years. Picture-perfect views, winding paths, lakeside walks and temples create a timeless landscape, reflecting the changing seasons. Full of hidden meaning, the gardens were created as an earthly paradise and still cast their spell today. The sheer size and space is perfect for those who love the outdoors and enjoy walking. A scenic walk from New Inn takes you into the gardens where another world awaits. Stowe is great to explore all day long when you venture out to the far reaches of the garden and parkland. Come back time and time again to discover new routes in the garden or take a vigorous ramble in the parkland where more monuments wait to be explored, and see new views you won't find in the garden.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Send and Pandemic - 2021 Communication and language - 2024 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with us. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Every six months I hold a review meeting with the parents to discuss any feedback, advice and concerns. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I update a daily diary for all the children which is communicated to and reviewed by the parents. By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible, for example adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

local_offer: We support children with SEND  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a registered childminder, we have a Key Contact at Buckinghamshire Council with the Early Years Team, from whom we can access advice and information. They are happy to answer our questions or signpost to other appropriate services. Professionals are welcome to meet the child at our setting if parents wish. We are keen to expand our knowledge and expertise. We will undergo further training when required. As I am a Pacey member, I have access to a range of online resources. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work in partnership with parents to better understand the needs of the children. We share information about their child’s learning, development and progress on a regular basis in a manner which suits them, mainly during drop-off and collection. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they are able to approach us about anything relating to their children. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We observe and assess all children attending the setting. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and we prepare and implement a joint action plan for the child. With the parent's permission, we may involve other services if required. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and outside. The indoor environment provides a safe, secure yet challenging space for children. For some children, it is like a second 'home', providing a place for activity, rest, eating and sleeping. The indoor environment contains resources which are appropriate, well-maintained and accessible for all children. The outdoor play areas are fenced to keep children safe and have a back entrance door in emergencies. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. When children arrive at our setting we encourage families to have a settling-in period and complete an ‘All about Me’ sheet. We then jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and Pacey. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. We aim to address any issues and monitor and report progress.

local_offer: New Millside is fully committed to providing an inclusive environment accessible to all children from the ages of 2 to 5 giving all children the opportunity and resources to develop and extend their development across all seven areas of learning. We strive to provide a nurturing and stimulating environment where children can feel safe and cared for building their confidence to grow and develop. We feel passionate that all children deserve the right to learn and develop in their own individual way and offer a curriculum that caters to all abilities ensuring that all children are given the support and resources to have their voices heard. All staff have extensive experience and training in how best to support children with SEN including children with EAL. New Millside were praised in their recent Ofsted report for their support of children with SEN and the progress the environment enabled those children to make. We provide individual support tailored to the child's needs and work in partnership with parents and outside professionals to ensure your child receives the support they need in a caring and understanding environment. We offer visual support and knowledge of Makaton to develop alternative areas of communication. We follow the Graduated approach to ensure every need is identified and recognise the importance of early intervention.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have a SEN Team with a SENDCo supported by two deputy SENDCo's. We regularly access support from a variety of specialist services such as Speech and Language Therapy, Specialist Teaching services including Downs Syndrome Specialist Teachers and all staff have had the training to support those children on the Autistic Spectrum. We also have established links with the OT service and have developed a wide range of resources across all areas. We have staff trained to use Makaton and all staff are trained to use visual support. The SENDCo has had PECS training and achieved levels 1, 2 and 3 for supporting children on the Autistic Spectrum and SEN support staff have been trained to deliver PALS. We have a dedicated SEN room to provide a distraction-free environment for key workers to work on SEN plans and APDR outcomes with their children and this is also used by visiting professionals when necessary. Staff have extensive experience and training in supporting children with communication and language difficulties and the setting is well equipped with resources to support language development. We have worked closely with the Hearing support team and have experience working with children with Cochlear implants. Staff are all First Aid trained including the use of Epipen. We have experience and training to support children with Epilepsy and the use of medications to support this and those children who have diabetes or allergies. We have a named Inclusion Consultant and are supported by Bucks Early Years Service. We aim to support each child to reach their fullest potential and have high expectations for all children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Early Years Language Group training - 13/9/23 - 4/10/23 Level 3 SENCO completed by Senco and Deputy Senco - May 2023 Identifying Speech and Language Needs Developing Targets - 02/05/2019 Being two, understanding and supporting the needs of 2-year-olds - 17/10/2019 A guide to observation, assessment and planning in Early Years - 21/10/2019 Good Autism Practice - 14/10/2019 Understanding Children's and Young People's Mental Health - 01/02/2019 Makaton - 14/05/2019 Personal Care and Managing Medicines for children and young people - 20/06/2019 Effective Transition and Emotional Wellbeing in the Early Years - 06/11/2020 Supporting Children with SEND in Early Years - 09/11/2020 Speech, Language and Communication 09/11/2020 SEN Support and Beyond - 25/02/2021 Leading Good Autism Practice - 09/03/2021 Autism Awareness - 30/06/2021 Developmental Language Disorder - 15/09/2021 Speech Therapy Course (Diploma) - 24/10/2021 Early Years Good Autism Practice - 17/03/2022 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have an open door policy and parents are welcome to stay and play sessions and meet with the key worker, manager or SENDCo at any time. Parents are also encouraged to join the committee and are directly involved in decision-making for the preschool. We also welcome regular or Adhoc volunteers and have Grandparents that come in to read and play with the children each week. We use Tapestry an online learning Journal and parents are encouraged to upload photos and observations of achievements at home, so we can link these to the EYFS for a more complete journal. On starting we ask for a family profile and individual child one-page profile so that we can understand and support your child effectively. We have a Facebook page which has a messenger facility for any out-of-hours concerns or questions. We also post regularly to keep you updated on events. We will contact you by email, text, phone call and letters sent home via your child. You can specify your preferred method of contact and we will also offer translation facilities wherever possible. We have a parent suggestion box and also send out parent questionnaires so you can give us feedback to improve the setting. We offer two parent evenings a year with individual allocated time slots. Parents are given the time that their child's keyworker has their office time each week and can call in to speak to the keyworker during this time if they wish to do so, or can ask for the keyworker to call them, so that regular and personal communication can be maintained. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We do baseline and 2-year progress checks and next steps for all children which are shared with parents. We offer two Parents evenings a year with individual allocated time slots and have an Open door policy, individual meetings with the key worker, Manager or SENDCo can be arranged at a time to suit you, or you can call during the keyworkers office hour each week as you wish. Individual developmental trackers are sent out to parents three times a year. We encourage parents to contribute to their child’s individual Learning journey by uploading photos and observations from home. Children with SEND have individual APDR (Assess, Plan, Do, Review) targets shared with parents and individual SEN Plans. Parents are invited to contribute to these plans and identify areas they would also like to focus on. Feedback is given from outside professional visits such as Speech and Language and invites to attend meetings with outside professionals so that their views can be heard. Open door policy to meet with SENDCo. Parents are invited to attend reviews for EHCP’s. We share resources with parents to support achievements of outcomes for those children with SEN. We offer a separate quiet SEN room so that individual activities to support development can be carried out in a distraction-free environment with a key worker and outside professional. We use home-to-school books to support those families whose children may have communication difficulties to ensure their day can be shared and that effective communication can be maintained to support the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have wheelchair access at the front and rear of the building and a toilet that also provides wheelchair access. We have a dedicated SEN room to provide a distraction-free environment for key workers to work on SEN plans and APDR outcomes with their children and this is also used by visiting professionals when necessary. The SEN room has sensory and visual equipment including adapted seating and sensory lap blankets. We use visual timetables as a group and individually and have a blackout tent and ear defenders for children with sensory sensitivities. We also have a Connevans sound system in the building which ensures even distribution of sound to support all children, especially those with hearing difficulties. The outdoor area is spacious and easily accessible and usable for all children. We use home-to-school books to support those families whose children may have communication difficulties to ensure their day can be shared and that effective communication can be maintained to support the child. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children with additional needs and their families have individual transition meetings with the SENDCo and we arrange individual transition meetings with the SENDCo and reception lead the term before they move up to reception including a series of individual transition visits which are arranged in addition to group transition visits. We ensure that each child receives individualised transition plans that include images of their next setting, opportunities to have early access to uniforms and time to familiarise themselves with the new environment. For children entering preschool, we offer play and stay sessions before the start date and individual meetings with parents to discuss any concerns, we can also apply for funding with identified needs before the start date If necessary, so we can increase our adult-to-child ratio to allow an individual support worker to be put in place. We have a move-up day and offer all new children the opportunity to attend a two-hour session with other new starters. Where necessary we will do home visits before the start date. Where necessary we follow the Penny Tassoni 5 steps to leaving policy to ensure that all children feel safe and secure when starting at preschool. We have an EAL Lead and have a structured support system, we offer communication methods that best suit the individual including staff able to translate Urdu AND Punjabi. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to give all staff Makaton training and continue to develop and train staff in Autistic Spectrum Disorders and how to support Speech and Language difficulties. We plan to continue with the development of our SEN room and to develop a SEN area on our outside grounds.

local_offer: The Children's and Families Act (2014) outlines the government's plans to require local authorities to publish information on services and provision across education, health and social care for children and young people aged 0 to 25 with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). The purpose of a local offer is to enable parents and carers to see more clearly what services are available for children with SEND in their area and how to access them. The process extends to early years settings and all the information below forms our local offer and shows how Newton Longville Pre-School provides for children with special educational needs and disabilities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is to support our children with SEND and their families so that they are able to achieve their full potential. We aim to do this by ensuring that they have individualised support to so that their needs are understood and supported. We aim to help children make progress in all areas of their development and create an inclusive environment where children can engage with their peers and participate in activities. We aim to build children's self-esteem and promote independence where possible. We aim to collaborate with families to support the children's development both at home and within our setting. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? NCFE CACHE Level 3 Award for Special Educational Needs Coordinators in Early Years Settings - Lucy Boyce Understanding Autism - Amanda Holt Early Years Good Autism Practice of the Early Years AET Professional Development Programme - Lucy Boyce Suporting children with SEND in the Early Years - Lucy Boyce SEND Training for New and Aspiring SENCOs - Lucy Boyce Understanding and Supporting Children's Behaviour in the Early Years - Amanda Holt, Sherri Collins, Lucy Boyce Seeing beyond behaviour - Amanda Holt Autism and ADHD in Girls - Lucy Boyce Supporting Children's Speech, Language and Communication in the Early Years - Lucy Boyce Emotional Regulation - Lucy Boyce Leading the Way in Good Autism Practice - Lucy Boyce Making Sense of Autism - Sherri Collins Sensory and Motor Strategies - Lucy Boyce Developing Play in the Early Years of the Early Years NEN Inclusive Practice Development Programme - Lucy Boyce How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We operate an open-door policy, meaning that parents/carers are welcome to speak to us at any time to discuss their child’s development and needs in an informal manner. We can also use email and communication books for those who are not able to visit the setting regularly and offer stay-and-play sessions so parents/carers can see their child in action. We complete 2 years checks and offer parents consultations. Our online learning journal (Tapestry) is updated regularly to show the children's activities in the setting. We also encourage parents to use Tapestry to record and share their child’s learning moments at home, as this provides additional information about their preferences, allowing us to work together to set the next steps and plan effective learning experiences. We are also a committee-run setting and we encourage all parents/carers to join our management committee to give them a direct say in how we operate. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children have a key person who will work with them and their families, sharing information as noted above. In addition, for children with SEND, their key worker and our SENCO will meet more regularly with parents or carers to discuss progress and co-produce documents such as Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR), SEN Support Plans, referral requests and requests for additional funding if appropriate. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We work closely with all families to ensure our setting is as inclusive as possible and will make adaptions where reasonable and practical. We have a ramp at the front entrance and a disabled toilet in our reception area. Child-sized toilets and sinks are inside the main building. There are two steps to the outside area, but once outside the playground is flat with a grassed section. We also create areas for focused learning (both indoors and outdoors) where distractions are minimised. The purpose of a local offer is to enable parents and carers to see more clearly what services are available for children with SEND in their area and how to access them. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are reviewing our sensory environment and are planning dedicated spaces both indoors and outdoors to create more stimulating experiences.

local_offer: I have enjoyed worked in partnership with many families and their children of various ages and abilities for a number of years years. Children enjoy a safe and stimulating environment in which they can learn through play and I aim to be as flexible as possible in order to meet each childs specific needs. Every child is appreciate for being their unique self and a valued member of our happy group. I am keen to work closely with parents and other professionals to achieve best outcome for each child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to create an enriching environment with resources that can be fully accessed by all children and a space where children can progress and reach their full potential. I aim to work closely with parents and relevant professional and share information with families to support the child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I build strong, trusted relationships with parents where we can have open two way dialogues about their child in my care. I ask parents to tell me about the child's likes/dislikes, special people to them, significant events etc and I share updates about their child's learning, development and progress. I welcome information about their achievements at home and will create opportunities to extend this whilst in my care along with sharing ideas for use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I provide a book for each child that goes between home and my setting. It will detail general information about the childs day as well as what I've observed and next steps to progress learning opportunities. Parents are welcome to feedback in the book about the child when at home. I also create other opportunities for communication such as in person, via a private Whats app chat and other methods convenient for the family. When a particular need is highlighted I will support the implementation of a joint action plan for the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our house is situated on a very quiet road with ample parking outside. There is a small threshold at the front entrance leading into a wide, open hallway. The large bathroom is downstairs with easy access. Children have plenty of space to play in the light and airy lounge and separate playroom, both of which have double doors onto a large garden. Two small steps lead off the patio down to the grassed area with plenty of mature shrubs to explore. I will discuss with parents the best sleeping arrangements for their child. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are welcome to visit my setting and discuss their child's needs with me before completing an application. When a child starts, families are asked to complete an 'all about me' booklet to help me get to know their child and special people and things in their life. Parents are asked to provide any comforters, photos of family/important people and are welcome to keep a special box here for their child containing important toys and familiar things from home to ease the transition to my setting. Settling in visits are also very useful and are encouraged both with and without parents. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I endeavour to continue to be flexible in order to meet support each family and am keen to complete relevant training to support the children's specific needs. I keep up to date with new information from the local authority and regularly access their website.

name: Nisai Learning
description: Nisai has been delivering specialist online education since 1996, working in partnership with Local Authorities, schools and families across the UK and internationally. Our mission is to ensure that all learners, regardless of background or need, can access high-quality education and develop the skills to flourish through innovative, inclusive online learning. We provide a supportive learning community from Upper Key Stage 2 through to Key Stages 3, 4 and 5, enabling students to achieve recognised qualifications including Functional Skills, GCSEs and A Levels, and progress to further education, employment or training. Students with SEN/EHC Plans represent over 90% of our cohort. We support a wide range of needs, including autism, ADHD, SEMH, speech and language difficulties, dyslexia, global delay, and moderate learning difficulties. As a DfE Section 41 approved provider, we are recognised as specialists in supporting learners with SEND. 97% of our students present with at least one barrier to learning, with 82% experiencing multiple needs. Quality of Education We have designed an ambitious, inclusive curriculum that is carefully adapted to meet the needs of all learners. Teaching is delivered by qualified, subject-specialist teachers who receive ongoing professional development in adaptive teaching, SEND, and trauma-informed practice. Our teaching is characterised by: Highly effective adaptive teaching and personalised learning pathways Structured differentiation, including scaffolded and stretch tasks Use of evidence-based interventions, including Units of Sound (literacy support) and WordQ (word prediction and text-to-speech support) Assessment is rigorous and continuous, enabling staff to monitor progress closely and adapt provision. As a result, pupils make strong progress from their individual starting points. Learning Environment and Engagement The online environment is purposefully designed to reduce barriers to learning: Small, secure classes (typically no more than 15 students) Short, focused lessons to reduce cognitive overload Flexible communication methods All lessons recorded for revision and consolidation This structure supports learners who benefit from routine, reduced anxiety, and a low-pressure, inclusive learning environment. Personal Development, Behaviour and Welfare Pupils benefit from a highly supportive and inclusive environment where well-being is prioritised. A structured induction captures the student and family voice, ensuring provision is tailored from the outset. Our team provides: Ongoing pastoral care and wellbeing monitoring Access to virtual mentoring and in-person mentoring to support confidence, life skills and emotional wellbeing Careers guidance and enrichment opportunities Close communication with families and professionals Pupils are encouraged to develop confidence, resilience and independence, and to build positive relationships. They also have access to a secure, moderated Social Space, where they can interact with peers in a safe and structured environment. Please contact us directly.

It is our mission to give traditional and non-traditional learners the skills to flourish through innovative education and by influencing positive institutional change. We provide a friendly, supportive learning community and offer our students incredible opportunities. In essence, we support learners from Key Stages 1 to 5 and help create pathways to further education and employment through personalised learning. Our goal is to ensure that every student can complete their education and gain accredited academic and vocational qualifications within Functional Skills, GCSEs and A-Levels. local_offer: Before you join college for the first time, our teams will have received your Education, Health and Care plan (EHCP) if you have one. Even if you don’t have an EHCP in place, you’ll have a chance to tell us about any types of support you need with your studies when you meet our ALS and curriculum staff at your interview. Once we’ve assessed the information you’ve given us, and we’ve spoken to you and people like your parent/carer or teacher (as appropriate), we’ll then make a plan with you for the type of support you may need. This may include assistive technology and training on how to use it, in-class support, adapted learning materials, and out of class support. This is all part of the UK Government’s SEND review (2022), to provide the “right support, right place at the right time.” You don’t need an EHCP to receive Additional Learning Support from NHC. You may be eligible for learning support if you have, or are receiving a diagnosis of: Hearing or sight loss Autism spectrum condition Specific learning difficulties such as dyslexia, dyscalculia, or dyspraxia ADHD Moderate learning difficulty Mental health difficulty Physical difficulty Processing difficulty Personal care needs Medical needs A requirement to use specialist resources A requirement to use a scribe or reader If you have an additional need that isn’t included in this list but think you may still be entitled to ALS support, then please get in touch with our team to discuss your options. https://www.nhc.ac.uk/discover/student-life/additional-learning-support-als/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?
