name: Parent Portal by Speech Link
description: Speech and Language Link believes that every family should have access to clear and comprehensive information and easy-to-use home resources to help support their child’s speech, language and communication needs (SLCN). Our award-winning ‘Parent Portal’ provides fun and accessible ideas, advice, and activities for developing your child’s speech, language and communication at home. Covering each stage of your child’s development from early talkers through to key stage 3, our portal was created by our in-house team of speech and language therapists (SaLTs). Resources include engaging videos, games and everyday activities which can be woven into your daily routine. Our portal aims to make it as easy as possible for you to implement our activities and to give you the information and tools you need to help you support your child in reaching their full potential.
organisation: Speech Link Multimedia Ltd | Speech and Language Service for Schools Schools use our online serviced packages, Language Link and Speech Link, to identify and support children with mild to moderate speech or language difficulties. The assessments, resources and support are designed by speech and language therapists and specialist teachers. We know that the best indicator of how a child will cope with school is their understanding and use of spoken language. The standardised assessment identifies pupils with difficulties understanding core language skills. Over 160,000 children were screened in 2017/18 using our packages. Identified pupils receive a targeted programme of interventions. The classroom strategies, small group interventions and 1:1 supplementary teaching sessions make the best use of a TA's time and expertise. Teacher engagement ratings and parent and pupil views support evidence of improvement, essential for Ofsted and the Pupil Premium. For a week’s free trial, visit our website, email, or call. Speech Link in Buckinghamshire Speech Link is a project which will be launching in the autumn term and will be in schools supporting 5 to 7-year-olds over the next academic year. It is a programme that can support in the assessment and provision of children with speech language and communication needs, jointly commissioned by education and health here in Buckinghamshire, enabling schools to identify need and support children as early as possible. The programme has been used by several other Local Authorities, producing good outcomes and tracked progress has come from this, indicating that this will be beneficial. Developed by Speech and Language Therapists, the SpeechLink support packages provide a screening tool and intervention resources for use in the classroom and indicate the need for further support when required. liz.isaac@speechlink.co.uk https://speechandlanguage.info/

We are a diverse population that forms one positive and progressive community. Our individualised approach underpins all our work and is supported by high staffing ratios and close monitoring of progress, potential and social, physical and emotional well being of every young person. Every child has the right to enter school every morning feeling respected and safe. They should know that what they are expecting to be taught is appropriate to them and will challenge them. They should also get regular opportunities to sense the amazing feeling of success. Staff and pupil relationships are a strength of this school. Staff and pupils build mutual respect through talking and sharing time throughout every minute of the school day. Our standards of behaviour and discipline have been noted as outstanding by two different external inspectors. Behaviour begins in the classroom. Excellent teaching nearly always brings excellent behaviour. Further to this, our pupils know their boundaries and are taught and encouraged to behave rather than told to behave. Incidents are dealt with professionally and swiftly and appropriate action is taken. Our new approach to the curriculum inspires learning and promotes relevance by providing opportunities to use and apply skills as they develop. We make no apologies for a heavy emphasis on literacy and numeracy, but we balance this out with a broad range of other subjects, many of which carry outside accreditation. We are very proud of our growing vocational opportunities. We continue to provide construction and small animal care, horticulture, painting and decorating as well as car maintenance. All pupils in Years 9, 10 and 11 complete ASDAN accreditation that develop their personal and social skills. description: Mixed-gender independent specialist day and residential school in Swadlincote, Derbyshire for 7 to 19-year-old. With severe learning disabilities, autism, and associated challenging behaviour. Many of our students also have mental health and therapy needs. The School is situated on the grounds of Caldwell Hall; five miles from Burton on Trent on the borders of Staffordshire, Derbyshire, and Leicestershire. The ethos of Pegasus School is our individualised approach. Every element of a student's package is bespoke to that individual; whether that be the number of nights they stay, their specific routine, the input from professional services, diet, cultural and religious preferences. Until students are 16 years old, education and care are located in one building with on-site professional support services. This gives us the opportunity to truly build a multi-disciplinary package around the young person. This integrated approach means we are able to fully meet the needs of young people with very complex needs and ensure they make progress, develop independent skills, and are able to engage socially with others. This level of support continues when the students move to the on-site college at the age of 16.
organisation: SENAD Group Alderwasley Hall School and Sixth Form is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 5 to 19 years with Specific Language Disorders, Aspergers Syndrome and High Functioning Autistic Spectrum Disorders, all of whom experience complex speech, language and communication needs. The School and Sixth Form are located on separate sites within five miles of each other and are situated in Derbyshire, close to the towns of Matlock, Belper and Wirksworth. The City of Derby is also within easy access. The aim of all aspects of the curriculum is to prepare students for adult life by fulfilling their social and academic potential. Young people are supported to develop and achieve academic and vocational plans, develop independent living skills and a clear sense of identity, enabling them to contribute to society in adult life. description: Our Princes Risborough Baby Nursery is a friendly baby nursery located within the children’s centre at Princes Risborough Primary School. As one of the only dedicated baby nurseries in the UK, our nursery specialises in caring for babies from 3 months to 24 months old. Once our babies are ready, they graduate to our sister nursery just a few minutes away. We pride ourselves on building strong relationships and partnerships with our parents to provide a home from home feel within our nursery. As our nursery is dedicated to the needs of babies, all our equipment is tailored for the learning and development to suit their needs in a safe and stimulating environment. Our nursery has a story nook, a construction zone, an inviting outdoor space, and a comfy corner which includes a black and white sensory zone designed for very young babies who have not yet developed the ability to see colour. We are located within easy reach of the local train station which has connections to London, Luton, and Oxford. We also have bike and buggy storage available so you can leave these with us when you head off to work.

name: Perinatal Mental Health Support and Postnatal Wellbeing Groups
description: The Perinatal Mental Health Pathway for Buckinghamshire is designed to promote positive emotional well-being and mental health for new and expectant mothers. The pathway is to support mothers across a range of concerns from mild anxiety or depression to more severe mental illness and gives access to a variety of services. This can include GPs, midwives, individual or group therapy through the Healthy Minds service, or access to the Specialist Perinatal Mental Health Team. The pathway aims to take into account individual needs and to ensure mothers make informed decisions about their care in partnership with healthcare professionals, preconception, during pregnancy, and after birth. The Pathway has been designed to ensure that women concerned about their mental health can be referred to the appropriate service by healthcare professionals, community support organisations (such as Family Hubs) or by contacting the services directly themselves. The aim is that women can get the right support in a streamlined, timely, consistent and appropriate way. Postnatal Wellbeing Groups offer support and treatment for postnatal women with mild to moderate depression and/or anxiety. The programme teaches skills in monitoring and managing mood and ways to deal with negative thinking. A crèche is provided. Currently, these groups are being run online. The pathway has been developed with the help of many dedicated healthcare colleagues across a wide range of specialities and aims to support women when they need it the most which in turn, makes a difference to the lives of their babies, young children, partners and families too. For further information contact a Health Visitor, GP or Healthy Minds.

name: Talkback Personal Development Skills
description: Our Personal Development and Skills Programme helps individuals build essential life skills, confidence, and friendships, while focusing on their strengths and goals to promote self-esteem and independence. Life Skills Building life skills is at the heart of everything we do. We support individuals to grow at their own pace, from staying safe and travelling independently to managing money, cooking, and preparing for work. Our flexible, person-centred approach ensures each programme evolves with our members’ needs, helping them achieve real, meaningful outcomes. Key areas include: - Travel Training: Building confidence to travel safely, from local journeys to wider travel - Health and Wellbeing: Promoting healthy lifestyles through nutrition, cooking, and physical activity - Employability: Developing practical skills for volunteering and paid work - Independent Living: Managing a home, finances, appointments, and daily responsibilities - Healthy Relationships: Building strong, positive, and lasting connections Social Skills We create safe, supportive spaces where people can build confidence, express themselves, and make friends. Our groups offer: - User-led activities tailored to interests- from cooking to gaming and sports - Community engagement to build independence and confidence in real-life settings Work Experience Our work experience opportunities combine hands-on learning with practical skills development, supporting individuals to explore pathways into volunteering or employment. Through partnerships with local organisations, members gain: - Strong communication and customer service skills - Confidence in handling money and transactions - Experience in real workplace environments - Essential teamwork and people skills Working Outdoors Our outdoor programme combines practical work with wellbeing, helping individuals build skills while enjoying the benefits of nature. Focus areas include: - Teamwork and communication - Time management and responsibility - Horticultural skills and seasonal awareness - Hands-on experience in planting, growing, and maintaining outdoor spaces Expressive Arts Our creative sessions encourage self-expression, confidence, and communication through art, music, and movement. Participants develop: - Creativity and imagination - Emotional awareness and self-expression - Communication through visual and sensory art - Confidence and an ‘I Can’ mindset Performing Arts Our theatre group offers a platform to build confidence, creativity, and teamwork, working towards live performances each year. Participants develop skills in: - Acting, scriptwriting, and storytelling - Communication and collaboration - Confidence through performance - Goal-setting and personal achievement Sport and Good Health We make staying active fun, inclusive, and accessible- supporting healthier lifestyles and strong social connections. Our sports programme promotes: - Teamwork and confidence - Inclusive coaching and skill development - Leadership and employability skills - Opportunities for qualifications and real experience - Access to community sports and activities At Talkback, we support people to grow, connect, and thrive - building the skills and confidence needed for greater independence and a more fulfilling life.

name: Ashbourne Day Nursery at Princes Risborough
description: Our Princes Risborough day nursery is a small and friendly setting situated in the heart of Princes Risborough. The nursery is located minutes away from the local train station for an easy commute into London, Luton, or Oxford. We aim to provide a safe yet inspiring environment for our children to play, learn and develop. We use a variety of resources to spark their imagination and encourage learning through play. We support the children in making their own choices promoting independence and self-confidence. Our nursery has an on-site chef who creates healthy and delicious meals daily for the children. We understand that all children are unique which is why we adapt to the needs of every child in our care.

name: Pilates with Kate
description: Pilates with Kate classes in South Buckinghamshire, for clients of all ages and abilities. My teaching method will guide you through the vital principles of Pilates and will also offer some challenging moves to work towards. I'm a certified Level 3 mat work Pilates instructor with a Level 4 qualification specialising in lower back pain. I like to build the moves, giving optional progressions so that people of all levels can enjoy Pilates together. Pilates is highly beneficial; it can improve core strength, posture, and muscular problems, tone your body, and give a sense of well-being. It is also a fantastic way to tone your body after pregnancy and childbirth. Please visit my website to learn more and book a class.

name: Pitstone Recreation Ground
description: Pitstone Recreation Ground has new facilities, all installed in the last few years: a wooden adventure play area, concrete skate park, multi-use ball court, and cricket practice nets. The play equipment includes: - 2 springers - sunken trampoline - Cheops maxi climbing pyramid with slide - Climbing whirl - Cableway - Fortuna play course - Wide embankment slide - Toddler swings - Viking rope swing - Cantilever swing - Junior swings - Nest carousel - Birds nest tree - Picnic benches Adjacent to the play area is a spray concrete skate park. The multi-use ball court is still under the ownership and responsibility of Nicholas King Homes. A new double-lane set of cricket practice nets was installed in 2023. Please contact Ivinghoe and Pitstone United Cricket Club, and they'll provide you with the combi access code. The recreation ground also includes football pitches used by the local Junior Football Club and a cricket pitch used by Ivinghoe and Pitstone United Cricket Club. At the same site is Pitstone Memorial Hall, which also houses CuriosiTea rooms.

suitabilities: 
local_offer: As a nursery, we support a wide range of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) by creating an inclusive, welcoming and nurturing environment where every child feels valued and supported. We work closely with children, parents, carers and relevant professionals to identify individual needs and put appropriate strategies and adjustments in place. This may include adapting activities, providing visual aids, using sensory resources, offering additional communication support and creating personalised learning opportunities. Our aim is to ensure that every child can participate, develop their skills and reach their full potential at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our nursery aims to provide an inclusive, nurturing, and supportive environment where children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) can learn, play, and thrive alongside their peers. We support children to develop confidence, communication, social skills, independence, and a love of learning through activities that are tailored to their individual needs and interests. We work closely with parents, carers, and other professionals to ensure each child receives the right support and that their strengths, needs, and aspirations are understood. Through a child-centred approach, we aim to promote positive wellbeing, reduce barriers to learning and participation, and help every child make progress and reach their full potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? At our nursery we regularly under take high quality SEND training to ensure our team is fully equipped to support every child's unique learning journey, covering key areas such as speech and language, autism awareness, sensory processes and positivity behaviour strategies. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At our nursery we place parents at the heart of the SEND process recognising that you are the experts on your child. We work in close, transparent partnership with you through regular catch up and review meetings and open daily communication. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We track and share daily achievements, developmental milestones and observations. We have twice yearly parents evenings to discuss children's development and meet to review children's ADPR targets and progression half termly. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our nursery is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible environment for all children, including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Our indoor and outdoor spaces are designed to be welcoming, safe and accessible, with suitable equipment, resources and adaptations available to support individual needs. We work closely with children, families and relevant professionals to make reasonable adjustments where needed, ensuring that every child can participate, explore, learn and play to the best of their ability. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Before they start, we work closely with the child, family and relevant professionals to understand their individual needs, strengths and interests. We use this information to put appropriate support and reasonable adjustments in place, helping each child feel welcomed, included and able to participate from the beginning. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to develop an inclusive environment by revamping the sensory shed to provide a calm, engaging space with a range of sensory resources. Create a sensory garden with herbs, vegetables and varied plants, giving children opportunities to explore different smells, textures and colours while developing independence, confidence and wellbeing. Both areas should be accessible and adapted to meet individual needs, particularly for children with SEND.

local_offer: How are the setting’s resources allocated and matched to a child’s Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities? Our practice is fully inclusive for all the children in our care. Through regular monitoring, observations and sharing information with parents, key carers will make decisions alongside the nursery SENDCo as to the needs of the individual child. Whenever possible we will use space, equipment and resources that we already have available in the nursery setting and garden. However, if deemed necessary staff will make changes to the provision in order that every child regardless of their needs will be able to access the early year’s curriculum. If needed, we can borrow equipment from other professionals such as occupational therapists. If it is deemed that we cannot adequately provide for a child within the setting then we will seek to access higher needs funding from the local authority. There is a list of SEN descriptors held by local authorities which may apply to the children, if so then we can request extra financial support. How is the decision made about what type and how much support a child with SEND will receive? The SENDCo, key carers and parents will work together to decide on the best way forward for the child. If appropriate, the child will also be involved in the decision-making process. Staff use their knowledge of the children to advise professionals of the children’s choices and wishes. It is the responsibility of the key carer to make the SENDCo aware of any concerns about a child’s health or development. The SENDCo will carry out observations and research before informing parents and with their permission we will contact other professionals for guidance and support. This may be medical personal, educational personal or both. It all depends on the child’s needs. As an Ofsted registered setting we have access to the Inclusion Officers at the local authority. They come to the setting to offer advice and expertise to staff team and the parents. How are parents involved in the setting? All our families are valued and their input and support is necessary in helping us to get the best outcomes for their child. We view the parents as the first educators. They know their child best and we encourage relationships that are based on mutual respect with the child at the heart of our ethos. We recognise that it can be very difficult for parents when their children have SEN so we are sensitive to their needs and wishes too. The SENDCo is very involved in supporting the child and their family. However, it is the key carer who is the main support as they are the person that has a close bond with the child and a positive relationship with the parents. Forming caring and trusting relationships with our parents is essential when supporting all our children but even more so when a child has SEN. We take time to research and provide them with all the information needed to support them and their child. Some parents are very proactive and are able to access professionals to get the help they need for their children. Other parents are less confident about seeking the help they need and this is when we can provide information about accessing the support and resources to help them to help their child. What future plans does your setting have for developing its SEND provisions including training and facilities? Inclusion is ingrained in out ethos, therefore we constantly reflect on our practice. We will regularly implement training needs both in house and off site. It is our intention that all our staff will be able to recognise any development, health or learning concerns that the children may display. We want all out staff to be able support all our children in fully accessing the curriculum. The SENDCo and staff will continue to maintain contact with outside agencies especially the Inclusion Officers from the local authority. We will always seek to get the views of the children whenever this is appropriate. We will never become complacent and continually strive to get the very best outcomes for the children in our care. We will continue to value the advice and support we get from our parents. We will comply with current legislation at all times. Which Local Authorities/Counties/health providers do you have contracts with? Buckinghamshire and Berkshire How will the child with SEN be included in activities outside the setting? This will be dependent on the needs of the child so staff will implement plans accordingly. Children are able to access the garden from two separate exits. The nursery has double doors leading to the garden which can accommodate a wheelchair or other support equipment. Risk assessments will be produced so that the children can fully access the outside area and early year’s curriculum. When children leave the nursery setting to go out for walks, feeding the ducks: correct ratios are always adhered to. If necessary the ratio for children with SEN will increase to 1:1 whenever staffing numbers allow. How accessible is the setting’s environment (inside and outdoors) The nursery building benefits from a large entrance area which can easily accommodate both wheelchairs and specially adapted pushchairs. We have an accessible downstairs toilet. The building does not have a life however the staircase is wide therefore equipment that is manageable can be carried between floors. Resources are placed so that children can access then independently. However we will always investigate ways to adjust the rooms when caring for children with SEND. Staff are very experienced in supporting parents and children whose first language is not English. How will the staff prepare and support a child with SEND to join the setting or transfer to a new setting/school? All children have a series of settling in sessions and parents will accompany them when necessary. A child with SEN will have more and/or longer times to settle if needed. During the sessions the child and their parent(s) will spend time in the room getting to know the key carers. It is an opportunity to share information and to make a start on the special caring relationship between the child and their key carer. We recognise that for parents, particularly those with SEN that trusting and open relationships with carers is very important in order to support the child and remain sensitive to the parent’s needs. Parents complete paperwork that helps the carers know all about the individual child and their needs and difficulties. Carers will then use this information to monitor the child and implement activities to support them in all areas. Initially we focus on personal, social and emotional needs as this encourages the child to interact with the environment, the carers and other children. Regular observations and monitoring starts as soon as the child joins the nursery setting, the child’s ongoing development is recorded. Parents thoughts and views and sought and valued on a daily basis through regular verbal communication. When children transfer to school or another setting, the SENDCo will organise a transition meeting that the parents and all the professionals involved will be invited to. If deemed appropriate the child will spend some time in their new setting with their key carer before making the transition completely. Once the transition is complete the child’s Learning Journey which includes the child’s needs and progress will be passed on to the new setting. Key carers also complete a transition document that will go with the child. This helps the new key carers to support the child. What support does the setting offer for a child with SEND overall well-being? The well-being of the children in our care is entwined in our ethos. Our highly skilled practitioners understand the importance of not only keeping our children safe but about helping them to feel secure and valued. In order to do this we endeavour to constantly raise the levels of the children’s well-being and involvement during their time with us. This applies to all our children but we want any child in our setting with SEN to benefit from well-being and involvement too. We put a great deal of emphasis on the relationships between the child, his/her key carer and the parents. These relationships are nurtured and valued for the benefit of everyone involved. Key carers are the first point of contact for the parents. The SENDCo works alongside the key carers to offer support with planning and health care. Both the SENDCo and key carers attend regular training sessions offered by the local authority and other trainers. Outside professionals such as health staff, inclusion offers and speech therapists are regularly involved in the care and support of the children. What Specialist services and expertise are available at, or accessed by the setting? The practitioners at Poppies nurseries have a variety of qualifications, skills and experience which can be called upon to fully support all of our children and parents. We value and implement regular training for our staff to keep them abreast of legislation and the best approach to supporting any child with Special Educational Needs. We can regularly call on the expertise and support of outside agencies that we have formed professional relationships with. We liaise with health visitors in the local community for advice and information. What training have the staff supporting children with SEND had or are having? The nursery has a trained Lead SENDCo and assistant SENDCo. All staff working with the children attend in house training that helps them to identify any child that may have other needs and may not be progressing as expected for their age and development stage. We have paperwork in place that staff can use to record any concerns that is then passed to the SENDCo to investigate. Any specific type of training particularly for children with medical needs can be arranged and implemented either in the setting or off-site. Training is regular and ongoing, depending on the needs of the individual children. The SENDCo carries out regular research, both on the internet and in trade publications in order to keep up to date with any new developments for children with SEN. How does the setting know if a child will need extra help and what should families do if they think their child may have Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities? The children are regularly observed and monitored by their carers. As all our staff are either qualified or in the midst of getting qualified. This means that they have the skills to recognise when there may be a development or health concern for a child. The concern is recorded and passed to the SENDCo. Following more investigation and observations, the parents will be sensitively informed and an action plan will be put in place. As we have developed trusting and mutually respectful relationships with our parents, this has helped them to feel that they can approach the carers about concerns and worries. We understand how difficult it can be for parents to acknowledge that their child may have SEND therefore we would never dismiss their concerns. We offer suggestions about the best way to address their worries. It may be a visit to their GP or we can offer to access other professionals on their behalf. We always do everything to reassure our parents and offer them a listening ear. Sometimes just voicing their concerns can make their worries slightly easier to manage. How will the staff in the setting support a child with SEN? Our carers will do everything possible to support both the child and their parents. Inclusion for all the children runs through our ethos. It is our passion that every child in the nursery will have opportunities to learn through play and high-quality activities and experiences regardless of age, development stage and individual needs. Through observations, parental input, advice from health and other educational professionals, a SEN support plan will be produced and implemented. This will be updated regularly depending on the child’s progress and needs. Everyone involved will communicate regularly and share information for the benefit of the child. How will the curriculum for the setting be matched to a child with SEND needs? Everything depends on the needs of the child. Physical changes can be made if necessary and appropriate for large equipment and resources to allow the child full access to toys, resources, experiences and activities. Children with hearing or speech impairments will have access to classroom and individual visual timetables. Some of our staff have Makaton training which the children can also learn and use to communicate. PECS (Picture Exchange Communication System) can be used to support children if necessary. Carers will plan activities to suit the needs of the individual children. Our aim is for all the children to achieve, therefore support and learning will be planned and implemented accordingly. SEND is a barrier to learning. However, it is the role of the nursery staff team to do all they can to overcome these barriers. We have high but achievable expectations for the children. This, in turn, supports the child’s feeling of self-worth and willingness to attempt new experiences. How will staff work with families about how a child with SEND is doing and how to support a child’s learning? Parents will have regular communication, both written and verbal with carers and the SENDCo to keep them fully informed about their child’s progress. We operate an open-door policy that allows parents to talk with carers, outside professionals and the nursery SENDCo. The child remains at the heart of our practice and we recognise the value to the children when parents and staff work in partnership. Melody Music French teaching by Nursery class teacher. Buckinghamshire Early Years adviser regularly visits to ensure up to date and best practise. Nikki Patton our EYFS coordinator - audits and supports our curriculum What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The SENCOs have attending several training courses to enable them to support all staff who work with children with SEND. All information received during training courses is shared at staff meetings. The SENCO works closely with staff members to ensure they are confident dealing with individual needs for children with SEND. If specific training is required for a child, such as EpiPen training, this will be attended by all staff working closely with the child. Our most recent training was for Autistic Spectrum Disorder completed Feb 2020. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Poppies has strong relationships with the parents, they are encouraged to share their views and opinions to the staff and management. The nursery holds two parents evenings per year and sends out annual questionnaires for feedback on the setting. Newsletters are also sent out every three months to share news and what has been happening at the nursery. Parents are encouraged to upload developmental milestones, information about weekend activities onto our online learning journal (Tapestry). The nursery has a partnership with parent’s notice board in the entrance hall where information on this can be found. The nursery invites the parents in for events such as Mother’s Day Breakfast and Father’s Day messy play afternoons. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Your child will have an Educational Health Care Plan put in place and outside agencies are involved , where appropriate. We have close links with outside agencies and a good understanding of any extra funding entitlements that are available. We have a SEND curriculum included in our Tapestry online journals to allow individual tailored support and assessment. Regular meetings are held to ensure all of our team are working in partnership with families to support individual learning needs. We have two full time SENCO trained team members. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We are on one level. For areas where there may be one step to access main entrance adaptations can be made. The Poppies environment, both inside and out, can be adapted to suit the needs of individual children; additional equipment can be added if necessary. All of our buildings and rooms are on ground floor level. Activities are planned with individual children in mind and are adapted to suit the each child’s development stage. Individual next step activities are also planned for each child. We work closely with any families who have English as an additional language, to ensure all information shared is understood by everyone. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children are able to visit for hour long bursts – as many visits as you feel required and based on child’s individual needs and their reaction to the environment. We work in partnership with families to come up with a tailor made plan for settling in little ones. Settling in sessions are free of charge and you have as many as you need. Parents stay with their children for the first few and then gradually leave their child for longer periods of time. Each child has an allocated key person who will take extra special care of the child and help them feel secure. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Poppies continues to reflect on our practice and develop in all areas. The SENCO will continue to attend regular training and meetings to ensure all information is kept up to date. We will continue to access appropriate training for staff for every child that requires it. The nursery will continue to have strong relationships with outside agencies, to enable us to gain their expertise in certain areas if required.

name: Best of You Coaching Consultancy
description: Positive Psychology and Coaching, helping parents when they need a little support as we all can at times. As a mother of six, I understand some of the challenges. As a Psychologist who coaches, I work with parents but also with teenagers or whole families. I am the author of the kindle book ‘parenting the child with conduct disorder' under the author name Caralyn Bains, which provides a useful resource for parents. I also have a strengths-based positive psychology book for parents on Amazon kindle. I have two books on Parenting children with ADHD on amazon kindle or available as paperback: 'Parenting the Girl with ADHD', and 'Parenting the Boy with ADHD'. Both books look at moving into teens and some of the challenges. I was one of the first people in the UK to hold a Masters in Applied Positive Psychology (MAPP) from Buckinghamshire New University and this is my predominant focus or knowledge base that I use when coaching. My research interests are savouring and its application, mindfulness, and resilience. I have presented at conferences on Trauma and Post Traumatic Growth, with Peer reviewed papers published in Journals. I am a well-being practitioner and utilise my BSc (Honours) in Psychology with my knowledge base from the MSc in Applied Positive Psychology to enable clients to find their best version of themselves. I also work with children from primary age through to teens, providing help and strategies if they need support. I am familiar with ADHD, ASD, sensory issues, and sleep issues.

name: The Power to Change Programme
description: This programme is based on the idea that women working together in a safe, friendly and non-judgemental environment can change their lives for the better. The programme is self-referral only and is open to those who have already completed the Freedom Programme or similar. For the self-help group to work effectively participation must be an autonomous choice. It is a closed programme which will last for 12 consecutive weeks. The purpose of the course is: - To increase understanding of the dynamics of abusive relationships - To benefit and draw strength from being in an environment with other survivors of domestic abuse - To gain coping mechanisms, techniques and strategies around; assertiveness, being able to say NO, confidence building, dealing with authority figures, equal relationships, understanding and prioritising needs, understanding feelings, such as; grief, anger, guilt, shame, and fear and implementing boundaries - To increase self-esteem and self-worth, improve confidence, improve and encourage healthier relationships, cope with authority figures, benefit from being understood and heard by others, to feel our experiences have been affirmed, gain self-determination and autonomy and a better understanding of ourselves If you are interested in attending the Power to Change Programme or would like further information about it, please contact Jo. The next programme will start in September 2023

local_offer: Prestwood Infant school is an inclusive mainstream school with an attached Pre-School which will consider entry for all pupils regardless of special educational need or disability. At Prestwood Infant School we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve their full potential. We believe all children have individual needs, strengths and talents which should be met through a challenging, enjoyable and enriched curriculum which provides opportunities for all children to learn at their own level and pace. All teachers and learning support assistants are committed this vision. We recognise that some children may require additional support or challenge throughout their learning journey and strive to identify this early, thus ensuring we meet each child’s needs quickly and effectively. https://www.prestwoodvillageschools.co.uk/key-information/send-and-inclusion What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? 1. Identify children’s needs as early as possible and put steps in place to support children. 2. Work in partnership with families and professionals in adopting a multi-agency approach. 3. Ensure that all our staff are committed and trained to enable them to support children with SEND. 4. Provide a SENDCo who is committed to managing the provision for children with SEND. 5. Work within the guidance of the SEN Code of Practice. 6. Ensure that a commitment to inclusion is placed at the heart of our school and underpins everything that we do. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our staff receive regular training based on the current needs of the children in our setting. Recently this has included ASD training, Attachment training and training to support a child with particular physical needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are invited to attend termly SEN meetings to review provision and targets. For children with an Education, Health and Care plan, there will be an annual review meting for parents, staff and all professionals involved to review the provision and long term outcomes for the child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? In addition to two parents evenings and a formal report, parents will receive copies of termly reviewed support plans (or EHC Plans). How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our school building is DDA compliant. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? School admissions are handled by Buckinghamshire County Council What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are committed to the ongoing development of our SEN provision and our SENDCo has an action plan which outlines the next steps in moving our provision forward

name: Prestwood Junior School
description: At Prestwood Junior School, we are proud to offer a warm, nurturing, and stimulating environment for children aged 7 to 11. As part of the Prestwood Village Schools family, our school is dedicated to fostering both academic and personal growth, ensuring that each child thrives and reaches their full potential. Across our schools we strive to create a nurturing and stimulating environment where every child can thrive and reach their full potential. But success at Prestwood Junior School is about more than just numbers. We are passionate about delivering an innovative and exciting curriculum, designed to inspire curiosity, creativity, and a love of learning in every child. Our unique campus-style setting provides a spacious, open learning environment where each classroom is its own individual block. With two large playgrounds and a vast field, our students have plenty of space to learn, play, and grow. We believe in creating a vibrant, inclusive community where all children feel valued, supported, and encouraged to shine. We are very proud to be part of the Great Learners Trust, where we benefit from working collaboratively with a number of local schools. The staff at Prestwood Village Schools regularly work alongside other Trust schools to help improve the teaching and learning of all pupils. Through our dedicated staff, innovative teaching methods, and a rich curriculum, we aim to inspire a love for learning and foster the development of well-rounded individuals. Whether you're a current parent, prospective parent, or simply interested in learning more about our school, we hope you find inspiration and excitement in learning more about what makes Prestwood Village Schools such a special place. Please reach out with any questions you may have, or to truly understand our fantastic schools, please contact us to arrange a visit. We can't wait to meet you.

local_offer: Princes Risborough Primary School, class teachers are aware of the needs of all their children, who are monitored carefully to measure the progress they are making. This ensures that any special educational needs are identified as early as possible. Our teaching is inclusive for all pupils, with lesson content and delivery considered in terms of the impact on differing levels of pupil ability. If a child is finding a learning area particularly difficult, the majority of their needs should still be met within the classroom through quality first differentiated, personalised teaching. A pupil is identified as having special educational needs if he/she finds it significantly more difficult to learn than the majority of others of the same age. For these pupils, there are therefore occasions when additional support may be required, for a variety of reasons. Additionally Resourced Provision (ARP) Princes Risborough Primary School also has a 12 place Additionally Resourced Provision (ARP) for children with a diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder. We pride ourselves on the personal and friendly service that we provide, with special emphasis on attention to individual requirements and preferences so that we are able to meet the children's individual needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? If a child requires support from outside professional services parents will be spoken to prior to any support being put into action. Some professional services may attend the setting and observe children in the nursery environment. Parents may be offered extra support and advice through parenting classes, playgroup schemes, support with speech and language, paediatricians, occupational therapists, and classes that will enable a child to develop within their identified area of learning. The SENDCO will offer advice to parents and colleagues and ensure that we are following the correct protocol when looking to access support for the child(ren). What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Laura Madill carried out the SENCO Training for Nominated New and Inspiring SENCOS November 2022, she is supported by the manager Samantha Burton. Staff attend any relevant training as and when required to ensure they keep on top of new information and staff share their training within the setting with their colleagues. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parent partnership is vital when caring for young children and is something we believe is the biggest asset to ensuring the children are happy and settled. All parents have access to their child’s learning journals that are completed via our early years online app. Parents are welcome to speak to staff at any time about their child’s developmental progress. The nursery holds regular parents’ evenings which is a good time to have an in-depth discussion about the child’s development. Our team of staff ensure that all children’s needs are identified and information on how we are supporting them is shared with the parents and other relevant professionals if required. To support further communication with parents we use email, our online app (EyLog), daily diaries and ensure staff give a good handover when children are dropped off or collected. We welcome parents to stay and play sessions during the year and we will add anything they suggest to our planning to support parental input. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child is allocated a key person who is responsible for settling them in to the nursery as well as planning for them based on their individual needs. Monitoring their progress is extremely important and is carried out daily by the key person. We have two Special Educational Needs Coordinators who have received training through our local authority. We also attend regular update meetings to ensure that we are providing colleagues, children and parents with the best support methods possible. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Every child has a unique personality and will access the nursery experiences in different ways; therefore, we plan for your child’s development based on observations that are personal to their own learning journey. The environment is adapted in ways that will capture your child’s individuality and allows them to explore at their own pace with the support from their key person and other staff within the setting. On occasions the staff take the children out to explore our local community where they may visit places like the local library and museum. A full risk assessment is carried out for each outing to ensure that the area is suitable for every child as well as being safe. A higher adult/child ratio is used when on outings. The front entrance of the setting has been adapted where we have a built in ramp to make the nursery more accessible. The younger children are based in three upstairs rooms which do require walking up a staircase, however the Pre-school is situated on ground level and therefore more accessible to all. There are accessible toilets both upstairs and on ground level. To the garden there is a clear path with three small steps that lead to the garden area and at the back of the garden there are steps that lead up to the back-play area. The setting identifies what resources are required to meet the children’s individual needs through carrying out room and setting reviews as well as resource audits. The Early learning advisor supports the manager and SENDCO with identifying what resources or changes to the environment may be needed to best support children attending. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When a place is offered to a child, we carry out settling in sessions, this allows for parents and children to develop a stronger bond with the key carers and for the staff to gain more information about the child and family. Some settling in periods may require to be longer or be extended based on the child’s individual needs. When a child is transitioning to school the key person, SENDCO and manager will complete a transition report which informs the receiving school about the current development and needs of the child. With the parent’s permission, information such as individual support plans will be shared and a meeting will then be arranged, usually in the second half of the summer term. The meeting will include parents, the SENDCO, the school SENDCO and any invited additional professionals to meet and discuss the child’s needs to ensure that the transition runs smoothly. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The SENDCO attends termly liaison groups to ensure we are keeping up to date with the most current policies and procedures. All staff carry out core training and are then provided with additional training when required allowing for continuous CPD. The Nursery SENCO, Manager, Owner and Early Learning Advisor attend local early years meetings where we are kept updated with local and national changes in childcare. Any information gained from these meetings are then discussed through staff training and any changes are implemented where required.

local_offer: Psychotherapy Space is aimed at facilitating young people in their ability to make good long lasting and productive relationships. We facilitate emotional development that enables pupils to reach their full academic potential. Having a space to think about difficulties and relieving symptoms will reduce worries and enable a child to participate fully in school life.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Psychotherapy Space has the skills and expertise to work with the emotional worries and concerns that children and young people with SEND and their families might present with. This can come in many forms, from anxiety, low mood, behavioural issues, and more. To offer the children, young people, and their families a space either individually, as a family, or through staff groups in schools or other agencies, where the mental well-being can be addressed and improved upon. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Extensive experience in working in Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service, also in schools as an Inclusion Manager and as SENCo. Training undertaken for Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy is intensive and in depth. Ongoing Continued Professional Development in line with the professional bodies to which we belong. A number of specific Neurodiverse workshops and seminars. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parent consultation and parent groups available. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We are accessible via the telephone, Skype, email, letters, text and in person. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Psychotherapy Space has a ramp to the consulting room but there is a step up into the room itself. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If therapeutic work is done through the family, an initial discussion will take place with the parents, carers on the phone, email, and then a consultation in person to think about what the needs and worries are. An assessment with the young person may then follow. Other agencies might want to contact us for an initial telephone consultation. We are also available to email. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We would like to further develop services working in schools. This might include group work for a variety of mental health issues and offer training, consultation and supervision to staff around these issues.

If you or your child is suffering with emotional distress or if there has been a trauma, Psychotherapy Space might be able to support you in relieving the symptoms. Work is tailored to the age of the person seeking support, from using play therapy through to talking therapy. Difficulties such as anxiety, attachment troubles, depression, eating disorders, low self-esteem, self-harm, mental distress due to neurodiversity, and behavioural problems are some of the issues that can be resolved. Training for organisations in understanding issues surrounding a variety of mental health difficulties, as well as supervision and consultation to professionals, is also available. Working closely with statutory organisations with adopted and fostered children and their families is a particular specialty.

High quality teaching and a challenging curriculum is vital; however for some children there are occasions during their school life when additional support may be needed to help them to achieve their targets. All pupils, including those with a special educational need or disability (SEND) have the right to be fully involved in all that the school offers.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Children who are not making expected progress are picked up through our termly pupil progress meetings with the class teacher and Head/Deputy Head teacher. A discussion takes place concerning why individual children may be experiencing difficulties and what further support can be given to help them. We Assess – Plan – Do – Review What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All our staff are trained to make ‘reasonable adjustments’ according to the needs and differing abilities of children in their class. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim for all pupils to be included in our curriculum and will provide the necessary support to ensure that this is successful. name: Rachael Hill
description: Based in Wooburn Green. Provide wrap around care for St Paul's school and Juniper Hill school. Welcome to Rachael’s Childcare. Currently have vacancies for immediate start and September 2026 Funded places available for 0-5 years and I accept tax free childcare and childcare vouchers. Recent Ofsted inspection May 2025: I’m a reliable and diligent OFSTED registered childminder of over 20 years’ experience based in Wooburn Green, within easy access of the M40 motorway and both Beaconsfield and Bourne End train stations. I live with my husband Jonathan, who works as my assistant, my grown up son and daughter. We also have a small, and very friendly, Lhasa Apso dog. My husband and I pride ourselves in providing a safe and happy family home environment, where the children we care for are valued both as individuals, and as part of our welcoming group. Children receive one-on-one attention to ensure that their individual needs are met, and that they feel at home at all times. local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes and play, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Understanding Autism & ADHD How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with us. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. Although I live in a flat, the building has a lift and wide corridors. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ sheet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for

local_offer: Our aims are: To provide an environment in which all children, including those with SEND are supported to reach their full potential. To support parents and children with SEND. To ensure that all necessary information is recorded and children's needs are made known to all who are likely to support them within the nursery. To follow the SEND code of practice. To liaise with outside agencies to ensure all children receive the best support possible.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have a member of staff that has attended basic Makaton training, which helps to support children to communicate and use these both within the setting and at home. We welcome outside agencies such as speech and language and Buckinghamshire Early Years Services to support the development of both children and the setting. We also have another nursery with which we work closely with and share our experiences and tools to support children in our care. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Kayleigh Braginton is completing her SENCO training and holds a level 3 in early years. Another member of staff is due to attend the training in the Autumn term to ensure support is available throughout the setting to all staff and children. Other staff have attended Buckinghamshire training to further their knowledge with the APDR cycle and the support they can apply for to help children with SEND. Many of the staff within the nursery have completed an Autism Awareness course. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We build parent / practitioner relationships during handovers at the beginning and end of each day, and through the induction period prior to childrens start dates. Each child is assigned a key person who families can build strong relationships with and feel at ease to discuss their child's development. We host parent consultations each term and have an open door policy, where parents can speak to their child's key person at any time. We encourage parents to come for the first initial settling session so we get a holistic view of each child. We encourage parents to upload observations from home to support us with our planning to ensure it is based around individuals interests and needs. Plans, next steps and APDR's are shared with parents. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We complete relevant assessments for all children within the setting including 2 year checks, transition paperwork between rooms and transitional reports when children leave the setting to start school / other settings. Each child's APDR is reviewed with parents input and then shared with them once in place. Observations specific to the targets on an APDR and any small steps of progress are shared via FAMLY and also at a hand over at the end of each session. Where requested a communication book is in place to support the home and nursery consistency. If we have a concern regarding the needs of an individual child, staff will communicate with the SENCo who will work with the key person to support the child and their family on next steps of support. It is also known as an APDR (Access, Plan, Do, Review) document to evidence support that is being put in place. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There is wheelchair access to the pre-school room and accessible toilet. There are external paths to access external doors. Internally there are steps which link the younger rooms to the toilet area. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When children move to each room within the setting a transition report is completed and shared from the previous key person to the new key person, and the parents via FAMLY. A meeting with the family and the new key person is held to ensure a new relationship can be formed and all relevant information can be shared prior to starting settles into the new room. When children move from our setting to school, we welcome teachers to come in and observe them and communicate with us. We also visit the local school where possible to aid the transition. We encourage parents to allow us to share information regarding development. We complete a transition report to go to their new teachers, either via FAMLY or a report template sent by the new setting. When children move to another setting we welcome their practitioners to approach us and share information, we also complete a transition report for their new setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will have 2 SENco' s to ensure both sides of the nursery are supported fully. More staff will attend any relevant training to support the children in our care as and when needed.

organisation: The RAF Families Federation The RAF Families Federation represents the views and concerns of RAF regular and reserve personnel, single and married and their family members on the issues that affect them as part of an RAF family. Whether you are regular or reserve, a spouse, a partner, a parent, a grandparent, a child or a sibling of a member of the RAF, we are here to act on your behalf. We are an independent organisation and operate entirely outside the RAF chain of command so we can always promise an independent and confidential service. By gathering evidence we put your views and concerns in front of the people who can make a difference, such as senior RAF and MoD staffs and Ministers. local_offer: The Pre-School is on one level including the outside area, with three entrance doors two of which are suitable for wheelchair access. Parents and carers are encouraged to visit the setting with their child to discuss their child's needs and any additional support which may be required, prior to the child's start date. Subsequent visits are an ideal opportunity to meet the child's allocated key worker and the staff team, whilst discussing any concerns or needs that they may have.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have two pre-school SENCO’s (Special Educational Needs Co-Ordinator’s) that have been trained through the local authority to support the Key Person, child and families to ensure that the child’s individual needs are met. Your child’s Key Person will work with you and your child to ensure a good relationship is formed and that knowledge concerning your child and their development can be shared. Our SENCO’s are Caron Rhodes and Dawn Drummond both attend regular Buckinghamshire Council SENCO Liaison Groups and training courses. All staff have access to a range of online training courses to ensure that the team are kept up to date with the latest information to ensure that they offer the best support to our SEND families. The setting has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor. We actively encourage visits from all professionals involved with the child provide a continuity of care and foster a relationship of joint professional respect. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Caron Rhodes - SENCO Manager EY SENCO Training Inclusion Training SEND Supporting children with SEND in the EY Supporting Early Language Development SEND Code of Practice Termly SEND Liaison Meetings Dawn Drummond - SENCO Deputy Manager EY SENCO Training Equality and Inclusion in the EY SEND Reforms Makaton Foundation Training Supporting Early Language Development Termly SEND Liaison Meetings Ongoing All Staff Early Years Practitioners SEND Code of Practice Equality and Inclusion in Early Years Settings Special Educational Needs and Disability Supporting Children with SEND in the Early Years Supporting Early Language Development How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are valued partners in our pre-school and are welcomed in on regular occasions to see pre-school life in action and share their skills and knowledge (festivals, themed events, fundraising events). Parents and selected relatives have access 24 hours a day to their child’s online learning journal and are actively encouraged to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents are invited to attend termly progress meetings with their child’s key worker and can request additional meetings with their child’s Key Person at any time to discuss any concerns or worries. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The manner in which parents and carers are supported by the staff and encouraged to be active members in the life of pre-School are the same for every family. In addition to this, parents of children with SEND are invited and encouraged to attend regular meetings at the Pre-School with all outside agencies involved with the child. Our excellent staff – child ratios, permit both the SENCO and the child’s Key worker to attend meetings off site with outside agencies. These meeting vary in frequency depending on the child’s needs and the discretion of the agencies involved. We also offer updates through email or phone calls if this is more convenient. The SENCO team regularly monitor the short term outcomes for children with SEND and invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting is on one level including the outside area, with three entrance doors - two of which are suitable for wheelchair access, the third requiring a shallow ramp to access the patio. There is an accessible bathroom. The staff use foundation Makaton to aid communication with all. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? To ensure that the transition from or to another childcare provider is as smooth and un-stressful as possible for both the child and their carers, we liaise with fellow providers exchanging records and essential information. Pre-start visits are encouraged to enable both the child and parents to familiarise themselves with both the setting and the staff team. Our relationships with other local providers are good, enhanced by SENCO liaison groups and training courses. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As a team we constantly review and renew our SEND resources keeping in mind the needs of the children who are currently attending the setting and those who are on our waiting list. The staff team keep up to date with changes to SEND policies and thinking by attending training courses and liaising with outside agencies.

description: Rainbow Trust Children’s Charity supports seriously ill children and their families in the family home and local community. Families who have a child or young person up to the age of 18 with a life-threatening or terminal condition (for example cancer, some neurological conditions, babies in neonatal intensive care) are eligible and referrals can come from any source. We enable families to manage everyday life while caring for a sick child and to make the most of time together; providing expert, practical, and emotional support through a Family Support Worker. Families have complete choice about the type of support they receive - wherever and whenever they need it. Rainbow Trust’s support can include short breaks from caring, family activity days, drop-in groups, support with hospital visits, including transport to and from appointments, support for siblings and bereavement support. To find out more about the services available in your area, please contact us. Support is generally available from Monday to Friday between 8am and 6pm, frequency and duration depending on family choice and needs. Rainbow Trust operates a 24-hour service for families in crisis, which includes a 24-hour dedicated on-call number, and the possibility of extended hours of family support during weekdays and weekends.

Families have told us that there are five key areas where we make the biggest difference in their lives: We improve the family’s ability to manage stress; We maintain parents’ /carers’ stability and confidence; We enable families to spend quality time together; We improve the quality of children and young people’s lives; We enable families to keep communicating through loss and bereavement.
