local_offer: Our nursery aims to provide the best inclusive care and education for all children under the age of five. This includes any child who may require additional services or help to reach their full potential and improved outcomes. We will work with external support systems as well as utilising our well-trained staff to help all children to develop.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We liaise with the Buckinghamshire Council Early Years Service and follow their support and advice, as well as the LA SEN team. We speak with speech and language therapists, health visitors and outside agencies such as occupational therapists who give us extra support should we need it. In the past, we have sought advice from a parent who is a trained speech and language therapist. Most of our practitioners have received Speech and Language training. All of our team use basic Makaton. We also have two other nurseries, with which we work closely and share our experiences and tools to support children in our care. We have one Level 3 Trained Sendco What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Early Bird Autism Training – Spring Term 2020 – Deb Prentice Sign language – March 2020 - All staff SENCO training - 4 June 2021 - Debs Prentice SENCO Training – 11 June 2018 - Lisa Hubbard CACHE Level 3, supporting children and young people’s speech, language and communication – 09 May 2014 – Lisa Hubbard Level 3 Senco Award - May 2023 Debs Prentice Speech and Language training - Nov 2021 - All Staff Deputy Senco Training - March 2022 - Emma Fellows How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to offer a setting that is welcoming and inclusive to all families, so they feel able to approach us regarding their child’s development. We have excellent parent partnerships. Each day a member of familiar staff will give each family a handover. This handover will be tailored to each family, as we know some would rather know about their day rather than food and sleep. As we get to know you, staff will learn what is important to you as a parent and ensure the feedback reflects this. Children will receive a baseline assessment, once their child is settled with us and this forms the basis of their learning journey with us. We share summative assessments with our parents and hold an informal parent’s evening. This allows you to discuss your child’s development with their key person. We use the Famly app as an observation system to compile your child’s learning journey. You as parents are able to add observations from home and this then enables us to extend this learning at nursery. Parents can comment on a member of staff’s observation and read reports when they are published. We send out an annual questionnaire to all parents to ensure we are listening to their views and are offering a service that meets their needs. When parents request a meeting we aim to meet with them as soon as possible. Parents are given the email address of their room leader to ensure they have a way of communicating with them and sharing messages. We hold events, enabling parents to become more involved in nursery life, such as sports day, Mother's day and Father's day teas, stay and play sessions, a childrens library service and charity fundraising events throughout the year. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We complete a basline and two-year progress checks which are then shared via Famly and at parents evening. When a child moves onto another setting, or to another room within the nursery, we compile transition reports to ensure they can be supported on the next step of their learning journey. At our termly parent’s meetings, parents can speak with their child’s key person regarding their development and time at nursery. We offer an open-door policy and aim to make ourselves available for informal opportunities at the families request. We complete progress summaries – this is shared via Famly and explained to parents prior to sending it out. Our SENCO supports each key person to complete assess, plan, do review and SEN support plans, these are shared with families and are compiled with parents, alongside other professionals reports. We will seek advice from other professionals to best support each child whilst we may be awaiting referrals or reports. We also use various tools that are recommended by our local authority, we share these resources with families and staff caring for the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have a ramp to the front door, the children’s toilets are at ground level and do not require steps to access them. The baby room is upstairs in the setting, along with the babies sleep room. All outside opportunities are accessible for all children and families, we use open farmland, a small meadow and garden space directly outside the front door. Our Piglets and Roosters rooms have free flow access to the outdoor area, every day. We have reading and quiet areas within each room for children to use if they wish to, these have soft furnishings to make them cosy and inviting. We have access to the farmland so have the opportunity to explore many different sensory opportunities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that leaving your child for the first time can be a big decision and can be very emotional. We always reassure parents with telephone calls and photos when they collect. We also encourage parents to call during the settling sessions and their first day to put their minds at rest. We offer settling in sessions to each family, tailored to each child's individual needs, so they can all meet the staff within the room and complete the relevant paperwork to support their child’s journey with us. We offer a welcome leaflet which gives them an idea of what we offer and expectations within that specific room. We make notes on their all about me forms if parents tell us anything which we feel is relevant. We tailor the settling in sessions to each individual child, with flexibility on start dates should they need longer to settle. We offer three initial sessions and for babies, we offer more to fit with their routine. If a child transitions from another setting we seek parental permission to contact this setting and discuss their development, to ensure we find out all information regarding the child and their family. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We use reflection tools to ensure we are offering children, staff and their families the support they need. These are available for each room on request. Our staff will attend further training, where a need is identified.

description: Mixed-gender university technical college in Reading specialising in Engineering and Computer Science for 14 to 19-year-olds. Life as a student at UTC Reading will be unlike any school experience you’ve ever had before. The UTC specialises in Engineering and Computer Science, alongside a broad and balanced curriculum and benefits from the support of local and national employers and leading universities. Using the latest technology, you will learn through projects and practical activities. Teaching staff run lessons and seminars to introduce new topics and are always on hand to offer support in our independent learning spaces. You’ll also work closely with our industry partners on projects and challenges they set. Wednesday and Friday afternoons will give you a break from your studies as you get involved in creative or sporting enrichment activities. You won’t need to take any work home with you, as our long day means that you have time to complete it at the UTC. At UTC Reading you can study for a range of GCSEs, BTECs and A-Levels. Find out more about studying in Year 10 or Post 16. You don’t need to pass any tests or pay any fees to join UTC Reading in Year 10. If you’re interested in becoming a student at UTC Reading, then why not come along to one of our open events?

local_offer: Special Educational Needs Aspire is committed to providing outstanding SEN Provision to meet the needs of all students. When students first attend they are assessed as part of their induction to enable staff to identify and understand their strengths and needs for support. The resulting information is used to plan the most appropriate programme and support package so as to ensure students’ learning and progress. Aspire encourages parents who have concerns or queries about a student’s learning difficulties to contact the Special Educational Needs Coordinator. As all our students are taught in small groups, students receive close monitoring and support to ensure their needs are met. Exam access arrangements are made for students when appropriate, for instance when a student has a reading or writing difficulty. If students need some additional, ongoing support above what they receive in the classroom it may be that they have some form of SEND. There are 4 areas of SEND: Cognition and Learning: for instance, perhaps a student has Dyslexia or struggles to process information at the same speed as their peers. Sensory and Physical: a student may have a visual impairment or Cerebal Palsy. Communication and Interaction: An example of this may be a speech and language delay or problems with social interaction. Social, Emotional and Mental Health: A student may have this as their primary SEND, such as clinical depression or it may be a secondary SEND as a result of other learning differences such as ADHD or ASD. https://www.aspireap.org.uk/SEN-at-Aspire/SEND-at-Aspire/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? name: The Recreation Ground (Wingrave)
description: The Recreation Ground is bounded on the north by Church Street, on the west mostly by the 19th Century Rothschild Cottages, the south by Moat Lane which has a number of Rothschild Cottages. On the eastern side of the Recreation Ground it is bounded by Moat Lane. The Recreation Ground is used for many sports events, including Football matches, Bowls and Croquet. The area already has protected status and is historically significant to the village as it is part of the Rothschild legacy from the 19th Century. The Recreation Ground is 18,224 sq metres and is clearly in character with the surrounding 19th Century Rothschild Cottages. The site is also home to Wingrave Playground, a newly installed area (2020) with a range of equipment for children up to the age of 12.
organisation: Wingrave Parish Council The Knolls is a south-west facing steeply sloping field on the northwest side of Church Street just past Cobblers Wick. The field is used to graze a number of ponies but it has considerable recreational and amenity value to the village. For over thirty years it has been the location of the village bonfire and firework display to celebrate Guy Fawkes. In winter it has been used for more than living memory as the village tobogganing and sledging field as it has the most appropriate slope for such activities in the village. The field has spectacular far-reaching panoramic views over the Vale of Aylesbury to the Chilterns and on towards Chinnor. For all these reasons the field has considerable green space and amenity to the village. The Knolls is 1.4 hectares and is in character with the adjacent Church Street and the bounding agricultural land. info@wwrpc.org.uk http://wingravewithrowshamparishcouncil.org.uk/contact-details/

name: Red Kite Housing
description: Red Kite is a tenant-led, not for profit, charitable housing association. We own and manage more than 6,700 homes in the Wycombe District. We're a social landlord who provide homes and services to our customers. On the surface, that might be true, but in reality we do so much more. We put roofs over heads, provide services like repairs and maintenance, and work with our customers to make sure they get the best possible service. We are registered with the Homes and Communities Agency (HCA) who monitor and regulate what we do to make sure that we meet the standards for managing and maintaining homes. Buckinghamshire Council will also be monitoring what we do. Our tenants and leaseholders are our customers and have an important role in making sure that we keep to the promises that were made in the Housing transfer Offer Document. As a stock transfer from the local District Council in 2011, we own and manage more than 6,700 homes in the Wycombe District. These are mainly on estates in the urban centres of High Wycombe, Princes Risborough, and Marlow, with others on estates in rural areas such as Lane End, Stokenchurch, and Bourne End.

local_offer: Special Educational Needs Aspire is committed to providing outstanding SEN Provision to meet the needs of all students. When students first attend they are assessed as part of their induction to enable staff to identify and understand their strengths and needs for support. The resulting information is used to plan the most appropriate programme and support package so as to ensure students’ learning and progress. Aspire encourages parents who have concerns or queries about a student’s learning difficulties to contact the Special Educational Needs Coordinator. As all our students are taught in small groups, students receive close monitoring and support to ensure their needs are met. Exam access arrangements are made for students when appropriate, for instance when a student has a reading or writing difficulty. If students need some additional, ongoing support above what they receive in the classroom it may be that they have some form of SEND. There are 4 areas of SEND: Cognition and Learning: for instance, perhaps a student has Dyslexia or struggles to process information at the same speed as their peers. Sensory and Physical: a student may have a visual impairment or Cerebral Palsy. Communication and Interaction: An example of this may be a speech and language delay or problems with social interaction. Social, Emotional and Mental Health: A student may have this as their primary SEND, such as clinical depression or it may be a secondary SEND as a result of other learning differences such as ADHD or ASD. https://www.aspireap.org.uk/SEN-at-Aspire/SEND-at-Aspire/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? description: Reflexology, Maternity Reflexology and Indian Head, Back, Neck and Shoulder Massage. Reflexology is a non-invasive holistic treatment with a number of health benefits. These range from stress and tension release; digestive assistance with conditions such as Constipation and IBS; Circulatory stimulation; mobility improvement particularly if the hips/back are a concern; improvement in sleeping patterns and importantly a lovely treatment if you want relaxation. Gift vouchers also available to pamper someone who deserves some TLC or perfect for Birthdays, Christmas, Valentines, Mothering Sunday, and Fathers Day. I am a Reflexologist who also has a Maternity Reflexology Practitioner Diploma. This covers pre-conception (if there are difficulties becoming pregnant), pregnancy, labour and the postnatal period. Maternity Reflexology is safe for mother and baby after 14 weeks of pregnancy. In addition to Reflexology, I now also offer Indian Head, Back, Neck and Shoulder Massage. This alternative holistic therapy is ideal if you suffer with tension in these areas as it can lead to headaches; pain and discomfort and sleep difficulties due to tension. This treatment also stimulates the circulation and lymphatic system; aids toxin elimination and stimulates hair growth. I have a Psychology Degree with professional qualifications having worked as a Midwife, Health Visitor therefore, I understand the importance of the relationship between mind and body. Additionally, I have taught Baby Massage (achieving a Baby Massage instructor Diploma) as I feel it is a beneficial way to aid parent and child bonding. I teach groups of up to 8. I am a mobile practitioner who visits you in the comfort of your own home and strives to provide ultimate relaxation.

description: Our Refresher courses revisit all the important information you learned from your previous baby. Everyone is welcome, you don't need to have had previous experience of an antenatal course to attend. You’ll reflect and build on your past labour experiences, and prepare for the birth you want. With every new baby, your family life changes forever. Learn about the impact of introducing your baby to your older children, sibling rivalry and how your relationship with your partner can change. You will be able to address any feeding challenges you might have had before, and get evidence-based advice and non-judgmental support. Courses include dedicated time to discuss this, with support and information however you decide to feed your baby. The courses are a great way to meet other local parents whose babies will be around the same age as yours. We keep classes small and welcoming, with plenty of time to chat and get to know each other.

name: Refugee Support | British Red Cross
description: Refugee Support (British Red Cross). The British Red Cross helps refugees, asylum seekers and vulnerable migrants living in the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, and Oxfordshire areas become familiar with their local area and access essential services. We provide free, impartial, and confidential advice including practical help, advice, information, and emotional support. How do we help people? In an emergency, the British Red Cross supports refugees, asylum seekers, and vulnerable migrants with: food parcels, toiletries, essential clothing, sleeping bags, small cash hardship payments, and travel costs to essential legal, Home Office, and health appointments. We can also provide you with: asylum support, legal advice, social services, welfare benefits advice, family reunion travel assistance, health services, housing and homelessness advice, and education and employment services. We can also signpost and refer to other specialist help organisations, provide you with information about local, cultural, faith, and community groups, refer you to other Red Cross services, including our International Family Tracing service if you have lost contact with a relative and help you to access volunteering opportunities within the Red Cross and your local community. International Family Tracing Service: The British Red Cross helps people find missing relatives abroad through international family tracing service if they have been separated by war, natural disaster or migration. How can you get help to contact your family? We may be able to help individuals in the UK find missing family, send a message to family members and get a certificate of detention for people who have been imprisoned. This is a free and confidential service to help families reconnect. We may be able to help in other circumstances where there is a humanitarian need. For example, if you have suddenly lost contact with a relative in the UK or abroad.
organisation: British Red Cross The British Red Cross helps people in crisis, whoever and wherever they are. We are part of a global voluntary network, responding to conflicts, natural disasters and individual emergencies. We help vulnerable people in the UK and abroad prepare for, withstand and recover from emergencies in their own communities. "It doesn’t matter whether it’s a flood or loneliness. When crisis strikes, there’s always an impact – whatever the scale. And we refuse to ignore it." contactus@redcross.org.uk https://www.redcross.org.uk/

local_offer: Special Educational Needs Aspire is committed to providing outstanding SEN Provision to meet the needs of all students. When students first attend they are assessed as part of their induction to enable staff to identify and understand their strengths and needs for support. The resulting information is used to plan the most appropriate programme and support package so as to ensure students’ learning and progress. Aspire encourages parents who have concerns or queries about a student’s learning difficulties to contact the Special Educational Needs Coordinator. As all our students are taught in small groups, students receive close monitoring and support to ensure their needs are met. Exam access arrangements are made for students when appropriate, for instance when a student has a reading or writing difficulty. If students need some additional, ongoing support above what they receive in the classroom it may be that they have some form of SEND. There are 4 areas of SEND: Cognition and Learning: for instance, perhaps a student has Dyslexia or struggles to process information at the same speed as their peers. Sensory and Physical: a student may have a visual impairment or Cerebal Palsy. Communication and Interaction: An example of this may be a speech and language delay or problems with social interaction. Social, Emotional and Mental Health: A student may have this as their primary SEND, such as clinical depression or it may be a secondary SEND as a result of other learning differences such as ADHD or ASD. https://www.aspireap.org.uk/SEN-at-Aspire/SEND-at-Aspire/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? name: Open Gardens
description: We continue to welcome you to Lindengate, where nature breathes new life into anyone looking for a little support with their wellbeing. Our Open Gardens sessions are open to all and allow people to explore our unique, 6 acre garden and nature reserve. Free entry to wander through our gardens, discovering, learning, relaxing and connecting with nature. Drop in and support your wellbeing through the power of nature. At Lindengate, we believe the natural environment contributes to improving wellbeing through nature, so why not arrange your next gathering at Lindengate, whether for a business team meeting, with a group of friends, or by yourself with a good book. Bring a hot drink and take time to re-connect, surrounded by the sights and sounds of nature. Get in touch to book ahead, if coming with a larger group. Please refer to our Website for details of opening times for our gardens. Please email or call us if your require more information.
organisation: Lindengate Our free drop-in support sessions are for anyone who may be struggling with their wellbeing or mental health. Set on a 5-acre site, our therapeutic gardens and wildlife haven are accessible to anyone who needs space and time to "be". Finding time to give yourself space can be difficult in the best of weather, but in Winter, the challenge becomes even greater. There are many benefits to spending just a few minutes a day outdoors. Here are a few of them: 15 minutes outdoors every day can improve both our moods and our physical health, leading to reduced stress and increased self-esteem Builds our immune system, as the cold weather actually kills off bacteria. With the current restrictions in place, we can meet up with a friend, which will improve our mental wellbeing, through social interaction. We have plenty of sheltered areas dotted about to meet with a friend or family member for a chat or to bring a book and enjoy the peace, amongst the wildlife. charlie.hughes@lindengate.org.uk http://www.lindengate.org.uk

name: Restore Hope
description: Restore Hope Latimer is a family-focused Christian charity based at Latimer Park. A special space in the countryside, set in the heart of the Chess Valley, just outside Amersham and Chesham has been operating since 2002 with a proven record of bringing change and help to children and families in need of support. We believe in the value of healthy, happy, and stable families. We also believe that no matter how bad a situation may seem there is always hope. Our vision is that every struggling family in the Chilterns finds help and hope for the future. We continually look to adapt and improve our services to meet local needs. We aim to inspire, train and equip children, young people and families to find hope through a wide range of family support, fun-filled activities and volunteer opportunities. Since the pandemic, we have been offering a food support programme called FoodLife, which offers fortnightly fruit and vegetable boxes to local families in need. This requires families to meet certain criteria and get an external referral. Please contact us for more information. This site is not open to the general public. Please see our separate activity and events postings for opening times and any costs.

A special space in the countryside set in the heart of the Chilterns, just outside Amersham and Chesham and has been operating since 2002 and has a proven record of bringing change and help to people in need. We believe in the value of healthy, happy and stable families. We also believe that no matter how bad a situation may seem there is always hope. Our vision is therefore that every struggling family in the Chilterns finds help and hope for the future. This is clearly a big aim and one that requires us to continually increase our influence, effectiveness and reputation. We aim to achieve our vision by advancing and developing the programmes that we offer and continually looking for ways to engage with those most in need. We operate a clear strategy, with deliberate focus and dogged determination. We empower and equip key volunteers to lead various elements of our work, and support a motivated core staff team. RHL seeks to make best use of the fantastic facilities that Latimer Park offers and, where appropriate, grows into other spaces in the community to offer easy access to our programmes and to further develop the reputation of the charity. naomi.meech@restorehopelatimer.org http://www.restorehopelatimer.org

local_offer: Special Educational Needs Aspire is committed to providing outstanding SEN Provision to meet the needs of all students. When students first attend they are assessed as part of their induction to enable staff to identify and understand their strengths and needs for support. The resulting information is used to plan the most appropriate programme and support package so as to ensure students’ learning and progress. Aspire encourages parents who have concerns or queries about a student’s learning difficulties to contact the Special Educational Needs Coordinator. As all our students are taught in small groups, students receive close monitoring and support to ensure their needs are met. Exam access arrangements are made for students when appropriate, for instance when a student has a reading or writing difficulty. If students need some additional, ongoing support above what they receive in the classroom it may be that they have some form of SEND. There are 4 areas of SEND: Cognition and Learning: for instance, perhaps a student has Dyslexia or struggles to process information at the same speed as their peers. Sensory and Physical: a student may have a visual impairment or Cerebal Palsy. Communication and Interaction: An example of this may be a speech and language delay or problems with social interaction. Social, Emotional and Mental Health: A student may have this as their primary SEND, such as clinical depression or it may be a secondary SEND as a result of other learning differences such as ADHD or ASD. https://www.aspireap.org.uk/SEN-at-Aspire/SEND-at-Aspire/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? description: I have been a childminder since 2006. I provide a warm, safe, friendly, home environment with a family atmosphere where children feel valued, and can play, learn and develop. Children will receive a lot of individual attention whilst enjoying interacting with others. I appreciate that parents are the most important people in a Child's life and therefore consult with parents on all aspects of their Child's care. I have a playroom (Full of toys, games and so on), kitchen and dining room which is open plan, I also have a sitting room and an enclosed big garden. I have my car with full road tax, up to date service, insurance and RAC cover. We are out most mornings attending farms, libraries, parks, walks, singing groups, gymnastics, Ashridge, seeing friends, places of interest and many more. In the afternoon we do quiet time or nap time, storytime, games, puzzles, outdoor toys, role play, writing, colouring, painting, sticking, free play and many more. Any of my parents are willing to give a reference should you require one or talk to you on the telephone. Some things Ofsted said about me on my last inspection: "The childminder is passionate about her work with children and has a clear vision for the future such as developing knowledge and skills. For example, she is booked onto purposeful courses to support the outcomes for children". Positive comments from parents include "my child thoroughly enjoys it" and "it is a home-from-home environment". Offer funding for children.

description: I have been a childminder since 2006. I provide a warm, safe, friendly, home environment with a family atmosphere where children feel valued, and can play, learn and develop. Children will receive a lot of individual attention whilst enjoying interacting with others. I appreciate that parents are the most important people in a Child's life and therefore consult with parents on all aspects of their Child's care. I have a playroom (Full of toys, games and so on), kitchen and dining room which is open plan, I also have a sitting room and an enclosed big garden. description: Rhyming Multisensory Stories - Storytelling Through the Senses. Free, fully resourced, step-by-step multisensory stories, training videos and resources aimed at connecting individuals with special educational needs and disabilities aged 3 to 19, Early Years, Primary and Speech and Language students to literature, culture, history, poetry and topic in a fun and engaging way. The stories are fully resourced, and their step-by-step format make them accessible to teaching professionals, parents, carers, families and anyone with an interest in storytelling through the senses. Visit the blog page to learn how to make sensory bags, bins, sensory tents, a free monthly teaching activities calendar and more. I also offer 'Multisensory Storytelling and Engagement Through Sensory Activities' workshop via Zoom tailored to your needs Your questions, queries, comments, and feedback are always welcome.
organisation: Rhyming Multisensory Stories | Storytelling Through the Senses Free, fully resourced, step by step multi-sensory stories and poems for parents, carers, teaching and childcare professionals, librarians and storytellers and anyone with an interest in storytelling through the senses. The website is full of sensory ideas, inspiration and strategies. There is a story library of free, fully resourced, step-by-step multisensory stories aimed at helping individuals age 3 to 19 with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities to build communication skills and connect to literacy, culture and topic in a way that is meaningful to their lives. Multisensory stories tell a story using props to back up the spoken word. The props are low budget items found around the home and garden. The resources are free and are in word.doc and eBook format and include Speech and Language visual support, themed sensory extension activities and 'How to tell a multisensory story guide' and much more! The stories and poems are aimed at 3 to 19-year-olds and include: 'A Different Day' helping individuals with SEN understand the Covid-19 Pandemic 'Washing Hands' Helping individuals with SEN with their hand hygiene during the Covid-19 pandemic 'A Train Ride Through India' A sensory exploration of the Indian culture 'The Three Little Pigs' Join the pigs on a sensory adventure 'The Haircut' Helping individuals overcome barriers to their personal grooming and hair care 'The Dentist' - Helping individuals overcome barriers to their dental hygiene 'The Weather' A sensory exploration The website is packed with sensory ideas and inspiration and to join keepup with the lastest news there is a blog. The activities in the stories promote communication and independence skills and link to areas of the EYFS and National Curriculum.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? There are many benefits to multisensory storytelling. Stories create a bond between the storyteller and the story explorer enhancing and enriching experiences. The stories connect the individual to literature, culture, history and topic in a fun, engaging and motivating way. They form an excellent base on which to scaffold learning, providing opportunities for the individuals to work towards personal learning goals and targets ​ The activities in the stories are designed to promote: Communication Skills: Eye contact, listening, shared attention and language development. Self-confidence & Well-being: Trying out new ideas and skills, practicing self-care, independence and enjoying achievement. Self-awareness: Asking for 'help', 'again' and 'more'. Opportunities to explore cause and effect and to build anticipation skills. Physical Development: Fine & gross motor skills.) Understanding of the environment and the world around us. Engagement in scientific experimentation and mathematical concepts. Development of social and Emotional Skills: Turn-taking, sharing and teamwork. The blog is packed with ideas and information. local_offer: The Risborough Family Hub offers universal and specialised support to families in the local area. We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. The Risborough Children’s Hub can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our provision provides support services for all families with children aged 0 to 19 years and up to 25 years for those with a SEND. Our aims are to improve parenting, health and children’s development and to provide a safe and stimulating environment for children, young people and their families to flourish, develop and learn. Parents provided with good information so they can make decisions, which will have a significant effect on their children’s life chances. Parents to know, what support and services are available to help them bring up their children, and how to access them. Families signposted into support as appropriate feel confident to provide good life chance for their children. Children to develop social skills in preparation for starting pre-school, nursery or school. Children to enjoy a variety of fun activities and play and learn through this participation. Parents to feel confident in parenting and picking up parenting skills and support through attendance. Personal, Social and Emotional Development. Physical development. Communication and Language Development. Outreach support, action plan to specifically help the family with individual needs. Emotional and practical support from Outreach Worker. Safeguarding First Aid Early Language Development Programme Hey Programme (Healthy Eating in Young Children) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? name: The Rise School
description: Mixed-gender special school in Feltham, Middlesex for 4 to 19-year-olds. The Rise School is registered with the Department for Education as SEND Free School and opened in September 2014. The Rise School is for pupils between 4 to 18 years old who can access an age-appropriate curriculum but find it difficult to thrive in a mainstream environment. They are educated in small classes of 8 pupils with additional support from Teaching and Learning Assistants. Our curriculum is carefully designed to take into consideration their holistic development. Two pillars underpin all that we do at The Rise: the academic and social progress of our pupils. The curriculum is divided into nine zones, each of which contributes to the development of the key skills (academic and personal) to be successful: - Social Curriculum/Personal Development - English/Literacy - Maths/Numeracy - Science - History/Topic - Computing - Vocational - Arts - Body Our social curriculum is a fourth “core” subject and is essential for the well-rounded development and wellbeing for our young people and consists of PSHE and Citizenship, Wellbeing and Yoga lessons. Pupils work towards a range of qualifications at KS4 which include: - Functional Maths - GCSE Maths - IGCSE English - Entry Level Science - GCSE Science - BTEC Level 2 Food Tech - iMedia Level 2 - City and Guilds Level 1 Construction.? - Duke of Edinburgh Learning also takes place outside of the classroom with a large number of trips – both in the community and into wider London.

A number of picnic tables and benches have been placed in the grass, close to the river, surrounded by magnificent Poplar trees. The Marlow Rugby Club playing fields are to be found behind the trees. The Thames footpath passes through the site, an unmade track leading to Bourne End downstream and Marlow town upstream.

name: Road Farm Countryways CIC
description: Countryways CIC offers care farming, educational visits, animal-based activities, and community events for people of all ages and abilities. Through meaningful involvement in the life of a working Chilterns farm, participants can develop confidence, practical skills, social connections, and improved wellbeing in a safe and supportive outdoor environment. Surrounded by open skies, green fields, hedgerows, and wildlife, the farm provides a rich sensory experience. The sounds of animals, birdsong, and rustling trees, alongside natural textures, sights, and smells, create opportunities for exploration, learning, and engagement for people with a wide range of needs and abilities. Research by the Sensory Trust and Natural England highlights that many people are becoming increasingly disconnected from the countryside, nature, and food production. Farm-based experiences can help reconnect people with the natural world, support physical and mental wellbeing, and provide valuable opportunities for hands-on learning beyond the traditional classroom. Whether attending a care farming session, educational visit, family event, or community activity, visitors are welcomed to discover new skills, build confidence, improve health and wellbeing, and experience the benefits of nature, animals, and farming in the heart of the Chilterns.

local_offer: For Care Farming, people facing various challenges may join us for a whole or part day (10am to 3pm) to be involved in various activities around the farm. This may involve working with the animals and countryside, using tools, cooking, learning new skills like wood-work, as well as growing independence. If you’re interested in attending (or responsible for someone who is), please contact us or fill in an initial enquiry form. We're developing a special programme of response for the impact of Coronavirus. Health and safety are important to us: we have numerous written policies which we review and adhere to; staff and volunteers are DBS checked and we avoid one to one settings as far as is possible.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our service meets the needs of those who need space, open air, personal time without crowds. Farm Helpers can show care for other living things and grow in their independence through learning life skills. We provide a guided, unpressurised environment with a natural stimulus to learn and grow in well-being. The Outcomes we anticipate are increased calmness, confidence to do something, independence, better physical health through activity and being in fresh air, increased creativity and knowledge. There are many more happiness, gladness and anticipation to attend a regular day, providing focus that helps with other routine elsewhere. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Training through CEVAS (Countryside Educational Visits Accreditation Scheme) Accreditation; various volunteers hold teaching qualifications; we require support workers or school staff to be present with most individuals. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Verbal communication, some widget symbols; whichever method of communication best suits the family. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We require a support worker to be present for those with Special Needs, either in the background or alongside, as appropriate, whether this is a relative or specific care staff; we provide all farm guidance and gentle leadership into activities here. We have excellent toilet facilities including adult disabled changing facility with hoist. We have an excellent all terrain manual wheelchair which visitors can transfer to if this helps. We encourage people to consider how this could help all ages in the family to get out and about together. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please do contact us by telephone or email. A simple referral form can be downloaded from our website and emailed. New Farm Helpers need to visit the farm first, helping us to decide how best we can work together for good. There is no charge for this first stage, but we do charge for future visits to help us remain sustainable as a service. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We have an amazing setting which our young people do not want to leave! Continually networking to try to find good ways forward. We would appreciate more volunteer help and funding to improve our delivery.

local_offer: At the Roald Dahl Museum and Story Centre we welcome all visitors and aim to do everything we can to make sure every visitor has a buzzwangling time. Getting around the site: The Museum and Shop are all fully wheel and pushchair accessible, as we are a step-free site. We have a manual wheelchair which you may borrow, though we do advise calling in advance to ensure it is available. We have two fully accessible toilets. Some rooms are located on the first floor, but there is a lift to this level. Carers receive free admission. D/deaf and hard of hearing: We have British Sign Language interpretation throughout the Museum via the Museum's Signly. Simply hold you phone up to the QR codes around the galleries to see sign language interpretation on-screen. We have a hearing loop, and transcripts of audiovisual presentations. Visually impaired: There are audio clips and sound effects played in the galleries and toilets. We have display information in audio. We have our Museum guide and Story Ideas Books in large print. Visitors with children: We have a baby change room as well as baby changing facilities for parents/carers in wheelchairs. There is a buggy store available. Neurodiversity We run a programme of SEND visits for schools and groups. We run SEND days for general visitors in the school holidays (see website for dates). Quieter times to visit are after 2.30pm Thursday to Sunday outside of the school holidays. You can borrow one of our free SEND Explorer Bags from the ticket desk. This includes sunglasses, ear defenders, baseball cap, Makaton cards, fidget toys, torch, magnifying glass, large photographs, Museum map, basic trail and emotions card. There’s a pop-up Quiet Space Kit available to use free of charge. This includes a pop-up tent, weighted blanket, ear defenders, Museum map and emotions card. Ask at the ticket desk. Customer care: We have emergency evacuation procedures for disabled visitors. We have two Evac+ chairs located on the first floor areas, with all Duty Officers being trained in their use. All staff have disability awareness training. Some staff have Next Generation Text training. Some staff have BSL training. local_offer: Robertswood School’s SEND provision At Robertswood School we aim to support all children to enable them to achieve their personal potential. Quality First teaching is at the heart of delivering a broad and balanced curriculum and we welcome children with Special Educational Needs as part of our inclusive approach. We have high expectations of our children and want them all to feel a valued part of our school community. We operate a ‘whole pupil, whole school’ approach to the management and support of pupils with Special Educational Needs. Our aim is to raise the aspirations and expectations of all children, including those with SEND. Robertswood School’s SEND policy We recognise that children may have special educational needs either throughout or at any time during their school career. We work within the guidance provided in the SEN Code of Practice, 2014. The Code recommends a ‘Graduated Approach’ to SEND involving a 4-stage cycle – Assess, Plan, Do, Review. Assess A pupil is identified as having SEND where their learning difficulty or disability calls for special educational provision, namely provision different from or additional to that normally available to pupils of the same age. At Robertswood School we aim to work in close partnership with parents and identify additional needs at the earliest point in order to improve the long-term outcomes for the child. Additional needs are identified through a variety of ways including: - Liaison with Early Years settings and previous schools, where appropriate. - Teacher concern that a child is performing below age related expectations and/or not making expected progress relative to - Concern over progress in areas of social or emotional need. - Parent/carer concern. - Medical diagnosis or identified disability under the Equality Act 2010. - Specialised assessments from external agencies and professionals. - Pupil view. Plan The purpose of identification is to work out what action the school needs to take to address these difficulties using well evidenced, targeted interventions. High quality teaching, differentiated for individual pupils, is the first step in responding to pupils who have SEND. Where progress continues to be less than expected, the teacher and the SENDCo, working together, identify the interventions required to secure better progress. These interventions are recorded on the child’s SEND Support Provision Map. Specialist services such as Speech and Language, Specialist Teaching and Occupational Therapy are consulted as appropriate. Parents are always involved in any decision to involve specialists. Do High quality teaching, differentiated for individual pupils, is the first step in responding to pupils with Special Educational Needs. We regularly invest in training our staff to improve the understanding and delivery of SEND Support. Examples of training for Teachers and Teaching Assistants includes using Shape Coding to support oral and written language, Autism Awareness, Attention Autism programme, Anxiety Awareness and Dyslexia. Interventions are usually delivered in small groups or one to one if more specialised support is needed. Outcomes may be curriculum related or may relate to wider issues such as developing positive social relationships or making a successful transition to a different phase of education. The SENDCo monitors the quality and effectiveness of SEND support and this is reviewed termly by the school’s Senior Leadership Team. Review SEND Support Provision Maps are formally reviewed three times a year and discussed with parents at parent consultations. However, monitoring provision is an active process and Provision Maps are reviewed at other times to reflect, for example, advice from specialists or the changing needs of the child. Provision for children in Early Years may be reviewed more frequently. Multi-agency Provision Plan meetings (MAPP) are held for children who receive significant external support. Children who have an Education and Health Care Plan also have an Annual Review. The Special Educational Needs register is maintained by the SENDCo and is kept under regular review. The SENDCo provides monitoring information to the school’s Senior Leadership Team and Governors on a termly basis. https://www.robertswoodschool.co.uk/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs&pid=38 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Robertswood School we aim to support all children to enable them to achieve their personal potential. Robertswood School’s approach to teaching pupils with SEND High quality teaching, differentiated for individual pupils, is the first step in responding to pupils who have or may have Special Educational Needs. Pupils with Special Educational Needs are included as fully as possible in the whole class environment. Sometimes it may be appropriate to withdraw a pupil for individual or small group support in order to acquire, reinforce or extend skills more effectively. Teachers are responsible and accountable for the progress and development of the pupils in their class, including where pupils access support from teaching assistants or specialist staff. The SENDCo provides professional guidance to colleagues and works closely with staff, parents and other agencies to ensure that pupils with Special Educational Needs receive appropriate support and high-quality teaching. The SENDCo has day to day responsibility for the operation of SEND policy and, with the Head Teacher and Governing body, determines the strategic development of SEND policy and provision. The social and emotional well-being of all pupils, including those with SEND, is a key priority at Robertswood School. To support this, all children have access to high-quality PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic) education, alongside a strong and responsive pastoral support system. The school actively encourages the participation of all pupils, including those with SEND, in extra-curricular activities, school clubs and educational visits, recognising the importance of wider school experiences in promoting confidence, independence and a sense of belonging. Children are also supported to take on positions of responsibility, such as Playground Leaders or Prefects, helping to foster leadership skills and self-esteem. Each week, pupils from every class are nominated for recognition as either a Skills Superhero or Star of the Week. These awards celebrate individual effort, achievement in learning, or commitment to the Essential Skills and Robertswood Star Values. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Appropriate Continued Professional Development is provided to staff in order to support the needs of SEND children within our school. Specialist expertise is obtained by the school by engaging professional advice as necessary. Training can take the form of child-specific training support or be of a wider SEND nature. Examples of recent training include: - Shape Coding to support oral and written language development. - Paediatric First Aid training. - Emotional Literacy support. - Nurture Networking including how nurture supports well-being. - Autism Awareness. - Attention Autism. - Sensory Integration. - Step Up. - Anxiety Awareness. - Supporting SpLD – Dyslexia. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents/carers and children are central to the School’s SEND processes and procedures. Teachers and the SENDCo work closely with parents/carers in the support of children with Special Educational Needs through: • Ongoing dialogue and active partnership. • Parent consultation meetings. • Provision Maps outlining targets and reviewing progress. • Reports from outside agencies. • SEND events run by the SENDCo/SEND team to inform and share knowledge e.g. Reading Eggs demonstration. • SEND noticeboard. Where appropriate, children are involved in their target setting and reviewing their learning with the teacher and/or SENDCo. Children who have an Education and Health Care Plan are encouraged to give their views via the ‘All About Me’ document. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all of our parents/carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed and agreed with the parents. We also offer updates through home/school books if this is more appropriate and convenient. We regularly monitor the short term outcomes for children with SEND via a SEN Support Provision Plan and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals such as Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists etc. are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits too. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Robertswood school is fully accessible to wheelchair users. There is a designated disabled parking space at the front of the school and flat access to the school’s main entrance. The school has facilities for personal care, including toilets, for pupils with physical disabilities in both the main school and the nursery. Ancillary aids and adaptions are made to accommodate the needs of individual children following guidance from specialists. Classes are well resourced for children with additional needs. For example, visual timetables, writing slopes and sensory cushions are all regularly used. We have a wide range of Occupational Therapy resources to support both fine and gross motor skills. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We fully understand that each child’s transition needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including home visits, visits to previous settings, settling in sessions, shortened sessions, if appropriate, and transition booklets. We are also happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible, where possible, to meet your child’s needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We regularly audit the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and carry out specific training or continuous professional development accordingly. Our SENDCo shares national and local SEND developments with colleagues to ensure all staff have relevant and up to date knowledge. Our resources and facilities are continually reviewed, and where needed adapted, to ensure they meet the needs of all children in the setting.

local_offer: Robertswood Nursery caters for up to 30 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet the needs of all of our children. We also offer all children a range of exciting and engaging opportunities which all link with our Early Years Curriculum. We are able to offer flexible entitlement in our Nursery. The setting has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or an on-site visit with parental agreement. We also receive regular visits from an Early Years Advisor. We are happy for professionals involved with any child to visit our Nursery and welcome this opportunity to develop our knowledge. Prior to joining the Nursery, our staff endeavour to carry out home visits. Where this is not possible, children and invites to attend Nursery with their parent/carer. This enables us to meet the child in their home environment and to establish a relationship between the child and nursery staff. It also enables an exchange of information with parents/carers so that we can get to know the child’s needs and plan an appropriate settling in programme. Once started at Nursery, we welcome parents into our setting on regular occasions to see 'Nursery life' in action. This is done through a range of ‘Stay and Play’ sessions, a teddy bears’ picnic, ‘Parent Sharing’ sessions, Mystery readers, pet sharing sessions, and more. We use Tapestry as a way of sharing the children's learning experiences with parents, and we ask that parents use Tapestry to share any wow moments or learning at home, with us. Parents are greeted by the Nursery Teacher daily at the door and are also welcome to request a meeting with the Nursery Teacher at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible. We also have two Parent Consultations during the school year where you will receive an update on your child’s progress and have the opportunity to discuss their likes, dislikes, achievements, and any concerns you may have. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all of our parents/carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed and agreed with the parents. We also offer updates through home/school books if this is more appropriate and convenient. We regularly monitor the short term outcomes for children with SEND via a SEN Support Provision Plan and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals such as Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists etc. are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits too. During the nursery year, nursery children come to the main school for weekly PE and Library sessions, which help them become familiar with the main school. description: Mixed-gender Independent special school in Winslow, Bromyard for 11 to 19-years-olds. Provides individualised care and education programmes for children and young people with severe learning disabilities, autism, and challenging behaviour. Rowden House School is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 11 to 19 years with severe learning difficulties and challenging behaviour. We offer day and residential placements ranging from 38 to 52 weeks. Each student has their own learning programme which meets each learner's needs in a holistic way. We place a strong emphasis on developing students' communication skills and improving behaviours. Young people receive specialised input from clinical professionals, including Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, and Clinical and Educational Psychology. All our students are individuals in their own right and we value their diversity. Our aim is to support all of the young people in our care to fulfil their potential, develop their independence and equip them with the skills for adulthood. We encourage all our students to develop a positive self-image, promoting their ability to express their personal preferences through informed choice. This develops confidence, enabling them to realise their full potential and grow into happy and healthy adults.

name: Rowden House School (Herefordshire)
description: Mixed-gender Independent special school in Winslow, Bromyard for 11 to 19-years-olds. Provides individualised care and education programmes for children and young people with severe learning disabilities, autism, and challenging behaviour. Rowden House School is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 11 to 19 years with severe learning difficulties and challenging behaviour. We offer day and residential placements ranging from 38 to 52 weeks. Each student has their own learning programme which meets each learner's needs in a holistic way. We place a strong emphasis on developing students' communication skills and improving behaviours. Young people receive specialised input from clinical professionals, including Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, and Clinical and Educational Psychology. All our students are individuals in their own right and we value their diversity. Our aim is to support all of the young people in our care to fulfil their potential, develop their independence and equip them with the skills for adulthood. We encourage all our students to develop a positive self-image, promoting their ability to express their personal preferences through informed choice. This develops confidence, enabling them to realise their full potential and grow into happy and healthy adults.

local_offer: At the Royal Latin School, we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve their potential at school. Quality teaching is vital: however, for some children, there are occasions during their school life when additional support may be needed to help them to achieve their targets. The SEND provision at The Royal Latin School is on an individual needs basis and includes but is not limited to: 1:1 sessions and dyslexia support sessions are carried out by suitably qualified Learning Support Assistants (LSAs) or qualified teachers. Social skills sessions are provided for students who need more targeted support; these are carried out in conjunction with the specialist teaching service. LSAs are used for both in-class support, small focus group support and for 1:1 sessions. The type of support depends on the students’ needs and the requirements of the subject teacher. Access arrangements are made for exams where a specialists report identifies a need. Types of provision may include the use of a laptop or additional time. Where there is an identified medical need further arrangements may have to be made. Where a student needs more specialised support, external agencies and other professionals may become involved Additional 1:1 support in specific subjects is provided in exceptional cases. Extra-curricular activities: We promote inclusion to include children/young people with SEND both inside the classroom and during extracurricular activities and trips. Pastoral support and Emotional Wellbeing: Emotional and social development is supported through various avenues including the form tutor and Head of Year (HOY), subject teachers, the Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO) and LSAs that may be supporting the student. The school uses specially trained peer listeners from years 12 and 13 to support other students and we have access to school counsellors where appropriate. Some students require more targeted support which is offered through social skills groups and in a small number of cases Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHs) support may be needed. https://www.royallatin.org/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The school’s main buildings are Disability Discrimination Act (DDA) compliant. The main buildings are accessible for wheelchair users and there are lifts available in the main block and new block to access classrooms on higher floors. name: Aston Clinton Park
description: A large, well-maintained playground with a cafe, soft play, stream, playground, and fitness trail. A hidden treasure, this larger-than-average park is camouflaged by mature trees from the busy main road. Once inside, a secret paradise is found for walkers, joggers, and those with other sporting interests, including tennis, bowls, and outdoor circuit training. Park benches are provided at regular intervals for spectators and the less active. They can enjoy the view of the Chiltern Hills while the cows feast in the lush green field to the perimeter. Located neat to the grounds of the Green Park activity centre and its camp area. A river runs along the far edge, displaying signs of revitalisation as a restoration project redirects its course. Newly planted black poplar trees enhance the area. This ideal family spot includes a cafe offering a full range of food and beverages, a social gathering point, and a respite from inclement weather. As the Chilterns face the impacts of new development and an increasing population, Aston Clinton Park provides a rare amenity—a rural oasis amid the suburban bustle. Opening times: Winter | 7am to 9pm Summer | 7am to 10pm

name: Royal National Institute of Blind People (RNIB)
description: RNIB is the Royal National Institute of Blind People (RNIB), one of the UK’s leading sight loss charities and the largest community of blind and partially sighted people. We recognise everyone’s unique experience of sight loss and offer help and support for blind and partially sighted people – this can be anything from practical and emotional support, campaigning for change, reading services, and the products we offer in our online shop. We’re a catalyst for change – inspiring people with sight loss to transform their own personal experience, their community, and, ultimately, society as a whole. Our focus is on giving them the help, support, and tools they need to realize their aspirations. Services include expert advice: Our Sight Loss Advice Service can answer queries on a wide range of topics ranging from benefits to education to so much more. Eye health: Understand more about your eye condition and how it can be managed with informed help from our Eye Health Information Service. Support and counselling: We provide emotional support and counselling for anyone who needs it. These sessions are confidential and are offered on a one-to-one or group basis. Make new friends: Our Talk and Support service gives you the opportunity to make new friends and socialise. Benefits and concessions: Learn more about what you may be entitled to by contacting our Benefits and Tax service. Useful products: Our Online Shop has a great range of useful and practical items that help you stay independent and in control of your life.

This means we ensure that whilst we strive for academic excellence, the foundation subjects of the curriculum, as well the personal and social development of each child, have a high priority too. We do this through a variety of ways including trips, 'wow' events, our breakfast and after-school club, extracurricular clubs and special events. Children thrive best in an environment of praise and so each week we celebrate children's successes in our Praise Assembly. Our facilities enable us to provide a broad, balanced and stimulating curriculum for the children and this means when they leave our school, they are ready to continue their learning in the next stage of their education and beyond.

description: Rushmere Country Park in Leighton Buzzard is a great place to discover nature and enjoy outdoor leisure pursuits. Come and view herons nesting in Spring from our outdoor café terrace, discover fairy doors and the Giant’s Chair along our Sculpture Trail, walk the dog, bring your bike we’ve something for everyone. Managed by The Greensand Trust, working in partnership with Central Bedfordshire Council, the park is run on a not-for-profit basis for the benefit of visitors and wildlife. Visitors can enjoy this wonderful park with over 400 acres of woodland, heathland and lakes - parking charges apply. Attractions include: - An ‘access for all’ Sculpture Trail where visitors can search for fairies and have a photograph in the Giant’s Chair - Play areas and play spots around the site - The heronry where you can watch herons raise their young in the Spring - A network of walking, cycling, and horse-riding trails - Areas where dogs can be walked on and off the lead, including a dog fun area specifically for our canine friends - Access to the Visitor Centre, toilets, the deck, Tree Tops Café, Herons Hatch, meadow for picnics, and Stockgrove Visitor Centre and cafe Rushmere Country Park is the holder of a TripAdvisor® Certificate of Excellence as a result of the high number of excellent reviews it receives via the website.

name: The Rye and Holywell Mead | Wycombe
description: The Rye is situated in the town centre of High Wycombe, a short walk from the High Street. In 2013 it was awarded the prestigious Green Flag award which recognises excellence in park management. The park covers an area of more than 22 hectares (53 acres) and is the second largest park in the district. The park includes the grassland area formerly known as Rye Mead, on which historically the townspeople of High Wycombe had the right to pasture their cattle, and additional areas which were formerly part of the Wycombe Abbey Estate once owned by the Carrington family. The park also extends to include the area of Holywell Mead, the site of a Roman villa and former watercress beds. There are two children's playgrounds in the park and football pitches are laid out on the grass during the season. Changing rooms are available for hire. To hire facilities please go to Book a Pitch on the website. The Dyke on the Rye is a large stretch of open water which is fed by water from the Abbey School grounds and allows permit fishing along part of the lake with pleasure craft for hire at the western end. The water spills over a waterfall and into a stream that flows out of the park toward the east. Public toilets are situated at the car park, approached from Bassetsbury Lane, a turning off of the A40 London Road which borders the park. local_offer: At S4A we believe that there is something 4 all. Our expertly planned activity timetables are produced to be accessed by any child that we care for. Our aim is to provide children with every opportunity to develop and learn in an environment which is suited for them. We offer wrap-around care within schools 7:30am to 8:45am and 3:15pm to 6pm While also offering holiday camps 8am to 6pm inside the school holidays. Our care is aimed at 4 to 13 year olds.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to meet the needs of all children at all of our primary schools and provide parents with full accessible extended care to meet the demands of their work life. Childcare is accessible through out the mid-term holiday periods for children and parents who need it regardless of their background. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our staff have various qualifications. Among these qualifications our staff have completed Team teach Understanding Autism Various childcare qualifications How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use behaviour and feeling charts and verbal communication with the children we work with. Parents are able to come in and speak to our team at our offices. Communicate with us over the phone and via email. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Activities are staff lead and facilities take place within a school setting which has access for all. We ensure staff ratios go above the recommended limit and we place 1:1 support where appropriate and financially possible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? They can use the service right away. By completing the medical form on our website making us aware of any needs that they might have. If they would like to speak to a member of staff in detail then they are able to ring and place a booking over the phone or via email with our team. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to apply for grants in order to employ a part-time member of staff who would be able to work 1:1 with children. We plan to send staff on more training courses to better meet the needs of the children we work with. We aim to train staff in British sign language in order to better communicate with children who are non-verbal.

description: Welcome to Sunrisers and Sunsetters, our fabulous wrap around care provided by Sports 4 All. Sunrisers opens at 7:30am and Sunsetters closes for the day at 6:00pm. organisation: S4A Group Ltd, Sports Development and School PE Provision S4A offer holiday camps in Buckingham, Grendon Underwood and Patishall. Providing childcare during the school holidays. We offer activities such as football, basketball, science and seasonal craft activities, a full list of which can be found on the s4a website. S4A also work in 13 different schools in Buckingham and surrounding areas providing high-quality PE provision. We teach a huge variety of different Sports with our coaches' being highly qualified in a range of Sports. We tailor our lesson plans to suit each classes specific needs, giving children the opportunity to learn new skills and develop existing ones whilst always maintaining the importance of enjoyment and fun. As well as providing PE provision in these schools we also provide extended care across in the area. We run breakfast and after school clubs offering a range of activities tailored to meet the interests of the children in attendance, from science clubs to sports clubs S4A cater for all. Helping them develop physically, emotionally, socially and mentally in an environment that is fun and exciting. S4A Development is about helping children reaching ''their'' next level. Our Boys and Girls Development Centre sessions are on a Monday evening in Buckingham with our Juniors section on a Saturday morning in Buckingham and Gawcott. All sessions are professionally designed and delivered in line with the 'England DNA' to offer a player-focused approach and develop players on an individual basis while allowing them to progress at their own speed and in a low pressure but testing environment. name: Safe Haven Buckinghamshire Mind
description: Bucks Safe Haven offers a safe and supportive environment, for anyone living in Buckinghamshire ages 18 years or over as an alternative to A and E, for people experiencing mental health crisis. Bucks Mind works with you to empower you and provide emotional listening support as well as helping you to manage your mental health better. The Bucks Safe Haven service works in partnership with Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust and most recently we have been fortunate to secure dedicated workers from Citizens Advice Bucks and Connection Support to provide expertise on issues such as benefits, unmanageable bills, housing crisis, such as risk to tenancy/becoming homeless and substance misuse. We help you to understand where to go for help in the local community, but most importantly to feel safer and create safety plans if you are struggling to keep yourself safe due to thoughts of self-harm or of ending your life. The service offers face-face groups with the option of a one-to-one discussion with a trained crisis support worker. Last entry is at 10:30pm. We are also offering 30-minute telephone or video support calls for people who cannot access the service face-to-face. Last entry is at 11pm. Safe Haven allows you to talk openly about how you are feeling and to build trusting relationships with supportive members of staff, without the fear of being judged. We work with you in a very empathetic and genuine way, no matter what the crisis is. How to access the service: The Bucks Safe Haven service is operating in Buckinghamshire in the following locations: High Wycombe: 7 nights a week. 6:30pm to 11:30pm. 260 Desborough Road, High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire, HP11 2QR (accessed via West Richardson Street, HP11 2SB) Aylesbury: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. 6:30pm to 11:30pm. Peach Tree House, Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust, Bierton Road, Sapphire Way, Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire, HP20 1EG Please note that we will ask for some brief contact details during the first call. We would encourage self-referrals where possible. However, if you are a professional and would like to make a referral to the service, please email us at the Bucks Safe Haven email address. Please note, our email address is accessed from 6pm to 11:30pm daily, and we will aim to contact the individual on the day they are referred to us. Safe Haven is not a drop-in service. There is no limit to how many nights you can call us, although we would only be able to offer one call per evening.

local_offer: Every child's needs are considered and action is taken where there is a requirement. Myself and one of my assistants are SENCO trained.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to provide equal opportunities and care for all children in our setting. We hope to help them become confident, independent individuals who then can consider many options for school when they leave us. We want to help children achieve their full potential and not feel held back by what they can or cant do in an Early years environment. We strive for the best relationship possible with families, supporting them as much as we can and having a none judgmental, open and friendly support network as a team. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Myself and my assistant Amie have completed our SENCO training with Buckinghamshire Council. We also regularly update our knowledge and all staff have ongoing training and ideas to help support children in our setting with additional needs. 3 of us also have BSL training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We try to include all parents as much as we can with the children's activities and learning. We are very open for discussions and ideas and trying new things. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We do a review every term, sometimes more often if needed. We offer parents evenings/phone calls and use an app called Famly to share photos, ideas and support. We regularly liase with the Early Years Team to discuss how to help the children we care for. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment is very outdoors based, it is a large area and a large hall, it is an old building but there are measures we can put in place to make it accessible to all if needed. It is an environment that encourages high independence from children but we can adapt and support where possible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Depending on your child's needs we can offer care for what you need. Because we are very outdoor based please consider if we are a suitable setting for your child, as much as we advocate for inclusion we want to keep children safe and happy within our setting. It may be that we need some time to risk assess and find suitable changes and options to support you and your family. We recommend a meeting/discussion of thoughts on how to do this before your child starts. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We hope to have all staff SENO trained in the next 2 years. We also have some resources that we are slowly gathering to help support children currently in our setting but also for the future.
