local_offer: It is the aim of The Sandcastle Nursery to provide a safe, secure, and stimulating environment for children from the age of birth to 8 years within the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory framework. We are an all-inclusive setting endeavouring to provide children with the best possible care outside their family, with facilities appropriate to a child’s age, abilities and interests. We promote a family atmosphere supporting children in building relationships and developing attitudes of caring and sharing. For all children in our setting, we offer a differentiated curriculum which is regularly evaluated to make sure all children are making satisfactory progress. The Nursery is open to all members of the community and our admissions policy considers neither personal characteristics nor disability status as relevant considerations. Information is provided in clear language, emphasising equality of opportunity. The Nursery aims to promote the development of each child in accordance with their individual requirements, particularly in adapting activities to allow inclusion of disabled individuals as detailed in our inclusion policy. We value the parents involvement and encourage their contributions and opinions. We treat all information and discussions with parents sensitively and in confidence.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? In order to provide our children with the highest possible quality of care and with maximum opportunities for their development, the Nursery employs a high proportion of experienced and well-qualified staff. The Nursery’s aim of continuous improvement dictates that all of our staff are encouraged and helped to develop their personal skills, and to broaden their knowledge and skills in caring for children and in promoting their development. Within our setting we have two trained and very well experienced members of staff (SENCO) with responsibility for SEN issues: Name: Ms Francesca Smalley and Mrs Hannah Byford Date Appointed:01/09/2002 Within our setting, we have a trained member of staff (SENCO) with responsibility for: Overseeing record keeping Monitoring progress Support child and staff members and parents Liaise with parents/carers and any outside agency Attend training and network groups and conferences and Early Years up-date evening meetings Transfer information regarding to next provider with parental permission The SENCO’s work with a number of trained professionals from outside agencies who work alongside and support nursery staff in the setting assisting with the implementation and delivery of key focused targets. Adult/child ratio would be altered to provide extra support for the child pending on the individual needs of the child. We will complete an SEN Support Plan and devise an individual structured programme to meet the individual child’s needs. In some cases, the outside agencies extend their services beyond the clinic by offering advice and support for the family in their home environment. All staff will read and abide by the SEN Policy and will be aware of the procedures for identifying, assessing and making provision for children with special educational needs. Information from network groups and training is relayed to staff through meetings. Staff are encouraged to attend external training courses during normal working hours, whenever appropriate. Staff are encouraged to pass on their knowledge to others working within the nursery. Attend regular Buckinghamshire Council EYCS meetings as appropriate for example EYFS Network Meetings, SEN/inclusion training sessions, Advice and Business Networks. Support in whole staff or small team in-house training events hosted by SENCO’s/Early Years Teaching Service/Early Years Advisers in relation to all aspects of SEN. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The named SENCO’s within the Sandcastle Nursery are Mrs Hannah Byford and Ms Francesca Smalley. They in consultation with staff, will inform parents as soon as we possibly can, of any concerns regarding their child's progress and/or development/behaviour. Our system of observations and record-keeping, which operates in conjunction with parents, enables us to monitor children's needs and progress on an individual basis. Staff are trained to recognise and monitor the needs and interests of each individual child, as well as to record accurately their developmental progress. This comprehensive system of planning and record-keeping identifies the child's needs and determines any shift in emphasis required to maximise progression. This ensures that key workers maintain an appropriate focus on the progress and needs of each individual child. Because these records are regularly shared with parents we can ensure that each child’s learning and welfare needs are effectively met. Staff are trained to recognise and monitor the needs and interests of each individual child, as well as to record accurately their developmental progress. This comprehensive system of record-keeping identifies the child's needs and determines any shift in emphasis required to maximise progression. We aim to provide a curriculum that is stimulating, enjoyable and sufficiently flexible for each individual child to flourish and thrive happily and within their own capabilities. By using an extensive range of activities, games and experiences we foster individual physical and intellectual development, self-awareness and confidence building with social interaction and consideration for others. We value children's views and would take these into consideration when planning provision for them. We understand ascertaining the child's view may not always be easy. Very young children and those with severe communication difficulties may present a significant challenge for education, health and other professionals. The principle of seeking and taking into account the ascertainable views of the child is an important one. We would use a variety of methods to ensure the child's involvement. We would: Listen to the child Listen to the parents/carers Offer the child choices Use observations to extend understanding Acknowledge the child's views/preferences The nursery works in close partnership with parents for the benefit of their children. Consequently, parents will be advised that staff, management and Ms Francesca Smalley are always available to discuss any concerns or suggestion which they may have. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We value the parents involvement and encourage their contributions and opinions. We treat all information and discussions with parents sensitively and in confidence. The dialogue between parents and nursery staff is particularly vital when a child has a learning difficulty or disabilities and for those whom English is an additional language to ensure that the activities that we provide and the expectations are consistent and relevant. We welcome and encourage parents/carers into the nursery throughout the year to celebrate a Variety of festivals and events to share in their children's experience. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? During their first induction meeting, parents will be introduced to their child’s key worker, the room leader and any other staff caring for their child. They will be given a developmental record book which contains an entry profile for them to complete. Parents will also have the opportunity to define any specific and reasonable requirements they may have regarding their child’s care, and the nursery will make every effort to comply. The nursery works in close partnership with parents for the benefit of their children. With parental permission, we welcome contact with outside agencies to ensure continuity and consistency of support for child and family. We welcome visits from Early Years SEN officers visiting the Nursery to offer advice and support. We hold regular Child Achievement Progress Day's when parents and staff meet to exchange information regarding the child's achievements and progress and to plan future strategies to improve development. Regular meetings will be held to review a child’s individual SEN Support Plan Form and ADPR form, targets will be set and reviewed after an agreed period of time to ensure the Nursery continues to offer best provision for the child, discussions with parents, whole team professional discussions and shared care settings. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? At the Sandcastle Nursery, we believe that children learn through their first-hand experiences and gain a greater knowledge and understanding by visiting places of interest. The Nursery aims to promote the development of each child in accordance with their individual requirements, particularly in adapting activities both indoors and outdoors to allow inclusion of disabled individuals as detailed in our inclusion policy. We provide as many opportunities for fun days out as possible, linking outings wherever appropriate with what the children are currently learning at the nursery. These range from walks to the local park and shops, forest school, to visiting wildlife parks, the theatre, library and other places of interest. Parents of children involved in these outings are notified well in advance and their consent for the visit is sought. In conjunction with our policy of partnership with parents, we actively encourage parents/guardians of children taking part in outings to join us. Support available within the setting for children with SEN * The building is one level and therefore accessible to all. * The building has ramp access * We have disabled access and facilities. * Adult/child ratio would be altered to provide extra support for the child Wherever possible we accept and integrate children with additional needs taking into consideration the direct needs of the children and our available facilities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? At the Sandcastle Nursery, we aim to provide smooth and caring transitions that promote positive self-esteem for the children and provide reassurance for the parents. To ensure that the transition from the home or previous carer to the Nursery is a positive experience, with the least amount of anxiety for the child and their parents we adopt the following procedure. Prior to a child starting at our nursery, we arrange a series of visits for the parent/carer with their child, which we call “settling in sessions.” These take place approximately two weeks before the child is due to start. This gives us the opportunity to arrange more visits within this time if needed, taking into account individual needs. Usually, we arrange three settling in sessions. The times are agreed so that they fit in with both the child, the parent’s commitments and the nursery routine as much as possible. For new children joining our setting if necessary we shall, with parental permission, contact previous or current additional early years settings to discuss children's development. We will transfer records and liaise with new settings when a child moves on to ensure relevant information is passed on. In some cases will, with parental permission, arrange a meeting with staff at the child’s new setting to exchange information prior to the child’s start date. Prior to a child starting school, with parent consent, we invite the child's new teacher to visit the nursery. This helps the teacher to see the child in familiar surroundings, it enables the child to speak and ask questions alongside their keyworker, and it also gives opportunity for staff to share information about the child's developmental stage, progress and achievements. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Staff will continue to regularly attend network up-date meetings, conferences, day release courses, request in house training to strengthen staff knowledge (led by Early Years Advisers and Early Years Teaching Service Specialists). Through all the work that we undertake with the children we are providing the foundations for their future growth and development, taking care to meet all the requirements as defined by the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory guidance. We are an all-inclusive setting endeavouring to provide children with the best possible care outside their family, with facilities appropriate to a child’s age, abilities and interests.

name: Autism Early Support | Outreach Service
description: Autism Early Support Trust Limited (AES) delivers early support and specialist education to autistic children and children with sensory, communication, and interaction differences. At the same time, we provide a comprehensive programme of support for their parents. Founded in 2001, we support families from Buckinghamshire and the surrounding counties. We believe every child has the right to timely and appropriate, high-quality education and that they should be given the best chance to find their place in the world, communicate their needs, and learn alongside their peers with acceptance and support. We believe their parents should be equipped with strategies and knowledge to fully support and advocate for their child. Our positive impact is achieved by supporting children to navigate their feelings and learn new communication and interaction skills and by giving parents peer support, practical solutions, and guidance. Our Outreach Service supports autistic children and children with communication, sensory and interaction differences in the community (including homes, schools and early years settings) and online. The support we can offer includes: The Parent’s Portal: An online platform for parents offering resources to watch and read; live and recorded workshops; and online discussion forums (free for Buckinghamshire residents from Sunday 1 December 2024). Parent Support Groups: These frequent online sessions for families offer emotional support, practical guidance and knowledge sharing in a kind, safe and non-judgemental space (part of The Parent's Portal). Assessments and Support Packages: We work directly with children in their homes, school or early years setting to provide speech and language or occupational therapy assessments and support packages (fees vary depending on the package required).
organisation: Autism Early Support Trust Limited (previously The Puzzle Centre) Formerly known as Puzzle Centre Autism Early Support Trust Limited Assessment and support services for parents and practitioners. Training courses available for parents and professionals. We offer outreach to both families and settings. This can be in the form of assessment or support, as well as training on a variety of training courses. We are also linked to the Buckinghamshire Family Support Services providing Parent Support Groups within the High Wycombe, Chesham and Aylesbury Areas. name: Autism Early Support | Outreach Service
description: Autism Early Support Trust Limited (AES) delivers early support and specialist education to autistic children and children with sensory, communication, and interaction differences. At the same time, we provide a comprehensive programme of support for their parents. Founded in 2001, we support families from Buckinghamshire and the surrounding counties. We believe every child has the right to timely and appropriate, high-quality education and that they should be given the best chance to find their place in the world, communicate their needs, and learn alongside their peers with acceptance and support. We believe their parents should be equipped with strategies and knowledge to fully support and advocate for their child. Our positive impact is achieved by supporting children to navigate their feelings and learn new communication and interaction skills and by giving parents peer support, practical solutions, and guidance. Our Outreach Service supports autistic children and children with communication, sensory and interaction differences in the community (including homes, schools and early years settings) and online. The support we can offer includes: The Parent’s Portal: An online platform for parents offering resources to watch and read; live and recorded workshops; and online discussion forums (free for Buckinghamshire residents from Sunday 1 December 2024). Parent Support Groups: These frequent online sessions for families offer emotional support, practical guidance and knowledge sharing in a kind, safe and non-judgemental space (part of The Parent's Portal). Assessments and Support Packages: We work directly with children in their homes, school or early years setting to provide speech and language or occupational therapy assessments and support packages (fees vary depending on the package required).

We are very happy to talk to parents on an individual basis to see whether we are able to offer suitable childcare to support families within our setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to be fully approachable and support families and their children while we are providing caring childcare for them. We will work with any other agencies the children are receiving support from so we can unite the care given and work towards positive, nurturing outcomes as children thrive, learn and develop with us. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? MGM Training - basic autism awareness. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? we collect information about the children we look after each day to show how they are achieving and developing with us and share with parents on a regular basis. We also speak to parents as and when needed (usually at the beginning and end of the day) to share information that helps us support the children each day. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We speak to parents on a daily basis about how the children's day has been and what we have achieved or would like to spend more time on. Each child has their own SEND file and we document their progress/monitor achievements. We liaise with our SENCO officer for support and advice and share this information when children receive extra support from outside agencies like SALT and also when they progress onto other settings. We arrange to stay in contact with outside agencies for continuity of support and invite them to see the child in action within our setting. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Unfortunately, we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We are very happy to speak to families to see if we are able to help and then work with them to decide the best plan to introduce and settle children in our setting. name: Sarah Allen
description: My name is Sarah Allen, before qualifying as a Childminder in November 2020 I was an NNEB-trained Nanny from 1995 until 2018 when I had my own children I live in Aylesbury on a lovely development called Berryfields with my partner and my 7 year-old boy and girl Twins. I also run structured activities with the children like messy play, cooking, games, and other interactive activities involving myself and the children. local_offer: I can help families with needs similar to those I have experience with, which are detailed below.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? For a parent to know that their child has been well cared for and looked after to be able to move on to other settings knowing that they have developed in their abilities What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have been self taught and family led with my SEND training over the course of my childcare career before becoming a childminder. I have cared for two children with cerebral palsy who were both wheelchair bound and one of whom was blind so I was taught to manage a ketogenic diet and the other had a PEG feeding system which I would make up and administer. Both children had epilepsy so I was able to manage and understand how to deal with the seizures and be able to administer the medicine needed to manage the condition. I would assist with the physical and medical development of these children with the use of hoists, motorised bath, toilet and standing machines. I worked alongside key people in their lives like physiotherapists who would regularly attended the home, I would copy the important exercises to perform as well as attending the bobath (weekly exercise and sometimes swimming sessions). I spent a lot of other time playing with and interacting with the children with the use of a dynamic communicator which uses switches and more recently the Eye Gaze system which allows the child to play games and make choices using their eyes. I was always on the lookout for all the fun and interactive toys I could find to assist them during play and learning e.g. Musical instruments, wind up toys, chewing toys for sensory development along with foil blankets and noisy or vibrating things to lay on. I would take one of the children in the car (modified for wheelchairs) which I had to learn to drive and learn all the skills for securing the wheelchair in the car safely. Both of these children had siblings that did not have any special needs so I would spend a lot of time interacting with them and getting them involved with the different style of play so they had an understanding of how to manage their playtime with their sibling when they were alone with them. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I would always involve the parents in my setting by giving them an incite into what I am going to be teaching their child with regular parent consultations and giving them a forward plan of my activities at the beginning of the week and welcoming any feedback or requests they might have. I will always give them informal feedback at numerous times either at pick up time or through email or Kinderly. I would ask parents to share information about their child’s likes and dislikes. I will provide the children with the correct activities for their age group while constantly challenging their potential, to get the best out of them. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I will provide all necessary checks and progress reports needed for your child including the 2-year progress check, end of term assessment summaries as well as coproducing Assess, Plan, Do, Review (ADPR) and coproducing SEN Support plan. I commit to involving an action plan if necessary with other services but with parent’s permission of course. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My premises is a ground floor flat with wheelchair access and although we have no outside space ourselves we are on a development that has accessible playgrounds and open spaces. I would always talk through with the parents what the needs of their child were and work together to come to an agreement. I have a separate room for quiet time, which could become a sensory space if needed. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please get in touch so we can discuss your needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I will be constantly updating my training in this area and complete as many ongoing courses as necessary for being able to keep my children safe, well looked after and still able to learn and have fun too. I will make purchases of important key equipment and resources to aid my children through their learning and development.

local_offer: I offer 30 hours funding to 9 months to 2 yr olds with eligible working parents. And 30 hrs for 3yr old with eligible working parent. Also care for babies from around 6 months . If there is a particular need that your child has ,then I will talk to parents about if or how I can go forward to implement help. With parent's permission, I can contact and involve other services which may help and support parents and children. I have a contact within the Early Years Service from whom I can access advice and information. They will be happy to answer questions and refer to other services.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I provide a caring and enabling environment for children, where learning through play is key to my setting. The ages and stages of the children are considered as well as their individual needs, to ensure they have fun, enjoy their time with me, and progress and develop in their learning. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Paediatric infant and child first aid FEB 2025 Prevent duty JAN 2025 equality and diversity. JAN 2022 Safeguarding lead JUNE 2024 altogether now inclusion workshop NOV 2014 stage, not age: child development OCT 2013 Promoting positive behaviour JAN 2012 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents and encourage conversation about your child at drop-offs and pick-ups and at any time that is suitable for both parties. Also by text if it’s difficult to find time to chat. I ask parents to fill in a child record form and include any likes /dislikes their child has regarding food, activities, sleep aids, favourite toys.I also occasionally ask parents to fill in a questionnaire, asking if they are happy with the care their child receives and the progress they are making and if there is anything I can do to improve my setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I regularly share information with parents about their children’s learning, development and progress by talking to the parents at drop off and pick up. I send pictures and videos by text to parents/carers of each child under school age, showing what the children have been doing throughout the day and I comment on my observations of their children’s progression and development. I explain how each observation is showing their progression in the areas of learning and development and how they can progress further. If a particular need becomes apparent through the observations, then I will talk to parents about how we can go forward to implement help. With the parent's permission, I will contact and involve other services to support families. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My house is situated 10 minutes walk from a bus stop in Flackwell Heath. I have a large drive for drop-offs and pick-ups. Easy access to my house although a small step up at the front door into the house and small step down at the back door. I have an outdoor patio with an outdoor table and chairs for eating outside and an umbrella for shade. The patio is also good for the use of trikes, scooters, play cars. I have a large lawn with some shade and play equipment, including a trampoline, slides, swings and climbing frame. A outdoor kitchen and playhouse is available .There is room for running, hopping, football, water play and bug hunting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I can be contacted by email, what’s app, or text. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? If a child with a particular mild special need attends my setting, I could attend training in that area. I am also interested in looking at some training in autism. And I will look at attending a more up to date course regarding promoting positive behaviour and inclusion .

name: Sarah-Jane Turner
description: About Me: I am a kind, caring individual who simply adores looking after children. I have been in the industry for 30 years, and the children never fail to surprise me! I simply love supporting the development of each child; they often have me in fits of giggles with their creative minds and wonderful imaginations. I pride myself on being incredibly reliable, hard-working and trustworthy and these qualities run through every aspect of my care provision. My interests include cooking, socialising with friends and venturing into the great outdoors. My child care philosophy: At the core of my practice lies the belief that every child is truly unique; I am child-led in supporting development. I want every child in my care to feel valued and celebrated. I aim to create a family atmosphere with every child being given a role in all the activities I provide. I believe it is essential to work in partnership with parents/carers and I take a large amount of time during the settling-in period to get to know each child and their families to ensure I support the same type of care that the child is receiving in their home environment. I believe in experiential learning, and where possible I take the children out of the home environment each morning. This could be to the park, fruit picking, the garden centre or the play centre, weather depending. I then use the afternoon session at home to work on numeracy, literacy, ICT, expressive art or movement skills. My home environment: I live at home with my husband and Archie Cat. Archie Cat likes to join the group from time to time to be petted or have a general nose! I have a separate playroom for the children to create a 'nursery feel'. The children are able to use the toilet to learn about personal hygiene as well as develop independence skills. I have a wide variety of toys which are stored at floor level, meaning the children are able to make choices over what they would like to play with. I also have a lovely large garden which is full of toys and a range of lovely flowers to enhance the sensory experience of children. The children all receive freshly prepared food which is nutritionally balanced. Meeting the needs of your child: I conduct consistent, regular observations of your child which are stored in their learning journey booklet. Some of these are informal, where I will observe your child for a certain amount of time and take notes on what they are achieving. Every six weeks I carry out a formal assessment against the EYFS age-related criteria to help support the Next Steps element of my planning. This progress will be shared with you daily through verbal feedback and also at formal reporting points. At any time should you wish to know more about your child's progress, or if you have any concerns you only need to ask me for a longer discussion. A typical day in my care: After completing the school run, the younger children in my care and I will choose our out of house activity. This could be either a trip to the park, toddler group, a play centre, fruit picking, the library, or the garden centre; this list is by no means exhaustive! Each child, where possible, has a chance to choose the activity across the week. In the case of very young children who may not yet talk, I will closely observe which activity they seem to enjoy the most and I will let that guide which activity we select when it is their turn to choose. We then return home for lunch and/or a nap. In the afternoon I will carry out one-to-one work with each child based on my Next Steps Planning for them following their formal assessment. We also play group games which are aimed at developing their skillset across the EYFS specification. Cuddles and encouragement are offered throughout the day; I want your child to feel as though they are at a 'home away from home' as I believe that when a child feels happy and secure in their environment, they truly flourish.

In the case of very young children who may not yet talk, I will closely observe which activity they seem to enjoy the most and I will let that guide which activity we select when it is their turn to choose. We then return home for lunch and/or a nap. In the afternoon I will carry out one-to-one work with each child based on my Next Steps Planning for them following their formal assessment. We also play group games which are aimed at developing their skillset across the EYFS specification. Cuddles and encouragement are offered throughout the day; I want your child to feel as though they are at a 'home away from home' as I believe that when a child feels happy and secure in their environment, they truly flourish.

name: Schools of Chesham Carnival (Annually every June)
description: The carnival traditionally takes place on the 2nd Saturday in June each year. It is a charitable event run by a committee of volunteers made up of parents, both past and present, from ten local schools. Schools of Chesham Carnival is a registered charity raising valuable funds for all the participating schools who help organise this home-grown event. Each year there is a theme to the carnival and the children, parents and teachers of the schools create their floats to complete for the winner’s trophy! Some themes have included celebrating Roald Dahl, the 1970s, Fairy Tales and Music. Many local business, pubs, clubs and community projects also join in the procession to make it a truly community-based event. The procession lasts approximately 50 minutes starting in Asheridge Road continuing onto Bellingdon Road and Townsend Road and finally proceeding down Chesham high street. After the procession, Lowndes Park becomes very much the central hub of carnival day with amusements for all the family - such as a petting farm, bouncy castles, trampolines, face painting, henna designs and craft activities. There are around seventy stalls selling homemade sweets, chocolates and artefacts with others running games plus a choice of fair-ground attraction stalls for all ages. There is the bottle tombola stall with approximately 400 bottles to win, all contributed by families from the local schools. Food, refreshments and a bar are also available. Throughout the day local dance schools and clubs display their routines, skills and talents in the main arena in the park. Additionally, the Town Mayor announces the winners of the trophies for the best school and local business floats. Not forgetting the Grand Draw Raffle organised and run by the committee with prizes predominantly donated from local retailers and businesses. Registered Charity No: 1029408

local_offer: Schorne Pre-School is an inclusive setting. We are able to support children with SEND and their families through SEN support plans. We meet regularly with parents and any other professionals involved in a child's care. We have additional support from Buckinghamshire Early Years who are able to assess the individual needs of the child, working alongside the pre-school. We plan activities for all children individually to meet their needs. Each child is assigned a key worker but they are also supported by all of the other staff members. We have a SENCO at our setting who attends regular training and network meetings along with SENCOs from other settings and SEND professionals. This information is then passed onto the rest of the team. The SENCO and Manager work together to provide the best care for each child. Our staff have attended a wide range of courses and training is up to date. We are able to attend training in any area that would support a child and enable them to attend our setting. We have experience of attending to the additional needs of a looked after child and their carers, from fostering through to adoption. We have also had some medical training in the following areas: -Allergies and the use of Epi Pens. -Stoma bag. -Diabetes and insulin Pens.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? All specialist services provided by Buckinghamshire Council are available for us to access when needed: -Speech Therapist -Physiotherapist -Occupational Therapy -Specialist Teacher support -Early Years Consultant support What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? -Early Birds alongside parents -Good Autism Practice -Leading Good Autism Practiceakaton Level 1 -Initial SEN Training -Level 3 SENCO Training -Introduction to Down Syndrome How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents/carers are an integral part of co-producing their child's SEN plan. Autism early support and advice can be found here: https://portal.autismearlysupport.org.uk/ Parents/carers are invited to join our voluntary committee to help us provide the best possible care for all of the children. We invite parents to join us for a summer fun day and a Christmas celebration. Parents/carers are invited to an annual parents meeting and we provide an open door policy. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Practitioners will work alongside parents to make sure that everyone is on the same page and that all information is shared. Forms can be filled in together and staff will support parents with any meetings needed to discuss their child's care with other professionals. We use Tapestry to showcase photos of the children's day and to track their progress; parents/carers can view this at any time from home. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have access to a large garden area and where possible children have access to outside play daily. This includes walks around the village and visits to the local shop & park. There is a ramp to access the front entrance of the building. We have a large accessible toilet. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Support is in place to assist the transition from home to Pre-School. We provide information about the Pre-School and each child is allocated a Key Person. We can offer home visits and children can have a staggered settling in period if we assess that it is required. We also provide support to assist the transition to Reception Class. We have close links to the surrounding schools. We are part of the Providers in Partnership programme with other local Pre-School and Schools - this makes sure that we are all providing the same experiences to aid the child and parent with their transition to School. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We undertake frequent training to keep our knowledge up to date. We are beginning to use a programme called Calming Cats to support children with their emotional wellbeing.

description: Our service is here to help Buckinghamshire children and young people with SEND aged 0 to 25 years and their parents or carers. We offer information, advice, and support on all matters related to SEND. We are a small team of advisers supported by business support officers. Some of our team are volunteers. We operate all year round, including in school holidays. Our service is: - free of charge - confidential - impartial and neutral- we don’t take sides - at arm’s length from Buckinghamshire Council and health services All our advisers are trained in SEND law, but are not legally qualified. local_offer: How we respond to you Email You should expect an email response within 10 working days of submitting your contact form. This email will contain information to help answer your query. This may include weblinks and written information, short films and webinars. Make use of the information. If you find this difficult, you could ask a friend to help you. If you have provided your email address and do not receive an email response within 10 days of contacting us, check your spam or junk folder. Telephone You should expect a call from an adviser if our email response says you will be getting one. You may have to wait several weeks for a call from an adviser or you may get a call in a few days, it depends on the query you have. We will do our best to get to you as quickly as we can. Whilst you wait for a call, make use of the information we send you. The adviser will refer to the information in their call. A trainee Volunteer SENDIAS Adviser may join the call to listen in for training purposes. Support with meetings and tribunals Our advice may include helping you to prepare for a meeting. In exceptional circumstances we may be able to attend a meeting with you, this will usually be remotely. We can help you to start a Tribunal appeal and can provide advice once you have received your response from the local authority. In exceptional circumstances we will act as your representative, provide case management support and/or attend hearings.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Children and young people with SEND and their parents/carers: - feel more confident navigating the SEND system. - voices are heard in decision-making. - gain knowledge about their rights, available support, and choices. - develop improved relationships with education and other providers. - experience improved well-being What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The SENDIAS team undertakes a range of training including independent SEND legal training provided by the National Information, Advice and Support Service Network. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Staff trained specifically to support parents and/or children, and young people. Ground floor site with good parking and bus routes nearby. Wheelchair ramp available. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact SENDIAS using our contact form available on our webpages: https://www.buckinghamshire.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/bucks-sendias-service/contact-sendias/ Alternatively, with your permission, a friend or professional can contact us on your behalf. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We have recorded webinars and short films and occasional events relating to SEND: https://www.buckinghamshire.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/bucks-sendias-service/news-events-and-webinars/

local_offer: I am able to help people learn to enjoy life to the full and live with the condition of autism - as a positive celebration, not a disability. After studying and working in the Social Care industry for three decades, I found myself travelling the UK to be alongside families, teachers, organisations, people young and old showing them my unique way of handling difficult emotions. I am autistic. I grew up wanting to be neurotypical but now I would not swap places with you for the world. Autism is a way of life. See it our way. I help you to live a happy functioning life day by day. What our clients say about us: "Superb, lots of food for thought" "Very inspirational. Great to have first-hand knowledge from the trainer and would love to hear more" "More in-depth training on triggers and profiling" "Fantastic training and I would have stayed all day to listen to more" "Brilliant speaker – really enjoyed the training" "Excellent – I now feel I want to know and learn more. Bring back, Richard!" "The training was great, I really enjoyed it" "Excellent – Thank you" "I would certainly attend another talk with Richard Maguire" "Absolutely brilliant – couldn’t have recommended it highly enough and well done to Richard, can’t be an easy job!"  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? A life worth living with autism. I show people how to interact with an autistic individual by being autistic myself and training for years with learning disabled people. Walk with me is my philosophy. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Decades of experience in working high-level operations with training and qualifications to match. I speak on the national stage at NAS events. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We do ask that parents get involved in sessions and have sessions themselves. Autism mentoring is never about making the autistic individual change and more about helping them to understand themselves and the people around them, that should involve the parent too. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We are happy to discuss progress at the end of each session. Depending on your child's needs and comfort you should also be able to sit in on sessions and be fully involved in the process. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We aim to make every session accessible for the individual. We are happy to meet you, in person, outside in a place where you are comfortable. We also now run most of our sessions online, using Zoom and Skype to connect. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Get in contact using one of the above numbers, send us an email or visit our website to see how to get going. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The support I have from prominent doctors and organisations in this field shows my results work. I am defined by my autism. I am defined by my success rate - please call to discuss working with me. Testimonials: Richard Maguire is one of the most inspirational people I’ve had the privilege to know. Diagnosed with Asperger’s syndrome as an adult, many might consider Richard to be ‘mildly affected by autism. He has extraordinary skills as a trainer, a wonderful sense of humour, drives a car, holds down a job and is married with a son. On the face of it, his life does not seem to have been overly troubled by autism. This outward appearance belies the extreme of the difficulties he faces and needs to overcome daily in order to succeed. Richard is a highly valued core member of our Autistic Training Team at Autism Oxford and I hope that his book reaches into the hearts and minds of those who can make a difference to people who, like him, live as actors on life’s neuro-typical stage. Kathryn Erangey BPhil Autism, PE Cert ASC Managing Director - Autism Oxford of all the autobiographies by people with autism that I've read, ' I Dream in Autism' is different. It isn't just an account of the author's (often painful) experiences but takes one right into the centre of what it feels like to be on the autistic spectrum. From the beginning Richard invites the reader into his head, to share his sensory distortions and goes on, 'Are we sitting uncomfortably? Then we are ready to begin.' My attention was grabbed. The ensuing text is long, meandering and at the same time, absolutely riveting. Personally, I find his technical descriptions of his cameras fascinating, especially where he is able to relate these to his ability to crystallise how he feels. Holding emotions through a viewfinder was a new idea to me and there were many others. Every teacher should read this book. I Dream in Autism tells us just how misleading some current ideas about autism are: People with autism do not feel emotion. Wrong. People with autism do not have a sense of humour. Wrong. Children with autism are 'lazy', 'naughty', stupid'. Wrong. That 'being quiet' necessarily indicates improved behaviour rather than deeper withdrawal. Wrong. (I wrote this in a report about a child a few weeks ago before reading this book. I was told she was more tolerant of children kicking the patterns she was assembling on the floor and this indicated an improvement.) Phoebe Caldwell DSC Richard has impressed me both as a person and as a writer. In meeting and getting to know him I discovered someone who has had to learn about the rules of being a human almost from scratch… acquiring them the hard way, diligently writing about this journey for us all to see. His book is a testament to the heart and spirit of people who have autism - a subject that is often overlooked by the media and some professionals working in this area. I find it significant that most people are interested in the 'autistic mind' but clearly Richard reminds us of the importance of his heart which feels both pleasure and suffering like any other. Following his heart, along with his wish to understand and be understood, Richard used his intellect to map out a way of living that he uses and refines every day in being within his world. Fortunately, his propensity for sharing has allowed him to develop and offer this gift to the many clients he works with and those reading this book. Not everything we read here is straightforward or easy to understand and that is wonderfully deliberate. Richard makes an audience wrestle with trials and tribulations to understand his own experience and that of others like him. This is not an autobiography in the traditional sense but a sharing of a state of mind - an invitation to both understand and communicate. It is also a subtle offer to many neurotypical readers that through the course of absorbing his story they begin to change both personally and, if necessary, professionally. Dr Emilios Lemoniatis MBBS, BSc, AKC, MRCPsych Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist at The Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust, London

description: Sexual health services in Buckinghamshire are provided by a number of different organisations. There are clinics at Wycombe Hospital (the SHAW clinic) and Brookside in Aylesbury, both run by Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust. In addition, there is a range of community clinics offering both contraception and STI testing. This service is being run in conjunction with the Brook charity. GP surgeries provide a range of basic sexual health services, including long-acting reversible contraception (LARC methods include implants and IUD/IUS’s) and Chlamydia screening, and some community pharmacies offer free emergency hormonal contraception. The Sexual Health Buckinghamshire website has a handy Local Service Finder where you can locate your nearest: Sexual Health Clinic, Free Condom Site, Sexual Assault Referral Centre, and GP Surgery. There's also free information and advice on lots of topics, including: - Contraception - Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) - Post-exposure prophylaxis after sexual exposure to HIV - HIV and Prep (Pre-exposure prophylaxis) - Teenage pregnancy and young parents - Sexual Assault - Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) - Consent and healthy relationships - Understanding the body - Information for all ages, including the 50-plus years - Information for Parents - Easy-to-read information for people with learning disabilities

local_offer: I am an Ofsted registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? AET- Making sense of Autism – January 2022 Speech and Language – Selective Mutism and stammering – February 2022 SEN- Completing paper work effectively – April 2022 SENCO Level 3 - May 2024 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in close partnership with parents to gain as much information as possible to help their child settle in. Parents can help by sharing their child’s routine and letting me know what their likes/dislikes are and any special requirements their child has that I need to be aware of. Parents can share what activities their child enjoys and what their child needs support with. Parents can attend settling-in sessions with their child until they feel comfortable enough to leave them. If needed I can do a home visit to help the child get familiar with me. Once settled parents can keep in contact throughout the day so they can feel at ease and be updated about what their child is doing. I will regularly share with parents’ information about their child’s learning, development, and progress. Parents can also share with me what their child has been doing at home this could be any new interest or a milestone they have reached so they can be celebrated with others in the setting. Information sharing is vital for the continuity of care. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending the setting are observed and their learning and development progress is monitored and shared with the parents. There will be regular communication letting parents know what activities have been done during the day. Parents can share with me information about their child through text messages, emails, or any paperwork that needs to be shared with other professionals involved with the child. We will have regular meetings to assess the child’s needs and put into place strategies/ interventions to support your child. We will regularly arrange time review the plans. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. The setting is near a regular bus route for those needing public transport. I have two small steps leading to the front door there is also access via a side entrance through the large back doors which also have steps up. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to visit my setting and have a settling-in period with their child before deciding to choose my setting. They will alongside other paperwork need to complete an ‘All about me’ form to give me as much information as possible about their child. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their learning and development. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I currently keep up to date with SEND information and new training offered through the Local Authority. I regularly review my settings environment the toys, resources, activities, and what new experiences I can offer to each individual child. I am willing to go on any additional training needed to support an individual child and their family.

description: Shared Lives Plus is an alternative housing option for victims of domestic abuse where the victim is matched with a host (or host family) and moves into their home to live with them for a temporary period which typically lasts between 3 to 9 months depending on the victims needs and plans. Hosts are carefully chosen and trained by Ategi. Leaving an abusive relationship is not an easy option, but Shared Lives hosts will offer the victim a safe place to live, care and emotional support and help to tackle loneliness whilst allowing independence, belonging and personal choice. local_offer: Our outdoor learning experience enables children of all abilities to access each individual area of learning through a broad, balanced and differentiated access to the curriculum. We pride ourselves on being a totally child-led environment. This approach to learning enables children, of all abilities, to be able to be in control of their own learning. We aim to provide opportunities for children and young people with SEND to access the Early Years curriculum. We hope that it is this positive and relaxed environment that enables children with SEND to excel in other areas of their development, including toileting and emotional regulation. Our child-led journey aims to enable children to control their own learning, ensuring that their next steps for learning are achievable and manageable. We aim for children and young people with SEND to be thoroughly supported within their own learning, just as all of our children are. We also aim for a child to create new relationships with both staff and peers and support them in creating firm foundations for their future. We offer flexible settling in sessions, following both parent and child’s needs and wants. We will also be offering home visits to ensure that the transition period is as smooth as possible for the child. When transferring to a new setting/school, we will make close connections to each setting so that information can be shared to guarantee a smooth transition. Our indoor area has wide door frames, ensuring that children with additional equipment can access inside. There are steps up to the indoor area and the decking area, which can be easily adapted by small ramps for those who may not be able to use the steps. Our indoor area also has tie-up blinds, enabling the yurt have low lighting if required. Our outdoor area is all on the same level. The ground is mud and can be soft when wet. To ensure that all children, especially those with extra equipment, can access this area, we have bark chippings that enable easier access to every area of the outside space. We offer an open door policy, which allows parents to share any concerns that they may have at any point. We also encourage parents to meet with their child’s Key Person regularly, to share observations and the Learning Journey’s. We aim to encourage parents onto any trips that we may have and, in the future, we hope to have regular parent-helpers for snack times, reading and other activities on site. Our SENCO will be responsible for ensuring that all members of staff access regular training to support children with SEND. Areas of training include Behavioural Management, Autism Awareness, Makaton Sign Language and then training which is required for individual children’s needs at that moment in time. We will be regularly reviewing our Barriers to Learning and Provision, ensuring that facilities and resources can be adapted or provided when needed. We will also be accessing regular training, for all staff, to the needs of their key children.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO Training - 2 Day Training Course For Nominated New and Aspiring SENCOs completed in February 2020. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use an online tracking programme that allows us to update you with your child's development. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our outdoor space is relatively flat however this is mainly grass or wood-chip. Our indoor space is an open yurt which there are 3 steps to, however it is possible to make this to a ramp. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We tailor our transition arrangements to the child and families personal needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: I have recently completed an adult learning course in Understand Autism. Through completing the course, I feel I have a better understanding of how to support and help children in my setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? With all children in my care, I aim to prepare and nurture your child and have them ready for and reach for their next steps. I will work together with parents and children to ensure their learning is extended so they can reach their full potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 2 Understanding Autism. May 2022 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents, sharing information about their child’s learning, development and progress on a regular basis. By sharing information from the setting with parents and learning about your child's home life, I can fully understand your child’s likes and dislikes, the activities which they find difficult and those which they enjoy the most. I aim to provide children with activities which will extend and support them to meet their potential with me and share ideas with parents to do at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? With permission, I will send regular photos and updates on your child's activities with me, and ideas on how we can both extend their learning. I will share any progress checks I make and any areas in which I identify as requiring additional support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to most children and families. I have plenty of off-street parking available, I'm on a bus route, and within walking distance of the London Underground. I have a car which I use to transport childminded children in, which is fully insured and mechanically well maintained. Within my house, I have a dedicated playroom, with plenty of resources and materials for children to play with and enjoy. I have a mix of educational toys and books, and toys children can use for imaginative play. My outside space is completely level with no steps, it is laid to lawn with a patio where we can learn and play together. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact me, we can arrange a visit so you can meet me, my setting and the current children in my care. We can discuss individual requirements and plans already in place. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I have recently completed an adult learning course in Understand Autism, it has helped me understand more about how autism presents in different people, which has enabled me to reflect upon how i can support children in my care. I am able to access training as necessary and extend my understanding further.

name: NCT Antenatal courses | Aylesbury and Thame
description: Our ever-popular antenatal classes and postnatal courses grow your knowledge and your network, allowing you to feel prepared and confident moving into the next chapter of your life. Discover and learn with other local parents-to-be, and make vital connections and life-long friends in your local community. We lead the field in parenting education. Every NCT antenatal class leader is trained, licensed and professionally developed to deliver you a gold-standard antenatal or postnatal course packed with the very latest trusted information, practical skills and in-depth local knowledge. Our antenatal classes contain plenty of built-in bonding time - you’ll work in different pairs and small groups, practising new skills to get conversation flowing and connections sparking. With mountains of advice out there for parents, it's easy to feel overwhelmed and unsure. We provide evidence-based information and help you explore your options. We empower you to decide which information to trust and confidently make your own decisions that are right for you and your family. Course themes include: • Planning for a positive birth experience • Understanding and caring for your baby • Feeding your baby • Taking care of physical and mental health • Your family, relationships and finding support

local_offer: The Children and Families Act 2014 puts into perspective the government’s plan to require local authorities and agencies to publish information on provision and services across education, health and social care for children and young people aged 0 to 25 years with special educational needs and disabilities. The rationale of the ‘Local Offer’ is to empower and enable parents and carers to easily access local services to them and their children, which offer help and support for their individual needs. The information below forms our ‘Local Offer’ and demonstrates how we support children and families with special educational needs and disabilities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? All staff have accessed child development training and have experience with the Early Years age group. We have a robust ongoing professional development training programme, to include external courses in-house training and on-line training with Laser short courses. We work alongside the specialist services that may be involved with your child who are welcome to visit our setting. This includes speech and language services, occupational therapy, educational psychologists, paediatricians, specialist teaching service. We are supported by the Buckinghamshire Early Years’ Service, who aim to help Early Years practitioners provide the best possible experience for all children in our setting. The team will support practitioners in meeting children’s individual needs through offering advice over the telephone, observing children in their setting, suggesting ways to support individual needs, planning next steps and sign posting to further training. We always obtain parental agreement before the Early Years’ Service team become involved with any child. The Early Years’ Service will support settings in working together with other agencies that may already be involved with a child What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Samina Noor is named SENDCO for the setting and she is supporting the team. She has completed Role of SENCo, Autism Awareness Training, ICAN Training, Early years SENCO webinar, Recognizing and supporting children with SEN courses. Weronika Siankiewicz has also completed SENDCO training. All staff members have completed Autism Awareness training, a few staff members are trained in ICAN so they can support the program across the nursery. We also look for appropriate opportunities for all practitioners to go on training courses to progress their knowledge in dealing with any new SEND children that join us. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have very effective communication system with parents through Newsletter, emails, zoom meetings and visits. We have EY Man online learning journal system in place to upload children’s daily care dairy, observations and termly reports for parents to view and give feedback. This system is two-way communication and is working very well. Parents are involved in helping staff identify needs, sharing information, identifying targets and next steps to focus on at home and in the setting and in reviewing progress towards these targets at review meetings. Parents’ permission will always be sought before involving outside agencies. We also regularly put posts on our Facebook page and this is an excellent way of keeping up to date with day-to-day happenings at Nursery. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Once a term we have a parent meeting where Keyworker shares an in-depth report on the child’s development across the framework. These meetings can also be arranged if the parent or carer is finding things difficult at home or have concerns, they want to be addressed immediately, our managers and staff team are always happy to facilitate meetings as and when they can even with very short notice. Robust assessment systems are in place such as the 2-year progress check, developmental tracking records and learning journey which are all linked to the EYFS ages and stages of development. Each key person observes and prepares individual weekly activities for each child, based on individual targets and needs. The planning is uploaded on EYMan learning journal on for parental viewing. Regular review meetings for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities are held to discuss the child’s targets and how the parent can support the child at home. Parents will also receive a termly update meeting with the child’s key person and SENCO. If parents/carers work or are unable to attend meetings, telephone calls or emails are welcome to update you on your child’s progress. Newsletters are sent via email on a half termly basis to keep you up to date with what is happening at the setting. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The indoor environment offers good accessibility y across the rooms which are all on one level and there is vast outdoor space. However, there are a number of steps into the nursery and to the outdoor area; these would make access for a wheelchair quite challenging without some form of a ramp being put in place. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have a robust settling process for children whether it is their first time at nursery or coming from another setting; we offer the initial transition into nursery in a way that supports the families home life, building up from an hour or so to cover sleep and lunchtimes. We ask other settings to provide us with their data on child assessment and using our EYMan system we are able to transfer full files for children. We work with local schools during the summer term to identify which children are going to their school and ensuring a full report of their developmental stage is shared with both parent and school. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Throughout the year staff will be put on training courses to progress further. We have developed a sensory room to support children with SEND.

name: Simply Walk
description: Walking is a great way to get out and about and meet new people while improving your health and wellbeing. Simply Walkers are out in all weathers, smiling, talking, and enjoying each others company. Our volunteer-led walks run all year, with over 700 walkers who join us on one of over 65 walks across the county every week. Volunteer leaders are there to help you walk at your own pace, so there is no need to worry about being left behind, lost, or feeling left out. Most walks are weekly, but we also hold fortnightly and monthly walks at some locations. All new walkers are welcome whether you are fit and active, haven't exercised in a long time, or have been advised to join by a doctor. So, why not join us and start walking. We have walks to suit almost everyone, so come along. Before attending your first walk, you need to register for Simply Walk online. Please visit the link provided. If you're unable to register online, paper copies of the registration form will be available from your walk leader on-site.
organisation: Simply Walk Walking is a fantastic way to get out and about, meet new people, improve your health and well being and help the environment. Simply Walk has over 50 organised walks throughout Buckinghamshire that are led by trained volunteers. This is a great way to explore the county. All new walkers are welcome to the scheme whether you are currently fit and active, or haven’t exercised in a long time. There are also specific walks for ladies to help them stay healthy during pregnancy. It couldn’t be easier to get started. name: Simply Walk
description: Walking is a great way to get out and about and meet new people while improving your health and wellbeing. Simply Walkers are out in all weathers, smiling, talking, and enjoying each others company. Our volunteer-led walks run all year, with over 700 walkers who join us on one of over 65 walks across the county every week. Volunteer leaders are there to help you walk at your own pace, so there is no need to worry about being left behind, lost, or feeling left out. Most walks are weekly, but we also hold fortnightly and monthly walks at some locations. All new walkers are welcome whether you are fit and active, haven't exercised in a long time, or have been advised to join by a doctor. So, why not join us and start walking. We have walks to suit almost everyone, so come along. Before attending your first walk, you need to register for Simply Walk online. Please visit the link provided. If you're unable to register online, paper copies of the registration form will be available from your walk leader on-site.

local_offer: As an Ofsted registered childminder I am a qualified Early Years Teacher. As a childminder, I work alone, with occasional support from an assistant. I am therefore solely responsible for planning in the setting. I have attended inclusion training and I use this knowledge and information to create individual learning plans for children with special educational needs. These are reviewed each term with parents. Learning Journeys are available online for parents to view at any time and are encouraged to contribute with comments and photographs. More in-depth discussions take place during home visits which can be arranged to suit parents. Parents are encouraged to contribute to children’s planning and suggestions for home learning can be provided. Parent input, alongside talking, observing and listening to the children enables the childminder to discover what they are interested in and to make plans to help them progress.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I acknowledge children individually and adapt my setting to meet each child's needs. Respect towards self, others and the environment will always be emphasised. I plan activities and play opportunities which are linked to the Early Years Foundation Stage to develop children’s Emotional, Physical, Social and Intellectual capabilities. I monitor the progress of each individual child, following the EYFS framework. I speak to both parents and children on a daily basis to review progress and adapt their needs accordingly. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Recognising and supporting children with SEN Autism Awareness ADHD awareness All updated in April 2022 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I am always available for an informal discussion at drop off and collection times. Each child has a daily diary that parents can use to communicate information. Home visits can be arranged to discuss children’s progress more in-depth. Each child has an online Learning Journey to which parents can log in, they can view activities, next steps and progress. Children’s progress is tracked following the Early Years Foundation Stage Outcomes which are reviewed regularly and shared with parents through summative assessment. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Information will be shared via informal chats at drop off and collection Photos and messages will be sent during the day Regular meetups and home visits will also take place How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? For those with access issues, the setting can be accessed via the back of the property which is on one level. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact me to discuss the way forward What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I will continue to add to my SEN training portfolio

description: Sing and Sign Baby Signing classes are perfect for babies from 6 weeks to around two and a half years. Babies use all kinds of signs and gestures as a natural part of learning to talk. local_offer: Our SEND Department caters for a variety of needs with a specialism for hearing Impairment. https://www.swr.school/Special-Needs/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The school promotes a mainstream inclusive education for all students, empowering everyone to achieve. We aim to promote a positive learning environment for all students and aim for them to be active and independent learners. We also strive to ensure students are prepared for their transition onto further education and adulthood. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Teachers and support assistants receive on-going training to further their professional development. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have a wide range of options when it comes to communicating with parents. Regular email or phone communication, and /or 1:1 meetings. A representative from the SEND department is always present at parent information evenings. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Information is reported home termly to parents on Arbour. This includes information of academic progress and attitude to learning. For SEND students, this may also include a meeting to discuss actions taken and next steps. The annual review for students with EHCP's is also used to look in detail at academic progress and review this alongside the outcomes on the EHCP. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our school is DDA compliant in terms of its building and services throughout 90% of the school. We provide a good acoustic environment for students with a hearing impairment and continue to develop acoustic treatment for ceilings in classrooms which are currently untreated. Students with a physical disability are able to access lessons upstairs if suitable to their needs, as there is lift access and staff are EVAC trained in the case of an emergency. Where it is not suitable for a student to use the EVAC equipment, students have access to ground floor classrooms as an alternative.
