How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? The nursery has a designated special educational needs co-coordinator who works closely with all parents and carers to draw upon their knowledge and expertise to support the planning of provision for their child. The setting will support families sensitively and in confidence, developing individual Education and health care plans. The nursery will assess and observe children when they join, to ensure they are meeting their expected milestones and we will have meetings with parents to discuss the children's stages of development. When parents are registering and inducting, there is a discussion, to find out about the children. This gives the opportunity to discuss any concerns the parents may have about the children's development and health. We assess children using tapestry which is an online programme that tracks children’s development, all of the information is securely uploaded and the parents have access to this via e-mail, there are opportunities for them to contribute to this by adding their own observations and comments about their children. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parent involvement is of primary importance; you will be kept fully informed throughout, regular meetings to discuss your child’s progress and support plan, we value your expertise on your child as you know them best. We will invite you to meet with any outside agencies who may be involved with your child’s developmental needs when they visit the setting. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The nursery has been purpose-built to accommodate all users, it is a single storey setting which is fully accessible to all, this includes our garden which has soft surfaces and a grassed area that will keep everyone safe. We have a separate sensory room, with soft floor area, calming bubble tube, lights, fibre optics and resources to support a calm sensory learning environment. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We pride ourselves on working closely with a wide range of schools and settings. When moving to school we will accompany the children on their transition visits where possible, we invite the schools into the nursery to meet the children in a familiar environment to ensure the children are given the best opportunities to move with the least amount of disruption. local_offer: I aim to provide the best home learning and nurturing environment for any child. I aim to give all families opportunities to access care for their children, whatever their needs. Learning through play is key in my setting: the age and stage of the child is considered as well as their individual needs to ensure they enjoy their time with us. I have experience of caring for children with Dyspraxia and ADHD, and am keen to work closely with both parents and other professionals to support each child to reach their full potential. I work in partnership with parents, priding myself on sharing information about their child’s learning, development and progress on a regular basis in a manner which suits them. I ask parents to share information about their child’s likes and dislikes, the activities which they find difficult and those which they enjoy the most. I aim to ensure that activities are extended to support children to meet their potential within the setting and share ideas with parents for use at home. I observe and assess all children and where there is a particular need, I offer support in the preparation and implementation of a joint action plan for the child. With parents’ permission I may involve other services. As with all registered Childminders in Buckinghamshire, I have a Key Contact within the Early Years Service, from whom I can access advice and information. They are happy to answer my questions or signpost to other appropriate services. Professionals are welcome to meet the child at our setting if parents wish. I am keen to expand my knowledge and expertise. I will undergo further training when it is required. My home is accessible to most children and families. I am on a regular bus route for those needing public transport. I have somewhere suitable for the children to rest when needed and would always discuss options with parents. As I have my own children, I have links with several local schools and pre-schools who work closely with me in supporting children through transitions. When children arrive I encourage families to complete an ‘All about Me’ sheet, provide family photos and any special comforters (regardless of age of the child). I am happy for practitioners from other settings to come and visit us before a child starts to help them to settle (whether new to me or moving on elsewhere). I encourage parents to have some ‘settling in visits’ with their child. I am constantly aware of the need for flexibility within my setting to ensure that children’s needs can be met. I access training as necessary. I keep updated with new guidance from the Local Authority and use their website regularly. name: Odyssey PDA Support Group
description: Odyssey PDA is a peer-to-peer support group for parents / caregivers of individuals (both adults and children) diagnosed with, or thought to have, the autism profile of Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA). The group is co-ordinated by Hilary and provides an opportunity to meet informally, share experiences, and positively support each other. The group can’t promise to solve problems but everyone who joins is willing to listen and share ideas. Professionals interested in learning more about this profile are also warmly welcomed. The group originally started in July 2015 as the South Bucks PDA Support Group. Membership has grown to over 600 families and professionals but over a much wider area than South Bucks, so in September 2025 the name changed to Odyssey PDA to better reflect the wider membership area, and highlight support shared throughout a PDA journey. Members generally live within Buckinghamshire, Berkshire, and Oxfordshire but we also have several families from other neighbouring counties and beyond! As well as ‘drop-in’ coffee mornings, family events and in-person or on-line evening sessions are organised. Local speakers are invited to attend some meetings and training seminars are organised when needed to help families and professionals learn more about this profile of autism. There is also a weekly member newsletter that shares information, blogs, tips, links and details about local and national activities. As well as week-day meetings in High Wycombe, South Bucks, Milton Keynes and Oxford there are also specific opportunities for carers who support a PDA adult to meet and share experiences together either on a Saturday or on-line. For more detailed information about meetings, the support group or a PDA profile please see our website. Please note that although Hilary is a serving Trustee of the PDA Society this group is not directly connected to the charity itself as they do not run their own support groups and only signpost to groups supporting PDA families. This is a peer-to-peer support network although information and resources about PDA are always shared from the PDA Society.

name: Odyssey PDA Support Group
description: Odyssey PDA is a peer-to-peer support group for parents / caregivers of individuals (both adults and children) diagnosed with, or thought to have, the autism profile of Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA). The group is co-ordinated by Hilary and provides an opportunity to meet informally, share experiences, and positively support each other. The group can’t promise to solve problems but everyone who joins is willing to listen and share ideas. Professionals interested in learning more about this profile are also warmly welcomed. The group originally started in July 2015 as the South Bucks PDA Support Group. Membership has grown to over 600 families and professionals but over a much wider area than South Bucks, so in September 2025 the name changed to Odyssey PDA to better reflect the wider membership area, and highlight support shared throughout a PDA journey. Members generally live within Buckinghamshire, Berkshire, and Oxfordshire but we also have several families from other neighbouring counties and beyond! As well as ‘drop-in’ coffee mornings, family events and in-person or on-line evening sessions are organised. Local speakers are invited to attend some meetings and training seminars are organised when needed to help families and professionals learn more about this profile of autism. There is also a weekly member newsletter that shares information, blogs, tips, links and details about local and national activities. As well as week-day meetings in High Wycombe, South Bucks, Milton Keynes and Oxford there are also specific opportunities for carers who support a PDA adult to meet and share experiences together either on a Saturday or on-line. For more detailed information about meetings, the support group or a PDA profile please see our website. Please note that although Hilary is a serving Trustee of the PDA Society this group is not directly connected to the charity itself as they do not run their own support groups and only signpost to groups supporting PDA families. This is a peer-to-peer support network although information and resources about PDA are always shared from the PDA Society.

It is important to be mindful, when deciding whether or not to assess a student, of the JCQ requirements with regard to Access Arrangements in exams as discussed below. In some cases, this might necessitate a delay in the assessment process. A published process for determining a student’s individual needs is available to staff and parents. name: Specialist Teacher Support
description: As part of our Tiered Approach to supporting schools, Specialist Teachers will be able to provide advice for early intervention for pupils on SEND Support and for those with EHC plans. To Access Specialist Teacher Support please book an advice session using the appropriate link on our website. These sessions include Cognition and Learning, Autism Support, and Language Support. Each session provides half an hour, of support for an individual school or setting and if necessary a follow-up visit will be arranged to provide further advice and support for meeting the needs of individual pupils. Prior to an advice session, we will ask you to complete a proforma outlining your needs which allows us to best prepare for the meeting. Feel free to discuss an individual pupil’s needs (anonymously) or a range of school-based approaches which may help across a number of learners. Advice Sessions are free to book. In order to allow fair access please do only book one session at a time although you are, of course, more than welcome to attend again if needed. If there are no sessions available or you are having trouble booking onto a session please contact the team by email and we will ensure we find you a suitable session. Please note advice sessions are primarily for Aylesbury Area Schools. Please contact your local area hub team (Chiltern and South Bucks or Wycombe) for SEND support requests in other areas.

name: Speech Link Multimedia Ltd | Speech and Language Service for Schools
description: Speech and Language Link empower SENCos, teachers, and Teaching Assistants in their work with speech, language, and communication needs (SLCN) to ensure that every child is supported in realising their full potential. We do this through our range of online, speech and language packages which include assessments and interventions, and staff training and support. Each of our packages is tailored to a different age range, from reception to year 9. Our packages, created by our in-house team of speech and language therapists (SaLTs), are available to schools via annual subscriptions. The assessments are standardised and the 1:1 and small-group interventions accompanied by video guides presented by our SaLTs. Our SaLTs are contactable throughout the year via our Help Desk for direct support on using our assessments and interventions. Our packages are universal in that they support schools and their SaLT teams by providing a quick and easy way to assess all students. This enables early identification of speech and language communication needs (SLCN) and ensures that no student, even those with milder difficulties, falls under the radar and that those identified with severe needs, receive timely SaLT referrals. Our interventions and whole-class teaching strategies and lesson plans are designed around a ‘whole-school approach’, to develop the speech, language and communication skills and raise the attainment of all students, especially those who would not usually meet the SaLT referral criteria. Speech and Language Link’s aim is for all schools to have access to up-to-date SLCN information and resources for staff and families. In addition to our packages, we offer SLCN information and advice via our termly magazine ‘The Link’, a monthly newsletter, blog-posts and termly staff training webinars. Find out if your school subscribes to one of our packages and how you can access our home-practice resources for families.
organisation: Speech Link Multimedia Ltd | Speech and Language Service for Schools Schools use our online serviced packages, Language Link and Speech Link, to identify and support children with mild to moderate speech or language difficulties. The assessments, resources and support are designed by speech and language therapists and specialist teachers. We know that the best indicator of how a child will cope with school is their understanding and use of spoken language. The standardised assessment identifies pupils with difficulties understanding core language skills. Over 160,000 children were screened in 2017/18 using our packages. Identified pupils receive a targeted programme of interventions. The classroom strategies, small group interventions and 1:1 supplementary teaching sessions make the best use of a TA's time and expertise. Teacher engagement ratings and parent and pupil views support evidence of improvement, essential for Ofsted and the Pupil Premium. For a week’s free trial, visit our website, email, or call. Speech Link in Buckinghamshire Speech Link is a project which will be launching in the autumn term and will be in schools supporting 5 to 7-year-olds over the next academic year. It is a programme that can support in the assessment and provision of children with speech language and communication needs, jointly commissioned by education and health here in Buckinghamshire, enabling schools to identify need and support children as early as possible. The programme has been used by several other Local Authorities, producing good outcomes and tracked progress has come from this, indicating that this will be beneficial. Developed by Speech and Language Therapists, the SpeechLink support packages provide a screening tool and intervention resources for use in the classroom and indicate the need for further support when required. liz.isaac@speechlink.co.uk https://speechandlanguage.info/

The nursery was initially managed by the RAF and is now supported by Spring - Action for Children. Currently, over 54 families access our nursery. Each room has direct access to outdoor spaces, including a covered outdoor area and a large open outdoor play space. local_offer: St. Andrew’s Playgroup welcomes all children and their families and is committed to meeting the needs of all children through fully inclusive practices that promote and value diversity and difference. We strive to meet the individual needs of all the children in the playgroup. providing opportunities to develop children’s emotional, physical, social and intellectual capabilities. This is made possible by operating at a higher adult ratio than is legally required.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? St. Andrew’s Playgroup treats every child as an individual with different/specific needs. It is our aim to provide a nurturing environment which enables all children to thrive and reach their potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We have a Level 3 SENDCo who has undertaken additional SEND training and keeps up-to-date with current policies and procedures by attending courses and termly Early Years SENDCo Briefings. They also have a Level 2 British Sign Language qualification. All staff have had in house Speech & Language training and basic Makaton training. We have lead practitioners for Positive Behaviour, English as an Additional Language and Cultural Diversity. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? A strong setting/family relationship is very important to us and is paramount to the children’s learning and development. The staff at our playgroup are always available at the start and end of every session and we welcome parents/carers to use this time to discuss any issues or concerns. The children have detailed records which can be accessed at any time and progress and targets are shared with parents/carers termly. Each term we have time allocated for consultations when we share information regarding progress and offer ideas about how the next steps can be supported at home. Parents are regularly invited to spend time in our playgroup to give them an insight into what and how their children are learning and to join us in celebrating special events. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The staff at our playgroup are always available at the start and end of every session and we welcome parents/carers to use this time to discuss any issues or concerns. Every child is monitored closely by their key person who tracks their development and progress through the cycle of “assess, plan, do, review”. Their individual records can be accessed at any time and progress and targets are shared with parents/carers termly. Each term we have time allocated for consultations when we share information regarding progress and offer ideas about how the next steps can be supported at home. Tracking a child's progress highlights if a child is struggling in any areas of development. For these children the key person and SENDCo work together to provide appropriate additional support. At this point the setting works together with the families to provide a co-ordinated approach with advice and support from other professionals when necessary. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The main hall is fully accessible by wheelchair and there is a slope to the garden from the car park. The hall also has an accessible toilet. The large hall has sound boards which provide good acoustics for hearing aid wearers. We use Makaton, visual timetables and visual prompts to assist children with the daily routine. Dual language books are shared with families of children with English as Additional Language to aid communication. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Before starting with us each child/family is invited to an induction session or visited at home. During this time information is shared between the family, key person and (where necessary) the SENDCo. This allows us to plan/prepare effectively from the outset. We provide each family with an induction booklet designed to share with their child including information about their Key person and the playgroup. We work closely with each family to develop a settling routine to match the child’s needs. We use a visual timetable and picture cards to prepare children for transitions within the playgroup and to prepare the children for any events or changes in routines. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? All staff will continue to access training in order to update their knowledge and understanding of how all children learn, whatever their ability, and how they can be supported effectively. The SENDCo will continue to attend all Liaison Group Meetings and any relevant training and then cascade the information to all staff. All staff will gain training required to support a specific child with additional health or development needs as necessary. We continually review our learning environment and update our resources to cater for the needs of all the children in our care.

local_offer: St Bernard’s Catholic Grammar School is committed to upholding its Mission in relation to students who have Special Educational Needs and Disabilities. The school has a number of students with a range of diagnosed conditions and a highly-effective SEND team which offers specialist individual and group support. In line with our school policy and the Children and Families Act 2014 (Code of Conduct), these students are supported in classrooms by their normal subject teachers, who are trained in appropriate strategies by the school’s SENCo. A small number of students have a Specialist SEN Teaching assistant as part of their Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). The school is a selective state school, and as such is bound by its admissions arrangements to admit only those students who have achieved the eligibility score in the Slough Consortium 11+ examination. This means that the school can only consider for admission children who have achieved in the 11+ test, irrespective of whether the school is named on their Statement. Should a statemented (EHCP) student (whose statement names St Bernard’s Catholic Grammar School) achieve in the 11+ test, then their application will be given priority over all other students for admission. http://www.st-bernards.slough.sch.uk/381/special-education-needs What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? local_offer: The local authority allocates ‘notional’ funding through the school’s budget. All other children’s needs will be met through the school budget and reasonable adjustments will be made in line with The Equalities Act 2010. Where a child’s needs are impacting on their learning, and reasonable adjustments alone are no sufficient, an ‘SEN Support Plan’ will be put in place. Only children with the most complex and long term needs, which impact on learning, will require an ‘Education, Health and Care Plan’. For children whose needs are not long term but do have an impact on their learning and cannot be met within the school’s budget, ‘High Needs Funding’ may be applied for. The funding is spent to meet the needs of the children through class teacher and Special Needs Co-ordinator (SENDCo) time, educational Psychologist, Teaching Assistant support time, Specialist Teacher Service (STS), Health Services, In-service training (INSET) and purchase of resources. The Head Teacher delegates the responsibility of the SEND budget to the SENDCo; spending is mostly based on the needs of the children and priority areas identified by the Senior Leadership Team and set out in the School Improvement Plan. In the first instance class teachers take responsibility for ensuring that pupils with Special Educational Needs have full access to the curriculum. They provide suitably differentiated work for the pupils, and any adapted equipment required. With guidance from the class teacher, the TAs assist in delivering work programmes for the children. local_offer: Teachers are responsible and accountable for the progress and development of all the pupils in their class. All pupils will be provided with high quality teaching that is differentiated to meet the needs of all learners. Teachers refer to the Ordinary Available Provision Document (Buckinghamshire) when planning the provision for children in their class. Pupils with a disability will be provided with reasonable adjustments to overcome any disadvantage experienced in schools and increase their access to the taught curriculum. Where it is decided during early discussion that special educational provision is required by a child, parents will be informed that the school considers their child requires SEN support and their partnership is sought to improve attainments. Risk assessments are carried out and procedures are put in place to enable all children to participate in all school activities. The school ensures it has sufficient staff knowledge to ensure that no child with SEND is excluded from any school provided activity. Adaptations to the curriculum and learning environment may include the following: • adapting resources and staffing; • using aids such as coloured overlays, visual timetables; • differentiating our curriculum by teaching style, lesson content, grouping and 1:1 work; • differentiating our teaching, for example, by giving longer processing times, pre teaching of key vocabulary, or by reading instructions aloud. The support we provide consists of a four-part process. • Assess • Plan • Do • Review This is a continuous cycle to enable the provision to be refined and revised as the understanding of the needs of the pupil grows. This cycle enables the identification of those interventions which are the most effective in supporting the child to achieve good progress and outcomes. Teachers will use a range of assessments and gather information on progress which feeds into the review cycle. The class teacher will plan SEN provision, in conjunction with the SENDCo and detail it on the child’s provision plan, which is a part of the SEN Support Plan. The Support Plan is constructed by the SENDCo with input from parents and class teacher. The provision plan is agreed with the parents to reinforce or contribute towards progress at home. Outcomes may be measurable, include small steps which are planned to be achievable, as well as longer term ambitious outcomes. Provision and outcomes are reviewed termly, in discussion between parents and teachers. Views of parents and adults working with the child are sought and views of the child are also encouraged. We support all children with their social and emotional development, through a carefully planned program of PSHE lessons along with additional methods which are personalized to the needs of the child. For example, our ELSA works with individuals or groups as appropriate, with areas such as friendship, bereavement, homework support, anger management and self esteem. There are opportunities to be part of a social and talking group or for further individual talking time with children and parents as necessary. Regular visits from the PAT dog take place in the SNUG. Our Anti-bullying Policy can be found on the school website. https://www.stjohnsce.org/send-and-mental-health/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At St John's we aim to provide an inclusive education for all. We encourage and support children to recognise their strengths and barriers to learning, assisting them to develop useful strategies with a positive mindset. These strategies help children to overcome challenges, feel successful, and gain independence. We aim to build positive and collaborative relationships, working together, signposting and supporting parents as required. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? When a new pupil with SEND joins St John's, either before or after an initial settling in period, the SENDCo will aim to meet parents to discuss individual needs. There will be a termly opportunity to meet SENDCo / Class teacher, and review provision. Where a pupil has an EHCP, an Annual Review will be arranged. Provision is detailed on an Individual Support Plan. Parents are also invited to contact the SENDCo outside of these times. Parents evenings are held in the Autumn and Spring Terms and a School Report is issued in the Summer Term. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Some ramps for wheel chairs are provided, although some changes of level in EYFS. We have an additional, low arousal room called The Snug which has been designed to be a calm space for individuals or small groups of children. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact the School Office Contact Bucks admissions. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: We are an inclusive school that welcomes and celebrates diversity. We have children from 2 to 7 years old. We believe that every child is entitled to an education which enables them to fulfil their potential and become independent and confident learners. All staff are committed to working together with all members of the school community. We pride ourselves on having a caring, understanding team who look after all of our children. We believe that by nurturing the whole child they are able to thrive spiritually, morally, socially and academically. We offer support to parents and carers of children with SEND and access additional support from other professionals as appropriate. Termly SENCO Liaison Group meetings provide us with up to date information on policy and procedures. https://www.stjosephsrcinfant.bucks.sch.uk/our-school/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to prove an education that enables all pupils, whether they are identified as SEND or not, to fulfill their potential and to enable them to thrive spiritually, morally, socially, and academically. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The Head Teacher is the Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Co-ordinator for class teachers, and the Deputy headteacher SENDCo is the CPD Co-ordinator for teaching assistants. Both roles ensure that all staff have the skills they require to support pupils. Medical training to support pupils with medical care plans such as epilepsy, asthma and Epi-pen training is up to date in line with the needs of our current pupils. Teaching assistants across the school have attended Speech and Language webinars, training to supporting those with ASD and emotional regulation training (calming kittens) over the past academic year. SENDCo is Step On train the trainer and has held in-house training with teachers and teaching assistants. All school staff have had the following recent training: Read, Write Inc, Attachment and Trauma training, Step on Positive Behaviour Management Training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Strong parent partnerships are important to St Joseph’s. We welcome parents to Stay and Play sessions, celebration events, ‘book looks’ and seasonal celebrations such as our Nativity concerts, Easter Bonnet Parade and Sports Day. Pupil progress meetings are held with the Head Teacher, SENDCo, and class teacher to discuss strategies to support the class and individual pupils to succeed. Class teachers will assess pupils using national standards which we attend regular training on within the Local Authority. We invite parents to discuss pupil’s progress and their next steps/targets as part of Parents’ Evening. Where necessary, this may include the SENDCo alongside the class teacher. In Pre-School, parents are invited to parent meetings at the end of each term where we share what learning is seen at home and Pre-School. We will support parents’ understanding of the curriculum through Parent Information Events such as Phonics Information meeting and Year 2 SATS Assessment meeting. We value day to day informal chats, communication by email and telephone calls, to ensure the wellbeing of all children. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Strong parent partnerships are important to St Joseph’s. We welcome parents to Stay and Play sessions, celebration events, ‘book looks’ and seasonal celebrations such as our Nativity concerts, Easter Bonnet Parade and Sports Day. Pupil progress meetings are held with the Head Teacher, SENDCo, and class teacher to discuss strategies to support the class and individual pupils to succeed. Class teachers will assess pupils using national standards which we attend regular training on within the Local Authority. We invite parents to discuss pupil’s progress and their next steps/targets as part of Parents’ Evening. Where necessary, this may include the SENDCo alongside the class teacher. In Pre-School, parents are invited to parent meetings at the end of each term where we share what learning is seen at home and Pre-School. We will support parents’ understanding of the curriculum through Parent Information Events such as Phonics Information meeting and Year 2 SATS Assessment meeting. Parents of children with SEND are invited to contribute to recording systems such as Learning Plans (which contain the Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) cycles). As appropriate, when professionals such as speech and language therapists visit the setting, we invite parents for joint discussion. We are available at each session to discuss any concerns regarding a child’s learning and/or well-being. We support regular communication with parents. We share what children have enjoyed and taken part in at school and parents are invited to contribute to this by adding what progress they are seeing at home. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We regularly review the school environment to reflect the needs of our children. To benefit all children and especially children with sensory sensitivities, we have developed low arousal areas where minimising distraction supports focused play and learning. All rooms have blinds fitted to enable us to adjust the light levels and the building has wheelchair access as well as an adult disabled toilet facility. We work with professionals and parents to access specialist equipment that may be required and to make additional adaptations where reasonable and practical. For example this might include enhancing our sensory area or purchasing specific resources. The school is on a split level site and several steps access the Key Stage 1 classrooms and the hall. The steps have child level handrails and level access is available around the outside of the building to these lower areas. • We have an accessibility plan, which is available to view. • We have developed a sensory room and areas to support children regulate their emotions How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? local_offer: St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School provides inclusive, broad, and balanced educational opportunities in order to meet the differing needs of the pupils attending. St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School’s SEND Policy: At St Joseph’s School children are identified as having SEND through a variety of ways including: • Liaison with Early Years settings • Liaison with feeder schools • Child performing below age expectations or not making expected progress relevant to their starting points • Concerns raised by parents • Concerns raised by the class teacher • Liaison with external agencies • Medical diagnosis Progress against targets is measured and discussed termly with staff and parents. St Joseph’s School SEND policy can be accessed from the school website. St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School’s approach to teaching pupils with SEND: The teachers at St Joseph’s School teach using ‘Quality First Teaching’ practices; all children in the class are taught by the teacher, who ensures that effective differentiation and targets are personalised for each child. The teacher is responsible for tracking the children’s progress which is monitored by the SENDCo. Children with SEND identified through the processes stated above and requiring additional and/or specific intervention are placed on the School’s SEND list. Appropriate provision is planned for the children delivered through specific targets, small group work, or access to programmes devised by external agencies as necessary. The social and emotional well-being of pupils is of paramount importance. To ensure this, all children have access to quality PSHE and strong pastoral support systems. St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School’s Facilities to include pupils with SEND Appropriate adjustments are made to accommodate the needs of individual children following guidance from specialists. St Joseph’s School Single Equality Scheme and Plan can be accessed from the school website. St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School’s SEND Training: Appropriate Continued Professional Development is provided to staff in order to support the needs of SEND children within our school. Specialist expertise is obtained by the school by engaging professional advice as necessary. St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School’s Family consultation: Parents, carers, and children are central to the School’s SEND processes and procedures. They are kept fully informed about their child’s targets and progress through:- • parent consultation meetings with the class teacher and/or SENDCo • support plans • provision maps • reports from outside agencies Where appropriate, children are involved in their target setting and reviewing their learning with the teacher and,or SENDCo. St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School’s Partnerships: Following identification of need, appropriate support services are engaged to meet the needs of pupils and their families. St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School’s Transfer to other educational establishments: Meetings for teachers, children, and parents are arranged between educational settings as appropriate to ensure a smooth transition. Educational establishments may include: • Early Years settings • Local schools • The Oaks Pupil Referral Unit • Special schools St Joseph’s Catholic Primary School contact details for support: Parents are informed of the contact details of any support service or education providers through 1:1 discussion as appropriate. local_offer: We are an inclusive school that welcomes and celebrates diversity. We have children from 2 – 7 years old. We believe that every child is entitled to an education which enables them to fulfil their potential and become independent and confident learners. All staff are committed to working together with all members of the school community. We pride ourselves on having a caring, understanding team who look after all of our children. We believe that by nurturing the whole child they are able to thrive spiritually, morally, socially and academically. Termly SENCO Liaison Group meetings provide us with up to date information on policy and procedures. https://www.stjosephsrcinfant.bucks.sch.uk/our-school/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are an inclusive school that welcomes and celebrates diversity. We have children from 2 – 7 years old. We believe that every child is entitled to an education which enables them to fulfil their potential and become independent and confident learners. All staff are committed to working together with all members of the school community. We pride ourselves on having a caring, understanding team who look after all of our children. We believe that by nurturing the whole child they are able to thrive spiritually, morally, socially and academically. We offer support to parents and carers of children with SEND and access additional support from other professionals as appropriate. Termly SENCO Liaison Group meetings provide us with up to date information on policy and procedures. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The Head Teacher is the Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Co-ordinator for class teachers, and the SENDCo is the CPD Co-ordinator for teaching assistants. Both roles ensure that all staff have the skills they require to support pupils. Medical training to support pupils with medical care plans such as epilepsy, asthma and Epi-pen training is up to date in line with the needs of our current pupils. Teaching assistants across the school have attended Speech and Language webinars over the past academic year. SENDCo has training in Infant Language Link and has held in house training with teachers and teaching assistants. All school staff have had the following recent training: Read, Write Inc, Attachment and Trauma training, Step on Positive Behaviour Management Training Pre-School Training includes: Jo Stone: Early Year’s Qualification Level 3 completed July 2021/ SENCo Training 2017 / Makaton Introduction, 2021 / Autism Education Trust Training, 2022/ NAS Early Bird (Autism) / Autism in the mainstream setting, 2021 / ELKLAN training 2021 / Speech Language & Communication course with Speech & Language UK, January 2022 / Nuffield Language Intervention Training completed by all practitioners 2021 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? • Strong parent partnerships are important to St Joseph’s. We welcome parents to Stay & Play sessions, celebration events, ‘book looks’ and seasonal celebrations such as our Nativity concerts, Easter Bonnet Parade and Sports Day. • Pupil progress meetings are held with the Head Teacher, SENDCo and class teacher to discuss strategies to support the class and individual pupils to succeed. Class teachers will assess pupils using national standards which we attend regular training on within the Local Authority. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We invite parents to discuss pupil’s progress and their next steps/targets as part of Parents’ Evening. Where necessary, this may include the SENDCo alongside the class teacher. In Pre-School, parents are invited to complete observation slips to share what learning is seen at home. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We regularly review the school environment to reflect the needs of our children. To benefit all children and especially children with sensory sensitivities, we have developed low arousal areas where minimising distraction, supports focused play and learning. All rooms have blinds fitted to enable us to adjust the light levels and the building has wheel chair access as well as an adult disabled toilet facility. We work with professionals and parents to access specialist equipment that may be required and to make additional adaptations where reasonable and practical. For example this might include enhancing our sensory area or purchasing specific resources. The school is on a split level site and several steps access the Key Stage 1 classrooms and the hall. The steps have child level handrails and level access is available around the outside of the building to these lower areas. • We have an accessibility plan, which is available to view. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Our Pre-School team is highly qualified in Early Years Education through both qualification and experience. Across the school we have experience of meeting the needs of a wide range of children with SEND. Currently we have teachers and teaching assistants who have had training in the following areas: • speech and language development, Attention Autism, STEPS and STEP On training for managing behaviour, whole school training Attachment and Trauma In support of children with SEND we have liaised with a range of outside agencies, including the Buckinghamshire Early Year’s Service, Portage, Health Visitors, Speech and Language Therapists, Feeding Clinic, Occupational Therapists, Education Psychologists, Pupil Referral Unit and other Early Years settings. We access a range of online resources to support our service such as: Communication Carousel, Speech & Language UK, Autism Education Trust (AET), National Association for Special Educational Needs (NASEN) and SEND Gateway. Additionally we use advice session and access webinars from Children and Young Peoples Integrated Therapies (speech and language, physio and occupational therapy services). Staff attending termly SENCo meeting and training courses, cascade new information to the team to ensure knowledge is shared What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We continue to embed visual display resources across the school and Makaton to support children’s understanding. We continually reflect on our practice, review staff training and make adjustments wherever possible to include all children attending our school.

local_offer: We are an inclusive Nursery and welcome all children irrespective of their background or circumstances. If your child has special needs and you are considering applying for a place at our Nursery please make an appointment to come in and talk to us. if you would like more information about our SEN policies and procedures including who our SENCO is then please go to the main school website. We are a two-form entry mainstream primary school and can cater for a range of special needs. Although we have improved our accessibility greatly to cater for children with physical disabilities (provision of accessible toilets, removal of steps, wide corridors, removal of some doors) we still have parts of our school with narrower corridors. We urge any parents considering our school to arrange for a personal visit where we can discuss their child's needs and whether our school is the best school to meet them. https://www.stlouisrccschool.co.uk/key-information/sen/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? In the nursery, both the Lead Practitioners and SENCO have completed their SENCO courses and one attends the liaison groups to keep up to date with the latest information. Alongside the nursery SENCO we are able to liaise with the school's SENCO and gain invaluable advice from her, therefore giving us the greatest support for our children. The team has had autism training from a SEN advisor, speech and language support after these courses and new information gathered, we filter down to all our staff and into our staff meetings. The nursery have had training for Signs 4 Learning, PALS and Jigsaw PHSE. These are used with all our children and are valuable to those with SEND needs and EAL. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At St Louis nursery we believe parent partnership is key, we encourage an open communication between the parents and ourselves. During your admission process, we allow you to come in and view the nursery and ask any questions you may have or view our 360 degree photos on the main school website. We like our parents to be involved right from the start, you know your child best and are therefore able to tell us about your child, allowing us to plan and teach your child to their onw needs from the beginning. At the beginning of the year we have an induction period, where your child will experience several different sessions. The first of which would be with yourselves and you can get stuck into activities and meet your child's key person. Throughout the year we have several events for everyone to participate in (for example, Christmas songs and parents evening). We like to learn about outside professions and in normal times we welcome you in to teach us about your job or craft. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At the end of the day you will get verbal feedback from the teacher and we are able to speak with you for longer during a planned meeting in our office. We promote open communication between ourselves and parents. We hold two parent's evenings per year where we will update you on your child's progress but we have an open door approach and this will not be the first time you are approached about any issues. If your child has SEND or suspected, we will speak with you more frequently throughout the year and have regular meetings between yourself, the SENCO and key person to update you on your child's progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The school site is accessible from both entrances and our nursery is all on one level, with step free access and an open planned layout throughout, both indoors and outdoors allowing freedom to explore. Our nursery room connects straight out into our garden which is all one level, with a slight raised forest area to the side. We have low level sinks and toilets, as well as a disabled adult toilet situated in our building. In the room we have adjustable tuff trays which allow different types of activities to be available. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? When completing your admission form, you will have an 'All About Me' sheet and a SEN form to fill in, these will allow us to gain an insight into your child's current development. Through this we can connect with parents and previous settings to provide us with information to create the smoothest transition for each child. All children will be invited to join us in two weeks of settle sessions where they will be joining in with all the different aspects of our setting. This will allow them to feel comfortable in their new surroundings and promote the best start to their nursery journey. Any form of transition for a child can be difficult, regardless of their development and therefore we want to make it an enjoyable experience. Not only is this for the children but also the families, this allows for them to get to know us and begin our partnership. they can begin to build a relationship with their key person and open this line of communication. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are also striving to further our practice through new training and involving our staff to build on their own professional development, which would also benefit the children. At St Louis nursery we aim to be inclusive and accommodating to all children, allowing them to have the most beneficial time spent with us and helping them to develop at their own pace.

local_offer: We are an inclusive school; we welcome and celebrate diversity. All staff believe that children having high self-esteem is crucial to a child’s well-being. We have a caring and understanding team looking after our children which includes Teachers, Teaching Assistants, and non-teaching staff. All work within class is pitched at an appropriate level of challenge to ensure that all children are able to access a broad and balanced curriculum according to their specific needs. Typically this might mean that in a lesson there would be three different levels of work set for the class, however, on occasions this can be individually differentiated. The benefit of this type of differentiation is that all children can access a lesson and learn at their level. Children who have similar identified needs (for example a specific need in Maths or Reading or Social Skills) may also be taught in smaller groups, sometimes by a Teaching Assistant, but always under the direction of a Teacher. These small group provisions are a highly effective way of addressing the very specific needs of a smaller group of children in both academic and social learning. If a child requires specialist equipment to help them access a broad and balanced curriculum, this can be provided by the school or as a part of the child’s EHCP. For example, an Occupational Therapist may recommend equipment such as a wobble cushion or desk slope to help a child overcome sensory or physical needs. Class Teachers (in close collaboration with their phase team) have the principal role in the planning and delivery of appropriately differentiated teaching for the children with SEND in their class. They play a key role in the school’s procedures for pupil assessment and are involved in the analysis of the data of pupils with SEND. They use this data to inform their planning across the wider curriculum to ensure that all lessons recognise the learning needs of all pupils. Where the pupil is on the special needs register, the Class Teacher discusses the range of additional support available with the SENDCo and will be instrumental in the drawing up of, implementation of and monitoring/assessment of any SSPs and EHCPs. The school also employs Teaching Assistants to support the Class Teachers to deliver effective whole class teaching as well as the SENDCo in delivering learning programmes to children with SEND throughout the school. They are deployed across the school to support in lessons and to work with individual children and with small groups on very specific intervention programmes. They meet regularly with the SENDCo and Class Teachers to plan and review and to adapt the learning programmes they are delivering if necessary. Their observations will form a key part of evidence for any SSP or EHCP. The Teaching Assistants run a wide variety of provisions (under the direction of the SENDCo) aimed at supporting the individual needs of the child. These include: Maths, Spelling, Reading, precision teaching, fine and gross motor skills, social skills and confidence building programmes. Where a child has an EHCP, the school may also employ a Teaching Assistant to work alongside that child in accordance with their plan. local_offer: As a school, we are constantly monitoring the children’s progress. Where children are experiencing difficulties, the following action will be taken. Some children may work their way through all the steps, where others may only need the first 3 or 4. 1) In the first instance, the class teacher will adapt the curriculum to make it accessible to the child – this could take the form of extra adult support from either the teacher or another adult or providing equipment such as numberlines or wordbanks to support the child. 2) If the child continues to experience difficulties, the teacher will discuss their concern with the child’s parent / carer and arrange for the SENDCo to come and observe the child so that a support plan can be put in place. 3) The SENDCo will work together with the class teacher to provide an Individual Provision Map (IPM) to provide extra support in the child’s area of need. This may take the form of individual or group work outside of normal lessons to help the child. These will be reviewed termly in conjunction with the parent / carer 4) If required, the SENDCo will talk to professionals such as Speech Therapists, Occupation Therapists (in the case of physical needs) or the Educational Psychologist to provide additional assessment / support 5) If none of the above steps seem to be providing the necessary support for the child, the school, with the parent / carer’s permission will apply to the Local Education Authority for an Educational Health Care needs assessment (EHC) (Formally known as “Statementing) 6) The Local Education Authority will assess the request for an Educational Health Care needs assessment and either agree to or decline the request. If the request is agreed, the Local Education Authority have 20 weeks to complete the request and issue its decision (either granting or declining an EHC Plan) 7) If the Local Education Authority do not grant an Educational Health Care Plan or agree to an Educational Health Care needs assessment, they must give their reasons for doing so. At this point, the parent has the right to appeal the decision. Facilities for the Disabled All schools are required to provide information about the arrangements for taking disabled pupils into the school, the steps taken to ensure they are treated on equal terms with other pupils and the facilities provided to help them with access to the school. As a Faith School, we are bound by the County's Admissions Policy, which ensures that there is no discrimination against pupils with disabilities. All disabled pupils are fully integrated into the school. The children with Statements of Special Educational Needs are only withdrawn for separate support when the lesson is of such a nature that they would not be able to access the learning. https://www.stmarysfarnhamroyal.org/page/?title=Policies&pid=22 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The main entrance of the school is accessible for someone in a wheelchair. As the school is on one level, it is easy to negotiate in a wheelchair. Children with a Statement of Special Educational Need or with an Education, Health and Care (EHC) plan naming St Marys Farnham Royal Church of England Primary School will always be offered places. If there are fewer applications than places available, all children will be offered places. If there is greater demand for admission than there are places available, the following criteria will be applied in the order set out below: 1 Looked-after children and children who were previously looked after, but ceased to be so because, immediately after being looked after, they became subject to an adoption, child arrangements or special guardianship order. (See Note 2) 2 Families who have exceptional medical or social needs that make it essential that their child attends St Marys Farnham Royal Church of England Primary School rather than any other. These needs must be fully supported by written evidence from the appropriate professional person involved with the family. (See Note 3) 3 Children with a normal home address (See Note 4) in the Ecclesiastical Parish of St Mary’s, Farnham Royal and with a sibling (see Note 5) on the roll of the school at the time of application or whose parent has accepted an offer of a place at the school and who is expected still to be in attendance at the time of entry to the school. 4 Children with a normal home address in the Ecclesiastical Parish of St Mary’s, Farnham Royal. 5 Children with a normal home address outside the Ecclesiastical Parish of St Mary’s, Farnham Royal and with a sibling on the roll of the school at the time of application or whose parent has accepted an offer of a place at the school and who is expected still to be in attendance at the time of entry to the school. 6 Other children. Proximity of the child’s home, as measured by the straight line distance (see Note 6) between the home and the school with those living nearer being accorded the higher priority, will serve to differentiate between children in criteria 1 to 6 should the need arise. In the event that two distance measurements are identical, the school will use random allocation to decide which child should be offered the place. The process will be conducted in the presence of a person independent of the school. St Mary’s Farnham Royal Church of England Primary School Page 3 of 8 All Other Admissions Admission to the school during the school year depends on whether or not there are places available. Year groups Reception - 6 at the school have 50 places. Applications for places at our school should be made to Buckinghamshire Council and not the school. Applications take up to 20 days to process. If there is a vacancy, and there is no child on the relevant waiting list with a higher priority (according to the over-subscription criteria 1-6 above), a place will be offered. In-year admissions or admissions at the beginning of school years other than Reception will only be considered by the Governing Body up to half a term [using the three term year] in advance of the desired date for entry. For example for entry in January, the application will not be considered until after the October half term break. local_offer: Within our setting, we aim that every student with identified SEND will have a package of support to meet their needs and the majority of students have their needs met by the School with the help of outside agencies and other specialists where necessary. This provision is “additional to, or otherwise different from, the educational provision made for pupils in their year.” (Code of Practice 2014). St.St. Mary’s recognises that SEND is a continuum and thus the Learning Support provision required will vary between individuals as their needs will be different. A student’s individual needs may best be met in the class within curriculum subjects, through appropriate differentiation; all subject teachers are responsible for catering for these needs and for supporting and monitoring progress accordingly. Teaching staff are supported in their lesson planning by the Learning Support Team and the student’s Provision Passport (drawn up by Learning Support) which gives recommendations for appropriate strategies that can be used in their lessons. This is reviewed and updated at each Key Stage, unless an update is required earlier. The SENDCO for Prep and the Head of the Preparatory Department liaise regarding learners who may need support. The SENDCO for Prep and the Head of the Preparatory Department liaise with class teachers on a termly basis to review the support and redirect it as necessary. It is sometimes deemed appropriate for learners in KS3 and KS4 to have a reduced curriculum, thus they are exempt from a specific subject/s. In those lessons they may receive additional learning support, work independently to complete tasks/work as directed or be given time for supervised private study. Prior to a learner being exempt from a subject, there must be consultation with the class teacher, Deputy Heads, Learning Support and parents, before final authorisation can be sought from the Headmistress. Learners in KS3 may be invited to attend small group Learning Support sessions, if they have an identified specific learning difference or need some additional help with their learning. These are run as a lunchtime ‘club’, usually in blocks and focus on specific study skills and multisensory learning strategies. https://stmarysschool.co.uk/school-information/policies/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? local_offer: Our Mission: We are committed to providing a happy, safe, and nurturing environment in the heart of Taplow Village. Encouraging our children to explore, learn and thrive through play. Our staff offers true team spirit enriching the outcomes for all children in our care.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim that all children will be supported to the best of our ability to make the best progress they can, relative to their stage of development. To ensure this happens, if appropriate, we will work with families to seek support from outside agencies and will implement recommended strategies according to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 3 Early Years SENCO, February 2026. Curiosity Programme Training, October 2025. Makaton Levels 1 and 2, March 2025. Making Sense of Autism, July 2024. Good Autism Practice, March 2024. SENCO Training, November 2023. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Volunteering, we welcome any parents to come in and do an activity with the children. Outings, we may ask some parents to come on trips. Events, most of our events parents and grandparents are invited to join. Committee, we are run by a committee which needs to be mainly existing parents. Always a great opportunity to get involved and help with the fundraising for the playgroup. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At St Nicolas Playgroup we are using Ovivio which is an online journal parents are able to access when they would like. The children's journals are updated regularly from the observations carried out in the setting and families are also able to update for practitioners to see what fun children have had over the weekend. We have drop-in mornings which is similar to a parents evening. This takes place in a morning session, we ask parents and children to come along for a short period where the practitioners can show you any reports or trackers that identify your children's progress through their time at playgroup. Ultimately we are always available to speak to parents/carers at any given day if there are concerns or enquiries on their children. We are happy to arrange meetings to discuss further if needed. For children with SEND we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents. Their short-term outcomes will be regularly monitored and parents are invited to be part of this review and planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist...) are visiting, we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have a 'free flow' setting. After registration, we open up all doors inside and outside and the children are able to move around where they would like. We have staff in all areas and abide by a staff to child ratio. Around our outdoor area, we have a gate that is secure to stop the children from going any further. We make some adaptions when we are trying to meet individual needs. To ensure the safety of some children we may keep some doors closed for a period of time. We also sometimes keep our top room as a quiet area and a place where we can have one-to-one interaction with individual children to help support their development. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? At St Nicolas Playgroup we work with the children and families on what they think will be the best transition for them. We believe that every child is unique. We will support the parents decision and will also advise what we may think will work. We have close relationships with the local schools and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We would like to attend more training and to provide more resources.

local_offer: Our children follow a curriculum that aims to engage, challenge, and inspire. Teachers differentiate lessons appropriately to meet the needs of all pupils including those with special educational needs. The learning environment is adapted by the class teacher to meet the needs of different learning styles and the teachers ensure that pupils are able to access the curriculum whatever their need may be. However some SEND children may need more individualised support which could include, but is not limited to: - Environmental changes in the classroom such as visual timetables, seating arrangements, wobble cushions, reading overlays, and desk supports. We also offer the use of laptops or iPads if this supports the child’s needs. - 1:1 teaching assistant support where appropriate - LSAs used for group and individual interventions – this provision is flexible and supports the child’s access to a broad and balanced curriculum - Small group or individually guided work with the class teacher or LSA - 1:1 RWI catch up sessions - Number shark to improve number work - Word shark to develop their spelling capability - 1:1 reading - The school purchases support from Specialist teaching services for individuals when required for example ASD specialist teaching, cognition and learning or occupational therapists. Professionals provide intervention that may take the form of assessing pupils, liaising with class teachers and the SENDco to meet the needs of SEND pupils, and staff training. - Social skills groups - Mindfulness groups - Individualised provision maps which detail individual targets for the children - Transition to secondary school support – the SENDco and the class teacher will liaise with the secondary school to ensure a verbal handover - Transition from nursery to primary school support – visiting the nursery to understand the child’s needs, a home visit to discuss the child’s needs with the parents and relevant meetings with the parents, agencies and SEND professionals. - In year transfer transition - class buddy provided to help the child settle, monitoring by the LSA and class teacher - Reasonable adjustments can be made for children with disabilities to ensure they are able to access the taught curriculum - Regular monitoring of SEND provision in the classroom by the SLT and the SENDco through learning walks, book scrutiny and data analysis to ensure high quality provisions are being made - Half termly reviews of provision maps to ensure the children are making progress For a very small percentage of pupils whose needs are significant and complex and the SEND support required cannot reasonably be provided from within the school’s own resources, a request will be made to the local authority where the child is resident to conduct an assessment of education, health and care needs. description: St Paul’s Nursery is situated in a self-contained building close to St Paul's C of E Combined School. It has a wide range of facilities both inside and out including a large nursery garden. The outside area benefits from adventure playground apparatus, a trim trail, mud kitchen, storytelling chair and reading, sand and water and building sheds. We admit children at the beginning of the term after their 3rd birthday. The aims of the nursery are to ensure: Your child is safe and happy Your child makes a gentle transition from home to Nursery We work in partnership with parents to create the best learning environment for your child We provide a broad and balanced curriculum through the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum - the learning environment included provision both indoors and out Children are encouraged to learn through play and first-hand experience Learning is tailored to the individual through close observation and monitoring by all the staff - topics and activities are planned around the interests and needs of each child
organisation: St Paul's CofE Combined School (Wooburn Green) St Paul's is located between the villages of Wooburn Green and Bourne End on a quiet housing estate. It benefits from extensive grounds with the countryside and a park nearby. The school has a caring ethos based upon Christian principles where children are encouraged to take responsibility for their learning and embrace challenge. Our experienced and dedicated staff are committed to providing a high-quality education for all pupils. We offer a well-balanced and stimulating curriculum that encourages children to develop a positive attitude to their learning. We aim for teaching and learning to be engaging, relevant and responsive to current events, bringing the world into the classroom. We set high standards and have high expectations for all our children both in their learning and behaviour. We strive to ensure that all cultures, faiths and backgrounds are embraced and children show respect for each other and the school. We aim to ensure our pupils develop enquiring minds and acquire the relevant skills, attitudes and knowledge, including a life-long love of learning, to prepare them as they progress in their education. We also encourage a healthy attitude towards physical activity, diet and emotional well-being. A wide range of extra-curricular activities is offered so that children can further develop their sporting, musical and artistic talents. Parents are encouraged to be closely involved in their child's education and we are fortunate to have a very supportive and active PTA. Governors at the school ensure that our aims and objectives are met through strategic planning and budgeting to guarantee high-quality resources and facilities for the children in our care. office@stpaulswooburn.school https://www.stpaulsschool.co.uk/

local_offer: Identifying Pupils: Children with SEND are identified using observations and speech and language screening tools from the SENCo and class teacher and, on occasion, external agencies such as Educational Psychologists will complete assessments of children, specific to their needs. Parents will also discuss any concerns they have with the class teacher and SENDCo. Pupils’ progress is also closely monitored and used as a basis for identifying needs. https://www.stpeterscofe.org/sendsenco/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? St Peter’s school family provides a safe, nurturing, environment, inspiring compassionate, confident, individuals ‘achieving with all their might’ through the joy of learning. With love and respect, we encourage pupils to flourish academically, emotionally, spiritually, and socially, rooted in our parish but confident of our place in the global community What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? This year the SENDCo has delivered training in adaptive teaching, the graduated approach, and early identification of needs, for example using scaffolding. Staff have accessed specific webinars on children that they support. Class teachers have received training on the plan, do, review process. Staff working with children with complex needs have completed training on strategies for autism, speech and language, and sensory integration from OTs, Specialist Teachers, and Speech and Language Therapists. Staff training is conducted by either the SENDCo or external professionals, depending on the needs of the children and the school. Educational Psychologist has trained teachers on developing working memory. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Children with SEND are identified using observations from the SENDCo and class teacher. Parents will also discuss any concerns they have with the class teacher and SENDCo. Parents of pupils who are on the SEND register, are invited to termly SEND plan reviews with class teachers. Pupils’ progress is also closely monitored and used as a basis for identifying needs. Pupils with an EHCP are also invited in half termly to review their SEND plan with the pupil attending (wherever possible), the class teacher and the SENDCo too. Parents attended a working memory workshop provided by school and an educational psychologist. The recording is available on the school website. Information is regularly advertised on the school SEND page. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents of children who are identified as having a special educational need are consulted throughout their child’s school journey. Class teachers and the SENDCo will meet with the parents/carers and the children to discuss support required. This is recorded and reviewed up to three times a year with the child and their parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The outdoor area is flat. There is a step to enter every classroom and all pupil areas of the school. However, there is accessible access through the staff door which is on one level. The interior of the school is on one level. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents can refer to the admission policy and school website. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Specialist expertise is obtained by consulting external agencies such as Bucks Council/private educational, speech and language therapists, specialist teachers, occupational therapists, paediatricians, the virtual school (in some children's cases), health visitors, and family resilience workers. External agencies will also conduct specific training upon request.

name: Stocklake Park School
description: Stocklake Park School is a secondary provision and is part of the Vale Federation of Special Schools. We offer educational provision for students with complex learning difficulties, from 11 to 19 years of age. The curriculum designed to build upon knowledge gained at primary level with specific focus on developing the skills students need in order to prepare for life after school. We are a relatively small school with just over 105 students, with class sizes of 6 to 10 students. The curriculum is organised around key themes and gives students the opportunity to experience and explore different subjects. Central to this is the development of communication and functional skills relating to real life situations. Students also engage in a range of creative arts and explore aspects of personal, social, moral, and emotional education. All our work is based in a belief in each student’s capacity to achieve and be the best they can be, and in enabling them to be as independent as possible. Our ethos is about encouraging students to value themselves and each other, maximising their enjoyment of learning, whilst developing self esteem and confidence. Students have access to a range of therapies, multi-agency professionals, and specialist staff, including speech and language therapists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and specialist teachers.
