local_offer: The Stoke Poges School is a two-form entry, maintained mainstream primary school; we do not have an additionally resourced provision (ARP) for pupils with SEN. In line with the SEN Code of Practice (2015), and Buckinghamshire’s Local Offer, provision for children with special educational needs at The Stoke Poges School focuses on meeting the needs of a child. This is offered as a graduated response to observed need and is not dependent on a formal diagnosis. Teachers use the Buckinghamshire model of Ordinarily Available Provision, within a framework of high-quality teaching and learning experiences, to remove barriers to learning, and support children who present with a range of needs across the four areas of SEN. Adhering to the SEND Code of Practice’s definition of SEN provision as that which is ‘additional to, or different from’ the general classroom offer, teachers make further adjustments using the ‘Support for Broad Areas of Need’ within Buckinghamshire’s Ordinarily Available Provision guidance. This equitable approach recognises that some children require bespoke reasonable adjustments to the curriculum and learning environment, as well as additional scaffolding from staff to access learning tasks, in order to fully achieve their potential over time. https://www.stokepoges.school/page/?title=SEND+%28Special+Educational+needs+and+Disability%29&pid=60 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are committed to providing an appropriate, high quality and challenging education for all pupils. We believe that every child is entitled to reach the highest level of personal achievement. We believe that educational inclusion embraces diversity and equal opportunities for all learners, regardless of their age, gender, ethnicity, religion, impairment, disability, attainment or background. The Stoke Poges School recognises the statutory definition of Special Educational Needs. The Stoke Poges School adheres to the Buckinghamshire model of ‘Graduated Approach Principles and Processes’, as we use our ‘best endeavours’ to support all learners, and to identify children with special educational needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The SENDCo. has a breadth of knowledge and experience regarding supporting pupils with SEND. She regularly shares her expertise with colleagues through individual or whole staff continuing professional development (CPD). Teaching and support staff have attended a range of training courses provided through the Specialist Teaching Service or Speech and Language Therapy Services. Many staff have also accessed further or more specific CPD training opportunities relating to supporting pupils with SEND, facilitated by specialists or external training providers. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are proud to work in partnership with children and their families, recognising that families know their children best, and ensuring a child’s voice is central to the process. We form a ‘Team Around the Child’. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? For children in receipt of SEN Support, or with EHCPs, we offer three meetings per year. We adhere to the model of 'Assess, Plan, Do, Review'. The meetings are an opportunity to review a child's progress against short term outcomes, and plan for next steps. Children and their families are invited to contribute to this process. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The school is compliant with the Equalities Act 2010. Entrances to the front and rear of the school are accessible by wheelchair and it is possible to gain access to the playground via a ramp through the memorial garden. Key Stage Two classrooms are located on the ground and first floors of the building and lift access is provided between the hall and the Year Three teaching areas on the ground floor. All doors have sufficient width to allow wheelchair access. The school building is spread over a wide area, which means that pupils located in the Key Stage One teaching area need to travel some distance to gain access to the main hall and dining room. A disabled toilet is located near the school’s administration office and a disabled parking bay is marked at the front of the school. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

description: Mixed-gender special school in Amersham for 11 to 19-years-olds. Stony Dean is a Special Educational Needs School for boys and girls. Pupils present with language, communication and interaction needs associated with moderate learning difficulties, autistic spectrum disorders and some sensory impairment, for instance, hearing or vision. We currently have 214 pupils on the roll, who all have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and receive teaching and specialist support in small groups.
organisation: Stony Dean School Stony Dean is an Outstanding Special School for boys and girls aged 11 to 19 years. Pupils present with language, communication and interaction needs associated with moderate learning difficulties, autistic spectrum disorders and some sensory impairment, for instance hearing or vision. We currently have 185 pupils on roll, who all have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and receive teaching and specialist support in small groups. Our objectives are to drive attainment and outcomes for pupils who attend SDS to achieve effective communication and interaction, Independence and Employability. These are at the core of the provision for our pupils from Year 7 through to the Sixth form. We aspire to provide a broad, balanced and flexible education which takes our pupils through their transition from primary school and prepares them for further education/training and future employment. Our curriculum and flexible programmes are tailored to reduce the impact of communication, interaction and cognition difficulties not only on academic performance and learning but also on social development and well-being. We pride ourselves on our expertise in recognising barriers to learning and providing support to pupils with Communication, Interaction, Cognition and Learning difficulties. Linked to our core aims, there is a strong focus on developing life skills for independence and preparation for employment where communication and interaction skills are developed. Most pupils follow a secondary school model with six lessons differentiated to an appropriate level to meet the individual needs of our pupils. The curriculum at Stony Dean is flexible and strives to incorporate the aspirations of all our pupils including pupils who find it challenging to learn in conventional ways, for example, our alternative curriculum, flexi-schooling and life skills-based courses (6th form) are examples of different ways in which the we aim to meet the needs of many of our pupils. Communication and interaction is a specialism for our school, and our speech and language therapy team form an integral part of the school. A “language-rich” environment, in which therapeutic strategies supporting Speech, Language and Communication Needs (SLCN) and Literacy development are fully integrated into the whole school day. Our highly-skilled, specialist and committed staff work closely with our pupils and their families to provide excellent outcomes. Utilising a range of interventions and programmes, staff create an environment conducive to learning and personal development. We strive to improve the quality of teaching and learning, through continued evidence-based training for staff. With realistic and viable employability high on the agenda, our dedicated sixth form and work-related learning teams strive for all our pupils in key stage 4 and 5, to gain employability skills through assisted, tailor-made work placements alongside high-quality vocational courses. We have clearly defined pathways offering suitable, industry-recognised qualifications and courses emphasising practical skills. The teaching of effective and appropriate communication skills in formal and informal, individual and group situations are driven throughout the school from KS3 to KS5. What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? With parents’ permission, we may involve other services. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our home is accessible to all children and families, our home is en route to local busses and trains. description: Sunnyside Rural Trust Day service for adults with Learning disabilities. We are a horticultural and social enterprise-based day service for adults with Learning disabilities and Dementia. We are based across 3 sites in Hemel Hempstead, Berkhamsted, and Northchurch. We offer training in horticulture, growing fruit, and veg, harvesting, cooking, jam, chutney making, woodwork, animal care, selling to the public on our market stall, and we run two cafe/farm shops. A typical day: From 8am onwards: You will arrive at the Sunnyside site between 9am and 9:30am. You may do this independently, or we may be able to offer minibus transport for which there is a charge. 9am to 9:30am: Make a drink and meet with the staff team who will tell you about the plans for the day and what work you will be doing; put on work boots and protective clothing. 9:30am to 11am: Activity, collect tools and equipment and carry out tasks with your team. 11am to 11:15am: Break. 11:15am to 12 midday: Activity. 12 midday to 1pm: Lunchtime you will need to bring a packed lunch; sometimes cooked lunch is available in Berkhamsted for a small charge. 1pm to 3pm: Activity. 3pm to 3:30pm: Break – Change out of work boots; prepare for leaving the site; travel home. Our mission statement: To provide services that will empower people to fulfill their potential for their own benefit and for the benefit of the wider community and environment. Our values: 1. We value our people and work as a team. We: - Listen to each other and show respect. - Empower people to reach their goals in a safe environment. - Support everyone in a fair and inclusive way. 2. We care deeply about our environment. We offer inventive and sustainable services to the community. We stand for: - Quality and stewardship - Enterprise - Reliability 3. We have a passionate, "can do" approach to our work. We are: - Resilient - Creative - Dedicated.

description: Supported Internships with Buckinghamshire College Group. Buckinghamshire College Group offers a wide range of high-quality supported learning opportunities for young people with learning difficulties and, or disabilities. These help to develop independence and skills, and provide a chance to prepare for the next step in life. The Aylesbury Campus provides a Supported Internship Study Programme designed to help young people with special educational needs to prepare for adulthood and to move forward into employment. Students must be in receipt of the Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Buckinghamshire Council has worked in close partnership with our Further Education Colleges and other supporting agencies to provide specialist provision linked with social care, health and supported living placements. For those that need it, we can offer a 5 day a week bespoke learning programme across the county, 1:1 support and small class groups. We believe that choosing to attend a local college can lead to a smoother transition from school into further learning and, at the end of the placement, from learning back into the local community. Please note due to safety Buckinghamshire cannot offer further education/college placements to those young people who present a danger to themselves or others. Individual support: If an Education Health Care Plan identifies a personal care need then the young person can be accompanied by their carer, or care can be provided by another agency subcontracted by the college. Communication: College staff and Sub Contracted agencies supported by Speech and Language Therapy provided by Oxford Health Foundation Trust. Many college staff are trained in a variety of techniques and strategies specific to the communication needs of the student in order to enable them to access the curriculum at college. The Speech and Language Therapy service support the use of and maintenance of low and high tech Augmentative Alternative Communication systems across the college context. College learning support staff are able to offer other methods of communication support including Dragon Software. All colleges are fully accessible, as are many of the community venues. Adapted software, equipment and Assistive Technology that is specified in a young person’s EHCP may be provided by the college given sufficient notice. Links to other departments: Young people benefit from an inclusive department with good links to other vocational departments within the colleges. Length: Programmes last 34 to 36 weeks. As the provision is bespoke with the learning, it can start in the home with travel training to college. A typical day runs from 9:30am to 3:30pm. Fees: All students with an EHCP will have their fees met by the local authority (aged 19 years or over). These fees include tuition, registration, exam fees and all other course-related costs. Transport: Some assistance with this may be available depending on your circumstances and the latest government funding position.
organisation: Buckinghamshire College Group Buckinghamshire College Group was formed from the merger between Aylesbury College and Amersham and Wycombe College in October 2017. We deliver our courses from three main campuses, in Amersham, Aylesbury and High Wycombe. With over 29 subject areas and 400 courses, each campus boasts recent investment in facilities, giving our students access to industry-standard workshops, software and equipment. Our Amersham Campus benefits from large workshop spaces where Art and Design students can spread their artistic wings, with facilities including Photography studios, print rooms and Fine Art studios. Come to an Open Day We hold several Open Day events at all three of our campuses throughout the year. Come along and explore the facilities, meet the students and speak to our tutors. See our upcoming events. admissions@buckscollegegroup.ac.uk https://www.buckscollegegroup.ac.uk/amersham

name: Susan Buhler
description: I have been childminding from my home for 19 years. I have no vacancies until Sept 26 (Tuesday to Thursday). In 2020 I moved outdoors and now operate 8am to 6pm in the woodlands at the bottom of our garden using a cabin for shelter in adverse weather conditions. We have slides, a treehouse, food tables, blackboards, bug hotels, wormeries, butterfly/ bee havens, digging pits, pallet houses and swings to name a few areas. A large lawned play area is adjacent to the woodland for active games and more traditional activities such as dressing up and creating beautiful art. Beyond our woodland area is a secure locked gate that offers direct access into Great Bois woods, Chesham Bois Village pond and Amersham town centre. We go on daily outings and host activities in the woods. There will be messy play, arts and crafts, music and outdoor cooking. In addition, there are a number of quiet areas made from bed frames and sandpits where children can relax. There are outdoor sleeping arrangements should naps be required. I hold a Level 3 qualification in Child Development, a Level 5 Early Years with Oxford Brookes University and a degree in Business Studies. I am also a qualified Forest School Leader. I am fully current on First Aid, Safeguarding , food hygiene and activity creation ideas. As an early years provider, I am registered with Buckinghamshire Council to provide 15 or 30 hours of funded childcare per week and attend Council network meetings twice a year. In this setting, your child will spend all day outdoors in all weather they will get dirty and wet but always be kept warm and well-fed. There is also a passion for music as a channel for learning. Ofsted inspections since registration in 2008 have consistently been 'outstanding’. The latest inspection July 2022 and again was ‘outstanding in all areas’ We have a Dog and a cat to add to the children's experience.

local_offer: I aim to work with parents and other settings to make the transition of children coming easy for both parents and the children. I will help children where possible with SEN needs to the best of my abilities and seek further training where necessary. My own daughter is awaiting an autism assessment, so I can understand the emotions a family goes through.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As with all registered Childminders in Buckinghamshire, I have a Key Contact within the Early Years Service, from whom I can access advice and information. They are happy to answer My questions or signpost to other appropriate services. Professionals are welcome to meet the child at My setting with parents consent. I am keen to expand My knowledge and expertise. I will undergo further training when it is required via Bucks or other training providers. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents, priding ourselves on sharing information about their child’s learning, development, and progress on a regular basis in a manner that suits them. I ask parents to share information about their child’s likes and dislikes, the activities which they find difficult and those which they enjoy the most. I aim to ensure that activities are extended to support children to meet their potential within the setting and share ideas with parents for use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children and where there is a particular need, we support the preparation and implementation of a joint action plan for the child. With parents’ permission, I may involve other services. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to most children and families. I am on a regular bus route for those needing public transport. I aim to find somewhere suitable for the children to rest when needed and would always discuss options with parents. My outdoor area is mainly laid to lawn it is accessible for most children however there are some small steps. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? As a family and a Childminder, we have links with several local schools and pre-schools who work closely with us in supporting children through transitions. When children arrive I encourage families to complete an ‘All About Me’ sheet, provide family photos, and any special comforters regardless of the age of the child. I am happy for practitioners from other settings to come and visit me before a child starts to help them to settle whether new to me or moving on elsewhere. I encourage parents to have some ‘settling in visits’ with their child and then their child on their own. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am constantly aware of the need for flexibility within my setting to ensure that children’s needs can be met. I access training as necessary, I keep updated with new guidance from the Local Authority and use their website regularly. I’m currently doing a diploma in ADHD.

name: Susan Lee
description: With over 22 years of experience in nurseries, preschools, and childminding, I hold Level 3 qualifications in both Home-Based Childcare and Preschool Care. I am experienced in delivering the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum and keep fully up to date with current legislation and childcare requirements. I also offer funded childcare places and support with Tax-Free Childcare. I hold qualifications in safeguarding, paediatric first aid, behaviour management, and supporting maths in early years, alongside extensive childcare training and experience. I provide a warm, friendly, safe, and nurturing home environment for children under 8 years old, where they can learn, play, and grow with confidence. My approach is child-led, focusing on each child’s individual interests, development, and wellbeing through play, nurture, and positive relationships.I am passionate about nurture and nature-based learning, encouraging children to explore the outdoors, build confidence, and develop independence through hands-on experiences and everyday discovery. My setting includes a large garden with swings, ride-on cars, scooters, a sandpit, ball pit, and plenty of outdoor play equipment to encourage active learning and fun. I am passionate about helping children learn from a young age and supporting them as they prepare for nursery, preschool, and school. I encourage independence, confidence, good manners, and social skills through everyday activities and play. As part of our daily routine, we enjoy outings to parks, libraries, swimming pools, museums, baby and toddler groups, and nature walks to help children socialise and explore the world around them. We love arts and crafts, free play, play dough, puzzles, drawing, painting, baking, counting games, and learning the alphabet — all while having lots of fun in a caring environment.

local_offer: The SEND provision at The Three Schools is on an individual needs basis and includes but is not limited to: - Literacy interventions are carried out by teachers and Teaching Assistants for children who are identified as having weak phonics, reading and writing skills and who are not working at their expected level in both KS1 and KS2. - Individual reading/comprehension intervention for children who are not reading accurately and fluently and have a lack of understanding of the text using an accelerated reading programme. - Additional 1:1 or group reading and comprehension sessions are provided by the class teacher or teaching assistant. - Phonics intervention for any child in Year 2 who did not meet the expected level in their Year 1 phonics screening test. - Phonics intervention for children in lower KS2 who have gaps in their phonological knowledge from KS1. - Numeracy intervention sessions carried out by teachers and Teaching Assistants for children who are not working at their expected level in both KS1 and KS2. - TAs are used for both in-class support, small focus group support and for 1:1 sessions. The type of support depends on the children’s needs and the requirements of the subject teacher. - Access arrangements are made for exams, tests where a specialist's report identifies a need. Types of provision may include the use of a laptop or additional time. Where there is an identified medical need further arrangements may have to be made. - Where a child needs more specialised support, external agencies and other professionals may become involved. - Additional 1:1 support in specific subjects in exceptional cases as and when required. - Phonic group sessions, provided for those children working below the expected level in reading, writing or phonics, using the ‘Little Wandle' guidance. - Social skills sessions, provided for children who need more targeted support such as Lego therapy, talk about social programme, learning mentor support sessions. - Occupational Therapy programmes. https://www.threeschools.org/inclusion-and-send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? name: Aylesbury Town Council
description: Aylesbury Town Council is the council closest to the residents in the Parish of Aylesbury. The Town Council is here to be a voice for the residents by representing their views on issues affecting them. Please contact the office for cost information for allotments, burial fees, and the Jonathan Page Play Centre fees.
organisation: Aylesbury Town Council (inc Jonathan Page Play Centre) Jonathan Page Play Centre Afterschool Club and Holiday Scheme, welcomes all children from the age of 4 up to their thirteenth birthday from all schools, so it's a great place for your child to make new friends in a safe, stimulating and, above all, fun environment. Your child can choose between structured activities and free play opportunities which take place indoors and outdoors ranging from arts and crafts, board games, table football, ball games, pool table, role play, a wide range of toys and books and much more. The secure outdoor area has a multi-use games area, football pitch, go-kart track, activity climbing frames, and a Learning Lodge which enables the children to spend plenty of time in the fresh air no matter what the weather is like. Our qualified and DBS-checked playworkers understand the importance of play, taking a keen interest in each child’s development, providing fun activities that meet each child’s social, physical, intellectual, creative and emotional needs. Caring for your children after school in our After School Club We offer a friendly and relaxed environment for your child to enjoy after the school day. To attend After School Club, children must be 4 years of age and in reception. We know and understand that most children are hungry straight after school. This is why we provide a healthy snack sat at a table so everyone can socialise and catch up. The children help clear up and are encouraged to try new foods. After their snack, the children play with our vast range of toys, get creative at the craft table, play outdoors, and generally have lots of fun with their friends until they are collected by their parents/guardians. Our team has regular feedback sessions with the children talking about ideas for future topics, what they enjoy and what they don’t do that the team can plan effectively. Hours The After School Club runs from 3:15pm to 6pm Monday to Friday during term time. School Collection Service: A collection service from a number of schools in and around Aylesbury is offered for a small daily fee: Walking Collection Service: Thomas Hickman School Minibus Collection Service: Turnfurlong Junior and Infant School Elmhurst School Buckingham Park School St Louis Catholic School If your child’s school is not listed above, please contact us and register your interest in a school collection to be arranged where possible. Holiday Playschemes Whether your child wants to come and join us for half a day, only on some days or the entire school holidays, we offer a wide range of activities that will ensure that your child has lots of fun at each and every visit. Our friendly and experienced team of Play-workers ensure that every day is bursting with fun activities for every child. No matter what time your child arrives with us, they will be greeted with a smile, made welcome and are able to relax and play straight away. At about 9 am, we have a morning meeting where we go over the safety rules and any news that the children or staff would like to share. We tell the children which adult-led crafts are available, and any special events and activities that are coming up. After the meeting, the children are free to play. We provide healthy snacks in the morning and afternoon and water is available for the children throughout the day, however, you will need to provide a packed lunch for the picnic-style lunch, which is followed by organised team games for all. After team games, it’s free to play again. A light snack is served at 4 pm, followed by more free play until they are collected. Bookings We accept advance and last minute bookings for the After School Club and Holiday Playschemes through our online booking system. To register and book activities for your child please visit our website. jpplaycentre@aylesburytowncouncil.gov.uk https://www.aylesburytowncouncil.gov.uk/jppc

name: Bucks Youth Drug and Alcohol Support Service
description: If you’re affected by your own or someone else’s drug use, we’re here to help. We’re a free and confidential service for anyone aged under 18 in Buckinghamshire, or those aged 18 to 24 with additional needs, such as neurodiversity, learning needs, or other challenges. We provide: - Friendly, non-judgmental support tailored to your needs. - Flexible appointments – we can meet at our hub, your school, college, or any other location you feel comfortable. - Confidentiality – we’ll keep your information private unless there's a risk of harm to you or someone else. - Engaging sessions led by you – we help you to meet your own goal, and to feel safe, heard and supported. You don’t need to be dependent on drugs or alcohol to use our service- we’re here for anyone looking for support. Get in touch to find out more about the support we can offer you. You can get support from our service by making a referral. A referral is a form that gives us the information we need to support you. You can refer yourself or someone else to the service by filling out our online referral form, calling, or emailing us. Once you reach out, a friendly team member will contact you to discuss the next steps and arrange your first session. All you need to bring is yourself and any goals or questions you have.

name: Talkback Employability
description: Talkback offer a wide range of employment programmes that cater for all ages and abilities; comprising of training, through to work experience, supported internships, and support to maintain paid work. We draw on our 24 years’ of experience of working with people with learning disabilities and/or autism to break down barriers that hinder access to paid employment. With clear progression pathways through the different stages of a person’s life, our Equip Programme works with young people aged 16 to 25 years with an Education and Health Care Plan; or our Employability and Personal Development Skills Programme can be accessed via adult social care funding or by direct payment. Talkback follow 5 key steps that enable people to build real-world work skills and move closer to their employment goals: 1. Training (Job Clubs and Job Coaching) 2. Social Enterprise (The Accessible Workshop) 3. Work Experience (unpaid work placements/ volunteering) 4. Supported Internships (for young people between 16 to 25 years with an Education, Health and Care Plan 5. Paid Employment (with ongoing workplace support)

description: Talkback offer a wide range of employment programmes that cater for all ages and abilities; comprising of training, through to work experience, supported internships, and support to maintain paid work. We draw on our 24 years’ of experience of working with people with learning disabilities and/or autism to break down barriers that hinder access to paid employment. With clear progression pathways through the different stages of a person’s life, our Equip Programme works with young people aged 16 to 25 years with an Education and Health Care Plan; or our Employability and Personal Development Skills Programme can be accessed via adult social care funding or by direct payment. Talkback follow 5 key steps that enable people to build real-world work skills and move closer to their employment goals: 1. Training (Job Clubs and Job Coaching) 2. Social Enterprise (The Accessible Workshop) 3. Work Experience (unpaid work placements/ volunteering) 4. Supported Internships (for young people between 16 to 25 years with an Education, Health and Care Plan 5. Paid Employment (with ongoing workplace support)

name: Talkback Your Voice
description: People with a learning disability have their own voice. Talkback help people find that voice. Since we began in 1998, we have developed a world of possibilities for people with learning disabilities and autistic people. We have supported those we work with in gaining life skills, from personal life skills through to helping them influence councils and employers with insights into reasonable adjustments. We enable people to take on new activities or volunteer placements, complete training courses, and form positive relationships within a social environment. In addition, we have prevented homelessness by supporting people to find a new home. As well as offering wellbeing courses and developed initiatives like the health passport. We also work in some sensitive areas, including bereavement, end-of-life, and domestic abuse. And we always advocate for meaningful change wherever we can. Your Voice helps to get the BEST decisions for people with learning disabilities and autistic individuals. We want Councils, Statutory Authorities, and other commercial and not-for-profit organisations that provide services, to make the right decisions. Based on a wealth of knowledge of what is required from the people affected. Because the people we engage with do not want special treatment. They just want the same rights and chances as everyone else. Our Your Voice services for professionals Through our range of services and work with community groups, we gather views and experiences. Then we feed them back to Councils, the NHS, Statutory Authorities, and other organisations. Our aim is to improve services for those that they support, whilst promoting respect, choice, and opportunity. Co-production and Engagement Designed by people with learning disabilities and autistic people. Our service is rooted in the core principles of co-production laid out by the Social Care Institute for Excellence. Equality, diversity, accessibility, and reciprocity. Experts by Experience This service is provided by a professionally trained team of people with learning disabilities and autistic people. So, they use their lived experiences to educate others. That can be a review of a hospital, a leisure centre, a shop, a hotel, or a sports or social venue, amongst others. Autism Insights Training We use the lived experiences of our members and team to educate people on the challenges faced by those people who have learning disabilities and autism. As well as the practical changes they can make to eradicate barriers to inclusion.

local_offer: Courses taken and experience in autism ADHD, patience and lots of different strategies used each tailored for the individual child  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I provide a caring environment where all children are welcomed and supported. I do my best to meet the needs of all children so that they can take part in all aspects of our setting and reach their full potential. I work closely with any involved professionals to help to support the children. I involve parents at every opportunity and work to support them as well as the children. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I don't have any staff How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents, sharing information about their child’s learning, development, and progress on a regular basis in a manner which suits them. I ask parents to share information about their child’s likes and dislikes, the activities which they find difficult and those which they enjoy the most. I aim to ensure that activities are extended to support children to meet their potential within the setting and share ideas with parents for use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children and where there is a particular need, I will support the preparation and implementation of a joint action plan for the child. With parents’ permission i may involve other services. I provide increased opportunities for communication for families of children with SEND and are flexible in how we communicate, for example, in person, on phone, email or electronic messages. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to most children and families. I am on a regular bus route for those needing public transport, and although there is a small threshold to the front door it has been used for wheelchair access. I aim to find somewhere suitable for the children to rest when needed and would always discuss options with parents. Our outdoor area is mainly laid to lawn with mature borders a small patio ans path surrounding, although not large it is accessible for most children, How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All families are welcome to visit and see my home before making a decision to attend. I have a welcome pack that includes most information parents need to know, but I am more than happy to answer any questions. When children arrive, i encourage families to complete an ‘All about Me’ sheet, provide any special comforters (regardless of age of the child). I encourage parents to have some ‘settling in visits’ with their child. I am happy for practitioners from other settings to visit us before a child starts to help them to settle (whether new to us or moving on elsewhere). What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am constantly aware of the need for flexibility within my setting to ensure that children’s needs can be met. I access training as necessary. I keep updated with new guidance from the Local Authority and use their website regularly.

description: TVAP Tadpoles at Thames Valley Adventure Playground is an integrated fun group for toddlers aged 5 and under, with or without a special need. A great opportunity to enjoy the facilities of the adventure playground, including soft play and sound room, crafts, toys, games, and outdoor play in a supported, friendly and relaxed environment. Sessions typically run on Tuesdays during term time from 10 am to 11:30 am. All children must be accompanied by an adult. Please see our website for opening times for specific groups.
organisation: Thames Valley Adventure Playground Association Committee We are currently open for individuals with special needs (children and adults) and non special needs children. We are running 2 sessions per day. Booking by phone is essential. Please phone or see our website for further details. Playground (indoor and outdoor) for children and adults with all types of special need, however, mild or profound, their siblings and parents/carers. Open Tuesday to Saturday all year round, Fridays are reserved for adults with special needs The Thames Valley Adventure Playground has provides a chance for children and adults with all types of special need to enjoy the fun, freedom and friendship afforded by the opportunity to play and share experiences in a safe and stimulating environment, with users travelling from Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire, London and beyond. Facilities and Activities Wheelchair-accessible roundabouts and swings elevated walkways allowing someone with profound and multiple problems to enjoy the excitement of 'climbing' trees multi-sensory rooms to stimulate and relax, with specially-trained staff to provide help and support - these are just a few of the things on offer. reama@tvap.co.uk http://www.tvap.co.uk

name: Taryn Cooper
description: I'm Taryn, an Ofsted Registered Childminder based in Hazlemere, offering a safe, caring and welcoming home-from-home environment where children can feel happy, secure and thrive. I received GOOD grading in all areas on my Ofsted Inspection in 2025. As a parent of two children myself, I understand how important it is to find childcare that is nurturing, reliable and supportive of each child’s individual needs. I have over 20 years of experience working with children of all ages. Before becoming an Ofsted Registered Childminder, I worked within the NHS Children’s Occupational Therapy Team for seven years, specialising in child development and supporting children in schools and early years settings. I worked closely with parents, staff and other professionals to assess developmental milestones, identify areas where additional support may be needed, and deliver engaging therapy sessions and adapted activities to help each child reach their full potential. I've been able to use these skills and I have set up a dedicated playroom for early years children, filled with high-quality resources to support all areas of learning and development. I also have a large garden creatively designed for all children as I believe outdoor play and curiosity about the world around us is fundamentally important. I follow the EYFS framework and tailor my curriculum around each child’s individual interests. I create fun and engaging activities and experiences that support learning, helping children to build strong foundation skills, grow in confidence, and become school ready when the time comes. Most importantly, I help children develop a love of learning. Every term I set Next Steps in each of the 7 areas of development to work towards and share this with parents/carers so we can work in partnership. I love the outdoors so the children go on lots of outings to farms, national trust places, animal sanctuaries, museums, libraries, parks etc as well as attending playgroups, gardening club, music groups to support their social skills. The children will get involved in growing their own vegetables, sowing seeds and flowers and learning about how to recycle and ways to look after our planet. If you have any questions please don’t hesitate to contact me. Additional Information: Open Monday to Thursday Term time only (I open during Easter and summer holidays for ad hoc childcare) Ofsted Registered (GOOD in all areas) DBS checked First Aid trained fully insured Member of PACEY (Professional Association for Childcare in Early Years) Accept 15/30 hours funded- childcare work vouchers- Gov tax free childcare scheme Complete several training courses each year to keep my knowledge up to date My Qualifications Training completed: PACEY preparing to work in home based childcare Level 4 Childcare and Education Paediatric first aid Safeguarding Makaton sign language Introduction to pure Phonics and cued articulation Supporting children with speech, language and communication needs Delivering the EYFS Understanding multi-sensory concepts Understanding child development and direct work with children Understanding challenging needs Level 2 Autistic types and behaviours Epilepsy awareness and administration of medication Children’s starting points in development Eat better- start better Early maths Resources to promote learning British Values Characteristics of Effective Learning EY Curriculum Roadshow for childminders Perfectionism in Children Keeping children safe on the internet Science in Early Years Benefits of junk modelling and non-directive play Planning and the EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage) Building a learning journal

local_offer: I have many years of experience working with children of different ages and abilities and children with a wide range of disabilities. I have worked in the paediatric Occupation Therapy team, therefore, delivered programmes and treatment sessions based on a key area of development and support required for individual children. I’m now a childminder but I’m happy to provide support and care for families and children following my Ofsted ratio.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As with all registered Childminders in Buckinghamshire, we have a Key Contact within the Early Years Service, from whom we can access advice, and information and be signposted to other professions. Due to previously working in children's Occupational Therapy, I worked alongside other professional teams on a weekly basis. I had the opportunity to gain a broader understanding of the role and support they offer to childcare providers and families. I am happy to contact other professionals or make referrals. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT website) are available for people to access. I will share relevant information with parents so we can work consistently to support the child. I am happy to attend Multi-Professionals Meetings if required and have any professional visit the child in my home. I am always keen to expand my knowledge and expertise so I am happy to undergo further training when it is required. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Makaton Intro to pure Phonics and cued articulation Supporting children with speech, language and communication needs Understanding multi-sensory concepts Understanding child development and direct work with children Understanding challenging needs Level 2 Autistic types and behaviours Epilepsy awareness and administration of medication How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Working in partnership is a key part of a child’s learning. I pride myself in sharing information to ensure I know all about the children in my care and for parents/carers to clearly understand what their child has been doing throughout the day, the progress they are making and the next steps to work on together. When a child starts, I will ask parents to share as much information about their child (likes, dislikes, comforts, activities they enjoy the most, routines, celebrations) as this is so important that the child feels safe, secure and happy whilst with me. We will continue to work together, getting involved in topics and sharing essential information about what we have been doing and getting the family at home involved. A home communication book is used daily for both myself and my parents to write in, as well as newsletters, learning journals, sharing photos and face-to-face discussions How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children in my care, highlighting their Wow moments of achievements and areas where they may need extra support. A development tracker is completed as well as written observations which are shared with parents/carers. A detailed 2-year progress check is completed alongside the Health Visiting team's progress check. With the parent's permission, I may get other professionals involved to support the child best. I give all children in my care the opportunity to reach their full potential. Sometimes this means adapting an activity to the child’s ability and stage of development, providing additional resources or giving one child more attention and support than others during a particular activity or routine. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents/carers and I will work on a joint action plan in supporting their child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to most children and families. I have some steps leading to the front door however access can be used through the garden gate and up a ramp from the back door. My garden is on split levels with steps so therefore it would be be accessible to a wheelchair user however the lower level directly leading from the house is filled with a wide variety of toys. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible for example adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, the local catchment school, pre-schools to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling-in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. I am happy for practitioners from other settings to come and visit me before a child starts to help them to settle (new to me or moving on elsewhere). I will support the child and family by suggesting visuals, social stories and photos of the new setting or other ideas that will support the individual child to help the child process and understand the transition. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? After working for many years supporting children with SEN needs, this will always be a keen interest of mine so I will continue to keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

local_offer: I am committed to providing an inclusive and supportive environment for children with Special Education Needs. I have attended courses om autism, regularly updated my knowledge within the SEN sector, and continue to take part in future in future training to strengthen my practice.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I have some experience supporting children with autism, hearing impairments, and those with little or no language, adapting care to meet each child's individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? As mentioned above I regularly update my knowledge within the SEN sector. I am also due to attend additional SEN training in early May, which will further build my confidence and enhance my ability to provide high-quality, tailored support for children with additional needs within my setting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I believe in a strong partnerships with parents are essential to supporting each child's development. From the point of registration, I work closely with parents to understand their requirements, ensuring a smooth transition into my setting. Morning and afternoon feed back is always key, I also message/send pictures to parents through the day. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I regularly observe children during a range of activities to monitor their development and use this inform termly planning. These plans are shared with parents so they can clearly see what their child is working towards and how they are progressing. I maintain open and honest communication an am always happy to work alongside other professionals, welcoming them into my setting to provide additional support where needed for both the child and their family. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is based in a three-bedroom semi-detached home. There are steps to entre the house, as well as additional steps leading to the play room and garden area, which may affect accessibility for some families. I am also happy to discuss individual needs and will do my best to accommodate where possible. I warmly welcome parents to to arrange a visit to view the setting and explore whether it is suitable for their requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children with SEN and their families can start to using my services by getting in touch to discuss their child's individual needs and arranging an initial visit. This allows us to meet, talk through routines, support requirements, and ensure that my setting is the right fit for the child and family. Following this, the parents are required to complete the registration process before their child can begin to attending. I am happy to work closely with families and any professionals involved to support a smooth and positive transition into my setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am committed to continually developing my SEN provision to ensure I can offer the best possible support for children and their families. I plan to build on my existing knowledge by attending further specialist training, including upcoming SEN courses, to strengthen my confidence and understanding of a wider range of additional needs. I will continue to keep my CPD up to date and stay informed about current best practice within the sector. I also aim to develop stronger links with other professionals and services to enhance the support available within my setting, as well as review and adapt my my environment and resources to ensure they are inclusive and accessible for all children. Moving forward, I will continue to reflect on my practice, ensuring that each child's individual needs are met through tailored strategies and nurturing, inclusive approach.

local_offer: At Teatimers our care for children with special needs focuses on how we can meet those needs and help their ongoing development. To this end, we work with parents and relevant professionals to adjust our practice to support the child and include them in the life of the setting. Special needs may become apparent during a child's time in our care, and we will discuss this confidentially with parents to agree on the steps to take. Please call us to discuss how we can help.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our main outcome is to provide all children with the opportunities to learn and develop. We will support children and families with special needs by making them feel included. We will do this by adapting our room and activities when needed and also requesting additional support from other multi agency professionals. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff have access to an online training platform where courses can be completed to support them in their role. Our SENCO has refresher training and can also attend SENCO liasion meetings where other settings give advice and support each other. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We have an open door policy at Teatimers where we always encourage parents to come in and see us. Keyworkers develop close relationships with their key children and will involve parents in all areas of their child's development especially where special needs are recognised. Parents evening and any other meetings to support a child are held How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting has a large open indoor space where activities are setup daily. Children of all abilities can access these activities independently or with the support of an adult. We have a covered outdoor area which has a fenced sandpit and mud kitchen area and we also have access to a large playground, where children of all abilities are provided with outdoor equipment to promote their physical development. However, our outdoor area is not accessible for wheelchair users. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can arrange a visit to come and meet our staff and see our setting. We will work together and make appropriate changes so the setting is safe, secure and supports the need of the individual child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Teatimers will continue to provide an inclusive, supportive and caring setting. All children are recognised as individuals and given the opportunities to develop and learn.

local_offer: At Teeny Queeny Day Nursery, we are committed to providing an inclusive environment where every child can thrive. We recognise that all children develop at their own pace, and we offer tailored support for those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Our SENCo works closely with parents, carers, and outside professionals to create individual support plans that meet each child’s unique needs. We use a range of strategies and resources to support communication, physical development, and learning, ensuring all children can fully participate in nursery life. Regular observations and reviews help us track progress and adapt our approach as needed. Our goal is to provide early intervention, build confidence, and help every child reach their full potential in a nurturing and understanding setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? For all children regardless of additional needs to have the best opportunity to thrive in their early years. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Both SENCO's have completed the full two day training course provided though the local authority and keep up to date on changes with the regular liaison groups. Other staff that may benefit have also been added onto the 'I'm not the SEN but ...' course to further improve their knowledge. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work closely with parents when any areas of concern are observed and we then work in partnership through the rest of the process, they have involvement with any APDR or SEN support plans that may be required and they are invited to any visits/discussions that may take place with the Early Years SEND advisors at Bucks council. We are able to help and support should an EHC plan be required and are able to signpost parents to any available training courses that may be offered by our Local authority such as the Early Bird Programme. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use an online system that gives all parents live updates about their activities during the day and the development goals they are working towards, we provide quarterly summative assessments, we also share any APDR targets (if relevant) as and when they are updated and offer regular meetings to discuss any additional support that may be in place for individual children. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have disabled access to the front of the building and the majority of the building is on single story and does have disabled access toilet. The garden is mostly accessed by steps from the rooms however there is a rear gate that is more assessable. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families would need to contact us to check if we have any current availability via phone or email. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: Abingdon and Witney College have high aspirations for every learner. Whether you are on a journey to employment, an apprenticeship, a supported internship, higher education and/or achieving greater confidence in being independent; our support can help. There are many different entry points to studying at college. Through our Access to Learning provision we can help students prepare for the journey into employment and/or onward study on a vocational programme with us. Our application process If you have an Education and Health Care Plan (EHCP), your application to the college will be managed alongside information provided by the Local Authority. This is to ensure that we are able to support your special educational needs at the college; course offers are conditional until this agreement is in place. During the application process, we will enquire about SEN support received in school or at other colleges. We can then plan to ensure that staff and resources are in place for when students join; this includes information on Exam Access Arrangements (EAA). For this information to be shared, your consent is required. Please ensure you complete the relevant consent sections on your application. Support with transition to college There are many types of transitions; whether that is taking the first steps into college, moving between different levels of study, transitioning into work, beginning to live independently, or starting higher education. We know that some parts of transitions can feel overwhelming, and often students need someone to be able to talk to and get the clarity they need. description: Learning with a difference. Forget long hours in classrooms with textbooks – think practical skills applied in high-quality, career-specific surroundings. Think expert guidance. local_offer: Refer to our policy. https://www.theacademy.me/page/?title=SPECIAL+EDUCATIONAL+NEEDS&pid=99 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our objectives are: • To be an inclusive Academy Trust where all students are held in equal and positive regard. • To facilitate high levels of achievement for all students, enabling them to be prepared for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of adult life. • To take reasonable measures to overcome barriers to learning. • To identify students with SEND as early as possible. • To meet individual needs through a wide range of provision, including quality first teaching, support from Learning Support assistants, targeted intervention and individual or small group teaching. • To support Academy Trust staff to carry out their responsibilities for the delivery of a differentiated curriculum to meet the diverse needs of our students, including the identification and facilitation of training needs. • To regularly review the needs of students with SEND. • To involve families/carers in the support arrangements for their children and in the reviewing process to attain high levels of satisfaction from parents/ carers. • To put students with SEND at the centre of planning for provision, enabling them to view measures positively and allow full and positive engagement. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The team at Aylesbury Vale Academy have undertaken a vast range of training relating to the four broad areas of SEND need and recent circumstances. Our SENDCo has undertaken NASENCo training and EYFS SENDCo training. The Assistant SENDCo has also completed EYFS SENDCo training. Staff are encouraged to develop professionally and have undertaken a range of opportunities including: SEND CoP, Makaton, First aid, Child Protection, Communication friendly classrooms, Understanding Dyslexia, Autism, Depression and Anxiety, Team Teach, Speech and Language, NELI, Wellcomm and ICan accreditation. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents have access to a designated SEND email: sendco@theacademy.me and they are able to raise concerns via the online form: https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=vujYj3JiOk-ROacP9_VtsKSZm5iIcidJig5HlgRJQUZUMEVCUk1PMUZXRTg1UllUVVBaSFNYUFlCMi4u&web=1&wdLOR=cA359AD1B-53A8-5F47-9B1A-80EC4AFA2E4C How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Those children with possible SEND are supported by practitioners with early intervention which is documented using an APDR (Assess, plan, do, review) in consultation with parents. Where an underlying need is evident, staff and parents work together to produce an IPM (individual provision map) and may refer to external agencies for support and assessment. In some instances children display more complex needs and require ongoing and extensive support. We will work with parents to secure appropriate provision and funding. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Accessible How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Via email What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Ongoing CPD and accreditation.

name: The Theatre Shed
description: We are an inclusive theatre company offering expertly guided Performing Arts workshops in the heart of Chesham and Amersham. Our inclusive workshops are professionally led and allow our young people to explore performance skills such as acting, singing, dancing, physical theatre, and more in a supportive environment. Please visit our website for upcoming sessions and activities.
organisation: The Theatre Shed The aim of The Theatre Shed in Amersham is to inspire, innovate and include through the medium of Performing Arts. Our inclusive workshops are professionally led and allow our young people to explore performance skills such as acting, singing, dancing, physical theatre and more in a supportive environment. We would normally run in-person Workshops on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings with additional holiday Workshops. Initially when, due to the COVID-19 pandemic Lockdown and social distancing recommendations, we were unable to continue running Workshops at our normal venue at The Beacon School we were devastated. We didn’t give up and our Artistic team have worked extremely hard to keep The Theatre Shed up and running by going online. With so many young people needing a regular pattern to their lives we have been able to give continuity, stability and consistency. Good mental health at this time is so important. These sessions are really well attended once everyone got used to using Zoom and it now feels so natural to our members. This gives continuity, familiarity and activity in these extremely uncertain times. We didn’t stop there realising that there are others in the Community who would benefit from regular involvement in our activities so we expanded our activities to include Film Club for the Community. This is a chance to watch a film at the same time as your friends with an activity pack available to download from our website to go along with it. The chosen film is shown via our Zoom link so everyone can watch together. Our Community work continues with daytime workshops on a Tuesday between 2pm and 3pm and will have different themes (drama, dance, music etc.) each week. admin@thetheatreshed.co.uk https://thetheatreshed.co.uk/

name: They Are The Future | Parenting and Wellbeing Website
description: They Are The Future is a parenting and wellbeing website run by Dr. Lucy Russell, a clinical psychologist at Everlief Child Psychology in West Wycombe. Expert parenting and well-being information, with a weekly blog. You will find advice on children's mental health including anxiety, anger, friendship difficulties, self-esteem, attention and concentration, sleep, exercise, and nutrition in relation to mental health. The site also focuses on small, manageable steps to parenting a happy, thriving child in the real world.
organisation: Everlief Child Psychology Clinic Everlief have opened a private family-friendly clinic in the beautiful and historic West Wycombe All our clinical psychologists hold a Doctorate in Clinical Psychology and are Chartered Psychologists [Doctorate in Clinical Psychology, Chartered Psychologist]. All our clinical psychologists are registered with the BPS and the HCPC (health and care professions council). Our psychologists can support any child but also have areas of special interest such as anxiety, autism or eating disorders. Dr Lucy Russell, our clinical Director is also an associate fellow of the British Psychological Society, and is on their list of registered supervisors. Lucy is also a guest lecturer on the Oxford Doctoral Course in Clinical Psychology at the Oxford Institute of Clinical Psychology Training (University of Oxford). Everlief offering assessments, 1-1 therapy for children, parenting support and workshops. We work with all areas of emotional and behavioural difficulties in children and specialise in psychological therapies including CBT. Please consider Everlief for: Families seeking ASD diagnosis Difficulties associated with autism/Asperger’s syndrome Behavioural issues Worry and anxiety Low self-esteem, low mood, depression or self-harm Fears and phobias Faddy eating or eating difficulties Toileting issues Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) General parenting support and advice Everlief is also a specialist in carrying out autism assessments. Finally, Everlief also have an educational psychologist available for one-hour appointments. These are designed to help you plan the best way forward for your child's education needs. mikerussell@everlief.co.uk https://www.everlief.co.uk/

local_offer: The use of regular monitoring allows us to identify any child who may have SEN. We gain evidence in a number of ways including: conversations with parents/carers, teachers, specialist practitioners through the use of advice clinics and by identifying changes in behaviour and self-esteem. We use personalised special educational provision to target areas of difficulty with a drive to enable children to overcome barriers to learning and participation. Our support is child centred and frequent monitoring is carried out to assess the impact of the support we provide. This monitoring evaluates, not only academic progress, but may also track improved social and emotional development. The support we provide consists of a four-part process: - Assess - Plan - Do - Review This is a continuous cycle to enable the provision to be refined and revised as the understanding of the needs of the pupil grows. This cycle enables the identification of those interventions which are the most effective in supporting the child to achieve good progress and outcomes. name: Thomas Hickman School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Aylesbury for 3 to 11-year-olds. Thomas Hickman School is a two-form entry school located on Belgrave Road in the Meadowcroft area. Everything we do links back to our BIRDS Values (Bravery, Independence and Inspiration, Respect and Resilience, Determination, and Scholarship). We were inspected by Ofsted in September 2019, under the new inspection framework, and were judged as a Good school. Our Nursery offers mornings, afternoons or 30 hours for rising 4-year-olds, and we also have a younger class for some rising 3-year-olds who have access to additional funding. The school offers a breakfast club 5 mornings a week and there are also a variety of clubs that run before, during and after school. Our school community is very diverse and this is something which both staff and pupils are very proud of. There are No Outsiders Here; this is a campaign that is running across the school in order to celebrate our differences and our individual heritage to ensure that all members of our school feel valued. The Acorn Centre was established a few years ago as a community centre for our school. There are a number of parent courses which run each week, as well as other activities and opportunities for parents and pupils of our school. Our Pastoral Team includes Family Support Workers and a full-time Child Therapist. The Acorn Centre is used at lunchtimes for our "Aviary" which is for children who are struggling with life on the main playground (also known as "The Swoop"). We are proud of our Contagious and Courageous curriculum which is exciting and enriching and encourages children to demonstrate their skills and understanding across a wide range of subjects and experiences. This is enhanced by specialist teaching in PE, ICT, Performing Arts and Modern Foreign Languages. The Swoop is the name for our playground. Here children can take part in a range of activities including wild wheels (scooters), crazy golf, disco, a range of sports run by our PE team, junkyard modelling (giant 3D building) and giant tyres. You will find further information about the school along with our school policies on our website. We look forward to welcoming any visitors who wish to come and meet our staff and pupils.

The new National Curriculum is our starting point for our Contagious and Courageous Curriculum where planning strives to meet the specific needs of individuals and groups of children. Diversity is recognised as a valuable source in enriching and supporting the learning of all. A minority of children have particular learning, behavioural requirements, or other difficulties that could create barriers to their learning. These requirements are likely to arise as a consequence of a child having Special Educational Needs. Teachers take account of these requirements and make provision, where necessary, to support individuals or groups of children and thus enable them to participate effectively in curriculum and assessment activities. Children may have Special Educational Needs throughout or at any time during their school career. Staff ensure that curriculum planning and assessment for children with Special Educational Needs takes account of the type and extent of the difficulty experienced by the child. local_offer: At Thomas Hickman, we recognise every child’s right to a broad, balanced, relevant and challenging curriculum. The new National Curriculum is our starting point for our Contagious and Courageous Curriculum where planning strives to meet the specific needs of individuals and groups of children. Diversity is recognised as a valuable source in enriching and supporting the learning of all. Children may have Special Educational Needs throughout or at any time during their school career. Staff ensure that curriculum planning and assessment for children with Special Educational Needs takes account of the type and extent of the difficulty experienced by the child. This is then reflected in their SEN Support Plan.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? A minority of children have particular learning, behavioural requirements or other difficulties that could create barriers to their learning. These requirements are likely to arise as a consequence of a child having Special Educational Needs. Teachers take account of these requirements and make provision, where necessary, to support individuals or groups of children and thus enable them to participate effectively in curriculum and assessment activities. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Children on the SEN register have an SEN Support Plan. Parents are invited to come in and meet with teachers to discuss needs, progress and the type of support and reasonable adjustments that are needed to enable the children to thrive at school. Progress is then monitored carefully on a daily, weekly and more long-term basis. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children have specific interventions designed to meet their needs. The children will have SEN support plans that highlight their area for need and then their class teacher will break this down into steps that are achievable and highlight their progress in the most minute of detail. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Children may have Special Educational Needs throughout or at any time during their school career. Staff ensure that curriculum planning and assessment for children with Special Educational Needs takes account of the type and extent of the difficulty experienced by the child. This is then reflected in their SEN Support Plan. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? For children we offer an array of extra curricular clubs that we encourage all of the children to access, for families we have regular surgeries with the parents at Thomas Hickman to discuss a variety of topics and support with different issues such as EHCP's and high needs block funding. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Some children may require input from external experts and we have a close working relationship with many other professionals and agencies. We use them to assess pupils and provide additional support and ideas for staff in their management of specific children.

name: Tiger Martial Arts | High Wycombe
description: Tiger Martial Arts is the first school in the UK to bring traditional Martial Arts to the family in this unique way. We specialise in teaching families not just the skills of Martial Arts but the opportunities of Martial Arts on family life. Martial Arts is so much more than just learning the correct techniques of how to do each move they are invaluable life skills that last a lifetime. In a society of online instant access, Facebook, Twitter, computers, mobile phones, gaming consoles, and work/school families have less time to interact, grow imagination, and learn key skills with interaction. We at Tiger Martial Arts help focus all the distractions away and give families the opportunity to interact, have fun, and learn skills that will last a lifetime. Tiger Martial Arts could focus on all the accomplishments of the instructors and competitions how many black belts and students we have trained but our focus is so much more about the families we teach and what they have achieved. Tiger Martial Arts helps each individual and family set and achieve goals they are looking for, and through training, they watch and see themselves hitting each goal time and time again. They meet one goal they set another, which is the real achievement of Martial Arts. Don’t take our word for it look at what our families say by looking at our review or asking them directly on our Facebook page or groups. Here are just a few questions to ask yourself to see if our school is right for you: Do you want better respect, discipline, and grades for your children? Do you want to give your family the skills to minimise bullying and the effects of bullying? Are you looking for a place where the family can join in an activity all together and have fun while learning key life skills and getting fit? Are you tired of sitting and waiting for hours as each child has his or her turn? We don’t just offer classes. Tiger Martial Arts are dedicated to all aspects of family life from fun days out and Events, to birthday celebrations, to educational opportunities, workshops and seminars, and of course holiday celebrations. Part of a family Martial Arts is to celebrate and enjoy family life. Here are just some of the opportunities we have had this year: Day outing to Legoland Star Wars Day, Easter Egg Hunt, Marlow May Fayre, A visit from the Mayor, An evening tea at the Mayor’s Parlour. Is your child bully-proof?, Birthday Classes, pancake races, and so much more, and more still to come. All that plus 6 classes a week train in one or train in all a wide variety to suit your family’s needs. Still not sure? Get in touch for a no cost no obligation appointment to come to talk to us and try a class on us.
