suitabilities: 
local_offer: Within Iver Community Childcare we aim to provide an inclusive environment accessible to all children. We follow the Equality Act 2010, the SEND Code of Practice, and the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory guidance. Upon starting the setting key practitioner’s liaise closely with parents obtaining information about the child’s interests, preferences and current stage of development. At this point parents can share information about their child’s development. During the first two weeks of attending the setting the child’s starting points are completed based on the Early Years Foundation Stage Developmental Matters. For children under three we complete a two year old checklist - this highlights the children’s strengths and any developmental delays. In this way we aim to identify any additional need at the earliest point. Ongoing assessments are carried out on all children and progress is measured according to the expected levels for their age. Where any delays are identified measures are taken to narrow any gaps. Where special educational needs or any developmental delays are identified the special educational needs co-ordinator will liaise with the parents and discuss the needs. They will then monitor the child’s progress within the setting and will ensure the appropriate amendments within the environment and practice are made to meet the individual needs of the child. We will make individual Support Plans to ensure progress in being made. Developmental summaries will be carried about to record progress over time alongside regular observations. Where appropriate the setting will support parents to make contact with outside agencies such as speech and language therapy, educational psychologist, the Early Years Childcare services Inclusions Team, and the support from the local Children’s Centre amongst others. We aim to train our staff to a good level to meet the needs of all the children who attend the setting. Staff attend refresher courses and staff receive ongoing training internally and externally. We work closely with the local authority inclusion team and seek advice and support for each child’s additional needs. The learning environment will be tailored as far as possible towards the special educational needs of the child. At present the setting has wheelchair access, it is all based on the ground floor level. We have the use of three rooms the larger room contains all the noisy activities targeted at all the older children whereas the smaller room is a quiet space and the third room is set aside for use by our babies. Within the quiet space we have sensory toys, a cosy corner and various activities situated on the floor or on the table tops. We have access to a large outdoor space but do not operate on a free flow system. Children have access to the toilets. Transitions: Where a child attends another setting we share information (with parental consent) with them such as the child’s current developmental summary, individual education plans and any other information such as the outside agencies involved. We will also have a diary which gets filled in about what the child does at the setting, their interests, preferences and include any progress or updates. Transition to a new setting will be supported by arranging meeting with the new school/setting passing on information, documentation and arranging visits. We aim to be accessible to all families from the local community but we may not be able to offer your child the days and hours you require straight away. You may ask to go on our waiting list and you will be offered a place when one becomes available. Places are offered on a first come, first served basis within the correct age group for your child, siblings of children who already use services on the same day are given priority and where reasonable, priority is also given to those with SEN or disabilities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to support children's additional needs so that they can have fun, make friends and make developmental progress. Where children require EHCP's before starting school, we can support parents to complete the necessary paper to request assessment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? In the last year various staff have attended Sensory Motor Strategies, Autism and Play, Trauma Informed Childcare and Autism Awareness, How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved from the moment they enquire for a place at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children with indentified SEND will have the usually diary that all children have along with a development summary to track progress but in addition we will be completing and updated SEN support plans and where needed, more detailed development trackers. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The environment is accessible for all children, indoors and outdoors. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Enquire about a nursery place. We can't always offer a place but will do what we can. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Train additional staff around Autism awareness

local_offer: We are an inclusive Nursery setting with a welcoming and nurturing centre. We have wheelchair access throughout the Nursery. Our team are trained in supporting children with SEND and provide all of our children with a rich and accessible early years experience.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We respect every Parent as their child's first and most enduring educator. We will work closely with you before your child joins us to understand their needs, likes, dislikes and the aspirations you have. All of our families use the EyLog app to send in updates on home learning and home experiences which contribute to their child's learning journey. For our children with SEND we will liaise with the professionals supporting your child, and follow any programmes identified to support your child’s needs. We will complete cycles of ‘Asses, Plan, do and review’ which will potentially then be filtered in to a support plan for your child. Every child’s needs are unique to them. We will work closely with you to ensure that we understand the stage your child is at with SEND identification, and respond to your family’s needs accordingly. We are looking to update staff training to support children's speech and pronunciation.

Sign-posting for specialist needs Counselling service Referrals to refuges in other parts of the country Access to an awareness programme looking into the issues of power and control in relationships. Independent Domestic Violence Advocacy, assistance with child contact and access to the Freedom Programme and Therapeutic Playgroups also available. Accommodation located in Aylesbury but take referrals from other parts of the Country, Outreach and Aftercare in Aylesbury Vale. Open Door Policy for all women but the refuge accommodation cannot accommodate boys over 16 years of age.

name: New Meaning Training
description: At New Meaning Training (formerly ToolShed) we support young people aged 15 to 19 (and up to 24 with an EHCP) in their self-development, training, education, and employment so that they are able to learn how to earn their own living. We offer Education with a Difference. We have a range of programmes at our centres in High Wycombe, Aylesbury, and Milton Keynes, as well as Transition Support Tutors who come out to learners who are not centre-ready. Boost Workskills - This course runs at all of our Buckinghamshire centres. It offers an opportunity to build employability skills using the Skills for Employment, Training, and Personal Development (SET-PD) framework. Construction Multiskills - This course runs at both The Place in High Wycombe and NMT Milton Keynes. It combines crucial Health and Safety modules alongside practical skills like painting and decorating, tiling, and carpentry. Sports - This course is based at The Place in High Wycombe. It combines theory and practical work and offers great opportunities to learn about teamwork. This course supports future employability in a wide variety of careers. Hair and Beauty - This course is based at Baker House, High Wycombe. Learners benefit from an on-site salon called "Flow Hair and Beauty". The course combines theory with practical skills. A great foundation for further learning, an internship or work. Haircare, skincare, nailcare and customer care. Motor Mechanics - This course is based at The Place in High Wycombe. Learn essential car maintenance skills! This hands-on course covers identifying car parts, changing tyres, repairing punctures, oil and filter changes, replacing spark plugs, and key safety practices. Community Care - this course is based at NMT Enrichment Centre, Aylesbury. Catering - this course is based at NMT Enrichment Centre, Aylesbury and some learners will have the opportunity to work in our on-site enterprise business, Park View Café. All courses can include English and/or Maths Functional Skills. We support learners with and without an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP). Courses start in September, but we can continue to enrol through to October half term. We are glad to receive enquiries about placements for the next academic year. Please contact us for further information on the course.

name: New Meaning Training
description: At New Meaning Training (formerly ToolShed) we support young people aged 15 to 19 (and up to 24 with an EHCP) in their self-development, training, education, and employment so that they are able to learn how to earn their own living. We offer Education with a Difference. We have a range of programmes at our centres in High Wycombe, Aylesbury, and Milton Keynes, as well as Transition Support Tutors who come out to learners who are not centre-ready. Boost Workskills - This course runs at all of our Buckinghamshire centres. It offers an opportunity to build employability skills using the Skills for Employment, Training, and Personal Development (SET-PD) framework. Construction Multiskills - This course runs at both The Place in High Wycombe and NMT Milton Keynes. It combines crucial Health and Safety modules alongside practical skills like painting and decorating, tiling, and carpentry. Sports - This course is based at The Place in High Wycombe. It combines theory and practical work and offers great opportunities to learn about teamwork. This course supports future employability in a wide variety of careers. Hair and Beauty - This course is based at Baker House, High Wycombe. Learners benefit from an on-site salon called "Flow Hair and Beauty". The course combines theory with practical skills. A great foundation for further learning, an internship or work. Haircare, skincare, nailcare and customer care. Motor Mechanics - This course is based at The Place in High Wycombe. Learn essential car maintenance skills! This hands-on course covers identifying car parts, changing tyres, repairing punctures, oil and filter changes, replacing spark plugs, and key safety practices. Community Care - this course is based at NMT Enrichment Centre, Aylesbury. Catering - this course is based at NMT Enrichment Centre, Aylesbury and some learners will have the opportunity to work in our on-site enterprise business, Park View Café. All courses can include English and/or Maths Functional Skills. We support learners with and without an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP). Courses start in September, but we can continue to enrol through to October half term. We are glad to receive enquiries about placements for the next academic year. Please contact us for further information on the course.

local_offer: We are pleased to offer last-minute childcare to support families with flexible childcare needs: Full Day: £100 Half Day: £60 We are delighted to introduce several exciting improvements to our nursery: 🌟 New Baby Unit Our brand-new baby unit provides a warm, safe, and nurturing environment specifically designed to support the needs of our youngest children. 🌟 Expanded Pre-School Provision We have opened an additional pre-school room, creating more opportunities for children aged 2 to 4 years to learn, play, and develop in an engaging and stimulating environment. 🌟 New Dining Room Our purpose-built dining room allows children of all ages to enjoy mealtimes together, encouraging independence as they confidently collect their own lunch and tea while developing social skills through shared dining experiences. 🌟 Construction Zone Our exciting new construction area inspires creativity, problem-solving, and imaginative play, giving children the opportunity to become little builders as they design, build, and explore. 🌟 All-Weather Outdoor Learning Our newly built covered outdoor room ensures children can enjoy outdoor play and learning throughout the year. Whether it's sunshine or rain, children have continuous access to fresh air and enriching outdoor experiences in a safe, sheltered environment. We look forward to welcoming you to Tot Town Nursery, where we continue to invest in creating inspiring spaces that support every child's learning, development, and wellbeing.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? At Tot Town Nursery, I have undertaken several years of SENCO training to support children with additional needs and to strengthen inclusive practice across the setting. The training I have completed includes: The SEND Code of Practice and the role and responsibilities of the SENCO. Good Practice for Managing Behaviour in Early Years Settings. Good Practice in Supporting Children with Autism. Sharing Concerns with Parents and Carers. Promoting Positive Behaviour. In addition to my training: Six members of staff have attended Story Dough Training, enabling them to use storytelling and play-based approaches to support children's communication, language development, creativity, and engagement. Rachel has recently completed Behaviour Management Training, further strengthening our team's knowledge and approach to supporting children's emotional wellbeing and positive behaviour. This ongoing professional development ensures that our team is well equipped to provide high-quality, inclusive support for all children, including those with SEND. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Tot Town Nursery, we believe that parents and carers are a child's first and most important educators. We value strong partnerships with families and work closely together to ensure every child receives the best possible care, learning opportunities, and support. Our manager has an open-door policy and is available throughout the day to speak with parents and carers. Key persons are also readily available before, during, and after sessions to discuss children's wellbeing, learning, and development. We understand that leaving a child can be an emotional experience, particularly during the settling-in period, so we offer reassurance through phone calls, text messages, and photographs (where appropriate) to let families know their child is happy, settled, and enjoying their day. We are also happy to arrange telephone conversations or meetings at a convenient time to discuss a child's progress in more detail. For our younger children, detailed daily care sheets are completed, providing information about sleep, meals, nappy changes, bottles, activities, and general wellbeing. This ensures parents remain fully informed about their child's day. We regularly share children's learning journeys, observations, and achievements through email, celebrating their milestones and progress. Parents are encouraged to contribute their own observations and achievements from home, helping us build a complete picture of each child's learning and development. Parents and carers are warmly invited to participate in nursery life by attending special events and celebrations throughout the year, including: Father's Day Breakfast. Mother's Day celebrations. Graduation Ceremony for our school leavers. Stay and Play sessions. Communication Week activities, where families join in language-rich experiences and storytelling. Sports Day. Cultural celebrations and festivals. Christmas performances and celebrations. Charity events and fundraising activities. Open days and family workshops. These events provide valuable opportunities for parents to spend time in the nursery, engage in activities alongside their child, meet staff, and build relationships with other families. We encourage parents and carers to volunteer for nursery outings, share their occupations, hobbies, cultures, languages, and traditions with the children, enriching our curriculum and promoting diversity and inclusion. Feedback from families is extremely important to us. We regularly invite parents to complete questionnaires and feedback forms, and we actively use their suggestions to improve our provision. Parents are also encouraged to speak with the management team at any time if they have ideas, questions, or concerns. Through strong communication, mutual respect, and genuine partnership, we work together with families to ensure every child feels safe, valued, and supported to reach their full potential. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? There is no access by car to the site. There is a gate which parents can use to access the building How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We warmly welcome all children and families, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), to Tot Town Nursery. Families can begin by contacting the nursery via telephone, email, our website, or by visiting us in person to arrange a tour of the nursery. During the visit, the manager or a member of the leadership team will discuss the child's individual needs, interests, routines, medical requirements, and any support they may already be receiving. We encourage families to share any relevant reports or information from health professionals, such as Health Visitors, Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists, Paediatricians, or other specialists. This enables us to begin planning appropriate support before the child starts. Every child is offered settling-in sessions, which are tailored to meet their individual needs. For children with SEND, we can offer additional or extended settling sessions where appropriate, allowing the child to become familiar with the environment, staff, and routines at their own pace. Before a child starts, we work closely with parents and carers to complete an 'All About Me' profile, gaining valuable information about the child's strengths, interests, communication methods, likes, dislikes, routines, and any strategies that help them feel secure. Each child is allocated a dedicated Key Person who builds a strong relationship with the child and their family. Our SENCO works alongside the Key Person to ensure appropriate support is in place from the very beginning. Where needed, we liaise with external professionals to ensure a smooth transition into the nursery. We believe in working in close partnership with parents and carers throughout their child's journey. Regular communication, review meetings, observations, and shared planning help us monitor progress and ensure support continues to meet each child's individual needs. Our aim is to make every child and family feel welcomed, included, respected, and supported from their very first contact with Tot Town Nursery. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? At Tot Town Nursery, we are committed to continually developing our SEND provision to ensure every child receives the support they need to thrive. We have recently introduced Sing and Sign throughout the nursery to support children's communication, language development, and understanding. This approach benefits all children while providing additional support for those with speech, language, and communication needs. We have also strengthened our partnership with the Family Support Service, working closely with families to ensure consistency between home and nursery. Where appropriate, families are provided with games and activities to use at home that mirror those used in the nursery, helping children practise and develop key skills in familiar environments. To further enhance our SEND provision, we plan to: Set small, achievable individual targets for children with SEND, which are regularly reviewed with parents and, where appropriate, external professionals. Continue to develop and review Personalised Support Plans (PSPs) and Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) cycles to ensure interventions are effective and responsive to each child's changing needs. Continue to build staff confidence through ongoing SEND training, including communication strategies, autism awareness, behaviour support, and inclusive teaching practices. Strengthen partnerships with external agencies such as Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Health Visitors, and the Buckinghamshire SEND Inclusion Team to ensure children receive timely and coordinated support. Continue to enhance our communication-friendly environments by using visual timetables, Makaton signs, visual prompts, and sensory resources where appropriate. Work closely with parents and carers to ensure they are involved in setting targets, reviewing progress, and supporting learning at home. Our aim is to create an inclusive environment where every child feels valued, supported, and able to achieve their full potential through early identification, personalised support, and strong partnerships with families and professionals.

description: The Tourettes Action Helpdesk provides confidential and impartial support to adults and children living with Tourette syndrome (TS). Tourette syndrome (TS) is an inherited neurological condition. It affects one school child in every hundred and is more common amongst boys. Over 300,000 children and adults are living with TS in the UK. Key features: The key features are tics, involuntary sounds, and movements, which must be present for at least 12 months to meet the diagnostic criteria. Up to 85% of people with TS will also experience co-occurring conditions and features which might include attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and anxiety. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with me. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is accessible for all children both inside and out. I have easy access via a side door entrance. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ form together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

name: First Steps Early Years Autism Family Support
description: Our First Steps Early Autism Family Support programme is now available for families with autistic toddlers and young children (age 3 or less) who are diagnosed with or are showing signs of autism pre-diagnosis. We provide multidisciplinary support in the family home and the service is available in the following areas: - South Bucks - High Wycombe - Beaconsfield - Marlow - Princes Risborough - Haddenham - Other areas of Buckinghamshire (please enquire) - (We also operate in Oxford, Colchester and Suffolk) Families with autistic children are often left to work everything out by themselves, with little meaningful guidance or support available either on the practical aspects of managing life or, crucially, on how to interact with their children in a way that leaves them feeling nurtured, builds trust and lays the foundations for a safe, loving, trust-based relationship in which the child can develop and thrive. Our First Steps programme focuses on this vital area of promoting optimal communications between the autistic child and their caregivers, and empowering families to build strong relationships with them. We consider this to be a firm foundation for everything else. First Steps is a support programme informed by the latest scientific evidence about autism in young children. It has been specially designed for us by researchers from Norland (a world-leading childcare higher education provider based in Bath that has been at the forefront of early childhood and inter-disciplinary inclusive practices for over 130 years) with the input of experienced child therapists, autism experts and parents of autistic children. It has been licensed to be delivered by the Transforming Autism Project.
organisation: Transforming Autism We are committed to empowering the families and carers of autistic children to optimise their life prospects and unlock their true potential. Our unique conception of autism, emphasising its potential and not seeing it as a disability, is at the heart of all we do. We aim to support parents to transform the lives of their autistic children by helping them to truly understand the needs they are not able to clearly express, and to respond to these in ways that make them feel safe, protected, looked after and strongly connected to those close to them. We aim to do this through support in the home, parent groups, our proposed intentive Mifne Clinic, and online materials including webinars, articles, interviews, online tools and eventually our comprehensive Autism Parenting Hub. Early Intervention is a key part of giving the right foundational support and understanding to an autistic child that will provide them with the strength and confidence to be able to find the best in themselves in later life, and we aim to work with and advocate working with children at the earliest possible opportunity in order to achieve this. services@transformingautism.org https://transformingautism.org/

name: First Steps Early Years Autism Family Support
description: Our First Steps Early Autism Family Support programme is now available for families with autistic toddlers and young children (age 3 or less) who are diagnosed with or are showing signs of autism pre-diagnosis. We provide multidisciplinary support in the family home and the service is available in the following areas: - South Bucks - High Wycombe - Beaconsfield - Marlow - Princes Risborough - Haddenham - Other areas of Buckinghamshire (please enquire) - (We also operate in Oxford, Colchester and Suffolk) Families with autistic children are often left to work everything out by themselves, with little meaningful guidance or support available either on the practical aspects of managing life or, crucially, on how to interact with their children in a way that leaves them feeling nurtured, builds trust and lays the foundations for a safe, loving, trust-based relationship in which the child can develop and thrive. Our First Steps programme focuses on this vital area of promoting optimal communications between the autistic child and their caregivers, and empowering families to build strong relationships with them. We consider this to be a firm foundation for everything else. First Steps is a support programme informed by the latest scientific evidence about autism in young children. It has been specially designed for us by researchers from Norland (a world-leading childcare higher education provider based in Bath that has been at the forefront of early childhood and inter-disciplinary inclusive practices for over 130 years) with the input of experienced child therapists, autism experts and parents of autistic children. It has been licensed to be delivered by the Transforming Autism Project.

local_offer: The Treehouse Pre-School is part of Southcourt Baptist Church. The pre-school is based in our fully accessible Pre-School building just across the road from the Church. We care for children from the term following their second birthday until they reach statutory school age. We strive towards ensuring all children and families are included in all we do, and we support every child on their individual journey.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Naomi and Warda form our SENDCO team. They both support and meet the needs of all children (this includes Autism, physical disability and speech and language needs). Naomi and Warda liaise regularly with other professionals to include those from Early Years, Special Educational Needs, Speech and Language Therapists, Pediatricians, Health Visitors and the Specialist Teaching Services. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENDCO Liaison Group: Termly SENDCO 2 Day course. Makaton Level 1 training for all staff How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At the Treehouse Pre-School we have a welcoming, inclusive environment where we encourage parents to approach us about anything in relation to their child. Prior to the child starting with the pre-school we carry out home visits and also hold a stay and play morning, giving new starters the opportunity to begin building up a parent partnership and key worker system. Our website is also fully accessible and is able to be translated into different languages. Where a child has a special educational need we will set up a Special Educational Needs Support Plan to reflect their requirements. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We hold daily morning staff briefings to share important information in relation to the children. For children with Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities we put a Support Plan in place which we discuss with parents to gain their valuable input. We offer termly meetings to parents and initially this will be in the form of a 2 year progress check and then parents evenings. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have a fully accessible building which is all on one level. We ensure we try and make any reasonable adjustments to help children with their progress. We work with parents, children and other professionals to ensure appropriate training and areas are made to support all children's individual journeys. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Our parents partnership is paramount to us! We make sure we give all families enough time to discuss their child's needs. We liaise with all other professionals in order to get the best results for each individual child's needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? All our staff will receive basic Autism training. Our SENDco will continue to attend Sendco Liaison groups where possible, to continue to be informed about any changes/updates.

local_offer: Our Senco has experience of supporting us to meet the needs of children with a range of SEND (including hearing impairment, autism and speech, Global developmental delay and language needs). She has liaised with a range of professionals including those from the Early Years SEND team, Speech and Language Therapist and Occupational Therapist (OT) Physiotherapist and Paediatricians. She attends the Early Years SENCO Liaison Groups. As a setting we have built excellent relationships with our local health team and our local schools.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The Pre-school is committed to working alongside parents in the provision for their child’s individual needs to enable us to help the child to develop to their full potential. The pre-school is committed to working with any child who has a specific need and/or disability and making reasonable adjustments to enable every child to make full use of the pre-school’s facilities. All children have a right to a broad and well-balanced early learning environment, enabling them to reach their full potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Marion Thomas Autism in Early Years (May 18) Advanced Speech & Language Development (Oct 11) Intro to communication with children with Learning Disabilities (Feb 13) Epilepsy awareness (Dec 18) Makaton (May 13) Autism Training with Caroline Kirkup (May 2018): Attendees – Susan Black, Marion Thomas, Liz Rowe, Kelly King, Pavla Udall, Sam Noury and Sharon Janes Speech. Language and communication training (Mar 2021): Attendees – Liz Rowe, Sam Noury and Sharon Janes. Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (Feb 2024) – Sharon Janes Understand Behaviour that challenges, Level 2 (May 2024) – Sharon Janes Early Years SENCo, Level 3 (July 2024) – Jessica Roberts. Understanding Autism, Level 2, Sharon Janes & Kelly King (July 2024) The Curiosity Approach (Oct 2025) – Jessica Roberts. Seeing Beyond Behaviour – Liz Rowe & Jessica Roberts (Nov 2025) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Treehouse is a committee led pre-school and we actively encourage our parents to become involved with the preschool. We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive, where parents feel that they are able to approach us about anything relating to their children. We have many informal opportunities for parents to chat with the staff and their child’s keyperson. Parents can request a meeting, and we aim to meet with them as soon as possible. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We operate an open-door policy and strive to provide a warm, friendly, welcoming setting so that parents feel confident in talking to us regarding their children. Every child has a learning journey which is updated by their keyperson and play plans are created and shared with parents. A child’s Key Person will support children with their development and together with the SENCO will identify if any additional support is needed. If additional support is required, we will work with the family to ensure the child gets the appropriate support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take into account the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We try to create areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning and to create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing needs. We use Makaton with all children to aid communication and also use PEC’s (Picture Exchange Communication System). How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? In the first instance parents/carers should contact the pre-school on 01296 712333 and speak with the Administration Officer Sam Goss What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? An additional member of staff to undertake SENCO training. Continual professional development for all staff in relevant SEN training. Attending local Senco Liaison Meetings to keep up to date on all updates.

name: TreeHouse School (London)
description: Mixed-gender non-maintained special school in Muswell Hill, London for 3 to 19-years-olds TreeHouse School is registered with the Department for Education as a non-maintained special school. The school was founded in 1997 by parents of children with autism. It is located at the Pears National Centre for Autism Education, Woodside Avenue, London. TreeHouse School provides children with the specialist, intensive and integrated support to enable them to learn, thrive and achieve. Our approach is highly personalised to reflect the unique qualities of each individual. Our emphasis is on developing communication and interaction skills, increasing attention, promoting ‘learning to learn’, establishing life, leisure and vocational skills and fostering independence. We work closely with the child or young person and their families to identify the things that are important to them, and use these aspirations to plan an appropriate learning programme. It is this personalised and collaborative approach which enables us to provide the highest quality teaching, learning and support. The contexts for teaching and learning are flexible; the use of a range of learning environments being carefully planned in order to give each pupil the best learning potential. Contexts may include school, a joint or additional educational placement, home, extra-curricular ‘clubs’ and the local community. Teaching and learning takes places within a school-wide ethos of nurturing relationships and celebrating progress, achievement and success. Where possible and appropriate, learning takes places in context, for example in our laundry rooms, our pupil garden and our teaching kitchens. At TreeHouse School, we believe in forging strong links with local mainstream schools, to provide opportunities for our pupils to mix with their peers. Several of our pupils take part in a range of classes at local mainstream schools, and this enriches both their learning in particular subjects such as music or sports, as well as their social and communication skills. We also run a programme of ‘Reverse Inclusion’ where children from a local primary school visit TreeHouse once a week to act as ‘playmates’. Getting transition right for each individual can be a challenging process, and TreeHouse aims to meet this challenge by a combination of person-centred transition reviews; high-quality information on options and the participation of the young person and the families themselves. We know with the right support and opportunities, children and young people with autism can learn, thrive and achieve.

local_offer: In our primary school, secondary school, and college we provide education to physically disabled young people, with complex needs, from 4 to 25 years of age. We have a wide range of different pathways, depending on their aim of placement, and every programme is highly bespoke. Some students will acquire the skills and qualifications needed for employment or higher education, others may follow a sensory and integrated pathway. All will have a focus on maximising independence and preparing for life after Treloar’s. https://www.treloar.org.uk/reports-and-publications What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We provide specialist education, therapy and care for physically disabled children and young people, aged 4 to 25 years. Our curriculum is bespoke and we are able to offer students the opportunity to work at all levels from Pre-Entry Level to Level 3 (A-level/Level 3 BTEC). We also have a range of excellent work-based learning opportunities. We work closely with feeder schools and families to ensure that children and young people are supported fully in their move to Treloar’s. The development of independence skills and achievement of placement goals are a key priority for our students. As students approach transition points, both within Treloar’s and as they prepare to leave us, our Transition Team works closely to ensure the success of their next steps in life. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? A full programme of mandatory training is in place for all staff covering all the essential skills for their roles. Teaching staff are all fully qualified and hold a range of specialist qualifications. Care and class support staff have an appropriate Level 3 qualification or are working towards achieving this. There is also an extensive programme of specialist qualifications and training available which enables all staff to be more effective in working in the student focussed multi-disciplinary manner, which the Treloar’s approach requires. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents/carers are involved in the whole process from assessment as appropriate, through their time at Treloar’s and into transition to their future placement. Our approach includes: - Parents’ coffee mornings - Termly drop in sessions providing an opportunity to talk to other parents with advice and support offered by Treloar’s PTA. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Treloar School has gained external accreditation for its parent/carer involvement through the Leading Parent Partnership Award. Communications are a high priority and include parent/carer training and support programmes, nominated contacts, access to online information on student's progress, drop-in sessions, home-school books and parent/carer days. Each young person is supported by a dedicated multi-disciplinary team including key workers and lead tutors. Communication is also supported by a large team of specialised Speech and Language Therapists and an in-house Assistive Technology Team. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The School and College are located on a single purpose built campus at Holybourne close to the town of Alton. The campus is fully accessible with a high proportion of the facilities on our site being built over the last 10 years. The campus boasts state-of-the-art facilities which include: - Specialist classrooms - Enterprise and life skills laboratories - Specialist art and photography rooms - Technology Hub and interactive learning zone - Drama hall and facilities - Well-equipped therapy suites - A fully equipped health centre - Residential houses offering a home-from-home feel offering first-class care - Sports facilities for a wide range of accessible sports - Newly refurbished swimming pool and hydrotherapy pool. - Rebound therapy room How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact us to discuss a visit and to learn more about what Treloar’s can offer your child. A placement at Treloar’s will usually start in September but we do take students throughout the year. We also offer outreach and family support services in the wider community. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are expanding our Supported Internship programme and working with the Department for Work and Pensions and employers to provide more internships and work experience placements to support our students with their transition in to work. Continue to offer training to external agencies. Continue to expand our fundraising activities to enable our students and others to access the specialist staff, equipment and experiences they need to grow in confidence and live a fulfilled life.

description: The Tumble Tots physical development program is a gymnastics-based, all-round agility class with different levels for children 6 months to 5 years old. Our youngest class for movers to walkers helps get babies moving and up on their feet. Once walking confidently the walking to 2s class gets your child climbing and balancing at their own pace Then onto the 2 to 3s class where the equipment gets more challenging and a more structured approach is introduced including listening and following instructions. local_offer: At Turnfurlong Infant School we have a named teacher with particular responsibility for coordinating provision for children with Special Educational Needs. Her name is Mrs Sarah Gerhardt. She is our SENDco. Teachers are continually assessing the progress, learning and development of all the children that they work with every day and we regularly talk to parents about the progress that their children are making. Some children will require additional support or specific resources to enable them to access the curriculum and make good progress. When children are first identified as needing additional support with their learning and development we actively involve parents and carers, talking to them about what we have observed. We then seek permission from them to refer to other agencies where appropriate. This may include working with and following advice from outside agencies such as Occupational Therapists or Speech and Language Therapists. We will use this advice to make a plan for the child that has short, measurable, achievable and time-related targets that will support the child to make progress. Some children will join us in our nursery or Reception class with needs that have already been identified and the SENDco and class teachers will work closely with parents, settings and other agencies to enable an effective transition to school. Children with Special Education Needs, including children of very high ability, are integrated into the classroom and taught by their class teacher. They may also be supported on an individual and/or group basis to work on targeted interventions. The school works to a staged model of Special Educational Needs in line with the Department of Education's Code of Practice. We call this 'assess, plan, do'. We ensure that parents are involved through the stages. Progress is monitored closely and provision is reviewed regularly. https://www.turnfurlong-inf.bucks.sch.uk/page/?title=Special+Educational+Needs&pid=25 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? description: Turnfurlong Infant School opened a new nursery in September 2017. name: Twelve Leys Green (Wingrave)
description: Green space in Wingrave, Aylesbury. The Twelve Leys area of the Village is mostly a 1970s development. It has a small green area near the village School and is an important recreational area for the children of that part of the village. Twelve Leys has a housing density of 25 dwellings per hectare with large and often extended homes with consequently small gardens and it is important that there is a small recreational space where children can play whilst under the eyes of parents. This green space is already protected. The Twelve Leys Green is 1,489 sq metres and is in the character of the adjoining properties.
organisation: Wingrave Parish Council The Knolls is a south-west facing steeply sloping field on the northwest side of Church Street just past Cobblers Wick. The field is used to graze a number of ponies but it has considerable recreational and amenity value to the village. For over thirty years it has been the location of the village bonfire and firework display to celebrate Guy Fawkes. In winter it has been used for more than living memory as the village tobogganing and sledging field as it has the most appropriate slope for such activities in the village. The field has spectacular far-reaching panoramic views over the Vale of Aylesbury to the Chilterns and on towards Chinnor. For all these reasons the field has considerable green space and amenity to the village. The Knolls is 1.4 hectares and is in character with the adjacent Church Street and the bounding agricultural land. info@wwrpc.org.uk http://wingravewithrowshamparishcouncil.org.uk/contact-details/

name: Tylers Green First School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Penn, High Wycombe for 4 to 7-year-olds. Tylers Green First School are a small village Infant school, with children between the ages of four and seven years, arguably the most important years of a child's education. Whilst they are with us in our school family, the children are nurtured and supported to promote their holistic development. We have an active school council and Eco council so our children's voices are heard in our decision making (they even interviewed me as the new Headteacher). We are very proud of our school in the heart of our local community. Our school has been in use since 1876, some of our classrooms are in a beautiful old building. We are lucky enough to have a large school field and our own extensive woodland area. We have a strong focus on outdoor learning and we are proud of our Eco-School status. All of our class names are trees to reflect this and encourage the children in their love of the natural environment. We place a strong focus on developing the basic skills that the children need to be successful. In the Early Years department, child-initiated learning is at the heart of the planned activities. Early reading, writing, and maths skills are taught in small groups to make sure that the children get just the right level of support. Moving into Key Stage 1, the children develop their academic skills through whole-class teaching and group work, based around termly topics. As an Infant school, we provide as much hands-on learning as possible to engage and enthuse the children. Our community is strongly supported by our parents who are very much part of the day to day life of the school. We hope to respect the traditions and values of all parents and support them in their aspirations for their children's future. We have a super Parent Teacher Association that run a series of events throughout the year to support the school. If you are considering applying to Tylers Green First School for your child, you are welcome to come and visit us. Please contact the school office to arrange a time to come and see our school in action.

This is encouraged and nurtured through a variety of teaching and learning approaches including whole class, small group, and individual support and intervention programs. https://www.tylersgreenfirst.co.uk/page/?title=How+we+help+children+with+SEND&pid=79 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? High quality teaching is our first step in responding to pupils who have SEN. This will be adapted for individual pupils in order to meet their specific needs. We use a range of interventions, strategies and resources to support the children across the curriculum. We have experience of and support children with a wide range of needs including; • Sensory and Physical • Medical • Social, Emotional and Mental Health • Communication and Interaction • Cognition and Learning Any additional needs that children have, whether short term or for the duration of their time with us, will be met by working as a staff team alongside parents with other professionals as needed. We work alongside a number of outside agencies including Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapist, Specialist Teachers and Educational Psychologists. We currently provide the following interventions: Language Link Speech Link Social Communication and Interaction Groups Support for emotional well being What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Makaton level 1 Supporting children with communication needs Supporting children's social interaction skills Using visuals to support children Step On training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parent visits are warmly welcomed and meetings with the SENCo can be arranged via the school office. We run a termly parent group to signpost and share the support available to parents. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children with SEND will have a written plan of support, this will be reviewed on a termly basis and updated following each review. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our site is fully accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Once places have been allocated to children with an EHCP, the remaining places will be allocated in the following order: Children in public care for whom the Local Authority decides that the school is the most appropriate. Children living within the catchment area of the school. Siblings of children who are attending this school (in Reception to Year 2) or our linked primary school, Tylers Green Middle School in Years 3 to Year 6, at the time the LEA makes the allocation, or who have already been offered a place to start in the current academic year at either of these two schools. Children who have exceptional educational, medical, social or similar needs, which can only be met by this school. Once the above rules have been applied then further places will be offered in distance order. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: Upton Court Grammar School (Berkshire)
description: Mixed-gender, selective secondary school in Slough, Berkshire 11 to 18-year-olds. The school, previously known as Slough Grammar School, changed its name to mark the exciting transition into its second century. The school values its tradition of excellence and honours all of those who have, through their academic credentials and personal commitment, become outstanding members of the community and role models for the next generation. At the forefront of education for more than a century, Upton Court Grammar School successfully blends tradition with a forward-thinking, internationally-minded educational philosophy that truly meets the needs of young people venturing into adulthood in an increasingly complex world. I am personally driven by the desire to challenge able students and nurture them to think creatively, critically and reflectively. Of equal importance is finding the appropriate level academically and allowing them to develop as a whole person through nurturing and valuing non-academic skills. I believe achieving academic qualifications is important, but also look to develop personal qualities like leadership and teamwork, determination and flexibility, respect and consideration, confidence and self-belief. We understand that many of life’s successes are governed by attitude rather than innate intelligence and that a strong work ethic will take you far in life. As a selective school, we provide academic young people from all backgrounds with the means to compete in the challenging future labour market and become principled and active citizens. We also value personal growth and expect our students to act with integrity and honesty, with a strong sense of fairness, justice and respect for the dignity of the individual, groups and communities. I am proud to say that our students understand the importance of intellectual, physical and emotional balance to achieve personal well-being for themselves and others. They are a credit to the school and to their families. Education at Upton Court Grammar School is about inspirational teachers and aspirational pupils based firmly on high expectations. We expect nothing but the best from our students who continue to reward our trust with excellent exam results, sought after university offers and exceptional levels of participation in extracurricular and enrichment activities. Our results speak for themselves and have been validated by an Ofsted inspection grading of Outstanding in every category. Upton Court is a successful school community built on a strong culture and curriculum which takes into account the richness and diversity brought in by its members. As a world-class school, we take our commitment to the wider community very seriously and expect our parents to be active participants. I know I can count on every single member of the school community’s support to fulfil one simple aim

local_offer: The Special Educational Needs (SEN) Department at Upton Court Grammar School is proud of our proven track record of managing and meeting the special medical and additional educational needs of our students who have a wide range of disabilities and other difficulties. We are committed to provide a broad and balanced curriculum for all of our students including those with SEN. We devote time and energy to ensure that all of our students have every opportunity to reach their full potential academically, socially and emotionally. All pupils are given access to the prospect of experiencing the depth and breadth of opportunity that our curriculum and wider school life allows. They also have access to a wide range of additional activities, support and educational study visits to enhance the teaching and learning opportunities. On entrance to UCGS in year 7, all pupils complete a reading and spelling age assessment and appropriate support is given to encourage all students to reach their full potential in literacy across the curriculum to ensure that they can excel in all areas of school life and personal development. Further assessment and monitoring throughout their years with us ensures that we are able to highlight areas of concern and address issues as they arise with suitable and appropriate strategies of support. We have a dedicated SEN team who work alongside teaching staff and the senior leadership team to offer invaluable support to individual students and their families as well as to other members of staff as necessary. description: Bring your toddler to weekly swimming lessons. At Beaconsfield Swimming we teach the ASA 'Learn to Swim' Ducklings programme, building confidence and skills in the children through play and games. Our private pool is beautiful, and parents can sit poolside while their toddlers get settled. It's a very fun, relaxed environment. Maximum 6 children in the class, with two teachers. Chest height water so it's fun and safe for our little fishies! Set your child on the right pathway to swimming success, building foundations for one of the most important life skills they will ever learn. Weekly sessions during term time. Simple online booking. Easy monthly payments. Join and cancel anytime. Classes run at Maltman's Green School boasting an impeccable 6 lane, 25 metre pool with fantastic facilities and plenty of free parking. Please do contact us if you have any questions.
organisation: Beaconsfield Swimming Ltd Swimming lessons for Antenatal and children to 11 years old. Our goal is to develop a long-term bond with participants. Following the Swim England Learn to Swim Framework (Pre-school, School-age, and Adult) our ASA Level 2 qualified teachers help build water confidence, and from this foundation teach the skills required to enable a healthy progression to an outcome of pure swimming joy. We are passionately inclusive and will build classes to suit everyone, just ask. Venue Information: Maltman's Green School is a beautiful private girls' school nestled between Gerrards Cross and Chalfont St Peter. The pool is impeccable boasting 6 lanes at 25 metres long with fantastic facilities and plenty of free parking. name: Victims First
description: Victims First provides free emotional and practical support to all victims and witnesses of crime or abuse, as well as family members of victims. It is available across Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, and Oxfordshire and can provide help regardless of whether or not the crime has been reported to the police. Support is available for victims experiencing any type of crime. This includes burglary, fraud, rape and sexual assault, hate crime, exploitation, and domestic abuse. Victims First can offer telephone support, face to face support, help through the criminal justice system (if reported) practical help, restorative justice, counselling and a specialist service for victims under 18. Victims First is managed by the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner for Thames Valley.

Victims First Emotional Support Service (VFESS) In Buckinghamshire, Victims First Emotional Support Service is one of the support services offered by Thames Valley Partnership, providing support to victims of crime. This includes people who have been indirectly affected by crime such as friends and relatives of victims. VFESS provides emotional support and advocacy as well as practical help and information. VFESS encourages its clients to regain a sense of control in their lives after they have been affected by crime – helping them to move on to a brighter future. Clients are supported by our VFESS caseworkers and trained volunteers via telephone calls or face-to-face contact. Whilst VFESS provides a broad support service for victims, we also have a good understanding of specialist services across Thames Valley and can often signpost to other useful sources of help. description: Victims First provides free emotional and practical support to all victims and witnesses of crime or abuse, as well as family members of victims. It is available across Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, and Oxfordshire and can provide help regardless of whether or not the crime has been reported to the police. Support is available for victims experiencing any type of crime. This includes burglary, fraud, rape and sexual assault, hate crime, exploitation, and domestic abuse. Victims First can offer telephone support, face to face support, help through the criminal justice system (if reported) practical help, restorative justice, counselling and a specialist service for victims under 18. Victims First is managed by the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner for Thames Valley.

local_offer: I am an Ofsted registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child. I have experience of working with children with ASD, ADHD and work closely with both parents and other professionals to support each child to reach their full potential.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to provide any children in my setting with a caring and supportive home-based environment. I encourage all children to reach their full potential, adapting situations to the individual needs of the child and enabling all children to access all activities in a manner that best suits their unique requirements. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in close partnership with parents, informing them about their child’s learning, development and progress through a daily journal. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Strategies for helping the child overcome difficulties are shared as needed. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children to support their learning and development and where there is a particular need, I support the preparation and implementation of a joint action plan, with the parents, for the child. With my parents’ permission, I may involve other services. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My home is accessible to most children and families. I am on a regular bus route for those needing public transport. There is a small threshold to the front door. I aim to find somewhere suitable for the children to rest when needed and would always discuss options with parents. My outdoor area is mainly laid to artificial lawn with borders and shady trees. There is a narrow side alley from the back of the house to the front, which is secured by a tall, bolted gate. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? As a childminder of more than 10 years, I have links with several local schools and pre-schools with who I work closely within supporting children through transitions. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their children. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. I am happy for practitioners from other settings to come and visit us before a child starts to help them to settle. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

description: We are located opposite the common in Holmer Green. We pride ourselves in working in partnership with parents right from the start. We have a fully flexible settling-in policy, which allows parents to settle their child in a way that puts their child’s needs first. Preschool activities cover all areas of The Early Year Foundation Stage both indoors and outdoors. In the garden area, we have a designated growing garden in which the children help to dig, plant, grow and harvest produce and then get to eat it at snack time or take it home to share with their family. We have lending facilities that include library books, educational fun activities, and rhyme/story sacks. We have trips out in the local environment to include the park, local shops, duck pond, an annual visit to the environmental centre at Mop End, and the local primary school. We provide daycare and education for 2, 3, and 4-year-olds, both for funded and fee-paying children. We provide snacks for children daily. This may include hot/cold foods and the children take turns to help to cook the snack one day a week on a rotation basis. We endeavour to work with families to meet the individual needs of each child's cultural or dietary requirements and we have numerous experiences with many different food allergies and intolerances.

local_offer: The Village Centre is a single storey building that is easily accessible. We have a disabled toilet. The garden to the rear of the hall is down a slight incline but is then a reasonably flat grassed area. On pre-start visits to our preschool, your child will be allocated a key worker who will begin to establish a relationship with both yourself and your child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We work hard to access specialist services on an individual basis including Speech and Language therapists and liaising with the Integrated SEND Service at Buckinghamshire Council to access appropriate support for the needs of each child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our 2 SENCO practitioners attend the regular SENCO liaison meetings and update their official training when required. Both practitioners attended an Autism level 2 training course in February 2020 to widen their knowledge and understanding of working with children on the spectrum. 1 practitioner attended a Looking beyond behaviour course in February 2020 to look at ideas and methods for dealing with certain behaviours. All information was fed back to all staff and new ideas were implemented into our practices. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are encouraged to be involved in the preschool and their child's development. We encourage parents to come in and help, allowing them to observe their child's interactions and talk to their key person about their development on an informal basis. Parents are encouraged to help with offsite walks and trips to increase our ratios and also allowing another opportunity for parents to be involved. We actively encourage parents to share their own observations on their child's Tapestry account and for them to make comments on our observations. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We actively encourage parents to read their child's observations on their Tapestry account, make their own observations and make comments. Additional information can be added for children with SEND. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Please see opening statement. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents can pass on their child's Tapestry file to their next setting. We encourage teachers from 'next settings' to visit our preschool so that they see the children in familiar surroundings and this offers the opportunity to talk to key person(s). We take children to the local primary school on their initial pre-start visit for a picnic and stay and play session. We use information passed to us by previous settings and from parents to make baseline assessments. In the past, we have made special arrangements regarding visiting next settings to help children with severe anxiety. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to update our training for the setting and for the need of individuals.

name: The Village Green (Wingrave)
description: The Village Green is at the historic centre of the old village. The Parish War Memorial is located here and this is where the eleventh of November Remembrance festivals are held. The area is historically significant for the village as an open space used for the social congregation and is already a protected area. This Green Space is 891 square metres and is in character with the local area.
organisation: Wingrave Parish Council The Knolls is a south-west facing steeply sloping field on the northwest side of Church Street just past Cobblers Wick. The field is used to graze a number of ponies but it has considerable recreational and amenity value to the village. For over thirty years it has been the location of the village bonfire and firework display to celebrate Guy Fawkes. In winter it has been used for more than living memory as the village tobogganing and sledging field as it has the most appropriate slope for such activities in the village. The field has spectacular far-reaching panoramic views over the Vale of Aylesbury to the Chilterns and on towards Chinnor. For all these reasons the field has considerable green space and amenity to the village. The Knolls is 1.4 hectares and is in character with the adjacent Church Street and the bounding agricultural land. info@wwrpc.org.uk http://wingravewithrowshamparishcouncil.org.uk/contact-details/

local_offer: Our SENCO Karen Suckling accesses regular advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child-specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor. A private Speech and Language Therapist attends the nursery two days a week to support specific children and give advice. We use a range of online resources such as Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites. We are happy for professionals involved with the child to visit and welcome this opportunity to develop our knowledge. We have close links with the local Health Visitors’ team. We are happy to attend Multi-Professional Meetings.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The Village Nursery Bellingdon is a privately owned Nursery that caters to up to 45 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We are a family-run business priding ourselves on our personal approach to all aspects of the setting. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share their children’s successes, achievements, concerns and hopes for the future. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO Training July 2024 Karen Suckling Makaton introduction July 2010 Karen Suckling Making sense of Autism March 2021 All practitioners SEN Support and beyond February 2021 Karen Suckling completing paperwork How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents into the setting on regular occasions when possible to see nursery life in action (play and stay session, teddy bears’ picnics, singing sessions, visits…) Parents have access to our Whatsapp group and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can request a meeting with their child’s Key Person at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible, this may be done via Zoom or in person. There are also many opportunities to chat informally. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has an online learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time. We will discuss progress at Key Person meetings, through our 2-year-old progress checks and end-of-year summary assessment sheets. For children with SEND we try to ensure that we are able to meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. We offer regular updates through meetings as well as telephone calls. We will regularly monitor the short-term outcomes for children with SEND and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT) are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits too or arrange telephone/zoom calls. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our indoor environment has been built to be fully wheelchair accessible; the garden is also fully accessible. We take into account the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible at all times. We try to create areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning and to create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing issues. We use Makaton with all children to aid communication. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child’s needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including home visits, frequent settling sessions and shortened sessions. We will be happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible to meet their needs. We liaise closely with other settings which may be shared by children. We have close relationships with the local schools and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently planning a quiet/sensory area inside the building for quiet activities and for space for children to visit away from the busier parts of the setting. We are also updating our visual support resources with the support of our Speech and Language Therapist. We also intend to develop our ASD training across the setting as a whole.
