local_offer: We are a warm and friendly setting who place a strong emphasis on inclusion for all children who attend. We value and respect all our children and their families and work hard to build strong and trusting relationships with them. We spend time with parents and children to ensure all their needs are fully understood to ensure our provision is both appropriate and accessible. Our highly qualified team of staff provide a happy and nurturing environment in which all children can develop emotionally and socially. All children are given time to express their views which are respected and listened to. We strongly believe that children have the right to privacy and to have their dignity maintained and the setting has clear policies to support this. We promote children's independence and support children at all stages to provide them with foundations for life as well as preparation for their transition to school. The setting has a 'record of commitment' to the UNICEF Rights Respecting programme which is reflected in the modelling of respectful language and behaviour by all staff to all the children. In turn, children are encouraged to reflect this in their communication, behaviour and actions towards each other. We have a wealth of experience in the support provided by outside agencies and have built strong relationships with them. We refer and access their expertise with parental permission and encourage this support to be provided at the setting where possible to maintain a consistent approach for the child. Our motto is: "Hi ho Hi ho we're learning as we grow" Children at The Village Pre-school learn through play in an environment that enables them to grow, develop and reach their full potential.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are an inclusive setting that provides support to children with additional needs, our aim is to support them as best as we can and ensure equal opportunities. Many of our practitioners are training in Makaton (to level 8) and refresher training for all key carers took place in February 2020. ALL of our practitioners are Paediatric First Aid Trained and ALL attend regular Safeguarding training. They have ALL also completed the required Radicalisation and Cultural Awareness training which we keep updated on a regular basis. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Both the manager and deputy have been on the 2 day SENDCO training, as well as another member of staff who is also undertaking the SENDCO level 3 qualification. They are also very up to date with any Autism training that can be accessed as well as Speech and Language interventions. The SENDCO's and Manager attend the termly SENDCO Liaison Group Meetings which are held locally. All of our practitioners have taken Makaton training and we regularly have refresher sessions in our monthly Staff Meetings. Makaton is an important tool in language development, it is a visual way of developing communication skills using symbols, signs and speech. Several of our practitioners have first hand, personal experience of children (their own) with SEND (ranging from severe learning difficulties, ASD to severe allergies) and are able to offer support and training to the rest of the staff team. We have one staff member trained in the Curiosity approach and Bucket time. We have enough staff to ensure children’s individuals needs are met in small groups. We also have speech and language interventions for those children needing extra support in this area too. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We like to include parents from the beginning of their child's journey with us. Our settling in policy for 2 year olds is based on Penny Tassoni's (a well renowned author and childcare professional) Settling in without Tears. It involves parents leaving their child initially for just 10 minutes with us and then coming back regardless of how the child has coped. This process allows the child to build up trust in the staff that their parent will come back when we say they will and allows bonds to be formed with practitioners in their parent's absence. Having said this we do pride ourselves in tailoring settling in plans to the individual child and parents. Some children may need more settled than others. Depending on parents work commitments too, we ensure we have create a settling in plan that supports everyone. The time away from the parent is gradually increased until the child is able to stay for the whole session happily, without the parent. We pride ourselves on building relationships with whole families to support them and their child(ren). We are open to comfort parents in times of need and will of course support them as well as their child through any process as a result of early suspicion or identification that their child may have additional needs. Parents are openly encouraged to join our Parent's Committee which is predominantly responsible for the very important fundraising to allow us to provide additional resources and experiences for our children (that we wouldn't otherwise be able to provide). How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We operate an Open Door policy and are always available to talk to parents if they wish to. More formally, we hold Parents' Evenings throughout the year where we talk through the childs' progress report with the parent. If we have any concerns about a child we will not wait until Parents' Evening to discuss it with the parent and likewise, we encourage parents to approach us immediately if they have any concerns that we may not have brought up. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The front entrance to the building is accessible by wheelchair as are all areas within the building, including a disabled access toilet. There is slight difficulty in accessing the outdoor area at the back of the building during free play as the back door is too narrow for a full size wheelchair. However, there are workarounds that we could put in place to ensure that any wheelchair-bound child could access the outside space. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have very strong links with the local schools and every year share information with them about the children who are leaving us to go to their school. Once the school allocations come out each April, we provide parents with a list of all the leavers' names and ask that they input their child's allocated school. This enables us to buddy up children who will be going to the same school. We have a wall display that we put up in the Summer term (once school allocations are out) and it has our Pre-school logo in the centre and 'roads' leading to the receiving schools (logos) for that year. We put a photo of the children along their appropriate 'road' as a visual for the children as to where they are going and who will be going with them. For children with SEN, or for those who show anxiety at this transition (it is a huge move and most will transition comfortably but not all), we work with the receiving school and the parent to build a picture book of areas and people within the school that the child is likely to come into contact with. The child is given the book and both parents and Pre-school staff will frequently look through it with the child to build a familiarity with the school and it's teaching staff. We will also arrange transition visits to the school (as many as we can), so the child's key carer at Pre-school and the parent can attend the school on many occasions if necessary to help to familiarise the child and build their confidence. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We always keep up to date with the latest SEND requirements, legislation and current thinking by attending all local SEND network meetings. Practitioners attend training appropriate to their key children and the general cohort of the setting (as well as ALWAYS attending the core training of Paediatric First Aid, Safeguarding and the mandatory training around Radicalisation and Cultural Awareness). We will try to ensure that all future staff are trained in Makaton.

name: Waddesdon Church of England School
description: At Waddesdon, we believe that the purpose of education is to enable all people to flourish individually and collectively so that they can live a life of value. As a community, we strive to achieve these aims, believing genuinely and unequivocally in the capacity and potential of every child. Our ethos is rooted and grounded in the Christian values of love, compassion, kindness and inclusion which foster dignity and respect for all. Students tell us that they feel safe and happy at Waddesdon School. Self-confidence, self-belief, and agency are nurtured through praise, encouragement, acknowledgement of success, and celebration of achievement. Our vibrant and positive culture enables our students to fulfill their potential as self-disciplined, responsible, and productive citizens who are proud to claim that they are a part of the Waddesdon tradition, the ‘Waddesdon Way’. Standards and expectations are high and learning is developed through a broad range of engaging and rich educational opportunities. We are a dedicated and motivated staff who enable our students to work hard and achieve highly. However, our school cannot simply be measured by our outstanding outcomes alone; it is also measured by the development and character of our young people.
organisation: Waddesdon C of E School Waddesdon Church of England School is a co-educational 11 to 18 secondary school with just over 1,000 students on roll, and around 300 students in the Sixth Form. Our daily routines and educational practice are rooted in the twin values of Dignity and Respect. Just as it “takes a village to raise a child”, so does it take a whole school community, in partnership with families, to educate a young person for life. We believe in positive relationships and promote the value of being a purposeful and productive member of the community in our work with our young people. Since being inspected in September 2006, when the school was judged as Outstanding by Ofsted, our sustained high results have validated this judgment for ten successive years. We are amongst a handful of schools nationally who are in this position. As a Church of England school within the Diocese of Oxford, our values are grounded in the Christian faith, although we welcome equally young people and staff of all faiths and none. An inspection by the Society for the Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools in March 2018 also judged the school to be Outstanding as a Church of England school. office@waddesdonschool.com http://www.waddesdonschool.com/

description: Waddesdon Manor is an ideal place for relaxing with family and friends with art collections, gardens, walks, an aviary, and the Manor Gift and Wine shop. Waddesdon Manor also hosts holiday activities and events year-round. Explore this French Renaissance-style château built to entertain the fashionable world and to house his collection of fine art. Surrounded by views of Oxfordshire, the Chilterns Hills, the Vale of Aylesbury and just a train ride away from London. Step back in time in the Victorian-style gardens, gaze at flamboyant colours on the parterre amid the ornate fountains and statuary. Unearth the rare and exotic birds housed in the rococo style Aviary found in the heart of the gardens or you can spend a fun-filled day with the family, be an adventurer in the woodland playground which winds through the trees, making use of the natural environment to create a magical area to play. Why not explore the trail around the gardens; hunt for bugs and spot wildlife along our woodland walk? local_offer: Gravelled areas Most parts of the garden are accessible. However, there are gravelled areas immediately in front of the house, on the parterre, and also around the Aviary. Steep paths You’ll find steep and uneven paths on the way to the Stables and down to the Dairy. The boardwalk through the Woodland Playground and the pedestrian path from the Powerhouse to the Stables are steep in places, so may be unsuitable for some mobility requirements. We advise you to use our fully accessible shuttle bus from the fountain to the Stables. Please note: we have a woodchip path which takes you to and from the car park. It can be muddy in places, and because of the surface it is not suitable for pushchairs, wheelchairs or mobility scooters. Dogs Assistance dogs are welcome in the gardens and inside the Manor. Non-assistance dogs are welcome anywhere in the grounds with the exception of the Aviary, Parterre and Woodland Playground. Dogs are not allowed inside any building including the house, shops and catering outlets. Please keep dogs on short leads at all times. Dog water bowls can be found at the stables. You may sit with your dog in the Stables Courtyard, Manor Terrace and Coffee Bar for outdoor refreshment. For more access information please visit the website. We’re very happy to help you plan your visit. If there’s anything we can do to assist in any way, please call us on 01296 820414 or email. local_offer: We believe every pupil has an entitlement to develop their full potential. Educational experiences are provided which develop pupils' achievements and recognise their individuality. Diversity is valued as a rich resource, which supports the learning of all. In this school, we recognise a child's right to a broad, balanced, relevant, and challenging curriculum, which is appropriate to their individual abilities, talents, and personal qualities. Our Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator is responsible for ensuring that provision is made for special attention to be given to children who experience learning difficulties. Provision varies according to the needs of the individual child. There is an agreed procedure that is standard throughout the county. Parents are kept informed and are consulted at every stage. If we feel your child would benefit from having some form of extra support a meeting will be arranged with you, and an SEN Support Plan (SSP) will be set up to ensure your child receives focused support. The SSP sets out targets in small achievable steps and is written and reviewed by the parents and class teacher, with advice from the SENCo. You will be kept informed of your child's progress on a termly basis. Teaching assistants work on a 'one to one' or small group basis, under the direction of the class teacher, with those children who have been identified as needing extra support. If your child does not require an SSP but requires extra support then they will receive targeted support that is documented on a provision map. This records the intervention, the frequency of the intervention, and the child's start and end levels in order to track the impact of the intervention. A provision map is updated every 6 weeks and at the end of each academic year it is archived. This way the next teacher is aware of the interventions that each child has already received. name: Walking Netball | Stoke Mandeville Stadium
description: Walking Netball has evolved from a growing demand for walking sports. Often, one of netball’s strengths is that people never forget playing the sport and the memories as well as the love for the game never leave. Walking Netball is a slower version of the game; it is netball, but at a walking pace. The game has been designed so that anyone can play it regardless of age or fitness level. From those who have dropped out of the sport they love due to serious injury, to those who believed they had hung up their netball trainers many years ago, it really is for everyone. Women the length of the country have begun playing the game of Walking Netball for the fun, laughter and camaraderie the social session brings, as much as the health benefits on offer. It can give those who feel isolated an outlet, provide an activity for those who don’t deem themselves fit enough to run anymore and offer a stepping stone for those looking for a pathway back into netball.

local_offer: At Walton High we aim to meet the needs of individual students through effective quality first teaching and learning. We work in a flexible way to develop partnerships with students and their parents, staff, and professionals to ensure that the school can meet a broad range of special educational needs. Our aim is to support students’ academic progress and achievement by removing barriers to learning using a wide range of strategies. In line with the Code of Practice (2014), a student has SEN where their learning difficulty or disability calls for special educational provision. Making higher quality teaching available to the whole class is likely to mean that fewer students will require such support. Slow progress and low attainment do not necessarily mean that a student has SEN. The Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Information report should be read in conjunction with the 5DT SEND Policy which can also be found on the Policies section on the school’s website. Our school currently provides additional and/or different provision for a range of needs including: - Communication and Interaction, for example Autism Spectrum Condition, Asperger’s Syndrome and speech and language difficulties. - Cognition and Learning, for example, specific learning difficulties; dyslexia, dyspraxia - Social, Emotional and Mental Health difficulties, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). - Sensory and/or Physical needs, for example, hearing impairments, visual impairments, processing difficulties and epilepsy. Information on a student’s special educational need may come from the vigorous tracking and monitoring of the progress of all students throughout their time at Walton High, to achieve this we use a range of tools and assessments: - Primary school data and testing. - Based line testing in year 7, for example cognitive ability tests and reading ages. - Round robin teachers feedback, to gather the full picture of the student. - Learning walks - Book scrutiny. - Progress monitoring in line with common assessment points. - Parental concerns and conversations to build the big picture. - END referral forms - Student Profiles – sharing High Quality Teaching and monitoring the student’s progress. - Student observations - Professional reports (i.e. Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Educational Psychologist Service, Specialist Teachers) - Communication between individual child, parents, and other stakeholders/ If the child or young person has an Educational, Health and Care Plan, parents/carers, and anyone involved in the support of the child or young person, will be invited to an Annual Review, this process is coordinated by the SENDCo https://www.waltonhigh.org.uk/information/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? local_offer: The Service works with young people aged from 5 to 25 years (but mainly aged 13 to 19 years), providing creative and challenging activities to help them reach their full potential and contribute positively to their communities. We offer group work programmes and one to one support, as well as residential experiences to work more intensively with young people to meet specific needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The Service works with specific groups of young people who need additional support. We aim to create opportunities for development, encourage leadership skills, advocate on behalf of young people and make learning and development fun. Our activity programmes work with young people to develop skills based on 6 themes: - Health and Wellbeing - Choices and Behaviour - Employability - Learning and Achievement - Decision Making - Personal Development. Young people are encouraged to look at the skills they think they need to develop and to develop a plan to help them to do this. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All of youth workers are trained to meet the individual support needs of the young people they are working with. This includes general training on working with young people with SEND as well as more specific training as required. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Youth Workers are able to communicate with young people and their families in a variety of ways depending on what suits them best. This can include email, telephone, or face to face meetings. For some projects, letters will be sent to provide important information. We have access to a signer to support those with hearing difficulties. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All of the buildings that we use are able to be used flexibly to meet the needs of young people working with us. All of our staff are able to support young people with mild to moderate support needs. Where there are specific needs we will work closely with young people and their families to understand the young person and look at what can be done to help them engage in the activities we offer. Our Youth Workers are not trained to provide personal care for young people but we are often able to access this support if needed. We have access to a signer to support those with hearing difficulties. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Young people can access our service in 3 ways: A referral can be made for one to one support by completing a referral form. This can be completed by the family themselves or by a professional who is working with the family. Young people can sign up to any of the programmes advertised on the Bucks Family Information Service Website as per the individual joining instructions We can be contacted directly via our email mailbox to discuss the needs of the young person and recommend suitable programmes or activities that may be of interest. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to develop the service to ensure it is accessible to those needing additional support. We will also ensure that staff are equipped with the appropriate skills and abilities to work with young people, families and other organisations to help young people develop their skills.

local_offer: We offer a broad and balanced curriculum for all children, including those with SEN. Please look at the school website for information on the exciting curriculum. Teachers are responsible for the progress of all children and lessons are well differentiated to ensure success and progress for everyone. Support for children with SEN begins in the classroom with the class teacher, but depending on their need, some children may require: 1. Access to personalised resources or adaptations may be made to the physical environment. For example, some children will need movement breaks, sensory resources, fidget toys, different coloured paper. 2. Individual, pair or small group activities to teach specific skills, usually linked to a target. 3. Individual, pair or small group intervention programmes. The programmes offered are to boost and support learning and are delivered by a Learning Support Assistant. 4. Classroom support from an additional adult to enable children to access the classroom curriculum. Learning Support Assistants work with children with SEN to enable the child to be as independent as possible and access the mainstream curriculum. Learning Support Assistants support the children with SEN in a particular class and will work with several children. All Learning Support Assistants work with a range of children and no child is expected to have an adult with them at all times: all children are encouraged to be independent where possible. All interventions are monitored by the SENCo. Interventions may support a particular aspect of learning such as reading and comprehension or maths, but we also offer social/nurture support to enable children to develop communication and social skills and increase their self-esteem. All children with SEN have an individualised SEN Support Plan, which is a live document and changes as the child’s needs change. The Plan is formally reviewed once a term as part of the SEN Review process. local_offer: Here at Wildflower Wendover Day Nursery and Preschool, we provide a positive and welcoming environment and are committed to the full inclusion of all children. All children have the right to be cared for, supported, valued, and educated to their full potential alongside their peers through positive experiences supported by all our members of staff, our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator (SENDco) and their parents. Our SENDco is able to obtain advice from the Early Year's team and also attends any local training or network groups. Through phone consultations or on site visits, we may gain specific advice from the early years SEND advisor, all while having parental permission and support along the way. We are also able to give advice regarding higher needs funding, SEND support plans, health and care plans, and EHCP plans. All our staff have been thoroughly trained with our SEND policy that has been created with: •The SEND Code Of Practice 2015 • Children and Families Act 2014 (Part 3) • Equality Act, 2010 • Working Together to Safeguard Children (2018) • EYFS To ensure each child's unique needs are met and supported, we can make reas onable adjustments to the nursery environment to enable each child to be able to access all the nursery's facilities, having a broad and well-balanced learning environment. We have a specifically designed sensory room to assist in developing emotional regulation, communication skills and social skills through calming LED lights, multiple shapes of large sensory lights, a mirrored wall, soft wall and floor mats and beanbags.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The goals in our setting aim to achieve a holistic approach to every child’s needs, ensuring that all children are treated as individuals/equals and are supported to take part in every aspect of the nursery day according to their individual needs and abilities. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Bucks SEND for new and aspiring SENco's May 2021 Our teams have access to Azilo, an on line training platform, which has over 60 courses, covering a wide range of subjects to support Early Years practice and children with additional needs. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are a welcoming and positive nursery and seek to be approachable and warm to both parents and children. Any of our members of staff are willing and encourage parents to talk to us at any time regarding anything relating to their child. If a parent requests a more formal meeting, one will be arranged as soon as possible. Every child has a journal on the FAMILY app where parents can see each observation and daily post, we encourage parents to use the messages feature on the app to message back and forth with members of staff during the day. Termly we invite all parents in for an informal meeting to discuss their child's progress if they wish to, with the children's summative assessments to hand the staff are always prepared to discuss any concerns parents may have. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children will have one next step to work on a month based on their interests, we gather this information from our observations, "all about me" form from parents during settling in visits and liaising with parents. On the first of every month, each room will have a "trigger sheet" to fill out with something they have observed the child do and is interested in, the practitioner will then plan an activity based on the child’s interest they have just observed, they will then write about the skills the child/children have developed during this activity, this is done a minimum of 3 times a day. We carry out focus activities: a planned activity once a week based on a specific skill or activity which is planned, observed and reflected then logged onto our FAMILY system where parents are able to see the activity and observation. Each child will have a termly summative assessment. Using the knowledge of the child, observations, and reflections to assess the child against 17 areas and age bands, this is completed by their key person and looked over by the management to ensure each summative assessment is correct. Where we believe a child may have additional needs that have previously been unacknowledged, we will work closely with the child’s parents and any relevant professionals to establish if any additional action is required. Where a child has additional needs, we feel it is paramount to find out as much as possible, we will work together with the nursery SENDco and the child’s parents and use the graduated response system to assess, plan, do and review to ensure early identification of any SEND. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The building is on 2 floors and we have a specific wheelchair lift to ensure everyone has access to the whole building. The front entrance is wheelchair accessible with a sloped path. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Email us at manager@wendoverdaynursery.co.uk to book a tour and receive more information specific to you or your childs needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are constantly adapting and coming up with ideas to include all of our children's needs. We will make the necessary adjustments to accommodate a child with specific needs, be that a physical need or a medical need that requires training to perform. Having staff that are always willing to learn about each unique child helps us provide the high quality of care we expect.

local_offer: Wendover Preschool is a small, inclusive setting based at The Memorial Hall, Wharf Road, Wendover where we provide high-quality care and education. At Wendover Preschool every child is welcomed as a unique individual, and we are committed to supporting every child to thrive.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? On entry, we use our “All About Me” form to gather information from families. This helps us understand your child’s needs, interests and starting points. We observe children closely, celebrate their progress, and plan individual focus sheets tailored to their unique needs. We recognise that every child’s progress is different – sometimes small steps, sometimes big leaps – and support them at their own pace. When children are not reaching expected stages, or moving beyond them, we use targeted learning strategies to help them succeed. We work in partnership with outside professionals, including Buckinghamshire Council Early Years Team and Children and Young People’s Therapy Services, to ensure every child receives the right support. At WPS we believe: every child can make progress if they are given the right support. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? EYT : Speech, Language and Communication - April 2022 SENDCO : Buckinghamshire Council SENCO Training - November 2020, SEND Diploma - September 2020, Early Years AET Professional Development Programme Anxiety Module - November 2022, Open University Understanding Autism - February 2023, CACHE Level 3 Early Years SENCO qualification - October 2023, AET Impact Study with Buckinghamshire Early Years Service - November 2023 Our team is supported by an Early Years Specialist Teacher who fosters teamwork, reflection and a culture of continuous improvement. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We encourage open communication at drop-off, pick-up, by phone or email. Parents are always welcome to speak with their child’s key person or our Early Years Teacher about well-being, progress, or parenting support. We hold a SHINE (supporting home, inclusion, nurture and early development) meeting approximately 6-8 weeks after a child start at WPS. It is a positive collaborative meeting that brings together the most important people in a childs life to discuss and reflect on how your child has settled and to share ideas and aspirations for the months ahead. Parents can book appointments for more detailed conversations when needed. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a focus sheet, which parents/carers can access at any time. Summaries of learning and development are regularly sent home to share with extended family. For children with SEND, we provide: • We provide SHINE meetings • Regular updates on short-term outcomes and strategies used • Extended handovers at drop-off and collection How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We plan our environment carefully to ensure it meets the needs of every child. We provide an area for focused activities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are invited to contact our Administrator to arrange a visit. During your visit, we will discuss your child’s needs with our Manager/Early Years Teacher and SENCO. We will agree on any adaptations required and assess whether our setting is the right place for your child to grow and learn. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our SENCO attends termly Local Authority Liaison groups to stay up to date with research, policy and best practice. We continually reflect on our practice, improve our provision and extend our knowledge through training and professional advice. Our focus will always remain on recognising and meeting the unique needs of every child.

local_offer: At West Wycombe Pre-School we treat every child as a unique individual who is a valued member of our friendly community. As we are a small rural setting with only a maximum of 30 children per session, all staff will know your child well and understand their needs. We work as a team and discuss individual children's progress on a regular basis, both formally and informally, to ensure the best possible learning outcomes for your child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? That they are able to achieve the best of their individual ability during their time at the Preschool. Each child is unique and so is our support, we ensure that we are able to adapt our resources and support for the requirements of each child that is able to access our setting. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENCO, Sarah is extremely dedicated with a SENDCo Level 3 completed as well as courses attended for Speech and Language support, autism awareness and many other additional courses. She attends termly network meetings with other local SENCO's to gain further advise and support and is always open to additional training that will support the children she cares for. The Manager Jo has also acheived her SENCo Level 3 training. As a setting our entire team have attend training on setting SENCO targets for our key children along with autism training. We have a highly qualified team who are passionate about Early Years support and intervention at all levels. From September 2025 we have also go a Deputy SENDco, Emma Jones, who joins with a degree in supporting children with additional needs. Emma will be working hands-on with our children and staff to ensure that all children who require extra support receive the best we can offer to ensure each child gets their own carefully built support plan in place as soon as a need is identified. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are a committee owned pre-school. We need as many volunteers as possible to help with our committee. If you do not want an official role there is also lots you can do to help with fundraising and supporting the staff team. We love it when our families get involved as it creates a wonderful sense of community for our children to be part of. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Practitioners work very closely with families to plan out and guide children through next steps in their development. Next steps will be planned for children as individuals and families can receive guidance from us on how to implement areas of learning at home through simple and fun activities. Any SENCO children requiring additional support will be given a detailed Access, Plan, Do, Review a set of paperwork which we will build with parents to ensure our practice is as supportive as possible. Children's development will be broken down into smaller steps so we can focus on key points which will enable children to thrive within their development. For those that need a bit more support we will create a SEN Support plan to cover the support they need within Preschool as well as any other external agency support or what might be needed at home. We aim for a coordinated support approach working closely with the family and child to get the best outcomes for each individual. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment is based on two levels and there are stairs to go in to all of the rooms and the garden. Our legs get a good workout each day! How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We are offering in person show around sessions that we would invite all parents and children to attend before signing up for the Preschool. Once they have visited and should the family decide to join us we will offer a home visit and then settling in sessions so make sure that all children feel comfortable and confident when they start with us. We also work very closely with a number of primary schools to get teacher feedback on how we can ease children in to the classroom. We focus a lot on the children's developing independence skills and emotional well being and understanding. Their social skills are also a big priority for us as we want the children to leave us feeling confident and well prepared to meet the other children in their classrooms. Teachers visit us in the summer term and we liaise with them very closely in the last few weeks before school to ensure a smooth transition. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are always updating our training across the staff team to ensure we are up to date and review the current cohort of children's needs to make sure that our focus is at its most beneficial for those we are currently working with.

At West Wycombe School we are committed to giving all our children every opportunity to achieve their best. The achievement, attitude and well-being of every child matters and inclusion is the responsibility of everyone within our school. Every teacher is a teacher of every pupil, including those with special educational needs and disabilities. We respect the unique contribution which every individual can make to our school community. We want to create an atmosphere of encouragement, acceptance, respect for achievement and sensitivity to individual needs. • We are committed to developing a level of education that provides equality of opportunity and high achievement for all our children. • We will strive to ensure that if a child has a special educational need it is identified at the earliest opportunity and that early action is taken to meet those needs. • We place the rights of children with Special Educational Needs Disability (SEND) at the heart of school policy and ensure that children are involved with decisions taken about the education they receive. • We try to ensure that we have a clear and flexible strategy for working with children with SEND and parents are encouraged to play an active role in the education of their children. • We believe that all pupils, whatever their ability or specific need, have a right to a broad, balanced and differentiated curriculum relevant to their needs. • We value all children and recognise that all children may at some time be entitled to special needs provision. • We do their best to secure appropriate provision for any pupil who has an identified SEND. • We strive for an ethos where children with SEND maximise their potential, are included fully in our school community and make a successful transition to secondary school and into adult life. • We have a shared responsibility for identifying, assessing, meeting and reviewing individual pupil needs. • We strive to ensure that each pupil is fully integrated into the life of the school and is given every opportunity to develop self-confidence, self-esteem and independence. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? • Our SENDCo holds the National SENCo qualification and has been appointed from the Great Learners Trust to support West Wycombe School with SEND whilst the Deputy SENDCO trains alongside her. At least one day a week has been allocated to SEND provision. • We have a team of teaching assistants, including two higher level teaching assistants (HLTAs) who are trained to deliver SEND provision. • Our Lead LSAs have a specialist broad area of need and have received training in their research based interventions. • We use specialist staff for assessment of SEN and consult professionals within Buckinghamshire Council such as CAMHS and the Specialist Teaching Service (for Cognition and Learning, and Speech and Language) when required, and PRU for behaviour support. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We will have an early discussion with the pupil and their parents when identifying whether they need special educational provision. These conversations will make sure that: • Everyone develops a good understanding of the pupil’s areas of strength and difficulty • We take into account the parents’ concerns • Everyone understands the agreed outcomes sought for the child • Everyone is clear on what the next steps are Notes of these early discussions will be added to the pupil’s CPOMs record and copies of the minutes can be requested by the parents. • We will formally notify parents when it is decided that a pupil will receive SEND support and from then on we meet with parents of children who are on the SEND Register three times a year (this is in addition to Parent’s Evenings) as part of the SEN Support Plan cycle. At each meeting we review the previous SEN Support Plan and discuss the new one, taking in to account the views and opinions of the parents and child. This is all evidenced on the SEN Support Plan. Meetings are offered face to face or virtually through online platforms such as Zoom. All parents are required to sign their child’s SEN Support Plan as evidence that they have taken part in the termly co-production of SEN Support Plans. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? local_offer: Some children have special educational needs which affect their rates of progress and their access to the curriculum. Our school has an excellent SENCo (Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator) who oversees the support we offer to these pupils. Many pupils with special needs simply require their work to be adjusted in class so they can access it, while some require specialist assessment and adult support. Some children are supported through an EHCP (Education Healthcare Plan) which sets out what needs to be done to help them and how much adult support they should need. Others need a smaller amount of adult support. local_offer: At Wheatley Park School in Oxfordshire we aim to be an Inclusive school that serves our communities’ needs effectively. We believe in quality first teaching for all learners and promote the value of every stakeholder in supporting young people to achieve. We are developing our programme of support with a large emphasis on sharing and disseminating information about learners through distributed leadership across the school and effective partnerships with parents. We know that every child is different and constantly changing and want to focus on each individual's progress in their learning. In teams, we have developed our communication systems to ensure teachers and support staff have the information that they need to support the progress of our young people. By sharing our individual knowledge with one another we are able to gain a complete picture of each child. We use our student Inclusion profiles to support learners who have significant barriers to achievement. Promoting the concept of growth mindset, we disseminate the information we gather to produce up to date student profiles using easy to access cloud-based technologies. Through this, we move students beyond their barriers to learning into a positive state of flow. We recognise that parents, having known them all their lives, know their child’s needs better than anyone else. Parents have vast amounts of information that can help teachers to improve the learning experience of their child in school but need to be given the opportunity to share this. By having regular reviews with parents with a renewed emphasis on the voice of the parent and the child we have a more balanced dialogue that promotes partnership working to support young people. Listening to parents’ hopes and desires for their child’s education and respecting their broad knowledge of the whole child gives us an insight into how individuals can thrive at our school. The contribution of teachers, tutors, middle leaders (Heads of Year, Heads of Department), parents, teaching assistants (Progress coaches), external agencies and the child themselves combine to produce a comprehensive understanding of a strategy to help students to learn. A key development was to train middle leaders to be part of the review process and to monitor the impact of profiles in school. Through observation and feedback teachers are becoming more confident in effectively deploying the strategies identified for individual learners to make progress. Listening to the child and placing a renewed emphasis on formative assessment for the ‘hardest to teach’ we have increased staff engagement in learning dialogue focused on inclusive pedagogy. https://www.wheatleypark.org/index.php/policies What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? local_offer: Class and subject teachers, supported by the senior leadership team (SLT), make regular assessments of progress for all pupils and meet three times over the year to discuss those identified as not making progress in Pupil progress Meetings. The assessments seek to identify pupils making less than expected progress or much higher than expected progress given their age and individual circumstances and this information informs the progress meetings and the support then actioned by the team. This is characterised by progress which: - is significantly slower than that of their peers starting from the same baseline - fails to match or better the child’s previous rate of progress - fails to close the attainment gap between the child and their peers - widens the attainment gap - is significantly faster than that of their peers starting from the same baseline and is Gifted and Talented Identification also includes progress in other areas of attainment – for instance, where a pupil needs to make additional progress with wider developmental or social needs in order to make a successful transition to adult life, for example is diagnosed with Autistic Spectrum Disorders (ASD) https://whitchurchcombinedschool.ovw4.juniperwebsites.co.uk/page/?title=SEN+and+Disability+information&pid=206 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? local_offer: We have two Additionally Resourced Provisions (ARPs) for pupils with Education Health and Care Plans (EHCP) or a Statement of Special Educational Needs for: • A Speech and/or Language Disorder (SALT) • Physical Disability (PD) where all pupils are fully integrated into the mainstream classes. Pupils access individual programmes with specialists such as Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists and Physiotherapists. They are supported by our highly trained Speech and Language Teaching Assistants who have recently been recognised by Buckinghamshire Speech and Language Therapy Service for their practice and ethos when supporting pupils with Speech and Language Disorders or Difficulties. The SALT ARP pupils' academic progress is closely monitored and supported by the ARP Specialist Teacher who tailors an individual programme in parallel with the Speech and Language Therapist. School staff are trained in individual programmes of Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy in order to support PD ARP children and any other children who have been identified with such needs. http://www.williamhardingschool.co.uk/special-educational-needs What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Applications have to be made as per Local Authority ARP Criteria. Numbers change as per Local Authority requirements. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Future developments for SEND provision include: • To continue to embed the SEN Support that was demonstrated during the recent Ofsted for progressing our pupils' learning. • Monitoring the needs of the pupils on the SEN List to ensure their educational and pastoral needs are met. description: The afterschool club opens from the end of the children's school day and finishes at 6:00pm, with the exception of Fridays, when the club finishes at 4:30pm. Children are escorted from their classes to the club where they can begin their fun for the evening. Children can take part in the various planned activities happening all week, and there are toys and games on offer for children to choose from too. They are also given a chance to play outside, providing there is dry weather. For children that would prefer quieter play or to read a book, an area is provided for them to do so. The children will be provided with a light snack intended to keep them going until they arrive home. This meal changes every day and may include things such as wraps, sandwiches and pasta dishes. We may run themed menus to reflect activities happening in the club or in the school. Please note that on a Friday, due to the early finish time, children will not be given a snack.

local_offer: At Willows Day Nursery we are committed to providing inclusive provision in which all children, including gifted and talented children and those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) are treated fairly and supported to achieve the best possible outcomes. We have regard to the Special Educational Needs and Disability Code of Practice: 0 to 25 years and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014. We believe that early identification of any specific needs a child may have will aid us to meet the needs of that child and their family and enable us to signpost them to and work in partnership with other agencies for support. We appoint Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinators (SENDCOs) in all of our nurseries to lead our SEND provision. We appoint nursery Quality Leader to support the SENDCOs, cover in their absence and take a lead on issues relating to behaviour. We have clear arrangements in place to support children with SEND and ensure that all practitioners and parents/carers are aware of this policy.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Sam has been our SENDCO since 2017 and prior to this was SENDCO at a nursery setting attached to a school. Jaymie is the SENDCO for under 2's and will work alongside Sam to support the children attending our setting. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Makaton for babies - Whole team training over a number of sessions Sendco level 3 training Samantha Price Sendco Training Jaymie Kingdom How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an environment that is welcoming and inclusive and where parents feel that they are able to approach us about anything relating to their children. We have formal opportunities for contact with parents in the form of parent consultation and Parent forum meetings. There are also many informal opportunities to chat and when parents request a meeting we aim to meet with them as soon as possible. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journey that parents/carers can access at any time online through the Parent zone app. We will discuss progress at Parent consultation meetings which are held twice per year, usually in May and November. A 2 year old progress check is completed for all children along with a termly assessment of progress. For children with SEND we try to ensure that we are able to meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short term outcomes and to work together to plan new outcomes. We will also include recommendations from external agencies who form the wider support team around the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Willows Day Nursery is fully accessible. through the information that we gain from observations and assessments we are able to adapt activities and environments to provide a bespoke learning experience for all children. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. We regularly receive visits from the local schools to which the children are transferring to enable their new setting to see them in a familiar environment. We offer a school readiness programme to our pre-school children to prepare them for their next stage of learning. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to review and adapt our provision to provide appropriate learning focus's for all children. Training is a key area of focus with both Sam and Nicole continuing with the CPD and disseminating this to the remainder of the staff team.

description: Boys' secondary school in Windsor, Berkshire 13 to 18-year-olds. Our academic offer ranges from vocational qualifications – BTECS – to A Levels in a range of ‘traditional’ and ‘non-traditional’ subjects. These varied options enable you to attend top universities, apply for an apprenticeship, or go straight into employment. Outside the classroom, there are unparalleled opportunities to assume responsibility, to develop sporting and entrepreneurial skills, to achieve greater self-confidence, and to gain new interests. We recognize that education is for the whole person and for life. Thus – apart from showing any potential admissions tutor or employer that there is much more to you than what appears on certificates – lifelong interests, hobbies, habits, and friendships flourish during your time in the Sixth Form: if you make the most of it. The next two years are among the most important you will ever face. If you choose to enter our Sixth Form, you will be asked to commit to being the best young man you can be. Being a Sixth Former at The Windsor Boys’ School is a privileged position, and comes with attendant responsibilities. If you embrace these, you will have an excellent chance to achieve, whatever it is that you are aiming for.

name: Windsor Girls' School (Berkshire)
description: Girls' secondary school in Windsor, Berkshire 13 to 18-year-olds. With over 200 students choosing to study with us post-16, we retain a very large number of students who wish to share in the success we achieve and we are delighted to welcome so many of our Year 11 students back to study in the Sixth Form. In May 2013, Ofsted judged Windsor Girls’ School to be Outstanding. In particular the Sixth Form was recognised as having improved rapidly. We have restructured our curriculum so that all students are guided on to the appropriate course which is best suited to their ability. As a result, our students make very good progress and are able to move on to the next stage of their education or training. It is not only examination results that make a Sixth Form successful. We offer the breadth and depth of experience, not just in your academic studies, but also in extracurricular activities. You will have many opportunities to develop leadership skills, represent your school and collaborate with local and national companies. We offer an ‘Aspiring High’ programme designed to support entry into top Universities. Our Enrichment Programmes are designed to help you grow in confidence, as you prepare yourself for life after school so that you leave Windsor Girls’ School as the best version of yourself. There are numerous Student Leadership opportunities in the Sixth Form such as our Year Ambassador programme. Students take part in a range of enrichment activities such as The Rotary Interact Club, Duke of Edinburgh and mentoring in the lower school. Entry to our Sixth Form is open to all present Year 11 students and students from other schools and colleges in the area. Please take time to read our prospectus carefully, as the choices you make are not just important now, but will also affect university and careers options. Take time to ensure that you meet the subject criteria for entry and that you have talked to Subject Teachers so that you are fully aware of the implications of the subject choices that you are making. We look forward to welcoming you to our sixth form.

organisation: Wingrave Parish Council The Knolls is a south-west facing steeply sloping field on the northwest side of Church Street just past Cobblers Wick. The field is used to graze a number of ponies but it has considerable recreational and amenity value to the village. For over thirty years it has been the location of the village bonfire and firework display to celebrate Guy Fawkes. In winter it has been used for more than living memory as the village tobogganing and sledging field as it has the most appropriate slope for such activities in the village. The field has spectacular far-reaching panoramic views over the Vale of Aylesbury to the Chilterns and on towards Chinnor. For all these reasons the field has considerable green space and amenity to the village. The Knolls is 1.4 hectares and is in character with the adjacent Church Street and the bounding agricultural land. info@wwrpc.org.uk http://wingravewithrowshamparishcouncil.org.uk/contact-details/

local_offer: We are a village Pre school, open daily from 9am until 3pm, 38 weeks per year. We work closely with all our children, family and carers to provide a safe, enabling and happy environment where the children can develop and progress to the best of their abilities  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Local authority Early Years consultants, who support the setting to work at the highest standard. We work closely with other professionals, where required, to support the children, for example speech and language therapists, occupational therapists and physiotherapists. Our team have also completed training in Speech and language development, and behaviour management to support the children in session. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our other staff have also completed courses such as 'supporting children with SEND' 'Teaching and modeling speech sounds to young children', 'All about speech and language development' and 'seeing beyond behaviour. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are dedicated to creating great parent partnerships and encouraging our parents and carers to feel involved with what we do. We operate an 'open door' policy and staff are available to talk to at the end of each session. We ask parents to be involved through baby's days online, where they can comment on observations, and add their own. For families where people other than parents do drop of or collection (such as grandparents or childminders), we have home and preschool communication diaries so parents have a direct method of communication with their child's key person. We communicate regularly with parents using email, newsletters and social media. We are also run by a voluntary management committee, so parents and carers and their families can be involved in the running of the setting by joining our committee. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We works closely in partnership with families to ensure the best possible outcomes for their child. Observations and development outcomes are shared with parents constantly using our online learning journal, and the targets that are being worked on with each child are discussed verbally with the family. Each half term we complete written next steps which are handed out to parents and discussed together. The SENDco has regular meetings with multi agencies and parents, to ensure communication is clear and everyone is working towards the same outcomes for the child. Professionals regularly come into the setting to observe the children when required and will review targets with us and parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The indoor and outdoor environment is on a single level, with the entire play space accessible for all. We have small children's toilets, and access to a disabled toilet if the small toilets are not adequate for space. We have a private space near the toilets to enable us to change children that cannot be changed on the changing unit. We do have a outdoor grass area that it raised and has 3 step to this area. but we would be able to have a look at changing this should we need to. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We support transition to each children individual needs. Some of the tool we use are: children to arrive earlier later than others. building up session times from 1 hr to full time. toy from home to support them. Each child will need there own support with input from the parents. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our SENDco and other staff continue with their professional development throughout the year, by attending courses, training, meetings and workshops. We attend relevant network group meetings to liaise with other settings and share good practice, and have staff strained in Speech and language development, behaviour management. .

description: Rainbows Preschool is led by a team of highly skilled and dedicated practitioners, it provides a caring, happy, and stimulating atmosphere in which our young pupils thrive. The setting is safe and engaging and benefits from a wonderful all-weather outdoor area of its own, which the children love! The children are also able to access all of our school facilities, which supports their smooth transition to the Reception class. They have opportunities to visit the extensive school library, use the computing suite, play in the woodland and on the large playgrounds and fields of the school. “Rainbows Preschool is absolutely perfect for preparing little ones for big school and I would highly recommend it to all parents.” “Mornings at Rainbows Preschool is the highlight of my daughter’s day. A fantastic, friendly, and safe environment that affords her a fantastic start in her academic journey … and she has the most fun ever! Highly recommend.”
organisation: Winslow Church of England School Winslow Church of England School is a two-form entry primary school with a Nursery. We cater for children from 3 to 11 years. In 2017 Ofsted graded our school as good. We are a caring, friendly school offering a broad, inspiring, and challenging curriculum. Our curriculum provides opportunities for children to learn in different ways and aims to create children who are independent and life long learners. We offer a range of after school clubs run by our teaching staff and outside providers to enhance and enrich our curriculum further. Our school is located within the market town of Winslow. It is situated within a beautiful site with open, green spaces, two large playgrounds with a woodland of our own for children to learn and play in. Our Early Years provision, also includes two further outdoor areas for play and learning. We are a school that is committed to the importance of outdoor learning and the benefits that this brings to the development of our children. All our year groups access the outdoor areas regularly. We are a Church of England school with very strong links to St Laurence Church, Winslow. description: Our vision is ‘Let your light shine’. The rainbow symbolises God’s unconditional love for each individual. We seek to reflect that light in all we do: in our community, both local and wider, our communication, both word and action, with curiosity and courage, and with care and compassion for everyone, inspiring a love of learning. We are a mixed-gender primary school in Winslow, Buckingham for 3 to 11-year-olds. Winslow Church of England School is a two-form entry primary school with a Nursery. In 2017 Ofsted graded our school as good. We are a caring, friendly, school offering a broad, inspiring, and challenging curriculum. Our curriculum provides opportunities for children to learn in different ways and aims to create children who are independent and life long learners. We offer a range of after school clubs run by our teaching staff and outside providers to enhance and enrich our curriculum further. Our school is located within the market town of Winslow. It is situated within a beautiful site with open, green spaces, two large playgrounds with a woodland of our own for children to learn and play in. Our Early Years provision, also includes two further outdoor areas for play and learning. We are a school that is committed to the importance of outdoor learning and the benefits that this brings to the development of our children. All our year groups access the outdoor areas regularly. We are a Church of England school with very strong links to St Laurence Church, Winslow. The Church team support us in many ways: with visits to the church, assemblies led by the Church team, as part of the Governing Body, and support us with the mental health and wellbeing of our staff and pupils. We have a dedicated staff who all place children at the heart of all they do. All our families are very important to us. We work closely in partnership with parents to ensure that every child can be the best they can be.

local_offer: At Winslow Church of England School, we are committed to making sure that children who require additional support are well provided for. As such, staff receive regular update training on SEND provision and SEND across our school is coordinated by a highly-skilled SENCo who has National Accreditation. We know that all children need different forms of support at various stages of their school career and we believe that each pupil has individual and unique ways to achieve their full potential. Our school aims to be an inclusive school and adjustments are made to the learning environment and to the curriculum to ensure that children with Special Educational Needs can achieve as well as others in the school, and become independent and successful learners. https://www.winslowschool.co.uk/page/?title=Special+Education+Needs&pid=25 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Winslow Church of England School has high expectations, and aims for all children to reach their full potential through the removal of barriers to learning and participation. Educational experiences are provided which develop pupil’s achievements and recognise their individuality. We want all our children to feel that they are a valued part of our school community and diversity is valued as a rich resource, which supports the learning of all. Through appropriate curricular provision, we respect the fact that children: - Have different educational and emotional needs - Require different strategies for learning - Acquire, assimilate, and communicate information at different rates - Need a range of different teaching approaches and experiences What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our staff all receive regular training tailored to meet the needs of specific children. This includes: zones of regulation, social stories, comic strip conversations, meeting needs of children with ASC, dealing with anxiety, and school refusal. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We hold regular parent evenings, SENCO drop in clinics, SEND coffee mornings and we have an open door policy for parents to contact staff whenever they need to. School work in partnership with parents in planning and reviewing SEND provision for pupils. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Regularly reviewed SEND support plans and provision maps. Regular contact from SENDCO. SENDCO drop in clinics. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Necessary adaptations will always be made for a child's specific needs. Ramps are already in place. All main areas of the school are wheelchair accessible. No stairs in the school. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Access to SEND support can be triggered through concern that despite receiving high-quality teaching and scaffolded support focused on specific areas of weakness the pupil still has persistent and long-term difficulties. At this point, a Special Education support plan will be produced in liaison with pupils, parents and specialist support staff, and external professionals to record strategies for a pupil with SEND. This document will monitor progress and set targets and will be reviewed termly. Additional high needs block funding/ Educational healthcare plan may be requested if a child at Special Education needs support still gives cause for concern and fails to make adequate progress despite additional, appropriate support. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Ongoing focus on the mental health and wellbeing of pupils with SEND. Adaptations and enhancements to the teaching and learning environment. Further development of curriculum planning to meet the needs of all pupils including those with SEND. An inclusion base and sensory room is currently in development to support children on our SEND register who have complex communication and interaction challenges or social, emotional and mental health needs.

local_offer: We are surrounded by Woodlands and countryside and have a fantastic garden for children to play in and explore. Woodlands has been at the heart of the Downley community for over 40 years. We pride ourselves in offering a warm and inclusive environment. We have an experienced and enthusiastic team who strive to meet the needs of every child in our setting.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Bea Frost, our SENDCO has experience in supporting children with a range of SEND, including Down Syndrome, Autism and speech and language needs. She has liaised with a range of professionals including those from the Early Years SEND team, Occupational Therapists, Educational Psychologists and Speech and Language therapists. Bea ensures that parents are informed, supported and included at all times. Bea attends regular SENDCO liaison groups. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO training (January 2019) - Bea Frost SENCO training level 3 (January 2019) - Bea Frost Autism tier 2 (March 2019) - Bea Frost Autism tier 2 extended (March 2019) - Bea Frost SEN Support and Beyond: Completing Paperwork Effectively (February 2021) Making Sense of Autism (April 2021) Developmental Language Disorder (June 2021) Speech and language specialism: Supporting children with speech sound disorders, stammering and selective mutism (June 2021) Approaches to Autism (May 2022) Supporting Children's Speech, Language and Communication in the Early Years (May 2022) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All staff encourage open dialogue and good relationships with parents. Woodlands has an open door policy, and parents are welcome to help for the morning and talk to staff whenever they need to share concerns or achievements! We hold two yearly formal parents’ evenings where parents can meet with their child’s key worker. Parents are encouraged to take part in their children’s Woodlands journey and will often come in to talk to the children about their profession, play an instrument or come with us on one of our many outings. Woodlands prides itself at being part of the community, and as such parents are invited to share in our fundraising events which are a fantastic opportunity to meet other families. We produce a termly newsletter and regularly update our website and Facebook page. Parents are invited to join the committee at the AGM in the autumn term. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has an online learning journal that parents can access at any time. Progress is discussed at parents evenings. Woodlands completes developmental checks for two year olds and these are shared with parents. Children’s progress is tracked termly across the areas of learning within the EYFS. Children with SEND are also encouraged to take home a home/school diary. This enables the parent and key person to communicate daily regarding short term outcomes and to work together to support the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The needs of individual children are taken into account to make our setting as inclusive as possible. Woodlands welcomes the opportunity to discuss specific areas of need with parents before their children attend the setting. The Pre-School operates from a Scout and guide hut that is not owned by the Pre-School itself. This may mean we are unable to make certain changes to the building; however we endeavour to work with parents to accommodate needs wherever possible. The pre-school operates out of two rooms; however areas can be sectioned off for quiet time and focused learning. We use visual aids and Makaton to aid communication. We have plenty of areas to sit quietly and play, and lots of space for those that need to run and access our equipment. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We are sensitive to the transition process and liaise with other settings to ensure that transitions are as smooth as possible. Records are passed onto schools, and teachers are invited to visit the children during a session at Woodlands before the children have a school visit themselves. Bea communicates with the school SENDCOS for children with SEND to ensure the children are supported in their new environment, and parents are invited to share in the process. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are keen to provide all staff with the skills to support children in resilience. Giving children the skills to bounce back from stress, challenge and transition makes children braver, more adaptable and more curious. The team at Woodlands would like to enable children to learn strategies at an early age that will give them vital skills and encourage more self-assurance and strength of character that will benefit them throughout life. The SENDCO is keen to develop ongoing speech and language training for all staff to outstanding standard. Ongoing training ensures staff are able to use the graduated approach to support children with English as a second language and speech delay allowing them to flourish.
