name: Woodrow High House (Residential Centre)
description: As part of the charity London Youth, we’re on a mission to improve the lives of young people of all backgrounds and abilities, challenging them to become the best they can be. Young people need opportunities outside school and formal educational settings, to have fun with their friends, to learn new skills, and to make a positive change in their communities. Woodrow High House is a grade two listed manor house, buried deep in the Chiltern hills. But that’s just the start. There are 26 acres of grounds to explore, numerous activities to get stuck into - from high ropes to archery, raft-building, and pioneering. You can make a splash in the pool, or have a kick-about on the 3G Astroturf, or perhaps try your skills out on our brand new off-road mountain bike track. Stay with us for a residential, or make use of our leisure facilities: the choice is yours. London Youth has owned and operated Woodrow since 1945. Each year, more than 7,000 children and young people visit us. We give each and every one of them the experience of a lifetime. Our vision is that all young people grow up healthy, able to express themselves, navigate a fulfilling career, and make a positive contribution to their communities. Our mission is to support and challenge young people to become the best they can be; developing their confidence, resilience, and relationship skills. Outdoor Centre: Our outdoor learning centre has an exciting array of adventurous activities to choose from, as well as some mind-bending challenges to tackle. Our expert instructors will encourage each child and young person every step of the way, helping them to step outside their comfort zones. We believe in the power of outdoor learning and adventure and welcome groups of all backgrounds and abilities. We welcome schools (both primary and secondary), colleges and universities, youth groups and charities, faith groups, groups with additional needs, and many more. We work with groups of a variety of sizes too, so whether you’re looking to bring 10 or 110 people. We offer residential experiences, day visits, camping, accredited youth leadership courses and so much more. Our experienced and friendly team will work with you, on a one to one basis, to design a programme that works for your group, based on the desired outcomes of your stay and with your young people’s needs at the heart of it all.

name: Woodrow High House (Residential Centre)
description: As part of the charity London Youth, we’re on a mission to improve the lives of young people of all backgrounds and abilities, challenging them to become the best they can be. Young people need opportunities outside school and formal educational settings, to have fun with their friends, to learn new skills, and to make a positive change in their communities. Woodrow High House is a grade two listed manor house, buried deep in the Chiltern hills. But that’s just the start. There are 26 acres of grounds to explore, numerous activities to get stuck into - from high ropes to archery, raft-building, and pioneering. You can make a splash in the pool, or have a kick-about on the 3G Astroturf, or perhaps try your skills out on our brand new off-road mountain bike track. Stay with us for a residential, or make use of our leisure facilities: the choice is yours. London Youth has owned and operated Woodrow since 1945. Each year, more than 7,000 children and young people visit us. We give each and every one of them the experience of a lifetime. Our vision is that all young people grow up healthy, able to express themselves, navigate a fulfilling career, and make a positive contribution to their communities. Our mission is to support and challenge young people to become the best they can be; developing their confidence, resilience, and relationship skills. Outdoor Centre: Our outdoor learning centre has an exciting array of adventurous activities to choose from, as well as some mind-bending challenges to tackle. Our expert instructors will encourage each child and young person every step of the way, helping them to step outside their comfort zones. We believe in the power of outdoor learning and adventure and welcome groups of all backgrounds and abilities. We welcome schools (both primary and secondary), colleges and universities, youth groups and charities, faith groups, groups with additional needs, and many more. We work with groups of a variety of sizes too, so whether you’re looking to bring 10 or 110 people. We offer residential experiences, day visits, camping, accredited youth leadership courses and so much more. Our experienced and friendly team will work with you, on a one to one basis, to design a programme that works for your group, based on the desired outcomes of your stay and with your young people’s needs at the heart of it all.

name: Woodrow High House Day Camps (Holiday Scheme)
description: Wild Woodrow Adventure Camps (Holiday Scheme). Wild Woodrow Adventure Camps are fun, educational and inspiring too. Come rain or shine we run through the school holidays (Easter, May half term, Summer and October half term). If you are a busy parent looking for support with childcare or just want your children to have a happy, healthy holiday then Wild Woodrow Adventure Camps is the solution. Running every weekday throughout the school holidays we provide a great venue for children to be children. Woodrow High House, is a 17th century manor house set in beautiful surroundings of 26 acres of woodland and gardens providing a safe environment for children to explore and use their imagination. We are located on A404 just outside Amersham, Buckinghamshire. Wild Woodrow Adventure Camps provide an open access scheme. This is a play-based provision for children between the ages of 8 and 12. We are Ofsted registered and the Early Years and Childcare Registration Handbook can be downloaded on our website. Timings and Prices: Drop-off between 8.30am and 9am. Pick up between 5pm and 5.30pm. We offer various discounts, check our booking portal for current discounts. We are registered with Ofsted and so are able to accept childcare vouchers. You will find a list of the providers we accept on our booking form. Activities: Each day is designed to involve a selection of the wide range of indoor and outdoor activities on offer at Woodrow High House. A typical day* at Woodrow’s Day Camps may include some of the following activities: Searching for hidden items on a scavenger hunt. Learning to tie knots and work in teams to construct a giant catapult in ‘Pioneering’. Exploring the grounds and learning how to survive in the wilderness during ‘Shelter Build’ and ‘Bushcraft’. Learning the importance of teamwork and communication as they navigate an obstacle course (blindfolded!) in ‘Nightline’. Experimenting with colours and designs in arts and crafts. Trying something completely new as they have a go at archery. Learning to build (and race!) a raft in the swimming pool. Letting loose as they play fun team games including ‘Wacky Races’, ‘Hide and Seek’, ‘Puzzles’, ‘Parachute Games’ and more. Stepping outside of their comfort zone as they take on the Jacob’s Ladder, Leap of Faith, Crate Stacking or Traverse Challenge, and overcome obstacles on the Challenge Course. *Please note that some activities may be repeated at different times each week and are subject to change due to weather conditions, or for logistic/operational reasons. We tailor the day to suit the needs/abilities of the group and therefore these changes may be made at late notice, without warning.

name: Access to Work Programme | Assistance for those with a Disability
description: If you’re disabled or have a physical or mental health condition that makes it hard for you to do your job, you can: - talk to your employer about changes they must make in your workplace - get extra help from Access to Work, including mental health support You can check if you’re eligible before you apply using the link below. You’ll need to provide: - your workplace address and postcode - the name of a workplace contact who can authorise your Access to Work payments - your workplace contact’s email address or work phone number - your unique tax reference number (if you’re self-employed) You’ll also need to explain: - how your condition affects you at work or getting to work - what help you’re already getting - what else could help you It will help your application if you’ve spoken to your employer about reasonable adjustments before you apply for Access to Work. Your employer must make certain changes to make sure you’re not substantially disadvantaged when doing your job. These could include changing your working hours or providing equipment to help you do your job. If the help you need at work is not covered by your employer making reasonable adjustments, you may be able to get help from Access to Work. You’ll be offered support based on your needs, which may include a grant to help cover the costs of practical support in the workplace. An Access to Work grant can pay for: - special equipment, adaptations, or support worker services to help you do things like answer the phone or go to meetings - help to get to and from work You might not get a grant if you already get certain benefits. The money does not have to be paid back and will not affect your other benefits.

local_offer: At WrapAroundCare4u we believe in welcoming all children into the WrapAroundCare4u environment regardless of any special needs or disabilities. Our processes and procedures are designed to ensure that we provide the most appropriate care and education for all of the children in our care. Our vision is to provide a safe, stimulating and nurturing environment that promotes all children's learning and development giving additional support to those who may need it, and creating opportunities for play based peer group fun. Our SENCo leads have all undertaken training for Nominated New and Aspiring SENCO, and we have a Level 3 Special Educational Needs Coordinator who oversees all services We work in partnership with parents, to ensure that parents are kept informed of their child’s progress at all stages, and welcome parents into the WrapAroundCare 4U site, or whilst this is not available, we welcome parents to speak to carers outside club hours to support their child’s individual development and learning  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? name: Wycombe Homeless Connection
description: We help people who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. If you have lost your home, we can help you find emergency and longer-term accommodation; with free advice and support, like how to claim the benefits you are entitled to; with practical items like clothing, emergency food packs, and other support to help you stay healthy and safe. If you are worried about losing your home, we can help you with free, independent legal housing advice, help to liaise with your landlord; help to access financial support to tackle rental debt; help you understand your housing rights, and much more. How we help: We can help you at our drop-in support centre in Wycombe and Chesham, over the phone, by email, by video conference, and can arrange to see you face-to-face by appointment. Let us know what works for you.
organisation: Wycombe Homeless Connection This service has temporarily been moved to a telephone helpline during the Coronavirus pandemic - 01494 447699 - please call between 10am to 4pm Mondays to Fridays for assistance. We help people who are homeless or at risk of homelessness by providing advice and support. We can also assist with emergency food, clothing and bedding. In addition to this, we also work to find accommodation for people who are homeless, we work with the Wycombe Rent Deposit Guarantee Scheme to find private rented accommodation, we can assist clients to register and bid on Bucks Home Choice for social housing and we can assist in making applications to hostels such as the Old Tea Warehouse and the YMCA, in some cases, we can also offer some financial assistance for the costs of moving into accommodation. We also help people who are at risk of homelessness to try to help them avoid being evicted. This includes housing legal clinics where clients can see a legal aid solicitor for free. We help people to deal with some of the negative effects of homelessness, find housing and help people who are at risk of being evicted avoid it or find alternative accommodation. contact@wyhoc.org.uk https://www.wyhoc.org.uk/

local_offer: We support the needs of each individual child. Each child has their own learning Journey throughout their time at the Nursery. We have a dedicated team that ensures all children can access all that we offer. We have experience working with the local child development Teams.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We access relevant training for our staff through Buckinghamshire Council and work closely with trained professionals. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Lorraine Murphy - Senior manager has been the SENDco for many years. Nichola Bowles has recently completed her SENDco training in Spring 2023 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? On Induction to the Nursery parents are asked to share as much information to make sure we can support the child throughout their time with us. Through Observation we can establish 'Next Steps' with the parents to share at home and Nursery. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We have an 'Open house' policy where parents can arrange to meet with their child's Key person, Nursery Manager or SENDco to discuss their child's individual needs. We hold Open Evenings throughout the year. SEND children may have targets set through outside child professionals and through home and Nursery Observation that can be discussed with parents to develop and adapt them to suit the changing needs of the child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The main entrance to the nursery has steps, the second entrance has sloped access. All rooms in the nursery are accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? As long as we have availability, we have a settling in period of one or two weeks, this can be increased if we feel the child may need more time to adapt to the setting and being away from their parents/carers. name: Wycombe Swan
description: Wycombe Swan is one of the UK's leading regional theatres. Presenting an eclectic mix of productions throughout the year, the Wycombe Swan is home to great comedy acts (including the Chuckle Brothers), dance (including Swan Lake), drama, musicals (including Hairspray), special local events, as well as the Wycombe Swan Summer Youth Project - an annual musical production featuring over 100 local young people. It is also home to the Wycombe Swan Youth Theatre - a permanent Youth Theatre Company open to 7 to 18-year-olds. As well as running workshops and performance-based activities, the Youth Theatre present a show every year. Wycombe Swan complex consists of the main theatre, Old Town Hall and the Oak Room - an ornate setting for functions and parties. It has a capacity of 1076.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? No recent training How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with us. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with schools and day nursery’s to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey‘ What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information through online resources and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

name: Yoga for Mum and Baby (Wendover)
description: The body undergoes huge change during pregnancy and childbirth. YogaBellies for Mum and Baby is a unique postnatal yoga class which focuses on mum’s three main areas of concern: the back, the abdominal muscles, and the pelvic floor. We focus on rebuilding these three key areas post-natally, at a pace that suits you. As the integrity of each of these key areas is interconnected, we work on all three at once to help bring back structural integrity to your body. At YogaBellies for Mum and Baby, we don’t “put baby in the corner” while you practice yoga. Our exclusive postnatal classes also incorporate baby yoga postures for your little one too so that they can practice with mummy! As every aspect of your life will include baby now, we help you integrate baby into your yoga practice, while feeling the benefits of yoga for you too. You will also learn breath awareness and relaxation techniques, which help to increase energy levels and allow you to relax while with baby (yes it is possible) Yoga provides a wonderful resource for you and your baby that allows you to deal positively with stress, encourage mindful relaxation in your role as a mother, and to help gently guide the body and mind back to their former glory.

name: Pregnancy Yoga (Halton)
description: YogaBellies for Pregnancy sessions are unique, revolutionary prenatal yoga classes for pregnant women. We use traditional yoga postures (asana), adapted and beneficial for pregnancy and the common ailments associated with pregnancy. YogaBellies for Pregnancy classes also include an especially created combination of self-hypnosis and yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and breathing techniques for pregnancy and birth (pranayama). YogaBellies pre-natal yoga classes are gentle and safe for all women, whether you are new to yoga or have years of practice. Each class lasts 1 hour and 15 minutes and each week focuses on a different aspect of pregnancy and birth. This is more than just a yoga class, but also training in deep relaxation and preparation for birth and motherhood (I am certified in Birth Rocks training too). The classes are suitable from 14 weeks gestation onwards.

Schools get involved by contacting Jackie who will work with them to meet their individual needs for their students. description: The Young People's Service is a free service offered by Aylesbury Women's Aid for young women and men, living across Aylesbury Vale. The services can be delivered in schools, colleges and other youth organisations. The service aims to: • Offer a person-centered supportive approach to young people, enabling them to understand their rights to healthy, safe relationships. Raise awareness of the imbalance of power in relationships, and the influence this may have on young people’s intimate relationships. • Enable individuals to identify and reflect on their experiences and explore how they can express their feelings and behaviours in a positive way. • Increase self-esteem and confidence. • Empower young people to make informed choices within their relationships. • Educate young people on the early warning signs of unhealthy relationships, and where to seek support when needed. • One to one support available for those young people who have witnessed or been involved in domestic violence, in the family home or relationships. Our service welcomes all young people regardless of ethnic origin, disability, sexuality, nationality, and religious or cultural beliefs. All sessions will be run in line with our policies and procedures, including Equal Opportunities and Anti-Discriminatory Practice, Confidentiality and Access to Information, Protection from Abuse, and Safeguarding and Protection of Children and Young People. Copies of all policies are available on request. The service is available during term time only.

description: Young Persons' Psychiatric Clinic. Timely access to an experienced child and adolescent psychiatrist to help you and your child get things back on track. We have created a cosy private consulting room where a young person or whole family can be seen comfortably. There is also a cafe open on weekdays where you can have a drink or snack while waiting. Our initial assessment appointments are for an hour to enable a full discussion of the child’s strengths and difficulties and their background and life story. This enables a discussion about the nature of the difficulties and possible solutions. Some families may chose at that point to go and use self-help resources or to wait for NHS services, others may choose to proceed to treatment at our clinic. Treatment will be provided in 30 minute follow up appointments and will consist of talking treatment or prescribed medication or a combination of both.

name: Chalfont St Peter Youth Club | Young People with ASD
description: Youth Club for young people with Autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We run weekly session on Tuesdays during term time for autistic young people in years 7 to 11. We aim to provide a safe and calm environment for young people who wish to socialise but perhaps struggle to cope with larger, louder environments. The sessions are supervised by trained adults but benefit enormously from a team of trained young volunteer helpers. These helpers are on hand for each session to interact with the young people attending, encouraging play and social skills by modelling behaviour. The youth club has a state-of-the-art fenced outdoor AstroTurf sports court enabling the young people to play football, basketball and more. Also, air hockey, pool, table football, arts, craft and Lego are available at each session. The youth centre is the holder of the Queen's Award, the MBE for voluntary services which it received in 2013.

description: Youth Concern provides a safe place for young people to socialise and access support when you need it. The Drop-in Centre provides a range of activities including pool, games, free Wi-fi and free food for young people. We have excellent on-site facilities that are used by our clients including an opportunity to use IT and a purpose-built in-house Music Studio with high specification equipment and software and a large outdoor space. description: The aim of Youth Theatre at The Theatre Shed is to inspire, innovate, and include through the medium of Performing Arts. Our inclusive workshops are professionally led and allow our young people to explore performance skills such as acting, singing, dancing, physical theatre, and more in a supportive environment. organisation: The Theatre Shed The aim of The Theatre Shed in Amersham is to inspire, innovate and include through the medium of Performing Arts. Our inclusive workshops are professionally led and allow our young people to explore performance skills such as acting, singing, dancing, physical theatre and more in a supportive environment. We would normally run in-person Workshops on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings with additional holiday Workshops. Initially when, due to the COVID-19 pandemic Lockdown and social distancing recommendations, we were unable to continue running Workshops at our normal venue at The Beacon School we were devastated. We didn’t give up and our Artistic team have worked extremely hard to keep The Theatre Shed up and running by going online. With so many young people needing a regular pattern to their lives we have been able to give continuity, stability and consistency. Good mental health at this time is so important. These sessions are really well attended once everyone got used to using Zoom and it now feels so natural to our members. This gives continuity, familiarity and activity in these extremely uncertain times. We didn’t stop there realising that there are others in the Community who would benefit from regular involvement in our activities so we expanded our activities to include Film Club for the Community. This is a chance to watch a film at the same time as your friends with an activity pack available to download from our website to go along with it. The chosen film is shown via our Zoom link so everyone can watch together. Our Community work continues with daytime workshops on a Tuesday between 2pm and 3pm and will have different themes (drama, dance, music etc.) each week. admin@thetheatreshed.co.uk https://thetheatreshed.co.uk/

name: SHAW Sexual Health Clinic (Brookside)
description: The Sexual Health Buckinghamshire website has a handy local service finder where you can locate your nearest: Sexual Health Clinic, Free Condom Site, Sexual Assault Referral Centre, and GP Surgery. There's also free information and advice on lots of topics, including: - Contraception - Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) - Post-exposure prophylaxis after sexual exposure to HIV - HIV and Prep (Pre-exposure prophylaxis) - Teenage pregnancy and young parents - Sexual Assault - Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) - Consent and healthy relationships - Understanding the body - Information for all ages, including the 50-plus years - Information for Parents - Easy-to-read information for people with learning disabilities There are bSHaW clinics at: - Wycombe Hospital (the SHAW clinic) - Brookside in Aylesbury In addition, there is a range of community clinics offering both contraception and STI testing. To find your nearest service, please call or you can use the service finder tool. Chlamydia screening and the Emergency Hormonal Contraceptive pill (EHC): Young people under 25 years can order free and confidential postal chlamydia kits and can get free condoms at a list of registered outreach sites as part of the C-card Condom scheme. name: Sing and Sign Baby Signing Classes at Home
description: Sing and Sign Baby Signing classes at home. We want you and your baby to enjoy Sing and Sign whenever works for you both. Whether that be because your little ones' nap times are inconsistent, you're returning to work, or you're not ready to meet in the venue at the moment. So we have created: 'Sing and Sign at Home’. We run at Home classes across the following age groups: Stage 1: 6 to 14 months Stage 2: 15 months to 2 and a half years What will the @Home course involve? For our Stage 1 and 2, our @Home course is a 30-minute pre-recorded online session with a new theme each week, which you can enjoy with your baby as a ‘home class’ and which is available for 7 days to dip into again if you fancy. Online lessons will be delivered by a variety of sunny smiling teachers, with all the anticipation of our blue board songs, props, and surprises from the bag and Jessie Cat will also of course play her games in her inimitable style. For a sneak peek of our @Home courses please watch the provided Youtube video. name: NCT Antenatal courses | High Wycombe
description: Our ever-popular antenatal classes and postnatal courses grow your knowledge and your network, allowing you to feel prepared and confident moving into the next chapter of your life. Discover and learn with other local parents-to-be, and make vital connections and life-long friends in your local community. Please contact for dates and times as these vary on a needs basis We lead the field in parenting education. Every NCT antenatal class leader is trained, licensed and professionally developed to deliver you a gold-standard antenatal or postnatal course packed with the very latest trusted information, practical skills and in-depth local knowledge. Our antenatal classes contain plenty of built-in bonding time - you’ll work in different pairs and small groups, practising new skills to get conversation flowing and connections sparking. With mountains of advice out there for parents, it's easy to feel overwhelmed and unsure. We provide evidence-based information and help you explore your options. We empower you to decide which information to trust and confidently make your own decisions that are right for you and your family. Course themes include: • Planning for a positive birth experience • Understanding and caring for your baby • Feeding your baby • Taking care of physical and mental health • Your family, relationships and finding support

searchText:
name: NCT Refresher antenatal courses | Aylesbury
description: Our Refresher courses revisit all the important information you learned from your previous baby. Everyone is welcome, you don't need to have had previous experience of an antenatal course to attend. You’ll reflect and build on your past labour experiences, and prepare for the birth you want. With every new baby, your family life changes forever. Learn about the impact of introducing your baby to your older children, sibling rivalry and how your relationship with your partner can change. You will be able to address any feeding challenges you might have had before, and get evidence-based advice and non-judgmental support. Courses include dedicated time to discuss this, with support and information however you decide to feed your baby. The courses are a great way to meet other local parents whose babies will be around the same age as yours. We keep classes small and welcoming, with plenty of time to chat and get to know each other.

name: NCT Introducing Solid Foods workshops | Aylesbury
description: NCT Introducing Solid Foods workshops. Introducing your baby to solid foods can be a very exciting time but you'll also probably have lots of questions. We'll help you decide when the time is right, how to go about it and what to expect. Please contact for dates and times as these vary on a needs basis. Our Introducing Solids Foods online workshops give you all the information you need to make decisions that work for you. We make sure every parent comes away from our workshops feeling confident about feeding their baby. We’ll help you spot the signs your baby is ready for solids and give information on the risks of giving your baby solid food earlier. From baby-led weaning to traditional spoon-feeding, we’ll talk about all your options. We’ll discuss when and how to give fewer milk feeds, discuss meal and menu planning and make sure you’ve got all the important info you need to make your choice.

description: Introducing your baby to solid foods can be a very exciting time but you'll also probably have lots of questions. We'll help you decide when the time is right, how to go about it and what to expect. Please contact for dates and times as these vary on a needs basis Our Introducing Solids Foods online workshops give you all the information you need to make decisions that work for you. We make sure every parent comes away from our workshops feeling confident about feeding their baby. We’ll help you spot the signs your baby is ready for solids and give information on the risks of giving your baby solid food earlier. From baby-led weaning to traditional spoon-feeding, we’ll talk about all your options. We’ll discuss when and how to give fewer milk feeds, discuss meal and menu planning and make sure you’ve got all the important info you need to make your choice.

description: Independent special school in Derby for 6 to 16-year-olds. Maple View School is a new inspirational specialist school for children with moderate to severe learning difficulties, aged 6 to 16 years. Located in Mackworth, a suburb of Derby, the school is a short distance from the City Centre. The School is purpose-built with light, airy, and flexible education spaces, as well as quiet spaces and classroom, break-out rooms. The residential facilities are modern, spacious, and homely and the school has a large secure garden and play area, all making Maple View a fantastic place to live and learn. Children placed at the school have a range and complexity of needs including: - Autism - Moderate to severe learning difficulties - Speech, language and communication difficulties - Challenging behaviour
organisation: SENAD Group Alderwasley Hall School and Sixth Form is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 5 to 19 years with Specific Language Disorders, Aspergers Syndrome and High Functioning Autistic Spectrum Disorders, all of whom experience complex speech, language and communication needs. The School and Sixth Form are located on separate sites within five miles of each other and are situated in Derbyshire, close to the towns of Matlock, Belper and Wirksworth. The City of Derby is also within easy access. The aim of all aspects of the curriculum is to prepare students for adult life by fulfilling their social and academic potential. Young people are supported to develop and achieve academic and vocational plans, develop independent living skills and a clear sense of identity, enabling them to contribute to society in adult life. name: ReConnect
description: ReConnect is a specialist service in adult mental health services based in the Whiteleaf Centre, Aylesbury. We work with parents who have a child under 2 years and on a child protection plan. The service offers long-term therapy to parents who have severe and enduring mental health needs and a background of childhood trauma. Therapies offered support parents to stop repeating patterns of intergenerational abuse through treating their own trauma and learning to develop greater sensitivity to their child's emotional needs. The criteria for referral to the ReConnect service are: - Unborn baby or child under 2 is subject to a child protection plan. - Significant mental health needs in the parent where childhood trauma is present - The parent acknowledges the risks raised by the Local Authority and is willing to engage in therapy. How to Make a Referral: Any professional working with the family can make a referral to Reconnect with parental consent either by completing a ReConnect referral form. The referral form must be emailed to us using the contact email provided. Parents can also self-refer to the service. More information is available on our website. The ReConnect team also offer consultations to professionals and this can be requested through our team email.

name: Who's in charge?
description: Who’s in Charge? Child to Parent Violence and Abuse is the most hidden, misunderstood and stigmatised form of family violence. Programme and explanations It is a 9-week child-to-parent violence (CPV) programme aimed at parents whose children are being abusive or violent toward them or who appear out of parental control. The structure of the programme consists of 8 two-and-a-half-hour sessions with a two-month follow-up. Three-Part Structure | Group Programme Overall aims | Groups • Reduce parent’s feelings of isolation. • Challenge parent’s feelings of guilt. • Lessen deterministic thinking about causes (“he can’t help it.. he has ADHD” or “… he saw his father be violent”) – it is always multi-causal. • Reinforce belief in the possibility of change (without giving false hope or creating complacency). • Clarify boundaries of what is acceptable and unacceptable behaviour (harder than it sounds as there are many grey areas and we need to avoid imposing our values). • Arm parents with some simple concepts that have proved empowering: entitlement, and the power of being irresponsible. • Examine strategies for creating meaningful and practical consequences for unacceptable behaviour. The approach of most parenting courses and materials is to assume that children are basically cooperative and only need encouragement and positivity to be good. Finding consequences for children who care about little and don’t want to cooperate is very difficult. • Explore anger, both children’s and (often more usefully) parents’. • Encourage assertiveness. • Encourage self-care. • Reinforce progress and provide emotional support while parents are attempting to become more assertive parents. Programme Outline • Session 1 Introductions, questionnaires and genograms • Session 2 Cause and influences of abusive behaviour • Session 3 What is abuse? • Session 4 What can I control in my child’s life? • Session 5 Consequences • Session 6 Anger and breaking the myths of anger • Session 7 Assertiveness • Session 8 Self-care, future goal setting and evaluation • Session 9 Two month follow-up on goal achievement, evaluation and further goals.

local_offer: Acorn Montessori provide an environment and high staffing levels in which all children, including those with SEND are supported to reach their full potential. The excellent facilities provide a safe and accessible indoor and outdoor environment. At Acorn, we aim to help the children to work, play, co-operate with others and function in a group beyond the family. The children’s personal, social, moral and spiritual development will be nurtured, with emphasis on developing personal values and independence, gaining an understanding of themselves and others. Through close observations of each child who attends the setting, we are able to identify and monitor any early signs of SEND, liaise with the family concerned through early intervention meetings, to discuss any concerns. We can advise on the next best actions, and work with families to best deliver any additional support required during the child's school sessions. We willingly accommodate outside agencies and Specialists into our setting to observe, assess and if necessary, work with any individual child with SEND, and as a school, are able to support that child with an ongoing package of support and resources, during the child's daily sessions. local_offer: Barnowls Nursery & Preschool is an inclusive day nursery & preschool who support all children and their families. We regard each child as unique and plan for each child's individual needs. We want all children and their families to feel safe, happy, valued and listened to at Barnowls Nursery & Preschool allowing everyone a flying start.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to give all children who attend Barnowls Nursery & Preschool an inclusive start during their early years. We follow a personalised curriculum within Barnowls, supporting all children on their journey to school. Our curriculum - *Being independent *Being active *Being a good communicator *Love of reading *Magic at Maths For children with SEND we focus on the first 3 parts of our curriculum. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff attend regular network & SEND meetings. We have recently undertaken training called 'Understanding Autism' plus many other courses throughout the year including visual impairments, hearing, Makaton, speech & language. Several staff members have SENCO training. We have regular contact with the Early Years Inclusion Team at Bucks CC. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work very closely with all our families to provide continuity for all the children who attend Barnowls Nursery & Preschool. We hold regular meetings with SEND families to discuss progress and set new plans to support the children's progress. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Progress is shared in 'All about me' development files (nursery) or on Tapestry (preschool). We hold parents evenings throughout the year but we are happy to meet whenever is requested by parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment is fairly accessible, we have one internal low level step. When required, ramps can be put in place to access the garden which is all one level. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact us via email to arrange a visit enquiries@barnowlsnursery.com What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We plan to continue updating our knowledge through training and briefings. We plan to continue to build relationships with all outside agencies such as SALT, OT & Physio which will allow us to learn new techniques to support all the children at Barnowls.

As a result of the pandemic and people struggling to keep their children entertained and focussed, he has made his 30 minutes professionally produced magic teaching video free of charge for those people who get in touch. Children who learn magic have shown to increase their levels of concentration, dexterity, self-esteem and self-confidence. In a time where social interaction is more and more limited due to the pandemic, this is a small gift from Duncan to keep the young people of our country focused, excited and developing those skills the schools would have played such an integral role in helping nurture.

Our experience and child-centred approach is valued by students, parents and supporting local authorities who recognise that it has the potential to transform outcomes for students who struggle in a mainstream setting. organisation: Elstree Screen Arts UTC Reading opened in September 2013 for boys and girls aged 14 to 19 living in the catchment area. The UTC specialises in Engineering and Computer Science, alongside a broad and balanced curriculum and benefits from the support of local and national employers and leading universities. Life as a student at UTC Reading will be unlike any school experience you’ve ever had before. Using the latest technology, you will learn through projects and practical activities. Teaching staff run lessons and seminars to introduce new topics and are always on hand to offer support in our independent learning spaces. You’ll also work closely with our industry partners on projects and challenges they set. Wednesday and Friday afternoons will give you a break from your studies as you get involved in creative or sporting enrichment activities. You won’t need to take any work home with you, as our long day means that you have time to complete it at the UTC. At UTC Reading you can study for a range of GCSEs, BTECs and A-Levels. Find out more about studying in Year 10 or Post 16. You don’t need to pass any tests or pay any fees to join UTC Reading in Year 10. local_offer: At Elstree Screen Arts, we strive to support all learners and enable them to achieve at school. To do this, we take many steps to support them through their learning journey. All our staff strive to ensure our school is inclusive. We share a mutual ethos that every child matters; therefore, we aim to address each learner’s needs and support their development in the most appropriate way possible to ensure we celebrate effort as much as achievement. The identification of SEND is embedded in the whole school process of monitoring the progress and development of all learners. We recognise the benefits of early identification and making effective provisions for improving the long-term outcomes for children with SEND. The process of ongoing teacher assessments and termly learner progress meetings with the leadership team identifies those learners making less than expected progress given their age or where the attainment gap between the learner and their peers widens. We also value the importance of identifying the full range of needs, not simply the primary needs of a learner. This also may include areas other than attainment identified by the school pastoral teams. For example, social needs, mental health or ability to manage their emotions. The school’s first response is high-quality adapted teaching by the class teacher and additional pastoral support. Where progress continues to be less than expected, staff will discuss their concerns with the SENCo and where appropriate an assessment of their needs is undertaken. The SENCo will decide on the needed SEND provisions based on the information gathered from the school alongside the views of the parents/carer and learner. Where learners have higher levels of need, and with parental permission, the school may seek advice from external agencies. Alongside a process of ongoing teacher assessments and termly learner progress meetings other mechanisms for early identification and assessment are: - Cognitive assessment testing (CATs) - Verbal Reasoning Test - Dyslexia screening test - Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) If the support required can be provided by adapting the school’s core offer, then a learner might not be considered SEND or placed on the SEND register. organisation: High Wycombe Chair Making Museum CIC Visit our Chair Making Museum CIC at Kraft Village. We are now a CIC, not for profit company. Wycombe has a wonderful chair making heritage, we made 4,700 chairs a day here in 1875. Our Museum tour explains how the Bodgers in the local Beech woods cut and turned the round Bodgers, Bench men and Framers, that made the assembled the Windsor chairs. We include a demonstration of rounding a billet on the shave horse and show how a chair leg is turned on the pole and treadle lathes. Besides the various old tools, we also have a display of Windsor chairs and provide an explanation of the history and different types. Kraft Village also has a contemporary art gallery, craft gift shop and Kraftinwood wood-turning workshop, enquire about wood-turning lessons from Robert an RPT registered turner supported by the Worshipful Company of Turners. robert@kraftinwood.com http://www.kraftinwood.com/

local_offer: Acre Wood believes that all children are individuals; they have an equal right to be valued and listened to, and are entitled to access the nursery facilities. Acre Wood is committed to providing an inclusive environment and ensure that all children have the opportunities to reach their full potential where every child is able to access nursery care and education that stretches their learning and development. Children and their families are treated fairly regardless of race, sex, disability, age, religion or sexual orientation. Acre Wood prides ourselves on a welcoming environment, where staff are professional, friendly and committed to the setting. Children and families are supported throughout their time with Acre Wood to ensure a smooth transition through their early years and then to reception or school. We are committed to working together with parents/carers and other agencies. We aim to develop good practice and positive attitudes in the early years, and encourage an anti-discriminatory approach to the world in general and other human beings in particular. We believe all people should have equal opportunities to learn, develop and grow with dignity in a community of mutual respect. Acre Wood Nursery is committed to the inclusion of all children. All children have the right to be cared for and educated to develop to their full potential alongside each other through positive experiences, to enable them to share opportunities and experiences and develop and learn from each other. We provide a positive and welcoming environment where children are supported according to their individual needs.Acre Wood believes that all children have a right to experience and develop alongside their peers no matter what their individual needs are. Each child’s needs are unique; therefore any attempt to categories children is inappropriate. Acre Wood is committed to working alongside parents/carers in their provision for their child’s individual needs to enable us to help the child to develop to their full potential. Acre Wood is committed to working with any child who has a specific need and/or disability to enable every child to make full use of Acre Wood facilities. All children have a right to a broad and well balanced early learning environment. Acre Wood feels it is paramount to find out as much as possible about a particular child’s condition and the way the condition may affect his/her early learning or care needs by: Liaising with child’s parents/carers Liaising with any professional agencies Reading any reports that have been prepared Attending any review meetings with the local authority/professionals Regularly monitoring observations carried out on the child’s development All children will be given a full settling in period when joining the nursery to ensure all their individual needs are supported professionally. Acre Wood will aim to: Recognise each child’s individual needs and ensure all staff are aware of, and have regard for the “Special Educational Needs Code of Practice on identification and assessment of any needs not being met. Include all children and their families in our setting. Provide well informed and suitably trained practitioners to help parents and children with learning difficulties and or disabilities. Develop and maintain a core team of staff who are experienced in the care of the children with additional needs and name a Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO) who is experienced in the care and support of children with additional needs. Staff will be provided with specific training relating to Special Educational Needs (SEN) and the SEN Code of Practice. Be alert to the early signs of needs that could lead to later difficulties and respond quickly and appropriately, involving other agencies necessary. Identify the specific needs of children with learning difficulties and/or disabilities and meet those needs through a range of strategies. Work in partnership with parents/carers and other agencies in order to meet individual children’s needs, including the health and education authorities, and seek advice, support and training where required. Monitor and review our practice and provision and, if necessary, make adjustments, and seek specialist equipment and services if needed. Ensure that all children are treated as equals and are encouraged to take part in every aspect of the nursery day according to their individual needs, abilities and interests. Scaffold and challenge all children’s learning. Promote positive images and role models during play experiences of those with additional needs wherever possible. Encourage children to recognise their own unique qualities and the characteristics they share with other children. Celebrate diversity in all aspects of play and learning. description: Flag DV offers free legal advice appointment for victims of domestic abuse. The service is for anyone aged 18 years and over who needs advice about family law. Clients will be offered a telephone consultation however arrangements can be made if a face-to-face appointment is required and the service is free and available across the Thames Valley. The types of referrals Flag DV would expect to receive is where knowledge and advice are required about the following: - Divorce or separation - Child custody, residency, and arrangements including contact with a child in care - Advice about the legal aid process and application - Advice regarding non-molestation orders, occupational orders, forced marriage protection orders - Financial matters - General court proceedings understanding Referrals into the service are made through our website and can be made by you or a third-party professional. We offer an appointment in response to this referral being received. Consultation is given with a fully qualified family law solicitor. They will have knowledge and experience of family law including domestic violence or abuse. The advice clinic is designed to help give clients clarity on what people can do, and how to do it, so they can move in a safe way out of the abuse. Our service is open Monday to Friday during office hours, we also run a staffed helpline that is open Monday to Friday 11am to 1pm.

The types of referrals Flag DV would expect to receive is where knowledge and advice are required about the following: - Divorce or separation - Child custody, residency, and arrangements including contact with a child in care - Advice about the legal aid process and application - Advice regarding non-molestation orders, occupational orders, forced marriage protection orders - Financial matters - General court proceedings understanding Referrals into the service are made through our website and can be made by you or a third-party professional. We offer an appointment in response to this referral being received. Consultation is given with a fully qualified family law solicitor. They will have knowledge and experience of family law including domestic violence or abuse. The advice clinic is designed to help give clients clarity on what people can do, and how to do it, so they can move in a safe way out of the abuse. Our service is open Monday to Friday during office hours, we also run a staffed helpline that is open Monday to Friday 11am to 1pm.

local_offer: Both my wife and I have worked in the health and social care sector before with a combined experience of 20 years, cared for individuals with learning disability and Autism. With the experience gained previously, will work with both families and other professionals in partnership and give families the opportunities to access care for their children whatever their needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We offer a caring environment where all children are welcome and supported to reach their full potential. We work closely with other health care professionals to help us support children and their parents to ensure children are safe and their needs are met effectively. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Level 3 Award in Preparing to Teach in the Lifelong Learning Sector - August 2011 Level 3 NVQ in Health and Social Care - Children and Young People - December 2011 Positive Behaviour Support Training - December 2023 Learning Disability Training - September 2023 Behaviour That Challenge - January 2024 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Working in partnership with parents helps us keep parents and carers up to date on their children's progress and development. We encourage parents to share information about their children with us so that we are able to address any learning and development needs and also support the children and parents access support from health care professionals if required. Activities are extended to support children to their fully potential within our setting and share ideas with parents to use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Through continuing observations and assessments of children, we are able to identify if there is a particular need for the child. We support the preparation and implementation of a joint action plan for the child and other services are involved with parents permission. Families of children with SEND are given extra support, for example flexible in how we communicate with them, this could be in person, via phone, emails or electronic messages. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting is accessible to children and families, we have enough space for children to rest when needed. Our garden is securely fenced with a secure gate and we have park nearby and it is a 2 minutes walk from the setting. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We welcome all families to come and visit our setting before making a decision to join us. A welcome pack is provided to parents with information and happy to answer any questions. Parents complete All About Me form, we encourage parents to have settling visits with their children. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Access training and recruit qualified, skilled and experienced assistants to support us and ensure that children's needs are met. We regularly get updates with guidance from the Local Authority and their website. We constantly develop new strategies to support people with SEND and their families and aware of the need for flexibility within our setting.

local_offer: Princes Risborough Nursery has trained, experienced staff to support the individual needs of those attending. We have a trained SEND Officer, with all staff also trained in the SEND Code of Practice. As a setting, we work closely with parents/carers and professionals involved to provide the correct support needed to each child has the best early years start.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We intend for all children to feel confident, respected and have well-developed self-esteem to allow them to thrive in their learning and development before they go to school. As a setting, each child is valued by staff and peers and has the same learning opportunities as each other. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Early Years SENDCO Training Understanding Autism SEND Code of Practice Selective Mutism Asperger Syndrome Awareness Equality and Inclusion in the Early Years How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We communicate daily with parents using our online software system, but also online learning journeys, as a setting. To support SEND, we hold 6 weekly meetings to review outcomes and ensure there is support and consistency in both environments to support not only the child but our parents and carers. Princes Risborough Nursery also welcomes parents on outings and to annual events such as Christmas Nativities, Easter Parades, and Fund Raising Events. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As a setting, staff will communicate with you daily in person but also on our 'I Connect' Daily reports. Staff plan daily for individual children and observations will be shared online inclusive of photographs and videos. Termly (Or 6 weekly for SEND) we share learning reports and cohort trackers so parents have a learning journal of their child's progress and our future outcomes for the child. For children with SEND, this practice will still be followed, inclusive of 6 weekly meetings and specific outcomes - This is so we can identify what is working well, review progress at the setting and home and make early modifications in the provision to support learning. We will share reports with other professionals involved and work alongside professionals for greater outcomes and support. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Princes Risborough Nursery is a very inclusive and accessible setting, with disabled car parking on-site and wheelchair access via a ramp around the side of the building to the pre-school entry. Our garden is accessible via the pre-school room with a free flow option with level flooring. Our nursery is all on one lower level, with an accessible toilet and nappy changing area, low-level sleep pods in a separate sleep room, and separate, spacious eating facilities. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact us via email or telephone to book a show round, meet the team! local_offer: The kinds of Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) that are provided for at The Langley Academy: - The Academy has a specialist Hearing Resource Base with staff who have received specialist training in supporting students with a Hearing Impairment. - All members of staff are responsible for helping to meet students Special Educational Needs and for helping the Academy to identify students who may need extra support. - The school gives such support as can be reasonably provided by a mainstream school for a wide range of SEND, including Dyslexia, Autism, Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, hearing impairments, visual impairments, Dyspraxia, social and emotional difficulties, Epilepsy, Speech, and Language Disorder, as well as more specific learning difficulties and physical impairments. Students with SEND are allocated places in two separate and distinct ways: Those students with Education, Health, and Care Plans (EHCPs) have a separate admissions procedure overseen by the SEND team at Slough Borough Council. Those students who have SEND but do not have an EHCP are admitted via the normal school admissions process. As students learning needs may change over time, the SEND department and Heads of Faculty track progress on a termly basis. Student profile review meetings occur at least twice a year for all students on the SEND Register. Teachers, students and parents/carers can refer to the Academy Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCO) for an assessment of whether a learning need or disability is present. • Our SENCO is Joseph Matshazi. He has completed the National SENCO Award. Our Head of The Hearing Resource base is Arusa Ashraf. She is a qualified teacher of the deaf. The Academy identifies SEND students in several ways. name: Tring Park Associates | Holiday Camps
description: Classes at Tring Park Associates are available to children and young people from ages 3 to 19 years and offer dance - ballet, pointe work, contemporary, jazz, street dance, acro, modern, tap, and musical theatre dance, along with acting and singing. Classes run daily Monday to Friday after school hours and all day Saturdays during term time. They are held in the studios of Tring Park School and at nearby Victoria Hall. Entry from age 3 to 8 years is without audition with three auditions a year held for students from ages 9 to 19 years. There are also adult dance classes, and Dance for Parkinson's classes which run during term time. Classical Ballet Academy The Classical Ballet Academy is designed to discover talented children and provide them with the highest level of classical training available. The programme is designed to complement their studies with their regular dance teacher. The focus is on honing and developing technique, whilst working with other talented children who share the same goals and ambitions to have a career in dance. The Kick Start Programme for Boys A special programme for boys only who are interested in Dance and the Performing Arts. Creating an environment where males can be inspired by working alongside other male students, often for the first time, Kick Start is targeted at young, male dancers who may not have many male peers at their own dance school. Wherever possible, students are taught by a male faculty, assisted by senior male students from the Tring Park Dance Course. Tring Park offers three training days each term where boys may take ballet, street/jazz, and other genre workshops. Senior students also receive upper body and fitness training. There are also opportunities to move into other programmes, where appropriate. Holiday Courses run throughout the year and offer diverse experiences for a broad range of ages. Courses vary in length from one day to weekend non-residential, to our Easter and summer residential courses which are four or five days, depending on the genre. Residential courses are not limited to boarders – day pupils are very welcome. There is no audition requirement for any of the courses, however, each course does stipulate ages and recommended experience on the information and booking page. All booking takes place through the online page relating to the course and courses remain open until the stated closing date (on the booking page). However, residential course bookings may close sooner than initially advertised if all available dormitories become full, so early booking is advised. The teaching staff are recruited for their experience within the profession and their teaching skills. Some staff also work at Tring Park School for the Performing Arts, whilst others are guest teachers solely on the Holiday Courses. All courses are tailored to provide a valuable experience within the given genre. All courses will be the same price as 2019, and we are also introducing a discounted rate when booking 3 or more day or weekend courses.

local_offer: Bucks Activity Project is part of the Action for Children Countywide Integrated Short Breaks Service, commissioned by Buckinghamshire Council and provides community short breaks to children and young people aged 0-19 with disabilities and additional learning needs across Buckinghamshire. Children and young people can access our age-appropriate activities at weekends, evenings, and school holidays. Favourites include our play sessions with activities to support children's interests and learning, youth clubs, movie nights, cooking, general life skills, quiz nights, swimming, bowling, cinema, go-carting, water sports, laser tag and climbing, ice skating, mini golf, play in the park, farm visits, scavenger hunts and woodland walks to name a few. We seek the views of the children and young people when planning our programme of activities. Staff are trained to meet the needs of each individual child, supporting them to participate fully in the activity they are attending.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Short Breaks have positive benefits for both children and young people with disabilities and their parents and carers. They give children and young people time away from their family so they can develop independence, learn new skills, make friends and reduce loneliness whilst giving parents and carers a break from their caring responsibilities and providing time to spend with other children in the family. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All practitioners are trained in the following: Safeguarding Children BSCP Working Together to Safeguard Children Prevent Managing Equality and Diversity Manual Handling First Aid Staff are also trained in the following according to their role and the needs of the children and young people they are working with: Administration of Medication Asthma and Anaphylaxis Epilepsy Awareness & Administration of Rectal Diazepam Epilepsy Awareness & Administration of Buccal Midazolam VNS Training Oxygen Administration and safety Gastronomy and Naso Feed Positive Behaviour Management Team Teach SENCO Communication Makaton Autism Awareness Social Stories How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Practitioners aim to create a welcoming environment to parents and mutually share information at handover and collection. Practitioners also provide opportunities for parents to liaise further over the telephone/email. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Outcomes are measured for every child that attends. Practitioners share successes, wow moments and outcomes with parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All venues are fully accessible and have access to outdoors. Staff are mindful of children’s individual needs and are able to adapt environments and groups accordingly. Our staff are highly skilled in communicating with children and young people who have limited or pre- verbal communication, enabling every child to have a voice and communicate their hopes and needs. The staff and children and young people use a range of ways to communicate with each other. Staff use the child’s preferred method of communication alongside words. Makaton – simple sign language used alongside words. PECS – Picture Exchange Communication System – These are picture cards that the child or young person uses to indicate their needs or wants and can reduce their frustration and supports inclusion. These are usually tailored to the individual. Social stories – individually made to support children for particular activities or events so they understand what to expect and why. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact us on 01296 438230 or email bucks.activity@actionforchildren.org.uk to request registration forms. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We continually monitor and evaluate services, adapting to the needs of the children and young people.

name: Partou Old Town Day Nursery and Pre-School
description: Previously called Beaconsfield Day Nursery Ltd as Old Town Day Nursery We believe excellent childcare and education depend on: Providing rich enabling environments, and stimulating activities Having knowledgeable enthusiastic staff to support children’s learning and development Working in partnership with the parents and families of the children in our care Training, valuing and rewarding our staff for the crucial role they play in supporting children’s learning and development Children and adults having fun! Our Beaconsfield nursery is purpose-built with 2 large rooms, with lots of natural light and specially created features. These bright and airy rooms give our children lots of space to explore, play and learn. The nursery is warm and welcoming and has a homely feel which we love and are very proud of. We’ve developed 2 separate rooms – one for our babies and our toddlers (3 months to 24 months); and one for our 2 to 3 year olds and our preschool children (24 to 60 months), enabling us to resource each room appropriately for the age group. Each room creates the right environment for us to care for, nurture and encourage our children to explore and investigate – and each room is equipped with the latest resources and toys. We also have extremely well-equipped outdoor play areas for the younger and older children. We have a hard-standing area with space for running around and enjoying ‘ride-ons’; digging and planting areas for older children; and a space for our babies and toddlers to explore. Our digging and planting areas are used to teach the children about growing and about food. We have ‘sand play’ areas and a ‘mud kitchen’ in which children can dig, build and experiment with sand, mud and water as they discover what can be done with these different materials. We are committed to providing outstanding education and early learning opportunities for children aged 3 months to 5 years of age, and our nursery facilities and environment form an important part of that.

local_offer: We plan individually for each child, ensuring activities and experiences meet their current needs, and support their development and next steps. Staff complete Buckinghamshire Assess, Plan, Do, Review sheets which they share with parents and other professionals.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to provide care and support for all children to flourish and achieve their full potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Some members of our staff have carried out online training surrounding supporting children with Autism. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in monthly discussions about their child's interests, as staff then plan for the month ahead. daioly feedback is given via and app, and most importantly- verbally upon collection, informing parents and carers of their child's achievements and important daily information. We also carry out termly parent meetings to discuss in depth, each child's current stage of development and highlight any areas or additional required support. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Staff record weekly observations and complete termly trackers. This information is shared with the parents via the EYLog app. Those with SEND will also have specific APDR reports or plans in place that are reviewed every 6 weeks. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Ramp access through main gate and entrance to building. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please get in touch with the nursery manager to discuss your child's specific needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? SEN training coming up in the Autumn term

description: Beaconsfield Family Hub brings local support together for families, children, and young people from birth to 19 (up to 25 with SEND). We offer friendly, accessible support to help every child get the best start in life and run a varied timetable of activities. Regular sessions and support at the hub include: - Early Years and play activities - Health Visiting and maternity appointments - (text the Health Visitors on the number below- Hub staff can not make/change or cancel appointments for you). - Parenting advice and support - SEND drop-ins and guidance - Youth and family activities - Community-led groups and local services All activities at the Hub are offered free of charge. Please note that some services may need an appointment or be delivered virtually. To find our Hub, drive to the end of Beacon Close. Go through the double green gates on the right and follow the path to our Hub. There is parking available on-site. If you don’t currently have a Family Worker and need some help or advice you can contact the Buckinghamshire Family Information Service by phone, or you can make an online request for support. If you are concerned about the welfare of a child, you should contact First Response on the number provided.

name: Buckinghamshire Railway Centre
description: Buckinghamshire Railway Centre in Quainton occupies an extensive site in rolling Buckinghamshire countryside. There is so much to see and do. Exhibits range from large express passenger locomotives to the humble shunting engine together with a host of smaller items recreating the golden age of steam. Check our events programme to see what is happening on the day of your planned visit, steam trains operate on certain days and others are devoted to various special events. Types of Open Days: • Special Events: See 'Special Events' or 'Calendar' on the top options bar of our website for more information on these and to find out when they are. • Steaming Days: This is when we have a full-size steam train in action, ready to take you for a ride. We also have miniature ride-on steam trains. These are run by our sister Society VAMES, and there is a small charge for this. Steaming Days are every Sunday (March to October), and also Wednesdays during school holidays. • Static Viewing Days: This is when the site is open, but no steam trains or rides will be running. These days are much quieter and ticket prices are lower. We are open for static viewing Tuesdays, Wednesdays (term time only), and Thursdays. The cafe is only open for snacks (crisps/chocolate/biscuits) and self-service drinks (hot and cold) on these days. The shop is open. Food, Drink, Gifts, Travelling here: • Our cafe and gift shop are fully open on all Steaming and Special Event days • Signposted off A41 between Aylesbury and Bicester. Number 16 bus from Aylesbury/Bicester (not Sundays) There is full wheelchair access across the site, including a ramp onto the steam train. Wheelchair users can go into the brake van at the back of the train (at Christmas however, Father Christmas uses this van to hold all the children's presents), so please call us for more information before booking. If the visitor is capable of taking a few steps onto the train, then wheelchairs can be left on the platform, and the visitor can be shown to a seat closest to the door.

description: Welcome to BackWoods. At BackWoods you can discover a range of experiences that will get you doing something different. Perhaps it’s a skill you’ve always wanted to learn, or maybe you’ve tried all the best brunch spots near you, and you want to try something completely new? If you’re looking for something a bit different, then you’re in the right place. BackWoods was founded because our Instructors love what they do, and they want to share it with you. Our workshops and experiences are rustic, genuine, and surrounded by gorgeous woodland. BackWoods Instructors will make sure your time with us is engaging, so whether you’re a seasoned expert or are starting out and want to know more – there’s something here for everyone. Our experiences range from Campfire Cooking to Wreath Making, Art and Nature Workshops to Axe and Knife Throwing, all in the woodland setting of Stott’s Nursery in Stokenchurch, just a 30-minute train ride from London. We offer a programme of workshops throughout the year, as well as group bookings for corporate team days, Hen and Stag parties, birthday parties, and any other celebration. We also provide private workshops for larger groups on request. For a taste of what we can offer, head to the Group Bookings tab. To see the complete programme, take a look at our experiences tab. Want to see more? Head to our Instagram page for some inspiration.
