description: Mixed-gender primary school in Aylesbury for 4 to 11-year-olds, with a unit for ASD. As a school, we are constantly striving to improve and at the heart of everything we do is the belief that we want every child and member of staff to be nurtured, inspired and ultimately achieve the very best they can. We work hard to ensure that Bearbrook Combined School and Pre-school is a vibrant, exciting learning community, where children enjoy their education and make accelerated progress in a stimulating environment. We are committed to developing the whole child through their creativity and diversity. Our aim is for children to grow into confident, happy, independent, lifelong learners who can function as successful members of the community. In order to achieve this, we have high expectations with regard to attitudes to learning and behaviour, so that the children are ready for learning, are respectful and as a result, can keep themselves and others safe. One of the essential ingredients is a very close partnership between home and school. With your help and co-operation, we can create opportunities for your child to make the best possible progress, thus ensuring that your child’s years at Bearbrook are happy and rewarding. Not only do we want to build close partnerships with our families but also with other local schools. As a result, we are very proud to have become an academy and joined the Great Learners Trust. The Great Learners Trust operates with a strong vision of providing all children with outstanding learning opportunities and ensuring the best education for all children regardless of their starting points, level of disadvantage or family background. They believe that every child can be a great learner and have a strong set of values that are very similar to those at Bearbrook. They will not dictate how we work or organise ourselves, but they will provide high-quality support and recognise our strengths. They value their staff and will be mindful of work-life balance. They are also local, which is an advantage. At Bearbrook, we operate an ‘open door’ system. Should you have a query concerning your child’s welfare, you are always more than welcome to come into school to discuss it with me or any of the staff, often without an appointment. In addition, Senior Leaders and I are at the gate regularly, either at the start or the end of a day. Parents are always welcome in the school and offers of help, either generally, or with a particular skill, are always gratefully received. Therefore, on behalf of myself, the staff and governors, I would like to welcome you and your child to Bearbrook Combined School and Pre-school.

What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to give the families opportunities to access care for their children whatever their needs. Learning through play is key to my setting: the age and stage of the child is considered as well as their individual needs to ensure they enjoy their time with us. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? As with all registered Childminders in Buckinghamshire, I have a Key Contact within the Early Years Service, from whom I can access advice and information. They are happy to answer my questions or signpost to other appropriate services. Professionals are welcome to meet the child at my setting if parents wish. I am keen to expand my knowledge and expertise. I will undergo further training when it is required How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is going through a transformation to become accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a ramp leading to the front door, then a small step leading to the front door but that can be easily resolved. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g. adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Ideally, we will arrange a meeting so the parents and the child can see the setting. To keep up to date with SEND information and undertake necessary training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

local_offer: Bedgrove Infant School Nursery (Foundation 1) is a large nursery setting that caters for up to 96 children per session. Nursery experience can often be a child’s first venture into the larger world outside the family and home. What children encounter and learn at this stage in their lives can create strong and lasting foundations on which to build in later life, so we believe it is essential that these first experiences are of the highest possible quality. We consider the full needs of every child and will make reasonable adjustments to give a comprehensive and, where necessary, varying degree of support. Working in partnership with parents we aim to provide a safe, stimulating and challenging environment where children together with adults can explore, have fun, play, talk and learn together, developing happy, confident and independent individuals within our school community. https://bedgroveinfantschool.co.uk/our-school/impactful-inclusion/#annual-send-report What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to give children the best possible start to their education. To ensure this happens, if appropriate, we will work with families to seek support from outside agencies and will implement recommended strategies according to individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? National Awards for SEN Coordination - 11th October 2019 - Ellice Camfield-Grant Makaton Training - 28th February 2022 - All Practitioners In-house Makaton Training - 16th March 2023 - Tyler Sulston AET (Autism Education Trust) - March 2022 - All Practitioners Attachment and Trauma Training – EYFS focus - July 2022 - All Practitioners Talk Boost Training - February 2022 - Kate White and Hayley Wadsworth How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are children’s first teachers and at Bedgrove Infant School, we value the important job that you are doing as parents. We would like to work in partnership with you, to support you and your child on their first steps into education. Parents will be welcomed into the setting regularly to see what happens in Foundation One. We have an open door policy where parents can have a quick chat to their child’s key person/teacher on the gate or if they would like a longer discussion, parents can email in to arrange an appropriate time. Learning Journeys are also available for parents to look at. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents/carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed and agreed with the parents. We will regularly monitor the short-term outcomes for children with SEND and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT) …) are visiting or working with children, we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits or ensure the external professional calls to discuss their visit. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? - The school’s main buildings are DDA compliant. - The main buildings are accessible for wheelchair users. Ramps are either in place or portable ramps are available to allow access to areas where there is a raised curb or steps. - There is a toilet adapted for disabled users accessible in the main foyer. - A disabled parking bay is located immediately outside reception to provide easier access for children and parents/carers with mobility needs. - Hazard warning markings across the school for potential trip hazards - As a need arises, the school will always investigate the possibility of reasonable adjustments to facilitate inclusion and, when viable, implement them. local_offer: At Bedgrove Junior School we recognise that pupils may have barriers to their learning or that sometimes learning can be challenging for pupils. We provide quality first teaching for all pupils and when pupils have been identified as having additional needs we offer individualised support. Every child on the SEND register has a SEND support plan. This outlines desired outcomes, type of provision, time and financial costings. local_offer: We have the local authority SEN support team to help and support should we need too. Staff go on training courses to support children with additional needs. We keep in contact with other local settings to exchange knowledge and ideas.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? To provided What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Kelly Bartley = nursery named SENCO. Completed the course in 2015 and attends termly meets with the local boroughs’ SEN team to keep up to date with any new legislations that may have come in to play. Also, a chance to meet other settings SENCO and share ideas and thoughts on ways of implementing strategies into the setting that have worked well for other settings. I have also attended a Makaton course January 2020. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Here at Little Ducklings, our parent relationships start on the physical tour of the setting. Once enrolled at the nursery, the child is booked in for settling sessions – these are free of charge – and this is where we get to know not only the child but the parent too. We allow the parent into the setting daily for short periods of time over a two-week period to ensure that the child is fully settled and happy to be at the setting. We operate an open-door policy. Every term we hold a parent’s consultation where the key person will invite the parent in for a meeting to discuss their child’s progress and development. We give informal feedback daily at the door when parents come to pick up their child and we use an online platform called EYlog which allows the setting to upload photographs and observations and give more detail as to what their child has been doing throughout the day/week. This is used as a two-way communication tool between parents and the setting – the parents can drop an email to their child’s key worker and if you have been up to anything exciting over the weekend, have been on a holiday or celebrated a family occasion, parents can also upload photographs and notes for us at the setting so we can share this with our peers and carers. We strongly believe in equal opportunities and welcome everyone from all different cultures and ethnicities. We celebrate all festivals, and should a parent wish too, join the setting for a session to deliver an arts and crafts session, tell the children a story or if they have a special talent for example, can play a musical instrument, we more than welcome them in to show us. We also have an allotment patch and will constantly be looking for parents help and support to help grow lots of wonderful things. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At little Ducklings we do hold parents’ meetings termly where practitioners share the progress/ development of the child with their parents. Each key worker creates action plans (next steps of learning) for each of the children within their care. This is shared with parents so parents can see what their child is working on and what activities we as a setting provide for the child to meet those next steps of learning. Our online platform – Eylog, parents can access this and can see observations, pictures and a summary of what their child has been doing daily/weekly. Between the ages of 2 and 3 years old, a two-year-old progress will be completed by the child’s key worker and again shared with parents. For a child who as an additional need, a SEN support plan is completed by the parent and setting, and this is reviewed every 6 weeks. If an outside agency is involved, their input is also included on the SEN support plan. At the time when the child is ready to leave our setting and move onto reception, we write a transition report which is shared with the parents and forwarded on to the child’s next school. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our nursery is set in communal grounds, so we have a beautiful big open green space, with woodlands as well as a secure garden and an allotment which is the nursery sole use. The large car park ensures a safe drop off and pick up of the children to the setting. The setting is split in to two rooms – ducklings = 0-2years and preschool = 2years -4. We consider the needs of all the children and create the environment accordingly to make it as accessible as possible. We create areas for each learning area, so children are engaged and explore with a purpose. Activities are provided/set up according to the children’s interests and next steps of learning. There is large floor space, so it is accessible for all children and those with additional needs such as a wheelchair user. All our resources are specifically for children’s small hands, so we prepare them not only for school but for life. Promoting their independence and self-confidence and self-awareness. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Before any family starts to use our service they must attend the nursery for a tour and a discussion with the setting manager to ensure we can meet the child's needs. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? As the child grows at Little Ducklings, their needs obviously change. Through your child’s time at the setting, the key person will be getting to know your child well such as their likes and dislikes and where they are at developmentally. This helps tremendously with room transitions as a lot of detail can go into the room transition document for the new key person to have. The child will also be doing some settling in visits to their new room, to familiarise themselves with their new environment. Whether your child starts in our ducklings’ room or the preschool room, the parents and key person will sit together to go through an ‘all about me’ document. Transitioning from preschool to reception, a transition report is filled out, again by the key person, this is a detailed report as to where the child is developmentally and shared with the parents and forwarded on the new school. At Little Ducklings, we welcome reception teachers in to meet the child and have a meeting with the keyperson should they wish too as well as meet the child that will be going on to reception. We also contact the schools we know the children are going to and ask them to send us pictures of members of staff whom will be in reception, the uniform, what the classroom may look like, what the toilet/bathroom may look like, where the children will be eating lunch etc so we can start to familiarise and prepare the child/ren for their move. To continue to support staff and send them on training to further their knowledge and understanding of SEND.

local_offer: Bedgrove's Busy Bees is a Preschool which cares for children from the age of 2 years old to statutory school age. We strive to be an inclusive practice and welcome all children and families. We do our up most to meet each child’s needs, by identifying them and working with Parents/Carers as well as outside professionals, which allows every child to meet their full potential.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our SENCO Sarah Came will attend the SEND meetings set up by our local authority. The setting has access to The Early Years Team, Early Years Consultant, and a range of resources which can be accessed online (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites). We have professionals visit our setting and welcome the opportunity to learn and develop our knowledge from them. The manager has had a wide range of experience within her roles and she supports the SENCO and staff so the needs of children with SEN are met. We are happy to hold or attend multi-professional meetings. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO Training - Anaphylaxis Training - Hearing Impairment Training - How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are a very friendly preschool and seek to have a warm, welcoming environment for both children and parents. We aim to be approachable and encourage parents to chat with us at any time with regard to anything relating to their child. If a parent requests a more formal meeting, one will be arranged as soon as possible. Every child has a learning journal which is completed and monitored by their key person and the manager, it can be accessed at any time by the parents via Tapestry and we encourage parents to add their observations, photos and events from home. Stay and Play sessions are also available throughout the year, which gives parents the chance to see the preschool in action. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? From the initial visit and settling in session/s the keyperson will be discussing with the parent what they feel their child’s needs are and with joint discussions a plan will be put in place if required. Two year progress checks are undertaken and discussed with parents. We welcome regular meetings so we can discuss, assess, plan and review short-term outcomes. If a SEN support plan is needed, parents will be invited to a meeting so the plan can be co-produced by all who are involved with the individual child. If other professionals come into the setting (Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists) we would always give the parents the opportunity to meet with them. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We are in a large Church hall, which is bright and airy, the outside space is separate from the hall, and both are accessible by wheelchair. The hall has adult toilets attached and one has wheelchair access. We take into account the needs of the children attending when setting up the environment. Staff use Makaton with all children to aid communication. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have a flexible approach to transitions and consider individual needs. We offer flexible settling in sessions, can offer shorter hours and set up individual plans to help settle children into our preschool. We use visual cues and are happy to provide parents with the same ones to be consistent at home if needed. We have good links with our feeder schools they come to visit the children, to meet them and also speak with their key person with regard to individual needs and plans We are happy to hold multi-professional meetings where a more joined up approach would help a child transition to the next stage. We ask for photos of the staff, activities, and rooms from the schools so children with SEN can slowly be introduced to the new surroundings, with support from their families. We are happy to visit new settings with children and pass on a full report for every child. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? All Staff will undertake CPD training on SEND courses that have relevance to our children in the setting. We will constantly reflect on our environment and adapt to what is needed for the individual children attending.

organisation: S4A Group Ltd, Sports Development and School PE Provision S4A offer holiday camps in Buckingham, Grendon Underwood and Patishall. Providing childcare during the school holidays. We offer activities such as football, basketball, science and seasonal craft activities, a full list of which can be found on the s4a website. S4A also work in 13 different schools in Buckingham and surrounding areas providing high-quality PE provision. We teach a huge variety of different Sports with our coaches' being highly qualified in a range of Sports. We tailor our lesson plans to suit each classes specific needs, giving children the opportunity to learn new skills and develop existing ones whilst always maintaining the importance of enjoyment and fun. As well as providing PE provision in these schools we also provide extended care across in the area. We run breakfast and after school clubs offering a range of activities tailored to meet the interests of the children in attendance, from science clubs to sports clubs S4A cater for all. Helping them develop physically, emotionally, socially and mentally in an environment that is fun and exciting. S4A Development is about helping children reaching ''their'' next level. Our Boys and Girls Development Centre sessions are on a Monday evening in Buckingham with our Juniors section on a Saturday morning in Buckingham and Gawcott. All sessions are professionally designed and delivered in line with the 'England DNA' to offer a player-focused approach and develop players on an individual basis while allowing them to progress at their own speed and in a low pressure but testing environment. We offer three-hour Ofsted registered play sessions on weekdays and weekends with activities tailored to support your child’s interests and learning following the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework. These sessions give children aged 0 to 8 years a chance to be independent, explore different activities and socialise. Staff are trained to meet the needs of each individual child, supporting them to participate fully in the activity they are attending. How to book: If you haven’t already, please register your child with Bucks Activity Project by completing our information and consent form, found on our website, and email it to us. To book, return your booking preference form by the deadline (stated on the booking form for each period) to our office or by email. You can also call your preferences through to the office on 01296 438230 (Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm).

local_offer: Bucks Activity Project is part of the Action for Children Countywide Integrated Short Breaks Service, commissioned by Buckinghamshire Council and provides community short breaks to children and young people aged 0-19 with disabilities and additional learning needs across Buckinghamshire with over 400 children currently registered. For our Under 5s we offer Ofsted registered play sessions with activities tailored to support children’s interests and learning following the Early Years Foundation Stage and all services are currently awarded ‘Good’ by Ofsted. For those children attending full time school we offer weekend and school holiday activities which include arts and crafts, cooking, music, outdoor play and sensory play. Children and young people aged 8-19 can access activities at weekends, evenings and school holidays including our youth clubs, movie nights, cooking, quiz nights, swimming, bowling, cinema, go-carting, water sports, climbing, ice skating, farm visits, scavenger hunts and woodland walks to name a few.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Short Breaks have positive benefits for both children and young people with disabilities and their parents and carers. They give children and young people time away from their family so they can develop independence, learn new skills, make friends and reduce loneliness whilst giving parents and carers a break from their caring responsibilities and providing time to spend with other children in the family. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All practitioners are trained in the following: Safeguarding Children BSCP Working Together to Safeguard Children Prevent Managing Equality and Diversity Manual Handling First Aid Staff are also trained in the following according to their role and the needs of the children and young people they are working with: Administration of Medication Asthma and Anaphylaxis Epilepsy Awareness & Administration of Rectal Diazepam Epilepsy Awareness & Administration of Buccal Midazolam VNS Training Oxygen Administration and safety Gastronomy and Naso Feed Positive Behaviour Management Team Teach SENCO Communication Makaton Autism Awareness Social Stories How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Practitioners aim to create a welcoming environment to parents and mutually share information at handover and collection. Practitioners also provide opportunities for parents to liaise further over the telephone/email. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Outcomes are measured for every child that attends. Practitioners share successes, wow moments and outcomes with parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All venues are fully accessible and have access to outdoors. Staff are mindful of children’s individual needs and are able to adapt environments and groups accordingly. Our staff are highly skilled in communicating with children and young people who have limited or pre- verbal communication, enabling every child to have a voice and communicate their hopes and needs. The staff and children and young people use a range of ways to communicate with each other. Staff use the child’s preferred method of communication alongside words. Makaton – simple sign language used alongside words. PECS – Picture Exchange Communication System – These are picture cards that the child or young person uses to indicate their needs or wants and can reduce their frustration and supports inclusion. These are usually tailored to the individual. Social stories – individually made to support children for particular activities or events so they understand what to expect and why. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact us on 01296 438230 or email bucks.activity@actionforchildren.org.uk to request registration forms. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continually monitoring and evaluating our provision and adapting to meet the needs of the children and young people.

We offer three-hour Ofsted registered play sessions on weekdays and weekends with activities tailored to support your child’s interests and learning following the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework. These sessions give children aged 0 to 8 years a chance to be independent, explore different activities and socialise. Staff are trained to meet the needs of each individual child, supporting them to participate fully in the activity they are attending. How to book: If you haven’t already, please register your child with Bucks Activity Project by completing our information and consent form, found on our website, and email it to us. To book, return your booking preference form by the deadline (stated on the booking form for each period) to our office or by email. You can also call your preferences through to the office on 01296 438230 (Monday to Friday 9am to 5pm).

local_offer: At Beeches, we are a welcoming day nursery with experienced practitioners to support children with various needs. Children with special educational needs have and currently, attend the setting. We will work with parents and the local authority where necessary to ensure the correct support is in place for their child at the setting, ensuring we can meet all the child's needs. We are open Monday to Friday all year round (7.30 am until 6 pm), excluding bank holidays and closure over the Christmas period in December.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We offer a welcoming and inclusive environment, striving for all children to have access to equal opportunities, and supporting their learning and development. We will work closely with children and their families, to ensure a service is provided in the best interests of the child and their development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff have an understanding of SEND needs and the SENCO role within the setting. We have a dedicated SENCO working alongside our manager to support appropriate provision. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All parents are communicated with on a daily basis regarding their child's time at nursery. A weekly post is sent to all parent's regarding the activities in the nursery, including photos of activities children have taken part in. Children receive regular observations uploaded on our app. A monthly newsletter is sent to parents, informing them of future activities and planned events in the setting. We hold parent's evenings and events throughout the year. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use an online platform called Family for all parents. On the app, your child's day is shared with you regarding their eating, sleeping and toileting habits. If your child is over 3 years old, we then verbally hand over this information daily. On the app, we also share 2 observations a month including photos discussing your child's development. Children with SEND have additional support in place, including individual action plans with specific targets, to support their development. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The environment is all on the ground floor level with no stairs. We have an access ramp at our back door. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? To enquire in regards to our availability at Beeches Nursery please email enquiries@countrysidenuseries.co.uk or beeches@countrysidenurseries.co.uk. Alternatively, you can call the nursery on 01628 603800. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We intend to support in staff to complete further training to support children with SEND needs.

name: Action4Youth | The Junction
description: The Junction is a multi-service drop-in centre offering a range of planned sessions and activities 7 days a week. The service caters for young people aged 11 to 18 years (up to 25 SEND) and provides specialist support to those who are vulnerable, as well as a timetable of activities for all young people to get involved in. Support will be provided in the following areas: 1. Crisis support clinics: a drop-in service operating 4 days a week where young people can come in and access specialist support and signposting in the below areas from trained staff. - Homelessness - Sexual health/unplanned pregnancy - Family breakdown - Crime - Violence - Bullying - Substance misuse 2. Health and wellbeing: a timetable of weekly activities focusing on positive mental and physical wellbeing. • Nutrition and cooking - a weekly ‘cook along’ session will be available for young people to participate in where they learn the basics of cooking healthy and cheap meals. • A timetable of fitness sessions including boxing, yoga, and HIIT sessions. There will also be a ladies', girls' only weekly fitness class. • A fortnightly mental well-being session that will focus on topics such as positive body image, social media, mental resilience, stress management, and positive relationships. 3. A youth space for socialising and leisure activities: • Internet café • Pool table, football, table tennis, gaming consoles • Weekly homework/ study club • SEND Youth Group, open to young people with additional needs only who can come to socialise and also participate in sessions on life skills.
organisation: Action4Youth Action4Youth changes lives and creates better chances for young people by creating opportunities to discover their personal strengths and potential. We work with young people from all backgrounds and all abilities to make a real difference to their futures. We are a respected and dynamic charity based in Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes but reaching young people across the wider south east region. What we do Action4Youth is a leading delivery partner for the National Citizen Service (NCS) and consistently over delivers in terms of both quality and quantity. Action4Youth takes the strategic lead for the voluntary organisations supporting children and young people aged 5 – 25 years across its area. It has around 100 organisations in membership and offers a range of essential support and services. Our outdoor centre, Caldecotte Xperience in Milton Keynes, creates opportunities for young people to have amazing, challenging, fun and sometimes transformational experiences. They learn what they can do rather than what they can’t, building their confidence and self-belief. Action4Youth is the operating authority for Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes for Open Awards Groups for the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme. office@action4youth.org http://www.action4youth.org

local_offer: We offer SEND support for children with any level of Special Education Needs or Disability.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Aktiva Elmhurst Pre-School, we aim for all of our children to meet the outcomes for learning and development. we provide a fully inclusive environment, where are all children's needs are met and they are fully supported through the curriculum by highly trained staff. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENDco had completed the full SENDCO training and has many years of experience in a SENDco role. She has also completed an Autism awareness course and PALS training. The manager has completed Makaton training, and speech and language development training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? All parents are involved with the progress of their child through 'Parent Zone', which is our online learning journey, as well as regular updates from their child's key person and parents information meetings. Parents of children who require additional support will also have monthly meetings and reviews with the SENDco and their key person. Parents will be involved in their child's development and will be updated on all targets and support provided for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? In addition to the above points, we assess children's development termly to track progress, alongside regulars observations. All 2-year-olds will have a 2-year check to identify any areas where there may be support required. If a child is having other professionals involved, the SENDco will coordinate this support in Pre-School and ensure that parents are involved and updated on targets and are given copies of any reports or feedback. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The Pre-School is located in a local community centre which has access through the front doors via a ramp and has double door access. The whole setting is on one level, there are no steps so the entire provision is accessible for all. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If your child has a SEN or disability and you are interested in joining our Pre-School, we would welcome you to come in and meet the team and the setting. You will be able to talk to us about the requirements you have for your child, and any questions or concerns you may have. We will ensure that we work closely with you to support your child's transition into our Pre-School. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We constantly review our SEN support and strive to reflect and continually improve the service we offer to our families. We aim for all of our staff to have up to date and thorough knowledge of SEN and how we can support the children, so they can work alongside the SENDco to plan targets and review their development. We keep up to date with the latest information and training to ensure that our knowledge and skills are up to date. We plan to expand our SEN resources in the setting as we grow, to support the children in our setting who have additional needs.

description: Behavioural Optometry Assessments We provide comprehensive behavioural optometry assessments to evaluate how your visual system functions in relation to daily demands such as reading, learning, sports, and other activities. Appointments are available in-person, with the option of remote vision therapy programs where appropriate. Each assessment investigates a range of visual and neurodevelopmental functions, including: Visual Function in Daily Life – How your vision supports your everyday tasks and learning Ocular Health – Screening for any eye health concerns Visual Acuity – Clarity of sight at distance and near Eye Dominance and Hand Dominance – Understanding laterality and how it affects function Binocular Vision (Eye Teaming) – How well your eyes work together Oculomotor Control – Accuracy and control of eye movements Accommodation (Focusing Skills) – Ability to shift focus between distances Visual Perception – How visual information is processed and interpreted Visual-Motor Integration – Coordination of vision with body movements Peripheral Awareness – Awareness of surroundings beyond central vision Evaluating visual-motor coordination and fine motor skills Tracking and Eye Movements – Ability to follow moving objects or maintain focus while scanning Following the assessment, a detailed report is provided, including clinical findings and tailored recommendations. Where appropriate, an individualised vision therapy program may be recommended to support improved visual function.

name: PANS/PANDAS UK Charity
description: PANS (paediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric syndrome) and PANDAS (paediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric syndrome associated with strep) are devastating neuropsychiatric conditions that are currently poorly recognised, diagnosed, and supported both medically and in schools. One estimate suggests that up to 1 in 200 children suffer from this condition. Resources include: - Resources for parents include diagnostic criteria and details of local support groups. - Resources for medical professionals. - Resources for teachers and schools. - Teacher training package. - Facebook group for parents and caregivers. - Facebook group for young people aged 12 to 17 years with the condition. - Facebook group for adults. - Links to further research. - Advocacy and support from the charity. Any children aged 4 to 19 years who are displaying symptoms associated with the condition and/or diagnosed with the conditions. Affected children can be mainstream, alternative, specialist provision, or electively home educated. All of Buckinghamshire is covered. We provide support via our Facebook group PANS PANDAS UK. Free at point of access, supported through the PANS/PANDAS UK Charity. Self-referral, Education provider (consent obtained), SEND Specialists, and Educational Psychologists. Please join our Facebook group PANS PANDAS UK, where you can obtain further support as and when needed.

description: Sing and Sign Baby Signing classes are perfect for babies from 6 weeks to around two and a half years. Babies use all kinds of signs and gestures as a natural part of learning to talk. Encouraging your baby with extra signs like 'milk', 'more', 'change nappy', or 'tired' will help your baby communicate. Baby signing with Sing and Sign is easy because we make it fun to learn. Your baby will recognise important words sooner and can use the signs to “talk” to you before speech. Age-specific classes are developed with the help and approval of speech and language therapists, designed to build the framework of good communication through song, music, and sign. name: Bells Hill Recreation Ground (Stoke Poges)
description: This beautiful Recreation Ground was bought with donations by the people of Stoke Pages in 1927 from Sir Walter de Frece of Sefton Park in the 19th Century and provides an open space for families and children with swings and an adventure playground with climbing apparatus, plus a separate outdoor gym in front of the tennis courts. There is also a running track. Within the park is an all-weather multi-use games area, marked out for football, basketball, and netball, opened in 2015 by Sir Matthew Pinsent. There is a superb football pitch and a state-of-the-art pavilion, completed in May 2015, which provides changing facilities and a large hall for use by scout, guide, and youth groups. Seating pods in the recreation ground provide an area for youths to meet and chat in their own space, with a target shooting wall available for footballers keen to develop their skills. Access to this recreation ground is through: - Footpath from Rogers Lane, beside Aldridge Place. - From Sefton Close. - Footpath from Rogers Lane, beside St Andrew’s Church. - From Bells Hill Road through the main gate.

name: SPACE Monthly Support group (Autism and ADHD)
description: SPACE Chesham and South Bucks is a support group for parents and carers of children with ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder, or who are undiagnosed. We aim to provide a space where you can find advice, support, and information. SPACE is a parent-led support group that meets monthly for a friendly social morning with speakers and discussions. We began in September 2005 with support from Parent Partnership and our numbers have grown steadily, we have been in touch with over 350 families, and are also pleased to welcome professionals in this field to our meetings. Our monthly meetings typically run on the third Wednesday of each month from 9:30am to 11:30am. Here you can get advice and support as well as hear from a range of speakers including: Carers Bucks; CAMHS; Bucks Family Info; Social Workers; Community Police; SENDIAS; SEND; PDA; and more. There are no fees associated with these meetings and refreshments are available. How can SPACE help you? - An opportunity to meet others in similar situations and share experiences. - Help and understanding in managing behavioural difficulties. - Emails giving information about relevant courses and events. We also have: - An extensive library. - A Facebook page. - Friendship and encouragement. Please check out our website below for more information.

name: Head2Head Sensory Theatre
description: Head2Head Sensory Theatre is a registered charity dedicated to the Special Needs’ Community. We are passionate about making theatre accessible to all and understand that families who have a child with a disability face many barriers. We are proud to offer a wide range of immersive multi-sensory experiences tailored to meet the needs of children and young people with diverse disabilities, including Special Educational Needs (SEN), Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), visual and hearing impairments, and complex health needs. Our Makaton trained professional actors and facilitators bring creativity and inclusivity to every performance, ensuring that everyone can fully engage and participate. Our multi-sensory theatre experiences go beyond traditional performances. From stimulating live shows and pantomimes to interactive storytelling sessions, hands-on crafts, engaging videos, immersive experiences, and empowering drama workshops, there is something for everyone to enjoy and explore. In addition to our live performances and workshops, we are thrilled to offer a free YouTube learning channel. Here, you’ll find a collection of Makaton Friendly content, including our exciting new series – Sensory Squad. These resources extend the reach of our work, providing valuable educational and entertainment content to individuals beyond our physical locations. At Head2Head Sensory Theatre, we are dedicated to breaking down barriers and creating unforgettable experiences for individuals of all abilities. Join us on our mission to make theatre and film accessible and inclusive for everyone!

SEND Diploma Level 2,3, & 4 January 2021 Sandy Bridges (Deputy Manager) EY SENCO Training (Bucks) May 2022 Sandy Bridges (Deputy Manager) EY SENCO Training (Oxfordshire) May 2016 Joanne Titcombe (Nursery Manager) SEND Code of practice June 2021 Sadie Astorga (Pre-School room) Introduction to Speech, Language and Communication June 2022 Sadie Astorga (Pre-School room) CACHE Level 2 Understanding Autism June 2018 Joanne Titcombe (Nursery Manager) British Sign Language January 2021 Sandy Bridges (Deputy Manager) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome the parents into the setting firstly during the settling-in week when their child first starts nursery. These sessions are a great opportunity for the parents to see the room their child will be based in and how they interact with the staff and other children. local_offer: The School's curriculum, teacher planning and schemes of work take proper account of the needs of all pupils, including those with SEND. The School regularly reviews pupil progress to help monitor whether children are making expected progress. Slow progress and low attainment do not necessarily mean that a child has SEN (and should not automatically lead to a pupil being recorded as having SEN). However, where the School reasonably considers that a pupil may have a learning difficulty, for example where there are early indications that a pupil is not making expected progress, the School will do all that is reasonable to report and consult with parents and the pupil (as appropriate) to help determine the action required including whether any additional support is needed. The School may request parents to obtain a formal assessment of their child (such as by an educational psychologist), the cost of which will usually be borne by the parents. Where parents wish to request a formal assessment from outside of school, they must liaise with the School in advance of the assessment being carried out and ensure the School is given copies of all advice and reports received. If there are significant emerging concerns, or identified SEND, the School will take action to put appropriate special educational provision in place taking into account any advice from specialists. Parents should be consulted and kept informed of any action taken to help their child, and of the outcome of this action. Due weight will also be given to a pupil's wishes (according to their age, maturity and capability). Please note that whilst acknowledging the importance of dealing with all situations sensitively and each on a case-by-case basis, it is the School’s belief that children should normally be informed, considerately, of their diagnoses in order that the relevant and most appropriate provision might be made. The School will have due regard to any request by a parent or pupil (who has sufficient understanding of the nature and effect of the request) to treat the nature or existence of a person's disability as confidential. Arrangements for special educational provision and support are made through the school’s graduated approach to SEN support: assess - plan - do - review: - Assess: The School will carry out an analysis of the child's needs so that support can be matched to need. If not already done so the School may, in consultation with parents, engage external agencies and professionals to help assess the child's needs and advise on any support needed. Any specialist advice received will usually be discussed with the child's parents. - Plan: Where appropriate, the Head of Learning Support (Senior and Sixth), Learning Support Leads or SENCO for the relevant part of the School will agree in consultation with parents and the pupil the adjustments, interventions, support and any teaching strategies or approaches that are to be put in place. These will be recorded on iSAMS. - Do: Teachers will work closely with the Head of Learning Support (Senior and Sixth), Learning Support Leads or SENCO for the relevant part of the School to assess and monitor the targeted plan of support and the impact of support and interventions in place for the child. - Review: The effectiveness of any support and its impact on the child’s progress will be reviewed as agreed between the School and parents. Teachers, working with the Head of Learning Support (Senior and Sixth), Learning Support Leads or SENCO for the relevant part of the School, will revise the impact and quality of the support and interventions in light of the pupil's progress and development and will decide on any changes to the support in consultation with parents and the pupil (as appropriate). The School recognises that some pupils with a SEN may also have a disability. The School will do all that is reasonable in order to meet the needs of pupils with disabilities for which, with reasonable adjustments, the School is able to cater for. https://www.berkhamsted.com/sixth-form/policies/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? description: Inspire Bucks is a registered charity serving children, young people, and families throughout Buckinghamshire. We formed our charity in 2021 to continue and build upon the success of the well-established county-wide Christmas Gift Appeal, which for several years has supported vulnerable children and families in Buckinghamshire to experience a better Christmas. We are continuing to provide that important support to families across Buckinghamshire at Christmas through our annual gift appeal. As well as this we have plans to do so much more for the benefit of children, young people and families who are vulnerable or disadvantaged, or who are known to social care teams and health professionals within Bucks. Our current projects include the Smile campaign and Alice's Positivity Boxes. We have also started to put together a group of Young Leaders to design and deliver their own community projects with our support. Through this, young people will have the opportunity to get valuable experience and skills while delivering projects that matter to them. We would particularly like to encourage those with experience of care to join our Young Leaders team.

For all children to feel safe, happy and cared for in my setting. To work with families in the best interest of the child. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority. No specific training as present but happy to attend training that is needed. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis and daily messages using WhatsApp. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. We aim to ensure that activities are extended to support children to meet their potential within the setting and share ideas with parents for use at home. Parents are asked to share the child’s news and things they have been learning at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. 2 year checks will be completed between the age of 2 and 3; this is shared and discussed with the parents and they will get a copy of what to expect. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our home is accessible to most children and families, however I live in a town house and the main area we use is on the second floor; this is due to having no toilet or hand washing facilities downstairs. To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. description: Family Hubs offer support for children, young people and families from birth up to age 19 (or up to 25 for those with special educational needs and disabilities, known as SEND). The help available is based on what local families and communities need. This means each Family Hub may look a little different, but all follow the same core approach to make sure support is friendly, consistent and easy to access. All activities at the hub are offered free of charge. Our programmes change regularly so please take a look at our directory listings or follow us on Facebook for the most up to date information. Berryfields Family Hub is within the same building as Aylesbury Vale Academy Primary School. The entrance to the Hub is to the right of the main school entrance. searchText:
name: St Mary's Church - Burnham
description: At St Mary's, Hitcham, you'll find a warm welcome, whether you're new to the area, new to church or a ‘seasoned’ person of faith. We are a diverse community of people of all ages and backgrounds, and enjoy coming together to worship God and spend time with one another in His presence. We are a church with both contemporary and traditional elements and a real heart for mission, rooted firmly in the Christian Gospel that Jesus came to bring. Our mission statement is 'Growing in the Love of Christ and Sharing His Love with Others' and this is at the heart of everything we do. Being welcoming, hospitable and sharing with our church family and wider community is incredibly important to all of us here. If there is an excuse to gather for lunch, a party, a picnic, we'll find it! We also try to share Christs love in more practical ways through helping families, supporting charities in our local area and visiting those in nursing homes and the elderly. Many have found a new home here at St Mary's, Hitcham - we hope you will too!

name: The Bicester School
description: A fully comprehensive secondary school in Bicester, Oxfordshire for 11 to 19 year-olds. The Bicester School is a high-achieving, stimulating and creative learning environment with a caring, compassionate, and challenging ethos. Our pupils are aspirational, responsible, self-disciplined, and able to function as citizens in a diverse, changing, and interconnected world. The Bicester School provides a safe and inspirational start to our students’ lifetime learning journey. In our Good Ofsted report of March 2024, the following appeared in the main headline statements: Pupils are warm and friendly. They form positive relationships with each other and with staff. Staff share a commitment to provide pupils with the best possible education. As a result, pupils thrive at this inclusive school. Pupils conduct is calm and orderly. They behave well. They treat one another with respect. Pupils are well prepared for adult life. Parents are positive about the school. They like its caring and supportive ethos. As one parent said, expressing views typical of other parents, 'All pupils are looked after and given what they need. The Bicester School go es above and beyond to help students and families''. The sixth form curriculum is equally ambitious as in the rest of the school and builds on what pupils have studied in the previous key stages. Sixth form provision is a strength of the school, outcomes for A level are strong and students in the sixth form greatly benefit from their time there.
organisation: The Bicester School (Activate Learning Education Trust) The Bicester School a high-achieving, stimulating and creative learning environment with a caring, compassionate and challenging ethos. Our pupils are aspirational, responsible, self-disciplined and able to function as citizens in a diverse, changing and interconnected world. The Bicester School provides a safe and inspirational start to our students’ lifetime learning journey. In our Ofsted report of June 2018, the following appeared in the main headline statements: Leaders have successfully installed a culture of high expectations and a curriculum which aims to give wider opportunities to pupils. Teachers work hard so that pupils learn well. They have high expectations that lead to pupils being ambitious. Pupils work hard to meet these high standards. As a result, they learn well and have very positive attitudes to learning. Pupils’ behaviour is good. Conduct around the school is calm and orderly. Pupils are well mannered and polite. Relationships between staff and pupils are very positive. Pupils are well cared for. We are now seeking to build on these strengths and create a three-fold mission statement for the school, where the thread of high expectations, standards and excellent conduct and behaviour underpin our three key aims below: High levels of achievement which provides a solid base for aspiration Our vision is that the overwhelming majority of our students will achieve their personal bests and move into higher education or high-quality employment areas at the end of Year 13. This will be achieved through the provision of an academic, creative and sporting curriculum, delivered by good and outstanding specialist teachers in an increasingly high-tech environment. High levels of personal development Our vision is to support students in achieving their wider personal development goals as citizens and well-rounded individuals. This includes the spiritual, moral, social and cultural aspects of life. Students will learn about their rich cultural heritage and at the same time through our recently-awarded Internationalism status develop an understanding of the global community that we are all a part of. Students will belong to one of the four houses, named after influential, inspirational people: a key part of this will be gaining house points by raising money for charities, involvement in team sports, drama and musical productions. Alongside this, there will be opportunities to take on responsibilities such as prefect duties, student counselling roles and belong to a diverse range of clubs such as Christian Union, literature appreciation society, Duke of Edinburgh Award, chess, art, music, computing, etc. High levels of employability and aspiration Our vision is to work with students, parents, employers, universities and the wider community to develop the qualities, skills and attitudes required by employers and universities. These include: integrity, resilience, self-discipline, teamwork and leadership alongside key skills in numeracy, literacy and technology. This will be achieved through the house or tutor system and wide access to leadership and team-building programmes, enrichment, careers information, community and co-curriculum opportunities which will be available to all students.

local_offer: Big Top Nursery has recently become part of the Kindred Family, we cater for up to 60 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families. We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share their children’s successes, achievements, concerns and hopes for the future. We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our SENCO Sophie attends the termly Local Authority SENCO Liaison Groups. The setting has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites) We are happy for professionals involved with the child to visit and welcome this opportunity to develop our knowledge. We have close links with the local Children’s Centre and Health Visitors’ team. We are happy to attend Multi-Professional Meetings What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Sophie has many years experience of working with children within the setting who have additional needs. Sophie has attended Sendco training, attends termly meetings and has recently signed up to complete a Level 3 Sendco qualification. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents have access to our online record system and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can request a meeting with their child’s Key Person at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible. We will meet regularly with parents to update on your child’s progress and discuss their likes, dislikes, achievements and any concerns you may have. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents/carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed and agreed with the parents. We also offer updates through home/school books, email or phone calls if this is more convenient. We will regularly monitor the short term outcomes for children with SEND and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT)) are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits too. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our nursery is set over 2 floors. Our baby and toddlers are on the lower floor, and our 2 to 4 year olds are on the 1st floor. This is accessible via 2 flights of stairs. This may cause issues for access. However, we do have an entrance to our garden area that will then allow access to the upper floor, with 1 flight of stairs rather than 2. Dependant on the child's needs, we may be able to support them within the baby/toddler room should it be appropriate to do so. Our outside space is all on one level and consists of wet pour and fake grass. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child’s transition needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including home visits, frequent settling sessions, shortened sessions and transition booklets. We will be happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible to meet their needs. We have close relationships with the local schools and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently auditing the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and will plan our training accordingly.

description: You can hire a wheelchair, scooter, walker, or power chair free of charge to help you move around the town centre. We are closed on weekends. To use our services, you must be registered with Aylesbury Shopmobility.

name: Pitstone Youth Café
description: Pitstone Parish Council offers a Youth Cafe service for senior school children aged 11 to 18 years on a Wednesday evening during term time at Pitstone Pavilion. We contract with a specialist in the field of youth cafes and youth work to provide this service. Sessions run from 6:30pm to 8pm, £2 per child, no need to book. The cafe was created in recognition of the fact that other ‘youth clubs’ in the village had all ceased operating and Bucks County Council had withdrawn all funding and support, leaving young people with nowhere safe to meet, socialise, and learn new experiences. This left the young people gathering outside the shops, restaurants, bus stops, and playgrounds. The young people asked for somewhere warm, dry, and safe to meet. It provides a particularly valuable service in our rural community where children tend to dissipate between a wide number of senior schools (Tring, Wing, Aylesbury, and Stoke), giving them a means of keeping in touch with other local children and sharing experiences. We have a range of equipment that they can use whilst on site, such as skate ramps (helmets must be worn), basketball, and frisbees. Indoors we have console/board/card games and other activities. We provide a range of snacks such as toasties or chocolate bars. The young people can speak with our youth workers about any personal or social problems they may be experiencing. Thames Valley Police try to attend the cafe sessions on an ad-hoc basis, and the young people are welcome to speak to them about any concerns, policing matters, and bullying. Over 1000 local children have benefited from our youth cafe service since its launch in November 2011, showing the scale of local need. The cafe is not a traditional youth ‘club’ and does not provide structured or enforced activities in the same way as more formal organisations such as the Scouting or Guiding movements. All activities are optional. Some young people just prefer to chat and hang out, whilst some prefer to be active. Pitstone Parish Council meets all the running and employment costs. In recognition of the fact that parish councillors are not trained youth workers, the management of the cafe is contracted to a specialist in the field. The cafe is also supported by several volunteers who attend, supervise, and interact with the young people. If you would be interested in joining the voluntary team, please contact the parish clerk, as more helpers are always required. It is vital that we have accurate contact details for the parents of each child on site, therefore, parents must sign an application form before the child can attend. Visit our website and register.

local_offer: We support a local charity Accessible Boating Thames which provides water-sports for all levels of ability and ages on the Thames. We are a RYA Sailability Centre of Excellence and provide sailing opportunities to those who thought that accessing the water would not be achievable. We work with SEND schools within a 50 mile radius of the National Sports Centre and provide on the water experiences to approximately 400 participants per year.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We provide a safe and fun experience on the water. Our qualified teams first aim it proved access to water-sports where previously it was not considered an option. Our second aim is to train those who are ready to do so to become independent on the water. Often this results in a whole family engaging in water-sports often lead by the participant with the disability. For example, we will often train a participant in our wheelchair accessible powerboat to drive and captain the boat, then he/she can take the rest of the family out on the River. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff carry full RYA qualifications with DBS checks and valid First Aid qualifications, our paddle coaches are BCU qualified and have DBS checks and valid First Aid qualifications. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We communicate via SEND school, the Web and social media. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have modified all our facilities to ensure that they are chair accessible. For example. We have chair accessible classroom, toilets, changing rooms, outdoor spaces, pontoons and jetties with ramp access to all areas with wheelchair accessible powerboats and hoists to access sailing boats that have been deliberately designed or modified to suit those with limited or no limb strength. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Some start with a visit arranged by their SEND School. Others call and arrange to visit at a set time. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently relaying the outdoor space beside the classroom and the route to the changing rooms to make it smoother for chair users. We are in the process of removing the last of our timber jetties and replacing with floating wheelchair accessible pontoons to enable us to get more users into boats at any one time.

name: Bladon House School (Staffordshire)
description: Mixed-gender independent special school in Burton-on-Trent, Staffordshire for 5 to 19-years-olds. Bladon House School in Staffordshire specialises in SEN, special educational needs, including autism, communication disorders, moderate to severe learning difficulties, and associated behavioural difficulties. Through our work, we have also developed skills in achieving significant progress and successful outcomes for children and young people with Prader Willi Syndrome. We offer day and residential placements ranging from 38 to 52 weeks. Each student has their own learning programme which meets each learner's needs in a holistic way. Our aim is to support all of the young people in our care to find a way of life that suits them, achieve their maximum possible sense of physical and emotional well-being, be able to self-manage their behaviour and develop their independence skills. Young people receive specialised input from experienced qualified teachers and care staff and an onsite Health Team including Speech and Language Therapists, an Occupational Therapist, and a Physiotherapist.
organisation: SENAD Group Alderwasley Hall School and Sixth Form is an independent specialist day and residential school for young people aged 5 to 19 years with Specific Language Disorders, Aspergers Syndrome and High Functioning Autistic Spectrum Disorders, all of whom experience complex speech, language and communication needs. The School and Sixth Form are located on separate sites within five miles of each other and are situated in Derbyshire, close to the towns of Matlock, Belper and Wirksworth. The City of Derby is also within easy access. The aim of all aspects of the curriculum is to prepare students for adult life by fulfilling their social and academic potential. Young people are supported to develop and achieve academic and vocational plans, develop independent living skills and a clear sense of identity, enabling them to contribute to society in adult life. The individual needs of students, as set out in their Education, Care and Health Plan are met through Therapy and educational programmes, underpinned by high-quality care. info@senadgroup.com https://senadgroup.com/alderwasley/

name: Blue Pencil Art Therapy Service
description: Blue Pencil Art Therapy Service for children, young people and their families, carers. I am able to provide all services in person,online or via telephone so do please get in touch. Qualified and experienced Art Therapist/Psychotherapist with an MA Art Therapy and registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and a member of the British Association of Art Therapists (BAAT). I am also a trained and experienced EMDR Therapist, Play Therapist and Private Practitioner. As the Clinical Director of Blue Pencil Art Therapy, I aim to draw clients closer to health and well being creatively. Clinical experience also includes working with people with learning disabilities and mental health difficulties such as depression and anxiety. Also experienced in working with eating disorders, self harm, addictions and substance misuse, sexual abuse, domestic violence, offending behaviour, homelessness, grief and Post Traumatic Stress Disorder. The therapeutic relationship offers a safe non-judgemental environment to express and communicate difficulties through the artwork or play objects that otherwise might be hard to locate, articulate and convey. Art and Play Therapy can help children and young people with: - Emotional and behavioural problems such as anger, low self-esteem, anxiety and depression. - Social, peer, communication and/or speech and language difficulties. - Learning of physical disabilities or diagnoses such as ADHD, ADD or Autistic Spectrum difficulties. - Those struggling with a particular life event such as bereavement, changes in family structure or illness. - Those who have suffered abuse, bullying, domestic violence or trauma. - Those at risk of exclusion or with attendance issues. This list is not exhaustive so if you feel Art Therapy might benefit you with your difficulties please feel free to call to discuss. We offer: - Consultation - Assessment and evaluation - Individual and group art therapy sessions - Dyadic parent/carer and child interventions - Art Therapy Workshops - Written and verbal feedback - Attendance at multi-disciplinary meetings - Clinical reports I work collaboratively with a team of qualified art therapists with different specialities all registered with the HCPC and full members of BAAT. We adhere to strict ethical codes in line with these professional bodies and carry Professional Liability Insurance. We hold enhanced DBS Certificates and are registered with the Data Protection Organisation. All our therapists are qualified, empathetic and caring people with experience of working with children and young people in a wide range of settings. Our therapists are available to work in Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire, Berkshire and London. A specially designated therapeutic room is available in Little Chalfont for appointments, however, most of the time it is preferable to work with children/young people and their families/carers in their school environment during the school day. Please call to discuss. Initial telephone consultation free. Bespoke full and half-day rates available upon request. Referrals welcome from parents, carers, Teachers, SENCOs, GPs and Social Services.

This form of intervention is especially useful for people with communication difficulties or who lack the emotional intelligence to understand how they feel. I also have a private practice and work with children, young people and parents/carers and adults.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Facilitate communication of thoughts and feelings through the use of art and/or play so they can build resilience and be encouraged to make positive changes. Draw children and young people with SEND and their families closer to health and well being creatively. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Empathic communication treated confidentially with any safeguarding issues at the forefront of clinical practice. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? This type of intervention is ideal for children and young people with SEND and their families and can usually be fully integrated into the child/young person's school day. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? No previous experience or skill in art is needed, just a willingness to use the art and play materials/objects as a safe and supportive way to communicate within the therapeutic relationship. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Continued Professional Development is at the heart of my professional practice.

name: Leckhampstead Village Hall
description: Leckhampstead village hall is a multi-purpose, affordable, venue in a charming rural setting opposite the village green. Recently completely refurbished inside and out, it is run and maintained by a committee of villagers, with other volunteers lending a hand with any work that may need doing. Now boasting a fully equipped kitchen and access for disabled people, it is used for a wide variety of events, meetings, classes, parties, and activities, often with the additional use of the village green, and is available for hire. Hiring of the Village Hall, which has a fully equipped kitchen and stage, with 2 toilets and disabled access. The hall can be hired for as little as £15 or £90 per day. Hire charges include: - The use of a large kitchen with oven, fridge/freezer, microwave, water heater, crockery, cutlery, glasses, and dishwasher - 2 toilets (one accessible) - Six 6ft and four 4ft collapsible tables, plus 50 chairs - Wall heaters - Free Wifi Two 6 by 3 metre pop-up marquees can also be hired for use on the village green opposite the hall. Please visit our website for more information.

name: Recreation Ground Hall - Little Horwood
description: Set in the idyllic rural village of Little Horwood, the Recreation Ground Hall was at one time the village primary school. The school was taken over on its closure by residents of the village who turned it into a “Pavillion”. The facilities include a recently refurbished kitchen with electric cooker and refrigerator. There are male and female toilets and showers. Within the hall itself, there are chairs and tables available. The hall has wooden laminate flooring and is suitable for a range of functions such as celebrations and parties, discos, and it is particularly suitable for children’s parties as there is an adjacent enclosed outdoor play area. The hall is available for hire for both residents of Little Horwood and non-residents. It can accommodate a maximum of 72 persons if seated at tables, 120 if close standing, and any number if the outside is being used. For more information, please visit our website.
