name: St Mary's Church - North Marston
description: St Mary's Church is located in North Marston. Many people pass through its doors each year, be it on a church pilgrimage, or to worship and celebrate in the inclusive and open Christian church. The congregations of St Mary’s Church and the Methodist Church within the village are joined together in Local Ecumenical Partnership and this is reflected in our services, the use of liturgy and hymns. We are welcoming and friendly congregation, committed to serve God and share his love with others. We strive to be a community where people feel supported as they explore and deepen their understanding of God on their journey of faith. We play an active role at the heart of our village community and offer many events throughout the year. Please join us for our Sunday Services which run as follow: First Sunday- Family Service 10 am Second Sunday- Holy Communion 9 am Third Sunday- Family Service at Wesley Centre 9:30 am Fourth Sunday- Holy Communion 9:30 am Fifth Sunday- Family Service 9:30 am We also run coffee mornings on fridays, lunches at Wesley Centre on the second Wednesday of the month and Messy Church sessions on the second Sunday of the month.

description: St. Michael’s Church is situated in the village of Steeple Claydon. It is one of three churches within the Parish of the Claydons. As a Christian fellowship, we aim to make relevant connections with all in our community and those in need. We enjoy traditional and contemporary worship, have bible studies, have an active prayer ministry and provide pastoral care. name: Westbury Village Hall
description: Situated between Brackley and Buckingham on the A422, the 2016 design award winning building is available for private hire. The hall is owned by Westbury Parish Council and is run by Westbury Village Hall Association (WVHA). Please note the hall is not available for Saturday daytime hire and has limited Saturday night availability during cricket season (May to September). The hall has a wooden sprung floor, excellent audio facilities, and availability of good quality tables and chairs. Depending on the date of your booking, there is a small kitchenette available for sole use and the provision of a well-stocked bar. Please check with the Bookings Secretary in advance to check availability and to arrange a viewing of the Hall. The hall has large glass sliding doors which open onto the playing field, this is available to enjoy, when not being used by local sports clubs. Half of the main hall measures 5m by 8m, holding approximately 60 people standing or 40 sitting at tables. The entire hall area is 10m by 8m and can hold approximately 120 persons standing or 80 seated at tables. Prior to making your booking, please email the Bookings Secretary for further details and to check availability as the Hall is also home to Westbury Cricket Club as well as our many other regular hirers.

name: Wing Village Hall
description: Wing Hall is a spacious, flexible and very well-equipped community facility. Outside, it’s an imposing but welcoming building, in the distinctive Rothschild style, so characteristic of the region it inhabits. Inside, it’s dignified but friendly, with warm panelled rooms, historic portraits on the walls, wooden floors and, in the Large Hall, a lofty high ceiling, and a big proscenium arch stage with professional-standard lighting, a forestage and even a trapdoor. The building offers a choice of two meeting and function rooms, from very large, to cosy. It has a superbly equipped kitchen, an atmospheric period snooker room with two tables – and a whole lot of warmth and charm. Wing Hall is popular with social groups, ballroom dancing enthusiasts, keep-fit fans, amateur dramatic groups, badminton players, book sale promoters, bingo players – even model plane enthusiasts.

Booker Hill Nursery is an Early Years provision based on the site of Booker Hill Primary School. All key workers work hard to ensure that all children reach their potential through well planned and exciting play opportunities in a safe and stimulating environment. We recognise the need for engaging and stimulating play opportunities to develop children’s early skills however know that some children need extra support and provision to help them to achieve. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We monitor the progress and attainment of all children at Booker Hill which helps to us to identify children who need extra intervention. name: Bounce and Rhyme at Aylesbury Library
description: You and your child can share the Bounce and Rhyme experience joining with others and reciting simple songs and nursery rhymes. It is a good way to meet people and a good opportunity for babies and toddlers to mix socially with children of their own age. Babies and toddlers like short simple songs with repetition to help with the use of words and memory. As they grow older they can make their own rhythms with simple musical instruments and perform more complicated action songs. Join in with our bounce and rhyme sessions at the library and after the session borrow a book. Please don't be worried that your child might accidentally damage a book, we won't charge you for any accidental damage to pre-school books. We look forward to singing with you soon. Term time only.

local_offer: The school’s motto is Believe. Engage. Aspire. This applies to all the students that attend Bourne End Academy, and the school aims to not only ensure the best possible educational outcomes for students but also to aid in students’ social and emotional development. The school also has an Additional Resource Provision (ARP) for those students with Autistic Spectrum Disorder. The ARP is an 18 place unit that is attached to the mainstream school. Students are expected to be able to access at least 60% of mainstream lessons with LSA support. The students will spend some of their week being taught specific lessons within the ARP. This includes: - Social Skills - Life Skills - Speech and Language sessions - Literacy and Numeracy Catch up Admission to the ARP is made by Buckinghamshire LEA and not Bourne End Academy. Only students with an EHCP can gain a place within an ARP. https://bourneendacademy.e-act.org.uk/pupil-support/supporting-our-send-students/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The admission arrangements for students with SEND do not differ from those without a SEND. Admission is according to LEA policy and is based on the principles of equality of opportunity and access. All students who live within the school’s catchment area are entitled to a place at the school, in accordance with the Admissions Policy. This applies equally to students with SEN, provided that it is agreed by the LEA that their needs can be best met in a mainstream school. If applications for admission exceed the number of places available, places are allocated according to LEA Policy guidelines. According to the 1992 Education Act (Paragraph 160) “parents of statement students have the right to name a preferred school”. LEA's are obliged to accept this preference unless they can show that it would be inappropriate or not an efficient use of resources. Admission to the ARP is made by Bucks LEA and not Bourne End Academy. Only students with EHCP/statements can gain a place within an ARP. All teachers are teachers of students with Special Educational Needs and initial provision is made through high-quality teaching which is differentiated and personalised to meet the needs of the student. Through collaborative working, all staff at Bourne End Academy are dedicated in supporting the progress of all students, regardless of need. Some students may need something ‘additional to and different from’ what is provided and this would be assessed by the teacher and SENDCo in the first instance to determine the best type of provision and intervention. Students access specialist provision once there has been an identification and assessment process. Those students who may require assessing may be due to the following reasons: • Students who are working at National Curriculum levels significantly below those designated for their age • Teacher or parental concern • Students who make little or no progress despite receiving a differentiated curriculum • Students who display poor communication skills, expressively and/or receptively • Students requiring greater attention than most in the class because of learning and/or behaviour difficulties • Students requiring specialist materials/equipment or support for sensory/physical problems • Students who score poorly on group tests or individually administered standardised tests of attainment and/or ability • Students who display a specific difficulty in an area of the curriculum A student transferring to the school with a school-based assessment/SEND status already in place. The identification process begins with transition meetings which are held with all feeder junior schools in the summer term before prior to the September term. Information about new Year 7 SEND students is collected and detailed information that outlines the child’s needs and specific strategies to support them is compiled for each student into the SEND Support list which all teachers have a copy of on the first day in September. On entry, all students are assessed and the data from these tests is then analysed by the SENDCo and class teachers to identify any potential areas of need. The assessments taken by the students on entry include: • Reading comprehension and spelling tests • Single Word reading tests if required • Baseline Assessments for each subject On-going identification is also completed as each term data is collected and analysed in all subject areas. Teachers can refer students to the SENDCo if they have concerns. As well as this, the SENDCo meets fortnightly with each Head of Year to discuss SEND students’ progress, behaviour and any apparent concerns. As well as discussing SEND student, the Head of Year may want to discuss students who may require SEN intervention due to any of the concerns listed above. On-going assessments are also completed throughout your child’s time at Bourne End Academy. These include: • Reading and spelling tests each summer (all year groups) • Subject-based tests • End of year exams Additional information may also be collated through the following means: • Feedback from classroom teachers • Referrals from outside agencies • Parents • Observations • Access for exam testing ( Year 9, 10 and 11) • Dyslexia screening tests Liaison with outside agencies for example: • Educational Psychologists • Speech and Language Therapist • Integrated SEND Service • CAMHS • Cognition and Learning Team What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The school is continually evaluating its training needs based on its changing cohort of students. Staff training will continue to be regularly delivered both on a whole school level and with smaller groups of teachers that work with students with specific needs. Training opportunities will continue to be sought both in house and from external providers. The SENDCo is a qualified teacher since 2006 and has gained the National Award for SEN Coordination. She is supported by a team of experienced LSAs who also have expertise in a range of areas including Downs Syndrome, Autistic Spectrum and behavioural difficulties. New staff at The Bourne End Academy are given SEND training as part of their induction package in September. This includes: A brief outline of the SEND Code of Practice including the graduated approach: • SEND support plans • An overview of the needs of SEND within the school • What the different SEND diagnosis’/disorders mean and • Strategies to support the areas of SEND need • How to use LSA’s effectively in the classroom A booklet which outlines all of the difficulties and what they mean At the start of the new academic year, the new Year 7’s SEND needs are introduced to all staff via the SEND Support list. Specific SEND training is offered to both teachers and LSA's at least twice a year covering one of the high areas of need. The training is either delivered by the SENDCo, Educational Psychologist. Most recently staff have had specific training from our hearing impaired Specialist teacher.

We have an established Inclusion Team who provide a variety of support for all staff, children and their families; enabling us to make appropriate provision for a child’s short term needs in order to support any difficulties and prevent them from escalating. The Inclusion Team have experience in supporting children and families where there may be; • Disability or illness • Bereavement • Attendance and punctuality difficulties • Health and welfare concerns (including housing) • Divorce or separation • English as an Additional Language • Eligibility for Pupil Premium • Looked after children • Service children We operate an open-door policy and the Inclusion Team can be contacted discretely and in confidence for advice or support. https://www.bourtonmeadow.co.uk/school-information/policies What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? When deciding whether special educational provision is required, we will start with the desired outcomes, including the expected progress and attainment, and the views and the wishes of the pupil and their parents. We will use this to determine the support that is needed and whether we can provide it by adapting our core offer, or whether something different or additional is needed. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We have 32 teaching assistants who are trained to deliver a range of interventions. They provide a higher staff to pupil ratio, which maximises learning potential for all of our children. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work collaboratively with parents and external professionals to ensure we provide high-quality teaching so all our pupils can fulfil their whole potential. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All of our extra-curricular activities and school visits are available to all our pupils, including our wrap around care, and after-school clubs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: Wye Valley Volunteers
description: Wye Valley Volunteers was established in 1984 and is a registered charity that serves the area of Bourne End, The Wooburns, Flackwell Heath, and Little Marlow. It runs various services, designed to help those in need in the community, including home visiting, community transport, and several activities to encourage social contact for those less mobile and perhaps more isolated. It is run entirely by volunteers. Each year, about 800 trips to medically related appointments are arranged for clients of the Voluntary Transport Scheme, and a similar number of visits are made to elderly clients by the home visiting service. Over 40 older people regularly attend and enjoy the monthly lunch club, and the two weekly drop-in coffee mornings are very popular. Wye Valley Volunteers offers services to people in need, residents in the communities of Bourne End, The Wooburns, Flackwell Heath, and Little Marlow. Volunteers are welcome from any area.

name: South Bucks Talking News
description: South Bucks Talking News How would you find out what’s going on in your area if you were unable to read a newspaper? You would have to rely on relatives, friends and neighbours - unless you were receiving a Talking Newspaper. South Bucks Talking News (SBTN) is a service which is completely free to our listeners. We’re a charity, founded in 1984, entirely run by volunteers from all walks of life, and dedicated to bringing local news to those in the southern part of Buckinghamshire who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise unable to read the news. Our teams record articles every week from the Bucks Free Press Group and other local journals covering southern Buckinghamshire. These articles are supplemented with useful items from RNIB, Bucks Vision and The Macular Society, and a weekly quiz. We regularly have other interesting features that make it more like a magazine you are listening to. Typically, there are 75 to 100 minutes of recordings each week. It is recorded on Fridays, the day that the Bucks Free Press is published, copied onto small USB memory sticks and posted on Saturday in specially designed plastic envelopes to recipients, who can then listen at their convenience at home. When they have finished, the listener, or their carer, sends the message stick back to us in the same envelope; both the stick and the envelope are then re-used time and time again. We also loan out to our listeners USB players, which are specially designed for easy use by people who are visually impaired. Thanks to the Royal Mail’s ‘Articles for the Blind’ service there is no charge for postage and the entire service is free. The weekly recordings are also available on our website.

local_offer: When a child is identified as having Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND), appropriate additional support and interventions are put in place following the Graduated Approach. All children receive high-quality, inclusive-first teaching. Where a child requires support in addition to this, provision is carefully planned to meet their individual needs. All children have access to a range of resources and equipment to support their learning and development. These may include practical resources such as Multilink cubes and writing frames, as well as sensory and regulation tools. Resources and strategies are individualised according to each child’s needs. Where appropriate, children may also access targeted interventions, either as part of a small group or on a 1:1 basis. All interventions are carefully planned, with clear outcomes linked to the needs of the individual child or group. The Class Teacher and SENCo monitor and assess the impact of interventions and additional support. They work closely with Teaching Assistants (TAs) to review children’s progress and ensure that provision is appropriate and effective. Class Teachers and TAs work collaboratively to plan and deliver support, with the SENCo providing advice, guidance, and support to staff where required. The impact of SEND provision is regularly monitored, and one of the school governors has responsibility for overseeing SEND provision and ensuring that the quality and effectiveness of support is maintained. https://brillschool.org.uk/about/sen/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our aim is for all children with SEND to feel included, valued, supported and able to participate fully in our setting. We strongly believe in equity of opportunity, making appropriate adjustments and providing the right support so that children with SEND can participate meaningfully and achieve alongside their peers. We want every child to be confident, ambitious, and grateful, and we therefore offer them opportunities to develop in a rich, broad, and inclusive curriculum. This happens through varied enrichment, leadership, and outdoor learning, community partnerships, and purposeful experiences that broaden horizons and prepare them to live “with the wind in their sails.” At Brill, we know that there is no limit to what children with SEND can achieve and aim to support them to reach their potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff have recently been trained in High Quality SEND teaching and Trauma and Attachment. Some staff members have completed training on delivering sensory circuits and running nurture groups. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We value the strong relationships we build with parents. Parents are invited in termly to discuss their child's SEN targets and review their previous targets in line with the Code of Practice, however, parents are invited to make a meeting with the class teacher/SENCo at any time if they wish to discuss concerns relating to their child's progress. We also host termly information sessions on a range of topics. More information can be found on our website. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Your child’s class teacher is the first point of contact and will share day‑to‑day updates in person, by phone or by email. If your child is on the SEND register you will be invited to formal review meetings at least three times a year where we review progress against agreed outcomes on your child's support plan (Individual Support Plans). The SENDCo is always available for follow‑up meetings, and any external assessment reports or EHCP review paperwork will be shared with you and used to inform next steps. Where appropriate we involve the child in reviews so you also see their views. If your child has an EHCP, you will also be invited for an annual review once per academic year. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our environment offers flat access through the main doors and to classrooms, however, some fire exits are raised. Some classrooms are reached through narrow corridors. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact the school to arrange a tour and find out more. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently developing sensory rooms in our school. We aim to have 3 sensory rooms, each one serving a different purpose, for example an alerting room, a calming room and a room which is a combination of both. Our new Inclusion Strategy will be published on our school website in the Autumn term.

For nearly thirty years, The BRIT School has successfully nurtured creative skills in students from every type of background alongside a robust and full academic curriculum. And it does so for free. If you chose to come here, you will be given the tools to carve out your career, the space to think, and the environment to be you. This is a playground with professional boundaries where the raw talent of 14 to 19-year-olds meets the nurturing expertise of world-class teachers. The BRIT School revolutionizes the lives of its students; just under 100% of all students who have graduated find work in a huge range of creative industries or enrol for higher education. We are proud to be a Croydon school and equally proud to have national and international friends who support the school with professional and unique opportunities. As the Good School Guide states, “You’ll find BRIT graduates’ words, music, performance, directorial and backstage talents just about everywhere you look, from fashion shows to musicals, national theatre to community arts, in the UK and internationally.” This is a hardworking, fun, passionate school packed with dedicated individuals who love the creative and performing arts and recognise the importance of a thorough and robust education in all subjects. We believe in developing well-rounded, articulate, kind and dynamic young people.

name: South Bucks Counselling
description: South Bucks Counselling (SBC) provides affordable, professional, and compassionate individual counselling to adults in the heart of High Wycombe. We pride ourselves on having no waiting list, allowing for immediate self-referral. We offer both in-person and online therapy sessions to help address a range of issues, including anxiety, depression, low self-esteem, relationship difficulties, family challenges, trauma, bereavement, stress, life dissatisfaction, or simply the desire to gain a deeper understanding of oneself. All of our counsellors are either fully qualified or in the advanced stages of professional training on BACP, UKCP, or BPC-accredited training courses. Each counsellor receives close supervision from highly experienced professionals to ensure the highest standard of care. We adhere to the ethical and professional conduct standards set by the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy (BACP) and are proud to be an accredited BACP service. Visit us on Facebook at South Bucks Counselling.

local_offer: Broughton Junior School is a mainstream school. We are committed to providing an appropriate and high-quality education to all the children living in our local area. We believe that all children, including those identified as having special needs have a common entitlement to a broad and balanced academic and social curriculum, which is accessible to them, and to be fully included in all aspects of school life. We aim to engender a sense of community and belonging, and to offer new opportunities to learners who may have experienced previous difficulties. This does not mean that we will treat all learners the same way, but that we will respond to learners in ways which take account of their varied life experiences and needs. https://www.broughtoncommunityschools.com/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Children in our care are monitored closely through observation and assessment. All staff are aware that children learn differently and we provide quality teaching and learning in all subjects, meeting individual needs through a differentiated curriculum. If a child is found as having educational needs that are significantly different to others within the class, the class teacher and SENDCO will meet with parents to discuss the child’s progress and options. The SENDCO will, in the first instance contact outside agencies and request their involvement in supporting this child. Any outside agency working with a child requires parental permission before they start any work. We listen to parental concerns, and arrange meetings to discuss their child with them. Parents are welcome to raise any issues and concerns they have about their child with their child’s class teacher in the first instance. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To ensure that we deliver a good quality education to all pupils with SEND, by regularly updating our ideas and practise, and responding to challenges presented.

name: YMCA High Wycombe Hostel
description: High Wycombe Hostel offers housing for men and women over 18. We take people by self-referral or from outside services and offer emergency provision for 28 nights, through 4 council beds. We offer short and longer-term housing. Residents begin their time with us in one of 73 rooms, each with a kitchenette and shared showers and toilets. After a settling period, residents may move to one of our bedsits, where they can stay for up to 18 months in total. We work closely with the integrated offender management team across Buckinghamshire, as well as working with TVP and probation services. Our team works directly with the prison service to conduct telephone assessments for release accommodation. A safe place to sleep is only the beginning. Our experienced staff offer guidance and signposting for relevant support. We offer resettlement advice and mental health support, as well as drug and alcohol support. We also work with service users who have complex needs. Our Chaplaincy team provides spiritual and emotional support to both residents and staff.

description: We aim to provide a programme of events for young carers in the Buckingham and Winslow area aged between 7 and 18 years, to meet together to learn new skills, share experiences, develop social skills, encourage confidence and boost their own self-esteem away from the caring environment. We aim to achieve these objectives through a structured activity programme. We offer one-to-one support and run specific support workshops including ones for young carers who have siblings with disabilities. We encourage young carers to actively contribute to the planning and running of the youth club. We sponsor leadership training and confidence-building activities. We look to enhance the life chances of all young carers through our varied and wide-ranging activities, particularly focusing on increasing future job opportunities. name: Buckingham Family Hub
description: Family Hubs offer support for children, young people and families from birth up to age 19 (or up to 25 for those with special educational needs and disabilities, known as SEND). The help available is based on what local families and communities need. This means each Family Hub may look a little different, but all follow the same core approach to make sure support is friendly, consistent and easy to access. Support available: - Early Years and play activities - Health visiting and maternity appointments - Parenting advice and support - SEND drop-ins and guidance - Youth and family activities - Community led groups and local services Some services may require you to book an appointment in advance, and some may be offered online (virtually), as well as in person. All activities at the hub are offered free of charge. Our programmes change regularly so please take a look at our directory listings or follow us on Facebook for the most up to date information. Buckingham Family Hub is within the George Grenville Academy site. To enter the Hub, press the intercom for the Hub at the pedestrian gate, followed by the bell key twice. Please note the intercom may say Family Centre rather than Hub. When you enter through the gate, the Family Hub is on the top right-hand side of the playground. On street parking is available nearby to the Hub.

name: Buckingham Park Church of England Primary School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Aylesbury for 3 to 11-year-olds. Buckingham Park Church of England Primary School is a large primary school serving the local community. Our aim is to provide a school which provides an outstanding education, to be at the heart of the local community, and to set Christian values as the foundation for all that we do. The school is based in the town of Aylesbury, at the centre of Buckingham Park, a large housing development at the northern side of the town centre. The school is inclusive to all and provides a high quality, broad and balanced curriculum, which is appropriate for children of all abilities, irrespective of their ethnicity, social background or faith. Our admission policy reflects this by prioritising local children. The school opened in 2012 and has 420 pupils, with 60 in each year group. In addition, the school has a 39 place nursery with the potential for up to 78 pre-school children across morning and afternoon sessions. We accept 30 hr funding and have paid for lunch provision. The school is housed in a modern, purpose-built school building, which forms part of the central square, Jubilee Square, on Buckingham Park alongside a large community centre, public park space and local shops.

local_offer: At Buckingham Park Church of England School, we aim to provide the highest quality all-around education, for each and every child, in partnership with parents, within the context of a Christian community. To achieve this we must offer positive relationships with every child that allow us to know them individually, high-quality teaching for all children and strong links with all of our parents. We recognise that every child who we work with has individual needs and sometimes it may be appropriate for a child to receive further additional support to help them achieve their individual targets. The Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator is Mrs Ann Whytwood, who is also our Early Years leader. The special educational needs and disability code of practice: 0 to 25 years: Statutory guidance identifies statutory duties placed on the school. Whenever we make decisions, we give consideration to what the code says. We have a duty to ensure that our pupils are not discriminated against and we make reasonable adjustments, including the use of auxiliary aids and services to ensure that all children with SEN are not at a disadvantage compared with that their peers. These could include the provision of services and the provision of education. We make reasonable adjustments to meet all needs which could include specific interventions, the use of aids and personnel to support learning and using a different approach to meet the needs of individuals. For children with disabilities, our duty is anticipatory – it requires thought to be given in advance to what disabled children and young people might require and what adjustments might need to be made to prevent that disadvantage. We promote equality of opportunity for disabled children. Any targets are specific and measurable, we commission services to support the needs of individuals and arrangements in place to support all pupils with SEN to ensure that they get the support they need. All children with SEN engage in activities of the school alongside children who do not have SEN. We regularly review and evaluate the breadth and impact of the support we offer or can access to ensure that we take an active role to involve with all agencies and following advice. We make the best endeavours to make sure that a child with SEN gets the support they need – this means doing everything we can to meet children and young people’s SEN. We regularly review and evaluate the breadth and impact of the support we offer, or can access, and we promote training for individual staff members or whole staff to ensure that we can follow updated recommendations for pupils in our care. For further information, please see the information on our website.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We can access the SEND Local Offer, SALT/ OT/ and other SEND Advice Clinics. We have a designated Early Years SEND advisor who regularly visits the setting. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? ICAN Accredited /Helicopter Stories/ Speechlink and Language Link Training / SALT-Shape coding/ Making Sense of Autism Training/ EYFS Send Network Meeting/ Level 1 EYFS SEN Award/ BBO Maths Hub Supporting Nursery Mathematical Development/ Level 3 EYFS SEN Award/ SAFEGUARDING for SEND Pupils/ Little Talkers/ Hearing Impairment Training from STS/ NELI/ Child Bereavement Training/ Post Adoption Support Attachment Training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Outside of Covid times, parents are always welcome to attend 'Stay and Play' sessions where they can come in and learn alongside their child, taking part in all provisions on offer. Parents are kept well informed by daily communication and interaction with key workers as well as via the online learning journey platform. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? In the Nursery, we have two parent-teacher meetings per year. We also have opportunities for regular communication with your child's keyworker at drop-off and collection time. For children with SEND, there are regular updates to Assess-Plan-Do- Review paperwork and this will be communicated regularly with parents. There are also times when Specialist Teachers may come into the setting to offer advice to parents and practitioners about how to best support the specific needs of a child. We would expect that parents would engage in all meetings required to ensure that communication is open and detailed about how to best support their child. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our Nursery is purpose build to be accessible for all learners. It is on one level throughout, with softcore surface and artificial turf in the outside area. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? For children transitioning into our Nursery setting, we have a number of 'Stay and Play' sessions for New to Nursery Parents to attend alongside their children. These sessions are held at the end of a school day so that it is a quieter time when keyworkers can meet the children and parents. We hold an information session for parents detailing the curriculum, timetable and general information. Details can be found on our school website. All children will have a home visit where their keyworker and another member of staff go to visit their home. Children also have a staggered start to Nursery to build their confidence and individualised timetables where necessary. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our EYFS leader has undertaken the Level 3 SEN award and is the SENCO at the school. the EYFS Leader is also a Specialist Teacher in Early Years and Phonics. We have also recently received our ICAN accreditation to recognise the high-quality spoken environment and the quality of the interactions between staff and the children and all staff are Makaton Level 1 trained.

local_offer: At Buckingham Primary Nursery, we believe that every child has a right to access a full and enriching curriculum, no matter what their ability or background. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for all, regardless of race, faith, gender, or capability. We promote self and mutual respect and a caring, non-judgemental attitude throughout the Nursery.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our SENCo attends the Local Authority SENCo Liaison Groups. The Nursery has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor. The Nursery has access to a wide range of online resources (Speech and Language Communication Carousel, Occupational Therapy resource packs, Autism Toolkit, to name a few). We work closely with Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, the Health Visitor team and Family Support Service. There is also a Family Support and Nurture worker on site throughout term time. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Encouraging positive behaviour completed Oct 2019 - Emma Tarbuck Supporting children to deal with difficult social skills - Lindsey Aris SENCo Liaison - Nov 2019 - Sarah Gammon NVQ level 3 SENCo April 2023 Ceri Browsill How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are welcomed into the Nursery and develop strong working relationships with staff, including their child's Key Person. Parents are invited to 'Stay and Play' sessions termly and there are there are additional events such as Sports Day, followed by a Teddy Bear picnic. Parent consultations take place twice a year with your child's Key Person, to discuss progress, achievements, likes and dislikes, and any concerns you may have. Parents can also request a meeting with their child's Key Person at any time, and an appointment will be made as soon as possible. We use Tapersty to share learning with parents and parents are encouraged to add information from home. We also have Feedback sheets for parents to complete. Communication of events and information takes place through a half termly newsletters and Parentmail. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Learning journals and Parent Consultations as detailed above are opportunities to share information about your child's progress. Tracking of progress is completed through daily learning opportunities and observations, recorded on our Tapestry system. In addition there are specific opportunities such as the 2 year old progress check outcome. For children with SEND, there are opportunities to meet more regularly and in particular to discuss or review additional support through the Assess, Plan, Do, Review cycle or SEN Support plan. Sometimes other external professionals may have involvement with a child, such as Speech and Language Therapist or Occupational Therapist. They will usually also liaise with parents, but we also update parents with new targets or advice. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is on one level and is fully accessible for wheelchair access. The main Nursery room is a large, bright and airy room with zoned areas, such as a book corner, wet play area. There are two additional rooms and two sets of toilets with changing areas. A quiet area is available and sensory resources as required. There are three large outdoor areas with fixed and mobile equipment, all of which are suitable for wheelchair access. The Nursery also has access to the playground, Astro and fields of the adjoining school. Staff are mindful where adaptations may need to be made to support children with, for example sensory processing difficulties and these are made to enable every child to participate. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child's transition needs are individual and work with parents to provide a range of options including transition visits, information about the Nursery, a transition document and individualised transition plans. We work closely with the primary school adjoined and local schools to support transition. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? In addition to the training detailed above, staff are currently being trained in Early Talk, ICAN cards for children from birth to 5 and phase one from Time for Phonics. name: Buckingham Primary School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in Buckingham for 4 to 11-year-olds. We are extremely proud of the nurturing and happy environment we provide for our children and which underpins the strong relationships we form with our children, parents, and the wider community we serve. Our children enjoy learning within our amazing grounds which include a multi-use games area, open green space with large playing fields, forest school, large pond, and natural area as well as an incredible performing arts room. Our wrap-around care begins at 7:30am and ends at 6pm, providing parents with additional support and childcare when needed. We pride ourselves on being in the heart of our community and provide all our children many opportunities to learn and develop within the context of their hometown. From interviewing local veterans and performing to our Age Concern friends to exploring historical and geographical studies within the town and neighbouring areas such as Stowe Landscape Gardens, we value, respect, and appreciate the community our children thrive in. We have a dedicated team who hold high aspirations for all of our children and work hard to ensure they are happy and successful learners. We aim for our children to flourish into emotionally resilient, confident, life-long learners that become the very best that they can be. We encourage this through our exciting curriculum which is planned to challenge and inspire all of our children. Home-school relationships are central to our children’s success and we work closely with our parents and carers to build positive relationships that will support children in their learning journey. Our website provides a brief introduction to the unique experiences we offer the children at Buckingham Primary School and Nursery. With this in mind we extend a warm welcome to both you and your children to visit us and experience BPS for yourselves.

local_offer: Buckingham Primary School provides for children with a wide range of special educational needs including those with: Communication and interaction needs; this includes children who have speech, language and communication difficulties including autistic spectrum conditions. Cognition and Learning needs; this includes children who have moderate learning difficulties and specific learning difficulties such as dyslexia, dyspraxia and dyscalculia. Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs; this includes children who have Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Attachment Disorder or Anxiety. Sensory and/or Physical needs; this includes children who have visual impairment, hearing impairment, epilepsy or a physical disability that affects their learning. https://www.buckinghamprimary.co.uk/SEN/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Buckingham Primary School we have an inclusive ethos and we are committed to making sure that children who require additional support are well provided for. We know that all children need different forms of support at various stages of their school career and we believe that each pupil has individual and unique ways to achieve their full potential. Adjustments are made to the learning environment and to the curriculum to ensure that children with Special Educational Needs can access the learning and progress to reach their potential and we liaise closely with parents and outside agencies to facilitate this. Please see our Special Educational Needs Annual Report https://www.buckinghamprimary.co.uk/SEN/ What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? A number of our staff have received Earlybird Autism training and / or training through Autism Education Trust. Ongoing, individually tailored training is provided through on demand courses at National College and Creative Education. In addition, webinars provided through health therapy services are accessed. To provide support for Speech and Language difficulties, training is provided through Speech and Language Link and NELI. Staff are trained to deliver a range of interventions, including those recommended by Educational Psychologists. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work collaboratively with parents and external professionals to ensure pupils are well-supported and in order that they meet their full potential. We have an open door policy and aim to establish trusting relationships with parents. We hold a number of events such as Parent workshops and opportunities for parents to spend time in classes, supporting their children's learning. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Parents are provided with termly updates regarding their children’s progress through Parents Evenings, reports and sharing of targets. Parents of children with SEND receive additional information through reviews of Assess Plan Do Review (APDR) or SEN Support Plans. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The environment has been adapted to be accessible for all, for example with ramps and lifts. Our Accessibility Plan can be viewed on the school website https://www.buckinghamprimary.co.uk/SEN/ How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families are always welcome to visit school and there are regular open mornings. Admissions are co-ordinated by Buckinghamshire Council and the School Office are available to support with information. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? At Buckingham Primary School we are excited to be continually developing SEND provision. We have expanded our SEND team, with dedicated lead staff in each key stage. We have recently created a sensory room alongside our dedicated nurture room and have plans to develop the adjoining courtyard into an outdoor sensory garden. Staff access training and follow current research and guidance to continually review provision and develop high quality support for children with SEND.

description: Come and find out more about what we do at Burnham Beeches Rotary and our various community activities. We work in and around the community in many ways to help others with their projects and fundraising, some are featured here: Members and friends involved in creating an outdoor learning area at Farnham Common Junior School. We meet regularly to raise money, assist the community and make charitable donations. We hold meetings twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesday evening at Burnham Park Hall at 8pm. name: Aston Clinton Bowls Club
description: The aim of Aston Clinton Bowls Club is to promote and foster the game of Flat Green Bowls and provide facilities for the social needs of its members. Full membership is open to men and women over 18 years, Junior members between 14 and 18 years and Social members who enjoy the non-playing facilities of the Club. The Club caters for both beginners and experienced players with three qualified coaches. The Club fulfils a programme of friendly matches with neighbouring clubs, both at weekends and weekdays from April to September each year. Members can elect to play in these matches, Club competitions or 'roll-ups' entirely at their choosing. Experienced players can represent the Club in competitions organised by the County. The Club has a licensed bar and catering is provided as appropriate.

name: MK Food Bank
description: MK Food Bank supports people in crisis across Milton Keynes with food, care and understanding. We welcome everyone with kindness and respect, offering both immediate help and the chance to regain stability. Working alongside our community, we make sure people feel seen, heard and supported and can find their feet again, one step at a time. If you are struggling financially and need urgent help with food, you will need a Food Bank voucher number in order to access a food parcel for yourself and members of your family. You can be issued with up to 6 Food Bank vouchers within a rolling 12-month period. You can get a voucher number through an agency referral or a self-referral via the Food Bank helpline. description: We work in partnership with Buckinghamshire Council to offer an integrated service to children, young people, and adults in Buckinghamshire with hearing, sight, or dual sensory loss. This service is called Buckinghamshire Integrated Sensory Service (BISS). If you live in Buckinghamshire, BISS offers a range of services to support you with your sensory loss. A holistic assessment at home is offered, which will focus on your sight, hearing, or dual sensory needs. However, other identified needs and issues will be discussed, and information and advice will be offered to meet any additional needs or personal goals. description: We work in schools and the local community to support all children and young people with medical, emotional or educational needs. Our aim is to support each person we care for to achieve their potential for physical, emotional, and social well-being so that they can get the most from life and education and become responsible for their own health. We work in partnership with children and young people, their families and other health and education professionals in a range of locations, including schools, clinics, and family homes. We also work with colleagues in health, care, and education services across Buckinghamshire to help shape children’s services. Our service is part of the Healthy Child Programme 0 to 19 (24 for SEND) years which is a national framework, based on best evidence, to promote and protect the health of children as they grow. name: Buckinghamshire Portage Service
description: Portage is an early years home visiting educational service for children aged 0 to 3 years, with SEND and their families. We support children with a delay in two areas of their development by a minimum of six months. Occasionally the service does support children aged 3 plus. Priority is given to children not yet attending a setting or known to Social Care. We have an open referral system and parents and carers can request the service themselves. Criteria for Accessing the Service, Request for Involvement Form and Leaflet are available from the Portage office. Appointments are arranged by the child's Portage Worker. We offer different portage packages depending on the needs/age of your child, involving regular home visits within the family home and working alongside other professionals, agencies. We aim to support the gaps in your child’s development via play activities and regularly monitor their progress. Following a development assessment, the Portage Worker will identify and agree on achievable learning goals, with the parent, carer, which will become the basis of their Portage programme. Parents, carers work in close partnership with the Portage Worker to implement the teaching techniques and play activities on a daily basis. Each goal will be broken down into smaller steps to enable the child to participate and learn new skills at their own pace in order for them to reach their identified learning goal. All Portage Workers are qualified early years practitioners and trained in Makaton Sign Language and we have someone who is experienced and holds qualifications in British Sign Language and the Picture Exchange Communication system. We use sensory play and stories. The Portage Workers have had additional SEND training, for example, Autism Spectrum Disorder, Down Syndrome, and Sensory Integration.

name: Buckinghamshire Portage Service
description: Portage is an early years home visiting educational service for children aged 0 to 3 years, with SEND and their families. We support children with a delay in two areas of their development by a minimum of six months. Occasionally the service does support children aged 3 plus. Priority is given to children not yet attending a setting or known to Social Care. We have an open referral system and parents and carers can request the service themselves. Criteria for Accessing the Service, Request for Involvement Form and Leaflet are available from the Portage office. Appointments are arranged by the child's Portage Worker. We offer different portage packages depending on the needs/age of your child, involving regular home visits within the family home and working alongside other professionals, agencies. We aim to support the gaps in your child’s development via play activities and regularly monitor their progress. Following a development assessment, the Portage Worker will identify and agree on achievable learning goals, with the parent, carer, which will become the basis of their Portage programme. Parents, carers work in close partnership with the Portage Worker to implement the teaching techniques and play activities on a daily basis. Each goal will be broken down into smaller steps to enable the child to participate and learn new skills at their own pace in order for them to reach their identified learning goal. All Portage Workers are qualified early years practitioners and trained in Makaton Sign Language and we have someone who is experienced and holds qualifications in British Sign Language and the Picture Exchange Communication system. We use sensory play and stories. The Portage Workers have had additional SEND training, for example, Autism Spectrum Disorder, Down Syndrome, and Sensory Integration.

local_offer: The Buckinghamshire Primary Pupil Referral Unit provides support for children across Buckinghamshire experiencing significant social, emotional and behavioural difficulties in their mainstream school. We have three sites county wide, The Oaks based in Amersham covering the Chiltern and South Bucks area, Pathways servicing Aylesbury Vale and Woodlands in High Wycombe for the Wycombe and surrounding area. The support we provide is holistic in nature and we work closely in partnership with families and other professionals to help ensure the best possible outcomes for the pupils that we work with. Once referred by their schools children may be supported either by outreach intervention within the school environment or by a part-time placement at one of our sites. We also provide the statutory entitlement for education for children who have been permanently excluded. For the pupils that attend one of our three sites, teachers provide a broad-based high-quality curriculum consistent with that provided by mainstream schools. name: Buckinghamshire Youth Justice and Support Team (YJST)
description: Bucks YJST is a multi-agency Service consisting of Social Workers, Probation Officers, Police Officers, and staff with health and education backgrounds. Our core aim, shared by all teams nationally, is to prevent offending and re-offending by children and young people aged 10 to 18 years. Young people and their parents working with the YJST will be provided with relevant information through leaflets and documentation. The role of the YJST is defined by legislation and includes: Co-ordinating all youth justice services in Buckinghamshire. Working with those at risk of entering the criminal justice system for the first time, delivering interventions to try and divert them from offending behaviour. Preparing reports for the court to advise on what services are available and to assist in decisions about sentencing for young people. Assessing young people who have received a Police or Court disposal, designing an individual intervention programme to address the issues that have led them to offend. Engaging with parents and carers, helping them support their young person in moving away from offending behaviour. Working with victims of youth crime, offering advice, information, and opportunities to share with the young person the effect of the offence on them, either directly or indirectly. Referrals come from other professionals only, no self-referrals. However, YJST can provide advice and signposting.

local_offer: Bucks Activity Project is part of the Action for Children Countywide Integrated Short Breaks Service, commissioned by Buckinghamshire Council and provides community short breaks to children and young people aged 0-19 with disabilities and additional learning needs across Buckinghamshire with over 400 children currently registered. For our Under 5s, we offer Ofsted registered play sessions with activities tailored to support children’s interests and learning following the Early Years Foundation Stage and all services are currently awarded ‘Good’ by Ofsted. For those children attending full-time school, we offer weekend and school holiday activities which include arts and crafts, cooking, music, outdoor play and sensory play. Children and young people aged 8-19 can access activities at weekends, evenings and school holidays including our youth clubs, movie nights, cooking, quiz nights, swimming, bowling, cinema, go-carting, water sports, climbing, ice skating, farm visits, scavenger hunts and a woodland walk to name a few.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Short Breaks have positive benefits for both children and young people with disabilities and their parents and carers. They give children and young people time away from their family so they can develop independence, learn new skills, make friends and reduce loneliness whilst giving parents and carers a break from their caring responsibilities and providing time to spend with other children in the family. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All practitioners are trained in the following: Safeguarding Children BSCP Working Together to Safeguard Children Prevent Managing Equality and Diversity Manual Handling First Aid Staff are also trained in the following according to their role and the needs of the children and young people they are working with: Administration of Medication Asthma and Anaphylaxis Epilepsy Awareness & Administration of Rectal Diazepam Epilepsy Awareness & Administration of Buccal Midazolam VNS Training Oxygen Administration and safety Gastronomy and Naso Feed Positive Behaviour Management Team Teach SENCO Communication Makaton Autism Awareness Social Stories How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Practitioners aim to create a welcoming environment to parents and mutually share information at handover and collection. Practitioners also provide opportunities for parents to liaise further over the telephone/email. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Outcomes are measured for every child that attends. Practitioners share successes, wow moments and outcomes with parents. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All venues are fully accessible and have access to the outdoors. Staff are mindful of children’s individual needs and are able to adapt to environments and groups accordingly. Our staff are highly skilled in communicating with children and young people who have limited or pre-verbal communication, enabling every child to have a voice and communicate their hopes and needs. The staff and children and young people use a range of ways to communicate with each other. Staff use the child’s preferred method of communication alongside words. Makaton – simple sign language used alongside words. PECS – Picture Exchange Communication System – These are picture cards that the child or young person uses to indicate their needs or wants and can reduce their frustration and supports inclusion. These are usually tailored to the individual. Social stories – individually made to support children for particular activities or events so they understand what to expect and why. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please contact us on 01296 438230 or email us to request registration forms. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continually monitoring and evaluating our provision and adapting to meet the needs of the children and young people.

name: Handy Helpers
description: The Handy Helpers project is a support service which provides elderly/disabled Buckinghamshire residents with external maintenance, preventive measures and practical tasks in and around their homes. Funded by a grant from Buckinghamshire Council, the service can be accessed for free or on a donation basis, according to an assessment of need. It also offers befriending to provide much needed social interaction. Please note that we are not a cleaning service. We are also not able to undertake electrical or plumbing works; instead Community Impact Bucks will signpost clients to Trading Standards which holds a list of approved, qualified tradespeople. Please call or email for more information, or see our website for a referral form.
organisation: Community Impact Bucks We support people and groups to get involved and make a difference in local Buckinghamshire communities. We do this by offering expert advice and training, helping people to find volunteering opportunities, and helping charities and not for profit groups to get started, be effective and grow. We also have a number of directly delivered community services that focus on supporting those most in need – the elderly, vulnerable, and socially isolated. As an independent charity, we are the Council for Voluntary Service, Volunteer Centre, and Rural Community Council for Buckinghamshire. We are also the parent company of Healthwatch Bucks, an independent local organisation set up by the government to ensure that decision-makers and health and social care services put the experiences of people at the heart of their work. Community Impact Bucks and Healthwatch Bucks are both here to help improve the lives of people who live in Buckinghamshire: Community Impact Bucks inspires, supports, and enables voluntary and community action in the county. Healthwatch Bucks improves health and social care services by listening to you. It makes sure that what you have to say is heard by the people who deliver services and it works with groups whose views are not always being heard. We work together to make Bucks a better place to live. info@communityimpactbucks.org.uk https://communityimpactbucks.org.uk/

local_offer: Castlefield School is a large, vibrant, primary school offering high-quality educational experiences to children aged between 2 and 11 years old. At Castlefield School we believe in achievement, ambition and progress for all children. We aim to meet the needs of individual children through highly effective teaching and learning. There is an emphasis on early identification of needs through supportive and preventative strategies which reduce barriers to learning. We work in a flexible way to develop effective partnerships with children and their parents/carers, teaching and support staff within school, the SENDCo and external professionals such as speech and language therapists and occupational therapists to ensure that the school can meet a broad range of special educational needs. https://www.castlefieldschool.co.uk/web/special_educational_needs/285906 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? All children are included in all parts of the school curriculum and we aim for all children to be included on school trips. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents/carers are welcome to book an appointment with the class teacher throughout the school year to discuss concerns they may have regarding special educational needs or disabilities. Parents/carers are also able to book an appointment with the SENDCo How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The school is built on a sloping sight and has a small number of class rooms upstairs; it has two disabled toilets, slopes, hand rails and wide doors. With the exception of the upstairs and lower level class rooms and the MUGA, the school is easily accessible to wheel chair users. The allocation of class rooms and the timetable are adapted to allow wheel chair users to access the curriculum with the rest of their class. name: Ascott House
description: Ascott House presents as an ‘Old English’ manor house of black and white half timber, with red–tiled roofs and shafted brick chimneystack. Its core is an old farmhouse thought to date from 1606. The original farmhouse has undergone many changes since being acquired by the Rothschild family in 1873. Ascott houses an exceptional collection of paintings, fine furniture, and superb porcelain. The extensive gardens are an attractive mix of the formal and natural, with specimen trees, shrubs, and beautiful herbaceous borders.

name: Chilterns Countryside
description: Situated in the picturesque Chiltern Hills, this group of popular beauty spots offers fabulous walking opportunities. Pleasant day long walks with a pub stop can take you through the intimate landscape of woods, farms and hamlets that make up much of the Chilterns. The largest sites include Coombe Hill near Wendover, which has far-reaching views over Aylesbury Vale. Bradenham Estate, between West Wycombe and Princes Risborough, is a pretty village and patchwork of woodland and chalk grassland. Watlington Hill and Woods is at the top of an escarpment where red kites and ravens soar and play over views of Oxfordshire stretching into the distance. Smaller sites worth exploring include Pulpit Hill and Low Scrubs near Wendover, and Aston Wood and Juniper Bank near Stokenchurch.

name: Pitstone Windmill
description: This unusual survivor is one of the oldest post mills in Britain. Pitstone windmill ground flour for the local village for almost three hundred years until a freak storm in the early 1900s left it damaged beyond economic repair. Donated to the National Trust in 1937 Pitstone Windmill has been faithfully restored by a dedicated team of local volunteers. Today you can explore both the inner and outer workings of the windmill; including the massive post upon which the mill turns and the tail pole which the miller used to position the sails into the wind, while also taking in spectacular views of the surrounding Chilterns countryside.

name: Long Crendon Courthouse
description: The courthouse is a fine example of an early medieval timber-frame construction, set in an idyllic village. The ground floor (now tenanted) was the village poor house. You can visit an exhibition on village life in the upper floor of this property. Please note, there are very steep stairs. The courthouse was the base for parish activities for four hundred years and was the venue for the annual manorial court which dealt with tithes and crimes such as selling bad fish, brewing without a licence, or overcharging customers.

local_offer: Each child will need different support and we will support in the best way we can for their individual needs. Staff have a wealth of experience and training and will work in partnership with parents and other professionals to ensure each child makes good progress in a nurturing environment  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We will work in partnership with parents and other professionals to support each Childs individual needs What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Buds that Blossom we have an open environment that is welcoming and friendly to ensure parents/carers feel at ease to share information regarding their children. We have many opportunities for parents to have a chat with their child’s key person and other staff within the room. In addition to this, we also use the Famly App so parents/carers get regular updates about their child throughout the day. We have parent partnership bags ranging in topics from potty training to early literacy skills that are shared with parents regularly and we share information on subjects such as oral Health and communication skills. We have an open door policy and believe good parent partnership to be at the heart of our policies and procedures How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children have a Famly account where observations will be made and they will be tracked according to developmental stages they have reached. We will also do 2-year checks on children and carry out summative assessments when we update the child’s tracking each term. For children with SEND, we would have more information to share and discuss so we would ensure we have more regular meetings with parents to keep everyone up to date. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take the needs of the children into account when planning and amending our environment. We use baby signs with the children and now and then boards with visual aids to assist communication and have many sensory toys to promote sensory development. We have made a quiet area within each room to ensure that children have the opportunity to recuperate and relax. Access to our building is wheelchair friendly. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have transition paperwork that will be filled in when moving between the two rooms. Each individual child will have a folder with all the developmental progress, tracking and support in which can be handed to their new key person or shared with a new setting. We encourage lots of communication with parents/carers at this vital time and to have visits with their new key person/setting to ensure that the transfer process can run as smoothly as possible and they have the best understanding of the children. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? speech and language courses, SENDCO liaison group , child specific training as and when needed

local_offer: At Burford School we recognise that education involves children, parents, staff, governors, the community and the local authority, and that for optimum benefit all should work closely together to support the process of learning. https://www.burfordschool.co.uk/send/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Burford School believes that all pupils should receive a broad and balanced curriculum, relevant to their individual needs. To achieve this we have adopted an Inclusive Quality First Teaching (IQFT) approach to delivering our curriculum. This is supported by using different methods and tools to present learning opportunities to children and carefully scaffold their learning to match individual needs. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Staff at Burford School are trained and have a wide range of qualifications to enable them to support all pupils. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are important partners in their child’s education. All parents are encouraged to discuss any concerns, issues or successes by arranging a meeting with the teacher at the earliest opportunity. The teacher may observe the child further and/or consult with other teachers and the SENDCo before feeding back to parents about their concerns and next steps. If, after consulting with the teacher, parents are still concerned then they are welcome to contact the SENDCo. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The school carefully monitors the progress and attainment of all pupils and quickly identifies those not making adequate progress in line with expectations. In addition to the autumn and spring termly parents’ evenings, parents of children with a SEND Support Plan are also invited to meet with teachers three times a year to discuss in more detail their child’s learning and progress including areas in which they need extra support or additional challenge. What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We offer universal and specialised support to families in the local area. We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. We can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families. Our provision provides support services for all families with children aged 0 to 19 years and up to 25 years for those with a SEND. Our aims are to improve parenting, health and children’s development and to provide a safe and stimulating environment for children, young people and their families to flourish, develop and learn. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Safeguarding First Aid Early Language Development Programme Hey Programme (Healthy Eating in Young Children) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents provided with good information so they can make decisions, which will have a significant effect on their children’s life chances. Parents to know, what support and services are available to help them bring up their children, and how to access them. Families signposted into support as appropriate feel confident to provide good life chance for their children. Children to develop social skills in preparation for starting pre-school, nursery or school. Children to enjoy a variety of fun activities and play and learn through this participation. Parents to feel confident in parenting and picking up parenting skills and support through attendance. Personal, Social and Emotional Development. Physical development. Communication and Language Development. Outreach support, action plan to specifically help the family with individual needs. Emotional and practical support from Outreach Worker. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We welcome all families to all of our services, staff are dedicated to supporting families using our Hub and its services. Our building is fully compliant with the disability requirements. We provide a warm, welcoming and fun learning environment for children and their families. Large and inviting outdoor play environment. Sensory equipment available during sessions. Accessible toilets. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can attend our services and register by completing a Family Hub Membership form. Outreach support can be provided by self-referral or by referral from a health visitor or other professional. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?
