local_offer: Burnham Montessori School provides a rich learning environment in which children of all ages, stages of development and needs are supported to reach their full potential. We aim to support the children in their work and play, help them to co-operate with others and become an integral part of the school community.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our SENCO Sonia Grewal attends the termly SENCO Liaison Groups meetings. The setting has access to advice from the Integrated SEND Service, Access and Inclusion team, and with parental agreement, to child-specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor. We have access to a range of online resources and can offer details of professionals to parents. We have close links with the Health Visitor team and we are happy for professionals involved with the child to visit the setting, and are happy to attend any multi-professional meetings. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SEND Code of Practice (Level 2) - 16/01/18 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents into our setting on a regular basis to see nursery life in action (for example through reading sessions, circle time presentations, nativity productions, sports day and school parties). Parents can request a meeting with their child’s key-person or with the Head Teacher at any time. We also hold termly parent-teacher meetings where parents have the opportunity of looking through both their child’s learning journal and termly assessment, and to discuss levels of progress and achievements, as well as address any concerns there might be. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents and carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND. We offer regular meetings, (at least half termly), to discuss plans for our children with SEND and to discuss outcomes with parents. We will closely monitor the short term outcomes for children with SEND and invite parents to be part of the review and planning session for new outcomes. Should other professionals need to be involved, such as Speech and Language therapists, Occupational therapists or Paediatricians, we welcome them into our setting and ensure we give parents the opportunity to meet with the professionals during their visit. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We understand that each child's transition is individual to them, and in order to ensure this is as smooth as possible, we aim to get as much background information from parents prior to children starting, to assist their transition. We offer a range of options such as settling in sessions, shortened phase in sessions and transition booklets. We are flexible and open to listening to all suggestions on how best to meet children's needs. We liaise closely with local schools that our children transfer to, and invite their teachers to visit our children prior to their move into Reception. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Staff are committed to promoting the welfare and development of all children within our care, and as a setting we aim to continuously update our knowledge and training. We regularly monitor the needs of all the children within the setting and adapt/add activities on offer wherever/whenever necessary.

description: At Holmer Green Baptist Church we believe that the Church is a place where everyone should feel welcome. We are a diverse family of people who meet together to worship God, encourage and help one another grow in faith and tell others about the Good News of Jesus Christ. We have 2 church services every week: - Our Sunday service from 9:45am to 11am has something for all the family, with worship and teaching and children's activities running throughout. After the service, refreshments are available to enjoy whilst meeting others in a warm and friendly environment. All are welcome, but if you can't make it in person, please join us live on YouTube. - Our Wednesday service from 1:30 to 2:15pm is a more traditional service, with prayer, hymns, and a short message. On the first and third Wednesdays of the month, there is also a "Pop-In" lunch preceding this service at 12:15pm, whilst on the second and fourth Wednesdays of the month, the service is followed by tea and cake.

name: Little Hampden Church
description: Little Hampden Church is part of the Parish of Great Missenden. Services at Little Hampden typically take place on the second and fourth Sundays of each month. If you would like to visit Little Hampden Church, please contact the Parish Office, who will arrange to open the building for you. It can be dated at least from the 12th century. Because of common ownership of land in Little Hampden and Hartwell, the church was linked with the church at Hartwell. Small daughter Churches like Little Hampden often had no dedication and this is still the case today. This association lasted until 1892 when Little Hampden church was joined with Great Hampden. Following the death of the Rev Percival Hill, the last Rector of Great and Little Hampden in 1985, Little Hampden was joined to the parish of Great Missenden.

local_offer: The Children and Families Act 2014 puts into perspective the government’s plan to require local authorities and agencies to publish information on provision and services across education, health and social care for children and young people aged 0 to 25 with special educational needs and disabilities. The rationale of the ‘Local Offer’ is to empower and enable parents and carers to easily access local services to them and their children, which offer help and support for their individual needs. The information below forms our ‘Local Offer’ and demonstrates how we support children and families with special educational needs and disabilities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We do not have special services available at our Out of School Clubs but we can signpost parents. Staff seek further guidance/signposting through the Early Years Department of Buckinghamshire Council and can pass this on to the parent. No specialist services will be contacted without the specific agreement of the parent. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Busy Living has an Operations Manager, Amy Herring, who is a qualified SENCo with many years experience across a broad spectrum of SEN. All location Managers are trained SENCo's and Amy's role is to offer advice and support to club Managers and to communicate with parents on the care for their child in advance of them starting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in helping staff identify needs, sharing information, identifying targets, settling in procedures, trial visits before the child starts and communications with parents to ascertain the individual needs of the child and to ensure these can be met appropriately. Parents’ permission will always be sought before involving outside agencies. Parents see how their child is at collection time and feedback is shared by staff as to how the child has been that day, or any messages passed on by the school exchanged. Staff maintain photos of activities enjoyed by the children which can be viewed by parents at collection time and this is an excellent way of keeping up to date with day to day happenings at the club. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The club manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All Busy Living locations are accessible as we operate from school premises. We have access to a disabled toilet and risk assessments are in place. Adaptations may have to be made to accommodate wheelchair users to allow for turning space where space is limited and table heights may need adjusting which is achievable. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The club manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? local_offer: The Children and Families Act 2014 puts into perspective the government’s plan to require local authorities and agencies to publish information on provision and services across education, health and social care for children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and disabilities. The rationale of the ‘Local Offer’ is to empower and enable parents and carers to easily access local services to them and their children, which offer help and support for their individual needs. The information below forms our ‘Local Offer’ and demonstrates how we support children and families with special educational needs and disabilities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We do not have special services available at our Out of School Clubs but we can signpost parents. Staff seek further guidance/signposting through the Early Years Department of Buckinghamshire Council and can pass this on to the parent. No specialist services will be contacted without the specific agreement of the parent. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Busy Living has an Operations Manager, Amy Herring, who is a qualified SENCo with many years experience across a broad spectrum of SEN. All location Managers are trained SENCo's and Amy's role is to offer advice and support to club Managers and to communicate with parents on the care for their child in advance of them starting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in helping staff identify needs, sharing information, identifying targets, settling in procedures, trial visits before the child starts and communications with parents to ascertain the individual needs of the child and to ensure these can be met appropriately. Parents’ permission will always be sought before involving outside agencies. Parents see how their child is at collection time and feedback is shared by staff as to how the child has been that day, or any messages passed on by the school exchanged. Staff maintain photos of activities enjoyed by the children which can be viewed by parents at collection time and this is an excellent way of keeping up to date with day to day happenings at the club. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The club manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All Busy Living locations are accessible as we operate from school premises. We have access to a disabled toilet and risk assessments are in place. Adaptations may have to be made to accommodate wheelchair users to allow for turning space where space is limited and table heights may need adjusting which is achievable. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The club manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? None, other than that mentioned above. To keep staff training up to date and to be able to offer and work with the school for any changes in the environment to cater for and suit the child as needed.

local_offer: The Children and Families Act 2014 puts into perspective the government’s plan to require local authorities and agencies to publish information on provision and services across education, health and social care for children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and disabilities. The rationale of the ‘Local Offer’ is to empower and enable parents and carers to easily access local services to them and their children, which offer help and support for their individual needs. The information below forms our ‘Local Offer’ and demonstrates how we support children and families with special educational needs and disabilities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We do not have special services available at our Out of School Clubs but we can signpost parents. Staff seek further guidance/signposting through the Early Years Department of Buckinghamshire Council and can pass this on to the parent. No specialist services will be contacted without the specific agreement of the parent. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Busy Living has an Operations Manager, Amy Herring, who is a qualified SENCo with many years experience across a broad spectrum of SEN. All location Managers are trained SENCo's and Amy's role is to offer advice and support to club Managers and to communicate with parents on the care for their child in advance of them starting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in helping staff identify needs, sharing information, identifying targets, settling in procedures, trial visits before the child starts and communications with parents to ascertain the individual needs of the child and to ensure these can be met appropriately. Parents’ permission will always be sought before involving outside agencies. Parents see how their child is at collection time and feedback is shared by staff as to how the child has been that day, or any messages passed on by the school exchanged. Staff maintain photos of activities enjoyed by the children which can be viewed by parents at collection time and this is an excellent way of keeping up to date with day to day happenings at the club. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The club manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All Busy Living locations are accessible as we operate from school premises. We have access to a disabled toilet and risk assessments are in place. Adaptations may have to be made to accommodate wheelchair users to allow for turning space where space is limited and table heights may need adjusting which is achievable. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The club Manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? None, other than that mentioned above. To keep staff training up to date and to be able to offer and work with the school for any changes in the environment to cater for and suit the child as needed.

We do not have special services available at our Out of School Clubs but we can signpost parents. Staff seek further guidance/signposting through the Early Years Department of Buckinghamshire Council and can pass this on to the parent. No specialist services will be contacted without the specific agreement of the parent. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Parents are involved in helping staff identify needs, sharing information, identifying targets, settling in procedures, trial visits before the child starts and communications with parents to ascertain the individual needs of the child and to ensure these can be met appropriately. Parents’ permission will always be sought before involving outside agencies. Parents see how their child is at collection time and feedback is shared by staff as to how the child has been that day, or any messages passed on by the school exchanged. name: St Michael's and all Angels Church - Amersham
description: Welcome to St Michael’s, the parish church of Amersham on the Hill and part of the Church of England. Everyone is welcome to come in to sit, to light a candle, or to leave a card on the Prayer Tree. Beyond the glass screen behind the altar, the Lady Chapel has been set aside as a quiet place for private prayer. There are doors into it from both sides, just beyond the altar. The Quiet Garden to the right of the church is available 24/7. Services and sessions: Usually there are weekly communion services at 8:30am and 10am on Sundays, and on Tuesdays at 10:30am. Morning Prayer takes place on Tuesdays at 9am in the Lady Chapel. Gathered Round on the second Sunday of each month (except August) is a more informal, interactive, all-age service. The whole service takes place in the main body of the church with chairs seated around tables enabling the congregation to look at each other, as well as at the President. Families are particularly welcome on these occasions. Messy Church, on the third Saturday of each month (except August) is a fun, informal, activity for all the family combining creative activities, biblical teaching, and a light lunch. Please contact the office if you would like further details about any of these sessions.

local_offer: The Children and Families Act 2014 puts into perspective the government’s plan to require local authorities and agencies to publish information on provision and services across education, health and social care for children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and disabilities. The rationale of the ‘Local Offer’ is to empower and enable parents and carers to easily access local services to them and their children, which offer help and support for their individual needs. The information below forms our ‘Local Offer’ and demonstrates how we support children and families with special educational needs and disabilities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We do not have special services available at our Out of School Clubs but we can signpost parents. Staff seek further guidance/signposting through the Early Years Department of Buckinghamshire Council and can pass this on to the parent. No specialist services will be contacted without the specific agreement of the parent. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Busy Living has an Operations Manager, Amy Herring, who is a qualified SENCo with many years experience across a broad spectrum of SEN. All location Managers are trained SENCo's and Amy's role is to offer advice and support to club Managers and to communicate with parents on the care for their child in advance of them starting. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved in helping staff identify needs, sharing information, identifying targets, settling in procedures, trial visits before the child starts and communications with parents to ascertain the individual needs of the child and to ensure these can be met appropriately. Parents’ permission will always be sought before involving outside agencies. Parents see how their child is at collection time and feedback is shared by staff as to how the child has been that day, or any messages passed on by the school exchanged. Staff maintain photos of activities enjoyed by the children which can be viewed by parents at collection time and this is an excellent way of keeping up to date with day to day happenings at the club. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The club manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All Busy Living locations are accessible as we operate from school premises. We have access to a disabled toilet and risk assessments are in place. Adaptations may have to be made to accommodate wheelchair users to allow for turning space where space is limited and table heights may need adjusting which is achievable. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The club Manager and/or Operations Manager are happy to speak to parents face-to-face, or via phone if preferred. When parents register their child we ask specific questions relating to the child's needs and this forms the basis of staffs' understanding of the needs of the child before they start at the club. Parents are contacted before the child starts to gather any further information and parents are also invited to bring their child to the club for settling in sessions so the child feels comfortable when the time comes to be in the club on their own. We consider whether additional staffing is required, which staff may need to be allocated to the child and whether any further equipment is required. We consider the environment and risk assess the needs to ensure the child and others around them are safe. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? None, other than that mentioned above. To keep staff training up to date and to be able to offer and work with the school for any changes in the environment to cater for and suit the child as needed.

local_offer: The success of Buttercups is founded upon a fundamental commitment to quality education combined with fun and care. Our philosophy is learning through play the Buttercups way. We believe that every child is an individual, a unique combination of vitality and delight, of excitement and inquisitiveness. What they all have in common is a wealth of potential. Buttercups provide opportunities for each child to fulfil their potential by developing self-confidence so that they are happy with themselves and with each other, and by giving them care, love and a world of new experiences. We strive to balance established educational principles and acknowledged values with current trends in nursery care and educational thinking. We plan all activities with the core educational curriculum in mind and select the best elements from the Traditional, EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage), Montessori and High Scope pre-school approaches. We believe that every child is an individual with a wealth of potential We train our team to have appropriate skills, aiming to exceed the Ofsted requirements for skill levels We foster parent partnerships through daily feedback on their child's day, parents evenings and social events, whilst providing and encouraging opportunities for parents to become involved in their child’s day Parents return to use our service for their child’s new siblings and recommend us to their friends We are well resourced, enabling our team to deliver the high level of service parents expect We respect and acknowledge the efforts, achievements and qualifications of our team members Our buildings and grounds are well maintained to provide a safe and healthy environment for all children  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We are committed to giving every child the best possible start in life. For children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities, we work in partnership with families to support their development, learning and well being. We aim to help each child make progress across all areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage. We support children with SEND to learn and develop at their own pace, feel included and valued in all activities, communicate and gain independence and thrive with support from their families and professionals. We work closely with parents to create a positive, supportive start to every child’s learning journey. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Special Educational Needs training: completed 2015 All Things Autism SENDCo and Inclusion Coordinator: completed by Lucy Boote (SENDCO) - 2020 Attending termly webinars offered by Bucks Early Years Service. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We ensure we have regular chats and parent meetings to share progress and next steps. We work together with parents on Support Plans or EHCPs, where needed. We listen to parents views and use your knowledge to shape support. We share ideas and activities to help you support your child at home. We keep parents informed through daily feedback (email, on collection and online communication), photos, and parent consultations. Parents are encouraged to get involved by joining in with stay-and-play sessions or parent events. We also ensure parents are part of planning and review meetings to help set goals for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We share regular updates on your child’s progress through daily feedback at drop-off and pick-up as well as our online communication tool where we share pictures of activities throughout the day. We complete learning journals with photos, observations, and milestones. We hold parent meetings to discuss development and next steps. We also complete two-year progress checks and transition reports. For Children with SEND we also use individual support plans and APDR with clear targets, reviewed with you regularly. We also hold more frequent meetings with our SENCO to review progress and adjust support where necessary. We also work together on Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) requests, if needed We make sure you're fully involved in your child’s learning journey and always kept informed. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our buildings are not accessible by wheelchair All rooms have designated quiet areas and spacious outdoor areas How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We welcome all children, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities, and aim to make the transition into our setting as smooth and supportive as possible. We offer tailored settling-in that suits each individual child and their family. Contact us directly for more information on how to start with us. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Ongoing staff training to deepen our understanding of different needs, including autism, speech and language delays, and social, emotional development

local_offer: Buttons keep our in the moment curriculum under constant review and are committed to developing, refining and improving their teaching for the benefit of every child. Preschool policy statements are always available for all parents/carers and can be accessed through our website or copies requested from the setting manager. The staff at Buttons Preschools have developed a sound approach towards children with special education needs, including those who are gifted, able or talented, based upon the following principles: Every Child has the right to a broad and balanced early years curriculum, which is relevant and appropriately differentiated to allow individuals to fulfil their potential. A positive and active participation with all parents/carers. To identify needs promptly and to introduce appropriate teaching/learning strategies. To monitor and evaluate progress effectively. All staff involved in teaching children with special needs are supported and enhanced through working alongside various external agencies. The preschool has established a programme of assessment to identify the needs of individual pupils in all areas of the curriculum (fact/Fact +) . These assessments identify children who may be experiencing difficulties and the appropriate provision is made to meet these needs. We ensure that every child with special needs joins in all the activities of the preschool with their peers as far as is reasonably practical. We aim to integrate children fully within the setting and achieve this by: Extra input from the keyworker 1-1 inclusion support as required Differentiated activities. Methodology appropriate to particular needs. Working in small groups or one-to-one. Involvement with the occupational therapist, speech therapist, educational psychologist, health visitor Regular dialogue with parents/carers and professionals to ensure that children are developing and making good progress both inside preschool and at home. Buttons is a provider of choice, offering excellent provision for all children regardless of "ability" or need, children are offered home visits prior to enrolling within the preschool and IEP are put in place ready for the child to join us.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Fully inclusive Individual Education plans specific to each childs' needs Highly trained and motivated staff teams with a passion for early years and SEND What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use Eylog (early years education log) as a platform for sharing all aspects of the preschool, this encompasses learning and development alongside the targets a child is working towards, the platform is two way and parents can access and add to every area. We have open door policy and parents are encouraged to chat with keyworkers/manager . How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Fully accessible building an external areas, a local park is situated within the grounds of the preschool which has adapted resources suitable for all. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact us via email or telephone to request registration paperwork and prospectus, arrange a visit to the setting (we do offer an open door policy), book a home visit, regsiter and look at sessions available, start date will be confirmed once we have everything in place to ensure the child will be fully supported from day one. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The need for services across the sector has continued to grow, Buttons is committed to continue to be a provider of choice, future plans include upskilling staff further in the areas of need, delivering training via our internal training academy, supporting local families to ensure places are available across the portfolio.

name: Weedon Golf Society
description: The Weedon Golf Society is open to residents and previous residents of all ages, abilities, and handicaps. Women and men play alongside each other in mixed groups. Golf outings are usually on Thursday afternoons once a month from April to October. Dinner in a private room at The Unicorn in Cublington follows on the Friday evening, to which partners are also invited. The match programme is varied between individual and team play and suits all levels of golfer. The social side is playing golf is very much to the fore. The aim of the Society is to promote social relationships and fellowship amongst the residents of Weedon and the surrounding villages through the game of golf. The Society is open by invitation to players of all ages, abilities, and handicaps but is limited to a maximum of 40 playing members. Golf fixtures are usually held on Thursday afternoons on the second Thursday of each month from April to October, though intermediate additional fixtures may be arranged fortnightly during the warmer months of the summer. The competitions at each fixture are varied and include both individual and team events to suit all levels of golfing ability; members' handicaps currently vary between 9 and 45. Each event consists of 18 holes of golf, preceded by coffee and bacon roll (alternatives available), with tee-off times between 12 midday and 1pm. In addition to the trophies (only available to members), additional prizes are given for various achievements at every match. Whilst the social side of playing golf is very much to the fore in the Society, members can compete for six trophies during the season; The Men's Champions Cup, The Ladies' Champions Shield, The President’s Trophy, The Absent Friends Trophy, The Rose Bowl, The Weedon Shield and The Mike Moore Memorial Trophy. New members (annual membership fee £25 for 2025) and guests at individual fixtures are always welcome.

description: The Club welcomes new members whether experienced or novice and those wanting to learn the sport of dinghy sailing. Great Moor is a club for all ages, all abilities, and all seasons, come and take a look. When we are open, organised sailing takes place every Sunday throughout the year (except February) with races for those that are interested. Club dinghies are available for hire to members at low rates, following government guidelines. Not all members sail - an increasing number windsurf, paddleboard, and canoe. The club also owns sit-on-top kayaks and Canadian canoes for hire to members also at low rates. There are also Social and Fishing Memberships so we cater for a wide range of interests. Several Scouts Groups, and a Sub Aqua group also have memberships. Members are also allowed to camp at the site. Join us on 9 May for our open day. Membership fee information is available on the website.

name: Giocoso Concert Band
description: The name 'Giocoso' means playing in a friendly, humourous manner, and that is exactly what we try to do. We meet every Thursday evening from 8pm to 9:45pm in Greenacre Hall, Drayton Parslow. Everyone is welcome, and there are no auditions. The Giocoso Concert Band was formed in 2003 and was based in Swanbourne for 18 years. Due to its increasing membership, in 2021, the band moved to a larger rehearsal venue in Drayton Parslow. Since its formation, the Giocoso Concert Band has performed at engagements such as summer fetes, local music festivals, and community Christmas Carol concerts. With a repertoire comprising music ranging from Mozart to the Beatles, there is usually something for everyone. If you play a woodwind, brass or percussion instrument and are interested in joining the Giocoso Concert Band, then please phone either Dave or Julie.

name: Cadmore End Church of England Combined School
description: Mixed-gender primary school in High Wycombe for 3 to 11-year-olds. Cadmore End C of E Combined School is a happy, warm, and friendly church school nestled in beautiful woodland that fosters pupil's love for outdoor learning. We make extensive use of our woodland setting and have a rich programme of extracurricular activities including Forest School. As a member of the Church of England our values and religious ethos can be seen in all aspects of our care and education. We value every child and believe we provide an education encouraging many core learning values - creativity, independence, thinking, and emotional intelligence. Children, staff, parents, and governors are on the journey of education as partners in learning, and we value highly the support we receive from our parents. It is vitally important to us that parents and families share our vision and work in partnership with us for the benefit of the children. We believe that a successful start to your child’s education will enable them to become life-long learners and responsible citizens in our fast-changing world. We help them to succeed at Cadmore End but aim to foster in them a desire to continue to succeed long after they leave us. Hopefully you will find our website informative and interesting – it is but a snapshot of some of the many things which are going on in a thriving, busy school such as ours. If you would like to find out more about us please do not hesitate to use the ‘Contact Us’ pages for further information. If you choose to join our team as a parent, staff member, governor or child we look forward to meeting you and learning together.

local_offer: Cadmore End is a mainstream setting with up to 15 children in each year group from N1 to year 6. It has four vertically grouped classes – Years N2 and R, Years 1 and 2, Years 3 and 4, Years 5 and 6. We ensure that all children are valued equally regardless of their abilities and/or social, emotional or behavioural problems. We are a small school with a ‘can do’ attitude. Our values are empathy, love, respect, honesty, faith and courage. We aim to: • Provide a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum, differentiated to meet each child’s individual needs, and allowing each child to fulfil their potential. • Meet the requirements of the National Curriculum. • Work in partnership with the child, parents, carers and any other agencies involved. • Ensure that individual needs do not constrain any educational entitlement. • Ensure equal opportunities. Additional needs or disabilities which can affect a child’s learning fall under the following areas: • Communication and interaction: speech, language and communication needs, Autistic Spectrum Disorder. • Cognition and Learning: learning difficulties, specific learning difficulties (such as dyslexia, dyspraxia, dyscalculia) • Social, emotional and mental health difficulties: Behaviour reflecting underlying mental health difficulties (such as anxiety, depression), Attention Deficit Disorder (ADD), Attention Deficit Hyperactive Disorder (ADHD), attachment disorder • Sensory and/or physical: hearing or visual impairment, physical disability, multi-sensory impairment The school’s Equalities and Inclusion Policy and Objectives for 2023-2024 and Special Educational Needs Policy can be found on the school website. https://www.cadmoreendschool.org/web/send_and_inclusion/329795 What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? local_offer: The type of SEND provision that Cadmore End C E Combined school caters for: Cadmore End is a mainstream setting with up to 15 children in each year group from N2 to year 6. It has four vertically grouped classes – Years N2 and R, Years 1 and 2, Years 3 and 4, Years 5 and 6. We ensure that all children are valued equally regardless of their abilities and/or social, emotional or behavioural problems. We are a small school with a ‘can do’ attitude. Our values are empathy, love, respect, honesty, faith and courage. We aim to: • Provide a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum, differentiated to meet each child’s individual needs, and allowing each child to fulfil their potential. • Meet the requirements of the National Curriculum. • Work in partnership with the child, parents, carers and any other agencies involved. • Ensure that individual needs do not constrain any educational entitlement. • Ensure equal opportunities. Additional needs or disabilities which can affect a child’s learning fall under the following areas: • Communication and interaction: speech, language and communication needs, Autistic Spectrum Disorder. • Cognition and Learning: learning difficulties, specific learning difficulties (such as dyslexia, dyspraxia, dyscalculia) • Social, emotional and mental health difficulties: Behaviour reflecting underlying mental health difficulties (such as anxiety, depression), Attention Deficit Disorder (ADD), Attention Deficit Hyperactive Disorder (ADHD), attachment disorder • Sensory and/or physical: hearing or visual impairment, physical disability, multi-sensory impairment The school’s Equalities and Inclusion Policy and Objectives for 2019 to 2020 and Special Educational Needs Policy can be found on the school website.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The school is committed to reduce and eliminate barriers to access to the curriculum and to full participation in the school community for pupils, and prospective pupils, with a disability. The school provides all pupils with a broad and balanced curriculum, differentiated and adjusted to meet the needs of individual pupils and their preferred learning styles; and endorses the key principles in the National Curriculum framework, which underpin the development of a more inclusive Curriculum. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We work in partnership with parents and appropriate professionals to set up relevant and effective programmes. This provision is regularly reviewed and, where appropriate, further advice is sought from external agencies such as speech and language and Educational Psychologists. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? While we are making regular improvements to increase accessibility across the whole site, the school buildings have developed since the Victorian era which can make accessibility challenging. Access to around half of the building is currently possible, including the main school hall, and there is a specially adapted toilet for those requiring increased access. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The school continues to take account of the needs of pupils and visitors with physical difficulties and sensory impairments when planning and undertaking future improvements and refurbishments of the site and premises.

name: Yoga for Women - Halton
description: There are many types of yoga, and these classes are a beautiful blend of different styles. We incorporate hatha yoga (a physical and mental practice that aims to prepare the body and mind); vinyasa yoga (a faster-paced, aerobic-style workout where poses flow into one another); yin yoga (a meditative style that involves stretches and poses that help improve flexibility and mobility), and restorative yoga (focusing on winding down after a long day and relaxing the mind). We practice these different types of yoga by creating our own unique practices, which we work through on a rolling three-week cycle: 1) Luna by YogaBellies (the pace fluctuates with the phases of the moon) 2) CorePlay by YogaBellies (a vinyasa or flow class, with a set routine of postures) 3) Chakra classes (which work on stimulating different energy centres in the body)
organisation: Yoga with Alice D The body undergoes huge change during pregnancy and childbirth. YogaBellies for Mum and Baby is a unique postnatal yoga class which focuses on mum’s three main areas of concern: the back, the abdominal muscles and the pelvic floor. We focus on rebuilding these three key areas post-natally, at a pace that suits you. As the integrity of each of these key areas is interconnected, we work on all three at once to help bring back structural integrity to your body. At YogaBellies for Mum and Baby, we don’t “put baby in the corner” while you practice yoga. Our exclusive postnatal classes also incorporate baby yoga postures for your little one too so that they can practice with mummy! As every aspect of your life will include baby now, we help you integrate baby into your yoga practice, while feeling the benefits of yoga for you too. You will also learn breath awareness and relaxation techniques, which help to increase energy levels and allow you to relax while with baby (yes it is possible!!) Yoga provides a wonderful resource for you and your baby that allows you to deal positively with stress, and encourage mindful relaxation in your role as a mother and to help gently guide the body and mind back to their former glory. alice@yogabellies.co.uk https://yogabellies.com/teachers/alice-drewett-wendover-halton-tring-buckinghamshire-hertfordshire/

description: Wendover Woods is a truly special place in the Chilterns and we hope you enjoy a safe, relaxing visit. Various activities include: 4 walking trails, a Juniper cycling trail, 3 running routes, a fitness trail, horse riding, Orienteering, Go Ape, a picnic area, Cafe. Dogs welcome. organisation: Wendover Woods Situated in the beautiful surroundings of the Chilterns, Wendover Woods is home stunning trails, Go Ape and picturesque views Before your visit, you can download the glide parking app which enables contactless payment for car parking. Wendover Woods is a truly special place in the Chilterns and we hope you enjoy a safe, relaxing visit. Please remember that it is your responsibility to follow the guidance on staying safe outside your home. Try the new Gruffalo Spotters 2 trail. Download the app, buy the pack for from the Information Point and follow the trail to interact with all the Gruffalo characters in the woods and finish at the Gruffalo sculpture! Please think carefully before you visit and come prepared: BBQs are not allowed in any of our forests Make sure you have suitable footwear, and if you plan to cycle, an appropriate helmet Plan for what you will do if the site is closed or looks busy and be prepared to go somewhere else less busy, or return home and visit another time Be kind. Be patient. This is a new experience for all of us. We need your help to make this work. At a glance we offer: 4 walking trails Juniper cycle trail 3 running routes Fitness trail Horse riding Orienteering trails Go Ape Nordic Walking Play area Picnic Area and barbecues - no barbecues Café - open for takeaway only Dogs welcome How to Get There: Chiltern trains to Wendover, then short taxi ride or 50 minute walk. London Midland trains to Tring, then short taxi ride. Bus 50 (Monday to Saturday) and T1 (Monday to Friday) to Wendover/Halton Camp, then 40 minute walk. Bus 161 (Sunday and Bank Holidays) to near entrance gate, then 20 minute walk. Entrance located on St Leonards Road, off B4009 Wendover to Tring road. wendoverwoods@forestryengland.uk https://www.forestryengland.uk/wendover-woods

name: Action4Youth | The Caldecotte Xperience | Holiday Camp Adventure Days
description: Join us for big adventure, fresh air, and brilliant memories- with flexible multi-date booking. Holiday Camp Adventure Days are designed for young people who want to get active, try new things, and come home buzzing from a day outdoors. Expect a fun mix of water-based sessions, climbing-style challenges, bushcraft, games and team activities, all delivered by our experienced instructors. Book one day, a few days, or build a full holiday plan by selecting multiple dates across 2026 in a single checkout. Holiday Camp Adventure Days are action-packed and varied, with activities that may include: - Water sports - Climbing-style activities - Bushcraft and outdoor skills - Team challenges, games and more No previous experience is needed. Our friendly instructors guide everyone, from first-timers to confident adventurers. All specialist equipment is provided – you just need to bring lunch, a drink, and spare clothes for outdoor fun. All instructors hold enhanced DBS checks (including barred list) and relevant industry qualifications, with regular training in safety and safeguarding. They also have experience supporting a wide range of young people. Extended Day option If you need earlier drop-off and later pick-up, select Extended Day on the booking page. Extended Day times: 8:30am to 5:30pm Extended Day price: £5 (inclusive of VAT) per selected day Selecting Extended Day applies it to all the dates in that booking. Please visit our website to learn more and to book.
organisation: Action4Youth Action4Youth changes lives and creates better chances for young people by creating opportunities to discover their personal strengths and potential. We work with young people from all backgrounds and all abilities to make a real difference to their futures. We are a respected and dynamic charity based in Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes but reaching young people across the wider south east region. What we do Action4Youth is a leading delivery partner for the National Citizen Service (NCS) and consistently over delivers in terms of both quality and quantity. Action4Youth takes the strategic lead for the voluntary organisations supporting children and young people aged 5 – 25 years across its area. It has around 100 organisations in membership and offers a range of essential support and services. Our outdoor centre, Caldecotte Xperience in Milton Keynes, creates opportunities for young people to have amazing, challenging, fun and sometimes transformational experiences. They learn what they can do rather than what they can’t, building their confidence and self-belief. Action4Youth is the operating authority for Buckinghamshire and Milton Keynes for Open Awards Groups for the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme. office@action4youth.org http://www.action4youth.org

local_offer: Calibre Audio provides an audiobook lending service to people of all ages who have a print disability. Membership is completely free of charge for children and young adults with SEND who are under the age of 25 years. A print disability is any health condition, learning difference or disability which impacts on the ability to read or enjoy reading print. Qualifying conditions include: - Visual impairments - Learning differences such as dyslexia - Neurodivergent conditions like Autism, ADHD or Tourette's - A brain injury - Chronic fatigue - Long Covid - Dementia - Health conditions that impact on physical dexterity such as Multiple Sclerosis, Motor Neurone Disease, Parkinson’s, arthritis, or paralysis - Cancer related cognitive disorder - Terminal illness  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Calibre Audio is a national audiobook charity and is delighted to be working with Buckinghamshire schools on an exciting project to use audiobooks to support children with their reading and literacy, and to encourage reading for pleasure at home. Children will listen to an audiobook and follow the text in a printed book at the same time. Research shows that this method is highly effective at improving reading skills. In addition, we would like to encourage the children and young adults to listen to audiobooks at home for pleasure. They will not need a printed book for this and they are eligible for a free account with Calibre Audio enabling them to access a wide selection of different age-appropriate audiobooks. Research also shows that simply listening to an audiobook stimulates the same parts of the brain as reading itself and that it helps improve comprehension, sentence structure, and general knowledge, as well as helping with relaxation and wellbeing. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We work in partnership with professor Janice Wearmouth and her team at the University of Bedfordshire. Some staff/ volunteers have completed British Dyslexia Association, ADHD Foundation, and Autism Oxford training. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents consent to their children becoming members of Calibre Audio and are asked to contribute feedback via email or online survey. https://www.calibreaudio.org.uk/splash/calibre-audio-and-bucks-schools-audiobook-project-2024-parents How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? No, we don't share information about children's progress. The schools involved in our project may be able to share information related to progress after the audiobook intervention. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our audiobooks are downloaded or streamed in a location of the member's choice. If the child is accessing the audiobook as part of the schools project, their teacher or learning support assistant will access the resource in the classroom, library or learning base. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If the child or young person has a print disability their parent or guardian can sign them up for their free audiobook membership via our website or by contacting our membership services team by phone in office hours What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We hope to roll out the school audiobook project to more schools and establish book groups with local SEND charities.

name: Buckinghamshire CAMHS CRISIS team
description: The Buckinghamshire CAMHS Crisis team are a specialist service who provide intensive support for young people and families experiencing a period of acute mental health crisis. This is no definition of a crisis that would cover everyone’s experience. Not every crisis a young person experiences will require a crisis intervention but where this is appropriate, we can offer an enhanced level of support. As a team we want to help and support young people and through families through what can be an extremely challenging time in their lives. Our aim is to understand what is causing the difficulties and whether we can improve a young person's situation or that of their carers with a mental health crisis intervention. When deciding if to offer a crisis intervention, we consider the level of risk and how it relates to a mental health difficulty. We aim to support in stabilising and lowering these risks. Our team consists of trained Mental Health Nurses, Psychiatrists, Social Prescribers, Social Workers, Speciality Doctors, and Support Workers who provide intensive levels of care for children and families in Buckinghamshire. We can offer face to face sessions, home visits, telephone contacts, and virtual appointments. Who is the service for? Young people and families need to be: - Under the age of 18. - In an acute mental health crisis that can be managed in the community (with increased support). - Based in the Buckinghamshire area or registered with a Buckinghamshire GP. - Requiring an increased intensity of support in managing high levels or sudden increases of risk. What do we do? We provide intensive support during a mental health crisis. We will offer a range of interventions, to reduce the likelihood of admission to inpatient hospital services and enable early discharge with a safe and appropriate plan of support. Our work is informed by lots of different therapies and our main aim is to support you and the people around you to keep you safe. We can work with you, your family, and other professionals involved in your care. Crisis support focuses on helping you manage a time when things feel out of control or overwhelming. It is therefore support that is short-term and intensive, usually for between 2 and 6 weeks. I need help - You can contact Buckinghamshire CAMHS teams on the number provided between 8am and 6pm Monday to Friday (excluding bank holidays) - NHS 111 has a mental health support team you can contact anytime. It’s an emergency - Please contact 999 or attend your local Accident and Emergency department if you feel you need to access immediate support.

name: Buckinghamshire Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS)
description: Buckinghamshire CAMHS helps children and young people up to 18 who are finding it hard to cope with everyday life because of difficult feelings, behaviours, or relationships. Just as we go to the doctors when we are physically ill, sometimes we will need extra help with our mental health. We can all feel sad, worried, angry, or stressed, but sometimes these feelings can become harder to manage and get in the way of our lives. CAMHS can help young people understand why they feel that way, what it can be hard to deal with and work with them to find a way to make it better. We support young people and their families who are facing challenges and difficulties with behaviour, as well as more complex mental health concerns. Our teams are made up of different professionals who all have specialised skills and expertise, such as psychologists, psychiatrists, therapists, nurses, and social workers. They are specialists in dealing with conditions such as: - Anxiety - Depression - Eating Disorders - OCD - PTSD - Self-harm - Psychosis - Attachment Disorders - Body Dysmorphic Disorder In addition to mental health support, CAMHS will help children and young people who have or may have autism and/or ADHD. The service carries out assessments, provides a diagnosis and offers advice and support. The team can also help some young people with medication for ADHD, where this is appropriate. How To Get Help Our Single Point of Access (SPA) team is the first point of contact for referrals and getting advice. There is no referral criteria for Buckinghamshire CAMHS SPA team, only that we will seek to support all Children and Young People (CYP), families, and professionals where there is concern regarding the emotional wellbeing of any young person up to their eighteenth Birthday. Any professional, parent, or carer can make a referral, and any young person over 16 years old can make a self-referral. Our SPA team will find out more about the difficulties the young person is having and decide if the CAMHS teams can help and provide support. Referrals can be made by phone, email or through a form accessible on our website. CAMHS CRISIS Team Our Crisis team are a specialist service who provide intensive support for young people and families experiencing a period of acute crisis. They provide intensive support during a mental health crisis. They will offer a range of interventions to reduce the likelihood of admission to inpatient hospital services and enable early discharge with a safe and appropriate plan of support. To watch a video about our crisis offer, please view the links below.

name: Camp Mohawk (Wargrave, Berkshire)
description: Camp Mohawk is a multi-functional day centre for children with special needs and their families, set in 5 acres of beautiful countryside, just outside Wargrave, Berkshire. Throughout the year the centre provides a range of activities, facilities and natural space to encourage children with a variety of special needs to play, socialise, and learn in a secure and caring environment. Registration is mandatory for families and all visits need to be booked in advance. To make a booking, or if you have any questions regarding upcoming events listed here, please contact us via email or call the centre. Contact for details There is a voluntary 'registration fee' at a suggested £5 per month or £60 per financial year. Camp Mohawk is a charitable organisation and as such, this fee is voluntary. If you do not wish to, or do not feel able to contribute at this level your registration and ability to access services will not be affected. Contributions can be made by cheque (payable to Camp Mohawk), or by standing order using the registration fee (standing order) form. We can also take cash and card payments on site, and direct transfers into our bank account (please contact us for bank details).

local_offer: We provide the children and young people with stimulating workshops, sensory and social activities that are led by experienced enthusiastic staff and carefully designed to address the common developmental requirements of children with special needs. We also provide their families with some short term respite, a support network and friendly advice. Both our centre and approach work sympathetically with the challenging behaviour that often accompanies disability in young people. We provide this support for families in all school holidays except Christmas, term time Saturdays, plus some evenings and weekends, and also liaise locally with special needs schools and support groups. Our Short Breaks scheme, which is specifically for children and young people aged 8 to 25 years who have a primary diagnosis of High Functioning Autism or Asperger's Syndrome, provides after school sessions for different age groups on Tuesdays and Thursdays in term time, plus full days of activities during school holidays.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to help children and young people to develop their confidence, independence and social skills through play. We aim to increase opportunities for children and young people with SEND, and their families, to access natural environments and approrpiate outdoor and indoor play facilities. We aim to provide and facilitiate a support network for parents, carers and siblings. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our core staff team have a wealth of experience working with children and young people with SEND. We regularly undertake Team Teach positive handling training as well as various other training relating to Health and Safety. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We regularly consult with parents on our activities and planned developments and are keen to welcome parents to enter into discussion with us, including joining our Board of Trustees. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We do not send information or reports as standard but are able to provide supporting documentation when required to assist with applications for PIP, EHCPs, assistance from Social Care. Any incident reports are available on request to the registered parent(s)/carers of a young person. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have a network of accessible paths that extend to most areas of the site. We have a range of accessible play equipment and strive to make our play areas as inclusive as possible. We have accessible changing facilities and toilets. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families simply need to download our registration forms from our website and send them to us by post for processing, after this families are invited to join our mailing list through which they will recieve notification about our activities and booking procedures. Alternatively, families can get in touch by phone and we will explain the registration process. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: Farnham Common Village schools are mainstream two form entry schools with a part-time nursery for children from 3 years old in the Infant school. The two schools are now a Federation with one Headteacher. They are inclusive schools and offer a broad and balanced curriculum for all children. The schools aim to create an environment that is creative and fun.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The infant school is also a Forest school, and all children participate in forest school activities on a regular basis. Both schools place much emphasis on outdoor learning. At the Farnham Common Village Schools, we aim to support all children in their learning and help them to achieve their full potential. Farnham Common Village schools provide a nurturing and caring environment and all children have access to quality Personal, Social, Health Education (PHSE). What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Systems are in place to ensure children are supported socially and emotionally. The schools also have four ELSA trained LSAs (Emotional Literacy Support Assistants) who run Nurture groups and will work with individual children when needed. We believe that Quality First teaching is essential to ensure progress but acknowledge that some children will require additional support to achieve this. Work in class is differentiated, and intervention programs are provided for children needing support. Adjustments to the physical environment are made as needed for children with physical disabilities, and individual support is provided when needed usually for children with EHCP Plans. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Reasonable adjustments are made to accommodate the needs of individual children under the guidance of health and education specialists as needed. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

description: We are a large group of volunteers who help with shopping, prescription help, and telephone calls. We are connecting people and providing local support to people in need. Please contact for further information. A group of parishioners have put themselves on a list and a WhatsApp group to provide local support to people in need. In addition, the local police have said they will respond as far as they can to anyone in need, too. If you need support in any way, then please get in touch with the Clerk by email, and we can pass on your contact details to someone on the WhatsApp group list or the local police (as you wish), who will be in touch as soon as possible. Our email is monitored daily. You can also contact us by telephone. Please note that this line is only checked twice a week. name: Carina Nash
description: I am an Ofsted registered childminder living with my husband Carl, 2 children and pets in Hag Hill Rise for 10 years. I enjoy spending time with my children reading, walking the dogs and going to the gym when I find the time! It is important to me that the children in my care are physically active and we spend as much time outside in places such as Burnham Beeches, Windsor Great Park and local parks as the children desire and weather permits! I have a wide range of resources and toys for the children and including visits to the library during our routine, with trips during the school holidays to places like Odds Farm, safari parks and museums. I live in a quiet cul-de-sac location with ample parking for drop off and collection as well as a good-sized garden with lots of outdoor toys and activities, such as sand and water play, scooters and bikes as well as a well equipped play park at the end of the road. I regularly send photo updates. We have 2 Cocker Spaniels - Tig is 7 and Mabel is 18 months old. I have a first-class BA (Honours) degree in Childhood Studies and a Foundation Degree in Childhood Studies: Education. I hold a valid First Aid Certificate, and food hygiene accreditation and have attended training courses in areas such as safeguarding children, Inclusion, positive behaviour, food hygiene, phonics phase 2, planning and observations and risk assessments. I have also completed my level 3 Diploma For The Children And Young Peoples Workforce. I view training as an ongoing responsibility to the children I care for and is imperative to their well-being that I am as knowledgeable and skilled in my profession as possible.

local_offer: As a childminder, I would be the first point of contact for the families of children with SEND needs. I am to make the child's time with me fun, enjoyable and to be as inclusive and supportive as possible. I am to provide an enriching environment accessible to those with a SEND requirement.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I strive to provide equity in a child's early education. I aim to work with parents and outside agencies to implement ideas and recommendations to provide the best start to children's early education. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Makaton - ongoing Speech and Language How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I form a close relationship with all parents and will provide opportunities for the parent to get involved with their child's care and education. Parents can contact me at any time to discuss their child's progress and termly reports can be provided upon request so parents can see evidence of their child's progress. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Regular conversations, meetings and reports are standard for every child but I welcome the opportunity to discuss progress at the parents' request. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Small step to front door. Small step to back door. Small step to grassed garden area. Ramps can be provided. The only toilet facilities are upstairs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If a space is available, I can offer as many settling in sessions as is required to ensure the child is settled and happy in the setting. I am happy to have regular meetings with the family to aid settling in - parents are welcome to stay during the sessions. I can be flexible and allow shortened visits if necessary. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Further training courses are planned and I am happy to undertake any training required by the family to assist in the care of the child.

name: Buckingham Foodbank
description: If you don't have enough food to eat, we can help. We run a local Foodbank distributing non-perishable and fresh food in Buckingham and the surrounding villages. Simply ask to be referred by: Citizens Advice, your doctors' surgery, Community Nurses, Health Visitors, Social Services, Local churches, or Buckinghamshire Council Helping Hand team. Our team of volunteers will then deliver supplies directly to your home, or confidentially through your referring agency. We also have nappies, toiletries, female sanitary products, and other special items on request and can take note of special dietary needs, for example, allergies or intolerances. This service covers short-term emergencies such as sudden unemployment or loss of benefits. Therefore it’s crucial that the underlying issues leading to your food crisis are also dealt with, which is why it is important you seek help from an agency such as those listed above. Sorry, we do not take calls directly from the public. Those referring you will advise us of your food needs including the number of food parcels you may require. The Foodbank is open between 10:00am and 12:00pm every Tuesday to drop off food items, toiletries, and so on. Sorry, we can't accept fresh food or baby food but will gratefully accept most other things. Or if you would like to give a monetary donation please visit our website for more details. Thank you for your generosity.

Strategies such as using technology, now and next boards, movement breaks and chunking of tasks are used widely across the school. More specific, individualised provision is detailed within pupil support plans; carefully designed alongside both pupils’ teachers and parents/carers to ensure effectiveness. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The SENCo attends regular training with the Oxford Diocese Buckinghamshire Schools Trust to ensure we have the most up-to-date practice and information in school. The SENCo is part of the Buckinghamshire Council SEN liaison groups which meet half termly to support the provision for SEN across schools. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome your feedback on how we provide for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities and endeavour to provide regular opportunities for parents and carers to share their views and opinions around SEND support at Great Horwood. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All pupils will be provided with high quality, inclusive, teaching that is differentiated to meet the needs of all learners. The quality of classroom teaching provided to pupils with SEND is monitored through a number of processes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have an outdoor wheelchair lift which allows access from the outside buildings and car park into the main school building. The main reception entrance is accessible via the car park and pedestrian gates. There are two automatic accessible doors from the school hall and downstairs cloakroom leading outside. However, we also have a number of double doors inside the main building that would require support in an emergency evacuation. Children and young people with SEN have different needs, but the general presumption is that all children with SEN but without an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) are welcome to apply for a place at our school, in line with the school admissions policy. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

local_offer: I am an Ofsted registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and we will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?
