description: Every week we send out free Fresh Fruit and Veg Boxes to families in tough situations. Our Fresh Food Boxes are delivered to the doorstep by one of our lovely volunteers and will always include a hope-filled, positive and personal conversation as well as the opportunity to pray. Our delivery drivers feedback anything relevant so that we can ensure the families are getting all the support that they require, be that physical, practical or emotional. We use the produce that we grow in our gardens in our Fresh Food Boxes, this is done by a group of volunteers and some of our families as they learn how to grow and cultivate their own produce. We also have over 150 chickens which enables us to send out free range eggs with our Fresh Food Boxes. Please contact us for further information.
organisation: Restore Hope Restore Hope Latimer is a family focused charity based at Latimer Park. A special space in the countryside set in the heart of the Chilterns, just outside Amersham and Chesham and has been operating since 2002 and has a proven record of bringing change and help to people in need. We believe in the value of healthy, happy and stable families. We also believe that no matter how bad a situation may seem there is always hope. Our vision is therefore that every struggling family in the Chilterns finds help and hope for the future. This is clearly a big aim and one that requires us to continually increase our influence, effectiveness and reputation. We aim to achieve our vision by advancing and developing the programmes that we offer and continually looking for ways to engage with those most in need. We operate a clear strategy, with deliberate focus and dogged determination. We empower and equip key volunteers to lead various elements of our work, and support a motivated core staff team. RHL seeks to make best use of the fantastic facilities that Latimer Park offers and, where appropriate, grows into other spaces in the community to offer easy access to our programmes and to further develop the reputation of the charity. naomi.meech@restorehopelatimer.org http://www.restorehopelatimer.org

name: Townfield House Mosque
description: Wycombe Islamic Mission and Mosque Trust Ltd. (WIMMT) functions as an umbrella organization overseeing the operation of four mosques in High Wycombe, including Townfield House Mosque. Each mosque offers religious services and is staffed by resident Imams who provide prayers, teaching, advice, and guidance. The Muslim community in High Wycombe predominantly comprises immigrants from South Asia, particularly Azad Kashmir, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, as well as their descendants. Additionally, there is a growing number of converts to Islam, whose needs are also recognized and supported. Most worshippers at WIMMT mosques adhere to traditional Sunni Islam, following the Hanafi school of jurisprudence, which emphasizes peace, justice, and harmony for all, irrespective of faith, background, culture, or race. Nevertheless, the mosques welcome Muslims from all branches of Islam, providing an inclusive space for worship and learning.

local_offer: Our School believes that every pupil has an entitlement to develop their full potential. Educational experiences are provided which develop pupils’ achievements and recognise their individuality. Diversity is valued as a rich resource, which supports the learning of all. In our School, we recognise a child’s right to a broad, balanced, relevant and challenging curriculum, which is appropriate to their individual abilities, talents and personal qualities.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? At Great Kingshill Church of England Combined School we are committed to providing the best learning opportunities for all pupils, including those with SEND. We believe all children are individual and the needs, strengths and talents for every child will be different. We believe we can meet these needs through a curriculum which is challenging, enjoyable and enriches learning while providing opportunities for every child to work at their own level and pace. We recognise that many children may require additional support or additional challenge at some point within their learning journey. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Specialist training has been accessed for staff to meet the needs of individual/groups of children. Individual staff has had further, or more specific training on how to support pupils with individual needs from specialists or through external training courses. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? In consultation with the pupil and parent/carer, pupil profiles or SEN support plans are written by the class teacher and are overseen by the SENDCO; these are reviewed termly. These methods are also used to show how support is targeted and the effectiveness of the intervention. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Each pupil who has been identified as having special needs will have an SEN Support Plan that is written by the Class Teacher and reflects the needs of the child. These are shared termly with Parents at the termly review meetings. Parents can meet with Class Teacher or SENDCo at any time if they feel it would be helpful. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The school’s governing body involve other bodies (including health, social care, BC support services) to meet the needs of pupils with SEND and their families by using outside agencies.

name: One Can Trust Foodbank (High Wycombe)
description: One Can Trust provides weekly food parcels for anyone in South Bucks who is financially challenged. As part of our service, we can provide one parcel per household without a referral but thereafter, requests for support must come through one of our referring partner organisations. Organisations include the Helping Hand Team at Buckinghamshire Council, housing associations, Citizens Advice Bureau, Connection Support, Health Visitors, and schools. The majority of food parcels are delivered by a team of volunteer drivers. Clients living in certain geographical pockets (such as Downley) collect their parcels from dedicated hubs. We deliver to all of South Bucks including Iver, Bourne End, Stokenchurch, Princes Risborough, Holmer Green, Beaconsfield, and Marlow. If you need help and don’t have contact details for one of our referring partners, please contact the number below. We will be very happy to provide an emergency food parcel and put you in touch with the most appropriate referring partner for ongoing support. If you wish to donate food, you are very welcome to drop it to the warehouse in Duke Street which is open from Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 3:30pm. If these times are not convenient, please let us know as on some days, we have evening teams in the warehouse. Should you wish to volunteer with One Can Trust, please get in touch via the volunteering email address. Thank you.

name: Carrieann Glasgow
description: Childminder located in Aylesbury, close to town centre, in the District of Aylesbury Vale. I am a registered childminder with experience of more than 10 years of childcare, worked as a nanny and as a nursery practitioner prior to settling as an established childminder. I have brought this knowledge and ideas into my own home environment, providing a stimulating area for children to develop. My environment consists of a purpose play room with areas for sensory exploring, a quiet area for reading, role play area, small children's table, art easel for mark making and floor space to access a range of low level equipment. I also have a separate kitchen area with a table for snacks/ meals, and some big craft activities, and a garden available all year round with a special fake grass area with sensory table and building area, a grass area and a growing area at the bottom of my garden. I also have an older children's space in my dining room, which provides a sofa, older games and puzzles, crafts and their own space away from the younger children. I take children out on a regular basis to local groups and activities, which include parks and we love exploring outside in open spaces and woods. Lighthouse toddler group, Cha Char Chimps music group, and I hold annual passes to Whipsnade Zoo and Hogshaw Farm which we visit regularly too. I have 2 children of my own, 1 is in year 3 at Broughton Community School and the other is at secondary school in year 9 at The Grange. Every day brings new experiences to my own children and all the children in my care. My Local Offer is I have 2 spaces available come September 2025 due to 2 of my current full time children leaving to start school. The spaces I have available are full-time Tuesday to Friday 8:00am to 5:00pm. I am registered to receive local funding, Tax-free childcare and Kiddicare vouchers and am happy to accept any other voucher systems you use with your own jobs. I also have spaces available for before and aftercare for Broughton Community schools. I am open for school holiday cover too, providing outdoor day trips and home experiences of cooking and crafts days for the summer holidays and half terms so please do not hesitate to phone and ask for a visit.

local_offer: I have a large space for providing any care a child may need. I am happy to support parents with children who have additional needs and will support them with providing the best care that I can.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I like to work with families to provide the best care suitable for each individual child's needs, I am happy to take extra training and advice for this to be achieved. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I hold a Level 3 Diploma in Childcare and Education, and I like to keep myself updated with local training. I am happy to take any other additional training which may be needed to meet the individual needs of each child. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work alongside parents, making a WhatsApp group to communicate and a daily dairy. When a child first starts in my care, I ask for daily routines from home and any other religious or learning difficulties they may have. I like to have a good background knowledge of them and what they can already achieve. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I set up a WhatsApp when you start with my provision which I use to share daily routine, meals and photos of what your child is up to. I also use these to communicate with you during the day. I use all the photos in a child's individual tracker which I share with your every term to show how your child is developing. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All my setting is on a ground floor basis, which include a playroom with all 7 areas of learning, and an outdoor garden space which has grass and astro turf. I also have a single bathroom for toileting but is available on the first floor by a set of stairs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I am happy to meet any families and chat about their needs and care they would like me to provide. I have a profile book which is available for any new parent to look through which shows my up to date training, first aid certificate, parent feed back forms and pictures of outings and activities that I have provided in the past. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I have a growing area in my garden which I would like to expand, and I am currently working on some new resources to encourage different outdoor play. I am also looking at visual labels and pictures to brighten up my playroom.

description: The Victims First Specialist Service provides specialist support for victims and witnesses of crime including rape and sexual abuse, exploitation and modern slavery and can provide Restorative Justice services. The service helps those with longer term or more complex needs and focuses on the individual and the impact the crime has had on them, regardless of the crime they have experienced. The support will be provided by specialist Independent Sexual Violence Advisers (ISVAs), Restorative Justice Practitioners, Exploitation Specialists and staff with other relevant specialist skills and knowledge. Support includes trauma-informed interventions in individual or group settings, advocacy support including help to access mental health or drug and alcohol services, restorative justice conferencing, as well as practical and emotional support to navigate the criminal justice process. If you would like to get support for yourself or someone else you can do so by calling us or completing our online referral form.

local_offer: Our SENCO is available to discuss with parents the individual needs of your child. We will adapt our curriculum and environment to meet the needs of all children.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Della Ashton has been our SENCO ( special needs coordinator) for over 20 years. We have regular in house training for all staff. When parental consent has been obtained we can seek advice from Buckinghamshire Early Years Service. Our SENCO has formed close links to outside agencies including Speech and Language Therapy (SALT), Occupational Therapists (OT), Pediatricians and specialist teaching services. Referrals can be made when necessary. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENCO/manager Della Ashton has an advanced certificate in SENCO training along with Diane Arthur our Deputy. We regularly attends termly briefing sessions. All staff will be updated as well as in house training. Our policies and procedures remain up to date. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Our setting values and welcomes all children. We have a high adult to child ratio, ensuring all children reach their full potential. During your child's introduction visit before your child starts at our preschool, you and your child will meet with their key person and SENCO. They will discuss what support your child needs and what level of support you would like your child to have, developing a partnership between parents and staff. We will discuss concerns, health issues, reports and assessments made by any professionals. The SENCO (Special Needs Co-Ordinator) will source resources and adapt the environment where necessary, as well as extra training if necessary. Parents are involved in all planning for their children's targets. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All parents have access to view their child's learning journals at any time. Parents are welcome to discuss their child's progress with their key person and SENCO to give updates and discuss the Assess, Plan, Do, Review (APDR) targets. Parents are involved in their children's SEN Support Plan. Termly reviews will be discussed with you. If needed children with additional needs maybe be allocated some one to one time with their key person to work on their targets, set by the SENCO or other professionals. Where more intervention is needed through a SEN Support plan or an Educational Health and Care plan, funding would be applied to support the child's needs. When necessary resources are sourced to support your child. All staff are aware of our confidential policy. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our setting is on one level although a ramp would be needed to access outside. We can adapt the room if required and we have a lovely big outside area for the children to explore. We support children by using visual timetables, picture exchange and Makaton. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We know that it is a big step for both parents and children to start in any setting and we want it to be as smooth as possible. Through meetings and planning, with you and your child, discussing your child's needs, skills and interests. We can be flexible on times, and help with visuals (pictures of staff and environment). We have good links with the schools and will make their transitions as smooth as possible, accompanying them on extra visits when necessary and transition meetings. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our SENCO and SENCO deputy, will continue attending the termly briefings and any other SEND updates and training available. In house training. (including makaton) Continue to source resources for support and child's interests. All staff are aware of the allergies of all the children in our care, and when required additional training can be completed.

name: Children and Young People's Mental Health Education
description: We work with children aged 4 to 18 years old in various settings, including: infant, primary and secondary schools, colleges, universities, youth clubs, and sports clubs. We also deliver sessions to adults, including teachers and parents, regarding their own mental wellbeing and that of the children they work with and look after. We deliver various educational sessions, including assemblies, workshops, and full training days. Our team creates bespoke training to suit individual school needs, from a one-hour workshop focusing on anxiety, to a full day’s training on general mental health awareness and reducing stigma. We are keen to encourage children and young people to start the conversation around mental health and to teach them that it’s okay to open-up about the way they feel, in some cases preventing future mental ill-health. All sessions include engaging content that not only helps children and young people understand the definition of mental health but encourages discussion around it. The sessions also provide content to recognise signs of declining mental wellbeing, practical strategies that they can adopt and signposting of other organisations available that may help.

searchText:
name: Adult Counselling
description: We provide high-quality one-to-one counselling to adults with a variety of mental health needs. We can work with people who are experiencing anxiety, depression, loss, relationship issues, difficulties with anger, recovery from traumatic events, or are struggling to cope with the pressures of life. We can offer counselling to people over the age of 18. Our service may not be suitable for some people, but this will be decided between the counsellor and the individual during the initial appointment. Face-to-face and online appointments (using a secure link) are available. Our core purpose is to provide a confidential counselling service available to individuals regardless of age, gender, sexuality, disability, religion, or background. We are an independent service, operating separately from GPs and other Statutory Agencies. We will only report issues to other agencies if we have concerns about the safety of a service user or someone they tell us about. Individuals will be offered an initial appointment to ascertain that we are the right service for them. Following this, they will be provided weekly counselling sessions with their allocated counsellor. The duration of each session is 50 to 60 minutes. Please be aware that due to the high demand for this service, individuals may have to go onto a waiting list for their ongoing counselling to start. Our service is an organisational member of the British Association of Counselling and Psychotherapy, and our counsellors adhere to and work within the BACP Ethical Framework for the counselling professions.

local_offer: Here at Green Ridge, we pride ourselves on being a highly inclusive school. We believe that each pupil has individual and unique needs. However, some pupils require more support than others to achieve well. We acknowledge that a significant proportion of pupils will have Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEN/D) at some time in their school career. Many of these pupils may require help throughout their time in school, while others may need a little extra support for a short period of time to help them overcome more temporary needs. https://www.greenridgeacademy.co.uk/policies/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? If pupils are to achieve their full potential, we must recognise this and plan accordingly. Our school aims to provide all pupils with strategies for dealing with their needs in a supportive environment, and to give them meaningful access to the National Curriculum. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Within the academy we have access to a range of support and advice for specialist SENCo children. Within our setting we have children with a range of needs and regularly have professionals come into the school to support our staff in how to meet the children's needs in the classroom. We also have teaching assistants who are trained to work with individuals and small groups to support social and emotional aspects of development The SENCo deploys support staff based on skills and experiences which best benefit the children with individual needs How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Green Ridge, we operate an open-door policy, welcoming parents to contact the school office to arrange a meeting with the SENCo and/or their child’s class teacher to discuss any concerns. Parents also have online access to their child’s Learning Plans, which are updated termly to ensure transparency and collaboration. In addition, we host termly SEND Coffee Mornings where parents and carers can meet with staff and hear from Local Authority specialists who share their expertise. We also offer ‘Stay and Learn’ sessions, inviting parents into the classroom to observe and participate in their child’s learning. To further support families, we provide practical workshops designed to help parents address challenges they may face at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Most children with SEND have a Learning Plan that outlines their individual strengths and areas of difficulty, along with short-term SMART targets to support their progress. These plans are reviewed termly by the class teacher and shared with parents via our secure online platform. For children with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), we hold an Annual Review meeting to update the plan, celebrate achievements, and set new goals in collaboration with parents and professionals. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Green Ridge is built on one level and is accessible for all where there are steps/ ramps in place should they be needed for access. The academy has several wide disabled toilets for pupil/adult use. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? name: Citizens Advice Bucks
description: We are your local advice charity offering expert, independent advice. Our services are free and we are completely confidential. We work for you and only you. We offer quality checked and up to date advice on debt, benefits, housing, employment, immigration, and consumer issues as well as other areas. This is a free and strictly confidential service. We have availability for face to face appointments in our Aylesbury, Buckingham, Chesham, and High Wycombe offices. These appointments are currently open to those with priority needs and will be offered to those who will benefit from seeing one of our advisers in person. If you need some advice please call our Bucks Adviceline or use our contact form. If we think you need a face to face appointment we will arrange this with you. Our reception doors are open during the following times for handing in of documents: Aylesbury; Monday, Wednesday and Friday 10am to 2pm Buckingham: Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday 10am to 3pm Chesham: Tuesday 09:30am to 12:30pm and 1:30 to 4:30pm High Wycombe: Thursday 10:30am to 1pm. Important Notice: Crisis Support If you are in crisis, we will do our best to support you immediately or arrange a call back as soon as possible. If your issue falls outside our scope, we will signpost you to an alternative organisation that can help.
organisation: Citizens Advice Bucks Citizens Advice provides a free, confidential, impartial and independent service available to all in the community. Staff are fully trained and can advise on a wide range of issues including managing money and debt; benefits; housing; employment; relationship breakdown; immigration and legal rights. Call our national phone line You can contact an adviser through our national phone service, Adviceline: Adviceline or Textphone Adviceline is available 9am to 5pm, Monday to Friday. It’s usually busiest at the beginning and end of the day. It's not available on public holidays. If you call from a mobile, we’ll ask you to enter a local landline number on your keypad. This can be any number - we only use it to send your call to a local adviser if one’s available. There are a few parts of England we don’t cover yet. If you’re in one of these areas, we’ll give you other options when you call. We’ll answer as soon as we can - at busy times you might need to wait up to an hour. If the wait is long, we’ll tell you about other ways to get advice. You can also try calling again later. Calls cost the same as calls to landline numbers. See more about our call charges. Talk to us online Chat lets you talk to a trained adviser online. You can: talk to us about a debt problem - we can usually help between 8am and 7pm, Monday to Friday talk to us about any other kind of problem - we can usually help between 10am and 4pm, Monday to Friday Spare time? The Citizens Advice is always looking for new volunteers. If you are interested in gaining new skills and contributing to this valuable work, go to “Volunteering with the Citizens Advice network”.  https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/

local_offer: Castlefield Family Hub offers universal and specialised support to families. We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. Castlefield Family Hub can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We offer universal and specialised support to families in the local area. We work closely with partners, such as the Health Team and local Early Years settings and schools, to ensure that we are meeting the needs of the children in our local community. We can offer particular support to children with additional needs and/or disabilities and their families. Our provision provides support services for all families with children aged 0 to 19 years and up to 25 years for those with a SEND. Our aims are to improve parenting, health, and children’s development and to provide a safe and stimulating environment for children, young people, and their families to flourish, develop and learn. Parents provided with good information so they can make decisions, which will have a significant effect on their children’s life chances. Parents to know, what support and services are available to help them bring up their children, and how to access them. Families signposted into support as appropriate feel confident to provide good life chance for their children. Children to develop social skills in preparation for starting pre-school, nursery or school. Children to enjoy a variety of fun activities and play and learn through this participation. Parents to feel confident in parenting and picking up parenting skills and support through attendance. Personal, Social and Emotional Development. Physical development. Communication and Language Development. Outreach support, action plan to specifically help the family with individual needs. Emotional and practical support from Outreach Workers. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Safeguarding First Aid Early Language Development Programme Hey Programme (Healthy Eating in Young Children) How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?  How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We welcome all families to all of our services, staff are dedicated to supporting families using our Hub and its services. Our building is fully compliant with the disability requirements. We provide a warm, welcoming and fun learning environment for children and their families. Large and inviting outdoor play environment Sensory equipment available during sessions Accessible toilets How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Families can attend our services and register by completing a Family Hub Membership form. Outreach support can be provided by self-referral or by referral from a health visitor or other professional. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?

name: Voluntary Transport - Home to Health
description: Wye Valley Volunteers offers a service in which volunteers use their own cars to drive clients to medical appointments such as to hospitals, GP surgeries and dentists. We help those who would have difficulty in getting around independently, whether through age, infirmity or other needs. We maintain a team of 40 plus drivers who cheerfully undertake these trips and find pleasure themselves in relating to clients. If you need transport for a medical, or medically related, appointment, you should contact the team at the office with the full details including the date, location of your appointment, as well as your full name, address and telephone number. local_offer: All children new to this setting are assessed to give a starting point to see individual progression. I have extensive knowledge of child development. This has been gained through training and via 40 years of working in childcare in a variety of settings. Any concerns I may have will be discussed with the parents and any further advice and support, with parental permission, would be sought from professionals.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? All registered childminders have a key contact within the Early Years Service and, from this contact, advice and information can be accessed. They can also answer questions and offer advice on other appropriate services. Professionals are very welcome to meet the child at this setting if that is desired. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Autism and Play, completed September 2010 Supporting children with speech, language and communication needs, completed February 2015 Supporting children's emotional well-being, completed March 2015 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I work in partnership with parents and share information about their child's/children's development and progress. This is done regularly in an agreed way to suit the parents. I ask parents to share information regarding their child's likes and dislikes, activities that they enjoy the most and those they may be having difficulty with. This information is used when planning activities and to offer support so that children may reach their potential within this setting. I share ideas with parents for use at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I observe and assess all children in my care. Where a need is identified I support the parent/parents with preparing and implementation of a joint action plan for their child . If appropriate, and with parental permission, other agencies may be involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? This setting is accessible to most children. Steps lead from street level to the front door. These steps are wide and can accommodate prams, pushchairs and wheelchairs. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I have formed links with local pre schools and schools and we work together to support children through transition. I am happy for practitioners from other settings to contact me. I encourage parents to make use of settling in sessions for their children. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am aware of the need for flexibility within this setting to ensure that all children reach their full potential and that all their needs can be met. I keep updated with new guidance from the Local Authority and use their website regularly. I acknowledge the need for training where appropriate.

name: Tots Go Wild at Black Park
description: Explore and get messy at Black Park Forest School-style sessions aimed at 1 to 5 years olds (from when they can walk independently until they are in full-time education). Join us in Black Pines Camp for some fun in the woods. We have a variety of activities for your Tot to go wild, including the mud kitchen, digging pit, water play, bug hunting, weaving, balancing, and more. Each week, there will be a themed activity, plus multiple other activity stations. The sessions are child-led, with the children being encouraged to choose what they would like to do to help them build on their self-esteem, confidence and independence. Tots Go Wild sessions take place on most Fridays during term time throughout the year and run from 10:00 am to 11:30 am and 1 pm to 2:30 pm. We stagger the release of our tickets in line with the start of each new school term. You can casually book the date(s) you'd like to attend, or block book the full half-term to guarantee a place each week and receive a discount. We go ahead in all weathers - unless deemed unsafe - so please dress appropriately. Please note that all children must be accompanied by an adult at all times. £7.50 per child (plus booking fee). There is no charge for accompanying adults. Please note pay and display parking charges apply at Black Park.
organisation: Buckinghamshire Country Parks Black Park has 530 acres of attractive woodland, grassland and heathland with a centre-piece lake. SSSI heath land and Local Nature Reserve. It has miles of surfaced tracks and woodland trails through the woods; tarmac path around the lake with seating every 100m; lakeside cafe and toilets; orienteering course and children's woodland play area. Picnicking is welcome but not fires or BBQs. Dogs are welcome but must be kept under control. Go Ape hire wire adventure course We host a range of events throughout the year for children and adults. This includes open air cinemas, trails, forest school and much more! For events please check out our Facebook page. Black Park has achieved the Green Flag Award which recognises quality green space in the UK. countryparks@buckinghamshire.gov.uk https://www.buckscc.gov.uk/services/culture-and-leisure/country-parks/black-park/

name: Thames Valley Autism Alert Card
description: The aim of the Thames Valley Autism Alert Card scheme is to provide a simple way for autistic people, or their parent or carer, to quickly and easily explain their condition to others, giving cardholders more confidence to go out and about. Autism Berkshire issues the Alert Card free of charge to anyone with a diagnosis of autism in Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire, and Milton Keynes. The card is intended to be shown if the cardholder finds themselves in a situation where they cannot easily explain their behaviour to people around them or to the emergency services and when they may need assistance, such as at hospitals, in shops or on public transport. Along with simple advice about autism spectrum conditions, the card gives the cardholder’s name and details of two emergency contacts, such as parents or carers, so that those shown the card understand they are dealing with an autistic person and find out what they can do to help them.

We are dedicated to offering high-quality, personalised tuition and alternative provision to students of all ages, with a focus on delivering exceptional face-to-face and online learning experiences.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our work aims to help students to engage with learning and academia, by creating a customised learning plan for each lesson for each student. We focus on fostering a healthy attitude to learning and personal development in our students. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All our educators have a wealth of experience working with a range of special educational needs and disabilities. They receive regular, needs-specific, training to ensure they are at the forefront of support techniques for students. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? When working with learners, we understand that we're working with families, not just students. Parents are involved in target setting, support, and creating a healthy learning environment. We provide lesson-by-lesson feedback of progress to parents. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Each lesson we note topics, understanding, breakthrough moments, key challenges, attitude, and behaviour. This is fed back to parents to keep them engaged on their child's progress. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We offer flexible provision that be made accessible to any student. Whether at home, online, or in school, we have customised resources for each learner. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? If you'd like academic support for your child, reach out to us by email, phone, or on our website. We'll work with you to arrange student-specific support. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? In the future, we aim to open an accessible learning centre that can provide classroom and 1:1 environments for any SEND student.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I am planning to Enrol in behaviour management,Speech and language trainings. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with us. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a couple of steps leading to the back door but easy access via a front entrance. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools, and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

name: Family Rights Group
description: Family Rights Group promotes policies and practices that keep children safe within their family and strengthen the family and community networks of those children who cannot live at home. We campaign for families to have their voice heard, be treated fairly, and get help early to prevent problems escalating. We are a national charity that advises parents, grandparents, relatives, and friends about their rights and options when social workers or courts make decisions about their children’s welfare. We work with parents whose children are in need, at risk, or are in the care system and with wider family members and friends who are raising children (known as kinship carers). Online advice service: Visit our website for easy-to-follow, online advice. Features include an A to Z, Frequently Asked Questions, films, ‘top tips’, and legal advice sheets. You may also want to visit our advice forums, where parents and kinship carers (also known as family and friends carers) can get legal and practical advice on the child welfare system. Call our Freephone Telephone Advice Line Monday to Friday.

Our mission is to enhance The Chiltern's habitats through conservation, education and community engagement. We do this by helping people to work together outdoors on a range of sites within the Chilterns to restore habitats and improve the biodiversity of the area. This is all achieved with the help of volunteers of all ages, abilities and backgrounds, plus community organisations, charities, social enterprises, schools, colleges and other partners all have key roles too. local_offer: At Chalfont St Giles Village School children are identified as having SEND through a variety of ways including: • Liaison with Early Years settings • Liaison with feeder schools • Child performing below age expectations or not making expected progress relevant to their starting points • Where progress is limited, despite Quality First Teaching and Intervention • Concerns raised by parents • Concerns raised by the class teacher • Liaison with external agencies • Medical diagnosis If a special need is suspected, the class teacher plans suitable interventions with advice from the SENDCo and outside agencies as appropriate. Parents and carers are always informed of interventions taking place, both as part of the identification process and once a special need has been identified. If the response to the interventions is poor and the progress made continues to be limited, the child is placed on the schools SEND register. Parents are informed of this. Children identified as having SEND access additional intervention which is planned and evaluated by the class teacher. The SENDCo oversees the provision, monitors its effectiveness and advises the class teacher. Progress against targets is measured and discussed termly by staff and parents and where appropriate, outside agencies. local_offer: CSG Playgroup is a mainstream setting. We are, however, a wholly inclusive playgroup. All children are given equal opportunities to participate in all our activities, regardless of any additional needs they may have. We aim to remove barriers to learning and support personal and academic growth. We believe in providing every possible opportunity to develop the full potential of all children so that all children are valued and their self-esteem promoted.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? -two level 3 qualified practitioners and one level 2 -SENDCO liaison What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Tracey has recently attended SENCO Training a 2 day training course for Nominate New and Aspiring SENCOs. Tracey will also attend regular SENCO liaison meetings. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are involved as part of the committee. The Pre-School Trustees and Committee have the overall responsibility for ensuring that it runs successfully in accordance with its aims. The Committee is formed at the Annual General Meeting (usually September) of parents of Pre-School children and meets once every half-term with the Pre-School Leader and Deputy. We also regularly involve parents in our fundraising events, and we are always looking for parent volunteers. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We use Tapestry to share information with parents on progress and day to day life at playgroup. This includes a progress tracker and daily photos and notes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The setting is primarily flat and accessible however, we do have 2 low steps into the main building and a step running alongside our main building which would not be accessible. We share our facility with the cricket club any adaptations need to go to their committee meeting. General outdoor setting is accessible which is where most of the daily activities are set up. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We work very closely with CSG nursery school to ensure a smooth transition to school. We also work on routines and structure as part of the pre-school day. We work closely with our parents to ensure that the transition to pre-school from home is smooth and we offer flexibility in terms of the settling in time scale. There isn't a one size fits all approach. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are currently looking into viable resources to promote any SEND.

name: Speen Playing Fields
description: Speen has two playing fields the main Playing Field located in the centre of the village behind the King William IV (ex) pub and Ridgley’s Field which is accessed from Moses Plat Lane. We are very proud of our playing fields. They provide vital open spaces in our village for people to use for recreation, sports and family fun and are a focal point for many of our community activities such as the village fete, FunDay, Bonfire Night, and the bi-annual Speen Festival. Speen Playing fields are held in charitable trust for the benefit of the community, are managed by a committee of volunteers and supported through grant aid and fund raising. We rely on charitable donations to maintain our playing fields and to purchase new equipment. The maintenance and upkeep of the fields is also a community activity with many villagers helping out on our Spring and Autumn work parties carrying out maintenance jobs and installing new play equipment. These work parties are a fun community activity where we cut back trees and hedges, repair equipment, fix the pavilion, and complete other miscellaneous jobs. Outside of these work parties we invite those who may wish to help with maintenance to choose an activity from our maintenance list to carry out alone or with neighbours in their own time. This playing field is a dog-free area.

name: Domestic Abuse App: Bright Sky
description: If you are concerned about domestic abuse, we know it can be hard to find support. That’s why Bright Sky was developed. Bright Sky is a safe, easy-to-use app and website that provides practical support and information on how to respond to domestic abuse. It is for anyone experiencing domestic abuse, or who is worried about someone else. Bright Sky helps you to spot the signs of abuse, know how to respond, and help someone find a safe route to support. Download Bright Sky today because you never know when you might need it to save someone’s life. The app can be downloaded for free via the app stores. Please only download the app if it is safe for you to do so and if you are sure that your phone isn’t being monitored. Launched in partnership with Vodafone Foundation and Thames Valley Partnership, the app hosts a UK-wide directory of specialist support service and offers users assessment tools to help you spot the signs for someone experiencing domestic abuse. It has had over 80,000 downloads since its launch in 2018. The website is focused on how to spot the signs of domestic abuse, advice on how to support someone you have concerns for, and ways to find help. Features: The app is available in 5 languages: English, Urdu, Punjabi, Polish, and Welsh. A unique UK-wide directory of specialist domestic abuse support services with contact details. Content to help you understand if you or someone else is at risk. Links to further resources and information on domestic abuse. Information to help you to stay safe online. If you are in immediate danger, always call the police on 999.

name: Savera UK
description: Savera UK is one of the leading charities tackling 'honour'-based abuse and harmful practices in the UK. It campaigns to eliminate harmful practices, including forced marriage, female genital mutilation, virginity testing and breast ironing. The organisation provides life-saving services to those at risk, regardless of age, culture, sexuality or gender. ‘Savera’ means ‘new beginning’ in Hindi, a theme that is symbolic of the support the charity provides to those who are at risk of harmful practices. Since launching its one-to-one service in 2017, Savera UK has helped hundreds of clients out of abusive environments into their ‘Savera’. We help survivors of ‘honour’-based abuse and harmful practices to rebuild their lives with safeguarding and advocacy, helping them to gain economic independence and move forward into their future with confidence. Savera UK campaigns to eliminate harmful practices by raising awareness. The charity speaks out to challenge harmful attitudes, prejudice and practices that violate individual human rights and educate and empower others so they can join our fight. We contribute to research, provide consultancy and deliver training to raise awareness of harmful practices and their signs among people outside of at-risk communities. We also campaign to encourage everyone to recognise and report instances of 'honour'-based abuse and harmful practices.

We welcome all children and their families and will make all reasonable adjustments to ensure their needs are met. We are a small friendly Montessori setting and pride ourselves on our personal approach. We aim to build positive relationships with children, their families and any professionals who are needed to support their development. We encourage parents to be fully involved with their children's success. We have high aspirations for all the children in our setting and aim to work together with parents to support each child in their personal journey. At Chalfont St Peter Montessori School we treat each child as an individual. Your child will be allocated a key person who will be responsible for your child's development and care. Through on-going observations, monitoring and assessment we are able to identify any concerns which we will share with you.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The Principal and SENCO Support have experience of working with children with SEND. We aim to provide the individual support required to ensure each child can access the full curriculum. We regularly liaise with professionals from the Integrated SEND Service, Speech and Language Therapists, Occupational Therapists and Paediatricians. We attend the Early Years SENCO liaison groups What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? SENCO: F Bullivant June 2017, R Shah May 2016, J McCarthy Feb 2025 LEADING BEHAVIOUR: J McCarthy May 2017. UNDERSTANDING BEHAVIOUR: J McCarthy Mar 2019, F Bullivant May 2021, R Shah June 2020, F Jammoul May 2025, C Rogers June 2025, J Burridge July 25 NAS EARLYBIRD (AUTISM): J McCarthy June 2018, F Bullivant June 2017 SEND CODE OF PRACTICE: F Bullivant May 2019, J McCarthy Mar 2019, R Shah Mar 2020. SUPPORTING CHILDREN WITH SEND: J McCarthy June 2019, F Bullivant Mar 2019, R Shah Apr 2020. SPEECH, LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION: J McCarthy Sept 2019, F Bullivant Aug 2019, R Shah Aug 2019 MAKATON INTRODUCTION J McCarthy, F Bullivant, R Shah, J Burridge How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents into our setting to discuss their child's progress and any concerns they have. We also have regular parent events, for example parent's breakfast, reading sessions. Parents can request a meeting with their child's key person, the Principal or Deputy Principal at any time. We use Tapestry to share regular observations and photographs about a child's learning journey. We also encourage parents to use the Tapestry App to share news and activities their child has been enjoying at home. To support the children's learning at home we also share videos of Montessori activities which can be replicated at home and Home to School learning resources. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The above opportunities are available for all parents, carers and family members. In addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to work with parents of children with SEND. We offer a range of options including home visits, frequent settling in sessions, shortened sessions and social stories to support the child. When the child is moving on to Primary school we offer accompanied transition visits to their next school and we invite future teachers to our school to meet the child. We also have a Time to Say Goodbye booklet to assist parents in preparing their child for the next steps. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? name: Early Intervention, The Pace Centre
description: Our expert team of children’s therapists offer advice, support, assessment and practical help for babies and children with developmental delay. The reason for the delay may be unknown but we have experience in working with children who have been born prematurely or have a neuro-disability such as cerebral palsy. We can provide a comprehensive assessment of your child’s strengths and challenges and provide family centred therapy to support your child’s development. Therapists work with children and families to develop a therapy plan to help children to achieve their full potential. We support also support parents to increase their knowledge and skill. Our team include specialists in paediatric: occupational therapy physiotherapy speech and language therapy conductive education We help with movement skills, sensory needs, communication, attachment, self-soothing and regulation, feeding, sleep, play and learning skills. Therapy can be delivered directly at our therapy centre or remotely using teletherapy (video calls).
organisation: The PACE Centre Pace is a family centred school that specialises in educating children with Cerebral Palsy and related disorders. Pace provide an innovative education tailored to the child’s individual abilities setting and achieving academic and functional goals. Due to the complex nature of many Pace children, Pace also has an on site nursing team. Our unique Pace approach brings together input from paediatric occupational therapists, physiotherapists, speech and language therapists, conductive educationalists and teachers. This breadth of expertise means your “whole child” remains at the centre of their education. At Pace we believe in every child’s ability to achieve and progress, and it is our job to ensure that children have the right skills to do just that. A bespoke curriculum is developed for each child, at a just right level to ensure they are challenged and make progress functionally and academically. The differentiated delivery by class and the tailored learning by individuals means the curriculum is rich, and the range of methodology in toolkit for delivery adds real depth and value to the learning experience. Pace School is a nurturing, positive total communication environment that empowers the children to demonstrate knowledge, access and engage in their education. We celebrate success with your child, their class and with you. The principal of which is that recognised achievement is motivational, as such the children continue to progress. Our early years' group includes our nursery age children, early therapeutic intervention is combined with The Early Years Foundation Curriculum, to provide a unique approach for children aged 2 to 5 with sensory-motor challenges. Focusing on the development of fundamental skills the children need to access and engage with their education. Our Key Stage one and two groups cater for a range of both physical and cognitive abilities from very complex challenges relating to their sensory-motor difficulties, to children who have mild to moderate physical difficulties and related learning needs. Key Stages three and four benefit from a highly personalised functional and life skills-based curriculum to help prepare them for their future lives as young adults in the community. There are opportunities to develop and apply their problem solving and academic skills, for example through purposeful trips to the supermarket followed by cooking activities, which have been carefully planned to work on particular gross/fine motor and mathematical skills. We operate from two sites: The Bradbury Campus, Wendover Road, Stoke Mandeville, which offers the following educational services:- School Service: Key Stage 3 and 4 Secondary Services for young people aged 11 to 16 who have motor disorders and related challenges such as sensory impairments and communication difficulties. Coventon Road, Aylesbury, offers the following services:- Primary School Services for children aged 5 to 11 who have motor disorders and related challenges such as sensory impairments and communication difficulties. Early Years Services for children aged 3 to 5 years who have learning challenges as above, related to a motor disorder. Children may attend full-time or part-time with dual placements and outreach support available. In both centres, we provide a full assessment and reporting service carried out by a highly trained and experienced trans-disciplinary paediatric team which includes: Occupational Therapists Physiotherapists Speech and Language Therapists Conductors (professionals specially trained in working with people with movement disorders such as cerebral palsy) Early Years Professionals Special Needs Teachers Many of our staff are able to use British sign language and are experienced in supporting children with complex communication difficulties through the use of augmentative and alternative communication strategies. Across the entire range of our services we also offer advice for further input, provision and equipment needs; family and carer training; counselling; a family residential programme and home visits. All our facilities are purpose-built and fully accessible. Pace has a very strong partnership with parents and families facilitated by the Pace Parent Partnership (PPP) which meets regularly and provides support, advice and social opportunities for both children and families. info@thepacecentre.org https://www.thepacecentre.org/

name: Charlie's Gift
description: Charlie’s Gift is a local based charity, which provides grants of money to support children 0 to 18 years who face challenges in life because of health issues, special needs, bereavement, or poverty. The aim of the charity is to lend a financial helping hand to children whose lives are touched by adversity, living within Hertfordshire, Bedfordshire, and Buckinghamshire. The hope is that the grants of money will make a positive impact on these children’s lives by helping to make life a little happier and a little easier for them. What can you apply for: Requests for grants must be of clear and direct benefit to the child. Examples may include funding for a specialised piece of equipment (medical, educational, or recreational) for use solely by the child, specialised training for family members to better support their child, help with medical treatment costs, or residential trips and days out or holidays. Please note: they do not provide grants for white goods (large domestic electrical items such as fridges or washing machines), or general home renovations. Who can apply for a grant: Individual: Applications for grants of money can be made on behalf of individual children by a parent or guardian, or by a Health, Educational, Social, or Welfare professional. Applicants should have direct contact or be working with the child on a regular basis. Organisations and Charities: Organisations and Charities can also apply for a grant from Charlie’s Gift. Such organisations should be working with children up to the age of 18 years and be operating out of Hertfordshire, Bedfordshire, or Buckinghamshire. The applicant should either be a Trustee or a person in a position of leadership within your charity or organisation.

What can you apply for: Requests for grants must be of clear and direct benefit to the child. Examples may include funding for a specialised piece of equipment (medical, educational, or recreational) for use solely by the child, specialised training for family members to better support their child, help with medical treatment costs, or residential trips and days out or holidays. Please note: they do not provide grants for white goods (large domestic electrical items such as fridges or washing machines), or general home renovations. Who can apply for a grant: Individual: Applications for grants of money can be made on behalf of individual children by a parent or guardian, or by a Health, Educational, Social, or Welfare professional. Applicants should have direct contact or be working with the child on a regular basis. Organisations and Charities: Organisations and Charities can also apply for a grant from Charlie’s Gift. Such organisations should be working with children up to the age of 18 years and be operating out of Hertfordshire, Bedfordshire, or Buckinghamshire. The applicant should either be a Trustee or a person in a position of leadership within your charity or organisation.

My aim for your child/children is to look after their needs and fill their day with fun whilst being in a secure safe environment, working with in the EYFS framework, which will enhance your child's development needs. Food can be provided which will be healthy and nutritious, but if you would like to provide your own or if your child has allergies then I am more than happy to meet you and your child's individual needs. A child who is unhappy or tense will not learn or be able to play properly, so it is very important for yourself and I to work together to help the child feel confident and secure. I will update you every evening on collection on how we have filled our day and how your child has been. This will be verbal as I feel and believe you will agree that my time is best spent encouraging and stimulating your child. In order to feel free to explore and experiment with all kinds of materials, I would like to suggest that simple clothing to be worn. This will also enable them to move freely not only playing but whilst potty training if they are at that stage, also this will help them to become more independent.

local_offer: I am a childminder who offers a nice home, for children to be nurtured, to learn and grow in a safe and caring environment. Although I have no children with SEND needs in my setting at this time. I would be happy to accommodate any child whatever their needs. I want all children to be included, happy and catered for in my care. In the past, I have had some experience caring for children with autism and hearing difficulties.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I welcome any child to my setting, support and encourage them to reach their full potential. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have done training for autism and ADHD in the past and hope to do more soon. If I had a child with SEND I would go on the correct training for the particular area I need to. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I would work in partnership with the parents frequently. Verbally or by email have a folder on their child and have regular meetings to discuss any concerns or changes. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As above, I would chat or send emails to parents and have regular meetings so we can all be on the same side and we all have the information we need. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? At this time my house and garden are reasonably accessible to all children. there is a small step on the front and back doors and three steps in the garden. I would be happy to adapt my setting and put the necessary ramps etc in place if needed. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? On first contact, I would arrange for the family to come and visit and find out what needs they require. I always get the parents to go through my welcome pack and fill in the paperwork before their child comes to me. I allow the children to have a few settling-in visits before they start properly. They fill in an 'All about me' form before coming. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I need to revisit my training and adapt my home/garden when I find out the needs for the child.

description: Hope Tots is a referral only group that runs during term time. The sessions are focused on the early years foundation stage and how to best support your children with their early years development. We base the programme on each child's individual needs using activities that support the 3 key prime areas. Hope Tots is located in Hope Place, a lovely, peaceful dedicated Early Years room, fully equipped with lots of fun toys and different areas for sensory, messy, and imaginative play, indoors and out. Parents attending Hope Tots will find support and encouragement throughout the often overwhelming journey of parenthood. We run various other courses which you will have access to here at Restore Hope. We run an exciting programme using the beautiful grounds at Restore Hope, enjoying Gruffalo walks, bear hunts, teddy bear picnics, nature crafts, and much more. Restore Hope is a Christian charity offering a wide range of family support services. There is a minibus pickup service available in the local area (Little Chalfont/Amersham/Chesham).
organisation: Restore Hope Restore Hope Latimer is a family focused charity based at Latimer Park. A special space in the countryside set in the heart of the Chilterns, just outside Amersham and Chesham and has been operating since 2002 and has a proven record of bringing change and help to people in need. We believe in the value of healthy, happy and stable families. We also believe that no matter how bad a situation may seem there is always hope. Our vision is therefore that every struggling family in the Chilterns finds help and hope for the future. This is clearly a big aim and one that requires us to continually increase our influence, effectiveness and reputation. We aim to achieve our vision by advancing and developing the programmes that we offer and continually looking for ways to engage with those most in need. We operate a clear strategy, with deliberate focus and dogged determination. We empower and equip key volunteers to lead various elements of our work, and support a motivated core staff team. RHL seeks to make best use of the fantastic facilities that Latimer Park offers and, where appropriate, grows into other spaces in the community to offer easy access to our programmes and to further develop the reputation of the charity. naomi.meech@restorehopelatimer.org http://www.restorehopelatimer.org

name: Helping Hands - Support with Food, Bills and Finances
description: Our Helping Hand team are available to help individuals or families in need, those on low incomes and those who are experiencing a financial emergency or crisis. Let us know if you are struggling to afford food, you cannot keep on top of your bills, you are in debt, you are struggling to pay for essential goods in your home. Help with food - If you are struggling to afford or access food, our team can give support and make referrals on your behalf to a local food bank. Help with fuel and household bills - If you are struggling to top up your pre-payment meter or pay your energy costs to keep your home warm, we can discuss the options available to you and help you apply for grants from third party organisations. We may also be able to help with any other essential bills. Help with essential items for your home - If you need help with essential furniture, we can explore the best support for you. Some external charities can help with essential furniture if you are on a low income. Whether you get in contact by phone or the online form, we will ask you a few questions about your situation so that we can offer the best support or advice.

organisation: Marsworth CE Infant School Our school was founded in 1841 and caters for all children from the age of 4 to 7. All children can start in the term after they are four, either part-time or full time depending on parental choice. Our classes are organised into Nursery and Reception, and Year one and two, Our teachers are skilled at planning for mixed-age classes and children work to their ability not necessarily their age. We have a very high staff pupil ratio to ensure all children are supported in their learning. Our school consists of two main classrooms, and a well-equipped library. We have recently extended our facilities by building a large resources/dining room to the rear of our school and a canopy outside Class one. Outdoors the school has a large secure all-weather playground and a large grassy play area. These contain some great facilities for playtimes like the chalet, wildlife area and children's garden, adventure trail, play panels and a wooden train. Unusually for a small village school, there is weekly access to all year round swimming lessons and sports facilities. We also have a French club, Yoga club and a visiting football/athletics coach which are held during lunchtimes. office@marsworth.bucks.sch.uk https://www.marsworthschool.co.uk/

name: Therapy for Mainstream Primary School Children, The Pace Centre
description: Our therapy team at Pace can offer assessment, therapy, and advice for children aged between 3 and 11 who attend mainstream schools who have challenges in the following areas Dyspraxia, developmental coordination disorder Sensory processing Attention and Regulation Fine motor skills Gross motor skills Handwriting Social emotional Therapists work with children, school and families to develop a therapy plan to help a child, young person to achieve their full potential. We also support parents and school to increase their knowledge and skills through training. Our teams include specialists in paediatric: occupational therapy physiotherapy speech and language therapy conductive education Therapy can be delivered directly at our therapy centre, in school or remotely using teletherapy (video calls) .
organisation: The PACE Centre Pace is a family centred school that specialises in educating children with Cerebral Palsy and related disorders. Pace provide an innovative education tailored to the child’s individual abilities setting and achieving academic and functional goals. Due to the complex nature of many Pace children, Pace also has an on site nursing team. Our unique Pace approach brings together input from paediatric occupational therapists, physiotherapists, speech and language therapists, conductive educationalists and teachers. This breadth of expertise means your “whole child” remains at the centre of their education. At Pace we believe in every child’s ability to achieve and progress, and it is our job to ensure that children have the right skills to do just that. A bespoke curriculum is developed for each child, at a just right level to ensure they are challenged and make progress functionally and academically. The differentiated delivery by class and the tailored learning by individuals means the curriculum is rich, and the range of methodology in toolkit for delivery adds real depth and value to the learning experience. Pace School is a nurturing, positive total communication environment that empowers the children to demonstrate knowledge, access and engage in their education. We celebrate success with your child, their class and with you. The principal of which is that recognised achievement is motivational, as such the children continue to progress. Our early years' group includes our nursery age children, early therapeutic intervention is combined with The Early Years Foundation Curriculum, to provide a unique approach for children aged 2 to 5 with sensory-motor challenges. Focusing on the development of fundamental skills the children need to access and engage with their education. Our Key Stage one and two groups cater for a range of both physical and cognitive abilities from very complex challenges relating to their sensory-motor difficulties, to children who have mild to moderate physical difficulties and related learning needs. Key Stages three and four benefit from a highly personalised functional and life skills-based curriculum to help prepare them for their future lives as young adults in the community. There are opportunities to develop and apply their problem solving and academic skills, for example through purposeful trips to the supermarket followed by cooking activities, which have been carefully planned to work on particular gross/fine motor and mathematical skills. We operate from two sites: The Bradbury Campus, Wendover Road, Stoke Mandeville, which offers the following educational services:- School Service: Key Stage 3 and 4 Secondary Services for young people aged 11 to 16 who have motor disorders and related challenges such as sensory impairments and communication difficulties. Coventon Road, Aylesbury, offers the following services:- Primary School Services for children aged 5 to 11 who have motor disorders and related challenges such as sensory impairments and communication difficulties. Early Years Services for children aged 3 to 5 years who have learning challenges as above, related to a motor disorder. Children may attend full-time or part-time with dual placements and outreach support available. In both centres, we provide a full assessment and reporting service carried out by a highly trained and experienced trans-disciplinary paediatric team which includes: Occupational Therapists Physiotherapists Speech and Language Therapists Conductors (professionals specially trained in working with people with movement disorders such as cerebral palsy) Early Years Professionals Special Needs Teachers Many of our staff are able to use British sign language and are experienced in supporting children with complex communication difficulties through the use of augmentative and alternative communication strategies. Across the entire range of our services we also offer advice for further input, provision and equipment needs; family and carer training; counselling; a family residential programme and home visits. All our facilities are purpose-built and fully accessible. Pace has a very strong partnership with parents and families facilitated by the Pace Parent Partnership (PPP) which meets regularly and provides support, advice and social opportunities for both children and families. info@thepacecentre.org https://www.thepacecentre.org/
