name: Therapy for Children with Neuro-Motor Disabilities, The Pace Centre
description: Therapy for children with neuro-motor disabilities ages 3 to 18 years at The Pace Centre in Aylesbury. Our expert team of children’s therapists offer advice, support, assessment, and practical help for children and young people with neuro motor disabilities for example, cerebral palsy. This may include therapy for: Rehabilitation following surgical procedures for example Selective Dorsal Rhizotomy (SDR), orthopaedic surgery Gross motor skills Postural assessment Fine motor skills: bimanual, constraint induced movement therapy Alternative communication for example switching eye gaze Sensory processing Our teams include specialists in paediatric: Occupational therapy Physiotherapy Speech and Language therapy Conductive education Therapist work with the child’s existing therapy team to work on joint targets. Therapy can be delivered directly at our therapy centre or, in some cases, remotely using teletherapy (video calls).
organisation: The PACE Centre Pace is a family centred school that specialises in educating children with Cerebral Palsy and related disorders. Pace provide an innovative education tailored to the child’s individual abilities setting and achieving academic and functional goals. Due to the complex nature of many Pace children, Pace also has an on site nursing team. Our unique Pace approach brings together input from paediatric occupational therapists, physiotherapists, speech and language therapists, conductive educationalists and teachers. This breadth of expertise means your “whole child” remains at the centre of their education. At Pace we believe in every child’s ability to achieve and progress, and it is our job to ensure that children have the right skills to do just that. A bespoke curriculum is developed for each child, at a just right level to ensure they are challenged and make progress functionally and academically. The differentiated delivery by class and the tailored learning by individuals means the curriculum is rich, and the range of methodology in toolkit for delivery adds real depth and value to the learning experience. Pace School is a nurturing, positive total communication environment that empowers the children to demonstrate knowledge, access and engage in their education. We celebrate success with your child, their class and with you. The principal of which is that recognised achievement is motivational, as such the children continue to progress. Our early years' group includes our nursery age children, early therapeutic intervention is combined with The Early Years Foundation Curriculum, to provide a unique approach for children aged 2 to 5 with sensory-motor challenges. Focusing on the development of fundamental skills the children need to access and engage with their education. Our Key Stage one and two groups cater for a range of both physical and cognitive abilities from very complex challenges relating to their sensory-motor difficulties, to children who have mild to moderate physical difficulties and related learning needs. Key Stages three and four benefit from a highly personalised functional and life skills-based curriculum to help prepare them for their future lives as young adults in the community. There are opportunities to develop and apply their problem solving and academic skills, for example through purposeful trips to the supermarket followed by cooking activities, which have been carefully planned to work on particular gross/fine motor and mathematical skills. We operate from two sites: The Bradbury Campus, Wendover Road, Stoke Mandeville, which offers the following educational services:- School Service: Key Stage 3 and 4 Secondary Services for young people aged 11 to 16 who have motor disorders and related challenges such as sensory impairments and communication difficulties. Coventon Road, Aylesbury, offers the following services:- Primary School Services for children aged 5 to 11 who have motor disorders and related challenges such as sensory impairments and communication difficulties. Early Years Services for children aged 3 to 5 years who have learning challenges as above, related to a motor disorder. Children may attend full-time or part-time with dual placements and outreach support available. In both centres, we provide a full assessment and reporting service carried out by a highly trained and experienced trans-disciplinary paediatric team which includes: Occupational Therapists Physiotherapists Speech and Language Therapists Conductors (professionals specially trained in working with people with movement disorders such as cerebral palsy) Early Years Professionals Special Needs Teachers Many of our staff are able to use British sign language and are experienced in supporting children with complex communication difficulties through the use of augmentative and alternative communication strategies. Across the entire range of our services we also offer advice for further input, provision and equipment needs; family and carer training; counselling; a family residential programme and home visits. All our facilities are purpose-built and fully accessible. Pace has a very strong partnership with parents and families facilitated by the Pace Parent Partnership (PPP) which meets regularly and provides support, advice and social opportunities for both children and families. info@thepacecentre.org https://www.thepacecentre.org/

local_offer: We are an inclusive football team and community network of SEN/disabled/autistic children and their parents. We offer an extracurricular opportunity for children, who may not otherwise get to take part in this kind of activity, to do exercise, have fun, learn a new skill, be part of a club and to make friends. It also offers the opportunity for their parents to connect with other parents and become part of a supportive and helpful community.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Our primary aim is for the young people to have fun, feel welcomed and included, and to take part in our football sessions in whatever way they can with no pressure. We want them to enjoy exercise and being active while learning to play football. Each session includes a range of activities including football skill drills, penalty shootouts, team games, play against the adults, friendlies against other inclusive teams and more. The young people can improve their self-esteem through the weekly improvements and achievements they see themselves making, inclusion in the weekly ‘match report’ club round-up WhatsApp message, and the awards at the end of the season which recognise everyone’s achievements. Parents are encouraged to join our WhatsApp group, which, as well as providing information on the weekly training sessions, is also a source of support and comfort to the parents. We regularly exchange information on SEN issues such as EHCPs and signposting to charities, as between us, we have a wealth of experience and knowledge to share. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our coaches (who are all parent volunteers) have all done their FA football training and this includes some information on football for young people with SEN. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We encourage parents to take part in the football sessions as much or as little as they want. It is also fine just to connect and chat with the other parents. We support them to train as a coach if appropriate and get even more involved. We sometimes play adult walking-football games. There are always opportunities to get involved behind the scenes, such as organising socials, should people wish. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We ask parents/carers to stay with their children so they will be able to witness the progress for themselves and parents/carers are always welcome to chat to any of the coaches informally. All children get recognition at an end of season awards ceremony. This club is only for SEND children and their siblings/friends. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We play at two different locations (winter astro pitch and grass pitches the rest of the year). Both locations have parking on site. The grass pitches have level access from the car park. The astro pitch is up a couple of stairs so wouldn’t be completely accessible, but this is only used for 8 weeks of the year. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Just give us a ring (Call Frank) and then come down one Saturday morning and give it a try to see if you like it – or give it a few tries to be sure and to settle in your child gradually. Everyone is welcome and the sessions are free. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? The club has already developed significantly from a small start of 4 or 5 families we now have approximately 40 children on our books. We are always trying new things and getting more funding to provide free kits for the players among other things. We are advertising in local schools and on social media in order to find others who may benefit from our club. We will aim to have more parents train as coaches to split into smaller training sessions as we grow further.

local_offer: Chepping View follow the graduated approach to supporting children with SEN. The SEN information report shows the type of provision (interventions and support) that is provided at Chepping View. https://www.cheppingviewprimaryacademy.org/Office/Legal-Information/ What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? ‘Everybody Matters at Chepping View’ underpins the school’s culture and behaviour. We therefore have the highest expectations of all our children and aim to reduce and remove inequalities and barriers that already exist so that all our children can reach their full potential academically, socially and emotionally. We foster positive attitudes, relationships and a shared sense of belonging. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? The Academy's arrangement for training staff in relation to pupils with SEND is: • Whole staff in-service training sessions are arranged as appropriate, in response to particular needs within the school. • Reading and discussion of relevant documentation and keeping up to date with DfE guidance. • SENDCo/teacher meetings are considered to be part of staff development, as well as a time to share information. • The SENDCo and other relevant staff attend LA meetings and INSET as appropriate. • Newly appointed teaching and support staff meet the SENCo to discuss SEND procedures in the academy. • Specialist expertise is obtained by the school/nursery school. The Academy may make referrals to a range of external agencies if further specialist expertise is required. Each agency has its own referral criteria. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents of children on the SEN register within our Academy are invited to termly meetings where their input is valued and their views are included. Additionally, we encourage parents to become involved in the Academy's community through joining the PTA. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Children's progress is shared through parents'/carers' evenings twice a year and a report at the end of the year. Children on the SEN register have an additional parents' evening (3 in total) which allows for parental input into the child's support plan (APDR). How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The Academy is DDA compliant. Reasonable adjustments are made to make sure the Academy’s environment is as accessible as possible. All the Academy’s buildings are at ground level. Where there are steps, there is alternative access via ramp. Steps have handrails and are highlighted with yellow paint to make them more visible. Modifications are made to fixtures as appropriate. There is an allocated disabled parking bay which can be used by parents who hold a disabled parking badge. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? The academy follows the normal LA procedures for admission to a mainstream school. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Chepping View provides ongoing SEND training for staff and actively updates and develops the SEND resources available to pupils.

local_offer: "It is an outstanding school where students come first" The school believes that: - every student has a right to develop to their full potential, - every student has a right to a broad, balanced, relevant and challenging curriculum which is appropriate to their abilities - diversity supports the learning of all The schools objectives are to: - address the needs of all students irrespective of whether they have physical, sensory, emotional, behavioural, specific or general learning difficulties - ensure discrimination or prejudice is eradicated - identify barriers to learning and participation, and to address students’ needs - recognise, value and celebrate achievements, however small work in partnership with parents/carers in supporting their child’s education - provide appropriate resources (both human and material) as funding permits - involve the student in the process of identification, assessment and provision, ensuring that their wishes are taken into account - implement the statutory recommendations - guide and support all school staff, governors and parents in SEND issues. https://www.cheshamgrammar.org/774/send What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? name: Climb Quest: Autism-Friendly and SEND Climb
description: The centre is described as where the climbing centre meets the theme park, featuring over 20 amazing-looking walls suitable for all ages, abilities, and confidence levels. There are assistance climbing hoists for climbers with physical disabilities and the activity is extremely successful for children with autism. Climb Quest says they receive fantastic feedback for their SEND sessions, particularly around how accessible the activity is and how it helps build confidence. Special Needs Session: Regular public SEND sessions run on Sundays at 10am (excluding the third Sunday of the month), as well as selected times in the holidays (typically Wednesdays at 10am). Siblings can join in these sessions as well. These sessions have quieter music and an increased number of instructors with a maximum number of 14 young people per climbing session. Availability for exclusive sessions for SEND groups on request. Age Range and Facilities: Public and SEND sessions are suitable for all ages from 4 plus. They also run regular pre-school sessions for 2 to 4-year-olds. There is a Café on site serving hot and cold drinks, food, and snacks. General Opening Times - Monday to Friday term time from 2pm - Weekends and Holidays open all day, from 10am - See website for session times and availability - Opening times may vary

local_offer: Our climbing walls are suitable for all ages, abilities and confidence levels. Climbing instructors are on hand to provide support, encouragement and where required active climbing help such as operating our assistance climbing hoist. https://www.climbquest.co.uk/climbing/autism-friendly-and-send-climbing What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? The biggest outcome is helping to build confidence. The climbing activity also helps with: - Experience in facing fears and overcoming challenges - Communication - Literacy, numeracy, and problem solving - Teamwork What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Training is on the job. Managers and supervisors are in regular dialogue with the SEND schools and organisations we host for climbing sessions, to learn how we can continually improve our SEND offer. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents are invited onto the climbing arena during the session and are taught how to attach and detach their children from the climbing walls, which is an easy and failsafe method. You or their siblings can also book a space to climb with them. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? You will see the progress first hand, parents are amazed at how their child's confidence grows over the session. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have a mezzanine seating area but seating is available on the ground floor, where all other parts of the centre are accessed (climbing arena, cafe, toilets). How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We host public SEND sessions where music is turned off and our capacity is reduced. We accept Short Break vouchers and run numerous HAF sessions funded by MK City Council. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to work with schools, charities, councils and other organisations to support the SEND community in the area. We are always keen to build links with new organisations.

name: Community Transport Hub
description: The Community Transport Hub is funded by Buckinghamshire Council and delivers signposting information, advice and guidance to Buckinghamshire residents without access to public or private transport. Specifically, the service aims to assist those from vulnerable groups, who are struggling to maintain independence and who have a wide variety of needs and circumstances. The Community Transport Hub provides information on all aspects of community transport providers in Bucks, from Dial-a-Ride to community car schemes, minibus hire to wheelchair-accessible taxis. Please note we cannot make or take any bookings but we can provide advice on the most appropriate method of transport to meet your needs.
organisation: Community Impact Bucks We support people and groups to get involved and make a difference in local Buckinghamshire communities. We do this by offering expert advice and training, helping people to find volunteering opportunities, and helping charities and not for profit groups to get started, be effective and grow. We also have a number of directly delivered community services that focus on supporting those most in need – the elderly, vulnerable, and socially isolated. As an independent charity, we are the Council for Voluntary Service, Volunteer Centre, and Rural Community Council for Buckinghamshire. We are also the parent company of Healthwatch Bucks, an independent local organisation set up by the government to ensure that decision-makers and health and social care services put the experiences of people at the heart of their work. Community Impact Bucks and Healthwatch Bucks are both here to help improve the lives of people who live in Buckinghamshire: Community Impact Bucks inspires, supports, and enables voluntary and community action in the county. Healthwatch Bucks improves health and social care services by listening to you. It makes sure that what you have to say is heard by the people who deliver services and it works with groups whose views are not always being heard. We work together to make Bucks a better place to live. info@communityimpactbucks.org.uk https://communityimpactbucks.org.uk/

organisation: Restore Hope Restore Hope Latimer is a family focused charity based at Latimer Park. A special space in the countryside set in the heart of the Chilterns, just outside Amersham and Chesham and has been operating since 2002 and has a proven record of bringing change and help to people in need. We believe in the value of healthy, happy and stable families. We also believe that no matter how bad a situation may seem there is always hope. Our vision is therefore that every struggling family in the Chilterns finds help and hope for the future. This is clearly a big aim and one that requires us to continually increase our influence, effectiveness and reputation. We aim to achieve our vision by advancing and developing the programmes that we offer and continually looking for ways to engage with those most in need. We operate a clear strategy, with deliberate focus and dogged determination. We empower and equip key volunteers to lead various elements of our work, and support a motivated core staff team. RHL seeks to make best use of the fantastic facilities that Latimer Park offers and, where appropriate, grows into other spaces in the community to offer easy access to our programmes and to further develop the reputation of the charity. naomi.meech@restorehopelatimer.org http://www.restorehopelatimer.org

local_offer: Setting Name: Chesham Prep School SENCO: Danielle Burridge Contact: dburridge@cheshamprep.co.uk Chesham Prep is an independent school, for pupils aged 3 to 11.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Chesham Prep’s aim is that all pupils can access and benefit from the provision. We aim that all children will be supported to the best of our ability to make the best progress they can, relative to their stage of development. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? • The SENDCo has been awarded the National Award for SENCOs (NASENCO). • Our expertise is constantly updated via our SENDCos attendance at SEN ISI national conferences, SENDCo forums and other training courses and also via specialist SEND publications. • All School Staff have access to TES Learning Platform and IAPS online, both of which have a variety of SEND training options. • The Teachers, TAs, LSAs and SENDCo have expertise and training in different areas. All staff are encouraged to engage in Continuing Professional Development. • Training on SEND-specific issues are often included in INSET training days. • The SENDCo sends regular email training updates to staff regarding provision for our SEND pupils. • There is a SEND notice board in the staffroom to continually update staff knowledge on SEND issues, support and provision How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? • Parent Teacher Association (PTA) - Class reps • Open Door Policy • Social Media Posts • Coffee mornings • Reading record • Official reports about individual children’s progress • Parents’ evenings • Whole-school events, such as Speech Day, May Fair, Carol Service and Shows. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? • School Reports are written for all children twice each year. • All parents are invited to meet the class teacher at least twice each year at Parents Evenings. • All children on the Inclusion List have an Individual Learning Plan, which details the support in place, SMART targets and progress towards these targets. • The school employs an Open Door policy so parents can make an appointment to discuss progress at any point if they feel there is a need. • Parents of a child on the Inclusion List are invited to meet with the SENDCo at least twice each year How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We consider the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We try to create areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning. We run a forest school one day a week and we make a variety of adjustments to ensure all children can participate. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Parents and families are welcome to come along to our open day sessions to look at the setting, meet the team and talk through any queries. Parents with children with SEND are invited to make a special visit to discuss how we can best meet their needs. We have a flexible approach to transition and listen to the needs of the children and their families to endeavour to make this as smooth as possible. We liaise closely with settings that the children transfer to, passing on records and encouraging visits. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Continuous plans for SEND training with all teaching staff including the dedicated learning support team.

name: Absolutely Together
description: We put smiles on the faces of families with children and young adults with additional needs. We are Absolutely Together a Registered Charity formed in 2009 operating leisure venues across the South of England. Through our charitable work we have provided use of our facilities to local community groups and charities enabling them to fulfill their objectives or raise funds for their causes, as a result of this work Absolutely Leisure has helped over 100,000 people. In 2017 we made the decision to further our charitable works by developing our own schemes to help one of the most vulnerable and socially isolated groups in our society. These families often experience emotional and practical pressures which restrict the opportunities available to them. This can lead to social isolation, mental health problems, and an inability to get their children active. Many of these families also suffer significant financial difficulties which further restricts their ability to access leisure activities in the community. All family leisure time should be something that is cherished, but for many, it can be an incredibly stressful time. ​Absolutely Together helps these families by providing free access to exciting activities in the communities we work in. Helping put smiles on faces and create memories that will last a lifetime.

This can be those with ongoing physical or mental health problems, epilepsy, acquired brain injuries, be at high risk of a fall, plus many more conditions. Our GPS alarms are also used so adults with learning disabilities can have more independence than they might otherwise have. They are also used by older people that want to maintain their independence but still feel safe. SureSafe’s broad range of alarms can increase the safety of the alarm wearer, as well as give added peace of mind to the person’s loved ones or carers.

name: Yellow Submarine
description: Yellow Submarine is an award-winning Oxfordshire charity that believes people with learning disabilities and autism deserve to live life to the full. We tackle the problem that many people with learning disabilities leave school with limited life skills and as a result poor life chances. This often leads to isolation and being marginalised. Our projects start working with young people in community settings from the age of 11 onwards, to build their social skills, confidence, independence and ultimately their employability. At the same time we are supporting families and carers with respite. We’re unusual in the world of charities (and local authorities) in that with the same team of staff we assist young people on their journey through childhood into adulthood. This allows us, often over many years, to gain both trust and a real insight as to how best to create a person-centered plan to support each individual. What makes us different? We are willing to go the extra mile and are unashamedly ambitious to make things better. Our approaches have an emphasis on fun and innovation, embracing enterprise and technology. The terms “learning disability” and “autism” cover a huge variety of needs. Our specialism is helping individuals with mild to moderate needs. Find out about our projects on our website. How did it all start? Yellow Submarine started with the Staveley family. One of their number, Max, wanted (and needed) a holiday and his dream destination was Disneyland. However, Max had Down Syndrome, meaning the cost of holidays were astronomical, including not just Max, but the costs of multiple carers, their food, tickets and accommodation. The family felt it was unfair that someone with an already limited income must bear these costs in order to spend away from home. And so, the seeds of Yellow Submarine were sown. Toby and Lucy Staveley drew on their existing skills and began running holidays for people in Max’s position. The emerging charity set about helping those who needed a break the most and by proxy, their families or carers too.

name: Super 1 Disability Cricket Hub
description: Buckinghamshire Cricket has launched its first Disability Cricket Hub in the community. Super 1s gives young people with a disability aged 12 to 25 the chance to play regular competitive cricket while improving confidence and independence. We give participants the chance to compete against their peers and enjoy the benefits of playing sport. For many young people with a disability, loneliness has been identified as a major issue, and opportunities to take part in regular competitive sports can be extremely limited. Super 1s provides these opportunities and helps young people realise their potential. It improves their physical and mental well-being, giving them a sense of belonging as they make friends and gain skills for life such as confidence and independence. These sessions are free, and all disabilities are welcome. For more information contact Samina Mehrab.

local_offer: We endeavour to monitor all children who are not making adequate progress in the four broad areas specified in the SEND Code of Practice (DfE 2014), these are: communication and interaction, cognition and learning, behaviour, social, emotional and mental health difficulties, and sensory and/or physical needs. We work closely with all parents to listen to their views so as to build on children’s previous experiences, knowledge, understanding, and skills so that they develop in all aspects of the curriculum. Parent/carer involvement and support is vital to the success of the education of the children and especially those with SEN. Children with SEN are fully integrated into the life of the school and the curriculum, recognising the strengths of every individual as well as any areas for development, and ensuring all contribute to the social and cultural activities of the school. We believe in equal opportunities and work to meet the physical, emotional, and intellectual needs of all our children. https://chestnutlane.bucks.sch.uk/parents/policies What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have high aspirations for all the children Chestnut Lane School and work together with families to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace. We communicate regularly with parents and regular reviews keep parents and staff working closely together. In addition we have close working relationships with a range of outside agencies who provide expertise within their fields. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Morphology Training Deaf Awareness Training Makaton Level 1 and 2 SEND Inclusion Conference New to SEND Leadership Bereavement Training Precision Monitoring Dyslexia Elklin Speech and Language Supporting Executive Function in the classroom Leading a Neurodiverse classroom Supporting Emotional Regulation Creating Sensory Friendly Environments Impact of Anxiety Introduction to Down syndrome Postgraduate National Award for SEND SEND updates Sensory Circuits Trauma and Attachment Speech and Language How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents into school regularly. Parents have access to our online learning journey platform, and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can catch up with the teacher informally at the beginning and end of the session or can request a meeting with at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible. We also have termly parents' evenings where parents will receive an update on their child’s progress and can discuss their child’s likes, dislikes, achievements, and any concerns they may have. We provide age-appropriate suggestions of how your child’s development can be supported at home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? In addition to the opportunities listed above, we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEN, depending on the needs of the child. We regularly monitor the short-term outcomes for children with SEN and invite parents to be part of reviews and the planning session for new outcomes. If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT)) are visiting we would give parents the opportunity, where appropriate, to liaise with the therapists. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our buildings are all on one level. The main building has ramps and handrails and a disabled toilet. There is also a ramp into each year block. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? As a community school we follow the Buckinghamshire Council's admission rules for primary schools. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We will continue to keep up-to-date with appropriate training and new strategies to support children with SEND in our setting.

local_offer: Kiddies Cove Day Nursery is a private owned Nursery that caters for up to 60 children per session. We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs. Building positive relationships with the children and their families is very important to us. Here at Kiddies Cove Day Nursery, we understand that every child is unique and we have high aspirations for all children. We encourage working together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Jo Ashmore has a level three certificate for Early Years Special Needs Coordinators in Private, Voluntary and Independent Settings. She completed this qualification in July 2021. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We aim to create an inclusive environment where parents and carers can feel happy and confident communicating openly with us regarding their children. We are regularly available to have formal catch-ups with parents to discuss their child’s needs and provide term reports regarding each child’s progress that the key worker will discuss in detail with the parent. We speak daily with parents at drop off and pick up and communicate through our online parent app, Blossom Educational. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has a learning journal that parents/carers can look at any time by asking their child’s Key Person. Parents also see these at our informal parent's evenings that we hold twice a year. We will discuss progress when we complete termly key worker reports, through our 2-year-old progress checks and during our termly COHORT evaluations. For children with SEN, we try to ensure that we can meet more frequently to discuss progress towards their short-term outcomes and work together to plan new outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take into account the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We try to create areas where distractions are minimised for focused learning and to create sensory areas to support children with sensory processing issues. Our setting has a wheelchair ramp for access to the ground floor and has a disabled toilet that is accessible for wheelchair users. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?  What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We would like to further our sensory resources by creating a sensory area in our soft playroom. We feel that this would benefit many of our children and help support their development.

description: Child Bereavement UK supports grieving children and young people (up to 25), and parents bereaved of a child to find hope. Through free expert guidance, resources, and compassionate support, Child Bereavement UK helps people to rebuild their lives, in their own time. Support is available if you’re 25 or under, or if your baby or child has died or is expected to die before their 26th birthday. We offer free, accessible online grief support, information and guidance to individuals, families and professionals throughout the UK. Our trained bereavement specialists are available to speak with Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm (excluding bank holidays) by phone, text or WhatsApp (13 plus); email, or live chat: click the ‘Chat with us’ button on our website. No appointment needed. Additional support is available through the online referral form; this is for one-to-one and group sessions which are delivered digitally. Child Bereavement UK designs and delivers training for professionals in health and social care, education, the emergency services, and the voluntary and corporate sectors.
organisation: Child Bereavement UK Child Bereavement UK supports families and educates professionals when a baby or child of any age dies or is dying, or when a child is facing bereavement. Every year we train almost 9000 professionals, helping them to better understand and meet the needs of grieving families. In the UK, when a baby or child dies, or a child is bereaved, many of those affected are unable to access good quality support which meets their individual needs. Child Bereavement UK believes all families should have the support they need to rebuild their lives when a child grieves or when a child dies. Our aim is to make sure they do. We offer the following services sessions: Face-to-face Individual, couple and family support sessions. Parents' support groups for baby and child death and support through subsequent pregnancy. Family group Programme for children (4 to 11) to attend with parents or carers. Young People's Advisory Groups for bereaved young people up to age 25. support@childbereavementuk.org https://childbereavementuk.org/

name: Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre (CEOP)
description: CEOP is a law enforcement agency and is here to help keep children and young people safe from sexual abuse and grooming online. We help thousands of children and young people every year who have been in a similar situation to you. CEOP are unable to respond to reports about bullying, fake accounts, or account hacking. They help and give you advice, and you can make a report directly to us if something has happened online which has made you feel unsafe, scared, or worried. This might be from someone you know in real life, or someone you have only ever met online. If you make a report to them about sexual abuse or grooming online it will be read by one of our Child Protection Advisors who will get in contact with you on the phone number or email address that you give to them to make sure that you are safe. They will also discuss with you what will happen next. Please try not to worry, you have done nothing wrong and they will do all they can to help you. CEOP works with lots of other professionals whose jobs are also to make sure you are safe, this includes other police agencies. If a crime has been committed they will work together and use our specialist skills to identify the person or people responsible and bring them into the criminal justice system. The CEOP Thinkuknow website also has information and advice to help you to stay safe if something has happened to you online. CEOP is unable to respond to reports about bullying but if you are being bullied and would like to talk to someone in confidence right now you can call Childline or talk to them online - no worry is too big or too small. Please also tell an adult that you trust, like a parent, carer, or teacher.

An Assess, plan, do review (APDR) will be put in place to support any children with a development delay. Parents are encouraged to share any concerns they may have, or any areas that they would like to support their child with while at the setting. If required, a meeting may be held to discuss the child's needs and any referrals that may need to done to outside agencies such as speech and language therapy. Children who have an APDR or SEN Support Plan will have their plan's reviewed frequently. The key person will share the plans with the families and the parents are included in the reviewing process. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Information will be shared with parents by frequent feedback. Daily feedback is given to the parent where the parents will be informed of their child's day and how they have been. Meetings can be held with the parent, key person and the SENCO to share any information. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? The pre-school setting is on two levels. We have a dark sensory room and also a light room that children are able to access in small groups with an adult. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We work closely with a range of local schools so that when children move to reception we try to ensure the transition is as smooth as possible. Where possible, we will attend a settling in session with the child at the school. The staff at the school are invited in to meet the child and the key person in our setting, where they can discuss the child's needs and any interests that they may have. A meeting will be held with the teachers from the school and the staff at pre-school to ensure all information and paperwork are supporting the child in their new setting. Parents will also be invited to this meeting to ensure everyone's views are shared What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? All staff to be trained to use Makaton, visual timetables in all rooms

name: Chesham Repair Café
description: We are a group of volunteers who help our community and the environment by repairing things that would otherwise end up in landfills. We operate on the fourth Saturday of each month - usually coinciding with Chesham Local Produce Market from 10am to 1pm (last orders by 12:30pm). Items are seen on a first-come, first-served basis. All of our repairers and team are volunteers, so we encourage pay-as-you-feel donations after your item has been seen, which helps us meet our running costs. We will always have electronic (including battery and mains powered, and IT computing) and sewing repairers available, as well as leather and ceramics repairers in selected months. Please check our Facebook and Instagram pages for the following date and location and the repair services that are expected to be available on that date.

local_offer: Princes Risborough Primary School, class teachers are aware of the needs of all their children, who are monitored carefully to measure the progress they are making. This ensures that any special educational needs are identified as early as possible. Our teaching is inclusive for all pupils, with lesson content and delivery considered in terms of the impact on differing levels of pupil ability. If a child is finding a learning area particularly difficult, the majority of their needs should still be met within the classroom through quality first differentiated, personalised teaching. A pupil is identified as having special educational needs if he/she finds it significantly more difficult to learn than the majority of others of the same age. For these pupils, there are therefore occasions when additional support may be required, for a variety of reasons. name: Childcare4U (Beaconsfield)
description: Childcare4 u Beaconsfield is an Ofsted Outstanding nursery with a homely feel providing the very best learning opportunities tailored to each individual child. Working closely with their parents our exceptional and caring staff team observe and plan according to each child’s development in a fun and engaging way, making use of our indoor and outdoor space as well as the community and local area on regular outings. We have an on-site chef who prepares all our meals from scratch, using organic produce which has gained us the Food for Life Served Here Soil Association Bronze award. We offer a weekly session of Forest School with our trained forest school lead for children aged 3 and over, and do forest school taster activities within our newly refurbished garden or in the local community with our younger children. We have also gained a level 5 Royal Horticultural Society gardening award as part of our Garden Champions activity. Garden Champions is our own bespoke extra-curricular gardening activity which is supported by the Royal Horticultural Society’s School Gardening Awards training programme. This activity extends children’s knowledge of the outdoor environment, habitats, caring for living things, growth cycles and growing vegetation outdoors. We also offer weekly cooking sessions, Spanish sessions, daily Wake up shake up sessions, and a range of bespoke activities which promote your child’s well-being and confidence, including Emotions Boxes and Chatterboxes, which also promotes early communication. We offer all inclusive fees, and have a highly qualified staff team with at least 80% of our staff qualified to level 3 or more in CCLD. Every member of staff has a certificate in First aid and refreshes this every 3 years.

description: Childcare4 u Beaconsfield is an Ofsted Outstanding nursery with a homely feel providing the very best learning opportunities tailored to each individual child. Working closely with their parents our exceptional and caring staff team observe and plan according to each child’s development in a fun and engaging way, making use of our indoor and outdoor space as well as the community and local area on regular outings. We have an on-site chef who prepares all our meals from scratch, using organic produce which has gained us the Food for Life Served Here Soil Association Bronze award. We offer a weekly session of Forest School with our trained forest school lead for children aged 3 and over, and do forest school taster activities within our newly refurbished garden or in the local community with our younger children. We have also gained a level 5 Royal Horticultural Society gardening award as part of our Garden Champions activity. Garden Champions is our own bespoke extra-curricular gardening activity which is supported by the Royal Horticultural Society’s School Gardening Awards training programme. This activity extends children’s knowledge of the outdoor environment, habitats, caring for living things, growth cycles and growing vegetation outdoors. We also offer weekly cooking sessions, Spanish sessions, daily Wake up shake up sessions, and a range of bespoke activities which promote your child’s well-being and confidence, including Emotions Boxes and Chatterboxes, which also promotes early communication. We offer all inclusive fees, and have a highly qualified staff team with at least 80% of our staff qualified to level 3 or more in CCLD. Every member of staff has a certificate in First aid and refreshes this every 3 years.

description: Would you like to feel better about life? Do you feel stuck and need some tips on how to move on? The group size is around eight to ten young people, with a maximum of twelve. The course is based on participation; however, we understand that joining a new group can be daunting for young people, so our facilitators will be in touch with you before the course starts to discuss any specific needs that a young person may have. Bucks Family Learning also offers courses for parents/carers which complement our youth courses. Online training and resources plus free information all written specifically for childminders Visit our website to find lots of free information and resources, such as suggestions for policies and blank risk assessments. In our shop you will find online training and resources that have been produced specifically with childminders in mind. All our training modules have CPD Accreditation Childminding UK are the only national organisation to receive the Princess Royal Training Award for ‘ensuring high-quality childcare through training and support’ Our Level 3 Ofsted recognised Online Introductory Training covers all the requirements of the Early Years Foundation Stage and will equip you to set up and run an Ofsted Registered Childminding Business. It also complies with the Common Core standards giving you a complete programme of everything that is recommended you need to work with children. Our Level 3 Common Core Training for the Childcare Register is designed for childminders caring for school aged children only, nannies, out of school clubs, and holiday and activity clubs. It guides learners effortlessly from the basics of child development to the Ofsted requirements of registration and working in an Ofsted registered setting. Online training courses will cover much of the CPD training requirements you will have. Our e-books and guides give information about topics such as attachment, well being, income tax, national insurance, equality, and diversity. The resource packs give information and forms to use in your every day practice such as Childminding Contracts, Childminding Accounts forms, Recording Children's Development which includes observation formats, duty of care pack which includes consent forms, risk assessments, attendance registers, policies and procedures, and much more. If you are a childminder who employs others, there is a supervisions and appraisals pack too. Annual Membership gives huge savings on the shop prices of our products. Find more information by visiting our website.

description: At S4A we strive to create a childcare environment that allows children to pursue their interests through a wide variety of exciting activities. We pride ourselves on playing a huge part in your child’s development, helping them to become creative and open-minded by providing role models in our high-quality provision.
organisation: S4A Group Ltd, Sports Development and School PE Provision S4A offer holiday camps in Buckingham, Grendon Underwood and Patishall. Providing childcare during the school holidays. We offer activities such as football, basketball, science and seasonal craft activities, a full list of which can be found on the s4a website. S4A also work in 13 different schools in Buckingham and surrounding areas providing high-quality PE provision. We teach a huge variety of different Sports with our coaches' being highly qualified in a range of Sports. We tailor our lesson plans to suit each classes specific needs, giving children the opportunity to learn new skills and develop existing ones whilst always maintaining the importance of enjoyment and fun. As well as providing PE provision in these schools we also provide extended care across in the area. We run breakfast and after school clubs offering a range of activities tailored to meet the interests of the children in attendance, from science clubs to sports clubs S4A cater for all. Helping them develop physically, emotionally, socially and mentally in an environment that is fun and exciting. S4A Development is about helping children reaching ''their'' next level. Our Boys and Girls Development Centre sessions are on a Monday evening in Buckingham with our Juniors section on a Saturday morning in Buckingham and Gawcott. All sessions are professionally designed and delivered in line with the 'England DNA' to offer a player-focused approach and develop players on an individual basis while allowing them to progress at their own speed and in a low pressure but testing environment. All skills and attributes developed will be in the following areas: Technical/ Tactical/ Physical/ Psychological and Social. matt.ogle@s4asports.co.uk https://s4asports.co.uk

name: SANEline
description: SANEline is a national out-of-hours mental health helpline offering specialist emotional support, guidance, and information to anyone affected by mental illness, including family, friends, and carers. Our helpline is here to support you – particularly if you feel you have reached a moment of crisis. We know that moment of crisis is different for everybody – some people can reach that point daily, and for some people, it is rare. Our trained helpline volunteers aim to be empathic and non-judgemental, providing space and time for you to talk about your mental health or the mental health of someone close to you.

description: SANEline is a national out-of-hours mental health helpline offering specialist emotional support, guidance, and information to anyone affected by mental illness, including family, friends, and carers. Our helpline is here to support you – particularly if you feel you have reached a moment of crisis. We know that moment of crisis is different for everybody – some people can reach that point daily, and for some people, it is rare. Our trained helpline volunteers aim to be empathic and non-judgemental, providing space and time for you to talk about your mental health or the mental health of someone close to you.

local_offer: Derwen College delivers exceptional programmes within a rich learning environment. Students who attend Derwen are aged from 16 to 25 years and have special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) including: - Learning and physical disabilities - Autism - Behaviours of concern - Moderate, Severe, Complex or Profound and Multiple Learning Disabilities We offer residential placements at our main campus in Gobowen, near Oswestry in North Shropshire, and also have day placements at Gobowen, Ludlow, Telford and Walford. Learning Programmes at Derwen include: - Vocational Study Programmes, which are delivered through our Learning Pathways at each of our four sites. - Learning for Life, which is a fun bespoke programme available for those students who need a bit of extra support before progressing on to a vocational pathway. - Nurture is our programme for students with complex and / or profound and multiple learning disabilities and is available at our Gobowen site. - Springboard is a non-educational route that gives further access to work experience opportunities and support to improve independence skills. - Supported Internships are available for anyone living locally who have completed a vocational study programme. Vocational pathways Depending on the location, we have the following vocational pathways available: - Hospitality and Food - Horticulture - Performing Arts - Retail and Enterprise - Work and Independence These have been developed to prepare students for the work place. Our accessible learning environments are designed and operated to industry standards. Students gain authentic work experience in our public-facing commercial outlets, including: garden centre and gift shop; Walled Garden Café; Station Café; The Vintage Advantage charity shop; The Orangery restaurant; and our very own hotel! We are also proud to offer our students a well-established network of high-quality employer partners in the wider community. We work closely with each of them to provide tailored and relevant work placements. Students are encouraged to choose one main and one secondary pathway, but they don’t have to. We work with every student to build a programme bespoke to them that fits their needs and interests. Come and talk to us about what would suit you. Not looking for a vocational route? Learning for Life pathway The Life Skills / Preparation for work pathway is designed for students not yet ready for a full-time vocational pathway. Students gain the necessary skills that support all aspects of life. This could be additional support with communication, personal development, interaction, teamwork and problem solving, or self-regulation. The pathway is personalised and tailored to meet each young person’s specific needs. Nurture Programme Nurture Programme is a bespoke Life Skills and Sensory programme, offering day and residential provision for students with Complex and / or Profound and Multiple Disabilities. What else will can students learn? Alongside each pathway, we will work with you students to develop an individualised programme, which will include: Functional Skills (English, maths and ICT); Employability Skills; Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE); and Independence Skills development including travel training to increase your potential to live independently once you students have graduated from college. What else can students get involved with? Each timetable will include opportunities to join in with sports and/or leisure activities depending on what students like to do. Many students discover new interests at college – we have lots of options to explore, including: - Access to our renowned Duke of Edinburgh’s Award programme at Bronze, Silver, and Gold level, at its dedicated base on campus - Our extensive sports programme taking full advantage of our fantastic facilities and location, for example canoeing, football, swimming, Boccia, dance, cycling, tennis, gym, running, yoga, basketball, and more. - Wellbeing clubs such as; - Gardening - indoor cricket, - drama, dance and music, - craft - Pray and Praise - Forest skills - Photography - Chill out sessions - Acts of kindness - Bee keeping And many more. - Trips, such as horse riding, theatre, museums, shopping - Student Union Board Student support Students have wraparound support, for example Personal Tutor, Key Worker. Learner Voice Learner Voice at Derwen College is very strong and student views influence everything that we do. We have a thriving Student Union (SU). The SU Board is very active across the college and beyond, helping to drive forward change for people with SEND. Students participate in the NATSPEC parliament twice a year, in which they work with other SEND specialist colleges from around the Country to highlight issues specific to them. In 2021 we worked on the rights of people with disabilities, and received a letter of thanks from the Minister for Disabled People, Health and Work, Justin Tomlinson, for our contribution to the National Disability Survey, which was collated during the Parliament session. Therapy An extensive range of therapies and wellbeing support is available including: Positive Behaviour Support; speech and language therapy; occupational therapy; counselling; and physiotherapy and Learning Disability Nurses. Our team uses the universal, targeted and specialist model to deliver a service which is based on individual need. Many of our therapy services are integrated across all aspects of college life including care, work and the social settings, to ensure student needs are met. Individual therapy sessions, for example hydrotherapy, are also available dependent upon funding. Students are able to join in wellbeing sessions of their choice – such as mindfulness, relaxation, Lego Therapy. name: Volunteer Bucks
description: Volunteer Bucks is managed by Community Impact Bucks, a local charity that enables people and organisations to get involved in voluntary and community action in Buckinghamshire. As the Volunteer Centre for Buckinghamshire, we help people find local volunteer roles that suit them, whether based on location, type of role, interests, or time commitment. From 2020 to 2024, we matched over 2200 volunteers with local charities and not-for-profit organisations through our Buckinghamshire Volunteer Matching Service. The Volunteer Bucks platform replaces this service, giving people the opportunity to browse and apply for volunteering roles themselves. It also allows organisations to post and manage their volunteer roles directly. Please visit our website for more information and to get involved.
organisation: Community Impact Bucks We support people and groups to get involved and make a difference in local Buckinghamshire communities. We do this by offering expert advice and training, helping people to find volunteering opportunities, and helping charities and not for profit groups to get started, be effective and grow. We also have a number of directly delivered community services that focus on supporting those most in need – the elderly, vulnerable, and socially isolated. As an independent charity, we are the Council for Voluntary Service, Volunteer Centre, and Rural Community Council for Buckinghamshire. We are also the parent company of Healthwatch Bucks, an independent local organisation set up by the government to ensure that decision-makers and health and social care services put the experiences of people at the heart of their work. Community Impact Bucks and Healthwatch Bucks are both here to help improve the lives of people who live in Buckinghamshire: Community Impact Bucks inspires, supports, and enables voluntary and community action in the county. Healthwatch Bucks improves health and social care services by listening to you. It makes sure that what you have to say is heard by the people who deliver services and it works with groups whose views are not always being heard. We work together to make Bucks a better place to live. info@communityimpactbucks.org.uk https://communityimpactbucks.org.uk/

name: Unity College
description: Unity College supports the educational needs of pupils aged 11 to 18 years with social, emotional and mental health difficulties (SEMH) who need a smaller, more nurturing educational placement in order to succeed academically. The college building offers a pleasant and spacious learning environment including specialist vocational learning spaces combined with designated teaching rooms. The college follows a therapeutic model offering a safe, secure and friendly environment for pupils. The college, as part of the Keys Group, provides placements for pupils who reside in nearby Keys Group homes. In order to meet the diverse needs of the young people at Unity College we ensure that the staff to pupil ratio is high, with typically a class comprising of no more than 4 pupils. Each class is staffed by at least one teacher and an educational support worker (ESW).

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as a unique individual and support them appropriately so that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Makaton – 2012 Deleloping self esteem in young children - 2019 Promoting positive behaviour - 2019 Managing behaviour - 2019 Supporting children with SEND - 2019 Difficult emotions and emotional regulation (SEND students) - 2025 Modelling and scaffolding for students with SEND -2025 Supporting children on the autism spectrum - 2025 Supporting children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder ADHD- 2025 Supporting children with dyslexia- 2025 Supporting children with dyspraxia 2025 How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? I work in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. All children attending the setting have their learning and development monitored and extended. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work jointly with them to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a small step leading to the front door. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I will work in partnership with other early years settings and schools to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ information sheet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will provide the new provider with transition information to help the child settle in their new setting. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am keen to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for. I have a real passion for SEND inclusion and will do everything reasonably possible to enable a child to access their education.

organisation: The Theatre Shed The aim of The Theatre Shed in Amersham is to inspire, innovate and include through the medium of Performing Arts. Our inclusive workshops are professionally led and allow our young people to explore performance skills such as acting, singing, dancing, physical theatre and more in a supportive environment. We would normally run in-person Workshops on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings with additional holiday Workshops. Initially when, due to the COVID-19 pandemic Lockdown and social distancing recommendations, we were unable to continue running Workshops at our normal venue at The Beacon School we were devastated. We didn’t give up and our Artistic team have worked extremely hard to keep The Theatre Shed up and running by going online. With so many young people needing a regular pattern to their lives we have been able to give continuity, stability and consistency. Good mental health at this time is so important. These sessions are really well attended once everyone got used to using Zoom and it now feels so natural to our members. This gives continuity, familiarity and activity in these extremely uncertain times. We didn’t stop there realising that there are others in the Community who would benefit from regular involvement in our activities so we expanded our activities to include Film Club for the Community. This is a chance to watch a film at the same time as your friends with an activity pack available to download from our website to go along with it. The chosen film is shown via our Zoom link so everyone can watch together. Our Community work continues with daytime workshops on a Tuesday between 2pm and 3pm and will have different themes (drama, dance, music etc.) each week. admin@thetheatreshed.co.uk https://thetheatreshed.co.uk/

name: Ukraine2chilterns.com
description: We are a group of 90 plus host families with over 200 Ukrainian individuals here, or arriving shortly, to Princes Risborough and the surrounding villages. We aim to provide support for the local hosts and their Ukrainian sponsored families. We are a large support network providing a matching service, visa application support, fundraising, help with schools, language, transport, job applications, settling in, events, plus any other needs as they arise. Our mission is to help provide safe sanctuary to the Ukrainian people during the Russian invasion, under the Government scheme 'Homes for Ukraine'. We are a collective community of villages in the Chiltern Hills, Buckinghamshire. It comprises of Princes Risborough, White Leaf, Monks Risborough, Loosley Row, Lacey Green, Speen, Great Hampden, Great Missenden, North Dean, Walters Ash and Naphill, Bledlow ridge, Bledlow, Hughenden Valley, Stoke Mandeville and is growing each week. We are a registered charity.

name: Roller Skating/Roller Disco (Haddenham Rollers)
description: Welcome to Haddenham Rollers. Haddenham enjoyed a tradition of roller skating in the enormous village hall since the 1950's. Everyone is welcome, young and old, any ability. The hall benefits from a smooth wooden floor and handrails around the perimeter for beginners to hold, should they need to. Roller skating is classed as an effective aerobic exercise that helps to strengthen the heart and improve muscle strength and endurance. With our years of running disco's experience running Em's Looney Tune Discos (contact us to book a private disco, children's party or private roller disco or to hire skates for your event) we make sure there's a party atmosphere every session. Come down and join the fun, everyone is welcome. It's easier than ice skating, you'll quickly find your balance. We run a reasonably priced café at every event selling hot dogs, fish finger sandwiches, home made cakes freshly baked on site, and hot and cold drinks. Additionally, there is a bar on the last Friday of every month. Weekly roller discos: Our weekly general sessions are currently pay on the door only. £7 skaters, £5 skate hire, non skaters and wheelchair users are free. Wheelchairs are allowed on the rink. Every Friday (with some exceptions please check website before visiting): - 4:30 to 5:30pm for ages 3 to 9 year olds, and supervising adults - 5:30 to 6:30pm 9 plus year olds including adults, whether supervising or not If you have children in different age groups wishing to skate together, contact us and we'll assess whether we can make an exception, depending on their abilities. Our main priority is safety. Monthly Adults only (18 plus) roller discos with bar the last Monday of the month: Doors open: 7:30pm Last orders: 10:45pm £10.50 Skaters, £2.50 non skaters, £5 Skate hire Roller Skate hire is available at our Roller Discos (online booking is essential for skate hire at the monthly adults only discos), kids skate hire is available on the door from size 6 junior upwards so are a limited number of adult sizes, first come first served). You are welcome to bring your own skates, but they must be clean and with no protruding sharp bits or loose, broken components. See our terms and conditions for more information.

name: Roller Skating/Roller Disco (Haddenham Rollers)
description: Welcome to Haddenham Rollers. Haddenham enjoyed a tradition of roller skating in the enormous village hall since the 1950's. Everyone is welcome, young and old, any ability. The hall benefits from a smooth wooden floor and handrails around the perimeter for beginners to hold, should they need to. Roller skating is classed as an effective aerobic exercise that helps to strengthen the heart and improve muscle strength and endurance. With our years of running disco's experience running Em's Looney Tune Discos (contact us to book a private disco, children's party or private roller disco or to hire skates for your event) we make sure there's a party atmosphere every session. Come down and join the fun, everyone is welcome. It's easier than ice skating, you'll quickly find your balance. We run a reasonably priced café at every event selling hot dogs, fish finger sandwiches, home made cakes freshly baked on site, and hot and cold drinks. Additionally, there is a bar on the last Friday of every month. Weekly roller discos: Our weekly general sessions are currently pay on the door only. £7 skaters, £5 skate hire, non skaters and wheelchair users are free. Wheelchairs are allowed on the rink. Every Friday (with some exceptions please check website before visiting): - 4:30 to 5:30pm for ages 3 to 9 year olds, and supervising adults - 5:30 to 6:30pm 9 plus year olds including adults, whether supervising or not If you have children in different age groups wishing to skate together, contact us and we'll assess whether we can make an exception, depending on their abilities. Our main priority is safety. Monthly Adults only (18 plus) roller discos with bar the last Monday of the month: Doors open: 7:30pm Last orders: 10:45pm £10.50 Skaters, £2.50 non skaters, £5 Skate hire Roller Skate hire is available at our Roller Discos (online booking is essential for skate hire at the monthly adults only discos), kids skate hire is available on the door from size 6 junior upwards so are a limited number of adult sizes, first come first served). You are welcome to bring your own skates, but they must be clean and with no protruding sharp bits or loose, broken components. See our terms and conditions for more information.

name: SENDsational Mornings at Tring
description: We are excited to present SENDsational Mornings at Tring, Hertfordshire at the Tring Museum. The gallery is shut to the public till 12 midday. You are welcome to stay longer but please bear in mind it will be busier. Children with neurodiverse conditions including autism and other sensory processing difficulties can enjoy the Museum with their families and siblings, free from the hustle and bustle of the general public. Our sister museum in South Kensington has been successfully running a similar event called Dawnosaurs for the past four years. What can you expect from the experience? - Visitors have access to a few activities including specimen handling, a big draw and a gallery trail. - All activities are supported by experienced, autism-aware facilitators. - A sensory space will be available for those children needing a quieter and calmer space. - All of the galleries, outdoor spaces and the shop will be accessible throughout the event. - This event is best for children aged 5 to 15 and siblings are welcome. Please visit our website to view upcoming dates. You will need to book a ticket in advance and walk-ups will not be possible. To join the mailing list to be notified about the release of tickets please contact us.

description: Chiltern Music Therapy is a not-for-profit organisation using music to help people of all ages connect, communicate, and thrive. Together we harness the power of music, inspire through human story, and fascinate through science to create a network of champions. local_offer: Chiltern Music Therapy are an award-winning not-for-profit organisation providing music therapy services to children and young people with additional needs. We pride ourselves on using evidence based practice and are dedicated to providing measurable and tangible outcomes for all client groups. At the heart of our work is our aim to provide an inclusive service, that is accessible to all. Music Therapy sessions are available to young adults and children in Post 16 Transition Services. Please get in touch if you would like more information about how to access these sessions at your local college.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Music Therapy is a therapeutic intervention using music, which looks at creating change and improvements in communication, physical, social, cognitive, and emotional needs. At Chiltern Music Therapy we help people with functional needs, such as helping develop skills in cognition, speech and communication, or motor skills. We also help people with psychological needs, working on emotional well-being and mental health issues. Music Therapy uses the influence of music to affect specific behaviours and outcomes and is a clinical and evidence-based process, tailored to each individual’s goals. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our Music Therapists are: - Qualified to a minimum level of a Masters in Music Therapy - Registered with and regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council - Registered with the British Association for Music Therapy - DBS (Enhanced) checked - Trained in the use of standardised and validated assessment tools and outcome measures for all client groups In addition, many of our team have additional training in Neurologic Music Therapy, Neonatal Intensive Care Music Therapy, Medical Music Therapy and MATADOC (Music Therapy Assessment Tool in Awareness for Disorders of Consciousness). How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?  How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Our evaluative approach means we constantly monitor and assess development and progress in music therapy, and our standardised outcome measures are used alongside parents, teachers, SENCOs and families. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our music therapy service is fully accessible in the community and also on a mobile basis. Our inclusive approach means that no-one is excluded because financial or geographical means. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Please visit our website to submit an enquiry or complete a referral form. Alternatively, please e-mail or call to speak to one of the team. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Chiltern Music Therapy aims to provide a music therapy provision wherever there is a need across Buckinghamshire and the surrounding counties. All our music therapists are continually undergoing specialist training to further professional development when working with children and young people with additional needs.
