description: Explore and experience life in the Chilterns over the last 2000 years at our award-winning open-air museum, a great day out for all the family. Over 30 superb rescued and reconstructed traditional Chilterns buildings, fascinating displays, and demonstrations, ‘hands-on workshops and exciting period re-enactments. Set in 45 acres of idyllic park and woodland, it’s a truly unique experience. Travel through time, from an Iron Age House through to a 1947 Prefab via historic buildings, crafts and skills, all brought vividly to life for you. A great venue for those seeking to hold a wedding, birthday party, corporate event, meeting, training day, club rally, exhibition, group picnic or barbecue or indeed almost any type of event. The Museum and historic buildings also provides a wonderful learning experience for schools and pupils of all ages and abilities. An enjoyable, educational and inclusive day for all school groups visiting us and to support your group's classroom learning. All of our many activity workshops support a wide range of curriculum areas.

local_offer: Concessions available to refer to those who are registered disabled. (evidence will be required). Free admission for one carer or companion of disabled visitors (standard admission events only). Accessibility: We are committed to being an accessible Museum. We try to ensure that our historic buildings can be enjoyed by all of our visitors. Disabled visitors have designated spaces close to the Museum entrance and where possible we provide ramps into our buildings. Accessible routes around the Museum are clearly marked on our Museum map. Blue badge holders: Concessionary rates are available for registered disabled visitors and carers can come in free. Parking and Vehicles: There are designated parking spaces for blue badge holders close to the Museum entrance. the Museum operates a ‘no vehicles on site’ policy during opening hours. However, electric mobility scooters are allowed, with a 5mph speed limit. Wheelchairs and Electric Scooters: The Museum has two electric scooters for hire. This is free of charge, although donations to the Museum are welcome. A security deposit is required while the scooter is on loan. Please ring the Museum Office on to check availability and to pre-book. Adult manual wheelchairs can also be borrowed from the Ticket Office. Users of this facility must have a carer to assist them. Pre-booking is advisable. The Museum has temporary ramps for the Prefab, Furniture Factory, Henton Mission Room and Borehamwood Dairy to enable wheelchair access. Please ask at the Ticket Office on arrival and staff will ensure the ramps are put out ready for use. Please be aware that our compact gravel paths are not ideal for wheelchairs and some paths can become very muddy in bad weather. If possible, we would recommend booking a mobility scooter in advance instead. The most accessible route around the Museum is marked by a dotted line on the Museum Map. We regret that the Woodland Walk is not suitable for wheelchairs. Loop Systems: Small portable loop systems are now installed at the Ticket Office and Tea Rooms for use by visitors with hearing aids. On request, the Museum can provide a portable loop for use on guided tours around the Museum for one user with a hearing aid. Please book in advance. Access Guides: A Visitors’ Folder with information about buildings with limited access is available at the Ticket Office free of charge. The Museum has audio guides and braille guides available. These offer short descriptions of the Museum buildings and landscape features. They are free of charge to use during your visit but we do require a deposit. Please book in advance by contacting the Museum Office. Dogs are welcome on site but, with the exception of Guide Dogs, must not go inside any of our residential buildings. All dogs must be kept on a short lead because of farm livestock. Toilet Facilities: The most modern and accessible facilities are the ‘Bakerloo’ Mid Site Toilets on the Village Green (No.14a on the Museum Map). there are two cubicles in the historic Caversham Public Conveniences (No.3 on the Museum map) have been adapted for wheelchair access, as far as possible. name: Mission EmployAble Supported-internships for Young People with SEND
description: We run supported internships for young adults (18 to 25 years) with a learning disability. We are a subcontractor for Buckinghamshire Colleges Group. A supported internship is a minimum 20-hour-a-week programme for a full academic year with 70% being work experience and 30% Maths, English, and Employability studies. At the end of the year, we help our interns search for paid employment and support them in this when they succeed. So far 90% have achieved paid employment All applicants need to have an EHCP, have passed at least entry level 1 Maths and English, and be working at entry level 2. They need to be able to get to us either independently or be working towards this. We will provide travel training. Some interns also use SEN taxis or parents/carers for transport. Interns can come from Bucks, Herts, or any of the surrounding areas. Our work experience includes catering in our purpose-built cafe on Chorleywood Common training in all aspects of the cafe - serving, taking orders, food prep, cleaning, and also with our partners 1. Restore Hope in Latimer where the interns learn warehouse-type work and deliveries and hospitality and catering 2. Sunnyside Rural Trust where interns learn high-level horticultural skills. 3. Woodoaks farm where interns learn land management and regenerative agriculture We also have other programmes including team building, creative retail, and ranger work and we support our interns with guidance from the DWP, Mental health teams, and Pet therapy.

description: Our mission is to enhance The Chiltern's habitats through conservation, education, and community engagement. local_offer: Those with SEND and other difficulties often have confidence issues which undermine their ability to achieve their potential. We have a very inclusive approach and foster a "can do" attitude in all our volunteers. The biggest difference is moving that position from one where the person is shy introverted and cannot even look you in the eye on day one towards a position where they can comfortably interact with other volunteers and staff. This enables them to start tackling other issues safe in the knowledge they can do things and make a difference.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We often find people with SEND struggle with things others find easy or the norm: confined spaces, being forced to communicate when they do not really want to or in a way they might find hard. Come and join us outdoors into the woodlands and nature reserves often with a mixed range of other people. Soon you will be able to communicate more freely as there is no pressure to rapidly gain self-confidence. Gain experience working as part of a team and see a project through from the beginning of the session to the end. The more you come out with us the more familiar the work becomes and this in turn improves your physical ability, social skills, and self-esteem. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All staff are trained in child and adult safeguarding. We have worked with people with a range of abilities for over 20 years. We have first-hand insight working with SEND individuals and work with a number of organisations who may also be the primary point of contact with the families. We would welcome additional training opportunities. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We are happy for parents to accompany their children and this is mandatory for some of our sessions. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? We have worked with children, young people and adults with SEND for many years so we are very experienced at communicating appropriately and giving them our time. As always it depends on their needs. One of our staff is a Makaton signer and has a daughter with Angelman’s Syndrome so we are able to communicate well with a broad spectrum of needs. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We have trained ranger staff who have many years of experience of working with people with SEND and they are sensitive to the possible issues that could arise. The work is physical and takes place outdoors in the woodlands therefore it is not suitable for wheelchair access or for some people with certain physical disabilities but we do try to accommodate as many people as possible so it is always worth discussing with us. We welcome carers/support workers as necessary – it’s about what the person needs to enable them to access the opportunity. If you are not sure, just call us to discuss. We have an adapted minibus for transporting people to Green Thursday sessions. We are signatories to the Bucks Disability Volunteer Charter as a commitment to making our opportunities as widely available as possible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Anyone can come along to our Green Thursday sessions meet at 10am at the Rye car park, High Wycombe. However, please contact us before the first session to discuss your situation and also to answer any specific queries. Children under 16 must be supervised by an adult. If you would like to join in one of our weekend sessions please look at the calendar on our website for dates of sessions. Have a look at our Facebook and Twitter pages for the latest information. We offer work experience placements and of course, this is open to people with SEND. For more information please give us a ring or look at our website. If they are part of an organisation, for example, scouts, DofE, youth clubs then we would welcome the opportunity to work with them, just get in touch. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Chiltern Rangers is expanding and we are hoping to attract more people with SEND to join us on these sessions. There will be more opportunities for people to volunteer and participate at the weekend.

name: Chiltern Way Academy (Secondary)
description: Chiltern Way Academy Trust is an award-winning special educational needs academy trust for boys and girls, aged 4 to 19, with Autism Spectrum Conditions (ASC) and Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs. We provide high-quality education and care for the range of needs that exists across the behaviour spectrum. We offer a compassionate and structured environment centred on a purposeful curriculum offer. Mathematics and English are offered at GCSE level and Science are offered at BTEC/GCSE level accompanied by a range of vocational subjects that are key to our primary objective of purposeful employment in the adult world. Our Wendover Campus caters for students 11 to 19 years old that have an Autistic Spectrum Disorder as their primary diagnosis. This is expected to be accompanied by behavioural difficulties and speech language and communication needs in the context of social communication. Our Prestwood Campus caters for students 11 to 19 years old that have difficulties that would be associated with Social, Emotional and Mental Health and/or ASC as their primary diagnosis. As at Prestwood, this is expected to be accompanied by behavioural difficulties and may feature speech language and communication needs in the context of social communication. Our admissions criteria states that students should be assessed in the broadly average cognitive range and that students would not normally display sensory issues that would require a low arousal setting

name: Pony Activity Days
description: We are an Equine Assisted Learning Centre with a difference. A Community Interest Company (not for profit) based near Long Crendon, on the borders of Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire and have been operating for over 12 years. All our staff running the SEN sessions are DBS checked, all are trained in safeguarding for children, First Aid, as well as qualifications in Horse Therapy and Horse care. We continue our training for all staff throughout the year. We are proud of our 5 star rating achieved from Aylesbury Vale Licensing in February 2019, February 2022, and February 2023 Our Special Educational Needs has taken on a new lease of life offering more than just riding. Sensory and connection work form part of each session, working with the child or adult at their own pace and ability. Each lesson is specific to the individual, non-rider or rider alike. We have introduced more core work and coordination for the SEN’s using both pony and other aids, basketball work, and visual aids. Our aim is to continually add to and review all our work we do with the SEN sessions. ​We also specialise in ground-based and riding activities for children, young people and adults with learning, behavioural and physical difficulties, such as autistic spectrum disorders, emotional, social and behavioural difficulties, low confidence, selective mutism, attachment disorders, Down’s syndrome and epilepsy. We also help; troubled youth, stress relief symptoms, depression, anxiety, infantile seizures, intrauterine stroke, cerebral palsy, Parkinson’s disease, paralysis, sensory integration dysfunction, shaken baby syndrome, angel man syndrome and sensory damage. ​The objectives of Horsewyse are to provide activities which benefit the community, to provide equine facilitated learning, to provide activities for children and adults with emotional, social, or behavioural difficulties, and more. Please visit our website to check out our Holiday and Half-term activities.
organisation: Horsewyse, Riding and EFL for children and adults with learning and behavioural difficulties Due to COVID we are not running sessions or BHS lessons during this lockdown. We hope to be up and running in February 2021, and also to offer school holiday activity days. Stay safe. We help children with emotional, learning, and/or behavioural difficulties, including autism, to improve their verbal and non-verbal communication, increase self-awareness, develop team-work, and increase confidence. Includes ground-based work and riding according to the individual person's needs. We also run activity days in school half terms, these are posted on our website. Sessions are available during the weekdays and weekends - please phone or e-mail for availability. name: Pony Activity Days
description: We are an Equine Assisted Learning Centre with a difference. A Community Interest Company (not for profit) based near Long Crendon, on the borders of Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire and have been operating for over 12 years. All our staff running the SEN sessions are DBS checked, all are trained in safeguarding for children, First Aid, as well as qualifications in Horse Therapy and Horse care. We continue our training for all staff throughout the year. We are proud of our 5 star rating achieved from Aylesbury Vale Licensing in February 2019, February 2022, and February 2023 Our Special Educational Needs has taken on a new lease of life offering more than just riding. Sensory and connection work form part of each session, working with the child or adult at their own pace and ability. Each lesson is specific to the individual, non-rider or rider alike. We have introduced more core work and coordination for the SEN’s using both pony and other aids, basketball work, and visual aids. Our aim is to continually add to and review all our work we do with the SEN sessions. ​We also specialise in ground-based and riding activities for children, young people and adults with learning, behavioural and physical difficulties, such as autistic spectrum disorders, emotional, social and behavioural difficulties, low confidence, selective mutism, attachment disorders, Down’s syndrome and epilepsy. We also help; troubled youth, stress relief symptoms, depression, anxiety, infantile seizures, intrauterine stroke, cerebral palsy, Parkinson’s disease, paralysis, sensory integration dysfunction, shaken baby syndrome, angel man syndrome and sensory damage. ​The objectives of Horsewyse are to provide activities which benefit the community, to provide equine facilitated learning, to provide activities for children and adults with emotional, social, or behavioural difficulties, and more. Please visit our website to check out our Holiday and Half-term activities.

description: The group is aimed at family members or friends who are supporting someone with complex emotional needs. name: Chiltern Way Academy (Primary)
description: Chiltern Way Academy Trust is an award-winning special educational needs academy trust for boys and girls, aged 4 to 19 years, with Autism Spectrum Conditions (ASC) and Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs. We provide high-quality education and care for the range of needs that exists across the behaviour spectrum. We offer a compassionate and structured environment centred on a purposeful curriculum offer. Our Bierton Campus educates students from 4 to 11 years and offers a developmental curriculum that encompasses all areas of the primary curriculum. This is supplemented with an enhanced section of the curriculum dedicated to social and emotional growth. Our admissions criteria states that students should be assessed in the broadly average cognitive range and that students would not normally display sensory issues that would require a low arousal setting. Our clear purpose is to make an enduring difference to our students’ lives, providing them with the knowledge, resilience and skills to enable them to have purposeful and lasting employment as they progress into adulthood.

name: Chiltern Wood School
description: Chiltern Wood School is a special school for children aged between 3 and 19 years. We cater for learners with a broad diversity of complex needs, from Profound and Multiple to Severe Speech, Language and Communication Needs and Complex Autistic Spectrum Conditions (PMLD to ASC). We are located on three sites in the High Wycombe area (Downley, Cressex, and Studley Green). The majority of learners come from the local area of High Wycombe, but we have a few students coming from neighbouring local authorities. Learners are taught in small classes (between 5 and 11 pupils) led by a class teacher, with a Senior Support Assistant and Teaching Assistant team. There are seven departments across the school. Studley Green Site - Little Wings – Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and KS1 Severe Learning Difficulties (SLD) and Complex Needs Cressex Site - Rainbow – Primary Complex Needs - Coppice – Secondary SLD - Treetops – Secondary SLD and Complex Needs Downley Site - Woodlands – EYFS – KS5 PMLD - Coral – Primary and Secondary Complex SLD - Gemstones – Primary SLD
organisation: Chiltern Wood School Chiltern Wood School is a special school for 190 children and young people with a broad diversity of complex needs, from Profound and Multiple to Moderate Learning Difficulties (PMLD to MLD). We are located on two sites in the High Wycombe area (Downley and Cressex) and cater for pupils from 3 to 19. Our vision is to further develop specialisms within all our departments, which are as follows: Cressex: Complex Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) age 3 to 19. Complex Speech, Language and Communication Needs, with separate departments within the Early Years, Key Stage 1 and 2 and Key Stage 3 to 5. Downley (co-located with The Downley School): Profound and Multiple Learning Difficulties (PMLD) age 3 to 19. Moderate Speech, Language and Communication Needs (KS2). Chiltern Wood School is the amalgamated school made up of (previously) Chiltern Gate and Maplewood Schools. Both schools have come through a positive change process, and through the hard work and dedication of skilled staff, were both recognised as good at our last inspections. We pride ourselves on putting the well-being of our children and staff at the centre of the learning process, as we believe that sustained success is only seen when embedded in a safe, secure and happy environment. office@chilternwood.bucks.sch.uk https://www.chilternwood.bucks.sch.uk/

local_offer: Needs Supported: Broad diversity of complex needs, from Profound and Multiple Learning Difficulties (PMLD) to Severe Learning Difficulties including autism (SLD). Vision At Chiltern Wood School we want everyone to engage in their learning so by the time they leave us our students have a purpose and they have developed the independence skills that would allow them to have a role in the community around them and enjoy their future lives. Values - Respect - Risk Taking - Nurture - Curiosity - Relationships - Wellbeing - Embedded Therapy https://www.chilternwood.bucks.sch.uk/send-information What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We aim to work with our families and learners to achieve a holistic education setting, where pupils learn and thrive in all areas of their lives. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We have a detailed plan of ongoing training for all staff which includes the following areas: - Curriculum learning and assessment focus training - School Development Areas - Child protection and Safeguarding - Health and Safety - First Aid and medical - including Administration of Medication, gastrostomy feeding, nasal-gastric feeding, De-Fib, epilepsy, anaphylaxis, and so on - Manual Handling - Team Teach - Food hygiene - Wellbeing - Mental health - Speech and Language therapy -including communication - Safe eating and drinking - dysphasia - Occupational therapy - Social communication, emotional regulation, and transactional support – adapted to the school setting - Rebound - Swim teaching In our weekly briefings we have: - De-escalation focus - Word of the week – core board and Makaton sign - Safeguarding focus – monthly - Wellbeing focus - monthly How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Chiltern Wood School we aim to fully include parents and families in the process of working together. This includes: - Initial visits to the school - Home/school messaging using ClassDojo for information exchanges and key messages - Monthly newsletter - Parent Ambassador and Family Support Worker - Parent Events – range of workshops and events arranged each half term - Parent/teacher meetings - End of year school report - Annual review meeting and report - Parent Forum – once a half term alternating in person and online - Parent/carer survey – summer term each year - Parental representation on the Governing Body - Open-door policy within school - Opportunities for parents/carers to book meetings with relevant staff to discuss individual pupils - Parents, families and friends are welcome to attend special events such as special assemblies, sports days, Christmas celebrations, Harvest Festival etc We have a great group of parent volunteers and we are keen for more parents to be involved in this or as part of the Friends of Chiltern Wood School. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Communication is key between families and Chiltern Wood School. This is done in a variety of ways: - Regular ClassDojo messages - Phone calls - Parents Evening/Meetings – either in person or online dependent on what works best for the family - Twice yearly (Pupil Progress and Provision) PPP report - End of year report - Once a year as part of the Annual Review process you will be given a report which outlines the progress your child is making. This will also be discussed at the Annual Review meeting. - In addition, you are welcome to make an appointment to discuss your son or daughter’s progress with school staff at any time throughout the year. All pupils have an SEND and an EHCP How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? All sites are fully accessible, apart from the upstairs part in Cressex as we do not have a lift. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All pupils have an Education, Health and Care Plan EHCP. Pupils will be placed at the school by the Local Authority following a Placement Panel. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are working with the Local Authority to provide additional places for pupils.

description: The Chilterns Neuro Centre is a charity that has been providing a wide range of treatment and support to people with multiple sclerosis (MS) for almost four decades and in 2022 opened up its doors to people affected by Parkinson’s and strokes. We provide comprehensive and holistic care such as physiotherapy, hydrotherapy, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, acupuncture, counselling, occupational therapy and Pilates as well as a wide range of wellbeing groups. We also have a dedicated carer support service as we know that neurological conditions affect loved ones too. The Centre is a charity that enhances the quality of life of individuals, families and communities of people affected by neurological conditions, helping them to live life to the full.
organisation: Chilterns Multiple Sclerosis Centre We have been providing advice and care to people with multiple sclerosis (MS) and their families for 35 years. Our main goal is to help people gain greater control over their MS so that they continue to lead happy and healthy lives. Everyone here understands MS, whether it’s our expert and approachable staff, our fantastic volunteers or one of our over 500 members themselves. MS is endlessly variable, totally unpredictable and can lead to disability. We provide comprehensive and holistic care such as physiotherapy, hydrotherapy, oxygen treatment, acupuncture, counselling, occupational therapy and massage. We also have a dedicated carers support service as we know that MS affects the loved ones of the people with MS too. We also offer several exercise classes and physio sessions via Zoom. The word ‘lifeline’ has often been used to describe the Centre, something that we are incredibly proud of. info@chilternsmscentre.org https://www.chilternsmscentre.org/

name: Alternative Education Provision- Orchard Therapeutic Farm
description: Orchard Therapeutic Farm (OTF) is a primary and secondary and post 16 educational alternative provision. We are a special alternative education provision which caters for pupils who have social, emotional, and mental health difficulties, including associated challenging behaviours. Many of the pupils that attend the alternative education provision have additional special educational needs such as autistic spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit and hyperactive disorders (ADHD) which many affect their speech and language development. Places for pupils are commissioned at the alternative education provision by several local authorities, including Oxfordshire, West Berkshire, Wiltshire, Buckinghamshire, and Slough. Pupils who are referred to the alternative education provision have an education, health and care plan. We are a small and nurturing therapeutic alternative education provision. Our learning community engages pupils and develops positive attitudes toward learning through our farming, enterprise and community work. OTF is set in a beautiful quiet, rural area of Oxford on a Farm. We have a purpose-built teaching space which includes an art room, vocational space and cookery school and extensive grounds, which we use for our animals and woodland activities. we are also able to offer a barn for those Students who need to work on a small ratio, along with our outreach and active programme's The alternative education provision follows a contextualised and practical approach to teaching and learning through its purposeful and appropriate vocational curriculum and farming activities. Orchard Therapeutic Farm is what it says on the tin. We are a smallholding farm, nestled within an apple orchard, with beautiful views and 7 acres of land. With rolling hill views, a lake with pure serenity, that you can only experience once you’re here. Like our apple trees, it is truly ‘scrumptious’.

All parents are encouraged to contribute to their child’s education. name: Chris Davy First Aid Training
description: Chris Davy First Aid Training. I am approved by Qualsafe Awards, an awarding organisation recognised by Ofqual to offer regulated qualifications. I teach a variety of courses tailored to the needs of clients. My courses include include: - Level 3 PFA (meets the requirements of Ofsted) - Level 3 EPFA - Level 3 FAW - Level 3 EFAW - AED - Basic Life Support Adults and Children - Epipen - Combined FAW and Paediatric - Activity First Aid - First Aid Essentials - CitizenAID - Forestry First Aid - Level 2 Safeguarding - Protecting Children and Young People and Adults at Risk Many of my courses give learners the option of Catastrophic bleeding. Non Qualsafe Awards courses: I offer FLAT STAN First Aid training workshops for pre-school age upwards. Children will have fun learning some First Aid and receive a booklet and certificate. For older primary/junior school-age children I offer First Aid training with a workbook and certificate of attendance. I also offer 'Super Medics' training, a First Aid programme for ages 8 to 14 years. The training given is adapted to the age group and fits well as a part of a school's PHSE lessons. All children receive a Super Medics reference book. I offer bespoke courses with a certificate of attendance and give talks relative to specific First Aid and health-related conditions on request. I am happy to undertake courses in a home environment if clients prefer. Further information may be obtained through my website.

We firmly believe that in order to do this, our role as an early years provider is to facilitate ‘opportunities without limits’. Our ethos is to support every child’s natural intrinsic, motivation to explore, find out and connect. We recognise the fundamental role that our colleagues play in expediting our vision for children. We are committed to securing a working environment that actively seeks to support individual progression, recognising each team member’s natural flair and providing a myriad of learning experiences for continued professional development. Instead of narrowing the curriculum in pursuit of standards, we offer a rich breadth of experience for both the children and colleagues.

local_offer: At The Beaconsfield all children are treated with the same care and respect regardless of their needs. Staff are able to support individual care plans and needs. If staff have any concerns around children's development these are raised with the parents straight away ensuring early intervention. We carry out settling in session with every child and this is then tailored to their individual needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Each outcome we aim to achieve is unique to the individual child, to identify where we can help support their growth and development based on the additional need the child has. This is supported by working in partnership with care specialists and the parents to help support working towards the same goal. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents meetings/evenings to discuss the child's development based on child assessments carried out on the child throughout the year. Open door policy for parents to communicate any worries/concerns they have around the child's development. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? The half-year assessments to identify growth and areas that may need support; monthly "next step goals based on the individual child which is evidenced through observation that highlights the child's achievements and learning based on the EYFS. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?  How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Applying for space within the setting, meeting to discuss needs before the start date to identify the child's needs so that we can plan effectively to support the individual and possibly add/remove resources from the environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Up-to-date training, reviewing resources and learning goals and development for individual children.

description: Team Green\: My name is Chrissie. I have four gorgeous children from toddler to primary school age. We have three dogs: Olive, Oreo and Bailey and two cats, Rosie and Marie, who are normally chilling somewhere. I work alongside my husband, Adam, and he is fantastic with the children. Together, we take a team approach and are 'Team Green'. About us: We enjoy walks with the dogs up the woods, especially day trips, and have a severe love of all things Disney. We truly are big kids at heart. We love cooking, as well as being outside when the weather is nice. We are honoured to have a large garden, so the aim is to provide outdoor learning, weather permitting. We offer a variety of opportunities, and follow a thorough inclusion policy that is embedded in our ethos and curriculum, which includes all cultures, races, dietary requirements, as well as all aspects of SEND that come our way. We also have various training, this includes a variety of disabilities and needs and some quite specialist training, for example, dysphagia; OT, Physio. We offer a home-from-home learning environment with lots of childcare experience and qualifications. We also offer funded places, accept childcare vouchers and the tax-free childcare scheme. We hope that you are happy with choosing us. Any questions, please ask. We offer an open-door policy. Chrissie

local_offer: We are a husband and wife team who work together to provide the best home from home learning environment for any child. We aim to give each family the opportunity to access care whatever their need may be. We include any child in all activities working in an atmosphere where learning through play is key and the age and stage of the child is followed to ensure they are enjoying and achieving. We have had various training in specialist courses and are always keen to improve our knowledge to help the children. We have a can do attitude here where every child is valued and encouraged to try their best. How does the early years setting know if children need extra help and what should I do if I think my child may have Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities? At Team Green we closely follow the EYFS and track all children and their development. We always work in partnership with parents and this is especially key with SEND children. If we observe any concerns we will record and raise these with parent’s; this may be through constant tracking, observation and planning or through the 2 year check which we carry out with all age appropriate children to ensure that any concerns for development will be discussed and a plan of action put into place of how we can help. We gather permission from the go from parents to share information with other agencies should the need arise as working with parents and these agencies getting early help for children is proven to help any needs in the long run. An ‘All About me’ is discussed with parents when any child starts at the setting and any needs identified. This provides starting points for their learning journeys and parents are encouraged to contribute to these; we ask parents in to view them usually with a cup of tea. We regularly ask for feedback from parents for any praise or concerns, through email, questionnaires and by phone; and have an open door policy here at Team Green. How will the early years setting support my child? At Team Green we are continuously working to help the children thrive here. We believe in learning through play planning and observation; which encourages development as when a person enjoys something they will learn without thinking; it is an in built desire to learn. This goes for any child; however small the achievement it is celebrated here as any progress is good for that specific child. We strive to encourage the children to meet milestones according to the EYFS and adapt activities to suit the children’s capabilities and likes. We work closely with parents to ensure continuity within the child’s life. We provide a safe and secure environment so that the children’s emotional well-being needs can be met; building their confidence and self esteem. How will the curriculum be matched to my child’s SEND needs? We believe every child is unique; and provide a learning-through-play environment. This means that we are able to adapt activities and resources to match the child’s needs with or without SEND. We provide guidance, support and encouragement to try new things; and through observations and planning are able to support the children with next steps in their personal development. We follow the EYFS curriculum for a child in Early Years and tailor activities to suit each child. We explore and go on adventures; which are fully inclusive to all children and this looks at different parts of the curriculum; as we believe learning opportunities are all around us. What support will there be for my child’s overall well being? We work closely with other agencies to ensure that a child as a whole is safe and secure; both emotionally and physically. We can signpost you to other support networks; as well as what we can provide ourselves. How will a child with SEND be included in activities outside the setting? When planning activities we take into account the needs of all the children in the setting. A risk assessment is carried out and adaptations if any will be made ensuring wheelchair or pushchair accessible. How will the staff prepare and support a child with SEND to join the setting or transfer to a new setting/school? We work closely with any person or organisation involved in transitions, passing on information; as parents will have given permission to do so when starting at Team Green. We are happy for any new teacher’s or new carers to visit us in the setting. We will also provide activities to get children ready for their new setting as well as settling in sessions for those coming in new to us. How are the setting’s resources allocated and matched to a child’s Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities? We are always looking at additional funding and there are extra sources available for SEND children. We have a variety of resources for any child here and always look at adapting activities to suit individual children and their needs. How is the decision made about what type and how much support a child with SEND will receive? With our planning and observations we are able to track development. From here we are able to work on areas, which need the extra help. We also work closely with other agencies and can get referrals in place with them to better support your child. We have support from other professionals. From here we will work with agencies and parents to ensure that the child is receiving the correct support. We also are able to complete plans such as the SEN plan with parents and other partners in the child’s life to ensure continuity throughout. Thanks Adam and Chrissie  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have access to and have accessed. variety of resources; including working with SALT; advisers from county for SEN, Occupational Therapists, physios, social workers. We will always look at who else might be needed for individual children and will access these as they are required. Chrissie has varied SEN knowledge due to outside commitments such as previous SEND governor at Bedgrove Infant School so is able to understand what is needed to be in place to support children who might be then attending school and pre School. Chrissie is also a qualified SENCO. We also are already working with physiotherapists and occupational therapists as well as dieticians and the paediatricians at Stoke Mandeville. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? CPD is always ongoing and when new areas come up they are looked at. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We welcome parents coming to visit; parent questionnaires etc. We encourage all children on large outings such as the farm or beach and if not contracted days ask parents along with the children who are not normally here. We incorporate parents in the learning of their children and keep them updated. We use WhatsApp for messaging any special moments or just a keeping in touch basis if needed during the day. This way you can receive up to date photos of what your child might be doing at Team Green. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Every child has the right to have their information shared as accessing the right information and people for individual is key. Working in partnership with parents is what childminders should be doing in every aspect not just with children with SEND. At every step of the way parent's will be a main concern of what is best for that child. We would look at what would be needed for that child. This might be more frequent meetings, a detailed paper diary instead of a verbal handover, we will adapt. The impact that the learning will be having on each child will be individual and for some the little steps might be smaller than others but it is important that each child is unique in what they require so this would be communicated frequently with parents and other professionals. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We operate mainly on the ground floor of our house; and whilst there is a small step both at the front and rear of the house; the toilet and washing facilities are located downstairs, we do have a cabin playroom accessible by steps. We have a large car that does have space for a wheelchair if needed, we are accessible by a variety of transport methods because of our location. We are able to make small adaptions if needed to be able to be as inclusive as possible to each child's needs. We have been known to purchase additional resources needed; work with Occupational Therapists to ensure that the environment is best suited to a child's specific requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We work closely with any person or organisation involved in transitions, passing on information; as parents will have given permission to do so when starting at Team Green. We are happy for any new teacher’s or new carers to visit us in the setting. We will also provide activities to get children ready for their new setting as well as settling in sessions for those coming in new to us. We visit new settings to speak with new members of their teams to ensure that all information is shared. We are also able to assist with transitions that might be within the home, such as moving house; new baby etcetera. We have a lot of resources to help with this, and will ask for help from the right people if we do not know the next step or the answer. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We have worked with other professionals such as paediatricians, physios, occupational therapists, private SALT; etc to help the children that need a little extra support or put in place EHCP. For Adam he will be incorporating this into part of his CPD however he has also worked with Occupational therapy, SALT and the SEN advisers from county. We are always open to taking on any children, SEN or not so this developing this area just depends on the specific children to which area out training might take us as we will always look at training that might be needed to support an individual child within our care.

organisation: S4A Group Ltd, Sports Development and School PE Provision S4A offer holiday camps in Buckingham, Grendon Underwood and Patishall. Providing childcare during the school holidays. We offer activities such as football, basketball, science and seasonal craft activities, a full list of which can be found on the s4a website. S4A also work in 13 different schools in Buckingham and surrounding areas providing high-quality PE provision. We teach a huge variety of different Sports with our coaches' being highly qualified in a range of Sports. We tailor our lesson plans to suit each classes specific needs, giving children the opportunity to learn new skills and develop existing ones whilst always maintaining the importance of enjoyment and fun. As well as providing PE provision in these schools we also provide extended care across in the area. We run breakfast and after school clubs offering a range of activities tailored to meet the interests of the children in attendance, from science clubs to sports clubs S4A cater for all. Helping them develop physically, emotionally, socially and mentally in an environment that is fun and exciting. S4A Development is about helping children reaching ''their'' next level. Our Boys and Girls Development Centre sessions are on a Monday evening in Buckingham with our Juniors section on a Saturday morning in Buckingham and Gawcott. All sessions are professionally designed and delivered in line with the 'England DNA' to offer a player-focused approach and develop players on an individual basis while allowing them to progress at their own speed and in a low pressure but testing environment. description: We know school holidays can be a juggling act — finding the right balance between giving your child a fun, active break and making sure they’re in safe hands. That’s where S4A Holiday Clubs at Wingrave come in. Our holiday clubs are designed to give children the chance to enjoy a wide range of activities, make new friends, and build confidence, all while you have peace of mind knowing they are well cared for by our qualified and friendly team. What Makes Our Holiday Club Different? ✔ Something for Everyone – Whether your child enjoys sports, arts and crafts, outdoor games, or themed days, there’s plenty to keep them engaged. ✔ A Safe, Friendly Space – Our experienced team makes sure every child feels welcome, included, and supported. ✔ Flexible Options – We know every family’s schedule is different, so you can book just the days that work for you. ✔ A Chance to Build Friendships – With children from different schools attending, it’s a great way for your child to meet new people and grow their confidence. 📅 Theme Days: 🏐 Dodgeball Day • 👩‍🍳 Cooking Day • 🎯 Multi-Activity Day • ✨ Glowventure Day • 🎪 Carnival Day There’s always something to suit your child’s interests – whether they’re into sports, games, arts and crafts, or just want to try something new. We also understand how important flexibility is, so we’ve made it easy to adjust bookings if your plans change. If you’re using childcare vouchers, we’ve kept that process simple too. If you have any questions or need any help, our friendly team is happy to assist — you can email us at info@s4aclub.co.uk, or give us a call at 01280 460560. We look forward to helping your child have a fun, active, and memorable Summer Holidays!
organisation: S4A Group Ltd, Sports Development and School PE Provision S4A offer holiday camps in Buckingham, Grendon Underwood and Patishall. Providing childcare during the school holidays. We offer activities such as football, basketball, science and seasonal craft activities, a full list of which can be found on the s4a website. S4A also work in 13 different schools in Buckingham and surrounding areas providing high-quality PE provision. We teach a huge variety of different Sports with our coaches' being highly qualified in a range of Sports. We tailor our lesson plans to suit each classes specific needs, giving children the opportunity to learn new skills and develop existing ones whilst always maintaining the importance of enjoyment and fun. As well as providing PE provision in these schools we also provide extended care across in the area. We run breakfast and after school clubs offering a range of activities tailored to meet the interests of the children in attendance, from science clubs to sports clubs S4A cater for all. Helping them develop physically, emotionally, socially and mentally in an environment that is fun and exciting. S4A Development is about helping children reaching ''their'' next level. Our Boys and Girls Development Centre sessions are on a Monday evening in Buckingham with our Juniors section on a Saturday morning in Buckingham and Gawcott. All sessions are professionally designed and delivered in line with the 'England DNA' to offer a player-focused approach and develop players on an individual basis while allowing them to progress at their own speed and in a low pressure but testing environment. All skills and attributes developed will be in the following areas: Technical/ Tactical/ Physical/ Psychological and Social. matt.ogle@s4asports.co.uk https://s4asports.co.uk

description: Autism Early Support's Circle Centre Nursery has been pioneering early support for autistic children and children with communication, interaction and sensory differences (2 to 5 years) since 2001. The nursery has a multidisciplinary team of specialist teachers, a speech and language therapist, an occupational therapist and learning support co-ordinators/assistants who design, develop and implement individually tailored educational plans for each child. Our specialist team create desirable and predictable learning environments that give children the tools and confidence they need to communicate, play and explore the world around them. By the time the child leaves our setting, their parents have a detailed, robust analysis of their child's needs, preferences, challenges and strengths; critical for their understanding of their child's educational needs and for the team who will look after their child in their next setting. We believe every child should have the chance to find their place in the world, be able to communicate their needs and learn alongside their peers with acceptance and support.

local_offer: Autism Early Support Trust Limited (AES) delivers early support and specialist education to autistic children and children with sensory, communication and interaction differences. In tandem, we provide a comprehensive programme of support for their parents. Founded in 2001, we support families from Buckinghamshire and the surrounding counties. We believe every child has the right to timely and appropriate, high-quality education and that they should be given the best chance to find their place in the world, communicate their needs, and learn alongside their peers with acceptance and support. We believe their parents should be equipped with strategies and knowledge to fully support and advocate for their child. Our positive impact is achieved by supporting children to navigate their feelings and learn new communication and interaction skills and by giving parents peer support, practical solutions and guidance. The differences can be monumental to family life. Our Approach: Our early support and specialist education encompasses specific, structured and targeted neuroaffirmative approaches founded on established research, evidence-based practice and our extensive experience. Through our services, we aim to equip all children with the tools and confidence they need to communicate, play and explore the world around them. In response to the child’s needs, wants and preferences, we make environmental adaptations and create the supports a child needs to feel ready to learn. We are: child-led, needs-led, focussed on a child's strengths, and neurodiverse affirming. Our Circle Centre nursery has been pioneering early support for autistic children and children with communication, sensory and interaction differences (2 to 5 years) since 2001. The nursery has a multidisciplinary team of specialist teachers, a speech and language therapist, an occupational therapist and learning support co-ordinators/assistants who design, develop and implement individually tailored educational plans for each child. Additional support is available through our Outreach Service, which has multiple programmes supporting families and autistic children (2 to 12 years) in the community (including homes, schools and early years settings) and online. These programmes include: The Parent’s Portal: This online portal is a game-changer for families as it offers resources to watch and read; live and recorded workshops; and online discussion forums (free access for Circle Centre parents). Parent Support Groups: These weekly online sessions for families offer emotional support, practical guidance and knowledge sharing in a kind, safe and non-judgemental space (free access for Circle Centre parents). Assessments and Support Packages: We work directly with children in their homes, school or early years setting to provide speech and language or occupational therapy assessments and support packages (additional charges apply).  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Through our services, we aim to equip all children with the tools and confidence they need to communicate, play and explore the world around them. In response to the child’s needs, wants and preferences, we make environmental adaptations and create the supports a child needs to feel ready to learn. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? All of our team undergo in house and external training that is specific to developing knowledge, understanding and approaches related to autistic children. We listen to and believe there is always more to learn from the neurodivergent population. We strive to adapt and tailor our support to reflect these perspectives. All of our staff undergo training related to the SCERTS framework and early years education. We are: Child-led. We look at everything through the child’s lens first, their well-being and happiness is always our priority. We focus on understanding and appreciating the child’s perspective, we do not work towards trying to change them. We accommodate each child’s needs to maximise independence and use their skills and strengths to enable the child to thrive, learn and develop. Needs-led. Regardless of diagnosis, we listen to the parent, we observe the child and we work with them to support the areas of need. Focussed on child’s strengths We design our support around the child’s strength, interests and preferences to optimise engagement and enable the child to thrive. Neurodiversity affirmative. We recognise that there a different ways of thinking, communicating and learning. We listen to and believe there is always more to learn from the neurodivergent population. We strive to adapt and tailor our support to reflect these perspectives. We are collaborative. The children and families we work with teach us so much. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? Parents play an incredibly important role at the Circle Centre nursery and we work alongside them throughout the time their child is at the nursery. Dialogue between parents and our team is key, for instance, at the end of each sessions, there is an allocated 'handover' time where parents can speak to practitioners and celebrate any successes from the day or share any concerns. Information is also shared with parents through Tapestry, an online learning journal, so that parents can view a record of their child's experiences and also share experiences from home. Every half term we sent families a newsletter that includes information about themes, learning topics, ideas and useful information for the weeks ahead. For new children, parent's are invited to a meeting with the child's allocated key worker and a teacher or therapist, so they can discuss who they are settling in. And all parents are invited to meet with a teacher and/or therapist, on a termly basis, to talk through progress and review targets. Finally, nursery parents are given free access to our online platform - The Parent's Portal - where they can access online resources, join live virtual workshops and take part in Parent Support Groups. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? For children new to the setting, parents are invited to attend a meeting with the child’s key worker and teacher, or therapist, so that you can discuss how your child is settling in. All children attending the nursery have been identified as having special education needs (SEND) and therefore each child has an individualised SEN support plan. All parents are then invited to a meeting with a teacher and/or therapists to talk through progress and review targets collaboratively (ADPR). These meetings will then take place termly to review and agree targets and supports. We support families through the SEN process including guidance and support in relation to the Education Health Care Plan (EHC) process. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Our nursery provides a specialist environment with educational/therapeutic approaches which are considerate of sensory and communication differences that a an autistic child may experience. We provide a highly structured session in a stimulating but uncluttered ‘low arousal’ environment. We have three main teaching rooms including a messy play space and soft play room, sensory room with specialist sensory resources, specialist communication resources and a wide variety of high-quality toys and other equipment. Our outside areas include a sensory garden and soft tarmac play area. The Specialist Nursery is all on one level and we will do all it can to ensure any child who may have mobility difficulties can be accommodated. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have comprehensive and carefully planned procedures for children joining and moving on from our setting. We ensure we carry out a comprehensive parent discussion and screening assessment that is carried out online prior to joining the nursery. The child is invited to a short taster session for an hour before starting full sessions. Transition to the child’s next setting is planned along with the child’s next school and parents. Autistic children and children with communication, sensory and interaction differences need to have aspects of the curriculum presented to them in a way that takes account of their unique learning styles. This means that, especially in the early years, methods and approaches which may be appropriate for neuro-typical children, will not necessarily help autistic children to access learning opportunities in the same way. Curriculum plans at the Autism Early Support Trust Limited (AES) nursery reflect a balance between the unique needs of each individual child and the broad and balanced requirements of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum. Our nursery is staffed by practitioners with specific expertise in this field. The nursery has two specialist teachers, one teacher will be allocated to your child as a key contact. Teachers and therapists work alongside learning support assistants and nursery coordinators and carry out assessment, contribute and participate in the SEN process (e.g. establish and implementing Special Education Need Support plans, termly targets, reviews, Education Health Care Plans). The teachers are responsible for ensuring that planning and supports are in place to promote learning and access to the curriculum. Our therapists work closely with the team to ensure that there are strategies and adaptations in placed to support communication and sensory differences children may experience. They will support and lead some small group learning activities (e.g. fun with food). Therapists will undertake the development and implementation of individualised ‘regulation support plans’. Some children will benefit from further therapeutic support but this will be determined by their specific needs after assessment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Autism Early Support's strategic plan includes ambitions to expand our Outreach Services to deliver a more comprehensive programme of support in the community.

name: Circle Centre Nursery, Autism Early Support
description: Autism Early Support's Circle Centre Nursery has been pioneering early support for autistic children and children with communication, interaction and sensory differences (2 to 5 years) since 2001. The nursery has a multidisciplinary team of specialist teachers, a speech and language therapist, an occupational therapist and learning support co-ordinators/assistants who design, develop and implement individually tailored educational plans for each child. Our specialist team create desirable and predictable learning environments that give children the tools and confidence they need to communicate, play and explore the world around them. By the time the child leaves our setting, their parents have a detailed, robust analysis of their child's needs, preferences, challenges and strengths; critical for their understanding of their child's educational needs and for the team who will look after their child in their next setting. We believe every child should have the chance to find their place in the world, be able to communicate their needs and learn alongside their peers with acceptance and support.

local_offer: Each child will need different support and we will support in the best way we can for their individual needs.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?  What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Buds that Blossom we have an open environment that is welcoming and friendly to ensure parents/carers feel at ease to share information regarding their children. We have many opportunities for parents to have a chat with their child’s key person and other staff within the room. In addition to this, we also have Famly so parents/carers get regular updates about their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children have a Famly account where observations will be made and they will be tracked according to developmental stages they have reached. We will also do 2-year checks on children and carry out summary assessments when we update the child’s tracking each term. For children with SEND, we would have more information to share and discuss so we would ensure to have more regular meetings with parents to keep everyone up to date. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take the needs of the children into account when planning and amending our environment. We use baby signs with the children to assist communication and have many sensory toys to promote sensory development. We have made a quiet area within each room to ensure that children have the opportunity to recuperate and relax. Access to our building is wheelchair friendly. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have transition paperwork that will be filled in when moving between the two rooms. Each individual child will have a folder with all the developmental progress, tracking and support in which can be handed to their new key person or shared with a new setting. We encourage lots of communication with parents/carers at this vital time and to have visits with their new key person/setting to ensure that the transfer process can run as smoothly as possible and they have the best understanding of the children. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? speech and language courses

description: At Twyford C of E School we strive to provide our children with an exciting, challenging and meaningful start to their learning journey. Our Early Years curriculum is designed to provide a broad and balanced education filled with rich and varied experiences to meet the needs and interests of all pupils. It is our intention that children experience the seven areas of learning through a balance of whole class/group teaching and play based learning. This is achieved through reflective and responsive practice that takes into account the children’s interests and needs, engaging themes and challenging continuous provision activities. Learning is carefully planned by the staff to support communication and language development; personal, social and emotional development; and physical development as well as literacy, mathematics, understanding of the world and expressive arts and design. We recognise the importance of partnership with parents and carers and work together with them to inspire independent, happy learners who thrive in our school and reach their full potential as they embark on their educational journey through the Early Years and beyond.

local_offer: I am an Ofsted registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a registered childminder, I have a Key Contact at Buckinghamshire Council with the Early Years Team, and with parental permission, I may contact them for further advice. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites…) are available for us to access. I welcome other professionals into the setting who may have involvement with a child and I am keen to access further training to support a child’s development for example speech and language (Speech Therapist). I am happy to attend Multi-Professionals Meetings if required What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and we will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a small step leading to the front door but easy access via a side entrance. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible for example adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they have the opportunity to visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

name: Claire Gordon
description: I'm an Ofsted registered childminder located in Hazlemere, HP15. I offer funded hours to qualifying parents. Children play and learn in a warm, welcoming home from home environment. I work to nurture each child’s natural desire to learn and understand the world around them through a mix of adult and child-led play, and following their interests. Children are unique, naturally curious and thrive in mixed-age environments focused on hands-on discovery and self-motivated growth. I place emphasis on independence and learning new applicable life skills. It is very important for children to spend time outdoors and to have a variety of experiences to develop a rich understanding of the world, the community and themselves. We visit local parks, meadows and woodlands, museums, National Trust sites, farms, animal sanctuaries, the library, the local green grocer and many others. I work with a co-childminder and her childminded children, which gives the benefit of experiencing two teaching styles, two adults on hand, and having lots of friends with which to socialise. I work in partnership with parents and other early years providers to ensure the best outcomes possible for each child. I provide wraparound care for Cedar Park Nursery and Cedar Park school in Hazlemere.

name: Marlow Local History Museum
description: We provide a museum of local history for Marlow and five surrounding parishes: Bisham, Little Marlow, Great Marlow, Marlow Bottom and Medmenham. The museum is of modest size and is run entirely by volunteers. Our plan is to get bigger. We have changing exhibitions, one-off events, and activities for children. We also work with local schools for educational visits and with care homes for reminiscences. We produce our own booklets of Marlow history which are for sale in Marlow library and other local places, as well as the museum. We are currently working towards Accreditation with Arts Council England. We are open Weds 2pm to 5pm and Sat and Sun afternoons 1 to 5pm from March to end of October. In winter, November to February , we are only open on Sundays from 2 to 4pm.

name: Wellbeing Services
description: Our wellbeing groups provide activities based around the Five Ways to Wellbeing: connect, be active, take notice, keep learning, and give. We aim to support your wellbeing and mood through activities such as art, crafting, cooking, interactive games, and group discussion. When possible, groups may go on outings and day trips to enjoy activities such as walking or bowling. Wellbeing groups are held in Aylesbury, High Wycombe, Chesham, and Chalfont St Peter, but are open to anyone aged 18 plus living in Bucks who is experiencing moderate to severe mental health difficulties. Wellbeing groups support you in your recovery journey and enable you to become more confident and independent. This can play a crucial role in an your recovery, leading to engagement with activities in the community, volunteering, and even paid work. We recognise that the social aspects of the groups are as important as the activity and we enable you to try new things in a supportive environment with others who have had similar experiences. You are supported by experienced Wellbeing Workers and fully trained volunteers . All standard materials and resources are provided. Once we receive your referral, you will be invited to visit the group with your referrer, where you will have the opportunity to try the group and meet other service users. When you are sure that the group is the right setting, we will agree a start date with you. Everyone will remember how they felt on their first day at the groups, so will try to help you feel as welcome as possible. You will be ‘Buddied’ with either a staff member, volunteer, or another person we support to help you settle in. Buckinghamshire Mind’s Wellbeing Service is self-funding and, for the service to continue, it is necessary to charge a fee. If you are being referred through the Community Mental Health Team or Adult Social Care you may be entitled to funding to help you pay for this.

local_offer: We are a mainstream, community primary school accommodating children from Nursery (3 Years old) to Year 6 (11 years old). Waterside Primary Academy is committed to providing a high quality and challenging education for all of our children. We believe every child is entitled to reach their highest level of personal achievement.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Waterside Primary Academy believes that educational inclusion embraces diversity and equal opportunities for all learners, regardless of their age, gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, attainment or background. We ensure that we provide inclusive, broad educational opportunities in order to meet the differing needs of our children. We are committed to removing barriers to learning and meeting the needs of our learners. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? We embrace our responsibility to ensure each and every child fulfils their potential and experiences success, including children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). name: Rape and Sexual Abuse Support Service (RSASS)
description: Free, confidential support for anyone affected by sexual violence or abuse. RSASS provides specialist support, information, and advocacy for people aged 16 and over who have experienced any form of sexual violence, whether recent or non-recent. We support people of all genders, backgrounds, and identities across South Buckinghamshire and Slough, offering a safe and non-judgemental space to be heard, believed, and supported. Our trained team can help if you have experienced rape, sexual assault, sexual harassment, childhood sexual abuse, domestic abuse, forced marriage, so-called honour-based violence, Female Genital Mutilation (FGM), or stalking. Support available includes: - Confidential helpline and telephone support - Specialist one-to-one counselling (in person or online) - Advocacy and practical support for appointments, housing, or health needs - Independent Sexual Violence Advocacy (ISVA) to guide and support you through the criminal justice process - Peer and group support to connect safely with others who have had similar experiences We are here for you. We will listen. We believe you.
