local_offer: Running Rabbits is an all-inclusive and supportive setting, that encourages the involvement and engagement of all. All staff are trained and knowledgeable in supporting and caring for children. Running Rabbits supports all children to be happy, respected and engaged to allow them to thrive in their first experience of education.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Through implementation of activities and play, designed and curated around the EYFS, we want all our children to be happy, independent, confident and inquisitive learners who feel valued, respected and included. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Our SENCO has completed numerous relevant training including, the role of the SENCO, Autism and ADHD, Supporting Downs Syndrome, and Awareness of Sign Language. All staff complete the following courses as part of their core training: Special Educational Needs, Safeguarding, and First Aid. Additional courses are completed frequently by our SENCO and all staff to raise awareness and good practice. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We encourage parent interaction and engagement through observations on the Learning Journey app (both from the setting and home), inviting them in for special events such as theme activities, stay and play sessions etc. Parents are also engaged through newsletters, home learning challenges and involvement in outings and visits. In addition, when a child starts at the nursery the parent will complete What My Child Can Do, All About Me and All About My Family forms that directly informs the key worker and nursery about the child and the family. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All our staff are approachable for parents, and parents have numerous opportunities and channels to contact and engage with staff e.g. email, through the Family app, parents evenings, daily feedback. All children have an assigned key person, who is a direct point of contact for the child and family. Dependent on the needs of the individual child, a Health Care Plan may be completed to assess and ensure that the needs of the child are being met. Parents are directly involved in this process, as well as reviews of the plan, and encouraged to inform and advise the nursery of any changes or developments to their child’s needs. Children with additional needs will be monitored and observed on a regular basis and parent input/meetings conducted frequently to ensure consistency of care and relevance of current targets and achievements. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Dependent on individual needs of children and families, the nursery makes reasonable adjustments to the environment and provision to ensure that everyone can engage and develop, both indoors and outdoors. Activities are adapted and personalised to suit individuals. Every room has varying areas such as quiet corners, messy play and more, allowing children to choose where they want to explore and engage. Our vast outdoor space allows children to connect with nature and explore their natural environment in a safe and secure space. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We liaise with and work alongside local schools, settings and families to facilitate smooth transitions and access to our setting. Parents and children are invited for settle visits when they start at the nursery, allowing the key worker and family to get to know each other. Relevant information and knowledge are shared between settings and professionals to support any family, either joining or leaving our nursery for continuity of care. This can include visits to and from settings of key workers or teachers, meetings with involved professionals and parent input. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Our sensory room is now open. We aim to continue and enhance this lovely area.

Pupils with SEND have an individual learning plan (ILP) which is created and maintained in conjunction with relevant school staff and the family. A pupil’s SEND needs will be identified as early as possible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Close discussion with parents is strongly recommended and is a requirement of our entrance procedures in order to ensure we can provide the right learning environment for the pupil. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Dair House School will recommend the use of outside agencies when appropriate.

description: Looking for a magical family day out? Enjoy a great selection of rides, shows and attractions at Gulliver's Land Milton Keynes. We’re a family-run theme park designed for children aged between 2 to 13. From the Runaway Train in Discovery Bay to the Jungle River Ride, there are plenty of exciting rides to ensure that all the family have a fun day out. There are also a number of rides and play areas designed for toddlers. We don’t have lots of additional theme park prices, parking is completely free. Save big on your giant adventure by booking theme park tickets at least two days in advance. If you want to extend the fun then explore the fantastic accommodation options available at the Adventurers Village Milton Keynes. Choose from themed lodges, cabins, dens and campsite pitches.

description: Expect Respect is a prevention toolkit that will help you to lead sessions around healthy relationships for children and young people aged 4 to 18. It contains age-appropriate activities that can be used in a range of spaces, but it can also be used with adults. It will help you to hold conversations about the root causes of violence, and educate young people on gender-based violence. Each session in the toolkit is designed to be active, fun and engaging, but also challenging. In order to access the Expect Respect toolkit and deliver it to children and young people, you will need to receive training to become an Expect Respect advocate. name: Monkey Music (Marlow)
description: Monkey Music Classes in Marlow run on Tuesdays. You will spend quality time with your little one; helping their learning and exploration as well as enjoying your time together. We have classes suitable for babies from 12 weeks, for toddlers and for those older little ones. For those clever older little monkeys of preschool age, we have our wonderful Ding-Dong curriculum where little ones are introduced to instruments of the orchestra and progress to beating crotchet, quaver and crotchet rest rhythms, a fantastic basis for learning a musical instrument when they are older. Monkey Music is fun and educational too. Our classes are grouped according to 4 age groups so that classes are tailored to the exact age of the child. Claire, who owns and runs Monkey Music Amersham, Beaconsfield and The Chalfonts is a former Monkey Music parent herself, loves music and plays piano and clarinet. She is a mum of two and works with Elen, Claire, and Lara to bring you lessons over the course of the week. We have four different classes where children are grouped according to their age, and this means that classes can be tailored to the social, linguistic, and musical development of that particular age group. Classes are small of no more than 15 in a class, so that the teacher can get to know your child and notice his or her progression. The Marlow venue is Christ Church United Reformed Church on Oxford Road near Sainsbury's car park. It does have its own car park with a small number of spaces at the front of the car park, but mums also park in the pay and display car park behind Sainsbury's.

name: Caudwell Youth Volunteer Mentoring for At-risk Young People
description: Caudwell Youth mentors at-risk young people aged 11 to 24 years into new futures over a period of 2 years. Founded in 2022 by four senior leaders with experience of charity-led mentoring provision and philanthropist John Caudwell. We are determined to ensure that the needs of at-risk young people are properly addressed. We currently work across Buckinghamshire. • Young people are referred to us by local partners including; local authorities, schools/colleges, youth offending teams, exploitation hubs, social workers, families, NHS (including CAMHS), Department for Work and Pensions, multi-agency safeguarding hubs, and charity partners. Individuals can also refer to us. • We provide a package of one to one person-centred mentoring and support to empower young people to build upon their strengths and resilience and fulfil their potential. • We match each young person with a trained volunteer mentor who has similar interests, an understanding, and, where suitable, lived experience of the challenges they are facing. • Through a trauma informed approach, we enable effective transition from isolation, exclusion, trauma, low self-esteem and harmful associations to positive choices, re-engagement with education, training, independent living, employment, building resilience, and making a positive contribution to communities.

name: Caudwell Youth Volunteer Mentoring for At-risk Young People
description: Caudwell Youth mentors at-risk young people aged 11 to 24 years into new futures over a period of 2 years. Founded in 2022 by four senior leaders with experience of charity-led mentoring provision and philanthropist John Caudwell. We are determined to ensure that the needs of at-risk young people are properly addressed. We currently work across Buckinghamshire. • Young people are referred to us by local partners including; local authorities, schools/colleges, youth offending teams, exploitation hubs, social workers, families, NHS (including CAMHS), Department for Work and Pensions, multi-agency safeguarding hubs, and charity partners. Individuals can also refer to us. • We provide a package of one to one person-centred mentoring and support to empower young people to build upon their strengths and resilience and fulfil their potential. • We match each young person with a trained volunteer mentor who has similar interests, an understanding, and, where suitable, lived experience of the challenges they are facing. • Through a trauma informed approach, we enable effective transition from isolation, exclusion, trauma, low self-esteem and harmful associations to positive choices, re-engagement with education, training, independent living, employment, building resilience, and making a positive contribution to communities.

name: Co-parenting - Keeping Your Child in Mind - Adults Working Together
description: The Keeping Your Child in Mind programme is for parents and carers of children of any age and aims to support parents / those in a parenting role with challenges with the parent-to-parent / co-parenting relationship. Session aims: Session 1: Self Awareness Session 2: Appropriate Expectations Session 3: Boundaries and Positive Discipline Session 4: Understanding Empathy The word “parents” in this context refers to anyone in a parenting role, for example, carers, grandparents, aunties, or uncles. This course is for parents who are ready to engage and can reflect on their own relationships, communication styles, and parenting to make positive changes for themselves and their child(ren). Using knowledge and research about the impact of parental conflict on families, the sessions will increase parents' understanding of the influence of parental relationships on children. We aim to support parents in understanding the importance of positive family relationships and enhancing the emotional health of children and parents. It will also support parents where a difference in parenting styles has caused a communication breakdown. It is important to note that the course will not cover specific relationship situations and challenges but focuses on a holistic overview of parental relationship influence and healthy communication strategies. These sessions are ran both in person and online, across 4 weeks, 1 full day or 2 half days. For more information or to discuss further please contact the Family Hub Team. To refer yourself to the programme please see the website link.

name: The Dash Charity
description: The Dash Charity has supported people in South Buckinghamshire since 1976. We provide confidential practical help and emotional support to women, men, and children experiencing domestic abuse. We have a range of services including a confidential Helpline, outreach, and advocacy support, and Refuge crisis accommodation. We can help with safety, putting you in touch with other professionals and services who can help you with legal advice, housing needs, and other types of support to ensure you have the wrap-around help you need. We have access to a national database of Refuge space if you need to flee out of the area and we will work with you until you get there safely. For those who want to remain in their home area, we can provide ongoing practical help and emotional support to help you stay safe and break the cycle of abuse. We also provide training and school workshops for children and young people so if you are interested in either of these aspects of our work, please get in touch to find out more.

name: Group Cycling
description: Cycling with like minded individuals using on and off-road routes. Welcome to Claydon Cycling Club. If you have a passion for cycling and fresh air, then we’d love to get to know you better. For us it’s all about ‘getting out there together’ in good company and enjoying safe and sociable rides. We are a fairly new club, launched in Spring 2020 but continue to grow week by week due to our open and welcoming vibe which attracts both men and women across a range of abilities. Whether it’s our founder members - aka ‘cycling gurus’ - or our newest Academy graduates, we pride ourselves on our cumulative cycling and life experience and are always ready to learn from each other. After all, it’s about looking out for each other - as well as the traffic. So, whether you’re a cycling veteran, need help training for an event or simply want to rekindle your lost love for your bike, we’re a good crew to know. Come rain or shine we’ll be out, because quite frankly it’s the best place to be, so why not come and join us?

name: Mini Monets Art School For Young Artists
description: Holiday Art Workshops and Parties. The art classes teach children to experiment away from judgment and self-criticism which is entirely liberating for the young and developing mind. It is more than a club, it’s an Art School run by professional artists with lots of support to help new students and those who need extra help. The school follows the national Key Stages and we encourage the younger Monets to start at age 4 in stage 1 and learn good art skills that will prepare them for the art challenge of stages 2 and 3 and hopefully a lifetime love of art-making and relaxing through the process of creative thinking. Start anytime or sign up for a trial class. The classes are lively and highly creative. We publish the term course in advance so you know what to expect. The children make new friends and enjoy an imaginative environment. We encourage group participation and use all mediums for projects. We make sculptures, and paintings, and learn about colour, art techniques, and drawing skills. We also offer graphic design and printing skills. We have our very own studio with lots of free parking. We host Mini Monet workshops and birthday parties in our studio. For larger workshops we can come to you or hire a larger space in Buckinghamshire and further afield. We will travel Nationwide for larger festivals and corporate opportunities.
organisation: Mini Monets Art School (Amersham) Mini Monets offers unsurpassed inspirational weekend art and holiday art camp workshops for children aged 5 to 15 years. Children not only get a real art education where they learn about techniques, materials and the great subject of ART from a professional artist. They also make new friends, relax, develop confidence and try out exciting things like pottery, graffiti, T-shirt design, have art exhibitions and much more. Above all, it is a unique opportunity to express themselves creatively. Established in 2013 by international artist Debra Franses Bean. This special community of young artists provides a wonderful break from their school week. Many children have been attending the art school since it opened and others return after taking a break from other activities. This year all her masterclass students were awarded Art scholarships at their chosen secondary schools, St Mary's Gerrards Cross, Pipers Corner, Godstowe, RMS, Royal Hospital Horsham. dfbean3@mac.com https://www.minimonetsuk.com/

How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Setting is fully accessible for children inside and out small step to front door two small steps in my garden. I'm happy to discuss a child's individuals needs and where possible to accommodate. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I would encourage families to have a settling period with their child and complete an all about me booklet, work with parent with starting points for their child. When their child is ready to move settings I would be happy for new setting to visit my home whilst child is with me to see them in my care. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date on SEND information and training though out the Local Authority. description: Hi my name is DAX and I'm a childminder living in Amersham. I have been childminding for the last 25 years and thoroughly enjoy my job. I am a qualified National Nursery Examination Board (NNEB). I have worked with children form the ages of 12 weeks upwards and with children with a special need. Since 20, I have worked in Social services and private nursery's, on children's hospital wards and worked in the community as a section 11 taking play and education into the community; then helped set up the nursery at the BBC, for children aged from 12 weeks up to the time they leave for school. I also offer a babysitting service. I have enjoyed every part of my journey working with children and the experience I have gained. Once my son was born, I became a childminder working from home starting with my anti-natal group parents children. So, my home setting and routine reflects the nursery routine but also more on family bases but with a smaller group of children. This also enabled me to take them out and about to explore and learn about their environment, playgroups, parks, museums, music lesson, library, interacting with other children, life skills and so one. I provide different activities to enhance the children's learning according to their age and ability but at the same time having that family time, experience and atmosphere with the other children I look after and at tea times when we all eat together. So creating a cosy family welcoming home environment is very important to me for the children and their well-being. My home is also a place I would like my parents to feel comfortable and welcomed.

description: Situated on Chiltern Avenue in Amersham, Partou Chiltern Avenue Day Nursery & Pre-School provides high-quality early years childcare and education for families in Amersham, Chesham, Little Chalfont and the surrounding Buckinghamshire area. We’re close to Amersham station on the Metropolitan and Chiltern Lines, making us a really convenient choice for families commuting into London, and we have on-site parking for easy drop-offs and pick-ups. Our long-standing team is at the heart of what makes Partou Chiltern Avenue special. Having familiar, consistent faces means children build strong bonds with the people who care for them, and families get to know a team they trust. Our nursery team are patient, attentive and genuinely invested in getting to know each child as an individual. Our large outdoor area gives children plenty of space to develop physical confidence, explore and enjoy being outdoors. It’s well-resourced with dens, mud kitchens and climbing frames, and outdoor play is an important part of every day here. Beyond the nursery, we regularly take children out into the local community on outings to the library, park, fire station and local market. These experiences are brilliant for building children’s confidence, broadening their understanding of the world and bringing their early years learning to life in a really meaningful way.

local_offer: In line with the requirements of the Early Years Foundation Stage, I make regular observations and assessments of each child’s development and plan a child’s further progress based on these. I encourage families to discuss any concerns with me to enable us to work together on instigating appropriate next steps n for their child’s development. I discuss and seek advice from the parents of a child with SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disability). I am willing to undertake any formal training necessary to further understand the individual needs of their child. I provide families with regular updates by face-to-face discussion, email, text or phone and share my observations and assessments with them. I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.A child with SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disability) joining my setting would be fully supported. I would discuss their individual needs with parents and seek information about them from their previous setting. Likewise, I would provide information as required by a new setting the child may attend and work alongside them, providing transitional information to help the child settle in successfully.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individual programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. I provide full support to children and parents alike to develop strategies to help those children with SEND, seeking advice from relevant agencies if necessary. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed training on Anxiety, Understanding Low Mood and Depression, Understanding Self-Harm, Partnership with Parents, Developing Self Esteem in Young Children, Supporting Learning Activities, Asperger Syndrome, Dyslexia, Dyspraxia, Supporting Children with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Caring for children with allergies, Equality and Inclusion in Early Years Settings Level 2, Supporting Early Language Development Level 2, Recognising and Supporting Children with SEN, and The role of the SENCO. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with me. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. I carry out training on any SEN problems that are present and share my learning with parents. We then discuss what and how relevant strategies are implemented both in my setting and in a child's home. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. I use WhatsApp to send through photos and updates and also write a daily diary that is send home with the children after every visit. I also compete learning journals. All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. This level of information sharing applies to both those children with or without SEN. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is mostly accessible for all children both inside and out. Unfortunately it is not currently wheelchair accessible. However I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate any other issues arising. We have artificial grass in the garden so the garden is always accessible. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? All families are welcome to visit and meet me and see my setting before making an application to attend and prior to that I send out an an information sheet about my setting and a copy of all my policies and procedures. I work in partnership with other childminders, schools and pre-schools to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an information sheet with as much information as possible to ensure continuity of care. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will provide full details of where the child is on their learning journey. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I keep up to date with SEND information through the Local Authority and their website I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for.

description: Our sessions are run by experienced coaches who ensure that training is adapted to everyone's needs. The training sessions are planned to cover a wide range of football skills and drills with the intention of developing their footballing abilities. This is balanced with the equally important need to ensure that all the participants are having fun as well! All abilities and challenges (physical and neurological) are welcome and can be accommodated. We run a training session every Saturday from 10:30 to 11:30 am for youth player aged between 8 and 15. We have also recently added a Adult Disability Training Session for players aged 16 and older which runs every Saturday from 11:30 am to 12:30 midday. For new members, the first four sessions are free to get a feel for the training and get an understanding whether it is right for you or your child. Once you register as a member then there is a a £75 membership fee for the season with training taking place from September through to May. Our youth training group have also recently started taking part in tournaments against other local disability football teams! If you want to find out more, or know anyone who might, don’t hesitate to get in touch with us using the contact details below.

local_offer: I am an OFSTED registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child. Transition periods for all children are done on an individual basis. I can take as much or as little time as each child needs in order for them to feel happy with me and in their new environment.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? I aim to treat every child as unique and to support them through individualised programmes, in order that they make progress in all aspects of their development. I work flexibly to try to include children in all aspects of life within my childminding environment. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities, and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met. I am happy to undertake any further training specific to the needs of the children I am caring for. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?  How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? I try to involve parents in all aspects of their child’s time with me. I value input from parents and always seek their advice and opinions. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child and they are kept updated through Private WhatsApp communication set up between ourselves. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes are shared, and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. Any concerns about a child’s development are shared with the parents and I will work on a joint action plan to support their child. I will discuss if further support is needed or if parents would like other services involved. I provide increased opportunities for communication for families of children with SEND and am flexible in how I communicate, for example, in person, on phone, email or electronic messages. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Unfortunately, there is no easy wheelchair access through the front door or at the back of the house. The patio has steps down to the lawn and into the back door. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible e.g., adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools and pre-schools, to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings, I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they can visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? I am constantly aware of the need for flexibility within my setting to ensure that children’s needs can be met. I keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact and I will access training as necessary.

description: Disabled Living has an excellent reputation of organising the very prestigious Kidz to Adultz event since 2001 and now hold five of the largest free UK exhibitions totally dedicated to children and young adults up to 25 years with disabilities and additional needs, their parents, carers and all the professionals who support and work with them. 100 to 180 exhibitors at each event. These free exhibitions are a one stop shop for the most up to date advice and information on mobility, funding, seating, beds, communication, sensory, transition, education, housing, employment, accessible vehicles, transport, style, sports, leisure and much, much more. Seminars – boost your CPD (Continuing Professional Development) portfolio. Gain credits by attending one or more of the free CPD accredited seminars taking place alongside the exhibition. Seminars are presentations covering a wide range of issues and interests to families and carers of children with disabilities and special needs, and the professionals who work with them. The speakers will also be on hand throughout the day to answer any questions you may have. For professionals, CPD certificates of attendance will be available to collect on the day. Entry is free on a first come, first served basis. Children are welcome to come along, try out the equipment and products, join in the fun and features and participate in the sporting activity sessions taking place throughout the day. Visit our upcoming Kidz to Adultz events page to find the nearest event location to you. Who visits Kidz to Adultz Exhibitions? Key buyers from across the UK which include: Care home owners and managers Healthcare professionals Nursing professionals Occupational therapists Physiotherapists Foster carers SEN teachers/assistants Mobility equipment suppliers Social workers Paediatric carers and therapists Please visit our website to book onto our free exhibitions.

name: Wellbeing Pathways (Low/Moderate Mental Health)
description: We work to support adults with poor mental health through our green therapy programme Wellbeing Pathways as well as our supported volunteering and volunteering opportunities. Wellbeing Pathways is our 3 to 6-month programme focused on supporting people with low to moderate/common mental health diagnosis. The programme works to improve mental health and support people to stay healthy through weekly 3-hour sessions in groups of up to 6 people. Each week, participants engage in nature-based activities and set goals structured around the 5 ways to wellbeing – connect, be active, take notice, keep learning and give. The programme aims to allow people, if they want, to transition into becoming an apprentice volunteer or volunteer at Lindengate.
organisation: Lindengate Our free drop-in support sessions are for anyone who may be struggling with their wellbeing or mental health. Set on a 5-acre site, our therapeutic gardens and wildlife haven are accessible to anyone who needs space and time to "be". Finding time to give yourself space can be difficult in the best of weather, but in Winter, the challenge becomes even greater. There are many benefits to spending just a few minutes a day outdoors. Here are a few of them: 15 minutes outdoors every day can improve both our moods and our physical health, leading to reduced stress and increased self-esteem Builds our immune system, as the cold weather actually kills off bacteria. With the current restrictions in place, we can meet up with a friend, which will improve our mental wellbeing, through social interaction. We have plenty of sheltered areas dotted about to meet with a friend or family member for a chat or to bring a book and enjoy the peace, amongst the wildlife. charlie.hughes@lindengate.org.uk http://www.lindengate.org.uk

name: Wellbeing Pathways (Low/Moderate Mental Health)
description: We work to support adults with poor mental health through our green therapy programme Wellbeing Pathways as well as our supported volunteering and volunteering opportunities. Wellbeing Pathways is our 3 to 6-month programme focused on supporting people with low to moderate/common mental health diagnosis. The programme works to improve mental health and support people to stay healthy through weekly 3-hour sessions in groups of up to 6 people. Each week, participants engage in nature-based activities and set goals structured around the 5 ways to wellbeing – connect, be active, take notice, keep learning and give. The programme aims to allow people, if they want, to transition into becoming an apprentice volunteer or volunteer at Lindengate.

description: If you would like to join a warm and friendly community, meet new friends, working together to support the wellbeing of people and the environment and help us maintain the beautiful 6 acre Lindengate gardens in Wendover, Buckinghamshire, then get in touch. We have a variety of volunteering opportunities from gardening, conservation and woodwork. Volunteering is available Tuesday to Saturday at Lindengate.
organisation: Lindengate Our free drop-in support sessions are for anyone who may be struggling with their wellbeing or mental health. Set on a 5-acre site, our therapeutic gardens and wildlife haven are accessible to anyone who needs space and time to "be". Finding time to give yourself space can be difficult in the best of weather, but in Winter, the challenge becomes even greater. There are many benefits to spending just a few minutes a day outdoors. Here are a few of them: 15 minutes outdoors every day can improve both our moods and our physical health, leading to reduced stress and increased self-esteem Builds our immune system, as the cold weather actually kills off bacteria. With the current restrictions in place, we can meet up with a friend, which will improve our mental wellbeing, through social interaction. We have plenty of sheltered areas dotted about to meet with a friend or family member for a chat or to bring a book and enjoy the peace, amongst the wildlife. charlie.hughes@lindengate.org.uk http://www.lindengate.org.uk

name: Deborah Johnson
description: Registered Childminder located in Ley Hill, Chesham in the District of Chiltern. I now offer funded early education to 2, 3 and 4 year olds In my childcare setting my aim is to look after your children as if they were in their own homes. I offer a very loving and homely environment. The children are cared for in my family home where we have a bespoke dedicated playroom, separate sleeping rooms, and a large, secure, and secluded garden. We have a wide selection of toys and we offer age-appropriate activities to promote their development. We offer home-cooked meals and we can cater for any dietary requirements. I am an experienced, mature lady, a qualified nurse, and mum to two young men I work with a childminding assistant, this affords us a great deal of flexibility when planning our activities. Between us, we have a wealth of childcare and caring experience. We live in a beautiful village just outside of Chesham and we try hard to utilise all that we have around our local community in our provision. I have professional references which are available on request. Being a childminder isn't just an informal arrangement between friends to babysit. I work using the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Framework (my legal requirements); this is the same as any other Nursery, Pre-School or education setting for a child up to the 31 August after their fifth birthday. We cover all aspects of learning; these include Literacy Numeracy Knowledge and Understanding of the World Expressive art and design Communication and Language Personal, Social and Emotional Development Physical Development In a nutshell, we promote curiosity, and independence and have lots of fun whilst learning. I can provide vegetarian, dairy-free, gluten-free, and nut-free diets. We try to embrace all cultural requirements. I offer high-quality, bespoke affordable childcare in a homely environment. I offer flexible hours that can be organised around shift work. Flexible childcare contracts are available, for example, term-time childcare. I offer your childcare all under one roof, accepting children from birth to 11 years of age. I am an Ofsted Registered Childminder with 11 years experience. I have a Paediatric First Aid Qualification. I am a retired Registered Nurse on Part 13 of the NMC register. I have completed my Safeguarding Children Certificate. I hold a Food Hygiene Certificate. I am a Registered Data Controller. My assistant and I have full, clean UK driving licences and we have a dedicated vehicle for use with the children, with appropriate car seating available for all ages of children and stages of development. My application has recently been approved to provide 15 and 30 hours supported funded childcare

We would normally run in-person Workshops on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings with additional holiday Workshops. Initially when, due to the COVID-19 pandemic Lockdown and social distancing recommendations, we were unable to continue running Workshops at our normal venue at The Beacon School we were devastated. We didn’t give up and our Artistic team have worked extremely hard to keep The Theatre Shed up and running by going online. With so many young people needing a regular pattern to their lives we have been able to give continuity, stability and consistency. Good mental health at this time is so important. These sessions are really well attended once everyone got used to using Zoom and it now feels so natural to our members. This gives continuity, familiarity and activity in these extremely uncertain times. We didn’t stop there realising that there are others in the Community who would benefit from regular involvement in our activities so we expanded our activities to include Film Club for the Community. This is a chance to watch a film at the same time as your friends with an activity pack available to download from our website to go along with it. The chosen film is shown via our Zoom link so everyone can watch together. Our Community work continues with daytime workshops on a Tuesday between 2pm and 3pm and will have different themes (drama, dance, music etc.) each week. admin@thetheatreshed.co.uk https://thetheatreshed.co.uk/

local_offer: I am an Ofsted registered childminder committed to providing quality flexible childcare for children and young people with additional needs. I work with parents/carers and other professionals to ensure the best outcomes for each individual child.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? As a registered childminder I have a Key Contact at Buckinghamshire Council with the Early Years Team, and with parental permission, I may contact them for further advice. A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites…) are available for us to access. I welcome other professionals into the setting who may have involvement with a child and I am keen to access further training to support a child’s development for example speech and language (Speech Therapist). I am happy to attend Multi-Professionals Meetings if required What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? I have completed online training courses with regards to ADHD and ASD. Most of my training has been from experience and with guidance from parents. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? By working in close partnership with parents, information about their child’s learning, development and progress is shared on a regular basis. Information about a child’s likes and dislikes is shared and activities are extended to support the child’s enjoyment and learning whilst at the setting. Routines are discussed with parents to ensure consistency throughout the day for their child. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? All children attending the setting are monitored and observed to support their learning and development. Any concerns regarding a child’s development are shared with the parents and we will work on a joint action plan in support of their child. We will discuss if further support is required or if parents would like other services involved. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? My setting is fully accessible for all children both inside and out. I have a small step leading to the front door and easy access via a side entrance. I am happy to discuss a child’s individual needs and will be accommodating where possible for instance adaptations to meet sensory needs or to accommodate dietary requirements. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? I work in close partnership with other childminders, schools, pre-schools and the local day nursery to ensure effective transitions for all children. I encourage families to have a settling in period with their child and complete an ‘All about me’ booklet together. We will jointly focus on a child’s starting points which will feed into their setting ‘learning journey’. When a child moves settings I will encourage the new provider to visit the child at my setting and in their home environment and ensure they have the opportunity to visit and settle in their new environment. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? To keep up to date with SEND information and training through the Local Authority and my Key Contact. I regularly review the environment, toys, resources, activities and experiences I offer to my families to ensure each individual child’s needs are met.

description: I am a fully qualified, registered art psychotherapist based in a studio in Wingrave and provide a mobile service to areas in and surrounding HP22 postcode. Art therapy is proven to support those suffering from psychological problems, poor mental health, and lack of well-being. Working with clients of all ages, suffering from psychological problems or poor mental health caused by chronic or acute illness, disability, anxiety, or familial, societal, or work-related stress or trauma, and related wellbeing and mental health issues. Specifically working with children, adolescents, and family anxiety; equality and diversity-related mental health concerns, disability, autism, and SEND issues affecting mental health and well-being and with those suffering bereavement, life-limiting illnesses. and dementia and needing psychological support. Art therapy is a psychodynamic therapy using art as a medium to support the expression of emotions. It enables clients to self-regulate and build emotional resilience and can support and reduce pain and anxiety. It is proven to be as efficacious as Cognitive Behavior Therapy. My modality is person-centred and mentalising based and uses mindfulness, breathing, and visualisation with 2D and 3D creative techniques. I work with groups and individuals, face-to-face and remotely. I offer arts in health workshops as well as art therapy. I also offer personal therapy to trainees undertaking creative psychotherapy courses. I am able to offer supervision to trainees and professionals

local_offer: Mental Health and wellbeing support. Experience of working with children, young people, and adults with SEND, including SEMH and Autism. Supporting processing illness, ideation, self-harm, disability, loss, trauma, anxiety, gender dysphoria, cyber and social media driven, and other mental health concerns and difficulties in managing emotional problems, leading to facilitating self-regulation and development of independence and sense of self. Using mindfulness based art therapy, referral and self-referral leads to assessment and ongoing evaluative formulation to support processing difficulties and lead to regulation and self care through mindfulness based art therapy techniques. Clients are taught strategies to enable self care throughout sessions and after completing therapy course to enable self regulation and improved outcomes for recovery and supporting them living to their full potential going forward.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Provide a person-centred mentalisation-based, therapeutic support which models outcomes and enables clients to recognise triggers, to process trauma and manage difficulties, learning to express and contain emotions and be able to live their best life. Supporting children, young people and their families to have functioning relationships and improved outcomes from awareness and understanding and ability to process issues as they arise, managing triggers and creating better window of tolerance to cope with daily living. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Ongoing SEND training in role and Continual Professional Development supporting working constantly with this client group in particular in educational settings. Fully compliant with SEND commissioning Bucks. Fully DBS cleared and safeguarding, prevent and risk assessment and GDPR updated regularly. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? From referral, regular oral and intermediate written reporting (as agreed on assessment within safe boundaries) as well as inclusion in sessions as appropriate as part of ongoing formulation, parents, carers and significant others are involved and included as apt to best support the client, safely and achieve their identified and agreed outcomes. Regular involvement of Multi-Disciplinary Teams as appropriate. Communication, modelling and support of wider network and family around child as appropriate. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? As part of mental health assessment and formulation process, appropriate information sharing is identified and agreed with all relevant parties. As this process is individual to each client, all needs will be met on a case by case basis. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Fully accessible, safe and contained with use of indoor and outdoor space for therapeutic gain. Service is also fully mobile to service Aylesbury and surrounding areas. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Contact Belinda Hunt. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Ongoing training and working in this space. 25 years of various working with ongoing SEND and SEMH issues in children, young people and adults in educational and community settings and more recently in hospice settings. Keeping uptodate with research in this area to support clients to optimum outcomes.

description: Residents in Buckinghamshire and the surrounding areas can make use of FasterBroadband’s free resources to check what internet options are available locally. The service is independent and straightforward to use, letting you compare both part fibre and full fibre broadband. By entering a postcode, you can see what types of broadband are available at an address and the speeds you can expect. The website also includes practical tools such as a broadband speed test, a data breach checker, and a broadband usage guide. For households on a low income receiving government support benefits like Universal Credit, there is a dedicated section that highlights social broadband tariffs. These are special, lower cost packages from major providers designed to help make broadband more affordable. To make things easier for everyone, the site has built in accessibility features. By selecting the icon in the bottom left corner, you can adjust the display and activate support options designed to help people with different visual or cognitive needs.

description: Our Jamming Group offers a welcoming space to explore music-making together in a relaxed and supportive environment. Group music therapy can play a powerful role in supporting mental health. It encourages self-expression and creativity, strengthens social and communication skills, and helps people feel more connected to their community. Research shows that even listening to meaningful or familiar music activates many areas of the brain, lifting mood, reducing anxiety, and creating lasting positive effects. Led by our Music Therapist, Laure, sessions provide a safe and structured space where participants can express themselves through improvisation, song sharing, listening, and reflection. The focus is not on performance or musical ability, but on connection, confidence, and wellbeing. Whether you’re an experienced musician or have never picked up an instrument before, you’re warmly welcome. Instruments are provided, and no musical experience is needed. Participants must be aged 18 or over to join the group Please contact us below if you or someone you know is interested in attending.
organisation: Chiltern Music Therapy Chiltern Music Therapy is an award-winning not-for-profit organisation that provides a music therapy service to people of all ages. Chiltern Music Therapy offers expertise in the fields of learning disabilities, mental health, brain injury, dementia and Alzheimer's, palliative care, neonatal and paediatrics. Our Music Therapists are qualified with a Masters in Music Therapy, are registered with the Health and Care Professions Council and the national body the British Association for Music Therapy. We pride ourselves on using evidence based practice and are dedicated to providing measurable and tangible outcomes for all client groups. At the heart of our work is our aim to provide an inclusive service that is accessible to all. local_offer: At Denham Green E-Act Primary Academy, we believe every child should be challenged to reach their potential. Some children may have needs which are different from, and additional to, their peers and therefore may require additional support or intervention to achieve their potential. Each pupil’s education programme will be planned by the class teacher. It will be differentiated accordingly to suit the pupil’s individual needs. This may include additional general support by the teacher or teaching assistant in class. The inclusion manager meets regularly with the team to ensure good practice is shared and any arising issues are addressed quickly. Learning support assistants support alongside the teacher in the classroom and when appropriate lead small group and one to one intervention to meet individual needs. If a pupil has needs related to more specific areas of their education, such as spelling, handwriting, numeracy and literacy skills, then the pupil will be placed in a small focus group. This will be run by the teacher or teaching assistant. The length of time of the intervention will vary according to need but will generally be for a term. name: Stable Futures
description: Therapeutic Equine, Small Animals, Outdoor Learning and Training programmes for children who can’t access mainstream education for a variety of reasons. We provide a safe and therapeutic space for Children to recover from difficult, and often traumatic life experiences. A space where they can process emotions, rebuild their view of the world and make connections to others. Stable Futures offers a Therapeutic Horsemanship–informed provision designed to support children and young people through structured, purposeful interaction with horses. Our animal care programme combines therapeutic interventions with engaging, science-based learning, helping children and young people explore the physical and emotional needs of animals while developing empathy, responsibility, and life skills. Stable Futures offer a great addition to your school curriculum. We are offering enrichment, personal development, and evidence for your Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural development. We can support achieving and evidence core outcomes for EHCPs/ ILPs. We hold a strong focus on evidencing and tracking attainment for learners, to ensure impact and success is recognised. Stable Futures can also offer next steps to learners unable to access a full curriculum in school. Through our Alternative Curriculum offer, there are a broad range of learning offers, including PSHE, Art and Design, Culinary Skills, Horticulture, Bushcraft, Careers, and Vocational to name a few. Stable Futures is an accredited Centre to deliver Riding for the Disabled (RDA), City and Guilds Entry level Maths, English and Employability Skills, alongside core ASDAN and AQA unit awards. Outcomes are at the heart of our provision. We are committed to enabling every learner to make tangible, individual progress, building confidence, independence, and skills for the future. Our team is trained in a wide range of areas to support children and young people with complex needs, including ASD, ADHD, Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA), and Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD). Staff are also experienced in applying PACE (Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity and Empathy) and Thrive approaches, ensuring relationships and emotional development are at the core of our practice. We place a strong emphasis on trauma-informed care, equipping staff with the knowledge and skills to support learners who have experienced adversity, including training in self-harm and suicide awareness. Safeguarding training is comprehensive and includes all areas of vulnerability and exploitation. We are investing in experiential and outdoor learning, replenishing Bushcraft resources and, from Summer 2026, expanding our outdoor education offer to include off-site activities such as water sports and mountain biking. These developments reflect our commitment to providing a rich, engaging, and inclusive learning environment that meets the evolving needs of children and young people with SEND. Our approach is holistic and collaborative. We work closely with schools, special schools, and virtual schools to ensure that targets remain appropriate, meaningful, and reflective of each child or young person’s needs. Progress is continuously monitored to demonstrate impact against agreed outcomes. In addition, we actively contribute to multi-agency working and can attend and provide reports for key professional meetings, including Annual Reviews, EHCP and Personal Education Plan (PEP) reviews, and Team Around the Family (TAF) meetings. This ensures that all professionals involved have a clear and consistent understanding of the learner’s development and achievements. Our enhanced communication and multi-agency involvement provide additional support for children and young people with SEND, ensuring their progress is effectively tracked, shared, and celebrated. Referrals to Stable Futures are made through the child’s school or local authority, and funding must be agreed to access our alternative provision. Referrals can be initiated easily through our website.

local_offer: All staff are trained in the therapeutic approach of PACE- Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity, Empathy. With the robust referral process, we assess and ensure the bespoke support package is created for each learner (ILP- Individual Learning Plan). The support is delivered by experienced staff members, with experience ranging from; Riding for the Disabled Association group coach, Level 3 Certificate in Supporting Teaching and Learning, Level 3 Forest School Leaders, Animal Lead Tutor, Equine specialists, First-Class Honours in Child and Youth Work with Psychology, HLTA SEND practitioners. Our aim: Our packages are bespoke and tailored to each child’s needs so aims and objectives differ for each child. But set below are some aims which may apply to your child. The ultimate aim is for children to have a space to feel safe, process their emotions and re-build their view of the world in a positive and healthy way. Some other aims from packages include: - To deliver bespoke programs which supports each child to have opportunities to progress, learn and reflect - To provide each child with the opportunity to learn new independence skills which will be helpful in their personal life - To create a safe space for children to learn and to explore their thoughts and feelings without judgment - To support children to transition into full time education placements with a level of confidence and self-belief - To support children to develop their social, emotional, and interpersonal skills - To support children to begin to develop positive relationships with others and with themselves - To support children to manage their emotions in a healthy and positive way - To plan sessions with a tailored approach, to discuss with the referrer, and with the child as their views, wishes and feelings remain a priority - To ensure children and young people feel accepted and un-judged throughout all sessions - To provide learning activities which are engaging and fun - To support children to realise their ambitions and their potential - To provide consistent, reliable, and skilled staff members to support the young people in their journey through Outdoor Learning When the children are able to, we help them understand and develop their sense of identity, develop the skills they will need to problem solve and plan for the future, and explore the impact their early experience has had on them. Stable Futures offer a great addition to your school curriculum. We are offering enrichment, personal development and evidence for your British Values and SMSC. We are able to support achieving and evidence core outcomes for EHCPs/ ILPs. We hold a strong focus on evidencing and tracking attainment for learners, to ensure impact and success is recognised. Stable Futures can also offer next steps to learners unable to access a full curriculum in school. Through our Alternative Curriculum offer, there are a broad range of learning offers, including PSHE, Art and Design, Culinary Skills, Horticulture, Bushcraft, Careers and Vocational to name a few. Stable Futures is an accredited Centre to deliver RDA, City and Guilds Entry level Maths, English and Employability Skills, alongside core ASDAN and AQA unit awards. Stable Futures welcomes from schools, local authorities and other professionals. Stable Futures works closely with Amegreen Education, a provider of SEND schools, as a key referral partner. Pupils from Haywards Farm and Northcroft School attend Stable Futures as part of their weekly provision. Amegreen Education received an ‘Outstanding’ rating in its Ofsted inspection, which included Stable Futures as part of the evaluated provision.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? Stable Futures aims to deliver meaningful, measurable outcomes for children and young people with SEND, working in close partnership with families and referral providers. Our provision is centred on the individual, with all learning aligned to each learner’s Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) or Individual Learning Plan (ILP). We set clear, personalised targets and closely track progress through ongoing weekly observations and structured assessment. This enables us to evidence impact effectively for both learners and referral partners. Formal half-termly reports provide detailed updates on progress, achievements, and next steps. Learners at Stable Futures have access to a range of recognised accreditation pathways, including RDA, ASDAN, AQA Unit Awards, and City and Guilds qualifications, supporting both personal development and future progression opportunities. We place strong value on working collaboratively with families, ensuring they are informed, involved, and able to celebrate their child’s achievements. Families are invited to attend annual celebration events, recognising the progress and successes of each learner. Outcomes are at the heart of our provision. We are committed to enabling every learner to make tangible, individual progress, building confidence, independence, and skills for the future. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Stable Futures staff undertake a comprehensive programme of ongoing training to ensure a high-quality, therapeutic and SEND-informed provision. Training is delivered through Amegreen Children’s Services’ training department, alongside specialist external SEND professionals. Our team is trained in a wide range of areas to support children and young people with complex needs, including Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA), and Foetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD). Staff are also experienced in applying PACE (Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity and Empathy) and Thrive approaches, ensuring relationships and emotional development are at the core of our practice. We place a strong emphasis on trauma-informed care, equipping staff with the knowledge and skills to support learners who have experienced adversity, including training in self-harm and suicide awareness. Safeguarding training is comprehensive and includes all areas of vulnerability and exploitation. In addition, staff are trained in physical intervention (where appropriate), first aid and mental health first aid, and the safe administration of medication, including Buccal Midazolam. Our provision is further enhanced through specialist qualifications such as Level 3 Forest School Leadership, Riding for the Disabled Association (RDA) coaching and Green Card certification, and Equine Facilitated Learning approaches, all of which support therapeutic, experiential learning opportunities. This breadth of training ensures that our team can respond effectively to individual needs, delivering a safe, nurturing, and therapeutic environment where children and young people with SEND can thrive. How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? At Stable Futures, we place strong value on working in partnership with parents and carers, ensuring they feel informed, involved, and confident in their child’s provision. Following a professional referral, families are invited to visit the setting to view the provision before making a final decision. This provides an opportunity to meet the team, explore the environment, and ask any questions. Once a child or young person begins their placement, parents and carers are kept regularly updated through weekly observations. These include narrative summaries and photos of learning activities, with a clear focus on progress towards agreed outcomes. Each learner is supported by a dedicated keyworker, who acts as the main point of contact throughout the placement, providing consistent communication and support for families. We also encourage family involvement through invitations to end-of-year celebrations and award ceremonies, where learners’ achievements are recognised. In addition, we host open days throughout the year, such as our Summer Party, offering further opportunities for families to visit and engage with the provision. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? At Stable Futures, we ensure that parents and carers are kept fully informed about their child’s progress through regular, structured communication. We provide weekly observations that include detailed updates on each learner’s activities, engagement, and progress. These observations incorporate both narrative summaries and visual evidence, clearly linked to the outcomes set within the learner’s Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) or Individual Learning Plan (ILP). Our approach is holistic and collaborative. We work closely with schools, special schools, and virtual schools to ensure that targets remain appropriate, meaningful, and reflective of each child or young person’s needs. Progress is continuously monitored to demonstrate impact against agreed outcomes. In addition, we actively contribute to multi-agency working and are able to attend and provide reports for key professional meetings, including Annual Reviews, EHCP and Personal Education Plan (PEP) reviews, and Team Around the Family (TAF) meetings. This ensures that all professionals involved have a clear and consistent understanding of the learner’s development and achievements. Our enhanced communication and multi-agency involvement provide additional support for children and young people with SEND, ensuring their progress is effectively tracked, shared, and celebrated. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? Stable Futures provides a fully accessible and thoughtfully designed learning environment, both indoors and outdoors. Our 32-acre farm features dedicated learning zones, with full wheelchair access to classrooms and outdoor areas. Our Forest site is easily accessible and, together with the farm, offers a safe and carefully planned setting that supports children and young people with SEND. Small group transitions between learning zones are facilitated to ensure comfort, familiarity, and effective learning, allowing each learner to engage at their own pace in a supportive environment. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? Referrals to Stable Futures are made through the child’s school or local authority, and funding must be agreed to access our alternative provision. Referrals can be initiated easily via our website. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? Stable Futures continues to grow and develop its SEND provision to meet increasing demand and ensure high-quality outcomes for all learners. We are expanding our staffing teams to provide the expertise and support needed to accommodate new referrals while maintaining personalised, therapeutic provision. Our learning zones and curriculum content are continuously enhanced, with new opportunities for accredited learning through City and Guilds, offering entry-level qualifications in maths, English, and employability skills. Post-16 pathways and a broad alternative curriculum are also in place to support progression, independence, and future opportunities. We are investing in experiential and outdoor learning, replenishing Bushcraft resources and, from Summer 2026, expanding our outdoor education offer to include off-site activities such as water sports and mountain biking. These developments reflect our commitment to providing a rich, engaging, and inclusive learning environment that meets the evolving needs of children and young people with SEND.

local_offer: In our setting, we treat each child as an individual. Your child will be allocated a key person who will be responsible for your child’s development and care. An initial meeting with your child’s key person to discuss your child in detail will be an opportunity to raise any initial concerns you may have and plan for their next steps and any support required. Through ongoing observations, monitoring and assessments we are able to identify any concerns which we will share with you, and with consent, we will contact other professionals if required.  What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families? We have two very experienced SENCOs in the setting and two SENCO support assistants who all have a variety of experience working with children with SEND. We have experience in working with children with autism, down syndrome, hearing impairment, global delay and speech and language difficulties. We liaise regularly with professionals from the Integrated SEND Service, Speech and Language therapists and Occupational Therapists and Portage. We attend the Early Years SENCO Liaison Groups and update our knowledge and training regularly. We have recently completer Attention Autism training and have completed training work shops on Sensory Processing Disorder and Developmental Co-ordination Disorder. We regularly seek advice and support from Speech and Language Therapists and Occupational Therapists. What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers? Louise Welsford, Kloe Hare SENCO working towards Level 3 SENCO Louise Welsford, Kloe Hare: AET (Autism) Training Louise Welsford, Kloe Hare, Jo Jinks, Loretta Macauley: Earlybird Training Kloe Hare, Loretta Macaulay: Sensory Processing Training All staff: Makaton Training How to run a speech and Language Group Loretta Macaulay, Joanna Guadgno Kloe Hare Attention Autism How do you involve parents and how can I get involved? We have an open-door policy and promote and value all parent's views and opinions. We invite parents to Stay and Play sessions in the nursery and encourage them to share their interests and skills. Using our online App we can communicate directly with parents sharing news of the nursery or individual posts and pictures of their child. We encourage parents to post pictures and news from home too. We hold regular meetings where parents meet with their child's key person to discuss their child's progress. How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND? Your child's key person will complete regular observations and assessments which will be shared with parents using our App. This will give an indication of the progress your child is making or if there are any areas of concern. For children with SEND, we will meet regularly to discuss their progress towards their short term outcomes. How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)? We take into account the needs of the children in the setting when planning our environment to make it as accessible as possible. We have a purpose-built cabin where we hold intervention group work using a range of strategies. We keep this area free of distractions for focused learning. We have two settings on the same site where we have a range of soft play and sensory equipment. We have a range of sensory resources to support children with SEND. We use Makaton with all of the children within the nursery and visual prompts to help aid communication. We also use PECs (picture exchange) with children with SEND. How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity? We have strong links with the local schools and with parent's permission to share information and best practice to support the smooth transition to school. We accompany children on visits to their new school and share pictures of the new setting with them. For children joining our nursery we offer a staggered start should this be necessary. We also offer home visits prior to the child starting so they can become familiar with their key person. What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision? We are continuously evaluating our practice. We seek advice from professionals on different strategies to support children with SEND and create individual or group work following this advice. We continuously update our SEND resources and attend regular training courses to improve our practice. We have a Team of very experienced staff working and supporting our children with SEND

description: These films will help you to learn more about some of the main issues we all face as we get older. Once we understand why certain things happen, we can take steps to prevent them and improve our lives at home. In the films you’ll find information about a wide variety of issues, ranging from Falls to Loneliness to Nutrition to Alcohol problems. We’ve interviewed an extensive number of experts and older people, to give you lots of practical advice and tips to help you live better at home. ### [Click here to access videos from the Ageing Well at Home Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/2btnv28k), these cover: * Loneliness and Isolation * Hydration * Nutrition * Oral hygiene * Alcohol * Having Care at home * Falls * End of Life discussions Our mission is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs. You can find [videos on a range of other long-term conditions on our services page](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/services).

name: The Sound Doctor: Ageing Well at Home
description: These films will help you to learn more about some of the main issues we all face as we get older. Once we understand why certain things happen, we can take steps to prevent them and improve our lives at home. In the films you’ll find information about a wide variety of issues, ranging from Falls to Loneliness to Nutrition to Alcohol problems. We’ve interviewed an extensive number of experts and older people, to give you lots of practical advice and tips to help you live better at home. ### [Click here to access videos from the Ageing Well at Home Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/2btnv28k), these cover: * Loneliness and Isolation * Hydration * Nutrition * Oral hygiene * Alcohol * Having Care at home * Falls * End of Life discussions Our mission is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs. You can find [videos on a range of other long-term conditions on our services page](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/services).

name: Piece of Mind
description: Jigsaw4u’s Piece of Mind service provides specialised therapeutic support for 11 to 24 year-old young people with symptoms or a diagnosis of depression and/or anxiety. Our team work on an outreach basis and meet young people in school, college or at our office. We cover the SW London Boroughs of Merton, Croydon, Sutton, Wandsworth, Kingston and Richmond. Jigsaw4u also offer young people access to a variety of opportunities, events and positive activities to help them overcome depression and/or anxiety long-term.

name: Physiotherapy
description: Your Healthcare Musculoskeletal Outpatient Physiotherapy Services provides comprehensive, high quality musculoskeletal physiotherapy services for the local population. Referrals must be made via your GP. Physical means are used to assess, diagnose, treat and prevent injury or disease, in order to enable individuals to achieve their maximum level of function and independence. The service also works closely with the Musculoskeletal Triaging services at Kingston Hospital, accepting referrals for physiotherapy into the community. Patients may attend for individual or group treatment. The range of different services and treatments offered includes: * Joint and soft tissue manual therapy * Spinal Assessment (including the following post graduate techniques McKenzie, Maitland, Mulligan approach) * Dynamic Stability * Paediatric Musculoskeletal Disorders * Muscle Balance * Electrotherapy * Acupuncture * Exercise Prescription * Neural Dynamics * Biomechanics Group work for patients includes: * General exercises and management strategies for persistent lower back pain * Osteoarthritis of the knees * Modified pilates for lower back pain Patients may attend for individual or group treatment Initial appointments consist of a 45 minute face-to-face assessment, followed by follow-up sessions. Individual and group work takes place between 8am - 4.45pm with evening appointments by arrangement Monday - Friday.
