name: Men's Yoga Class
description: At Be Happy Yoga, my goal is to make yoga truly inclusive – and that includes creating a space where men feel completely welcome. Yoga4Men is just like any other yoga class, except that everyone in the room is male. For too long, yoga has been seen as slow stretching that doesn’t fit traditional male fitness goals. But that’s not true. Yoga is a powerful, full-body discipline that requires strength, balance, and stamina plus the ability to rest and recover well. With regular practice, you’ll: * Move better * Sleep better * Feel better, inside and out **How You’ll Benefit** * Reduce the risk of injuries and chronic pain * Improve posture, spinal alignment, and core strength * Support athletic performance in other sports * Boost mental wellbeing and physical resilience — yoga improves heart rate variability * Increase mobility, flexibility, and quality of life * Develop greater self-awareness and proprioception **Who Can Join?** Yoga4Men is for all fitness levels. There’s a place for you here whether you’re: * A complete beginner * A regular gym-goer looking to enhance athletic performance * Recovering from injury * Seeking a new way to stay strong and mobile over the long term
intro: Yoga4Men is just like any other yoga class, except that everyone in the room is male. Whether you’re ‘sporty’ or not, you’ll find a place here. This is your chance to experience how yoga can improve your body, mind, and overall resilience – without the stereotypes.
organisation: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). useful_infos: Additional information Looking for a meaningful, flexible way to support others? Join the Talking Bubble Project and help tackle loneliness with the power of a simple phone call. We’re one of the few befriending services still offering regular phone-based companionship—and demand is growing. We're looking for compassionate, English-speaking UK residents to volunteer. name: Canbury Pavilion
description: Canbury Pavilion is a wonderful community resource in North Kingston which you can use for parties or to host a regular class or gathering. We are situated in the lovely Canbury Gardens, next the Thames. **Facilities Available at the Pavilion:** * The pavilion has a main area for parties and events, with tables and chairs to seat 48 people * A carpeted recreational area outside the pavilion, but within the fenced area, provides a nice child-friendly play space. * Ramps can be provided to enable wheelchair access. * Sound system to play music via CDs, a Bluetooth connection or through a USB socket. * Kitchen facilities (microwave, hotplate and a kettle). * Toilets & baby changing facilities. * Refreshments can be arranged with Canbury Secret Café (our neighbour in Canbury Gardens) **Bookings can be made by emailing [canbury.pavilion@gmail.com](mailto:canbury.pavilion@gmail.com).** The pavilion is available for private functions, including childrens' parties at the weekends. For terms and conditions, please go to the [Booking page our website](https://sites.google.com/site/canburypavilion/bookings). The Pavilion is run by the Canbury Community Trust. Volunteers rescued this 100 year old bowling pavilion weeks before it was knocked down and have turned it into a vibrant community resource for Kingston.

name: Pilates for Beginners
description: This course introduces the fundamentals of matwork Pilates, focusing on building core strength, flexibility, and body awareness through mindful movement. Run every Friday sessions run in six week blocks What should I do if -------------------- You will learn key Pilates principles, essential exercises, and proper techniques to gain fitness, enhance strength, posture, and mobility while cultivating a mind-body connection. Location -------- Classes run every Friday in block sessions over 6-7 weeks. **The Warehouse Community Hall** St John's Church Church Grove Hampton Wick Kingston upon Thames What to Bring ------------- Comfortable loose clothing suitable for gentle movements. Do not wear tight belts or bands around the waist. Footwear suitable for gentle exercise. It is advisable to have a top layer sweatshirt or thin fleece that can be worn during warm ups and removed as needed as the class progresses. It is advisable to bring a bottle with drinking water to the class. A yoga mat if you have one. If you do not have a yoga mat, please bring a large towel. **Explore Our Range of Session Times**

organisation: Kingston Adult Education Kingston Adult Education We have our core delivery: ESOL, English, Maths, Digital, Vocational, Health & Fitness, Arts, Crafts, Languages, Writing, History and we have some wonderful new courses for you to turn your hand to. Why not try our new Jewellery Making Workshop and if you like it, join the new course. Along with new craft workshops and courses, we’ve also added new art courses and workshops: Why not enjoy Botanical Watercolours, Drawing & Painting Animals, Landscape Painting, Oil Painting or Mindful Art? Whether you're looking to meet new people, explore new interests, get a job, gain qualifications for your career or keep your mind and body active we have something for everyone. Along with our wonderful Tai Chi, Pilates, and Mindful Movement courses, why not try our new Journaling for Wellbeing to help build your resilience and improve your wellbeing? With both **online** and **in-person** classes available at locations across the borough, you can easily find a course that fits your needs. In addition, many of our courses are **free** as they are government funded or offered at reduced rates, and we provide discounts based on your circumstances, so please contact us to find out more. Enjoy your courses and being a part of our wonderful adult education community. The vision involves various groups maintaining and developing the area. If you'd like to get involved please get in touch. **WHERE:** Mayberry Place entrance to Fishponds Park, KT5 9AL, left of the path as you come in. **HOW:** We host sessions, both one off and regular, using the space to come together, connect, have fun and garden. description: **About** The volunteers at Barnfield RDA give local children and adults who have mental or physical disabilities the chance to ride horses. This doesn’t just make their life more enjoyable – horse riding is medically recognised for its therapeutic benefits such as strengthening muscles, improving co-ordination, building confidence physically and through speech, relieving stress and giving general psychological encouragement. ​ ​Each rider needs up to three helpers – one to lead the horse and two side walkers to ensure safety. The helpers are extraordinary local volunteers who give up their time, all united in their desire to help those less fortunate than themselves​. **Volunteering** We are always looking for volunteers to help run our classes (no horse riding experience necessary). We provide training at the stables and all are welcome. Volunteers will perform the following duties - keep the register of riders; fit their riding hats; help them mount and dismount the horse; lead the horse; or side-walk. Volunteers should be able to attend at least one session a week - on either Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday afternoon. Volunteers will be required to complete a DBS check. **Fundraising** We are a totally standalone charity and need to raise around £50,000 a year in order to continue this facility. We have around 60 clients each week and our only regret is that the monetary constrictions mean there are not more.​ **More Information** To find out more about Barnfield RDA and our Lessons or ways in which you too could volunteer and support our valuable work [please visit our website](https://www.barnfieldrda.org/). Or Call Patsy at Barnfield Riding School on **020 8546 3616.​** Registered Charity number 1073731

name: FAIRFIELD COUNSELLING
description: My name is Tony Williams, and I am a counsellor working in central and North Kingston upon Thames. **How does counselling work?** We make a new relationship, you and I. In doing that, we are already making a vehicle for change. What’s the fuel for that vehicle? Well, you bring that. It’s your experiences, your thoughts, your feelings. And as we move along together, change can start to happen. **How do we work together?** Everything we do is a collaboration. Everything we do is for your benefit. We make choices; where you want to go; how fast; how much challenge do you want? How much support? When do you feel the work is done? **What do you pay me for?** My job is to hear you; not judge you; and to try to understand your experience, perhaps in great detail; to help you to reflect; to help you shape your journey; and to be available for you, throughout, with a safe place. Especially when it is most difficult. **Why me?** I’m a fully qualified Integrative-Relational counsellor; and a member of the British Association of Counsellors and Psychotherapists (MBACP). That means I can draw on a mixture of theory and practice developed over the last 150 years or so; and that I am bound by a code of ethics in how I work with you. It means I meet the right standards in competence and integrity. More than that, though, I am committed to making the extra step to meet you in the way you want to be met; where, when and recognising your individual needs. **What is Integrative-Relational Counselling?** **Integrative-Relational Counselling _integrates_ various theories and practices in counselling and psychotherapy to give an holistic approach to helping people. Principally it includes:** **Psychodynamic counselling:** how our early lives affect us, how we learn to be in relationship to other people and how we view the world; and how those early experiences determine our way of being in later life. **Humanistic counselling:** how we all have inbuilt drives to grow and achieve our potential; and how obstructions to these drives can cause us unhappiness and distress. It also includes an understanding of Transpersonal (spiritual) and Cognitive-Behavioural (how our behaviours shape our thinking). These theories and practices are combined with a focus on the relationship between counsellor and client and how this can mirror the client’s experiences in the world outside the counselling room. So an Integrative-Relational Counsellor is equipped with a full set of tools to help you, whether your issues stem from the past, frustration with the future, or are in the now.

name: FAIRFIELD COUNSELLING
description: My name is Tony Williams, and I am a counsellor working in central and North Kingston upon Thames. **How does counselling work?** We make a new relationship, you and I. In doing that, we are already making a vehicle for change. What’s the fuel for that vehicle? Well, you bring that. It’s your experiences, your thoughts, your feelings. And as we move along together, change can start to happen. **How do we work together?** Everything we do is a collaboration. Everything we do is for your benefit. We make choices; where you want to go; how fast; how much challenge do you want? How much support? When do you feel the work is done? **What do you pay me for?** My job is to hear you; not judge you; and to try to understand your experience, perhaps in great detail; to help you to reflect; to help you shape your journey; and to be available for you, throughout, with a safe place. Especially when it is most difficult. **Why me?** I’m a fully qualified Integrative-Relational counsellor; and a member of the British Association of Counsellors and Psychotherapists (MBACP). That means I can draw on a mixture of theory and practice developed over the last 150 years or so; and that I am bound by a code of ethics in how I work with you. It means I meet the right standards in competence and integrity. More than that, though, I am committed to making the extra step to meet you in the way you want to be met; where, when and recognising your individual needs. **What is Integrative-Relational Counselling?** **Integrative-Relational Counselling _integrates_ various theories and practices in counselling and psychotherapy to give an holistic approach to helping people. Principally it includes:** **Psychodynamic counselling:** how our early lives affect us, how we learn to be in relationship to other people and how we view the world; and how those early experiences determine our way of being in later life. **Humanistic counselling:** how we all have inbuilt drives to grow and achieve our potential; and how obstructions to these drives can cause us unhappiness and distress. It also includes an understanding of Transpersonal (spiritual) and Cognitive-Behavioural (how our behaviours shape our thinking). These theories and practices are combined with a focus on the relationship between counsellor and client and how this can mirror the client’s experiences in the world outside the counselling room. So an Integrative-Relational Counsellor is equipped with a full set of tools to help you, whether your issues stem from the past, frustration with the future, or are in the now.

name: Albany Outdoors
description: Albany Outdoors is an accredited outdoor, adventure and water activity centre by the Thames in Kingston. Albany Outdoors has a lively atmosphere with activities taking place at the centre and off site locations. Based on the River Thames between Kingston Bridge and Teddington Lock, the centre is well served by road, rail and public transport. We offer courses for adults and children, for all levels and abilities, from school holiday to adult weekend courses. **We have specific SEND sessions every Tuesday evening or can organise bespoke sessions to suit everyone's needs.** We can provide a wide range of specially adapted activities and courses for young people and adults with a learning disability or physical disability. Please see info on our website or contact us to discuss your specific requirements. We also provide: * activities for schools, colleges and youth organisations * corporate events * party packages * weekly youth club If you are booking for the first time, take a look at what we offer and why not challenge yourself to try something new? Whatever you choose to do you will be in safe hands and we look forward to meeting you soon.

name: Queen's Promenade Friends
description: The Queen's Promenade Friends is a community group that was set up by a few local residents who wanted to improve the Queen's Promenade along the River Thames in Kingston. Our volunteers vary in age from their twenties to seventies, and we all enjoy the company of each other while regenerating an area with plants and encouraging wildlife and biodiversity. This mixed group has become a synchronicity of mindfulness and learning, for example most of us had never constructed a path, restored heritage fencing or even thought about a planting plan! The Friends are in this project together and enjoy the stimulating challenges that a volunteer day brings; everyone learning from each other with no pressure. The outcomes have been significant. An area that was barren is now occupied regularly by The Friends who welcome all visitors to the site. For the first time in decades, flowers, often donated by the community, are blooming on the site and the biodiversity is increasing. A loggery for beetles and a stumpery for ferns have been constructed, five bird boxes and a bat box are sited in the trees, a bug hotel has been made along with three raised beds, a wheelchair friendly path and a dry-stone wall. Many heritage pieces like Victorian benches and railings have been dug up on the site which have been restored and reused for the first time in decades. Over the years we have pruned bushes back into shape, done copious amounts of weeding, planted perennials and have generally restored pride and beauty along the promenade. In so doing, we have created a Riverview Garden, a Figgy Garden, improved the entrances to the promenade with refreshed planting and have recently embarked on restoring to former glory an old Victorian Italian Garden on a section of terraces. There are a number of ways you can help out at Queen’s Promenade Pocket Park and we are always on the lookout for new volunteers. We meet twice weekly (Wednesday afternoon and Saturday morning). To get involved, send an email to [queenspromfriends@gmail.com](mailto:queenspromfriends@gmail.com). “We are proud of the creation of a pocket park and of the significant improvement of this beautiful stretch along the river Thames between Surbiton and Kingston.” – Stefan Gross, Chair

name: Combat Stress - Mental Health Support for Veterans
description: Mental health support for veterans and their families ----------------------------------------------------- Combat Stress provides **free specialist mental health treatment for veterans**, as well as advice and support for their families, carers and support networks. What support is available? -------------------------- Combat Stress can support veterans experiencing: * PTSD and complex PTSD * trauma and traumatic memories * anxiety and depression * anger and irritability * sleep difficulties * other mental health difficulties linked to military experiences. Treatment is tailored to the individual and can be provided **online or in person**. **[Click here to find out how Combat Stress can help.](https://combatstress.org.uk/get-help)** Support for families -------------------- Family members, carers and people supporting a veteran can also get help. Support can include: * confidential advice through the 24-hour helpline * help understanding a veteran's mental health and treatment * information and self-help resources * support for partners and families * help finding other appropriate services. Some family support may require the veteran's consent. **[Click here to find out about support for families.](https://combatstress.org.uk/support-for-families-of-veterans)** Who can get specialist treatment? --------------------------------- Specialist clinical treatment is available to eligible **UK Armed Forces veterans, non-operational reservists and former Merchant Navy members**. Veterans accessing treatment must live in the UK and be registered with a UK GP. Family members can still contact the helpline for advice and support. How do I get help? ------------------ Veterans can contact Combat Stress directly or be referred by a professional. **24-hour helpline:** 0800 138 1619 **Text:** 07537 173683 **Email:** [helpline@combatstress.org.uk](mailto:helpline@combatstress.org.uk) The helpline is **free and confidential** and is available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

name: Full Cycle Bicycle Project
description: Full Cycle is a non-profit organisation involved in several local projects in Kingston to supply refurbished bikes to refugees and those on low incomes with an essential means of travel. We also supply subsidised bicycles to encourage and assist people who want to take up cycling or return to riding. What is on offer: * **Bicycle Maintenance Training** - fix and restore donated bicycles in our workshop in Berrylands. You will be able to learn transferable manual workshop skills including tool use, health & safety in the workplace and team work. You will also be part of an inclusive and welcoming community. * **Fix Your Own Bike Sessions** - these sessions are run by experienced instructors, and are for those who wish to maintain their own bike, or learn how to recycle and build a bike. * **Repairs & Servicing** - contact us to find out more about our repairs and servicing options. All profits are invested back into cycle-related initiatives across the Kingston community. * **Volunteering** Our [volunteering webpage](https://fullcycle.org.uk/volunteer/) sets out ways you can get involved. Volunteering will offer the opportunity to learn new skills , as well as supporting the local community.
intro: Our mission is to refurbish and rehome unwanted bikes, minimising waste, promoting active travel and giving people from all backgrounds access to affordable cycling.

name: Full Cycle Bicycle Project
description: Full Cycle is a non-profit organisation involved in several local projects in Kingston to supply refurbished bikes to refugees and those on low incomes with an essential means of travel. We also supply subsidised bicycles to encourage and assist people who want to take up cycling or return to riding. What is on offer: * **Bicycle Maintenance Training** - fix and restore donated bicycles in our workshop in Berrylands. You will be able to learn transferable manual workshop skills including tool use, health & safety in the workplace and team work. You will also be part of an inclusive and welcoming community. * **Fix Your Own Bike Sessions** - these sessions are run by experienced instructors, and are for those who wish to maintain their own bike, or learn how to recycle and build a bike. * **Repairs & Servicing** - contact us to find out more about our repairs and servicing options. All profits are invested back into cycle-related initiatives across the Kingston community. * **Volunteering** Our [volunteering webpage](https://fullcycle.org.uk/volunteer/) sets out ways you can get involved. Volunteering will offer the opportunity to learn new skills , as well as supporting the local community.

name: Princess Alice Hospice - Community Bereavement Support
description: At Princess Alice Hospice, we believe that bereavement support should be available for everyone, so we work in partnership with other organisations to provide bereavement support in the community. Community Bereavement Cafés and Walk & Talks can be found in all parts of our care area, and drop-in sessions are open to all bereaved people, regardless of how and where their loved one died. ### Bereavement Cafes They not only offer a warm welcome, but, more importantly, a safe place to share experiences with other bereaved people and the volunteers that have had training from the Hospice. Please see here for more details about our [bereavement cafes](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/bereavement-cafe). ### Bereavement Walk & Talks Join our volunteers for a gentle walk with other bereaved people. The walks last for around 1 hour and afterwards we encourage people to stay for a cuppa and a chat in the cafe. Walks take place in the following locations: * 1st Thursday - Bushy Park * 1st Friday - Bushy Park * 2nd Wednesday - Richmond park * 2nd Thursday - Horton Country Park * 3rd Wednesday - Painshill * 4th Thursday Claremont Landscape Gardens. The walks are free to join but places are limited. please email walkandtalk@pah.org.uk for more details, and to reserve your space. ### Bereavement support library When a friend or family member dies, you may not feel ready to talk to anyone about what you’re feeling. Reading about death and grief, whether real or fictional, can help people make better sense of grief and bereavement. The Hospice Library has a loanable collection about bereavement. You’ll need to join the Library and complete a Library induction before borrowing resources. Email [library@pah.org.uk](mailto:library@pah.org.uk) to book an appointment. [Join the library](https://goo.gl/forms/8Sk8X22xkdK62mww2)

name: The Bradbury Centre
description: **What we offer:** * A bright, purpose-built day centre close to the centre of Kingston. * Experienced, warm and welcoming staff and volunteers who will ensure you feel respected and at home. * A huge variety of activities including chair-based exercise, singing, art activities, book club, cooking, gardening, mindfulness sessions, quizzes, puzzles, games, visits from local schools, visiting speakers, hand massage and occasional local daytrips. * An enclosed patio garden and summer house for use in the warmer months of the year. * Light refreshments. * A daily 2-course lunch included. **When:** * We are open on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays from 10:00-14:30. * You can [find our current timetable online](https://www.staywellservices.org.uk/Handlers/Download.ashx?IDMF=735f46d2-16b8-4dc1-95c2-0d67829d541b) Please note that people using the centre will need to be able to manage their own personal care. The Bradbury can accept members from within or near Kingston Borough, including Chessington, Surbiton, New Malden, Kingston, Tolworth, Ham and Hampton Wick. Our day centre is the perfect place to connect with like-minded people aged over 65 who are looking for opportunities for social contact, cognitive stimulation, gentle exercise and traditional food in a safe and well-supported environment. Our trained staff are experienced at supporting people living with a mild to moderate dementia or cognitive impairment as well as many other health issues and frailty. We are able to provide personalised support as well as signposting to a variety of other services offered by Staywell including Raleigh House Day Centre, Help at Home services, Handyperson services, Information and Advice and specialist support. Respect and dignity are at the heart of what we do, ensuring that everyone who attends The Bradbury is valued, welcomed and seen. We can't wait to welcome you! name: The Bradbury Centre
description: **What we offer:** * A bright, purpose-built day centre close to the centre of Kingston. * Experienced, warm and welcoming staff and volunteers who will ensure you feel respected and at home. * A huge variety of activities including chair-based exercise, singing, art activities, book club, cooking, gardening, mindfulness sessions, quizzes, puzzles, games, visits from local schools, visiting speakers, hand massage and occasional local daytrips. * An enclosed patio garden and summer house for use in the warmer months of the year. * Light refreshments. * A daily 2-course lunch included. **When:** * We are open on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays from 10:00-14:30. * You can [find our current timetable online](https://www.staywellservices.org.uk/Handlers/Download.ashx?IDMF=735f46d2-16b8-4dc1-95c2-0d67829d541b) Please note that people using the centre will need to be able to manage their own personal care. The Bradbury can accept members from within or near Kingston Borough, including Chessington, Surbiton, New Malden, Kingston, Tolworth, Ham and Hampton Wick. Our day centre is the perfect place to connect with like-minded people aged over 65 who are looking for opportunities for social contact, cognitive stimulation, gentle exercise and traditional food in a safe and well-supported environment. Our trained staff are experienced at supporting people living with a mild to moderate dementia or cognitive impairment as well as many other health issues and frailty. We are able to provide personalised support as well as signposting to a variety of other services offered by Staywell including Raleigh House Day Centre, Help at Home services, Handyperson services, Information and Advice and specialist support. Respect and dignity are at the heart of what we do, ensuring that everyone who attends The Bradbury is valued, welcomed and seen. We can't wait to welcome you! name: Healthy Start: Food and Vitamins
description: **What is Healthy Start?** -------------------------- If you’re more than 10 weeks pregnant or have a child under 4, you may be entitled to get help to buy healthy food and milk. From April 2026. the weekly payment amount has increased. If you’re eligible, you’ll be sent a Healthy Start card with money on it that you can use in some UK shops. We’ll add your benefit onto this card every 4 weeks. You can use your card to buy: * plain liquid cow’s milk * fresh, frozen, and tinned fruit and vegetables * fresh, dried, and tinned pulses * infant formula milk based on cow’s milk You can also use your card to collect: * Healthy Start vitamins – these support you during pregnancy and breastfeeding * vitamin drops for babies and young children – these are suitable from birth to 4 years old **How to apply?** ----------------- **If you get Universal Credit, your family's monthly 'take-home pay' from employment is £408 or less, and are more than 10 weeks pregnant or have parental responsibility for at least one child under 4 years old.** You can [apply online](https://www.healthystart.nhs.uk/how-to-apply/). To apply, you will need your: * name * address * date of birth * National Insurance number * baby’s due date (if you’re pregnant) * Universal Credit statement (your application for Healthy Start must match these details) [Kingston's Children's Centres](https://kr.afcinfo.org.uk/pages/community-information/information-and-advice/children-centres) are able to help you complete the Healthy Start application if you need support.

name: Healthy Start: Food and Vitamins
description: **What is Healthy Start?** -------------------------- If you’re more than 10 weeks pregnant or have a child under 4, you may be entitled to get help to buy healthy food and milk. From April 2026. the weekly payment amount has increased. If you’re eligible, you’ll be sent a Healthy Start card with money on it that you can use in some UK shops. We’ll add your benefit onto this card every 4 weeks. You can use your card to buy: * plain liquid cow’s milk * fresh, frozen, and tinned fruit and vegetables * fresh, dried, and tinned pulses * infant formula milk based on cow’s milk You can also use your card to collect: * Healthy Start vitamins – these support you during pregnancy and breastfeeding * vitamin drops for babies and young children – these are suitable from birth to 4 years old **How to apply?** ----------------- **If you get Universal Credit, your family's monthly 'take-home pay' from employment is £408 or less, and are more than 10 weeks pregnant or have parental responsibility for at least one child under 4 years old.** You can [apply online](https://www.healthystart.nhs.uk/how-to-apply/). To apply, you will need your: * name * address * date of birth * National Insurance number * baby’s due date (if you’re pregnant) * Universal Credit statement (your application for Healthy Start must match these details) [Kingston's Children's Centres](https://kr.afcinfo.org.uk/pages/community-information/information-and-advice/children-centres) are able to help you complete the Healthy Start application if you need support.

name: Mind: Money and Mental Health
description: Learning how mental health and money are connected might help if you're struggling. Sorting things out might feel like an overwhelming task. And lots of things may be out of your control. But try taking things one step at a time. The tips on this page are to help you get started. * [Mental health can affect the way you deal with money](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/money-and-mental-health/the-link-between-money-and-mental-health/#mental-health-can-affect-money) * [Money problems can affect your mental health](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/money-and-mental-health/the-link-between-money-and-mental-health/#money-can-affect-mental-health) * [Feelings associated with money](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/money-and-mental-health/the-link-between-money-and-mental-health/#feelings-associated-with-money) * [Get to know your money and mood patterns](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/money-and-mental-health/the-link-between-money-and-mental-health/#get-to-know-your-money-and-mood) * [Overspending when you’re unwell](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/money-and-mental-health/the-link-between-money-and-mental-health/#overspending) Mental health can affect the way you deal with money ---------------------------------------------------- These are some common ways your mental health can affect the way you deal with money: * If you're feeling [low or depressed](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/types-of-mental-health-problems/depression/about-depression/), you may lack motivation to manage your finances. It might not feel worth trying. * Spending may give you a brief high, so you might [overspend ](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/money-and-mental-health/the-link-between-money-and-mental-health/#overspending)to feel better. * You might make impulsive financial decisions when you’re experiencing [mania or hypomania](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/types-of-mental-health-problems/hypomania-and-mania/about-hypomania-and-mania/). * If your mental health affects your ability to work or study, this might reduce your income. * You might avoid doing things to stay on top of your money, like opening bills or checking your bank account. You might try to avoid thinking about money completely. * Having a mental health problem might affect your [insurance](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/guides-to-support-and-services/insurance-cover-and-mental-health/your-insurance-rights/), so you end up paying more. Money problems can affect your mental health -------------------------------------------- These are some common ways money can affect your mental health: * Certain situations might trigger feelings of [anxiety and panic](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/types-of-mental-health-problems/anxiety-problems/understanding-anxiety/), like opening envelopes or attending a benefits assessment. * Worrying about money can lead to[ sleep problems](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/types-of-mental-health-problems/sleep-problems/). * You might not be able to afford the things you need to stay well. This might be housing, food, water, heating, or treatments like medication and therapy. See our information on [what to do if you can’t afford the things you need](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/money-and-mental-health/organising-your-finances/#if-you-cant-afford-bills-or-food). * Money problems can affect your social life and relationships. You might feel [lonely or isolated](https://www.mind.org.uk/information-support/tips-for-everyday-living/loneliness/), or like you can’t afford to do the things you want to.

description: The Association for Post-Natal Illness is a Registered Charity established in 1979 to: * Provide support to mothers suffering from post-natal illness; * Increase public awareness of the illness; * To encourage research into its cause and nature. The work of the Association is essential as post-natal illness affects between 70,000 and 100,000 women and their families in the UK every year. The Association offers a helpline, information packs for people and professionals, and a network of volunteers who have themselves recovered from postnatal illness. **Our helpline is free to access**, via telephone, email or online chat. The helpline is open Monday-Friday 10am-2pm. Our staff will do everything that they can to help you and they will be able to offer you information and reassurance. You can also get in touch using [our contact form](https://apni.org/contact/) if you prefer.

name: Express CIC Autism Service’s & Support
description: Welcome to Express. Express is an independent user led voluntary sector organisation supporting autistic young people and their families. We are not a commissioned service. We are not an urgent service. We are not funded to provide our professional services and therefore do have to charge for those but this does mean we are not restricted by boundaries so we are open to all and all are very welcome to attend any of our events or groups. **We offer five support streams: ** [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/what-we-do](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/what-we-do) and our [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/impact](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/impact) **Counselling** both for parent/carers & a specialist service for autistic people age 11+ [counselling@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:counselling@expresscic.org.uk) **Creative Therapy **both at Express & Outreach to schools or home - 1:1 & small groups for autistic people age 5+ (play therapy 4+) alongside sibling groups. We are also able to offer family consultations and family therapy [therapy@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:therapy@expresscic.org.uk) **Occupational Therapy** offer including assessments and reports [therapy@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:therapy@expresscic.org.uk) **Clubs** for autistic people from age 8+ [clubs@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:clubs@expresscic.org.uk) **Peer Support** for parents/carers Mum’s group, Dad’s group, specific PDA group, specific Gender group. Facebook closed forum, WhatsApp, online and in person [jane@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:jane@expresscic.org.uk) **Training, Workshops & Events** [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/training](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/training) & [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/events](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/events) We offer support both pre and post diagnosis. **Whilst our peer support services are free, there is a charge for therapy and counselling services.** We rely on donations and fundraising to ensure this is heavily subsidised. Bursary places may be available for local families where there is evidenced need and we have financial capacity. In some cases, organisations, schools and professionals buy in the service from us. **Please note**: We offer predominantly low level preventative work but we are also able to offer specialist packages for a higher level of need where the referral is direct from an NHS service for example SWL ICB and funding has already been agreed. All our therapy services are run by qualified counsellors or therapists experienced in working with autistic children and young people. Our therapists have completed PDA society training. All our therapies and groups have an assessment process prior to an offer being made to ensure the service is providing the best support for both the individual and the group. Please see details of **fees** where funded by parent/carers [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/fees](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/fees) . Professional referrals are on a case by case basis and as part of a multi-agency package (different costs apply). **Join Express** **Register with us** - complete & return the attached registration form - select if you would like to be added to a WhatsApp group - specify which one. There is a wealth of peer support and experience shared. **Access our services** - email the relevant lead email listed above to request further details and a referral form **Keep up to date** with our services - sign up to our eNewsletter [here](https://expresscic.us3.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=f01719d4eb48d6a9956c5eea9&id=688812c108)

name: Express CIC Autism Service’s & Support
description: Welcome to Express. Express is an independent user led voluntary sector organisation supporting autistic young people and their families. We are not a commissioned service. We are not an urgent service. We are not funded to provide our professional services and therefore do have to charge for those but this does mean we are not restricted by boundaries so we are open to all and all are very welcome to attend any of our events or groups. **We offer five support streams: ** [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/what-we-do](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/what-we-do) and our [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/impact](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/impact) **Counselling** both for parent/carers & a specialist service for autistic people age 11+ [counselling@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:counselling@expresscic.org.uk) **Creative Therapy **both at Express & Outreach to schools or home - 1:1 & small groups for autistic people age 5+ (play therapy 4+) alongside sibling groups. We are also able to offer family consultations and family therapy [therapy@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:therapy@expresscic.org.uk) **Occupational Therapy** offer including assessments and reports [therapy@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:therapy@expresscic.org.uk) **Clubs** for autistic people from age 8+ [clubs@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:clubs@expresscic.org.uk) **Peer Support** for parents/carers Mum’s group, Dad’s group, specific PDA group, specific Gender group. Facebook closed forum, WhatsApp, online and in person [jane@expresscic.org.uk](mailto:jane@expresscic.org.uk) **Training, Workshops & Events** [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/training](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/training) & [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/events](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/events) We offer support both pre and post diagnosis. **Whilst our peer support services are free, there is a charge for therapy and counselling services.** We rely on donations and fundraising to ensure this is heavily subsidised. Bursary places may be available for local families where there is evidenced need and we have financial capacity. In some cases, organisations, schools and professionals buy in the service from us. **Please note**: We offer predominantly low level preventative work but we are also able to offer specialist packages for a higher level of need where the referral is direct from an NHS service for example SWL ICB and funding has already been agreed. All our therapy services are run by qualified counsellors or therapists experienced in working with autistic children and young people. Our therapists have completed PDA society training. All our therapies and groups have an assessment process prior to an offer being made to ensure the service is providing the best support for both the individual and the group. Please see details of **fees** where funded by parent/carers [https://www.expresscic.org.uk/fees](https://www.expresscic.org.uk/fees) . Professional referrals are on a case by case basis and as part of a multi-agency package (different costs apply). **Join Express** **Register with us** - complete & return the attached registration form - select if you would like to be added to a WhatsApp group - specify which one. There is a wealth of peer support and experience shared. **Access our services** - email the relevant lead email listed above to request further details and a referral form **Keep up to date** with our services - sign up to our eNewsletter [here](https://expresscic.us3.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=f01719d4eb48d6a9956c5eea9&id=688812c108)

name: NHS Health Checks
description: For people aged between 40 and 74 who have not been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, heart disease, stroke or kidney disease. This service offers a free NHS Health Check to identify risk of Cardiovascular Disease (CVD). **How do I get an NHS Health Check?** ------------------------------------- If you're aged 40 to 74 and do not have a pre-existing health condition, you should be invited to an NHS Health Check by your GP or local council every 5 years. In some areas, you may be invited to do your NHS Health Check online. If you have not been invited for an NHS Health Check and think you're eligible, contact your GP practice. **What happens at an NHS Health Check?** ---------------------------------------- Your NHS Health Check will usually be done by a healthcare professional such as a pharmacist, a nurse at your GP surgery, or a healthcare assistant. The check takes about 20 to 30 minutes and usually includes: * measuring your height and weight * measuring your waist * a [blood pressure test](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/blood-pressure-test/) * a [cholesterol test](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/high-cholesterol/getting-tested/), and possibly a blood sugar level test You may be asked to have a blood test at or before the NHS Health Check. You'll also be asked some questions about your health including: * whether any of your close relatives have had any medical conditions * if you smoke, and how much * if you drink alcohol, and how much * how much physical activity you do Your age, sex and ethnicity will also be recorded.

description: This 2 hour online class will cover all the information you need to get breastfeeding off to a good start. Partners are welcome to attend. Topics covered include * How to establish breastfeeding * Stimulating your milk supply * Signs your baby is feeding well * Skin-to-skin contact * Common challenges * Coping strategies * How partners can become involved We recommend attending your antenatal infant feeding class from when you are 34 weeks into your pregnancy. name: Blue Badge Scheme
description: Displaying the Blue Badge in your car allows you to park in dedicated parking bays. This helps you park closer to your destination. Even if you don't have a car you can use your Blue Badge in someone else's car, when they drive you somewhere. When you automatically qualify for a Blue Badge ----------------------------------------------- You automatically qualify for a Blue Badge if you're aged 3 or over and at least one of the following applies. You: * receive the higher rate of the mobility component of the [Disability Living Allowance (DLA)](https://www.gov.uk/dla-disability-living-allowance-benefit) * receive the mobility component of [Personal Independence Payment (PIP)](https://www.gov.uk/pip): * score 8 points or more under the 'moving around' activity * or score 10 points under descriptor E of 'planning and following journeys' (unable to undertake any journey due to overwhelming psychological distress) * are registered blind (severely sight impaired) * receive a War Pensioners’ Mobility Supplement (WPMS) * have received a lump sum benefit within tariff levels 1 to 8 of the Armed Forces and Reserve Forces (Compensation) Scheme, and have been certified as having a permanent and substantial disability that causes inability to walk or very considerable difficulty in walking * are terminally ill and include an SR1 medical report with your application If your qualifying award is time-limited, your Blue Badge will only be issued for that period (up to 3 years). When you may qualify for a Blue Badge ------------------------------------- You may be eligible for a badge if one or more of the following apply. You: * cannot walk at all * cannot walk without help from someone else or using mobility aids * find walking very difficult due to pain, breathlessness or the time it takes * find walking is dangerous to your health and safety * have a severe disability in both arms and drive regularly, making it impossible or very difficult to operate parking machines * have a child under the age of 3 with a medical condition that means the child always needs to be accompanied by bulky medical equipment * have a child under the age of 3 with a medical condition that means the child must always be kept near a vehicle in case they need emergency medical treatment * are constantly a significant risk to yourself or others near vehicles, in traffic or car parks * struggle severely to plan or follow a journey * find it very difficult or impossible to control your actions and lack awareness of the impact you could have on others * regularly have intense and overwhelming responses to situations causing temporary loss of behavioural control * frequently become extremely anxious or fearful of public or open spaces Your disability should be expected to last for at least 4 years. [Find out more about who can get a Blue Badge on GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/blue-badge-can-i-get-one/can-i-get-a-blue-badge) [Apply for a Blue Badge on the Council website](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/roads-and-travel/accessible-travel/apply-blue-badge).
intro: A Blue Badge is a parking permit which allows people with disabilities or health conditions to park closer to their destination.

name: Blue Badge Scheme
description: Displaying the Blue Badge in your car allows you to park in dedicated parking bays. This helps you park closer to your destination. Even if you don't have a car you can use your Blue Badge in someone else's car, when they drive you somewhere. When you automatically qualify for a Blue Badge ----------------------------------------------- You automatically qualify for a Blue Badge if you're aged 3 or over and at least one of the following applies. You: * receive the higher rate of the mobility component of the [Disability Living Allowance (DLA)](https://www.gov.uk/dla-disability-living-allowance-benefit) * receive the mobility component of [Personal Independence Payment (PIP)](https://www.gov.uk/pip): * score 8 points or more under the 'moving around' activity * or score 10 points under descriptor E of 'planning and following journeys' (unable to undertake any journey due to overwhelming psychological distress) * are registered blind (severely sight impaired) * receive a War Pensioners’ Mobility Supplement (WPMS) * have received a lump sum benefit within tariff levels 1 to 8 of the Armed Forces and Reserve Forces (Compensation) Scheme, and have been certified as having a permanent and substantial disability that causes inability to walk or very considerable difficulty in walking * are terminally ill and include an SR1 medical report with your application If your qualifying award is time-limited, your Blue Badge will only be issued for that period (up to 3 years). When you may qualify for a Blue Badge ------------------------------------- You may be eligible for a badge if one or more of the following apply. You: * cannot walk at all * cannot walk without help from someone else or using mobility aids * find walking very difficult due to pain, breathlessness or the time it takes * find walking is dangerous to your health and safety * have a severe disability in both arms and drive regularly, making it impossible or very difficult to operate parking machines * have a child under the age of 3 with a medical condition that means the child always needs to be accompanied by bulky medical equipment * have a child under the age of 3 with a medical condition that means the child must always be kept near a vehicle in case they need emergency medical treatment * are constantly a significant risk to yourself or others near vehicles, in traffic or car parks * struggle severely to plan or follow a journey * find it very difficult or impossible to control your actions and lack awareness of the impact you could have on others * regularly have intense and overwhelming responses to situations causing temporary loss of behavioural control * frequently become extremely anxious or fearful of public or open spaces Your disability should be expected to last for at least 4 years. [Find out more about who can get a Blue Badge on GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/blue-badge-can-i-get-one/can-i-get-a-blue-badge) [Apply for a Blue Badge on the Council website](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/roads-and-travel/accessible-travel/apply-blue-badge).

name: Sight and Hearing Service
description: Our sight and hearing team provides specialist advice, equipment and rehabilitation for adults with sight or hearing loss. **Local organisations that can help:** We work closely with local organisations who provide information and advice for sight and hearing loss, including: * [Surbiton Deaf Social Club](https://www.facebook.com/groups/113631768678496/) * [Remark! deaf community](https://www.remarkcommunity.org/) * [Kingston Association for the Blind (KAB)](https://www.kingstonassociationforblind.org/) * [more services for people with a physical disability on Connected Kingston](https://connectedkingston.uk/collections/disability-and-inclusion) **Get specialist support from the sight and hearing service:** Our sight and hearing service provides advice and support for adults who: * have sight or hearing loss * live in Kingston * are over 18 We provide services and support to help you maintain or regain your independence. If something has changed with your sight or hearing If you think something might have changed with your sight or hearing, you should contact your GP. We can’t diagnose conditions or give medical treatment. **What we can provide:** We can give advice over the phone, or visit you at home to talk to you and your family or carer about how you're affected in your everyday life. We’ll assess what you can do and what you find difficult to work out the best support to help you. We can offer advice, equipment, or rehabilitation services. **Advice:** We can provide advice about your condition, including: * travel options that might help you, like a Freedom Pass, Taxi card or Blue Badge * information about local and national organisations for people with sight or hearing loss * the benefits of registering as sight impaired **Equipment:** We can give you advice about, and might be able to provide, equipment like: * talking clocks, task lighting and kitchen gadgets * amplified phones and doorbells * alternatives to print books like library audiobook services * pager alerting systems * TV loops to hear the television * advice on accessible technology and help to use existing tools on smartphones and computers We’ll show you how to use new equipment to make sure you’re comfortable with how it works. There is no cost for most equipment. **Rehabilitation:** Our team members can give training and advice on activities like: * safe kitchen skills, like different ways of making a hot drink * getting out and about safely and teaching you to use the appropriate white cane **Contact the sight and hearing service:** Call the contact centre and ask to speak to the sight and hearing service, and a member of the team will contact you. Phone: 020 8547 5000

name: English & Maths classes
description: **Functional Skills English and Maths** Functional Skills courses help native and fluent speakers of English to achieve English language and Maths skills for life and work. Courses start at Entry Level and progress to Level 2. You will attend one class a week and are expected to attend every session. All classes are small. You will be supported by a high quality tutor throughout the course and work towards taking exams at the end of the year. **GCSE English and Maths** GCSE courses begin in September, with exams taken the following May/June. These are intensive courses and you will need to attend every session and be able to do at least 6 hours of independent study each week. **Fees** Courses are free if you are 19 years old or over and have lived in an EU Country continually for the past three years. Please note that if you hold a GCSE C/4 or above in your chosen subject you will need to pay for the GCSE course. **How to sign up** **[Complete the course form](https://bit.ly/KAE-EnglishMaths22-23) if you are interested in any of these courses.** All candidates must take an assessment before signing up to determine their level and readiness for the courses. If your assessment shows that an English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) course will be of more benefit you will be referred to an ESOL class. **Additional Learning Support** If you have a learning difficulty or disability we can arrange for you to speak to our Learning Support Manager to help decide the best ways to support you during your course. **We also offer:** * Support sessions for our GCSE and Functional Skills learners * Mock exams for GCSE learners * GCSE Maths Revision courses * Regular reviews of your progress with your tutor
intro: We offer courses to help you to develop practical English and Maths skills needed to live, study and work.
organisation: Kingston Adult Education Kingston Adult Education We have our core delivery: ESOL, English, Maths, Digital, Vocational, Health & Fitness, Arts, Crafts, Languages, Writing, History and we have some wonderful new courses for you to turn your hand to. Along with new craft workshops and courses, we’ve also added new art courses and workshops: Why not enjoy Botanical Watercolours, Drawing & Painting Animals, Landscape Painting, Oil Painting or Mindful Art? Whether you're looking to meet new people, explore new interests, get a job, gain qualifications for your career or keep your mind and body active we have something for everyone. Along with our wonderful Tai Chi, Pilates, and Mindful Movement courses, why not try our new Journaling for Wellbeing to help build your resilience and improve your wellbeing? With both **online** and **in-person** classes available at locations across the borough, you can easily find a course that fits your needs. In addition, many of our courses are **free** as they are government funded or offered at reduced rates, and we provide discounts based on your circumstances, so please contact us to find out more. Enjoy your courses and being a part of our wonderful adult education community. name: Champions for Change
description: What is Mental Health Stigma? ------------------------------ Mental health stigma is negative attitudes, pre-judgements, prejudices, and behaviours towards people with mental health conditions. Stigma includes misconceptions about the risks posed to the public by people affected by mental health problems, and the use of pejorative language in describing mental illness and those affected by it. Stigma may be exacerbated by the negative portrayal of mental illness in the media. What is a Champion? ------------------- Our campaign is led by Champions, people who consider themselves to have experience of poor mental health and/or who are currently living with poor mental health. You do not have to have a formal diagnosis of mental illness to be a Champion and you do not have to disclose (share) all of your experiences with us. If you have experience of mental ill-health, whether formally diagnosed or not, and you are looking to share your experiences (openly or anonymously) to help bust myths about what someone with mental ill-health is like, and to end the stigma of talking about mental health, then this could be the role for you. Want to get involved? --------------------- The Hub’s role is to get people in Kingston to talk about mental health and change the way people act and think about mental health. This could be a chat over coffee, a talk, a music event or an open day. These different events are led by champions. We are always looking for **champions**; people with lived experience of mental health who want to change behaviour and attitudes towards mental health in a more positive way. Champions will receive training and support so they can talk about mental health and help promote the Hub’s work. [Find out what a champion does](https://www.healthwatchkingston.org.uk/become-time-change-champion) or get in touch if you have any questions. If you would like to [sign up as a Champion, please fill out this brief form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeVvpy591BxLHrCo8I4mCPCSWVroMguUMAzl9lQ2RbB4W3DmA/viewform). name: Champions for Change
description: What is Mental Health Stigma? ------------------------------ Mental health stigma is negative attitudes, pre-judgements, prejudices, and behaviours towards people with mental health conditions. Stigma includes misconceptions about the risks posed to the public by people affected by mental health problems, and the use of pejorative language in describing mental illness and those affected by it. Stigma may be exacerbated by the negative portrayal of mental illness in the media. What is a Champion? ------------------- Our campaign is led by Champions, people who consider themselves to have experience of poor mental health and/or who are currently living with poor mental health. You do not have to have a formal diagnosis of mental illness to be a Champion and you do not have to disclose (share) all of your experiences with us. If you have experience of mental ill-health, whether formally diagnosed or not, and you are looking to share your experiences (openly or anonymously) to help bust myths about what someone with mental ill-health is like, and to end the stigma of talking about mental health, then this could be the role for you. Want to get involved? --------------------- The Hub’s role is to get people in Kingston to talk about mental health and change the way people act and think about mental health. This could be a chat over coffee, a talk, a music event or an open day. These different events are led by champions. We are always looking for **champions**; people with lived experience of mental health who want to change behaviour and attitudes towards mental health in a more positive way. Champions will receive training and support so they can talk about mental health and help promote the Hub’s work. [Find out what a champion does](https://www.healthwatchkingston.org.uk/become-time-change-champion) or get in touch if you have any questions. If you would like to [sign up as a Champion, please fill out this brief form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeVvpy591BxLHrCo8I4mCPCSWVroMguUMAzl9lQ2RbB4W3DmA/viewform). name: Hatha Yoga
description: Hatha Yoga at Be Happy Yoga is suitable for all levels, including complete beginners. If you join as a beginner, you will benefit from observing many students who already have a very established yoga practice. Thanks to many modifications and options, everyone finds the class interesting, approachable, rewarding, and enjoyable. It’s an excellent complement to more dynamic styles like YogaFlow or YogaStrong plus gentle practices such as YogaChill, allowing students to explore the more technical and foundational elements of yoga breathwork and asana. Hatha Yoga is a traditional yoga style that focuses on slow, mindful movement, precise postures (asanas), and breath control (pranayama). Yoga means union and the word “Hatha” comes from the Sanskrit words “ha” meaning sun and “tha” meaning moon, symbolising the balance of opposing energies – strength and ease, activity and calm. Hatha Yoga offers a gentle but strengthening practice that connects body, breath, and mind, creating greater inner harmony. This class emphasises alignment and precision, often holding postures longer than in dynamic styles to deepen awareness and experience of the energetic effects of each pose. This practice is rooted in the yogic principles of Sukham (ease) and Sthiram (steadiness) – teaching us how to maintain stability in the body paired with comfort and relaxation. **What to Expect** * A varied class with weekly themes focusing on different breathwork techniques and yoga postures * Slower pace to allow time to refine alignment, cultivate precision, and deeply feel each posture’s impact * Use of props like the wall for support and alignment assistance * Classes ending with savasana, a deep relaxation to integrate your practice * Small group setting ensuring plenty of individual attention from the teacher

organisation: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). name: Hatha Yoga
description: Hatha Yoga at Be Happy Yoga is suitable for all levels, including complete beginners. If you join as a beginner, you will benefit from observing many students who already have a very established yoga practice. Thanks to many modifications and options, everyone finds the class interesting, approachable, rewarding, and enjoyable. It’s an excellent complement to more dynamic styles like YogaFlow or YogaStrong plus gentle practices such as YogaChill, allowing students to explore the more technical and foundational elements of yoga breathwork and asana. Hatha Yoga is a traditional yoga style that focuses on slow, mindful movement, precise postures (asanas), and breath control (pranayama). Yoga means union and the word “Hatha” comes from the Sanskrit words “ha” meaning sun and “tha” meaning moon, symbolising the balance of opposing energies – strength and ease, activity and calm. Hatha Yoga offers a gentle but strengthening practice that connects body, breath, and mind, creating greater inner harmony. This class emphasises alignment and precision, often holding postures longer than in dynamic styles to deepen awareness and experience of the energetic effects of each pose. This practice is rooted in the yogic principles of Sukham (ease) and Sthiram (steadiness) – teaching us how to maintain stability in the body paired with comfort and relaxation. **What to Expect** * A varied class with weekly themes focusing on different breathwork techniques and yoga postures * Slower pace to allow time to refine alignment, cultivate precision, and deeply feel each posture’s impact * Use of props like the wall for support and alignment assistance * Classes ending with savasana, a deep relaxation to integrate your practice * Small group setting ensuring plenty of individual attention from the teacher

description: The project is supported by **peers** - volunteers who have their own experiences of mental health issues. Volunteers have been trained in Intentional Peer Support which is a course that focuses on how to support people as equals by using shared experiences, by listening and by moving forwards. Peers are matched with a service user and work on specific goals to improve their mental wellbeing, improve self-confidence and self-esteem and connect people with others in their local community. You can self-refer, but we also take referrals from GPs, Care Coordinators or other medical professionals. Service users must be from the borough of Kingston upon Thames.

name: The Sound Doctor: Back Pain
description: If you've got low back pain life can be pretty miserable. It can stop you doing the things you enjoy and keep you off work as well as being incredibly painful. We hope that after watching these short films you'll feel much more confident and better equipped to deal with your back pain and stop it happening again. You don't have to watch all the films and you can watch them in any order. But there's something in all of them that'll help you recover or cope better with your pain. You may find the case studies helpful - remember, you're not alone! - and the simple exercises explained in the last section can help you keep your back in good shape for life! ### [Click here to access videos from the Back Pain Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/23tlote4), these cover: * Understanding Back Pain * Coping with Back Pain * Therapies that may help * Exercises * Case Studies You can also [register for free to our Back Pain course.](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/courses/backpain-course) Our mission is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs. You can find [videos on a range of other long-term conditions on our services page](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/services).

name: Migrant Advocacy Service
description: Who do we support? ------------------ We support vulnerable migrants who live, work or study in Kingston. We give guidance to people with immigration restrictions and without access to public funds and benefits. We are able to support those with limited digital skills or English as a second language. We have advisers and volunteers who speak Arabic, French, Farsi, Pashto, Dari, Urdu, Russian, Ukrainian, Punjabi, Nepali _Please Note:_ We unfortunately cannot give immigration advice at this time. Find a certified immigration adviser near you on the government portal [https://portal.oisc.gov.uk/s/adviser-finder](https://portal.oisc.gov.uk/s/adviser-finder) …………………………………. What service do we provide? --------------------------- **Face to face, telephone and email advice** Our trained multi-lingual advisers can assist clients on a wide range of subjects including: housing, benefits, disability, education, health, eVisas, and bills. You can attend drop-ins on **Mondays and Fridays** at Guildhall 2, KT1 1EU (opposite the Job Centre) **10am - 12pm** **New eVisa Advice Project (see details of days and times below)** We can support you with your eVisa, including by: creating a UKVI account, accessing your eVisa account, creating a share code, and using your account. EVisa appointments are on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 9:30 am - 3:30pm at Guildhall 2, KT1 1EU (opposite the Job Centre) Please book an appointment in advance by filling in the form on our website [https://www.migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk/evisas](https://www.migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk/evisas), calling us on our main number or emailing us at [evisa@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk](mailto:evisa@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk) …………………………………. General Telephone or Email Advice --------------------------------- Our advisers are available to take your calls between **10am and 5pm Monday to Friday** Main phone line: **0203 488 0638** WhatsApp: **07738 762 636** Email: **advice@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk** ………………………………….

name: Migrant Advocacy Service
description: Who do we support? ------------------ We support vulnerable migrants who live, work or study in Kingston. We give guidance to people with immigration restrictions and without access to public funds and benefits. We are able to support those with limited digital skills or English as a second language. We have advisers and volunteers who speak Arabic, French, Farsi, Pashto, Dari, Urdu, Russian, Ukrainian, Punjabi, Nepali _Please Note:_ We unfortunately cannot give immigration advice at this time. Find a certified immigration adviser near you on the government portal [https://portal.oisc.gov.uk/s/adviser-finder](https://portal.oisc.gov.uk/s/adviser-finder) …………………………………. What service do we provide? --------------------------- **Face to face, telephone and email advice** Our trained multi-lingual advisers can assist clients on a wide range of subjects including: housing, benefits, disability, education, health, eVisas, and bills. You can attend drop-ins on **Mondays and Fridays** at Guildhall 2, KT1 1EU (opposite the Job Centre) **10am - 12pm** **New eVisa Advice Project (see details of days and times below)** We can support you with your eVisa, including by: creating a UKVI account, accessing your eVisa account, creating a share code, and using your account. EVisa appointments are on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 9:30 am - 3:30pm at Guildhall 2, KT1 1EU (opposite the Job Centre) Please book an appointment in advance by filling in the form on our website [https://www.migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk/evisas](https://www.migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk/evisas), calling us on our main number or emailing us at [evisa@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk](mailto:evisa@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk) …………………………………. General Telephone or Email Advice --------------------------------- Our advisers are available to take your calls between **10am and 5pm Monday to Friday** Main phone line: **0203 488 0638** WhatsApp: **07738 762 636** Email: **advice@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk** ………………………………….

description: Let’s quit smoking together this **Stoptober**. There’s no need to go it alone. name: Friends of Latchmere Recreation Ground
description: Friends of Latchmere Recreation Ground (FoLaR) aims to achieve: * Community cohesion, * well-being and * environmental improvements Working with the Council and our stakeholders, we are increasing biodiversity on the Rec through: * planting trees * creating a sensory garden * Children's Nature Zone and * a Wildlife Pond. **Other activities / facilities** * Kingston Little League has been providing excellent football opportunities for young people of all abilities for the past 40 years; * we host a Junior Parkrun every week; and * we are home to The Latch Cafe, which serves tasty and healthy refreshments. We aim to increase the range of recreational activities providing something for everyone. **Volunteering with FoLaR** There are many opportunities for engaging with nature while helping on our projects.
