name: Mind Football Team
description: Kingstonian Mind United FC is run by Mind in Kingston and affiliated to Kingstonian FC, Kingston’s local football club. It and meets once a week for training and competes in the Surrey Community league. The team has been running for over 5 years and some of our current players were the founders of our first club A3 Milan FC, which was established in 2002. There is a strong ethos for inclusivity in that everyone whatever their footballing ability has an equal say and can fully participate. **When:** * Tuesdays: 3.30 - 4.30pm * Wednesdays: 3-5pm **How to sign up:** Please complete our Services and Support Enquiry Form on our website. A member of our team will get back to you. If you are working with clients who are experiencing or recovering from mental ill health, and who feel they may benefit from this project, please complete our Services and Support Enquiry Form on our website. Our short video features footage of our training sessions, and you can hear more about the project here. We are supported in both training sessions by coaches from the Chelsea FC Foundation. The training sessions are free to attend and we offer a trial period for new members. There is currently a waiting list to join. We welcome referrals for adults aged 18 years and over and of any gender, though the majority of the current players do identify as men. Beginners and all experience levels welcome – the sessions have a welcoming and supportive atmosphere. **For additional info please contact:** [wellbeingactivites@mindinkingston.org.uk](mailto:wellbeingactivites@mindinkingston.org.uk)

description: Join us for: **Tea and Toast:** An opportunity to connect with other carers and our team over a hot drink, with a different speaker each month. When: 10-12pm, last Friday of the month. name: Buddy Scheme
description: The Buddy scheme helps people who are socially isolated to get out and enjoy fun activities with someone they like and trust. It helps with confidence, social skills, self-esteem, mental health, communication skills and more. Recent quotes from our service users about their experiences include: * 'Makes me feel good' * 'Happy, exciting' * 'Gives me a social life and helps with my mental health' For volunteers it offers a meaningful opportunity to make a positive difference to someone in the community. The most common words used by our volunteers about being on the scheme are 'rewarding', 'enjoyable', and 'fun'. The Buddy Scheme is oversubscribed and we are always looking for more volunteers. No experience is required and training is provided. If you have just a few hours a month to spare and are kind, considerate, patient and reliable, then we would love to hear from you. [Find out more and join the scheme on our website](https://kva.org.uk/support-for-communities/buddy-scheme/).
intro: The Buddy Scheme is a befriending project in Kingston that matches volunteers with a "buddy" who has a learning disability or autism. You will meet on a regular basis to take part in leisure activities together.

name: First Steps in Digital Skills
description: On this 10 week course you will cover basic digital skills for everyday life using computers and smartphones. **You do not need any prior experience** or skills as you will start with the very first steps. You do not need to bring your own personal computer or smartphone as we will provide all the equipment you need. However, if you have your own smartphone, feel free to bring it with you. **When?** Next course starting soon - contact us for more details **Where?** At the Hook Centre, Chessington, KT9 1EJ **Join our 10 week course and learn how to:** * Turn on and shut down a computer / device * Connect to the internet and WiFi * Use a keyboard and touchscreen * Create basic documents * Get confident with passwords * Spellcheck and do basic editing * Set up and use emails safety * Search for websites using browser software * Create online accounts * Shopp online * Comple forms and add payment details * Introduction to types of smartphones - Android, Apple, and WhatsApp To enrol or find out more details please email or phone (details to the right) or [visit our website](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/kingston-adult-education/find-a-course) to find a course.
intro: Want to improve your digital skills? Join our FREE course.
organisation: Kingston Adult Education Kingston Adult Education We have our core delivery: ESOL, English, Maths, Digital, Vocational, Health & Fitness, Arts, Crafts, Languages, Writing, History and we have some wonderful new courses for you to turn your hand to. Why not try our new Jewellery Making Workshop and if you like it, join the new course. Along with new craft workshops and courses, we’ve also added new art courses and workshops: Why not enjoy Botanical Watercolours, Drawing & Painting Animals, Landscape Painting, Oil Painting or Mindful Art? Whether you're looking to meet new people, explore new interests, get a job, gain qualifications for your career or keep your mind and body active we have something for everyone. Along with our wonderful Tai Chi, Pilates, and Mindful Movement courses, why not try our new Journaling for Wellbeing to help build your resilience and improve your wellbeing? With both **online** and **in-person** classes available at locations across the borough, you can easily find a course that fits your needs. In addition, many of our courses are **free** as they are government funded or offered at reduced rates, and we provide discounts based on your circumstances, so please contact us to find out more. Enjoy your courses and being a part of our wonderful adult education community. name: First Steps in Digital Skills
description: On this 10 week course you will cover basic digital skills for everyday life using computers and smartphones. **You do not need any prior experience** or skills as you will start with the very first steps. You do not need to bring your own personal computer or smartphone as we will provide all the equipment you need. However, if you have your own smartphone, feel free to bring it with you. **When?** Next course starting soon - contact us for more details **Where?** At the Hook Centre, Chessington, KT9 1EJ **Join our 10 week course and learn how to:** * Turn on and shut down a computer / device * Connect to the internet and WiFi * Use a keyboard and touchscreen * Create basic documents * Get confident with passwords * Spellcheck and do basic editing * Set up and use emails safety * Search for websites using browser software * Create online accounts * Shopp online * Comple forms and add payment details * Introduction to types of smartphones - Android, Apple, and WhatsApp To enrol or find out more details please email or phone (details to the right) or [visit our website](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/kingston-adult-education/find-a-course) to find a course.

description: Kingsnympton Out to Lunch Club ------------------------------ Open to everyone! Join us every Thursday during term time at our Lunch Club which is part of Together Thursdays. A wonderful team of volunteers will welcome you and offer you a delicious home cooked meal, followed by mint tea and cakes. If you prefer a builder's brew or coffee, we've got that too. ### When and Where? Come to our Out to Lunch Club every Thursday during term time 12-2pm. At Kingsnympton Park Youth and Community Centre, Kingston Hill, KT2 7RP. ### Further information: * Find out more about Together Thursdays Activities. [https://connectedkingston.uk/services/together-thursdays](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/together-thursdays) * There's a Pilates class on at 12pm so if you fancy a bit of exercise before lunch, you can do that too. Just turn up and start stretching. Some mats are available if you don't have your own. * See our ESOL page to see about English Classes * If you are an external speaker and would like to run a workshop or talk at one of our sessions, please get in touch - [info@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk](mailto:info@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk) …………………………………………………………………………. Rise Cafe --------- Open to everyone! Join us every Wednesday during term time at our weekly Cafe/ Lunch Club in collaboration with the Quaker Centre that provides: * Hot food and cold food from the MAS Community Fridge * Drinks * Games * An opportunity to meet new people ### When and Where? Come along to Rise Cafe every Wednesday from 12:30 - 3:30pm. At the Kingston Quaker Centre, Fairfield East Kingston upon Thames, KT1 2PT …………………………………………………………………………. Hong Kong Welcome Cafe ---------------------- This Cafe is orientated towards people who have come from Hong Kong. Join us on Wednesdays: You can share refreshments and a light lunch with us. All talks, activities and food and drinks served are free of charge. Wednesdays get busy but you can let us know you're coming. ### When and Where? Come along to our Hong Kong Welcome Cafe every Wednesday from 10am - 12pm. At Welcome Cafe @ Kingston Library, KT1 2PS ### Further information: * We run special talks and activities on most Wednesdays so check the [News and Updates](https://www.migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk/blog/categories/whatson) pages to find out what's going on in the coming weeks. * If you are an external speaker and would like to run a workshop or talk at one of our sessions, please get in touch - [info@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk](mailto:info@migrantadvocacyservice.org.uk)

name: Christ Church Surbiton Hill
description: ### MORNING SERVICE (10:30AM) We love having people of all ages at Christ Church. Our morning service is informal and friendly. We start the service with everyone together, then the children and young people go into groups to learn more about God and have fun, allowing parents to participate fully in the service. At the end of the service, there’s an opportunity to pray together and to chat over coffee. ### Online Service We would love to see you in person, but if you can't our services are [live-streamed](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLa79Hdh09g2bViiaM9OOXi9ZVRGRCxXhV) - for privacy, the cameras are focussed only on the platform (NB the back of heads in the front two rows are in view). ### Evening Services We have occasional gatherings for prayer, worship and discussion. ### Encounter An evening of worship, bible teaching and prayer. See our full schedule of prayer events on our [prayer page](https://www.ccsurbiton.org/prayer). ### CHILDREN & YOUTH Children and Youth are an important part of the life of Christ Church and we long for them to understand how great God is and what Jesus has done for us. We run groups for children right from 2.5 through to 14 years old, with a parent-led creche for 0-2.5. We want to ensure that the times that children are at church are happy times and provide a solid foundation for their faith. For more info on the Children's Ministry, please click here, and for more info on Youth Ministry, please click [here](https://www.ccsurbiton.org/ccyouth).
intro: Christ Church is a friendly, welcoming, informal Anglican evangelical church. We serve people of different ages and backgrounds in Surbiton and the wider world, sharing the good word of Jesus. We believe in the Bible, are filled by the Holy Spirit, and are a servant-hearted family.

description: We provide fully subsidised Cycle Skills training to suit your needs, meaning you can start improving your skills for free. This subsidy is provided by Transport for London and is subject to conditions, availability and funding. **Free one-to-one, family or small group sessions ** ---------------------------------------------------- We can fully subsidise cycle skills up to 8 cycle skills sessions Our professional cycling instructors are nationally accredited and available seven days a week to meet you at a time and place to suit you. * Adults - 1 to 1 sessions or small groups of 2/3 adults. * Families - up to 2 adults and up to 3 children Adults: Beginners, and anyone looking to borrow a cycle for the lesson can meet our instructor at Kingston Guildhall or Kingsmeadow. For those able to ride and who have access to a cycle, we can also meet you at home or a nearby area. Families: Gain confidence and learn skills to cycle as a family with a free family cycling session. In the session a qualified instructor will teach you how to cycle with children, using quiet routes and parks. These sessions offer the opportunity to build on or prepare for Bikeability skills taught in schools. We are unable to provide children's bikes for these sessions and an adult must be present. 1:1 cycling sessions: are currently paused, you will not hear back in the usual timelines - when reopened you will hear back from the team You can find available time slots on the booking form below. Please note a £10 administration may be chargeable for any cancellations within less than two working days of a session. [Adult and Family Cycle Sessions Booking Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScGpAtXG-PWUTfffg8O4ySe7opzAWQpoQYIGS57vf1RADiQOw/viewform) **Online courses** ------------------ Before your session we recommend you complete the [TfL's online Cycle Skills course](https://cycle-skillsonline.tfl.gov.uk/). The course provides easy to follow tips and advice to get you going. There are four short modules to try, including how to cycle as a family.
intro: Whether you are a first time rider or a regular cyclist looking to improve your skills, we could provide fully subsidised tailored training courses to suit your individual abilities and goals.

name: National Dyspraxia Support
description: Dyspraxia, also known as developmental co-ordination disorder (DCD), is a common disorder that affects movement and co-ordination. Dyspraxia does not affect your intelligence. It can affect your co-ordination skills – such as tasks requiring balance, playing sports or learning to drive a car. Dyspraxia can also affect your fine motor skills, such as writing or using small objects. ### Symptoms of dyspraxia Symptoms of dyspraxia can vary between individuals and may change over time. You may find routine tasks difficult. If you have dyspraxia it may affect: * your co-ordination, balance and movement * how you learn new skills, think, and remember information at work and home * your daily living skills, such as dressing or preparing meals * your ability to write, type, draw and grasp small objects * how you function in social situations * how you deal with your emotions * time management, planning and personal organisation skills Dyspraxia should not be confused with other disorders affecting movement, such as [cerebral palsy](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cerebral-palsy/) and [stroke](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/stroke/). It can affect people of all intellectual abilities. See a GP if you think you may have undiagnosed dyspraxia or problems with your co-ordination. It's a good idea to keep a diary of your symptoms. ### Support for people living with dyspraxia Dyspraxia can have a big effect on your life. It might help to talk to others with dyspraxia. name: Staywell - Saturday Support Circle
description: The Saturday Support Circle offers a unique space where our guests can access both shared and independent support: * **Peer Support:** An opportunity for carers and family members to connect, share experiences, and exchange advice with others in similar situations. * **Information & Advice:** Access to guidance on navigating dementia care and managing day-to-day challenges. * **Respite & Independence:** Structured activities enabling carers and their loved ones to spend a little time independent of each other within the same safe building, as well as enjoying social time together. * **Social Connection:** A warm, relaxed atmosphere provided by a dedicated team, yummy refreshments and occasional visits from community guests (including therapy animals). **4th Saturday of every month - 10:30-12:30** at Raleigh House Day Centre, 14 Nelson Road, New Malden, KT3 5EA. Our facilities are purpose-built and fully accessible with step-free access, creating a practical, bright and positive environment. Caring for a loved one who is living with a dementia can be exhausting and relentless. It is a round-the-clock job and it's hard to find people who fully understand the challenges that families face. Dementia is a unique condition for all those diagnosed and the journey is complex and ever-changing. Whilst the Saturday Support Circle can't solve these problems, we can provide an opportunity for carers to meet others who may have similar experiences, be able to share knowledge, empathise, connect and support each other along the way. name: Helmar Care and Community Services
description: Helmar Care run projects that include supporting communities with welfare and wellbeing, skills, training and care work. We all know what it is like when you want things done. Helmar Care is there just when you need us in order to give you a piece of mind. Personal Care is provided following a Care Plan that will be agreed with you and your family. You can choose a combination of personal and practical care to create an individually tailored service to meet your specific needs. **The Personal care service includes:** * Washing * Dressing * Bathing * Showering * Shaving * Incontinence care * Assistance to get up and go to bed * Monitoring of prescribed medication **The Practical Care Service includes:** * Meal preparation * Light housework * Shopping * Laundry * Social support and companionship **Our Care staff are trained to:** * Treat you as an individual, and to assist you to make your own decisions on matters that affect life. * Maintain your privacy in relation to your personal affairs and belongings * Respect you and never to put you in a situation where you are likely to feel demeaned * Encourage you to be as independent as possible * Not discriminate against anyone for any reason e.g. race, age, colour, religion, disability, sexual orientation, physical and financial circumstances. * Encourage you to keep in touch with friends, relatives, religious leaders etc and to assist you where necessary in making arrangements

name: National Bereavement Services
description: **Support after someone dies** **[Cruse Bereavement Care](https://www.cruse.org.uk/)** provides support for children, young people and adults. **[Sudden Helpline](https://kingston.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=4f9693900f570d3a4ca3b6e39&id=e50cf6307a&e=ab14fc3bbf)** if someone has died suddenly or too soon in their lives or any other cause: 0800 2600 400. **[Survivors of bereavement after suicide](https://uksobs.org/we-can-help/)** is for anyone who has been bereaved or affected by suicide. **[The Bereavement Advice Centre](https://www.bereavementadvice.org/)** offer practical support and advice on what to do after a death. **[The Jewish Bereavement Counselling Service](https://jbcs.org.uk/)** help and support Jewish individuals through loss and bereavement. **[The Loss Foundation](https://thelossfoundation.org/training/)** specialises solely in supporting those who lose a loved one to cancer, whether that be spouses, family members, friends or colleagues. We provide a variety of free support events, in-person and online, to help people at any point during their loss. **[WAY Widowed and Young](https://www.widowedandyoung.org.uk/)** are for anyone who's lost a partner before their 51st birthday. **Support after a child dies** **[Child Bereavement UK](https://childbereavementuk.org/)** helps children and young people (up to age 25), parents, and families, to rebuild their lives when a child grieves or when a child dies. **[A Child of Mine](https://achildofmine.org.uk/)** support families after a baby or child has died. **[Grief Encounter](https://www.griefencounter.org.uk/)** provide support to bereaved children, young people and their families. **[Sands](https://www.sands.org.uk/support-you)** supports anyone who has been affected by the death of a baby before, during or shortly after birth. **[The Lullaby Trust](https://www.lullabytrust.org.uk/bereavement-support/)** offer confidential bereavement support to anyone affected by the sudden and unexpected death of a baby or young child. **[Winston’s Wish](https://www.winstonswish.org/)** provide support to children and young people after the death of a parent or a sibling.

name: English lessons
description: Our English lessons are free and delivered by trained volunteers. **Referrals** We accept referrals from health and social care professionals, government and educational organisations, and other charities. We are currently unable to accept referrals from family members or friends or self-referrals. Referrals are prioritised according to need. If you want to refer someone for English one to one or group support, please do so through [our online referral form](https://www.learnenglishathome.org.uk/refer-someone). **Eligibility** To be eligible, the individual needs to: * be a resident of either Kingston upon Thames, Richmond, Hounslow or Merton boroughs * have low level English language skills and need help to communicate their basic or everyday needs * be someone who is unable to attend adult education classes regularly for any of the following reasons * They have additional social needs e.g. domestic violence or victims of trafficking. * They have a young child/children at home with additional needs e.g. a disability. * They have physical or mental health problems. * They are carers who cannot leave home because of their caring duties. Clients who have pre-school aged children and no additional needs can be referred but will be a low priority and so may have to wait longer. Whilst we make every effort to find a suitable tutor as soon as possible, there is a waiting list. Where appropriate, we will refer people onto a further agency.

name: Table Tennis and Social Wellbeing Sessions
description: These friendly weekly sessions are for people aged 18 and over who are experiencing a physical health or wellbeing challenge, including low mood, reduced confidence or loneliness. You do not need a diagnosis or professional referral to attend. Enjoy table tennis at a comfortable pace, meet new people and have some light exercise in a relaxed and supportive environment. The sessions are suitable for beginners, with optional coaching available from experienced coaches. All equipment is provided, so you only need to wear comfortable clothing and suitable shoes. Carers and support workers are welcome to attend to help someone feel comfortable and take part. Sessions run every Tuesday from 2pm to 3pm throughout the year, subject to sufficient attendance. Your first session is free. After that, the cost is £20 per month, covering all Tuesday sessions that month. A reduced fee may be available if cost is a barrier. Please contact Jane Barella before attending, preferably by email at [jbarellatt1@msn.com](mailto:jbarellatt1@msn.com) or by calling 07894 905850. Please note that the table tennis hall is on the first floor and can only be accessed by stairs. There is no lift or wheelchair access.

description: This monthly Cancer Connections group is a space specifically for individuals who are post-cancer treatment or living in remission to meet others, share stories, and feel supported—over a warm drink in a welcoming, non-medical setting. **What to expect:** * A safe and welcoming space to share stories, listen and connect * Find comfort with others who understand * No pressure to talk, just come as you are * Tea and coffee available from Wesley's Cafe from £1.20 **When we meet:** Every 4th Friday of the month, 12:30pm - 2:00pm at Wesley’s Community Hub, New Malden Methodist Church, KT3 4BY **Upcoming 2026 Dates:** 24 April · 29 May · 26 June · 31 July · 28 August · 25 September · 30 October · 27 November Please refer to our [Group Guidelines](https://www.newmaldenmethodistchurch.com/nmmethodistchurch/assets/documents/cancer-group-guidelines) for more information. **By participating, you confirm that you understand and accept these guidelines, helping us create a safe and respectful environment for all.** **_For the Post-Cancer & Remission Only_**: _Hosted by Wesley's Community Hub in conjunction with Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust and Macmillan Cancer Support, at Wesley’s Café, New Malden Methodist Church!_

name: Hook & Southborough Bowls Club
description: * Bowls is a great leveller – players of all ages, young or old can play against each other on an equal basis. Age, gender and physique have little effect on playing a game of bowls. * Bowls clubs are great places to relax and meet new friends. In the clubhouse at Hook & Southborough we have our own club bar and it’s a good place to socialise and feel a part of the local community. * Bowls is a relatively inexpensive sport to play. You only really need a pair of shoes that have flat soles like trainers. Our club have spare sets of bowls that you can try out. * The club also organises various social events like Quiz Evenings and Race Nights for members to take part in throughout the year. * As well as playing against other club members, the club organise friendly matches against other clubs in Kingston. We play men, ladies and mixed games. We also play in the Kingston & District League, Racal Decca Mixed League, Evening Mixed Triples League and Club Single Day Events. **When do we play?** We play bowls throughout the summer months from April to September, why not come along and join us for a roll up to see what it’s like? We play: Tuesday afternoons — 2pm for a 2.30pm start. Friday evenings — 5.30pm for a 6pm start (Apr-Jul). Friday evenings — 5.00pm for a 5.30pm start (Aug-Sept). We are sure once you have tried it out you will be hooked!

name: Reading Well Book Collections
description: Book collections available free through Kingston borough libraries focused on health and wellbeing. Part of a national scheme, the books have been endorsed by health professionals. Issues covered include mental health for all ages and long-term physical conditions such as arthritis, diabetes, heart disease and pain. There are also books aimed at those with dementia or those caring for someone with dementia. The titles offer practical information and advice to help you understand and cope better with your condition. The latest Reading Well for Families collection supports family wellbeing in pregnancy and the early years. [https://reading-well.org.uk/](https://reading-well.org.uk/) As well as physical copies of the Reading Well titles to support mental health, many are available in eBook and eAudio formats. There are titles for children, young people and adults. These can be borrowed free with a library card on the OverDrive platform: [https://llc.overdrive.com/collection/1175275](https://llc.overdrive.com/collection/1175275) [https://tlc.overdrive.com/collection/1703959](https://tlc.overdrive.com/collection/1703959) To join the library and for more information on resources available from home, see: [https://www.kingston.gov.uk/libraries](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/libraries)
intro: Reading Well supports you to understand and manage your health and wellbeing using helpful reading. The books are all recommended by health experts, as well as people with lived experience of the conditions and topics covered and their relatives and carers.

name: Reading Well Book Collections
description: Book collections available free through Kingston borough libraries focused on health and wellbeing. Part of a national scheme, the books have been endorsed by health professionals. Issues covered include mental health for all ages and long-term physical conditions such as arthritis, diabetes, heart disease and pain. There are also books aimed at those with dementia or those caring for someone with dementia. The titles offer practical information and advice to help you understand and cope better with your condition. The latest Reading Well for Families collection supports family wellbeing in pregnancy and the early years. [https://reading-well.org.uk/](https://reading-well.org.uk/) As well as physical copies of the Reading Well titles to support mental health, many are available in eBook and eAudio formats. There are titles for children, young people and adults. These can be borrowed free with a library card on the OverDrive platform: [https://llc.overdrive.com/collection/1175275](https://llc.overdrive.com/collection/1175275) [https://tlc.overdrive.com/collection/1703959](https://tlc.overdrive.com/collection/1703959) To join the library and for more information on resources available from home, see: [https://www.kingston.gov.uk/libraries](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/libraries)

name: Community Connectors
description: Community Connectors are trained Social Prescribing Link workers lined up with local GP practices in **Surbiton and Chessington**, working with Staywell. They can help you to make positive changes to your life by connecting you to volunteers, activities and voluntary/community groups, helping you to: * feel more involved in your community * meet new people * make some changes to improve your health and wellbeing * deal with things that can affect your health such as debt, caring responsibilities or loneliness They encourage you to help yourself. They support and work with you to create and follow a personal action plan. They listen to you and focus on what matters to you. They will also help you to access services and/or resources wherever possible, in order to address any non- medical needs you may have. They are experienced in working with people with Dementia. In order to be introduced to a Community Connector, please use the email address listed or ask at your GP.
intro: Community Connectors are trained Social Prescribing Link Workers aligned with local GPs. They work in partnership with Staywell, a local charity. They help people make positive changes in their lives. They do this by linking them to volunteers, activities and community groups who provide support.

name: English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL)
description: Kingston Adult Education offers several classes for English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) with employment skills. You will improve your English, develop your CV and practice looking for jobs, interview and IT skills. We have classes at all levels, from beginner to advanced. **Exams** You will study for exams in Speaking and Listening, Reading and Writing. You will need to study outside the classroom. **How can I join a class?** Please click on the [course interest link](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeDERVlJR4lTKwUX_p1Npl5y3wHNgd3jDCxN4U0t6JabTMpdA/viewform) and we will contact you when a course becomes available. Courses for new learners will start from September. **Fees** ESOL classes may be free for learners who are unemployed, looking for work and receive certain benefits. **Job Centre Plus** * Do you receive Job Seekers' Allowance? * Do you receive Employment Support Allowance (work related)? * Do you receive Universal Credit? Talk to your Job Centre Plus adviser about joining an ESOL course to boost your skills for employment. Your adviser can refer you to a course.
intro: ESOL classes are for adults permanently settled in the UK. There are classes at all levels and they are in the morning, afternoon and evening.
organisation: Kingston Adult Education Kingston Adult Education We have our core delivery: ESOL, English, Maths, Digital, Vocational, Health & Fitness, Arts, Crafts, Languages, Writing, History and we have some wonderful new courses for you to turn your hand to. Why not try our new Jewellery Making Workshop and if you like it, join the new course. Along with new craft workshops and courses, we’ve also added new art courses and workshops: Why not enjoy Botanical Watercolours, Drawing & Painting Animals, Landscape Painting, Oil Painting or Mindful Art? Whether you're looking to meet new people, explore new interests, get a job, gain qualifications for your career or keep your mind and body active we have something for everyone. Along with our wonderful Tai Chi, Pilates, and Mindful Movement courses, why not try our new Journaling for Wellbeing to help build your resilience and improve your wellbeing? With both **online** and **in-person** classes available at locations across the borough, you can easily find a course that fits your needs. In addition, many of our courses are **free** as they are government funded or offered at reduced rates, and we provide discounts based on your circumstances, so please contact us to find out more. Enjoy your courses and being a part of our wonderful adult education community. name: Kingston Talking Therapies
description: We offer a range of treatments for adults experiencing anxiety and depression. These include: * Cognitive Behaviour Therapy * Interpersonal Psychotherapy * Dynamic Interpersonal Therapy * Behavioural Couples Therapy * EMDR We treat: * Depression, recurrent depression, and peri and post natal depression * Generalised Anxiety Disorder * Panic disorder * Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder * Phobias * Social Phobia/Anxiety * Post-traumatic stress disorder * Health Anxiety * Mixed depression and anxiety * Anxiety/ depression for those with long term health conditions Our treatments are delivered over the telephone; face-to-face; online and within group workshops. We accept self-referrals (online), with a link on [our website](https://swlstg.nhs.uk/kingston-referrals). Referrals for Canbury GP Surgery patients are currently being managed by Richmond Talking Therapies. There is a different self-referral link for Canbury Surgery patients, also on our website. Referrals from GPs or any other Health Care Professionals can be made via the professional referral form. You will be offered a telephone or face to face assessment, followed by treatment recommendations or signposting to alternative services.

name: The Sound Doctor: Early Onset Diabetes
description: This film library will help you find out more about how to look after yourself better with Early Onset Diabetes. name: New Malden Little League Football
description: **New Malden Little League has provided organised League and Cup football to boys and girls of all abilities between 7 and 12 years of age since 1978. Whilst there is a competitive element involved, our objective is to provide an environment where children can enjoy their football and have fun. Emphasis is placed on team spirit and sportsmanship amongst players and parents alike.** **The League is based in [Manor Park, New Malden](https://btckstorage.blob.core.windows.net/site973/manor%20park%20map.bmp), where games are played on Saturday mornings starting at 09:30 and 11:45am kick offs. The League is split into two separate Divisions: Juniors, ages 7, 8 and 9 and Seniors, ages 10, 11 and 12. Within the Senior Division, the football league season is split into two separate championships; one before Christmas (1st Half Season) and one after Christmas (2nd Half Season). There will be play-offs, if required, to determine the overall League Champions.** **The League is a non profit organisation, run by a committee made up of past and present parents and other volunteers and any money received from donations, sponsorship and money raising events is used to pay for the hiring of the playing pitches and buying kit and equipment. There is always room for more volunteers, similarly if you would like to sponsor a team we would be very glad to hear from you.** **The League has a Child Protection Policy and all officials and team managers are subject to enhanced disclosure checks via the Criminal Records Bureau.**

name: Kingston Women's Centre
description: Kingston Women’s Centre is a welcoming space run by women for women. We support women of all backgrounds and ages from the local community. Our goal is to provide a safe, confidential environment where you can talk freely about anything that may be troubling, confusing, or painful, without fear of judgment. We offer weekly counselling for up to two years, providing support with: * Anger issues * Anxiety * Bereavement * Childhood sexual abuse or difficult childhood experiences * Domestic abuse * Depression * Identity issues * Life changes or crises * Panic attacks * Pregnancy and parenting challenges * Relationship difficulties * Sensitivity and shame * Trauma * Work-related issues Whatever you’re facing, we’re here to support you every step of the way.
intro: Kingston Women’s Centre is a long standing charity run by women for women. Since 1982, we have supported thousands of women with their mental wellbeing through our low cost counselling service.

name: Moving on Together Community Support
description: The Moving on Together Community Support Group is a peer-led voluntary group run by ex-clients of the Kingston Wellbeing Service. Our members have overcome their own addictions and decided that they would like to help others in the local area who are still struggling on their own journey of recovery. **So what do we do?** Most of our members are peer mentors, who have been in your shoes. They know what it is like to be held back from achieving your full potential because of addiction and they fully understand the problems that accompanies this. They are all here to support people throughout their recovery. **So how do we manage this?** On Thursday afternoons, between 1pm and 4pm at Queen Mary's Hall, Cambridge Gardens KT1 3LJ, we provide an outreach and social club for people to drop in for a chat and meet with friends. We also help to co-facilitate groups at Kingston Wellbeing Service and can give information and advice on questions around recovery. We also provide a hot meal and a safe space. For further information, contact: [ceris@movingontogether.org.uk](mailto:ceris@movingontogether.org.uk) or [lucy@movingontogether.org.uk](mailto:lucy@movingontogether.org.uk)

name: Princess Alice Hospice - Bereavement Cafes
description: The Community Bereavement Cafés are mainly monthly drop in sessions, open to all bereaved people. They are run by organisations that have partnered with Princess Alice Hospice and the volunteers who run them have all received bereavement support training from the Hospice. They offer a chance to talk with someone who is trained to listen and to share experiences with other bereaved people. Refreshments are provided. We run Bereavement Cafés in the following locations in Kingston: * **All Saints Church KT1 1JP**: **2pm** to **3:30pm** every other Wednesday Other locations outside Kingston are also available. For more information and directions to the locations, please scroll down to the '**Where can I access it?**' section below. Bereavement is an individual experience, however at a Bereavement Café you will connect with others who have been through loss and who understand what you are going through. Bereavement Café is a place where you can talk about how your loss is affecting you.

name: Princess Alice Hospice - Bereavement Cafes
description: The Community Bereavement Cafés are mainly monthly drop in sessions, open to all bereaved people. They are run by organisations that have partnered with Princess Alice Hospice and the volunteers who run them have all received bereavement support training from the Hospice. They offer a chance to talk with someone who is trained to listen and to share experiences with other bereaved people. Refreshments are provided. We run Bereavement Cafés in the following locations in Kingston: * **All Saints Church KT1 1JP**: **2pm** to **3:30pm** every other Wednesday Other locations outside Kingston are also available. For more information and directions to the locations, please scroll down to the '**Where can I access it?**' section below. Bereavement is an individual experience, however at a Bereavement Café you will connect with others who have been through loss and who understand what you are going through. Bereavement Café is a place where you can talk about how your loss is affecting you.

name: Get Active - Exercise Referral Programme
description: ### Please note: you must have a referral from your GP to access the Get Active Programme. It is not possible to self refer to this service. It can be challenging to stay physically active when you have a medical condition or disability. We offer a **low cost** 12-week physical activity programme for adults with a medical condition, delivered by qualified exercise referral specialists. **Why Physical Activity?** Some of the benefits include: * Boosts wellbeing and mood * Strengthens and improves the function of muscles, bones and joints * Improves cardiovascular fitness * Contributes to maintaining a healthy weight * Helps to prevent or manage diabetes * Promotes sleep quality * Improves posture and balance * And many more! **What we can offer you:** * A 12 week exercise programme including 5 one-to-one sessions with an exercise specialist, ongoing support, motivation and advice. * A personalised training programme to suit your abilities, at your own pace, and * In-person gym sessions available at one of the participating local leisure centres\* **\*Each gym session or one-to-one session with the exercise specialist costs £3.** **A reduced rate gym membership is offered to those completing the full 12 week programme.** The gym programme is available from the following Kingston leisure centres: * [Malden Centre](https://www.placesleisure.org/centres/malden-centre/) * [Tolworth Recreation Centre](https://www.placesleisure.org/centres/tolworth-recreation-centre/?utm_campaign=january22nonpromo&utm_source=google&utm_medium=paid&gclid=CjwKCAjwsMGYBhAEEiwAGUXJaccAAWn-oNq3iXVcZ6BkBIPm6YYuy6NgzrRhnMen8_nuClsEDIpJuRoCRCcQAvD_BwE) * [Weir Archer / Kingsmeadow](https://www.placesleisure.org/centres/weir-archer-athletics-and-fitness-centre/) **How do I qualify for this programme?** * Be 16 years old or over * Live, work or study in Kingston * Exercise less than 60 minutes a week * **Have a Get Active referral form - your GP surgery will have access to this** You must also have a recognised physical or mental health condition that may include one or more of the following: * At risk of coronary heart disease such as: family history, overweight, hypertension, type 2 diabetes * Mild depression, anxiety, stress and controlled mental health problems * At risk of developing or diagnosed with osteoporosis * Well controlled respiratory problems * Mild mobility problems e.g. arthritis, multiple sclerosis, joint problems * Motivated to give up tobacco or other substances * Controlled hypertension * Long COVID Get Active also provide weekly exercise classes for people living with or at risk of diabetes at a rate of £3 per class. The [NHS 'know your risk' tool](https://riskscore.diabetes.org.uk/start) can quickly help identify your personal risk for Type 2 diabetes. **Speak to your GP, practice nurse or local health professional to request a referral form.** Give us a call on **0208 547 6666** for more information or email **getactive@kingston.gov.uk.**

name: Get Active - Exercise Referral Programme
description: ### Please note: you must have a referral from your GP to access the Get Active Programme. It is not possible to self refer to this service. It can be challenging to stay physically active when you have a medical condition or disability. We offer a **low cost** 12-week physical activity programme for adults with a medical condition, delivered by qualified exercise referral specialists. **Why Physical Activity?** Some of the benefits include: * Boosts wellbeing and mood * Strengthens and improves the function of muscles, bones and joints * Improves cardiovascular fitness * Contributes to maintaining a healthy weight * Helps to prevent or manage diabetes * Promotes sleep quality * Improves posture and balance * And many more! **What we can offer you:** * A 12 week exercise programme including 5 one-to-one sessions with an exercise specialist, ongoing support, motivation and advice. * A personalised training programme to suit your abilities, at your own pace, and * In-person gym sessions available at one of the participating local leisure centres\* **\*Each gym session or one-to-one session with the exercise specialist costs £3.** **A reduced rate gym membership is offered to those completing the full 12 week programme.** The gym programme is available from the following Kingston leisure centres: * [Malden Centre](https://www.placesleisure.org/centres/malden-centre/) * [Tolworth Recreation Centre](https://www.placesleisure.org/centres/tolworth-recreation-centre/?utm_campaign=january22nonpromo&utm_source=google&utm_medium=paid&gclid=CjwKCAjwsMGYBhAEEiwAGUXJaccAAWn-oNq3iXVcZ6BkBIPm6YYuy6NgzrRhnMen8_nuClsEDIpJuRoCRCcQAvD_BwE) * [Weir Archer / Kingsmeadow](https://www.placesleisure.org/centres/weir-archer-athletics-and-fitness-centre/) **How do I qualify for this programme?** * Be 16 years old or over * Live, work or study in Kingston * Exercise less than 60 minutes a week * **Have a Get Active referral form - your GP surgery will have access to this** You must also have a recognised physical or mental health condition that may include one or more of the following: * At risk of coronary heart disease such as: family history, overweight, hypertension, type 2 diabetes * Mild depression, anxiety, stress and controlled mental health problems * At risk of developing or diagnosed with osteoporosis * Well controlled respiratory problems * Mild mobility problems e.g. arthritis, multiple sclerosis, joint problems * Motivated to give up tobacco or other substances * Controlled hypertension * Long COVID Get Active also provide weekly exercise classes for people living with or at risk of diabetes at a rate of £3 per class. The [NHS 'know your risk' tool](https://riskscore.diabetes.org.uk/start) can quickly help identify your personal risk for Type 2 diabetes. **Speak to your GP, practice nurse or local health professional to request a referral form.** Give us a call on **0208 547 6666** for more information or email **getactive@kingston.gov.uk.**

name: BuddyUp
description: BuddyUp is a local service run by RAID that helps disabled young people aged 14 to 17 in Kingston and Richmond. Each young person is paired with a volunteer around the same age to go on fun outings together, like going to a café, bowling, or taking the bus. These outings happen about twice a month for six months and are designed to help build confidence and everyday life skills through socialising. Activities are based on what each pair enjoys doing. There are also group outings for everyone in the service, which are great for those who aren’t quite ready for a one-on-one pairing. If you know a young person in Kingston who might benefit from BuddyUp, please share our contact details. Feel free to get in touch if you have any questions or want to talk about making a referral.
intro: BuddyUp is a service run by RAID for 14-17 year olds in the Kingston and Richmond Boroughs. We run a befriending scheme pairing disabled teenagers with volunteers of a similar age to go on outings in the local area.

useful_infos: Signing up It is so easy to get involved! As long as you are 14-17 years old with an additional need and/or disability and you are a resident of the Kingston or Richmond Borough, you are eligible for this scheme. For more information on BuddyUp Richmond: please email Beatriz: buddyuprichmond@raid.charity For more information on BuddyUp Kingston: please email Eliana at: buddyupkingston@raid.charity If you would like to be a volunteer for our BuddyUp service, we’d love to hear from so please just contact us using the emails above. 1 Meeting up Who will buddy me? We will take the time to talk to you and your family to learn more about your interests and hobbies. We ensure our volunteers are reliable, fun and enthusiastic and try to match them to our young people through similar tastes and interests. We will then give you and your family the chance to meet your volunteer buddy before getting started on BuddyUp. Young people will be matched with a volunteer buddy who will support and encourage them to access activities and public transport, whilst building a real friendship. This is a great way to try new opportunities and to get out and about in your local area. Our buddy pairs go out for a few hours every fortnight at a time suitable for all – this can be during the day/after school/weekends or holidays! 2

name: Nuffield Health Joint Pain Programme
description: If you've had any of the below, we can help: * Osteoarthritis * Psoriatic arthritis * Rheumatoid arthritis * Other arthritis * Gout * Fibromyalgia * Spondylitis * Lupus. Alternatively, if you've suffered with chronic pain for many years with no formal diagnosis, this programme is for you. You don’t have to be a gym member to join the programme – it’s **free and open to anyone living with joint pain**. _Please note that if your joint pain is very severe, or if you’ve had joint surgery within 12 weeks, you may not be able to take part in the programme._ **What is the Joint Pain Programme?** This is a 6-month programme, which begins with 12 weeks of lifestyle advice and exercise sessions led by a Rehabilitation Specialist. This will equip you with the tools to better manage your pain. And it works. People who’ve completed the programme have shown improvements in mobility, pain, general fitness levels and overall quality of life. **What can you expect from the programme?** Twice a week you'll have an hour-long group session. This is split into a 15–20 minute educational workshop, with 40–45 minutes of exercise. **Exercise sessions include:** * strength training * flexibility training * stability training * yoga * circuits **Educational workshop:** * pain management * the importance of exercise * improving sleep * mental health * eating well **How can I take part in the programme?** Simply apply now via the [Nuffield Health website](https://www.nuffieldhealth.com/about-us/our-impact/healthy-life/joint-pain-programme/joint-pain-programme). name: Nuffield Health Joint Pain Programme
description: If you've had any of the below, we can help: * Osteoarthritis * Psoriatic arthritis * Rheumatoid arthritis * Other arthritis * Gout * Fibromyalgia * Spondylitis * Lupus. Alternatively, if you've suffered with chronic pain for many years with no formal diagnosis, this programme is for you. You don’t have to be a gym member to join the programme – it’s **free and open to anyone living with joint pain**. _Please note that if your joint pain is very severe, or if you’ve had joint surgery within 12 weeks, you may not be able to take part in the programme._ **What is the Joint Pain Programme?** This is a 6-month programme, which begins with 12 weeks of lifestyle advice and exercise sessions led by a Rehabilitation Specialist. This will equip you with the tools to better manage your pain. And it works. People who’ve completed the programme have shown improvements in mobility, pain, general fitness levels and overall quality of life. **What can you expect from the programme?** Twice a week you'll have an hour-long group session. This is split into a 15–20 minute educational workshop, with 40–45 minutes of exercise. **Exercise sessions include:** * strength training * flexibility training * stability training * yoga * circuits **Educational workshop:** * pain management * the importance of exercise * improving sleep * mental health * eating well **How can I take part in the programme?** Simply apply now via the [Nuffield Health website](https://www.nuffieldhealth.com/about-us/our-impact/healthy-life/joint-pain-programme/joint-pain-programme). You'll receive an email with a link to a questionnaire. Complete the questionnaire, as it allows us to find out i the programme is suitable for you to join.

We offer adventurous activities designed to get boys off their phones and learning a new skill. We help boys challenge themselves, develop their self confidence and develop a bond with the male role model in their life. We do this through _Adventure Camp Weekends_**,** _Climb & Connect_ relationship building course and _Activity Days_. * **Dedicated Volunteer Support and Opportunities -** we are fortunate to have an extremely strong team of volunteers and staff that help us support over 100 families a year. To ensure we can deliver the best programme possible, and prioritise our staff/volunteer development, we have a number of opportunities built into what we do. These are unique - it is extremely rare to get as emotionally close to both adults and children as MAN&BOY programmes offer.

description: KAN Kingston is a vibrant Christian community based in Kingston upon Thames, bringing people together through faith, fellowship and a shared desire to see lives transformed. Our parent church is Kingdom Ambassador Centre (KAC), and we are one of many Kingdom Ambassador Networks (KAN's) across the UK and Europe. We exist to create a welcoming environment where people from all works of life can connect with God, build meaningful relationships and grow in their faith. At KAN Kingston, we believe that church is more than simply attending a service - it is about doing life together. Through worship, teaching, prayer, community and practical support, we encourage people to discover their identity and purpose in Christ and to develop meaningful connections with others. Our community welcomes people at every stage of their faith journey, whether they have followed Jesus for years, are exploring Christianity for the first time, or simply want to find a supportive and welcoming community. We are passionate about creating spaces where people feel seen, valued and able to belong. Whether you're looking for a church community, wanting to explore your faith, hoping to meet new people or simply looking for somewhere you can feel at home, KAN Kingston would love to welcome you.

name: KAN Kingston
description: KAN Kingston is a vibrant Christian community based in Kingston upon Thames, bringing people together through faith, fellowship and a shared desire to see lives transformed. Our parent church is Kingdom Ambassador Centre (KAC), and we are one of many Kingdom Ambassador Networks (KAN's) across the UK and Europe. We exist to create a welcoming environment where people from all works of life can connect with God, build meaningful relationships and grow in their faith. At KAN Kingston, we believe that church is more than simply attending a service - it is about doing life together. Through worship, teaching, prayer, community and practical support, we encourage people to discover their identity and purpose in Christ and to develop meaningful connections with others. Our community welcomes people at every stage of their faith journey, whether they have followed Jesus for years, are exploring Christianity for the first time, or simply want to find a supportive and welcoming community. We are passionate about creating spaces where people feel seen, valued and able to belong. Whether you're looking for a church community, wanting to explore your faith, hoping to meet new people or simply looking for somewhere you can feel at home, KAN Kingston would love to welcome you.

name: Kingston Camera Club
description: Rather than “snap and forget” your photos, come and join a bunch of friendly club members whose images are regularly exhibited in print. New members joining a year ago say how much they enjoy learning tips that improve their pictures, while being in a social environment with people with similar interests. Comments from a keen member: “Having an independent judge constructively comment on my images has helped me think more critically about my work. This feedback has encouraged me to focus on improving my skills and shifted my mindset from merely "taking a snap" to "creating an image”. “What has made my experience even more rewarding is the supportive and friendly nature of fellow members. They express genuine interest in any images shared and offer encouragement. The sense of community and shared passion for photography has been motivating and enriching”. _Kingston Camera Club meets in term time on Monday evenings 7.30 pm for 8.00 pm start until 10 pm at St Andrew’s Church Hall, Church Road, Ham, TW10 5HG. Parking is available. Come and visit us for two free evenings before making a decision to join. Our new season opens on Monday 2 September 2024. Further information on our website:_ Go to [www.kingstoncameraclub.co.uk](http://www.kingstoncameraclub.co.uk/) for fuller details.

description: **Gentle Movement and Breathwork** ---------------------------------- **with Richard Moody** ---------------------- Enjoy combining slow, flowing movements and breathwork to help you reconnect with your body, manage stress, and aim to improve physical wellbeing through gentle exercise. The movements accompanied by natural breathing can help to exercise the lungs, muscles, tissues, nervous system, circulation - in fact all of the body's organs and functions to help increase energy, create focus and assist in general physical health. Relax and calm the mind, easing worries and nervous tension. Improve balance, posture, and overall movement. You will learn a series of warm-up and cool-down movements. Along with our wonderful Tai Chi, Pilates, and Mindful Movement courses, why not try our new Journaling for Wellbeing to help build your resilience and improve your wellbeing? With both **online** and **in-person** classes available at locations across the borough, you can easily find a course that fits your needs. name: National Tools for Developing Computer Skills
description: * [My Computer My Way](https://mcmw.abilitynet.org.uk/) offer free how-to guides to make your device more accessible. Plus they have a number of excellent factsheets on their main website. * [Free IT support](https://abilitynet.org.uk/free-tech-support-and-info/request-free-it-support-home) at home is delivered by a network of trained volunteers who can help older people and people with a disability of any age with IT challenges, e.g. setting up new equipment. Sign up online or call 0800 048 7642 * Vodafone and Lloyds Banking Group have created a social impact company called [WeAre Group](https://www.wearegroup.com/training) that can help people to use digital skills confidently and is designed to make sure nobody gets left behind. You will learn how to book a GP appointment only, shop online safely, manage your online banking. * The Department for Education has launched a new [Skill Toolkit](https://theskillstoolkit.campaign.gov.uk/#sw) that offers free courses to help you learn new skills or get a new job. * [Microsoft Digital Skills Support Programme](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/paths/digital-literacy-and-productivity-learning-pathway?success=true&u=0&accountId=0&authUUID=3B0jPKF5QzOhl9boVmRZLg%3D%3D&src=direct%2Fnone&veh=direct%2Fnone) is free to all learners and provides an interactive, hands-on training platform that helps people learn basic technical skills. As well as the above, please check out [our offer of local support that can help you develop your IT skills](https://connectedkingston.uk/categories/getting-by-online) so you can do more online.

name: National Tools for Developing Computer Skills
description: * [My Computer My Way](https://mcmw.abilitynet.org.uk/) offer free how-to guides to make your device more accessible. Plus they have a number of excellent factsheets on their main website. * [Free IT support](https://abilitynet.org.uk/free-tech-support-and-info/request-free-it-support-home) at home is delivered by a network of trained volunteers who can help older people and people with a disability of any age with IT challenges, e.g. setting up new equipment. Sign up online or call 0800 048 7642 * Vodafone and Lloyds Banking Group have created a social impact company called [WeAre Group](https://www.wearegroup.com/training) that can help people to use digital skills confidently and is designed to make sure nobody gets left behind. You will learn how to book a GP appointment only, shop online safely, manage your online banking. * The Department for Education has launched a new [Skill Toolkit](https://theskillstoolkit.campaign.gov.uk/#sw) that offers free courses to help you learn new skills or get a new job. * [Microsoft Digital Skills Support Programme](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/paths/digital-literacy-and-productivity-learning-pathway?success=true&u=0&accountId=0&authUUID=3B0jPKF5QzOhl9boVmRZLg%3D%3D&src=direct%2Fnone&veh=direct%2Fnone) is free to all learners and provides an interactive, hands-on training platform that helps people learn basic technical skills. As well as the above, please check out [our offer of local support that can help you develop your IT skills](https://connectedkingston.uk/categories/getting-by-online) so you can do more online.

name: Kingston Food Banks
description: **How to get help** ------------------- If you need help from our foodbank there are a few simple steps to follow. **The most important step is to get a foodbank voucher.** We work with local agencies to provide the most appropriate help for your circumstances and situation. If they feel you are struggling to put food on the table, they will issue you with a foodbank voucher. The local agency can also provide long-term support, if needed, to help address some of the issues or reasons for your crisis. Agencies we work with include: Citizens Advice, housing support officers, children’s centres, health visitors, social services and some local charities. **1\. Arrange a visit to the referral agency.** They will discuss your situation and supply you with a [foodbank voucher](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/foodbank-vouchers/) where appropriate. **2\. Bring your foodbank voucher to your nearest foodbank centre.** You can find a [list of our local centres and opening times here](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/locations/). When you arrive, we’ll welcome you with a warm drink, and our trained volunteers will chat with you about your situation. We’ll also discuss any dietary needs you may have and exchange your foodbank voucher for [a parcel containing three days of emergency food](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/get-help/whats-in-a-food-parcel/). We’ll also help to support you in any other ways that we can. Most of our foodbank centres offer a café-style environment and our aim is to provide non-judgemental support at the point of crisis. **3\. Get in touch with us.** If you [call or email](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/contact-us/) our foodbank, we can talk through your situation and put you in touch with a relevant local agency. If you have any further questions our [FAQs page](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/get-help/faq/) may help, or feel free to give us a call on 02083911100.
intro: We provide three days’ nutritionally-balanced emergency food and support to local people who are referred to us in crisis.

name: Kingston Food Banks
description: **How to get help** ------------------- If you need help from our foodbank there are a few simple steps to follow. **The most important step is to get a foodbank voucher.** We work with local agencies to provide the most appropriate help for your circumstances and situation. If they feel you are struggling to put food on the table, they will issue you with a foodbank voucher. The local agency can also provide long-term support, if needed, to help address some of the issues or reasons for your crisis. Agencies we work with include: Citizens Advice, housing support officers, children’s centres, health visitors, social services and some local charities. **1\. Arrange a visit to the referral agency.** They will discuss your situation and supply you with a [foodbank voucher](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/foodbank-vouchers/) where appropriate. **2\. Bring your foodbank voucher to your nearest foodbank centre.** You can find a [list of our local centres and opening times here](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/locations/). When you arrive, we’ll welcome you with a warm drink, and our trained volunteers will chat with you about your situation. We’ll also discuss any dietary needs you may have and exchange your foodbank voucher for [a parcel containing three days of emergency food](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/get-help/whats-in-a-food-parcel/). We’ll also help to support you in any other ways that we can. Most of our foodbank centres offer a café-style environment and our aim is to provide non-judgemental support at the point of crisis. **3\. Get in touch with us.** If you [call or email](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/contact-us/) our foodbank, we can talk through your situation and put you in touch with a relevant local agency. If you have any further questions our [FAQs page](https://kingston.foodbank.org.uk/get-help/faq/) may help, or feel free to give us a call on 02083911100.

name: Nature Conservation
description: We offer an array wildlife conservation activities, focused across the Kingston borough harnessing a rewilding narrative. We work in nature reserves and greenspaces, working to enhance the land for the wildlife and the community. We are also working on species reintroductions. Citizen Zoo works to pioneer community led conservation through a rewilding narrative. By this we mean we want to 'Rewild People' i.e educate and reconnect them to the natural world. We also work to 'Rewild our Land', this means we want our environment and ecosystems to function well, supporting a wealth of biodiversity. This makes our land more resilient, more aesthetic and provides more services that are critical to human and community well being. We work across the Kingston Borough, with the aim to provide outstanding nature reserves and exceptional greenspaces, making Kingston a leading borough for the environment, and how our local people engage with the natural world that surrounds though is seldom noticed. We run weekly conservation days and that are both on weekends and weekdays, carrying out all sorts of conservation objectives. Such as planting trees and hedgerows, creating habitats such as ponds and tackling invasive species. We also are focused on species reintroductions where appropriate. We are currently running a community led water vole project, which one day will see these charismatic critters returning to our water ways. There are so many ways in which you can get involved so please do get in touch.

name: Apply for an HM Armed Forces Veteran Card
description: What is the HM Armed Forces Veteran Card? ----------------------------------------- The HM Armed Forces Veteran Card is a free card that provides proof that you have served in the UK Armed Forces. It can make it easier to prove your veteran status when accessing services and support available to veterans. Who can get a Veteran Card? --------------------------- You may be eligible if you have previously served in the UK Armed Forces, including as a regular or reservist in the: * Royal Navy * British Army * Royal Air Force * Royal Marines Some people who served in the Royal Fleet Auxiliary, Merchant Navy or other eligible groups may also be able to get a card. [Click here and check whether you are eligible.](https://www.gov.uk/veteran-card) Do I need to apply? ------------------- If you left the UK Armed Forces **before December 2018**, you will need to apply for a Veteran Card. If you left **after this date**, you should have received a Veteran Card as part of your service leaver's pack. How to apply ------------ Applying for a Veteran Card is **free**. You can apply online using GOV.UK. You will need information including: * your service number * your National Insurance number * the approximate years you started and ended your Armed Forces service * a recent digital passport-style photograph [Click here to apply for a Veteran Card.](https://www.gov.uk/veteran-card/apply) If you cannot apply online, contact the Veterans UK Helpline for help with applying by post. How long will it take? ---------------------- You will usually receive your Veteran Card **within 10 weeks of applying**. What can I use the Veteran Card for? ------------------------------------ The card can be used to prove your veteran status and may make it easier to access services and benefits available to veterans, including: * health and wellbeing support * employment support * housing support * veteran discounts and travel offers * registering your veteran status with your GP * proving your identity for certain services, including voting Need help applying? ------------------- Contact the **Veterans UK Helpline**: **Phone:** 0808 1914 218 **Email:** [veterans-uk@mod.gov.uk](mailto:veterans-uk@mod.gov.uk) **Opening hours:** Monday to Friday, 8am to 4pm

name: Hestia - The Good Energy Club
description: The ‘Good Energy Club’ is a physical exercise programme for anyone over the age of 18 living with a mental health condition in the Royal Borough of Kingston. The project encourages members to get outside and to engage with others in varied physical activities to boost their physical and mental health. The timetable runs on weekdays and encompasses many different exercises including tennis lessons, yoga, badminton, walks and classes at the Kingfisher centre such as Zumba, Box fit and Circuits. **Wellbeing walks** run every week, with a brisk walk on Tuesdays in Richmond Park and a gentle walk along the river. These are free and no booking is required. Anyone who lives in the Kingston borough and struggles with their mental health or physical well being is welcome to refer themselves. **For more information** on the walks or any other activities contact **07854211218 or email john.blon@hestia.org**

name: Marie Curie Telephone Bereavement Support
description: If you want to talk to someone following a bereavement, we’re here for you. Whether your bereavement was expected, happened recently or was some time ago, we can help. We can also support you before your loved one dies. When you start using the service, you'll be matched with a specially trained volunteer who'll give you regular bereavement support. They'll provide a safe space where you can talk openly about the things that are worrying you. You can access up to six telephone sessions of 45 minutes. Marie Curie Telephone Bereavement Service is not a counselling service. Our volunteers are here to offer you a safe, confidential space to discuss your feelings and emotions around bereavement. The service may not be suitable for people who require a greater level of support, such as counselling or psychotherapy.

description: If you want to talk to someone following a bereavement, we’re here for you. Whether your bereavement was expected, happened recently or was some time ago, we can help. We can also support you before your loved one dies. When you start using the service, you'll be matched with a specially trained volunteer who'll give you regular bereavement support. name: Help to Claim Universal Credit
description: **Call our Help to Claim Service on 0800 144 8444** This service helps local people to make a Universal Credit claim online from the start (i.e. setting up an email account) through to the first correct payment. Universal Credit is a benefit that can help with your everyday living costs. **You might be able to get it if you are not working or if you are on a low income.** Universal Credit has been gradually replacing 6 other benefits, these are: * Housing benefit * Income related Employment and Support Allowance * Income - based Job Seeker's Allowance * Child Tax Credits * Working Tax Credits * Income Support You can't usually claim Universal Credit and any of these benefits at the same time. If you need help to make and manage your claim online, we can support you to do this. We will work with you through a 'to do' list set out by Job Centre Plus, and will help you to check if there is any other help you can get. For instance, we can guide you on other sources of money while you wait for your claim to be processed. Please contact us and we will make an appointment for you as soon as possible. Are you worried about how to cope with the cost of living increases? We have information and advice to help you here through our [cost of living information](https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/debt-and-money/cost-of-living/get-help-with-the-cost-of-living/)

name: Yoga Strong
description: Yoga Strong is an active, dynamic and physically challenging class but it is also fun and inclusive. Expect your heart rate to rise and your endurance to be tested — alongside moments of breath-led focus and calm. Afterwards you will feel energised, super grounded and empowered to achieve your best. Every class offers lots of options so it’s beginner friendly and you can work at the level that’s right for you. As we age, we all lose muscle mass (sarcopenia) and bone density, which can lead to osteopenia or osteoporosis. This is important for everyone to be aware of is especially a concern for women during and after menopause. Health experts recommend resistance training to counteract these changes. Yoga Strong delivers this by combining bodyweight resistance from traditional yoga with additional weight training, helping maintain muscle and bone strength while keeping practice mindful and enjoyable. **What You’ll Gain** * Increased muscle strength and tone * Improved bone density and joint stability * Enhanced stamina and cardiovascular health * Greater focus, presence, and mental resilience * Support for healthy, active ageing
intro: Yoga Strong is a unique class that blends the mindful flow of yoga with the muscle-building power of strength and conditioning training using weights. It’s designed for yoga lovers who want to enhance their practice while building total-body strength.
organisation: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/).
