name: Yoga Strong
description: Yoga Strong is an active, dynamic and physically challenging class but it is also fun and inclusive. Expect your heart rate to rise and your endurance to be tested — alongside moments of breath-led focus and calm. Afterwards you will feel energised, super grounded and empowered to achieve your best. Every class offers lots of options so it’s beginner friendly and you can work at the level that’s right for you. As we age, we all lose muscle mass (sarcopenia) and bone density, which can lead to osteopenia or osteoporosis. This is important for everyone to be aware of is especially a concern for women during and after menopause. Health experts recommend resistance training to counteract these changes. Yoga Strong delivers this by combining bodyweight resistance from traditional yoga with additional weight training, helping maintain muscle and bone strength while keeping practice mindful and enjoyable. **What You’ll Gain** * Increased muscle strength and tone * Improved bone density and joint stability * Enhanced stamina and cardiovascular health * Greater focus, presence, and mental resilience * Support for healthy, active ageing

name: Yoga & Pilates Fusion
description: Yoga & Pilates Fusion blends the mindful flow and stretch of yoga with the targeted strength and stability of Pilates. It’s a mat-based class that helps you build a stronger core, improve posture, and increase flexibility while keeping a sense of calm focus. Born from personal experience, this class was inspired when I turned to Pilates during my recovery from major foot surgery. As a dedicated yogi, I thought my core was strong — until Pilates showed me a whole new level of strength. The combination proved so effective and transformative, it became a regular part of my own training and evolved into this fusion class. Every class draws from a wide range of yoga and Pilates practices, so no two sessions are the same. You might focus on: * Back strength and spine health * Deep core activation and stability * Balance and coordination * Upper body and postural strength * Hips and lower body conditioning * Gentle but effective stretches for mobility Core strength work and mindful, breath-led movement are always at the heart of every session. Expect to leave feeling both strengthened and energised. ### **Why It Works** * Core Power – Pilates’ precision builds deep muscle strength that supports your back, hips, and posture. * Mindful Flow – Yoga’s breath-led sequences help you stay present and enhance flexibility. * Total-Body Balance – The fusion blends strength, stretch, and stability training for complete wellness. * Endless Variety – New focuses every week keep the body challenged and the mind engaged.

name: Kingston Green Business Community
description: **Our vision** A free-to-join community of businesses and organisations based or operating in Kingston of all sizes and sectors, from well established to start-ups. The Kingston Green Business Community aims to help members to save resources, as well as reducing their environmental impact and running costs. **Objective 1: People.** Creating green jobs, skills, education & training opportunities. **Objective 2: Product.** Stimulating green innovation & business growth. **Objective 3: Operations.** Helping businesses decarbonise their operations. Collaborative work with academia, sustainability experts and other organisations will lead to the co-creation of solutions to reduce local emissions and access funding. You can [join the community by completing this form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdrHafxELC9ldt1uymNqvCou_AyyGP0cAQGzL6gptaFXkj5-g/viewform). **Activities** _Networking_ * Connecting all businesses and organisations that have an interest in achieving net-zero emissions through adoption of sustainable solutions * Sharing best practices, project ideas, knowledge and intelligence and promoting peer to peer learning * Bringing together businesses with academics, policy makers, training providers, ecological and social entrepreneurs and stimulating eco-innovation * Facilitating opportunities for businesses to identify new potential customers and markets * Encouraging peer to peer mentoring _Knowledge sharing_ * Developing a repository of complementary skill sets, capacity and expertise to help businesses participate in a greener economy * Signposting to other relevant websites and agencies _Capacity building_ * Organising and facilitating participation in workshops, training related to green skills development and other events to learn about net-zero emissions and relevant solutions; raise awareness of business opportunities created from the transition to a green economy; and access programmes and funding aiming to develop green skills, eco-innovation and/or reduce the negative impact of business activities on the environment. _Recognition_ * Maintaining an online database of Kingston Green Business Community members and documenting best practice case studies * Promoting projects and businesses that adopt sustainable solutions and make a positive impact on the environment * Creating opportunities for businesses to add environmental and socio-economic value to other local community groups and across the Borough **Membership** Membership is free and the community is open to all businesses and organisations based and/or operating in Kingston. The Kingston Green Business Community is linked with other existing and future green and wider business communities with similar objectives. You can apply to [become a member of Kingston Green Business Community by completing this form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdrHafxELC9ldt1uymNqvCou_AyyGP0cAQGzL6gptaFXkj5-g/viewform). Please also read through our [Code of Practice](https://forms.gle/qBF58qVxi1JdYjhN6) to understand and agree with the terms. Find [further information about Kingston Green Business Community's current activities](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/climate-change/climate-change-information-businesses) and Members. **Founding Members: ** Aviva, Bentall Centre, Energy Group/Transition Town Kingston, Genuine Solutions, Imperial College, IQ in IT, Kingston Chamber of Commerce, Kingston Council, Kingston First, Kingston Hospital, Kingston University, Lidl, South London Partnership, South Thames Colleges Group, United Business Group, WSP.

name: Kingston Green Business Community
description: **Our vision** A free-to-join community of businesses and organisations based or operating in Kingston of all sizes and sectors, from well established to start-ups. The Kingston Green Business Community aims to help members to save resources, as well as reducing their environmental impact and running costs. **Objective 1: People.** Creating green jobs, skills, education & training opportunities. **Objective 2: Product.** Stimulating green innovation & business growth. **Objective 3: Operations.** Helping businesses decarbonise their operations. Collaborative work with academia, sustainability experts and other organisations will lead to the co-creation of solutions to reduce local emissions and access funding. You can [join the community by completing this form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdrHafxELC9ldt1uymNqvCou_AyyGP0cAQGzL6gptaFXkj5-g/viewform). **Activities** _Networking_ * Connecting all businesses and organisations that have an interest in achieving net-zero emissions through adoption of sustainable solutions * Sharing best practices, project ideas, knowledge and intelligence and promoting peer to peer learning * Bringing together businesses with academics, policy makers, training providers, ecological and social entrepreneurs and stimulating eco-innovation * Facilitating opportunities for businesses to identify new potential customers and markets * Encouraging peer to peer mentoring _Knowledge sharing_ * Developing a repository of complementary skill sets, capacity and expertise to help businesses participate in a greener economy * Signposting to other relevant websites and agencies _Capacity building_ * Organising and facilitating participation in workshops, training related to green skills development and other events to learn about net-zero emissions and relevant solutions; raise awareness of business opportunities created from the transition to a green economy; and access programmes and funding aiming to develop green skills, eco-innovation and/or reduce the negative impact of business activities on the environment. _Recognition_ * Maintaining an online database of Kingston Green Business Community members and documenting best practice case studies * Promoting projects and businesses that adopt sustainable solutions and make a positive impact on the environment * Creating opportunities for businesses to add environmental and socio-economic value to other local community groups and across the Borough **Membership** Membership is free and the community is open to all businesses and organisations based and/or operating in Kingston. The Kingston Green Business Community is linked with other existing and future green and wider business communities with similar objectives. You can apply to [become a member of Kingston Green Business Community by completing this form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdrHafxELC9ldt1uymNqvCou_AyyGP0cAQGzL6gptaFXkj5-g/viewform). Please also read through our [Code of Practice](https://forms.gle/qBF58qVxi1JdYjhN6) to understand and agree with the terms. Find [further information about Kingston Green Business Community's current activities](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/climate-change/climate-change-information-businesses) and Members. **Founding Members: ** Aviva, Bentall Centre, Energy Group/Transition Town Kingston, Genuine Solutions, Imperial College, IQ in IT, Kingston Chamber of Commerce, Kingston Council, Kingston First, Kingston Hospital, Kingston University, Lidl, South London Partnership, South Thames Colleges Group, United Business Group, WSP.

name: Raleigh House Day Centre
description: * A purpose-built, fully accessible day centre for up to 40 people per day to find companionship and wellbeing. * A full and varied programme of activities, a freshly-cooked lunch and delicious refreshments. * Fully-accessible transport options available. * Trained and experienced staff who make everyone feel respected and seen. * Expertise in dementia, frailty and other common physical and mental health conditions. * Purpose-built, airy and bright facilities including a sunny courtyard garden and pool table. * Access to a range of additional services including podiatry, hairdressing, help at home, handyperson, information and advice and specialist services. Raleigh House is a warm and vibrant centre with a wonderful team of staff and volunteers ready to take care of you for the day. A full day's attendance includes a two-course lunch, plenty of refreshments and a full and varied activity programme. Our modern, purpose-built centre is spacious and fully accessible, with a large, airy lounge and dining area, space for arts and crafts, a hairdressing salon, podiatry clinic, accessible shower room and a sheltered courtyard garden and terrace. A huge variety of activities are provided, including chair-based exercise, singing, gardening, cooking, bingo, craft, pool, board games, puzzles, quizzes and a nail bar. We have regular live entertainment, visits from therapy pets and occasional day trips in and around the local area. Fully-accessible transport is available for those who need it, or we can help you access alternative transport such as Dial-a-Ride. The Raleigh House team support people living with mild to moderate dementia, as well as people with other additional health, mental health and wellbeing needs. We offer personal care support and can refer members on to additional Staywell services including Help@Home, The Bradbury, Handyperson, Information and Advice and other specialist services. We are able to provide day-time respite for carers with the added reassurances of a secure, safe, warm, supportive and respectful environment staffed by a trained, experienced and dedicated team of professionals and volunteers. name: Cheaper Home Broadband
description: If you have broadband already, contact your provider online or by phone. How a social tariff could help you ---------------------------------- * **It's available to those on a variety of benefits.** If you or someone in your household claims Universal Credit, you could switch to any of the tariffs available. * **It's cheaper than a regular package.** Current prices range from £10 to £24. * **Fast, unlimited broadband.** Most tariffs offer superfast broadband at speeds over 30 Mbit/s – fast enough for you to keep in touch with friends and family, stream HD films or shop online. * **You'll pay next-to-nothing to get set up.** If you do have to pay any setup costs, these should only be small. Your provider should tell you before you sign up. * **It could cost nothing to switch.** If your provider offers a social tariff, you can switch to it at any time, free of charge. * **The price won't go up mid-contract.** You won't pay any more than what you agree at the start of the contract. * **It costs nothing to leave.** You won't pay a fee to leave the tariff before the end of your contract. If you are thinking of getting broadband you can visit the [Ofcom website](https://www.ofcom.org.uk/phones-telecoms-and-internet/advice-for-consumers/costs-and-billing/social-tariffs) or the [Money Saving Expert website](https://www.moneysavingexpert.com/compare-broadband-deals/broadband-social-tariffs/) to find out more. If your current provider doesn’t offer cheaper broadband, it is often easy to move to a provider that does.
intro: Many home broadband companies offer cheaper deals to people on Universal Credit and some other benefits. They offer good speeds and are committed to keeping prices low.

name: The Sound Doctor: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
description: This series of films will help you understand more about COPD - whether you've had the condition for a long time or been recently diagnosed. The films will help you really understand what COPD is and give practical advice on how to reduce the risk of exacerbations, to use your inhalers more effectively and to make sure you get the most out of life. We've interviewed a wide range of experts who'll give you the information you need to take control of your COPD. There’s a lot you can do to make life easier. If you watch these films we hope you'll cope better with breathlessness and have fewer flare-ups. The films are grouped into a few categories. Use them how you want and consider watching the ones that matter to you more than once. Knowledge is power. ### [Click here to access videos from the COPD Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/274dbo5s), these cover: * Understanding COPD and Getting Started * Exacerbations and Breathlessness * Medicines * Getting the Best Out of Your Inhaler * Living Well with COPD * Asthma You can also [register for free to our How to Live Well with COPD course](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/courses/copd-course). This course provides top quality advice and information in five modules, based around films. Easy to watch and understand, the course is engaging and effective. It will help you understand more about your condition and give you tips and techniques to help you live life to the full. Contributors include many of the UK’s leading respiratory specialists as well as expert patients. Our mission is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs.
intro: Bite-sized, easy to understand and easy to watch videos to help you manage COPD.

name: Berrylands Pilates
description: If you suffer from back pain, a shoulder or sports injury, or want a friendly environment to maintain your postnatal fitness, come and rediscover the joy of movement at one of Berrylands Pilates classes. ### **Pilates classes** * Face-to-Face Pilates Classes Mondays 9:30 am (1hr) * Lunchtime Face-to-Face Pilates Classes Fridays 12.30 pm( 50min) * Online Pilates Classes Wednesdays 10:30 am (1hr) ### Strength and Balance Classes These classes are designed to strengthen muscles, improve bone health, and improve balance. They are suitable for people with osteoporosis, osteopenia, and osteoarthritis. description: **[Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/kingston-adult-education/kingston-adult-education-course-directory?search_api_fulltext=send&f%5B0%5D=localgov_directories_facets%3A12)** --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Kingston Adult Education provides a range of courses specifically designed for individuals with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). We provide a welcoming and supportive atmosphere, encouraging learners with learning difficulties and disabilities to grow and develop their skills and talents. For those who have a love for arts and crafts, we offer an engaging programme that allows you to tap into your creativity and enjoy activities such as crafting, drawing and painting. In our drama and performing arts course, you will explore acting and movement in a relaxed and safe environment. We strive to have regular productions, with recent performances at the cornerHOUSE Arts Centre. Our computer courses are designed to teach you digital skills for everyday life and encourage internet safety, and our cookery classes are designed to teach you how to prepare different recipes. Come along, work together, have fun, make new friends, and learn at your own pace. **_[“Helps me make new friends and be more confident in the kitchen.”](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/kingston-adult-education/kingston-adult-education-course-directory?search_api_fulltext=send&f%5B0%5D=localgov_directories_facets%3A12)_** For further information, contact **[adult.education@kingston.gov.uk](mailto:adult.education@kingston.gov.uk)** or **[020 8547 6700](tel:020%208547%206700)** or Visit the [Kingston Adult Education Course Directory](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/kingston-adult-education/kingston-adult-education-course-directory?search_api_fulltext=send&f%5B0%5D=localgov_directories_facets%3A12)

description: We are a statutory body that acts as the independent champion for health and social care services in and around the borough. We gather feedback and evidence from local people about health and social care issues and use this to influence the design and delivery of these services. We engage with people from the local community and support them to be involved and have a say in the way their health and social care services are run. We work closely with providers and commissioners to help improve services, and ensure that the voice of local people is heard. **Volunteer with us!** ---------------------- * Make a difference in your local community by giving people the opportunity to speak up about their health and social care * Make new friends as you become part of the Healthwatch team * Boost your CV as you develop new skills and confidence in the workplace * Use your skills to contribute to the success of Healthwatch across our different projects, youth outreach projects and/or reducing mental health stigma.

description: We are a statutory body that acts as the independent champion for health and social care services in and around the borough. We gather feedback and evidence from local people about health and social care issues and use this to influence the design and delivery of these services. We engage with people from the local community and support them to be involved and have a say in the way their health and social care services are run. description: **CLICK** is always **FREE** to attend. You can come any Monday to Friday from **2pm-6pm** (**9pm on Tuesday**) and **10am - 4pm** on Saturdays. No booking necessary. If you need support you can come with your PA, support worker, family member or friend. Everyone is welcome. **CLICK is open on Tuesday evenings from 2pm through to 8pm.** We will also be running structured activities through the evening which people can choose to join in. **CLICK will be open on Saturdays from 10am to 4pm.** There will be a structured programme of activities throughout the day. This will include things like: sensory activities, art & craft, exercises, easy baking, discussion groups. Everyone is welcome. Whilst our focus is upon local disabled people, other people who are lonely or isolated are also welcome. CLICK offers food & drink at low prices (no obligation to buy). It also provides space to be with other people, have a chat, play board games or just chill. On some days we also have other entertainment such as: quizzes, Karaoke, snooker, and other fun things. This is a drop in facility with no need to book and no charge. We cannot provide care, but carers and families are very welcome. We also welcome volunteers. Address: 13 Geneva Road Kingston KT1 2TW Phone number: 07904 235 305

name: Royal British Legion - Support for the Armed Forces Community
description: ### What support can I get? The Royal British Legion (RBL) provides support to serving and former Armed Forces personnel and their families. You can get help with a range of issues, including money, housing, employment, health and care. If you're not sure what support you need, the RBL Support Team can talk through your situation and help you find the right support. ### Money, benefits and debt You may be able to get help if you are struggling financially. Support includes: * benefits and debt advice * help with financial difficulties * financial assistance where eligible * practical support to help you get your finances back on track. **[Click here to find out about financial support from RBL.](https://www.britishlegion.org.uk/get-support/how-we-help/financial-support)** ### Housing RBL can provide advice and practical support if you: * are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless * are having problems with your housing * are relocating * need to adapt your home because of mobility or medical needs. RBL may also be able to help you access appropriate housing support. **[Click here to find housing advice and support.](https://www.britishlegion.org.uk/get-support/expert-guidance/housing)** ### Help to live independently RBL may be able to help eligible members of the Armed Forces community live safely and independently at home. Depending on your circumstances, support may include: * small home adaptations * specialist equipment * mobility aids * personal alarms. ### Physical and mental health RBL provides information and guidance to help you find appropriate physical and mental health support. Recovery services are also available to help serving personnel and veterans who are experiencing challenges following an injury or illness. ### Care and dementia RBL provides guidance and practical support for people with care needs and for family members or friends who care for someone. Specialist dementia support is available through RBL's Admiral Nurse service, which supports members of the Armed Forces community and their families who are living with dementia. RBL also has care homes for the Armed Forces community and their families, including homes offering specialist dementia care. ### Employment RBL provides guidance for serving personnel, veterans and their families who are moving into civilian life or looking for work. This can include information and guidance about: * finding and applying for jobs * returning to work * moving from military to civilian employment * finding employment support if you have a disability or health condition. **[Click here to find employment support and guidance.](https://www.britishlegion.org.uk/get-support/expert-guidance/employment)** ### Feeling lonely or isolated If you are feeling lonely or isolated, RBL can help you find ways to connect with other people. The Telephone Buddy service offers companionship and a friendly person to talk to. **[Click here to find support if you're feeling lonely or isolated.](https://www.britishlegion.org.uk/get-support/how-we-help/social-support)** ### War Pensions and Armed Forces Compensation RBL provides guidance about War Pensions and the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme. You may also be able to get support if you want to appeal a decision, including representation at a tribunal. ### Who can get support? RBL supports serving and former members of the Armed Forces and their families. For people who have previously served, RBL support can begin after one day's service and continue throughout life. Support may also be available to family members, dependants and carers. **[Click here to check who can get support from RBL.](https://www.britishlegion.org.uk/get-support/who-we-help)** ### Not sure what help you need? You do not need to know which RBL service is right for you before getting in touch. Contact the RBL Support Team and an adviser can talk through your situation and help you find the most appropriate support. If RBL cannot provide the help you need, they may be able to direct you to another organisation that can. **Call:** 0808 802 8080 **Opening hours:** 8am to 8pm, 7 days a week You can also contact RBL using its online chat. **[Click here to see all support available from the Royal British Legion.](https://www.britishlegion.org.uk/get-support/how-we-help)**

description: Employment support for veterans ------------------------------- The Poppy Factory provides **free, personalised employment support** to veterans with physical or mental health conditions. You will work with an employment consultant who can help you identify your goals, build your confidence and take practical steps towards finding and staying in work. What can I get help with? ------------------------- Support is tailored to you and can include: * writing or improving your CV * searching for suitable jobs * completing job applications * preparing for interviews * exploring different careers and opportunities * identifying training that could help you move towards work * building confidence and overcoming barriers to employment * support when returning to work after a period away * support after you start a job to help you settle in and stay in employment You do not need to have a CV or know exactly what type of work you want before asking for support. Who can get support? -------------------- You may be eligible if you: * have served for at least one day in the **Armed Forces or Reserves** * identify as having a **physical or mental health condition** * are unemployed and considering returning to work. Your health condition does **not** need to have been caused by your Armed Forces service. The Poppy Factory may also be able to support you if you are facing redundancy, are away from work because of long-term sickness, or feel that your current job is having a negative effect on your health. **[Click here to check the eligibility criteria and find out more about employment support.](https://www.poppyfactory.org/are-you-looking-for-work/)** How does the support work? -------------------------- The support is based around your individual circumstances, rather than a one-size-fits-all programme. An employment consultant will work with you to understand your experience, skills, health, circumstances and employment goals. Together, you can identify the support you need and the steps that could help you move towards suitable employment. Support can continue **after you start work**, helping you overcome difficulties and sustain your employment. How do I get support? --------------------- You can contact The Poppy Factory directly to discuss employment support and find out whether the service is right for you. **Phone:** 020 8940 3305 **Email:** [support@poppyfactory.org](mailto:support@poppyfactory.org)

name: Perinatal Mental Health Support
description: **Most of us expect to feel happy, excited and positive during pregnancy and when our baby is born, but it doesn’t always happen like this.** You can feel many different emotions, including love and pride, but it is natural to also feel stressed and anxious. **This is normal.** You may: • Already have a mental illness when you got pregnant • Be worried because you have had mental health problems before. • Develop a mental health problem for the first time It is important that you get the right support if you have, or are at risk of developing, mental health problems during pregnancy or in the first year after the birth. **Who are we?** We are a specialist mental health service for people who are planning a pregnancy, are pregnant or have a baby up to 12 months old. We are made up of different professionals including psychiatrists, mental health nurses, psychologists and allied health professionals such as occupational therapists, social workers and nursery nurses. **Our aim is to:** • Help you stay as well as possible during pregnancy and after your baby is born. • Make sure that you, your family and other professionals can recognise any signs that you are becoming unwell as early as possible. • Make sure that you, your partner and family have the information you need and can get advice about mental health problems and treatments. • Work together with you, your partner and family, and the other professionals involved in your care. **Referral process** We accept referrals from health and social care professionals, including GPs, obstetricians, midwives, health visitors, and any mental health professional who has reviewed you. Unfortunately, it is not possible to self-refer so if you have concerns please speak with your GP, midwife or health visitor who will make a referral if appropriate. The majority of women referred to us will be seen within six weeks of referral. **Useful online resources for perinatal mental health:** * **[Action on Post-Partum Psychosis Leaflets](https://www.app-network.org/what-is-pp/app-guides/)** on topics including Postnatal Psychosis, Bipolar in Pregnancy and Advice for Partners * **[Bipolar UK](https://www.bipolaruk.org/Pages/FAQs/Category/women-and-bipolar):** Women and Bipolar Information about Pregnancy * **[Association for Post Natal Illness](https://apni.org/leaflets/post-natal-depression/):** Postnatal Depression information * **[Maternal Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD)](https://maternalocd.org/)** * **[Birth Trauma Association](https://www.birthtraumaassociation.org.uk/)** * **[Best Beginnings](https://www.bestbeginnings.org.uk/out-of-the-blue):** Out of the Blue Campaign to improve awareness and access to help for perinatal mental health problems, including informative videos. * **[Perinatal Positivity](https://perinatalpositivity.org/):** a short video using the real voices and experiences of women

description: **What we offer:** * **Counselling and Coaching** we offer short term counselling and coaching to help deal with your current life circumstances and make positive change * **Complementary therapies**, such as aromatherapy, massage, acupuncture, reiki, reflexology and shiatsu. * **One to one support** emotional support, legal advice, soul midwife support and welfare and benefits support * **Wellbeing classes,** yoga, Pilates, tai chi, health walks, relaxation techniques, poetry sessions, art classes and craft classes * **Workshops** on a range of subjects such as managing stress, headscarf tying, body image, nutrition, emotional freedom technique and many more * **Support groups** for men, patients and those who have been bereaved * **Drop in** we have a beautiful garden space and a welcome area All of our services are free and we have no postcode boundaries.

description: Happy Feet walking group, is run by Mind in Kingston. Our mantra is “**Come as you are, however you’re feeling. You don’t have to be ‘at your best**’. ” Our aim is to support people to feel more confident about walking in the local area. We are inclusive and always welcoming to new participants. Details of our walks: **Day:** Every Monday (except Bank Holidays) **Meeting Point:** 11:30am **Walk Start time:** 11:40am (IMPORTANT: please note we will leave at 11:40am, and can't wait past this time) **Meeting Point:** Kingston Station (We meet by the flower bed outside Kingston train station). **Please contact:** [wellbeingactivities@mindinkingston.org.uk](mailto:wellbeingactivities@mindinkingston.org.uk) to find out more and be added to the group. **Not sure this is the right service for you? You can complete our Services and Support Enquiry Form** on our website. A member of our team will get back to you to assist you.
intro: Join our friendly group every Monday at 11:30am to get some fresh air and explore Kingston’s green parks and riverside.

description: This course is for people who have been left with on-going symptoms of: * breathlessness * fatigue * anxiety * disordered breathing Learn breathing and singing techniques to help you manage symptoms and get support from course tutors and fellow course guests. name: Healthier You: NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme
description: 12.3 million people in the UK are at risk of developing type 2 diabetes - and type 2 diabetes is serious. In Kingston, more than 14,000 people are estimated to already have, or are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Roughly three in five cases of type 2 diabetes can be prevented or delayed by maintaining a healthy weight, eating well and being active - and **support is available to help you**. **The Healthier You: NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme** identifies those at high risk and refers them onto a behaviour change programme. You can register if you have had a recent blood test by your GP and received a letter/text or email regarding your risk of type 2 diabetes. To self register you will need: * Your NHS Number * Blood Test Result (either your HbA1c or FPG reading) * Date of Blood Test (must be within the past 12 months) To find out your risk of type 2 diabetes you’ll need a few spare minutes, scales and a tape measure. Visit the [Diabetes UK Know your Risk tool](https://riskscore.diabetes.org.uk/start) when you’re ready, and start your journey there. If you already have a type 2 diabetes diagnosis, as a Kingston resident, you also have free access to the [Diabetes Book and Learn website](https://diabetesbooking.co.uk/), where it is possible to search for local diabetes education programmes that are delivered online, remotely.
intro: The Healthier You: NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme aims to reduce people’s risk of developing Type 2 diabetes across England, and is available to people in Kingston.

name: Language Courses
description: Kingston Adult Education provides a full programme of courses to broaden your language skills or help you embark on a rewarding career as a community interpreter. Whether you want to learn a new language from scratch or advance your existing skills, we have a language class for you! We offer varying levels in French, Italian and Spanish giving you the opportunity to expand your grammar as well as your conversational skills. Have you ever thought about using your language skills and becoming a community interpreter? Our accredited qualification courses provide a great introduction to the role of an interpreter as well as the skills and knowledge needed for the job. For further information, contact [adult.education@kingston.gov.uk](mailto:adult.education@kingston.gov.uk) or Call us on 020 8547 6700 or visit the [Kingston Adult Education Course Directory](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/kingston-adult-education/kingston-adult-education-course-directory?search_api_fulltext=Languages)
intro: Learn a Language at Kingston Adult Education. We have a range of language classes for learners, some of which are offered at different levels. French, German, Italian and Spanish. There's something for everyone!
organisation: Kingston Adult Education Kingston Adult Education We have our core delivery: ESOL, English, Maths, Digital, Vocational, Health & Fitness, Arts, Crafts, Languages, Writing, History and we have some wonderful new courses for you to turn your hand to. Why not try our new Jewellery Making Workshop and if you like it, join the new course. Along with new craft workshops and courses, we’ve also added new art courses and workshops: Why not enjoy Botanical Watercolours, Drawing & Painting Animals, Landscape Painting, Oil Painting or Mindful Art? Whether you're looking to meet new people, explore new interests, get a job, gain qualifications for your career or keep your mind and body active we have something for everyone. Along with our wonderful Tai Chi, Pilates, and Mindful Movement courses, why not try our new Journaling for Wellbeing to help build your resilience and improve your wellbeing? With both **online** and **in-person** classes available at locations across the borough, you can easily find a course that fits your needs. In addition, many of our courses are **free** as they are government funded or offered at reduced rates, and we provide discounts based on your circumstances, so please contact us to find out more. Enjoy your courses and being a part of our wonderful adult education community. description: There's always plenty to do for helpers of all abilities, Find out more, including confirmation of or changes to our weekend gardening sessions and opportunities available, on [our Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/groups/canburycommunitygarden/). **More about the community garden** Since summer 2016, volunteers have been transforming the neglected edge of Canbury Gardens into a productive, wildlife-friendly, community garden. If you’d like to learn more about wildlife-friendly gardening, or you're a keen gardener with skills you could share, or you’d enjoy working alongside other people to grow herbs and other foods, come along to one of our events or weekend gardening sessions. There's always plenty to do, depending on the season, your abilities and the time you can spare. * watering * weeding * planting * harvesting * tidying * composting **Children accompanied by a responsible adult are welcome too.** The basic principle is that those that do the work share in the harvest - and we have had some excellent harvests of runner and broad beans, tomatoes, herbs, courgettes, spinach and more. Canbury Community Chicken Collective keep a few chickens in a run in the garden; they are out and about during gardening sessions and fun to watch. There's [plenty of evidence that outdoor activity can help fight depression](https://www.theguardian.com/society/2019/may/13/green-therapy-gardening-helping-fight-depression) - though that's not the only reason to come along!

name: The Sound Doctor: Keeping Well at Work
description: Most of us spend a lot of time at work, and so it’s very important to make sure we are as happy and healthy in the workplace as we can be. We have interviewed leading national and international experts, covering a wide range of workplace issues, all related to our health and wellbeing. Even if you don’t think you have any problems yourself, our library of over 50 films about keeping well at work, will have information to help you assist friends, colleagues and team members who might be struggling. There is a wealth of information broken down into coherent, bite sized chunks. Sleep, for example, is something we all do, but we’re not all very good at it. If you haven’t taken the issue of sleep seriously, or accept a poor sleep pattern as inevitable, these films are for you. All our information is designed to prevent or manage health problems caused by your work environment. ### [Click here to access videos from the Keeping Well at Work Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/28nxjt3a), these cover: * Your mental health * Stress and Anxiety * Workplace relationships * Relaxation and Mindfulness Exercises * Management structure and Culture * Sleep * Your office environment * Building activity into your working day * Diet and nutrition Our mission at The Sound Doctor is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs.
intro: Bite-sized, easy to understand and easy to watch videos to help keep well at work.

name: Dementia Adviser
description: Our Dementia Adviser service provides information and advice for people affected by dementia in Kingston. We provide support for people living with dementia **and their carers and families** through telephone support and home visits. We also run Peer Support groups for Carers and our Carers information workshops. We work closely with other organisations in the borough to ensure we provide up to date information on local support and activities for people living with dementia. Anyone can refer into the service or self-refer. You can contact us by phone or email. \*Consent should be obtained from the individuals to receive our services. Call **0207 423 5115** or email kingstonoffice@alzheimers.org.uk ### **You can also signpost to the following services:** * Dementia Support line: 0333 150 3456 Support line opening hours: Monday to Wednesday 9am-8pm, Thursday and Friday 9am-5pm, and Saturday and Sunday 10am-4pm * [Dementia Support Forum](https://forum.alzheimers.org.uk/) Helpful online community where anyone who is affected by dementia can receive valuable support. It's free, open day or night, and can be accessed online. * [Alzheimer’s Society Dementia Directory](https://www.alzheimers.org.uk/find-support-near-you)

description: **What we offer:** * All abilities are welcome * In-person and online group classes * Teen classes * Chair-based classes * Private sessions * Vinyasa, hatha, restorative, pilates and more You can [find out more about what classes we offer on our website](https://www.behappyyoga.fit/book-yoga-class-yoga-therapy).
intro: Be Happy Yoga offers yoga therapy and classes. During our classes, you will work on your postures, breathing and meditation.
organisation: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). description: KVA's Surplus to Supper Hub is a community driven initiative aimed at tackling food insecurity in Kingston. With 1 in 4 households with children facing food challenges, this project seeks to provide nutritious food to those in need while reducing food waste. Our aim is to ensure that our community experiencing food insecurity has access to healthy, nutritious food. By redistributing surplus food to those in need, we help improve diets and overall well-being, particularly for vulnerable individuals and families.

description: The [My Computer My Way](https://mcmw.abilitynet.org.uk/) 'how to' tool can help you to set up accessibility features on your digital devices including: * How to use zoom control to make text larger * How to use speech to text services * How to avoid unwanted key strokes * How to change the colour of the mouse pointer * How to make your device read text aloud You can tailor the guides based on your needs. [AbilityNet](https://abilitynet.org.uk/) (who provides all the guides for My Computer My Way) support a wide range of users; from older or disabled people looking for help with their technology - visit their website for more free factsheets and guides.

name: AtaLoss
description: Our aim is to ensure service information for people who are bereaved is always up to date and accurate. Bereavement is different for everyone so we list services of all types, including * counselling * peer support groups * death cafes * information services * people that help with the legal stuff * support for bereaved children. There services are available for all ages, faiths and types of loss. In summary, we provide: * Easy to search and find bereavement support services from over 1400 providers nationwide * Search your area for local support services * Find practical support to help you to deal with admin after a loved one dies * Find helpful reads in our resources library and well being pages * Find helplines if you need to talk * Use our free online bereavement chat service to chat with a professional counsellor- Monday to Friday 9am-9pm
intro: We are a signposting and information service for people who are bereaved and professionals supporting them.
organisation: AtaLoss ### **AtaLoss was established as a charity in 2016, to ensure that no one in the UK should be left without support when someone dies.** _Do you, or does someone you know need support because of bereavement? If someone important has died visit AtaLoss.org the UK's leading signposting website to get or provide advise on local and national support options._ Our mission is to change the culture of bereavement, so that every bereaved person can have timely and holistic support, to navigate their grief and changed circumstances for healthy outcomes. We do this by addressing the first three tiers of the adult bereavement care pyramid: * Raising awareness of the effect of bereavement * Providing a central signposting and information service for everyone bereaved * Training and equipping community support. name: Slimming World
description: The Slimming World active lifestyle programme can help you build everyday positive habits to improve your overall health and wellbeing. It combines * A healthy eating plan * A step-by-step approach to gradually increasing your physical activity levels * Supportive weekly group sessions across Kingston * Digital online service offering extra personalised tools In order to qualify for this programme, you need to: * Be 16 years old or over * Live, work, study or be registered with a GP in the Borough of Kingston, **and** * Have a Body Mass Index (BMI) equal or above **28**; or * Have a BMI equal or above **25** with a weight related comorbidity; or * Have a BMI equal or above **23** and from a Black African, African-Caribbean, South Asian or Chinese ethnic group * Be ready to change! If you have been a member of Slimming World in the last 12 months you will not be eligible for a free 12 week voucher (existing Kingston Healthy Lifestyle Referral clients who had a starting BMI >35 are eligible to receive a second set of 12 weeks free if they have reached 5% weight loss at 10 weeks). You can [find out your own BMI with the NHS calculator](https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/healthy-weight/bmi-calculator/). You will need to know your height and weight before getting started. You can also [find out more about what Slimming World offers on their website](https://www.slimmingworld.co.uk/). Get in touch with us directly on 01773 546050, **or if you'd like to speak to a member of the Kingston Public Health team first for more information**, complete the [Healthy Lifestyles sign up form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd2UxSIo3SHWFIisnjscDVXMcU8Zq1wlzmRqyCrDUW3xk_00g/viewform) and check the Slimming World box.

name: Slimming World
description: The Slimming World active lifestyle programme can help you build everyday positive habits to improve your overall health and wellbeing. It combines * A healthy eating plan * A step-by-step approach to gradually increasing your physical activity levels * Supportive weekly group sessions across Kingston * Digital online service offering extra personalised tools In order to qualify for this programme, you need to: * Be 16 years old or over * Live, work, study or be registered with a GP in the Borough of Kingston, **and** * Have a Body Mass Index (BMI) equal or above **28**; or * Have a BMI equal or above **25** with a weight related comorbidity; or * Have a BMI equal or above **23** and from a Black African, African-Caribbean, South Asian or Chinese ethnic group * Be ready to change! If you have been a member of Slimming World in the last 12 months you will not be eligible for a free 12 week voucher (existing Kingston Healthy Lifestyle Referral clients who had a starting BMI >35 are eligible to receive a second set of 12 weeks free if they have reached 5% weight loss at 10 weeks). You can [find out your own BMI with the NHS calculator](https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/healthy-weight/bmi-calculator/). You will need to know your height and weight before getting started. You can also [find out more about what Slimming World offers on their website](https://www.slimmingworld.co.uk/). Get in touch with us directly on 01773 546050, **or if you'd like to speak to a member of the Kingston Public Health team first for more information**, complete the [Healthy Lifestyles sign up form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd2UxSIo3SHWFIisnjscDVXMcU8Zq1wlzmRqyCrDUW3xk_00g/viewform) and check the Slimming World box.

name: Better Bones Service
description: Face to face sessions, includes: **Bone health information sessions -** bone health and looking after your joints, osteoarthritis management, lifestyle factors including diet and physical activity. These sessions are available for anyone interested including out of borough clients. **Better Bones Exercise Classes:** Only for people living /working/studying in Kingston or registered with Kingston GP surgeries. **Strength & balance exercise class -** if you have one or more long term condition, and need general exercises to improve or maintain your muscle strength and balance. **Osteoarthritis knee exercise class -** exercise and information for people diagnosed with osteoarthritis of one or both knees, that haven’t been replaced. **Osteoporosis risk exercise class -** weight bearing, bone and muscle strength and balance exercises if you have a diagnosis of osteopenia or osteoporosis, or are at risk of developing these. Risk factors include * low trauma fracture * family history of hip fracture * early menopause (before 45) * rheumatoid arthritis * cancer treatments * taking oral steroids * age - women over 50 * low parathyroid or high thyroid levels * eating disorders or avoiding major food groups (e.g. coeliacs) * smoking * drinking more than 3 units of alcohol per day. If you are interested in taking part in any of the available sessions, or if you want to find out more, please contact us on **0300 123 8086** or email us on [swlicb.betterbones@nhs.net](swlicb.betterbones@nhs.net). Sept term 2026 -------------- **Information sessions:** for anyone interested, out of borough clients, families, friends welcome 1. **Bone Health:** 24 Nov (13.00-14.30pm), New Malden library, 48 Kingston Road, New Malden KT3 3LY Learn about how to look after your bones. We will discuss diet, exercise and lifestyle factors that affects our bones and how to keep them healthy and strong. 1. **Physical Activity:** 29 Sept (13.00-14.30pm), New Malden library, 48 Kingston Road, New Malden KT3 3LY Learn about Physical activity and the type and amount of activities we need to do to maintain our health and wellbeing. Also learn about simple exercises to do at home. 2. **Osteoporosis and Bone Health:** 14 Oct (12.30-14.30pm) Chessington Sports Centre, Garrison Lane, Chessington KT9 2JS Learn about how to manage or prevent osteoporosis. We will discuss diet, exercise and lifestyle factors that affects our bones and how to keep them healthy and strong. 3. **Self management in Osteoarthritis:** 27 Oct (13.00-14.30pm), New Malden library, 48 Kingston Road, New Malden KT3 3LY Learn about osteoarthritis and how to look after your joints using lifestyle factors. 4. **Bone Health:** 24 Nov (13.00-14.30pm), New Malden library, 48 Kingston Road, New Malden KT3 3LY Learn about how to look after your bones. name: Alfriston Outreach Service
description: Alfriston provides a number of services in the community that can be delivered into people’s homes to help reduce isolation and loneliness, and ensure that no one is forgotten or left behind. * Hot Lunch Delivery – Hand cooked with love in the Alfriston Kitchen and delivered ready to eat. This service is currently at capacity. £7 a meal. * Laundry – We travel to users’ houses, collect their washing, clean it, dry it and fold it, ready to be returned in a few days – £12 a load (e.g 8KG, a bin liner full) * Collecting and Delivering Prescriptions – We are able to collect and deliver urgent prescriptions – Free * Providing Hearing Aid Batteries – We provide free Hearing Aid batteries via the NHS – Free * Shopping – We can shop at Sainsburys for those unable to leave their home – £3 * Urgent Support – We provide urgent support such as emergency food bags, bedding, etc to those who have recently been discharged from hospital, or moved into a new address and do not currently have the support in place that they need.

description: ### The NHS Quit Smoking app can help you stop smoking by providing daily support and motivation. If you stay smokefree for the 4-week programme you're up to 5 times more likely to quit for good. Plus, you can track the days you've been smokefree and see how much you're saving! **Smoking is bad for your health, but exactly how will stopping make life better? Here are some of the [ways your health will improve when you stop smoking](https://www.nhs.uk/better-health/quit-smoking/why-quit-smoking/benefits-of-quitting-smoking/).** * [download the app from iTunes](https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/nhs-smokefree/id687298065) * [download the app from Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.doh.smokefree&hl=en_GB&gl=US)

description: This Stop Smoking course has been created to help you quit. **TOGETHER WE CAN DO THIS! ** It’s really hard to give up smoking, but success is achievable and if you don’t succeed first, second or third time, don’t worry. Just try again, and hold onto that motivation to quit. When it does happen, the good news is, 95% of ex-smokers notice positive changes within just two weeks of quitting. Our films and courses are designed to support you through this journey, providing effective strategies to help you become smoke-free, with information from some of the UK’s leading national and international specialists. There are three modules in the course. Films include: **Module 1** * Getting started * Why we smoke * What's in a cigarette? * How nicotine works * Habits and triggers * The health risks of smoking * More about the risks of smoking * Stories from former smokers who have COPD - audio * The benefits of quitting * Finding your motivation **Module 2** * Preparing to quit * The best way to quit successfully * An introduction to Nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) * Preparing to quite * How actress Linda Robson quit - audio * Some more preparation techniques * Some reasons to quit * Are you ready to quit? **Module 3** * While you are quitting * Withdrawal and cravings * Coping with cravings * More techniques to manage cravings * A short breathing exercise * Dealing with triggers * More tactics for managing tricky situations * Lapse and relapse * More about NRTs * E Cigarettes/vaping [You can access the course here.](https://tinyurl.com/29r3afk8) Our mission at The Sound Doctor is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs.

name: Kingston Mental Health Carers' Forum
description: Advice, information and guidance for those giving unpaid care to someone with mental health difficulties. Break your feelings of isolation by coming along to our Peer Support Group, or by receiving 1:1 support. Face-to-face sessions are available each month on wards and community service at Tolworth Hospital. From time to time, we offer free social events to our members. Signing-up as a member costs absolutely nothing, but allows us to keep in touch with you. As a partner with Health and Social Care Providers and complementary Voluntary Organisations, we can answer your questions about mental health and the services available. These relationships also enable us to campaign effectively on your behalf for improvements to services. We also strive to de-stigmatise Mental Health by encouraging open discussion with members of the public at (for example) Community Fairs or through direct enquiry.

description: Are you looking for support to help you manage your weight? Kingston has a range of **free** or low cost programmes that can help you. Choose from: * [Slimming World](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/slimming-world) (12 weeks free, free membership) * [NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/healthier-you-nhs-diabetes-prevention-programme) (for people at high risk of developing Type 2 diabetes) * [Get Active](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/get-active-exercise-referral-programme) (12 weeks, low cost) \*please note a GP referral is required for this programme To be eligible for the 'by referral' programmes, you must: * Live or work in Kingston and be above 16 years of age * Have a Body Mass Index (BMI) equal or above **28**; or * Have a BMI equal or above **25** with a weight related comorbidity; or * Have a BMI equal or above **23** and from a Black African, African-Caribbean, South Asian or Chinese ethnic group If you need to check your weight and BMI, your nurse, GP or pharmacist will help you, or you can [use the NHS BMI healthy weight calculator](https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/healthy-weight/bmi-calculator/). You can [sign up to these programmes and more by completing our Healthy Lifestyles form](https://forms.gle/F7Ku7ueZLqUCUWe97).

name: Staywell - Older People's Community Team
description: Most of us want to go on living in our own homes as we grow older. There are times, however, when some extra support can make all the difference. **Our team may be able to support you if:** * You or your your carer experience a period of illness * You have any long-term health problems, including Dementia * You have recently been to hospital * A little support and advice would help you stay at home **How it works:** We can support you to: * Access health services such as an optician, dentist and podiatrist * Recuperate at home after an illness or fall (e.g. support with collecting prescriptions, shopping and light meal preparation, caring for your domestic pets) * Get back on your feet after a fall or illness (e.g. accompanying you on shopping trips, get help around your home and garden, building your confidence) * Move around your home more safely by clearing trip hazards * Choose social activities e.g. outings and befriending * Access transport and community services e.g. blue badges, taxi cards, Dial-a-Ride * Check that you are getting the money and benefits and grants you are entitled to You can [find out more about what we offer on our website](https://www.staywellservices.org.uk/community-support-team).

description: Most of us want to go on living in our own homes as we grow older. There are times, however, when some extra support can make all the difference. **Our team may be able to support you if:** * You or your your carer experience a period of illness * You have any long-term health problems, including Dementia * You have recently been to hospital * A little support and advice would help you stay at home **How it works:** We can support you to: * Access health services such as an optician, dentist and podiatrist * Recuperate at home after an illness or fall (e.g. support with collecting prescriptions, shopping and light meal preparation, caring for your domestic pets) * Get back on your feet after a fall or illness (e.g. accompanying you on shopping trips, get help around your home and garden, building your confidence) * Move around your home more safely by clearing trip hazards * Choose social activities e.g. outings and befriending * Access transport and community services e.g. blue badges, taxi cards, Dial-a-Ride * Check that you are getting the money and benefits and grants you are entitled to You can [find out more about what we offer on our website](https://www.staywellservices.org.uk/community-support-team).

name: GoodGym Kingston
description: GoodGym is not an ordinary gym. We offer a way to volunteer that **fits into your life** easily, making it easy to commit for the long-term. **Anybody can join**, no matter your fitness level. All you need is a pair of trainers. You can **attend as often or as little as you like**. Once you’re a member we'll do our best to help you achieve your fitness goals. We also organise social events like parties and races so that you can get to know other members in our **vibrant community**. **Time to do a bit more?** **Good Gym Missions** involve helping at local community projects, as well as a run, all within 90 minutes. **How this works?** * Meet the group at the area start point, drop your bag and run to a local community organisation * Work hard with the group digging, lifting, scraping and clearing for a good cause * Push yourself on the run back with some intervals or a fitness session * Our qualified area activator will help you stretch and celebrate what we've achieved To find out more [visit GoodGym Kingston's webpage](https://www.goodgym.org/v3/areas/kingston-upon-thames).

description: Green Drinks is an international movement bringing like-minded people together. TTK hosts Kingston Green Drinks on the evening of the last Tuesday of every month (apart from public holidays and Covid restrictions), when you can meet people interested in environmental issues in an informal pub setting, and get to know what's happening in the Kingston environmental community and find interesting things to do. Buy yourself a drink, look for the Green Drinks symbol on a table and join us! Find out more and, nearer the time, confirm venue, dates and times at [https://e-voice.org.uk/ttkingston/events](https://e-voice.org.uk/ttkingston/events) or [https://www.facebook.com/groups/ttkingston](https://www.facebook.com/groups/ttkingston)

description: What is on offer at Kingston Libraries? --------------------------------------- **Our libraries are free** (though there may be a charge for some activities) and everyone is welcome. Libraries offer the following for loan: * Books * Large Print books * Spoken Word CDs Our libraries also provide: * Free public computers to use as well as plug-benches and free wi-fi to access; * Newspapers & magazines, and comfy chairs to sit and read; * Space to study; * Free collections of e-books, e-audio and e-magazines to download remotely; * Online reference resources to help with homework and research queries; * Regular activities for both adults and children, including reading groups, knit and natter groups, rhyme times and story times; * One off events, such as author talks, workshops and craft sessions, and * Council information and staff, who can signpost you to other organisations if you need further advice or guidance.

description: **All Girls Basketball – Kingston Lions** Kingston Lions Basketball Club offers a welcoming and inclusive environment for girls to get involved in basketball, whether they’re new to the sport or looking to play competitively. The club runs competitive girls’ teams from U10 to U18, with the main season running from September to May. Trials for these teams take place in May, with training beginning in early summer (June/July). Training sessions are held across venues including Coombe Girls’ School, Raynes Park High School and Richard Challoner School, typically between 5pm and 8pm, Monday to Thursday, with games taking place at weekends. For girls who prefer a more informal or non-competitive option, the club offers a weekly U13 open session (Years 4–8). This takes place on Mondays, 5:25–6:25pm at Coombe Girls’ School and is ideal for beginners or those looking to build confidence and skills in a relaxed setting. There is currently no waiting list, but all enquiries should be directed to Coach Andrew before signing up. For more information or to get involved, please contact Coach Andrew (email preferred): andrew@lionsbasketball.co.uk | 07874 030 454

name: Richmond Aquaphysio Group
description: **Richmond AquaPhysio Group** Richmond AquaPhysio Group is a voluntary self-financing community group that organizes group hydrotherapy classes in Teddington Hydrotherapy Pool, at the lowest possible cost. We offer ten half hour classes every week on different days and times. A maximum of seven members are allowed in the pool at any one time, along with the physio who is leading the group. The Hydrotherapy pool is purpose-built and all necessary items of equipment are supplied, including buoyancy aids. **Regular exercise in warm water** Regular exercise in warm water helps to maintain movement, develop muscle strength, improve balance, aid post-operative recovery, lessen pain sensitivity, improve blood flow and circulation and helps to develop a sense of wellbeing. Exercising as part of a group helps to develop friendships. Our physios offer a great deal of support and encouragement. **Seated Pilates** Seated Pilates are also offered, and are an excellent addition to hydrotherapy sessions, especially for people with musculoskeletal problems. **Becoming a member** Adults aged over eighteen are eligible for membership. The group is committed to operating digitally wherever possible, and uses a club management system called Coacha for holding membership and class records. **[Sign Up at Coacha Click Here](https://hosted-uk.coacha.app/member_signup/U00SEDRAI1)** f you would like to join Richmond AquaPhysio Group, please register your interest on Coacha using the following link. **You can also call us or email at us at:** 0208 580 0810 chair@rapg.org.uk

name: Community Choir
description: The Musical Director **[Julian Collings](https://www.teddingtonchoral.co.uk/professional-staff/)** was appointed to take over in 2019. Over the last few years the choir has enjoyed a growing reputation for their repertoire of outstanding modern music alongside the established classic music. **[Phil Culling](https://www.teddingtonchoral.co.uk/teddingtonchoir/assets/documents/accompanist-phil)** is the exceptional accompanist. TCS currently has around 110 members. New singers are very welcome for 'taster sessions', particularly male voices and those who are altos wishing to sing tenor. Three main concerts are performed during the year. Workshops are a regular feature, as well as social evenings. TCS is thriving with past successes and inventive programmes. We like to rehearse and perform with our sense of humour switched on. Teddington Choral is friendly and is a great asset to the local Arts scene and the Community. Come and **_\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*_** Our next concert: **Anything goes!** Saturday July 11. At the landmark Arts Centre, Ferry road, Teddington TW11 9NN at 7:30pm (doors open a 6:45pm). As is tradition now, Teddington Choral Society will be performing a varied and engaging lighter summer concert. This year, the choir will be singing a medley of compositions from the 1950’s. From Ralph Vaughan Williams’s “Five Mystical Songs” to Frank Loesser’s Guys and Dolls, as well as Irving Berlin and Cole Porter medleys, the evening promises to be both an evocative and entertaining one. Teddington Choral Society will be joined by baritone Dominic Sedgwick and accompanied at the piano by Elspeth Wilkes. Do not be surprised if you find yourself singing along while enjoying cheerful and well known tunes! **Tickets**: £20 (under 16s free) through the Landmark Arts Centre: **Online**: [https://www.landmarkartscentre.org/](https://www.landmarkartscentre.org/) **Phone:** 020 89777558 **Information**: [www.teddingtonchoral.co.uk](http://www.teddingtonchoral.co.uk)
intro: Teddington Choral Society was founded in 1951 and performed under several famous conductors. Their repertoire covers a wide range of genres. name: Debt advice from StepChange
description: If you are stressed about being chased for money you owe, it is time to get some help. By getting debt advice you will find out what options you have for dealing with your debt. There may be more ways than you are aware of. The easiest way to get started is to use our [online debt advice service](https://www.stepchange.org/setting-expectations.aspx) - start anytime, day or night. We don’t judge you, we just want to help. **Getting debt advice does not affect your credit file.** Alternatively, you can contact us on [0800 138 1111](tel:+448001381111). Monday to Friday 8am to 8pm and Saturday 9am to 2pm. What support you can get ------------------------ StepChange can help you: * Understand your financial situation and create a budget * Get clear advice on your debt options * Set up a plan to repay your debts at an affordable rate * Explore solutions like debt relief orders (DROs), Individual Voluntary Arrangements (IVAs) or bankruptcy * Find ways to increase your income or reduce costs We’ll advise you of your recommended solution, and also inform you of other solutions that are appropriate to your circumstances. This may include debt solutions that we cannot provide for you and where this is the case, we’ll inform you of other sources of information and help. If you've been made redundant and want to find out about what to do and how to protect your finances, visit our [Redundancy and Debt webpage](https://www.stepchange.org/debt-info/redundancy-and-debt.aspx?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=redundancy-guide). Why choose StepChange --------------------- * Free and confidential service * Available online 24/7 * Flexible – start, pause and return when it suits you * You prefer online and telephone support * Regulated and trusted UK charity * No judgement or pressure

description: We are Kingston's only indoor bowls club and offer bowls 7 days a week. We have experienced and qualified coaches for beginners along with leagues matches and competitions for those that have bowled before. If it's your first time, all you need to do is make sure you wear flat soled shoes, we can provide all the equipment that is needed. Bowls is a great sport to try for team building exercises, staff outings, friends nights out. We have hosted wedding receptions, club presentation evenings, wakes and, of course, parties. **MEETING ROOM** As well as the lounge we also have a small meeting room that can seat up to 18 people, suitable for small clubs and societies for one-off meetings or on a regular basis. **ADDITIONAL** We also have a Pool table and dart board **SOCIAL BOWLS** We are introducing social bowls on a Friday and Saturday nights. Groups of up to 8 people can come and be given basic instructions on how to play and then left to have fun and enjoy a new found sport. Enquiries from people who have never played this before are very welcome.

name: King George Field Indoor Bowls Club
description: We are Kingston's only indoor bowls club and offer bowls 7 days a week. We have experienced and qualified coaches for beginners along with leagues matches and competitions for those that have bowled before. If it's your first time, all you need to do is make sure you wear flat soled shoes, we can provide all the equipment that is needed. Bowls is a great sport to try for team building exercises, staff outings, friends nights out. It's something different and those that have tried it, have loved it! **PARKING** We have a large car park and the K2 bus stops right outside. **FACILITIES** We have our own in-house caterers who can offer excellent meals and snacks, along with a fully stocked bar at club prices. **VENUE HIRE** We have a large lounge area that can seat about 80 people and is a great venue for hiring for that special function. We have hosted wedding receptions, club presentation evenings, wakes and, of course, parties. **MEETING ROOM** As well as the lounge we also have a small meeting room that can seat up to 18 people, suitable for small clubs and societies for one-off meetings or on a regular basis. **ADDITIONAL** We also have a Pool table and dart board **SOCIAL BOWLS** We are introducing social bowls on a Friday and Saturday nights. Groups of up to 8 people can come and be given basic instructions on how to play and then left to have fun and enjoy a new found sport. Enquiries from people who have never played this before are very welcome.

name: Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service
description: Clients facing the loss of their home are entitled to help from the moment they are informed that possession of their home is being sought by their landlord or mortgage lender. Advice can continue until there is a substantive possession hearing (i.e. the court makes an outright possession order, dismisses the possession claim or makes directions for the future conduct of the proceedings). It does not cover representation at court. HLPAS is a non-means tested service, which means no financial assessment is required. To be eligible for advice under HLPAS, a client is required to show written evidence that there is a risk of possession proceedings, loss of their home or an illegal eviction. This includes: * A letter or notice to quit from a landlord, where they have an informal licence or a lack of security of tenure. * A letter before action, or notice seeking possession (e.g. a Section 21 or Section 8 notice). * A letter from the court notifying the client that possession proceedings have been issued. * A record of events that shows there may be an illegal eviction. To request an appointment please call 020 8767 2777 or visit the [South West London Law Centres website](https://swllc.org/get-advice/housing/).

name: SeeAbility
description: **[Eye care](https://www.seeability.org/eye-care)** We provide life changing support and champion better eye care for people who have learning disabilities or who are autistic, many of whom have sight loss. organisation: Kingston Adult Education Kingston Adult Education We have our core delivery: ESOL, English, Maths, Digital, Vocational, Health & Fitness, Arts, Crafts, Languages, Writing, History and we have some wonderful new courses for you to turn your hand to. description: Come and try pickleball at Beverley Park in New Malden. Pickleball is a fun and sociable racket sport played with paddles and a lightweight ball on a smaller court. It is easy to learn and suitable for beginners as well as more experienced players. These friendly group sessions will introduce the fundamental skills of pickleball, including movement, footwork and game play, with personal guidance from an experienced coach. All abilities are welcome, so no previous experience is needed. Sessions begin on 12 and 14 October 2026 and take place: * Mondays, 11am–12pm * Wednesdays, 5–6pm New participants can enjoy a two-week free trial. Sessions cost £9 per person after the trial. Please wear comfortable sports clothing and suitable trainers, and bring a bottle of water. Paddles and balls will be provided.

It is easy to learn and suitable for beginners as well as more experienced players. These friendly group sessions will introduce the fundamental skills of pickleball, including movement, footwork and game play, with personal guidance from an experienced coach. All abilities are welcome, so no previous experience is needed. Sessions begin on 12 and 14 October 2026 and take place: * Mondays, 11am–12pm * Wednesdays, 5–6pm New participants can enjoy a two-week free trial. Sessions cost £9 per person after the trial. Please wear comfortable sports clothing and suitable trainers, and bring a bottle of water. Paddles and balls will be provided.
