name: Cocoon - Care After Care
description: We provide different kinds of assistance to care- experienced young adults to improve living conditions, support aspirations, reduce feelings of isolation, alleviate hardship and to navigate through everyday stresses and strains. Our amazing volunteers provide flexible short and long-term practical support. Whether it's help with filling in forms, decorating and DIY, dealing with housing issues or utility companies, accompanying to appointments or helping them to access to other support services - it is always done with kindness and care. ​We remove financial barriers to improve current circumstances and increase future opportunities. We don't want anything to stand in the way of their development, ambitions or enjoyment of life.

description: **[Have you ever thought about using your language skills and becoming a community interpreter?](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/kingston-adult-education/kingston-adult-education-course-directory?search_api_fulltext=Community+Interpreting)** ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Our accredited qualification courses provide a great introduction to the role of an interpreter as well as the skills and knowledge needed for the job. intro: Have you ever thought about using your language skills and becoming a community interpreter? Our accredited qualification courses provide a great introduction to the role of an interpreter as well as the skills and knowledge needed for the job.
organisation: Kingston Adult Education Kingston Adult Education We have our core delivery: ESOL, English, Maths, Digital, Vocational, Health & Fitness, Arts, Crafts, Languages, Writing, History and we have some wonderful new courses for you to turn your hand to. Why not try our new Jewellery Making Workshop and if you like it, join the new course. Along with new craft workshops and courses, we’ve also added new art courses and workshops: Why not enjoy Botanical Watercolours, Drawing & Painting Animals, Landscape Painting, Oil Painting or Mindful Art? Whether you're looking to meet new people, explore new interests, get a job, gain qualifications for your career or keep your mind and body active we have something for everyone. Along with our wonderful Tai Chi, Pilates, and Mindful Movement courses, why not try our new Journaling for Wellbeing to help build your resilience and improve your wellbeing? With both **online** and **in-person** classes available at locations across the borough, you can easily find a course that fits your needs. In addition, many of our courses are **free** as they are government funded or offered at reduced rates, and we provide discounts based on your circumstances, so please contact us to find out more. Enjoy your courses and being a part of our wonderful adult education community. description: Our efforts focus on building community support around food, celebrating our diverse culture, and improving the economic, social, and health outcomes for everyone. **What We Do** * **Central Network Hub**: Making nutritious food accessible and affordable for everyone in Kingston * **Training & Support**: KVA empowers local organisations with training in food safety, nutrition, and operational efficiency, alongside support in securing funding. * **Strategic Planning**: In partnership with local authorities, KVA community food are working towards improving health and wellbeing outcomes for residents and communities. * **Community Engagement**: Events like the Kingston Good Food Event bring together food groups to share ideas, celebrate successes, and plan for a more food-secure future. **Why It Matters** * As of 2024, **1 in 5 households in the UK** experienced food insecurity, with **families with children, disabled individuals, and those on low incomes** being most affected. * In Kingston upon Thames, local data suggests that **over 25% of households with children** have struggled to access sufficient food at some point during the year. * Nationally, **over 4 million children** live in households that have experienced food insecurity in the past month. These initiatives are vital; not only providing immediate relief but also working toward long-term, systemic change. Together, we are building a future where no one in our community goes hungry.
intro: The Good Food Group is dedicated to uniting community groups, organisations, and residents in Kingston to ensure that healthy, nutritious, and delicious food is available to all.

description: Singing for the Brain brings people affected by dementia together to sing a variety of songs they know and love, in a fun and friendly environment. name: Love to Sing
description:
Home Instead Wimbledon and Kingston are proud to be partnering with the British Gymnastics Foundation to bring you Love to Move. We are inviting older people to enjoy a sing a long session This benefits older people, including those with dementia and mild cognitive impairment, by enabling the left side and right side of the brain to process information separately. It helps to improve cognitive function, co-ordination and the ability to carry out daily activities more independently, It is also a great way to socialise! The sessions take place **every Friday** from **10:30-12pm** at the Quaker Centre - Kingston **Refreshments provided** To book your seat, please contact **Suzzie at Home Instead** on **020 8942 4137**

Singing for the Brain brings people affected by dementia together to sing a variety of songs they know and love, in a fun and friendly environment. Home Instead has been supporting the Alzheimer’s Society for many years, to bring this well attended activity to the borough. * Come and join in fun vocal warm-ups and sing a wide variety of familiar and new songs. * Express yourself, feel positive and make new friends. * Feel supported by our skilled, compassionate and experienced staff who are available to support you with anything you need. 100% of people who go along to Singing for the Brain sessions say they’ve improved their life in some way. Join us every Friday from 10.30am – 12 noon The Quaker Centre • Fairfield East • Kingston KT1 2PT Refreshments provided Attendance £5 per session To book your seat please contact Ellie at Home Instead on 020 8942 4137 or email s.speedy@wk.homeinstead.co.uk

name: Fighting With Pride
description: Support for the LGBTQ+ Armed Forces community --------------------------------------------- Fighting With Pride supports **LGBTQ+ veterans, serving Armed Forces personnel and their families** with their health and wellbeing. They provide information, support and community connection, and can help you find organisations and services that are appropriate for your needs. What help can I get? -------------------- Fighting With Pride can help you: * find appropriate health and wellbeing support * connect with organisations that provide specialist help * access information and advice relevant to the LGBTQ+ Armed Forces community * connect with other LGBTQ+ veterans and members of the Armed Forces community * find opportunities to meet others through events and community activities * understand what other support may be available to you. You can contact Fighting With Pride even if you're **not sure which service or organisation you need**. Find support ------------ Fighting With Pride provides information about organisations offering different types of support to the LGBTQ+ Armed Forces community. **[Click here to find LGBTQ+ veteran support services.](https://www.fightingwithpride.org.uk/support/get-support/)** Who can get support? -------------------- Support is available to **LGBTQ+ veterans, serving Armed Forces personnel and their families**. How do I ask for support? ------------------------- You can register with Fighting With Pride if you would like support, information or to connect with the community. **Phone:** 0203 981 3810 **Email:** [info@fightingwithpride.org.uk](mailto:info@fightingwithpride.org.uk) **[Click here to register with Fighting With Pride and request support.](https://www.fightingwithpride.org.uk/register-with-fwp/)**

name: Fighting With Pride
description: Support for the LGBTQ+ Armed Forces community --------------------------------------------- Fighting With Pride supports **LGBTQ+ veterans, serving Armed Forces personnel and their families** with their health and wellbeing. They provide information, support and community connection, and can help you find organisations and services that are appropriate for your needs. What help can I get? -------------------- Fighting With Pride can help you: * find appropriate health and wellbeing support * connect with organisations that provide specialist help * access information and advice relevant to the LGBTQ+ Armed Forces community * connect with other LGBTQ+ veterans and members of the Armed Forces community * find opportunities to meet others through events and community activities * understand what other support may be available to you. You can contact Fighting With Pride even if you're **not sure which service or organisation you need**. Find support ------------ Fighting With Pride provides information about organisations offering different types of support to the LGBTQ+ Armed Forces community. **[Click here to find LGBTQ+ veteran support services.](https://www.fightingwithpride.org.uk/support/get-support/)** Who can get support? -------------------- Support is available to **LGBTQ+ veterans, serving Armed Forces personnel and their families**. How do I ask for support? ------------------------- You can register with Fighting With Pride if you would like support, information or to connect with the community. **Phone:** 0203 981 3810 **Email:** [info@fightingwithpride.org.uk](mailto:info@fightingwithpride.org.uk) **[Click here to register with Fighting With Pride and request support.](https://www.fightingwithpride.org.uk/register-with-fwp/)**

name: Health Visiting
description: If at any time during your child's first 5 years you have concerns around behaviour, development, feeding or anything that is causing you anxiety, the **[Health Visiting service](http://www.yourhealthcare.org/services/health-visiting/)** is here to help. To get in contact with the service call 020 8339 8000 or email [hvadminhub@yourhealthcare.org](hvadminhub@yourhealthcare.org) **Mental Health Support - Monday Mums:** Monday Mums is a peer support group for mothers experiencing low mood and/or anxiety. The group runs for 6 weeks on Mondays from 10am to 12pm, alternating between Tolworth Children’s Centre and Old Malden Children’s Centre. You can be referred onto this group by Health Visitors, ICOPE, Perinatal Mental Health Team and GP’s or you self refer. E-mail us if you think you would benefit from this group. **Infant Feeding Support** Pop along to a drop-in on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday or speak to your Midwife /Health Visitor/Nursery nurse regarding a referral for more specialist 1-1 support. Please visit the [Infant Feeding Support page](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/infant-feeding) for further information. **Introduction to Solids & Play Development** For advice and support when your baby is ready to move on from milk alone and what to expect when your baby reaches 6 months. Monday’s and Friday’s at 1pm at Children’s Centres. [Book Intro to Solids & Play & Development](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSe0kMQNb6gYC3URzIhH5tka_0Wti7e0mlR5ggU3IPgHClfxdQ/viewform). **Antenatal Groups** We offer antenatal support from 28 weeks of your pregnancy. Contact your Health Visitor or [book your free place on the antenatal groups online](https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/418877442707). **Postnatal Groups** Postnatal group for mothers with babies under 12 weeks. These sessions are run over 4 weeks and are undertaken within the children centres and include: * bonding and attachment, * Emotional Wellbeing/Baby Massage Taster * Crying/Sleeping and * Communication/Play. Please speak to your Health Visitor to book your place. **[Well Baby Clinic](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/well-baby-clinic)** General health clinic open to families with children under the age of 4. Drop in clinics available. **Support for young mums - Babettes Young Mums Antenatal Group:** For mum's to be, under 24 years old, please come along to our antenatal group, which runs: Fridays 1.30-3pm for 6 weeks every half term at The Hub, 38 Surbiton Road, KT1 2JR. This group is to support you in your pregnancy - learn about signs of labour, when to call the hospital, labour and pain relief, as well as feeding baby, bringing baby home, attachment, what to expect in the early days and contraception. For further information contact the Health Visitors via email. **Babes Young Mums Postnatal Group:** For mum's aged under 24 years, please come along to our drop-in postnatal group offering health advice and support with housing and benefits. This runs: Every Tuesday 1.30-3.30pm at The Hub, 38 Surbiton Road, KT1 2LR. For further information email the Health Visitors. **MECSH - Home visiting for families** The Maternal Early Childhood Sustained Home Visiting programme is a structured program of home visiting for families. The programme provides professional support for you and your family as your baby grows and develops. It is available to families who meet the criteria. Contact your Health Visitor for more info.
intro: Health Visitors are all qualified nurses, who specialise in child development and health. They will be able to advise you during your pregnancy and on all aspects of development and health promotion until your child is 5 years old.

name: Online Qi Gong
description: **Korean Style Qi Gong – Awakening Energy, Restoring Balance** The Korean style of Qi Gong I teach is a deeply holistic practice designed to harmonise the body, mind, and spirit. Rooted in ancient Korean healing traditions, it combines slow, intentional movements with deep breathing, rhythmic tapping, and mindful awareness. Unlike some forms of Qi Gong that focus only on flow, this practice also works with clearing energy blockages, strengthening the core, and activating the three main energy centres known as the _Dahn Jons_. Through gentle yet powerful exercises, Korean Qi Gong awakens your natural healing ability, improves circulation, lowers stress, and restores inner balance. It’s a practice that meets you exactly where you are—whether you’re looking to release tension, improve mobility, boost vitality, or reconnect with your authentic self. This style is particularly effective for ageing well, regulating blood pressure, easing stiffness, and calming the nervous system. But it also goes deeper, helping you expand consciousness, awaken your inner strength, and connect to the wisdom already within you. It’s not just movement—it’s a moving meditation that transforms how you feel physically, emotionally, and spiritually.

description: **What we offer: ** * STI testing: for people who have mild or no STI symptoms, and would like to get themselves checked. * Free regular and emergency contraception by completing a simple, secure online consultation. **How it works:** * [Complete a short online consultation](https://www.shl.uk/) to get started. We'll ask you a few questions to find out what service you'd like to use and make sure it's right for you. * Orders are assessed the same day, usually within an hour. Receive your test kit or contraception quickly and discreetly. * Our clinical team will keep you up to date with the progress of your order or test results. When your results are ready, we'll send you a text or email.

description: Norbiton Community Fridge ------------------------- ### **Open: 10am - 2pm** Sunday/Monday/Tuesday/ Friday Open to everyone, the Norbiton Community Fridge (Old name: Surbiton Community Fridge) is a communal space where households can share food (fresh and ambient and frozen) that would have been otherwise wasted. It is a project run by Migrant Advocacy Service. The food is free to take, as they have been given to us freely by our contributing donors. Though donations are welcome, to support us with keeping the van running and lights on! We belong to the Neighbourly.com food brokering system as well as the Co-op Community Fridge Network. **All of this food is free of charge.** ………………………………….. Can't make it to our main centre? --------------------------------- **Come to one of our outreach locations:** \-> Monday - Methodist Church, Ewell Road, Surbiton _11am - 1pm_ \-> Tuesday - 29 The Keep, KT2 5UA _11am - 1pm_ \-> Wednesday - Kingston Quaker Centre _12 - 2pm_ \-> Thursday-Kingsnympton Youth &Community Centre _12:15-2pm_ \-> Friday - Old Malden Family Centre (start date tbd) ………………………………….. Full list of community fridge venues and further information can be found on our website, facebook page and [Good Food Group](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/community-lunches) page. ………………………………….. Want to Support us by volunteering? ----------------------------------- Our community fridge needs volunteers to help it run \-> Drivers to collect from local supermarkets; \-> Shop staff to sort, display and select goods for clients; \-> Backups for school holidays and to cover sickness. Are you ready to be a Food Hero? If so call Nadia on 07886 216619
intro: Fresh food and goods are available for free at your local Community Fridge in Norbiton and at various outreach centres.

description: Norbiton Community Fridge ------------------------- ### **Open: 10am - 2pm** Sunday/Monday/Tuesday/ Friday Open to everyone, the Norbiton Community Fridge (Old name: Surbiton Community Fridge) is a communal space where households can share food (fresh and ambient and frozen) that would have been otherwise wasted. Though donations are welcome, to support us with keeping the van running and lights on! We belong to the Neighbourly.com food brokering system as well as the Co-op Community Fridge Network. **All of this food is free of charge.** ………………………………….. Can't make it to our main centre? --------------------------------- **Come to one of our outreach locations:** \-> Monday - Methodist Church, Ewell Road, Surbiton _11am - 1pm_ \-> Tuesday - 29 The Keep, KT2 5UA _11am - 1pm_ \-> Wednesday - Kingston Quaker Centre _12 - 2pm_ \-> Thursday-Kingsnympton Youth &Community Centre _12:15-2pm_ \-> Friday - Old Malden Family Centre (start date tbd) ………………………………….. Full list of community fridge venues and further information can be found on our website, facebook page and [Good Food Group](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/community-lunches) page. ………………………………….. Want to Support us by volunteering? ----------------------------------- Our community fridge needs volunteers to help it run \-> Drivers to collect from local supermarkets; \-> Shop staff to sort, display and select goods for clients; \-> Backups for school holidays and to cover sickness. Are you ready to be a Food Hero? If so call Nadia on 07886 216619

name: Grow Baby Kingston
description: Growbaby provides good quality, new and second-hand, baby clothes and equipment (up to 5 years), completely free of charge, to anyone who needs it, regardless of their income, background, or faith. We accept baby clothes and equipment from anyone who chooses to donate; we simply ask that potential donors ensure that they are in excellent, clean condition. Growbaby is open for you to come and choose your clothes and equipment on Wednesdays between 10am and 2pm (last sign in at 1.30pm) at the Hub. You don’t have to make an appointment you can simply drop in. We don’t need a referral form for clothes and equipment, everyone is welcome regardless of income, faith or background. You can stay for a cup of tea, biscuit, and lunch too, we would love to get to know you. If you want to donate your clothes and equipment then please see the link on the website to check what we need at the moment and when is best to drop it off to the Hub. We do much more than give away clothes and equipment. We host antenatal classes for young parents in conjunction with the local health visiting team, run a young parents group called Babes and a course for those parenting children with sensory processing difficulties. For more information on how to access these groups, please contact us via the contact form, email or phone. At Christmas Growbaby also provides a link between the pupils and staff of Epsom College and various local agencies so that children across Kingston Borough receive a gift at Christmas. In December 2023 we were able to provide over 3000 gifts to children who may not have received much else.

name: The Sound Doctor: High Blood Pressure
description: This short course will help you understand more about hypertension or high blood pressure. High blood pressure doesn’t usually have symptoms, so you won’t know you’ve got it until you have a test. By following this short, video-based course you will learn: 1. What high blood pressure is and how it can affect you 2. Understand what causes high blood pressure and how you can lower it We've interviewed a wide range of experts who'll give you the information you need to take control. [Click here to access the course](https://tinyurl.com/2xguwtls). Films include: * What is hypertension? * How can it affect me? * What causes high blood pressure? * Getting a blood pressure test * How can I lower my blood pressure? Our mission at The Sound Doctor is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. description: This short course will help you understand more about hypertension or high blood pressure. High blood pressure doesn’t usually have symptoms, so you won’t know you’ve got it until you have a test. By following this short, video-based course you will learn: 1. What high blood pressure is and how it can affect you 2. Understand what causes high blood pressure and how you can lower it We've interviewed a wide range of experts who'll give you the information you need to take control. [Click here to access the course](https://tinyurl.com/2xguwtls). Films include: * What is hypertension? * How can it affect me? * What causes high blood pressure? * Getting a blood pressure test * How can I lower my blood pressure? Our mission at The Sound Doctor is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. description: It's important to make sure that you get all the help that you're entitled to. These pages give you information about the benefits you may be eligible for as well as practical support on how to apply for them. **What’s available? Understanding grants, benefits and changes to your allowance** * [entitledto](https://www.entitledto.co.uk/benefits-calculator/Intro/Home?cid=e4b6cf63-eba1-4f2f-ab0e-52889a94609c) can help you find out which welfare benefits you are eligible for * [Understanding universal credit](https://www.understandinguniversalcredit.gov.uk/employment-and-benefits-support/#lse) * [Migrant Advocacy Service](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/migrant-advocacy-service) can provide language-assisted advice and guidance * [Money talks](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/money-talks) from Citizens Advice Kingston can help you to budget and save money by switching energy or phone suppliers **How do I make a claim? Practical employment & benefits support** * [Jobcentre Plus](https://www.gov.uk/contact-jobcentre-plus) can support you to find employment and access benefits * [Moving from benefits to work](https://www.gov.uk/moving-from-benefits-to-work) advice and information * [Help to claim universal credit](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/help-to-claim-universal-credit) service from Citizens Advice Kingston can offer practical support right up to your first benefit payment * Kingston Centre for Independent Living (KCIL) offers information, advice, and support to people with disabilities, their families and/or carers * [Appealing a benefits decision](https://swllc.org/get-advice/benefits/) **Other useful links** **Financial abuse** is when someone might stop you from having control over your money as a way of trying to exert power over you. This is a crime. Find out more about [protecting yourself against financial abuse](https://www.moneyadviceservice.org.uk/en/articles/protecting-against-financial-abuse#things-to-consider). If you don’t have any savings and are facing an emergency cash shortfall, borrowing may feel like your only option. Take care when considering **borrowing money**, and read these [borrowing basics from the Money Advice Service](https://www.moneyadviceservice.org.uk/en/articles/borrowing-and-credit-basics). Financial difficulties can cause a lot of stress. If you are **feeling anxious or worried**, make sure to take steps to look after your mental health. name: Macular Society Kingston Support Group
description: **Peer support groups ** We currently have a mixture of groups meeting face to face and/or via our telephone conference calling system. Either way its a wonderful way for people affected by macular disease to make friends and grow in confidence. Our Kingston group meets on the second Tuesday each month: 10.30am – 12.30pm at the Rose Theatre. **Face to face support group in your local community** We have groups meeting in local venues all across the UK. To search for your local group visit our local group page: [Local support groups - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/support/support-group/local-groups/) Or contact your local regional manager detailed on our regions page: [Our regions - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/about/organisation/regions/) or call our groups admin team on 01264 560 259. **Telephone support groups** We have various groups meeting over the telephone. Also, due to the pandemic, some of our face to face groups are opting to meet via our telephone conference Calling system. In just an hour you’ll hear useful information, important updates and (most importantly) friendly voices. To find our more about these Calls, also please contact the groups admin team on 01264 560 259. **Working Age and Young People’s (WA&YP) support ** Our groups are for anyone over the age of 18. Younger people and people of working age often like to come together and share peer support and hear about Specific advice and information about welfare, benefits, employment and access to work. If you are looking for advice on any of these subjects please either Contact groups admin to find out if a group is meeting in your local area, or visit our Working Age and Young People support page: [Are you a young person or of working age? - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/support/wayp/) **Online condition-specific communities** Join an online community of people with the same type of macular disease as you. The society also has groups that are specific to particular types of macular disease. Online condition specific groups include: * Best disease group * Diabetic macular oedema group * Myopic macular degeneration group * Sorsby’s fundus dystrophy group * Punctate Inner Choroidopathy (PIC) group For more information see our online condition-specific communities page: [Online condition-specific groups - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/support/support-group/condition-specific-groups/) or contact Colin Daniels on colin.daniels@macularsociety.org.

name: Macular Society Kingston Support Group
description: **Peer support groups ** We currently have a mixture of groups meeting face to face and/or via our telephone conference calling system. Either way its a wonderful way for people affected by macular disease to make friends and grow in confidence. Our Kingston group meets on the second Tuesday each month: 10.30am – 12.30pm at the Rose Theatre. **Face to face support group in your local community** We have groups meeting in local venues all across the UK. To search for your local group visit our local group page: [Local support groups - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/support/support-group/local-groups/) Or contact your local regional manager detailed on our regions page: [Our regions - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/about/organisation/regions/) or call our groups admin team on 01264 560 259. **Telephone support groups** We have various groups meeting over the telephone. Also, due to the pandemic, some of our face to face groups are opting to meet via our telephone conference Calling system. In just an hour you’ll hear useful information, important updates and (most importantly) friendly voices. To find our more about these Calls, also please contact the groups admin team on 01264 560 259. **Working Age and Young People’s (WA&YP) support ** Our groups are for anyone over the age of 18. Younger people and people of working age often like to come together and share peer support and hear about Specific advice and information about welfare, benefits, employment and access to work. If you are looking for advice on any of these subjects please either Contact groups admin to find out if a group is meeting in your local area, or visit our Working Age and Young People support page: [Are you a young person or of working age? - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/support/wayp/) **Online condition-specific communities** Join an online community of people with the same type of macular disease as you. The society also has groups that are specific to particular types of macular disease. Online condition specific groups include: * Best disease group * Diabetic macular oedema group * Myopic macular degeneration group * Sorsby’s fundus dystrophy group * Punctate Inner Choroidopathy (PIC) group For more information see our online condition-specific communities page: [Online condition-specific groups - Macular Society](https://www.macularsociety.org/support/support-group/condition-specific-groups/) or contact Colin Daniels on colin.daniels@macularsociety.org.

description: **Please contact us on 020 8547 1552 or email** [info@kbscharity.org.uk](mailto:info@kingstonbereavementservice.org.uk) **for support.** **Please note that if you need a death certificate following a death in hospital, you need to contact the Bereavement Office at Kingston Hospital. Click [here](https://kingstonhospital.nhs.uk/department/bereavement-office/) for their details.** Our bereavement counselling is for adults, children and young people who live, work, study or are registered with a GP in Kingston upon Thames. The Adult Service is for those 18 and over and we offer free individual bereavement counselling for up to 10 sessions and group bereavement support groups facilitated by qualified counsellors. The Saying Goodbye Project is for children and young people and we offer 1:1 counselling and support and advice to parents/carers. We also provide specialist Bereavement Awareness Training and advice to other agencies, including schools and health care practitioners.

name: The Sound Doctor: Weight Management
description: You will learn: * How and why we gain weight * Be inspired to become healthier and more active * Learn some simple and effective ways to lose weight * Make the right choices about how you eat * Take control of your weight and achieve your personal targets Follow the link to our [free weight management course](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/courses/weight-management). The Sound Doctor provides nationally accredited, Qismet certified structured education courses. This course on weight management has been created to help you understand more about your weight and your health. There are three colourful modules, with lots of short and engaging films, and interactive Q and A’s.The films contain information from some of the UK’s leading national and international specialists .You can do the course in your own time, at your own speed, wherever you choose. Our mission at The Sound Doctor is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions! We bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs.

name: Mental Health & Money Advice
description: We’re here for anyone with a mental illness who is struggling with their money, as well as anyone whose financial problems are affecting their mental health. What does Mental Health and Money Advice do? -------------------------------------------- [Our website](https://mentalhealthandmoneyadvice.org/) provides free and impartial information, support and advice for anyone affected by mental health and money issues. That includes support for friends, families, carers and professionals working in the area. name: Good Boost - Joint Pain and Recovery Support
description: **What is Good Boost?** Good Boost is a gentle exercise programme that helps you move more and feel better. The exercises are made just for you, based on your health, how you feel, and what you can do. You can choose to exercise in the pool or on land. You will use a small, easy-to-use handheld computer (provided by the centre) that shows you what exercises to do. The exercises change as you improve, so they always stay right for you. The movements are slow and supportive, and can help with: * Back, shoulder, hip or knee pain * Building strength * Improving balance * Feeling fitter and more confident You go at your own pace, and support is always available if you need help. **Good Boost 8-Week Course** You'll enrol on one of our 8-week aqua or land courses. These provide weekly 45-minute group sessions led by a facilitator, in the pool or in the studio. **Good Boost Grab & Go Sessions** Alongside your 8-week course, you will have access to Grab & Go sessions where you can complete your exercise independently in the gym or in one of our existing pool sessions. You can continue to attend these sessions even after your 8-week course has ended. **How to Sign Up** To sign up for Good Boost, delivered in partnership with Places Leisure, a referral form must be completed. This can be completed either by yourself or by a health professional on your behalf. [https://secure.refer-all.net/referrals/PlacesLeisure/refer](https://secure.refer-all.net/referrals/PlacesLeisure/refer) Good Boost is accessed via a monthly membership. For £34.50 per month, access: \- No joining fee (usually £30) \- 8-weeks of facilitator-led Good Boost sessions in the pool or gym at Malden Centre \- Unlimited access to Good Boost Grab & Go sessions at the Malden Centre \- Access to gym, swimming and group exercise classes at all of our Leisure Centres in Kingston Borough\* \*Malden Centre, Tolworth Recreation Centre, Weir Archer Fitness and Athletic Centre

name: Good Boost - Joint Pain and Recovery Support
description: **What is Good Boost?** Good Boost is a gentle exercise programme that helps you move more and feel better. The exercises are made just for you, based on your health, how you feel, and what you can do. You can choose to exercise in the pool or on land. You will use a small, easy-to-use handheld computer (provided by the centre) that shows you what exercises to do. The exercises change as you improve, so they always stay right for you. The movements are slow and supportive, and can help with: * Back, shoulder, hip or knee pain * Building strength * Improving balance * Feeling fitter and more confident You go at your own pace, and support is always available if you need help. **Good Boost 8-Week Course** You'll enrol on one of our 8-week aqua or land courses. These provide weekly 45-minute group sessions led by a facilitator, in the pool or in the studio. **Good Boost Grab & Go Sessions** Alongside your 8-week course, you will have access to Grab & Go sessions where you can complete your exercise independently in the gym or in one of our existing pool sessions. You can continue to attend these sessions even after your 8-week course has ended. **How to Sign Up** To sign up for Good Boost, delivered in partnership with Places Leisure, a referral form must be completed. This can be completed either by yourself or by a health professional on your behalf. [https://secure.refer-all.net/referrals/PlacesLeisure/refer](https://secure.refer-all.net/referrals/PlacesLeisure/refer) Good Boost is accessed via a monthly membership. For £34.50 per month, access: \- No joining fee (usually £30) \- 8-weeks of facilitator-led Good Boost sessions in the pool or gym at Malden Centre \- Unlimited access to Good Boost Grab & Go sessions at the Malden Centre \- Access to gym, swimming and group exercise classes at all of our Leisure Centres in Kingston Borough\* \*Malden Centre, Tolworth Recreation Centre, Weir Archer Fitness and Athletic Centre

description: Long Ditton Cricket Club is launching a **brand new Under 11 Girls Cricket Team** and is inviting girls in **Years 4-6** to come along to some **FREE indoor taster sessions**. These sessions are designed for **beginners and first-timers**. No kit is needed, just trainers. All other equipment will be provided. Girls will be introduced to basic cricket skills and simple gameplay, with the emphasis firmly on: * having fun, * building confidence, and * trying something new. We'll be using a soft ball for all taster sessions and for our first season of matches, making it a sage and friendly introduction to the game. **FREE indoor taster sessions:** Sundays, 10-11am on 22 February and 22 March 2026 at The Gym at Southborough High School, Hook Road, Surbiton, KT6 5AS. **Interested?** Get in touch to book a place on email: juniors@longdittoncricketclub.com or text Kendrick Oliver (U11 Girls Manager) at 07940 568 449.

We maintain a focus on developing our junior sections from vibrant mixed Dynamos and Allstars all the way through to our U17 teams, and have 3 senior Teams; a First and Second team both playing competitive League Cricket and a Sunday team that plays friendlies at our ground every Sunday. We hold local events at the pavilion, including wedding anniversaries, birthdays, and fundraisers. In 2024 we opened our brand new practice Net facilities, thanks to an Elmbridge Council Grant and a generous private donor, which are state of the art and open to the public. We welcome players of all abilities, ages, gender and background, and look forward to meeting you all over the summer. Come and join us in our idyllic surroundings at Stokes Field. name: Aphasia Support
description: **Our support is long-term, for as long as people need it. ** Having so many years of experience, in leading groups for people with stroke acquired aphasia, we know that people have different needs at different stages of recovery. Unlike many other long-term UK aphasia providers, we have tailored our services to reflect the different needs of people and their families at the different stages of recovery. Our services are specialist led by Speech and Language Therapists (SLTs). Dyscover’s services are a structured group set-up, which identifies and then develops skills for purposeful conversation/ functional communication. Our groups are between 8-20 people, led by an SLT and supported by a fixed and regular team of volunteers. Our in-person groups will run for 2.5hrs per session and our online groups for 1.5hrs. These sessions run every week across three terms a year (40/52 weeks). Each weekly conversation group costs between £15-£20. In addition we ask for an annual £20 membership subscription. We would not want anyone to miss out on support due to the financial challenges this may pose so ask that you let us know if this might be a problem.

description: If you are expecting a baby the information on this page can help you to find out what services are available to you. **Speak to your midwife** about online courses or face to face support they can offer you before and after giving birth. **[NCT antenatal courses](https://bumpandbabyclub.com/antenatal-classes/kingston):** Practical baby care courses. There is a charge however discounts are available if you are claiming benefits or have a low income. **[WelCare Kingston PlayPlus:](https://www.kingstonwelcare.org.uk/playplus)** The PlayPlus Project helps mums to manage postnatal depression by bringing mothers and babies/toddlers together to enjoy sensory play sessions. **[Antenatal infant feeding](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/infant-feeding)** classes. **Join your [local Children’s Centre](https://kr.afcinfo.org.uk/pages/community-information/information-and-advice/children-centres/children-s-centres-in-kingston)** where all families with children under 5 years, expectant mothers and fathers, can go to help their children to get the best start in life. If you haven’t visited one of our Centres in the past or you are an expectant or new parent complete an [online registration form](https://afc-self.achieveservice.com/service/family_hubs_registration). Join **[Kingston Baby Talk](https://www.babytalk.uk/kingstonuponthames)** to find out what’s happening near you or online. If you are pregnant and receive benefits or are under 18 you could be eligible for **[Healthy Start Vouchers](https://kr.afcinfo.org.uk/pages/community-information/information-and-advice/get-help-to-buy-food-and-milk-at-children-s-centres-healthy-start)**. With Healthy Start, you get free vouchers every week to spend on milk, fresh, frozen, and tinned fruit and vegetables, fresh, dried, and tinned pulses, and infant formula milk. You can also get free vitamins. **[Sure Start Maternity Grant](https://www.gov.uk/sure-start-maternity-grant)** is a one-off payment you might get to help with the cost of baby things if you are getting certain benefits or tax credits. Find out what other maternity and paternity benefits and leave you may be eligible for on the **[NHS website](https://www.nhs.uk/pregnancy/finding-out/maternity-and-paternity-benefits-and-leave/)**. **Talk to your [health visitor](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/health-visiting).** From 28 weeks of pregnancy, you will be sent a letter offering you an antenatal appointment with a Health Visitor should you wish one. The letter also offers an online antenatal class which is free to join. The Health Visitor will discuss many aspects of pregnancy, parenthood, and health and wellbeing with you and can answer questions if you have any concerns. If you've not heard from your health visitor and you think you should have, please contact 020 8339 8000.

name: Chair and Gentle Yoga
description: If you are older, have an injury or health condition, or maybe you just find it challenging to get up and down from the floor, regular yoga classes can feel out of reach. That’s where Gentle and Chair Yoga comes in. This unique class combines gentle mat work with chair-based poses, allowing you to choose the level of movement that suits your body on any given day. Based on the Yoga4Health framework, developed by leading yoga professionals in partnership with the NHS, this class is designed to safely improve your strength, mobility, and wellbeing. **Why Yoga4Health?** -------------------- Yoga4Health is an evidence-based, NHS-approved model that uses yoga to support physical and mental health in accessible, therapeutic ways. It’s especially recommended for people managing long-term health conditions or mobility challenges. The program focuses on: Gentle movement tailored to individual ability Breathwork to reduce stress and enhance relaxation Mindfulness and guided meditation for mental clarity Improved balance and coordination to reduce the risk of falls Blending chair and mat practice creates a totally inclusive experience where you move at your own pace and can see how much progress you are making.

organisation: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). _relatedProvenance: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). name: Chair and Gentle Yoga
description: If you are older, have an injury or health condition, or maybe you just find it challenging to get up and down from the floor, regular yoga classes can feel out of reach. That’s where Gentle and Chair Yoga comes in. This unique class combines gentle mat work with chair-based poses, allowing you to choose the level of movement that suits your body on any given day. Based on the Yoga4Health framework, developed by leading yoga professionals in partnership with the NHS, this class is designed to safely improve your strength, mobility, and wellbeing. **Why Yoga4Health?** -------------------- Yoga4Health is an evidence-based, NHS-approved model that uses yoga to support physical and mental health in accessible, therapeutic ways. It’s especially recommended for people managing long-term health conditions or mobility challenges. The program focuses on: Gentle movement tailored to individual ability Breathwork to reduce stress and enhance relaxation Mindfulness and guided meditation for mental clarity Improved balance and coordination to reduce the risk of falls Blending chair and mat practice creates a totally inclusive experience where you move at your own pace and can see how much progress you are making.

description: We are the local Kingston group of the [London Cycling Campaign](http://www.lcc.org.uk/), promoting cycling in the borough and speaking up for everyone on bikes – children as well as adults. ### We promote cycling by: * Liaising with the [Kingston Council](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/cycling) and [TfL](https://tfl.gov.uk/modes/cycling/) on the provision of local cycling facilities, lanes, paths and routes including the [Mini Holland](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/mini-holland-3/) schemes * Campaigning to persuade the borough and Transport for London to improve cycling facilities * Organising a varied programme of [bike rides](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/category/rides-and-outings/) for all experience levels and ages, from family-friendly routes to more challenging cycling adventures * Leading a ride to and from the annual summer RideLondon [FreeCycle](https://kingstoncyclecampaign.wordpress.com/2018/07/24/ridelondon-freecycle/) event in central London as well as the annual [Women’s Freedom Ride](https://lcc.org.uk/campaigns/womens-freedom/) * Supporting London Cycling Campaign’s [Cycle Buddies scheme](https://lcc.org.uk/groups/cycle-buddies/), a free service which connects new and experienced cyclists in the same area to help build confidence and be introduced to new routes * Providing [local cycling information](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/local-information/) for members, including [‘Get Cycling’](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/contact-us/), downloadable maps and directions for traffic-free and quiet rides * Providing personal cycle route guides – [request yours here](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/contact-us/) Find out about London Cycling Campaign [membership](https://membership.lcc.org.uk/join-lcc) options and, in addition to helping make London safer and more enjoyable for everyone, you’ll receive a host of [benefits](https://lcc.org.uk/membership/), from cycling insurance and legal advice to discounts in local shops.

description: We are the local Kingston group of the [London Cycling Campaign](http://www.lcc.org.uk/), promoting cycling in the borough and speaking up for everyone on bikes – children as well as adults. ### We promote cycling by: * Liaising with the [Kingston Council](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/cycling) and [TfL](https://tfl.gov.uk/modes/cycling/) on the provision of local cycling facilities, lanes, paths and routes including the [Mini Holland](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/mini-holland-3/) schemes * Campaigning to persuade the borough and Transport for London to improve cycling facilities * Organising a varied programme of [bike rides](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/category/rides-and-outings/) for all experience levels and ages, from family-friendly routes to more challenging cycling adventures * Leading a ride to and from the annual summer RideLondon [FreeCycle](https://kingstoncyclecampaign.wordpress.com/2018/07/24/ridelondon-freecycle/) event in central London as well as the annual [Women’s Freedom Ride](https://lcc.org.uk/campaigns/womens-freedom/) * Supporting London Cycling Campaign’s [Cycle Buddies scheme](https://lcc.org.uk/groups/cycle-buddies/), a free service which connects new and experienced cyclists in the same area to help build confidence and be introduced to new routes * Providing [local cycling information](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/local-information/) for members, including [‘Get Cycling’](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/contact-us/), downloadable maps and directions for traffic-free and quiet rides * Providing personal cycle route guides – [request yours here](https://kingstoncycling.org.uk/contact-us/) Find out about London Cycling Campaign [membership](https://membership.lcc.org.uk/join-lcc) options and, in addition to helping make London safer and more enjoyable for everyone, you’ll receive a host of [benefits](https://lcc.org.uk/membership/), from cycling insurance and legal advice to discounts in local shops.

description: ### **Football For All – Disability Football (Just Play / Learn to Play)** This is an inclusive FA Just Play disability football session for players aged 16+, open to both males and females, delivered as part of our Football For All programme by Motspur Park Community FC. Sessions are led by **FA-qualified coaches** and run weekly, providing a welcoming and supportive environment for players of all abilities. The focus is on enjoyment, confidence, and being part of a football community, with opportunities to develop skills at your own pace. As part of this programme, we currently have three adult teams competing at different ability levels in the Surrey Football For All League. For players who wish to progress, there are pathways into training and team football, but there is no pressure to do so — participation and enjoyment always come first. **This session is free to attend.** Selecting this item registers an **expression of interest only** and helps us manage numbers and ensure sessions remain safe, inclusive, and well supported.

name: Malden Lime Grove Bowling Club
description: About us ======== The Malden Lime Grove Bowling Club offers a clubhouse with changing rooms (no showers) and limited on-site parking. We have a large selection of bowls for beginners to try out until they find the right size for themselves. Coaching is also available for beginners. What we have to offer --------------------- * Coaching * Changing facilities with lockers * Off-street parking * Different levels of bowling skills * Opportunity to play in competitions * Good social environment * Quiz nights ### How the club is run As a private members' club, it is run by the members for the members. Committees are comprised of members who have been chosen by all the membership at the Annual General Meeting for a minimum of one year. All the tasks within the club are carried out by the members so that costs can be kept down, it's especially valuable where members have skills that they are happy to share for the running and maintaining of the club. **The maintenance of the green is carried out professionally by a contracted green-keeper.** Why not give us a call to arrange a visit and let us take you round and show you what we have to offer?

description: About us ======== The Malden Lime Grove Bowling Club offers a clubhouse with changing rooms (no showers) and limited on-site parking. We have a large selection of bowls for beginners to try out until they find the right size for themselves. Coaching is also available for beginners. What we have to offer --------------------- * Coaching * Changing facilities with lockers * Off-street parking * Different levels of bowling skills * Opportunity to play in competitions * Good social environment * Quiz nights ### How the club is run As a private members' club, it is run by the members for the members. Committees are comprised of members who have been chosen by all the membership at the Annual General Meeting for a minimum of one year. All the tasks within the club are carried out by the members so that costs can be kept down, it's especially valuable where members have skills that they are happy to share for the running and maintaining of the club. **The maintenance of the green is carried out professionally by a contracted green-keeper.** Why not give us a call to arrange a visit and let us take you round and show you what we have to offer?

name: Connect To Work- Kingston & Sutton
description: If you’re already employed but worried about losing your job, Connect to Work can provide tailored support to help you keep your role and progress in your career. Our approach is based on the proven IPS (Individual Supported Employment) model: **place, train and maintain**. You may be eligible if you: * Are aged 18 or over and live in either the London boroughs of Kingston or Sutton * Are not currently on another DWP-funded programme. * Are unemployed, or employed but at risk of losing your job (after 3+ months in your role, excluding zero-hour contracts). * Have a health condition or disability or face significant barriers to work. * **_We also welcome referrals_** **_from:_** * Carers and ex-carers. * People with experience of the criminal justice system. * Homeless individuals. * Former members of the Armed Forces and their partners. * People affected by substance dependency. * Care leavers and care-experienced young people. * Refugees and those on resettlement schemes. * Survivors of domestic abuse or modern slavery. * Young people at risk of serious violence. This means we work with you to: \*Understand your skills and aspirations through vocational profiling. \*Connect you with employers who value diversity and inclusion. \*Provide personalised training and ongoing support once you start work. We also offer guidance for employers and self-employment options where appropriate. As a Connect to Work participant, you’ll have a dedicated Employment Specialist to guide you every step of the way. Support includes: \*A personalised action plan and vocational profiling. \*Access to a wide network of employers \*Health-related interventions. \*CV and cover letter support. \*Interview preparation and mock interviews.\*Better-off calculations. \*Skills assessments via the National Careers Service. \*Travel planning. \*Ongoing in-work support and career development.
intro: Connect to Work is a voluntary programme funded by the UK Government, designed to help Kingston and Sutton residents overcome barriers to employment. Whether you’re living with a disability, managing a health condition, or facing complex challenges, we’re here to support you into work – and help you

We support carers of all ages. We are also committed to giving carers a stronger voice. We make sure their experiences, views and needs are heard across the borough so that local services, health and social care provision and community support reflect the real lives of carers. **Our services include:** * Advice and Advocacy for unpaid carers (see more below) * Peer support groups for carers including carers of people with dementia * Wellbeing activities * Carers' Assessments on behalf of Kingston's Adult Social Care * Counselling and emotional support * Discounted complementary therapies * Young Carers Project for carers aged 5-18 including: respite activities; weekly youth groups; mentoring; advice and advocacy; and targeted support. **We can offer advice and advocacy on:** * Welfare benefits and other entitlements * Lasting Powers of Attorney * Health and social care services * Being involved in the planning of patient care and preparation for discharge * Carers’ rights Any unpaid carer supporting someone in the borough of Kingston can access our services. **Getting in touch** Complete our referral form here: [https://www.kingstoncarers.org.uk/adult-carers/making-a-referral/](https://www.kingstoncarers.org.uk/adult-carers/making-a-referral/). (We prioritise cases by need, please include any urgent deadlines otherwise it will be 3 -4 weeks) **If you are already registered,** you can email [admin@kingstoncarers.org.uk](mailto:admin@kingstoncarers.org.uk). name: Maggie's
description: We’re here for everyone with cancer and all the people who love them. We support people whatever type of cancer they have, and whatever stage they’re at. All our support is free, and you don’t need an appointment or referral. There’s also no time limit on our support; we’re here for as long as you need us. Maggie’s isn’t part of the NHS, but we work alongside it to offer expert support. Our centres sit in the grounds of cancer treatment centres, and we have excellent relationships with our NHS colleagues. Many of our staff are NHS-trained, and all our Cancer Support Specialists have extensive experience and expert knowledge about cancer and its treatment. Our workshops, courses, one-to-one and group support help people change the way they live with cancer. Every Maggie’s centre is a welcoming space where you can find support with money worries, tips on managing stress, and a friendly place to go when you need someone to listen. Our support is shown to improve physical and emotional wellbeing and to help people take control when cancer turns life upside down. Understanding everyone's individual circumstances is central to what we do. It means we can guide people to the support that will make the most difference to them. We evaluate our support regularly and use research and external reviews to improve it. We work with world-leading architects to design our centres because we know that light, colour, and a connection to nature can help people feel better. We thoughtfully design each Maggie’s to be calming and welcoming; a place to escape from the clinical environment of the hospital. There are no reception desks and no clocks; instead, we have comfy sofas and plenty of time. Our centres have large open spaces for group activities and a kitchen table to chat to other people. We also make sure there are plenty of peaceful corners for quiet moments and a chance to gather your thoughts.

description: Pain Concern has created resources and created partnerships to support people living with pain, and their healthcare professionals. **Pain Concern provides guidance on:** * Understanding pain * Activity * Mood * Sleep * Medicines * Healthcare appointments * You can also find our award-winning, NICE-recognised resource for healthcare appointments: **[The Navigator Tool](https://painconcern.org.uk/the-navigator-tool/)** **Online Pain Education video** With the NHS, we have created an online video for anyone who has had pain for more than 12 weeks. It will give you a better understanding of your pain to help you manage it more effectively in the long term. * **[The Pain Education Session](https://painconcern.org.uk/pain-education-sessions-funding/)** **Free online mindfulness sessions** Pain Concern is delighted to offer a range of free online mindfulness sessions. Mindfulness doesn’t take the pain away, but it can change how we relate to it. Our sessions are led by a trained and accredited mindfulness teacher. Visit the website for dates for the mindfulness sessions and booking information. **HealthUnlocked** HealthUnlocked is an online support network for patient groups. It aims to gather the knowledge and experience of patients to share it with a wider patient audience, as well as providing information to health professionals about patients’ views and experiences. Connect with others living with pain at: [https://painconcern.org.uk/forum/](https://painconcern.org.uk/forum/) **Helpline** Our trained, confidential and compassionate helpliners provide information and support to people living with pain. Contact us at any time. Just leave a message with your name and phone number and we will get back to you as soon as we can – usually on the next working day. ☎ **[0300 123 0789](tel:03001230789)** ✉ **[help@painconcern.org.uk](mailto:help@painconcern.org.uk)** **Please note that we are not a crisis line.** If you need immediate help call: Samaritans - call 116 123 (free, 24/7); NHS 111- call 111 for 24-hour medical advice or visit 111.nhs.uk

name: HENRY - Healthy Start, Brighter Future
description: ### What is HENRY? The HENRY programme supports the whole family to gain the confidence, knowledge and skills they need to help the whole family adopt a healthier, happier lifestyle and to give their children a great start in life. There is support for fussy eating, screen time, healthier teeth, sleep, getting active and healthy family eating behaviours. ### The HENRY programme aims to: * increase parents’ knowledge and skills in healthy eating and understanding of the benefits of physical exercise * improve parenting confidence (belief in their own skills as a parent) and healthy behaviours (healthy eating, screen time, sleep and activity) * promote emotional wellbeing to support families to develop healthy lifestyle habits, including in relation to food, activity and daily routines We offer free 8 week group programmes and individual one-off workshops. They are delivered online or face to face. ### How is the service run? The programme is delivered by health visitors and school health, who have been trained in the HENRY approach. For the group programme, parents and children attend weekly sessions over an eight week period online or at a children’s centre. The workshops are delivered online or at a children’s centre. ### Upcoming HENRY Workshops and Programmes **For children aged 0-5:** **Healthy Families Right from The Start, 8-week Programme** Online: Tuesday 8th September to Tuesday 27th October 2026, 10am - 11:15am (every Tuesday). Face to Face: Thursday 1st October to Thursday 26th November 2026, Tolworth Children's Centre, 09:30am-12:00pm (every Thursday). name: HENRY - Healthy Start, Brighter Future
description: ### What is HENRY? The HENRY programme supports the whole family to gain the confidence, knowledge and skills they need to help the whole family adopt a healthier, happier lifestyle and to give their children a great start in life. There is support for fussy eating, screen time, healthier teeth, sleep, getting active and healthy family eating behaviours. ### The HENRY programme aims to: * increase parents’ knowledge and skills in healthy eating and understanding of the benefits of physical exercise * improve parenting confidence (belief in their own skills as a parent) and healthy behaviours (healthy eating, screen time, sleep and activity) * promote emotional wellbeing to support families to develop healthy lifestyle habits, including in relation to food, activity and daily routines We offer free 8 week group programmes and individual one-off workshops. They are delivered online or face to face. ### How is the service run? The programme is delivered by health visitors and school health, who have been trained in the HENRY approach. For the group programme, parents and children attend weekly sessions over an eight week period online or at a children’s centre. name: Macmillan Information & Support Service
description: This service is a joint venture between Macmillan Cancer Support and Kingston Hospital. We want to ensure that if you are affected by cancer, you have access to comprehensive, expert information and support. Our service is staffed by a health professional and trained volunteers, some of whom have experience of living with cancer. We can help anyone – patients, their relatives, friends and carers – with concerns about cancer. **Our information and support** When you visit our information centre, you’ll be greeted either by our manager or a trained volunteer. You’ll find a range of information leaflets on all aspects of cancer. Some of our resources are available in different languages or a larger print. We also have a range of information for people with learning disabilities. **We run a range of different services and groups, including:** * **Wellbeing workshops** on topics such as mindfulness and relaxation * **Look good feel better workshops** which are makeup and confidence building workshops * **Scarf tying workshops** where you can be taught how to tie scarves properly and a large selection are available to purchase * **Benefits and finance advice service** is a free and confidential service for people living with cancer, their families and carers * **Support groups** For more information, please contact us on 0208 973 5001 or email [khft.macinfoswru@nhs.net](mailto:khft.macinfoswru@nhs.net)

description: This coming January, don’t drag your tree to the tip. Let the Princess Alice Hospice Elves collect it right from your doorstep for recycling! Every tree collected is transformed into compost for local parks and gardens. More importantly, your donation helps provide compassionate, expert end-of-life care and bereavement support to local families when and where they need it most. Simply book your collection through our website, make a donation to Princess Alice Hospice, and we will collect your Christmas tree between 8th and 11th January 2027. 100% of the proceeds go directly to Princess Alice Hospice. In January 2026, Princess Alice Hospice collected more than 1,300 Christmas trees and was able to raise over £28,265 to support our patients and families. With your help, we can raise even more in 2027! Collection capacity is limited and available only in selected postcode areas, so be sure to register your interest today for early access to booking. Please note that collections are only available in eligible postcodes. Visit our website to check whether your area is included.

name: Swimming Lessons
description: **Overview** At AquaBubble Swim School, our mission is to provide high-quality, child-focused swimming lessons that go far beyond just learning strokes. We help children feel safe, confident, and empowered in the water — no matter their starting point — by creating a calm, nurturing space where they can learn at their own pace. Through patient guidance, playful learning, and lots of encouragement, we aim to help every child leave the pool not only a stronger swimmer, but a more confident version of themselves — equipped with life skills, resilience, and memories that last long after the lesson ends. **Our Purpose Built Location** All AquaBubble lessons take place in a custom-built, family-friendly pool designed specifically for young swimmers. With warm water, a calm environment, and thoughtful facilities, it’s the ideal space for building water confidence from the very first splash. We’ve chosen a location that’s safe, welcoming, and easy to access — with everything parents and children need for a smooth swim session. **Our Classes** At AquaBubble Swim Academy, we offer friendly, structured swimming lessons for children from 16 weeks old and up. Our programmes are designed to help swimmers gain water confidence, develop essential skills, and enjoy every splash along the way. All group lessons are 30 minutes long and priced equally. Our **Baby Bubbles** programme is perfect for introducing your baby or toddler to the water alongside you. These joyful, relaxed sessions are all about play, comfort, and connection — setting the stage for a lifelong love of swimming. **Little Swimmers** - These small-group classes are designed to gently transition your child into independent swimming. Through imaginative games and carefully guided techniques, they build confidence and skills — all without a grown-up in the water. **Super Swimmers** - Progressive Lessons for Every Young Swimmer. From first-time paddlers to future competitors, our staged swim programme helps children grow at their own pace. We group swimmers by confidence and ability — not just age — to ensure they thrive in the water. **Adult Lessons** - Whether you’re a total beginner, returning to swimming after years away, or looking to refine your technique, our adult sessions are tailored to you. These small group lessons offer a calm, encouraging environment to build skills and confidence at your own pace.

name: Learning Disability Service
description: We work with adults (18 years and older) with a learning disability who have a GP in the Richmond or Kingston Borough. Our team includes: Community Nursing, Dietetics, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Psychology, Psychiatry, Behaviour Analysis, and Speech and Language Therapy (including Dysphagia). ### **Our service** The learning disabilities team offers a range of assessments, interventions and advice for improving health and wellbeing including: * Communication * Behaviours which challenge * Dysphagia (swallowing difficulties) * Mobility / exercise / postural management * Health promotion * Participation and performance of occupations/ tasks/ activities of daily living * Diet management/ healthy lifestyles * Epilepsy * Audiology (hearing) * Significant emotional & relationship difficulties ### **Moving from children’s to adult services** Our learning disability service is for adults (18 years and over) who have a GP in Kingston or Richmond. We also support teenagers aged 16 years and over to move smoothly from the children’s service to the adult service. We understand that moving to adult healthcare services can be confusing and stressful when people reach 18. We hope to make this easier. Take a look at this leaflet for more information on the support that is available: [Adult Learning Disability Healthcare Transition](https://yourhealthcare.org/modules/downloads/download.php?file_name=214) ### **Contact us** You can call us by telephone: [020 8339 8005](http://tel:020%208339%208005/). Or email: [nds@yourhealthcare.org](mailto:nds@yourhealthcare.org)
intro: Sometimes it is not possible or appropriate for people with a learning disability to use mainstream health services and this is when specialist services, like ours, should be involved.

name: The Loss Foundation - Bereavement Support
description: Grief can be an isolating experience, and the power of conversation is invaluable. We believe in creating spaces where discussions around death are not taboo and providing a supportive community of individuals who have faced similar challenges. We provide a variety of support events to help people at any point during their loss to cancer, providing them with the chance to connect with others who share similar experiences. Our charity offers a variety of free grief support events, in-person and online. All our services are tailored to address the expressed needs of our users. * **[Support Groups](https://thelossfoundation.org/how-we-can-help/get-support/workshops/)** - Online bereavement groups for sharing stories and experiences. * **[Connect](https://thelossfoundation.org/how-we-can-help/get-support/speak-to-someone/)** - Matching together two individuals with a similar loss to share their experiences to form a mutually supportive, meaningful connection and friendship. * **[Therapy Groups](https://thelossfoundation.org/how-we-can-help/get-support/access-therapy/)** - 12-week bereavement therapy led by Clinical Psychologists. * **[Grief Workshops](https://thelossfoundation.org/how-we-can-help/get-support/workshops/)** - Focused sessions addressing common grief-related challenges. * **[Retreats](https://thelossfoundation.org/how-we-can-help/get-support/retreats/)**\- Weekend retreat combining therapy and peer support. * **[Walk and Talks](https://thelossfoundation.org/how-we-can-help/get-support/walkandtalks/)** - Our fastest growing service, our Walk and Talks take place throughout the UK - providing space for people to take steps through grief together. * **[Grief resources](https://thelossfoundation.org/grief-resources/)** - worksheets, meditation, videos and more to support people in managing grief. **_Please note that we are not a crisis service, so if you are in need of immediate support please do reach out to Samaritans who provide immediate listening support. They can be reached on 116 123._**
intro: We are a UK charity offering bereavement support for those affected by a loved one’s death from cancer.

description: Fulham Memories is a welcoming, healthy, inclusive, safe, and fun environment, allowing participants to train their bodies and minds, make new connections, whilst boosting their abilities to move and socialise. It’s a free weekly group session for older adults with reduced mobility. We can support those living with, or at risk of, the following: loneliness, dementia, or any other health issues.
