name: Drop-in Cafes
description: **Join us however you feel. No need to book** We provide low‑level support, promote social inclusion, and offer free tea, coffee and biscuits. **Wednesday ( The Bridge Cafe) 6:15-8:45 pm** Kingston WelCare 53-55 Canbury Park Road Kingston, Surrey, KT2 6LQ Find us [HERE](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Kingston+Welcare/@51.4133444,-0.2987079,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x48760be91e44b5b9:0x80f7d33c10ab3de5!8m2!3d51.4133411!4d-0.296133!16s%2Fg%2F1v3_24kz?entry=ttu) **Thursday (The Star Cafe) 7:00 -9:00 p.m.** Alfriston Day Centre 3 Berrylands Road Surbiton ,KT5 8RB Find us [HERE](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Alfriston+Outreach+Service/@51.3935801,-0.2998637,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x48760bcdcfd2a2c1:0x383c1b14dbcff725!8m2!3d51.3935801!4d-0.2972888!16s%2Fg%2F1tczdcqf?entry=ttu) We hope to run occasional film nights and workshops throughout the year, including arts, crafts and drama. We may also offer other activities and themed evenings from time to time. Please email us at [dropincafe@mindinkingston.org.uk](mailto:dropincafe@mindinkingston.org.uk) for further information. **Not sure this is the right service for you or want to find out more about our Drop-in cafes service? ** 📝 **[Complete the Services and Support Enquiry Form](https://forms.office.com/e/KDj05b51ru)** Your responses will help us understand your needs and connect you with the most suitable support. 📝If you need support completing the form, email us at [support.me@mindinkingston.org.uk](mailto:support.me@mindinkingston.org.uk) with the subject **“Call Back”** and one of our team will contact you. We aim to process all service enquiries within **5 working days**, and a team member will be in touch as soon as possible to discuss your needs and the next steps.

description: Support ------- If at any time during your child's first 5 years you have concerns around behaviour, development, feeding or anything that is causing you anxiety, the **[Health Visiting service](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/health-visiting)** is here to help. To get in contact with the service call 020 8339 8000 or email hvadminhub@yourhealthcare.org **Breastfeeding and Infant feeding support:** from Your Healthcare **[Sleep Workshops](https://kr.afcinfo.org.uk/pages/community-information/information-and-advice/children-centres/children-s-centres-in-kingston):** Understand more about sleep and how to establish a bedtime routine. Online workshops for parents of babies between 4 months to 3 years. Find out more by emailing [kingstonccs@achievingforchildren.org.uk](mailto:kingstonccs@achievingforchildren.org.uk) **Talk to Me**: For families with children under 2. Discover ways of encouraging the language and communication skills of your child. Email [communitylearningkae@kingston.gov.uk](mailto:communitylearningkae@kingston.gov.uk) to find out more. Please note there may be a charge for this course. **[Beyond Birth](https://www.beyondbirthlivinglibrary.org/peer-support)**: This programme is set up to help parents who have had unexpectedly difficult or challenging birth-related experiences and need support after leaving the postnatal ward or maternity care. **[HENRY:](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/henry-healthy-start-brighter-future)** support for families to provide the best start in life for babies and children Play sessions ------------- Join **[Kingston Baby Talk](https://www.kingstonbabytalk.co.uk/)** to find out what’s happening near you or online **[Stay and Play sessions](https://www.kingstonwelcare.org.uk/stay-and-play)**: Welcare, Tuesdays & Wednesdays: 9:30 AM - 11:00 AM. All Saints Church, Mondays & Thursdays: 10:00 AM - 11:30 AM **[Online interactive rhyme time](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSe1QaJZmebX7n63shZvD9OKbNeDhj72cnGMNQMpBAOErIZs1w/viewform)** every Monday and Wednesday with Kingston Children’s Centre. Lots of fun, action songs and rhymes for you and your children. **Online Toy Library**: where you can borrow toys for free to help keep your children occupied and engaged. For more information email [kingstonccs@achievingforchildren.org.uk](mailto:kingstonccs@achievingforchildren.org.uk) Children's Centres ------------------ [Kingston Town](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/kingston-town-childrens-centre) [Tolworth](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/tolworth-childrens-centre) [Old Malden](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/old-malden-childrens-centre) [Chessington](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/chessington-childrens-centre) Keeping active -------------- Mother & Baby Pilates: Suitable for all mums and babies aged from 6-8 weeks to pre-crawlers (after post-natal check). Email [communitylearningkae@kingston.gov.uk](mailto:communitylearningkae@kingston.gov.uk) to find out more. Please note there may be a charge for this course. Need some additional help ------------------------- **[Growbaby](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/growbaby-kingston)**: Growbaby provides formula, nappies, baby food, baby clothes and equipment (up to 5 years) **[Little Village HQ](https://littlevillagehq.org/get-help/)**: Provide free baby equipment. To receive support, you need to be referred by a professional, such as a midwife, health visitor, food bank or local mutual support groups. If you are pregnant and receive benefits or are under 18 you could be eligible for **[Healthy Start Vouchers](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/growbaby-kingston)**. With Healthy Start, you get free vouchers every week to spend on milk, fresh, frozen, and tinned fruit and vegetables, fresh, dried, and tinned pulses, and infant formula milk. You can also get free vitamins. **[Sure Start Maternity Grant](https://www.gov.uk/sure-start-maternity-grant)** is a one-off payment you might get to help with the cost of baby things if you are getting certain benefits or tax credits. Find out what other maternity and paternity benefits and leave you may be eligible for on the **[NHS website](https://www.nhs.uk/pregnancy/finding-out/maternity-and-paternity-benefits-and-leave/)**.

name: Feel Good Moves
description: Participants are welcome to be chair-based if they have mobility issues. The sessions include gentle stretching and movement. The key is to feel included, gain confidence, and meet others who are facing the same challenges, whilst moving and having fun. Visual impairment can be very isolating and we are seeing a big increase in macular-related eye conditions as our population ages. The class is every other Thursday at Emily's Studio 17A The High Street New Malden KT3 4BY. Upcoming dates are 24 September, 8 and 22 October, 12 and 26 November, 10 December. The class runs between 2.45 and 3.45pm. The first taster session is free and from then on we charge £5.
intro: We run an exercise class called Feel Good Moves. It is specifically for the visually impaired community in and around the Kingston area and most of the class is audio described by our fitness instructor, Marion. The class is a mixture of yoga, tai chi and very gentle martial arts.

name: Exploring London & Wednesday Walks
description: **Exploring London and Wednesday Walks - Exploring London with Dr Stephen Goss** Discover the drama, intrigue and secrets that surround different parts of London. These hugely popular historical walks provide a great opportunity to keep fit, make friends and learn more about London’s fascinating history. The _Exploring London_ courses consist of a talk about an area of London, which takes place at the Hook Centre, followed the week after by a guided tour of that area. The _Wednesday Walks - Exploring London_ course are weekly guided walks. These walks introduce you to some of the most popular parts of London. Each walk will be led by an academic historian who is an expert tour guide, who will show you the secrets of London. By the end of the course, you will have greater appreciation of popular London areas and will be able to revisit the places, with enhanced enjoyment, on your own or with friends.

name: The Sound Doctor: Diabetes
description: This series of films will help you understand more about diabetes - whether you've had the condition for a long time or been recently diagnosed. There’s masses of useful, practical advice about diet, activity, blood glucose monitoring and medicines you may be prescribed. Our aim is to help you avoid the complications of diabetes. We've interviewed a wide range of experts who'll give you the information you need to take control. We wish you the very best and do remember there's a lot you can do to make life easier. ### [Click here to access videos from the Diabetes Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/2blyr7pw), these cover: * Understanding Diabetes * Beginning to take control * Diet and Exercise * Staying in control * Medicines * Complications * Patient Stories You can also [take our free How to Live Well with Diabetes course](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/courses/diabetes). This course provides top quality advice and information in four modules, based around films. Easy to watch and understand, the course is engaging and effective. It will help you understand more about your condition and give you tips and techniques to help you live life to the full. Contributors include many of the UK’s leading diabetes specialists as well as expert patients. Our mission at The Sound Doctor is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs.

name: The Sound Doctor: Diabetes
description: This series of films will help you understand more about diabetes - whether you've had the condition for a long time or been recently diagnosed. There’s masses of useful, practical advice about diet, activity, blood glucose monitoring and medicines you may be prescribed. Our aim is to help you avoid the complications of diabetes. We've interviewed a wide range of experts who'll give you the information you need to take control. We wish you the very best and do remember there's a lot you can do to make life easier. ### [Click here to access videos from the Diabetes Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/2blyr7pw), these cover: * Understanding Diabetes * Beginning to take control * Diet and Exercise * Staying in control * Medicines * Complications * Patient Stories You can also [take our free How to Live Well with Diabetes course](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/courses/diabetes). This course provides top quality advice and information in four modules, based around films. Easy to watch and understand, the course is engaging and effective. It will help you understand more about your condition and give you tips and techniques to help you live life to the full. Contributors include many of the UK’s leading diabetes specialists as well as expert patients. Our mission at The Sound Doctor is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs.

name: Kingston Wellbeing Service Substance Misuse
description: If you are worried about your own or someone else's alcohol or drug use, we offer free, confidential advice, care and support for people in Kingston aged 18 and over. Coming into our service for the first time might seem difficult, but our friendly team will do their best to help you feel comfortable. You’ll meet with one of our support workers, talk about your concerns and make a plan together. **Our service includes:** * Assessment and personal recovery care plan developed with each individual * Advice and information on reducing harm * Specialist detoxification programmes to manage withdrawal symptoms and safely wean you off alcohol or drugs * Opioid Substitution prescribing * Naloxone issued * One-to-one and group therapies aimed at reaching the core of the problem, creating ways to deal with cravings and avoid repeating past mistakes * Motivation, support and advice from people with “lived experience” (those that have previously had problems with alcohol or drugs and who have successfully overcome them) * Group activities and social networks, e.g. men and women’s groups, relapse prevention and abstinence groups, life skills advice, mindfulness sessions, ear acupuncture and complementary therapies. Family and friends support group * Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Motivational Interviewing interventions * Physical health clinics and Blood Borne Virus testing * Joint working with employment agencies, training providers and housing associations to help you get back on track * Help and support for carers to help build sustainable recovery The path to recovery can be difficult but support is available. It’s never too early to ask for help and it’s never too late to start again. Getting treatment really can help you overcome life’s obstacles and allow you to develop a better relationship with yourself and others. Please complete a referral using the 'referral' button on this page. **We will get back to you within 3 days.**

name: Repair Cafe Kingston
description: Repair Café Kingston takes place on the **first Saturday morning of every month, 10.30am - 1.00pm,** in **Kingston Library's community room**, helping residents to save money and keep repairable stuff out of the waste system. * **Visitors** can bring all sorts of broken items to fix on the spot with the help of our volunteer repairers and refreshments while you wait, watch and learn. description: Counselling is sometimes called a 'talking therapy'. A counsellor aims to provide you with a safe, independent and confidential space where you can talk about your concerns, feel listened to, respected, understood and not feel judged. People of all ages and walks of life seek counselling. They find it can help them to cope or to deal with difficult emotions or situations. Carers may have particular concerns or difficulties associated with their caring role. Our counselling team are skilled in working with carers to maintain their health and wellbeing while addressing these difficulties. Please contact Helen, counselling@kingstoncarers.org.uk, for further information, or to raise any questions you may have.

name: Housing Crisis Intervention Service
description: We offer advice to people on housing and benefits, statutory rights and accessing health services. Our drop-in only Advice Service (the 'Housing Crisis Intervention Service') offers advice on: * Housing and benefits * Statutory rights * Accessing health services * Securing accommodation. KCAH prioritises those clients with a connection to Kingston upon Thames, in line with Homelessness Legislation. New clients should come to one of our **morning drop-in sessions which run Monday – Friday 10am to 12:30pm.** If you are coming for the first time please aim for 10am and it must be before midday (because it takes time to get you registered). Occasionally, we need to close the drop-in early when we have long queues in the waiting room or staff are unavailable due to training. It is always best to arrive early. Due to the high level of demand, we are unable to deal with enquiries over the phone or by email. Find out more about the registration process on [our website](https://kcah.org.uk/hcis-housing-crisis-intervention-service/), including eligibility information and what to expect on the day.

Occasionally, we need to close the drop-in early when we have long queues in the waiting room or staff are unavailable due to training. It is always best to arrive early. Due to the high level of demand, we are unable to deal with enquiries over the phone or by email. Find out more about the registration process on [our website](https://kcah.org.uk/hcis-housing-crisis-intervention-service/), including eligibility information and what to expect on the day.

description: Kingston Carers Network supports carers of all ages by offering clear advice, helpful information, and practical support. This includes help with understanding carers’ rights, benefits they may be entitled to, Lasting Powers of Attorney, and accessing health and social care services. We also have a dedicated Benefits and Tribunal Representative who can provide carers with detailed advice and support around a range of benefit-related issues including: * Supporting carers through each step of the benefits claims process * Checking what benefits someone might be eligible for * Help filling in claim forms * Preparing for and speaking on behalf of carers at appeal hearings We help with appeals on many issues, such as whether someone qualifies for a benefit, complicated calculations, or disagreements about disability and caring responsibilities. We gather evidence, write supporting documents, and attend tribunal hearings to represent carers. This support has helped many carers receive significant financial benefits.

description: Elmbridge Eagles is a Rugby League club for all ages, genders and abilities. Everyone is welcome. You can find out more about our Primaries, Junior Boys, Girls and Women, and Open Age / Masters programmes on our website, including specific training dates and how to register. ### **Wheelchair Rugby League at Elmbridge Eagles** If you saw the Storyville documentary about the rivalry between Great Britain and France at the end of 2023 you'll know that Wheelchair Rugby League can be just as tough and competitive a sport as its outdoor counterpart. Like its outdoor cousin, however, it can also be a recreational sport played for fun and a social experience. In fact Wheelchair Rugby League can justifiably claim to be the most inclusive team sport of all. Our Wheelchair Rugby League club is open to all genders from ages 16 to >60, and you don't need to be a wheelchair user to play. If you're interested, drop us an e-mail for more information. **To train and play you must be [registered with and insured by the RFL](https://membership.mygameday.app/regoform.cgi?aID=25834&pKey=dee904952cd85a8f3b5c7e6c5138419b&formID=100560&erMsg=1).** And if you haven't seen the [Storyville Documentary, we've linked to it on BBC iPlayer](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episode/m001r9zl/storyville-made-of-steel-wheelchair-rugbys-fiercest-rivalry). You must have a valid TV license to view it.

name: Togetherall
description: Togetherall offers a safe space for people to look after their mental wellbeing, particularly those who may be waiting for support, in between sessions, or are not ready to access face-to-face services. **Togetherall provides:** * **24/7 access to an anonymous peer-to-peer support community**, where people can share experiences and connect with others facing similar challenges * **Clinical moderation by trained mental health professionals**, ensuring a safe and supportive environment * **Self-guided tools, resources and courses** on topics such as anxiety, depression, stress, and sleep Togetherall is **accessible anytime, from any device,** making it a flexible and inclusive option for a wide range of individuals. **How to Signpost Someone to Togetherall** Referring someone to Togetherall is a quick and easy process. Simply direct them to: * **[togetherall.com/swlondon](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Ftogetherall.com%2Fswlondon&data=05%7C02%7Csue.doherty%40kva.org.uk%7Cd5d8e1e59aa8454d39ac08dde9551660%7C5bcd2573e8c446c8b9402046c9bc1785%7C0%7C0%7C638923273848751965%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=8nVqB7qYWnBL51%2FgllEhhS81wHdGnXIHbGJCNJ6ULj0%3D&reserved=0)** They can **register in minutes**, and get immediate access to support. Use this service in your conversations, signposting pathways, or local engagement work to help more people take a first step toward mental wellbeing. [Click here find out more about referring to Togetherall.](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftogetherall.com%2Fen-gb%2Freferswlondon%2F%3Futm_source%3DInternal%26utm_medium%3DStaffIntranet%26utm_campaign%3DSouthwestlondon&data=05%7C02%7Csue.doherty%40kva.org.uk%7Cd5d8e1e59aa8454d39ac08dde9551660%7C5bcd2573e8c446c8b9402046c9bc1785%7C0%7C0%7C638923273848792855%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Q3MNCzRvmFtZxLeh3kiT7CibeCOuo7xN8pb3OIEeIQw%3D&reserved=0)

name: Reduce your risk of falling at home
description: ### General falls and bone health resources [Get up and Go leaflet](https://www.csp.org.uk/publications/get-go-guide-staying-steady-english-version) for information on how to help people who have fallen or may be at risk of falling. [Getting up from a fall web page](https://www.nhsinform.scot/healthy-living/preventing-falls/dealing-with-a-fall/what-to-do-if-you-fall) for information on what to do if you have a fall. [Better Bones Service](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/better-bones-service) for talks on bone health. ### How to reduce your risk of falling at home Most falls happen in the home/garden but there are preventive measures you can take. See [NHS Inform](https://www.nhsinform.scot/healthy-living/preventing-falls/) for information on identifying fall hazards in the home. [RBK Occupational Therapy](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/living-well-home) can help if your home needs adapting with things such as grab rails and sensor lights. [AskSARA](https://www.kingston.gov.uk/living-well-home) gives impartial advice on equipment for the home. ### Eating well and preventing dehydration Eating healthily is important for your overall health and wellbeing and can help prevent falls. Eating regular, nutritious meals and drinking plenty of non-alcoholic fluids can help to avoid problems that can lead to a fall. See [NHS Inform](https://www.nhsinform.scot/healthy-living/preventing-falls/keeping-well/how-to-eat-well) for information on eating well. ### Looking after your vision and hearing Make sure you have regular hearing and eye tests. You qualify for **free** NHS eye tests at least once every two years if you are over 60 or receiving certain benefits. You may also be eligible for a free eye test at home if you can't get to an optician. [Royal National Institute for Deaf People (RNID)](https://rnid.org.uk/) has an online hearing check which will suggest if your hearing is in a normal range or if you may have hearing loss. Your GP can also arrange a hearing test. Information about the [RBK Sight and Hearing Service](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/sight-and-hearing-service) is available on Connected Kingston. Information about [Kingston's Association for the Blind (KAB)](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/kingston-association-for-the-blind-kab) service is also available on Connected Kingston. ### Manage Bladder and bowel conditions If you have a bladder or bowel condition that causes you to rush to the toilet, or visit more often during the day or night, you could be at an increased risk of falling. Continence problems, and the symptoms of bladder irritability, can often be improved with the correct treatment. Visit the [Continence team](https://yourhealthcare.org/services/continence-care/) webpage to find out how to be referred. ### Manage your medicines Some medicines can affect your balance and some react if taken together. Make sure your GP knows about all the medications you are taking, including non-prescription medication. Tell your GP if any of your medication is making you feel dizzy or unwell and ask your GP or pharmacist for a review of your medication every year. ### Look after your feet Look after your feet by trimming toenails, using a moisturiser, wearing well-fitting shoes and seeing a GP or podiatrist about any problems. Talk to your GP to see if you qualify for free NHS foot care services. Visit the [Podiatry Team website](https://yourhealthcare.org/services/podiatry/) for more information. ### Alcohol As you get older, the effects of alcohol increase. This can make you more unsteady on your feet than you used to be. If you’re on medication and choose to consume alcohol, be aware of the effects alcohol may have. [Via - Kingston Wellbeing Service](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/kingston-wellbeing-service-substance-misuse) can provide support and advice. See [Preventing Falls](https://connectedkingston.uk/services/preventing-falls) for more information.

description: **Always wanted to learn to paint?** ------------------------------------ **Now’s your chance.** ---------------------- ### Discover the joy of watercolour in a friendly, supportive class where you’ll learn new techniques, build confidence and enjoy the relaxing, mindful process of creating beautiful artwork. name: Mind Counselling Services
description: We particularly welcome people who are currently in employment, education or have caring responsibilities and are unable to access daytime counselling. We will offer up to 12 sessions (with a possibility for an extension if necessary). Each session will last 50 minutes and will take place on a weekly basis at a regular date and time at our Drop-in Cafe premises in Kingston. There is a fixed fee of £20 for your assessment. The fee for each session is between £15 and £35 depending on your financial circumstances. Fees will be discussed during your initial assessment appointment and will be means tested. The lower fees will only be available to people on benefits or very low income. **About our Counselling Service for the local Korean community** 본 카운슬링 서비스는 Mind in Kingston 의 카운슬링 서비스의 일환으로 한국어로 카운슬링을 받으실수 있습니다. 킹스턴과 그주변에 거주하시는 만18세 이상 한국인 분들에게 제공되는 성인 심리 정서 지원 및 마음 건강 회복을 위한 상담 서비스입니다. 이 서비스를 신청하시면 한국인 카운셀러에 의해 진행되며 내담자분의 편의에 따라 한국어 혹은 영어로 상담이 가능합니다. Our counselling service is coordinated by a fully qualified counsellor, who oversees intake and allocation of clients, recruitment of new counsellors, supervision of counsellors and the administration for the service. Counselling is a talking therapy which takes place in a safe and confidential setting. It allows individuals to explore their thoughts, feelings and behaviours and learn to manage those better. At Mind in Kingston, we believe that the counsellor's role is to work alongside individuals to help them discover alternative ways to improve their lives and resolve current and past issues. Our counsellors offer professional and confidential support to people who wish to enhance their quality of life. To access our counselling service, you can either be referred by a GP, the CMHT or a voluntary organisation, or you can contact us directly by completing our [Services and Support Enquiry Form](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=kPRGrLJKpUmS1ZIeGcA9LLp1W7rVX-dAvY236WVEz1pUQVdMTFRQM0NSNzY0TzNKTklGMkREQkZDWC4u&route=shorturl) and a member of our team will get back to you. You can also call us on 020 8255 3939 Once we receive your enquiry form submission, we will invite you for an assessment which will give you, and us, an opportunity to discuss your issues and decide if counselling is the best way forward. If you are referred for counselling, we will put you on our waiting list. The waiting time depends on the number of people requesting the service.

The fee for each session is between £15 and £35 depending on your financial circumstances. Fees will be discussed during your initial assessment appointment and will be means tested. The lower fees will only be available to people on benefits or very low income. **About our Counselling Service for the local Korean community** 본 카운슬링 서비스는 Mind in Kingston 의 카운슬링 서비스의 일환으로 한국어로 카운슬링을 받으실수 있습니다. 킹스턴과 그주변에 거주하시는 만18세 이상 한국인 분들에게 제공되는 성인 심리 정서 지원 및 마음 건강 회복을 위한 상담 서비스입니다. 이 서비스를 신청하시면 한국인 카운셀러에 의해 진행되며 내담자분의 편의에 따라 한국어 혹은 영어로 상담이 가능합니다. description: Social Tariff Broadband Support in Kingston ------------------------------------------- If you live in the Kingston area and currently receive government benefit support, you might be eligible to [switch to a cheaper broadband package](https://www.fasterbroadband.co.uk/social-broadband-tariffs). Social tariffs are discounted plans designed to make broadband and mobile services more affordable. **FasterBroadband** is an independent comparison service that hosts the UK’s largest free to use, not for profit social tariff comparison tool. It helps users find and compare discounted broadband deals available to people on low incomes, including tariffs from smaller, independent broadband providers. **The free service can also offer:** * Clear explanations of the difference between regular [broadband deals](https://www.fasterbroadband.co.uk/broadband-deals) and [social tariffs](https://www.fasterbroadband.co.uk/social-broadband-tariffs) * Guidance on how long you can stay on a social tariff * [Independent broadband reviews](https://www.fasterbroadband.co.uk/best-broadband-reviews) based on expert research, Ofcom data, Trustpilot feedback and user experiences * Help if you are already in a contract but struggling to keep up with payments * A free [broadband availability and speed checker](https://www.fasterbroadband.co.uk/tools/check-broadband-speeds-in-my-area) to see if full fibre is available at your address and what speeds are achievable in your street The website also includes built in accessibility features and a jargon help tool to support people who may find broadband terminology confusing or difficult to navigate. ### Eligibility criteria for social tariffs include: * Universal Credit * Pension Credit * Income Support * Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance (JSA) * Income-based Employment & Support Allowance (ESA) * Personal Independence Payment (PIP) * Attendance Allowance * Care leaver support or other local authority assistance

name: Community Library Service
description: The Community Library Service (CLS) provides a service for anyone who can't get to a library. This could be because of disability, frailty or caring responsibilities. Temporary membership is possible if someone is recovering from an illness, hospital admission or surgery. The CLS will visit people every month and we can bring normal print books, large print books, spoken word CDs or tapes, music CDs, DVDs, videos - and jigsaws. The team speak with the borrower to ensure what they bring matches people's interests and needs. The service can also visit care homes and sheltered housing to deliver to people or to leave items in common areas for all to enjoy. This service operates across Kingston, and staff can be contacted by phone or email. Volunteers with DBS checks will help to deliver the books.

name: Macarena Jumps Kangoo Rebound Dance Fitness/Aerobics Classes
description: Macarena Jumps Kangoo Rebound Club is more than a fitness class — it’s a community built on positivity, rhythm, and the pure joy of bouncing. We’ve created a space where people of all ages and fitness levels can experience the unique benefits of Kangoo Jumps: reduced joint impact, improved cardiovascular endurance, enhanced balance, and a surprising boost in mood and confidence. Our classes combine structured training with expressive movement. We teach everything from foundational bounce techniques to full choreographed routines set to upbeat music that keeps the energy high. Each session includes warm‑ups, cardio sequences, strength intervals, and cool‑downs, all designed to be safe, effective, and incredibly fun. What makes Macarena Jumps special is the atmosphere. We focus on encouragement, inclusivity, and helping every participant feel successful. Whether someone joins to get fit, relieve stress, meet new people, or simply dance in rebound boots, they’re welcomed with enthusiasm. Over time, the club has grown into a supportive community where people celebrate each other’s milestones, challenge themselves, and rediscover how enjoyable movement can be. Our mission is to inspire confidence, build strength, and create unforgettable fitness experiences — one bounce at a time :)

name: Abundance - Making the Most of our Local Harvest
description: **Do You Hate Food Waste?** Join **Abundance**, a local project that saves surplus food from gardens, allotments, and street trees. We harvest and redistribute fresh, organic produce that would otherwise go to waste—and you can help! ### How You Can Get Involved: * **Volunteer:** Spend a couple of hours outdoors picking fruit (mainly from fruit trees). We provide all the equipment. It's a great way to meet people and enjoy some of the harvest. * **Share Locations:** Let us know about trees with fruit that might go to waste. * **Take Fruit:** Collect at least 5kg of fruit (mostly apples and pears) to use yourself or share with others. * **Spread the Word:** Help us find more trees to harvest. * **Make Juice:** Join us at local events to create fresh apple juice or borrow our press to make your own. Contact us at: [abundance@ttkingston.org](mailto:abundance@ttkingston.org) or phone 07749 633973 and help save local food waste
intro: Abundance Kingston saves locally grown fruit from gardens, streets and allotments and repurposes the fruit within the community wherever it is wanted and can be used. What can't be rehomed is made into juice at local farmers markets and community events.

description: We run Infant Feeding drop in sessions every week at Children Centres and other family friendly venues, offer telephone calls or online support. name: The Sound Doctor: Dementia
description: We'll guide you on your journey from diagnosis to the later stages of dementia and explain how you can make life easier. There’s advice on how to communicate and cope with changing behaviour, how to plan ahead and manage personal and financial affairs and how to make you can live well at home for as long as possible. Some of the films may contain a small amount of information you may find upsetting but if you watch them all you'll find yourself more able to cope positively with dementia and live well with it. ### [Click here to access videos from the Dementia Film Library](https://tinyurl.com/2d65s68q), these cover: * Understanding Dementia * The Symptoms of Dementia * Discovering You Have Dementia * Planning Ahead * Caring for Someone with Dementia * Living Well with Dementia Our mission is to improve the quality of life for people with long-term mental and physical health problems by educating them, their carers and their healthcare professionals about the most effective ways of managing their conditions. Our vision is to bring practical, effective and credible information together in one place that will treat long term health as a complex and interconnected web of conditions and recognise that people with one condition may have other pressing needs. You can find [videos on a range of other long-term conditions on our services page](https://www.thesounddoctor.org/services).

name: Yoga Chill
description: Yoga Chill is a deeply restful and therapeutic class designed to help you unwind physically and mentally. This is your chance to leave your busy life at the studio door and create space to rebalance your nervous system. Through passive stretching and supported postures, your body can gently release held tension while your mind settles into stillness. Yoga Chill is suitable for absolutely everyone — all ages, all bodies, beginners and experienced practitioners alike. **Science Behind Yoga Chill** Modern life often means we are stuck in the sympathetic nervous system mode, our “always on” stress response. Yoga Chill counters this and activates the parasympathetic nervous system through the vagus nerve, shifting you to a state of calm, safety, and deeper self-regulation. It has been scientifically proven that this style of yoga has a very beneficial effect on balancing our autonomic nervous system and the way we automatically respond to stress triggers. **What to Expect** * Use of yoga props e.g. bolsters, blankets, bricks to support your body fully * Long holds in comfortable, supported positions (mainly lying down) * Gentle breath awareness and guided relaxation * Fewer postures than a regular class, with more time for each * Class content varies each week to focus on different areas of the body
intro: A chance to leave your busy life at the studio door and rebalance your nervous system. It’s a full reset for your mind and body. You will leave feeling lighter, calmer, and more connected to yourself, ready to face whatever is ahead with greater clarity and energy.
organisation: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). _relatedProvenance: Be Happy Yoga Be Happy Yoga is an award-winning, community studio offering inclusive, therapeutic yoga for every body. Rooted in community and science-informed practice, surrounded by nature, its an oasis of calm for busy living. A friendly and welcoming place where you can become physically and mentally stronger. A place that meets you wherever you’re at now – whatever your age or life stage. Are you ready to discover _your best self_? **Small Group Yoga Classes** Small group classes run throughout the week and offer: * Hatha Yoga for all levels * Men's Yoga * Gentle and Chair Yoga - based on the NHS approved Yoga4Health framework * Yoga and Pilates Fusion * Yoga Strong (yoga with weights) View the [Yoga Class Finder](https://behappyyoga.fit/yoga-for-everybody/) page to see the different classes available. There is something for every body **Private Yoga and Yoga Therapy** Private yoga classes and one to one yoga therapy for specific health conditions are also available. Most people know the benefits of yoga: reduced stress, greater flexibility, improved posture, and better sleep. Yoga therapy goes deeper. It is a medically informed, gentle and holistic practice that views an individual through the 5 layered Yoga Kosha model plus other yoga philosophy models and addresses specific health concerns with proven, targeted techniques. The most powerful part of yoga therapy is the way it can empower you to become more aware of your whole body and how you can support yourself in the future to achieve greater wellbeing. In yoga philosophy, its known as activating the Vijnanamaya kosha layer – your intuition or wisdom body. **How could Yoga Therapy help improve your wellbeing?** Yoga therapy offers a personalised approach to using the tools of yoga – gentle movement, breathwork, relaxation and meditation – to improve whole person health and support healing. Unlike a general yoga class, therapy sessions are tailored to your individual needs, whether you are living with a chronic condition, recovering from illness, or simply seeking greater balance in body and mind. Yoga therapy can support people managing: * Asthma, insomnia, and chronic fatigue * Anxiety, stress, or depression * Insomnia and disturbed sleep * Back pain, arthritis, migraines and joint issues * Digestive concerns such as IBS and heartburn * Menopause and peri-menopause symptoms * Post-cancer treatment recovery * Autoimmune conditions and chronic pain. It is particularly effective when health concerns are worsened by stress or when long-term management is needed. Read some [yoga therapy success stories](https://behappyyoga.fit/case-studies/). name: Yoga Chill
description: Yoga Chill is a deeply restful and therapeutic class designed to help you unwind physically and mentally. This is your chance to leave your busy life at the studio door and create space to rebalance your nervous system. Through passive stretching and supported postures, your body can gently release held tension while your mind settles into stillness. Yoga Chill is suitable for absolutely everyone — all ages, all bodies, beginners and experienced practitioners alike. **Science Behind Yoga Chill** Modern life often means we are stuck in the sympathetic nervous system mode, our “always on” stress response. Yoga Chill counters this and activates the parasympathetic nervous system through the vagus nerve, shifting you to a state of calm, safety, and deeper self-regulation. It has been scientifically proven that this style of yoga has a very beneficial effect on balancing our autonomic nervous system and the way we automatically respond to stress triggers. **What to Expect** * Use of yoga props e.g. bolsters, blankets, bricks to support your body fully * Long holds in comfortable, supported positions (mainly lying down) * Gentle breath awareness and guided relaxation * Fewer postures than a regular class, with more time for each * Class content varies each week to focus on different areas of the body

name: Post Abortion Support
description: Pregnancy termination affects 16.5 per 1,000 women in the United Kingdom, and while not everyone feels the need for support following an abortion, many women experience difficult emotions that may surface days, weeks, or years after the termination. We offer both group and individual support for anyone seeking healing, or the opportunity to talk through difficult emotions following an abortion, so that they can face the future with renewed hope and a positive outlook. Healing emotional hurt following an abortion is possible, and the process starts as soon as you are willing to say you would like some support. Many have already been helped to come to terms with their termination, either with one-to-one or in a group, using a sensitive recovery programme called ‘Step by Step’. If you would like to find out more about post termination support for you or someone you love, please contact us either via the email address included on this page, or by calling 020 8540 7675.

name: Kingston Eco-op
description: Kingston Eco-op is a project where vulnerable adults can socialise with a friendly and understanding community. You can develop your skills through supported learning and take part in different activities. We welcome referrals from Kingston or any of our neighbouring local authorities, NHS services or self-referrals. Our service supports adults over 18 years of age who have mild to moderate learning disabilities, mental health difficulties, are neurodiverse or are at risk of social exclusion. **Kingston Eco-op runs a variety of sessions**, including: * Arts & crafts workshop * Gardening * Drumming workshop * A walk club * Accessible cycling * Fun keep fit * Move to music * Well-being workshop * Health Club * English lessons * Maths lessons * IT lessons We collaborate and work with a number of other organisations such as Richmond and Hillcroft Community College, Wheels for All, United Response and others. Eco-op members can take part in activities and workshops as they wish. In addition to group workshops there are a variety of individual or small group activities such as playing board games, building models, jigsaw puzzles, colouring in, knitting, nail painting and more. Sometimes people just like to come to our centre to relax, soak up the atmosphere, chat to friends and staff, take part in the sessions when they feel like it and simply enjoy being in a friendly, supportive, fun community. If you have an idea for an activity or workshop, we will do what we can to help develop your interest. **We aim to:** * reduce isolation * encourage personal growth * increase skill levels * help manage personal well-being * be sociable and fun **Who is it for?** The project is open to you if you live in Kingston or the surrounding boroughs. Placements are arranged for a particular day or number of days in the week on a full or half day basis. **When?** The service runs five days a week, Monday - Friday from 9.30 - 3.30. Half day sessions are available.

name: Kingston Eco-op
description: Kingston Eco-op is a project where vulnerable adults can socialise with a friendly and understanding community. You can develop your skills through supported learning and take part in different activities. We welcome referrals from Kingston or any of our neighbouring local authorities, NHS services or self-referrals. Our service supports adults over 18 years of age who have mild to moderate learning disabilities, mental health difficulties, are neurodiverse or are at risk of social exclusion. **Kingston Eco-op runs a variety of sessions**, including: * Arts & crafts workshop * Gardening * Drumming workshop * A walk club * Accessible cycling * Fun keep fit * Move to music * Well-being workshop * Health Club * English lessons * Maths lessons * IT lessons We collaborate and work with a number of other organisations such as Richmond and Hillcroft Community College, Wheels for All, United Response and others. Eco-op members can take part in activities and workshops as they wish. In addition to group workshops there are a variety of individual or small group activities such as playing board games, building models, jigsaw puzzles, colouring in, knitting, nail painting and more. Sometimes people just like to come to our centre to relax, soak up the atmosphere, chat to friends and staff, take part in the sessions when they feel like it and simply enjoy being in a friendly, supportive, fun community. If you have an idea for an activity or workshop, we will do what we can to help develop your interest. **We aim to:** * reduce isolation * encourage personal growth * increase skill levels * help manage personal well-being * be sociable and fun **Who is it for?** The project is open to you if you live in Kingston or the surrounding boroughs. Placements are arranged for a particular day or number of days in the week on a full or half day basis. **When?** The service runs five days a week, Monday - Friday from 9.30 - 3.30. Half day sessions are available.

description: Our Gardening Thursday group meets from 10.30am until 12.30pm and includes helping with the following: * maintaining the plants in our yard and in the containers outside the Centre; * tasks include weeding, watering, dividing plants, sowing seeds etc and * helping to prepare plants for plant sales to raise funds. **Kingston Environment Centre (KEC)** This group is run by Kingston Environment Centre. who work with local individuals and environmental organisations to secure a sustainable future for Kingston Upon Thames.
